{"assignees":[],"body":"## Request (orchestrator work — changes database STRUCTURE)\n\nOwner ruling 2026-09-25 (Laura, POP licensing, relayed by Albert): WildBrain has exactly one POP Strawberry Shortcake Property, *Strawberry Shortcake Classic*. Business rule: `docs/business-rules/licensing-master-data.md` → *WildBrain Strawberry Shortcake property scope* (PR #3544). Albert asked for it to be implemented in the database and on DB Data Admin now.\n\nThe current schema cannot hold it:\n\n1. **No WildBrain Submissions vocabulary table.** Add `plm.wildbrain_submission_property_option` (same shape as `plm.sesame_submission_property_option`) and a `wildbrain-submissions` section in `api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory`. Only ONE option is to be loaded: MediaBox source id `e608bfe3-a3e2-439a-899d-dc88a59e9b58`. The other 49 captured options must not be loaded.\n2. **Resolution writer is OPA-only.** `api.db_data_admin_decide_property_match` hard-codes `disney_opa` / `plm.opa_property` members, so it cannot record: `wildbrain_tenovos | plm.wildbrain_era | 38` → mapped, and `… | 44` → mapped, both to the WildBrain submissions option above.\n3. **No \"excluded / do not ingest\" state.** Eras `41`, `42`, `43` (`wildbrain_tenovos | plm.wildbrain_era`) must be marked do-not-ingest and hidden or flagged in Scraped Properties instead of showing red as unmapped. The ledger (`plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution.creative_decision_state`) only allows mapped/unmapped/conflict.\n\nRow data (the one option row and the five decisions) will be loaded by the application session from the private repo `u2giants/licensor-source-data` (`wildbrain/creative-to-submissions-strawberry-shortcake.csv`, PR #97 there) once the shape exists. {"assignees":[],"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 3\ndepends_on: popcre/shared-db#3464\nobjects:\n  - function public.update_bulk_operation\n```\n\n## Request (follow-up to #3418 / #3464; consumer u2giants/popdam3#92, branch head 86a2e8ec)\n\nThis is a residual crash window, found by the approved exact-head review of PopDAM #92. The worker saves the applied results of a finished provider batch and then clears `external_job`, in two back-to-back writes. If the worker crashes between them, the operation keeps a terminal (applied/finished) `external_job` whose submission lease has expired. `update_bulk_operation` never re-issues a receipt for it and refuses to drop it, so the operation stays stuck for good.\n\nAdd a governed clear for exactly this state: allow clearing `external_job` when its phase is terminal (all results already applied), its lease has lapsed, and the provider batch ID is bound and recorded as finished. Keep every other protection: no clearing of live (prepared/submitting/pending/applying) jobs, no clearing of ambiguous jobs, a revision match, and no receipt remint for live work.\n\nBehavior tests: terminal+expired clears once; live phases refuse; ambiguous refuses; wrong revision refuses; a second clear is a no-op.\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABXVfukQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"<!-- ai-blocker-watch:unowned:popcre/shared-db#3543 -->\nThis open issue blocks u2giants/popdam3#92 and has gone 54h with no owner: no assignee, no `owner:` line, no open linked pull request, no activity.\nTake it (assign yourself, or add an `owner:` line naming who owns it) or hand it to a named queue owner. Listed in today's ai-blocker-watch digest. {"assignees":[],"body":"## Owner request (Albert Hazan, this chat, 2026-09-25), verbatim\n\n> pixar is part of disney and should not be its own licensor.\n> if something was scraped from disney_dcpvault, or lucas_dcpvault, or marvel_dcpvault, why is 'Licensor not yet determined'? IT SAYS IT IN THE VERY SOURCE SYSTEM NAME!\n\n## Structural change required (orchestrator work — changes a database function)\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nservice_class: standard-application\nchange_type: migration\napplication_return_to: u2giants/popdam3\nlive_assertion: authenticated production page check shows Disney grouping for Pixar and zero *_dcpvault rows in Licensor not yet determined\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\npriority: 5\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory\n```\n\nObject: `api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory(text,text,text,integer)` (current body from migration 20260917144950), all three entity branches (property, character, style_guide).\n\n1. **Pixar belongs to Disney.** Every row whose `licensor_key` is `pixar` or `pixar-opa` returns `licensor_group_key = 'disney'`, `licensor_group_name = 'Disney'`. Section labels say Disney (Pixar may remain as the portal/brand in parentheses). `licensor_key` and `row_key` stay unchanged so paging cursors stay stable.\n2. **DCP Vault licensor comes from the source system.** A row from `source_system` `disney_dcpvault` groups to Disney, `marvel_dcpvault` to Marvel, `lucasfilm_dcpvault` to Lucasfilm / Star Wars — regardless of mapping authority status. Authority/mapping conflicts may still be shown as a row status or mapping state, but must never move the row into \"Licensor not yet determined\". This supersedes the #2905 rule that sent unresolved-authority DCP rows and `plm.marvel_dcp_property` \"non-authoritative Marvel tag\" rows to the `unresolved` group.\n3. Update `docs/db-data-admin-scraped-properties.md` (Canonical licensor grouping section) to state both rules.\n\nLive counts (production, read-only, 2026-09-25): `plm.dcp_property` 237 rows all `disney_dcpvault`; `plm.marvel_dcp_property` 18 rows `marvel_dcpvault`; `plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property` 70 rows `lucasfilm_dcpvault`.\n\n## Acceptance\n- No section named Pixar; Pixar rows appear under Disney.\n- Zero rows with source_system `*_dcpvault` in the \"Licensor not yet determined\" group, in all three entity kinds.\n- Preview proof, PR, merge, production promotion, authenticated production page check.\n\n## Separate finding, no DB change here\nStrawberry Shortcake Submissions: no Submissions scrape exists in any Supabase project or in `u2giants/licensor-source-data` (its WildBrain submissions-hunt handoff of 2026-08-20 is still OPEN). {"assignees":[],"body":"## HANDOVER from u2giants/popdam3#107 — PopSG nightly refresh_style_guide_matviews still times out on change nights\n\n### Problem\n#3023 (PR #3118) did not end the PopSG nightly refresh failures. Production evidence (`public.style_guide_crawl_runs`): every night with a real library change (deactivations or new files) times out with `canceling statement due to statement timeout`, run left in `lifecycle_state = reconciling`. Only no-change nights pass.\n\nThe caller (popdam3 `supabase/functions/agent-api/index.ts`, `complete-style-guide-crawl`) makes one RPC call with `p_search_batch_size=5000`. Inside that one statement, the function runs `refresh materialized view concurrently` on both `style_guide_file_groups` and `style_guide_folders`, then syncs the search documents. That goes past the 8 s authenticator ceiling.\n\n### Required outcome\nKeep the refresh plus search sync under the normal statement ceiling on a change night, with no timeout increase. Options: split the two matview refreshes and the search sync into separately callable steps (the caller already loops on `search_documents_synced`), or make the concurrent refresh incremental. If the RPC contract changes, name the new caller contract so popdam3 can adapt after the merge.\n\n### Acceptance\nA production crawl with more than 0 deactivations or new files reaches `completed`. Blocks popdam3 u2giants/popdam3#107.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 2\nservice_class: standard-application\nchange_type: public.refresh_style_guide_matviews\nreads:\n```\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on {"assignees":[],"body":"## HANDOVER from u2giants/popdam3#97 â€” semantic score floor for PopDAM hybrid search\n\n**Requesting app:** PopDAM (u2giants/popdam3#97, \"Finish and safely enable PopDAM hybrid search\").\n\n### Problem (verified read-only against production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, 2026-09-23)\n`public.search_dam_documents(text,jsonb,int,int,text[],extensions.vector(384),real)` exposes only `p_min_rank` applied to the **blended** rank. PopDAM needs a real floor on the **semantic leg only** before it can enable hybrid mode.\n\n### Minimal contract\n1. Add trailing optional `p_min_semantic_score real default null` (new signature with 8 args). Drop the old 7-arg signature in the same migration. Re-grant execute to `authenticated, service_role`. Return columns unchanged.\n2. Apply the floor inside `semantic_candidates` only: `where ... and (p_min_semantic_score is null or greatest(0,1-(d.embedding <=> p_query_embedding)) >= p_min_semantic_score)`, clamped to [0,1] in `params`.\n3. Keyword hits with below-floor semantic score survive with `semantic_rank = null`.\n4. `total_count`, `has_more`, facets and offset/limit ordering remain server-side from the same filtered set.\n5. `p_min_rank` keeps current meaning (blended rank, default 0); `null` floor = today's behaviour.\n\n### Behaviour tests (preview, required before merge)\nT1 null floor identical to current function. T2 keyword-only survives. T3 semantic-only removal. T4 mixed doc keyword + below-floor semantic. T5 pagination exactness. T6 floor=1 no keyword match â†’ zero rows; floor=0 â‰¡ null. T7 no embedding â†’ floor has no effect. T8 old 7-arg signature gone; grants on new one.\n\n### Consumer follow-up (not in this issue)\nAfter merge PopDAM will read `admin_config.SEARCH_MIN_SEMANTIC_SCORE` in `supabase/functions/dam-search-ai` (tracked in u2giants/popdam3#97). Do not ship the rejected client-side experiment branch `codex/issue-97-search-score`.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 3\nservice_class: standard-application\nchange_type: function\napplication_return_to: u2giants/popdam3\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\nlive_assertion: On production, public.search_dam_documents has the 8-arg signature with p_min_semantic_score real default null, the 7-arg signature is dropped, execute is granted to authenticated and service_role only, a semantic floor is applied only inside the semantic leg before blend, and null floor preserves prior blended-rank behaviour exactly.\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function public.search_dam_documents\n  - function public.search_assets_full_text\n  - function public.search_style_groups_full_text\nreads:\n```\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on {"assignees":[{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","login":"u2giants","name":"","databaseId":55610577}],"body":"## Goal\nProvide a governed, target-specific migration route for the separate DesignFlow sandbox Supabase project so structural issue #2204 can be rehearsed and verified there without treating shared preview or shared production as that sandbox.\n\n## Verified blocker (2026-09-23)\n- `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml` accepts only `target: preview` or `target: production`; both target different projects.\n- This repository exposes only preview and production deployment environments and database-password secret names. No sandbox apply credential is configured here.\n- Sandbox has no `app.user_notification.created_at`, lacks ledger version `20260905072856`, and already has `app.user_notification.user_notification_unread_user_created_idx` on `(user_id_fk, created_date DESC) WHERE unread = true`. The merged migration's `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` cannot replace that conflicting definition.\n- PR #3341 for #2986 adds read-only sandbox drift observation; it does not provide an apply lane and remains open.\n\n## Required result\nCreate a separate fail-closed sandbox route with a verified target identity, least-privilege credential provisioned through the approved secret path, explicit migration-version allowlist, exact main/source-PR binding, fresh ledger and catalog preflight, serial target lock, dry-run, independently reviewed apply evidence, and post-apply catalog/index/ledger proof. It must refuse missing target/credentials and any name collision before writing. Reuse the existing guarded components where their invariants hold; do not expand production or shared-preview targets. The structural forward repair for #2204 remains with its orchestrator issue and protected author lane. Do not apply migration `20260905072856` to sandbox as-is.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: ci\nreturn_to: popcre/shared-db\nwrites:\nreads: sandbox migration ledger, app.user_notification catalog/index definitions\n```\n\nowner: u2giants (repository-maintenance queue; coordinate with current orchestrator marker before sandbox dispatch)\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0cb03-daa2-79d2-85fd-6a8904abfc53 on EDGE-DEV","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABWUCGyA","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Read-only route audit on current `main` `57c2c3079` (2026-09-23): no sandbox migration was dispatched or applied.\n\n- The existing dispatch offers only `preview` and `production` (`.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml:13-17`). Its single non-PR serialization group covers those targets (`:121-127`), but the migration author lanes define no distinct sandbox apply lock (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:739-755,8883-8884`). Do not reuse the preview or production lock as proof of sandbox exclusivity.\n- The production migration guard records `designflow-nonprod` for classification, but its allowlist rejects migrations targeted away from production (`scripts/production_migration_guard.py:296-321,1034-1075`). Atomic apply accepts only preview/production (`scripts/atomic_migration_apply.py:97-99,278-280`). Adding a third workflow input alone would bypass or break these gates.\n- GitHub has only `preview` and `production` deployment environments, no sandbox project variable, and no sandbox database-password secret. A private vault item for the DesignFlow non-production project exists, but its least-privilege status is unverified and it has not been copied or provisioned to GitHub. The currently configured Supabase access token was used by #3341 for read-only observation, not qualified as an apply credential.\n- Existing bounded checkout, exact-main/source-PR checks, dry-run, pinned review artifact, and post-apply verification can be adapted; a separate sandbox route still needs a verified sandbox ref, approved least-privilege secret path, sandbox-specific allowlist and lock, collision-safe catalog preflight, and target-bound evidence before any write. The same-name `app.user_notification` index mismatch means migration `20260905072856` must not be applied there unchanged.\n\nIssue #3428 remains open as a non-orchestrator repository-maintenance blocker for structural #2204. No source or target state was changed.\r\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0cd3b-50a4-7810-a590-cbf5ae1ace7f on EDGE-DEV\r\n","createdAt":"2026-09-23T09:28:43Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3428#issuecomment-5792368328","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABW1QRdQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"repo-maintenance/documentation (marker #3496): a repo session owns this — left open, not orchestrator work. Slot 2 Muse sequence 3548 already recorded a durable APPROVE. The sanctioned slot 1 replacement then drew Muse again as sequence 3554 because replacement selection excludes slot 1 when filling slot 2, but does not exclude occupied slot 2 when refilling slot 1. The review was not run. Two approvals from one provider must never satisfy the independent-review gate.\n\nRepair assignment and replacement symmetrically for every live exact-head slot; fail closed on idempotent retries of conflicting durable records and at the exact-head approval gate. Provide a guarded, immutable, slot-specific conflict recovery that releases only the erroneous assignment and its lease, records the true allocation defect rather than a provider failure, and redraws a different provider while preserving the valid slot 2 verdict. Test adversarial slot ordering, retries, and unchanged production safety gates. {"assignees":[{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","login":"u2giants","name":"","databaseId":55610577}],"body":"owner: shared-db orchestrator queue\r\n\r\n## What\r\n\r\nAdd a stored, extracted **product phrase** to items and RFQ items, so HTS classification does not re-derive it on every run.\r\n\r\nWhy: CBP CROSS search ANDs every query token. Sending a full item description (licensor, property, artwork, colorway, finish, size, pack count, style code) returns zero rulings. The classifier needs the bare article + material phrase, e.g. \"MDF lap desk\". Today nothing stores it.\r\n\r\n## Structure change requested\r\n\r\nSchema `dflow` (the schema the app runs on).\r\n\r\n**`dflow.\"itemHeader\"`** — add:\r\n- `hts_product_phrase` `text NULL` — extracted article + material phrase, lowercase, no brand/licensor/artwork/size/pack tokens.\r\n- `hts_product_phrase_source` `text NULL` — how it was produced (`ai`, `manual`, `import`).\r\n- `hts_product_phrase_at` `timestamptz NULL` — when it was produced.\r\n\r\n**`dflow.\"RFQItem\"`** — add the same three columns.\r\n\r\nNo defaults, no NOT NULL, no backfill in the migration — the application fills them (see linked DesignFlow issue). No index needed initially; these are read by primary key alongside the row.\r\n\r\nSource descriptions the extractor reads (for reference, unchanged by this ticket):\r\n- `dflow.\"itemHeader\".item_descr_name` / `item_displ_descr_name`\r\n- `dflow.\"RFQItem\".rfqItem_description`\r\n\r\nNote: this is unrelated to the existing merch-group `productTypeId` hierarchy; that is a taxonomy key, this is free text for ruling search. {"assignees":[],"body":"owner: Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n\nSplit out of #3346, which is now resolved operationally. The outage in #3346 was **not** caused by a namespace past its ceiling — it was a transient read failure reported with the wrong words, and that misreporting cost a session an hour and produced a wrong root-cause diagnosis.\n\n## The defect\n\n`findBusyReviewers` (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`) fails open with a bare `return null` in **six** places: the `io.readRef` capability check, the cutover read, the lease snapshot read, the per-ref `readRef`, the `getCommit`/`parseReviewLease` parse, the `readReviewStates` read, and the per-lease `getPr` read. Every caller then reports the same sentence:\n\n```\nactive reviewer leases are unreadable; <operation> refused\n```\n\nThe code already carries `markReviewRefListingRefusal` / `isReviewRefListingRefusal` so a *determinate* listing refusal survives with its prefix and row count. Nothing equivalent exists for the ordinary transient path, so an HTTP 5xx, a secondary rate limit, an occupied `refs/db-coordination/author-acquisition` mutex and a genuinely malformed lease ref are all indistinguishable at the caller, and the message names a namespace that may be entirely healthy.\n\nObserved live on 2026-09-20: `--archive-old-review-verdicts --apply-recovery` refused once with `REFUSED: refs/db-coordination/author-acquisition is occupied` and succeeded on the next attempt 45s later — exactly the class of transient that the fail-open catches turn into \"unreadable\".\n\n## What is needed\n\n1. Carry the underlying cause on the refusal: which read failed, which ref, and the transport error, the way the listing-refusal path already does.\n2. Distinguish transient (retryable, name the retry) from determinate (name the retirement command) in the message itself.\n3. Do not weaken the fail-closed behaviour — every current `return null` must still refuse; only the wording changes.\n\nCheck whether PR #3338 (`fix(reviewer): fail fast before a draw, and front-load the probe checklist`) already covers part of this before starting.\n\n## Serialization note\n\n`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` is a protected coordination source with twelve open PRs contending for it as of 2026-09-20. This work should land behind that queue, not jump it. Recommended landing order is recorded on #3346.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\n```\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0c07c-44cf-7f23-ae21-d401319ac5ed on 916-ALIEN\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABW1Qxiw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"repo-maintenance/documentation (marker #3496): a repo session owns this — left open, not orchestrator work. Posted by MiMo chat unknown on edge-dev","createdAt":"2026-09-25T05:17:21Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3349#issuecomment-5827211659","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABW3R_Nw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"**Still not fixed on origin/main at `33d5ec0d000552b204fbc2dbaae10ca2d5784c1c` (2026-09-25). Leaving open.**\n\nChecked against live `main`. `findBusyReviewers` (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, from line 5127) still fail-opens with bare `return null` at every site named in this issue — the `io.readRef` capability check, the cutover read, the lease snapshot read, the per-ref `readRef`, the `getCommit`/`parseReviewLease` parse, the `readReviewStates` read, and the per-lease `getPr` read. Callers still emit the generic sentence:\n\n```\nactive reviewer leases are unreadable; <operation> refused\n```\n\nat `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:5407`, `:5557`, `:5606`, `:5627`, `:5944`, `:6568`, `:6631` — with no cause, no ref, and no transient/determinate distinction.\n\n**What PR #3338 did cover** (and what it did not): it isolated the *determinate* listing-refusal path (`markReviewRefListingRefusal` / `isReviewRefListingRefusal`) so a row-ceiling or paginated refusal survives with its own message. That is a different path from the ordinary transient fail-open this issue is about. PR #3338 does not close this.\n\n**What is still needed** (unchanged from the issue body):\n1. Carry the underlying cause — which read, which ref, and the transport error — the way the listing-refusal path already does.\n2. Distinguish transient (retryable, name the retry) from determinate (name the retirement command) in the message itself.\n3. {"assignees":[{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","login":"u2giants","name":"","databaseId":55610577}],"body":"## Outcome\r\n\r\nBounded structural successor to #1275 (orchestrator work): let the existing Disney DCP metadata loader atomically publish property/character lifecycle after a qualified full capture. Retained captures and source relationships remain immutable. Missing identities are marked, never deleted; reappearance preserves first-seen and first-withdrawal history. This does not implement delta-only ingestion or canonical licensing changes.\r\n\r\nowner: Codex chat 01a0bf82-feca-7351-b6d2-bc6021a2fc9c on 916-ALIEN, coordinated by root orchestrator marker #3297.\r\n\r\n## Verified starting point\r\n\r\nOn 2026-09-20 production target qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai was proved using supabase_read_only_user with transaction_read_only=on. Both retained DCP metadata runs are complete with failed fetches; zero complete zero-failure baselines exist. Property/character identities retain first/last metadata-run references. Existing metadata migrations and the earlier DCP asset lifecycle migration are applied.\r\n\r\nThe current completion contract intentionally permits recorded terminal fetch failures. Preserve that evidence-only capability. The existing finalizer performs running-to-complete publication; completed runs cannot subsequently be edited. Existing caller: u2giants/licensor-source-data, disney-dcpvault/scripts/load-collected-to-supabase.mjs. Its begin/load/finalize call path will receive a separately owned application integration.\r\n\r\n## Approved engineering boundary\r\n\r\nReuse existing tables and begin/load/finalize functions. No new parallel publisher or identity table. Add explicit opt-in disabled/bootstrap/full-comparable lifecycle mode, qualified baseline/coverage provenance and aggregate publication results to the run. Entity lifecycle starts unqualified, never positively active from historical or unqualified observations. Bootstrap activates only observed qualified identities; untouched historical identities remain unqualified. Preserve first/current withdrawal history.\r\n\r\nLegacy callers retain evidence-only completion. Bootstrap never withdraws. Comparable publication requires a current qualified same-scope baseline, full authenticated exhaustive source coverage, zero failed metadata fetches, no unresolved gaps (including waived gaps), immutable scope/derivation provenance and a serialized finalization transaction. A caller-supplied boolean is not proof of authenticated coverage: the owning loader must bind privately retained evidence to the run and validate it before requesting publication.\r\n\r\nWithdrawals greater than min(2% of baseline active entities,100) refuse per entity type. This is an approved engineering safety choice, not an owner business ruling; independent review must verify exact arithmetic and boundary behavior.\r\n\r\nFix the whole concurrency class: chunk loading and finalization share locking and re-read run status after acquiring it. Prevent stale-baseline/out-of-order publication. Preserve all source observations, identity keys, first sightings, legacy resolution guards, term-guard behavior, grants/RLS and hardened search paths. No core writes, media content, studio-sibling changes, or inferred property-character relationships.\r\n\r\n## Required verification\r\n\r\nPreview tests: zero-withdrawal bootstrap; qualified disappearance; unchanged reappearance; immutable first history; failed/signed-out/not-found/rejected fetch refusal; scope/authentication/derivation mismatch; unresolved or waived-gap refusal; empty scope; threshold equality and first failing boundary; stale baseline; concurrent chunks/finalizers; atomic rollback; legacy completion compatibility; unchanged source/resolution freezes and access restrictions.\r\n\r\nGenerated types are required and must match the final contract. Actual source-backed live proof returns to the private loader repository. It must execute new qualified full captures through the production loader, reconcile lifecycle counters to retained observations, and prove failed-fetch runs cannot publish. Current retained captures are not eligible baselines. If source data supplies no disappearance/reappearance, retain that limitation explicitly: preview proves those branches; live execution proves authenticated integration. Do not substitute a catalog-only check for the live assertion.\r\n\r\n## Admission status\r\n\r\nBlocked until exact column/constraint/index/trigger claims and the private loader qualification contract are finalized and root allocates the lane. Global queue repair #3313 is non-orchestrator work and is tracked separately; no claims, versions, migrations or database writes are authorized by this issue creation. The root approved the bounded design, not immediate schema execution. Do not close parent #1275 for this one successor.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: blocked\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\nservice_class: standard-application\r\nchange_type: table\r\napplication_return_to: u2giants/licensor-source-data\r\nlive_assertion: the private DCP loader publishes fresh qualified full metadata captures in production with lifecycle counters reconciled to retained observations and immutable first history, while failed-fetch or incomparable runs cannot publish lifecycle\r\ngenerated_types: required\r\npriority: 580\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table plm.dcp_metadata_run\r\n  - table plm.dcp_property\r\n  - table plm.dcp_character\r\n  - function plm.begin_dcp_metadata_run\r\n  - function plm.load_dcp_metadata_chunk\r\n  - function plm.finalize_dcp_metadata_run\r\n  - function plm.dcp_metadata_run_freeze\r\n  - function plm.dcp_reject_completed_metadata_identity_change\n  - trigger trg_dcp_metadata_run_freeze on plm.dcp_metadata_run\n  - trigger trg_dcp_property_source_immutable on plm.dcp_property\n  - trigger trg_dcp_character_source_immutable on plm.dcp_character\n  - index plm.idx_dcp_metadata_run_lifecycle_publication\n  - index plm.dcp_metadata_run_lifecycle_bootstrap_uk\r\nreads:\r\n  - table plm.dcp_crawl\r\n  - table plm.dcp_crawl_section\r\n  - table plm.dcp_crawl_gap\r\n  - table plm.dcp_asset_crawl\r\n  - table plm.dcp_portal_tile\r\n  - table plm.dcp_metadata_asset\r\n  - table plm.dcp_metadata_chunk_ledger\r\n  - table plm.dcp_metadata_load_exception\r\n  - table plm.dcp_asset_property_observation\r\n  - table plm.dcp_asset_character_observation\r\n  - table plm.dcp_term\r\n```\r\n\r\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf82-feca-7351-b6d2-bc6021a2fc9c on 916-ALIEN\r\n\r\n\n## Exact design revision — root-approved guards\n\nThe three named existing triggers gain INSERT coverage; preserve their UPDATE/DELETE behavior, legacy resolution guards and the term branch. All inserts start unqualified with no fabricated qualified lifecycle history. The initial implementation permits one qualified account/scope stream because source identities are global; a different stream refuses rather than withdrawing another account's identities.\n\nChronology uses capture-produced UTC start/end timestamps bound to the immutable private manifest. Require start < finish and current start >= baseline finish. Reject overlapping or older captures. Never substitute database execution time, a caller boolean or private commit ordering. Any future overlap exception needs a separately reviewed comparability rule.\n\nExact additions to plm.dcp_metadata_run: lifecycle_mode; lifecycle_baseline_metadata_run_id; lifecycle_scope_sha256; lifecycle_contract_sha256; lifecycle_evidence_sha256; lifecycle_capture_started_at; lifecycle_capture_finished_at; lifecycle_published_at; lifecycle_counts.\n\nExact additions to each of plm.dcp_property and plm.dcp_character: lifecycle_status (unqualified|active|withdrawn, default unqualified); withdrawn_at; first_withdrawn_at; lifecycle_metadata_run_id. Preserve existing first_seen_metadata_run_id and last_seen_metadata_run_id as source observations, not qualification pointers.\n\nExact new run constraints: dcp_metadata_run_lifecycle_mode_chk, dcp_metadata_run_lifecycle_baseline_fk, dcp_metadata_run_lifecycle_contract_chk, dcp_metadata_run_lifecycle_chronology_chk, dcp_metadata_run_lifecycle_publication_chk, dcp_metadata_run_lifecycle_counts_chk. Exact new per-entity constraints are dcp_property_lifecycle_status_chk, dcp_property_lifecycle_run_fk, dcp_property_lifecycle_history_chk, dcp_character_lifecycle_status_chk, dcp_character_lifecycle_run_fk, dcp_character_lifecycle_history_chk. These are alterations of the already claimed owning tables; the scope parser has no standalone constraint kind. The two new indexes and three existing trigger replacements are explicitly listed in writes.\n\nPrivate loader contract v1 is now defined as a reviewable draft: capture-produced UTC interval and immutable manifest; authenticated preflight/postflight receipts bound to origin/account scope; exhaustive preplanned scope and terminal listing receipts; exact zero-failure metadata membership; digest-bound extractor interpretation; immutable private source commit; content-hash and path-safety verification; matching SQL/loader scope digest test vectors; mode/baseline-aware resume; nonzero failure on qualification refusal. No retrospective authentication or chronology evidence may be invented for historical captures. The database validates stored membership and relational provenance; it does not pretend that accepting a digest authenticates a browser.\n\nImplementation remains blocked pending root allocation, independent review of the exact contract, and a named private-loader implementation owner. No claim, version, source edit or SQL mutation has occurred.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf82-feca-7351-b6d2-bc6021a2fc9c on 916-ALIEN\r\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABVtujKQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Owner instruction from the current chat: do not contact Disney. The vendor-inquiry draft was never sent; no Disney outreach is authorized, and no recipient or contact approval is requested.\n\nAuthentication is working, but the inspected supported surface has not established comparable effective visibility across captures. Missing assets must not be classified as withdrawn without qualifying evidence. Keep that acceptance requirement intact and pursue only existing supported evidence; do not silently substitute positive-only capture as completion of this outcome.\n\nowner: Codex chat 01a0bf00-fa7b-73d1-b447-fc4c89c50b96\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf00-fa7b-73d1-b447-fc4c89c50b96 on 916-ALIEN\r\n","createdAt":"2026-09-20T19:44:35Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3347#issuecomment-5752202025","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABWO_79A","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Private DCP producer owner: Codex chat 01a0cba0-3480-7170-95da-08470a39c199 on 916-ALIEN. The private output location and authenticated DCP content were verified. The current 44 navigation sections match the prior private plan; fail-closed source parsing and durable capture components are being integrated. No full qualified two-pass capture, comparable baseline, or production publication is claimed.\n\nPlease assign the structural author and independent contract reviewer for the configured-scope digest, SQL/loader test vectors, and lifecycle admission. Keep this issue blocked until those gates and the private live evidence pass. No Disney outreach is authorized or needed; no licensed rows are included here.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0cba0-3480-7170-95da-08470a39c199 on 916-ALIEN","createdAt":"2026-09-23T00:52:28Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3347#issuecomment-5787089908","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABW0pvjQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Disney withdrawal communication — answer received\n\n**Date received:** 2026-09-25\n**Speaker:** Ilona (business; one of the named Licensing reviewers)\n**Relayed by:** Albert Hazan, from a direct conversation (quotation of Ilona)\n**Form:** Direct quotation, not paraphrase.\n\n**Question:** When artwork disappears from DCP Vault, what notice or status do you use to confirm that Disney withdrew it?\n\n**Answer (quoted):**\n> There is usually not a notice that gets sent out unless it's a huge change.\n> The style guide image will say \"UPDATED\" – it is up to us to notice what got removed & then we manually remove it.\n> Or: The style guide specifically has a sunset date already from the moment it's created.\n\n**Business meaning:**\n1. Disney usually sends **no formal withdrawal notice**. A notice is the exception for a huge change, not the normal path.\n2. The normal operational signal is a style-guide image marked **\"UPDATED\"**. POP must notice the removal itself and then manually remove the corresponding item. Confirmation of withdrawal is therefore observation of that UPDATED removal plus our manual action — not a letter.\n3. Alternate path: the style guide carries a **sunset date from creation**. That pre-existing date is the withdrawal signal.\n\n**Limits preserved:** This is Ilona's report of how the team works with Disney's portal. It is not a Disney written policy document. It does not authorize treating mere portal absence as withdrawal, and it is not a legal-rights determination. Disappearance, confirmed vendor withdrawal, and legal rights remain separate facts.\n\n**What this settles for #3347:** The open business question of \"what notice or status confirms withdrawal\" is answered: there is usually no notice; the qualifying signals are a style-guide UPDATED removal (observed and manually actioned) or a pre-existing sunset date. Technical capture-qualification gates on this issue are unchanged and still need their own proofs. Independent producer work continues on its own route.\n\n**Not the licensing identity worksheet** (issues #1941 / #2601). Those remain separate.\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on edge-dev","createdAt":"2026-09-25T04:12:55Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3347#issuecomment-5826572173","viewerDidAuthor":true}],"createdAt":"2026-09-20T16:20:18Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. Its STATUS table will track each independently verifiable step. This tracker is a progress index, not a dependency that applications must wait on. Implementation issues retain their own owners and scope; no migration objects are claimed here.\n\nReuse existing work after refreshing its live status: #2708, #2832, #2824, #2596, #2836, #3002, #3273, #2530 and #2923 (all non-orchestrator work). Completed #3199 and #3027 (non-orchestrator work) are implementation references, not work to repeat.\n\nAcceptance: each plan step has its own merged implementation or evidence-backed policy disposition and required live proof; final measurements preserve safety and explicitly report insufficient samples rather than claiming an unmeasured improvement. A successor must explicitly accept ownership before performing the implementation; do not dispatch this tracker to the structural orchestrator.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 60\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf54-3c7d-7872-aeb9-142c4a73c0f2 on 916-ALIEN\n\n## Ordered audit track for comprehensive current-state analysis\n\nTake the first unticked child below, do only that one, tick it when its acceptance is proven, comment on this parent with the next child, and stop. This ordered audit track does not pause independently owned implementation already in progress and is not an application dependency. Add further child issues only after the audit identifies a verified gap; reuse existing implementation issues instead of duplicating them.\n\n- [ ] #3597 — comprehensive delivery audit and refactor-plan reconciliation (non-orchestrator work; first child).\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0e5c8-89f4-7832-a193-9f1591f7b0cc on edge-dev3\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABVsVL8A","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Planning publication is complete on branch codex/orchestrator-workflow-refactor-plan at bcdfa53e31768c3fd2a1632e2015358f778243ed, PR #3318 (non-orchestrator repository-maintenance work). Self-audit and independent exact-head planning review passed; focused documentation/handoff tests passed.\n\nPlan: https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/blob/codex/orchestrator-workflow-refactor-plan/plan_shared_db_workflow_refactor.md\n\nPublication-to-main blocker, owned by this session: after independently confirming that all five changed files are Markdown and the repository classifier reported \"all 5 changed file(s) are lightweight prose documents\", the authorized prose-only command `gh pr merge 3318 --squash --admin --match-head-commit bcdfa53e31768c3fd2a1632e2015358f778243ed` was refused by GitHub:\n\n> GraphQL: 13 of 13 required status checks have not succeeded: 1 expected. (mergePullRequest)\n\nRead-only protection inspection confirmed enforce_admins=true, despite this identity having admin permission. No settings or protections were changed. {"assignees":[],"body":"owner: shared-db.orch Codex chat 01a0cb03-daa2-79d2-85fd-6a8904abfc53 on EDGE-DEV (current marker #3405; re-resolve on handover)\r\n\r\n## Qualification hold (updated 2026-09-23)\r\n\r\nThis issue remains blocked. Exact global NOLOGIN role collision accounting is tracked by #3398 (non-orchestrator repository maintenance). The newer locked owner and independent reviewer ruling at https://github.com/u2giants/poppim-web/issues/9#issuecomment-5788297664 sets pilot-v1 writes to administrator-only for comments, dependency/decision/reminder records, and Jev accept/dismiss. Sales, licensing, and designer grants are deferred to a later evaluated release and a separate governed shared-db change. The prior owner-matrix request here is superseded for pilot v1; no new owner role-matrix question is required.\r\n\r\nThe current PM plan has expanded beyond this issue's preliminary writes list: it includes comment body revision/trigger, reservation and eligibility ledgers, additional claim/fence/impression/evaluation/cutoff RPCs, and a separately deployed app-owned Deno gateway. Before any structural claim, reconcile the exact objects and contract against the current plan and administrator-only pilot boundary. No role, migration version, preview, or production action is authorized by this note.\r\n\r\n## Why\r\n\r\nPoppim issue u2giants/poppim-web#9 proposes a human-confirmed Jev pilot that classifies newly posted product comments as routine updates, blockers/dependencies, decisions, or follow-up reminders. The browser must never hold the provider credential, Jev must never create business records automatically, and ordinary non-admin staff must work through least-privilege database contracts.\r\n\r\nThe current direct inserts are not a safe foundation: `app.comment.created_by_profile_id` has no default, and the generic `app.comment`, `app.activity`, and `app.notification` write policies are administrator-only. The pilot also needs atomic idempotency, rate limiting, review outcome recording, and exactly-once acceptance without broadening table grants.\r\n\r\n## Requested structural contract\r\n\r\n1. Add `pim.ai_activity_triage` for redacted provider/result metadata only. It must never store comment text, product title, email, URL, customer/licensor name, credential, or other raw prompt data.\r\n2. Add a unique idempotency key covering comment, normalized-input hash, exact model, and contract version; bounded indexes for caller/review lookups; checks for states and closed labels.\r\n3. Add narrow RLS so a signed-in PM user can read only triage rows they requested and administrators can audit. Direct browser insert/update/delete remains denied.\r\n4. Add `api.pm_add_product_comment(...)` to require an active profile, PM app access, role `administrator` for pilot v1, and caller-readable product; deny viewer/vendor/anonymous; trim and require 1â€“4,000 characters; allow tab/newline but reject NUL and other control characters; insert with `created_by_profile_id` and return the row.\r\n5. Add `api.pm_begin_activity_triage(...)` to repeat those independent checks, require caller-authored comment on the same product, atomically return an existing result or create/lease one attempt, and enforce a per-profile rolling request limit without a read-then-insert race. The lease has a random token and expiry; fresh leases cannot be stolen.\r\n6. Add signed `api.pm_complete_activity_triage(...)` and `api.pm_fail_activity_triage(...)` wrappers callable under the original caller JWT. They derive the actor from `auth.uid()`, require that actor to remain the row requester, verify an HMAC-SHA-256 canonical envelope using an environment-specific secret read only by the definer from Supabase Vault, and close only the matching current lease. The private implementation is owned by a dedicated NOLOGIN role with rights only on the triage table/functions; authenticated callers cannot execute it directly. Permit stale takeover after at least two provider timeouts; reject late completion from the old lease. This requires no service-role key or custom token issuer.\r\n7. Add `api.pm_get_activity_triage(...)` so the owning user can recover an unreviewed result after tab/product changes or reload.\r\n8. Add Jev-independent `api.pm_create_dependency(...)`, `api.pm_create_decision(...)`, `api.pm_create_reminder(...)`, `api.pm_update_dependency_status(...)`, and `api.pm_update_reminder_status(...)`. They enforce the same active-profile/PM-access/staff-role/readable-product checks and exact field allowlists below. Existing manual Operations UI will use these RPCs whether Jev is on or off, so rollback never depends on a triage row.\r\n9. Add `api.pm_accept_activity_triage(...)` and `api.pm_dismiss_activity_triage(...)`. Re-authorize active profile, PM access, allowed staff role, caller-readable product/business unit, and stored actionable label independently of comment ownership. The client cannot choose department or action kind. Field contract: dependency title 1â€“200 with fixed `blocked_by/open` and no related product; decision type 1â€“100 and notes â‰¤2,000 with fixed `decided`; reminder title 1â€“200, valid optional due date, current caller, fixed `open/follow_up`. Acceptance must lock the triage row, invoke the same validated creation path as the non-AI RPCs, create exactly one record, and mark the outcome in the same transaction. Retry after an ambiguous response returns the original record.\r\n10. Revoke function execution from public/anonymous roles and grant only the exact authenticated wrappers required. Revoke direct execution on private worker functions. Preserve existing table policies; do not add broad table writes or a LOGIN role.\r\n\r\nThe app-owned Edge Function source and deployment stay in `poppim-web`; this issue owns only shared database shape and preview/prod migration evidence.\r\n\r\n## Acceptance evidence\r\n\r\n- Preview migration and rollback rehearsal pass.\r\n- Direct-RPC comment tests reject empty/whitespace, over 4,000 characters, NUL/control characters, invalid product, and oversized request values before insertion.\r\n- The pilot-v1 administrator can post through the RPC, owns the recorded author profile, begins/retrieves its own triage row, and accepts/dismisses once against separately tested Licensed, Generic, and Software products. Sales/licensing/designer/viewer/vendor/anonymous are denied for pilot-v1 writes.\r\n- A different signed-in user cannot read or mutate that row; product/business-unit access is rechecked at acceptance.\r\n- Concurrent begin calls produce one logical row/active lease; stale takeover works after expiry and late old-worker completion fails; concurrent/retried accept calls produce one business record.\r\n- Signed completion/failure rejects missing, malformed, expired, replayed, wrong-actor, wrong-lease, or wrong-environment envelopes; its NOLOGIN owner cannot read or write unrelated application rows.\r\n- Existing comment and operating-record behavior remains green.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: blocked\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\nservice_class: standard-application\r\nchange_type: migration\r\napplication_return_to: u2giants/poppim-web\r\nlive_assertion: After the administrator-only pilot-v1 contract and app handback, authenticated PM administrators can post comments and accept one actionable triage suggestion exactly once; non-admin and anonymous users cannot write through these RPCs or read or mutate another user's triage row; manual operations work with Jev off.\r\ngenerated_types: required\r\npriority: 3\r\ndepends_on: 3398\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table pim.ai_activity_triage\r\n  - function api.pm_add_product_comment\r\n  - function api.pm_begin_activity_triage\r\n  - function api.pm_complete_activity_triage\r\n  - function api.pm_fail_activity_triage\r\n  - function pim.pm_complete_activity_triage_worker\r\n  - function pim.pm_fail_activity_triage_worker\r\n  - function api.pm_get_activity_triage\r\n  - function api.pm_create_dependency\r\n  - function api.pm_create_decision\r\n  - function api.pm_create_reminder\r\n  - function api.pm_update_dependency_status\r\n  - function api.pm_update_reminder_status\r\n  - function api.pm_accept_activity_triage\r\n  - function api.pm_dismiss_activity_triage\r\n  - policy pm_ai_activity_triage_select_own on pim.ai_activity_triage\r\n  - policy pm_ai_activity_triage_admin_audit on pim.ai_activity_triage\r\nreads:\r\n  - table app.comment\r\n  - table app.activity\r\n  - table app.notification\r\n  - table app.profile\r\n  - table pim.product\r\n```\r\n\r\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0cb6f-6caa-7e70-bddf-8d81be08942b on EDGE-DEV\r\r\n\r\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0cc65-a5c9-7453-bf7b-7c689fba04b3 on edge-dev\r\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABVsKP2Q","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"App-side architecture for #3298, revised to avoid unrestricted `service_role`, a direct LOGIN, or a custom token issuer:\n\n1. `poppim-web` remains a static SPA. Its app-owned trusted gateway is an authenticated Supabase Edge Function `pm-jev-triage`, with source planned under `edge-runtime/supabase/functions/pm-jev-triage/` and protected preview/production workflows. The browser invokes it with the existing user bearer JWT and only `{productId, commentId}`.\n2. The Edge Function uses the caller JWT for profile/product/comment reads and `pm_begin_activity_triage`. It never holds or uses a service-role key.\n3. Completion/failure uses the same caller JWT plus a canonical HMAC-SHA-256 envelope. The Edge Function holds an environment-specific signing secret; the database verifier reads the matching value from Supabase Vault through a SECURITY DEFINER wrapper owned by the proposed least-privilege NOLOGIN worker. Production placement of both secret copies remains an explicit owner-authorized action.\n4. Canonical signed fields, in fixed order/version: `envelope_version`, `environment`, `triage_id`, `requester_profile_id`, `comment_id`, `input_hash`, `model`, `contract_version`, `lease_token`, `lease_expires_at`, `status`, `kind`, `probabilities`, `confidence`, `provider_request_id`, `input_tokens`, `latency_ms`, `error_code`, `completed_at`. Nullable fields use explicit JSON null; numbers use a documented canonical decimal representation; unknown keys reject. Signature is base64url HMAC-SHA-256 over canonical UTF-8 JSON.\n5. The wrapper derives profile identity from `auth.uid()` and requires it to equal both the signed requester and stored row requester. It checks environment, exact row metadata, current lease token/expiry, allowed state/labels/ranges, and a bounded `completed_at` skew. The row state makes replay idempotent; a conflicting replay rejects. Raw comment/title/prompt is never in the envelope or triage table.\n6. The private NOLOGIN worker can update only the matching triage row. It cannot read comments/products or create operating records. Accept/dismiss and all non-AI manual Operations RPCs remain caller-JWT RPCs with independent staff-role/product/field authorization.\n\nApp payload contracts requested:\n\n- Comment: trimmed body 1–4,000 characters; tabs/newlines allowed; NUL/other controls denied.\n- Dependency: title 1–200; fixed `blocked_by/open`; no related-product link in this pilot.\n- Decision: `decision_type` 1–100; optional `notes` ≤2,000; fixed `decided`.\n- Reminder: title 1–200; optional valid due date; assigned to current caller; fixed `open/follow_up`.\n- Allowed writers: active profile + PM app access + role `administrator|sales|licensing|designer` + caller-readable target product. Viewer/vendor/anonymous denied. No separate user/department map exists today; test Licensed, Generic, and Software products through their actual product RLS and stop for an owner rule if that does not provide the intended boundary.\n\nThe implementation plan also requires expiring leases/stale takeover, old-worker rejection, Jev-independent manual create/update RPCs for feature-off rollback, and direct-RPC/concurrency/ambiguous-response tests. The issue body has been updated to match. Poppim owns the Edge Function and frontend; shared-db owns the table, NOLOGIN worker, Vault verifier/wrappers, grants/RLS, and migration proof.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-20T14:55:27Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3298#issuecomment-5750558681","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABWQzIgA","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Pilot-v1 qualification update (2026-09-23): the newer locked owner + independent reviewer ruling at https://github.com/u2giants/poppim-web/issues/9#issuecomment-5788297664 supersedes this issue's earlier request for a role/action/business-unit decision. {"assignees":[],"body":"## Outcome\n\nThe live ColdLion `/proddetails` feed has falsified the second proven identity of `coldlion.prod_detail`: one production order now returns two rows with **distinct `pkey`s sharing one `prodLineSeq`**, which the table's `unique (company_code, prod_order_no, prod_line_seq)` constraint (migration `20260916001944`, issue #2863) refuses — by design. `pkey`, the real vendor row id and primary key, remains unique. Decide and apply the structural response: drop or re-key the falsified unique constraint so the colliding orders can land, or rule they stay refused.\n\nThis is STRUCTURE work: the constraint is database shape. The loader side is done and merged (#3221, #3230, #3233): identity collisions are recorded as durable per-key refusals (`coldlion.sync_run`, `status='failed'`, `request_params->>'refused'='identity-collision'`), never collapsed, and counted in every run's reconciliation.\n\n## Live evidence (2026-09-17, structure only — no row values)\n\n- Order 20344 (EDGEHOME): 10 rows; one group with `prodLineSeq` appearing twice; the two rows have **different `pkey`, `itemPkey`, `prodQty`, `prodCost`, `labelCode`, timestamps** — two real distinct lines, not an echo. Field names and counts only; the diagnostic is reproducible read-only against the live feed.\n- The 2026-09-15 grain proof (`docs/coldlion-unit-5b-grain-proof-20260915.md` §2) measured `(prodOrderNo, prodLineSeq)` unique over 166 rows from 45 orders; the falsification appeared deeper in the population during the production backfill.\n- Re-derive the refusal population live, never from a number pasted here:\n\n```sql\nselect count(distinct (request_params->>'prodOrderNo')::bigint) as refused_orders\n  from coldlion.sync_run\n where endpoint = '/proddetails' and company_code = 'EDGEHOME'\n   and status = 'failed' and request_params->>'refused' = 'identity-collision';\n```\n\n## Options for the owner\n\n1. **Drop the unique constraint** (keep the `(company_code, pkey)` primary key): the landing layer records what arrived; `pkey` remains the proven identity. The refused keys are then re-fetchable in place (`--mode keys`) and land under the existing upsert.\n2. **Replace it with something true** — e.g. uniqueness of `(company_code, pkey, prod_line_seq)` — if the intent is still to detect re-keying, though that is implied by the PK.\n3. **Rule the collisions stay refused** — no schema change; the refusals remain durable evidence and the source-data outcome on #3180 closes with the refused set explicitly excluded.\n\nTracker: #2081 (ColdLion landing completion). Source-data outcome: #3180.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nservice_class: standard-application\nchange_type: constraint\npriority: 50\ndepends_on: 2863\napplication_return_to: popcre/shared-db\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\nlive_assertion: On production coldlion.prod_detail retains primary key (company_code,pkey), the falsified unique (company_code,prod_order_no,prod_line_seq) constraint is absent, and authenticated and anonymous landing-table access remain denied. Preview rollback behavioral proof admits two distinct pkeys sharing the same order and line without weakening the primary key or nonnull checks.\nwrites:\n  - table coldlion.prod_detail\nreads:\n  - table coldlion.sync_run\n```\n\n\nMetadata recovery note: The current orchestrator selected removal of only the falsified order/line UNIQUE, retaining the real company/pkey primary key and existing nonnull checks. Constraint changes lock the parent table. The paired application-owned loader rejection must also be repaired before the source-data outcome is complete. No production result is asserted.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf01-b3d7-7d62-b7ed-5c7bad7af40a on 916-ALIEN\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABVk1oUw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"<!-- ai-blocker-watch:unowned:popcre/shared-db#3234 -->\nThis open issue blocks popcre/shared-db#3180 and has gone 24h with no owner: no assignee, no `owner:` line, no open linked pull request, no activity.\nTake it (assign yourself, or add an `owner:` line naming who owns it) or hand it to a named queue owner. Listed in today's ai-blocker-watch digest. (ai-blocker-watch)","createdAt":"2026-09-19T15:01:32Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3234#issuecomment-5742880851","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABVs4rYw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Live re-measurement 2026-09-20 and the question to send ColdLion\n\nThe full `/proddetails` population was re-scanned read-only today (every `prodOrderNo` 1–60000 for EDGEHOME; **3,819 orders return rows**). **11 collision groups across 9 orders** carry two or more rows sharing one `prodOrderNo` + `prodLineSeq`. `pkey` is distinct in every group and unique across the population.\n\n**This partly falsifies the issue body's premise.** The body says the collisions are \"two real distinct lines, not an echo\". Some are (different `itemNo` on one line). Others are not: order 20959 line 1 carries two rows identical in every business field, created 140 ms apart; order 23475 line 1 carries seven rows of one item at seven different costs. Option 1 (drop the unique constraint) would land those as-is, and if any group should have been summed rather than kept apart, landed cost is wrong for that order. **The structural decision should not be taken before ColdLion answers.**\n\nQuestion text below, with the five observed shapes. Field names, order numbers and item codes only.\n\n---\n\n# Question for ColdLion — `/proddetails`: two or more rows sharing one `prodLineSeq`\n\n**Company code:** EDGEHOME · **Endpoint:** `GET /EhpApi/proddetails?companyCode=EDGEHOME&prodOrderNo=<n>`\n**Observed live:** 2026-09-20, read-only. All examples below are reproducible with a single call each.\n\n## Background\n\nLast August you added `prodLineSeq` to `/prodHistory` to resolve the duplicated production\nreference numbers, and we confirmed it live. We assumed the same field behaved as a line\nidentifier on `/proddetails` and built our loader on that assumption.\n\nScanning the full production-order population on `/proddetails` (3,819 orders that return\nrows), **9 orders produce 11 groups where two or more rows carry the same `prodOrderNo` and\nthe same `prodLineSeq`**. `pkey` is always distinct, and `pkey` is unique across every row we\nhave seen, so we can still tell the rows apart — but we cannot tell what they *mean*.\n\nThe groups do not all look alike, which is why we are asking rather than guessing. There\nappear to be at least four different shapes.\n\n## Examples\n\n### A. Same item, same quantity, same cost — rows created ~140 ms apart\n\n| order | line | pkey | item | qty | cost | created |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 20959 | 1 | 11057 | MB93SW01 | 1600 | 1.73 | 2021-05-10 07:14:08.350 |\n| 20959 | 1 | 11058 | MB93SW01 | 1600 | 1.73 | 2021-05-10 07:14:08.490 |\n\nEvery business field is identical (item, prepack PPK903, label DD, quantity, cost). Only\n`pkey` and the sub-second timestamps differ.\n\n**Is this one line double-written, or two genuinely separate 1,600-piece buys?**\n\n### B. Same item, quantity split across the rows\n\n| order | line | pkey | item | qty | cost | created |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 23465 | 1 | 40281 | BRT6601 | 400 | 2.21 | 2025-07-07 18:34:46.153 |\n| 23465 | 1 | 40282 | BRT6601 | 200 | 2.21 | 2025-07-07 18:34:46.263 |\n| 23465 | 2 | 40283 | AAPT001 | 400 | 2.19 | 2025-07-07 18:34:46.323 |\n| 23465 | 2 | 40284 | AAPT001 | 200 | 2.19 | 2025-07-07 18:34:46.387 |\n\nAlso: order 21918 line 3 (SQZ26MVSP03, 524 and 277), order 21928 line 7 (SQZ26VMSB01, 250\nand 257).\n\n**Should these be added together — 600 pieces of BRT6601 on line 1 — or are they separate\nline items that happen to share a line number?**\n\n### C. One line number carrying many rows at different costs\n\n| order | line | pkey | item | qty | cost |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 23475 | 1 | 40315 | SF9252024 | 2 | 17.00 |\n| 23475 | 1 | 40316 | SF9252024 | 2 | 16.00 |\n| 23475 | 1 | 40317 | SF9252024 | 1 | 22.00 |\n| 23475 | 1 | 40318 | SF9252024 | 15 | 22.00 |\n| 23475 | 1 | 40319 | SF9252024 | 1 | 52.00 |\n| 23475 | 1 | 40320 | SF9252024 | 2 | 45.00 |\n| 23475 | 1 | 40321 | SF9252024 | 2 | 49.00 |\n\nSeven rows, one item number, one line number, seven different costs. Line 3 of the same\norder does the same thing four times (VSZ36MVAV13 at 14, 16, 22 and 49), and line 6 twice.\n\n**What distinguishes these rows from one another? Is there a field we should be reading —\nsize, dimension, a component of the line — that `/proddetails` does not return?**\n\n### D. Different items sharing one line number\n\n| order | line | pkey | item | qty | cost |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 21907 | 22 | 23849 | SQZ26MVAV07 | 260 | 1.95 |\n| 21907 | 22 | 23850 | SQZ26MVAV09 | 249 | 1.95 |\n| 23587 | 1 | 41038 | MFZ42NFRM02 | 4200 | 1.372 |\n| 23587 | 1 | 41039 | MFZ42NTRN01 | 4800 | 1.372 |\n\nTwo different item numbers on the same line number of the same order.\n\n### E. A zero-quantity row shadowing a real one\n\n| order | line | pkey | item | itemPkey | label | qty | cost | created |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 20344 | 10 | 4496 | VSZ48DCJG01 | 8161 | AM | 40 | 2.50 | 2020-08-11 19:41:52 |\n| 20344 | 10 | 4499 | VSZ48DCJG01 | 5348 | *(blank)* | 0 | 0.00 | 2020-08-11 20:06:59 |\n\nSame item number but a **different `itemPkey`**, no label code, and zero quantity and cost,\ncreated 25 minutes later.\n\n**Is a zero-quantity row like this a cancelled or superseded line we should ignore, or does\nit carry meaning?**\n\n## What we need from you\n\n1. **What uniquely identifies a `/proddetails` row?** Is it `pkey` alone, or is there a\n   combination of fields that is the real line identity?\n2. **What is `prodLineSeq` on this endpoint?** On `/prodHistory` you added it to separate\n   real lines. Does it mean the same thing here, or is it a different number that is simply\n   allowed to repeat?\n3. **For each shape above — A through E — should we treat the rows as separate production\n   lines, add their quantities together, or drop one of them?** If some are data-entry\n   artifacts, say which, and whether you intend to clean them up at source.\n4. **Is there a status, cancellation, or revision flag on a production-order line that\n   `/proddetails` does not currently return?** Several of these shapes would be explained by\n   one.\n5. **Do any of these rows affect what we owe the factory?** If B or C should be summed, our\n   cost figures for those orders are currently wrong.\n\nWe are holding these 9 orders out of our load until we hear back, so nothing has been\nrecorded incorrectly. {"assignees":[],"body":"## Symptom (production, live site)\n\nEvery duty-research classification on https://designflow.app fails its precheck:\n\n```\n[hts-rag] precheck-v2 failed correlationId=451f8478-5fee-4671-b8be-0308f7b2ec0e relation \"designflow.hts_rag_precedents\" does not exist\n```\n(Cloud Run service `popcre-core-prod`, project `lithe-breaker-323913`, 2026-09-17T16:10:48Z; `POST /api/hts-rag/precheck-v2` returns 502 on every attempt.)\n\n## Cause\n\nThe HTS RAG tables live in their own `hts_rag` schema, created by\n`supabase/migrations/20260909121403_hts_rag_split_isolated_schema.sql` (and the\nleast-privilege roles migration `20260911210709_...`). Those migrations are\napplied for the alsand sandbox database only. The production database has\nneither the `hts_rag` schema nor the tables, and `popcre-core-prod` runs with\n`HTS_RAG_DB_ENABLED=false`, so the models fall back to the primary connection\nand resolve to `designflow.hts_rag_precedents`, which does not exist.\n\n`popcre-albert-core-sandbox` works because it has `HTS_RAG_DB_ENABLED=true`,\n`HTS_RAG_DB_SCHEMA=hts_rag` and the HTS_RAG_DB_* connection secrets.\n\n## Ask (orchestrator work — this changes database structure)\n\nApply the HTS RAG schema migrations to the production database, so the\nproduction `hts_rag` schema and its tables/roles exist and match the sandbox\ncontract (`supabase/tests/hts_rag_shared_schema_contract.sql`,\n`hts_rag_durable_precedent_contract.sql`, `hts_rag_audit_contract.sql`).\n\n## Not part of this ticket\n\nSetting `HTS_RAG_DB_*` env/secrets on `popcre-core-prod` is a Cloud Run change,\nnot a database change; it must follow the production apply and is owned by the\napp/infra side.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: database-read\nreturn_to: popcre/designflow-backend\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\nMetadata recovery note: September 18-19 comments agree no shared-db structure is missing. Remaining app-side production proof/configuration belongs to DesignFlow; comments disagree about current HTS enablement, so status stays blocked pending current app verification. {"assignees":[],"body":"Follow-up to #2794 / PR #2821 (review finding 2, slot-1 review seq 3116).\n\n## Problem\nThe DesignFlow PLM master-data sync is retired (#1090, #2794). Nothing writes `ingest.sync_run` rows with `source_system = 'designflow_plm'` / `source_name = 'plm_master_data_api'` any more.\n\n`plm.record_taxonomy_parallel_observation(date, jsonb)` (last defined in `supabase/migrations/20260905043023_coldlion_taxonomy_health_live_hash_guard.sql`, ~lines 573 and 678-690) still requires a `succeeded` DesignFlow run inside `max_age`. Otherwise it counts an unexplained `designflow_lane` difference. So every observation is now unexplained, and the Phase 6 taxonomy cutover-readiness gate can never pass. `plm.check_taxonomy_sync_health` has a similar DesignFlow leg (~lines 194-246) that should be checked in the same change.\n\nThis is pre-existing (since #1090), not caused by #2821.\n\n## Wanted\nA governed structural change that removes or retires the DesignFlow leg, so readiness reflects only live sources. An alternative is retiring the gate itself. Keep history rows. Do not weaken the ColdLion leg or the live-hash guard.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 50\nservice_class: standard-application\nchange_type: function\napplication_return_to: popcre/shared-db\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\nlive_assertion: Both taxonomy detectors no longer require a DesignFlow sync run; ColdLion checks, live-hash refusal, baseline checks, and execution restrictions remain intact.\ndepends_on: #2794\nwrites:\n  - function plm.record_taxonomy_parallel_observation\n  - function plm.check_taxonomy_sync_health\nreads:\n  - table ingest.sync_run\n```\n\n\nScope clarified after #2794 production completion: retire only DesignFlow freshness/status. Preserve historical rows and source-reference baseline checks. Compatibility designflow_ok=true must carry explicit retired/not-required metadata, never hide an active-source failure. No columns or public wrapper signatures change.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf3f-a354-7d43-9e89-edfca32697dc on Run on 2026-09-25 at about 3:30 PM EDT.\n\n**Sample:** 1,525 distinct descriptions, made up of:\n- 400 stratified random rows (seed 3024, covering all 199 gold types)\n- 101 Faux Book correction descriptions\n- all 1,024 unreadable descriptions\n\n**Method:** six fresh labellers worked from frozen definitions only. Every disagreement went to an adjudicator that saw the two candidates without knowing which was which.\n\n- Blind labels agreed with gold on type 924 times, on status 1,024 and on material 1,120.\n- 675 items disagreed on a gate field (type, status or material), and all 675 were adjudicated:\n  - 122 upheld the reader/gold label.\n  - 71 were confirmed wrong values by the reader: 34 in the stratified sample and 37 among the Faux Book corrections, where the adjudicator chose Storage Box.\n  - 482 were reader abstentions on text the definitions treat as readable.\n- Faux Book corrections: the blind label matched the reader 0 times out of 101. On adjudication, 64 were judged both acceptable and 37 went to the blind label.\n- The rule-of-three bound does not apply because the error count is not zero.\n\nThe full report is in the private data repository.\n\nPosted by Claude chat 8200fc94-7b9f-4bf4-a88d-14aace57a23c on edge-dev\n","createdAt":"2026-09-25T15:34:51Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3024#issuecomment-5835061954","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABXBgFuQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Owner rulings from the review chat, 2026-09-25 (Albert Hazan, ~5:40 PM EDT)\n\nRecorded here so the implementing session applies them; documented in the rulebook by PR #3561.\n\n1. **Non-inventory items are ignored for product type.** Quoting Albert: *\"if that says 'yes' (like it should for 'HANG TAB'), ignore those items\"*. Live census: `coldlion.item_header.non_inventory_item` = `Y` on 36 of 18,990 current items (flag under-used; only one of the two HANG TAB items is flagged).\n\n2. **Prepack parents inherit their codes from children.** Quoting Albert: *\"if yes, they shouldn't be in this list because they should inherit the mgcategory and MG01-MG04 codes from their children items\"*. Identification: `archive.erp_items_current.prepack_code IS NOT NULL` → 1,437 live parents in `coldlion.item_header`; note `coldlion.prepack_detail.item_no` lists the child **components** (6,515), not the parents.\n\nBoth exclusions are already applied in the owner review workbook (`Dropbox/ai/issue-3024-product-type-review-rulings-2026-09-25.xlsx`): 1,473 items excluded across the tabs, with an excluded-count column added to the vocabulary tab.\n\nPosted by ZCode chat unknown on EDGE-DEV","createdAt":"2026-09-25T21:41:19Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3024#issuecomment-5840045497","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABXCA3tg","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Third exclusion ruling: assortment-worded items (2026-09-25, ~6:30 PM EDT)\n\nAlbert, quoting: *\"'Disnys Asst, lic, Calandar, 65x10' and 'Asst multiple licensed ottoman srtorage' and 'ASST LIC MDF WALL PLAQUES' didn't have prepack codes? these are all assortments.\"*\n\nRuling applied: assortment-worded items (\"Asst\"/\"Assorted\") are excluded from the product-type review lists exactly like prepack parents, even when ColdLion gives them no prepack code. Measured: 714 assortment-worded live items, only 309 carry a prepack code; 405 additional items excluded (total exclusions now 1,878).\n\n**Impact on the gold key (for the implementing session):** the current key ACCEPTS 621 assortment-worded rows as single products (e.g. the three named above -> Calendar / Storage Ottoman / Wall Plaque). Under this ruling they must stop carrying an independently derived product type. {"assignees":[],"body":"## Request (structural — orchestrator work)\n\nDesignFlow PLM needs a job table so HTS AI classification turns run in the background (Cloud Tasks push into the existing backend). Owner: Albert. Canonical spec: `popcre/designflow-frontend` branch `sandbox-albert`, `plan_hts-background-classification.md` Step 1 and D3/D4.\n\n### New table `hts_rag_classification_jobs`\nSchema: same schema as `hts_rag_determinations` / `hts_rag_debate_runs` in the environment DesignFlow runs on (app uses `SCHEMA=dflow`; plan text says `public` — orchestrator to confirm the correct schema before authoring).\n\n- `id uuid pk`\n- `determination_id uuid not null` fk -> `hts_rag_determinations`\n- `session_id uuid not null`, `turn_index int not null`\n- `kind text` CHECK in (`initial`,`answer`)\n- `status text not null default 'queued'` CHECK in the plan's D4 status list (queued, running, needs_answer, ready, applied, failed, cancelled — confirm against plan D4)\n- `owner_key text not null`, `created_by jsonb`\n- `input jsonb not null`, `result jsonb`, `error_code text`, `error_message text`\n- `rfq_id`, `rfq_item_id` nullable — integer type must match the deployed RFQ tables\n- `source text not null default 'hts_lookup'` CHECK in (`hts_lookup`,`rfq`)\n- `claimed_at timestamptz`, `claimed_by text`, `lease_expires_at timestamptz`\n- `attempt_count int default 0`, `max_attempts int default 3`\n- `estimated_cost_usd numeric`, `actual_cost_usd numeric`\n- `notified_at timestamptz`, `applied_at timestamptz`, `applied_by jsonb`\n- `created_at`, `updated_at timestamptz`\n\nConstraints/indexes: unique `(determination_id, turn_index)`; indexes `(status, created_at)`, `(owner_key, status)`, `(rfq_id, rfq_item_id)`. RLS and grants identical to `hts_rag_debate_runs` (issue #2535 precedent).\n\nAlso verify `hts_rag_provider_responses` has uniqueness on `(session_id, turn_index)` or equivalent; if not, include it (guards re-billing on Cloud Tasks redelivery).\n\n### Gate for the app\nMerged AND applied to the DesignFlow sandbox database; `select to_regclass('<schema>.hts_rag_classification_jobs')` returns the name.\n\n### Routing\nStructural change → orchestrator work. The DesignFlow app session waits on this before building Step 3+.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nservice_class: standard-application\nchange_type: table\npriority: 100\napplication_return_to: popcre/designflow-backend\ngenerated_types: required\nlive_assertion: The DesignFlow sandbox HTS connection can use hts_rag.hts_rag_classification_jobs for leased background classification with the requested determination/turn idempotency and existing debate-role least privilege.\nwrites:\n  - table hts_rag.hts_rag_classification_jobs\n  - index hts_rag.hts_rag_classification_jobs_status_idx\n  - index hts_rag.hts_rag_classification_jobs_owner_idx\n  - index hts_rag.hts_rag_classification_jobs_rfq_idx\n  - policy hts_rag_prod_worker_access on hts_rag.hts_rag_classification_jobs\n  - policy hts_rag_prod_worker_insert on hts_rag.hts_rag_classification_jobs\n  - policy hts_rag_prod_worker_update on hts_rag.hts_rag_classification_jobs\n  - policy hts_rag_alsand_worker_access on hts_rag.hts_rag_classification_jobs\n  - policy hts_rag_alsand_worker_insert on hts_rag.hts_rag_classification_jobs\n  - policy hts_rag_alsand_worker_update on hts_rag.hts_rag_classification_jobs\nreads:\n  - table hts_rag.hts_rag_determinations\n  - table hts_rag.hts_rag_debate_runs\n  - table hts_rag.hts_rag_provider_responses\n```\n\nMetadata recovery note: The current HTS recovery established isolated schema hts_rag, with determination_id referencing hts_rag.hts_rag_determinations(id); earlier public/dflow guesses are superseded. Existing provider-response uniqueness on (session_id,turn_role,turn_index) is preserved.
