Nothing was re-applied: the three migrations were already applied on 2026-09-15 by the owner's explicit instruction, and this change performs **no database write of any kind**.\n\n**What it does**\n\n- `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs` gains `--target sandbox`.\n- `.github/workflows/migration-ledger-drift.yml` now compares **production and sandbox** on the same push and daily schedule legs, each with its own independently throttled alarm issue. Production keeps its original alarm title so the existing throttle still matches. `preview` stays on-demand only, because it is rebuilt and a scheduled comparison against it would report the rebuild rather than a mistake.\n\n**One deliberate deviation from the wording here, stated plainly.** The request was for a mode \"reading the `DB_*_SANDBOX` secrets\". The sandbox is a hosted Supabase project (`xupnyeifmpsacrqahwwm`), and the existing `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` already reads its ledger — verified by a live read-only query before any code was written. So the check uses the same Supabase Management API transport, the same one constant `select version from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`, and **adds no new secret to this repository**. No value of any `DB_*_SANDBOX` secret was placed in a commit, a log, a command argument or a chat message; they are referenced by name only. If you would rather it went through the five `DB_*_SANDBOX` values as a matter of policy, say so and it becomes a small follow-up.\n\n**Scope, because the sandbox is not the shared database.** It was seeded from a structure dump and stamped only with the DesignFlow contract migrations applied afterwards, so it is owed a subset of the merged tree. Comparing all 703 merged versions against its 8-row ledger would report ~695 false gaps on the first run, and a check that is red on day one is trained away within a week. A merged version is in scope when it is already in the sandbox ledger, or when it touches the `dflow` schema and is not older than the baseline **derived** from the ledger's earliest row. The baseline, the rule and the excluded count are printed on every run, so the scope claim is visible and challengeable rather than silent.\n\n**Live read-only run on the branch, against the real sandbox — it already finds drift:**\n\n```\nMigration ledger drift — sandbox (xupnyeifmpsacrqahwwm)\n  merged on origin/main: 9 version(s)\n  applied in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations: 8 version(s)\nDRIFT FOUND.\nMERGED BUT NOT APPLIED — 3 version(s): 20260905072856, 20260909084253, 20260911210709\nAPPLIED BUT NOT ON THE BASE BRANCH — 2 ledger row(s): 20260904183000, 20260904183100\n```\n\nThat drift is pre-existing. This change surfaces it; it does not create or resolve it. The two orphan rows have no file on `main` at all, which means DDL reached the sandbox from outside merged history. Whoever owns the DesignFlow non-production database should decide what to do about all five entries; this session did not write to that database.\n\n**This issue is NOT closed yet.** PR #3341 is open with its checks driven and its agent work contract recorded, but it cannot be merged: the governed reviewer gate is down repo-wide (issue #3346), and every governed reviewer command refuses on the same line —\n\n```\nREFUSED: active reviewer leases are unreadable; reviewer assignment refused before mutex acquisition\n```\n\nThe reviewer gate was not bypassed and no shared coordination ref was hand-edited. This issue closes when #3341 merges.\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n","createdAt":"2026-09-20T17:37:45Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2986#issuecomment-5751472945","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABVtEIew","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"<!-- ai-blocker-watch:parked -->\n## What this is about\n# Blocked: PR #3341 needs one governed exact-head review\n\n## Waiting on\npopcre/shared-db#3346 — Governed reviewer draw is down repo-wide: refs/db-review-assignments is past the 1000-ref ceiling and both sanctioned recoveries refuse on the same condition\n\n## Resume brief\n# Blocked: PR #3341 needs one governed exact-head review\n\n## What this work is\nPR #3341 on `popcre/shared-db`, branch `claude/2986-sandbox-ledger-drift`, closes two\nnon-orchestrator issues:\n\n* **#2986** — adds `--target sandbox` to `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs` and puts the\n  DesignFlow consolidated non-production database on the same push and daily schedule legs as\n  production, with its own independently throttled alarm. Read-only: the same one constant\n  `select version from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` over the Supabase Management API,\n  no new secret, no database write. The migrations themselves were already applied on 2026-09-15.\n* **#2492** — sizes `ai-grok-review`'s `--max-turns` to the changed migration lines, so a large\n  migration no longer exhausts the wrapper's 20-turn default and returns no verdict. A refusal now\n  names the budget the reviewer was given. {"assignees":[],"body":"## Goal\nProvision separate least-privilege production Supabase identities for DesignFlow backend, Item Master, Tracking, and Data Sync against `dflow_prod` on project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` so the rehearsed Cloud SQL cutover can run without `postgres` or a shared credential.\n\n## Required contract\n- Inventory each service's Sequelize table/view/function/sequence usage from its current production code and publish the exact role/object/privilege matrix.\n- Create NOLOGIN grant roles plus LOGIN runtime identities for the four services; credentials are provisioned separately through 1Password and ALTER ROLE after canonical promotion.\n- Grant USAGE on `dflow_prod` and only the SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, sequence, and function privileges each service actually needs. No CREATE, TRUNCATE, ownership, cross-schema `dflow`, browser, anon, authenticated, or service_role access.\n- Backend HTS access remains through the already-created `designflow_hts_prod_runtime` / worker roles and must not widen operational grants.\n- Add contract tests for allowed paths and explicit cross-schema/admin/refusal controls.\n\n## Target and safety\nProduction target: `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`. Author through canonical migration, preview first, then production promotion through the shared-db orchestrator. No application rows are to be changed.\n\n## App dependency\npopcre/designflow-backend#94 and its production Supabase implementation plan.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 100\nservice_class: standard-application\nchange_type: grant\napplication_return_to: popcre/designflow-backend\ndepends_on: 2874, 2875\nwrites:\n  - schema dflow_prod\nreads:\n```\n\nMetadata recovery note: The requested least-privilege grant matrix requires both production parity surfaces and a current four-service usage inventory. The named schema is the known boundary; exact grants, roles, generated types and live assertion remain unresolved. No role or credential is created by this proposal.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf01-b3d7-7d62-b7ed-5c7bad7af40a on 916-ALIEN\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABWems9g","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Owner decision 2026-09-23: no new direct database logins except trusted in-house server services, because Supabase declined to remove the PUBLIC grant on the `net` schema (pg_net). The four DesignFlow LOGIN identities planned here fall under that exception and will be able to reach pg_net; the grant matrix should state this. See docs/security/pg-net-direct-login-rule.md (https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3461).\n\nPosted by Claude chat 8d6aaf03-e7f1-460f-b278-eecf8de5f88c on edge-dev","createdAt":"2026-09-23T21:43:52Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2873#issuecomment-5803453686","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABWfH43A","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"**Independent review verdict (Qwen 3.8 Max): APPROVE, keep the exception.** pg_net reach comes from a PUBLIC grant, so every alternative has the same exposure. Four scoped identities come out ahead on privilege scope, attribution and revocation.\n\nStructural conditions for this issue's migration:\n- Each LOGIN role: `NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION`. Privileges sit on NOLOGIN grant roles and the LOGIN role only holds membership (the pattern in `20260911210709`). Set a connection limit.\n\nRule routing and any guard tooling are not orchestrator work. The Claude session that wrote the rule is handling them (PR #3462).\n\nPosted by Claude chat 8d6aaf03-e7f1-460f-b278-eecf8de5f88c on edge-dev\n","createdAt":"2026-09-23T22:27:59Z","includesCreatedEdit":true,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2873#issuecomment-5803997404","viewerDidAuthor":true}],"createdAt":"2026-09-14T03:35:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"assignees":[],"body":"## 2026-09-20 bounded outcome and complete successor inventory\n\nowner: Codex orchestrator marker #3297, chat01a0bf00-fa7b-73d1-b447-fc4c89c50b96 on916-ALIEN.\n\nThis issue's executable outcome is now ONLY the six-view grant boundary already declared in its unchanged db-work-scope and protected claim #3294/version20260920005114, implemented by PR #3304. It is complete only after exact production/live proof. The original broad report below is retained as history; closing this bounded unit never means every historical finding is remediated.\n\nAll unresolved work is explicitly retained elsewhere:\n- #3327 — orchestrator structural outcome: preserve audit-history event IDs while joined profile fields respect existing own-user/admin visibility; exact view public.style_tracker_audit_log_with_user. Root marker3297 owns delivery.\n- #3328 — NON-orchestrator investigation: establish intended Styles/OrderList bridge/RFQ projection visibility, preserving open signed-in Styles. Owned by access_contract_recovery until delegated. Explicitly overlaps #1431's same view but does not inherit its cutover authorization or dependencies.\n- #3329 — NON-orchestrator investigation: establish intended canonical item-serving projection for actual browser/server consumers. Owned by access_contract_recovery until delegated; no presumed bug or blanket revoke.\n- #2326 — NON-orchestrator current function-execution census; explicit owner/checklist recorded at https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2326#issuecomment-5750785999 . Historical function counts remain unverified, not cleared.\n\nCorrected findings, based on fresh production catalog and actual application code:\n- api.crm_customer_picker_list and api.pm_customer_list ALREADY use app.has_explicit_app_access(crm/pm); api.dam_customer_list and api.dam_factory_list ALREADY gate app.has_app_access(dam) OR public.has_app_access(auth.uid(),popdam), all security_barrier=true. Production ledger20260723223000 and20260723212500 present; these July migrations precede the September report. The assertion these four lacked caller gates is disproved. No redundant structural work is warranted; this statement is catalog/source proof, not a newly performed browser role test.\n- public.style_guide_file_groups and public.style_guide_folders are authenticated-readable materialized projections over public.style_guide_files, whose explicit authenticated SELECT policy is USING(true). Current PopSG browser calls both (PopSGLibraryPage601/631 at popdam3 mainf3fb0c943af7f216b74507b50c242555f65226b1). Their broad-read premise matches the source contract; definer/materialized semantics alone are not an unauthorized-access finding. Preserve the existing library capability.\n- Prior CRM gate/invoker work is PR #2764, ledger20260911124746 present. Four-table grant tightening is separate delivered #2848 / PR #2815; actual merged migration version is20260914155226, NOT stale20260911225108 in older comments. Live all four tables retain RLS and grant anon/authenticated no SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Historical comments remain unchanged.\n\nThe six-view db-work-scope/live_assertion below is unchanged. PR3304 may close this issue after its own complete governed production outcome because the remaining work now has explicit owners and durable links.\n\n---\n\n## Preserved original report\n\nReproduced during plan Step 2 (#2326). Evidence: `docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260910T002917Z/api-access-matrix.md`.  ## What was proved  A **PopDAM viewer** — the lowest-privilege identity of a *different* application on the same Supabase project — reads across the application boundary over the Data API:  | Object | Rows returned | |---|---| | `api.crm_account_list` | 826 CRM accounts | | `api.crm_customer_list` | 826 CRM customers | | `public.style_tracker_rows_with_bridge` | 15,742 PLM style-tracker rows | | `public.style_guide_file_groups` | 22,045 style-guide file-group rows |  Counts only — no row contents were fetched. The same identity gets **0** from `api.crm_contact_list` and `api.crm_opportunity_list`, which filter by the caller, so the probe discriminates rather than always succeeding.  ## Cause  Definer-semantics views and materialized views bypass RLS entirely, and they carry a blanket `authenticated` grant. Sixteen `api` views are in this class (`crm_account_list`, `crm_contact_list`, `crm_contact_segment_counts`, `crm_contact_segment_list`, `crm_customer_list`, `crm_customer_picker_list`, `crm_factory_picker_list`, `crm_ingested_domain_list`, `dam_customer_list`, `dam_factory_list`, `opa_disney_property`, `opa_lucasfilm_property`, `opa_marvel_property`, `pm_customer_list`, `pm_factory_list`, `source_capture_inventory`), plus five `public` views and two materialized views (RLS cannot apply to a materialized view at all).  ## Remedy  Per object, one of: set `security_invoker=true` and let the underlying RLS apply; add an explicit in-view caller filter as `crm_contact_list` already does; or narrow the grant to an application-specific role. Each is a shape change and belongs to the orchestrator as its own governed claim.  ## Also carried forward from Step 2  - **Medium:** four `public` tables (`ai_sentinel_cleanup_log`, `dam_search_documents`, `dam_search_synonyms`, `scanner_ai_ignores`) hold RLS with zero policies and full `SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` for both `anon` and `authenticated`. Every read is denied today only because an empty policy set denies all; one permissive policy added for an unrelated reason would open all four. Revoke the grants. - **Not measured, with cause:** 38 `SECURITY DEFINER` functions are executable by `anon` and 111 by `authenticated`, and 78 trigger-returning functions carry an `anon`/`authenticated` EXECUTE grant. Exercising an RPC is a write-shaped call against production, which is out of scope for a read-only session. Needs preview fixtures.  ```yaml status: owner-decision work_type: structural route: shared-db-orchestrator depends_on: [] ```  Whether this is *unauthorized* is a business judgement about who should see CRM customer lists. The technical fact is settled: any authenticated identity on this project can. Albert's ruling on the access contract is needed before the per-object work is dispatched.   ```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\nservice_class: standard-application\r\nchange_type: grant\r\napplication_return_to: popcre/shared-db\r\nlive_assertion: in production, authenticated has no SELECT privilege and service_role retains SELECT privilege on all six claimed views\r\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\r\npriority: 1\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - view api.crm_factory_picker_list\r\n  - view api.pm_factory_list\r\n  - view api.source_capture_inventory\r\n  - view api.opa_disney_property\r\n  - view api.opa_lucasfilm_property\r\n  - view api.opa_marvel_property\r\n  - table api.crm_factory_picker_list\r\n  - table api.opa_disney_property\r\n  - table api.opa_lucasfilm_property\r\n  - table api.opa_marvel_property\r\n  - table api.pm_factory_list\r\n  - table api.source_capture_inventory\r\n```\r\n\r\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bc45-4bcf-7781-a12c-7a01889f2d42 on EDGE-DEV\r\n\r\n\r\nRecovery classification: the six table labels in the scope are parser aliases of the same six catalog-proven views, not additional objects. This issue stays open for the remaining batches.","createdAt":"2026-09-11T18:01:32Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2662#issuecomment-5638661531","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABUEOsXA","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Part B — per-object remedy plan and blast radius (NOT applied)\n\nPart A (the four zero-policy tables) is split out into PR #2815, lane claim #2812, migration `20260911225108`. **Nothing in Part B is applied here.** This comment is the plan the owner ruling is needed against.\n\n### First: the object list in this issue's `writes:` block is stale\n\nRe-derived against production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` on 2026-09-11 using `pg_class.reloptions` + `has_table_privilege` (not `information_schema`, which is a documented false negative here). Compared with the 2026-09-10 evidence file:\n\n- **Now already invoker, no longer in scope:** `api.crm_contact_segment_counts`, `api.crm_contact_segment_list`, `api.crm_ingested_domain_list`, `public.sg_archive_usage`. Four of the six objects named in this issue's `writes:` block are among these — the block should not be worked as written.\n- **Definer but never listed:** `api.plm_item_list`. It carries definer semantics plus a blanket `authenticated` grant and was missed by the original census.\n\nLive definer-or-materialized objects granting `SELECT` to `authenticated` today: **14 `api` views, 2 `public` views, 2 `public` materialized views** (18 total). None grants `anon`.\n\n### Blast radius method\n\nThree independent sources, because no single one answers it:\n1. **Catalog** — semantics, grants, and the RLS state of every underlying source table (`pg_depend`/`pg_rewrite`).\n2. **Production edge logs, 24h to 2026-09-11** — who actually calls each object, and with which client (`supabase-js-web` = browser/user JWT; `supabase-js-deno`/`SupabaseEdgeRuntime` = edge function on the service role).\n3. **Application source** — `popcrm-web`, `popdam3`, `poppim-web`, `dflow_plm`, `apps/db-data-admin`, separating browser anon-key+JWT callers from service-role callers.\n\n**Only browser/user-JWT callers are blast radius.** A service-role caller bypasses RLS and ignores grants to `authenticated`, so it cannot be broken by any of these remedies.\n\n### Group 1 — no caller at all. Safe to narrow now (7 objects)\n\nZero references in any application repo **and** zero Data API traffic in 24h.\n\n| Object | Remedy |\n|---|---|\n| `api.crm_account_list` | revoke `authenticated`, grant `service_role` |\n| `api.crm_factory_picker_list` | same |\n| `api.pm_factory_list` | same |\n| `api.source_capture_inventory` | same |\n| `api.opa_disney_property` | same |\n| `api.opa_lucasfilm_property` | same |\n| `api.opa_marvel_property` | same |\n\n`api.crm_account_list` is one of the two objects that produced the original 826-row cross-application read. Narrowing the grant closes it outright with no caller to break. **This group needs no business ruling** and could ship as a Part A-style tightening if you want the highest-value half of the finding closed quickly.\n\n### Group 2 — live browser callers. Remedy known, but it changes who sees what (7 objects)\n\nThese are read from a browser with a user JWT today. Setting `security_invoker=true` makes the *underlying* RLS apply, which is the correct fix **only if** those policies admit the app's own users. That is the business judgement.\n\n| Object | Browser caller | Underlying RLS | Proposed remedy | Risk |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `api.crm_customer_list` | popcrm-web | `core.customer` 2 pol, `plm.customer_import` 1 pol | `security_invoker=true` | Med — already has an internal caller filter; verify policies admit CRM users |\n| `api.crm_customer_picker_list` | popcrm-web | `core.customer`, `crm.customer_ext` 2 pol each | `security_invoker=true` | Med — **no** internal caller filter today |\n| `api.crm_contact_list` | popcrm-web | 4 sources, all RLS+policies | **leave as-is** | Low — already filters on `app.has_app_access('crm')`; this is the object that correctly returned 0 to the DAM viewer |\n| `api.dam_customer_list` | popdam3 | `core.customer`, `dam.customer_ext` | `security_invoker=true` | Med |\n| `api.dam_factory_list` | popdam3 | `core.factory`, `dam.factory_ext` | `security_invoker=true` | Med |\n| `api.pm_customer_list` | poppim-web | `core.customer`, `pim.customer_ext` | `security_invoker=true` | Med — no internal caller filter |\n| `public.style_tracker_audit_log_with_user` | popdam3 `StylesPage` | `public.profiles` 3 pol, `style_tracker_audit_log` 1 pol | `security_invoker=true` | Low-Med |\n\n**The ruling needed:** should a signed-in user of one app see another app's customer/factory master lists? `core.customer` and `core.factory` are shared Master Data, so \"yes\" is a defensible answer — in which case the remedy for most of Group 2 is to leave the read open and document it as intended, not to flip the flag.\n\n### Group 3 — remedy is NOT a flag flip. Genuine design work (4 objects)\n\n| Object | Why the simple remedy fails |\n|---|---|\n| `public.style_guide_file_groups` (matview, **22,045 rows**) | **RLS cannot apply to a materialized view at all**, so `security_invoker` does not exist as an option. Read from the browser by popdam3 `PopSGLibraryPage`, so revoking `authenticated` breaks the PopSG library. Needs either a `security_invoker` view wrapped over the matview with the grant moved to it, or a DAM-specific role. |\n| `public.style_guide_folders` (matview) | Same, same page. |\n| `public.style_tracker_rows_with_bridge` (**15,742 rows**) | Read from the browser by popdam3 `StylesPage` and `useOrderList`. Sources include `dflow.RFQGroup` and `dflow.RFQItem`, which have **no RLS and no `authenticated` grant**, plus `api.plm_item_list`. Flipping to invoker would deny every current caller, not restrict them. Needs the caller filter approach, not the flag. Note `public.style_tracker_rows` is intentionally open to all signed-in users per AGENTS.md §0.4 — do not \"harden\" that. |\n| `api.plm_item_list` | **6,288 calls in 24h**, almost all from an edge function on the service role, plus 3 browser calls. Sources include `coldlion.item_detail` and `public.popdam_item_state`, which are **RLS-enabled with ZERO policies** — so `security_invoker=true` would deny all reads, including the 6,288/day. Remedy is to narrow the grant to `service_role` **after** identifying the 3 browser calls. |\n\n### Recommended sequence\n\n1. **Group 1 now** — 7 objects, no callers, no ruling needed. Closes `crm_account_list`.\n2. **Group 2 after Albert's ruling** on cross-application visibility of shared Master Data.\n3. **Group 3 as individual claims**, each with its own preview rehearsal; `style_tracker_rows_with_bridge` and the two matviews touch live PopDAM pages.\n\nEach object above should become its own governed claim rather than one migration, so a rollback never has to unpick seven applications at once.\n\n### What is still not measured\n\nThe 38 `SECURITY DEFINER` functions executable by `anon` and 111 by `authenticated`, plus 78 trigger-returning functions carrying an `anon`/`authenticated` EXECUTE grant. Exercising an RPC is a write-shaped call and needs preview fixtures. Carried forward, not cleared.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T22:58:46Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2662#issuecomment-5641579612","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABUERRaA","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Work contract published at `refs/db-contracts/2662/7` (sha256 `e9041f03ea4b24faa593e1a493381cb5e5d58aaa8c33cc19bd5f55a023fedf9f`).\n\nThis comment is a human-readable COPY. every live writer of these tables is server-side and must keep working.\",\n    \"Do not run direct production DDL, and do not weaken any guard to make a check pass.\"\n  ],\n  \"required_checks\": [\n    \"bash scripts/check-sql.sh\"\n  ],\n  \"assumptions\": [\n    \"All four tables have RLS enabled with zero policies, so anon and authenticated are already denied and removing their grants changes no behaviour today.\",\n    \"The only live traffic to these tables is service-role, which bypasses RLS and is untouched by this migration.\"\n  ],\n  \"stop_conditions\": [\n    \"Stop if any of the four tables is found to have a policy, since a grant revoke would then remove access something relies on.\",\n    \"Stop if edge logs show a browser anon or authenticated caller succeeding against any of the four tables.\",\n    \"Stop before production promotion: that gate needs the owner to name the exact resource and action, and the owner is asleep.\"\n  ]\n}\n```","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:03:37Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2662#issuecomment-5641621864","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABUER1Ig","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Correction to the Part B plan above — batch 1 is already merged\n\nMy previous comment is **wrong in an important way** and I am correcting it rather than editing it away.\n\nI reported that four objects had \"drifted\" to `security_invoker=true` since the 2026-09-10 evidence file, and treated that as unexplained catalog drift. It is not drift. **PR #2764 (\"gate cross-app CRM definer views (#2662 batch 1)\", merge `99aa8cfa`) is already merged**, carrying migration `20260911124746_crm_definer_views_caller_gate.sql`. It was authored by a separate lane on this same issue, under contract `refs/db-contracts/2662/1`. I did not check for merged sibling work before writing the plan.\n\nWhat that migration actually did:\n\n- `api.crm_ingested_domain_list`, `api.crm_contact_segment_list`, `api.crm_contact_segment_counts`, `public.sg_archive_usage` → flipped to `security_invoker = true`.\n- `api.crm_customer_list` and `api.crm_account_list` → **deliberately left `security_invoker = false`** and instead given an in-view caller gate, `WHERE (SELECT app.has_app_access('crm'))` — the same pattern `crm_contact_list` already used.\n\n### Two corrections that matter\n\n**1. `api.crm_account_list` is already closed.** I listed it in Group 1 as having no caller and being safe to narrow. It was in fact the higher-value target — one of the two objects behind the original 826-row cross-application read — and #2764 already gated it. A PopDAM viewer now gets 0 rows because `app.has_app_access('crm')` is false for them. **No further work is needed on it**, and my proposed grant revoke would have been redundant.\n\n**2. `api.crm_customer_list` is already closed too**, by the same gate, and my Group 2 entry proposing `security_invoker=true` for it is superseded. Note the merged migration chose the caller-gate remedy over the flag flip *on purpose*, because these views read `core.customer`, shared Master Data whose RLS policies would not admit the CRM app's users directly. That is a useful precedent for the rest of Group 2 and it partly answers the business question I raised: for shared Master Data the house pattern is an explicit app-access gate in the view, not invoker semantics.\n\n### The revised remaining scope\n\nStill open and unremediated, as far as I can verify against `origin/main` and the live catalog today:\n\n- **Group 1, revised (6 objects, no callers, no ruling needed):** `api.crm_factory_picker_list`, `api.pm_factory_list`, `api.source_capture_inventory`, `api.opa_disney_property`, `api.opa_lucasfilm_property`, `api.opa_marvel_property`. (`crm_account_list` removed — already done.)\n- **Group 2, revised (5 objects):** `api.crm_customer_picker_list`, `api.dam_customer_list`, `api.dam_factory_list`, `api.pm_customer_list`, `public.style_tracker_audit_log_with_user`. The recommended remedy for the customer/factory ones is now the **#2764 caller-gate pattern**, not `security_invoker=true`.\n- **Group 3 unchanged (4 objects):** the two style-guide materialized views, `public.style_tracker_rows_with_bridge`, and `api.plm_item_list`.\n\n### One further constraint I missed\n\nContract `refs/db-contracts/2662/1` names `api.plm_item_list`, `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties` and `api.pim_item_picker` as **owned by other active claims**. So `api.plm_item_list` is not free for this issue to take, which is a second reason to leave it alone beyond the 6,288-calls-a-day risk I described. Whoever picks up the revised Group 1 should re-run a merged-sibling check first; I did not, and that is what produced the error above.\n\nThe Part A scope (the four zero-policy tables in PR #2815) is unaffected by any of this — it shares no object with #2764.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:04:25Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2662#issuecomment-5641631010","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABUES7SA","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Work contract published at `refs/db-contracts/2662/8` (sha256 `236ef48f113e69abd26d5ff828dd13ccee7a45ccfe19467ca9f091f5d0fc733e`).\n\nThis comment is a human-readable COPY. {"assignees":[],"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\ndepends_on:\n```\n\nReviewer `grok-4.6` (`ai-grok-review`) fails to produce a recordable terminal verdict on large migrations.\n\nThird confirmed occurrence: PR #2409 (1798-line migration) returned `REFUSED: review wrapper did not produce a recordable terminal verdict (exit 1)` and had to be released as `turn_limit_cancelled` and replaced. It succeeded on the smaller PR #2490 (914 lines).\n\nCost: every occurrence burns a reviewer slot, a release, a replacement and a full re-review.\n\nNext step: measure the actual size threshold, then either raise grok's turn/step budget in the wrapper or make the allocator skip grok when the PR's migration exceeds that size.\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABVtCJEA","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Diagnosed and fixed in **PR #3341**. The fix is in this repository; `popcre/ai-devops` was **not** touched.\n\n**It is not an input-size or token ceiling.** The whole brief already reaches the provider through `--prompt-file`, so nothing is truncated. The limit is a **turn budget**: `ai-grok-review` defaults to 20 agent turns (`AI_GROK_MAX_TURNS`, `D:\\repos\\ai-devops\\bin\\ai-grok-review` line 121), and a reviewer reading a 1798-line migration spends them opening files before it ever writes a verdict line. The two occurrences on this issue bracket the threshold between **914 changed lines** (PR #2490, succeeded) and **1798** (PR #2409, failed three times). Turn exhaustion maps to `turn_limit_cancelled`, which is exactly the terminal state that was observed.\n\n**Why the fix belongs here and not cross-repo.** `--max-turns` is documented in that wrapper as overridable per call — a runtime bound, not part of the cached prompt prefix — so the caller that knows how big the review is can size it. Raising the wrapper's global default would charge every small review for the largest one, and `popcre/ai-devops` is on `feature-branch-pr` with a merge queue (its `AGENTS.md`: work on a branch and pull request, never push to `main`), so it would be a separate governed PR there. No blind cross-repo change was made.\n\n**Why raise the budget rather than skip grok on large migrations.** Skipping a reviewer on exactly the changes that carry the most risk is the wrong half of the choice this issue offered.\n\n**What landed**\n\n- New `scripts/lib/reviewer-turn-budget.mjs`. The budget rises with changed migration lines, is capped, and **can never fall below today's default**. An unmeasurable size is treated as large, not small. The measurement never throws and can never block or fail a review — a measurement that could veto one would be a new way to lose a reviewer slot, which is the defect.\n- A round that still ends without a verdict now **names the budget it was given** — \"was launched with 60 turn(s): 1798 changed migration line(s) were granted 60 turns\" — so the failure is diagnosable from the refusal alone instead of costing a fresh hand investigation. It stays a loud `REFUSED`, and the existing `turn_limit_cancelled` reroute path is unchanged.\n- Reviewers with no `--max-turns` contract are launched exactly as before.\n\n**Regression tests verified to fail first.** Against pristine `origin/main` in a throwaway worktree, 3 of the 4 new `#2492` tests in `scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs` fail (82 tests, 79 pass, 3 fail) and `scripts/lib/reviewer-turn-budget.test.mjs` cannot load at all. After the fix: 93 pass, 0 fail.\n\n**This issue is NOT closed yet.** PR #3341 cannot be merged while the governed reviewer gate is down repo-wide (issue #3346), which refuses with:\n\n```\nREFUSED: active reviewer leases are unreadable; reviewer assignment refused before mutex acquisition\n```\n\nThe gate was not bypassed. This issue closes when #3341 merges.\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n","createdAt":"2026-09-20T17:38:02Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2492#issuecomment-5751474448","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABW1ROjw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"repo-maintenance/documentation (marker #3496): a repo session owns this — left open, not orchestrator work. #2478 status: merged to main, NOT promoted to production, and blocked on reviewer coverage\n\nPR #2746 merged to main (merge commit `26d9345b`, 2026-09-11 22:32:17Z) with **one** reviewer approval, not two. That was not a lane error and not a bypass — the Guarded Merge workflow ran and passed. The merge gate has no minimum slot count, so a never-drawn slot 2 was invisible to it and one approval satisfied it. Filed as #2837.\n\nAll nine durable verdicts for `2478-2746` are `slot=1`: eight APPROVE (grok-4.6 ×3, muse-spark-1.3-contributor ×4, glm-5.3 ×1) and one REVISE (grok-4.6). Slot 2 was never drawn at any head, in any namespace.\n\n**Ruling: not promoted to production, and not retro-closed.** The merged SQL is real and was reviewed by one reviewer — the gap is authorization coverage, not correctness. Promotion stays frozen until two independent verdicts exist at one head.\n\n**Slot 2 cannot be completed against PR #2746.** A draw would be *accepted* (`reviewTargetEligible` admits a merged PR whose merge commit is proven in main), but `recordReviewVerdict` requires an open PR and an exact head match, so recording could never succeed — burning a reviewer sequence and stranding a lease the release path cannot free. Sequence 2510 is deliberately untouched. Do not draw it.\n\n### What the successor lane must know\n\n**The migration is ALREADY ON MAIN** — `supabase/migrations/20260911212849_shared_style_group_sku_key.sql`, blob `9fcc0b3c9fcb0be234bb8a7eb68b1b6e1ec46ea8`. So a fresh PR **cannot** re-add it: that is an empty diff, which gives two reviewers nothing to review and yields no verdict artifact.\n\nThe route is a **NEW version file timestamped after `20260911214438`** that re-declares the same function. Two migrations have landed since (`20260911213429_popsg_search_v2_production_performance`, `20260911214438_plm_factory_time_templates`) and the merge gate's Guard B refuses any migration sorting before the base branch's newest version. The old version string `20260911212849` stays in the tree, unapplied to production, permanently.\n\n**Claim:** issue **#2745** is still open and holds the objects — `public.style_group_key_for_sku`, `public.rebuild_style_groups_batch`, `public.reconcile_style_group_drift`. **Reuse it.** A second claim on the same branch cannot be released.\n\n**Contracts, both already on main, needing no change:**\n- `supabase/tests/style_group_key_for_sku_contracts.sql` — blob `9ac3ce99b27f25f1db626aacc59d89f2d3c8c3d8`\n- `supabase/tests/style_group_drift_reconciler_contracts.sql` — blob `cf26f087e8c5d62b1bda9a902c817f2784219050`\n\nNeither is quarantined. Do not add speculative entries to `supabase/tests/ci-quarantine.txt` — a nonexistent filename there fails the job.\n\n**What does NOT carry over.** The ephemeral evidence is pinned to dead head `39be641f` (check job `103440920775`, run `34653549438`, artifact `10284907352`, digest `sha256:6648b6a3…`) and a new head needs its own run. The low-risk classification (`preview_required_reasons` → 0) was computed for the string `20260911212849`; a new version string must be **reclassified, not assumed**.\n\n**Two traps.** \"Documents-only merge authorization\" fails on a migration branch and is not among main's twelve required contexts — expected red, not a blocker. And draw BOTH reviewer slots at the same head before running either: this entire incident is one drawn slot re-reviewed across nine heads.\n\n— shared-db orchestrator (marker #2758)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-12T00:44:58Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2478#issuecomment-5642270233","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABUE8dzQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Correction to my earlier comment — two claims in it are wrong\n\nI ran the gate correctly this time and it contradicts what I recorded above. Both errors were mine.\n\n**1. \"The gate returns `REFUSED: PR number is unavailable` because the PR is closed\" — FALSE.**\nThat string was operator error. `check-exact-head-approval.mjs` reads `PR_NUMBER` from the environment\n(line 286) and `REQUESTED_SHA` (line 287, defaulting to the PR's live head). It accepts **no `--pr` or\n`--head-sha` flags**; passing them means it never receives a PR number at all. Closed-ness had nothing\nto do with it. Correct invocation:\n\n```\nPR_NUMBER=2746 node scripts/check-exact-head-approval.mjs\n```\n\n**2. \"Carry-forward fired correctly and line 423 was silent\" — FALSE at the final head.**\nRun that way, the gate exits **2** and refuses, verbatim:\n\n```\nREFUSED: head 39be641f5e909e60e7c7c63b0f72420062f443f6 has no durable APPROVE artifact;\na review that wrote no artifact never authorizes a merge; an APPROVE cannot be carried\nforward because this head has reviewer records of its own (assignment, return or verdict),\nso it is judged on those alone\n```\n\nSo line 423 is **not** silent at `39be641f` — it is the operative clause, and the head has no durable\nAPPROVE of its own. I had conceded the opposite to the #2746 lane after it corrected me, and I was\nwrong in the other direction. That makes three times on this file that I reasoned about the mechanism\ninstead of querying it.\n\n**What this does and does not change.**\n\nIt does **not** revive #2478 or change the ruling: still merged to main, still **not promoted to\nproduction**, still not retro-closed, and slot 2 still must not be drawn against the merged PR\n(`recordReviewVerdict` requires an open PR at an exact head, so the draw would be accepted, the\nrecording could never succeed, and a reviewer sequence would burn while the lease stranded).\n\nIt **does** change the diagnosis of how the merge happened. The merge did not rest on this check\npassing at the final head — the check refuses that head. Whatever authorized the merge, it was not\nthis gate agreeing there was coverage. Recorded on #2837.\n\nEverything else in my earlier comment stands: the migration is already on main\n(`20260911212849_shared_style_group_sku_key.sql`, blob `9fcc0b3c…`), so a fresh PR must carry a NEW\nversion file dated after `20260911214438`; claim **#2745** must be reused; the contract blobs are\nunchanged; and the old evidence pair does not carry over — the low-risk classification was computed\nfor the string `20260911212849` and must be reclassified, never assumed.\n\nVerify anything I assert about this gate by running it yourself, with the invocation above.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-12T00:53:45Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2478#issuecomment-5642329549","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABUE-KXQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Closing the loop: the merge was legitimate. Forensics disprove that.\n\nThe Guarded Merge run (**34654341789**, success) invoked the gate against the exact final head `39be641f` **twice** — pre-flight and again under the merge lock — and it PASSED both times, carrying forward from approved head `a0110723`. The head was committed thirteen minutes before the run began; the merge was pinned with `--match-head-commit`; no `--admin`, no bypass, merged by `app/github-actions` under a required status context with `enforce_admins` enabled.\n\nThe gate refuses **today** only because a reviewer assignment (`sequence=2510 reviewer=glm-5.3`) was written at that head at 22:48:40Z — sixteen minutes AFTER the 22:32:17Z merge — which permanently closes the carry-forward path the merge had lawfully used. That later review could not record: *\"review target is no longer the exact open PR head.\"*\n\n**So nobody did anything wrong on this PR, and my line above that \"whatever authorized the merge, it was not this gate agreeing there was coverage\" is withdrawn — the gate did agree.** What it agreed on is the problem: `1 approval(s), 1 pinned assignment(s)`. {"assignees":[],"body":"## What happens\n\n`--assign-reviewer --issue 2441 --pr 2446 --head-sha b1e588e5… --review-slot 2` printed:\n\n```\nREFUSED: release of refs/db-coordination/author-acquisition could not be proved after atomic deletion; RECOVERY REQUIRED: refs/db-coordination/author-acquisition expected SHA ef2b5425bd7caebb29f9ec7eb05dbab30b84fd3d. Use the guarded recover-author-mutex.yml procedure and do not retry blindly\n```\n\nThe assignment had in fact **succeeded**:\n\n```\n$ git ls-remote origin 'refs/db-coordination/*'\n657224d2…  refs/db-coordination/reviewer-index-cutover\n0385a268…  refs/db-coordination/reviewer-round-robin      <-- advanced from 377f1630\n```\n\n`refs/db-coordination/author-acquisition` is absent, so the atomic deletion worked; only the verification read was stale. And the lease commit exists:\n\n```\ndb-coordination reviewer-cursor sequence=1479 reviewer=codex-gpt-5.6-sol issue=2441 pr=2446 head=b1e588e5… slot=2\n```\n\n## Why this is worse than a noisy warning\n\n1. **The caller loses the result.** The success path prints the sequence, reviewer and wrapper as JSON. On this path it prints nothing, so the operator does not learn which reviewer was drawn or what sequence to run — the assignment is invisible unless someone thinks to read `refs/db-review-active/*` by hand and `git cat-file` the commit. I only found sequence 1479 because I went looking.\n2. **It sends the operator to a guarded recovery against healthy state.** The message names `recover-author-mutex.yml` and says \"do not retry blindly\" for a condition that is not present. Running that procedure on a healthy mutex is the actual risk this message creates.\n3. **A blind retry draws a SECOND reviewer**, spending another rotation slot on a PR that already has one, because the caller believes nothing happened.\n\nSeen at least three times today: twice on `--replace-failed-reviewer` during PR #2409's slot-2 replacement, and here. Each time the ref was confirmed absent and a plain retry (or a manual ref read) showed the operation had completed.\n\n## Requested\n\nBefore reporting an unproved release, **re-read the ref with a bounded retry**, and treat \"the ref is absent\" as proof of release rather than as failure to prove it — absence is the intended end state. Only report `RECOVERY REQUIRED` when the ref is actually still present and owned by someone else.\n\nIf the operation completed, print its normal JSON result. An operation must never succeed silently and report a recovery instruction.\n\nRelated: #2456, #1767.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 88\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABVsXr3A","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Fixed in PR #3316 (open, checks running).\n\n**#2457 and #2844 are the same root cause and are fixed once.** After the mutex is deleted by an accepted `git push --atomic --force-with-lease`, the release was re-read three times over ~3s from a git replica that lags that deletion; a lagging answer became `RECOVERY REQUIRED`, and because the release runs in a `finally` the successful draw's result was discarded.\n\nWhat changed (the refusal itself is kept — an orphaned mutex is never assumed released):\n\n- the readback now uses the same bounded ladder `releaseOwnedRef` uses (0/500/1000/2000/3000/4000 ms);\n- an answer that still names our owner commit is confirmed once against GitHub's ref API, which is not the lagging replica, before anything is refused;\n- proving the release no longer draws on the derived 25-request ceiling (#2844's squeeze) — the ceiling is **not** widened, a hard-bounded allowance covers the release proof alone;\n- a completed operation never loses its result: it is carried on the refusal with an explicit \"this already succeeded, do not retry\" line.\n\nThree regression tests, verified non-vacuous: against `origin/main`'s unfixed script the suite reports `pass 609 / fail 3`, with the fix `pass 612 / fail 0`.\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n","createdAt":"2026-09-20T15:35:38Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2457#issuecomment-5750778844","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABVsYU0w","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Work contract published at `refs/db-contracts/2457/1` (sha256 `fbb4b53067939822f5d1d713eb5730fcc85863ecf8f15b46e8ad7c228319a98c`).\n\nThis comment is a human-readable COPY. {"assignees":[],"body":"> **CURRENT POSITION — supersedes the original text below, which is kept for history.**\n> The evidence in this issue was gathered in an **8.1-day window that contained zero writes to `asset_tags`**, and that table turns out to be bursty, not static: 671,014 rows created in the last 30 days, written on only 26 distinct days since March, last write 2026-08-27 — one day before the statistics reset that zeroed the counters. So the window was not merely thin, it was **mistimed**: any index serving the import path is idle in exactly the period measured, and `asset_tags_forward_asset_id_idx` (206 MB, 6 scans) is precisely that shape.\n>\n> **Two classes of candidate, and only one survives a bad window:**\n> - **Structural — holds in any window.** `idx_asset_tags_asset_id` (42 MB) is a strict leading-column prefix of both `asset_tags_forward_asset_id_idx` (asset_id, id) and `asset_tags_asset_id_tag_key` (asset_id, tag). It cannot serve a query either of those could not. This argument does not depend on a counter.\n> - **Usage-only — blocked.** `asset_tags_forward_asset_id_idx` (206 MB), `idx_asset_tags_source` (37 MB), `idx_style_guide_file_tags_file_status` (22 MB). These rest entirely on scan counts from a window now known to be unrepresentative.\n>\n> **Never droppable regardless of scan count:** `asset_tags_asset_id_tag_key`, `asset_tags_pkey`, `style_guide_file_tags_pkey` — they back a constraint or primary key.\n>\n> **Re-read gate, mandatory, in order — stop at the first failure:**\n> 1. `pg_stat_bgwriter.stats_reset` must equal the baseline `2026-08-28 21:01:01 -04`. If it moved, the window was lost: take a fresh baseline, propose a new date, recommend nothing. Do not subtract across a reset — it yields an absurdly low delta that reads as \"unused\".\n> 2. **The new window must contain a real write burst to `asset_tags`, proved from the `created_at` row distribution and not from `pg_stat`.** If the window is quiet, the measurement is void: say \"the window was quiet, so this proves nothing\" and stop. A second quiet window reproduces the same zeros and would read as confirmation.\n> 3. Only then subtract the baseline and report deltas alongside the burst size and the number of write days.\n>\n> Earliest re-read 2026-09-29. **No drop on any number currently in this issue, by anyone.** Drops go through the orchestrator as their own migration, `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, each justified by its own delta over a stated window that is proved to contain a burst.\n\n---\n\nSplit out of #2417, where the evidence was gathered. Read-only investigation first; no drop should be proposed until the observation window below has run.\n\n## The opportunity\n\n`public.asset_tags` carries **723 MB of indexes on a 456 MB table**, and a single index appears to carry all the traffic.\n\n| index | size | scans | note |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `asset_tags_active_asset_idx` (asset_id, tag) WHERE status='active' | 127 MB | **2,009,225** | essentially all traffic |\n| `asset_tags_forward_asset_id_idx` (asset_id, id) | **206 MB** | 6 | largest index on the table |\n| `asset_tags_asset_id_tag_key` UNIQUE (asset_id, tag) | 176 MB | 0 | enforces a constraint — **not a candidate** |\n| `asset_tags_pkey` (id) | 135 MB | 0 | primary key — **not a candidate** |\n| `idx_asset_tags_asset_id` (asset_id) | 42 MB | 4 | strict leading-column prefix of both indexes above it |\n| `idx_asset_tags_source` (source) | 37 MB | 6 | |\n\n`public.style_guide_file_tags` adds one: `idx_style_guide_file_tags_file_status` (style_guide_file_id, status), 22 MB, 0 scans.\n\nCandidates total roughly **285 MB** across three indexes. `idx_asset_tags_asset_id` is the clearest on structure alone — it is a strict leading-column prefix of `(asset_id, id)` and `(asset_id, tag)` and cannot serve a query neither of those could.\n\nBoth tables are effectively static (see #2417: `asset_tags` records zero lifetime writes against two million index scans), so this is disk and backup weight rather than write amplification. That lowers the urgency but does not remove the value.\n\n## Why this is not yet actionable — the gate\n\nThe scan counters above share a statistics reset with the write counters on the same tables. `asset_tags` reports **zero lifetime inserts** while holding 2.18 million rows, which is only possible post-reset. So \"6 scans\" means six *since an unknown date*, not six ever.\n\nThis is the same trap as the `n_live_tup` error that opened #2417, and as the earlier incident where a field was called dead on 291 rows and turned out 70% populated across 3,981. A low number over an unknown window is not evidence.\n\n**No index may be dropped on the numbers above.** Required first:\n\n1. Establish the counter reset date. If it cannot be established from the platform, say so explicitly rather than assuming one.\n2. Record a baseline of `idx_scan` per index on both tables, with a timestamp.\n3. Re-read after a window covering at least one full monthly cycle — month-end and quarter-end reporting are exactly the paths that would use an otherwise-idle index.\n4. Only indexes still at or near zero across a known window, and not backing a constraint or primary key, become candidates.\n\n## Then\n\nDrops go through the normal branch-and-PR route as a structural change, one migration, `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, and each drop justified by its own observed count over the stated window. Record the pre-drop sizes so the saving is measurable afterwards.\n\nRelated: #2417, #2209.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 40\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - index public.idx_asset_tags_asset_id\nreads:\n  - table public.asset_tags\n```\n\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABSzZzrg","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Classified by the shared-db orchestrator (marker #2404).\n\n**Admission test: ACCEPT** — dropping an index is a shape change. **Blocked**, and the block is a measurement window, not a dependency on other work.\n\nThe gating in this issue is right and it stays: no drop on the current numbers, by anyone. Establish the counter reset date, take a timestamped baseline, re-read after a window covering at least one month-end. The scan counters share the reset that zeroed the write counters, so \"6 scans\" means six since an unknown date, and an index that serves only a month-end or quarter-end path looks identical to a dead one in a short window.\n\n**One inconsistency to resolve before the static-table conclusion is relied on.** The issue argues correctly that the scan counters cannot be read as lifetime figures because of the reset. The same reset zeroed the write counters. So \"`asset_tags` records zero lifetime writes\" is also \"zero writes since an unknown date\" — the same weakness, applied to the load-bearing half of the reasoning rather than the cautious half. That matters twice over:\n\n1. It is the basis for calling the table static, which is the basis for saying the 2026-09-05 ANALYZE holds indefinitely.\n2. A table that takes writes only at month-end or during an import would show zero writes in a short window and be misread as static.\n\nThe fix is cheap and belongs in this issue's first step, since the reset date is being established there anyway: read the write counters against that same date, and if the window does not cover a month-end, say the question is open rather than closed. `idx_asset_tags_asset_id` being a strict leading-column prefix of two larger indexes is a **structural** argument and does not depend on any counter — it is the one candidate that could survive a bad window. The other two rest on usage evidence and must wait for it.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 40\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - index public.idx_asset_tags_asset_id\nreads:\n  - table public.asset_tags\n```\n\nRead-only work on this issue may proceed during the structural merge freeze (#2424); the final drop step may not.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:13:50Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2427#issuecomment-5556827054","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABSzaBgg","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Step 1 and step 2 are done. The reset date **is** establishable, which changes what this issue is waiting for.\n\n## The counter window is known: 8.1 days\n\n```\npg_postmaster_start_time()        2026-08-28 21:01:01 -04\npg_stat_bgwriter.stats_reset      2026-08-28 21:01:01 -04\noldest autovacuum/autoanalyze\n  timestamp anywhere in the db    2026-08-29 18:59:11 -04\nreading taken                     2026-09-06 00:14:11 -04\nPostgreSQL 17.6\n```\n\nThe bgwriter reset timestamp is identical to the postmaster start time to the second, and no autovacuum timestamp anywhere in the database predates that restart. PostgreSQL 17 discards cumulative statistics when the server does not shut down cleanly, so the counters were lost at that restart and have been accumulating since.\n\nThat also explains the `asset_tags` anomaly that flagged the reset in the first place — zero lifetime writes against 2.18 million rows simply means the table has taken no writes **since 2026-08-28**, which is consistent with the static-table finding in #2417 rather than in tension with it.\n\nSo the window is **8.1 days**, not unknown. Every count below is per 8.1 days.\n\n## Baseline, taken 2026-09-06 00:14 -04\n\n`public.asset_tags` — heap 456 MB, indexes 723 MB:\n\n| index | size | idx_scan in 8.1 d |\n|---|---|---|\n| `asset_tags_active_asset_idx` | 127 MB | 2,009,225 |\n| `asset_tags_forward_asset_id_idx` | 206 MB | 6 |\n| `asset_tags_asset_id_tag_key` (UNIQUE) | 176 MB | 0 |\n| `asset_tags_pkey` | 135 MB | 0 |\n| `idx_asset_tags_asset_id` | 42 MB | 4 |\n| `idx_asset_tags_source` | 37 MB | 6 |\n\n`public.style_guide_file_tags` — heap 350 MB:\n\n| index | size | idx_scan in 8.1 d |\n|---|---|---|\n| `idx_style_guide_file_tags_tag_status` | 119 MB | 324 |\n| `style_guide_file_tags_unique_source` (UNIQUE) | 103 MB | 22,898 |\n| `style_guide_file_tags_pkey` | 44 MB | 0 |\n| `idx_style_guide_file_tags_file_status` | 22 MB | 0 |\n| `idx_style_guide_file_tags_source` | 13 MB | 3 |\n\n## What the window does and does not cover\n\nIt contains one month-end boundary (31 August into 1 September). It contains **no quarter-end**, and 8.1 days is thin by the standard that produced the earlier error of calling a field dead on 291 rows when 3,981 showed it 70% populated.\n\nSo the counts are now real measurements rather than meaningless ones, but they are still thin measurements. The revised gate:\n\n1. ~~Establish the reset date~~ — **done, 2026-08-28 21:01 -04.**\n2. ~~Record a timestamped baseline~~ — **done, above.**\n3. Re-read on or after **2026-09-29**, giving a window of roughly one month that spans a full month-end close. Subtract the baseline above to get the delta; the delta is the evidence, not the raw counter.\n4. Candidates are indexes still at or near zero *in the delta*, excluding `asset_tags_asset_id_tag_key`, `asset_tags_pkey` and `style_guide_file_tags_pkey`, which back a constraint or primary key and are not droppable regardless of scan count.\n\nOne caveat for step 3: if the server restarts uncleanly again before 2026-09-29, the counters reset and the window restarts with it. Whoever does the re-read must re-check `pg_stat_bgwriter.stats_reset` against the baseline timestamp above and, if it has moved, discard the delta and start again rather than subtracting across a reset — that subtraction would silently produce a negative or absurdly low count and read as \"unused\".\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:14:39Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2427#issuecomment-5556830594","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABSzadow","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"**Third correction on these same counters, and this one is against my own correction.** The orchestrator challenged that I had applied the reset caveat to only half my reasoning — refusing to read \"6 scans\" as a lifetime figure while happily reading \"zero lifetime writes\" as one. That challenge was correct, and the row data refutes the conclusion I drew from it.\n\n## Evidence that does not depend on the counters at all\n\nBoth tables carry `created_at` and `updated_at`, so their entire write history is readable from the rows themselves, immune to any statistics reset:\n\n| | `asset_tags` | `style_guide_file_tags` |\n|---|---|---|\n| rows | 2,173,392 | 1,156,758 |\n| first row created | 2026-03-13 | 2026-07-26 |\n| **last write** | **2026-08-27** | 2026-09-04 |\n| created in last 30 days | **671,014** | 64,135 |\n| created in last 90 days | 775,297 | 1,156,758 |\n| distinct days with writes | **26** | 28 |\n| written since the 2026-08-28 reset | 0 | 10,302 |\n\n## `asset_tags` is not static. It is bursty.\n\nIt took **671,014 rows in the last thirty days** and has been written on only 26 distinct days in nearly six months. Its last write was 2026-08-27 — one day before the statistics reset. So the 8.1-day window of apparent silence is not evidence of a static table; it is the gap between two batch loads, which is exactly the false-static case the challenge predicted.\n\n**Retracting the correction I posted on #2417**: \"these tables are static, so old statistics stay accurate indefinitely\" is wrong for `asset_tags`. It is a periodically bulk-loaded table, and after its next load the statistics from 2026-09-05 will describe a table that no longer exists.\n\nWhat partially rescues the outcome, by a different mechanism than the one I claimed: a bulk load of that size does cross the autoanalyze threshold (roughly 50 + 0.1 × rows, so about 218,000 modifications at current size), so autoanalyze should fire during the load itself. The practical risk is smaller than \"no statistics forever\", but it is not zero and it is not the reason I gave. The reasoning was wrong even where the conclusion partly survives.\n\nWhat does still stand from #2417: autovacuum has never fired because inserts create no dead tuples, so the dead-tuple count stays near zero regardless of load volume. There is no daemon fault. That part rested on the control — 290 autovacuums on `style_groups`, same database, same settings — not on the write counters.\n\n## Consequence for #2427: the window is worse than thin, it is mistimed\n\nThe 8.1-day baseline window contains **zero writes to `asset_tags`**. If the table is only written during periodic imports, the indexes supporting those imports are idle in exactly the window I measured. `asset_tags_forward_asset_id_idx` at 206 MB with 6 scans and `idx_asset_tags_source` at 37 MB with 6 scans are precisely the shape an import-path index would show between imports.\n\nSo the re-read date of 2026-09-29 is not merely preferable, it is mandatory, and it must be validated rather than assumed: the re-reader must confirm the new window actually **contains a write burst** to `asset_tags` before drawing any conclusion from its index counts. A second quiet window would produce the same numbers and mean nothing again.\n\n## The one candidate that survives all of this\n\nPer the orchestrator's separation, which is the right one: `idx_asset_tags_asset_id` is a strict leading-column prefix of both `asset_tags_forward_asset_id_idx` (asset_id, id) and `asset_tags_asset_id_tag_key` (asset_id, tag). It cannot serve a query either of those could not, and that argument is **structural** — it holds whatever the counters say, in any window, burst or quiet. 42 MB.\n\nThe other two candidates rest entirely on usage evidence and cannot survive a mistimed window. They stay blocked.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:16:19Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2427#issuecomment-5556837795","viewerDidAuthor":true}],"createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:13:04Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"assignees":[],"body":"**Blocked by #2419 (reconciler). Do not merge before that is live and reading clean.**\n\n## What\n\n`queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups()` enqueues `{\"force_restart\": true}` at cursor 0 every night — a full keyset walk of every non-deleted asset (135,251 live today), whether or not anything changed. Lifetime cost of the rebuild is ~2,982 ms × 3,973 calls = **~11,849 s**.\n\nReplace the nightly full walk with a watermark: process only assets changed since the last **successful** run, plus any asset with a NULL `style_group_id`. Keep a weekly full pass as a convergence backstop.\n\nNote the ordering: #2408 (the `IS DISTINCT FROM` guard) removes the *write* cost of the nightly no-op pass; this issue removes the *read* cost of walking rows that cannot have changed. Both are worth doing, and #2408 should land and be measured first — its effect may change the size of the remaining prize.\n\n## Guards this needs, from the reviews\n\n1. **`modified_at` is app-maintained, not trigger-maintained.** It exists and is NOT NULL, but no database trigger sets it — only application code does. Any write path that changes `relative_path` or a taxonomy column without bumping it becomes invisible to the watermark for up to a week. Either add a database-level trigger to maintain it, or treat the weekly full pass as load-bearing rather than a backstop. Do not assume the column is trustworthy without checking the writers.\n2. **A partial run must never advance the watermark.** Advance it only after a fully successful run. A run that fails mid-way and still moves the mark loses its change set permanently, with no error.\n3. **Group- and tag-definition changes do not bump any asset's `modified_at`.** Editing a `style_groups` row, or the tags attached to one, changes what its assets should look like without touching the assets. The watermark must include a second input — groups changed since the last run, expanded to their member assets — or those edits go unprocessed until the weekly pass.\n4. **The weekly full pass must run with the guard from #2408 in place**, or it reintroduces the churn this whole line of work removes.\n\n## Why the reconciler comes first\n\nBoth reviewers raised this independently. The nightly full walk is currently the system's brute-force self-healing pass. Once it only visits changed rows, anything the change detection misses — see guards 1 and 3 — stays wrong until someone notices bad data in the DAM. #2419 makes that visible. Ship it, run it across at least one weekly cycle after this change, and treat a non-zero drift count as a regression in the change detection, not as noise.\n\n## Baseline (production, 2026-09-06)\n\nlive assets 135,251 — grouped 97,658 — ungrouped 37,593 — `style_groups` 10,869 — orphan group references 0.\n\nInstrumenting rows-examined vs rows-written per phase (the B5 item from the parent plan) is cheap and is what will prove this change worked; worth folding in here.\n\nRelated: #2408, #2419, #2417, #2209.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 60\ndepends_on: 2419, 2408\nwrites:\n  - function public.rebuild_style_groups_batch\n  - function public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups\nreads:\n  - table public.assets\n  - table public.style_groups\n```\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABSzXhFA","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Classified by the shared-db orchestrator (marker #2404).\n\n**Admission test: ACCEPT. Blocked on #2419**, and the issue's own recommendation to land and measure #2408 first is adopted as a dependency rather than a suggestion — #2408's guard may shrink the remaining prize enough to change whether this is worth its risk at all. Re-measure before authoring; do not author against the ~11,849 s figure.\n\nThe three guards recorded in the body are treated as blocking requirements, not notes. The third is the dangerous one: group- and tag-definition edits bump no asset's `modified_at`, so a watermark keyed on it will silently miss exactly the class of change that a definition edit causes. An author must resolve that with a second input, not with a comment acknowledging it.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 60\ndepends_on: 2419, 2408\nwrites:\n  - function public.rebuild_style_groups_batch\n  - function public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups\nreads:\n  - table public.assets\n  - table public.style_groups\n```\n","createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:05:27Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2421#issuecomment-5556789524","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABT5qqMA","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Fresh production detector result after2548promotion:6392of135278 liveassets have missing/wronggroup; unexpectedgroup/orphans0 and sampledtagdrift0of5000. Detector works, but clean-cycle condition FAILS, so watermark/full-walk retirement remains blocked. No application rows were changed. This issue and #2420 remain BLOCKED.**\n\nRead-only measurement against production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` (proof: `get_project_url` → `https://qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai.supabase.co`; `current_database()` = `postgres`). Phase 2 was **not** started.\n\n### The \"live\" half is confirmed satisfied\n\n| probe | result |\n|---|---|\n| `select count(*) from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations where version='20260907031246'` | **1** (applied) |\n| `pg_proc` lookup for `public.reconcile_style_group_drift` | **1** (present) |\n| `select count(*) from public.assets where is_deleted=false` | **135,278** |\n\n### Why \"reading clean\" still cannot be claimed\n\n**1. There is no observation series at all — this is the \"zero counter means never measured\" trap, applied to the series rather than to a single count.**\n\n`public.reconcile_style_group_drift` is `STABLE` and records nothing by design. #2419 specifies *\"a scheduled read-only job\"*. **That job does not exist in production.**\n\n```sql\nselect\n (select count(*) from cron.job where command ilike '%reconcile_style_group_drift%') as cron_jobs_calling_reconciler,\n (select count(*) from cron.job where command ilike '%clear_style_group_batch%')      as cron_jobs_calling_clear,\n (select count(*) from cron.job)                                                      as control_total_cron_jobs,\n (select count(*) from cron.job where command ilike '%rebuild_style_groups%')         as control_cron_jobs_calling_rebuild;\n-- cron_jobs_calling_reconciler: 0\n-- cron_jobs_calling_clear:      0\n-- control_total_cron_jobs:      8    <- positive control, the query can see jobs\n-- control_cron_jobs_calling_rebuild: 1  <- positive control, ilike matching works\n```\n\nA repo-wide search for a scheduled caller outside the database (`*.yml`, `*.ts`, `*.mjs`, `*.js`) returns **no hits** for `reconcile_style_group_drift`. So every reading ever taken of this detector — including mine — is an ad-hoc one-off. A gate phrased as *\"live and reading clean\"* over *\"at least one full cycle\"* cannot be satisfied by a detector nothing runs on a cycle.\n\n**2. A non-zero reading was recorded today.** The comment above at `2026-09-11T06:37:32Z` records **6,392 of 135,278** live assets with a missing/wrong group. Per this issue's own terms that is *a regression in change detection, not noise*. Whatever window the gate requires, its clock starts no earlier than that reading — roughly thirteen hours ago, against a requirement of at least one full weekly cycle.\n\n**3. My own readings are clean, and they do not help.** Two spaced readings, re-deriving the shipped function's body verbatim:\n\n```sql\nwith live as (\n  select a.id, a.style_group_id,\n    (select seg from unnest(string_to_array(a.relative_path,'/')) with ordinality as t(seg,ord)\n      where seg ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9]+$' and seg ~ '[A-Za-z]' and seg ~ '[0-9]' and length(seg) >= 7\n        and ord < array_length(string_to_array(a.relative_path,'/'),1)\n      order by ord limit 1) as sku\n  from public.assets a where a.is_deleted = false\n), resolved as (\n  select l.*, expected.id as expected_group_id, (held.id is not null) as held_group_exists\n  from live l\n  left join public.style_groups expected on expected.sku = l.sku\n  left join public.style_groups held     on held.id     = l.style_group_id\n)\nselect now(), count(*) as live_assets,\n  count(*) filter (where sku is not null and (expected_group_id is null or style_group_id is distinct from expected_group_id)) as check_1a,\n  count(*) filter (where sku is null and style_group_id is not null)                                                            as check_1b,\n  count(*) filter (where style_group_id is not null and not held_group_exists)                                                  as check_2\nfrom resolved;\n```\n\n| observed_at | live_assets | grouped | 1a missing/wrong | 1b unexpected | 2 orphan refs |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 2026-09-11 19:08:51-04 | 135,278 | 98,035 | **0** | **0** | **0** |\n| 2026-09-11 19:10:14-04 | 135,278 | — | **0** | **0** | **0** |\n\nCheck 3, sampled effective-tag projection drift (verbatim re-derivation, sample 5,000): `missing_rows 0`, `extra_rows 0`, `drifted_assets 0`, controls `desired_rows 76,023` / `actual_rows 76,023`.\n\nTwo readings **83 seconds apart are not an observation window**, and both were taken minutes after a `nightly-rebuild-style-groups` pass — jobid 11, `*/10 * * * *`, twelve consecutive `succeeded` runs in the last two hours (19:00, 18:50, 18:40 … 17:10). That job is the brute-force self-healing pass these two issues propose to remove. Reading zero drift while it is running every ten minutes measures the net, not the absence of drift. The 6,392 at 06:37 collapsing to 0 by 19:08 is consistent with exactly that: the net caught it.\n\n**4. Positive controls — the zeros are real zeros, not a malformed query.** Same predicate shapes with a deliberately perturbed join key (`expected.sku = l.sku || 'ZZZ'`):\n\n```\ncontrol_1a_shape_must_be_nonzero: 98,035\ncontrol_1b_shape_must_be_nonzero: 98,035\ncontrol_2_shape_must_be_nonzero:  98,035\n```\n\nPlus derivation controls on the real query: `assets_without_sku 37,243`, `assets_with_sku 98,035`. The counters fire when there is something to count.\n\n### Two caveats recorded rather than smoothed over\n\n- **I could not execute the shipped function.** `has_function_privilege(current_user,'public.reconcile_style_group_drift(integer)','execute')` = **false**; `current_user` = `supabase_read_only_user`; a direct call returns `42501: permission denied`. EXECUTE is granted to `postgres` and `service_role` only. Every figure above is a verbatim re-derivation of the function body, **not** the function's own output. A defensible clean reading needs the function itself, run as `service_role`.\n- **Production is running the `20260907031246` body, not the newest one.** `20260911212849_shared_style_group_sku_key` (the shared `style_group_key_for_sku` helper) is merged but **not applied** — latest applied version is `20260911210709`, and `public.style_group_key_for_sku` does not exist in production. That is why the re-derivation above inlines the expression.\n\n### Consequence for #2420 specifically\n\n#2420's stated verification is *\"run the reconciler across at least one full weekly cycle with the ungroup arm live and `clear_style_group_batch` still scheduled.\"* **`clear_style_group_batch` is scheduled nowhere in production** — zero cron jobs reference it (probe above; positive controls fire). That verification scenario is not reproducible as written and needs re-specifying before #2420 can be dispatched at all.\n\n### What would actually close this gate\n\n1. Schedule `reconcile_style_group_drift` in production as `service_role`, persisting each row (it returns `observed_at` and the population figures precisely so a series can be recorded rather than pasted into a document).\n2. A reading taken by hand minutes after a self-healing pass cannot distinguish \"no drift\" from \"drift was just repaired\".\n\nUntil then this issue stays `status: blocked`.
