{"assignees":[],"body":"**Blocked by #2419 (reconciler). Do not merge before that is live and reading clean.**\n\n## What\n\n`clear_style_group_batch` blanks `assets.style_group_id` in keyset batches, and the nightly cycle runs it before `rebuild_style_groups_batch`. It costs ~34,617 ms per call × 287 calls = **~9,935 s lifetime** — the single most expensive routine in the measured set, and it exists only to give the rebuild a blank slate.\n\nThis issue removes it from all scheduled paths, keeping the function itself for explicit operator recovery.\n\n## Why it cannot ship on its own\n\nThe clear-then-rebuild cycle is doing two jobs at once, and only one of them is waste.\n\nGLM 5.3 disproved the \"just retire it\" premise from the function body: `rebuild_style_groups_batch` **only ever SETs** `style_group_id`. Its `assets_ungrouped` return value is a count of `asset_skus WHERE sku IS NULL` — a counter, not an action. The function has no path that unsets. So the rebuild is idempotent but **not convergent**: it converges monotonically toward \"assigned\", and a stale assignment is never cleared by it. The only unsetting paths in the whole system are `clear_style_group_batch`, the FK's `ON DELETE SET NULL`, and manual SQL.\n\nConcrete failure if this ships alone: a folder is renamed so no path segment matches the SKU rule. Today, clear + rebuild leaves the asset ungrouped and the trigger strips its group-scoped tags. After retirement, the asset keeps its stale group **permanently** — and because `filter_effective_assets` resolves licensor, property and customer facets through `style_groups` for grouped assets, that asset keeps appearing under the **wrong licensor** in the DAM libraries, indefinitely, with no error anywhere. That is an attribution fault, not a performance one.\n\n## Prerequisites, both required\n\n1. **#2419's reconciler live and reading clean**, so drift becomes visible rather than silent. Its check 1(b) — assets carrying a `style_group_id` that should not — is exactly the class the rebuild cannot detect.\n2. **An ungroup arm in the rebuild**, so it becomes genuinely convergent. In the same batch, alongside the existing assignment: unset `style_group_id` for batch rows whose SKU did not derive and which currently carry a group. The existing `assets` trigger then removes the group-scope projection rows. Note this arm must carry the same `IS DISTINCT FROM`-style guard as the assignment (here, `AND style_group_id IS NOT NULL`), or it reintroduces the no-op rewrite that #2408 removes.\n\nWhether the ungroup arm belongs here or in #2408 is a scoping call for the orchestrator; it is listed here because retirement is what makes it load-bearing.\n\n## Verification before removing from schedule\n\nRun the reconciler across at least one full weekly cycle with the ungroup arm live and `clear_style_group_batch` still scheduled. Zero drift on checks 1 and 2 across that window is the evidence. Then remove it from the schedule and keep the reconciler running.\n\nRelated: #2408, #2419, #2417, #2209.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 70\ndepends_on: 2419, 2408\nwrites:\n  - function public.clear_style_group_batch\nreads:\n  - table public.assets\n  - table public.style_groups\n```\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABSzXg5g","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Classified by the shared-db orchestrator (marker #2404).\n\n**Admission test: ACCEPT** (the retirement lands as a change to scheduled database objects). **Blocked on #2419**, which is itself blocked on #2408 — so this is two deep, not one.\n\n**Scoping call, decided:** the ungroup arm stays in **#2408**, where it is already dispatched and where the author brief already carries it along with the GLM `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... WHERE` / `RETURNING` suppression trap. It does not move here. Rationale: the missing ungroup arm is a correctness defect in the rebuild function today — a renamed folder leaves an asset attributed to the wrong licensor indefinitely — and it must not wait behind a performance retirement that is two dependencies deep. Splitting it here would also put a second author in a function body another lane already claims.\n\nThis issue is therefore purely the retirement, and it inherits a precondition: it must not merge until #2408's ungroup arm is live, or retiring the clear pass makes stale group assignments permanent.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 70\ndepends_on: 2419, 2408\nwrites:\n  - function public.clear_style_group_batch\nreads:\n  - table public.assets\n  - table public.style_groups\n```\n","createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:05:26Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2420#issuecomment-5556789478","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABT5qpuw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Fresh production detector result after2548promotion: reconcile_style_group_drift(5000) returned200 in49.2s at2026-09-11T06:35Z,135278 liveassets with6392missing/wronggroup,0unexpectedgroup/0orphans; sampledtagdrift0of5000. Read live today on the current pair:\n\n| | preview `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs` | production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` |\n|---|---|---|\n| breaker `coldlion_licensor_property` | closed | closed |\n| unacknowledged alerts | 0 | 0 |\n| `taxonomy_parallel_observation` rows | 0 | 0 |\n| `taxonomy_baseline_activation` rows | 0 | 0 |\n\nThere is nothing to reset and nothing in scope to acknowledge. #552 (the structural half) closed 2026-09-05, so the dependency is clear.\n\n**What was actually blocking the lane.** `plm.check_taxonomy_sync_health()` refused on BOTH databases with `environment: \"unconfigured (db=postgres)\"`. Neither database had ever been named — `plm.deployment_environment` still held the loud placeholder seeded by `20260804120100`, whose header prescribes the exact one-time `UPDATE` and deliberately refuses to guess. `plm.activate_taxonomy_baseline()` refuses outright while a database is unnamed, so no baseline could have been activated in this state.\n\n**Step 1 executed** — Albert instructed \"name them\" in chat on 2026-09-06. One `UPDATE` per database, using the statement prescribed in the migration header, each inside a transaction guarded by a migration fingerprint so it could not fire against the wrong target:\n\n- preview guard: `20260906035323` present AND `20260828052706` absent\n- production guard: `20260828052706` present AND `20260906035323` absent\n\nThe first attempt REFUSED and was correct to: it asserted `20260802171000` (the FR owner ruling) was applied on preview, and it is not — that migration is held off both databases (#1848). The guard was rebuilt on a fingerprint derived from the live diff of both migration ledgers rather than an assumption.\n\nResult — `plm.check_taxonomy_sync_health()` now identifies each database correctly:\n\n```\npreview    -> {\"ok\": false, \"reason\": \"no_active_baseline\", \"environment\": \"preview mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs\"}\nproduction -> {\"ok\": false, \"reason\": \"no_active_baseline\", \"environment\": \"production qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai\"}\n```\n\n**Still open — step 5, the production baseline.** Production holds only `phase4_preview` pins (12 current). Those must NOT be activated on production: pin `1476fc37-1518-4a6a-a7e2-015050a7c14e` says so explicitly, because `20260802171000` is held off production, so production still has FR active and its `licensor_status_hash` legitimately differs. Production needs its own `baseline_key` derived from production, authored as a governed migration. That is the remaining work on this issue and it returns to Albert for authorization before activation.\n\n**Housekeeping.** Production alert `e9c6bc32-555f-4b90-87b7-3152f9a11a58` (severity `warning`, \"refused: no active taxonomy baseline\") was raised by the first health check I ran while the database was still unnamed. {"assignees":[],"body":"## Goal  Finish the canonical notification storage contract needed for accurate ordering, bounded unread reads, action traceability, and exact RFQ deep links.  ## Confirmed gaps  Read-only production catalog inspection on 2026-09-03 shows `app.user_notification.created_date` is `date`, not `timestamptz`, and the canonical app table lacks #1987's workflow-action/idempotency columns. Repository migration `20260827132637` adds the unread `(user_id_fk, created_date desc)` partial index only to `dflow.user_notification`, while the current backend maps notification reads to `app.user_notification`.  Date-only values cannot reliably order two notifications created on the same day, and the legacy-schema index does not accelerate the application's canonical unread list/count path.  ## Required contract  - Give new canonical notifications true timestamp precision with a safe default. Preserve legacy dates without inventing within-day order. - Provide workflow-action linkage and per-recipient idempotency on `app.user_notification` if #2202 has not already supplied them. - Add the partial unread index on the actual application table for bounded newest-first per-user reads/counts, with a deterministic ID tie-breaker where useful. - Ensure the action link is sufficient to resolve the immutable RFQ item identity used by the frontend deep link; do not duplicate prices, customer-private text, or notes into notification rows. - Preserve all existing task/mention/legacy notification rows and read-state behavior. - Add migration tests for mixed legacy/workflow rows, timestamp precision, same-time deterministic order support, uniqueness, FK integrity, and the canonical unread index definition. - Rehearse on preview and provide exact catalog/readback evidence.  Do not edit applied migrations. {"assignees":[],"body":"Unit 5b of the ColdLion landing split, from §9 Step 6 of `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md`. Split out of #2175 on 2026-09-02 after the live field census on #2081 (comment 5519573718). Structure only; no row loads.\r\n\r\n## What this unit will build\r\n\r\nLanding tables for the five remainder endpoints whose grain **cannot be proven from sampling today**: `/pickticket`, `/receiving`, `/prepackDetail`, `/proddetails`, and `/itemImages` metadata.\r\n\r\n## Why every one of them is blocked\r\n\r\n**Corrected 2026-09-02** (#2081 comment 5519596972). An earlier reading of the census called four endpoints broken. That was wrong on two counts, and the correction matters because it changes what the blocker actually is.\r\n\r\n| feed | status |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| `/pickticket` | **Conditionally failing, breadth-dependent.** `minTransactionNo=999999` (matches nothing) returns 200; `minTransactionNo=0` or `1` (match everything) return **HTTP 500 with an empty body**; any date narrowing returns 200. This is an unguarded server-side failure on a broad result set, not parameter validation — validation would return the 400-plus-JSON that `/orderHistory` gives for an over-wide date range. Tracked as vendor defect #2178. |\r\n| `/receiving` | **Not broken.** Same parameter signature, and it returns a well-formed empty page for every call including the unfiltered one. Status is \"empty, cause unknown\", not \"broken\". |\r\n| `/prepackDetail` | **Not enumerable.** Requires a `prepackCode`; there is no list endpoint. Probes with codes harvested from `/inventory` returned empty for both candidate company codes. |\r\n| `/proddetails` | **Not enumerable.** Requires a `prodOrderNo`; a probe with a live `prodOrderNo` from `/prodtracking` returned empty. |\r\n| `/itemImages` | Requires an `itemNo`. Typed as `ItemImageDTO` (16 fields) but includes `resourceContent` and `thumbnail128`, which the projection must **explicitly exclude** — metadata only, no bytes, per owner decision. |\r\n\r\n### Do not let \"0 rows\" harden into \"no data\"\r\n\r\nEvery `/pickticket` and `/receiving` call that returned 200 reported `totalElements=0` — unfiltered, June 2025, June 2026, and Aug-Sep 2026. **But the `/pickticket` requests that fail with a 500 are exactly the broad ones that would reveal whether data exists.** The correct statement everywhere in this split is: *the narrow windows we are able to query are empty; the broad query that would settle it fails server-side.* The difference between \"there is nothing to load\" and \"we cannot see what there is to load\" is the entire point, and no downstream document may collapse the two.\r\n\r\n### So the blocker is two things, not four broken feeds\r\n\r\n1. **One vendor defect** — the breadth-dependent `/pickticket` 500, tracked in #2178. (#2178 is a vendor-tracking issue and deliberately **not** structural; it must never take an author lane, which is why it is referenced here in prose rather than as a `depends_on` edge.)\r\n2. **One visibility question** — whether these feeds hold data at all, which cannot be answered until either the vendor fixes the broad query or a window known to contain pick tickets and receipts is identified.\r\n\r\nOn top of that, three of the five are lookup-only endpoints reachable solely through keys harvested from feeds that have not been loaded yet. **This unit therefore belongs after the loaders (plan §9 Step 7), not in front of them** — a real amendment to the plan's ordering, not a scheduling preference.\r\n\r\nThere is also no owner ingest/ignore disposition for any of the five feeds; `docs/coldlion-field-decisions-20260819.csv` has zero rows for all of them, and D5 makes an omission permanent.\r\n\r\nThe table names in the write list below are placeholders derived from the endpoint names, claimed so the unit is dispatchable and collision-checked. If the eventual census proves a different grain or a repeated group needing a child table, **amend this `writes:` list before dispatch** rather than working outside it. Never label a guessed key as natural: use a surrogate row UUID plus a uniqueness contract over the smallest proven source identity and the source hash.\r\n\r\n## Gate (plan §9 Step 6)\r\n\r\nEach endpoint has a documented grain proof, a complete owner field disposition, an idempotent replay test, and no unexplained duplicate collapse. No image-content column.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: blocked\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 5\r\ndepends_on: 2172, 2173, 2174, 2175\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table coldlion.pick_ticket\r\n  - table coldlion.receiving\r\n  - table coldlion.prepack_detail\r\n  - table coldlion.prod_detail\r\n  - table coldlion.item_image_metadata\r\nreads:\r\n```\r\n\r\nblocker: two things, not four broken feeds. (1) Vendor defect #2178 — `/pickticket` returns HTTP 500 with an empty body on broad result sets while narrow queries return 200, so the query that would show whether pick-ticket data exists is the one that fails. (2) A visibility question: every 200 response from `/pickticket` and `/receiving` reported `totalElements=0`, but that means the narrow windows we can query are empty, NOT that there is no data. `/receiving` itself is not broken. `/prepackDetail`, `/proddetails` and `/itemImages` are lookup-only and reachable only via keys harvested from feeds not yet loaded, so this unit sequences after the loaders in plan §9 Step 7. Owner ingest/ignore disposition is also missing for all five.\r\n\r\nTracker: #2081. Its latest evidence says every tested `/pickticket` request terminates before a response, so no row or grain is observable. `/receiving` responds correctly but returns zero rows in tested windows, so it still has no observed field/grain proof; this is not evidence that the feed contains no data.\n\nTherefore the three lookup feeds now have current private field/grain evidence, but #2179 remains blocked on the 53 owner field decisions and the two #2476 visibility/vendor outcomes. No database or schema write occurred.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-08T03:56:55Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2179#issuecomment-5578932850","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABUEVSzw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Gate re-verification, 2026-09-11 — two gates CLEAR, one still CLOSED\n\nLive re-verification of this issue's two stated gates. Read-only throughout: no schema change, no author lane claimed, and `status:` deliberately left at `blocked` (see Gate 3).\n\n### Gate 1 — dependency tables on PRODUCTION: **CLEAR**\n\nA closed issue is not a delivered migration (#2699), so each dependency was confirmed in the **live production catalog**, project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` (proved via `get_project_url` -> `https://qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai.supabase.co`):\n\n| unit | issue | table | live on production |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 2 | #2172 | `coldlion.item_header` | present (18,953 rows) |\n| 2 | #2172 | `coldlion.item_detail` | present (26,156 rows) |\n| 2 | #2172 | `coldlion.item_merch_group` | present (246,448 rows) |\n| 2 | #2172 | `coldlion.merch_group_detail` | present |\n| 3 | #2173 | `coldlion.order_history_line` | present (115,840 rows) |\n| 3 | #2173 | `coldlion.order_history_component` | present (115,960 rows) |\n| 3 | #2173 | `coldlion.order_history_invoice_ref` | present (98,672 rows) |\n| 3 | #2173 | `coldlion.order_history_pick_ticket_ref` | present (98,692 rows) |\n| 3 | #2173 | `coldlion.history_page_ledger` | present (2,203 rows) |\n| 4 | #2174 | `coldlion.prod_history_line` | present (61,785 rows) |\n| 4 | #2174 | `coldlion.prod_history_component` | present (66,258 rows) |\n| 4 | #2174 | `coldlion.prod_history_last_lookup` | present (64,340 rows) |\n| 5a | #2175 | `coldlion.inventory` | present |\n| 5a | #2175 | `coldlion.prod_tracking` | present |\n\nAll four dependencies are genuinely **applied**, not merely merged.\n\n### Gate 2 — vendor defect #2178: **CLEAR, and the feed carries data**\n\n**The ticket chain proves nothing.** #2178 was closed by a RETURN, not a fix: #2178 -> #2476 -> `u2giants/licensor-source-data#67`, which is **still OPEN with no comments**. Closure was routing, not resolution. Verified by live call instead — two runs several minutes apart, identical results, **positive controls first**:\n\n| request | run 1 | run 2 |\n|---|---|---|\n| POSITIVE CONTROL `/divisions?companyCode=EDGEHOME` | 200, totalElements=4 | 200, totalElements=4 |\n| POSITIVE CONTROL `/merchGroupHeaders` | 200, totalElements=57 | 200, totalElements=57 |\n| POSITIVE CONTROL `/prodtracking` | 200, bare array 3,943 rows | 200, bare array 3,943 rows |\n| `/pickticket?size=1` | **200, totalElements=885** | **200, totalElements=885** |\n| `/pickticket?minTransactionNo=0&size=1` | **200, totalElements=885** | **200, totalElements=885** |\n| `/pickticket?minTransactionNo=999999&size=1` | 200, totalElements=0 | 200, totalElements=0 |\n| `/pickticket?createdFrom=2026-01-01&size=1` | 200, totalElements=2 | 200, totalElements=2 |\n| `/pickticket` (unfiltered) | **200, totalElements=885** | **200, totalElements=885** |\n| `/receiving?size=1` | 200, totalElements=0 | 200, totalElements=0 |\n| `/receiving?createdFrom=2026-01-01&size=1` | 200, totalElements=0 | 200, totalElements=0 |\n\n**`/pickticket` is fixed and is populated: 885 pick tickets.** The `minTransactionNo=0` shape that previously returned HTTP 500, and the unfiltered call that had degraded to dropping the connection (#2476), both now return a clean 200. `minTransactionNo=999999` still returns 0, so the endpoint is discriminating rather than blanket-answering — the bisection boundary previously recorded at 892/893 is consistent with 885 live records.\n\n**This retires the standing caution in this issue's body.** The broad query that would reveal whether pick-ticket data exists now answers, and the answer is 885 records. The earlier \"0 rows\" readings were the defect itself, exactly as #2081 warned they might be.\n\n`/receiving` is unchanged: a well-formed 200 with 0 rows, on the same key in the same minute. Consistent with the owner's business context (pick tickets and receipts cover USA-warehouse stock orders only), and per #2081 it is **not** a defect.\n\n### This issue's body is now WRONG about enumerability on three of five feeds\n\n| feed | body says | live 2026-09-11 |\n|---|---|---|\n| `/pickticket` | breadth-dependent HTTP 500 | **fixed**, 200, 885 records, 39 fields |\n| `/receiving` | empty, cause unknown | unchanged: 200, 0 rows |\n| `/prepackDetail` | \"not enumerable\" | **enumerable**: 200, bare array, 2-4 rows per code, 18 fields |\n| `/proddetails` | \"not enumerable\" | **enumerable**: 200, 1 row, 21 fields |\n| `/itemImages` | requires an itemNo | **works**: 41 of 200 items returned metadata, 16 fields |\n\n**How the `/proddetails` probe nearly went wrong, recorded deliberately.** Calling `/proddetails?prodOrderNo=<live>` returns `HTTP 400 \"Required String parameter 'companyCode' is not present\"`. Supplying **both** returns 200 with a real row. Reading a failed call as \"not enumerable\" is the documented wrong-parameter trap. Same for `/prepackDetail`, which answers on a harvested `prePackCode` and returns a clean 0 rows for `ZZZNOSUCH` — a working negative control.\n\n**`/itemImages` was NOT recorded as empty on a 0-row answer.** A 0-row answer is indistinguishable from a malformed query, so a positive-control sweep of 200 distinct `itemNo` values from `/items` was run: **41 returned rows, 159 returned 0, 0 errors.** The endpoint works, so a 0-row answer for a given item is genuine absence. Live field list (16): `colorCode, companyCode, createdTime, createdUser, divisionCode, fileName, fileType, itemImageDesc, itemNo, labelCode, modTime, modUser, pkey, resourceContent, resourceId, thumbnail128`. Note `/items` itself carries a `hasImage` flag, which is the cheap way to avoid sweeping blind. **`resourceContent` and `thumbnail128` must be excluded from any projection** per the standing owner decision — metadata only, no bytes.\n\n### Gate 3 — owner ingest/ignore disposition: **STILL CLOSED. This one needs Albert.**\n\nPlan `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md` §9 Step 6 is explicit: *\"Obtain the owner ingest/ignore disposition before creating columns.\"* Verified against `origin/main` (not a stale worktree): `docs/coldlion-field-decisions-20260819.csv` covers nine feeds — `customers, itemDetails, items, merchGroupDetails, merchGroupHeaders, orderHistory, prodHistory, vendors` — and carries **zero rows for all five feeds in this unit**. The 14 apparent matches are `prePackCode`/`itemImage` fields belonging to *other* feeds, not dispositions for these.\n\nUnder owner decision **D5 an omission is permanent**, so this cannot be inferred, defaulted, or decided by a reviewer — it is owner authority. It is the one thing standing between this unit and `ready`.\n\nThe ask is now much smaller than when this issue was written, because the field lists are live and measured: 39 fields on `/pickticket`, 21 on `/proddetails`, 18 on `/prepackDetail`, 16 on `/itemImages`. `/receiving`'s field list remains unobservable while it is genuinely empty, and privacy review matters on `/pickticket`, which carries bill-to and ship-to address fields.\n\n### Load order\n\nThe body sequences this unit after the Step 7 loaders. Partly overtaken: `coldlion.item_header` already holds 18,953 rows on production, so lookup keys **are** harvestable today, and both lookup endpoints answer. But `tools/coldlion-landing/` still ships only `backfill-history.mjs` and `sync-history.mjs` — there is **no `sync-masters.mjs`** — and `coldlion.inventory`, `prod_tracking`, `customer`, `vendor`, `season` and `division` are all still 0 rows on production. {"assignees":[],"body":"Unit 6 of six, and last, split out of tracker #2081 by §9 Step 1 of `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md`. Structure only; no row loads under this issue.\n\n## What this unit builds\n\nStep 8 of the plan — publish safe consumer contracts over the ColdLion landing layer.\n\n- For each feed, decide **separately** whether promotion belongs in `plm.*`, `core.*`, or an application-owned schema. Licensor/property authority rules stay intact.\n- Expose **views or functions**, never grants on landing tables. Application roles must remain unable to query `coldlion.*` — that closed posture on `schema coldlion` is this unit's structural write.\n- Sales-history reporting may aggregate the approved per-design quantities, but must **not** infer fulfilment from document-number presence and must not claim a source-document type: ColdLion exposes no source-document marker (plan §6.6, §13 open question 1 — do not re-ask the vendor).\n- No automatic promotion into `core.*` without a separately reviewed authority rule.\n\n## Why this is blocked\n\n1. **It depends on the other five units.** There is nothing to expose until the landing tables are correct and populated; a contract written over a superseded grain would have to be rewritten.\n2. **The promotion target is an open decision.** Plan §9 Step 8 requires a per-feed decision between `plm.*`, `core.*` and an application-owned schema. Until that ruling, the exact view and function names cannot be written, and this issue deliberately does **not** invent them.\n\nThe `writes:` list therefore claims only what is certain today: the grant/RLS posture on `schema coldlion`. **Every promotion view or function must be added to this `writes:` list before dispatch**, once the per-feed target schema is decided.\n\n## Gate (plan §9 Step 8)\n\nApplication roles cannot query `coldlion.*`; authorized consumers can read only reviewed fields through stable contracts; authority and duplicate-abstention tests pass.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 5\ndepends_on: 2171, 2172, 2173, 2174, 2175, 2177, 2179, 2180\nwrites:\n  - schema coldlion\nreads:\n```\n\nRevised 2026-09-02 after the live field census on #2081: the upstream split grew from five units to eight (#2171, #2172, #2173, #2174, #2175, #2177, #2179, #2180), and all eight are dependencies.\n\nblocker: the per-feed promotion target (`plm.*` vs `core.*` vs an application-owned schema) is undecided, so no exact view or function object can be named yet; and all five upstream landing units must land first.\n\nTracker: #2081 (holds the U1-U20 reviewer objection ledger). {"assignees":[],"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nchange_type: migration\napplication_return_to: popcre/shared-db\nlive_assertion: designflow_frozen_20260710 is absent and the validated art_piece_attachment and RolePermissions foreign keys resolve to dflow parents with unchanged child counts and identity matches\ngenerated_types: required\npriority: 3\ndepends_on:\nowner_repo: popcre/shared-db\nwrites:\n  - schema designflow_frozen_20260710\n  - sequence designflow_frozen_20260710.\"Factory_id_seq\"\n  - sequence designflow_frozen_20260710.\"Roles_Id_seq\"\n  - sequence designflow_frozen_20260710.\"StandardizedVersionDetail_id_seq\"\n  - sequence designflow_frozen_20260710.\"StandardizedVersion_id_seq\"\n  - sequence designflow_frozen_20260710.art_piece_id_seq\n  - sequence designflow_frozen_20260710.artists_id_seq\n  - sequence designflow_frozen_20260710.comments_id_seq\n  - sequence designflow_frozen_20260710.customers_customers_id_seq\n  - sequence designflow_frozen_20260710.product_category_id_seq\n  - table app.\"RolePermissions\"\n  - table designflow_frozen_20260710.\"Factory\"\n  - table designflow_frozen_20260710.\"Roles\"\n  - table designflow_frozen_20260710.art_piece\n  - table designflow_frozen_20260710.artists\n  - table designflow_frozen_20260710.comments\n  - table designflow_frozen_20260710.customers\n  - table designflow_frozen_20260710.product_category\n  - table plm.art_piece_attachment\nreads:\n  - table dflow.art_piece\n  - table dflow.Roles\n```\n\nCarried forward from `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-27T1730Z-edge-dev-claude-needs-albert-sweep.md` (contract issue #778) so the obligation is not lost when that file is retired under #2105.\n\n## What happened\n\n#778 froze the orphan `designflow` schema by renaming it to `designflow_frozen_20260710` (migration `20260827160000`, PR #1670, production-applied and verified). The rename was chosen deliberately over a DROP.\n\n## What is still owed\n\nThe schema is **not empty** and the DROP was explicitly deferred, not cancelled:\n\n- 1,385 rows across 7 tables.\n- Two inbound foreign keys that still resolve: `app.RolePermissions` -> `designflow_frozen_20260710.\"Roles\"` (4 rows), and `plm.art_piece_attachment` -> `designflow_frozen_20260710.art_piece` (2,276 rows).\n\nThe DROP stays deferred until those children are disposed of. An earlier plan to re-point the 2,276 attachment rows onto `dflow.art_piece` and then drop was **reviewed and rejected** by Grok 4.6; the report is at `.ai/reviews/grok-orphan-designflow-repoint-20260827T152007Z-1390799.md` on the machine that ran it.\n\n## Owner decision required\n\nWhether to dispose of the two dependent sets and drop the frozen schema, or to leave it frozen indefinitely. #778 retained `needs-albert` for exactly this and is now closed, so nothing else tracks it.\n\n## Backup\n\nA full pre-rename capture of all 1,385 rows exists only as a machine-local file on EDGE-DEV (`backups/designflow-orphan-schema-backup-2026-08-27.json`). It is gitignored on purpose â€” it contains real email addresses and this repository is public. **Never commit it.** If that machine is lost the backup is lost; #778 recorded that as an accepted trade.\n\nRelated: #2105.\n\n\n\n\n## Current retirement admission — 2026-09-20\n\nThis scope replaces the stale `owner-decision` classification. Albert's explicit September 6 ruling, recorded in the September 7 comment, authorizes retiring this schema and repointing its two inbound foreign keys to `dflow`. No new owner decision is being requested. The historic issue text and rejected-review pointer above remain preserved as history.\n\nFresh read-only production verification confirmed the target project and `supabase_read_only_user`, with transaction read-only enabled. The schema contains seven tables / 1,385 rows and nine sequences. The applied freeze version is `20260831041658`; the older timestamp in the historical body is not the current ledger version.\n\nExactly two external catalog dependencies remain: `plm.art_piece_attachment.art_piece_attachment_art_piece_id_fkey` and `app.RolePermissions.RolePermissions_RoleId_fkey`. All 2,276 attachment rows and four permission rows resolve to their proposed `dflow` parents. The 1,114 distinct art parents match on key, description, art number, creation time and other common columns except historical art-source/update metadata; both referenced roles match on all common columns. Specifically, 532 art parents have different art-source values and corresponding dictionary codes/descriptions; 532 update timestamps and 497 update-user values also differ. These differences are disclosed for independent review. This retirement does not authorize overwriting live parent values with historical ones.\n\nThe protected vault backup remains available: seven tables / 1,385 rows, 260,392 bytes, original-byte SHA-256 `916be84f738eee32ec2d70020c80dbe1f75fa788fc3f96007410b9d81f50eb72`. A local protected restore succeeded after redacting 11 contact values before insertion and isolating 18 external foreign-key dependencies. It verified data and internal constraints, not a full-system restore; recovery must supply external dependencies and must never restore contact values. The disposable local database is stopped. Automatic cleanup was refused by machine policy; its protected files remain outside the repository pending permitted cleanup.\n\nNo database function/view text references the frozen schema. Bounded source searches in named consumers found no direct frozen-schema references. The current production Item Master deployment was checked at its actual deployed revision: it uses Cloud SQL's `designflow`, not this Supabase frozen schema. This is not an exhaustive claim about every dynamic or external consumer.\n\nThe prior rejected review has not been recovered locally. Its exact historical pointer remains above, and its absence must be stated in the eventual PR; fresh independent review is required. The author must use a single transaction, exact inventory/dependency and identity preconditions, validate the two replacement foreign keys without child loss, then explicitly remove the allowlisted tables/sequences and finally the schema using `RESTRICT`. No `CASCADE`. Unknown objects/dependencies abort. A committed read-only production proof and generated-types evidence are required.\n\nThis update is admission preparation only: no author claim, reserved migration, SQL implementation, preview or production write has occurred. Authoring awaits the orchestrator's queue-repair clearance and reserved version.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf3f-3ac6-7280-ace5-cbc1a0f187cf on 916-ALIEN\n\r\n\n\n### Exact retirement object expansion — 2026-09-20\n\nThe root approved naming all seven retiring tables and nine sequences explicitly, in addition to the schema and two child tables. This preserves the already authorized inventory and RESTRICT-only behavior; it adds no data overwrite, CASCADE, or production-write permission. The protected claim must expand atomically before the revised authoring contract is published. Read-only; nothing was changed.\n\nThe `designflow_frozen_20260710` schema holds 1,385 rows in 7 tables, all last written 2026-07-10: 1,114 `art_piece`, 175 `Factory`, 57 `customers`, 14 `artists`, 13 `comments`, 7 `product_category`, 5 `Roles`.\n\nContact data in it is far smaller than this issue implies. That materially changes the cost of this issue against what is written above.\n\nThe Grok 4.6 review that rejected an earlier re-point plan could not be read — `.ai/reviews/grok-orphan-designflow-repoint-20260827T152007Z-1390799.md` exists only on EDGE-DEV and is not in the repository. {"assignees":[],"body":"Split out of #1722 at the owner's request. **Read the correction in the first section before planning any work** — the one-line ask I made at the end of #1722 (\"repack the bridge, ~108 MB of unreclaimable empty space\") is stale, and the real finding is different and bigger.\r\n\r\n## Correction to what I said in #1722\r\n\r\nWhen I measured `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` on 2026-08-27 it was **132 MB of heap for ~24 MB of live data** with `n_dead_tup = 0`, and I concluded it needed a manual repack because autovacuum could not reclaim it. **That was wrong.** Autovacuum ran on 2026-08-29 and reclaimed most of it:\r\n\r\n| | 2026-08-27 | 2026-08-30 |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| heap | 132 MB (16,943 pages) | **53 MB (6,804 pages)** |\r\n| live data | ~24 MB | ~25 MB (15,734 rows x 1,574 B) |\r\n| ratio | ~5.5x | **~2.1x** |\r\n\r\n~2.1x is unremarkable for a table under update churn. **A repack of that table is no longer worth requesting, and I withdraw the ask.** My error was treating one `n_dead_tup = 0` reading as proof autovacuum was helpless, when it just had not run yet.\r\n\r\nWhat is left is the *mechanism* that inflated it in the first place, and that mechanism is not confined to one table.\r\n\r\n## The actual finding: high-churn tables cannot do HOT updates\r\n\r\n`n_tup_hot_upd / n_tup_upd`, production, 2026-08-30:\r\n\r\n| table | rows | heap | indexes | index size | updates | HOT % |\r\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\r\n| `public.style_guide_files` | 294,896 | 263 MB | **17** | 559 MB | 444,631 | **0.0%** |\r\n| `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` | 15,734 | 53 MB | 10 | 11 MB | 10,742 | **0.0%** |\r\n| `public.dam_search_documents` | 145,108 | 262 MB | 10 | 257 MB | 1,053,024 | **6.5%** |\r\n| `public.assets` | 171,955 | 2,024 MB | **35** | 1,082 MB | 429,322 | 43.5% |\r\n\r\nA non-HOT update writes a new heap tuple **and** a new entry in *every* index on the table, then leaves both to be vacuumed. At 0% HOT with 17 indexes, one logical update to `style_guide_files` is 18 physical writes. That is why these tables bloat, why their index sets are larger than the tables themselves, and why vacuum has so much to do.\r\n\r\nNone of these tables sets `fillfactor`, so they all use the default 100 — no free space is reserved on a page for an updated row to stay put, which is a precondition for HOT.\r\n\r\nTwo candidate causes, and they need separating before anything is changed:\r\n\r\n1. **`fillfactor = 100`** leaves no room on the page. Lowering it (typically 85-90) on the high-churn tables is the standard, reversible remedy.\r\n2. **The updates touch indexed columns.** HOT is impossible in that case regardless of fillfactor. This has to be checked per table against the actual update statements in the app and worker code — I have not done that, and it is the part most likely to change the recommendation.\r\n\r\n## Second finding, and it needs a measurement window, NOT a drop list\r\n\r\nAcross those four tables, **1,411 MB of indexes report `idx_scan = 0`**, including `idx_assets_relative_path_trgm` (278 MB), `idx_sgf_relative_path_trgm` (125 MB), `idx_assets_ai_tag_all_candidates` (106 MB) and `idx_dam_search_documents_tsv` (66 MB).\r\n\r\n⚠️ **Do not treat that as a drop list.** The statistics collector on this database has demonstrably lost data: eleven large tables report `n_live_tup = 0` and `autoanalyze_count = 0` while genuinely holding 100k-2.3M rows (`public.asset_tags` reports 0 live tuples against 2,173,392 real rows). `pg_stat_database.stats_reset` is null, so I cannot date the loss. `idx_scan = 0` under those conditions may mean \"never used\" or may mean \"counter lost\". `idx_dam_search_documents_tsv` showing zero scans is itself a red flag — that is the full-text index behind DAM search, which is certainly in use.\r\n\r\nWhat is safe to conclude: **planner statistics are intact** (`reltuples` is accurate and every column has entries in `pg_statistic`), so query plans are not affected. This is a monitoring-visibility problem, not a planning one.\r\n\r\nThe right first step is to **reset index statistics and observe for a defined window** (a fortnight covering a full crawl/import cycle), then revisit with counters that can be trusted. Dropping a 278 MB index on a lost counter risks a production search outage to save disk.\r\n\r\n## What I am asking for\r\n\r\n1. A decision on lowering `fillfactor` on the high-churn tables above — preceded by the check in cause (2), since it may make fillfactor pointless for some of them.\r\n2. A statistics-reset-and-observe window so the unused-index question can be answered on evidence rather than on counters of unknown age.\r\n3. Nothing urgent. No application is currently harmed by this; PopDAM's `/orders` was the original symptom and it is fixed (#1657, #1722, `popdam3#100` closed — cold exact count 3,365 ms to 107 ms).\r\n\r\n## Scope and risk\r\n\r\n- Everything here is **structural** and belongs to shared-db.\r\n- `alter table … set (fillfactor = N)` is metadata-only and affects only pages written afterwards; it is reversible and needs no rewrite. It does **not** shrink an already-bloated table.\r\n- Any index drop is destructive and outside this request until the observation window closes.\r\n- Four schemas' worth of applications write these tables (DAM assets, style-guide crawl, search, PLM bridge), so cause (2) needs each owning app's input, not a database-only decision.\r\n\r\n## Evidence\r\n\r\nAll figures read-only from production (`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`) on 2026-08-30 via `pg_class`, `pg_stat_all_tables`, `pg_stat_all_indexes`, `pg_statistic`, and direct `count(*)`. No writes of any kind. `pgstattuple` and `pg_repack` are **not** installed on this instance; `hypopg` 1.4.1 and `index_advisor` 0.2.0 are.\r\n\r\nRequester: PopDAM session, worktree `issue-100-4a0376`. Split from #1722.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: blocked\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 100\r\ndepends_on:\r\nblocker: index-usage observation window open 2026-09-03, closes 2026-09-17; no index drop before that date, and the drop decision returns through the shared-db orchestrator (see comment 5519526901)\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table public.style_guide_files\r\n  - table plm.style_tracker_item_bridge\r\n  - table public.dam_search_documents\r\n  - table public.assets\r\nreads:\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABRi0HAw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Routing note: current orchestrator marker is #1869 (route_id `01a052f3-c9a9-7bf1-a5b0-ea5cd663b6c0`). As with #1657 and #1722, a Claude session cannot dispatch to it — the orchestrator is a Codex CLI process and `codex-reply` from here answers `Session not found`. Queued on `db-work`; Albert is notifying it directly. Explicitly **not urgent** — no application is currently harmed.","createdAt":"2026-08-31T00:43:24Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1966#issuecomment-5472323331","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABSOB7YQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Answer to the gating question: yes — the updates touch indexed columns. `fillfactor` cannot buy HOT on three of the four tables.\n\nChecked each table's real update paths in application and shared-db code against its actual index set (including **partial-index predicate columns and expression-index inputs**, which block HOT exactly as indexed columns do).\n\n### `public.style_guide_files` — 0.0% HOT, and correctly so\n\nAll three real update paths write indexed columns:\n\n| path | sets | indexed? |\n|---|---|---|\n| `refresh_style_guide_file_tag_cache()` (`20260723170000_popsg_file_tags.sql:171`) | `tag_names`, `tag_search_text` | **both** — `idx_style_guide_files_tag_names`, `idx_style_guide_files_tag_search_trgm` |\n| crawl staleness cleanup (`20260507191146_…:15`) | `is_active` | **yes** — predicate of `idx_style_guide_files_active_modified` |\n| render completion (`agent-api/index.ts:3046,3051`) | `thumbnail_url`, `thumbnail_error` | **yes** — both in the predicate of `idx_sgf_render_errored` |\n\n0.0% is not a tuning failure, it is arithmetic. **`fillfactor` would buy nothing here.**\n\n### `public.dam_search_documents` — 6.5% HOT, and the 6.5% is the tell\n\nThe dominant path is the embedding pipeline (`20260825010603_…:375-421` and its successors): claim sets `embedding_lease_token`, complete sets `embedding`, `embedding_model`, `embedding_updated_at`.\n\n`embedding` carries **two** indexes, and one of them — `dam_search_embedding_claim_idx`, partial on `embedding IS NULL` — is a work-queue index **whose whole design is that every completed embedding moves a row out of it**. Every successful write is therefore necessarily non-HOT. The 6.5% that does go HOT is the error/retry updates that happen to touch no indexed column. **`fillfactor` cannot help the main path.**\n\n### `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` — 0.0% HOT\n\nIts updates are the Master Data merge and reconcile functions, which set `company_id`, `factory_id`, `style_group_id`, `creative_designer_id`, `erp_item_id`, `plm_item_id` — **every one of them indexed**. **`fillfactor` cannot help.**\n\n### `public.assets` — 43.5% HOT, the only one where the question stays open\n\nUpdates set `is_deleted`, `thumbnail_url`, `style_group_id`, `ai_tagged_at`, `status` — all indexed or in partial predicates — but it already achieves 43.5%, so a meaningful share of its write traffic evidently touches non-indexed columns. This is the one table where a `fillfactor` change might return something, and also the one where it matters least per row (2 GB heap, 35 indexes).\n\n## What this means for #1966\n\n**Item 1 is effectively closed as a shared-db tuning change.** I withdraw the fillfactor request for `style_guide_files`, `dam_search_documents` and `style_tracker_item_bridge`; it would be a migration with a false premise. Only `assets` remains arguable, and weakly.\n\n**The live question is the index set, not the storage parameter.** These tables are not badly tuned — they are heavily indexed relative to how often they are written. `style_guide_files` carries **17 indexes and 559 MB of index against a 263 MB table**; `dam_search_documents` carries 257 MB of index against 262 MB of table. The productive conversation is which of those indexes earn their write cost, and that is blocked behind the statistics-reset-and-observe window in item 3 — which is now the **only** unblocked next step in this issue.\n\nOne specific candidate for that conversation, flagged rather than requested: `dam_search_embedding_claim_idx` is a queue index over a column written once per row for 145,108 rows. Whether a partial index is the right shape for that claim pattern is an application design question for the search owner, not a database tuning question.\n\nItem 2 is answered; item 1 is withdrawn except for `assets`; item 3 stands and should be dated.\n\nEvidence: index sets from `pg_index` / `pg_attribute` including `indexprs` and `indpred` on production (`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`), read-only, 2026-09-02, cross-referenced against update sites in `u2giants/popdam3` and `u2giants/shared-db`. No writes.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-02T23:04:17Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1966#issuecomment-5517638497","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABSOCRbQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Orchestrator re-scope — the fillfactor ask is withdrawn for three of the four tables\n\nRecording the answer to the gating question so the next reader does not re-derive it.\n\nThe PopDAM session checked each table's real update paths against its actual index set, **counting partial-index predicate columns and expression-index inputs**, which block HOT exactly as plain indexed columns do. That distinction changed the answer for two of the four tables, so a plain \"is this column indexed\" check would have been wrong.\n\n- `public.style_guide_files` (0.0% HOT) — all three update paths write indexed columns, including `is_active` as a predicate of `idx_style_guide_files_active_modified` and the thumbnail columns as predicates of `idx_sgf_render_errored`. The 0.0% is arithmetic, not a tuning failure.\n- `public.dam_search_documents` (6.5% HOT) — the dominant path writes `embedding`, and `dam_search_embedding_claim_idx` is a partial work-queue index on `embedding IS NULL` whose whole design is that a completed embedding leaves it. Every successful write is necessarily non-HOT.\n- `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` (0.0% HOT) — the Master Data merge/reconcile functions write six columns, all indexed.\n- `public.assets` (43.5% HOT) — the only one still arguable, and the one where it buys least per row.\n\n**So no fillfactor migration will be routed for the first three.** Lowering fillfactor where HOT is structurally impossible costs disk and buys nothing; that is a false-premise change and this repo has been caught by those before.\n\n## What is actually left\n\nThe productive question was never the storage parameter. It is that these tables carry heavy index sets relative to their write rate — `style_guide_files` at 559 MB of index against a 263 MB table with 17 indexes, `dam_search_documents` at 257 MB against 262 MB. Which of those indexes earn their write cost is worth answering, and it is gated on the dated statistics-reset-and-observe window.\n\n**Nothing is dropped on the current counters, and that is not negotiable.** This database's stats collector has demonstrably lost data — eleven large tables report `n_live_tup = 0` while holding 100k to 2.3M real rows, `public.asset_tags` reporting 0 against 2,173,392 — and `pg_stat_database.stats_reset` is null, so the loss cannot be dated. `idx_dam_search_documents_tsv` reports zero scans and is certainly in use. A drop list built on those counters risks a production search outage to save disk. Planner statistics are intact, so this is a monitoring-visibility problem, not a planning one.\n\nAlso withdrawn upstream and not to be actioned: the earlier manual-repack ask on `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge`. Autovacuum ran 2026-08-29 and left the heap at roughly 2.1x live, which is ordinary.\n\nWhether a partial index is the right shape for the embedding claim pattern is an application design question for the search owner, not a shared-db tuning change.\n\nScope block updated below: still `blocked`, still priority 100, and the blocker is now named precisely.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-02T23:04:57Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1966#issuecomment-5517644141","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABSP1L9Q","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Observation window opened — 2026-09-03, closes 2026-09-17\n\n**Owner authorization.** Albert Hazan authorized this action in chat on 2026-09-03, in these words: *\"yes, reset the production statistics counters.\"* That authorized one action and nothing else. Index definitions re-read from production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` on 2026-09-03 (`pg_index` with `indpred` and `indexprs`); update statements read from live function bodies via `pg_get_functiondef` on the same database, plus application code in `u2giants/popdam3`. Nothing was written, and no statistics counter was touched.\n\n**The earlier cause-(2) comment is correct on three tables. On `dam_search_documents` it is wrong, and in the direction that matters.**\n\n### Confirmed: `public.style_guide_files` — fillfactor is pointless\n\nEvery update path on production writes an indexed column or a partial-index predicate column:\n\n| function / call site | sets | blocked by |\n|---|---|---|\n| `public.refresh_style_guide_file_tag_cache` | `tag_names`, `tag_search_text` | `idx_style_guide_files_tag_names`, `idx_style_guide_files_tag_search_trgm` |\n| `public.deactivate_stale_sg_files` | `is_active` | `idx_sgf_is_active` (direct key) plus the predicates of `idx_style_guide_files_active_modified` and `idx_sgf_render_errored` |\n| `public.retry_sg_render_errors` | `thumbnail_error` | predicate of `idx_sgf_render_errored` |\n| `supabase/functions/agent-api/index.ts:3039` and `:3044` | `thumbnail_url`, `thumbnail_error` | predicate of `idx_sgf_render_errored` |\n\n1,338,566 updates, 0 HOT. That is arithmetic, not tuning. **No fillfactor migration.**\n\n### Confirmed: `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` — fillfactor is pointless\n\n`plm.refresh_style_tracker_item_bridge` is a single `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (style_tracker_row_id) DO UPDATE SET …`. Its SET list includes `sku`, `match_status`, `style_group_id`, `company_id`, `factory_id`, `erp_item_id`, `plm_item_id` — and `sku` feeds the expression index `idx_style_tracker_item_bridge_sku` on `upper(sku)`, so even an unchanged-looking value is re-indexed. Every one of those seven is indexed. 10,742 updates, 0 HOT. **No fillfactor migration.**\n\n### Correction: `public.dam_search_documents` — fillfactor is NOT ruled out, and this is the one to look at\n\nThe earlier comment said the dominant path writes `embedding` and is therefore structurally non-HOT. Half true. Reading the four update statements in `public.claim_dam_search_embedding_batch`, `public.upsert_dam_search_embedding`, `public.mark_dam_search_embedding_error` and `public.reset_dam_search_embedding_errors`:\n\n- **Completion** sets `embedding` — indexed twice (`idx_dam_search_documents_embedding_hnsw`, and the `embedding IS NULL` predicate of `dam_search_embedding_claim_idx`). Structurally non-HOT. Confirmed.\n- **Claim / lease** sets `embedding_lease_token`, `embedding_lease_owner`, `embedding_lease_expires_at`, `embedding_attempts`. **None of these is indexed, and none appears in any predicate or expression** on this table.\n- **Error and reset** set `embedding_error`, `embedding_error_category`, `embedding_next_retry_at` and the lease columns. **Also none indexed.**\n\nSo most of the write traffic on this table is HOT-*eligible* by column, and it is still only 6.6% HOT (3,271,673 updates, 215,191 HOT — roughly 22 updates per row across 145k rows). Column choice is not what is blocking it; **page space is**. `reloptions` is `null` on all four tables, so every one is at the default fillfactor 100 — a HOT-eligible update has nowhere on the page to go.\n\nThe honest caveat, so nobody opens this as a free win: heap size / live rows is about **1.9 KB per row** here (the 384-dim vector sits inline), so roughly four rows fit a page. Buying one free slot per page means dropping to about fillfactor 75, which is a real ~30% heap growth on a 271 MB table in exchange for cutting index write amplification on ~3M updates across ten indexes. That trade may well be worth it, but it is a measured change, not a one-liner.\n\n### `public.assets` — unchanged, and still the weakest case\n\nNow 46.2% HOT (1,334,056 updates, 616,247 HOT) on the current counters, so a meaningful share of its traffic already avoids indexed columns and already finds page space. 35 indexes on a 2 GB heap. Nothing here argues for a storage-parameter change.\n\n### Recommendation\n\nOpen a fillfactor migration for **`public.dam_search_documents` only**, and for that table treat the number as a decision to be measured rather than assumed. The withdrawal stands for `style_guide_files`, `style_tracker_item_bridge` and `assets`.\n\nNothing in this comment touches the index-drop question. That remains frozen behind the observation window that opened 2026-09-03 and closes **2026-09-17**, and no index on these four tables should be dropped before then.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-03T12:04:48Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1966#issuecomment-5525453029","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABSpa5Dw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Marker #2320 is closing under Path B. Live on production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`: `public.dam_search_documents` reloptions = `{fillfactor=75}`. Cumulative `n_tup_upd/n_tup_hot_upd` now 8,315,928 / 1,428,605 (17.2% HOT, up from 6.6% at the 2026-09-03 reading; cumulative counters, so the post-change ratio is higher). The withdrawal for `style_guide_files`, `style_tracker_item_bridge` and `assets` stands.\n- **Redundant/unused index drops remain frozen** behind the observation window opened 2026-09-03, which closes **2026-09-17**. pg_stat_reset is denied on this instance, so the decision uses the baseline recorded above minus a fresh `pg_stat_user_indexes` read on or after 2026-09-17.\n- No claim, version or PR was created for #1966 in this session. Issue stays open until the 2026-09-17 delta reading is taken and any drop is routed as a governed request (index drops must use `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY` or an equivalent low-lock path).\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T12:45:33Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1966#issuecomment-5634627751","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABUEV2jQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Day-8 delta reading of the observation window — read-only, no migration authored\n\nDispatched as a migration-author lane for #1966. **No lane was claimed, no version reserved, no\nmigration written, nothing applied.** The reason is at the bottom; the day-8 delta is the useful\npart, and some of it is unrecoverable after the window closes.\n\n### Target proof\n\n| fact | value |\n|---|---|\n| project ref | `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` — **production** |\n| `current_database()` / `current_user` | `postgres` / `supabase_read_only_user` |\n| `inet_server_port()` | `5432` |\n| server version | PostgreSQL 17.6 |\n| migration head | `20260911210709` |\n| read at | `2026-09-11 19:11:35 -04` |\n\nRead-only throughout (`pg_class`, `pg_stat_all_tables`, `pg_stat_all_indexes`, `pg_index`,\n`pg_constraint`, `pg_depend`). No write of any kind, no statistics counter touched.\n\n### Correction: the counters are not \"lost\". They are *dated*.\n\nThe issue opens by treating `idx_scan = 0` as untrustworthy because the stats collector appeared to\nhave lost data and `pg_stat_database.stats_reset` is null, so the loss could not be dated. It can\nnow be dated, and the answer is better than feared:\n\n- `pg_stat_bgwriter.stats_reset` = `2026-08-28 21:01:01.326349 -04`\n- `pg_postmaster_start_time()` = `2026-08-28 21:01:01.043332 -04`\n- `pg_stat_database.stats_reset` for this database = `null` (cross-checked in the same read)\n\n**283 ms apart.** The counters were never hand-reset, and the null `pg_stat_database.stats_reset`\nconfirms no selective per-database reset either; they simply date from server start. So the tables\nreporting `n_live_tup = 0` against millions of real rows were not a collector defect — they were a\ncluster restart on 2026-08-28 that every `pg_stat_*` counter starts from.\n\nThat is good news for this issue and it does **not** loosen the gate. It means the usable window is\n2026-08-28 → now, the 2026-09-03 baseline sits inside it as a valid anchor, and a delta against that\nbaseline is as meaningful as a reset would have been. It also means the converse trap is real and\nunchanged: **an index created after 2026-08-28 has no observation window at all, and a zero counter\non it means \"never measured\", not \"unused\".**\n\n**Caveat the 2026-09-17 reader must not skip:** at gate close no index will have more than 20 days\nof coverage (2026-08-28 → 2026-09-17), and pre-restart usage is genuinely gone. That is sub-monthly.\nA clean zero on the 17th therefore does **not** prove disuse for any monthly- or quarterly-cadence\nconsumer — a job that last ran 2026-08-20 or next runs 2026-09-20 is invisible at both ends. Treat a\nzero as \"no evidence of use in a 20-day window\", and drop only with a prepared\n`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` rollback, or give specific suspects a longer window.\n\n### The delta, 2026-09-03 baseline → 2026-09-11 (day 8 of 14)\n\n**Thirteen indexes that read `idx_scan = 0` at the baseline are now non-zero. They are PROVEN IN USE\nand permanently out of any drop list**, whatever they read on 2026-09-17:\n\n| table | index | size | 09-03 | 09-11 |\n|---|---|---|---:|---:|\n| `public.assets` | **`idx_assets_filename_trgm`** | **72 MB** | 0 | **36,138** |\n| `public.style_guide_files` | `idx_style_guide_files_active_modified` | 18 MB | 0 | 6,466 |\n| `public.assets` | `idx_assets_status` | 6392 kB | 0 | 681 |\n| `public.style_guide_files` | `idx_sgf_render_errored` | 576 kB | 0 | 99 |\n| `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` | `idx_style_tracker_item_bridge_match_status` | 1112 kB | 0 | 88 |\n| `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` | `style_tracker_item_bridge_pkey` | 1288 kB | 0 | 58 |\n| `public.style_guide_files` | **`idx_sgf_relative_path_trgm`** | **129 MB** | 0 | **12** |\n| `public.style_guide_files` | `idx_sgf_crawl_run_id` | 21 MB | 0 | 6 |\n| `public.assets` | `idx_assets_is_licensed` | 6064 kB | 0 | 6 |\n| `public.style_guide_files` | `idx_sgf_root_label` | 5216 kB | 0 | 5 |\n| `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` | `idx_style_tracker_item_bridge_erp_item` | 1192 kB | 0 | 2 |\n| `public.style_guide_files` | `idx_sgf_property_folder` | 17 MB | 0 | 1 |\n| `public.style_guide_files` | `idx_sgf_licensor_name` | 12 MB | 0 | 1 |\n\n**Two of those are headline candidates from the original 1.4 GB figure.**\n`idx_sgf_relative_path_trgm` (129 MB) was named in the issue body as a drop candidate and is now\ndemonstrably used. `idx_assets_filename_trgm` (72 MB) went from zero to 36,138 scans. This is exactly\nthe failure the window exists to prevent, and it has now happened twice on real evidence rather than\nas a hypothetical. `idx_dam_search_documents_tsv` — the issue's standing red-flag example — has also\nmoved, 150 → 187.\n\n**The candidate pool has already shrunk from ~1,411 MB to ~676 MB at day 8**, and it will shrink\nagain before the window closes. The 24 indexes still reading `idx_scan = 0` today, which are\ncandidates and **not** a drop list:\n\n- `public.assets` ≈ 428 MB — `idx_assets_relative_path_trgm` (279 MB), `idx_assets_tags` (81 MB),\n  `idx_assets_full_text_search` (60 MB), `idx_assets_program_trgm` (24 MB),\n  `idx_assets_customer_trgm` (11 MB), `idx_assets_ai_tagged_at` (9224 kB), `idx_assets_stage`\n  (8736 kB), `idx_assets_file_type` (8456 kB), `idx_assets_program` (6584 kB),\n  `idx_assets_workflow_status` (6448 kB), `idx_assets_customer` (6224 kB), `idx_assets_compat_audit`\n  (4168 kB), `idx_assets_product_material_gin` (2952 kB)\n- `public.style_guide_files` ≈ 221 MB — `idx_sgf_directory_path_trgm` (109 MB),\n  `idx_style_guide_files_tag_search_trgm` (72 MB), `idx_sgf_normalized_name` (16 MB),\n  `idx_style_guide_files_tag_names` (13 MB), `idx_sgf_style_guide_folder` (11 MB)\n- `public.dam_search_documents` ≈ 35 MB — `idx_dam_search_documents_embedding_hnsw` (25 MB),\n  `idx_dam_search_documents_asset_id` (7792 kB), `idx_dam_search_documents_style_group_id` (2336 kB)\n- `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` ≈ 2.4 MB — `idx_style_tracker_item_bridge_sku` (1472 kB),\n  `idx_style_tracker_item_bridge_company` (624 kB),\n  `idx_style_tracker_item_bridge_creative_designer` (384 kB)\n\n**Blast-radius shape of those 24, captured now so the 09-17 decision does not have to discover it:**\nall 24 are `indisvalid = true`, none is unique or primary, **none backs a constraint**\n(`pg_constraint.conindid` null for every one) and **none has a non-auto `pg_depend` dependent**. So\nevery one of them, if it survives to 2026-09-17 still unused, is a plain `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`\n— no `DROP CONSTRAINT`, no dependent view to reroute. All 24 also have `idx_tup_read = 0` and\n`idx_tup_fetch = 0`, not merely `idx_scan = 0`, so there is no partial-use signal hiding beneath the\nscan counter.\n\n### Five indexes have NO baseline and must be excluded from the 2026-09-17 decision\n\nThese exist today but are absent from the 73-index 2026-09-03 baseline, so they were created after\nit and carry no observation window on this anchor. They must not be judged by it in either\ndirection (all five already show scans anyway):\n\n`public.assets` — `idx_assets_tag_rls_visible_ids` (8352 kB, 428,090), `idx_assets_tag_visible_facets`\n(19 MB, 16), `idx_assets_tag_pending_facets` (168 kB, 456).\n`public.style_guide_files` — `idx_sgf_reconcile_root_active_run_id` (48 MB, 24),\n`idx_sgf_active_preview_category` (3392 kB, 625).\n\n### HOT status today, per table — the fillfactor question is closed\n\n| table | reloptions | `n_tup_upd` | `n_tup_hot_upd` | HOT % | idx | `n_dead_tup` | last autovacuum |\n|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|\n| `public.dam_search_documents` | **`{fillfactor=75}`** | 9,049,288 | 1,620,711 | **17.9%** | 10 | 11,658 | 2026-09-11 13:19 |\n| `public.assets` | null | 3,182,749 | 974,368 | **30.6%** | 39 | 1,600 | 2026-09-11 18:08 |\n| `public.style_guide_files` | null | 2,909,961 | 1,085 | **0.0%** | 19 | 16,027 | 2026-09-10 22:05 |\n| `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` | null | 334,087 | 58,302 | **17.5%** | 10 | 0 | 2026-09-11 14:31 |\n\n`dam_search_documents` is confirmed live at `fillfactor=75` (#2196, PR #2201, merge\n`e05d7292469a2ccda6289edb59314232c2b9cc1c`) and its HOT ratio has risen 6.6% → 17.9% on cumulative\ncounters. **That was the whole of the well-founded HOT work and it is delivered.**\n\n`public.style_guide_files` remains at 0.0% over 2.9 M updates. At that ratio the problem is not\npage headroom — it is that the HOT precondition never occurs, because every update path writes an\nindexed column or a partial-index predicate, exactly as the two prior cause-(2) reviews found.\n`fillfactor` cannot help that; it would cost page density and scan I/O and buy nothing. The\nwithdrawal stands and I authored nothing. **The durable fix for this table is application-side** —\nstop writing indexed columns whose value did not change — and that is not authorable from this lane.\n\n**One new observation worth a look after the window closes:** `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` was\n0.0% HOT at 10,742 updates and is now **17.5%** at 334,087. Something in its update mix changed\nsince 2026-08-30 — the `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE` path can no longer be writing all seven indexed\ncolumns every time. Not actionable today; flagged so the 2026-09-17 reader does not carry the\n\"structurally 0%\" conclusion forward unchecked.\n\n### Worth capturing before 2026-09-17, because it is unrecoverable afterwards\n\nCounters are cumulative, so on the 17th you can compute (close − baseline) but never *when in the\nwindow* the usage happened. \"Flipped by day 8\" is stronger evidence than \"non-zero at close\", and\nthat shape disappears if it is not written down. Recorded above: the day-8 `idx_scan` /\n`idx_tup_read` / `idx_tup_fetch` snapshot with its timestamp, index sizes, per-table HOT ratios,\ndead tuples and autovacuum times, and the constraint/dependency status of all 24 candidates. Still\nworth adding before the gate: bloat estimates for the three non-HOT tables, and — if\n`pg_stat_statements` is available — the query texts hitting the flipped indexes, which would give\nthe drop decision query-level provenance instead of counter inference alone.\n\n### Why no migration was authored\n\n1. **The HOT work is done.** The only table where lowering fillfactor was well-founded was\n   `dam_search_documents`; it shipped in #2196 / PR #2201 and is live. The other three are\n   twice-verified false premises, and `style_guide_files` is now disconfirmed live at 0.0%.\n2. **Every index drop is frozen until 2026-09-17** by this issue's own blocker, six days out. Two\n   headline candidates flipped to in-use inside the window, which is the argument for the gate, not\n   against it. \"Drop only the indexes older than the counter epoch\" does not escape this — being\n   older than the restart gives an index *more* unobserved history, not less.\n3. **This issue's `db-work-scope` is `status: blocked`.** Only `ready + structural +\n   shared-db-orchestrator` may enter a migration-author lane. A claim here would have locked four of\n   the busiest tables in the database and permanently burned a reserved migration version to produce\n   no migration.\n\nAlso considered and rejected today: `REINDEX CONCURRENTLY` for bloat (no bloat measurement exists\nyet — that would be the same unmeasured-premise error as the fillfactor change); and marking an\nindex disabled instead of dropping it (PostgreSQL has no supported DDL for that; flipping\n`pg_index.indisvalid` by catalog update is unsupported and would bypass this freeze invisibly).\n\nNothing was dropped, nothing was altered, no lane or version was consumed. #1966 stays open for the\n2026-09-17 delta reading, which should re-run this read, subtract the 2026-09-03 baseline, exclude\nthe five no-baseline indexes, apply the sub-monthly-coverage caveat above, and route any surviving\ndrop as a governed structural request using `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`.\n\nThis decision was put to an independent AI reviewer before posting, which concurred that authoring\nzero migrations is correct rather than an avoidable failure to deliver, and supplied the\nsub-monthly-coverage caveat, the `pg_stat_database.stats_reset` cross-check and the capture-today\nlist now incorporated above.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:12:48Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1966#issuecomment-5641696909","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABWR0lwg","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Post-window production reading — 2026-09-23 06:15 UTC (read only)\n\nProduction project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` was verified directly. `pg_stat_database.stats_reset` is still NULL and `pg_postmaster_start_time()` is 2026-08-28 21:01:01 EDT. All 73 indexes in the 2026-09-03 baseline still exist, and no `idx_scan` counter decreased. This makes the September 3-to-23 delta usable. The Supabase performance advisor's 2026-09-23 06:15 UTC `unused_index` list agrees with the remaining zero counters; it is a signal, not a drop authorization.\n\nOf those 73: **49 had scans during the window; 23 had zero scans at baseline and still have zero; one (`dam_search_embedding_claim_idx`) had 4,336 scans before baseline but none in this window.** Fourteen baseline-zero indexes became visibly used, including `idx_assets_ai_tagged_at` since the September 11 day-eight reading. Eight indexes created after baseline have no comparable delta and are excluded; all eight already report scans. The 23 unobserved indexes total 796,205,056 bytes (759.3 MiB), are valid and non-unique, and none owns a constraint or has a non-automatic dependent.\n\nThe 23 **not observed in this 20-day window**, grouped by table (not a drop list):\n\n- `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge`: `idx_style_tracker_item_bridge_company`, `idx_style_tracker_item_bridge_creative_designer`, `idx_style_tracker_item_bridge_sku`.\n- `public.assets`: `idx_assets_compat_audit`, `idx_assets_customer`, `idx_assets_customer_trgm`, `idx_assets_file_type`, `idx_assets_full_text_search`, `idx_assets_product_material_gin`, `idx_assets_program`, `idx_assets_program_trgm`, `idx_assets_relative_path_trgm`, `idx_assets_stage`, `idx_assets_tags`, `idx_assets_workflow_status`.\n- `public.dam_search_documents`: `idx_dam_search_documents_asset_id`, `idx_dam_search_documents_embedding_hnsw`, `idx_dam_search_documents_style_group_id`.\n- `public.style_guide_files`: `idx_sgf_directory_path_trgm`, `idx_sgf_normalized_name`, `idx_sgf_style_guide_folder`, `idx_style_guide_files_tag_names`, `idx_style_guide_files_tag_search_trgm`.\n\nCurrent consumers forbid a counter-only drop decision: the deployed `search_dam_documents(...)` function still performs vector distance ordering, `filter_effective_assets(jsonb)` still has `relative_path ILIKE`, and the PopSG library UI searches `directory_path ILIKE`; these are relevant to three unobserved indexes. Counter absence means the planner did not choose them in this window, not that the feature is retired. The source and live function evidence should be checked for each prospective drop, with representative plans and the monthly/quarterly admin/import cycle, before authoring any separate guarded `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY` migration and rollback. The index absence/ledger gate in #2043 must also be observed.\n\nHOT data does not justify blanket fillfactor changes: `style_guide_files` remains 0.02% over 5.90 million updates; `dam_search_documents` has live `fillfactor=75` and 22.04% cumulative HOT; the PLM bridge is 17.45%. `assets` cumulative HOT has fallen to 17.93%; since the September 11 reading it gained 2,251,993 updates but only 96 HOT updates (0.0043% over that interval), suggesting a changed indexed-column write mix that needs the owning application to inspect. No statistics reset, index drop, fillfactor change, lane claim, or database write was performed.\n\n**Decision:** no index qualifies for removal on the evidence available today. Retain all 23 while the application owners identify rare consumers and representative plans; the dated September 17 gate is satisfied, but the proof for a destructive change is not. This is an evidence finding, not an owner request for a blanket drop.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0cb03-daa2-79d2-85fd-6a8904abfc53 on EDGE-DEV","createdAt":"2026-09-23T06:16:16Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1966#issuecomment-5790049730","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABWR48kA","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Follow-up: live write paths and fillfactor (read only, 2026-09-23)\n\nThe post-window index reading above does not justify a blanket fillfactor migration. Current production write paths explain why:\n\n- `public.style_guide_files`: only 0.02% HOT across 5.90 million updates. The crawl upsert writes indexed crawl and active fields (`popdam3/supabase/functions/agent-api/index.ts:2916-2950`); the current stale-file path invokes `reconcile_stale_sg_files_batch` (`agent-api/index.ts:3036-3056`), whose actual `SET is_active=false` is in `shared-db/supabase/migrations/20260915023506_popsg_reconcile_bounded_under_statement_ceiling.sql:309-315`. Thumbnail completion writes predicate fields (`popdam3/supabase/functions/_shared/sg-render-completion.ts:123-126`), and tag refresh writes indexed tag fields (`shared-db/supabase/migrations/20260723170000_popsg_file_tags.sql:171-175`). Page space cannot make these indexed-value changes HOT.\n- `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge`: 17.45% cumulative HOT. Its current conflict refresh sets indexed SKU, ERP item, style group, company, PLM item, and match status (`shared-db/supabase/migrations/20260911210844_retire_erp_items_to_archive.sql:423-455`); designer/manual resolution also sets indexed values (`20260710135700_reconcile_style_tracker_functions.sql:81-138,983-1016`). A lower fillfactor might help the subset whose indexed values do not actually change; that subset is not measured.\n- `public.dam_search_documents`: production already has `fillfactor=75` and is 22.04% HOT cumulatively. Lease claim/error updates touch fields that can be HOT if page space permits (`20260825082910_popdam_ai_search_reconciliation_and_activation.sql:2665-2677,2692-2702`). Embedding completion changes indexed `embedding` and partial-index membership (`:2681-2688`), so it cannot be HOT. The observed HOT increase does not establish that another fillfactor reduction would help; there were zero active leases at the read.\n- `public.assets`: default fillfactor, 17.93% cumulative HOT. From the September 11 reading to September 23, it gained 2,251,993 updates but only 96 HOT updates (0.0043%). A second short live sample gained 4,120 updates and zero HOT. The busiest observed SQL shapes set indexed style-group membership and scan metadata; source paths are `popdam3/supabase/functions/_shared/style-group-assignment.ts:103-110` and `agent-api/index.ts:1128-1148`. The deployed `agent-api` was checked against that source. Cumulative query-call counts do not apportion every updated row, but they support an indexed-write cause rather than a page-space-only cause.\n\n**Decision:** no fillfactor change is qualified for any of the four tables. Keep #1966 open while the application owners measure per-statement update mix, whether indexed values actually change, and page pressure for any narrow HOT-eligible path. No code, schema, statistics, or data were changed in this audit.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0cb03-daa2-79d2-85fd-6a8904abfc53 on EDGE-DEV","createdAt":"2026-09-23T06:23:46Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1966#issuecomment-5790121104","viewerDidAuthor":true}],"createdAt":"2026-08-31T00:43:09Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2YAgzg","name":"orchestrator","description":"Changes shared-database structure (or curated Master Data load): orchestrator work","color":"B60205"}],"number":1966,"title":"High-churn tables cannot do HOT updates (0% on style_guide_files and the PLM bridge), plus 1.4 GB of indexes with untrustworthy usage counters","updatedAt":"2026-09-23T06:23:46Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1966"},
{"assignees":[],"body":"## Owners\n\nBusiness review: Laura and Ilona  \nTechnical preparation and controlled ColdLion update: Licensing data support\n\n## Goal\n\nReview every Property received from authorized licensor sources and signed contracts, decide which Properties POP can and will use, inactivate unusable entries, and then bring ColdLion into line with the approved decisions.\n\n## Authority rules\n\n- Signed contracts and schedules are authoritative for POP's licensed entitlement and for any explicit Property-to-Licensor relationship they state.\n- A submissions system is authoritative for direct Property relationships it publishes within POP's entitled account view.\n- Creative libraries identify available style guides and assets. Their folders, labels, co-occurrence, and landing-table location do not establish Property ownership.\n- Name similarity is a review clue only. It never creates an approved match.\n- If accepted authorities disagree, leave the row unresolved and record the exact conflict; do not guess.\n\n## Review work\n\n1. Use the authenticated **Scraped Properties** page as the review queue, with the relevant contract schedule available alongside it.\n2. Review every source Property identity, not merely every distinct display name.\n3. Record one decision per identity:\n   - **Active — licensed and usable**\n   - **Inactive — not in our current license**\n   - **Inactive — not a Property / utility value**\n   - **Inactive — licensed but POP will not use**\n   - **Unresolved — more evidence or an owner decision is required**\n4. For every active row, select the exact approved licensor and exact canonical Property. Preserve the source ID and contract/portal evidence.\n5. For every inactive or unresolved row, record a plain-English reason. Never delete source evidence.\n6. Resolve duplicates as separate source identities first; merge only after evidence proves they are the same business Property.\n\n## ColdLion update\n\nAfter Laura and Ilona complete and sign off the review:\n\n1. Export and retain a recoverable pre-change ColdLion snapshot.\n2. Match approved rows by reviewed source identity/canonical Property, never by fuzzy name alone.\n3. Add or reactivate approved usable Properties and inactivate the approved unusable Properties.\n4. Do not delete historical Properties or transactions.\n5. Reconcile ColdLion totals and exceptions back to the signed review file.\n\n## Completion evidence\n\n- Every received source Property identity has exactly one current review decision.\n- No unresolved row was silently activated or inactivated.\n- Laura and Ilona's dated sign-off is retained.\n- ColdLion has a recoverable pre-change snapshot and an exact post-change reconciliation.\n- The Scraped Properties page and ColdLion agree on active/inactive status and canonical identity.\n- Aggregate counts by licensor, source, and decision status are recorded without publishing licensed Property names outside approved private systems.\n\n## Dependency\n\nBegin the business review only after shared-db #1658 and its successor corrections are production-verified, so the page presents contract authority, direct submissions authority, and Creative evidence correctly.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: curated-master-data\nroute: curated-master-data-governance\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on: 1658\n\n```","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABRh8zWw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Dependency cleared: #1658 is production-live and closed.
