{"assignees":[],"body":"Bounded successor to #1352, opened by orchestrator marker #1419 on 2026-08-24.\n\n## Why this exists\n\n#1352 carried a 430-object `writes:` list. A read-only verification on 2026-08-24 proved **428 of 430 are already delivered** by merged migration `20260824011750_create_dflow_prod_and_audit_archive.sql`, which is applied to preview **and already promoted to production**. Both `dflow_prod` and `dflow_archive` are empty as intended (103 tables, 0 live tuples).\n\nLeaving that stale 430-object list attached to a dispatchable issue is itself a hazard: if anyone flips #1352 back to `ready`, it re-advertises a phantom exclusive lock over 428 delivered objects, serialising every concurrent `dflow_prod.*` change and inviting a dispatcher to re-write objects that already exist — the documented `CREATE OR REPLACE` clobber class. This issue carries only the work that actually remains.\n\n## The remaining work\n\n`public.style_tracker_rows_with_bridge` still references `dflow`, not `dflow_prod`, on **both** preview and production. It is the single cross-schema dependency on the DesignFlow schema (#1352 measured: 0 foreign keys in or out, exactly 1 view referencing it).\n\n## Why it is NOT startable yet\n\nRepointing the view now would break it against a deliberately empty schema. This is a cutover step and must run in the cutover sequence, after the row copy, not ahead of it.\n\n## Blocked on\n\nOwner authorization for the live DesignFlow cutover, plus the non-structural prerequisites tracked on #1352: the `AuditLog` disposition decision, the `database-connection-contract.js` guard flip across the six application repos, the connection budget, and #771's timed rehearsal.\n\nOwner decision recorded 2026-08-24: the schema keeps the name `dflow_prod` (not `dflow_plm`).\n\n## Known hazard to carry into the cutover\n\n`dflow_prod` is a **static DDL snapshot** taken from live `dflow`. Nothing in the claim machinery forces a future `dflow` write to be mirrored into `dflow_prod`, so the two diverge from the next `dflow` migration onward and the divergence surfaces at cutover as shape drift. Any future claim writing `dflow.*` should carry the matching `dflow_prod.*` mirror as an explicit `writes:` obligation. Second hazard: repointing a service before the row copy yields empty tables returning success-shaped empty results rather than an error.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1150\ndepends_on: 1352\nwrites:\n  - view public.style_tracker_rows_with_bridge\nreads:\n  - schema dflow\n  - schema dflow_prod\n```","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABS6WivQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"**Live read of production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, 2026-09-06 — the drift hazard this issue warned about has already happened. Removing `needs-albert`: asking the owner to authorize the cutover today would be asking him to authorize a copy onto a stale target.**\n\n| fact | value |\n|---|---|\n| `dflow` base tables | **135** |\n| `dflow_prod` base tables | **104** |\n| in `dflow` but **missing** from `dflow_prod` | **21** |\n| in `dflow_prod` but not in `dflow` | 0 |\n| `dflow_prod` rows | 0 (still empty, as intended) |\n| `public.style_tracker_rows_with_bridge` still references `dflow` | yes |\n\n`dflow.art_piece` alone holds 1,116 rows, so `dflow` is live and being written. Note that `pg_stat_user_tables.n_live_tup` reports 0 for `dflow` — those counters have never been analyzed on this project and must not be used to judge emptiness here; the counts above are real `count(*)` / catalog reads.\n\n**What this means.** This issue's own \"known hazard\" section predicted exactly this: `dflow_prod` is a static DDL snapshot taken 2026-08-24, nothing forces later `dflow` migrations to be mirrored into it, and the divergence surfaces at cutover as shape drift. Thirteen days later the gap is **21 tables**. A row copy run today would silently leave 21 tables with no destination, and the second named hazard applies — services repointed at them would return success-shaped empty results, not errors.\n\n**Why the owner label comes off.** The remaining owner decision (authorize the live DesignFlow cutover) is real but not answerable yet. Its stated prerequisites are still open — the `AuditLog` disposition, the `database-connection-contract.js` guard flip across six application repos, the connection budget, and #771's timed rehearsal — and the copy target is now demonstrably behind the source. An authorization given against these facts would be authorizing a broken cutover.\n\n**Before `needs-albert` is re-applied, these must be true and evidenced in a comment here:**\n\n1. `dflow_prod` shape re-synced to `dflow` — the missing-table count re-measured at 0, not assumed.\n2. A standing mechanism, not a one-off re-sync, that makes any future claim writing `dflow.*` carry the matching `dflow_prod.*` mirror as an explicit `writes:` obligation. Without it the count is back above zero on the next DesignFlow migration and this comment gets written again.\n3. The four #1352 prerequisites closed.\n4. The exact question for Albert written out in the comment, in business terms, with the cutover's downtime and rollback stated.\n\nScope stays `blocked`, `depends_on: 1352` unchanged. Nothing here is startable and nothing is lost by leaving it.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-07T02:17:42Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1431#issuecomment-5564113597","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABUENEhw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"**Re-verified BLOCKED against live production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` (proved via `get_project_url`), 2026-09-11. Read-only; nothing was changed. The cutover has NOT happened, and the specific tables this view reads are still empty.**\n\n## The gate, stated precisely\n\nThis view may only be repointed **after** the DesignFlow row copy has populated `dflow_prod`. It has not. Repointing today would not error — it would return success-shaped empty results, which is the second hazard this issue already names.\n\n## Evidence checked today (live `count(*)` and catalog reads, not `reltuples`)\n\n| fact | value |\n|---|---|\n| `public.style_tracker_rows_with_bridge` still references `dflow` | **yes** |\n| the only `dflow` objects it reads | `dflow.\"RFQItem\"`, `dflow.\"RFQGroup\"` |\n| `dflow.\"RFQItem\"` / `dflow.\"RFQGroup\"` rows | **6,689 / 390** |\n| `dflow_prod.\"RFQItem\"` / `dflow_prod.\"RFQGroup\"` rows | **0 / 0** |\n| view rows returned today | **15,742** (unchanged from the earlier measurement) |\n| view rows currently carrying non-empty `rfq_groups` | **2,072** |\n| `dflow` base tables / `dflow_prod` base tables | 126 / 103 |\n| in `dflow` but missing from `dflow_prod` | **23** |\n| in `dflow_prod` but not in `dflow` | 0 |\n\n**The blast radius is now measured, not estimated.** Both RFQ tables *do* exist in `dflow_prod`, so a repoint would compile and run clean — and silently drop the RFQ data on **2,072 of 15,742 rows** to an empty array. That is the precise failure mode that makes this repoint dangerous rather than merely premature: there is no error to notice.\n\n## Shape drift has widened, not closed\n\nThe 2026-09-06 comment measured 21 tables missing from `dflow_prod`; today it is **23**. All 23 are `sample_*` / `item_*` tables, i.e. a whole feature area written into `dflow` after the 2026-08-24 static DDL snapshot. `dflow` is plainly live and being written (~2.8M estimated tuples across 126 tables). Nothing is mirroring those writes into `dflow_prod`, exactly as this issue's \"known hazard\" section predicted.\n\n*Method note:* the `dflow` base-table count reads 126 today against 135 on 2026-09-06. I did not reconcile that difference and am not claiming it is a deletion — it may be a different counting method. The load-bearing figures above (the two RFQ table counts, and the 23-table gap measured by set difference in one query) do not depend on it.\n\n## Unblocking condition — unchanged, and none of it is met\n\nThe four conditions in the 2026-09-06 comment still stand and still gate `needs-albert`. On today's reading condition 1 is further from met than when it was written. Adding the now-measured requirement:\n\n5. The row copy must populate `dflow_prod.\"RFQItem\"` and `dflow_prod.\"RFQGroup\"`, re-measured non-zero **in this issue**, before the repoint is authored. A repoint ahead of the copy loses RFQ data on 2,072 rows with no error surfaced to anyone.\n\nScope stays `blocked`, `depends_on: 1352` unchanged. Note that #1352 is now CLOSED, but closing it did not deliver its four non-structural prerequisites (the `AuditLog` disposition, the `database-connection-contract.js` guard flip across the six application repos, the connection budget, and #771's timed rehearsal) — a closed dependency is not a satisfied one, and this issue must not be read as unblocked on that basis.\n\nNo lane was claimed, no migration authored, and no file created. Nothing is startable here and nothing is lost by leaving it.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T22:54:58Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1431#issuecomment-5641553031","viewerDidAuthor":true}],"createdAt":"2026-08-24T16:01:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"assignees":[],"body":"Follow-up to [#1366](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/1366), which is complete and closed. Two switches were deliberately left off because their gates were not met on 2026-08-23. This issue exists so they are not forgotten.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 20\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n**Neither switch is a bug or an oversight.** Flipping either on 2026-08-23 would have stranded live work. The measured state and exact gates live in `config/agent-work-contract-activation.json`; this is the human-readable pointer.\n\n## Switch 1 — contract enforcement is `report-only`\n\nAudited 2026-08-23: **4 open pull requests, 0 carrying a contract.**\n\nEnforcing today fails every pull request that predates contracts. A guard that fails everything on day one gets switched off, and a switched-off guard protects nothing.\n\nReport-only already **fails** on a malformed contract or a report that contradicts its contract — it only tolerates their absence.\n\n**Gate:** every open pull request either carries a valid contract and report, or is listed by exact number in `grandfathered_prs`. Then set `mode: \"enforced\"` and `activated_at` in the same PR.\n\nMaking `Agent work contract` a **required context** on `main` is a *separate, later* action — only after enforced mode has run green for a full day. Use `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs`; never hand-edit branch protection.\n\n## Switch 2 — the legacy `objects:` alias is retained\n\nAudited 2026-08-23: **1 open claim and 29 open work issues** still use `objects:`.\n\nIt now emits a visible deprecation warning, because a silent alias never gets migrated — nothing ever reminds anyone it exists.\n\n**Gate:** zero open claims and zero open work issues using `objects:`, **plus** at least 14 days of documentation and examples using `writes:`/`reads:`.\n\n⚠️ **Do not retire it early.** A legacy `objects:` claim is read as a **write**. Breaking that reading would let a writer start against work already in flight — the exact collision the lanes exist to prevent.\n\n## Also outstanding, separately tracked\n\n- Six migrations merged 2026-08-14 and never applied anywhere → [#949](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/949)\n- Deferred Supabase per-PR branch pilot → [#1391](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/1391)\n\n## Verify before changing anything\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --queue-audit\ngh api repos/u2giants/shared-db/branches/main/protection\n```\n\nRe-run the audit rather than trusting the counts above; they were true on 2026-08-23. {"assignees":[],"body":"## Outcome needed\n\nLicensor scrape tables should be able to record **what changed since the last capture**, so a\nrefresh loads only new, edited and withdrawn rows instead of a full snapshot, and so a row that\ndisappears from a licensor portal is marked rather than lost.\n\nNo data is included in this issue. This is a structural request only.\n\n## Why\n\nStyle guides are living. Licensors add guides, replace art in place under the same file name, and\nwithdraw assets. The capture side now supports incremental runs (shared skill\n`licensor-incremental-capture`, in `u2giants/ai-devops`), which produces per-run\n`added` / `changed` / `withdrawn` deltas against a committed manifest.\n\nThe database cannot receive that yet. Today `plm.<licensor>_capture` models **one row per attempted\nfull load**, and the entity rows hang off a single `capture_id`. There is nowhere to say \"this asset\nwas first seen in June, last seen today\" or \"this asset stopped appearing on 19 Aug\".\n\nOwner ruling 2026-08-19: **a withdrawn asset is marked, never deleted.** Product may already have\nbeen made from that art, and withdrawals are frequently temporary (a guide is pulled and reposted).\n\n## Requested structure\n\n### 1. Lifecycle columns on every licensor entity table\n\nApplies to the asset, property, character and style-guide tables of every licensor that has\nthem today:\n\n| Licensor | Table prefix |\n| --- | --- |\n| NBCU | `plm.nbcu_*` |\n| Disney DCP Vault | `plm.dcp_*` |\n| Disney OPA | `plm.opa_*` |\n| Warner STARLABS | `plm.wb_*` |\n| Strawberry Shortcake / WildBrain | `plm.wildbrain_*` |\n| Peanuts | `plm.peanuts_*` |\n\nTwo licensors are **not** in this list because they have no tables at all yet: **Paramount** and\n**Sesame Workshop**. Both are captured to files in `u2giants/licensor-source-data` but have never\nbeen landed. Their initial schema is separate work; when it is designed it should include the\nlifecycle columns below from the start rather than retrofit them.\n\n| Column | Type | Purpose |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `first_seen_capture_id` | uuid FK -> `<licensor>_capture(id)` | capture that first indexed the row |\n| `first_seen_at` | timestamptz | source capture time of that run |\n| `last_seen_capture_id` | uuid FK -> `<licensor>_capture(id)` | most recent capture that still saw it |\n| `last_seen_at` | timestamptz | source capture time of that run |\n| `status` | text, `active` \\| `withdrawn`, default `active` | lifecycle state |\n| `withdrawn_at` | timestamptz null | first capture that stopped seeing it |\n| `change_signal` | text null | the value compared between runs |\n\n`change_signal` is whatever the portal actually publishes, strongest to weakest: Paramount\n`date_last_updated` + `version`, Warner `modified_date` + `file_size_bytes`, NBCU\n`display_modified` + `display_size`, Disney DCP Vault nothing at all (presence only). It is stored\nopaquely and only ever compared for equality.\n\nConstraint worth enforcing: `status = 'withdrawn'` exactly when `withdrawn_at is not null`.\n\n### 2. A deterministic upsert key on each entity table\n\nIncremental loading upserts on the licensor's own source key. Where a unique constraint on that key\ndoes not already exist, it is needed, otherwise a refresh silently duplicates rows.\n\n### 3. Delta-aware capture rows\n\nOn `plm.<licensor>_capture`:\n\n| Column | Type | Purpose |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `run_kind` | text, `full` \\| `incremental`, default `full` | which kind of run this was |\n| `baseline_capture_id` | uuid null FK -> same table | the capture this run diffed against |\n| `delta_counts` | jsonb, default `{}` | added / changed / withdrawn per entity type |\n\n`baseline_capture_id` must reference a capture whose `status = 'complete'`. A partial or failed run\nmust never become a baseline.\n\n## Safety note for whoever implements this\n\nThe dangerous failure mode is an expired portal login returning a short or empty index, which a diff\nthen reads as *the licensor withdrew their whole library*. The capture side already gates on this\n(authentication proof, per-scope coverage, and a shrink gate at 2% of baseline or 100 rows,\nwhichever is smaller). If any database-side guard is added, it should refuse a bulk withdrawal that\nexceeds a similar threshold rather than accept it silently.\n\n## Not requested here\n\n- No changes to `core.*` curated Master Data. Outside-sourced loads into curated Master Data remain\n  orchestrator work under the §6.4 carve-out.\n- No loader changes in this issue; the app repos own those once the columns exist.\n- Nothing about media files. Downloaded style-guide art goes to the NAS and is never loaded into the\n  database; the existing `media_downloaded = 0` check on the capture tables stays as it is.\n\n## Blocked until this lands\n\nRefresh runs currently produce their delta files in `u2giants/licensor-source-data` and load\nnothing.\n\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 580\ndepends_on: 1880,1881,1883\nwrites:\n  - table plm.nbcu_capture\n  - table plm.nbcu_asset\n  - table plm.nbcu_property\n  - table plm.nbcu_character\n  - table plm.nbcu_style_guide\n  - table plm.dcp_property\n  - table plm.dcp_character\n  - table plm.dcp_metadata_run\n  - table plm.wb_capture\n  - table plm.wildbrain_capture\n  - table plm.wildbrain_asset\n  - table plm.wildbrain_character\n  - table plm.wildbrain_guide\n  - table plm.wildbrain_era\n  - table plm.wildbrain_creative_group\n  - table plm.peanuts_capture\n  - table plm.peanuts_asset\n  - table plm.peanuts_character\n  - table plm.peanuts_style_guide\n  - table plm.peanuts_art_program\n  - table plm.sesame_capture\n  - table plm.sesame_asset\n  - table plm.sesame_character\n  - table plm.sesame_style_guide\n  - table plm.sesame_brand\n```","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABPu9RLw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Classified for the queue audit, and marked `blocked` — here is exactly what unblocks it\n\nAdded a `db-work-scope` block so this stops showing as **unclassified** in `--queue-audit`. It is set to `status: blocked` rather than `ready`, with an **empty `objects:` list**, and that is deliberate: this issue cannot be dispatched as written, for two reasons.\n\n### 1. The object list has to be enumerated before a lane can be claimed\n\nA migration-author lane is acquired against **exact, parseable object claims**, and the claim tool refuses overlapping or unreadable ones. This issue asks for seven new columns plus a constraint on *\"the asset, property, character and style-guide tables of every licensor that has them today\"* across six table families — roughly two dozen tables, none of them named individually.\n\nNobody can claim that, and guessing the list is worse than leaving it empty: a claim that misses a table silently leaves it unprotected against a concurrent author, and this repository has already refused two PRs for claims that omitted objects the SQL actually wrote.\n\n**What unblocks it:** enumerate the exact tables from the current migrations on main — not from this issue's prose — and paste them into the `objects:` list, then flip `status` to `ready`. That enumeration is a read-only task any session can do without a lane.\n\n### 2. Its premise is now stale in one respect\n\nThe issue states:\n\n> *Two licensors are **not** in this list because they have no tables at all yet: **Paramount** and **Sesame Workshop**.*\n\n**Sesame Workshop was landed and promoted to production today** — `20260819212002_sesame_workshop_netx_source_landing.sql`, 19 `plm.sesame_*` tables, applied to `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` and verified against production's own ledger (#1289).\n\nSo the advice in this issue — *\"when it is designed it should include the lifecycle columns below from the start rather than retrofit them\"* — **was not followed for Sesame, because Sesame landed before this issue was actioned.** `plm.sesame_*` now needs the same retrofit as the other six families, and it should be added to the table above rather than left in the not-yet-landed list. Paramount is still correctly listed as unlanded.\n\nThis is worth flagging loudly rather than quietly editing: the issue's reasoning was sound and the sequencing simply beat it. Any *future* landing schema should still carry these columns from the start, and that guidance is now more urgent, not less — it has already been missed once.\n\n### Unchanged and still correct\n\nThe owner ruling this rests on — **a withdrawn asset is marked, never deleted** — stands, and is the reason `status`/`withdrawn_at` exist rather than a delete. Product may already have been made from withdrawn art, and withdrawals are frequently temporary.","createdAt":"2026-08-20T03:11:03Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1275#issuecomment-5350838575","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABPu9_uA","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Object list enumerated from the migrations on main — read this before claiming a lane\n\nThe `objects:` list is now populated with **25 tables**, derived by grepping `create table` across `supabase/migrations/` at main `cef67d6`, not from this issue's prose. It stays `status: blocked` for the reason in the next section.\n\n### What I included, and the judgement calls I did NOT make for you\n\nThe issue scopes this to *\"the asset, property, character and style-guide tables\"*. For four families that maps cleanly:\n\n| Family | asset | property | character | style guide |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| NBCU | `nbcu_asset` | `nbcu_property` | `nbcu_character` | `nbcu_style_guide` |\n| DCP Vault | `dcp_asset` | `dcp_property` | `dcp_character` | `dcp_style_guide` |\n| Warner | `wb_asset` | `wb_property` | `wb_character` | `wb_style_guide` |\n| Disney OPA | — | `opa_property` | `opa_character` | — |\n\n**Three families do not have a table literally called \"property\" or \"style guide\", and I made a defensible guess that the author must confirm or overturn:**\n\n- **WildBrain** — no `wildbrain_property` exists. Its property-shaped concepts are `wildbrain_era` and `wildbrain_creative_group`, and its style guide is `wildbrain_guide`. I included `wildbrain_guide` and **excluded `era` and `creative_group`**.\n- **Peanuts** — I mapped property to `peanuts_art_program`. Also present and excluded: `peanuts_initiative`, `peanuts_holiday`, `peanuts_animation_title`, `peanuts_asset_type`.\n- **Sesame** — I mapped property to `sesame_brand`. Also present and excluded: `sesame_sub_brand`, `sesame_theme`, `sesame_category`, `sesame_art_style`.\n\n**I deliberately excluded every join table** (`*_asset_character`, `*_asset_style_guide`, `*_property_character`, …), every `*_capture` table, and Warner's `*_normalized` mirror tables. A join row's lifecycle is arguably the lifecycle of its two ends, but that is a design decision this issue does not make, and **whoever authors this must decide it explicitly rather than inherit my omission.** If join tables are in scope, the claim must be expanded before any SQL is written — two PRs were already refused this session for claims that omitted objects the SQL touched.\n\n### Why it stays blocked\n\nThe mapping above is a guess on three of seven families, and the join-table question is open. **A structural claim must be exact, and \"exact\" means someone decided, not that someone grepped.** Flip to `ready` once those two questions are settled; no lane is needed to settle them, because it is a read-only design decision.\n\n### Correction to this issue's premise, repeated here because it changes the table count\n\n**Sesame Workshop is now landed.** `20260819212002` was promoted to production today (#1289) — 19 `plm.sesame_*` tables. This issue's advice that a future landing should carry the lifecycle columns from the start **was already missed once**, because Sesame landed before this issue was actioned. `plm.sesame_*` is therefore in the retrofit list above rather than the not-yet-landed list.\n\nParamount remains genuinely unlanded and is correctly absent.\n\n**The guidance is now more urgent, not less: any landing schema designed from here should carry these seven columns from the start.**","createdAt":"2026-08-20T03:11:55Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1275#issuecomment-5350850488","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABRf_9mQ","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Live production catalog was re-read on 2026-08-30 against `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` using metadata-only, read-only queries. The umbrella is now split wherever the structural outcome is exact:\n\n- #1880 — DCP Vault asset/style-guide lifecycle plus complete crawl baseline (ready).\n- #1881 — Warner durable normalized entity lifecycle (ready).\n- #1883 — OPA durable property/character lifecycle (ready).\n\nI am leaving #1275 open and blocked because the remaining outcome cannot safely be represented as author-ready SQL yet:\n\n1. **NBCU, WildBrain, Peanuts, and Sesame are snapshot-per-capture models.** Their live primary/unique keys include `capture_id`; there is no cross-run entity key on which the requested incremental upsert can safely operate. A design decision must choose between preserving immutable snapshots plus a durable current-state layer, or changing the existing tables' identity. Adding lifecycle columns alone would mark snapshot rows, not source entities.\n2. **Relationship/join rows have no decided lifecycle.** Live tables encode observations, asserted evidence, derived membership, and source relationships differently. A missing join in a later run may mean withdrawal, incomplete coverage, or changed derivation. No successor claims those tables until the source-family rule says which meaning applies.\n3. **DCP property/character observations use metadata runs, not crawls.** Their complete-baseline and withdrawal boundary must be defined independently from #1880's portal crawl.\n4. **Warner capture is chunk-addressed by `(capture_id, chunk_number)`.** The baseline must identify a completed logical run/header without turning a chunk into a baseline.\n5. **The property-shaped entity remains undecided** for WildBrain (`era` vs `creative_group`), Peanuts (`art_program` vs other vocabularies), and Sesame (`brand` vs sub-brand/theme/category/art-style). I preserved those candidate objects in the blocked scope but did not guess.\n6. **Bulk-withdrawal refusal needs a source-family coverage contract.** The 2%/100-row safety rule cannot be attached honestly until each family's definition of a complete scope is named.\n\nThe umbrella scope now contains only these unresolved families/objects and depends on the three bounded successors. Decision 5 is settled for Peanuts and WildBrain, and the question itself was partly malformed.\n\nNo licensor values are reproduced here (public repo — `AGENTS.md` §6.14, owner ruling §6.19). Structure only.\n\n### Correction to this issue's premise, from the owner\n\n> \"ai or our software doesn't yet download the actual art files in the style guide yet. We're only collecting metadata.\"\n\nThis issue and the `licensor-incremental-capture` skill describe capturing \"assets\". **We capture asset *metadata*. No art binary is downloaded or stored.** Every lifecycle column requested here therefore tracks the lifecycle of a *metadata record*, not of a file. That changes what `change_signal` can honestly mean: it compares portal-published metadata, and it can never detect art replaced in place under an unchanged file name with unchanged published metadata. The issue's stated motivation — \"licensors … replace art in place under the same file name\" — is **not** fully solved by this work, and no successor should claim that it is.\n\n### Peanuts — `plm.peanuts_art_program` is the property-shaped entity\n\n> \"99% of the time we're designing product using 'what the art looks like'. retailer-specific style guides are exactly that: tied to only one specific retailer and only for a certain time period. we barely use those.\"\n\n`peanuts_art_program` (19 rows) is the durable entity and takes the lifecycle columns. `peanuts_initiative` (24 rows) is retailer- and period-bound by nature — it is a secondary tag, kept and searchable, but not the entity art belongs to. Correspondingly, `plm.peanuts_asset.initiative_key` is an attribute, and the multi-valued `plm.peanuts_asset_art_program` join is the real membership.\n\nNote for the author: an initiative is *expected* to stop appearing once its retail window closes. That is normal retirement, not withdrawal, and a lifecycle design that marks them `withdrawn` will generate false alarms every season.\n\n### WildBrain — the question was wrong; both are entities, on different axes\n\n> \"those are 2 completely different things, not things that are mutually exclusive … There are 'Classic' Style Guides, '2003' Style Guides, 'Berry in the Big City' Style Guides, etc.\"\n\n`wildbrain_era` and `wildbrain_creative_group` are **orthogonal, not alternatives**. Era is which version of the property; creative group is what kind of document. Every guide has one of each. The earlier framing on this issue — \"`era` vs `creative_group`\" — presented them as competing candidates and forced a false choice; **that framing is withdrawn.**\n\nThis is confirmed by the live catalog: `plm.wildbrain_asset` carries **both** `era_source_id` **and** `creative_group_source_id`. The owner's model is already the shape of the data.\n\nConsequence: **both tables get the lifecycle columns.** Era is the property-shaped entity for anything that needs a single parent; creative group is a document-type dimension of equal standing, not a child of it.\n\nOpen sub-item for the author, not for the owner: `plm.wildbrain_guide` (65 rows) has **no** era or creative-group column and is derived (`derivation_method`, `rule_version`, `relationship_truth`). If a guide is genuinely identified by era + creative group as the owner describes, that relationship exists today only at the asset level and is inferred at the guide level. Resolve that before writing guide lifecycle SQL.\n\n### Sesame — struck from decision 5\n\nAll five Sesame vocabulary tables are empty (see previous comment). Its equivalent decision follows its first real load. Do not ask the owner about it before then.\n\n### Status\n\nDecision 5 is **closed** for Peanuts and WildBrain. Decisions 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 remain open and are engineering decisions, not owner decisions — decision 1 (snapshot identity) is upstream of implementing this ruling. Scope stays `blocked` on those. `needs-albert` removed: nothing further is owed by the owner on this issue.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-07T14:55:10Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1275#issuecomment-5572426306","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABTEu8-g","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"Work contract published at `refs/db-contracts/1275/1` (sha256 `15c4eae0214daae9ffeff14f9579e6fada6193af1b98fe7885a71d8adf503a9a`).\n\nThis comment is a human-readable COPY. Exact successor object claims must be enumerated before authoring.\n\nTwo verified constraints change the design:\n- DCP metadata `complete` is not zero-failure coverage: `dcp_metadata_run_complete_chk` accepts `fetches_succeeded + fetches_failed = assets_expected`. Absence-based withdrawal additionally needs zero failed fetches and comparable, exhaustive membership evidence; a completed crawl is insufficient. [Existing constraint](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/blob/aef1504e7c3c7674a6a9709e42720b8f2a725f43/supabase/migrations/20260811050000_dcp_vault_metadata_landing.sql#L395-L406).\n- Current owner-rulings section 6.20 corrects the older comment: WildBrain era is mandatory, creative group optional. Both are lifecycle entities, but guides are inferred records; do not invent a mandatory era/group pair or promote inferred membership to source assertion. Peanuts art programs remain the property-shaped entity; initiatives remain searchable secondary tags, without seasonal withdrawal alarms. [Current ruling](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/blob/aef1504e7c3c7674a6a9709e42720b8f2a725f43/docs/owner-rulings.md#L1953-L2015), [WildBrain identity contract](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/blob/aef1504e7c3c7674a6a9709e42720b8f2a725f43/supabase/migrations/20260819014639_wildbrain_dam_source_landing.sql#L46-L80).\n\nProposed five bounded authoring successors:\n1. DCP metadata-run baseline and property/character lifecycle: independent metadata clock, zero-failure comparable coverage, preserved first-seen history.\n2. Warner capture baseline: reference the existing logical header (`chunk_number = 0`), same target and completed status; preserve chunk integrity and loader gates. [Header contract](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/blob/aef1504e7c3c7674a6a9709e42720b8f2a725f43/supabase/migrations/20260810130000_wb_chunked_capture_protocol.sql#L113-L172).\n3. NBCU durable state: preserve snapshots; qualify existing fallback keys and account/scope identity before defining cross-run uniqueness.\n4. Peanuts durable state: preserve source object IDs and vocabulary keys; distinguish art-program membership from initiative tags.\n5. WildBrain durable state: retain source IDs, inferred-guide derivation versions and optional creative-group evidence; no name-based character merging.\n\nAcross these successors, preserve relationship observations; publish current relationships only from qualified comparable evidence and active endpoints. Incremental omission alone cannot mean withdrawal. Remaining engineering proofs are stable identity, exact authenticated coverage boundaries, derivation compatibility, and concurrent publication locking. Tests must cover partial/authentication failure, incompatible scope, invalid baseline, reappearance, unchanged metadata, threshold boundaries, concurrent finalization, and unchanged access restrictions.\n\nThis issue's original body describes the capture-side shrink gate as 2% of baseline or 100 rows, whichever is smaller, but asks only for a *similar* database guard. Applying that exact threshold database-side is a proposal here, not a settled implemented rule; its denominator and boundary semantics must be explicit in the successor contract. {"assignees":[],"body":"## Current decision  Move the complete DesignFlow production `designflow` schema from Google Cloud SQL to the shared production Supabase project. This remains wanted. The timed preview rehearsal in #771 is complete, but the cutover must not be scheduled until the production-only measurements and authorizations named in the latest issue update are resolved.  This issue is the umbrella migration decision. #771 remains separate because it is the executable rehearsal and evidence gate.  ## Current architecture that this move must preserve  The destination is not a copy of the old authority model:  - Supabase `core.*` is the official shared licensing catalogue. - ColdLion owns official Licensor names. - Authorized licensor scrapes own Property names, Property ownership, Characters, Style Guides, Franchises, Asset metadata, and direct relationships inside their scrape coverage. - For a ColdLion-only Property under a Licensor with no authorized scrape data, ColdLion's Property name and owning Licensor are canonical truth. - ColdLion also owns Property Active/Inactive. - DesignFlow's old licensing import has no authority. - ColdLion API feeds land directly in the dedicated `coldlion.*` raw landing layer described in the current landing plan. The generic `ingest.raw_record` bucket is being retired for those feeds.  Controlling references:  - `docs/business-rules/licensing-master-data.md` - `docs/core-master-data-consolidation-aim.md` - `plan_licensing_master_data_implementation.md` - `docs/plan_coldlion-landing-phases-2-6.md` - Licensing implementation tracker #1090 - ColdLion landing tracker #1184  The full DesignFlow migration and the licensing/ColdLion programs are related but independent. Do not delay the official Supabase licensing catalogue or ColdLion landing layer until the Cloud SQL cutover. Do not use this migration to restore DesignFlow licensing authority.  ## Current measured migration facts\n\nRefreshed 2026-09-04 by completed #771:\n\n- Cloud SQL `designflow`: 103 tables, 186 indexes, 173 constraints, 17 sequences, 579,469,312 relation bytes, 963,810 estimated rows.\n- Preview `dflow`: 124 tables, 271 indexes, 419 constraints, 18 sequences, 572,719,104 relation bytes, 1,135,231 estimated rows.\n- Representative preview work: 1,006,439 rows, 97/97 main steps plus 10/10 sequence plans successful in 42.146 seconds; 537,387,008 scratch bytes.\n- This excludes production network export/restore, freeze delta, repoint/restart, and smoke-test time. A total downtime window remains unknown.\n## Required correction retained from the original analysis  The `AuditLog` high-water mark must use `id`, never `actionDate`. The earlier measurement found 32,823 rows whose `actionDate` moved backwards relative to `id`. A timestamp cutoff could silently miss rows.  ## Current cutover shape, subject to #771  1. Refresh the Cloud SQL and Supabase catalog, sizes, row counts, indexes, constraints, sequences, and application dependencies. 2. Reconcile current schema differences in the correct direction. 3. Pre-stage full `AuditLog` history while Cloud SQL remains live. 4. Pre-stage the remaining tables into an isolated staging area, never over live data. 5. In one measured window: freeze writes, copy the `AuditLog` tail by `id`, apply the remaining delta, repair sequences, validate, repoint, restart, and smoke-test. 6. Leave Cloud SQL read-only as the recoverable fallback until the Supabase result is proven. 7. Keep licensing and ColdLion authority enforcement in place throughout. A raw database copy must not reactivate retired DesignFlow writers.  Logical replication remains rejected unless new rehearsal evidence changes the tradeoff. It requires production Cloud SQL changes, does not copy sequences or schema changes, and previously offered little benefit for this database size.  ## Gate  Do not quote a downtime window or schedule a cutover until the exact production aggregate check and copy/export rehearsal are separately authorized and measured. #771 proves only the in-preview portion.  \n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 200\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - schema dflow\n```\n ","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABPmqBZA","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"**OWNER CONFIRMATION (Albert Hazan, in chat, 2026-08-19): still wanted.**\n\nReviewed during a triage pass over the open queue and explicitly kept, described to him as \"the largest item on the list\". He was told when confirming that the timed rehearsal (#771) was never run, so **every downtime figure in the plan is currently invented**, and he kept it anyway.\n\nOrder of work is unchanged: **run the timed cutover rehearsal (#771) before anyone quotes a window to a business user.** The measured plan (#770) and its id-versus-actionDate correction still stand.","createdAt":"2026-08-19T12:31:41Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/770#issuecomment-5342134628","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABP34n-w","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## Read-only reassessment 2026-08-20 (orchestrator marker #1338) — three findings that change the plan's ordering\n\n### 1. #1315 must finish BEFORE the #771 rehearsal, not after\n\n**The biggest risk in this migration is not the copy — it is the id collision.** Production Cloud SQL and Supabase `dflow` have been issuing overlapping primary keys into same-shaped tables for months. That has already re-issued live production ids twice (2026-07-29), which is what #1312/#1313 fixed for `art_piece` alone.\n\nEvery other `dflow.*_id_seq` is still unaudited (#1315, open). **If production rows are copied on top of Supabase rows whose sequences overlap, records collide silently and the damage surfaces weeks later in the wrong place.** A rehearsal run before that audit rehearses the wrong thing.\n\nRecommend: #1315 becomes a hard prerequisite of #771.\n\n### 2. The connection ceiling is tight and nobody has sized it\n\nMeasured on production Supabase `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` (target proved before reading): **`max_connections` = 90, with 34 already in use** before any production DesignFlow traffic arrives. Cloud SQL production allows **500**.\n\nFour production services, each scaling to ten Cloud Run instances, each with a Sequelize pool. The pooler absorbs some of this, but the compute tier and pooler limits have to be chosen deliberately rather than discovered during cutover.\n\n### 3. One cheap pre-check has never been run, and it can abort the copy partway\n\nSupabase `dflow` enforces unique `(item, role)` on `productUserAssignment`; Cloud SQL `designflow` does not. **If production holds duplicate pairs, the data copy fails mid-flight.** This is a single query against Cloud SQL production and it has never been run. Do it before scheduling anything.\n\n### Also worth recording\n\n- **Cutover requires a CODE change, not just configuration.** `designflow-backend/config/database-connection-contract.js` hard-fails any production service whose `DB_PROVIDER` is not `cloud-sql` on port 5432. That guard must be flipped in the same event, across six repos plus every prod trigger's substitutions.\n- **All non-production DesignFlow environments already write into the PRODUCTION Supabase project.** `DB_USER_DEV`, `DB_USER_STAGING` and `DB_USER_SANDBOX` are byte-identical (same MD5) and all resolve to `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`. It works today, but after cutover a bad sandbox run shares a database with live production data. That is a decision to take deliberately, not to inherit.\n- **The `AuditLog` is ~400 MB of the 542 MB** — three-quarters of the migration's weight is audit history, and nobody has decided whether it is copied, archived or moved separately. Documented trap: any delta cutoff must key on `id`, never `actionDate` (32,823 rows run backwards).\n- **Two planning documents are wrong and should not be followed:** `docs/cloudsql-first-migration-candidate-20260803.md` and `docs/age-group-cloudsql-migration-plan-20260804.md` both rest on `art_piece.age_group_id` having no enforced link. The 2026-08-10 capture proved it has a real foreign key — pointing at `merchGroup`, not `age_group`.\n- **\"R5\", cited across several documents as an owner ruling, could not be found to exist.** `docs/owner-ruling-r5-core-is-source-of-truth.md` is explicitly marked as reconstructed from citations; the original appears in no file, commit or issue. Anything resting on R5 rests on nothing verified.\n\n### Scope, honestly\n\nSchemas match to within **three objects** (one unique constraint, two indexes) excluding the deliberately-absent Sample Tracking feature (#707). No triggers, no stored business logic, no RLS to port (verified: 0 of 113 `dflow` tables have RLS, and none is needed for a trusted-backend design). Business data excluding audit log is ~140 MB. Twelve of sixteen deployed services already run on Supabase.\n\n**This is a data copy, a config change and a code guard flip — not a rewrite.** The remaining work is real but contained; the ordering above is what makes it safe.","createdAt":"2026-08-20T18:41:45Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/770#issuecomment-5360199675","viewerDidAuthor":true},{"id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABSrD3zw","author":{"login":"u2giants"},"authorAssociation":"MEMBER","body":"## #771 measurement gate completed — #770 current plan\n\n#771 is closed with merged tooling, exact target proof, timed preview evidence, and teardown proof. Current baselines are now Cloud SQL `designflow` 103 tables / 579,469,312 relation bytes / 963,810 estimated rows, and preview `dflow` 124 tables / 572,719,104 relation bytes / 1,135,231 estimated rows.\n\nThe representative in-destination rehearsal copied 1,006,439 rows, rebuilt indexes and constraints, validated foreign keys, validated data, analyzed the copies, and prepared 10 sequence repairs in 42.146 seconds. Scratch storage peaked at 537,387,008 bytes. All 97 main steps and all 10 sequence plans succeeded. `productUserAssignment (item, role)` was unique across the five preview rows. The scratch schemas are gone and the preview leases are released.\n\nMeasured phase totals: heap load 11.218 s; indexes 0.392 s; key constraints 1.199 s; FK add/validate 0.088 s; bounded full hashes 21.788 s; `AuditLog` count + `id` bounds + tail hash 1.397 s; analyze 5.484 s; sequence preparation 0.038 s. Use the full hashes for bounded transactional tables and the cheaper `AuditLog` gate. The `AuditLog` delta cutoff remains `id`, never `actionDate`.\n\n### Updated execution order\n\n1. Obtain the two exact owner authorizations below and measure the missing production terms.\n2. Reconcile current source/destination schema differences without restoring retired DesignFlow licensing authority.\n3. Pre-stage full `AuditLog` history, then other tables, in an isolated destination staging area.\n4. In the measured freeze: copy the `AuditLog` tail by `id`, apply remaining deltas, repair sequences, run bounded hashes plus the `AuditLog` gate, repoint/restart, and complete authenticated smoke tests.\n5. {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","is_bot":false,"login":"u2giants","name":""},"body":"Closes #3566\nWork issue #3566\n\nStep 8 follow-up of #2530 (non-orchestrator work: no database structure change).\n\n`configure-merge-queue.mjs --apply` activated ruleset 24024180 but exited 1 because its read-back compared queue parameters with `JSON.stringify`, and GitHub returns the same values in its own key order. `queueRulesetMatches` (which `queueMode()` uses in the guarded lane) had the same defect, so the lane would have treated the live approved queue as foreign. Both now use `queueParametersEqual`: the same key set, and every value strictly equal. Tests reproduce GitHub's order and still refuse any changed, extra, absent or retyped parameter.\n\nAdds `docs/verification/merge-queue-activation-*.json`: ruleset 24024180 read-back, main protection (16 contexts, strict false, enforce_admins true), and rollback `node scripts/configure-merge-queue.mjs --rollback --apply`.\n\nThis is the first real PR through the merge queue.\n\nPosted by Claude chat f059b471-9513-4c04-a25e-3ffaf099a129 on edge-dev3\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n<!-- codesmith:footer -->\n---\n<a href=\"https://app.blacksmith.sh/popcre/codesmith/shared-db/pr/3567?autoLogin=true&ref=codesmith_pr_footer\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-light-v2.svg\"><img alt=\"View with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"></picture></a> <a href=\"https://backend.blacksmith.sh/track/enable-autofix?expires=1792970277&installation_model_id=436274&pr_number=3567&ref=codesmith_pr_footer&repository=popcre%2Fshared-db&return_to=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fpopcre%2Fshared-db%2Fpull%2F3567&signature=b17a03034283461cc29c636c7c02de15f8350ca6a8e88ec04a866ae8437339e6\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-light.svg\"><img alt=\"Autofix with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"></picture></a>\n<sup>Need help on this PR? {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","is_bot":false,"login":"u2giants","name":""},"body":"## Summary\n- Owner ruling 2026-09-25 (Albert Hazan): curated Master Data loads do not need an orchestrator.\n- \\curated-master-data\\ now exits by \\data-session\\. A dedicated curated-data session owns the work end to end under §6.4.\n- Curation protections are unchanged (matched-row abstention; rules bind the session doing the typing). Only the orchestrator in the middle is removed.\n- Queue audit lists these under OUTSIDE ORCHESTRATOR — OWNED BY A DEDICATED SESSION (audit visibility only).\n\nCloses #3563\n\n## Verification\n- \\\node --test scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs\\ — 714 pass, 0 fail.\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on EDGE-DEV\n\n<!-- codesmith:footer -->\n---\n<a href=\"https://app.blacksmith.sh/popcre/codesmith/shared-db/pr/3564?autoLogin=true&ref=codesmith_pr_footer\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-light-v2.svg\"><img alt=\"View with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"></picture></a> <a href=\"https://backend.blacksmith.sh/track/enable-autofix?expires=1792965222&installation_model_id=436274&pr_number=3564&ref=codesmith_pr_footer&repository=popcre%2Fshared-db&return_to=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fpopcre%2Fshared-db%2Fpull%2F3564&signature=0f449aff53f72ff3da12916c6fc72fb7cd592a215ee179188c7bff001cb272cb\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-light.svg\"><img alt=\"Autofix with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"></picture></a>\n<sup>Need help on this PR? {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","is_bot":false,"login":"u2giants","name":""},"body":"## What\n\nIssue #2998's remaining acceptance (the 2026-09-20 audit comment), implemented as **one side-effect-free readiness result** — `assertReviewerDrawHandoff` — that runs before any cursor, assignment or replacement mutation on **both** draw paths (`--assign-reviewer` and `--replace-failed-reviewer`):\n\n1. **The carried brief is validated before the draw** (fix 1, sanctioned carry): both draw paths now accept `--prompt` / `--prompt-file`. A brief that is unreadable, empty, or binds a decision line to a different head refuses by name before anything is consumed. Brief arguments stay optional — `refresh-code-pr-branch` re-draws with no brief and the codex wrapper takes no prompt by design (#2244) — so the runner's pre-start prompt guard remains the backstop, unchanged.\n2. **The evidence pair is validated before the draw** (fix 3): `partial` / `conflicted` classifications refuse; a `current` pair is judged exactly like the CI gate judges it — schema, `reconcileReportWithContract`, the pull-request binding, and hash-equality with the immutable `refs/db-contracts/*` publication. `inherited` proceeds (the enforced CI gate remains the authority on whether a pair is required).\n3. **Current-with-main readiness** (fix 3): a definite `mergeable_state=behind` refuses on open pull requests; unknown/absent proceeds (GitHub computes it asynchronously), and merged-pull-request draws (#2915) are untouched.\n4. **Cross-PR collision before the draw** (fix 3): the repository's own protected-source guard and object-collision guard are reused, gathered only when this pull request edits a protected source or adds a migration — zero extra API calls otherwise.\n\nEvery transport failure proceeds, exactly as `assertReviewerDrawReadiness` always has: a transport fault never becomes a reviewer refusal, a refusal never contains an approval, and nothing here writes anything.\n\n## Why\n\nEach of these pre-conditions used to be checked only after the expensive step: the draft PR that burned two draws, the brief that was unrecordable, the merge that was declined for a collision discovered at merge time. The checks were always cheap; discovering the failure late was not.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `node --test scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs scripts/reviewer-wire-budget.test.mjs scripts/check-pr-source-collisions.test.mjs scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.test.mjs` — **770 pass / 0 fail** (15 new regressions: each refusal test drives the real CLI with a tripwire io proving the draw was never reached; a valid positive case and replacement equivalents included)\n- `node scripts/check-github-transport-conformance.mjs` — 318 files, all GitHub calls through the shared transport\n- `git diff --check` — clean\n- Mutation-verified: removing the prompt guard wiring fails the prompt CLI test; removing the behind refusal fails the current-main test; both restored and re-verified green\n- The wire-budget proof (#3187/#3206, ≤10 API requests per assignment) still passes unchanged: the readiness result reuses the two reads the guards always made, and both collision gathers skip their snapshot unless applicable\n\nContract: `refs/db-contracts/2998/7` (published before implementation).\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on edge-dev\n\n<!-- codesmith:footer -->\n---\n<a href=\"https://app.blacksmith.sh/popcre/codesmith/shared-db/pr/3528?autoLogin=true&ref=codesmith_pr_footer\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-light-v2.svg\"><img alt=\"View with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"></picture></a> <a href=\"https://backend.blacksmith.sh/track/enable-autofix?expires=1792925014&installation_model_id=436274&pr_number=3528&ref=codesmith_pr_footer&repository=popcre%2Fshared-db&return_to=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fpopcre%2Fshared-db%2Fpull%2F3528&signature=e693baf2a37f8c3ebb6781307d0bb86daeb86a21b59547443fae5c03c6009062\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-light.svg\"><img alt=\"Autofix with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"></picture></a>\n<sup>Need help on this PR? {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","is_bot":false,"login":"u2giants","name":""},"body":"## Summary\n- A \\silent_worker_observed\\ failure released with immutable evidence is a WORKER silence, not a provider judgment: the provider never produced a review or a verdict. The permanent \\\failedNames\\ exclusion deadlocks slot 1 once every other name has failed on the same head (PR #3309: 4 of 5 failed, the fifth holds the other slot). A matching \\\reviewer-failure-release\\ record with \\code=silent_worker_observed\\ now restores that name to the replacement draw.\n- Same-reviewer re-draw lands on ONE lease ref (same reviewer, head, slot): the replacement readback now expects the replacement lease at that ref instead of emptiness.\n- Fail-closed preserved: every other terminal failure code, and any \\\failure-ref=self\\ evidence, stays permanently excluded. Exact-head approval untouched -- the replacement still records its own fresh verdict and the two-reviewer rule stands.\n\n## Tests\n- 716/716 \\scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs\\ (2 new: re-draw when pool exhausted; non-silence release still refuses)\n- 23/23 \\scripts/orchestrator-flow/reviewer-start-watch.test.mjs\\\n- 4/4 \\scripts/reviewer-wire-budget.test.mjs\\\n- \\\node scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs\\ OK\n\n## Refs\nCloses #3527. Follow-up to #3492 (fixed the release path; this unblocks the capacity wall it exposed). {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","is_bot":false,"login":"u2giants","name":""},"body":"Closes #3349\n\n## The defect\n\n`findBusyReviewers` in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` fails open with a bare `return null` in seven places. Every caller then reports the same generic sentence:\n\n```\nactive reviewer leases are unreadable; <operation> refused\n```\n\nAn HTTP 5xx, a secondary rate limit, an occupied mutex, and a genuinely malformed lease ref are all indistinguishable at the caller. The issue title says it: the real cause is hidden.\n\n## The fix\n\nReplace every bare `return null` in `findBusyReviewers` with a cause-carrying `LaneError` throw:\n\n- **Transient failures** (HTTP 5xx, rate limit, transport errors) say `Retry the operation.`\n- **Determinate failures** (malformed lease, missing `readRef`) say `Retire abandoned leases with --reap-abandoned-review-leases --apply-recovery.`\n- Each error names **which read** (cutover, snapshot, per-ref, commit parse, review states, PR read, verdict read), **which ref**, and the **transport error**.\n\nFail-closed behaviour is unchanged: every operation that previously refused still refuses. Only the wording changes -- the cause is now visible.\n\n## Design\n\nFollows the existing `markReviewRefListingRefusal` / `isReviewRefListingRefusal` pattern:\n- `markLeaseReadFailure(error, detail)` / `isLeaseReadFailure(error)` -- exported for callers that need to detect the cause\n- `leaseReadFailureError(detail)` -- builds the message with kind (transient/determinate), read name, ref, and cause\n\nThe structural mismatch (lease ref not matching a recognized reviewer) is classified determinate. The `parseReviewLease` malformed error is classified determinate; transport errors from `getCommit` remain transient.\n\n## Tests\n\n- **Regression test `#3349`** asserts cause, ref, and retry/retire guidance for cutover read, per-ref read, and malformed lease parse failures.\n- **6 existing tests updated** to match the new message format (they asserted the old generic \"unreadable; nothing was reaped\" pattern or bare null returns).\n- **715/715 pass** on `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`.\n- **88/88 pass** on `scripts/orchestrator-flow/legacy-relation-alias.test.mjs` + `admission-outcome.test.mjs`.\n- **7/7 pass** on `scripts/queue-hygiene-report.test.mjs`.\n\n## Scope\n\n- Non-orchestrator (repo-maintenance tooling).\n- No database structure. No production. No secrets.\n- Files touched: `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`.\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on edge-dev\n\n<!-- codesmith:footer -->\n---\n<a href=\"https://app.blacksmith.sh/popcre/codesmith/shared-db/pr/3525?autoLogin=true&ref=codesmith_pr_footer\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-light-v2.svg\"><img alt=\"View with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"></picture></a> <a href=\"https://backend.blacksmith.sh/track/enable-autofix?expires=1792922366&installation_model_id=436274&pr_number=3525&ref=codesmith_pr_footer&repository=popcre%2Fshared-db&return_to=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fpopcre%2Fshared-db%2Fpull%2F3525&signature=d199f37e6765cc4da290a7a1a395197d46d71170a59198d19049d776d51fea88\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-light.svg\"><img alt=\"Autofix with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"></picture></a>\n<sup>Need help on this PR? {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","is_bot":false,"login":"u2giants","name":""},"body":"## Summary\n\nResolves #3398 (non-orchestrator). Adds a pure, offline accounting layer for the **cluster-global role axis** so structural issue #3298 can declare its dedicated NOLOGIN worker role (`role pm_jev_triage_worker`) honestly, instead of hiding roles under a fake schema claim.\n\nNew `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs` (with 25 focused adversarial/regression tests):\n\n- **Exact global role identity**, preserving quoted-identifier case. Unquoted names fold to lowercase; schema-qualified names are refused (roles are cluster-global, so a broad `schema` claim is never a reservation on a role).\n- **CREATE / ALTER / DROP ROLE** (plus the `USER`/`GROUP` spellings of the same command), **rename** targets, and **membership GRANT/REVOKE**. Same role conflicts across spellings; distinct roles stay independent. No name aliases, no count caps, no synthetic evidence.\n- **Ownership role dependencies** (`ALTER FUNCTION/TABLE … OWNER TO role`) are recorded as couplings and are **never** converted into an exclusive write on the role.\n- Reuses the collision parser's **literal DO / dynamic-SQL** rules and **fails closed** on dynamic role mutations hidden in `EXECUTE`/`format` strings, rather than skipping them.\n\nTests are wired into `tools-offline-tests.yml` so the role axis is guarded in CI (explicit named step — the repo's stated anti-pattern is tests that never run).\n\n## Scope note (issue #3398 file ownership)\n\nThe collision parser (`check-pr-object-collisions.mjs`) and the claim validator (`manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`) are **deliberately not edited here** — the issue holds them for confirmed owner clearance / active-owner release. This PR delivers the tested helper those two call sites will import to accept `role <name>` claims and emit `role <name>` collision keys. No database, role, migration, infrastructure, or secret is touched.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `node --test scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.test.mjs` → **25 pass, 0 fail**.\n- Covers: quoted-case identity, claim normalization, create/alter/drop, rename dual identity (not aliased), membership vs privilege-grant separation, same-role conflict / distinct-role independence, ownership-not-a-write, literal DO extraction, dynamic-mutation fail-closed, no synthetic evidence / no caps, and the real four-NOLOGIN-role shape from migration 20260911210709.\n- `.github/workflows/tools-offline-tests.yml` YAML validated.\n\nCloses #3398\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on edge-dev\n\n<!-- codesmith:footer -->\n---\n<a {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","is_bot":false,"login":"u2giants","name":""},"body":"Closes #2457\n\n## What this fixes\n\nIssue #2457 asks two things of a reviewer draw whose mutex-release proof fails: prove the release with a fresh bounded read before refusing, and **never let a completed operation lose its result**.\n\nThe first half landed on `main` through PR #3316, absorbed by #3354 (commit 905ec8e2): `finalizeReviewMutex` now re-reads on the bounded ladder `0/500/1000/2000/3000/4000 ms` and confirms an apparently-unreleased mutex once against GitHub's ref API before refusing, and `assignNextReviewerOperation` carries its completed draw on the refusal.\n\n**The second half was only half done.** `--replace-failed-reviewer` — the path the issue says reproduced this **twice on PR #2409** — draws its reviewer and writes the durable replacement record, then runs the *plain* `finalizeReviewMutex` in its `finally`. When the release still cannot be proved, that `finally` throws, the returned replacement is discarded, and the operator sees a bare `RECOVERY REQUIRED … do not retry blindly` for a mutex the atomic deletion already removed. That is precisely the instruction the issue calls \"the actual risk this message creates\": it sends an operator to a guarded recovery against healthy state, and a blind retry would draw a **second** reviewer on a PR that already has one.\n\n## The change\n\n`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` — `replaceFailedReviewerOperation` now captures its result in a `completedResult` local (all three return sites: fresh draw, atomic branch, non-atomic branch) and finalizes with the existing `finalizeReviewMutexPreservingResult` helper instead of `finalizeReviewMutex`. Nothing else changes:\n\n- the refusal itself is untouched — an orphaned mutex is never assumed released;\n- the readback ladder, the ref-API confirmation, the bounded release-proof allowance and `REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT` are all untouched (no derived ceiling is widened);\n- the helper only decorates when a result actually exists, so a failure *before* completion still throws exactly as it did.\n\n## Regression test\n\n`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` — `#2457 a refused mutex release still reports the completed replacement instead of losing it`. The compare-and-swap deletion really removes the ref; every subsequent read (replica ladder *and* ref-API confirmation) keeps answering with the owner that was just deleted. The test asserts the refusal carries `THE OPERATION ITSELF COMPLETED`, the drawn reviewer, `replacementSha`, and `error.completedResult`, and that the mutex ref is genuinely absent — i.e. retrying would indeed double-draw.\n\n**Non-vacuous, verified both ways**: with the source change stashed the suite reports `pass 713 / fail 1` with the new test failing at `finalizeReviewMutex` from `replaceFailedReviewerOperation`; with the fix it reports `pass 714 / fail 0`.\n\n## Validation (offline)\n\n- `node --test scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` — **715 passed, 0 failed** on `origin/main` 85566ccb3.\n- `node --test scripts/queue-hygiene-report.test.mjs scripts/reviewer-wire-budget.test.mjs scripts/lib/pr-content-equivalence.test.mjs scripts/check-dispatch-collision.test.mjs scripts/check-pr-source-collisions.test.mjs scripts/coordination-scenarios.test.mjs scripts/agent-work-contract.test.mjs scripts/record-review-verdict.test.mjs scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs` — **286 passed, 0 failed**.\n- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD` — clean.\n- No database, migration, production, infrastructure or secret change of any kind.\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on edge-dev\n\n<!-- codesmith:footer -->\n---\n<a {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","is_bot":false,"login":"u2giants","name":""},"body":"Closes #3427 (non-orchestrator, reviewer-tooling).\n\n## What changed\n\n**Symmetric peer-slot discovery.** otherSlotReviewers now discovers every peer slot for the requesting draw, not only slot 2 when filling slot 1. A slot-3 draw sees both slot 1 and slot 2; a slot-1 draw sees every higher slot. This closes the #3429 review advisory that a hypothetical slot-3 draw could duplicate slot 2's provider. Slot 2 keeps its zero-wire fast path (the production two-slot maximum), so the 25-request budget is unchanged.\n\n**Head-SHA normalization.** The request boundary now lowercases the head SHA so ref names and peer resolvers agree regardless of input case. \resolveSlotOneAssignment normalizes its comparison too. This closes the #3429 review advisory on asymmetric case handling.\n\n**Adversarial tests.** Three new tests cover slot-3 distinctness, slot-1 replacement after three slots (recovery preserves all peer verdicts), and head-SHA case normalization. The existing #3427 collision-recovery test and all production safety gates (25-request budget, two-reviewer rule) are unchanged and passing.\n\n## Verification\n\n- 807 tests pass: 713 manage-migration-author-lanes + 91 check-exact-head-approval (including 4 #3427 tests)\n- Truth audit OK (call_sites=316 sources=72)\n- \\git diff --check\\ clean\n- No database structure, no production command, no secrets\n\n## Scope\n\nRepository maintenance only. Code paths: \\scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs\\, \\scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs\\, truth-audit disposition catalogue.\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on edge-dev\n\n<!-- codesmith:footer -->\n---\n<a href=\"https://app.blacksmith.sh/popcre/codesmith/shared-db/pr/3521?autoLogin=true&ref=codesmith_pr_footer\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-light-v2.svg\"><img alt=\"View with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"></picture></a> <a href=\"https://backend.blacksmith.sh/track/enable-autofix?expires=1792916829&installation_model_id=436274&pr_number=3521&ref=codesmith_pr_footer&repository=popcre%2Fshared-db&return_to=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fpopcre%2Fshared-db%2Fpull%2F3521&signature=07d5bf2d3ff4f2ed7311030c99db284dace01ff14f12f1a4c412a460c2af625d\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-light.svg\"><img alt=\"Autofix with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"></picture></a>\n<sup>Need help on this PR? by `semantic_key`), so CI stayed green — but any refusal it printed named the wrong line, which is the exact stale-diagnostic symptom #3493 reported at `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2367`.\n\n## What changed\n\n| Catalogue | `site` values re-pointed |\n|---|---|\n| `scripts~manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs.json` | 31 |\n\nOnly the `site` key is touched. `semantic_key`, `line_sha256`, `disposition`, `reason` and `legacy_semantic_key` are byte-identical.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `node scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` → entries** (was 31)\n- Detector and its tests are untouched — the audit stays fail-closed\n- Independent exact-head review: APPROVE at `8fa04ca76303533350d9ec7f34c98c29c96f9217`, no findings\n\nCloses #3493\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","is_bot":false,"login":"u2giants","name":""},"body":"## Summary\n\nAdds scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.mjs: turns a check-migration-ledger-drift --json result into an issue-comment-ready status report with per-version introducing commits and clearly labeled merge/squash references from git first-parent history.\n\nThe migration-ledger drift check reports WHAT is drift but not WHERE each pending version came from or WHO owns its promotion. Alarm issues like #2508 accumulate hand-written status comments that go stale, and every successor session re-researches the same git history.\n\n**Read-only.** No database write, no workflow dispatch, no production touch.\n\n## Verification\n\n- 26 reporter tests pass, including producer-shaped input, refusal paths, attribution, and exit status.\n- 35 existing drift-check tests and 16 truth-audit tests pass.\n- The historical six-version snapshot is labeled as unverified commit references; current status must come from a fresh drift check.\n\n## Issue #2508\n\nThis PR adds the detection/reporting tooling the issue needs. The underlying ledger drift (six merged-but-not-applied versions) still requires production applies through the bounded Shared Supabase Migrations workflow — that is the orchestrator's production lane. The issue remains open until a read-only production ledger check proves the drift cleared after the orchestrator production lane acts.\n\nCloses #3587 (non-orchestrator reporter delivery). Supports #2508; does not close the production drift alarm.\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on edge-dev\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0e56d-14e5-76a2-a7d3-63f2d9b90b1d on edge-dev3\n\n\nPosted by Codex {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","is_bot":false,"login":"u2giants","name":""},"body":"## What this is\n\nNon-orchestrator (changes no database object): reviewer tooling only.\n\nThe runtime fix for #2678 already landed on `main` (commits `c395ddad1`, `e955f07e4`, absorbed by PR #3354): the governed runner spawns the wrapper with `reviewCallerEnvironment(...)`, the author-lane `doctor` probe does the same, and an unnamed doctor failure quotes the wrapper's stderr line. What never landed is the end-to-end proof on the runner side — the doctor probe has three `issue 2678` tests, but nothing asserted that `runGovernedReview`'s own wrapper spawn receives `AI_*_CALLER`.\n\n## Change\n\nOne new test in `scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs` captures the spawn environment the runner builds and asserts all three behaviours:\n\n1. Detected caller (`CLAUDECODE=1`) reaches the spawn as `AI_GLM_CALLER=claude`.\n2. An explicitly exported caller is never overruled by detection.\n3. With no caller and no detectable engine the runner invents nothing, and `prepareGovernedReview` still refuses up front naming the exact variable (fail-closed unchanged).\n\nNo production code touched. No secrets printed — the test only reads variable names and the two literal values `claude`/`codex`.\n\n## Proof\n\n- Mutation check: removing `...callerEnv` from the spawn env makes the new test fail (`actual: undefined, expected: 'claude'`), then restore green.\n- `node --test scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` → 801 pass, 0 fail (offline, no secrets, no database).\n\nCloses #2678.\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on edge-dev\n\n<!-- codesmith:footer -->\n---\n<a href=\"https://app.blacksmith.sh/popcre/codesmith/shared-db/pr/3516?autoLogin=true&ref=codesmith_pr_footer\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-light-v2.svg\"><img alt=\"View with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"></picture></a> <a href=\"https://backend.blacksmith.sh/track/enable-autofix?expires=1792913671&installation_model_id=436274&pr_number=3516&ref=codesmith_pr_footer&repository=popcre%2Fshared-db&return_to=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fpopcre%2Fshared-db%2Fpull%2F3516&signature=622239290d3e8a5f34e0f60428cdb5d30d01b9e141a5691c9b853ac67447012d\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-light.svg\"><img alt=\"Autofix with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"></picture></a>\n<sup>Need help on this PR? {"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","is_bot":false,"login":"u2giants","name":""},"body":"Harden the recovered ColdLion detail replay proof (issue #2863, recovered under #3302) with offline synthetic tests that fail loudly on an inauthentic or incomplete proof.\n\n## What this adds\n\nStructural assertions for every component of the #2863 live assertion:\n- idempotent replay (inserts/updates are zero on the replay run)\n- no duplicate collapse (empty change_log on every replay)\n- stable row counts (prior run counts match the replay)\n- lands and re-lands (both endpoints require a prior succeeded run)\n- table counts equal run counts (no row collapsed or lost)\n- counts derived from loader evidence, never hardcoded totals\n- RLS and privilege posture\n\nOffline false controls:\n- dropping either endpoint witness breaks the conjunctive gate\n- a write statement is refused by the probe shape guard\n\n## What this does not change\n\nNo probe SQL change, no migration, no database write. The live artifact\n(shared-db-live-proof-2863-b055a414, run 35787289542) already returned\npassed=true on production; this only makes the offline suite prove the same\nassertion cannot be silently weakened.\n\nValidation: 22 offline tests passed, 0 failed.\n\nCloses #3302\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on edge-dev\n\n<!-- codesmith:footer -->\n---\n<a href=\"https://app.blacksmith.sh/popcre/codesmith/shared-db/pr/3515?autoLogin=true&ref=codesmith_pr_footer\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-light-v2.svg\"><img alt=\"View with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/view-with-codesmith-dark-v2.svg\"></picture></a> <a href=\"https://backend.blacksmith.sh/track/enable-autofix?expires=1792913151&installation_model_id=436274&pr_number=3515&ref=codesmith_pr_footer&repository=popcre%2Fshared-db&return_to=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fpopcre%2Fshared-db%2Fpull%2F3515&signature=60db979b36b62dfc741f2383cfab741adb1ade54ee20e48ad4524f7a9db37186\"><picture><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"><source media=\"(prefers-color-scheme: light)\" srcset=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-light.svg\"><img alt=\"Autofix with [code]smith\" src=\"https://pr-comments-assets.blacksmith.sh/codesmith/autofix-with-codesmith-dark.svg\"></picture></a>\n<sup>Need help on this PR?
