{"body":"## Corrected investigation result: no permission change required\n\nowner: Codex chat 01a0bf3f-77d5-7741-8b3c-463d6d3bef1c on 916-ALIEN; root orchestrator marker #3297 accepted this corrected disposition.\n\nThis is now NON-ORCHESTRATOR investigation/resolution work. The provisional defect below confused direct profile-table access with the deliberately broader authenticated audit projection. No invoker migration is warranted. The original report and signature remain below as historical evidence, not the current access requirement.\n\nPR #326, merged as 35e8dee6caee4e7fab362fd9d694b7cdacfd4fce, explicitly preserved authenticated audit attribution including staff email while revoking anonymous access. Its applied migration 20260729210000 states that invoker semantics would remove other actors' profile information, gutting the audit trail. The PR says: “Adopting security_invoker is reasonable future hardening, but it is a refactor needing app testing, not a security fix.” This is established implementation intent; no new owner ruling is invented here.\n\nCurrent read-only production catalog at qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai: authenticated has SELECT on the view; anonymous does not. The source audit policy allows authenticated reads USING(true). The existing definer LEFT JOIN intentionally provides actor labels/email. No reader exceeding that authenticated audience was demonstrated. Current PopDAM main c49ee360175fb84a3382802b0f327879423f44f2 has the signed-in ProtectedRoute around /styles, reads this view at StylesPage.tsx:523 and renders actor label at :2183. Invoker would preserve event IDs but replace other users' readable actor labels with UUIDs via the existing COALESCE fallback. That would regress attribution rather than transparently repair a demonstrated leak.\n\nProduction target and supabase_read_only_user identity were verified before catalog reads. All three relevant audit migrations (20260708183000,20260710135600,20260729210000) are applied. Ledger comparison found three unrelated actionable pending versions, not a globally clean ledger. No database write, role impersonation, new browser proof, migration, claim or generated-type change was performed. Historical PR326 authenticated audit probe had zero rows; it is not passed off as a populated cross-user fixture.\n\nReferences: https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/326 ; https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/blob/35e8dee6caee4e7fab362fd9d694b7cdacfd4fce/supabase/migrations/20260729210000_close_anon_read_leaks_in_public.sql ; https://github.com/u2giants/popdam3/blob/c49ee360175fb84a3382802b0f327879423f44f2/src/pages/StylesPage.tsx\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 5\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\n## Preserved provisional report (superseded by evidence above)\n\n## Bounded successor to #2662: audit-history profile boundary  owner: Codex orchestrator marker #3297 (chat 01a0bf00-fa7b-73d1-b447-fc4c89c50b96); structural routing and delivery owner.  Preserve every audit event ID, existing columns and signed-in audit-history access while making joined profile fields respect the existing own-user/administrator profile policy. Do not restrict Styles editing or turn audit history into administrator-only access.  ### Verified evidence (2026-09-20, read-only production catalog) `public.style_tracker_audit_log_with_user` is owned by postgres, default definer semantics, authenticated SELECT and schema USAGE. It selects `profile.email AS changed_by_email` and uses profile name/email in `changed_by_label` with no profile caller restriction. The source audit table explicitly permits authenticated SELECT USING(true); the source profiles table permits only `(user_id = auth.uid())` or `has_role(auth.uid(), 'admin')`. All source RLS is not forced. This is a specific discrepancy between joined profile visibility and its existing policy, not an inference that all definer views are wrong.  Current PopDAM main f3fb0c943af7f216b74507b50c242555f65226b1, `src/pages/StylesPage.tsx:523`, reads this view with SELECT *, filtered by style row/cell. Preserve that supported read path and event count. Original discovery/history remains on #2662. No other open exact-object security successor found in the 110-issue census.  ### Delivery contract - Use the existing profile own-user/admin rule; no new business role or blanket grant revocation. - Non-admin readers retain the same event IDs and own permitted profile details, but other users' joined name/email fields must not disclose protected profile data; fallback labels must not leak email. - Admin readers retain profile visibility already permitted by profiles RLS. - Preview tests include own actor, different actor, admin, anonymous, preserved event IDs, and unchanged Styles editing. - Verify production behavior from the application; catalog/merge alone is not completion.  ```historical-db-work-scope status: ready work_type: structural route: shared-db-orchestrator priority: 2 change_type: view service_class: standard-application application_return_to: u2giants/popdam3 live_assertion: Authenticated audit-history readers retain the same audit event IDs while joined profile fields reveal only their own profile or profiles permitted by the existing administrator policy; anonymous access remains denied and Styles editing is unchanged. generated_types: not-applicable depends_on: writes:   - view public.style_tracker_audit_log_with_user reads:   - table public.style_tracker_audit_log   - table public.profiles ```  Posted by Codex chat 01a0bf3f-77d5-7741-8b3c-463d6d3bef1c on 916-ALIEN \n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf3f-77d5-7741-8b3c-463d6d3bef1c on 916-ALIEN\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T07:06:51Z","createdAt":"2026-09-20T15:35:48Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3327,"title":"Resolve audit attribution access investigation — existing authenticated projection is intentional","updatedAt":"2026-09-25T07:06:51Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3327"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 40\n```\n\nowner: Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien (self-assigned)\n\nNon-orchestrator work: it changes no database structure.\n\n#2708 moved the agent evidence pair to `.agent/work/<work_issue>/<generation>/`.\n`verifyMergedPrIssueBinding` in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` (the\n`merged_pr_issue_binding` operator escape hatch) still reads the fixed legacy path:\n\n    try{completion=JSON.parse(io.getFileAt('.agent/completion.json',livePr.head.sha))}catch{...}\n\nSo an operator binding a merged pull request that carried the keyed pair refuses with\n\"`.agent/completion.json` at pull request #N head is unreadable\". That FAILS CLOSED — it\nrefuses rather than binding wrongly — which is why it did not block PR #3323, but it should\nresolve the pair the way every other gate now does.\n\n**Fix:** resolve the pair from the merged head's tree (`io.treeFiles(head)`) through\n`scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs`, falling back to the legacy path. One regression test:\na merged head carrying `.agent/work/<n>/<g>/completion.json` binds; a head carrying neither\nstill refuses.\n\n**Why it was not done in #3323:** the worktree that session was handed carried another\nsession's uncommitted issue #2678 work in that same file, and editing it would have entangled\ntwo sessions' changes. {"body":"The combined admission/advance CLI captures its command timestamp before admission publishes entered/classified. It then publishes dispatched with an earlier embedded timestamp, corrupting lifecycle order although the command executed correctly. Observed on2611: entered87f9510ee9bcd4e0, classifiedbbe4eea14114c759, dispatched716e9f6122866e84.\n\nowner: Codex prepack_proof_recovery chat01a0bf3e-3a02-7242-bd2c-07007f1994e9 on916-ALIEN\n\nFix transition timestamp selection after prerequisite publication and regress actual CLI behavior. {"body":"Running the author-lane test suite mutates the working tree. It is a test suite; it must not write source files.\n\n**Reproduce on a clean current `main` (`7d98876e`) worktree:**\n\n```\ngit status --short          # clean\nnode scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs\ngit status --short\n```\n\nObserved after the run:\n\n```\n M scripts/run-governed-review.mjs\n?? scripts/lib/reviewer-caller-env.mjs\n```\n\nThe edit extracts `REVIEW_CALLER_VARIABLES` and `reviewCallerEnvironment` out of `scripts/run-governed-review.mjs` into a new `scripts/lib/reviewer-caller-env.mjs` and re-exports them, carrying a comment citing issue #2678. That is a plausible and possibly desirable refactor — but it is being applied by a test run, not by a commit, so it lands in whatever lane happens to run the suite next.\n\n**Why this matters.** Every lane runs this suite as a required check. A lane that runs it and then does `git add -A`, or that reads `git status` to decide whether its tree is clean, will silently absorb a foreign edit it did not author and cannot explain to an evidence gate. It also makes \"the tree was clean before and after\" unusable as a proof step.\n\nThis was noticed while verifying #2843; it did not affect that verification, which was taken from a reverted-clean tree on both sides of the revert-detector run.\n\n**Fix direction.** Either land the #2678 extraction as an ordinary commit and stop generating it at test time, or make the suite perform the extraction in a temporary directory. Do not resolve it by deleting the assertion that triggers the write.\n\nowner: unassigned pending triage by the repo-maintenance queue owner\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\npriority: 2\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T15:20:30Z","createdAt":"2026-09-20T15:18:28Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3312,"title":"Author-lane test suite writes source files: running it dirties scripts/run-governed-review.mjs","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T15:20:30Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3312"},

{"body":"The scheduled ColdLion masters sync on 2026-09-19 reached the database after every vendor fetch completed, then exhausted production's 120-second statement limit inside the `coldlion.change_log` insert for `item_header`. PostgreSQL logged the exact statement and role (`postgres`); no lock-wait message was emitted although `log_lock_waits` is enabled.\r\n\r\nThe statement performs a correlated \"latest prior raw row\" lookup for each changed item. The live plan scans `coldlion_change_log_table_changed_idx` by table name and filters natural-key JSON afterward; its full-change estimate is 177,283,848 cost units. The existing JSON GIN index does not serve equality plus newest-row order. This makes runtime depend sharply on how many items changed even when the snapshot size is stable.\r\n\r\nImplement a repository-tooling-only repair that computes the latest prior change row set once and joins it to changed staged rows. Preserve the same audit payload, transaction, upsert, and timeout. Add an offline regression test proving the generated SQL has no per-row correlated latest-row subquery. Do not change database structure or timeout settings.\r\n\r\nAcceptance:\r\n\r\n- generated master-load SQL preserves existing audit semantics and atomicity;\r\n- prior raw lookup is set-based rather than one ordered change-log scan per changed row;\r\n- focused and full ColdLion landing tests pass;\r\n- exact-head independent review approves and guarded merge completes.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\r\nroute: repo-maintenance\r\nservice_class: maintenance\r\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\r\npriority: 1\r\ndepends_on:\r\nobjects:\r\n```\r\n\r\nowner: Codex chat 01a0bc45-92ef-7f73-b936-4b661d76e979 on EDGE-DEV\r\n\r\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bc45-92ef-7f73-b936-4b661d76e979 on EDGE-DEV","closedAt":"2026-09-23T12:05:54Z","createdAt":"2026-09-20T00:52:30Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3295,"title":"Make ColdLion item change logging set-based after scheduled timeout","updatedAt":"2026-09-23T12:05:54Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3295"},
{"body":"The governed reviewer allocator cannot currently honor an owner-scoped provider set. A fresh assignment can select any healthy active reviewer, even when one workstream is restricted to a smaller known set. Global registry edits and fabricated provider failures are not acceptable substitutes.\n\nAdd a task-local `--reviewer-allowlist` to fresh assignment and governed replacement. The allowlist is permission, not readiness: accept known registered canonical names, then intersect them with live orchestrator independence, reconciled `ai-review-preflight usable` state, exact-head exclusions, and slot independence. Persist the canonical allowed set in durable assignment and replacement records so omitted retry input inherits the restriction and explicit mismatches fail closed.\n\nAcceptance:\n\n- empty, duplicate, unknown, or retired names refuse before allocation;\n- known temporarily unusable names remain valid permissions but are skipped until qualified;\n- fresh assignment, retries, slot 2, and replacement cannot widen the durable set;\n- existing calls without an allowlist retain current behavior;\n- exact-head checks, real preflight/quarantine, per-PR exclusions, and slot-2 independence remain unchanged;\n- same-provider concurrency remains unlimited for independent exact reviews;\n- focused tests prove the restricted pool `grok-4.6,muse-spark-1.3-contributor,qwen-3.8-max` cannot draw another provider.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n\nowner: Codex chat 01a0bc1b-3c51-7b23-9299-488c91b9cce4 on EDGE-DEV\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bc1b-3c51-7b23-9299-488c91b9cce4 on EDGE-DEV\n","closedAt":"2026-09-24T12:23:00Z","createdAt":"2026-09-20T00:30:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Non-orchestrator work (tooling only; no database structure). Part of #3242 (popcre/ai-devops#401 Step 7).\n\n**Problem.** Live on edge-dev on 2026-09-18, the unattended reviewer-start watcher reserved a reroute for the unstarted replacement on #3269 slot 2 (sequence 3299, drawn 19:37:25Z; reserved in the 19:51:54Z pass). Its reclaim step was then refused with `REFUSED: refs/db-coordination/author-acquisition is occupied` (another session was drawing). The lease was untouched, so the watcher mooted the reservation and, as designed, left the still-overdue lease for the lease scan to retry.\n\nThe lease scan never retried it. `priorReroutesForSlot` counts every `review-<issue>-<pr>-seq<S>-slot<N>` ref, including the lease's **own** reservation (same sequence). With one earlier reroute on the slot (seq 3272), the count reached `AUTO_REROUTES_PER_SLOT` (2), and every later pass logged \"automatic reroute budget exhausted (2 for this slot)\". A lease that was never rerouted is stranded after a single transient refusal.\n\n**Fix.** Count only reroutes of earlier draws: exclude the reservation whose sequence equals the lease's own. Re-picking the same lease reuses the same deterministic reservation ref, so the retry is idempotent and cannot loop past the budget. Two regression tests: one for the counter and one end to end (refused reclaim, then a successful retry on the next pass). Both fail on the current main.\n\nowner: Claude chat e55a0f04-d3a0-4c38-b262-8214e273d1cf (this session owns and closes it)\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\npriority: 60\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\nPosted by Claude chat e55a0f04-d3a0-4c38-b262-8214e273d1cf on edge-dev\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-18T22:32:48Z","createdAt":"2026-09-18T20:32:45Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3283,"title":"Reviewer start watch: a lease's own mooted reroute must not count against its slot budget","updatedAt":"2026-09-18T22:32:48Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3283"},
{"body":"Reported from `u2giants/popdam3` PopSG production-readiness #107 as a non-orchestrator consumer. Read-only: nothing authored, claimed or written. Routing to active marker #3275.\n\n## Summary\n\n`public.claim_pdf_backfill_batch` still exceeds the normal statement ceiling in production. It was part of #2792's scope and was reported with live agent evidence on #3009, but both of those closed on proofs of *other* functions (`reconcile_stale_sg_files_batch` and `search_style_guide_library_v2`). This defect has never been repaired and currently has no open issue — this is it.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- 2026-09-18, production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, `claim_pdf_backfill_batch(10)` (the size the Edge caller uses) inside a rolled-back transaction with `statement_timeout='8s'`: **SQLSTATE 57014 at 8.007 s**, context `SQL function \"claim_pdf_backfill_batch\" statement 1`.\n- 2026-09-16, the Windows render agent's own log on every heartbeat after the PopDAM queue was resumed: `agent-api claim-pdf-backfill-batch returned 500: claim_pdf_backfill_batch failed: canceling statement due to statement timeout`. Nothing was claimed. The job was paused to stop the failing query repeating every 30 s. Full detail is in the #3009 comments.\n- `count_pdf_backfill_remaining()` currently reports 2; those are licensing PDFs added after the queue completed on 2026-09-14.\n\n## Consequence\n\nThe PopDAM PDF queue cannot finish, and PopSG PDF extraction is serialized behind it in application code, so all 4,318 style-guide PDFs are blocked.\n\n## What would unblock the app\n\nProduction evidence that `claim_pdf_backfill_batch(10)` completes comfortably inside the normal `authenticated` ceiling on a **cold** call, repeated. No timeout increase, no row deletion, no app-side workaround.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 100\nservice_class: standard-application\nchange_type: migration\napplication_return_to: u2giants/popdam3\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\nlive_assertion: On production claim_pdf_backfill_batch(integer) and count_pdf_backfill_remaining() preserve their existing signatures, grants and eligible-row semantics, and each repeatedly completes below the existing eight-second request ceiling, including a cold call.\nwrites:\n  - function public.claim_pdf_backfill_batch\n  - function public.count_pdf_backfill_remaining\n  - index public.idx_assets_licensing_pdf_backfill_candidates\n  - table public.assets\nreads:\n```\n\nMetadata recovery note: The orchestrator selected typed enum predicates in both sibling routines plus one partial candidate index, preserving eligible rows, signatures and grants. Preview plan/timing proof precedes production promotion; timeout increases and application workarounds remain forbidden.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf01-b3d7-7d62-b7ed-5c7bad7af40a on 916-ALIEN\n\n\nScope clarification authorized by orchestrator: public.assets is the parser-required parent-table lock for creating the named index only; no column or row changes. Claim3300 expanded through guarded exact-head PR inspection preserving version20260920144819.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf41-42a3-7ce0-bdf3-ec5e3dc0a080 on 916-alien","closedAt":"2026-09-25T16:17:19Z","createdAt":"2026-09-18T20:03:05Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2YAgzg","name":"orchestrator","description":"Changes shared-database structure (or curated Master Data load): orchestrator work","color":"B60205"}],"number":3282,"title":"claim_pdf_backfill_batch still times out in production (missed by #2792 and #3009)","updatedAt":"2026-09-25T16:17:19Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3282"},
{"body":"Step 7 of `plan_shared_db_popcre_transfer_merge_queue.md` for tracking issue #2530 (repo-maintenance; not orchestrator work — no database structure change). Owner authorization: Albert's own words on #2530 (comment 5732749753): \"I approve turning on the GitHub merge queue for popcre/shared-db as the plan describes.\"\n\nRebuild the merge queue implementation from current `main` (closed PR #1950 is design history only):\n\n1. `scripts/merge-queue-contract.mjs` — queue-ref PR identity resolution with live re-verification, admission order (ascending earliest migration version among open non-draft migration PRs), 3,000-file ceiling refusal, exact queue-mode detection (active / inactive / unknown, never guessed), and the preview-hold primitive.\n2. `.github/workflows/merge-queue-gate.yml` — owns the cross-event `merge_group` work: exact-head approval, migration lease, object collision, SQL/order and production-sidecar gates re-run against the queued PR identity; bounded preview hold when the base commit added migrations.\n3. Every check-run workflow also emits its required context on `merge_group` with group runs never cancelled; PR-payload steps re-resolve the queued PR through the contract or skip only where the gate proves the equivalent.\n4. `shared-supabase-migrations.yml` publishes `Post-merge preview rehearsal: success` on the exact rehearsed `main` SHA after a successful apply; failure never posts success.\n5. `guarded-migration-merge.yml` goes dual-mode: direct merge while the queue is inactive, enqueue once the exact approved ruleset is active; exact head re-proved immediately before the call in both modes; no admin bypass anywhere.\n6. `scripts/configure-merge-queue.mjs` — dry-run by default; repository-identity, contexts/workflow, mutation-lane and main-tip-preview gates; queue-only rollback naming exactly the recorded `main merge queue` ruleset.\n7. `scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs` — maps every live required context plus `Merge queue gate` to its workflow/job and proves both triggers.\n8. `docs/merge-queue-operation.md` — admission, observation, removal, preview hold, bounded failures, queue-only rollback, recovery without bypass.\n\nThe ruleset is NOT activated from this work — Step 8 is a separate fresh session.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1200\n```\n\nowner: Kimi Work session conv-888fb90a07f61924a4c3c682 on edge-dev\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T07:53:09Z","createdAt":"2026-09-18T19:33:23Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Outcome\n\nA non-draft open PR that edits `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` currently holds its place ahead of every newer PR touching that file for as long as it stays open, regardless of its state. Implement the stale-place rule in `scripts/check-pr-source-collisions.mjs`: such a PR no longer precedes a newer PR when ALL of these hold:\n\n- (a) it has had no activity for 24+ hours,\n- (b) its latest checks are failing OR it conflicts with main, and\n- (c) the newer PR's session has posted a dated nudge comment on it naming the stale state.\n\nIt reclaims its place once refreshed and green. Repository maintenance on scripts and tests only — no migration, no schema object, no database write.\n\n## Evidence (2026-09-18)\n\nPRs #3215, #3217 and #3228 sat 8+ hours ahead of #3247 in the protected-source queue tonight. A PR that is inactive, red or conflict-dirty can block the queue forever; the only escape today is waiting for a human to merge or close it.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- `openProtectedCollisions` skips a preceding PR only when (a), (b) and (c) all hold for that exact pair.\n- No skip when any condition fails — in particular a green, recently-active PR is never skipped.\n- A refreshed-and-green PR precedes again (reclaim) without any manual state reset.\n- Tests in `scripts/check-pr-source-collisions.test.mjs` cover: nudge-gated skip, reclaim-after-refresh, and never skipping a green recent PR.\n- Fail closed: any unreadable signal (activity, checks, mergeability, comments) means no skip.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\nreturn_to: popcre/shared-db\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\nMetadata recovery note: Classify the explicitly script-and-test-only stale-place rule as repository maintenance; no database objects.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf01-b3d7-7d62-b7ed-5c7bad7af40a on 916-ALIEN\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T11:26:58Z","createdAt":"2026-09-18T16:54:39Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3273,"title":"Stale-place rule: a stale, red or conflicted protected-source PR must not hold the queue forever","updatedAt":"2026-09-25T12:26:23Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3273"},
{"body":"Non-orchestrator work: no database structure change. Found while proving #3242 (popcre/ai-devops#401 Step 7).\r\n\r\n## Defect\r\n`.github/workflows/reviewer-start-watch.yml` runs each pass as `node … > /tmp/pass.json` then `CODE=$?`. The step shell is `bash -e`, so a non-zero watcher exit ends the step on that line: the pass JSON carrying the failure is never printed, and the relay step is skipped, leaving the SLO unwatched until the cron restart net (every 3–4 hours here).\r\n\r\nSeen live: leg run 35342433808 reserved the reroute for PR #3269 slot 2 at 14:21:02Z, then ended `exit code 1` at 14:21:40Z with no pass line, no JSON, and no successor leg.\r\n\r\n## Fix\r\nCapture the code with `|| CODE=$?`; record a failed pass and keep watching (later passes resume the failed dispatch, bounded by the watcher's attempt limit); end the leg non-zero; relay on `!cancelled()`.\r\n\r\nowner: Claude chat e55a0f04-d3a0-4c38-b262-8214e273d1cf (the #3242 session)\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\r\nroute: repo-maintenance\r\nchange_type: ci\r\npriority: 60\r\nwrites:\r\nreads:\r\n```\r\n\r\nPosted by Claude chat e55a0f04-d3a0-4c38-b262-8214e273d1cf on edge-dev\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-18T20:46:14Z","createdAt":"2026-09-18T14:36:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3271,"title":"Reviewer start watch: a failed pass hides its error and stops the relay","updatedAt":"2026-09-18T20:46:14Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3271"},

{"body":"owner: Claude chat 3886eb83-7824-4477-a257-dd3adfd80d03 on edge-dev, until handed to a named owner\r\n\r\nNon-orchestrator work: it changes no database structure.\r\n\r\nThe guarded merge workflow merges as `github-actions`. GitHub starts no push workflows for pushes made with the workflow token, so `sync.yml` (trigger: `push` to `main` only) does not run after a guarded merge. Consumers stay stale until the next push to `main` that is not made by that bot.\r\n\r\nEvidence: #3254 merged as `2f204a48` by `app/github-actions` and started no workflows. #3260 and #3263 were merged by `u2giants` and did start syncs (run 35351543065). Details are on #2530.\r\n\r\nFix options: add `workflow_dispatch` to `sync.yml` and have the guarded lane dispatch it after merging, or push with a token that is allowed to start workflows. Done when a guarded merge produces a green sync run on its own merge commit.\r\n\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\r\nroute: repo-maintenance\r\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\r\npriority: 1200\r\n```\r\n\r\nPosted by Claude chat 3886eb83-7824-4477-a257-dd3adfd80d03 on edge-dev\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-18T17:01:53Z","createdAt":"2026-09-18T13:43:46Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3264,"title":"Guarded-lane merges never start the consumer sync","updatedAt":"2026-09-18T17:01:53Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3264"},

{"body":"Post-transfer regression from #2530. Since the repository moved to `popcre/shared-db`, four required PR checks fail on every pull request: SQL migration guards, Migration author lease, Cross-PR object collision and Documents-only merge authorization. Two of the affected pull requests are #3254 and #3243.\n\nCause: test fixtures hard-code `u2giants/shared-db` (for example `repository-maintenance-authorization.test.mjs` fakes `base.repo.full_name`), while the code resolves the live identity, which is now `popcre/shared-db`. Running `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=popcre/shared-db node --test <the 23 test files containing the old slug>` reproduces it locally: 25 of 1054 fail.\n\nFix: make the fixtures follow the resolved identity, or pin `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` inside the test. Keep the historical-alias tests. Change production code only where a failure reveals a real post-transfer bug (for example trusting `OWNER` where the account is now `MEMBER`). {"body":"## Outcome\n\nThe /proddetails loader's reconciliation read counts succeeded sync_run rows, but the refresh regime re-reads answered orders, so one key accumulates many runs. The first live refresh (2026-09-18, workflow run 35312282365) reported keysDone=7016 / rowsFetchedTotal=28765 against 3,753 keys / 17,303 landed rows and correctly failed its own agreement check — the landed table was perfect (tableRows=17303=distinctPkey; re-reads idempotent, zero collapse), only the report's arithmetic was wrong. Count each key once, at its LATEST succeeded run: the rows that run fetched are the rows that run's upsert landed.\n\nRepository-maintenance loader-code fix; no database objects.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: workflow\nreturn_to: u2giants/shared-db\npriority: 60\ndepends_on: 3180\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-18T09:47:45Z","createdAt":"2026-09-18T07:57:44Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Outcome\n\nThe nightly ColdLion Landing Sync job's 90-minute ceiling no longer fits the work now that the production-detail refresh rides it (#3180). Measured live on 2026-09-18 (dispatch run 35303647480, cancelled by the job timeout mid-prod-detail-refresh): setup + offline gate ~4 min, history ~2 min, masters ~4 min, prepack refresh ~43 min, prod-detail refresh ~1.9s/key over up to 2,000 recent orders ≈ 63 min — ~116 min worst case. {"body":"## Outcome\n\nFold case in the ColdLion `/prepackDetail` loader's key-coverage accounting, the\ncompanion to the #3235 guard fix. The re-dispatched final slice (Actions run\n35294603177) passed the request-identity guard — the case-fold worked — and then\naborted correctly on:\n\n```\nincomplete key coverage: the fetched rows do not account for every requested code\n```\n\nDiagnosis: the harvest holds BOTH spellings of the drifted key as distinct\ncodes (the vendor emitted `PPk133` through one feed and `PPK133` through\nanother), and both responses answer `PPK133`. The completeness check counts\nreturned codes case-sensitively, so two asked keys accounting against one\nreturned spelling read as a mismatch. This is the residual the #3236 review\nnamed (\"not case-folded, so two harvest spellings in one collect can still\nabort\"). Nothing was written; the failure is fail-closed and recorded.\n\nThe fix: account each asked key against returned codes case-insensitively —\nan asked key is answered when any returned row's code upper-cases to it;\nunanswered keys must equal exactly the zero-row keys. The per-row identity\nguard (already case-folded) still refuses any row answering a code unrelated\nto the request, so folding the count cannot hide a stray code. No migration,\nno schema object, no database write in this pull request.\n\nOutcome tracking stays with #3179, which this issue deliberately does NOT close.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: ci\npriority: 60\ndepends_on: 3235\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T15:18:37Z","createdAt":"2026-09-18T02:15:06Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3245,"title":"Fold case in the /prepackDetail key-coverage accounting (completes #3235)","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T15:18:37Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3245"},

{"body":"## Outcome\n\nTolerate vendor cross-feed case drift on the `/prepackDetail` request key. The\nenriched refusal from the final backfill slice for #3179 (Actions run\n35288752430) diagnosed it exactly:\n\n```\n/prepackDetail returned a row for another prepack code: asked PPk133, row answers PPK133\n```\n\nThe harvest population (landed `pre_pack_code` values the vendor itself emitted\nvia /itemDetails, /prodHistory or /orderHistory) holds `PPk133`, while\n/prepackDetail echoes the same real key as `PPK133`. This is the documented\nvendor key-inconsistency class (the /seasons defect precedent): one real\nprepack, two spellings, no signal in the response envelope. Nothing was written\n— the guard held — but the loader cannot complete the population while the\nguard compares case-sensitively.\n\nThe fix, minimal and fail-closed:\n\n- The request-identity guard folds case on `prePackCode` only (company codes\n  have never drifted; a future drift there still aborts loudly with both\n  spellings named).\n- The landed `prepack_code` keeps the ROW's own spelling, which is what the\n  /prepackDetail feed asserts as its own grain; a later replay through either\n  spelling upserts onto the same row, so identities cannot split.\n- Different codes still refuse; blank keys still refuse; nothing else changes.\n\nNo migration, no schema object, no database write in this pull request.\n\nOutcome tracking stays with #3179, which this issue deliberately does NOT close.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: ci\npriority: 60\ndepends_on: 3229\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T15:18:36Z","createdAt":"2026-09-18T00:07:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3235,"title":"Tolerate vendor case drift on the /prepackDetail request key (completes #3179 backfill)","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T15:18:36Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3235"},
{"body":"## Outcome\n\nEnforce the owner's 2026-09-17 ruling — **\"I never want GLM reviewing GLM code\"** — in\nthe reviewer draw. A GLM-engine orchestrator (a ZCode session; ZCode's engine is\nGLM-5.3) must never draw the `glm` reviewers, the same way a Codex orchestrator never\ndraws the Codex reviewer. Repository maintenance on scripts and tests only — no\nmigration, no schema object, no database write.\n\n## Evidence (verified 2026-09-17)\n\n- `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:553-557` — `reviewersForOrchestrator(engine, reviewers)` excludes only rows whose `orchestratorEngine` string-equals the live orchestrator's declared engine (normalized).\n- `:274` (`glm-5.3`) and `:280` (`glm-5.2`) carry **no** `orchestratorEngine`; `:557` treats a missing value as `''`, which never equals a real engine — so the glm rows are **never excluded**, for any orchestrator.\n- `:286` (`codex-gpt-5.6-sol`, `orchestratorEngine:'codex'`) is the only row carrying the field — the precedent to copy.\n- `scripts/lib/orchestrator-routing.mjs:66-84` — the marker's `orchestrator-routing` engine vocabulary is the closed map `ENGINES = { codex, claude }`; `:207-210` rejects any other value. A ZCode orchestrator therefore cannot declare itself today: an honest `engine: zcode` marker is rejected, omitting the engine makes `orchestratorEngineFromResolution` (`manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:630-634`) refuse reviewer assignment (fail closed), and the only way to a valid marker is to misdeclare `claude` or `codex` — which excludes the WRONG engine and leaves glm drawable. That misdeclared path is the one that violates the ruling.\n\n## Why now\n\nZCode is already a first-class harness in the workflow (ai-devops blocker-watch wakes zcode sessions; popcre/ai-devops#558 extends managed machine support to it), and ZCode sessions are doing repository work now. The first ZCode-orchestrated structural change here must not be able to draw a glm reviewer.\n\n## Requested change\n\n1. Add `orchestratorEngine:'glm'` to the `glm-5.3` row and the retained `glm-5.2` label row.\n2. Let a ZCode orchestrator declare an engine that excludes glm — either a `zcode` entry in `ENGINES` (ZCode session ids are `sess_<uuid>`) mapped to the glm engine family for exclusion purposes, or an equivalent family mapping. The exact mechanism is the implementing session's judgment within the acceptance criteria below.\n3. Tests in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`: (a) a glm-family/zcode orchestrator excludes both glm rows from the drawable set; (b) codex and claude orchestrations behave exactly as today; (c) a marker declaring no engine still refuses reviewer assignment.\n\n## Acceptance\n\nA read-only re-check: resolve with a marker declaring the zcode/glm engine and show `reviewersForOrchestrator` returns a set without `glm-5.3` and `glm-5.2`; the lane test suite is green; no reviewer's registration or rotation membership changes.\n\n## Not in scope\n\nAdding ZCode as a reviewer (permanently rejected by the same owner ruling — GLM never reviews GLM code); changing reviewer membership or the rotation; any migration or database write.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\npriority: 60\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-18T14:53:30Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T22:09:27Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3232,"title":"Reviewer independence: exclude glm reviewers for GLM-engine (ZCode) orchestrators","updatedAt":"2026-09-18T14:53:30Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3232"},

{"body":"Child of #2773 (Part D). Non-orchestrator: tooling only, no database structure.\n\nAdds a host-wide event-aware watcher. Anything that learns of a change (a webhook receiver, a finished workflow, this host's own mutation) records one event and every waiter on that resource wakes exactly once with no GitHub request. With no event, waiters fall back to window-aligned shared conditional reads (free 304s), honour x-poll-interval, back off 30/60/120/300s after failures, and sleep between local checks rather than busy-looping. The conditional-read and watcher tests join the offline CI job. Collision locks, migration version reservation and the one-at-a-time lanes are unchanged. Registering a GitHub webhook itself needs repository settings and is not part of this change.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: workflow\npriority: 550\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T15:48:32Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T14:35:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3208,"title":"Event-aware GitHub watcher: one wake per change, no busy-loop fallback (Refs #2773)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:07:54Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3208"},

The pre-mutex PR read becomes one GraphQL request that also carries the main commit base and the GraphQL quota. Collision locks, migration version reservation and the one-at-a-time lanes are unchanged; the in-mutex fresh re-proof is kept.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: workflow\npriority: 550\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T15:48:30Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T14:26:27Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3206,"title":"Silent reviewer reclaim and assignment retry within 10 API requests (Refs #2773)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:07:56Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3206"},
{"body":"Non-orchestrator work: documentation gap only, no database structure change.\n\n## Defect\n\nAGENTS.md §5.2 / §5.2-A catalogue flavours of \"a check that never really ran\" (stale verdicts, hosted-runner starvation, the removed apt-get stall) but not the one that cost a session ~30 minutes on 2026-09-17: **a push that leaves a pull request conflict-dirty produces NO `pull_request` workflow runs at all.** GitHub cannot build `refs/pull/N/merge`, so the synchronize event fires only the `pull_request_target` workflows (which check out the base); `gh pr checks` shows a couple of green contexts while every guard that judges the merge tree silently never started.\n\nLive evidence (PR #3200, 2026-09-17): three consecutive pushes (6b32d131, 987a446f, 721cbd38) produced only `Documents-only merge authorization`; an empty-commit re-push did nothing (no paths changed, and the merge ref still could not be built). After merging current `main` into the branch and resolving the conflict, the next push (1819ad5d) created all 19 check runs immediately. Note the discriminator: a PR that merely LAGS `main` (does not contain the base tip but auto-merges cleanly) still runs normally — the first push of that same PR ran everything while behind main. Only the unresolvable-conflict state suppresses runs.\n\nThis bites routinely in this repo because every merged PR carries its own `.agent/` evidence pair, and each such merge conflicts every open PR that also carries a pair — the same treadmill that forces contract-generation refreshes.\n\n## Proposed fix\n\nAppend this paragraph to §5.2-A (verbatim draft):\n\n> **A FOURTH flavour: NO `pull_request` runs at all after a push — the PR is conflict-dirty (observed 2026-09-17, PR #3200).** When a push leaves a pull request with unresolvable conflicts, GitHub cannot build `refs/pull/N/merge`, so no `pull_request` workflow starts; only `pull_request_target` ones (base checkout) run, and `gh pr checks` looks oddly green. Three pushes that day produced only `Documents-only merge authorization`; merging current `main` into the branch made the next push create all 19 runs at once. A PR that merely lags `main` but auto-merges cleanly still runs normally — only the conflicting state suppresses. This bites routinely here because every merged PR carries its own `.agent/` pair, and each such merge conflicts every open PR that carries one. Diagnose with `gh api repos/u2giants/shared-db/pulls/<n> --jq '{mergeable,mergeStateStatus}'` before concluding checks are lost; the cure is refreshing the branch, not re-pushing.\n\nAGENTS.md is a rulebook file, so the PR is NOT documents-only: it needs the `.agent` pair, a reviewer draw, and the guarded merge like any code change.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-24T01:44:47Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T14:16:38Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3205,"title":"AGENTS.md 5.2-A misses the fourth flavour of checks that never ran: a conflict-dirty PR silently starts no pull_request workflows","updatedAt":"2026-09-24T01:44:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3205"},
{"body":"Owner observation (2026-09-17): the orchestrator is always backed up and holds everything else back. Live queue evidence the same day agreed — merge-stage PR aging, ten unlabelled issues (including #2530 itself), one merged-but-unreleased expired claim — while author lanes were healthy. The bottleneck is attention, not capacity.\n\nThis issue tracks the program to reduce what MUST pass through the orchestrator without reducing safety:\n\n- **Phase A — queue hygiene:** label unlabelled issues (scope block verified first), close out expired claim #3089 through the guarded release path, add a read-only scheduled Queue Hygiene Report workflow (writes nothing).\n- **Phase B — self-service additive lane:** a fail-closed classifier + admitted route letting an application session claim a lane and land additive changes confined to `crm`/`pim`/`dam` (or a brand-new single-app schema) without orchestrator triage, keeping every existing gate: collision locks, version reservation, two reviewers, guarded merge, serial preview/promotion, #2758 rules unchanged.\n- **Phase C — zero-touch wait chain:** a written hop table for the #2758 ephemeral route between merge and production; automate only pure-mechanics hops, never guard judgments.\n- **Phase D — documentation:** AGENTS.md §0.0-C table sync, both `shared-db-change` skills, memory.\n\nThe controlling execution document is `plan_orchestrator_required_load_reduction.md` (lands on `main` via the pull request from branch `zcode/plan-orchestrator-required-load-reduction`). Read its STATUS table first. The merge-queue end-state stays owned by #2530; this issue does not re-plan or execute the transfer.\n\nExplicitly rejected (see plan §7): a second orchestrator session (for now), parallelizing the serial lanes, an auto-labeling bot, fewer reviewers for the lane, boundary creep into `plm`/`api`/`core`/`public`.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: workflow\npriority: 1150\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-18T13:07:45Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T13:26:03Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3199,"title":"Reduce required orchestrator traffic without reducing safety (self-service additive lane, queue hygiene, zero-touch wait chain)","updatedAt":"2026-09-18T13:07:45Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3199"},
{"body":"Non-orchestrator work: lease/lane tooling only, no database structure change.\n\n## Defect\n\nCommit 42ae9758 (PR #3184, issue #3183) made `dispatchObjectKeys` in `scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs` key every `grant`/`revoke` on a relation — with or without the `TABLE` keyword — as BOTH `table X` and `view X`. `scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.mjs` then requires the claim's `writes:` to declare `view X` too.\n\nSo a migration that does:\n\n```sql\ncreate table plm.sesame_submission_property_option (...);\nrevoke all on table plm.sesame_submission_property_option from public, anon, authenticated;\n```\n\nfails CI with `REFUSED: migration writes undeclared objects: view plm.sesame_submission_property_option` — live on PR #3190 (claim #3189). Verified by re-running the check: the migration's extracted keys are exactly `table plm.sesame_submission_property_option` and `view plm.sesame_submission_property_option`, the claim declares the table, and the view half is the parser's second name for the same newly created object.\n\nClaims cannot be amended after creation, so every table-creating migration that grants on the new table is blocked until this is fixed.\n\n## Fix (minimal, lease-side only)\n\nIn `check-migration-pr-lease.mjs`: when the same migration file contains `create table X` and the claim declares `table X`, treat the `view X` key produced by the grant dual-keying as covered. The relaxation is gated on the declared table, so an undeclared created table is still refused naming both keys.\n\nUnchanged on purpose: a grant on a relation the migration does NOT create still requires its `view X` (and `table X`) declaration — that is a pre-existing object and stays fully claimed. The collision guard's dual-keying itself is untouched.\n\nTests added to `scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.test.mjs` for both cases (created-in-migration grant covered; existing-relation grant still refused), plus the gate case.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T14:06:44Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T13:25:20Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3198,"title":"Lease check refuses grants on tables the same migration creates (blocks PR #3190)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:08:01Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3198"},
{"body":"Non-orchestrator work (tooling; no database structure change). Unblocks orchestrator work #3174 / claim #3189.\n\nSince #3183 (PR #3184) a keyword-less or `on table` grant is keyed as both `table` and `view`. The lease check then refuses PR #3190, which creates `plm.sesame_submission_property_option` as a table and grants on it:\n\n`REFUSED: migration writes undeclared objects: view plm.sesame_submission_property_option`\n\nFix: resolve the kind from the CREATE in the same migration (table -> table only; view/materialized view -> view only). With no CREATE, or a name created as both, keep both keys so #3183's view detection is unchanged. Tests for both cases.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 90\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T14:05:04Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T12:58:49Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3195,"title":"Lane object reader keys a grant on a table created in the same migration as a view write (blocks PR #3190)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:08:03Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3195"},
{"body":"Non-orchestrator tooling work (it does not change database structure). It unblocks orchestrator work #2794.\n\n## Problem\n#2794 (claim #2816, PR #2821, version 20260917102139) was rehearsed on preview by run 35216549909 at 8664e6a5 (the #2821 merge commit). Production run 35220652669 refused:\n\n> preview run checked out at 8664e6a5… produced evidence with a different scripts/lib/github-transport.mjs than exact main\n\nbecause two tooling-only merges changed that producer file after the rehearsal. A fresh rehearsal at current main (run 35221197402) then refused in the preview job with:\n\n> BLOCKED: already applied on production: 20260917102139\n\nThat refusal is correct but mislabeled: `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` is shared, and in the preview job its `--remote-ledger` is the PREVIEW ledger. The message sends operators toward a false conclusion and hides the correct next step.\n\n## Finding\nNo new mode is needed and the gate must not be weakened. The existing historical-recovery lane (`historical_preview_source_pr` + `historical_preview_original_run_map`, mode=apply) already re-proves the preview ledger state at exact current main with current producer scripts, and byte-binds to the original apply run pinned to the authoring merge commit. AGENTS.md §6 documents that it recovers a post-merge rehearsal that ran AT the authoring merge commit, which is this case.\n\n## Fix\n- Give the guard a `--ledger-name {production,preview}` (default production) so the refusal names the ledger actually read, and on preview names the historical-recovery lane as the route.\n- Pass `--ledger-name preview` at every preview-job guard call site; remove the workflow comment apologising for the wrong wording.\n- Tests for both labels and the workflow call sites.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 560\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T13:57:34Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T12:35:45Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3193,"title":"Preview guard says 'already applied on production' when it read the preview ledger","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:08:04Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3193"},

{"body":"Non-orchestrator work: lane/collision tooling only, no database structure change.\n\n## Defect\n`extractOperations` in `scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs` (the object reader used by the author-lane and dispatch collision checks) misreads PR #2835's migration `20260917090439_licensing_candidate_and_review_apis.sql`:\n\nVerified output on that file:\n```\n{\"action\":\"grant\",\"kind\":\"table\",\"target\":\"api.licensing_entity_candidates\"}\n{\"action\":\"grant\",\"kind\":\"table\",\"target\":\"api.licensing_relationship_candidates\"}\n... (no grant/revoke on api.licensing_resolution_queue at all)\n```\n\n## Root causes (reproduced)\n1. **Missed grant.** `normalizeSql` strips `--` line comments without regard for string literals. The `comment on view api.licensing_resolution_queue is '... Aggregate only -- it exposes ...'` literal loses its closing quote, quote pairing shifts, and the following `revoke all on api.licensing_resolution_queue ...; grant select on api.licensing_resolution_queue ...;` is swallowed into a stripped string.\n2. **Views keyed as tables.** A `grant ... on <name>` with no object-type keyword is keyed only as kind `table`, but Postgres uses that form for views too; the grant never collides with another PR's work on the same `view`.\n\n## Fix\nString-aware comment stripping, and keyword-less grants keyed as both `table` and `view`. Regression test using the real #2835 statement shapes.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T11:44:25Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T10:50:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3183,"title":"Lane object reader: grant on view keyed as table; '--' inside comment literal hides later grant (#2835)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:08:11Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3183"},
{"body":"Non-orchestrator tooling work (no database structure change).\n\nClaim #2745 (PR #2846, audit #3117) cannot supersede its backdated migration version. `--supersede-active-claim-version` refuses with `target worktree is dirty or not at the exact PR head` because the claim's recorded worktree (`recursing-poincare-85d3a9`) is now used by another session with uncommitted work. The lane tool has no way to move a live claim to a different worktree, so the claim is stuck even though the PR, owner and branch are intact.\n\nFix: add a guarded `--rebind-claim-worktree` mode to `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` that moves an active claim to a new clean worktree at the exact PR head:\n\n- owner proof: owner, branch, currently recorded worktree, issue and claim title must all match; the lease must be active and the version not retired;\n- the open PR head sha and branch must match; the new worktree must differ from the recorded one, be clean, be on the claim branch and sit at the exact PR head;\n- the old worktree is never inspected or touched;\n- runs under the coordination mutex, changes only the `worktree:` line of the lease block, reads the claim back field by field, rolls back on failure, and records create-only evidence under `refs/db-claim-worktree-rebinds/`; re-running is idempotent.\n\nTests cover success, idempotence, each refusal, readback-failure rollback and CLI wiring.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 560\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T13:24:47Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T10:45:09Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3182,"title":"Lane tool: guarded --rebind-claim-worktree to move a live claim to a clean worktree (#2745)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:08:14Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3182"},

It owns no database-shape change.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: source-data\nroute: source-data-session\npriority: 0\nreturn_to: u2giants/shared-db\ndepends_on: 2863\nwrites: []\nreads: []\n```\n\n## Required work\n\n- Extend the existing repository-owned ColdLion loader; do not create a second framework.\n- Harvest the complete approved `prodOrderNo` population from landed production history, then call `/proddetails` once per distinct key.\n- Fail loudly on unknown fields, malformed responses, incomplete key coverage, identity collisions, or target mismatch.\n- Add synthetic offline tests for projection, replay, duplicate refusal, empty responses, and resumability.\n- Add a bounded, resumable production backfill plus ongoing scheduled refresh.\n- Prove the production target immediately before every write. {"body":"## Problem\nAfter #3104 (live, PR #3131), the DB Data Admin **Scraped Properties** property feed (`api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory`) still has no section for Coca-Cola Submissions, WWE Creative, Peanuts Creative, or Sesame Workshop (any purpose). Follow-up of the same-class gaps listed on #3104; the orchestrator scoped them out there.\n\n## Evidence (read-only, production, 2026-09-17)\n- Live migration `20260917005650` property arms: Coke only `plm.coke_asset_property_option` (Creative); WWE only `plm.wwe_property` (`wwe-submissions`); no arm reads `plm.coke_approval_vocabulary_value`, `plm.wwe_creative_brand`, `plm.peanuts_art_program`, or any Sesame table. (`peanuts-creative` / `sesame-creative` exist only in the character arm.)\n- `select count(*) from plm.coke_approval_vocabulary_value where vocabulary_kind='brand'` -> 218 (109 per capture, 2 captures)\n- `select count(*) from plm.wwe_creative_brand` -> 2\n- `select count(*) from plm.peanuts_art_program` -> 19\n- Ledger `plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution` grouped by source: `peanuts_tenovos|source.tenovos_art_program` 19 approved/unmapped; `sesame_thelettera_netx|source.thelettera_brand` 25 approved/unmapped; `coca_cola_brandcomply|plm.coke_asset_property_option` 83 approved/unmapped; no WWE rows. Tables `source.tenovos_art_program` / `source.thelettera_brand` do not exist in production, so arm identities must reconcile to those ledger members.\n- `select count(*) from plm.sesame_capture` -> 0 (Sesame source data not loaded; see licensor-source-data issue). No Sesame Submissions (MediaBox property options) landing table exists.\n\n## Change\n1. Add property arms: Coca-Cola Submissions (latest brand vocabulary), WWE Creative (`plm.wwe_creative_brand`), Peanuts Creative (`plm.peanuts_art_program`), Sesame Creative (`plm.sesame_brand`), with row identities matching existing ledger members where they exist.\n2. {"body":"Non-orchestrator tooling work (no database structure change).\n\nThe production business-risk gate's preview producer pin (`prove_preview_producer_matches_main` in `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py`) refuses #2870 and #2866 at current main. Both previews ran at main-line commit 426cca7c (preview runs 35174395763 and 35175207318). Main later changed custody-only producers the preview job runs around the apply (freshness check, lane manager, repository identity helpers, the workflow's freshness flag and repository spelling). A read-only dry run at main 03d540a6 refuses both with: `produced evidence with a different .github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml than exact main`.\n\nFix: for an exact-main target only, and only once the preview ref is proved an ancestor of exact main, tolerate differences in an explicit custody-only producer set, and tolerate a workflow difference only when the two versions are identical after explicit custody-only rewrites. Apply-shaping producers (guard, derivation, atomic apply, instance binding, allowlist, supabase config, overlapping sidecars) stay byte-compared; tolerated paths are never counted as comparisons. Tests must fail before the fix; prove with a dry run against both previews at current main.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: workflow\npriority: 560\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T07:55:23Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T07:10:09Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3168,"title":"Risk gate producer pin refuses main-line previews over custody-only producer drift (#2870, #2866)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:08:33Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3168"},
{"body":"Follow-up to #3163 / PR #3164 for tracking issue #2530 (repo-maintenance; not orchestrator work — no database structure change).\n\n`trustedOutcomeComments` in `scripts/orchestrator-flow/outcome-lifecycle.mjs` trusts any comment with association `OWNER`, with no login check. {"body":"Non-orchestrator tooling work (no database structure change).\n\nThe production business-risk gate (`scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py`) classifies routine, behavior-preserving `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` and narrowing access grants/revokes as high risk, forcing the manual route.\n\nEvidence:\n- #3104 (PR #3131): the automatic route printed ENGINEER ACTION REQUIRED; recovered manually via run 35181367216.\n- #2866: same classification in the run 35177396554-era evidence.\n\nFix: classify behavior-preserving function replacements (same signature, same return type, same security/owner/grants) and narrowing grants (REVOKE, or GRANT that does not widen to anon/authenticated/PUBLIC) as routine. Stay fail-closed for real permission widening (new grants to broader roles, SECURITY DEFINER introduced, signature or return-type change, dropping data). Tests must include positive controls for each fail-closed case and fail before the fix.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: workflow\npriority: 550\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T09:16:10Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T04:29:03Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3159,"title":"Production risk gate: classify behavior-preserving function replacements and narrowing grants as routine","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:08:41Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3159"},
{"body":"Non-orchestrator repository maintenance (no database structure change). Follow-up from the round-2 review of PR #3151 (finding 3).\n\nAfter a request records `entered`, and before its db-claim issue exists, the request has no owner. The event alarm therefore never reads its events. The unentered-request alarm (#3152) also skips it, because it already has an entered event. A stall in that window raises no alarm at all.\n\nFix: have gatherLiveInput read the events of ready requests that have an entered event but no owning claim, and raise the alarm once the wait passes a threshold.\n\n\nImplemented in PR #3160.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T07:06:39Z","createdAt":"2026-09-17T04:16:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3158,"title":"Alarm blind spot: request between entered and claim creation is watched by neither alarm","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:08:43Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3158"},

{"body":"Non-orchestrator work (repository tooling; no database structure change).\n\n## Fault\nThe automatic production qualification job matches a refreshed PR head to an *older* head with an \"identical pull request diff\" and inherits that older head's REVISE, instead of the most recent approved head.\n\nObserved in run 35174156969 (job \"Automatic production qualification and dispatch\", step \"Re-prove current main, guarded merge, and durable exact-head verdict\") for PR #3118:\n\n```\nREFUSED: no reviewer was ever assigned head 72517a6f8bc891bb818a61b75cd4104dbccaa487; an assignment pinned to an earlier head does not carry forward to new commits; an APPROVE cannot be carried forward because head 01f73d190d1cd685adc92c93078782ad87dd5b61, whose pull request diff is identical to this head, carries a durable reviewer refusal\n```\n\n- 01f73d19 got REVISE. Later heads (cc580403, 919f70fb) changed the migration header, and 919f70fb got a durable APPROVE.\n- 72517a6f = merge of main into 919f70fb plus the .agent evidence pair. The guarded merge accepted the carry-forward at 72517a6f.\n- The qualification step therefore disagrees with the guarded merge. It appears to compare diffs in a way that treats 01f73d19 as identical (probably after main absorbed the rebased version-rename, or by excluding files it shouldn't), and a refusal on any matching head blocks the carry.\n\n## Expected\nThe carry-forward decision should use the latest head whose PR diff is identical, and should agree with the guarded-merge carry rule. {"body":"Repo maintenance, not orchestrator work (no database shape change).\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\n## 1. Production risk qualifier over-reports a low-risk additive migration (proven)\n`_classify_statements` in `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py` returns all three risks (data loss, downtime, access change) when any single statement is off ALLOWLIST. For #3036 / migration `20260916231639` (PR #3108) the only unmatched statement was a multi-action `ALTER TABLE plm.item ADD COLUMN ...` where `_alter_table_action_is_low_risk` was False only for an inline `CHECK` on a new nullable no-default column. Result: automatic run 35163423338 refused with all three conclusions although no data can change and no access changes; it needed the engineer route (reviewer approval + owner dispatch 35164319157). Evidence: https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/3036#issuecomment-5706285595\n\nFix direction: classify per risk instead of all-or-nothing; accept multi-action ALTER TABLE when every action is low-risk; treat a CHECK on a column added in the same statement (no default) as scan-only (downtime at most), never data loss or access change. Add tests.\n\n## 2. `--claim` refuses unsorted `--objects` (reported by orchestrator #3106, reproduce first)\n`node scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --claim ... --objects \"b,a\"` is reported to refuse when the list is not sorted. The command should normalise (sort/dedupe) the list, or its refusal must say exactly that order is required.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T15:18:28Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T23:55:26Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Owner authority (Albert, chat 2026-09-16, verbatim)\n> yes, file the issue with the orchestrator and give me the Issue #\n\n(Approving the two feed fixes below, after declining orchestrator routing for the data links, which were written directly: 85 approved mapped decisions, evidence PR #3103.)\n\n## Orchestrator work — changes `api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory` (structure)\n\n### 1. Warner Submissions section missing\n`plm.wb_property` holds 165 rows with `source_namespace='warner_product_catalogue'` (STARLABS Product catalogue = Submissions, captured 2026-08-07) alongside 360 `warner_art_assets` rows. The property branch (live def ~line 448) labels **all** of `plm.wb_property` as `'Warner Bros. - Creative (STARLABS)'` / `Creative`. Result: no Warner Submissions section; 165 Submissions rows appear as red Unmapped Creative rows (Warner shows 525 Creative / 0 Submissions).\nFix: classify `warner_product_catalogue` rows as Submissions (label `Warner Bros. - Submissions (STARLABS Product catalogue)`), `warner_art_assets` stay Creative. Existing ledger members already use `warner_starlabs|plm.wb_property|warner_product_catalogue:source_id:*` for 261 mapped decisions, so identities must stay unchanged.\n\n### 2. Show the mapped value in the Mapping column\nProperty rows return only `mapping_state`. Add:\n- Creative rows: `submissions` array `[{source_system, source_table, source_id, display_label}]` of the winning mapped decision's members (the popdam3 frontend `presentScrapedProperty` in `apps/db-data-admin/src/lib/data-admin.ts` already renders `submissions[].display_label` instead of \"Mapped\").\n- Submissions rows: the reverse — labels of Creative rows mapped to it (new field, e.g. `mapped_creative`), plus a small popdam3 frontend change to render it instead of \"—\".\nKeep privacy rules (no evidence locators/contract data to the browser) and cursor/row_key stability.\n\n### Acceptance\n- Warner shows one Creative (360) and one Submissions (165) section; Warner unmapped Creative = 99.\n- NBCU Creative \"Despicable Me 3 (2017)\" Mapping shows \"DESPICABLE ME 3\"; NBCU Submissions \"DESPICABLE ME 3\" Mapping shows its Creative labels.\n- Update `docs/db-data-admin-scraped-properties.md`.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nservice_class: standard-application\nchange_type: function\napplication_return_to: u2giants/shared-db\nlive_assertion: an authenticated Licensing Manager call to api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory for entity kind property returns 165 Warner Bros. rows with source_purpose Submissions and 360 with source_purpose Creative, mapped Creative rows carry a submissions array of member labels, and Submissions rows carry a mapped_creative array\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\npriority: 50\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory\nreads:\n  - table plm.wb_property\n  - table plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution\n  - table plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T08:07:40Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T21:32:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Owner request (Albert, chat 2026-09-16, verbatim)\n> can you link the obvious ones? for all the licensors. and in the 'Mapping' field in the Submissions table if something is mapped, instead of just a dash , put the value it's mapped to. and the same thing in the Mapping field of the creative table, instead of saying 'Mapped', put the value it's mapped to.\n\nContext: NBCU Creative \"Despicable Me 3 (2017)\" shows Unmapped while Submissions has \"DESPICABLE ME 3\".\n\n## Scope (orchestrator work — changes database structure + curated mapping load)\n1. **API shape:** `api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory` returns only `mapping_state` (Creative) and null for Submissions. Add the mapped counterpart display name(s) for Creative rows, and the reverse (mapped Creative name(s)) for Submissions rows.\n2. **Mapping load:** append superseding approved `mapped` decisions in `plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution(_member)` for obvious Creative→Submissions matches, all licensors (currently unmapped: NBCU 120, STARLABS 99, SEGA 104, Paramount 67, Coca-Cola 83, Disney DCP 84, Lucasfilm 26, WildBrain 28, Sesame 25, Peanuts 19, Marvel 6). Owner ruling above is the authority for \"obvious\" name matches (normalized title, year/prefix stripped, same licensor group); the doc line \"name similarity alone is never sufficient\" is superseded for unambiguous one-to-one matches only. Ambiguous/many-to-one stay unmapped. Record the candidate list + sha256 as evidence.\n3. **Frontend** (`apps/db-data-admin/src/lib/data-admin.ts:354-361`): show counterpart name(s) instead of \"Mapped\" / \"—\". Keep red Unmapped rows. Update `docs/db-data-admin-scraped-properties.md`.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","closedAt":"2026-09-16T21:28:19Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T21:20:57Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3102,"title":"Scraped Properties: link obvious Creative↔Submissions matches and show mapped names","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:45:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3102"},
{"body":"#3027 Step 7 live finding (PR #3098): the reviewer start watcher and the unstarted silence probe counted PR-wide activity (CI check runs, workflow runs, another slot's review) as the target reviewer starting, so a real non-start read `keep-active` and could never be rerouted.
