{"body":"## Request — structural (orchestrator work): new table for the persisted Production Tracking schedule\r\n\r\nSource plan: `popcre/designflow-tracking` `plan_prod-tracking-on-time-early-warning.md`, step 4 (decisions D5, D6 locked; D8 — names — proposed here).\r\n\r\n### Why\r\nProduction Tracking computes a needed-by date per milestone (`helpers/utility.js` `buildProductionStages()` and the licensing sub-rows) and throws it away. Overdue alerts (step 5) need a durable, de-duplicable copy.\r\n\r\n### Target\r\nSandbox DesignFlow database (production Supabase project, schema `plm`, next to `plm.\"ProdOrderHeader\"`, `plm.\"FactoryTime\"`). Additive only.\r\n\r\n### Proposed table `plm.prod_order_milestone_schedule`\r\nOne row per (production order, stage), plus SKU for licensing stages.\r\n\r\n| column | type | note |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| id | bigint identity PK | |\r\n| prod_order_header_id | integer not null | FK `plm.\"ProdOrderHeader\"(id)` on delete cascade |\r\n| sku | text null | null for order-level stages |\r\n| stage_name | text not null | e.g. `Mass Production Start`, `Submission` |\r\n| needed_date | date null | |\r\n| estimated_date | date null | |\r\n| actual_date | date null | |\r\n| status | text not null | Pending / Overdue / Complete / Delayed / licensing labels |\r\n| anchor_type | text null | e.g. `ship_date` |\r\n| anchor_date | date null | |\r\n| factory_time_id | integer null | FK `plm.\"FactoryTime\"(id)` on delete set null; null = no template |\r\n| sampling_days | integer null | values actually used |\r\n| mass_production_days | integer null | |\r\n| template_source | text null | human source text, or `no template` |\r\n| computed_at | timestamptz not null default now() | updated each upsert |\r\n| first_past_due_at | timestamptz null | set once, never overwritten by the writer |\r\n\r\nUnique: `(prod_order_header_id, stage_name, coalesce(sku,''))` (unique index on expression, or `sku text not null default ''`) so the writer upserts idempotently.\r\nIndex on `(status, needed_date)` for the overdue scan.\r\n\r\n### Grants\r\nSame role/grants as the other `plm` tables the tracking service writes (read + insert/update for the app role). No RLS change beyond matching siblings.\r\n\r\n### Done when\r\nMigration merged, applied to the sandbox database, and the table visible to the tracking service. Only then does `designflow-tracking` add the upsert writer.\r\n\r\n\r\n### Author note (orchestrator, 2026-09-16)\r\nLive read-only check: `plm.\"ProdOrderHeader\"` primary key is `\"prodOrderNo\"`; `id` is an identity column with no unique constraint, so a foreign key to `id` needs an additive unique index on `plm.\"ProdOrderHeader\"(id)` first. Included below.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\nservice_class: standard-application\r\nchange_type: migration\r\napplication_return_to: popcre/designflow-tracking\r\nlive_assertion: to_regclass('plm.prod_order_milestone_schedule') is not null with foreign keys to plm.\"ProdOrderHeader\"(id) and plm.\"FactoryTime\"(id) and the unique upsert index\r\ngenerated_types: required\r\npriority: 50\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table plm.prod_order_milestone_schedule\r\n  - index plm.prod_order_milestone_schedule_upsert_key\r\n  - index plm.prod_order_milestone_schedule_status_needed_idx\r\n  - index plm.prod_order_header_id_key\r\n  - table plm.\"ProdOrderHeader\"\r\nreads:\r\n  - table plm.\"FactoryTime\"\r\n```\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T08:07:39Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T19:25:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3091,"title":"Prod Tracking step 4: add plm.prod_order_milestone_schedule (persisted milestone schedule)","updatedAt":"2026-09-18T20:08:03Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3091"},

{"body":"Non-orchestrator repo-maintenance work for popcre/ai-devops#507 (child of #498 / #401):\n\n- **(a)** The guarded merge's required-checks pre-flight waits (bounded, default 15 minutes, re-reading each poll) while checks are still running or not yet reported, instead of refusing. A failing check still refuses at once.\n- **(b)** `scripts/refresh-code-pr-branch.mjs`: one step to bring a guarded code PR branch onto a moved main (merge main, keep `.agent/` off the implementation head, re-run the changed tests and diff check, rebind and validate the completion report, push, assign a reviewer at the new head). Refuses on a real conflict or a failing test.\n- **(c)** `scripts/dispatch-production-apply.mjs`: gathers evidence run artifact digests, checks every input name against the workflow on origin/main, and sends one JSON dispatch body. {"body":"Part of #3027 (Step 6 live proof).\n\n`validateTrain` in `scripts/orchestrator-flow/migration-train.mjs` requires passing **production** assertions for every entry, and `--authorize-train` calls it before dispatch. Production assertions can only exist after the production run, so no train can ever be authorized (circular). Fix: pre-dispatch validation requires preview assertions plus a clean dry-run against the exact target at the train main whose pending list equals the train list; production assertions are required only by `--close-train` (success). Tests included. No database change.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\n```\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T15:36:03Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T15:26:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\n```\n\nLinked to #3027 (popcre/ai-devops#401 Step 1). Tooling defect, not a schema change.\n\n## Symptom\nAutomatic production qualification (\"Automatic production qualification and dispatch\" job in Shared Supabase Migrations) passes and bot-dispatches a production apply using a preview apply run from an **older commit** than the merge commit that authored the migration. The production gate then correctly rejects the evidence as drifted. Qualification and gate disagree on what counts as matching evidence, so the dispatch is doomed before it starts.\n\n## Evidence (bot-dispatched runs)\n- Qualification 35061568370 (at 86da2d44) -> dispatched 35061726161, refused:\n  `original apply run 35060692115 dispatched at 3fdd16effbd154e1602c29aa5610161910138d68 produced evidence with scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260916033914.json absent where the merge commit 86da2d44... of the pull request that authored 20260916033914 has it present`\n- Qualification 35052040496 (at 6c9b149d) -> dispatched 35052182196, refused:\n  `original apply run 35047947727 dispatched at 0a11c42d3e373fe9b45e826a3015c93bb7cf4704 produced evidence with a different scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs than the merge commit 6c9b149d... of the pull request that authored 20260916001944`\n\n## Expected\nQualification must apply the same evidence-commit comparison the gate applies: either select a preview apply run whose evidence matches the authoring merge commit, or trigger a fresh preview apply / refuse without dispatching.\n\nThe other four bot dispatches since 09-10 (34987389408, 34989644100, 35056268596, 35067878423) were business-risk refusals by design and are not part of this defect.\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-16T13:12:08Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T11:56:07Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3039,"title":"Automatic production qualification dispatches with stale preview evidence the gate then rejects as drifted","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:10:26Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3039"},

{"body":"## Add product-type reader columns to plm.item\r\n\r\nStructural prerequisite for the product-type reader work (#3024, plan: https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/blob/main/plan_product_type_reader.md).\r\nOpened up front on owner instruction (2026-09-16) so the schema is ready when the reader passes its accuracy gate. The columns are additive and nullable; nothing writes them until the reader work lands.\r\n\r\nOwner ruling 2026-09-16: these live on our own product table `plm.item`, never on `coldlion.item_header` (ColdLion refreshes would overwrite them).\r\n\r\n### Columns (all nullable, with column comments)\r\n| column | type | meaning |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| `product_type` | text | physical product a merchant would name, e.g. `Storage Toy Chest` |\r\n| `product_construction` | text | construction/shape, e.g. `Stretched`, `Collapsible` |\r\n| `product_material` | text | material **stated in the description** only |\r\n| `product_treatment` | text | embellishment stated, e.g. `Glitter`, `Foil`, `LED` |\r\n| `product_type_status` | text, check in (`accepted`,`unreadable`,`placeholder`) | whether the reader could read it |\r\n| `product_type_rules_version` | text | reader rules version that produced the value |\r\n| `product_type_read_at` | timestamptz | when the value was computed |\r\n\r\nGrants: same as existing readable `plm.item` columns. No index needed now. Regenerate types.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\nservice_class: standard-application\r\nchange_type: migration\r\napplication_return_to: u2giants/shared-db\r\nlive_assertion: information_schema.columns lists the seven product_type columns on plm.item with the status check constraint\r\ngenerated_types: required\r\npriority: 50\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - column plm.item.product_type\r\n  - column plm.item.product_construction\r\n  - column plm.item.product_material\r\n  - column plm.item.product_treatment\r\n  - column plm.item.product_type_status\r\n  - column plm.item.product_type_rules_version\r\n  - column plm.item.product_type_read_at\r\nreads:\r\n```\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T08:07:42Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T11:51:07Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3036,"title":"HANDOVER: add product-type reader columns to plm.item","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:10:29Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3036"},

Related to #3009 — same statement-ceiling family, different function and a different, more visible consequence.\r\n\r\n## Summary\r\n\r\nThe ordinary nightly PopSG crawl **failed in production last night** at its final step. `public.refresh_style_guide_matviews` was cancelled by the statement timeout, so the run is recorded as `failed` with `lifecycle_state=refreshing` and the library's aggregates are stale.\r\n\r\nThe crawl itself was healthy — this is purely the aggregate refresh.\r\n\r\n## Evidence\r\n\r\nFrom `public.style_guide_crawl_runs`, most recent runs:\r\n\r\n| started_at | status | files_found | accepted | upserted | deactivated | stale_remaining | guard | refreshed |\r\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\r\n| 2026-09-15 22:00 | **failed** | 217,047 | t | 217,047 | 0 | 0 | ok | **f** |\r\n| 2026-09-14 22:00 | completed | 216,801 | t | 216,801 | 0 | 0 | ok | t |\r\n| 2026-09-13 22:00 | completed | 216,702 | t | 216,702 | 0 | 0 | ok | t |\r\n| 2026-09-12 22:00 | completed | 216,702 | t | 216,702 | 0 | 0 | ok | t |\r\n\r\n`error_message`: `Matview refresh failed: canceling statement due to statement timeout`\r\n\r\n`admin_config.STYLE_GUIDE_CRAWL_REQUEST` mirrors it: `status: failed`, `files_found: 217047`, `inaccessible_roots: []`.\r\n\r\n## Why it is structural rather than unlucky\r\n\r\n`refresh_style_guide_matviews` does all of this in a single statement under the 8 s `authenticated` ceiling:\r\n\r\n- `refresh materialized view concurrently public.style_guide_file_groups`\r\n- `refresh materialized view concurrently public.style_guide_folders`\r\n- a search-document sync batch, default 5,000 rows\r\n\r\nTwo concurrent refreshes over a 217,047-row base table will not fit in 8 s with any reliability. It passed on 11–14 September and failed on the 15th, which reads like the corpus simply crossing the line rather than a one-off.\r\n\r\nThe caller's only lever is `p_search_batch_size`, and that does not touch the dominant cost, so there is no honest application-side fix. Reducing it would hide the failure without repairing it.\r\n\r\n## Consequences\r\n\r\n1. The nightly crawl now reports `failed` even though ingestion and reconciliation were clean, so the three-consecutive-clean-night proof that popdam3 #107 depends on is broken and restarts from zero.\r\n2. `style_guide_file_groups` and `style_guide_folders` are stale, and the PopSG Guides grid and folder tree read from them.\r\n3. This will recur every night until repaired.\r\n\r\n## What would unblock the app\r\n\r\nA production-proven `refresh_style_guide_matviews` that completes inside the normal `authenticated` ceiling at current corpus size — for example by making the refresh resumable across calls the way the search-document sync already is, so the Edge caller can drive it in bounded slices. Repeat samples, cold, not a single warm call.\r\n\r\nNo timeout increase, no row deletion, and no app-side masking is requested or acceptable.\r\n\r\n\r\n## Orchestrator admission (#3106)\r\n\r\nRead-only diagnosis on production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`: the matview queries cost about 2.1 s (`style_guide_file_groups`) and 0.5 s (`style_guide_folders`) warm, but the search-document sync candidate scan costs **11.6 s even when it finds zero rows** — it walks every active file of the run and probes `style_guide_search_documents` for each one to recompute and compare the identity hash. That is the dominant cost and it grows with the corpus, not with the amount of changed work.\r\n\r\nFix: keep a durable `search_sync_pending` flag on `style_guide_files`, set by a row trigger only when an identity column actually changes (or on insert), with a tiny partial index over the pending rows. The refresh function then reads only pending rows, keeps its exact identity comparison and upsert, clears the flag for the rows it examined, and keeps its signature and caller contract. No timeout change, no row deletion.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\nservice_class: standard-application\r\nchange_type: migration\r\napplication_return_to: u2giants/popdam3\r\nlive_assertion: the next nightly PopSG crawl run on production records status completed with refreshed true, and public.refresh_style_guide_matviews completes inside the 8s authenticated statement ceiling at the current corpus size\r\ngenerated_types: required\r\npriority: 50\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table public.style_guide_files\r\n  - table public.style_guide_search_sync_queue\r\n  - function public.style_guide_files_queue_search_sync\r\n  - trigger trg_style_guide_files_queue_search_sync on public.style_guide_files\r\n  - function public.refresh_style_guide_matviews\r\nreads:\r\n  - table public.style_guide_search_documents\r\n  - table public.style_guide_pdf_text\r\n  - table public.style_guide_crawl_runs\r\n  - materialized view public.style_guide_file_groups\r\n  - materialized view public.style_guide_folders\r\n```\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-18T17:50:36Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T10:57:56Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3023,"title":"PopSG nightly crawl now fails: refresh_style_guide_matviews exceeds the statement ceiling at 217k files","updatedAt":"2026-09-18T17:50:36Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3023"},
{"body":"Migration `20260916033914` (issue #2988) is merged on main at `86da2d44bcd390b3177f322f947b212c8dc9bbc9`, but its production apply is refused:\n\n`Production business-risk gate rejected evidence: original apply run 35060692115 dispatched at 3fdd16effbd154e1602c29aa5610161910138d68 produced evidence with scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260916033914.json absent where the merge commit 86da2d44bcd390b3177f322f947b212c8dc9bbc9 of the pull request that authored 20260916033914 has it present`\n\nA migration that ships a new preview-producer sidecar can never rehearse on preview at a commit that already carries that sidecar on main, so the immutable original apply cannot be replayed. The repository's sanctioned remedy for this exact fact pattern (precedents: `docs/verification/issue-2570-...` and `issue-2863-historical-producer-restoration.md`) is a frozen entry in `scripts/historical-migration-restorations.mjs`, validated by `validateHistoricalProductionProvenance`. No guard is weakened, relaxed, or bypassed.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 70\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-16T07:26:20Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T06:16:22Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3020,"title":"Register 20260916033914 as an exact historical restoration (unblocks #2988 production apply)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:10:40Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3020"},
{"body":"Step 7 of `plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md`. Part of #2301.\n\nSteps 1-6 built the author-lane abandonment lifecycle. Step 7 is the completion step: run the full suites, verify the live behaviour read-only, fix whatever that live verification finds, record the final STATUS and definition of done, and retire the plan's handoff.\n\nLive read-only verification found two real defects that 980 unit tests could not see, both fixed here:\n\n- The claim-identity read ran outside the per-domain failure legs of the flow snapshot, so one live claim whose title predates the `#<number>` convention threw out of the whole snapshot and the hourly audit described no lane at all. The identity read is now its own failing leg: one unreadable claim is one unreadable row, reported as unverifiable in both domains.\n- A refusal on `--abandonment-audit` fell through to the generic handler, which exits `2`. On this command `2` already means \"an expired author lane was found\", so the scheduled job announced every read failure as an expiry report about lanes it had never read. A refusal on this command now exits `3`, because an instrument that could not read is exactly the unverifiable case and unverifiable outranks expiry. The refusal message is still printed in full, and every other command keeps exiting `2`.\n\nScope:\n\n- `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` - the two fixes above.\n- `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` - a test pinning each.\n- `plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md` - final STATUS row, definition of done, and the note that the plan is complete and must not be restarted.\n- `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-04T1453Z-edge-dev-codex-author-lane-lifecycle-plan.md` - retired, as the handoff-contract rule requires of a pull request that closes its issue.\n\nNo database, preview, production or infrastructure change. No ref, branch or worktree deletion. The lifecycle is not applied to any live expired claim to prove it.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-16T06:26:21Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T05:27:18Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3018,"title":"#2301 Step 7: full regression, live report proof, final STATUS, and plan completion","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:10:41Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3018"},

{"body":"Step 6 of `plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md`. Part of #2301.\n\nSteps 1-5 changed how author lanes behave. The rules that tell an operator what to do still describe the world before them, and a rule that lives in five files is really five rules the moment one of them is edited alone.\n\nThis step synchronizes the operating rules, records the abandonment evidence shape as an issue template, writes out the two procedures an orchestrator must be able to follow without chat context, states the settled authority boundary in every venue where it is operative, and adds static tests that turn documentation drift into a red build rather than a discovery made during an incident.\n\nScope:\n\n- `docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md` - the read-only audit command and its three exit codes, the abandonment record, quarantine/recovery, terminal retirement, the authority boundary.\n- `AGENTS.md` - the task-router entry for #2301.\n- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/author-lane-abandonment.md` - the durable, privacy-safe abandonment record.\n- `scripts/test_production_migration_guard.py` - agreement tests across those venues.\n- `plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md` - the STATUS table.\n\nThe canonical `popcre/ai-devops` orchestrator skill is the fifth venue and is synchronized in its own repository; `node scripts/check-skill-drift.mjs` must still report no contradictions afterwards.\n\nNo database, preview, production or infrastructure change.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T12:25:04Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T03:53:05Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3015,"title":"#2301 Step 6: synchronize operating rules, abandonment evidence template, and drift tests","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T12:25:04Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3015"},
{"body":"Sub-issue of #2301 (plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md, Step 5). Adds hourly and dispatch-time READ-ONLY detection of expired author lanes.\n\nAn expired lease locks a lane and nothing reports it. The queue behind it stays invisible until somebody tries to allocate and is refused, which can be days later — and the refusal names the lock, not the fact that the lock's author walked away.\n\nThis step adds a new `--abandonment-audit` command that runs the Step 4 reconciler with its write hooks removed before the reconciler ever sees them, so the audit cannot mutate even where a live sole-orchestrator marker exists; a new hourly `workflow_dispatch`-capable GitHub Actions workflow that runs it with a read-only token, a bounded timeout, concurrency cancellation and pinned runtime and actions, and that files no issue and no comment; three distinct exit codes so an expired lease (2) is never confused with a state the audit could not read (3), and neither is ever confused with a clean hour (0); and workflow-policy tests in the repository's canonical guard test that prove the schedule, the permissions, the timeout, the concurrency, the read-only command and the absence of every mutating flag from every scheduled workflow.\n\nExpiry is not abandonment. Nothing here transitions a claim.\n\nThe scope block below classifies this issue as repo-maintenance. It declares no database objects: the change touches only lane-governance scripts, one workflow, and their tests, with no migration path and no schema writes.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T12:25:00Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T02:33:43Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3012,"title":"#2301 Step 5 — hourly read-only detection of expired author lanes","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T12:25:00Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3012"},
{"body":"Sub-issue of #2301 (plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md, Step 4). Separates the reconciliation's capacity truth from its preview truth so one unreadable preview edge can no longer hide every other lane's readable capacity report; reports an expired-unconfirmed author lane with the facts an operator needs, with `queued_behind: null` meaning UNKNOWN rather than zero; recognizes an exact abandonment-audit issue as evidence and only then prints the separate guarded relinquishment command; and never transitions an expired claim automatically, with or without a live orchestrator marker.\n\nExpiry is not abandonment. An expired lease means a clock ran out; abandonment exists only if somebody wrote the evidence down.\n\nThe scope block below classifies this issue as repo-maintenance. It declares no database objects: the change touches only lane-governance scripts and their tests, with no migration path and no schema writes.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T12:24:57Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T01:10:34Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3011,"title":"#2301 Step 4: separate capacity and preview truth in author-lane reconciliation","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T12:24:57Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3011"},
{"body":"Reported from `u2giants/popdam3` PopSG production-readiness #107 as a non-orchestrator consumer. No shared-db change was authored here. Routing to the active orchestrator marker #3004.\n\n## Summary\n\n`public.search_style_guide_library_v2` is live-verified under #2860, but that proof used `p_result_mode=>'files', p_query=>null, p_limit=>1`. At the parameters the PopSG app actually uses (`p_limit=>50`, default landing view, no filters), the **unfiltered full-corpus browse** sits at 80–90% of the `authenticated` 8s statement ceiling and has been observed to exceed it.\n\nThe app cutover (plan step 4 of popdam3 #107) is therefore held. Cutting the customer-facing library over to this contract today would move it from a working legacy path onto one that intermittently returns SQLSTATE 57014.\n\n## Measurements\n\nProduction `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` (proven at connect time), role `authenticated` with `statement_timeout='8s'` and a real PopSG-entitled `request.jwt.claims`, 216,801 active rows. Repeated samples:\n\n| Call (all `p_limit=>50`) | Observed |\n|---|---|\n| `files`, no query, `modified_desc` | 3.4–6.6 s |\n| `guides`, no query, `modified_desc` | 6.4–7.3 s, **one 57014 timeout at 8.02 s** |\n| `guides`, no query, offset 1000 | 7.26 s |\n| `guides`, `p_licensors` filter | 0.07 s |\n| `guides`, `p_query=>'<term>'` | 0.75 s |\n| `files`, `p_query=>'<term>'` | 0.49 s |\n| `files`, zero-result query | 0.01 s |\n\n## Finding\n\nEvery **filtered or queried** call is fast. Only the **unfiltered whole-corpus** call is slow, and `guides` mode is roughly twice `files` mode. The unfiltered path is the default landing view — the single most frequent customer request — so the slowest case is also the most common one.\n\nThe cost appears to be the full-corpus facet aggregation (`licensors` / `properties` / `style_guides` built from the whole entity set) plus the exact total, both computed on every call with no way for a caller to opt out.\n\n## What would unblock the app\n\nProduction evidence that `search_style_guide_library_v2` completes comfortably under the normal `authenticated` ceiling for the unfiltered default view in **both** `files` and `guides` modes at `p_limit=>50`, with repeat samples rather than a single call, and with meaningful headroom rather than a value just inside the limit.\n\nNo timeout increase, no row deletion, and no app-side workaround is requested or acceptable.\n\n## Constraints observed\n\nRead-only investigation. No migration, schema edit, database write, branch, or PR was created from the app repository. Evidence above is aggregate and sanitized: no licensed filenames, paths, results, or credentials.\n\n\n## Orchestrator admission (#3106)\n\nRead-only diagnosis on production (EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the unfiltered Guides body): 6.35 s with cold reads. Time goes to materializing all ~217k active children (wide-table heap fetches), a 1.06M-row tag fan-out, and per-guide distinct facet aggregates. The unfiltered answer only changes when the corpus changes, so the fix precomputes the unfiltered totals, facets and guide rows into two small materialized views refreshed every 5 minutes, and the v2 function reads them only when no query and no filter is supplied. Filtered calls are unchanged. No timeout change.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nservice_class: standard-application\nchange_type: migration\napplication_return_to: u2giants/popdam3\nlive_assertion: unfiltered public.search_style_guide_library_v2 calls in both files and guides modes at p_limit 50 complete in well under 2 s on production, repeated, with no SQLSTATE 57014\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\npriority: 90\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function public.search_style_guide_library_v2\n  - function public.refresh_style_guide_library_default_snapshot\n  - materialized view public.style_guide_library_default_guides\n  - materialized view public.style_guide_library_default_summary\n  - index public.style_guide_library_default_guides_group_uidx\n  - index public.style_guide_library_default_guides_modified_idx\n  - index public.style_guide_library_default_guides_name_idx\n  - index public.style_guide_library_default_summary_mode_uidx\n  - table public.style_guide_library_default_guides\n  - table public.style_guide_library_default_summary\nreads:\n  - table public.style_guide_search_documents\n  - table public.style_guide_render_queue\n  - table public.style_guide_files\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T10:32:21Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T00:45:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3009,"title":"PopSG v2 search: unfiltered default browse is at the authenticated statement ceiling (guides mode observed timing out)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:10:50Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3009"},

{"body":"Observed 2026-09-15 on PRs #2980, #2981 and popcre/ai-devops#477: agents serialise CI and the governed review, waiting for a full green run before requesting the review that must approve the merge. That roughly doubles wall-clock per PR.\n\n**Why it happens (structural, not a one-off):** review evidence binds to the exact head SHA, so any fix pushed after a review voids that review. Agents therefore learn to wait for CI first so they only \"spend\" one review. Two consequences follow:\n1. review and CI run in series when they could run together;\n2. every review round produces another push, and every push reruns the full matrix (the Windows jobs alone ran ~30 minutes).\n\n**Proposed change (needs a decision, not yet implemented):**\n- brief agents to start the governed review as soon as a head is pushed, in parallel with CI, and accept that a required fix costs one re-review;\n- require fixes to be batched into a single new head instead of one push per finding;\n- consider whether the merge gate can accept a review bound to a head whose only later change is test/evidence files.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\nreturn_to: popcre/shared-db\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\n\nMetadata recovery note: Replace unsupported route repo-session with repo-maintenance. Preserve the existing ready status for investigation; the suggested review-evidence relaxation remains a proposal, not approval.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf01-b3d7-7d62-b7ed-5c7bad7af40a on 916-ALIEN\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T19:47:41Z","createdAt":"2026-09-16T00:00:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":3002,"title":"Agents serialise CI and governed review, and re-push per finding — costs ~2x wall clock per PR","updatedAt":"2026-09-25T19:48:39Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/3002"},

{"body":"```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\r\nroute: repo-maintenance\r\nservice_class: maintenance\r\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\r\npriority: 4\r\ndepends_on:\r\n```\r\n\r\n> No `return_to:` is set on purpose. This work is owned by the tooling in **this**\r\n> repository (`scripts/`, `.github/workflows/`, `.agent/` evidence, the governed review\r\n> runner and the agent dispatch text). A same-repo `return_to` files the reject straight\r\n> back into this queue forever (#2836), so the address is deliberately absent rather than\r\n> self-referential. If the audit flags `NO RETURN ADDRESS`, the correct fix is to work it\r\n> here, not to add `u2giants/shared-db`.\r\n\r\n## Problem\r\n\r\nAgent-to-reviewer handoffs fail **late**. The failure is discovered after a reviewer draw has\r\nalready been consumed, after a PR is already open, or after an agent has already ended its turn —\r\nso the cost is a wasted reviewer slot and a stalled lane, not a fast error message. Every item\r\nbelow was observed repeatedly inside a single real session, not hypothesised.\r\n\r\nThe common shape: the pre-conditions for a successful handoff are all *checkable before the\r\nexpensive step*, and none of them are checked before the expensive step.\r\n\r\n## The four fixes\r\n\r\n### 1. Validate (or inject) the terminal VERDICT instruction before consuming a reviewer draw\r\n\r\nThe governed review runner must confirm that the outbound reviewer prompt ends with the strict\r\nterminal instruction `VERDICT: <DECISION> <head>` — and inject it when it is missing — **before**\r\nthe reviewer draw is consumed.\r\n\r\n**Failure it prevents:** an approval was given **twice** and could not be recorded either time,\r\nbecause the prompt that was sent never carried the terminal VERDICT line. The reviewer did the\r\nwork, said yes, and the verdict was unrecordable. Two draws were spent for zero recorded verdicts.\r\nThe check is a string test on a prompt we already build; it costs nothing and it is currently done\r\nnowhere.\r\n\r\n### 2. Generate `.agent/completion.json` from git, not by hand\r\n\r\nProvide a command that writes `.agent/completion.json` from the repository state:\r\n\r\n- `head_sha` = the implementation commit\r\n- `files_changed` = `git diff --name-only <base>..<head>`\r\n\r\nAgents currently hand-write both fields.\r\n\r\n**Failure it prevents:** roughly **five separate PR failures** in one session, every one of them a\r\nmismatch between the hand-written `files_changed` / `head_sha` and what git actually contained.\r\nNone was a real defect in the work; each cost a full red-check cycle to discover and a push to fix.\r\nA value that can be derived should never be typed.\r\n\r\n### 3. Add a pre-draw readiness check\r\n\r\nBefore a reviewer draw is consumed, assert:\r\n\r\n- the branch is current with `main`\r\n- there are no merge conflicts\r\n- the evidence pair is valid\r\n- the PR is **not a draft**\r\n- there is no cross-PR object collision\r\n\r\n**Failure it prevents:** a merge was **declined twice with no reason given** — the actual cause was\r\nsimply that the PR was still a draft. Nothing in the path said so. A one-line readiness assertion\r\nturns a silent, unexplained decline into an immediate, named refusal before any reviewer capacity\r\nis spent.\r\n\r\n### 4. Tell dispatched agents to keep polling\r\n\r\nAdd to the standard agent dispatch instructions, in the agent's own words:\r\n\r\n> Keep polling. Do not stop while waiting. Poll every 5 minutes. Never use `gh run watch`.\r\n\r\n**Failure it prevents:** agents **ended their turns mid-wait**, treating \"waiting for a check\" as\r\n\"finished\". The work was neither done nor handed back, and the lane looked busy while nothing was\r\nrunning. The 5-minute floor and the `gh run watch` ban also keep parallel agents off the GitHub\r\nburst limit.\r\n\r\n## Why these belong together\r\n\r\nAll four are the same defect class — a pre-condition checked after the irreversible step instead\r\nof before it — and all four are cheap, local guards on paths that already exist. Fixing one without\r\nthe others still leaves a handoff that fails late.\r\n\r\n## Not in scope for this issue\r\n\r\nNo implementation, and no pull request, is proposed here. This issue records the four fixes and the\r\nobserved failure behind each one so the work can be dispatched.\r\n\r\nMetadata recovery note: added the missing `change_type: reviewer-tooling` to the scope block. Governed reviewer assignment refused this issue with `REFUSED: repository-maintenance issue #2998 must declare a recognized non-structural change_type`; the work is reviewer tooling, matching sibling issue #2923. No other field was changed.\r\n\r\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T08:21:32Z","createdAt":"2026-09-15T23:08:48Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2998,"title":"Make agent-to-reviewer handoffs fail fast instead of wasting reviewer draws","updatedAt":"2026-09-25T11:59:03Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2998"},

{"body":"## Customer-visible failure\n\n`[redacted personal email]` cannot open PopDAM OrderList. The first bounded block fails with `canceling statement due to statement timeout`; administrator `[redacted personal email]` succeeds.\n\n## Production evidence (2026-09-15)\n\n- Target proven: shared production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\n- Both identities are active Supabase `authenticated` users.\n- Albert has `administrator`; Yzhou has no `app.user_role` row (CRM app access only).\n- The same representative 500-row default-sort query, under each user's JWT identity, took ~1.03s for Albert and ~4.20s for Yzhou on warm buffers. The authenticated role limit is 8s, so cold/load variance explains Yzhou's observed timeout.\n- Yzhou's plan spends ~3.44s scanning `core.customer` and ~0.41s scanning `core.factory`, removing every row while repeatedly evaluating role-dependent RLS. Albert spends ~0.65s and ~0.06s on those nodes.\n- `api.dam_order_list` is a security-invoker view that left-joins those two tables. Their `shared_read` policy calls `app.has_any_role(...)`; an `admin_write` policy separately calls `app.has_role('administrator')`.\n- Existing owner decision: every signed-in PopDAM user must see OrderList. The view's production-order/item/bridge inputs already have permissive authenticated OrderList read paths, but customer/vendor joins do not have an OrderList-specific path.\n\n## Required outcome\n\nMake the existing bounded 500-row OrderList query reliably finish for an authenticated PopDAM user with no business role, while preserving customer and vendor names and without raising the 8s timeout, loading the full dataset, or weakening unrelated `core.customer` / `core.factory` access.\n\n## Structural route\n\n- Work type: structural shared-db repair.\n- Route: `shared-db-orchestrator`.\n- Objects to inspect/change: `api.dam_order_list` and the least-privilege supporting function/policy contract needed for its `core.customer` and `core.factory` joins.\n- Do not solve this by making the whole view security-definer without a security review; open issue #2662 tracks cross-application leakage from definer views.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nservice_class: standard-application\nchange_type: view\napplication_return_to: u2giants/popdam3\nlive_assertion: a signed-in PopDAM user with no app.user_role row loads the first 500 default-sort OrderList rows in under 8s with customer and vendor names present\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\npriority: 10\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function app.dam_order_list_customer_directory\n  - function app.dam_order_list_vendor_directory\n  - function dam.dam_order_list_customer_directory\n  - function dam.dam_order_list_vendor_directory\n  - table api.dam_order_list\n  - table dam.dam_order_list_customer_directory\n  - table dam.dam_order_list_vendor_directory\n  - view api.dam_order_list\n  - view dam.dam_order_list_customer_directory\n  - view dam.dam_order_list_vendor_directory\nreads:\n  - table core.customer\n  - table core.factory\n```\n\n## Acceptance\n\n1. Preview contract and plan test as administrator and a no-business-role authenticated identity.\n2. Same rows and non-null customer/vendor names where linked.\n3. First 500 default-sort rows stay comfortably below 8s under realistic cold/load conditions.\n4. Anonymous access remains denied; unrelated direct core-table access is unchanged.\n5. Governed branch, preview, PR, merge, production apply, then signed-in Yzhou-equivalent production proof.\n\n\n\n\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-16T07:26:19Z","createdAt":"2026-09-15T20:44:11Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACoQNUrw","name":"bug","description":"Something isn't working","color":"d73a4a"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2988,"title":"PopDAM OrderList times out for authenticated users without a business role","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:11:14Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2988"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n**Orchestrator work.** Blocks PR #2984 (GitHub request waste fix, issue #2985) and every other PR needing a reviewer assignment.\n\n- Reviewer assignment refuses with \\`active reviewer leases are unreadable\\`. Root cause: the past-verdict store is at its 1,000-entry limit, so the verdict check refuses for the current glm-5.3 leases (PRs 2869, 2877); the assignment script swallows that refusal and prints the vague message.\n- No governed tool exists to prune old verdicts. Needed: (1) a governed prune/archive tool for old verdicts; (2) assignment path must surface the real cause.\n- Not hand-deleted on purpose (would bypass the lock).\n\nRelated finding for whoever owns #2981: \\`--queue-audit\\` in manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs lists open issues then re-fetches each issue plus its comments (2N+3 requests per run). Using the list payload, or one batched GraphQL read, removes the per-issue re-fetch. {"body":"Repository-maintenance fix for the production business-risk gate.\n\nProduction run 34987389408 for migration 20260915130626 (#2934, PR #2958) was refused by `classify_sql` in `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py`: the rule `\\bdrop\\s+(?!trigger\\s+if\\s+exists|policy\\s+if\\s+exists)` reported \"existing production data may be lost or permanently altered\", matched only by `drop function if exists public.deactivate_stale_sg_files(text, uuid);`.\n\nA DROP FUNCTION / DROP PROCEDURE without CASCADE removes no rows: Postgres refuses it while any dependent object (trigger, default, view, policy, constraint) exists, and the definition is reproducible from migration history.\n\nFix: per statement, do not flag `drop function|procedure [if exists] <name>(<args>)[, ...] [restrict]` without CASCADE. Keep CASCADE drops, name-only drops, and every other DROP flagged; do not change the preview-required check or any other rule. Regression tests for the #2958 statement, its CASCADE variant, DROP TABLE, multi-statement and comma lists, and drops inside comments.\n\nNo database, migration, preview or production work; no rehearsal or production dispatch.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: ci\npriority: 90\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-15T19:09:04Z","createdAt":"2026-09-15T15:23:06Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2969,"title":"Risk gate reports a non-CASCADE DROP FUNCTION as production data loss","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:11:36Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2969"},
{"body":"Repository-maintenance fix for the guarded merge claim read. After #2964, PR #2958's guarded merge run 34985444563 still refused with \"open claims seen (0): none\" in the exclusive merge lane, while the lease check in the same run, with the same `github.token` and the same `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/u2giants/shared-db/issues?state=open&per_page=100` read, verified claim #2957 sixteen seconds earlier. A write-blocked local run of the exact `--acquire-merge` path (admission included) sees all 9 open claims. The lane cannot currently tell an empty or PR-only read from a genuine absence of claims, and its refusal does not say what the read returned.\n\nFix, in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` only: the open-claim read refuses loudly when the open-issue listing has no non-PR rows; when it finds no claims it cross-checks GitHub search for open `db-claim` issues and refuses naming both counts if they disagree; the merge-lane refusal reports rows, pull requests and unlabelled issues the listing returned. Regression tests. {"body":"Repository-maintenance fix for the guarded merge claim lookup. Live reads at the time: GitHub's `issues?state=open&labels=db-claim` listing returned `[]`, while the unfiltered open listing and search both returned #2957 with the label.\n\nFix: list open claims unfiltered and filter the `db-claim` label client-side in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` and `scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.mjs`; make the closed-claim history lookup fail closed when its labels= listing is empty (history only grows, so empty means a GitHub fault and must not make a consumed version or object look free); make the lane refusal name the claims it saw and the head branch compared. {"body":"Repository-maintenance fix for the contract-test replay. After #2948 (merge 7c314992), `scripts/check_pass2_routine_supersession.py` replays a later applied drop only when `to_regprocedure(<target>)` is null at snapshot time. The captured pre-adoption baseline (`supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql`) is loaded BETWEEN pass 1 and pass 2 and re-creates objects a pass-1 migration dropped, so the guard sees the routine present and skips the drop. Observed on PR #2958 run 34973127156: 20260915130626 drops `public.deactivate_stale_sg_files(text, uuid)` in pass 1, the baseline re-creates it, 20260905104802 re-runs in pass 2, the drop is emitted but skipped, and contract 3 of `supabase/tests/popsg_bounded_crawl_and_search_contracts.sql` fails.\n\nFix: replay a later applied drop unconditionally when no applied migration after the dropping file declares that routine again; keep the catalog guard only when a later applied migration re-declares it. Add a catalog regression test reproducing baseline re-creation. No database structure, migration, row, preview, production, claim or lease work.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: ci\npriority: 70\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-17T17:17:51Z","createdAt":"2026-09-15T13:20:41Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: ci\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n## Outcome needed\n\n`scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.mjs` refuses an ADDED migration whose version is in the preview ledger. The governed flow applies an open PR migration to preview before merge, so any later push turns the required SQL migration guards check permanently red even with an identical file. Live case: PR #2933, check run 34922885252, guarded merge run 34923289466.\n\n## Fix\n\nAllow only an added file whose version is in preview and not production, and which reproduces exactly the statements preview ledger row recorded for that version. {"body":"Found by the independent review of PR #2933 (issue #2792), Medium severity, outside that PR's scope.\n\n`public.deactivate_stale_sg_files`, the compatibility wrapper from migration 20260905104802, loops at most 200 times over `public.reconcile_stale_sg_files_batch`. After #2792 each batch is capped at 500 rows, so one call handles at most about 100,000 rows. On a root with about 217,000 stale rows, one call returns a partial count with no signal that rows remain. The whole loop is also a single statement, so at that volume it likely never fit the normal statement timeout anyway.\n\nCallers that use the two batch functions directly are unaffected.\n\nNeeds: either return a done/remaining signal, or have callers use the batch functions and retire the loop. Owning application (PopDAM/PopSG) should confirm who still calls the wrapper.\n\nCallers confirmed 2026-09-15 (orchestrator read-only check): no live caller. popdam3 crawl calls reconcile_stale_sg_files_batch directly (supabase/functions/agent-api/index.ts:3001); no cron job; only shared-db contract tests reference the wrapper. Decision: retire the wrapper by dropping it, update contracts 3 and 10 in supabase/tests/popsg_bounded_crawl_and_search_contracts.sql, regenerate types.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 90\nchange_type: function\nservice_class: standard-application\napplication_return_to: u2giants/popdam3\nlive_assertion: A service-role call to public.deactivate_stale_sg_files on production fails because the function no longer exists, while public.reconcile_stale_sg_files_batch remains executable by service_role.\ngenerated_types: required\nwrites:\n- function public.deactivate_stale_sg_files\nreads:\n- function public.reconcile_stale_sg_files_batch\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-15T19:25:08Z","createdAt":"2026-09-15T03:02:30Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2934,"title":"PopSG deactivate_stale_sg_files wrapper silently truncates at ~100k rows","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:12:11Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2934"},

{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nA merged PR bound to its work issue by the verified `SHARED_DB_MERGED_PR_ISSUE_BINDING` (#2901) still cannot get a reviewer. `--assign-reviewer --issue 2506 --pr 2726 --head-sha feab7b9c38b51f2d6e27a42321711fa227e749d5` refuses:\n\n`REFUSED: pull request must close exactly one work issue; found 0`\n\nReviewer assignment and verdict recording read a GraphQL routing snapshot that bypasses the binding wrapper, and the governed review runner never applies the binding. {"body":"```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 40\r\nchange_type: column\r\nservice_class: standard-application\r\napplication_return_to: u2giants/popdam3\r\nlive_assertion: public.style_guide_files has a nullable boolean column has_talent_likeness with no default.\r\ngenerated_types: required\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table public.style_guide_files\r\nreads:\r\n  - table dam.style_guide_file\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Request\r\n\r\nExpose the nullable `has_talent_likeness` contract on the production `public.style_guide_files` table consumed by PopDAM/PopSG.\r\n\r\nProduction proof after #2802: `dam.style_guide_file.has_talent_likeness` exists as nullable boolean with no default, but `public.style_guide_files` remains the live application table and has no same-named column. PopDAM's `complete-style-guide-crawl` upserts into `public.style_guide_files`, so it cannot safely accept or persist the field yet.\r\n\r\nAdd a nullable boolean `public.style_guide_files.has_talent_likeness` with the same semantics as #2802: TRUE only for explicit source evidence of talent likeness, FALSE only for explicit source evidence of no likeness, and NULL when the source makes no determination. No data backfill, no filename/path/folder inference, and no production row updates are authorized by this intake. Preserve existing permissions and compatibility.\r\n\r\nThe migration must be preview-tested and production-ledger verified through the active shared-db orchestrator. {"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: workflow\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nA structural outcome whose `application_return_to` is `u2giants/shared-db` can never write its authoritative completion record. `--complete-outcome` requires a `db-outcome-evidence` block whose `live_evidence` is a successful shared-db Actions run at `application_commit_sha` carrying an unexpired artifact named `shared-db-live-proof-<issue>-<sha>` that contains `db-live-proof.json` (schema_version 1, work_issue, application_commit_sha, live_assertion verbatim, environment, result `passed`, observed_at). No workflow in any u2giants repository produces that artifact, and no issue has ever completed through `--complete-outcome`.\n\nLive case: #2848 (PR #2815, merge c40f587e, production run 34871556647). The ledger is at `live_verified`; the completion record refused with `evidence reference must resolve to exactly one db-outcome-evidence block`.\n\n## Fix\n\nAdd a dispatch-only, read-only `Shared DB Live Proof` workflow. It runs a committed per-issue probe (`supabase/live-proofs/<issue>.sql`) against production through the Management API with `read_only: true`, reads the live assertion verbatim from the issue's scope, and uploads the proof artifact only when the probe returns passed. Include the #2848 probe (catalog privilege checks only). No lane-script change.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T17:51:48Z","createdAt":"2026-09-14T17:06:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2906,"title":"No workflow produces the live-proof artifact, so a shared-db outcome can never complete","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:12:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2906"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nchange_type: function\nservice_class: standard-application\napplication_return_to: u2giants/shared-db\nlive_assertion: an authenticated Licensing Manager call to api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory for entity kind property returns every row with a licensor_group_key/licensor_group_name naming one real licensor (or the single unresolved group), and 129 NBCUniversal rows with source_purpose Submissions\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 100\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory\nreads:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties\n```\n\nOwner report (DB Data Admin > Scraped Properties > Properties): every licensor must show exactly two sections, Creative and Submissions, with Disney, Marvel and Lucasfilm / Star Wars as separate licensors. Today the page shows extra fake licensor groups (\"DCP Vault\", \"DCP Creative\", \"OPA\") and NBCUniversal Submissions shows 0.\n\nCauses:\n1. The RPC emits portal-named labels and purpose-specific keys (`disney-opa` vs `disney`, `marvel-opa` vs `marvel-asgard-creative`, `DCP Vault - Creative (authoritative Marvel scope)`), and the UI groups by splitting the label text.\n2. `plm.nbcu_property` rows with `source_kind` `property`/`franchise_asset` (129 current rows) were captured from the Product Submissions picker, but the property arm labels all NBCU rows Creative. Only `asset_metadata_label` rows are Creative. NBCU character and style-guide rows come from Creative asset pages only (verified from source_url), so those arms are unchanged.\n\nFix: add a stable canonical `licensor_group_key`/`licensor_group_name` to every row in all three arms (existing `licensor_key`/`row_key` unchanged so cursors stay stable), put rows whose licensor is genuinely unresolved or in conflict into one `unresolved` group (\"Licensor not yet determined\"), and classify NBCU picker rows as Submissions. The UI groups by the canonical field. Re-derived from #2903 (20260914164141) so its Warner arm repair is preserved.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T20:55:42Z","createdAt":"2026-09-14T16:50:35Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: workflow\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nA merged migration PR that never carried a GitHub closing link can never reach preview or production: `--resolve-admitted-issue-for-pr` refuses `REFUSED: pull request must close exactly one structural work issue; found 0`, and GitHub cannot add a closing link after merge.\n\nLive case: PR #2726 (issue #2506, migration 20260911213429) merged 2026-09-11 as e420cd86; merged-PR preview run 34862009488 refused with that line.\n\n## Fix\n\nAdd a governed, explicit binding: workflow input `merged_pr_issue_binding` = `PR:ISSUE`, used only for that exact merged PR and only when GitHub reports zero closing links. It is verified against the PR body's single `Work issue #N` line, any `issue-N` branch name, the merged head's `.agent/completion.json` (work_issue, pr, migration_versions equal to the PR's migrations), and a permanent `refs/db-claims` reservation for every version. Any mismatch refuses; issue admission runs unchanged. The automatic production dispatch forwards the binding.\n\nThe earlier automatic production 403 (run 34681414931) is already fixed on main by ebe83f77 (#2851).\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T19:31:38Z","createdAt":"2026-09-14T15:33:02Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nRepair the post-apply production catalog verifier's row-count report without reducing or bypassing catalog verification.\n\nProduction workflow run 34807646359 successfully applied its migration, then the `Post-apply catalog verification` step generated this query shape:\n\n`select jsonb_agg(x order by x->>'name') ... from (...) x`\n\nPostgreSQL treats `x` as a composite record, not JSON, so `x->>'name'` failed with SQLSTATE `42883` (`operator does not exist: record ->> unknown`). The verifier recorded the row-count failure instead of producing the intended report.\n\n## Required repair\n\n1. Add a regression test that fails on the current composite-record ordering expression and proves the emitted SQL is valid for one and multiple row-count targets.\n2. Repair the query to order by the record field (or an explicitly converted JSON value) with deterministic name ordering.\n3. Preserve the complete catalog verification path, enforcement mode, object checks, privilege checks, sidecar checks, and failure reporting. Do not disable, skip, soften, or replace row-count/catalog verification.\n4. Run the focused regression and the full production catalog-verification test suite.\n\n## Boundaries\n\n- Repository-maintenance only; no migration and no database structure or data write.\n- No preview or production dispatch.\n- Do not replay run 34807646359 merely to test the repair.\n- Do not touch excluded or unrelated queue items.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- The regression demonstrates the prior SQLSTATE 42883 defect and passes with the repair.\n- Generated row-count SQL uses deterministic `name` ordering that PostgreSQL accepts for composite rows.\n- The full catalog verifier remains enabled and all existing catalog-verification tests pass.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-24T17:44:00Z","createdAt":"2026-09-14T05:16:35Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2876,"title":"BUG: Post-apply catalog row-count ordering treats composite record as JSON","updatedAt":"2026-09-24T17:44:00Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2876"},

{"body":"Live acceptance for popcre/designflow-backend#94 found that designflow_hts_alsand_worker can insert source_environment=production. {"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\n```\n\n## What happened\n\nThe nightly `ColdLion Landing Sync` workflow failed on 2026-09-12 (run 34685660524) and 2026-09-13 (run 34751469115). Both failed while `sync-masters.mjs` saved the master snapshot (246,877 item slots):\n\n```\npsql could not be executed (EPIPE): spawnSync psql EPIPE — this is a CLIENT-SIDE tooling fault, not a database failure.\n```\n\n## Cause\n\n`tools/coldlion-landing/lib/db.mjs` `runSql` piped the whole SQL script to psql on stdin (`-f -`). When psql stops reading early, the pipe breaks and Node discards psql's exit status and stderr, so the real cause is lost.\n\n## Fix\n\nWrite the script to a private temp file (0600, removed afterwards) and run `psql -f <file>` with stdin ignored. No structure change, no objects, nothing weakened. Implemented by PR #2864.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T15:14:25Z","createdAt":"2026-09-14T02:38:51Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. The #2179 blockers (vendor defect #2178 and pick ticket visibility) do not apply to these two.\r\n\r\n## Out of scope (owner direction 2026-09-13)\r\n\r\n`/pickticket` and `/receiving` are not needed unless a needed feed depends on them. `/itemImages` metadata stays in #2179 pending an owner decision.\r\n\r\n## Gate (plan §9 Step 6)\r\n\r\nBefore dispatch the author must deliver, for each endpoint: a documented grain proof from a live sample, a complete owner field disposition (`docs/coldlion-field-decisions-*`), an idempotent replay test, and no unexplained duplicate collapse. Use a surrogate row UUID plus a uniqueness contract over the smallest proven source identity; never label a guessed key as natural.
