{"body":"Structural admission refuses PR #2818 (issue #2744) at head 93d3544538cb5c532053a97666c5aea52c68a298:\n\n> REFUSED: the pull request migration files contain no statement-leading schema DDL, so the actual change is not structural\n\nIts migration rewrites `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text,text,integer)` inside a do-block: it reads the current definition with `pg_get_functiondef`, asserts anchors, applies `replace()` edits, and EXECUTEs the result. That carries no statement-leading DDL, so `inspectPrStructuralChange` (`scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission.mjs`) refuses it. The gate was never tested against a do-block migration.\n\nFix: an admission-only recogniser for pg_get_functiondef-into-variable followed by EXECUTE of that same variable inside a do-block. The shared collision inventory stays unchanged; every existing refusal survives; row-only do-blocks still refuse.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\npriority: 1\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\n```\n\nShips no migration and changes no database shape. Files: `scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission.mjs`, `scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission-outcome.test.mjs`.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T01:52:14Z","createdAt":"2026-09-14T01:36:12Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2854,"title":"Structural admission refuses do-block function rewrites (pg_get_functiondef + EXECUTE)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:13:39Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2854"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\npriority: 900\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n\n## Outcome needed\n\n`inspectPrStructuralChange` in `scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission.mjs` (~line\n131) refuses any migration whose DDL is not **statement-leading**:\n\n```\nREFUSED: the pull request migration files contain no statement-leading schema DDL,\nso the actual change is not structural\n```\n\nA migration that derives a routine body from the live catalog inside a\n`do $migration$ … end $migration$` block (reading `pg_get_functiondef`, asserting\nanchors, then `execute`-ing the edited definition) has no statement-leading DDL\nkeyword, so it is refused and **no reviewer can be assigned**.\n\n## This is a tool defect, not a branch defect — four pieces of evidence\n\n1. **The gate is one day old.** `admission.mjs` first entered the tree\n   2026-09-11 (e7bec2fe, #2727) and was amended five times that same day.\n2. **The pattern is long-standing.** Of **673 merged migrations, 205 contain no\n   DDL keyword at all, and 18 are do-block migrations.** All predate the gate.\n3. **It was never tested against one.** `admission-outcome.test.mjs` contains\n   **zero** occurrences of `do $`, `EXECUTE`, or `pg_get_functiondef`.\n4. **The branch's own contract makes the pattern mandatory.** `.agent/contract.json`\n   on PR #2818 forbids re-introducing the retired whole-catalog asset context and\n   requires byte-identical results — deriving from the catalog is the correct\n   pattern there.\n\n## Scope\n\n`inventoryDdlVerbs` (`check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:824`) has exactly **one**\nnon-test consumer (`admission.mjs:130`), so a targeted fix is feasible.\n\n**Blast radius of the bug is one PR:** of the seven open migration-carrying PRs,\nonly **#2818** is stranded (2846, 2835, 2823, 2821, 2815, 2814 all have\nstatement-leading DDL). Issue #2579 is queued behind it.\n\n## Constraints\n\n- Add a test that covers the do-block pattern, and **prove it fails against\n  today's gate before it passes** against the fix.\n- **Do NOT widen the gate to let one PR through**, and do not weaken collision\n  detection to achieve it.\n- Rejected non-fixes, for the record: adding cosmetic DDL to the migration,\n  rewriting it as explicit `CREATE OR REPLACE` (its contract forbids this), or\n  seeking a flag that skips the gate.\n\nDetail: `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-12T0820Z-edge-dev-claude-production-queue-blocked-on-repairs.md` §0 item 2 and §5.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T03:22:10Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T08:29:30Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2852,"title":"Structural admission gate refuses do-block migrations (blocks #2744/#2818)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:13:41Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2852"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: workflow\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nThe `automatic-production-promotion` job in\n`.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml` declares `contents: read`\n(line ~977 as of main `da9ff0c6`) but its *Re-prove current main, guarded merge,\nand durable exact-head verdict* step calls `--resolve-admitted-issue-for-pr`,\nwhich creates a `db-coordination admission` git object. That needs\n`contents: write`, so the step fails:\n\n```\nREFUSED: GitHub command failed: gh: Resource not accessible by integration (HTTP 403)\n```\n\n## Why this is urgent\n\nIt fails **after** the preview apply has already succeeded, so the run shows\n`preview success` with production `skipped` — which reads like a deliberate skip\nrather than a defect. And it fails **before** *Write immutable automatic review\nevidence*, so no `review_run_id` / `review_artifact_digest` is ever produced —\nwhich the **manual** governed production path also requires.\n\n**One line blocks production by BOTH routes, for every migration.** Issue #2482\nis blocked on exactly this, and #2662 Part A is waiting behind it.\n\n## Notes\n\n- Two traps in the failed log: the `ENGINEER ACTION REQUIRED: main moved after\n  preview` lines are **echoed script source**, not fired errors — check\n  `origin/main` before believing them.\n- The activation gate PASSED; automatic promotion is **not** dormant.\n- Leave `contents: read` at lines 106 and 1322 alone — different jobs.\n- This is `repo-maintenance`, NOT orchestrator work (AGENTS.md §0.0-C).\n\nDetail: `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-12T0820Z-edge-dev-claude-production-queue-blocked-on-repairs.md` §0 item 1.\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T04:44:57Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T08:29:29Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2851,"title":"Production promotion job cannot write its own evidence (contents: read)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:13:44Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2851"},
{"body":"Part A of #2662, separated so the parent can stay open for its deferred scope.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 40\nchange_type: grant\nservice_class: standard-application\napplication_return_to: u2giants/shared-db\nlive_assertion: a Data API request as anon or authenticated against ai_sentinel_cleanup_log, dam_search_documents, dam_search_synonyms or scanner_ai_ignores is refused, while the service-role Edge Function insert into scanner_ai_ignores continues to succeed\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table public.ai_sentinel_cleanup_log\n  - table public.dam_search_documents\n  - table public.dam_search_synonyms\n  - table public.scanner_ai_ignores\nreads:\n```\n\n`public.ai_sentinel_cleanup_log`, `public.dam_search_documents`, `public.dam_search_synonyms` and `public.scanner_ai_ignores` each have RLS enabled with zero policies, yet grant full `ALL` to both `anon` and `authenticated`. This revokes both role grants and re-asserts RLS.\n\nThere is no behavioural change today — an empty policy set already denies both roles — but the grant is the real control surface, and one permissive policy added later would silently expose all four tables to every browser caller. `service_role` and `postgres` bypass RLS and are untouched.\n\nImplemented by PR #2815 under lane claim #2812, migration version `20260911225108`.\n\n**Deliberately out of scope:** the definer views and materialized views in the same finding. They can break live applications and carry a business judgement for Albert. They remain open under #2662.\n\nThis issue exists because the guarded merge requires a pull request to close exactly one work issue, and #2662 must not be closed while Part B is outstanding.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T17:02:57Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T06:03:44Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2848,"title":"Revoke anon/authenticated DML grants on four public tables with RLS enabled and zero policies (2662 Part A)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:13:46Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2848"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\n```\n\n## What happened\n\nThree `guarded-migration-merge` runs on PR #2814 (issue #2802) failed with:\n\n```\nREFUSED: outcome classified event did not read back exactly\n```\n\nRuns: 34676361001, 34676536810, 34676659552.\n\nThe **write succeeded every time**; only the read-back failed. `advanceOutcome` posts the comment, then immediately re-lists comments to verify. GitHub comment listing is eventually consistent, so the verification raced its own write (posted 05:49:21, threw 05:49:23).\n\n## The wedge\n\n`assertOutcomeTransition` runs *before* the post and reads the same stale list, so it did not see the first `classified`. Each retry therefore appended **another** `classified` with a different `event_id`.\n\nIssue #2802 now carries:\n\n| time | event | id |\n|---|---|---|\n| 01:12:46 | entered | `90afb0a3780a0c3d` |\n| 05:49:21 | classified | `319acf9b45c1f182` |\n| 05:52:21 | classified | `fdac51c049bb2af9` |\n\n`outcomeHistory` dedupes by `event_id`, not `event_type`, so these are not caught as duplicates. The second instead trips `index <= highest` and pushes:\n\n```\nclassified repeats or moves backward from classified\n```\n\nThat makes `history.valid === false`. `requireAdmission` (`manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:5578-5580`) throws `outcome history is invalid` before doing anything, so **every future `--acquire-merge` on #2814 refuses**. Its recovery loop only advances `entered` and `classified`, so no forward event can clear it.\n\n**There is no repair verb.** The only outcome flags are `--outcome-status`, `--advance-outcome`, `--complete-outcome`. `--reconcile-flow` operates on `refs/db-preview-ready-outcomes`, not the issue-comment ledger. Editing or deleting a coordination comment is audit-history tampering and was not done.\n\n## Impact\n\nPR #2814 is permanently unmergeable despite being fully approved (two verdicts at `refs/db-review-verdicts/2802-2814-f773ba7d...`, carried forward to head `8d217d08`) with all required checks green. No merge lock was orphaned.\n\nIssue #2848 (PR #2815) was subsequently wedged the same way, and every remaining work issue in the queue has an empty ledger, so this defect gates the entire remaining merge queue rather than two pull requests.\n\n## Suggested fixes\n\n1. **Make the pre-check authoritative** — have `advanceOutcome` treat a post-then-missing read-back as *possibly succeeded* and retry the read with bounded backoff before throwing, as the `--claim` dispatch path already does (`lanes.mjs:5765-5775`).\n2. **Idempotency** — derive `event_id` deterministically from `(issue, state)` so a re-post collapses instead of duplicating.\n3. **A governed repair verb** that appends a `refused`-result superseding event (the parser already skips `event.result === 'refused'`) rather than requiring comment deletion.\n\nFix 1 prevents recurrence; fix 3 is needed to free #2814 and any issue already wedged.\n\nImplemented by PR #2849.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T16:06:56Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T05:54:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2847,"title":"Outcome ledger wedges permanently after a duplicate lifecycle event (#2802 / PR #2814)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:13:48Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2847"},
{"body":"Filed by the shared-db orchestrator (marker #2758) from two independent governed reviews on 2026-09-11.\n\n## The defect\n\nWhen a branch is refreshed from main (merge or rebase) after its evidence pair was written, `.agent/contract.json` and `.agent/completion.json` keep the OLD `head_sha` and `base_sha`, while the recorded check results stay presented as current. A reviewer at the real head cannot treat any of those results as proof, because they were measured somewhere else.\n\nBoth PRs under review right now carry it:\n\n- PR #2825 (issue #2796), head `478c391b56b20c4a7dad1b7bded4afe971cbc159`, base `54e1e3c62fc5615de2297e5e12cfd397be598ae4`. Pair records head `7663fe04`, base `bfdb19c9`. Raised as a **High** finding; slot 1 returned REVISE partly on this.\n- PR #2842 (issue #2843), head `f2dc4dae50c424f52e6a1beacc09041a284d8ec6`, base `54e1e3c6`. Pair records head `8925a072bb218c77074168a1c479434db547c6a9`, base `bfdb19c9`, with test counts (536/57/1/6) measured at that earlier head. Raised as **Medium**.\n\nTwo different lanes, same failure, so this is structural rather than one lane being careless.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThe pair is the lane's own evidence. An evidence pair that names a head nobody is reviewing is worse than an absent one, because it reads as coverage. In both reviews the logic description was accurate — only the currency was false, which is exactly the shape that survives a skim.\n\n## What is NOT the fix\n\nDo not relax the reviewer expectation, and do not have reviewers ignore the mismatch. They were right to flag it.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nA check that refuses when `.agent/completion.json`'s `head_sha` is not the commit under test, and when `contract.json`'s `base_sha` is not the merge base. The pair already has to be regenerated at the final head after any refresh (AGENTS.md already requires a separate evidence commit); nothing enforces it.\n\nNote the ordering trap: the evidence commit itself becomes the new head, so the check must compare against the implementation commit it describes, not against itself.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T17:24:51Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T02:58:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2845,"title":"Agent evidence pairs are anchored to a superseded head after a refresh","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T17:24:51Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2845"},
{"body":"## What happened\n\nDrawing reviewer slot 2 for issue #2796 / PR #2825 at head `478c391b56b20c4a7dad1b7bded4afe971cbc159` refused twice with:\n\n```\nREFUSED: release of refs/db-coordination/author-acquisition could not be proved after atomic deletion;\nRECOVERY REQUIRED: refs/db-coordination/author-acquisition expected SHA <sha>\nUse the guarded recover-author-mutex.yml procedure and do not retry blindly\n```\n\n**The draw had actually succeeded.** Both of these exist and are correct:\n\n- `refs/db-review-assignments/2796-2825-478c391b...-slot2` -> grok-4.6\n- `refs/db-review-active-v2/grok-4.6/2796-2825-478c391b...-slot2`\n\nAnd `git ls-remote origin refs/db-coordination/author-acquisition` returns **empty** — the mutex was deleted successfully. Only the post-deletion *verification read* failed.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThe refusal is indistinguishable from a genuine orphaned mutex. It tells the operator to run a recovery workflow that is not needed, and its \"do not retry blindly\" warning is correct advice attached to the wrong diagnosis. An operator who believes the message either runs an unnecessary guarded recovery, or retries and risks a duplicate draw.\n\n## Evidence it is not a stale single read\n\nTwo consecutive attempts refused with **different** expected SHAs (`e80197b8...`, then `93edaf49...`). Each attempt created and deleted its own mutex, so this reproduces rather than being one unlucky race.\n\n## Probable cause, not yet confirmed\n\nThe first slot-2 attempt failed differently — on the request budget:\n\n```\nreviewer operation 'reviewer-operation' exhausted its derived 25-request budget\nbefore request 24 (2 held back as the mutex-release reserve)\n```\n\nThe release path is documented as costing 3 requests while the reserve is 2, and the comment at `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:1739` records slot 2 as *measured* at 23 of 25. So the release proof appears to be getting squeezed out at the end of an operation that now costs more than the derivation assumed.\n\n## What NOT to do\n\nDo not widen `REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT`. Per #2075 it is derived, not a default, and #2697 already shows the correct response is to re-measure and remove a redundancy rather than pay for it. The fix is either to re-derive the slot-2 cost from a written measurement, or to make the release verification distinguish a confirmed absence (HTTP 404) from an unproven read without consuming a request it may not have.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T07:35:29Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T02:46:15Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2844,"title":"Reviewer draw reports RECOVERY REQUIRED after a fully successful slot assignment","updatedAt":"2026-09-25T08:38:24Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2844"},
{"body":"The structural-admission gate's GitHub reads are billed against the **reviewer operation's** 25-request budget, which was derived before that gate existed. Every migration author lane lost the ability to draw a reviewer.\n\nVerbatim refusal, exit code 2 read unpiped:\n\n```\nREFUSED: GitHub command failed: reviewer operation 'reviewer-operation' exhausted its\nderived 25-request budget before request 24 (2 held back as the mutex-release reserve). This\nceiling is DERIVED for this operation, not a global default: see the derivation cited beside its\nconstant in scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs. Re-derive it from a written measurement\nrather than widening it (issue #2075)\n```\n\n**Cause.** `admitIssue` runs inside the same request-accounting wrapper `assignNextReviewer` installs, so admission's reads — the PR, the issue, the file list, file contents at the exact head, the closing-issue link — are charged to the reviewer draw. `REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT = 25` was derived in `docs/verification/reviewer-assignment-api-budget-2026-08-28.md` for a draw with **no admission step**; it predates `scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission.mjs` (landed in `e7bec2fe`). The gate is behaving correctly — it refuses to take the mutex unless the whole protected section still fits. The refusal fires at the entry gate, so nothing is stranded: no lease, no mutex, no reviewer spent.\n\n**Ruling.** Move admission **outside** the reviewer operation's request accounting. Admission is not reviewer work and its cost does not belong against a reviewer mutex reserve. Do **not** widen the ceiling and do **not** touch the reserve — the constant carries an explicit instruction to re-derive from a written measurement, and #2075 exists to stop exactly that shortcut. Widening it would silence a guard rather than fix the defect.\n\n**Why the obvious implementation is wrong.** The budget wrapper encloses the entire mutex section, so simply relocating the call site would also strip admission's mutex-ownership proof. Admission must stay in the same place, in the same order, under the same held mutex, refusing identically — only the accounting moves. That also matches every other admission call site (`acquireAuthorLane`, the guarded merge gate, preview preparation), which already run it with no reviewer budget installed.\n\nFixed by PR #2842.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T15:18:14Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T01:28:35Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2843,"title":"Admission is billed to the reviewer request budget, so no lane can draw a reviewer","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T15:20:20Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2843"},
{"body":"`dam.style_guide_file` carries **no table-level grant anywhere in the migration history**, unlike every other `dam` table an application reads, and the only written record of the exposed PostgREST schema list names `public, graphql_public, api, crm, pim, core, app` â€” **no `dam`**. The committed generated types likewise contain `core` and `public` and no `dam` section.\n\nIf both hold, #2802's `has_talent_likeness` column will land in production **correct and unreadable**: the migration will look finished while the value stays out of reach of PopDAM. That is the reason this is filed separately rather than folded into #2802 â€” a lane that widened its own scope to chase it would have been wrong, and the risk must not be lost when #2802 closes.\n\n**Important limit on the evidence above.** The #2802 lane confirmed only the *written record*, not the live setting. The schema-exposure comment it read is dated 2026-08 and omits `dam`, but a comment is not the setting.\n\n### First step, before any migration is written\nRead the **live** exposed-schema value from the running configuration, and read the actual grants on `dam.style_guide_file` on production. Do not settle either question from a comment or from migration history alone. It is entirely possible PopDAM reaches this table through the service role, a `public` view, or an RPC â€” all live patterns in this repo for `dam` tables â€” in which case no change is needed and this issue closes as verified-not-required.\n\n### If a change IS required\nIt is a `grant` and/or schema-exposure change and stays on this route. It must not be folded back into #2802, whose migration is already open as PR #2814.\n\n### Admission fields\n`application_return_to`, `live_assertion` and `generated_types` are deliberately **not** declared yet: the correct `live_assertion` depends on which access path the live reading establishes, and it is compared **verbatim** against production evidence after the fact. The orchestrator writes all five once the investigation above reports. Do not invent them, and do not edit this block â€” classification is the orchestrator's under AGENTS.md Â§0.0-C.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 300\ndepends_on: 2802\nchange_type: grant\nservice_class: standard-application\nwrites:\n  - table dam.style_guide_file\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T14:56:48Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T01:18:51Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2841,"title":"Confirm PopDAM can actually read dam.style_guide_file.has_talent_likeness (grants and schema exposure)","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T14:56:48Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2841"},
{"body":"Re-running `scripts/check-exact-head-approval.mjs` against a merged PR does **not** tell you whether that merge was authorized. Its answer changes after the fact, driven by records written after the merge — so it cannot serve as an audit path, and it currently misleads anyone who reaches for it as one. I did exactly that tonight and drew the wrong conclusion.\r\n\r\n**Worked example — PR #2746, head `39be641f`.**\r\n\r\nAt merge time the gate PASSED, twice (pre-flight and re-proven under the merge lock):\r\n\r\n```\r\n22:31:35Z Exact-head approval carried forward: PR #2746 head 39be641f… has the same pull request\r\ndiff as approved head a0110723…, so its merge-from-main refresh needs no new review\r\n(1 approval(s), 1 pinned assignment(s)).\r\n```\r\n\r\nToday the identical check REFUSES that head, exit 2:\r\n\r\n```\r\nREFUSED: head 39be641f… has no durable APPROVE artifact; … an APPROVE cannot be carried forward\r\nbecause this head has reviewer records of its own (assignment, return or verdict), so it is judged\r\non those alone\r\n```\r\n\r\nNothing about the merge changed. A reviewer assignment was written at that head at **22:48:40Z**, sixteen minutes AFTER the 22:32:17Z merge (`sequence=2510 reviewer=glm-5.3`), which trips the `ownAssignments.length` clause and permanently closes the carry-forward path the merge had lawfully used. That later review could not record at all: `review target is no longer the exact open PR head`.\r\n\r\n**Why it matters.** The refusal reads as \"this merge was never authorized,\" which is false and alarming. I posted that conclusion on #2478 before proving it wrong from the merge run. Anyone auditing a past merge — during an incident, most likely — hits the same trap.\r\n\r\n**Suggested fix.** Add an audit mode that evaluates against the records **as they stood at merge time** (bounded by the merge commit's timestamp, or by the merge run's recorded status), and make the ordinary path refuse outright on a closed/merged PR with a message pointing at that mode, rather than returning a misleading live verdict.\r\n\r\n**Do not change the live gate's conservatism to achieve this** — the refusal above is correct behaviour for an open PR. This is an additional, separate read path.\r\n\r\nNote the invocation, which is itself a trap: the script reads `PR_NUMBER` and `REQUESTED_SHA` from the **environment** and accepts no `--pr`/`--head-sha` flags; passing flags yields `REFUSED: PR number is unavailable`, which is operator error and says nothing about the PR.\r\n\r\nFound while investigating #2837; a distinct defect from the missing minimum slot count.\r\n\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\r\nroute: repo-maintenance\r\nservice_class: maintenance\r\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\r\npriority: 60\r\n```\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-24T03:01:05Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T00:58:56Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2839,"title":"Re-running the exact-head approval gate on a merged PR is not a sound audit","updatedAt":"2026-09-24T03:01:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2839"},
{"body":"`Documents-only merge authorization` publishes a FAILURE status that is not in main's required contexts, so it cannot block any merge. It is guaranteed red on every code and migration PR, and everyone correctly learns to ignore it — which is the worst state for a check to be in, because a genuine failure there is indistinguishable from the routine one.\n\n**Evidence.** On PR #2746 head `39be641f` the check was a FAILURE and the combined commit status read `\"state\":\"failure\"`, yet the PR merged legitimately at 22:32:17Z. Main's required contexts (readable, `enforce_admins` enabled) list `Migration author lease`, `Migration guarded merge authorization`, `Orchestrator marker guard` and others — **not** this one. Its own message is explicit: `Lightweight authorization refused; guarded code checks required`.\n\nIt is currently red on at least #2746 and #2808, and every lane tonight has had to be told individually that this red is expected — which is an ongoing tax and an invitation to wave through a red that matters.\n\n**Suggested fix — either, not both:**\n1. Make it report NEUTRAL or SUCCESS with an explanatory message when the PR contains code, so red means something; or\n2. Retire it, since the guarded path already enforces the real requirement.\n\nDo **not** add it to the required contexts — it is designed to refuse code PRs, so requiring it would block every migration.\n\n**Do not weaken or delete any other check to resolve this.** Found while investigating #2837; not the same defect and should not be fixed as part of it.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: ci\npriority: 60\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-15T19:07:46Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T00:58:55Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2838,"title":"Documents-only merge authorization is permanently red and cannot block anything","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:14:01Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2838"},
{"body":"## The merge gate has no minimum slot count — one approval can satisfy it\n\n**Proved on PR #2746 (issue #2478), which merged to production-bound main with exactly one reviewer approval.** This is not a bypass and not a lane error: the Guarded Merge workflow ran and passed. The gate itself is blind.\n\n### What happened\n\nMerge run `34654341789` (`guarded-migration-merge.yml`, `workflow_dispatch`), merge commit `26d9345b`, merged 22:32:17Z. The gate ran twice — pre-lock at 22:31:35Z and post-lock revalidation at 22:32:13Z — and both printed:\n\n> Exact-head approval carried forward: PR #2746 head `39be641f…` has the same pull request diff as approved head `a0110723…`, so its merge-from-main refresh needs no new review (**1 approval(s), 1 pinned assignment(s)**).\n\nOne approval. One assignment. Gate satisfied.\n\n### The defect\n\n`check-exact-head-approval.mjs` line 237 iterates `latestBySlot.values()` — it demands an APPROVE for every slot **it can see from pinned assignments**. There is no minimum slot count anywhere in the file: a grep for `REQUIRED_SLOT`, `requiredSlots` and `< 2` returns nothing.\n\nAcross all nine heads of `2478-2746` there is not one `-slot2` ref in **any** namespace — assignment, replacement, return, or verdict. All nine durable verdicts are `slot=1`. Slot 2 was never drawn, so the gate could not see it, so nothing ever required it.\n\nThe file's own comment already names this failure class — *\"a slot this gate cannot see is a slot it cannot require\"* — but for a **returned** slot. A **never-drawn** slot reaches the identical blind spot from the other side, and nothing in the file covers that direction.\n\n### Why this is systemic\n\nAGENTS.md requires two independent reviewers at the exact head. The gate enforces \"every slot that happens to exist approved\", which equals two only when two were drawn. Any lane that draws slot 1, never draws slot 2, and reaches the guarded merge gets a green gate on a single review. Nothing warns anyone, and the log line reads like success.\n\n### What NOT to do\n\n- Do not weaken or delete any existing check to reconcile this.\n- Do not treat carry-forward as the bug. It behaved correctly here: the comparison is the PR diff **against its base**, and a merge-from-main refresh moves the base too, so an identical diff over differing trees is the intended case.\n- Do not retro-close #2478. The merged bytes are real and reviewed by one reviewer; the gap is authorization coverage, not correctness of the SQL.\n\n### Suggested fix\n\nGive the gate a required minimum slot count from the same source AGENTS.md uses, and make a missing slot a refusal naming the slot number — so a never-drawn slot 2 fails loudly instead of being invisible. Precedent exists for the shape: `reviewer_cannot_read_repository` is a non-fault terminal code minted for exactly one wrapper-capability gap, so the tooling already distinguishes \"cannot\" from \"failed\".\n\n### Known consequence for #2478 / PR #2746\n\nSlot 2 cannot be completed against the merged PR. Drawing would be accepted (`reviewTargetEligible`, lines 4005–4032, admits a merged PR whose merge commit is proven in main by ancestry), but `recordReviewVerdict` (line 2277) requires `live.state === 'open'` and an exact head match, which a merged PR fails permanently. A draw would burn a reviewer sequence and strand a lease the release path (line 4654) also cannot free. Finishing it legitimately needs a fresh PR carrying the same migration.\n\nFiled by the shared-db orchestrator (marker #2758). Evidence gathered by the #2746 lane, which refused four times to promote on the single verdict and was right to.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: ci\npriority: 90\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T15:38:05Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T00:42:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2837,"title":"Merge gate has no minimum slot count: one approval satisfied it on PR #2746","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:14:03Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2837"},
{"body":"`returnIssueToOwner` files the returned copy into the SAME repository when `return_to` names this repo, and the already-returned guard does not catch the copy. The result is an endless cycle: each generation is re-flagged by `--queue-audit` as `NOT ORCHESTRATOR WORK â€” REJECT`, and returning it mints the next generation.\n\n## Proof, one full cycle already completed\n\n| original (CLOSED) | copy now OPEN and re-flagged |\n| --- | --- |\n| #2619 | #2692 |\n| #2620 | #2691 |\n| #2621 | #2690 |\n\nEach copy's body begins `Returned from u2giants/shared-db#<n> by the shared-db orchestrator.` and carries `Original issue: https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/<n>`. All three copies are open, all three carry `work_type: source-data`, `route: source-data-session`, `return_to: u2giants/shared-db`, and tonight's `--queue-audit` lists all three as REJECT awaiting `--return-issue`.\n\n## Why the guard misses\n\n`returnIssueToOwner` copies the original body wholesale into the new issue, scope block included, so the copy is indistinguishable from a fresh reject. The already-returned check reads **comments**:\n\n- the marker is commented on the issue being returned (the original), and\n- the marker is written into the **body** of the new copy.\n\nSo the copy has the marker in its body and nothing in its comments, and the guard passes. Validation at line 703 only checks that `return_to` matches an `owner/repo` shape; nothing rejects this repository's own slug.\n\n## Not simply a bad address\n\nThe same-repo address appears deliberate. The returned-issue text states the work belongs to \"the session working in this repository\", which is consistent with `source-data-session` being a session inside this repo rather than another repo. So the fix is not to forbid a same-repo `return_to` without deciding that question first.\n\n## Requested fix\n\nWhoever picks this up should decide between two shapes rather than patching the symptom:\n\n1. If a same-repo return is legitimate, the copy must be marked so it is **not** re-admitted â€” e.g. the copy carries the marker somewhere the guard actually reads, or its scope block is rewritten so `--queue-audit` stops classifying it as an orchestrator reject.\n2. If it is not legitimate, `return_to` must be rejected when it names this repository, and these issues need a real forwarding address.\n\nPlease do **not** weaken or delete the reject classification or the already-returned guard to make the audit pass. The audit is correct that these issues do not belong to the orchestrator; the defect is that returning them does not move them anywhere.\n\n## Immediate handling\n\nDo not run `--return-issue` on #2690, #2691 or #2692. Tonight's orchestrator is leaving all three open and commenting each one, rather than minting a third generation.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\n```\n\n\n\n---\nEdited to add `change_type: repo-maintenance` to the db-work-scope block; the reviewer-assignment gate refuses a repository-maintenance issue without one. No other text changed.\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T07:01:53Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T00:18:54Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## What happens\n\nOn the from-empty ephemeral replay, a migration whose effect is DROPping a routine is silently undone when an older migration that redeclares that routine lands in pass 2.\n\nConcretely, found while delivering #2794 (PR #2821):\n\n- `20260911225801` drops `plm.import_master_data(jsonb,jsonb)`. It applies cleanly in pass 1 and the function is genuinely gone.\n- `20260723183000_step11_bounded_production_forward.sql` does not replay from empty, so it lands in **pass 2, which runs after every pass-1 migration**, and its body redeclares `plm.import_master_data`.\n- The function is therefore present at test time, and the absence contract in `supabase/tests/licensing_write_authority_guard_contracts.sql` failed.\n\n## Why the repair does not catch it\n\n`scripts/check_pass2_routine_supersession.py` repairs exactly this class of ordering damage, but only for routine **definitions**: it snapshots the later definition and restores it after the pass-2 file runs.\n\nA drop leaves **no definition to snapshot**. The repair has no way to represent \"this routine must be absent after the later migration\", so there is nothing to restore and the pass-2 redeclaration stands.\n\nCompounding it, the script also reported this routine as unproven and therefore not snapshotted at all:\n\n```\nplm.import_master_data: 20260802170000_plm_import_preserve_curated_licensor_property_status.sql, 20260817124545_licensing_write_authority_guard.sql\n```\n\n## Why it matters beyond #2794\n\nThis is not specific to one function. Any future migration that retires a routine by dropping it will be silently reverted on the replay lane if any pass-2 file redeclares that routine. The migrations all report success; only a contract test asserting absence catches it. That is the same failure shape as the `api` grant incident that motivated the grant half of this repair.\n\n## Suggested direction\n\nTeach the supersession snapshot to express absence as well as definition -- e.g. when a proven later migration drops a routine an older pass-2 file declares, emit a guarded `drop function if exists` into the restore statement, alongside the existing `create or replace` restores.\n\n## Workaround in place\n\nPR #2821 does not touch the harness (it is outside that issue's allowed paths). It conditions the absence assertion on its precondition and records the resurrection with an explicit notice naming this mechanism. Still-present-as-the-#1090-stub remains a hard failure there.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 70\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T17:17:48Z","createdAt":"2026-09-12T00:03:09Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACoQNUrw","name":"bug","description":"Something isn't working","color":"d73a4a"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2833,"title":"Pass-2 order repair cannot express a dropped routine, silently resurrecting it","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T17:17:48Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2833"},
{"body":"## The problem\n\n`docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json` carries a single repo-wide `call_site_count` and a `call_site_sha256` digest over **every** discovered call site. `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` recomputes both across `scripts/` and `.github/workflows/` and fails the \"Tools offline tests\" check on any drift.\n\nConsequence: **any** pull request that adds or removes a line matching the tracked pattern (`missing`, `never created`, `not applied`, `NOT_DERIVABLE`, `_created_by_applied_dynamic_ddl`) in those trees must edit this one file. The count and digest are global, so two such PRs cannot both be correct at once — whichever lands second is forced to recompute, regardless of whether the changes overlap in any real sense.\n\nOn 2026-09-11 **eight open pull requests** touched this file: #2826, #2825, #2821, #2810, #2795, #2750, #2749, #2738. Delivering #2611 required taking an explicit coordinator-granted slot on it, ahead of two lanes already being sequenced against each other for the same file.\n\nThis is not a false-alarm report. The guard is doing its job and the dispositions it forces are valuable. The problem is purely the **shape of the artifact**: one global counter plus one global digest, serialising every unrelated lane behind a shared file.\n\n## What is NOT being proposed\n\n- Not weakening or relaxing the guard.\n- Not adding a blanket regenerate/`--update` flag. The absence of one is deliberate: each call site requires a hand-written disposition with a substantive reason, and a bulk regenerate would let new sites through unreviewed. That would defeat the guard while leaving it green.\n\n## Why this needs a design decision\n\nThe tension is real and not resolvable inside a single delivery lane: the guard's value comes from forcing per-site human review, while its current artifact shape forces unrelated lanes into conflict. Possible directions exist (per-file or per-directory digests, dispositions stored beside the code they describe, a merge-friendly record layout), but choosing among them needs someone with the whole picture of how the throughput guard is meant to evolve. Recording the contention accurately here rather than picking one.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: ci\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 40\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\nFiled from the #2611 prepack-exclusion lane, which hit this while adding 11 legitimate call sites.\n\n\n---\n\n**Correction (filing error, mine).** I filed this issue from the #2611 lane and I got the scope block wrong: I listed the audit file under `reads:`. That list takes database object kinds only, and for `repo-maintenance` work both `writes:` and `reads:` must be empty, so the block was rejected as malformed and this issue read as broken in the queue audit. The file is a repository document, not a database object; it belongs in the prose above, which is where it now stays. Scope block corrected to match #2820 and #2817. The substance of the report is unchanged.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T17:10:59Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:59:06Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2832,"title":"Throughput truth-audit count and digest are a global bottleneck every concurrent PR must edit","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T17:11:58Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2832"},
{"body":"The reviewer allocator can draw a provider whose wrapper is structurally incapable of emitting the verdict line the recorder requires. The draw succeeds, a sequence and a lease are spent, and the slot can then never be satisfied. Two PRs are deadlocked on this tonight and a third is suspected.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 60\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\n## The capability gap is real and provable in both directions\n\n`ai-muse` cannot produce a governed verdict:\n\n- `/c/repos/ai-devops/bin/ai-muse` contains **zero** occurrences of `governed-verdict`.\n- Its own `REQUIRE_VERDICT` grammar (line 316) accepts only `^VERDICT:[[:space:]]+(FINDINGS|NO FINDINGS)`, and its `review` subcommand (lines 462-464) injects that same instruction.\n\nThe recorder requires something that grammar cannot express. `verdictFromOutput` in `scripts/run-governed-review.mjs` accepts exactly one terminal line of the form `VERDICT: APPROVE|REVISE|REJECT <40-hex-head-sha>`. `FINDINGS` / `NO FINDINGS` is discarded.\n\nOnly two wrappers are given the flag. `wrapperVerdictContractArgs` (`scripts/run-governed-review.mjs:170`):\n\n```js\nconst name=wrapperBaseName(wrapper)\nif(!['ai-gemini','ai-qwen'].includes(name))return args\n```\n\n## The allocator cannot see that fact\n\nThe selector's eligibility predicate (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:4294`) is:\n\n```js\nconst notTaken=(row)=>eligibleNames.has(row.name)&&(concurrentLeases||!busy.has(row.name))&&row.name!==excludedProvider&&!exclusions.has(row.name)\n```\n\nIts four terms are orchestrator independence, `ai-review-preflight` usability, live-lease busyness, and durable exclusions. **There is no capability term.** `wrapperVerdictContractArgs` is exported from `run-governed-review.mjs` only to its own test file; `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` never imports it (the sole textual match is a comment at line 2282). The roster rows in `REVIEWERS` carry `wrapper`, `readsRepository` and `readsRepositoryVerified` — no verdict-capability field.\n\n`ai-review-preflight` cannot supply it either. Its decision (line 233) is:\n\n```sh\nif [ \"$healthy\" = 0 ] && [ \"$state\" = registered ] && [ \"$(printf '%s' \"$admission\" | jq -r .state)\" != backoff ]; then usable=true; else usable=false; fi\n```\n\nThree inputs, no capability dimension. And `config/reviewer-registry.json` has only three field names across every provider entry — `registry_state`, `reason`, plus the top-level `version`/`providers`/`description`. Accordingly `ai-review-preflight usable muse` returns exit 0 / `\"usable\":true`, so Muse passes `notTaken` and is drawn.\n\n## Evidence: this repeats, it does not self-heal\n\nPR #2814 (issue #2802) drew Muse three consecutive times — sequences 2511 @ `2f194ec5`, 2512 @ `027ebc2b`, 2517 @ `a66b50ac`. Moving the head produced a third Muse cursor rather than rotating past it.\n\nPR #2738, independently, holds two leases at head `79a4e9ef`: **sequence 2519 `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` in slot 1**, sequence 2520 `grok-4.6` in slot 2. Slot 1 can never satisfy `check-exact-head-approval.mjs`, whose refusal reads `REFUSED: head 79a4e9ef... has no durable APPROVE artifact; a review that wrote no artifact never authorizes a merge`. PR #2825 is parked behind #2738. A third data point is suspected but unproven and is recorded here as UNKNOWN: an earlier #2738 attempt failed at 21:34Z with `reviewer gemini-3.8-flash-high holds no active lease at all`, read at the time as lease timing.\n\n## No sanctioned route exists to clear it honestly\n\n`--replace-failed-reviewer` requires a `--failure-code` from `TERMINAL_FAILURE_CODES` (line 564):\n\n```js\nexport const TERMINAL_FAILURE_CODES = Object.freeze(['insufficient_quota','provider_unavailable','local_dependency_unavailable','wrapper_terminal_failure','turn_limit_cancelled','reviewer_cannot_read_repository'])\n```\n\nMuse has not failed. It is healthy, registered and allocatable; it simply lacks the flag. Every available code would be a misdescription. `replaceFailedReviewer` additionally refuses to spend a rotation slot until an operator names a failing check and states the fault is unfixable on this machine — correctly, since no fault occurred. Reviewer exclusions never clear and would strand the issue permanently.\n\n## The precedent that names the fix\n\nThis exact class of problem was already solved once, for a different capability. `recordReviewVerdict` refuses on a pure wrapper property (line 2252):\n\n> `This is a property of the wrapper: no retry and no re-run can satisfy it.`\n\nand the comment above `TERMINAL_FAILURE_CODES` states the dedicated code exists\n\n> `so the recovery route this tool NAMES is one an operator can actually run, instead of forcing a misdescription as wrapper_terminal_failure.`\n\nSo `reviewer_cannot_read_repository` is a **non-fault** terminal code minted specifically to express a wrapper-capability gap. There is no sibling for \"cannot emit a governed verdict.\"\n\n## Requested fix\n\n1. Give the roster a verdict-capability fact (mirroring `readsRepository` / `reviewerReadsRepository`) sourced from the same list `wrapperVerdictContractArgs` consults, and add it as a term in `notTaken` so a governed review never draws a provider that cannot record one.\n2. Add a non-fault terminal code — e.g. `reviewer_cannot_emit_governed_verdict` — with a replacement-command helper mirroring `nonReadingReviewerReplacementCommand`, so an already-spent slot can be redirected without asserting a fault that did not occur.\n3. Until (1) lands, treat a Muse draw for a governed review the way a non-reading reviewer's verdict is treated: as **absent** rather than as a refusal, which the code at 2425-2437 argues is the recoverable choice.\n\nFiled from the #2802 lane. Nothing was manufactured to clear either PR; both are held as reviewer-blocked.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n\nScope block: added change_type (required by reviewer admission). Posted by Claude chat 7545365a-8132-4fd6-b0a1-f737035df839 on edge-dev\n","closedAt":"2026-09-24T12:16:47Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:58:05Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2831,"title":"Reviewer allocator can draw a provider that cannot emit a governed verdict, deadlocking the slot","updatedAt":"2026-09-24T12:16:48Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2831"},
{"body":"work_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\n\n## The gate has no valid evidence path for repo-maintenance work\n\nThe `Agent work contract` check (`.github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml`) validates a\npull request's `.agent/contract.json` against an **immutable contract published to a git ref\nbefore the work began**:\n\n`scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs`, `verifyGitEvidence`:\n\n```\nconst published = validateContract(io.readPublishedContract(report.contract_ref))\nif (contractHash(published) !== contractHash(contract)) throw new GitEvidenceError('checked-in contract does not match the immutable contract published before the work')\n```\n\n`readPublishedContract` fetches `refs/db-contracts/<work_issue>/<generation>` from origin.\n\nThat ref is created when work is **dispatched as a structural migration-author lane**. Work that\narrives as repo-maintenance -- a defect fixed directly in the repository, with no migration and no\nauthor claim -- is never dispatched that way, so no such ref exists and none can be created\nafterwards without **fabricating pre-work evidence after the fact**. The gate is therefore\nunsatisfiable for this class of work by any honest route.\n\nThe existing escapes do not cover it either: the documents-only exemption (#2591) requires every\nchanged file to be prose, and the grandfathering config is a fixed activation list. A\nrepo-maintenance change to a script or workflow qualifies for neither.\n\n## Evidence: five open pull requests, all red on this check\n\n- #2825 -- repo-maintenance fix for #2796 (stored preview instruction omitted `mode=apply`)\n- #2818\n- #2821\n- #2823\n- #2826\n\nThis is a systemic gate misapplied to non-lane work, not a defect in any one of these changes.\n\n## What is NOT wanted\n\nDo not weaken, bypass or delete the check, and do not widen the documents-only exemption to\ncover code. The gate is doing real work for structural lanes, where the pre-published contract\nis the whole point. What is missing is a defined, honest evidence path for repo-maintenance --\nor an explicit classification that exempts it the way prose-only changes are exempted, decided\ndeliberately rather than by each lane inventing a workaround.\n\nFiled from the #2796 lane after declining to manufacture a contract ref to make the check pass.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 85\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T18:15:08Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:51:47Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2830,"title":"Agent work contract has no valid evidence path for repo-maintenance work","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T18:15:08Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2830"},
{"body":"Filed by the shared-db orchestrator's dispatched agent (marker #2758) while working #2426.\nThis is reviewer-infrastructure repair, **not** orchestrator work — filed and left.\n\n## The failure\n\nGrok's **evidence publication** fails with:\n\n    sandbox evidence head differs from invocation\n\nwhen Grok is run from a worktree that carries **another session's untracked files**.\n\nThe review itself is not the problem — the failure lands at the point where the sandbox\nevidence is published, because the head the sandbox computed does not match the head recorded\nat invocation once foreign untracked files are present in the tree.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nA reviewer that produces a verdict it cannot publish is, to the queue, a reviewer that\nproduced nothing — the verdict never becomes durable review evidence. The lane then has to\ndraw a replacement, which consumes scarce reviewer capacity for a purely local cause.\n\n## What this issue asks for\n\nMake the evidence head insensitive to untracked files that belong to no session's change set,\nor make the failure name the actual cause — foreign untracked files in the worktree — so the\noperator can clear them instead of guessing that the reviewer or the head is broken.\n\n## Explicitly out of scope\n\nSuppressing the evidence-head check, publishing evidence bound to a head the sandbox did not\nactually review, or retiring Grok from the rotation. The check is doing something real; it\njust misattributes its cause.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 60\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-23T02:44:04Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:47:15Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2829,"title":"Grok evidence publication fails: sandbox evidence head differs from invocation on foreign untracked files","updatedAt":"2026-09-23T02:44:04Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2829"},
{"body":"Filed by the shared-db orchestrator's dispatched agent (marker #2758) while working #2426.\nThis is reviewer-infrastructure repair, **not** orchestrator work — filed and left.\n\n## The failure\n\nThe **GLM OpenCode local server is down on this machine**, so GLM cannot be drawn as a\nreviewer here. Its own `server restart` **refuses** — restart is not a usable recovery path\nfrom a stopped server.\n\n## Why the doctor does not catch it usefully\n\nThe reviewer doctor (`reviewerExecutionPreflight`) only **probes the endpoint**. It correctly\nreports GLM as unavailable, but it **cannot start the server**. So the preflight refusal is\naccurate and is doing its job — it just leaves the lane permanently short one reviewer until\na human or a maintenance session intervenes.\n\n## The repair\n\n    ai-glm server start\n\n`server start` is the working repair. `server restart` is not — it refuses when the server is\nalready down.\n\n## What this issue asks for\n\nMake the down-server case recoverable without guesswork: either have the doctor's refusal\nmessage name `ai-glm server start` as the repair, or have the startup path handle a\nstopped server so `restart` is not a dead end.\n\n## Explicitly out of scope\n\nRemoving GLM from the reviewer rotation, weakening `reviewerExecutionPreflight`, or having\nany tool post a verdict GLM did not produce. The capability must be repaired, not bypassed.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\npriority: 60\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-18T14:53:35Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:47:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2828,"title":"GLM OpenCode local server is down; server restart refuses and cannot recover it","updatedAt":"2026-09-19T02:11:36Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2828"},
{"body":"Filed by the shared-db orchestrator's dispatched agent (marker #2758) out of the closure of\n#2426, to keep a policy risk from being lost inside a closed issue.\n\n## The risk\n\n`core.taxonomy_source_ref.source_licensor_id` deliberately records **who attributed a row**,\nnot **who owns the entity now**. When a character is re-licensed, the character moves to the\nnew licensor but the provenance row's stamped licensor deliberately stays at the **old** one.\n\nThis is intentional and is asserted by contract **D7d** in\n`supabase/tests/character_alias_and_source_provenance_contracts.sql` (lines 854-877), which\nfails if a freshness-only update silently re-derives `source_licensor_id` from the\nre-licensed target.\n\n## Why it needs its own issue\n\nAn independent reviewer (Muse Spark 1.3) flagged during the #2426 adjudication that this is a\n**policy judgement, not a mechanical fact**. Nothing in the schema forces a consumer to read\nthe column the way it is meant.\n\nIf royalty reporting — or any downstream consumer — ever reads `source_licensor_id` as\n*current* ownership, that becomes a real royalty bug: royalties would be attributed to the\nlicensor that originally supplied the name rather than the licensor that now owns the\ncharacter. The failure would be silent, exactly like the one #2426 existed to prevent.\n\n## What this issue asks for\n\nEstablish and document the authoritative reading of `source_licensor_id` — attribution\nprovenance, never current ownership — so that no reporting consumer can adopt the wrong\nreading by default, and so that the correct reading survives as a stated contract rather than\nas a test assertion nobody outside this repo reads.\n\nThis is **not** a request to change the column's behaviour. The behaviour is correct as\ndesigned and contract D7d should keep enforcing it.\n\n## Explicitly out of scope\n\nReopening #2426, or any change to the delivered alias/licensor protection in\n`20260911152203_character_alias_provenance_forward_repair.sql`.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: documentation\npriority: 55\n```\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T15:38:08Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:47:12Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2827,"title":"Royalty risk: source_licensor_id is attribution provenance, not current ownership","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:14:19Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2827"},
{"body":"Two governance holes in the db-work queue, found while repairing the #2543 -> #2357 dependency stall on 2026-09-11. Both are documentation/tooling gaps in this repository, not structural database work.\n\n## Hole 1 — no sanctioned command writes a scope block's `status:`\n\n`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` only ever **parses and validates** a `db-work-scope` block (`parseQueueScope`). Every `io.updateIssue(...)` call in that script targets a **claim** issue body (`request.claim` / `options.claim`) for lease version and object-list maintenance. There is no code path anywhere that writes `status:` on a db-work issue.\n\nConsequence: the `blocked` -> `ready` transition — the single most consequential edit in the queue, the one that makes work dispatchable — is today an **unaudited hand edit** via `gh issue edit --body-file`. It takes no mutex, gets no read-back, leaves no machine-readable trail, and cannot be distinguished after the fact from any other body edit. Compare `--complete-work`, whose entire design premise is that a caller must not be able to assert a release by hand.\n\nA hand edit is also demonstrably error-prone. The one recorded precedent: an attempt to update #2212's scope with `gh issue edit --body $updated` failed because PowerShell expanded the multiline body into separate arguments (`invalid issue format: status: ready`); a follow-up `gh api` attempt failed because the CLI output had become an array rather than one string (`HANDOFF.d/2026-09-04T2053Z-edge-dev-codex-priority-12-orchestrator.md`, section 4 item 2, line 71). No remote change occurred that time. A partially-applied body edit is the failure mode this has no guard against.\n\nSuggested shape (for the repo session to decide, not prescribed here): a guarded `--set-scope-status --issue <n> --status <ready|blocked|owner-decision> --reason <text>` that takes the mutex, re-parses the block, refuses a `ready` transition whose `depends_on` are not all satisfied by `merged` / `owner-ruling-recorded` completion records, writes exactly the one field, reads the body back, and comments an audit line.\n\n## Hole 2 — the operating manual gives no guidance for `--complete-work`\n\n`--complete-work` is the ONLY publishing path for a `db-work-completion` record, and a missing record is what stalled #2357 for a day. The manual's entire coverage of it is one bare command line in `docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md` line 144. Nothing documents:\n\n- the **report file's JSON schema** — `schema_version`, `work_issue`, `outcome`, and the conditional-required fields per outcome (`pr` + `merge_sha` + `migration_versions` for `merged`; `ruling_url` + `resolved_by` for `owner-ruling-recorded`; `reason` for `returned` / `cancelled` / `superseded` / `failed`);\n- which outcomes actually **release** a dependent (`merged` and `owner-ruling-recorded` only);\n- that `ready-for-merge` must NOT carry a `merge_sha`;\n- that `merge_sha` must be GitHub's `merge_commit_sha` (the squash commit), never the branch head;\n- that the record is **immutable** — there is no correction path, so a wrong first record is permanent;\n- a worked example of a report file.\n\nThe practical result is that sessions reach the end of merged work, find no instructions, and write prose instead. That is exactly what happened on #2543, which closed on 2026-09-10 carrying only \"PRODUCTION APPLY DONE\" where the record belonged — after the 2026-08-23 grandfather cutoff, so it got no pass, and #2357 stalled behind it.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- A documented, guarded command writes a scope `status:` field, with an audit trail; hand editing a scope block is no longer the sanctioned route.\n- `docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md` (or its successor) documents the `--complete-work` report schema, the per-outcome required fields, which outcomes release dependents, immutability, and one worked example.\n\n## Routing\n\nThis is **not** orchestrator work. Per AGENTS.md 0.0-C and the 2026-08-21 owner ruling (#1366), `repo-maintenance` exits `repo-session`: a separately started repository-maintenance session owns it end to end. Do not dispatch it to a lane. It ships no migration and claims no database object.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 120\ndepends_on:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T08:17:41Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:18:26Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2824,"title":"Queue governance: no sanctioned writer for scope status, and no manual guidance for --complete-work","updatedAt":"2026-09-25T11:38:17Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2824"},
{"body":"A migration that belongs to a **different Supabase project** appears in the production drift checker as ordinary promotable work, because no record names it as out-of-scope. Nothing currently prevents a future session from applying it to the shared production database.\n\n## What was found\n\nDuring the #2699 investigation (2026-09-11) the sixteen \"missing from production\" migrations were classified. Twelve were already live and three were deliberately held — but one belongs to a **different database entirely**: the `hts_rag_split` schema work, which per #2403 targets the **DesignFlow non-prod Supabase project**, not shared production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\n\nThe drift checker compares merged migrations against the production ledger. A migration that was never *meant* for production is absent from that ledger for a legitimate reason, but the checker cannot tell that apart from a migration that is genuinely overdue. Both present identically as \"merged, not applied\".\n\n## Why this is the #2699 failure pointed the other way\n\n#2699 was opened because closed claims were being read as delivered. This is the mirror image: a migration that is correctly absent is read as *undelivered work waiting to be promoted*. The consequence is worse than a stalled queue — acting on it would apply schema to a database it was never reviewed against.\n\nNote that #2403 is CLOSED, so an operator checking the issue would see finished work and no warning. Closure is not a signal here.\n\n## What is needed\n\n1. A way to mark a merged migration as **not production-scoped**, naming its actual target project, so the drift checker excludes it and says why.\n2. The `hts_rag_split` migration recorded under that marking, citing #2403.\n3. The checker to report such entries in a separate, clearly-labelled section rather than omitting them silently — an invisible exclusion is its own hazard, and a future reader must be able to see the claim and challenge it.\n\nDo **not** implement this by deleting or hard-coding a skip for the one version. The gap is that the checker has no concept of migration target, and a one-off skip leaves the next cross-project migration in exactly the same trap.\n\n## Verification note for whoever takes this\n\nProve the exclusion can fail before trusting it: feed the checker a known in-scope migration and confirm it is still reported. An exclusion mechanism that silently swallows everything looks identical to one that works.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\npriority: 150\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","closedAt":"2026-09-12T01:24:07Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:08:44Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2820,"title":"Drift checker lists a DesignFlow-only migration as promotable, so it can be applied to the wrong database","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:14:20Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2820"},

{"body":"Registry entry needed so PR #2808 (issue #2797) can clear the `SQL migration guards` check.\n\n## What happened\n\nThe #2797 lane dispatched the preview apply **before** merging, following the orchestrator step order. The repository rulebook requires the opposite — merge first, then rehearse on preview from merged main — and warns that a preview-apply performed before merging permanently red-checks the pull request. Preview run `34655606553` succeeded and wrote version `20260911221304` into the preview ledger, so the guard now refuses the PR as an already-applied version. The rehearsal cannot be re-run.\n\nThis is a process fault in the step order, not a defect in the migration. The guard is behaving exactly as designed.\n\n## Why registration rather than supersession\n\nRegistering in `scripts/historical-migration-restorations.mjs` lets the guard distinguish \"the exact applied bytes\" from \"an edit to an applied version\" — which is precisely the case here. Superseding at a newly reserved version would require a fresh claim (this claim's version is spent) and would discard a clean APPROVE for no safety gain.\n\nSame-day precedent: #2798 (for #2744) and #2768 (for #2535). In every case the entry was added under its own separate issue, never by the authoring lane inside its own PR — which is why the #2797 lane correctly refused to self-register, and why this issue exists.\n\n## Values (computed by the #2797 lane)\n\n- file: `supabase/migrations/20260911221304_db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql`\n- previewProject: `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs`\n- previewApplyRun: `34655606553`\n- dispatch and applied commit: `916b8005f4588ece389f1f137faf651bd78ef0a2`\n- fileSha256: `ecc847f602358edb27829cc49faba86b58e3788b6cf98c702eaccf8b8527904d`\n- statementBytes: `55149`\n- statementSha256: `a9171a6023e724b677655db8d89e572f4394ad8c1b4db41d37a52438b492d20e`\n- objects: `function api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory`\n\n**Omit `sourcePr` and `sourceMergeCommit`**, so this grants no production eligibility. Re-verify every digest independently against the file at that commit before writing the entry; do not copy these values on trust.\n\n## Consequence to plan for\n\nThis changes a non-`.agent` file, which voids the carried APPROVE on PR #2808 and forces a fresh exact-head governed review before merge. That is expected, not a regression.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 200\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","closedAt":"2026-09-14T15:34:19Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:02:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2817,"title":"Register historical restoration for 20260911221304 (db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:14:24Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2817"},

{"body":"## Defect\n\n`scripts/production_migration_guard.py` books a table's schema move as a **removal at the start of the statement**, then reads that **same statement's own qualified table name** as a later reference to an object that is now missing. Any migration that archives a table by moving it therefore self-flags, and the whole-batch preflight blocks it.\n\nFirst hit: preview run **34653889672** (issue #2482, PR #2779, migration `20260911210844_retire_erp_items_to_archive.sql`), which failed at \"Hard guard preflight\" with:\n\n```\nBLOCKED: whole-batch preflight failed; the batch cannot run end to end:\n  20260911210844 references missing public.erp_items_current (alter table); it was DROPPED (or renamed away) by 20260911210844 and not re-created -- would abort the batch (42P01 undefined_table / 42883 undefined_function). Adding versions to the allowlist cannot fix this: either 20260911210844 is referencing the wrong name, or 20260911210844 should not be in this batch.\n  20260911210844 references missing public.erp_items_raw (alter table); ...\n```\n\nThe SQL is correct: the full migration set replays green from an empty database in CI (run 34651929781).\n\n## Local reproduction\n\nFor a single statement `alter table public.erp_items_current set schema archive;`:\n\n```\nobject_events:          [(0, 'public.erp_items_current', False), (1, 'archive.erp_items_current', True)]\nhard_reference_events:  [(12, 'public.erp_items_current', 'alter table')]\n```\n\n`object_events` emits the removal at `SET_SCHEMA_RE.match.start()` (offset 0, the `alter` keyword), while `hard_reference_events` records the statement's own qualified name at `match.start(1)` (offset 12). `preflight_batch` sorts both streams by position, so the removal is consumed **before** the statement's own reference, and the reference is judged against a catalog state from which the table has already been withdrawn.\n\n## Proposed fix (one line of ordering, no weakening)\n\nRecord the SET SCHEMA removal at the statement's **end** rather than its start (and the new qualified name immediately after), so the statement's own name is judged while the object still exists. Patched locally at runtime against the real migration: both problems clear and no other object's ordering changes.\n\nThe guard must keep refusing genuinely missing references â€” that will be proved with a negative control alongside the archive case.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1\nchange_type: repo-maintenance\n```\n\nReclassified from `structural` to `repo-maintenance`: this ships no migration and changes no\ndatabase shape — it repairs a static checker under `scripts/`. A structural scope must name\ndatabase objects it writes, and this change writes none. Its routed exit is therefore\n`repo-session`: a repository session owns it, and it takes no migration lane or version.\n\nFiles: `scripts/production_migration_guard.py`, `scripts/test_production_migration_guard.py`.\n\nBlocks #2482's preview and production apply.\n\nðŸ¤– Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T12:29:10Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T22:30:16Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2809,"title":"Preflight guard self-flags any archive-a-table migration: a schema move is booked as a removal before the statement's own table reference is read","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T12:29:10Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2809"},

{"body":"Add a nullable boolean field `has_talent_likeness` to `dam.style_guide_file`.\r\n\r\nThe field belongs on the app-owned style-guide asset/file row, not on `core.property` or `core.character`. It must remain nullable: TRUE means the source explicitly indicates talent likeness, FALSE means the source explicitly indicates no likeness, and NULL means the source did not expose a determination. Do not infer the value from a filename; preserve the raw source filename/label separately. No production or data backfill is authorized by this intake request.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 40\r\nchange_type: column\r\nservice_class: standard-application\r\napplication_return_to: u2giants/popdam3\r\nlive_assertion: a PopDAM read of a style-guide file returns has_talent_likeness as true, false or null exactly as stored, with null distinguishable from false\r\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table dam.style_guide_file\r\n  - column dam.style_guide_file.has_talent_likeness\r\nreads:\r\n  - table core.style_guide\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-15T19:51:04Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T21:24:49Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake.
