{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nchange_type: function\nservice_class: standard-application\napplication_return_to: u2giants/shared-db\nlive_assertion: an authenticated Licensing Manager call to api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory returns paged inventory rows for entity kind property, character or style_guide, with Disney, Marvel and Star Wars as separate licensors and no matching, review or contract fields in the payload\ngenerated_types: not-applicable\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 100\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory\nreads:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties\n```\n\nThe production DB Data Admin page currently uses `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties`, whose response mixes raw scrape inventory with matching, contract, and authority-review classifications. That makes a read-only inventory page show extra review buckets, including DCP rows in misleading sections, and leaves no clean source contract for the requested Characters and Style Guides tabs.\n\nAdd one read-only, licensing-manager-gated, paged inventory RPC for the Data Admin application. It must accept an entity kind (`property`, `character`, or `style_guide`), search text, cursor, and bounded page size. Return a stable normalized row shape containing: row key; entity kind; source-declared licensor key/name; source purpose normalized to exactly `Creative` or `Submissions`; display label; source system/table/id/status; latest-seen/capture marker; and, for Creative property rows only, the existing mapped/unmapped indicator. Do not return matching controls, review reasons, decision guidance, contract status, or authority-derived presentation buckets.\n\nDisney, Marvel, and Star Wars must be separate licensors based on the actual scrape route/source authority. Preserve the raw evidence when one source record appears in more than one scrape route; do not deduplicate across licensors or infer identity from names. The inventory must cover all currently supported licensors and all retained source-declared Property rows already covered by the existing RPC, plus all available source-declared Character and Style Guide rows. A licensor/entity/purpose combination with no rows may be absent from the payload; the UI will render both Creative and Submissions sections for every licensor present in the selected tab.\n\nKeep `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties` unchanged for the existing Property Matching workflow and current dependents. Preserve licensed-data privacy, authenticated-only execution, the Licensing Manager gate, deterministic pagination, and the current 8-second request budget. Do not weaken or bypass #2744's performance repair or collide with its live claim.\n\nAcceptance must prove representative all-licensor coverage, exact Disney/Marvel/Star Wars separation, both purposes, entity-kind validation, search/paging, stable identity including source system, grants/security/search path, no private row content in public evidence, preview apply, independent exact-head review, merge, production apply, and authenticated production RPC checks. This issue is the structural dependency for the owner-requested Data Admin UI repair: Scraped Properties becomes inventory-only, Property Matches is renamed Property Matching, filter state is scoped to each section, and Characters/Style Guides tabs are added.\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T17:21:32Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T20:06:55Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Problem\n\n`--prepare-preview-dispatch` stores a preview dispatch instruction with no `mode`, so running it produces a dry run rather than an apply. Nothing reports this until the production gate refuses.\n\nThe `shared-supabase-migrations.yml` input `mode` defaults to `dry-run`. Dispatching exactly the stored instruction therefore runs a silent preview dry run, which uploads only a `preview-migration-dry-run-<sha>` artifact.\n\nOnce the automatic production risk policy is active, the production apply needs a `preview-migration-apply-<sha>` artifact. It refuses in \"Derive business risk from governed artifacts\" when `test -n \"$PREVIEW_RUN_ID\"` fails. That step exits with only \"Process completed with exit code 1.\" and no REFUSED message.\n\n## Evidence (#2741 / PR #2743)\n\nThe stored instruction came from `node scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --prepare-preview-dispatch 2741`, as ready ref `refs/db-preview-ready/b8d817cf319c4d5b78c9bdb7c3dbd539c352d617ff36f469099bfe647eb6f542`, with route `merged_rehearsal`:\n\n```json\n\"manifest\": {\n  \"target\": \"preview\",\n  \"preview_allowlist\": \"20260911152203\",\n  \"commit_sha\": \"120fb6125907386ce2b93bd9ae0a91de700fb738\",\n  \"merged_preview_source_pr\": \"2743\"\n},\n\"manifest_digest\": \"ae58482e05a77f077bd90a53539bced1b2f7dd3d767730d1009567bea5dd43d1\"\n```\n\nRuns:\n\n- **34633793571**: preview dispatched exactly as stored. It succeeded, but only as a dry run; its only artifact is `preview-migration-dry-run-120fb612…`.\n- **34635518461**: production apply. It failed in \"Derive business risk from governed artifacts\" because no preview-apply run or digest existed. Nothing was applied.\n- **34636081308**: the same manifest plus `mode=apply`, on main 153b7754. It succeeded with artifact `preview-migration-apply-153b7754…`.\n- **34636608231**: production apply using run 34636081308's evidence. It succeeded.\n\n## Proposed fix\n\n1. **Producer:** for every write route (`ordinary_preview_apply`, `merged_rehearsal`), include `mode: \"apply\"` in the stored manifest, and therefore in the manifest digest.\n2. **Validator:** in `scripts/orchestrator-flow/reconcile.mjs` (the manifest completeness check, around lines 16-22), refuse a write-route manifest without `mode === \"apply\"`. Add a case to `reconcile.test.mjs`.\n3. **Workflow:**\n   - In `shared-supabase-migrations.yml`, refuse `merged_preview_source_pr` / `merged_preview_source_pr_map` when `mode != apply`. A post-merge rehearsal is described as an apply, so a dry run there is never what the caller meant.\n   - Give the `test -n \"$PREVIEW_RUN_ID\"` / `$PREVIEW_ARTIFACT_DIGEST` checks REFUSED messages that name the missing input, as the `source_pr` check already does.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\npriority: 200\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T12:28:57Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T19:08:39Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2796,"title":"Stored preview dispatch instruction omits mode=apply, so the rehearsal silently dry-runs and production refuses","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T12:28:57Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2796"},

{"body":"## Problem\n\nThe GitHub Actions installation token runs out of API quota once about ten pull requests are active. When that happens, production applies fail on \"API rate limit exceeded\", even though nothing is wrong with the change being applied.\n\n## Cause\n\n- The cross-PR collision job reads every open PR's file list twice, once for the source check and once for the object check. It also reads every PR's timeline.\n- Guarded merge runs the object collision check twice: once before taking the lock and once under it.\n- The author-lane queue audit lists open issues more than once, and reads PRs that touch no migrations.\n- A quota exhaustion fails immediately, even when the quota resets a few minutes later.\n\n## Fix (tracked PR)\n\n1. One shared read of open-PR file lists for both collision checks. Timelines are read only for PRs that actually overlap.\n2. Drop the duplicate pre-lock collision run. The under-lock run stays.\n3. The lanes audit lists issues once and reads only PRs that touch migrations.\n4. The transport gets one bounded wait on a primary quota exhaustion: at most 15 minutes, and only when a reset time is stated. It fails closed otherwise. Every other 403 still fails at once.\n5. The production gate gets the same bounded wait, but only before taking the lane. With the lane held, it fails fast.\n6. A quota preflight step before heavy API work, plus cancel-superseded concurrency on PR workflows that lacked it. It is not added to any workflow that holds a lock.\n\nNo safety check is weakened, and collision detection finds exactly the same conflicts.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-11T18:09:27Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T16:29:20Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2785,"title":"Actions installation API quota runs out at ~10 active PRs and fails production applies","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:45:32Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2785"},
{"body":"Follow-up to #2712 (PR #2765, migration 20260911124845).\n\nThe migration creates four roles as NOLOGIN on purpose, so no password lives in this public repo:\n\n- designflow_hts_prod_worker\n- designflow_hts_alsand_worker\n- designflow_hts_prod_runtime\n- designflow_hts_alsand_runtime\n\nBefore designflow-backend can connect as these roles, credentials must be provisioned through a governed, non-repo path:\n\n1. Decide which roles actually need LOGIN (the runtime roles may be reached via SET ROLE from an existing login instead).\n2. Generate passwords into 1Password vault vibe_coding (secrets-to-1password), never in chat, SQL files, args, or logs.\n3. Apply `ALTER ROLE ... LOGIN PASSWORD` through an approved production path that does not commit the secret; if none exists, design one first.\n4. Verify with pg_roles.rolcanlogin and a connection test, without granting anything to PUBLIC, anon or authenticated.\n\nThe passwords were deliberately not set during #2712.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: security-settings\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 70\ndepends_on: 2712\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T02:39:26Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T15:37:57Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Tracking issue for PR #2782 (repository maintenance, owner-requested).\n\nProblem: production apply run 34615626046 (main `9da98ede`) lost its `SQL migration guards` job on attempt 1 — three historical-recovery tests errored with `OSError: [Errno 39] Directory not empty` while removing their temp git repo. Attempt 2 on the same SHA passed. Git 2.47+ spawns a detached `git maintenance run --auto` after every commit, which keeps writing `.git/objects` during removal.\n\nScope: set `gc.auto=0` and `maintenance.auto=false` in every temp fixture repo in the Python tests. {"body":"## Problem\n\nShared-db coordination can consume up to 25 GitHub API requests for one reviewer assignment or replacement. Multiple authenticated sessions independently repeat the same marker, claim, PR, ref, reviewer-capacity, and CI reads. Polling and retries multiply that traffic against the shared 5,000-request hourly bucket. A fixed author-lane capacity also makes otherwise independent structural work wait even when exact object claims prove it cannot collide.\n\n## Required outcome\n\n1. Remove the numeric author-lane capacity limit entirely. Any number of independently scoped authors may hold leases when their exact read/write claims do not conflict.\n2. Reduce a normal reviewer assignment or replacement to a measured target of 6-10 REST/GraphQL requests.\n3. Eliminate duplicate reads and per-session polling without weakening any safety proof.\n\nRemoving the limit does not remove author leases or the author-lane safety mechanism.\n\n## Scope\n\n- Delete the fixed MAX_AUTHOR_LANES admission ceiling and all full-capacity waiting behavior.\n- Preserve exact database-object read/write claims and conflict serialization. Overlapping writers and writer/reader conflicts must still refuse or wait.\n- Preserve the acquisition mutex, permanent migration-version reservations, owner/branch/workProvider identity, lease recovery, and fail-closed unreadable-state behavior.\n- Keep preview, preview recovery, merge, and production as exclusive single-holder stages.\n- Queue priority remains reporting guidance, not a numeric admission cap.\n- Consolidate mutable PR, issue, head, reviewer-capacity, and eligibility state into one bounded GraphQL snapshot where possible.\n- Use Git transport for immutable coordination refs and commits when it preserves exact evidence; Git transport does not consume REST/GraphQL quota.\n- Stop making explicit quota calls when response headers already provide the same current bucket facts.\n- Add one host-wide single-flight/read-through snapshot so concurrent sessions share identical reads; key by repository and exact head, and invalidate on relevant mutations or events.\n- Replace per-session polling with one event-aware watcher that broadcasts changes. Prefer GitHub webhooks; fallback polling must use authenticated ETags, x-poll-interval, exponential 30/60/120/300-second backoff with jitter, and stop at the reset time after exhaustion.\n- Preserve bounded retries, fail-closed unknown state, mutation serialization, and existing request-count regression tests.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- No numeric author-capacity constant or full-capacity refusal remains in live admission.\n- At least 100 concurrent non-conflicting author claims are admitted in deterministic tests.\n- The 101st conflicting claim is still refused for its exact object conflict, not admitted because capacity is uncapped.\n- Migration versions remain unique under concurrent acquisition and claims survive clock expiry until governed recovery.\n- Preview, merge, and production remain single-holder.\n- Wire-level fixtures state exact request totals for slot-1, slot-2, replacement, idempotent retry, and silent reclaim.\n- Normal assignment/replacement is at most 10 REST/GraphQL requests.\n- Ten simultaneous identical readers cause one upstream read per snapshot generation.\n- Unchanged polling consumes no primary quota when conditional requests return 304.\n- A webhook/event wakes every waiter once; missed delivery falls back safely without a busy loop.\n- Rate-limit exhaustion stops all shared callers until reset instead of allowing independent retries.\n- Existing exact-head, reviewer independence, mutex-race, verdict, rollback, object-collision, version-reservation, stage-exclusivity, and refusal suites remain green.\n\n## Ownership boundary\n\nStart only after PR #2767 lands because it currently owns the protected reviewer manager source. Integrate or supersede its proposed increase from 8 to 24 by removing the cap entirely; do not run competing edits against its active owner. Do not modify marker #2714.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 70\ndepends_on: 2766\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T15:48:35Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T14:43:00Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2773,"title":"Remove the author limit and reduce shared-db GitHub API fan-out","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:15:00Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2773"},

{"body":"## Every code/migration PR is now unmergeable through the guarded lane\n\n**Found driving PR #2755 (issue #2753).** Governed review APPROVE recorded at exact head `f78fd20625cc7db804fdd848a9446feddba4b3c2` (`refs/db-review-verdicts/2753-2755-f78fd206...` -> `74f7957a`); all mirrored required contexts green.\n\nGuarded merge run https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/actions/runs/34600285746 refused:\n\n> REFUSED: failing: Documents-only merge authorization (failure) on the reviewed head. The required list came from the committed mirror, so EVERY reported check must pass. No retry can clear this, so the merge lane was not taken.\n\n### Cause\n- The merge workflow token cannot read branch protection (HTTP 403), so `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs` `evaluateWithoutRequiredList` uses the committed mirror and requires **every reported context** to be green (line 158).\n- Since `documents-only-merge-authorization.yml` went live (first run 2026-09-11T09:12Z, #2715), every non-document PR receives a **failing** `Documents-only merge authorization` check run and commit status (\"Lightweight authorization refused; guarded code checks required\") -- the designed diagnostic for code PRs.\n- Those two rules contradict: the diagnostic that routes a code PR to the guarded lane makes that lane refuse it. Last successful guarded merge: run 34580600370 at 08:43Z, before the workflow existed. No code PR can merge today.\n\n### Deadlock\nA fix (exempt the diagnostic context in half two of `evaluateWithoutRequiredList`, or have the diagnostic report neutral/skipped instead of failure) is itself a code PR and receives the same failing diagnostic from main's workflow, so it cannot merge through the guarded lane either. Clearing it needs owner-level authority (e.g. an owner-approved one-time admin merge of the fix PR). Sessions must not use `--admin` on code PRs without that.\n\nBlocks: #2755/#2753 and poppim-web#5, and every other pending migration PR.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-11T22:40:08Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T12:44:06Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2759,"title":"Guarded merge refuses every code PR: documents-only diagnostic fails the committed-mirror preflight","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:45:40Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2759"},

{"body":"## Requesting app / session\n\nDesignFlow PLM — `popcre/designflow-tracking` (API), `popcre/designflow-frontend` (screens). Plan:\n`plan_prod-tracking-on-time-early-warning.md` on `designflow-tracking` `develop`, **step 2**\n(decisions D11–D15 locked by Albert Hazan, 2026-09-10). This is a STRUCTURE request; the app\nsession will write its own rows (templates, assignments) through the API afterwards.\n\n## Business need (plain English)\n\nProduction Tracking must compute \"Needed By\" dates from the factory lead time of each SKU's\n**product type**. People create **named, described, tagged lead-time templates** in the app and\n**apply them by hand to product types**. One template covers many product types; every product of\nthat type, on every order, inherits it. No automated or fuzzy matching of templates to products.\n\n## Requested structure (names are proposals — orchestrator decides)\n\nTarget schema: the one the app reads for `FactoryTime` — `plm` in the multi-schema map\n(`designflow-tracking/config/table-schema-map.js`: `FactoryTime: 'plm'`); `dflow.\"FactoryTime\"` and\n`dflow_prod` carry identical copies. Orchestrator to decide which copies change.\n\n### 1. `FactoryTime` becomes a template record\n\nToday: `id, product_category, product_subtype NOT NULL, sampling_days, resampling_days,\nmass_production_days, created_at, updated_at` (0 rows in `dflow` and `plm` on production, read\n2026-09-11).\n\nAdd / change:\n- `name text NOT NULL`, **unique** (case-insensitive unique index on `lower(btrim(name))` proposed)\n- `description text NULL`\n- `tags text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` (simple text array; a tag table is overkill for ~30 templates)\n- `updated_by text NULL` (app user email/id of last editor)\n- `product_subtype` → **NULLable** (it no longer describes a template; kept as information only,\n  nothing will match on it). `product_category` unchanged (already nullable).\n- `resampling_days` stays nullable; **drop its DEFAULT 0** so \"empty\" stays empty.\n- CHECK: `sampling_days`, `resampling_days`, `mass_production_days` are NULL or `>= 0`.\n\n### 2. New table: product type → template assignment\n\nOne row per product type; many rows may point at the same template.\n\n| column | type | note |\n|---|---|---|\n| `id` | bigint identity PK | |\n| `mg_category` | text NOT NULL | MG01 `mgCategory` |\n| `mg01_code` | text NOT NULL | Product Type code |\n| `mg02_code` | text NOT NULL | Product Sub-Type code |\n| `factory_time_id` | integer NOT NULL FK → `FactoryTime.id` **ON DELETE RESTRICT** | the DB also refuses deleting an in-use template |\n| `assigned_by` | text NOT NULL | |\n| `assigned_at` | timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() | |\n| `previous_factory_time_id` | integer NULL | value replaced by the latest reassignment |\n| UNIQUE | `(mg_category, mg01_code, mg02_code)` | |\n\nClearing an assignment deletes the row (history of the previous value is kept on reassignment only;\nif the orchestrator prefers a full append-only history table, the app can adapt).\n\n## Key choice: the product type is keyed WITHOUT division — evidence\n\nTaxonomy doc (`docs/business-rules/merchandise-and-product-taxonomy.md`) says codes are scoped by\ndivision and `mgCategory`, and that the same Product Types exist in each current division. Measured\non production `dflow.\"merchGroup\"` (project confirmed via `get_project_url`, read-only, 2026-09-11):\n\n- Active MG02 rows joined to their active MG01 parent (`parent_id`): **119 distinct\n  (MG01 code, MG02 code) pairs, and every pair belongs to exactly one `mgCategory`** — 0 pairs span\n  two categories, 0 null categories.\n- Within a single division, 0 (division, MG01, MG02) combinations are ambiguous.\n- All parent-linked rows (active+inactive): 334 rows across 3 divisions collapse to 120 distinct\n  (category, MG01, MG02) keys. Only 2 keys differ in description across divisions, both cosmetic:\n  Storage/P/B2 \"FAUX SHAPED BOX\" vs \"Faux Shaped Box\"; Storage/P/N2 \"Ottoman Non-Collapsible\" vs\n  \"Ottoman\".\n- **Item division is not reliable enough to scope on:** `itemHeader.div_code_fk` = 2 on 15,185\n  items with `div_code` NULL; id 8 is used for both `CW001` (10 items) and `SP001` (755); in\n  `merchGroup`, `EH001` appears with ids 2 and 9. Scoping the lookup on item division would drop\n  most items for reasons unrelated to their product type.\n\nSo one assignment per `(mg_category, mg01_code, mg02_code)` applies across divisions (matches \"the\nsame Product Types exist in each division\"). The app resolves a SKU by exact match of its\n`udf_merchgroup01`/`udf_merchgroup02` against **active** MG01→MG02 parent-linked rows; if that yields\nanything other than exactly one category, the SKU has **no product type** (never a fallback to code\ntext or descriptions). If a future division gives a pair a different meaning, the resolver refuses it\nand this key must be revisited.\n\n## Not requested\n\n- No data loads. Yuchen's 28 starting templates are application rows created by the app's API\n  (Rule 0.5); nothing is assigned to any product type by a loader.\n- No change to `LicensingTime`, `DesignTeamTime`, `merchGroup` or item rows.\n\n## Verification the app session will run after apply\n\nSandbox (`sandbox-albert` DB): create template, apply to two product types, delete refused while in\nuse (409 from API; FK RESTRICT underneath), SKU with pre-2025 codes shows \"Needs product type\".\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nchange_type: table\nservice_class: standard-application\napplication_return_to: popcre/designflow-tracking\nlive_assertion: production and sandbox-albert expose the named FactoryTime template columns and product_type_factory_time table with exact constraints while FactoryTime remains empty\ngenerated_types: required\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 40\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table plm.\"FactoryTime\"\n  - column plm.\"FactoryTime\".description\n  - column plm.\"FactoryTime\".name\n  - column plm.\"FactoryTime\".product_subtype\n  - column plm.\"FactoryTime\".tags\n  - column plm.\"FactoryTime\".updated_by\n  - table plm.product_type_factory_time\n  - column plm.product_type_factory_time.previous_factory_time_id\n  - index plm.factory_time_name_ci_key\n  - index plm.product_type_factory_time_factory_time_id_idx\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T14:49:08Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T05:01:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2724,"title":"DesignFlow: FactoryTime as named/tagged lead-time template + product type -> template assignment table","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:15:33Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2724"},

{"body":"## Owner instruction (Albert, 2026-09-11, in chat)\n\n> \"i don't want to name or authorize things anymore. just do the job.\"\n\n## Problem\n\nA migration can already be:\n- governed-reviewed at its exact head,\n- merged through the guarded merge,\n- rehearsed on preview right after that merge.\n\nIt still stops before production until Albert names the exact version in chat. #2699 shows the result: sixteen merged migrations are not on production. `20260910155753` (#2579 / PR #2681) is the newest; its post-merge preview run 34559282554 succeeded.\n\nThe owner is not a programmer and cannot evaluate those versions. Per the owner ruling of 2026-08-18 recorded in `shared-db-orchestrator`, *never gate on a human judgement the human cannot actually make*. The naming step is exactly that kind of gate.\n\n## Where the gate lives\n\nThree places:\n- Albert's global instructions: AI sessions are read-only for production until he names the exact resource and action.\n- The production rules in shared-db `AGENTS.md`.\n- The `shared-supabase-migrations.yml` production path, which takes an explicit `production_allowlist` plus a confirmation.\n\n## Wanted\n\nAutomatic production promotion for a migration that has all of:\n- a durable governed verdict at its merged head,\n- a guarded merge,\n- a successful post-merge preview rehearsal,\n- the existing automatic evidence gates.\n\nIt must still:\n- run serially, one at a time,\n- refuse on any failed or missing evidence and escalate to an engineer, never to Albert,\n- keep the production dry run first.\n\nAlbert's global instruction and the repo rules must be updated in the same change, so the documents and the workflow agree. The successor marker #2714 lists this as design/proposal scope; this issue is its durable record.\n\n## Scope\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\nwrites: none\nreads: none\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T13:22:30Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T04:18:47Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2716,"title":"Promote migrations to production automatically after governed review, guarded merge and post-merge preview (no owner naming step)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:15:41Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2716"},
{"body":"## Problem\n\nEvery PR to `main` must have the required status `Migration guarded merge authorization`. Only the `guarded-migration-merge.yml` workflow posts it (line 104), and the migration workflow posts it too (line 1367). A PR that never goes through that workflow stays `BLOCKED` even when every other check is green.\n\nThat includes PRs that change prose only. Example: PR #2713 adds a single `HANDOFF.d/` file. It has 14 checks passing and 4 skipped, but it is `BLOCKED` because that one status was never posted. Orchestrator sessions are forbidden from using `--admin`, so a handoff can be stranded unmerged at session end. That already happened to #2713 when marker #2689 closed.\n\n## Expected\n\nA PR whose changed files are all prose (Markdown, `HANDOFF.d/`, plans, docs) should be mergeable without dispatching the guarded migration merge.\n\nPossible approaches:\n- Have a lightweight workflow post the status as success when the full changed-file list is prose.\n- Or post it from the existing \"Domain ownership\" classifier.\n\nEither way, it must fail closed: any non-prose file means the normal guarded path applies. The fix must not weaken the guard for migrations, scripts, workflows or config.\n\n## Scope\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nobjects: none\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-11T09:15:10Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T04:18:36Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2715,"title":"Docs-only PRs are blocked forever: required 'Migration guarded merge authorization' status is only posted by the migration merge workflow","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:15:43Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2715"},

{"body":"Production target selected by Albert on 2026-09-11: Supabase project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`. This request implements the shared-knowledge boundary in popcre/designflow-backend#94. It does not authorize preview or production apply.\n\nCreate a new governed schema `hts_rag` as the sole shared HTS knowledge surface for Alsand and production. It must carry the complete ten-table contract, including the already-merged debate/promotion additions from migrations `20260902062827` and `20260908202651`. Do not use or silently fall back to the operational `dflow` or `dflow_prod` schemas. The current `public.hts_rag_*` tables are empty and must remain untouched until a separately reviewed retirement decision.\n\nSecurity contract:\n- No PUBLIC, anon, or authenticated access.\n- Separate roles for production read/runtime, Alsand read/runtime, production worker write, and Alsand worker write.\n- Runtime roles may read only qualified operative precedents and required public official evidence.\n- Worker roles may select/insert/bounded-update the shared contract and may not delete audit/evidence rows.\n- Every write carries explicit source-environment provenance; environment is metadata, not authorization.\n- Preserve immutable provider responses and promotion provenance.\n- Do not create a browser/Data API path.\n\nPrivacy contract: allow only normalized decisive facts, product/fingerprint hashes, public official evidence, reviewer outputs, policy/model metadata, source environment/determination id, hashes, promotion/refusal state, and timestamps. Forbid user/customer/licensor identity, RFQ/item ids, prices, attachments, raw chat or unapproved free-form descriptions, auth/session tokens, provider secrets, hidden reasoning, cache telemetry, and unrelated operational history.\n\nApplication return address: popcre/designflow-backend#94. {"body":"Raised as a MEDIUM finding by glm-5.3 in the governed review of PR #2695 at head `7a9d94719c477e3126f8c2ec252d5670f4c73fb8`. Recorded so it is not lost when that PR merges. Not a merge blocker for #2695.\n\nUnder the legacy model a stale lease lived at `refs/db-review-active/<reviewer>` and was implicitly cleared by that provider's next draw (`selectedStale`, ~4168). A v2 ref name embeds the dead head (`reviewActiveRef`, ~2384-2392), so no later draw ever computes that name again.\n\nExisting reclamation paths - verdict release (~2118-2150), exclusion return (~3082-3107), terminal-failure release (~4495-4501), silence reclaim (~3690-3698), replacement (~4576-4600, ~4747+) - none covers head-moved-without-verdict or PR-closed-without-verdict. `busy.stale` (~3570-3576) only classifies. No CLI command reaps review leases; `--cleanup-stale` (~6015) is author-claim cleanup.\n\nEvery abandoned review therefore leaves one permanent ref. At roughly 800 live refs the single GraphQL alias query built at ~1330-1334 exceeds the per-argument exec limit and surfaces as a raw spawn error that `isReviewRefListingRefusal` does not mark, so `findBusyReviewers` (~3543-3550) treats it as transient and every operation reports the generic \"active reviewer leases are unreadable\" - the exact wrong-cause failure the round-2 work was meant to end. At 1000 refs the loud ceiling refusal fires instead.\n\nEither way the end state is a repo-wide stop of every draw, release, replacement, exclusion and capacity report, with no sanctioned tool to retire the refs - AGENTS.md forbids hand-deleting `refs/db-review-active/*`.\n\nThis PR's own head movements are already generating these refs, so the count only grows.\n\nNeeded: a governed reap command for review leases whose PR is closed/merged or whose head has moved, plus classification of the exec-limit spawn error as a determinate refusal rather than a transient one.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 65\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T16:44:31Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T01:21:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2711,"title":"Assignment-keyed review leases have no reclamation path for head-moved or PR-closed-without-verdict","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:15:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2711"},
{"body":"Raised as a MEDIUM finding by glm-5.3 in the governed review of PR #2695 at head `7a9d94719c477e3126f8c2ec252d5670f4c73fb8` (durable verdict `refs/db-review-verdicts/2694-2695-7a9d94719c477e3126f8c2ec252d5670f4c73fb8-slot2`). Recorded here so it is not lost when that PR merges. Not a merge blocker for #2695.\n\nIn `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, the exact-lease gate (~2173-2190) throws before the standing-artifact branch (~2210). `finish()` deletes the v2 lease via `releaseRecordedVerdictLease` (~2118-2150), which on the production `githubIo` has `deleteRef`.\n\nSo the first run records the verdict and releases the lease; an identical re-run - an orchestrator retry after a lost response, which `scripts/run-governed-review.mjs` performs with no existing-verdict pre-check - re-spawns the entire reviewer wrapper and then refuses at the lease gate with \"reviewer does not hold the exact active lease ... draw or replace the reviewer\", for a review whose durable verdict already exists. It fails closed, so nothing is corrupted, but the operator is pointed at a replacement the verdict gate will also refuse, and a full reviewer run is burned each time.\n\nThe code comment at ~2188-2190 claiming \"including the idempotent re-run over a standing artifact\" holds only when the release FAILED; after a successful release that path is unreachable.\n\n`scripts/record-review-verdict.test.mjs` (~15-18) asserts create-only, assignment-bound, idempotent recording. It now passes only because its io fixture has no `deleteRef`, so the release returns false without deleting - the test no longer exercises the production shape.\n\nSuggested fix: check the standing artifact BEFORE the lease gate (the artifact's own `assignment_sha` binding preserves the late/conflicting-verdict guarantee), and give the idempotency test an io with `deleteRef`.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 65\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T19:24:49Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T01:21:47Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Both reviewers of PR #2695 at head `7a9d94719c477e3126f8c2ec252d5670f4c73fb8` raised a HIGH finding that the head delivers undeclared application changes to `apps/db-data-admin/src/lib/property-match.ts` and `apps/db-data-admin/src/PropertyMatchReview.test.tsx`.\n\nIt is a false positive. Both computed the three-dot diff from `aef1504e7c3c7674a6a9709e42720b8f2a725f43`, the PR's ORIGINAL base, and one explicitly asserted that SHA is the merge-base with main. It is not. After the update-from-main merge the merge-base is `5532d2bd401e67af39f0e60c6b08bcd1ebb0723f`:\n\n    git merge-base origin/main 7a9d9471  ->  5532d2bd401e67af39f0e60c6b08bcd1ebb0723f\n    git diff --name-only 5532d2bd...7a9d9471  ->  the 6 declared files only\n    git diff --stat origin/main 7a9d9471 -- apps/db-data-admin/  ->  empty\n\nThose two files arrived from main via commit `a7dc9b3d` (issue #2701, merged as PR #2702) and are byte-identical to main. The repository's own enforced `Agent work contract` check passes at this head, which is the authority the finding predicted would refuse the PR.\n\nConsequence: any PR that is updated from main before review is reviewed against a stale base, so every commit main gained in the interim is attributed to the branch as undisclosed scope creep. That is an automatic HIGH finding on a correct PR, and it recurs on every re-review round, so the PR can never clear. This is the merge-blocking defect behind #2695.\n\nFix: the evidence packet must pin the base the contract declares (`base_sha`), or recompute the merge-base against the current main tip — never reuse the PR's original base.\n\nRelated: #2708 (shared `.agent` evidence paths collide), #2705, #2707.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","closedAt":"2026-09-11T05:12:37Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T01:21:35Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2709,"title":"Governed review packet resolves the wrong base after an update-from-main merge","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:45:45Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2709"},
{"body":"```machine\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repository-maintenance\npriority: 75\n```\n\n**The pattern.** `.agent/contract.json` and `.agent/completion.json` are fixed paths. Every agent-authored pull request writes its own work evidence into those same two files. Confirmed on the three currently open coordination pull requests — #2640, #2684 and #2695 each change exactly those two paths — and on `main`, where the last six commits touching `.agent/` produced eleven changes to them.\n\n**The consequence.** Because the contents are per-pull-request and the paths are shared, any merge to `main` puts every other open pull request into conflict on those files, regardless of whether the two changes have anything to do with each other. Today #2702 merged through the guarded path, correctly and with the exclusive merge lock held, and it immediately conflicted both #2640 and #2695 — on the evidence files only. Neither pull request's actual change overlaps #2702 at all.\n\n**Why this is expensive rather than merely annoying.** Governed reviews are pinned to an exact head. Resolving the conflict moves the head, which voids every durable verdict at the old head and forces both reviewer slots to be drawn and run again. So one unrelated merge costs every other open pull request a full re-review — and while those re-reviews run, the next merge can land and do it again. With more than a couple of pull requests open this does not converge.\n\n**What it is NOT.** This is not a missing lock. `guarded-migration-merge.yml` holds a repository-wide exclusive merge lock and is the only path to `main`; it worked exactly as designed. The lock serializes merges. It does not, and arguably should not, reserve `main` for the duration of a review.\n\n**Asked for.** Give each pull request's work evidence its own path so that two unrelated pull requests cannot collide on it — for example keyed by issue number under a directory, the way the durable contract refs already are. Any scheme where concurrent pull requests write disjoint paths resolves this. The validating checks must move with it, and the evidence must remain exactly as strict as it is now; this is about the filename, never the standard.\n\n**Do not** fix this by freezing `main` during reviews, by relaxing the exact-head review rule, or by exempting `.agent` files from conflict resolution.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 75\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T17:25:01Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T00:56:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2708,"title":"Every pull request writes the same two .agent evidence files, so every merge conflicts every other open PR","updatedAt":"2026-09-24T12:24:51Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2708"},
{"body":"```machine\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repository-maintenance\npriority: 65\n```\n\n**What happened.** Three consecutive `ai-grok-review` runs on PR #2684 (sessions `rev2684c-s2`, `rev2684d-s2`, `rev2684f-s2`) failed identically. The governed runner reported each one as:\n\n`REFUSED: review wrapper did not produce a recordable terminal verdict (exit 1): the provider cancelled without a final answer`\n\nThat message is wrong about the cause. The raw provider stream for every one of the three records:\n\n`\"stop_reason\":\"cancelled\", ... \"numTurns\":20 ... \"cancellationCategory\":\"max_turns_reached\"`\n\nThe reviewer used its entire 20-turn ceiling exploring the repository — roughly 1.5 million tokens per run, most of it re-reading the `supabase/tests` tree — and never reached the point of writing a verdict. The provider was healthy throughout; `ai-review-preflight usable grok` exited zero before and after.\n\n**The defect.** The provider reports `cancelled` at the top level and names `max_turns_reached` one level deeper in the same record. The wrapper's `cancelled` branch fires first and never reads `cancellationCategory`, so the deeper, accurate reason is discarded before the runner ever sees it.\n\n**Why it matters.** \"The provider cancelled\" reads as transient, so the documented response is to retry — which is exactly what produced three identical failures at roughly 1.5 million tokens each. \"The reviewer ran out of turns\" reads as a scope problem, whose response is to narrow the review brief. The operator is steered toward the one action that cannot work. It also invites recording `provider_unavailable` against a reviewer that never failed.\n\n**Asked for.** When the provider reports `cancellationCategory`, surface it verbatim in the wrapper's refusal reason, and distinguish an exhausted turn budget from a genuine provider cancellation in the runner's message. Do not raise the turn ceiling — the ceiling is not the fault, and a wider ceiling would be exhausted by the same unbounded scope.\n\n**Evidence.** Raw stream for the most recent run: `C:\\Users\\ahazan\\.local\\state\\ai-devops\\grok\\isolated-home\\sessions\\...\\01a08ddf-caa6-7b91-8f2d-14638c6a3995\\updates.jsonl`. The other two sessions record the same category. This is machine-local state on EDGE-DEV, not repository content.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 65\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-15T03:22:55Z","createdAt":"2026-09-11T00:41:51Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2707,"title":"Reviewer wrapper reports \"the provider cancelled\" when the real cause is max_turns_reached","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:15:52Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2707"},

{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repository-maintenance\npriority: 60\n```\n\n**What happened, on 2026-09-10.** `--assign-reviewer --issue 2694 --pr 2695 --head-sha 4b80b051cae1b3e0e16be20e7b41329af48da10e --review-slot 1` drew `gemini-3.8-flash-high` / `ai-gemini` as sequence 2261. At that same moment `ai-review-preflight usable gemini` exited 3 with `{\"provider\":\"gemini\",\"status\":\"quarantined\",\"failure_class\":\"live-qualification-required\",\"registry_state\":\"registered\",\"usable\":false}`, and `ai-gemini doctor` exited 3 reporting `QUARANTINED agy=1.2.0 ... live-qualification=required`.\n\nThe orchestrator skill states the rule plainly: a provider may be assigned only when `ai-review-preflight usable <provider>` exits zero, and the selector must skip gemini unless it does. The allocator did not apply that rule, so `run-governed-review.mjs` refused at its own preflight after the slot was already consumed.\n\n**Why this matters.** The draw burns a sequence and occupies the slot with a provider that cannot run. Recovering needs the terminal-failure release path plus a replacement draw, which is heavier than simply not allocating an unusable provider. It also pushes the operator toward `--release-failed-reviewer ... local_dependency_unavailable --confirm-local-dependency-unfixable`, which records a failure against a reviewer that never actually failed.\n\n**Asked for.** Make the allocating selector consult the same reconciled preflight answer that `run-governed-review.mjs` consults, and skip an unusable provider at draw time rather than at run time. {"body":"## Business rule\r\n\r\nDisney OPA's Property picker exposes two views for the same route and authenticated account:\r\n\r\n- `Show Compliant Only` is the current-rights subset and may be offered for new styles.\r\n- `Show All` additionally contains non-compliant Properties. OPA does not distinguish never-held rights from formerly-held rights.\r\n\r\nNon-compliant Properties must remain stored and linked to historical styles, but must be inactive for new-style selection and must not be newly introduced into ColdLion. A later compliant observation may reactivate selection. Absence from `Show All` is not deletion authority.\r\n\r\nThe first private two-view evidence was captured on 2026-09-10 in `u2giants/licensor-source-data` PR #72. The private rows remain there; this public issue intentionally contains only the contract and aggregate-safe behavior.\r\n\r\n## Current gap\r\n\r\n`plm.opa_property_scope_membership` is append-only by route and capture, but has no compliance field. Its existing `approval_status` records review of evidence and must not be reused as a rights status. The 2026-09-10 capture has not been loaded into the database.\r\n\r\n## Required structural result\r\n\r\n1. Add a required, constrained source-observation field to `plm.opa_property_scope_membership`, named `compliance_status`, with exactly `compliant` and `non_compliant` for new two-view captures. Preserve prior rows without inventing historical compliance; use an explicit `unknown` legacy state if the additive migration requires a value.\r\n2. Keep status route- and capture-specific. Do not put a single mutable flag on `plm.opa_property`, because rights can differ by branch, line of business, product type, and time.\r\n3. Define current status from the newest approved complete observation for the exact route. `compliant` permits new-style selection; `non_compliant` blocks new-style selection while preserving the Property, existing ColdLion identity, and historical style relationships.\r\n4. Update `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text,text,integer)` and every current-rights consumer discovered through dependency inspection so non-compliant membership is not treated as present licensing authority. Keep non-compliant source rows visible to appropriately authorized data administration.\r\n5. Provide a private, guarded loader contract for the four PR #72 capture files. Loading the licensed rows remains a separate source-data operation and is not authorized by this structural issue.\r\n6. Add tests for compliant, non-compliant, reactivated, legacy-unknown, multi-route, and incomplete-capture cases. No absence-based deletion or deactivation is allowed.\r\n\r\n## Marvel boundary\r\n\r\nMarvel product submissions and current submission rights moved to Disney OPA, so Marvel OPA Properties use this same field. Marvel ASGARD separately exposes lifecycle/priority categories for creative style guides, including out-of-circulation guides, but those are guide-library states—not equivalent Property-rights evidence—and must remain source-native.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 70\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - column plm.opa_property_scope_membership.compliance_status\r\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties\r\n  - function plm.finalize_opa_property_compliance_capture\r\n  - function plm.guard_opa_property_compliance_capture\r\n  - function plm.guard_opa_property_compliance_membership\r\n  - index plm.opa_compliance_capture_route_time_idx\r\n  - index plm.opa_compliance_membership_capture_idx\r\n  - table plm.opa_property_compliance_capture\r\n  - table plm.opa_property_current_compliance\r\n  - table plm.opa_property_scope_membership\r\n  - trigger opa_compliance_capture_guard on plm.opa_property_compliance_capture\r\n  - trigger opa_compliance_capture_truncate_guard on plm.opa_property_compliance_capture\r\n  - trigger opa_compliance_membership_guard on plm.opa_property_scope_membership\r\n  - trigger opa_compliance_membership_truncate_guard on plm.opa_property_scope_membership\r\n  - view plm.opa_property_current_compliance\r\nreads:\r\n  - table plm.opa_property\r\n  - table plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution\r\n  - table plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\nExact constraints covered by the claimed parent tables (the allocator has no separate constraint object kind):\r\n- constraint opa_compliance_capture_pkey on plm.opa_property_compliance_capture\r\n- constraint opa_compliance_capture_key_key on plm.opa_property_compliance_capture\r\n- constraint opa_compliance_capture_shape_ck on plm.opa_property_compliance_capture\r\n- constraint opa_compliance_capture_counts_ck on plm.opa_property_compliance_capture\r\n- constraint opa_compliance_capture_status_ck on plm.opa_property_compliance_capture\r\n- constraint opa_compliance_capture_approval_ck on plm.opa_property_compliance_capture\r\n- constraint opa_compliance_membership_status_ck on plm.opa_property_scope_membership\r\n- constraint opa_compliance_membership_capture_fk on plm.opa_property_scope_membership\r\n- constraint opa_compliance_membership_shape_ck on plm.opa_property_scope_membership\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-11T18:44:59Z","createdAt":"2026-09-10T23:54:34Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2703,"title":"HANDOVER: add route-specific OPA compliant/non-compliant rights status","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:15:59Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2703"},
{"body":"## Problem\r\n\r\nIlona Kereki and Laura Arevalo cannot load **Property Matches** in production. The page reports only `The review queue could not be loaded.` after a fresh sign-out/sign-in. Screenshot supplied privately by the owner on 2026-09-10.\r\n\r\nRead-only production evidence from the existing admin-only user directory confirms both active accounts currently carry the `licensing` role and active `plm` app access. The live page succeeds for Albert and returns five pending rows. This is therefore not fixed by granting either person Administrator.\r\n\r\n## Root fault boundary\r\n\r\nThe browser starts `api.db_data_admin_property_match_queue` and the complete `api.opa_property_reconciliation` lookup in one `Promise.all`. Any PostgREST failure from the supporting OPA lookup discards the successful queue too. Supabase errors are plain objects, while the component only extracts a message from `Error` instances, so the real database error is replaced with the generic sentence shown in the screenshot.\r\n\r\n## Required repair\r\n\r\n1. Reproduce with a current Licensing-only + PLM principal and capture which browser request and safe database error code fails.\n2. Repair the application read path. Keep `api.db_data_admin_property_match_queue` Licensing-manager-gated and preserve all existing decision/write authorization and append-only controls. Do not grant Administrator or broaden raw licensed-source access.\n3. Do not let an optional OPA-name lookup erase an otherwise valid review queue. Surface a safe, actionable stage/error code without licensed row values.\r\n4. Add regression coverage for a Licensing + PLM user, including queue rows, candidate names/full OPA selection, and unchanged denial for a user without the Licensing gate.\r\n5. Preview-verify as a non-admin Licensing principal, ship through the repository workflow, deploy the exact merged head, then verify the live Property Matches flow for Ilona and Laura. HTTP/build health alone is not acceptance.\n\nThis issue is application/repository maintenance on the evidence currently available. If exact reproduction later proves that an existing database object's authorization is defective, open a separate structural issue naming that proven object and dependency; do not pre-route this application defect to the structural orchestrator.\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 10\n```\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T12:34:06Z","createdAt":"2026-09-10T23:05:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2701,"title":"Property Matches fails for Licensing users while Administrator succeeds","updatedAt":"2026-09-25T12:34:06Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2701"},

{"body":"## `--reclaim-silent-reviewer` cannot complete: it exceeds the derived reviewer request budget\n\nReclaiming a dead reviewer lease is currently impossible. Every attempt ends at the same place, deterministically:\n\n```\nREFUSED: GitHub command failed: reviewer operation request budget exhausted before request 24\n```\n\nReproduced twice, 20 seconds apart, with identical arguments and identical output — this is not a rate limit and not transient.\n\n### The exact command\n\n```\nnode scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --reclaim-silent-reviewer \\\n  --reviewer glm-5.3 --issue 2596 --pr 2607 \\\n  --head-sha 1adbde0d0894e90c5fbf779cd2fa787e12a4519f \\\n  --failed-sequence 1892 --review-slot 1 \\\n  --confirm-no-verdict --confirm-no-artifact\n```\n\nThe lease being reclaimed is genuinely dead. `--reviewer-capacity` classifies it `silence-reclaimable`: held since 2026-09-08T23:55:47Z (46.7 hours), last activity 2026-09-08T21:44:26Z — *before* the lease was even taken — no verdict present, PR still open, head still matching, and a recorded silence probe at 2026-09-10T20:03:40Z.\n\n### Why it cannot succeed\n\n`REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT = 25` (line 92). Its comment records exactly which paths the ceiling was measured against: slot-2 assignment (23 requests), slot-2 replacement (20), first replacement pre-mutex (9), post-mutex replacement section (11). **The silent-reviewer reclaim path is not among them.** It was added later and its request count was never derived, so it runs past the ceiling that was sized for the other operations.\n\nThis is stated deliberately: I am **not** proposing that the number be raised. The comment says `RE-DERIVED, NOT WIDENED (issue #2075)`, and `docs/verification/reviewer-assignment-api-budget-2026-08-28.md` (#1812, #1833, #2550) carries the derivation. The correct fix starts by counting what the reclaim path actually spends and why, in that document, exactly as the other paths were counted. If the reclaim genuinely needs more requests than an assignment does, the ceiling may be re-derived to cover it — but only from a written count, never from \"it refused, so make it bigger.\"\n\nNote also that `consumeReviewWireRequest` subtracts a `cleanupReserve` while the mutex is held, so the usable budget inside the locked section is smaller than 25. Any derivation must account for that, and for whether `io.atomicReviewMutexRelease` is available (reserve 2 vs 8).\n\n### Why it matters now\n\nThe reviewer pool is the throughput bottleneck. A dead lease that cannot be reclaimed occupies a reviewer permanently, and this is the *second* structural way the pool loses capacity — see #2693, where the global one-lease-per-reviewer rule stalled PR #2681 with healthy reviewers idle. Together they mean capacity only ever goes down. PR #2681 slot 2 is blocked right now, and this reclaim was the attempt to free a reviewer for it.\n\n### Ask\n\n1. Count the reclaim path's requests and record the count in `docs/verification/reviewer-assignment-api-budget-2026-08-28.md` alongside the existing derivations.\n2. Make the reclaim fit, or re-derive the ceiling from that written count.\n3. Make the refusal name the operation whose budget it is, and the derived ceiling for that operation. \"Budget exhausted before request 24\" does not say which budget, what the limit is, or that the limit was never derived for this command.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 30\nreturn_to: u2giants/shared-db\ndepends_on:\nwrites: []\nreads: []\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-17T16:06:52Z","createdAt":"2026-09-10T22:37:10Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2697,"title":"--reclaim-silent-reviewer always fails: its request count was never derived against REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:16:03Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2697"},
{"body":"## Owner policy\n\nAlbert Hazan confirmed on 2026-09-10 that reviewers have no simultaneous-job limit. The repository's one-active-lease-per-reviewer rule is therefore a false capacity refusal and must be replaced.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\nstructural_change: false\ndatabase_interaction: none\n```\n\n## Required outcome\n\nAllow a reviewer to hold concurrent independent review assignments while preserving durable, exact-head verdict binding, independent slots, safe failure release, and auditability. Do not weaken approvals, merge gates, or database protections.","closedAt":"2026-09-14T17:42:16Z","createdAt":"2026-09-10T20:57:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2694,"title":"Allow concurrent governed reviewer assignments","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:16:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2694"},
{"body":"## Ask\n\nLet one reviewer hold more than one live review lease at a time.\n\n## Why\n\nToday every reviewer in `ACTIVE_REVIEWERS` may hold exactly ONE live lease across the whole\nrepository. With six active reviewers that is a hard ceiling of six simultaneous reviews for\nevery PR in flight, and it is the reason PR #2681 could not be reviewed today.\n\nMeasured state at the time of the refusal (2026-09-10, PR #2681 head\n`1dc0028c5351c31b7368df0715ea7dd69b9b443b`):\n\n```\nno other independent reviewer is available for slot 2; no replacement reviewer is available:\n2 of 6 already failed on this exact head (kimi-k3, qwen-3.8-max);\n4 of 6 hold other live leases (grok-4.6 #2326/PR #2684, glm-5.3 #2596/PR #2607,\nmuse-spark-1.3-contributor #2579/PR #2681, gemini-3.8-flash-high #2326/PR #2684);\n0 are otherwise ineligible or excluded (none).\n```\n\nSo slot 1 approved and slot 2 could not be filled at all — not because of a provider problem,\nbut because the other four reviewers were each busy on a different pull request.\n\n## The limit is ours, not the providers'\n\nNothing in the wrappers or the provider APIs requires one-review-at-a-time. Each review already\nruns in its own detached worktree at its own pinned head, with its own session name and its own\ndurable verdict ref, so two concurrent reviews by the same provider do not share mutable state.\nThe single-lease rule buys serialisation we are not using.\n\n## What independence actually requires\n\nThe rule that matters is unchanged and must stay: **two slots on the SAME pull request head must\nbe two DIFFERENT reviewers.** That is what makes the second verdict independent. \"The same\nreviewer may not also be reviewing an unrelated PR\" is a different and much stronger claim, and\nit is the one costing throughput.\n\n## Suggested shape\n\n- Keep exact-object and exact-head locks exactly as they are.\n- Keep the same-head distinctness rule: a reviewer already holding a slot on this PR head is\n  ineligible for the other slot on that head.\n- Replace the global one-lease-per-reviewer rule with a per-reviewer concurrency cap, read from a\n  named constant beside `MAX_AUTHOR_LANES` so it is tunable without touching allocation logic.\n- Make the refusal message report the cap it hit, so a future exhaustion says which limit bound.\n\n## Not in scope\n\nProvider quota. Kimi and Qwen were genuinely unavailable today (usage limit, and a provider-side\ncontent filter that killed a review after 48 turns). Raising concurrency does not create credit.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\npriority: 30\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-10T22:47:30Z","createdAt":"2026-09-10T20:51:16Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2693,"title":"Reviewer allocation caps every reviewer at one live lease repository-wide, which stalled PR #2681 with four healthy reviewers idle-on-other-PRs","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:16:06Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2693"},
{"body":"Returned from u2giants/shared-db#2619 by the shared-db orchestrator.\n\nThis is **source-data** work. Under the shared-db admission test (AGENTS.md 0.0-C) it changes the CONTENTS of the shared database, not its SHAPE, so the session working in this repository owns it outright — no shared-db issue, no dispatch, no migration.\n\nOriginal issue: https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/2619\n\n---\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: source-data\nroute: source-data-session\r\npriority: 0\nreturn_to: u2giants/shared-db\ndepends_on:\nwrites: []\nreads: []\n```\n\n## What is needed\n\nThe ColdLion landing loader (merged as PR #2589, issue #2588) fills the order and\nproduction history landing tables. It does not yet fill the master-data landing\ntables that those history rows point at. Add the remaining master-data units to the\nsame loader so a history row can be resolved to a named customer, factory, division,\nsalesperson, season and merchandise group.\n\nOutstanding units, all landing-only (`coldlion.*`, never `core.*` directly):\n\n- customer master\n- vendor / factory master\n- division\n- salesperson\n- season\n- merch_group_header and merch_group_detail\n\n`item_*` is already partly populated by the merged loader; check what it actually\nholds before touching it.\n\nKnown vendor facts that constrain this work (all previously verified, all recorded\nas memories in this repo's session memory):\n\n- `/merchGroupDetails` returns 200 with zero rows for every query attempted.\n- `/divisions` contradicts `/items` on at least one division code (SPRUCE).\n- Division codes do NOT determine company: CW001 exists under three companies.\n- Out-of-enum parameter values return an empty success envelope, not an error, so a\n  typo reads as \"no data\".\n- Undeclared parameters are ignored rather than rejected; read the declared parameter\n  list before concluding a filter is broken.\n- A page size above the vendor's cap is silently reduced to 200.\n\n## Suggested prompt for the session that picks this up\n\nUse the loader that already exists rather than writing a second one: the HTTP paging,\nvalue normalisation, target proof, page-evidence ledger and per-window transaction in\n`tools/coldlion-landing/lib/` are all reusable. Master data is not windowed the way\nhistory is — decide deliberately whether each unit is a full snapshot replace or an\nincremental upsert, and write that decision down where the next reader will find it.\nEvery entry point must prove its target database before writing, exactly as the\nhistory loader does. No real payload value may be committed to this public repository.\n\n## Where the detail lives\n\n`tools/coldlion-landing/README.md` on `main`, and issue #2588.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T19:24:53Z","createdAt":"2026-09-10T20:32:55Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Returned from u2giants/shared-db#2620 by the shared-db orchestrator.\n\nThis is **source-data** work. Under the shared-db admission test (AGENTS.md 0.0-C) it changes the CONTENTS of the shared database, not its SHAPE, so the session working in this repository owns it outright — no shared-db issue, no dispatch, no migration.\n\nOriginal issue: https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/2620\n\n---\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: source-data\nroute: source-data-session\r\npriority: 0\nreturn_to: u2giants/shared-db\ndepends_on:\nwrites: []\nreads: []\n```\n\n## What is needed\n\nRun the merged ColdLion history backfill all the way back to the 2019-01-01 grid\nanchor, so the order and production history landing tables hold the full vendor\nhistory rather than only the recent weeks the nightly sync covers.\n\nThe loader and its workflow are already merged and proven end to end:\n\n- PR #2589, merge commit `7c32df1419db423e1310593ee9a748eb2c3d7409` (issue #2588).\n- The backfill workflow is `.github/workflows/coldlion-history-backfill.yml`. It is\n  the only sanctioned way to run against the real database.\n- The production connection secret `SUPABASE_DB_URL_PRODUCTION` exists (created\n  2026-09-09) and a `dry_run=true` dispatch succeeded: the target check passed and\n  the run reported the outstanding window/scope pairs.\n- The nightly sync is scheduled at 05:20 UTC and covers the trailing weeks.\n\n## What makes this delicate\n\n- **A loaded window is sealed forever.** Ledger triggers make the page evidence and\n  the loaded state immutable, so a window loaded on incomplete evidence cannot be\n  corrected by re-running. Never widen the batch to \"save time\".\n- The run is resumable by design: it reads the ledger and loads only outstanding\n  window/scope pairs. Run it in bounded batches with `--limit`, check the ledger\n  between batches, and stop on the first refusal rather than retrying blind.\n- The vendor caps page size silently at 200 and reports a refused history request as\n  HTTP 400 on the wire while its body claims 500. Permanence is decided by the wire\n  status, except 408 and 429 which mean \"later\".\n- ~350 weekly windows times the scope list is a long walk. Expect it to take days of\n  wall clock, not one run, and expect vendor-side rate limiting.\n\n## Suggested prompt for the session that picks this up\n\nDo not modify the loader to make the backfill go faster. Dispatch the existing\nbackfill workflow in bounded batches, oldest first, and after each batch read the\nledger to confirm every window it claims to have loaded carries complete page\nevidence. If a window refuses permanently, record which window and which scope and\nwhy, and move on rather than forcing it. Report progress as \"windows loaded of\nwindows outstanding\", from the ledger, never from the run log.\n\n## Where the detail lives\n\n`tools/coldlion-landing/README.md` on `main`, and issue #2588.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T02:30:30Z","createdAt":"2026-09-10T20:32:52Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## What happened\n\nOn 2026-09-10 both `ai-kimi` and `ai-muse` refused governed reviews with:\n\n```\nREFUSED: reviewer preflight: ai-<x> doctor reports \"doctor could not be run (exit 1) and named no check\" -- this is a LOCAL dependency fault on this machine\n```\n\nBoth reviewers are completely healthy. Run by hand with the caller variable set, they pass every check:\n\n- `AI_MUSE_CALLER=claude ai-muse doctor` -> all PASS\n- `AI_KIMI_CALLER=claude ai-kimi doctor` -> `auth : OK`\n\nWithout it, the wrapper exits 1 with `AI_<X>_CALLER must be set explicitly to codex or claude; credentialed execution never guesses the caller.`\n\n## The defect\n\n`scripts/run-governed-review.mjs` spawns the wrapper (and its preflight `doctor`) without setting `AI_<WRAPPER>_CALLER`. The preflight then reads a non-zero exit that named no check and reports it as a machine fault. Two consequences:\n\n1. Every reviewer whose wrapper requires the caller variable is unusable through the governed runner unless the operator happens to export it first.\n2. The refusal misnames its own cause, so the natural response is to hunt a local install problem that does not exist.\n\n## Fix\n\nThe runner knows which engine it is running as (it is the thing choosing `--wrapper`). It should set the wrapper's own `AI_*_CALLER` in the spawned environment, for both the preflight doctor and the review, and the preflight should surface the wrapper's stderr line rather than \"named no check\".\n\n## Scope\n\n```machine\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\n```\n\nNot orchestrator work under AGENTS.md 0.0-C: it changes no database object. Filed from orchestrator marker #2669 as an operational blocker encountered live.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 100\nservice_class: maintenance\nchange_type: reviewer-tooling\nreturn_to: popcre/shared-db\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\nMetadata recovery note: Add a machine-readable db-work-scope matching the existing machine block: wrapper caller-environment repair is reviewer tooling, not database structure.\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf01-b3d7-7d62-b7ed-5c7bad7af40a on 916-ALIEN\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T14:41:12Z","createdAt":"2026-09-10T15:41:04Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2678,"title":"run-governed-review.mjs does not pass AI_*_CALLER to the wrapper, so healthy reviewers refuse as local dependency faults","updatedAt":"2026-09-25T14:41:13Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2678"},

{"body":"## The history table cannot record the status the system actually produces\n\n`public.bulk_operation_runs` (issue #2439, migration `20260909202801_bulk_operation_runs_history_reissue.sql`)\nconstrains terminal status to:\n\n```sql\nconstraint bulk_operation_runs_status_check\n  check (status in ('succeeded', 'failed', 'interrupted', 'cancelled', 'stopped')),\n```\n\nLive production read on 2026-09-10 (project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`), the real terminal\nstate of the nightly style-group rebuild that finished this morning:\n\n```\nrun_id         3a5cdfaa-ee88-4728-8641-05d4e22e9d37\nstatus         \"completed\"\nstarted_at     2026-09-10T06:00:03.776Z\nupdated_at     2026-09-10T08:12:40.259Z\nresult_message \"Created 35974 style groups, assigned 98035 assets\"\n```\n\n`completed` is not in the allowed set. A PopDAM appender that copies the live\n`admin_config` terminal status through — the obvious and correct implementation —\nis rejected by the constraint on the very first successful run.\n\nThis blocks #2439's remaining half. The appender lives in `u2giants/popdam3`, and it\ncannot be written correctly against this constraint. Fix the vocabulary here first.\n\n## What is needed\n\n1. Enumerate the terminal statuses `admin_config.BULK_OPERATIONS` actually emits across\n   every operation, from production, rather than assuming this one.\n2. Reconcile the constraint with them — either widen the allowed set or define an explicit,\n   documented mapping the appender must apply. Do not guess which; derive it from the read.\n3. Whichever is chosen, make the rejected case visible. A constraint violation inside a\n   nightly worker is exactly the silent failure #2439 exists to end.\n\nFound by live verification during the #2439 business-flow proof, orchestrator marker #2669.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 20\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table public.bulk_operation_runs\nreads:\n  - table public.admin_config\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-10T22:42:52Z","createdAt":"2026-09-10T12:31:31Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 500\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function public.find_dam_order_list_row\nreads:\n  - view api.dam_order_list\n```\n\nPopDAM issue u2giants/popdam3#121 needs one bounded, authenticated lookup that returns the first matching OrderList row ID and its zero-based position in the current filtered and sorted full result set.\n\nThe current app implementation first queries the matching row, then downloads up to 24,000 order-line IDs in as many as 25 ranged requests to discover its position. The replacement must preserve the existing Google-Sheets-style Find behavior: search does not filter the grid, existing column filters and saved sort order still constrain/order the lookup, the matching row is highlighted, and surrounding rows remain visible.\n\nRequired contract:\n- SECURITY INVOKER behavior through api.dam_order_list; authenticated only; no anon/public execution.\n- Inputs use normalized, allowlisted filter and sort specifications from PopDAM, never interpolated unchecked identifiers/operators.\n- Search coverage must remain exactly aligned with PopDAM ORDER_LIST_SEARCH_COLUMNS.\n- Stable ordering must always end with order_line_id ascending.\n- Return at most one row: order_line_id plus zero-based row_index; return no row for blank/no match.\n- Add SQL contract tests for default and custom sort, text/number/date/null filters, wildcard escaping, stable ties, no match, and privileges/RLS.\n- Preview-first branch/PR/merge workflow. Production application remains an explicit owner gate under shared-db rules.\n\nCanonical implementation issue selected by active orchestrator2714; duplicate2665 references the same application contract and will be reconciled through2664.\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-11T17:40:43Z","createdAt":"2026-09-10T02:11:01Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Outcome\n\nRestore the preview-ledger gate for migration `20260909005945` without changing any merged migration bytes and without weakening malformed-declaration refusal for future migrations.\n\n## Observed failure\n\nThe migration header contains:\n\n`-- derived-from: the baseline body of queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups() carried in ...`\n\n`scripts/migration_derivation.py` correctly treats every such comment as a machine declaration and rejects the prose because it is not a 14-digit migration version. The same module's focused test explicitly requires that refusal. The migration replaces `public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups`, but has no earlier migration replacement; its actual source is the pre-adoption CI baseline, not a ledger version.\n\nThe affected migration was merged in #2440, renamed from `20260908204414` to `20260909005945`, and cannot be edited in place because merged migration bytes are promotion bindings.\n\n## Required repair\n\nAdd a narrowly keyed immutable-history metadata path for this exact already-merged version and exact known malformed line/source, classifying it as no migration-ledger base while retaining the baseline provenance. It must run before normal file parsing only for that pinned historical exception.
