{"body":"PopDAM issue: https://github.com/u2giants/popdam3/issues/107\r\nPredecessor: #2212 (closed and in Virginia production)\r\nPlan: `u2giants/popdam3/plan_popsg_production_readiness.md` sections 9.10-9.12.\r\n\r\n## Outcome\r\n\r\nComplete the governed PopSG search contract that #2212 partially delivered. The deployed `search_style_guide_library` handles file results, path/name/metadata/tags/PDF text, totals, facets, and stable file paging, but it cannot:\r\n\r\n- return guide-group results where a guide matches because any active child matches;\r\n- paginate/count guides rather than files in Guides mode;\r\n- filter preview state, render exception state, or PDF-content availability as required by the approved production-readiness plan.\r\n\r\nThe PopDAM application session owns all frontend/Edge/agent work. This issue owns database structure only. No licensed paths, filenames, or row exports are included.\r\n\r\n## Required contract\r\n\r\n- Add one non-ambiguous authorized v2 RPC rather than creating a PostgREST overload ambiguity.\r\n- Support `files` and `guides` result modes.\r\n- In Guides mode, filter child files first, then group, count, facet, sort, and paginate guides with a deterministic total order.\r\n- Support the existing filters plus preview state, render exception state, PDF-content availability, and modified-date range.\r\n- Keep active-state and authorization filtering inside the database contract before paging.\r\n- Return an exact total and facets for the same filtered result set.\r\n- Preserve the existing v1 RPC until the app rollout is accepted.\r\n- Use existing rows; no bulk backfill or full-corpus rebuild.\r\n- Prove authorization, excluded/inactive suppression, combined filters, guide-child matching, stable paging, and representative-volume query plans in preview.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 100\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table public.style_guide_files\r\n  - function public.search_style_guide_library_v2\r\n  - index public.idx_sgf_live_preview_ids\r\n  - index public.idx_sgf_live_missing_clean_ids\r\n  - index public.idx_sgf_live_missing_error_ids\r\nreads:\r\n  - table public.style_guide_search_documents\r\n  - table public.style_guide_render_queue\r\n  - table public.style_guide_pdf_text\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe migration author may add narrowly justified indexes after preview-plan evidence, but must update this block atomically through the lane manager and claim every exact final object before authoring.\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-15T01:18:49Z","createdAt":"2026-09-07T12:38:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. If an application mapping is wrong, forward that correction to the owning DesignFlow repository rather than adding an unjustified database object.\r\n\r\n## Safety boundary\r\n\r\n- Non-production `xupnyeifmpsacrqahwwm` only. {"body":"Returned by the required acceptance probe in u2giants/popdam3#111 on 2026-09-07.\n\n## Production evidence\n\nTarget was proved as Virginia production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`. Calls used the real PopDAM viewer login through authenticated PostgREST, not psql or service role.\n\n- `get_filter_counts({tagFilter:\"blue\"})`: 10/12 passed, 2/12 failed with PostgreSQL `57014` at 8.052s and 8.029s. Successful calls returned the expected total 39,621; after warming they were 0.382–0.483s.\n- `filter_effective_assets({tagFilter:\"blue\"})` with `count=exact`, head-only: 0/3 passed; all failed with `57014` at 8.056s, 8.052s, and 8.060s.\n- No-filter `get_filter_counts`: 3/3 passed at 6.569s cold, 3.914s, and 0.700s.\n\nThe reproducible redacted probe is committed in PopDAM under `verification/search/authenticated-api-performance-2026-09-07.json` as part of the #111 closeout work.\n\n## Required structural outcome\n\nMake filtered facet counts and the list-total path complete reliably below the existing approximately eight-second authenticated viewer ceiling. Preserve authorization, exact count/facet parity, filter semantics, pagination behavior, and existing fast warm performance. Do not raise timeouts and do not weaken RLS.\n\nInspect the current production definitions and plans for `public.get_filter_counts(jsonb)`, its effective-filter delegate, and `public.filter_effective_assets(jsonb)`. Use preview representative-volume evidence, repeated cold and warm authenticated-path tests, and production verification. If the safest contract is to return the list total from the already-computed filtered facet result rather than PostgREST `count=exact`, keep the API and consumer rollout ordered so PopDAM never enables an incomplete total.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 80\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table public.assets\n  - function public.get_filter_counts\n  - function public.get_effective_filter_counts\n  - function public.filter_effective_assets\n  - function public.get_effective_filter_counts_unchecked_1703\n  - index public.idx_assets_tag_visible_facets\n  - index public.idx_assets_tag_pending_facets\n  - index public.idx_assets_tag_rls_visible_ids\nreads:\n  - table public.style_groups\n  - table public.asset_effective_tags\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-11T14:17:14Z","createdAt":"2026-09-07T12:23:27Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Goal\n\nProvide a callable, non-forgeable server-side actor contract for the DesignFlow backend to use when assigning item owners and recording workflow actions.\n\n## Production integration blocker\n\nIssues #2202-#2204 corrected the canonical tables and workflow semantics, but both write functions still derive identity exclusively from `auth.uid()` and `auth.jwt()->>'email'`.\n\nDesignFlow does not authenticate staff through Supabase Auth. Its BFF/backend verifies a DesignFlow-owned RS256 JWT and connects to PostgreSQL through Sequelize. A database connection does not automatically receive Supabase `request.jwt.claims`. Read-only production inspection on 2026-09-07 also proved that all 28 active `dflow.users` rows have `app_profile_id IS NULL`, so there is no real Supabase UUID the backend can truthfully place in `actor_auth_user_id`.\n\nThe application therefore cannot call `dflow.set_item_user_assignment` or `dflow.record_item_workflow_action` as designed. Inventing a UUID or copying browser-supplied actor identity would corrupt the audit guarantee.\n\n## Required contract\n\n- Preserve the existing Supabase-authenticated entry points for any legitimate callers.\n- Add backend-only assignment/action entry points, or an equivalent trusted database-session contract, that accept the actor resolved from the backend's already-verified DesignFlow JWT.\n- Restrict the backend path to the actual backend database role; it must not be executable by `anon`, ordinary `authenticated` PostgREST clients, or browser-controlled SQL/RPC calls.\n- Resolve and validate the actor against `dflow.users`; require active status and an exact identity match appropriate to the backend token (integer user ID plus email where available).\n- Store truthful actor provenance. If `actor_auth_user_id` is Supabase-specific, make the model explicitly support the DesignFlow JWT identity source rather than generating or pretending a Supabase UUID.\n- Keep all #2202-#2204 guarantees: canonical `plm` item/step targets, atomic action/step/notification writes, immutable history, source-handoff linkage, stale-write refusal, required-recipient rollback, fallback labeling, and idempotency.\n- Add real-DML contract tests proving the backend role succeeds with a valid active DesignFlow user, rejects mismatched/inactive/missing users, and all public/browser roles are refused.\n- Rehearse and verify on preview, then use the governed production promotion path.\n\n## Application dependency\n\nBlocks `popcre/designflow-backend#81` Step 3. No application workaround should set fake `request.jwt.claims`, invent `actor_auth_user_id`, or bypass the immutable workflow contract.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 100\ndepends_on: 2202, 2203, 2204\nwrites:\n  - table dflow.item_user_assignment\n  - table dflow.item_workflow_action\n  - function dflow.set_item_user_assignment\n  - function dflow.record_item_workflow_action\n  - function dflow.current_designflow_user_id\nreads:\n  - table dflow.users\n  - table plm.RFQItem\n  - table plm.RFQStep\n  - table app.user_notification\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T14:48:30Z","createdAt":"2026-09-07T12:03:03Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2496,"title":"DesignFlow workflow: trusted backend actor entry point","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:18:37Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2496"},

{"body":"## What happened\n\nOn PR #2415 at head `8d9843eb`, grok-4.6 produced a slot-1 APPROVE. The runner created the durable verdict artifact `refs/db-review-verdicts/2355-2415-8d9843eb…` (commit `f66e5eb6`), then the create-only readback disagreed with it and the tuple was marked **permanently refused**.\n\n`check-exact-head-approval.mjs` names the exact cause:\n\n```\nREFUSED: verdict refs/db-review-verdicts/2355-2415-8d9843eb… is invalid: findings digest does not match the durable findings\n```\n\nThe findings comment (`#issuecomment-5563533360`) was created at 00:55:36Z and updated at 00:55:40Z — four seconds later. The digest stored in the artifact is over one version of the body; validation reads the other.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThe verdict ref is create-only. Once an invalid artifact occupies the tuple, **no valid verdict can ever be written for that (issue, pr, head, slot) again**. The only recovery is to move the PR head, which also voids the *other* slot's perfectly good verdict — so one bad digest costs two full reviews. That happened here: gemini-3.8-flash-high's valid slot-2 APPROVE at the same head had to be thrown away.\n\n## Where to look\n\n`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2015` computes `findings_digest: findingsDigest(findingsBody)` from a body read at record time. Anything that edits the comment between that read and the readback invalidates the artifact irrecoverably.\n\n## Suggested direction\n\n- Take the digest and the readback from the same immutable snapshot (pin the comment's node id + updated_at, or hash a body the runner controls end to end).\n- Do not create the ref at all if the digest cannot be re-verified against the live comment first — a refusal that leaves no artifact is recoverable; this one is not.\n- Consider whether an invalid artifact should be deletable by a guarded recovery path, so a single bad digest cannot permanently burn a head.\n\nFound during the shared-db orchestrator session of 2026-09-06/07.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","closedAt":"2026-09-07T05:32:37Z","createdAt":"2026-09-07T01:03:12Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2486,"title":"A governed verdict can be recorded with a findings digest that never matches its comment, permanently killing the head","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:46:00Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2486"},

{"body":"## Ask\r\n\r\nRetire `public.erp_items_current` and `public.erp_items_raw` — **after** the app-side work\r\nbelow, not before.\r\n\r\n## Why\r\n\r\nBoth tables hold the retired DesignFlow item feed. Verified read-only on production\r\n`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`:\r\n\r\n- `public.erp_items_current` — 17,703 rows, `source_system = 'designflow'` on every row,\r\n  last successful sync **2026-05-21**. The 2026-07-26 attempt failed with an ERP API 403 and\r\n  nothing has retried since.\r\n- The canonical replacement, `plm.item`, holds 19,362 ColdLion rows loaded 2026-08-26.\r\n\r\nPer the owner ruling, DesignFlow holds no authority in the Master Data model\r\n(`docs/core-master-data-consolidation-aim.md` §4), and the feed that maintained these tables\r\nhas already been deleted from PopDAM (u2giants/popdam3 commit `6b5d9160`). They are now frozen\r\ndata with no writer.\r\n\r\n## This is the third and last of a set — do not run it first\r\n\r\n| Order | Issue | What it does |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| 1 | #2466 | Repoint `api.plm_item_list` at `plm.item` so applications have a canonical item read path |\r\n| 2 | #2481 | Link `pim.product` to `plm.item` |\r\n| 3 | **this issue** | Drop the frozen DesignFlow tables |\r\n\r\nDropping these tables today would break PopDAM. They are still actively read.\r\n\r\n## ⚠️ Required app-repo work BEFORE this issue can be closed — `u2giants/popdam3`\r\n\r\nPopDAM reads `erp_items_current` in six places that must be repointed at the canonical item\r\ncontract first. This is app work, done in the app repo, on `main`:\r\n\r\n| PopDAM code | What it reads it for |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| `src/components/library/StyleGroupDetailPanel.tsx` | item description + the legacy-item date test (this is the consumer blocked on #2466) |\r\n| `supabase/functions/_shared/licensing-resolution.ts` | division / licensor / property codes per style |\r\n| `supabase/functions/_shared/admin-handlers/erp-handlers.ts` | enrichment apply |\r\n| `supabase/functions/_shared/admin-handlers/erp-browse-handlers.ts` | ERP items browser, review queue, enrichment stats — includes raw SQL against the table name |\r\n| `apps/worker/src/handlers/erp.ts` | batch enrichment |\r\n| `apps/worker/src/handlers/ai-tagging-shared.ts` | AI tagging context |\r\n\r\nThe export allow-lists in `supabase/functions/export-table/index.ts` and\r\n`export-sql-dump/index.ts` also name both tables and will need the entries removed.\r\n\r\n**One column has no home yet.** `erp_items_current.dismissed` is PopDAM application state, not\r\nsource data — it does not exist on `plm.item` and must not be recreated there. It needs a\r\nPopDAM-owned home before these tables can go. That decision belongs to the PopDAM session, but\r\nit blocks this issue, so it is recorded here.\r\n\r\n## Suggested sequence\r\n\r\n1. #2466 merges — canonical item read path exists.\r\n2. PopDAM repoints the six call sites and rehomes `dismissed`, in `u2giants/popdam3`.\r\n3. Soak. Confirm the enrichment, tagging, review-queue and style-tracker screens still behave\r\n   — visually, not by row count.\r\n4. Then this issue drops both tables.\r\n\r\nNothing here is urgent: the tables are frozen and harmless where they sit. The cost of dropping\r\nthem early is a broken DAM; the cost of leaving them is a stale table nobody writes to.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 0\r\ndepends_on: 2778\r\nwrites:\r\n  - function plm.refresh_style_tracker_item_bridge\r\n  - function public.resolve_product_category_prediction_item_identity\r\n  - policy legacy_erp_item_identity_admin_read on plm.legacy_erp_item_identity\r\n  - schema archive\r\n  - table api.plm_item_list\r\n  - table archive.erp_items_current\r\n  - table archive.erp_items_raw\r\n  - table plm.legacy_erp_item_identity\r\n  - table plm.style_tracker_item_bridge\r\n  - table public.erp_items_current\r\n  - table public.erp_items_raw\r\n  - view api.plm_item_list\r\nreads:\r\n  - table plm.item\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T04:58:07Z","createdAt":"2026-09-07T00:26:31Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2482,"title":"Retire public.erp_items_current and public.erp_items_raw (frozen DesignFlow feed) — after PopDAM repoints its six readers","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:18:46Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2482"},
{"body":"## The gap\n\n`pim.product` carries a `plm_item_id` FK to the canonical item master. It is **NULL on all\n17,909 rows** — verified read-only on production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, 2026-09-06:\n\n```sql\nselect count(*) total, count(plm_item_id) linked from pim.product;\n--  total | linked\n--  17909 |      0\n```\n\nSo the PM application's product records are not connected to the canonical ColdLion items,\nand nothing can currently answer \"which item is this product\" or \"which products exist for\nthis item\" through the modelled relationship.\n\n## Why this is worth its own issue\n\nThis is the same failure mode as #2466, in a second application. `plm.item` was populated\nfrom ColdLion on 2026-08-26, but the paths that let applications *reach* it were modelled and\nnever connected:\n\n| Path | State |\n|---|---|\n| `api.plm_item_list` (the app-facing item view) | still selects from the retired `public.erp_items_current` — #2466 |\n| `pim.product.plm_item_id` | 0 of 17,909 populated — this issue |\n| `dam.erp_item_snapshot` (FK to `plm.item`) | 0 rows |\n\nThe item master is fine. The publishing and linking layer around it is the unfinished part,\nand it is unfinished in at least three places. Worth deciding whether these are tracked and\ncompleted as one piece of work rather than three unrelated tickets.\n\n## What a fix needs decided\n\n1. **The match key.** `plm.item.item_number` is populated on all 19,362 rows and is the\n   natural key; `plm.item.style_number` is NULL on every row. `pim.product.code` /\n   `external_id` would need checking against it for format and coverage before any backfill.\n2. **Cardinality.** Whether one product maps to exactly one item, or whether a product can\n   span several items — the current single FK assumes the former.\n3. **Unmatched rows.** Whether products with no ColdLion item stay NULL, or are flagged for\n   review the way the licensing reconciliation work does it.\n4. **Who maintains the link going forward** — the ColdLion loader, the PM app on write, or a\n   reconciliation job.\n\nI did not measure the join coverage between `pim.product` and `plm.item`, because the key\nchoice in (1) is a decision, not an inference — the coverage number changes depending on which\ncolumn is treated as the key.\n\n## Raised from\n\nPopDAM session moving the DAM off the retired DesignFlow item feed; found while establishing\nhow applications are meant to read the item master.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: application-data\nroute: application-session\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\nreturn_to: u2giants/poppim-web\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T13:51:03Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T23:21:13Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2481,"title":"pim.product.plm_item_id is NULL on all 17,909 rows — PM products are not linked to the canonical item master","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:18:48Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2481"},
{"body":"## Summary\n\nThe ColdLion item loader derives an item's **licensor only through its property**. Where\nColdLion supplies a royalty code that names the licensor outright but leaves the property\nslot blank, the item resolves to **no licensor and no property**, and the stated licensor is\ndiscarded.\n\nVerified read-only on production, 2026-09-06. Scope: divisions CW001 and SP001 (EH001 and\nEP001 carry no licensed product per owner ruling 2026-09-06).\n\n## Evidence\n\n`plm.item.licensor_id` and `plm.item.property_id` are non-null on **exactly** the same rows,\nin every royalty-code group without exception — e.g. royalty code MV: 2,591 items,\n2,508 with a licensor, 2,508 with a property. Licensor never resolves independently.\n\n`plm.item_import_unresolved` shows why: for CW001 and SP001, merch-group slot 06 is mapped\nto `property`, and the failure reason on these rows is `property slot is empty` (1,994 items)\nor `property code did not match core.property.code` (22 items). There is **no licensor slot\nmapping at all** — slot 05 records `unknown division-scoped slot meaning` for all 19,362\nitems in every division, so no slot is configured to carry the licensor.\n\n**375 of these items carry a non-empty `royaltyCode` in the ColdLion payload.** Excluding\nfive genuine non-product rows (invoicing, sample charge, three test items), **373 real items**\nname a licensor that was thrown away.\n\n## Breakdown of the 375\n\n**Recoverable today — the code already exists in `core.licensor` (293 items):**\nSW 108 · MV 83 · DY 46 · DC 27 · VM 14 · PP 12 · PN 1 · WB 1 · ZZ 1.\nFor these the licensor could be set from `royaltyCode` without any new Master Data.\n\n**Blocked — the code is absent from `core.licensor` (82 items):**\n\n| Code | Items | What it appears to be (from item descriptions) |\n|---|---|---|\n| NL | 60 | descriptions read \"MIXED LICENSE\" — possibly a deliberate multi-licensor marker, not a licensor |\n| FK | 12 | Frida Kahlo — a real licensor with no `core.licensor` record |\n| NT | 6 | Ninja Turtles |\n| NA | 1 | NASA — **exists in `core.licensor` as code `X-NASA`**, so this is a code-form mismatch, not a missing record |\n| GEN | 2 | non-product (invoicing) |\n| RB | 1 | test item |\n\n## Not the cause — ruled out\n\nLetter case is **not** the problem. Lowercase royalty codes resolve normally (`dy` 620/620,\n`mv` 406/406, `sw` 339/339). An earlier suspicion that matching was case-sensitive is wrong.\n\n## Requested\n\n1. **Decide whether licensor may be derived from `royaltyCode` when the property slot is\n   blank.** This is a Master Data attribution question and needs an owner ruling, not an\n   author's judgement — a wrong licensor is a royalty error. If allowed, 293 items resolve\n   immediately.\n2. **Rule on `NL`.** If it means \"mixed license\" it is not a licensor and should be recorded\n   as a distinct outcome rather than a resolution failure. It is the single largest group.\n3. **Add `FK` (Frida Kahlo) and `NT` (Ninja Turtles) to `core.licensor`**, or rule that they\n   are out of scope. Note `core.licensor` also holds two rows with a NULL code (PAUL FRANK,\n   STEAL-A-BRAINROT) which cannot be matched by code at all.\n4. **Reconcile the `X-` code prefix.** ColdLion sends `NA`; `core.licensor` holds `X-NASA`.\n   Any code-based matching will keep missing these.\n5. **Configure a licensor slot, or record explicitly that there is none.** Slot 05 is\n   unmapped for all four divisions and all 19,362 items; whatever it holds is currently\n   being discarded silently.\n\nItem-level detail was delivered to the owner as a local CSV and is deliberately not\nreproduced here: `u2giants/shared-db` is a public repository.\n\nRelated: #2466 (repoint the item list at `plm.item`), #2450 (rationalization register).\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: curated-master-data\nroute: curated-master-data-governance\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T14:08:46Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T22:49:09Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2477,"title":"ColdLion item loader discards a stated licensor when the property slot is blank (373 items)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:18:51Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2477"},
{"body":"Returned from u2giants/shared-db#2178 by the shared-db orchestrator.\n\nThis is **source-data** work. Under the shared-db admission test (AGENTS.md 0.0-C) it changes the CONTENTS of the shared database, not its SHAPE, so the session working in this repository owns it outright — no shared-db issue, no dispatch, no migration.\n\nOriginal issue: https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/2178\n\n---\n\nColdLion's `GET /EhpApi/pickticket` returns HTTP 500 with an empty body whenever the request is not narrowed, and both `/pickticket` and `/receiving` report zero rows for every window we can successfully query. This blocks the Step 6b landing tables in `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md`: we have never observed a row from either feed, so we cannot state their fields or their grain.\n\n**This issue is not structural and must not take a migration-author lane.** It is vendor liaison. It stays open until ColdLion answers.\n\n### The defect, precisely\n\nFailure depends on breadth of match, not on a missing parameter:\n\n- `minTransactionNo=999999` (matches nothing) → HTTP 200\n- `minTransactionNo=0` and `minTransactionNo=1` (match everything) → HTTP 500, empty body\n- no parameters at all → HTTP 500, empty body\n- any date narrowing (`createdFrom`, `createdFrom`+`createdTo`, `transactionDate`) → HTTP 200\n- `createdTo` alone, and `sort=transactionNo&size=1` → connection dropped before response\n\nReproducible: three consecutive `?size=1` calls returned dropped-connection, 500, 500. Never once succeeded unnarrowed.\n\n`/receiving` has an identical parameter signature in `/v2/api-docs` and handles every one of those calls correctly, returning a well-formed empty page. Same key, same session, same minute — so this is not our credentials, our client, or rate limiting. `/divisions`, `/orderHistory` and `/prodHistory` all returned data on that key at the same time.\n\n### The entanglement worth remembering\n\nThe `/pickticket` requests that fail are exactly the broad ones that would show whether data exists. So we **cannot** conclude the pick-ticket feed is empty — only that the narrow windows we are permitted to ask are empty. Do not let \"0 rows\" harden into \"no data\" in any later summary.\n\n### State\n\n- Vendor problem report drafted with the full request/response table, the `/receiving` contrast, and the reproducibility evidence. Sent to Albert to forward to ColdLion; not yet sent to the vendor.\n- Corrections posted to #2081 (comment 5519596972), superseding the coarser §8 claim in the census that `/pickticket` was unconditionally broken and `/receiving` merely empty.\n\n### Done when\n\n1. ColdLion acknowledges and fixes the 500, or gives a workaround.\n2. ColdLion answers whether pick-ticket and receiving transactions should be visible to our API key.\n3. At least one row is observed from each feed, so field names and grain can be censused.\n4. Unit 6b is then unblocked and can be split into structural issues normally.\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: source-data\nroute: source-data-session\npriority: 3\nreturn_to: u2giants/licensor-source-data\n```\n\nClassified by the orchestrator on 2026-09-05 under AGENTS.md 0.0-C. Vendor liaison, not structural: it cannot take a migration-author lane. The approved private source-data repository owns the follow-through and must preserve all licensed evidence there.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-08T14:19:18Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T22:48:48Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2476,"title":"ColdLion vendor defect: /pickticket returns HTTP 500 unnarrowed, and both /pickticket and /receiving show zero rows (blocks Step 6b)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:18:52Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2476"},
{"body":"## Ask\n\nAdd a DAM-facing item contract view over the canonical ColdLion item master, following the\nexisting `api.<app>_<thing>_list` convention:\n\n```sql\ncreate view api.dam_item_list\n  with (security_invoker = true) as\nselect\n  i.id                              as item_id,\n  i.item_number,\n  i.description,\n  i.status,\n  (i.raw->>'modTime')::timestamptz  as erp_modified_at\nfrom plm.item i\nwhere i.source_system = 'coldlion';\n```\n\nplus an index on `plm.item (item_number)` if one does not already exist — PopDAM looks up\none item at a time by item number.\n\n## Why\n\nPopDAM is moving its item-description and item-age lookup off the retired DesignFlow feed\n(`public.erp_items_current`, last successful sync 2026-05-21, 403 since 2026-07-26) onto the\ncanonical ColdLion item master, per the owner ruling that DesignFlow holds no authority.\n\nThe grants on `plm.item` are already correct (`authenticated` has `USAGE` on `plm` and\n`SELECT` on `plm.item`), but `plm` is deliberately **not** in `pgrst.db_schemas`, so no\nbrowser client can reach it:\n\n```\nGET /rest/v1/item   (Accept-Profile: plm)\n406 PGRST106 — Invalid schema: plm\n```\n\nPer `AGENTS.md` §8.1, the fix is **not** to add `plm` to `pgrst.db_schemas` — that broadens\nthe shared API surface for every app. The house pattern is an `api.*` contract view, which is\nwhat this asks for. PopDAM already consumes exactly this pattern via `.schema(\"api\")` against\n`api.dam_order_list`, `api.dam_asset_library`, `api.dam_customer_list` and\n`api.dam_factory_list`.\n\n`api.plm_item_list` is not the answer — it is a view over the retired `erp_items_current`\nand is tracked separately in #2466.\n\n## Field notes (verified against prod)\n\n- **`plm.item.item_number` is the join key.** It equals `raw->>'itemNo'` on all 19,362 rows,\n  and it matches the item numbers PopDAM already holds — 17,483 of PopDAM's 17,703 legacy\n  rows join (98.8%). `style_number` is NULL on every row, so it cannot be used.\n- **`plm.item.description` is already the resolved item description** — it equals\n  `raw->>'itemDesc'` on all 19,118 rows where a description exists. No JSON extraction needed.\n- **The ERP modification time is only in `raw->>'modTime'`** — there is no resolved column for\n  it. It is present on all 19,362 rows and spans 2019-01-03 to 2026-08-26, with only 52 rows\n  falling on the load date, so it is a genuine ERP modification time rather than the import\n  timestamp. `plm.item.updated_at` is the load timestamp and is *not* a substitute.\n\n  PopDAM uses that timestamp for one thing: a \"legacy item\" test against a fixed 2025-05-14\n  cutoff. Across the 17,483 rows that join, `modTime` and the old DesignFlow `erp_updated_at`\n  agree on that test 97.4% of the time, and every disagreement is an item ColdLion knows was\n  modified after the stale DesignFlow copy was last refreshed. So the flag keeps its meaning.\n\n  If a resolved `erp_modified_at` column on `plm.item` is preferable to reading JSON in the\n  view, that works for us too — the view is the part PopDAM needs.\n\n## Downstream\n\nPopDAM's style-group detail panel is the only consumer waiting on this. The DesignFlow sync\nthat fed the old table has already been removed from PopDAM\n(u2giants/popdam3 commit `6b5d9160`). `public.erp_items_current` and `public.erp_items_raw`\nare now frozen; they are still read by PopDAM's enrichment/classification pipelines, so\nnothing should drop them yet.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-06T23:20:55Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T22:43:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2475,"title":"Add api.dam_item_list — DAM-facing contract view over the ColdLion item master (plm.item)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:46:04Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2475"},

{"body":"## Owner authorization\n\nAlbert Hazan, 2026-09-06, in session: repoint the item list at the canonical ColdLion\nitem table now, rather than waiting for the remainder of the Master Data rationalization.\nThis follows the standing ruling that ColdLion is canonical for item master and the\nDesignFlow PLM source will not be used (`docs/core-master-data-consolidation-aim.md` §4).\n\n## The defect\n\n`api.plm_item_list` is defined as a straight `SELECT ... FROM erp_items_current`. Verified\nread-only on production:\n\n- `public.erp_items_current` — 17,703 rows, `source_system = 'designflow'` for every row,\n  **last synced 2026-05-21**. The application item list has been serving 3.5-month-old\n  DesignFlow data.\n- `plm.item` — 19,362 rows, `source_system = 'coldlion'`, last updated 2026-08-26.\n- `pg_get_viewdef` on `api.plm_item_list` contains no reference to `plm.item`.\n\nSo the canonical source is populated, fresher, and larger, and nothing points at it.\n\n## What the repoint requires (this is not a rename)\n\nThe view's 21 output columns do not exist as columns on `plm.item`. Mapping, all verified\npresent in `plm.item.raw` (ColdLion payload) unless noted:\n\n| View column | Source on `plm.item` |\n|---|---|\n| `source_id` | `source_id` (or `raw->>'itemNo'`) |\n| `style_number` | `style_number` |\n| `item_description` | `raw->>'itemDesc'` |\n| `mg_category` | `raw->>'mGCategory'` |\n| `mg01_code` … `mg06_code` | `raw->>'merchGroup01'` … `'merchGroup06'` |\n| `size_code` | `raw->>'sizeRangeCode'` / `'sizeExplosionCode'` — needs a ruling on which |\n| `division_code` | `raw->>'divisionCode'` (populated on all 19,362 rows) |\n| `licensor_code`, `property_code` | **gap** — `plm.item` carries FK ids, not codes, and only 13,012 of 19,362 rows have them resolved |\n| `prepack_code`, `prepack_codes` | **gap** — not present in the ColdLion item payload; a separate prepack source exists |\n| `dismissed` | **gap** — application state, currently held on `erp_items_current` |\n| `erp_updated_at`, `synced_at` | `updated_at` |\n| `source_system` | `source_system` |\n\nThree real gaps, each needing a decision rather than an author's judgement:\n\n1. **Licensor / property codes.** 6,350 rows have no resolved licensor or property. Decide\n   whether the view exposes codes derived from `core.licensor` / `core.property`, exposes\n   the raw ColdLion `royaltyCode`, or serves null and lets the screen show unresolved.\n2. **Prepack.** Source it from the prepack feed or drop the two columns from the contract.\n3. **`dismissed`.** This is application state, not source data. It must be carried to a\n   table keyed on the ColdLion item identity or it is lost at cutover.\n\n## Requested\n\n1. Author the mapping above as a migration replacing `api.plm_item_list` over `plm.item`,\n   preserving the column contract so consuming screens do not change.\n2. Resolve the three gaps first — 1 and 3 are lossy if guessed.\n3. Note that item counts on screens will move (17,703 → 19,362) and that stale DesignFlow\n   rows will disappear; that is the intended effect, not a regression.\n4. After the cutover, `public.erp_items_current` and `public.erp_items_raw` have no\n   remaining reader in this path; propose their disposition separately.\n\nRead-only inspection only was performed for this issue. No structure was changed.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - view api.plm_item_list\nreads:\n  - table plm.item\n  - table core.licensor\n  - table core.property\n```\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-09T18:29:45Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T18:42:10Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2466,"title":"Repoint api.plm_item_list at canonical plm.item (ColdLion) — owner authorized 2026-09-06","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:00Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2466"},
{"body":"## Problem\n\nThe guarded merge staleness check names the wrong files, so its documentation-only exemption is unreachable and every PR behind any merge is forced into a full re-review.\n\n## Evidence\n\nRun 34050674333, PR #2461, head `3cd211d089f8f67c6866d384c665bb228b309ef4`:\n\n```\nREFUSED: origin/main (e82eec28dda8dc65813882735b020cefd91f912b) has moved past the dispatched commit (8fa7408b087f0b321d2021ced7d1ee4ab543f53e) with changes that are not documentation: scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs, scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs. Re-dispatch against the current tip.\n```\n\nBut `git diff --name-only 8fa7408b e82eec28` is exactly:\n\n```\nAGENTS.md\ndocs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md\n```\n\nMain moved by documentation ONLY. The two script files it names are the files **this PR** changes, not files main moved. The check appears to be classifying the PR's own diff, or a union of the two, rather than the movement in `main` that the message describes.\n\n## Consequence\n\nThe exemption can never fire for any PR that touches a non-documentation file, which is every code PR. So every merge that lands invalidates every PR behind it, forcing a branch update, a new head, and a fresh pair of reviewer slots — from a pool of five, two of which are currently unusable (#2458 wrapper defect, and quota).\n\nPR #2461 has now burned three heads and six reviewer draws for a two-line change that earned clean approvals at every head. Each cycle also risks the void-after-create failure in #2464, which permanently burns a tuple.\n\n## Fix direction\n\nClassify the files in `git diff <dispatched-base>..<origin/main>` — the movement the message already describes — and nothing else. Add a test that a documentation-only movement in `main` does NOT refuse a PR whose own diff contains code.\n\nDo not fix this by removing the staleness check; requiring a current main before merge is correct. The defect is only in which set of files gets classified.\n\n## Scope\n\nMerge tooling. No database object is touched.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\npriority: 90\ndepends_on: none\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T00:26:44Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T18:09:12Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2465,"title":"Guarded merge staleness check classifies the PR's files, not main's, so the docs exemption never fires","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:01Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2465"},
{"body":"## Problem\n\n`scripts/run-governed-review.mjs` can create a valid verdict artifact and then destroy its own validity in the same run, permanently burning the (issue, PR, head, slot) tuple.\n\nSequence observed:\n1. The reviewer returns a genuine verdict and the runner posts the findings comment.\n2. The runner creates the verdict ref successfully.\n3. The runner's create-only readback compares the artifact against the live comment, disagrees, and refuses:\n   `REFUSED: create-only verdict readback disagrees with the created object; this tuple is permanently refused`\n4. Voiding rewrites the findings comment body — which changes the digest the artifact recorded.\n\nThe artifact is left existing but permanently invalid: its `findings_digest` no longer matches the live comment, and because the ref exists, the tuple can never be re-recorded.\n\n## Evidence\n\nPR #2461, issue #2460, head `c5a186effd6207d05a763fc422670c1db53e1fea`, slot 2, gemini-3.8-flash-high sequence 1490 (replacement for codex sequence 1489).\n\n- Artifact created: `refs/db-review-verdict-replacements/2460-2461-c5a186effd6207d05a763fc422670c1db53e1fea-slot2-1489`, object `43340d958e411e91583f550b66f4b7f7e9602980`, verdict APPROVE.\n- Recorded `findings_digest` `e0f057e9…`; live comment digest after voiding `25ffd8b5…`.\n- Positive control: the same digest method reproduces slot 1's digest exactly, so the mismatch is real and not a measurement artifact.\n\nSecond sighting. The first was PR #2455 slot 2 (muse-spark) at head `845fc255`, where the runner rewrote the verdict line to `> VOIDED REVIEWER LINE - VERDICT: REVISE 845fc255…`. That instance was harmless only because both verdicts happened to agree.\n\n## Why this is serious\n\nThere is no sanctioned exit. Drawing another replacement requires `--confirm-no-verdict --confirm-no-artifact`, and both assertions would be false — the reviewer produced a verdict AND an artifact. Asserting them would fabricate a coordination-ledger fact. The only remaining move is to move the PR head, which voids every valid verdict already earned at the old head and spends more scarce reviewer slots.\n\nThe reviewer pool is five. Each occurrence burns one slot and one head.\n\n## Fix direction\n\nOrder the operations so the artifact is created only after the findings comment is final, or make the readback compare against the comment state the artifact was built from rather than a body the runner is about to rewrite. If a void is genuinely required, the artifact must not be left behind — a refused tuple with a dangling invalid ref is worse than no ref, because it forecloses recovery.\n\nAlso add a recovery path for an existing-but-invalid artifact that does not require asserting facts known to be false.\n\n## Scope\n\nReview tooling. No database object is touched.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\npriority: 95\ndepends_on: none\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T00:13:53Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T17:54:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2464,"title":"Governed review voids the artifact it just created, permanently burning the tuple","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:03Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2464"},
{"body":"Tracking issue for PR #2462.\n\nGemini is drawable in the rotation but a governed Gemini review can never record a verdict: `ai-gemini` opens its reply with a `## Verdict` heading and a bare decision word (voided here as a stray decision line) and prints a `PASS session=...` summary instead of the review body this runner reads from stdout.\n\npopcre/ai-devops#299 added `--governed-verdict <head>` to the wrapper. This change injects that flag in `run-governed-review.mjs` from the head under review, so no caller has to remember it and a mismatched head is refused.\n\n```machine\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\nobjects: none\n```\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 70\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-06T18:38:22Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T17:52:37Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2463,"title":"Give ai-gemini the governed verdict contract so its reviews can be recorded","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:04Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2463"},
{"body":"## Problem\n\nAn expired migration-author claim whose object list has legitimately grown beyond its work issue's scope block can never be recovered. All three exits refuse, and the refusals form a closed cycle.\n\nLive case: claim #2405, issue #2334, PR #2409 (`Migration author lease` check is RED with `REFUSED: claim #2405 is expired`).\n\n- `--renew-claim` → `REFUSED: claim does not cover parsed pull request objects: trigger assert_canonical_edge_still_supported on core.property_character_source_edge, … core.property_franchise_source_edge, … dam.asset_property_source_edge, … dam.asset_style_guide_source_edge`. Renewal needs the claim to already cover the PR.\n- `--expand-active-claim-from-pr` would add exactly those four triggers, but refuses with `target claim lease is legacy or expired`. Expansion needs an active lease.\n- `--recover-expired-claim-from-pr`, the tool built for precisely \"expired **and** uncovered objects\", refuses with `renewal issue objects do not exactly match the permanent claim objects`.\n\n## Root cause\n\n`recoverExpiredClaimFromPr` calls `renewalIssueScope(workIssue, lease, [issue])` at lines 4708 and 4729 without `allowClaimSuperset`, so it defaults to `false` and line 4606 enforces `issueObjects.length === claimObjects.length`.\n\nClaim #2405 lists 93 objects. Issue #2334's `db-work-scope` names 16 writes and 5 reads. Every issue object IS present in the claim — the subset test passes. Only the count equality fails.\n\n`resumeAuthorLease` passes `allowClaimSuperset: true` at both of its call sites (4633, 4658). `expandActiveClaimFromPr` grows a claim beyond its issue scope by design and does not call `renewalIssueScope` at all — it only checks that the work issue is open/ready/structural/orchestrator.\n\nSo a claim exceeding its issue scope is a **sanctioned, tool-produced state**, and the equality check in the recovery path makes recovery impossible for every claim that has ever been expanded. The equality is not a safety property; it is inconsistent with the rest of the family.\n\n## Fix direction\n\nPass `allowClaimSuperset: true` at lines 4708 and 4729, matching `resumeAuthorLease`. The meaningful guarantee — every object named by the work issue is covered by the claim — is preserved by the subset test at line 4606 and is unchanged.\n\nAdd a regression test: an expired claim holding a strict superset of its issue's scope objects, with uncovered PR objects, must recover. Assert it fails without the flag.\n\n**Do not** weaken anything else, do not touch the `--release-claim` guard, and do not \"fix\" this by editing issue #2334's scope block to enumerate 93 objects — the scope block states the work, not the accumulated lock set, and hand-editing a coordination ledger to satisfy a checker is not a repair.\n\n## Consequence\n\nPR #2409 cannot merge while this stands. It is the head of the structural merge queue.\n\n## Scope\n\nCoordination tooling. No database object is touched.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\npriority: 95\ndepends_on: none\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-06T21:43:42Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T16:43:38Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2460,"title":"Expired claim recovery is impossible for any claim that was ever expanded","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:46:06Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2460"},
{"body":"## Problem\n\n`recoverStaleAuthorMutex` (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:~1944) recognizes only an allowlisted set of owner-commit kinds. Three kinds that also take `MUTEX_REF` are absent from it:\n\n- `reviewer-exclusion-lock` — line 2451\n- `merged-claim-reissue-lock` — line 3601\n- `reviewer-release-lock` — line 3774\n\nA crash while holding the mutex under any of these strands an owner commit that recovery refuses to release. That wedges every claim, release, renewal and supersession in the repository — the same failure mode found on PR #2455 for `duplicate-claim-release` and fixed there.\n\n## Evidence\n\nFound by glm-5.3 during the governed review of PR #2455 at head `2143434da500942d300eca199ea631d14eeaa7b5` (artifact `refs/db-review-verdicts/2454-2455-2143434da500942d300eca199ea631d14eeaa7b5-slot2`). Reported as non-blocking for that PR because all three pre-date it at base; the PR introduced none of them.\n\n## Fix direction\n\nAdd the three kinds to the allowlist alternation, and add a recovery test per kind that strands a real owner commit on `MUTEX_REF` and asserts `recoverStaleAuthorMutex` releases it — matching the test PR #2455 added. Then audit for a structural fix so a new lock kind cannot be minted without being recoverable, rather than relying on a hand-maintained list that has now silently drifted twice.\n\n## Scope\n\nCoordination tooling in this repository. No database object is touched.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\ndepends_on: 2454\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-15T22:03:18Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T16:31:35Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2459,"title":"Three mutex lock kinds are missing from the stale-mutex recovery allowlist","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:06Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2459"},
{"body":"## Problem\n\n`scripts/run-governed-review.mjs` can never record a verdict from the `ai-gemini` wrapper, so Gemini can never authorize a merge even though it was just returned to the active rotation by #2441 / PR #2446.\n\n## Evidence\n\nGoverned review of PR #2446, issue #2441, head `b1e588e587358ec1c6119edeee74f9a2f69428e1`, slot 1, sequence 1470, reviewer `gemini-3.8-flash-high`:\n\n```\nREFUSED: review wrapper did not produce a recordable terminal verdict (exit 0)\n```\n\nExit 0 — not a quota, transport, or provider fault. `/c/repos/ai-devops/bin/ai-gemini` line 105 ends with `printf 'PASS session=%s report=%s\\n'` and writes the entire review body to a git-ignored report file. `run-governed-review.mjs` parses only stdout, so the `VERDICT: <decision> <head-sha>` line never reaches it.\n\nThe review itself was real and complete: report `gemini-gov-2446-slot1-20260906T162024Z-131860.md`, 12,647 bytes, conversation `fb20a578-d3b2-4920-a13a-184f88450db7`, terminal line `VERDICT: REVISE b1e588e587358ec1c6119edeee74f9a2f69428e1`, coverage stated over 20 file/line spans.\n\n`git ls-remote origin 'refs/db-review-verdicts/*2446*'` is empty. Only the two assignment refs exist.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nGemini was re-admitted to the rotation on the strength of producing a well-formed VERDICT line. It does produce one — into a file the governed runner does not read. Every slot Gemini is drawn for is spent and returns nothing, and the head-wide verdict check then obstructs re-drawing. The same structural mismatch is already known for `ai-codex-review`.\n\n## Fix direction\n\nEither have `ai-gemini` emit the terminal verdict line on stdout, or have `run-governed-review.mjs` read the wrapper's declared `report=` path. Do not work around this by pasting a verdict line — a hand-run review records nothing and a pasted verdict is a counterfeit.\n\n## Scope\n\nRepo maintenance / ai-devops tooling. Not a database structure change; this is not orchestrator work and must not occupy a migration-author lane.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\npriority: 85\ndepends_on: none\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-06T23:05:55Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T16:24:11Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2458,"title":"ai-gemini wrapper writes its verdict to a file the governed runner never reads","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:07Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2458"},
{"body":"## Observed 2026-09-06\n\n`--reviewer-capacity` on a five-reviewer pool:\n\n```\ngrok-4.6                   live                issue 2434 pr 2409 seq 1476 verdict false\nglm-5.3                    stale-reclaimable   issue 2334 pr 2409 seq 1472 verdict true\nmuse-spark-1.2-contributor stale-reclaimable   issue 2434 pr 2409 seq 1473 verdict true\ncodex-gpt-5.6-sol          free\ngemini-3.8-flash-high      live                issue 2441 pr 2446 seq 1470 verdict false\n```\n\nThree of five slots are held by leases on **one** PR. Two of those three are finished work: glm-5.3 delivered the round-2 REVISE, muse-spark delivered the round-1/round-3 APPROVE. Both verdicts are captured. Neither reviewer is doing anything.\n\n## The gap\n\nThere is an exit for a reviewer that **failed** and an exit for a reviewer that went **silent**, and none for a reviewer that **succeeded**.\n\n- `--reclaim-silent-reviewer` refuses: `silent reviewer reclaim requires explicit confirmation that the session produced no verdict and no artifact`. Correct — the verdict exists.\n- `--release-failed-reviewer` requires a code from `TERMINAL_FAILURE_CODES` (`insufficient_quota`, `provider_unavailable`, `local_dependency_unavailable`, `wrapper_terminal_failure`, `turn_limit_cancelled`, `reviewer_cannot_read_repository`). None describes a completed review, and using one would write a false permanent failure record against a working provider — the exact harm the code comments at lines 195-203 say this design exists to prevent.\n\nSo a successful review is the one outcome that leaves its slot occupied indefinitely. With the only free reviewer out of quota until 10:29 PM, the pool is effectively at zero and every other PR waits.\n\n## Requested\n\nAn explicit release for a **completed** lease, proved rather than asserted: the durable verdict artifact for that reviewer's sequence exists, and either the PR is closed/merged or its head has moved past the reviewed SHA. No failure code, no failure evidence, no rotation slot spent — the reviewer did its job.\n\nRelated: #1767 (reviewer-allocator redesign), `plan_reviewer_lease_capacity_truth.md` (steps 1-6 complete; that plan gave failure an exit and never gave success one).\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 85\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-15T20:57:52Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T15:52:35Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2456,"title":"A reviewer that finished cannot be released: only failure and silence have exits","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:10Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2456"},
{"body":"## Live blocker\n\nPR #2409 cannot merge. The required `Migration author lease` check fails:\n\n```\nREFUSED: migration PR branch claude/issue-2334-canonical-bridges must have exactly one active ref-backed claim; found 2\n```\n\nThe two claims are #2405 (the authoring claim, holding version `20260906033021`, which is the version the PR's migration file actually uses) and #2444 (a duplicate opened by an orchestrator dispatch error, holding a different version that the PR does not use).\n\n## Why nothing can clear it\n\n`scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.mjs` counts every open non-legacy claim whose lease branch equals the PR branch. Capacity state and expiry are not consulted, so relinquishing #2444's author lease does not reduce the count. Only closing it does.\n\n`--release-claim` refuses:\n\n```js\nif((io.openPulls?.() ?? io.prSources()).some((pr)=>(pr.head?.ref ?? pr.branch)===lease.branch))\n  throw new LaneError(`claim branch ${lease.branch} still has an open pull request`)\n```\n\nThat guard is right in the ordinary case — it stops a claim being released while its work is still in flight. It is wrong here because it cannot distinguish *the* claim for a branch from *a duplicate* on a branch another claim already owns. Every other recovery path is pinned to a historical incident (`--recover-same-owner-split` is hard-coded to claims #1058/#1063) or addresses a different condition.\n\nSo the only two ways out are hand-editing a claim's fenced block, which is forbidden, or bypassing a required check, which is worse. The capability is missing, not misused.\n\n## Requested repair\n\nAdd a narrow, provable release path for a duplicate claim. It must refuse unless **all** of these hold, each proved from live GitHub state rather than asserted by the caller:\n\n1. At least one **other** open non-legacy claim declares the same branch.\n2. The claim being released does **not** hold the migration version that any migration file in that branch's open PR actually uses.\n3. Another open claim on that branch **does** hold that version.\n4. Owner matches, and the mutex is held for the whole operation.\n\nDo not widen the existing guard, and do not add a caller-supplied override flag — the point is that the tool proves the duplicate is not the authority.\n\nAlso fix, in the same change, the close comment defect filed as #2448: a claim released this way must not be labelled \"Expired migration-author lease closed by guarded cleanup\", which asserts a sweep that never ran and sent a previous dispatch chasing an isolation failure that had not happened.\n\nShip with tests covering: the duplicate releases; the authority claim on the same branch is refused; a lone claim on a branch with an open PR is still refused.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 95\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-06T23:06:30Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T15:41:17Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2454,"title":"No sanctioned way to release a duplicate author claim while the branch legitimately has an open PR","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:12Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2454"},

{"body":"# CORRECTED — this issue was originally filed on a wrong premise\n\nThe original body of this issue reported \"duplicate masters\" across items, properties,\nlicensors and customers. **That framing is wrong and is withdrawn.** Per owner correction:\nper-source landing tables are the *intended* architecture, and rationalization into\ncanonical tables is deliberately in progress. `docs/core-master-data-consolidation-aim.md`\n§10 and §11 say exactly this, and `docs/master-data-cutover-scoreboard.md` warns in\nwriting that a previous AI session made this same misreading — both tables existing side\nby side is the *tell for a completed cutover*, not a defect.\n\nWhat follows replaces it: a status register of the rationalization, verified read-only\nagainst production. No row content is reproduced here.\n\n## Canonical target per entity — built? populated? pointed at?\n\n| Entity | Canonical target | Exists | Rows | App reads it? |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Licensor | `core.licensor` | yes | 27 | partly |\n| Property | `core.property` | yes | 261 | partly |\n| Property alias | `core.property_alias` | yes | 0 | no |\n| Character | `core.character` (+ `core.property_character_associations`) | yes | 0 / 0 | no |\n| Style guide | `core.style_guide` (+ `_character`) | yes | 0 / 0 | no |\n| Property↔Style guide | `core.property_style_guide` | **absent** | — | — |\n| Franchise | `core.franchise` (+ `_alias`) | yes | 0 / 0 | no |\n| Property↔Franchise | `core.property_franchise` | **absent** | — | — |\n| Asset metadata | `dam.asset` | yes | 0 | no — live data is elsewhere |\n| Item | `plm.item` (ColdLion-fed) | yes | **19,362** | **no** |\n| Customer | `core.customer` | yes | 826 | yes (cut over) |\n| Vendor | `core.factory` | yes | — | yes (cut over) |\n\n## The findings that survive\n\n1. **Item master is built but not connected.** `plm.item` holds 19,362 ColdLion rows.\n   The application-facing view `api.plm_item_list` still reads `public.erp_items_current`\n   (17,703 rows, DesignFlow-derived) and contains no reference to `plm.item` at all.\n   The canonical source the owner named is populated and unused. This is the single\n   highest-value remaining step.\n\n2. **The designed decision table has never been used.** `plm.source_resolution` — the\n   documented mechanism for recording which source wins for a given Master Data fact —\n   has **0 rows**. Meanwhile two ad-hoc property decision ledgers were built separately\n   and both hold rows (see #2449). The rationalization is being recorded outside its own\n   designed mechanism.\n\n3. **The last leg of the property pipeline was designed and never built.** Landing →\n   adapter view → decision → guarded consolidation into `core.property`: the consolidation\n   contract (plan Step 2.4) is still Open. That is why every downstream canonical table\n   (character, style guide, franchise, alias) is at 0 rows.\n\n4. **Two link tables the plan requires do not exist:** `core.property_style_guide` and\n   `core.property_franchise`.\n\n5. **`dam.asset` is canonical and empty** while the live asset relationships sit in the\n   `public` tables (145k assets and their tag/character/style-guide edges). No migration\n   into `dam` is documented. Any code aimed at the canonical schema reads zero rows and\n   reports \"no data\" instead of failing — a live trap.\n\n## Documentation defects found (each cheap to fix, each currently misleading)\n\n- The cutover scoreboard is stale: it reports counts that have since moved\n  (`erp_property` 0→10, taxonomy source refs 0→10, customer 862→826).\n- The licensing plan states `core.franchise` does not exist. It exists (0 rows).\n- Docs state `plm.item` is empty. It holds 19,362 rows and its Phase 4 was never done.\n- The relationship and intended fate of `plm.item` vs `plm.itemHeader` is documented\n  nowhere, despite the owner ruling that ColdLion is canonical and DesignFlow is not used.\n- The retirement of the `dflow.*` schemas rests on a ruling referenced as \"R5\" that is\n  marked DRAFT/UNCONFIRMED and appears in no file, commit or issue.\n- Nothing documents who owns licensor→property parentage after cutover.\n- `core.vendor`, `core.\"externalVendor\"`, `core.\"externalCustomer\"` and\n  `core.\"vendorGroup\"` have no documented disposition. These are what made the original\n  version of this issue look like duplicate masters.\n- The raw `coldlion.*` landing schema is empty; the decision to fill or drop it was\n  parked and is now due, since ColdLion is canonical.\n\n## Separately worth their own issues (not duplication)\n\n- 30 `source_id` values collide between the Lucasfilm and Disney DCP landing tables — a\n  real join hazard given the recorded lesson that opaque source IDs collide across\n  licensors.\n- Three `_canonical_property_edge` tables in the WB family were created and never\n  populated; likely dead structure.\n- Empty snake_case twins of live camelCase `core` tables (`merch_group`, `product_type`,\n  `product_category`, `product_subtype`) — a second naming layer started and abandoned.\n  `plm.merch_group_header` holds 2 rows against 45 in the live twin: a partial write into\n  the wrong table.\n\n## Requested\n\n1. Prioritise finding 1 — point the item list at `plm.item`.\n2. Build the consolidation contract (finding 3); everything else in `core` is blocked on it.\n3. Correct the documentation defects listed above; several actively mislead readers into\n   the same wrong conclusion this issue was originally filed on.\n4. Route findings 2 and 5 with #2449.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-20T15:33:47Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T14:49:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2450,"title":"CORRECTED: Master Data rationalization status register (canonical tables built, not connected)","updatedAt":"2026-09-20T15:34:15Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2450"},
{"body":"## Symptom (owner-reported, 2026-09-06)\n\nEvery Disney Creative title on the Scraped Properties page — Cinderella, Aladdin, Bambi and 145 others — still renders red/\"Unmapped\" despite having an **approved** match.\n\n## Root cause: two ledgers record the same fact and never sync\n\n- `plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution` (+`_member`) — 346 rows, 148 approved for `disney_dcpvault`. This is what `api.db_data_admin_decide_property_match` writes; it is the ONLY ledger the live Property Match Review screen writes.\n- `plm.creative_submission_property_resolution` (+`_member`) — 1,148 rows. This is what `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties` reads for `mapping_state`. For `disney_dcpvault` it holds 237 rows, **all `unmapped`**.\n\nEvidence:\n\n```\ncreative_source_system | creative_source_table | decision_state | count\nwarner_starlabs        | plm.wb_property       | mapped         | 261\ndisney_dcpvault        | plm.dcp_property      | unmapped       | 237   <-- zero mapped\n```\n\n```\nsource_property_id                    | approval_status | approved_at                    | members\ndcpvault:characters/ci/cinderella     | approved        | 2026-09-05 23:51:55.789837-04  | 1\ndcpvault:properties/al/aladdin        | approved        | 2026-09-02 22:16:18.262514-04  | 1\ndcpvault:properties/ba/bambi          | approved        | 2026-09-02 22:16:18.275090-04  | 1\n```\n\nThe same three IDs are `decision_state='unmapped'` in `creative_submission_property_resolution`.\n\n## Provenance\n\n- `20260828003806_creative_submission_property_resolution.sql` (issue #1713) created a **source-neutral** Creative→Submissions ledger.\n- `20260830130345_opa_authority_for_dcp_creative.sql` (issue #1658) created a **Disney-only** DCP→OPA ledger two days later, with the studio-split evidence columns Disney needs.\n\nNeither knew about the other. There is no writer function for `creative_submission_property_resolution` at all — `pg_get_functiondef` across `api`/`plm`/`public`/`core` returns only the reader plus two mutation-rejection triggers. Its Warner rows were loaded once by a migration and nothing has updated them since. So the general ledger is frozen while the Disney-specific one accumulates the real decisions.\n\n## Requested structural change\n\nCollapse to ONE Creative→Submissions decision ledger.\n\nDirection (author to confirm against `AGENTS.md`):\n\n1. Generalise the append-only decision ledger the live RPC already writes: widen `dcp_opa_property_resolution_identity_ck` beyond the three DCP source tables, and generalise `_member.licensed_property_id` (FK to `plm.opa_property`) to the generic `(submission_source_system, submission_source_table, submission_source_id)` triple the other ledger uses, preserving the OPA FK as a constrained case.\n2. Migrate the 278 existing `creative_submission_property_resolution_member` rows (261 Warner + 11 NBCU + 6 Sega mapped) into it, preserving `decision_version`/supersession.\n3. Repoint `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties`'s `mapping_state`/`submissions` enrichment at the single ledger.\n4. Retire `plm.creative_submission_property_resolution` and `_member`.\n\nAlso clear the stale duplicate **pending** rows sitting behind already-approved decisions (`dcpvault:properties/al/aladdin` has an approved version with 1 member and a pending version with 3).\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- Cinderella, Aladdin and Bambi read `mapped` on the Scraped Properties page.\n- Exactly one table in the database records \"which Submissions property does this Creative property map to\".\n- Warner's 261 mapped rows still read `mapped` after the migration.\n\nDo not dual-write the two ledgers — dual-write is the defect, not the fix.\n\nRelated: the wider duplicate-structure audit filed alongside this issue.\n\n\n---\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 90\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution\n  - table plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member\n  - table plm.creative_submission_property_resolution\n  - table plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties\n  - function api.db_data_admin_decide_property_match\n  - table plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_archive\n  - table plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member_archive\n  - column plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution.creative_decision_state\n  - function plm.enforce_dcp_opa_crosswalk_members\n  - trigger dcp_opa_property_resolution_mapping_members_check on plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution\n  - trigger dcp_opa_property_resolution_member_mapping_header_check on plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member\n  - trigger creative_submission_property_resolution_archive_no_insert on plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_archive\n  - trigger creative_submission_property_resolution_member_archive_no_insert on plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member_archive\n  - trigger creative_submission_member_archive_no_insert on plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member_archive\n  - policy dcp_opa_property_resolution_read on plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution\nreads:\n  - table plm.opa_property\n  - table plm.dcp_property\n  - table plm.wb_property\n```\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-08T12:16:44Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T14:49:07Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2449,"title":"Two ledgers record the same Creative-to-Submissions decision: 148 approved Disney matches read as unmapped","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:18Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2449"},
{"body":"Two defects surfaced during the #2433 preview rehearsal on 2026-09-06. The first made a correct operation look like a safety incident and cost a real investigation; the second silently breaks any claim whose title mentions a second issue.\n\n## 1. Every claim-close path posts the same \"expired lease / guarded cleanup\" comment, including paths that are neither\n\n`io.closeClaim()` (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:1573`) hard-codes one comment:\n\n> `Expired migration-author lease closed by guarded cleanup. Its migration version remains unavailable.`\n\nIt has exactly two call sites, and **neither of them is an expiry sweep**:\n\n- **`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:4403`** — the rollback inside `acquireAuthorLane` that closes a claim it *just created* after losing the coordination mutex.\n- **`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:5497`** — `--release-claim`, a deliberate, owner-confirmed, guard-checked release.\n\n`--cleanup-stale` (line 5501) closes nothing at all; it only reports and tells the operator to release each claim explicitly.\n\nSo the message asserts a cause that never applies. The audit trail on every closed claim in this repository currently says a lease expired and a sweep collected it, whichever of the two things actually happened.\n\n**What it cost.** Claim #2445 was closed at `2026-09-06T14:37:20Z` carrying `expires_at: 2026-09-07T02:35:24.472Z` — a lease nearly twelve hours in the future. The dispatched agent read the comment, correctly concluded that no sweep should have touched a live lease, and reported a wrongful-cleanup defect. The orchestrator then spent a full investigation confirming that `--cleanup-stale` cannot close anything before the message itself turned out to be the defect. A running agent was told its live claim had been swept out from under it, which is a serious-sounding isolation failure, by a string constant.\n\nThis is the same shape as the reviewer-replacement refusal that misstated its own cause: a message that describes a mechanism other than the one that ran is worse than no message, because it is believed and acted on.\n\n**Fix:** state the actual cause at each call site — a rollback after mutex loss, and an explicit owner-confirmed release — and stop claiming expiry. Note that `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:4815` currently *verifies* the exact hard-coded string when recovering a closed claim, so the recovery check has to be updated in the same change or it will start refusing valid closures.\n\n## 2. A second issue number anywhere in a claim title makes the claim permanently unusable\n\n`manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:1689` refuses with:\n\n> `open claim #<n> ambiguously identifies work issue #<issue>`\n\nwhenever `claimTitleIssues()` finds more than one `#NNNN` in the title. Claim #2445 was titled `CLAIM: #2433 HANDOVER: preview rehearsal owed for merged PR #2423` — the second number came from the work issue's own title, not from operator error, and the claim was dead on arrival until it was retitled by hand.\n\nAny handover issue that names its PR in its title will do this to the next claim opened from it, and nothing warns at claim-creation time. The refusal arrives later, from a different command, against a claim that already reserved a migration version.\n\n**Fix (either or both):** refuse at `--claim` time with a message that names the offending second reference, and/or have the claim helper strip trailing `#NNNN` references from the borrowed title so only the work issue survives.\n\n## Cost so far\n\nMigration versions `20260906143510`, `20260906143535` and the version reserved by #2445 are permanently spent on claims that authored nothing.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 40\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T07:16:19Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T14:45:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake.
