{"body":"## Authorised by Albert 2026-09-06: chain the counts reconcile to the rebuild's completion\n\nSplitting the one live item out of #2417 into its own actionable claim.\n\n## Verified production state\n\n```\njobid 6   45 3 * * *   nightly-reconcile-sg-asset-counts   SELECT public.refresh_style_group_counts_batch(array_agg(id)) FROM public.style_groups;\njobid 7   0  6 * * *   nightly-rebuild-style-groups        SELECT public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups();\n```\n\nSchedules are UTC; locally that is **23:45** and **02:00**. Job 6 recomputes the asset count for every style group **2 h 15 m before** the rebuild that changes which assets belong to which group.\n\nThe counts are therefore always computed against yesterday's membership. Every group whose membership changes in the nightly rebuild carries a stale count for a full day, and it is never wrong in a way anyone can see — the number is plausible, just old.\n\nJob 6 is also unbatched despite its name: `array_agg(id) FROM style_groups` passes **every** group in one array to a function measured at ~98.6 s per call. It is the most expensive thing in the nightly window and it is being spent on input that is about to be invalidated.\n\n## The change\n\nJob 6 stops running on a clock and runs when the rebuild finishes.\n\nThe rebuild is asynchronous — job 7 only enqueues, and an external worker drives it, recording state in `admin_config.BULK_OPERATIONS -> 'rebuild-style-groups' -> status`. So \"chain off completion\" means: **fire the reconcile on the transition into a successful terminal status**, not at a fixed time.\n\nTwo viable mechanisms; I recommend the first.\n\n**A. Worker-signalled (preferred).** The worker calls the reconcile as its own final stage on success, inside the run it just completed. Correct by construction — it cannot fire against a rebuild that did not happen, and it cannot fire twice.\n\n**B. Watcher job.** A short pg_cron job polling every 10 min that fires the reconcile once when the status transitions to completed *and* a per-run marker has not been recorded. Needs the `run_id` recorded to stay idempotent, or a stuck-completed state will re-reconcile every 10 minutes forever.\n\nEither way, delete job 6's `45 3 * * *` schedule.\n\n## Requirements\n\n1. **Never fire on a failed or interrupted rebuild.** As of today the live status is `interrupted` (#2439). Firing the reconcile there spends ~98 s to recompute counts from membership the rebuild never touched — the current behaviour, and exactly what this change exists to stop.\n2. **Idempotent per run.** Keyed on `run_id`, not on status alone.\n3. **Keep a floor.** If no successful rebuild completes for N days, counts silently stop refreshing and nothing says so. Either a weekly unconditional pass or an alert — the failure mode this change introduces is *silence*, and it must not be added without a detector. See #2437 rule on new failure modes.\n4. **Batch it.** While the call site is being moved, stop passing all groups in one array.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- **#2439** should be understood first. Chaining to a completion signal that currently never arrives would stop the reconcile entirely rather than reorder it. That is a strictly worse state than today's stale-but-running counts, and requirement 3 is what prevents it.\n- **#2408** changes what the rebuild writes. No conflict, but land in a known order.\n\n## Provenance\n\nOwner-authorised in chat, 2026-09-06: *\"go, chain the job\"*. Supersedes the `needs-albert` hold on #2417, which can now close once this is queued.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 25\ndepends_on: 2439\nwrites:\n  - function public.refresh_style_group_counts_batch\n  - function public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups\nreads:\n  - table public.admin_config\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-09T06:18:05Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T13:41:38Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2440,"title":"Chain nightly-reconcile-sg-asset-counts to the rebuild's completion instead of 45 3 * * * (owner-authorised)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:28Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2440"},
{"body":"## The nightly style-group rebuild failed this morning, and nothing reported it\r\n\r\nRead from production `admin_config.BULK_OPERATIONS -> 'rebuild-style-groups'` on 2026-09-06:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n\"status\": \"interrupted\",\r\n\"last_stage\": \"clear_assets\",\r\n\"error\": \"Database RPC batch failed (rpc=assets_exact_count, stage=clear_assets)\\nDatabase error supplied no message\",\r\n\"started_at\": \"2026-09-06T06:00:01.739Z\",\r\n\"updated_at\": \"2026-09-06T06:00:09.953Z\",\r\n\"interruption_reason_code\": \"unknown\",\r\n\"progress\": { \"total_processed\": 0, \"assigned\": 0, \"groups\": 0, \"cleared\": 0 }\r\n```\r\n\r\nIt died **8.2 seconds in, having processed zero assets.** The whole nightly rebuild did not happen.\r\n\r\n## The part that matters more than the failure\r\n\r\n`cron.job_run_details` reports job 7 `nightly-rebuild-style-groups` as **`succeeded`** for that exact run, and for every one of the last ten nights:\r\n\r\n```\r\njobid 7   succeeded   2026-09-06 02:00:00-04   \"1 row\"\r\njobid 7   succeeded   2026-09-05 02:00:00-04   \"1 row\"\r\n...\r\n```\r\n\r\nBoth statements are true. Job 7's entire body is:\r\n\r\n```sql\r\nSELECT public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups();\r\n```\r\n\r\nThat function only writes a `queued` row into `admin_config` and returns. **cron measures the enqueue, not the rebuild.** An external worker performs the actual walk, and its outcome is invisible to every scheduler-level check we have. The green tick is real and it means nothing about whether the work was done.\r\n\r\nSo: a rebuild can fail every night indefinitely while the only monitoring surface we have stays green. That is the live condition right now.\r\n\r\n## And we cannot tell how long\r\n\r\n`admin_config` holds **one** state object per operation, overwritten on every run. There is no run history. Today's `interrupted` erased whatever yesterday said. So the honest answer to \"how long has this been failing?\" is *unknown, and unknowable from what we store* — it could be one night or three weeks. That is the same defect shape as the reviewer ledger: the record answers \"now\", never \"when\".\r\n\r\nThe one clue that it is not longstanding: `refresh_style_group_counts_batch` shows only 6 lifetime calls at ~98.6 s each, consistent with the counts path having run rarely rather than nightly-and-failing.\r\n\r\n## Not an emergency tonight\r\n\r\n`queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups()` skips only when status is `running` or `queued`. `interrupted` does not block it, so tonight's 06:00 UTC run will re-enqueue normally and may well succeed. **No production write is needed now, and I have made none.**\r\n\r\n## Ask\r\n\r\n1. **Diagnose `assets_exact_count` at stage `clear_assets`.** The error carries no message — \"Database error supplied no message\" — which itself needs fixing; a failure that cannot say why costs more than the failure.\r\n2. **Persist run history.** Append terminal outcomes to a small `bulk_operation_runs` table (run_id, operation, status, stage, error, started_at, ended_at) rather than overwriting one JSON blob. Without it no failure here is ever measurable.\r\n3. **Alert on the worker's outcome, not cron's.** Any check that reads `cron.job_run_details` for this job is structurally incapable of detecting the failure it is meant to detect.\r\n\r\nRelated: #2417 (cron ordering), #2408 (rebuild guard + ungroup arm), #2437 (absence is not proof — this is the same error wearing a green tick instead of a zero).\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 20\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table public.bulk_operation_runs\r\nreads:\r\n  - table public.admin_config\r\n```\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-11T09:24:19Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T13:41:10Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2439,"title":"The nightly style-group rebuild failed this morning and cron reported success — the scheduler measures the enqueue, not the work","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:30Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2439"},
{"body":"## The pattern behind the near-misses\r\n\r\nAcross recent sessions, every close call with valid data has had the same shape. Not a missing document, not a careless operator — the same reasoning error, reached carefully each time:\r\n\r\n**A measurement reported absence, and absence was treated as proof.**\r\n\r\n| Session finding | The measurement | Why it was wrong | What was nearly lost |\r\n|---|---|---|---|\r\n| \"Two tables hold 1.8 GB of empty space\" | `n_live_tup = 0` on both | Statistics had been reset 8 days earlier | 2,173,392 and 1,156,758 real rows |\r\n| \"These indexes are unused, ~285 MB reclaimable\" | `idx_scan` = 0 or single digits | The 8.1-day counter window contained **zero writes** to the table | Indexes serving a bursty monthly load |\r\n| \"This migration is the newest definition\" | Newest file matching a grep | A later migration redefined the same function | A migration reverting a live fix |\r\n| \"The rehearsal database was deleted\" | Ref absent from `projects list` | Branches are not projects; wrong list | A day of frozen merges, plus a proposal to rebuild a healthy database |\r\n| \"This field is dead\" (earlier) | 291-row sample showed empty | 3,981 rows showed 70% populated | A wrong report already sent to a vendor |\r\n\r\nIn every row the measurement was real, the query was correct, and the number was accurate. What was wrong was the **window or the scope** the number covered — and nothing in the number itself said so. A zero from a reset counter is bit-identical to a zero from a genuinely unused object.\r\n\r\n## Why the existing guards did not catch any of these\r\n\r\n`scripts/production_migration_guard.py`, `check-sql.sh`, the nine-check merge gate and the business-risk gate are all substantial, and they all sit on the **migration path**. They inspect a governed SQL file on its way to production.\r\n\r\nNot one of these near-misses was a migration file. Every one came from the **analysis path**: a session reading production, forming a conclusion about what is empty / unused / dead / superseded, and then either acting on it directly or writing it into an issue for someone else to act on. That path has no gate on it at all. The most dangerous artifact we produce is not a migration — it is a confidently-worded issue body recommending a drop, because it launders a bad measurement into someone else's authorised work.\r\n\r\nConfirmed live: #2427's body proposed ~285 MB of index drops for a full day while the finding that invalidated it sat in a comment. The queue tool parses bodies and ignores comments.\r\n\r\n## Ask: gate the analysis path, in four rules\r\n\r\n**1. A claim of absence must carry its window, and the window must be shown to contain the activity.**\r\nNo conclusion of \"empty\", \"unused\", \"dead\", \"static\" or \"superseded\" is admissible without stating the observation window and a **positive control** — a case the same measurement *did* catch. `pg_stat_bgwriter.stats_reset` vs `pg_postmaster_start_time()` detects a reset in one query, and `n_tup_ins = 0` against a multi-million-row table is the cheap tell.\r\n\r\n**2. Absence must be confirmed by a second, independent source before it authorises anything.**\r\nIn all five rows above a second source was available, cheap, and would have flipped the answer: row timestamps beat `pg_stat` counters and survive resets; the branches API beats the projects list; the merged tree beats a grep for the newest filename. The rule is that the two sources must fail *differently* — re-running the same query is not corroboration, and neither is three sessions agreeing when all three read the same key.\r\n\r\n**3. Measurement and deletion must be separated in time, by a fresh re-read.**\r\nA session that produces a drop candidate may not authorise the drop. The candidate list goes to an issue with an explicit earliest-action date and a re-read protocol; the drop is authorised only by a later, independent measurement whose window is proved to contain real activity. This is already how #2427 is gated — it should be the standard, not one issue's local invention.\r\n\r\n**4. Structural arguments outrank usage arguments and may proceed without waiting.**\r\n\"This index is redundant because another index has it as a leading-column prefix\" is provable from the catalog and cannot be poisoned by a counter reset. \"This index has zero scans\" cannot be proved from anything but a trustworthy window. Split every candidate list into these two classes and say which class each item is in. Only the structural class can move immediately.\r\n\r\n## Mechanisable now\r\n\r\n- A checklist template for any issue proposing a DROP, TRUNCATE, VACUUM FULL, or bulk DELETE: window, positive control, second independent source, evidence class, earliest-action date. A CI check can require those headings in the **body** of any issue carrying a destructive-proposal label.\r\n- Extend the existing destructive-pattern matching in `check-sql.sh` beyond migrations to any SQL in a PR.\r\n- A one-query reusable snippet that returns the statistics reset time alongside any `pg_stat` reading, so a counter can never be quoted undated.\r\n\r\nFiling this as the general fix. #2429 is the same failure in the narrow case of project refs; #2427 is the live instance currently held under rule 3.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\r\nroute: repo-maintenance\r\npriority: 60\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\nreads:\r\n```\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-14T20:00:31Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T13:35:17Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2437,"title":"Guard the analysis path: absence is not proof — every near-miss with valid data has had one shape","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:32Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2437"},

{"body":"## What happened\r\n\r\n`scripts/run-governed-review.mjs` ran for PR #2415 at head `0fab4ace80f9e3d5785aee75711a4a49ed49285a`.\r\n\r\n1. The reviewer produced a clean terminal verdict.\r\n2. `recordReviewVerdict` created the create-only verdict ref successfully — `refs/db-review-verdicts/2355-2415-0fab4ace...` exists on the remote and holds a well-formed APPROVE commit.\r\n3. The readback at `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:1921` disagreed, so the recorder threw `create-only verdict readback disagrees with the created object; this tuple is permanently refused`.\r\n4. The runner's failure path then **edited the findings comment** to void its verdict lines.\r\n\r\nStep 4 changed the bytes whose digest step 2 had already committed into the artifact. The recorded `findings_digest` is `ec6195f6...`; the digest of the live comment is now `d49915a5...`.\r\n\r\n## Why this is a deadlock, not a retry\r\n\r\n- `validateVerdictArtifact` recomputes the digest from the live comment, so the artifact can never validate again.\r\n- The ref is create-only, so a fresh review at the same tuple hits the existing ref and refuses.\r\n- The sanctioned escape, `--replace-failed-reviewer`, requires `--confirm-no-artifact`. An artifact **does** exist, so that assertion would be false and must not be made.\r\n\r\nThe only honest exit is a new head SHA, which discards a completed, paid-for review.\r\n\r\n## Two defects\r\n\r\n1. **Ordering.** The failure path must not mutate the findings body once a verdict artifact has been created. Void only when no artifact exists; if the artifact exists, leave the findings intact and reconcile against the artifact instead.\r\n2. **Readback.** The recorder already readbacks inside `createRefWithReadback`; the second readback at line 1921 appears to have raced GitHub's ref read. A disagreement should re-read and compare the *content* of the winning ref against the intended record before declaring a permanent refusal — a matching artifact is a success, not a corruption.\r\n\r\n## Scope\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\r\nroute: repo-maintenance\r\npriority: 90\r\ndepends_on:\r\n```\r\n\r\nNot orchestrator work — this is repository tooling, for an independent repository session.\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T02:11:53Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T13:21:03Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2430,"title":"Governed review runner can void the findings it already hashed, permanently deadlocking a head","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:39Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2430"},
{"body":"## Problem\n\nA machine-local configuration overlay returned the ref of a Supabase project that had been deleted in August. Every session that resolved the preview target through that key linked against a dead ref, got `Resource has been removed`, and correctly concluded the project was gone. The live rehearsal branch existed the whole time; CI was using it, because CI reads a different source.\n\nCost: two author lanes blocked, and all structural merges frozen for most of a day on #2424.\n\nThe failure is not that a value went stale — values go stale. It is that a stale value is **indistinguishable from a deleted resource** at the point of use, and it degrades into the more alarming of the two readings.\n\n## What makes it worse\n\nThree independent sessions reached the same wrong conclusion and their agreement raised confidence. It should not have: all three read the same key. A shared lookup does not become three witnesses by being read three times.\n\n## Ask\n\nMake ref values verifiable rather than merely correct at the moment they are written.\n\nAny config key naming a Supabase project or branch should be checkable against the account's actual project and branch list — `supabase projects list` and `supabase branches list --project-ref <parent>` are both cheap and need no database credential. A checker that runs on demand and in CI, and reports each ref key as LIVE, RETIRED (present in a retired-ref key), or UNKNOWN.\n\nThen a stale entry fails loudly and names itself, instead of arriving at a session as a deleted project.\n\n## Notes\n\n- Root cause fixed in `u2giants/ai-devops-private-config` PR #1, merged `f37e4119040dd9a6e91d60ef301566db4f3cd34e`. This issue is about preventing the next one, not that fix.\n- The 1Password item for the rehearsal credentials already lists the four places that must be updated when the branch is rebuilt. The overlay was not among them. A checker would have caught that omission; a longer list would only have moved it.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\ndepends_on:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-15T13:36:20Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T13:00:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2429,"title":"A stale project ref is indistinguishable from a deleted project — verify ref config against the real account","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:41Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2429"},
{"body":"Successor to #2355 (PR #2415), filed by the shared-db orchestrator (marker #2404) from that author's follow-up 1.\n\n## The gap\n\n#2355 added character aliases and a guard preventing an alias from being bound to a character under a different licensor. That guard lives on the alias table, so it catches the dangerous direction it can see: an importer-style upsert repointing a provenance row at another licensor's character is refused, proven by contract test.\n\nIt cannot catch the other direction. **Re-parenting `core.character.licensor_id` after aliases already exist** silently moves the character under a different licensor while its aliases stay attached. Nothing refuses it and nothing detects it afterwards.\n\nThat needs a constraint trigger on `core.character`, which was read-only under claim #2410 — correctly, since it belongs to another lane's object space. It was deliberately left undone rather than reached for.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nLicensor attribution is a royalty-affecting fact. An alias surviving a licensor re-parent means a character's names remain associated with a licensor that no longer owns it, and the failure is silent — there is no error, no log line, and no count that moves.\n\n## Known constraint for whoever authors this\n\nThe author of #2355 could not add a composite foreign key because that requires a new unique index on `core.character`. Whatever approach is taken here inherits that: adding the index is itself a change to `core.character` and must be claimed as such, not assumed.\n\nAlso inherited from #2355's follow-up 2: the freshness presence rules are `NOT VALID`, so existing rows are grandfathered. Any later validating backfill will fail while a ColdLion circuit breaker is tripped — and that failure presents as a data problem when it is a breaker state. Anyone writing a backfill should check the breaker first and say so in their report.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 80\ndepends_on: 2355\nwrites:\n  - table core.character\nreads:\n  - table core.character_alias\n  - table core.taxonomy_source_ref\n```\n\nBlocked until PR #2415 merges, since the guard it complements does not exist until then.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-11T23:47:11Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:11:06Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2426,"title":"core.character licensor re-parent is uncaught once aliases exist (successor to #2355)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:44Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2426"},
{"body":"## The shared preview project no longer exists\n\nFound by author lane #2412 while attempting the mandatory dry-run for #2408, and independently confirmed by the orchestrator (marker #2404) on 2026-09-06.\n\n- `ai-private-config value supabase_shared_preview_ref` resolves to the ref it has always resolved to.\n- `supabase link --project-ref <that ref>` fails: `Authorization failed ... {\"message\":\"Resource has been removed\"}`.\n- The PAT is healthy. `supabase projects list` succeeds and returns six projects across two organisations. **The preview ref is not among them.**\n\nSo this is not a credential fault, not a rate limit, and not a transient outage. The project is gone from the account.\n\n## Why this stops everything\n\nEvery migration in this repository is proved by applying it to preview and asserting behaviour there. `AGENTS.md` requires a dry-run before any preview push and an apply-and-prove step before merge. With no preview:\n\n- No author lane can produce behavioural evidence. Static checks (`check-sql.sh`) still pass, but they prove syntax, not effect.\n- Merging on static checks alone would land unexercised changes. For #2408 specifically that means shipping an attribution fix — wrong-licensor exposure — that nothing has ever executed.\n- A local Docker fixture is not a substitute. It would miss the production triggers these contracts depend on, which is a failure mode already recorded in this repo.\n\n**Merges are frozen for structural work until this is resolved.** PRs may continue to be authored and opened; none proceed to preview or merge.\n\n## What is needed\n\nOwner-level establishment of what happened to the project and how preview is restored: whether it was deleted, moved to another organisation, or replaced by something that has not been recorded in `ai-private-config`. This is not something an AI session can or should resolve — it involves account-level state and possibly a restore.\n\nNote for whoever picks this up: a project named `designflow-nonprod` (created 2026-09-02) does exist in the list. It is **not** a substitute for the shared-db preview and must not be adopted as one; it is the DesignFlow consolidated non-production project referenced by #2403, with its own ledger and its own purpose.\n\n## Affected right now\n\n- PR #2423 (#2408) — authored, committed, contracts test written and **not executed**.\n- Author lanes for #2334, #2355, #2403, #2416 — all will hit the same wall at dry-run.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: security-settings\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 200\ndepends_on:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-06T13:00:28Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:08:15Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2424,"title":"BLOCKER: shared preview Supabase project no longer exists — no lane can prove behaviour","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:45Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2424"},

{"body":"Prerequisite for the two issues that follow it. Read-only; authorizes no write to application data.\n\n## Why this exists\n\nToday's nightly cycle self-heals by brute force: `clear_style_group_batch` blanks `assets.style_group_id`, then `rebuild_style_groups_batch` reassigns from scratch over every live asset. That is expensive (~9,935 s and ~11,849 s lifetime respectively), and #2408 removes most of its cost. But it is also the system's **only** correction mechanism, and it silently repairs manual edits, missed trigger firings, group merges and splits, and changes to the SKU derivation rule.\n\nBoth independent reviewers of the parent plan (Muse Spark 1.3 on the prevention half, GLM 5.3 on the rebuild half) arrived at the same objection without seeing each other's work: the proposed efficiency changes delete that safety net and put nothing in its place, so the first drift after they ship is invisible until a person notices wrong data in the DAM.\n\nThis issue builds the detector. Nothing that removes the net should merge before it is live and reading clean.\n\n## What it must compare\n\nA scheduled read-only job reporting counts only — no writes, no repairs:\n\n1. **Recomputed group assignment vs actual, in both directions.** Re-derive the SKU from `relative_path` using the current rule, resolve the expected `style_groups` row, and count (a) assets that should be grouped and are not or are in the wrong group, and (b) assets that carry a `style_group_id` but should not. Direction (b) is the one the rebuild cannot currently detect at all — see #2408: the function only ever SETs.\n2. **Orphan group references.** Assets whose `style_group_id` matches no `style_groups` row. **Baseline 0**, confirmed by real `count(*)` against production 2026-09-06.\n3. **Effective-tag projection drift.** For a sample of assets, the desired tag set — active `asset_tags` for the asset, plus active `style_group_tags` for its group — against actual `asset_effective_tags`. Sampled rather than exhaustive; the table holds 2,045,705 rows.\n\nAny non-zero result on 1 or 2 should alert. For 3, alert on a rate rather than a single row, since a sample will occasionally catch an in-flight transaction.\n\n## Baseline to record on first run (production, 2026-09-06)\n\nlive assets 135,251 — grouped 97,658 — ungrouped 37,593 — `style_groups` 10,869 — `asset_effective_tags` 2,045,705 — orphan group references **0**.\n\n## Watch out for\n\n- The SKU derivation rule has already changed once (`20260708150000_dam_strict_style_group_sku_regex.sql`). The reconciler must derive using the same rule the rebuild uses, or it will report drift that is really a rule mismatch. Sharing one function between them is the cheap way to guarantee that.\n- Do not let this grow a repair mode. A detector that fixes what it finds stops being evidence that the system is correct, and hides the recurrence rate that tells us whether the underlying fix worked.\n\nBlocks: the `clear_style_group_batch` retirement and the incremental-watermark issues filed alongside this one.\nRelated: #2408, #2417, #2209 (umbrella).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 100\ndepends_on: 2408\nwrites:\n  - function public.reconcile_style_group_drift\nreads:\n  - table public.assets\n  - table public.style_groups\n  - table public.asset_effective_tags\n  - table public.asset_tags\n  - table public.style_group_tags\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T05:32:28Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:01:05Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2419,"title":"Read-only reconciler for style-group and effective-tag drift (prerequisite for retiring the nightly full pass)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:51Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2419"},

{"body":"> **CURRENT POSITION — two claims in the original text below are withdrawn. Kept for history.**\n>\n> **Withdrawn 1 — \"autovacuum has never touched these tables\" is not a fault.** Autovacuum is healthy and stock. The positive control settles it: on the same database with the same settings, `style_groups` has been autovacuumed 290 times, `assets` 49, `asset_effective_tags` 16. These two tables are insert-only in practice, inserts create no dead tuples, and so they never approach the `50 + 0.2 × n_live_tup` threshold — 1,014 dead against 435,821 required, and 10,724 against 231,405. **There is no autovacuum work to do and no `reloptions` override to add.**\n>\n> **Withdrawn 2 — my own correction that these are \"static tables whose statistics never go stale\" is also wrong.** `asset_tags` is bursty, not static: 671,014 rows created in the last 30 days, writes on only 26 distinct days since 2026-03-13, last write 2026-08-27 — one day before the statistics reset. The apparent silence was the gap between two batch loads. The hand-run ANALYZE of 2026-09-05 will therefore be obsolete after the next load, not valid indefinitely. A load that size does cross the autoanalyze threshold, so the practical risk is smaller than \"no statistics forever\" — but by a different mechanism than the one I gave.\n>\n> **The lesson worth keeping:** prove that a table is static from the rows' own `created_at` distribution, never from `pg_stat` write counters, which a reset zeroes. Both errors here came from trusting a measurement window rather than the number in it.\n>\n> **What remains live in this issue:** only the **cron ordering**, labelled `needs-albert` — job 6 (`45 3 * * *`, style-group counts) runs two hours fifteen minutes before job 7 (`0 6 * * *`, the rebuild that changes those counts), so the counts are stale by construction. The fix is to chain job 6 off the rebuild's completion; a new fixed clock time re-opens the same race the first time the rebuild's duration changes. That is a production scheduling change, not a migration, so it needs owner authority.\n>\n> The index finding that came out of this investigation is split out as **#2427**, under its own gate.\n\n---\n\nFound while investigating #2408. Two scheduling/maintenance findings, no code change, no schema change.\n\n## 1. Nightly jobs run in the wrong order\n\nVerified against `cron.job` on production, 2026-09-06:\n\n| job | schedule | what it does |\n|---|---|---|\n| 6 | `45 3 * * *` (03:45) | `refresh_style_group_counts_batch(array_agg(id))` over **all** style groups |\n| 7 | `0 6 * * *` (06:00) | `queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups()` — the full rebuild |\n\nJob 6 recomputes every style group's counts **two hours and fifteen minutes before** the run that changes group membership. The counts are therefore stale from 06:00 until 03:45 the following morning — nearly the whole working day. Job 6 was measured at ~98.6 s average over 6 calls, so this is also the single most expensive scheduled statement running at the least useful moment.\n\nFix is a schedule change only: move job 6 to follow the rebuild's completion. Ideally it is chained off the rebuild finishing rather than pinned to a clock time, since the rebuild is queue-driven and its duration varies.\n\n## 2. `refresh_style_guide_matviews()` runs every 15 minutes\n\nJob 9 is `*/15 * * * *` — 96 calls a day at ~8.6 s each (535 lifetime calls, ~4,629 s). That is roughly **14 minutes of database time per day**, permanently, on matviews nothing appears to require at 15-minute freshness.\n\nTwo questions for whoever owns the style-guide views: what actually needs refreshing this often, and can it be event-driven off the writes that invalidate it instead? If 15 minutes is genuinely required for one view, splitting the function so only that view refreshes on the short cycle would recover most of the cost. Note #2408 also proposes ensuring this runs once per completed rebuild rather than per batch, which is a separate saving.\n\n## 3. Two large tables have never been autovacuumed or autoanalyzed\n\n`public.asset_tags` (2,173,392 rows) and `public.style_guide_file_tags` (1,156,758 rows) had `last_vacuum`, `last_autovacuum`, `last_analyze` and `last_autoanalyze` **all NULL** — the planner had no statistics for either.\n\nI ran `ANALYZE` on both under owner authorization on 2026-09-06 (1.6 s each via the pooler as `postgres`, no lock contention), so statistics now exist:\n\n```\nasset_tags            | live=2178856 dead=1014  | last_analyze=2026-09-05 23:57:37-04\nstyle_guide_file_tags | live=1156774 dead=10724 | last_analyze=2026-09-05 23:57:39-04\n```\n\n**The remaining question is why autovacuum had never touched either table**, because that will recur. Neither table carries per-table `reloptions` as far as I checked. Worth ruling out a stats reset that lost the counters, a restore that repopulated them outside normal write paths, or an autovacuum worker starvation pattern. Until that is understood, both tables will drift back to having no statistics.\n\nAlso recorded so it is not re-investigated: `n_live_tup` reported these tables at **0** and **10,286** rows respectively. Those were absences, not measurements — a table that has never been analyzed reports zero. An earlier reading of those counters produced a \"1.8 GB of reclaimable empty space\" claim that is **false**; measured bloat is ~98 MB on `asset_tags` and none on `style_guide_file_tags`, and no `VACUUM FULL` is warranted on either.\n\nRelated: #2408, #2209 (umbrella).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 50\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-06T13:41:49Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:00:02Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2417,"title":"Nightly cron ordering, 15-minute matview refresh, and two tables autovacuum has never touched","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:19:54Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2417"},
{"body":"Found while investigating #2408. Not a request to change production — a request to make the repo reproduce it.\n\n## The drift\n\nProduction `public.sync_asset_effective_tags()` runs the **diff-aware** body introduced by #2213: it computes a `desired` set and applies the difference. Verified by `pg_get_functiondef('public.sync_asset_effective_tags()'::regprocedure)` against production on 2026-09-06 — the live body contains the `desired` CTE.\n\nThe newest migration in this repo that defines the function is `supabase/migrations/20260830110517_popdam_effective_asset_filters.sql`, at `origin/main` 1d2be5ab. That body is the **pre-#2213 delete-all-then-reinsert** version. `grep -c desired` on it returns 0.\n\nSo replaying this repo's migrations onto an empty database produces a function that behaves differently from production: it rewrites every projection row for an asset on each firing instead of only the changed ones.\n\n## Why it matters beyond tidiness\n\n1. **Preview branches do not rehearse production.** Any change tested against a preview built from these migrations is tested against the wrong trigger body, on the hottest write path in the DAM.\n2. **It already cost a review.** In the #2408 review, GLM read the repo and correctly reported the body it found — delete-all-then-reinsert — and reasoned from it. I had read production. Both of us were right about our own source and wrong about the other's. Reviewers are pointed at this repo, so the repo's body is what every future review will reason from.\n3. It makes the churn attribution for `asset_effective_tags` ambiguous, because the two bodies produce very different write volumes for the same workload.\n\n## What is wanted\n\nEstablish which is authoritative and close the gap in the direction that keeps production behaviour. Production is diff-aware and #2213 intended that, so the expected resolution is a migration that brings the repo up to the live body — not a change to production.\n\nWorth checking as part of this whether #2213 was applied directly rather than through the migration path, and whether anything else went the same way. `20260830110517` is *newer* than #2213, so this is not a missing migration; it is a later migration that reintroduced the older body over the top. That reintroduction is the thing to understand — if it ran against production it would have reverted #2213, and production shows it did not, so the file and the deployed state have been out of step since at least 2026-08-30.\n\nRelated: #2408 (the guard and ungroup arm), #2209 (umbrella).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","closedAt":"2026-09-06T04:07:38Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T03:59:39Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2416,"title":"sync_asset_effective_tags: repo body is the pre-#2213 version, production is diff-aware","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:46:09Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2416"},
{"body":"## What happened\n\nIssue #2408 — a well-specified structural change to `public.rebuild_style_groups_batch`, adversarially reviewed by two reviewers before it was filed — was opened at 2026-09-06T03:42:23Z with no `db-work` label and no `db-work-scope` block. `node scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --queue-audit` did not report it anywhere: not as dispatchable, not as skipped, not under `NOT ORCHESTRATOR WORK`. It was invisible, not classified-and-skipped.\n\nIt was found only because the owner asked about issue numbers that were not in the audit output, prompting a raw `gh issue list` of all 87 open issues. Two of 87 carried neither `db-work` nor `db-claim`: #2408 and the orchestrator marker itself.\n\nLeft alone, that issue would have sat unstarted while the audit reported an accurate-looking picture of the queue — and it contains an active attribution defect (assets keep a stale style group after a folder rename, so they appear under the wrong licensor indefinitely with no error surfaced).\n\n## Why the current design cannot catch this\n\n`--queue-audit` enumerates by label. An unlabelled issue is not a classification failure it can report, because it never enters the set being classified. The audit's own `EMPTY LANE NOT PROVEN` line asks the operator to \"classify and label every open issue\" — but nothing tells the operator WHICH issues are unlabelled, so the instruction cannot be acted on without a manual full listing.\n\nThis is the same shape as a lesson already recorded elsewhere in this repo: a checker that reports a confident absence must be fed a known-missing case before it is trusted.\n\n## Required result\n\n`--queue-audit` must enumerate ALL open issues, not only labelled ones, and print an explicit `UNCLASSIFIED` block naming every open issue that carries neither `db-work` nor `db-claim` nor `orchestrator-marker`. An unclassified issue must make the audit exit non-zero, exactly as `NO RETURN ADDRESS` does — silence about an unlabelled issue is the failure being fixed.\n\nProve the check can fail: the regression test fixture must include an open, unlabelled issue and assert it is reported.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\n```\n\nFound by orchestrator marker #2404.","closedAt":"2026-09-11T12:41:44Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T03:54:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2414,"title":"Queue audit is blind to any issue without the db-work label","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:46:12Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2414"},

No migration, no schema change, no SQL, no code, no workflow.\n- `gh pr merge --squash --admin` is refused: \"11 of 11 required status checks have not succeeded: 1 expected\". {"body":"Umbrella: #2209 (Database efficiency and Data API security program). That plan requires each structural change to be split into its own orchestrator issue; this is that issue for the nightly style-group rebuild.\n\n## Problem\n\n`public.rebuild_style_groups_batch(uuid, integer)` writes `assets.style_group_id` unconditionally:\n\n```sql\nassigned AS (\n  UPDATE public.assets a\n  SET style_group_id = ug.id\n  FROM grouped_assets ga JOIN upserted_groups ug ON ug.sku = ga.sku\n  WHERE a.id = ga.id\n  RETURNING 1\n)\n```\n\n`queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups()` enqueues `{\"force_restart\": true}` with cursor 0, so every night this walks all live assets and re-stamps the ~97,658 that are already in the correct group. `style_group_id` is indexed, so none of those rewrites can be HOT: each produces a new heap tuple plus an entry in every index on `assets`, an FK re-check, and a firing of most of the 14 triggers on `assets` — including `trg_dam_search_assets_refresh`, which maintains `dam_search_documents` (731 MB).\n\nSame shape as the guards already added in #2213 and #2214.\n\n## Second, separate defect: the rebuild is not convergent\n\nThe function only ever SETs `style_group_id`. `v_ungrouped` is `(SELECT count(*) FROM asset_skus WHERE sku IS NULL)` — a counter, with no corresponding action. Nothing in the rebuild ever unsets a stale assignment; the only unsetting paths in the system are `clear_style_group_batch`, the FK's `ON DELETE SET NULL`, and manual SQL.\n\nConsequence: an asset whose folder is renamed so no path segment matches the SKU regex keeps its old `style_group_id`. Because `filter_effective_assets` resolves the licensor / property / customer facets through `style_groups` for grouped assets, that asset keeps appearing under the wrong licensor in the DAM libraries indefinitely, with no error surfaced. This is an attribution defect, not only a performance one.\n\n`clear_style_group_batch` is on no cron schedule (verified against `cron.job`), so today nothing automatic corrects this.\n\n## Proposed change (one migration)\n\n1. Add `AND a.style_group_id IS DISTINCT FROM ug.id` to the `assigned` CTE.\n2. Add an ungroup arm in the same batch: `UPDATE public.assets SET style_group_id = NULL WHERE id IN (<batch rows with sku IS NULL>) AND style_group_id IS NOT NULL`. The existing `sync_asset_effective_tags` trigger then strips the group-scope projection rows.\n3. Add a `WHERE` guard to the `ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE` on `style_groups` so a row is rewritten only when a value actually changes (mirrors #2214).\n\nNote for whoever implements 1 and 3 together: GLM flagged that `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... WHERE` suppresses the `RETURNING` row for a suppressed conflict, and `assigned` joins `upserted_groups` on that `RETURNING`. Deriving `ug` from `style_groups` directly rather than from the upsert's `RETURNING` is required, or guarded groups silently stop being assigned. This interaction must be covered by a test.\n\n## Measured baseline (production, 2026-09-06)\n\n- live assets 135,251 — grouped 97,658 — ungrouped 37,593\n- `style_groups` 10,869\n- `asset_effective_tags` 2,045,705 rows\n- orphan `style_group_id` references: **0** (real `count(*)`, not `n_live_tup`)\n\nLifetime cost via `pg_stat_statements` (reported by the Supabase advisor; `pg_stat_statements` is not directly readable by our role):\n`rebuild_style_groups_batch` ~2,982 ms x 3,973 calls ≈ 11,849 s; `clear_style_group_batch` ~34,617 ms x 287 calls ≈ 9,935 s.\n\n## Explicitly out of scope for this issue\n\n- Retiring `clear_style_group_batch` from scheduled paths, and making the nightly run incremental off a watermark. Both reviewers independently found that these remove the system's only self-healing pass with no detector in place, and that `assets.modified_at` is app-maintained rather than trigger-maintained, so a group- or tag-definition change never bumps it. A read-only reconciler must ship and read clean first. Separate issue.\n- Deriving the SKU into a generated column. GLM proved the expression is illegal in `GENERATED ALWAYS AS ... STORED` (it contains a subquery), that `public.assets.sku` already exists and is read by `parse_pdf_files_used`, and that `ADD COLUMN ... STORED` forces a full ACCESS EXCLUSIVE rewrite of a 3.2 GB table. If pursued at all it becomes an `IMMUTABLE derive_sku(text)` helper plus a concurrent expression index. Separate issue, and only after the incremental work is measured.\n- Statement-level rewrite of `sync_asset_effective_tags`. Viable only under a union-of-transition-tables advisory lock protocol that preserves the #1664 guarantee. Separate issue.\n\n## Non-issues, recorded so they are not re-investigated\n\n- **There is no 1.8 GB of reclaimable empty space.** `pg_stat_user_tables` reports `asset_tags` at 0 live rows and `style_guide_file_tags` at 10,286; the real counts are **2,173,392** and **1,156,758**. Both tables have `last_vacuum`, `last_autovacuum`, `last_analyze` and `last_autoanalyze` all NULL — the counters were never populated, and the zeroes were absences, not measurements. Estimated real bloat is ~98 MB on `asset_tags` and none on `style_guide_file_tags`. No `VACUUM FULL` is warranted.\n- **Worth doing separately:** neither of those two tables has ever been ANALYZEd, so the planner has no statistics for a 2.17M-row and a 1.16M-row table. `ANALYZE` on both is cheap and takes no exclusive lock. Also worth establishing why autovacuum has never touched either.\n\n## Repo-vs-production drift found while investigating\n\nThe in-repo body of `sync_asset_effective_tags()` is the pre-#2213 delete-all-then-reinsert version. Production runs the diff-aware #2213 body (read from `pg_get_functiondef`). The migrations do not reproduce production. Filing separately.\n\n## Reviews\n\nAdversarially reviewed by Muse Spark 1.3 (prevention half) and GLM 5.3 (rebuild-function half). GLM returned REJECT on the original plan; items 2 and 3 above and the out-of-scope split are the response to it. Reports under `.ai/reviews/`.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 120\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function public.rebuild_style_groups_batch\n  - table public.assets\n  - table public.style_groups\nreads:\n  - table public.asset_effective_tags\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-06T22:25:36Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T03:42:23Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2408,"title":"rebuild_style_groups_batch: guard the assignment write, and add the missing ungroup arm","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:20:01Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2408"},
{"body":"## Why this exists\n\nIssues #2151 and #2138 cannot close without one measurement that has never been taken, and it is not a database-shape change — so it must not sit in the structural queue.\n\nThe index-leading arm for the tag facet count shipped (`20260904121037`, on main and applied to production) and the `filter_effective_assets` row regression is fixed (`20260903075635`). But the only direct measurement on record, 2026-09-05, reads:\n\n- worst-case tag `blue`, 39,621 assets\n- cold 18.4 s, warm 0.36 s\n- viewer ceiling ~8 s\n\nand it was taken **against the database directly, not through the API**. #2138's remaining criteria are also unmet: `get_filter_counts` with a tag filter 0/12 (~8.1 s), `count=exact` over `filter_effective_assets` 0/3 (~8.1 s even unfiltered).\n\n## Required result\n\nRead-only, no writes of any kind. Using the real PopDAM viewer token through authenticated PostgREST — not psql:\n\n1. the worst-case tag facet count (`blue`, 39,621 assets), cold and warm;\n2. `get_filter_counts` with a tag filter, repeated enough times to state a pass rate;\n3. a list total for the same filter — `count=exact` over `filter_effective_assets`, or `get_filter_counts.total`.\n\nReport each against the ~8 s viewer ceiling with the raw timings, and say plainly whether a real user waits longer than the ceiling today.\n\nRecord the probe: an unlogged measurement cannot be defended.\n\n## What happens next\n\n- If every number is inside the ceiling: comment the evidence on #2151 and #2138 and both can close.\n- If any number is outside it: the remedy is a further database change, which is a NEW structural issue opened in `u2giants/shared-db` routed to the orchestrator. Do not author a migration from this issue.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: application-data\nroute: application-session\npriority: 60\nreturn_to: u2giants/popdam3\n```\n\nSplit out by orchestrator marker #2404 so the finished migration work is not re-dispatched as new authoring.","closedAt":"2026-09-06T03:34:59Z","createdAt":"2026-09-06T03:34:54Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2407,"title":"Measure PopDAM tag-facet and list-total through the authenticated API path","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:20:02Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2407"},
{"body":"## What happened\n\n`node scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --queue-audit` reported issue #2138 under `DEPENDENCIES NOT PROVEN` with the detail \"a closed claim has a merged migration version on current main\".\n\nThat is false. #2138's claim was #2225, which reserved version `20260903192801`. That version exists nowhere:\n\n```\ngit fetch origin\ngit ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- supabase/migrations | grep 20260903192801   # no output\n```\n\nIt is also absent from the production migration ledger. #2138's own 2026-09-03T19:31:20Z comment states it plainly: \"No migration was authored for this half; reserved version 20260903192801 was not spent and claim #2225 is released.\"\n\nThe fix for the object in that claim, `public.filter_effective_assets`, landed under an unrelated version from a different lane — `20260903075635_popdam_effective_filter_identity_append.sql`.\n\nThe same audit run reported #2151 correctly: claim #2227 reserved `20260904121037`, and that exact file IS on main and in the ledger.\n\n## Probable cause\n\nThe `authored-on-main` heuristic appears to match a closed claim to a merged migration by **object name** rather than by the claim's **own reserved version**. Any object touched by a later, unrelated migration would then make an unspent claim read as authored.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nPer the recorded lesson \"the reserved version settles it\": a claim reserves exactly one migration version, and whether that version is spent on a merged file is the fact that decides delivery. An object-name match is a different question and can never answer it. If this signal is ever used to auto-close or auto-dispatch, it will close undelivered work — #2138's tag-facet and list-total criteria are both still failing.\n\n## Required result\n\n`authored-on-main` must key on the claim's reserved 14-digit version and nothing else. {"body":"## Request\n\nCreate a new, empty schema `hts_rag_split` in the **DesignFlow consolidated non-production Supabase project** (the one reached by `DB_*_SANDBOX` in GCP `lithe-breaker-323913`; it is neither shared prod nor the `shared-db-schema-rehearsal` preview branch, but it *does* carry the governed migration ledger — latest applied version `20260904183100`).\n\nIn that schema, create nine tables structurally identical to the existing `public.hts_rag_*` tables:\n\n- `hts_rag_determinations`\n- `hts_rag_extraction_jobs`\n- `hts_rag_precedents`\n- `hts_rag_precedent_rulings`\n- `hts_rag_product_examples`\n- `hts_rag_product_family_allowlist`\n- `hts_rag_provider_responses`\n- `hts_rag_review_events`\n- `hts_rag_rulings`\n\nSame columns, types, nullability, defaults, primary keys, unique/check constraints and indexes. **No rows are to be copied** — the new schema must be empty (see \"why\" below). No foreign keys point out of this set; none of these nine tables are referenced by anything outside the HTS RAG services.\n\n## Why\n\nDesignFlow's full move to this backend keeps stalling on large dependent schema work. The HTS RAG (AI classification) tables are the one genuinely self-contained slice — nine tables, no outbound foreign keys, referenced only by HTS-RAG-named service files — so they are being used as a small, reversible pilot of a segmented move.\n\n`designflow-backend` now has an optional second database connection behind `HTS_RAG_DB_ENABLED` (default **off**, pinned off in `cloudbuild.yaml`), which re-points only those nine models. An independent review (GLM 5.3) approved enabling it in sandbox on one condition: **the secondary connection must not resolve to the same physical tables the primary reads**, and the new tables must not contain the rows the acceptance gate writes — otherwise a wrong-database read is masked and the test proves nothing. An isolated schema in the same project satisfies that without standing up another project.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- `hts_rag_split` exists with the nine tables, empty.\n- Structure matches `public.hts_rag_*` (a structure dump taken read-only from the live sandbox database on 2026-09-05 is below).\n- The application connects as the `postgres` role, so no additional grants are expected; add them if the project's convention requires an app role.\n- `public.hts_rag_*` is untouched.\n\n## Requesting session\n\nDesignFlow PLM work in `C:\\repos\\dflow_plm`, branch `sandbox-albert`, backend PR popcre/designflow-backend#87. Not the shared-db orchestrator; `check-orchestrator-marker.mjs --resolve` returned exit 3 (no active orchestrator), so this is queued rather than dispatched.\n\n<details>\n<summary>Structure dump from the live sandbox database (read-only, 2026-09-05)</summary>\n\n```\n== columns That refusal was correct for the entire session. {"body":"`docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260904T212459Z/run1/` and `run2/` each contain `foreign-keys.csv`, `indexes.csv`, `pg-stat-statements-top300.csv`, `relation-stats.csv` — 8 files flagged by the venue guard, present on `main` in this PUBLIC repository.\n\nAn independent read-only assessment on 2026-09-05 found **no private business data** in them: no licensor names as data, no contracts, customers, vendors, pricing, royalties, style-guide assets, row contents, or credentials. They are PostgreSQL structural statistics — relation sizes, index definitions, tuple counters, and `pg_stat_statements` text already normalized to `$1`/`$2` placeholders. Brand words appear only inside database object names such as `idx_marvel_dcp_asset_character_obs_run`, which already exist in this repo's public migration files.\n\nSo the guard's **rule** applies (any `.csv` outside a two-item allowlist) while its **rationale** does not. Decide one of: allowlist `docs/verification/database-efficiency/**`, or move future captures out of the repo. Any future timestamped capture reproduces this exactly.\n\nSeparate decision in the same commit: `run1/advisors-security.json`, `run2/advisors-security.json` and `environment-and-security.json` publish 340 security-advisor findings naming specific objects in the production project — security-definer views, functions executable by `anon`, RLS-enabled-no-policy, mutable function search paths, leaked-password protection disabled. On a public repo that is a targeting aid rather than a data leak, but it is worth an explicit decision.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 3\n```\n\nNot orchestrator work (AGENTS.md 0.0-C, REPO-SESSION exit).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-15T12:27:13Z","createdAt":"2026-09-05T10:41:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"The venue guard `scripts/public-data-venue.test.mjs` (test: \"licensed and internal data artifacts stay in the private source-data repository\") is invoked by **no workflow at all**. Grep across `.github/workflows/` finds every other guard test wired to a job and this one wired to nothing. It only fails for whoever happens to run the scripts tests locally.\n\nConsequence: PR #2340 (`docs: production baseline for #2209 Step 1`, merged 2026-09-05 02:01, commit `d3c8ccf`) merged 8 paths the guard flags, with all 14 checks green. The guard has existed since PR #1871 on 2026-08-30.\n\nThe guard itself works — its own second test feeds it a known-dirty set and it correctly flags all three entries. This is a wiring gap, not a broken check.\n\nAlso fix the extension asymmetry while wiring it: the `.json` twins of the flagged `.csv` files carry identical content and are 10x larger, but the JSON rule only applies under a hardcoded list of licensor-ish directory prefixes that does not include `database-efficiency`. {"body":"The preview Supabase database password stored in 1Password (`vibe_coding`) no longer authenticates. {"body":"Prose-only cleanup. Two documents still describe migration version `20260903200951` as \"genuinely pending\". It is not — it is now permanently retired and hard-blocked.\n\nFiles to correct:\n- `docs/verification/licensing-master-data-phase0-2026-09-04/README.md`\n- `plan_licensing_master_data_implementation.md`\n\nWhat actually happened: `20260903200951` was merged, correct and rehearsed, but permanently unpromotable — its only rehearsal ran pre-merge under superseded version `20260903115927`, whose preview ledger row was later renamed to `20260903200951`, so preview already holds it and no fresh ledger delta can ever be produced for it. Per `docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md`, \"The way forward there is a new migration, never a recovery.\"\n\nIt was therefore reissued byte-for-byte as **`20260905024139`** (`supabase/migrations/20260905024139_reissue_coldlion_division_reference_table.sql`, git blob `adc49fb5a103a70e03d9a98afc5be4b6518ac92a` — the same blob as the original, proven by object id). PR #2360 merged `cafeedb32a4a09fb617d54ac0594c61410a33942`. `20260903200951` is now in `HARD_BLOCKED` and `RETIRED_VERSION_REASONS` in `scripts/production_migration_guard.py`, naming the replacement.\n\nReword both documents so the pending version is `20260905024139` and `20260903200951` is described as retired/hard-blocked, replaced byte-for-byte. Do not rewrite the dated history of what was believed at the time — correct only the forward-looking \"still pending\" claims.\n\nDocs-only, so this does not wait for CI.\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 3\n```\n\nClassified by the orchestrator on 2026-09-05 under AGENTS.md 0.0-C. {"body":"Two documentation nits raised by reviewers on PR #2346 and deliberately deferred — fixing them at the time would have voided two head-pinned APPROVE verdicts mid-merge. Neither affects behaviour.\n\n1. `plan_author_lane_capacity_five_to_eight.md` §7 says Qwen \"is gated only by its own preflight qualification\". That is now inaccurate in a way that matters: the *retirement* label was lifted per the owner instruction of 2026-09-04, but Qwen remains **quarantined** in `ai-review-preflight` with `failure_class: live-qualification-required`. Live re-qualification was attempted on 2026-09-04 and failed (`terminal-result-error`; two hand runs died after 900s and 240s with no answer returned). Reword so the quarantine is not implied to be gone.\n\n2. `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` carries a comment still saying \"the same pattern used to pause Qwen\". The mechanism is now `QUARANTINED_REVIEWERS`, and \"pause\" is the retired vocabulary. Reword to match.\n\nDeliberately NOT to be changed: `plan_orchestrator_throughput_phase_2.md` line 27 is a dated audit record of what was believed at the time. Historical records stay; only forward-looking prohibitions were removed.\n\nContext: PR #2346 merged as `eced94af18a6f4741c0653b1a77d8d2caf90664c`, closing #2347. Related: `popcre/ai-devops#284` (Qwen provider failure), `popcre/ai-devops#289` (ai-devops prose half, merged).\n\nProse-only follow-up. Docs-only PRs on this repo do not wait for CI.\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 3\n```\n\nClassified by the orchestrator on 2026-09-05 under AGENTS.md 0.0-C. {"body":"#1090 structural successor: licensing candidate and review APIs\r\n\r\nAfter #2335 establishes source authority and relationship decisions, DB Data Admin needs browser-safe read contracts for entity candidates, relationship candidates, and the audited resolution queue. This issue creates only those API views.\r\n\r\nRequired result: expose ambiguity and evidence without licensed row leakage; preserve RLS; prove browser-role reads and unauthorized denial; preview, exact-head review, guarded merge, production apply and live API proof. No review decisions or curated rows are authorized.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 124\r\ndepends_on: 2335, 2543\r\nwrites:\n  - view api.licensing_entity_candidates\n  - view api.licensing_relationship_candidates\n  - view api.licensing_resolution_queue\n  - table api.licensing_entity_candidates\n  - table api.licensing_relationship_candidates\n  - table plm.source_resolution\n  - table plm.licensing_relationship_resolution\n  - table plm.opa_capture\n  - function plm.licensing_opa_observation_count\n  - index plm.source_resolution_open_status_idx\n  - index plm.licensing_relationship_resolution_open_status_idx\n  - index plm.opa_capture_status_captured_idx\n  - column api.licensing_entity_candidates.opa_evidence_readable\n  - column api.licensing_entity_candidates.opa_observation_count\nreads:\n  - table plm.licensing_source_scope\n  - table plm.opa_property_character_capture\nservice_class: standard-application\r\nchange_type: view\r\napplication_return_to: popcre/shared-db\r\ngenerated_types: required\r\nlive_assertion: Authenticated callers can SELECT all three licensing candidate/review views while anonymous callers are denied; unreadable or inapplicable OPA evidence is false/NULL; readable OPA counts use only the latest complete capture; relationship queue buckets preserve licensor identity and entity candidates do not imply unqualified licensor authority.\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nMetadata recovery note: Complete admission fields from the licensing worker contract. Preserve the existing protected claim and exact writes; this does not allocate another author or assert production completion.\r\n\r\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf01-b3d7-7d62-b7ed-5c7bad7af40a on 916-ALIEN\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-25T22:08:33Z","createdAt":"2026-09-05T01:30:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## What happened\n\nWhile parked on #2349 I tried to reach the orchestrator using **only** the address published by marker #2330, as the routing procedure requires. It failed.\n\n`node scripts/check-orchestrator-marker.mjs --resolve --json` returns **exit 0** and:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"state\": \"declared\",\n  \"routing\": {\n    \"identifier\": \"shared-db.orch\",\n    \"engine\": \"claude\",\n    \"routeId\": \"local_9f9c54c6-894c-4590-8344-2b4adf46b14f\",\n    \"sessionName\": \"shared-db.orch local priority-blockers\",\n    \"owner\": \"u2giants\",\n    \"machine\": \"local\",\n    \"started\": \"2026-09-04T21:15:00Z\",\n    \"handoverIssue\": 2320,\n    \"briefing\": \"none\",\n    \"howToReach\": \"Claude cross-session message to sessionId local_9f9c54c6-894c-4590-8344-2b4adf46b14f\"\n  },\n  \"message\": null,\n  \"marker\": 2330\n}\n```\n\nSending a cross-session message to exactly that `sessionId` fails, verbatim:\n\n```\nSession local_9f9c54c6-894c-4590-8344-2b4adf46b14f not found.\n```\n\n**Reproduced twice**, minutes apart — once on the real escalation and once as a clean probe with the body `Routing reproduction probe for marker #2330 — no action required if this arrives.` Both returned the identical error. It is not a transient transport failure.\n\n## What did work\n\nThe message reached the orchestrator only after I addressed a **different** session id, found in the session list:\n\n- `local_ad69b1f5-d3c8-42e1-a63d-08490b2f05f3`, title `shared-db.orch`, worktree `C:\\repos\\shared-db\\.claude\\worktrees\\shared-db-orchestrator-8ca8f3`\n\nThat send returned `Message sent to session local_ad69b1f5-... (\"shared-db.orch\")` and the orchestrator replied.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nThe orchestrator, replying, reasoned that because my message reached it the marker address must resolve. **It does not follow** — the message reached it at `local_ad69b1f5-…`, never at the marker's `local_9f9c54c6-…`. Delivery to one address is not evidence about another.\n\nThe failure mode is the dangerous one: **`--resolve` exits 0 and prints a confident, well-formed address that no session answers.** A worker following the documented procedure and nothing else routes into silence, and silence is indistinguishable from an orchestrator that is simply busy. Escalations queue behind an address that cannot receive them.\n\n## Not fixed here, deliberately\n\nThe orchestrator explicitly instructed that a worker must **not** edit marker #2330's routing block — a worker rewriting the orchestrator's routing is exactly the failure this guard exists to catch. I have changed nothing. This issue records the reproduction only.\n\n## What needs deciding\n\n1. Whether `local_9f9c54c6-…` is a stale/never-live id or a second orchestrator session that is genuinely unaddressable, and correct the marker accordingly (**orchestrator-owned**).\n2. Whether `check-orchestrator-marker.mjs --resolve` should exit 0 at all for an address whose reachability it has not established, or whether a liveness probe belongs in the resolver — today exit 0 asserts only that a marker *declares* an address, while its consumers read it as a route.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 60\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\nSurfaced from #2349 / marker #2330.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-15T21:21:10Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T22:57:37Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2350,"title":"Orchestrator marker #2330 resolves exit 0 to a session id that does not exist","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:21:11Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2350"},
{"body":"## Goal\n\nReissue the executable SQL of `20260903200951_coldlion_division_reference_table.sql` (issue #2171, source PR #2199) under a **fresh migration version**, and permanently hard-block `20260903200951`.\n\n`20260903200951` is the **only genuinely-pending production version** in the whole repository, and it is **unpromotable forever**. It is the sole cause of the red `Migration ledger drift` alarm #2191 (run 33926688025: 20 merged-but-unapplied, 19 retired/held, exactly one genuinely pending).\n\n## Why it can never be promoted\n\nVerbatim refusal from the production business-risk gate, run 33926573085:\n\n```\nProduction business-risk gate rejected evidence: original apply run 33754529571 dispatched at\n63d8441b37bf41fa7dd798ba313a58d666e2ea53 produced evidence with a different\nscripts/production_migration_guard.py than the merge commit\n477ef03cd516c79188d81b6c21260575a43a9239 of the pull request that authored 20260903200951\n```\n\nEstablished facts:\n\n- Its **only** preview apply (run `33754529571`) was a **pre-merge branch rehearsal** on `claude/2171-coldlion-division`, and it applied the SQL under the **superseded** version `20260903115927`.\n- `preview-ledger-orphan-reconciliation.yml` run `33821298999` renamed that preview ledger row to `20260903200951` (recorded in `config/preview-ledger-orphan-reconciliations.json`). **Preview therefore already holds the version**, an applied version never re-applies there, and **no fresh preview ledger delta for `20260903200951` can ever be produced.**\n- This is **not** the squash-orphan variant. `63d8441b` **is** contained in `main`'s history (`behind_by 0`). It is **producer-file drift** between the branch commit the rehearsal ran at and the merge commit that landed the version — `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` moved in between.\n- `prove_governed_historical_supersession` in `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` is hard-pinned to a single historical case (`20260827095753`) and does not cover this one.\n- The historical recovery lane cannot rescue it either: `docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md` requires the original run's commits to carry **the same producer files as the authoring PR's merge commit**, which is exactly what failed here, and states plainly: *\"The way forward there is a new migration, never a recovery.\"*\n\n## Route\n\n`docs/production-promotion-procedure.md` §5.1-A, the stranded-version exception:\n\n1. Reissue the **same executable SQL** under a fresh, centrally reserved migration version.\n2. Hard-block `20260903200951` in `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` (`HARD_BLOCKED` + `RETIRED_VERSION_REASONS`) and mirror it into `scripts/post_batch_app_verification.py`, with tests in `scripts/test_production_migration_guard.py`, `scripts/test_post_batch_app_verification.py` and `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.test.mjs`.\n3. Prove **executable-SQL equivalence** between the original and the reissue (byte-identical below the header comment).\n4. Take the fresh version through the normal governed path: branch + PR + merge, **post-merge preview rehearsal from merged `main`**, fresh review evidence at current `main`, production apply.\n\nPrecedent for the exact change shape: `2d5afa10` (#1517, `20260814170749` → `20260825201330`) and `c054efad` (#1532, `20260824181600` → `20260825192610`).\n\n## Notes for the author\n\n- The SQL is **idempotent** (`create table if not exists coldlion.division`, plus comments / `alter … enable row level security` / `revoke` / `grant` / verification `do` blocks), so re-applying it to a preview that already holds the table is clean.\n- `20260903200951` appears in **no** §6.8 bundle and **no** co-presence rule. The only non-migration references are `config/preview-ledger-orphan-reconciliations.json`, `scripts/test_preview_ledger_orphan_reconcile.py`, `supabase/tests/coldlion_master_landing_contracts.sql` and closed HANDOFF files.\n- Do **not** weaken, edit or bypass any gate to make this promote.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- New migration file carries executable SQL byte-identical to `20260903200951` below its header comment, with the equivalence proof recorded.\n- `20260903200951` is in `HARD_BLOCKED` and `RETIRED_VERSION_REASONS` in both guard scripts, with tests proving it cannot enter an allowlist and is classified `retired` by the drift checker.\n- Post-merge preview rehearsal from merged `main` succeeds for the new version.\n- Production apply succeeds; `Migration ledger drift` against production reaches **zero** genuinely-pending versions and #2191 is closed.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 100\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table coldlion.division\nreads:\n```\n\nBlocks #2191. Supersedes the promotion half of #2171 (source PR #2199).\n","closedAt":"2026-09-05T04:13:39Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T22:53:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2349,"title":"Reissue stranded 20260903200951 coldlion.division under a fresh version and hard-block the original","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:21:13Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2349"},
