{"body":"## Outcome\n\nGive the reviewer pool a governed way to reclaim a lease whose worker died silently, without inventing failure evidence and without weakening the release rules.\n\n## Evidence — observed 2026-09-04\n\nDraft PR #2237 held **two of four** active reviewer slots for ~6 hours: codex-gpt-5.6-sol (sequence 1304) and grok-4.6 (sequence 1305). Both drawn 16:19 UTC against head `94b910c3`. In the six hours after: no verdict artifact, no comment, no push, no workflow run. The worker was dead, not slow.\n\nThis stalled PR #2266 twice while it waited for a slot.\n\n## The gap\n\nReleasing a reviewer lease requires one of six terminal provider/tool failure codes **plus the exact failed sequence**. \"The worker went silent\" is not one of them, and that evidence can only be produced by whoever ran the wrapper and watched it fail — precisely the process that has died.\n\nSo a silently dead reviewer is unreclaimable by anyone except the dead process. The pool degrades monotonically until something unrelated happens to move the PR head.\n\n## How it was actually recovered (and why that is luck, not a procedure)\n\nThe branch was refreshed against current main. The merge happened to be **clean**, so pushing moved the PR head, which is the sanctioned route by which a lease becomes `stale-reclaimable`. Pool went 1-of-4 available to 3-of-4.\n\n**Had the merge conflicted, the slots could not have been freed at all.** The recovery depended on an unrelated property of the diff. That is not a release path.\n\n## Related known traps (do not re-derive these)\n\n- Reviewer release is welded to a replacement draw, so the pool deadlocks exactly when it is full.\n- A release-only path sharing the replacement path's create-only key frees everyone except its own PR.\n- `--replacement-sequence` takes the FAILED sequence, not the new one.\n- A replacement can be blocked by the failed reviewer's unrelated lease.\n- Reviewer allocation has no queue: a waiting lane can be passed over indefinitely and nothing records it.\n\nRead `plan_reviewer_lease_capacity_truth.md` STATUS before designing anything here.\n\n## Required work\n\nA liveness signal for a held lease — a heartbeat, or an explicit deadline after which a lease with no artifact, comment, push or workflow run becomes reclaimable on **recorded observation** rather than on invented failure evidence. A cap measures time, not progress, so it must distinguish \"slow but advancing\" from \"never started\"; both currently hit a timeout identically.\n\nDo NOT relax the six terminal failure codes, and do NOT make release unconditional. Prove any new reclaim rule against a lane that is genuinely still working before trusting it — a green run against a dead lane proves nothing.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 200\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-05T02:19:39Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T22:15:20Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2345,"title":"A silently dead reviewer has no legitimate release path","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:21:14Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2345"},
{"body":"## Outcome\n\nMake the claim workstream parser accept the claim-title forms that agents actually write, or make it refuse with a message that names the required form.\n\n## Evidence\n\n`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` `workstreamKey` uses:\n\n```\nconst match = /^CLAIM:\\s+(#[0-9]+(?:\\/#?[0-9]+)*)\\b/.exec(String(title ?? ''))\n```\n\nSo `CLAIM: #2212 ...` parses and `CLAIM: issue #2212 ...` does not. The second form is natural and has been written repeatedly.\n\nObserved twice:\n- Claim #2184, titled `CLAIM: Issue #2175 ...`, fails to parse.\n- On 2026-09-04, `--expand-active-claim-from-pr` on claim #2321 required retitling from `CLAIM: issue #2212 ...` to `CLAIM: #2212 ...` before it would proceed.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThe failure is silent in the sense that the refusal does not say the TITLE is the problem or what shape is required, so it reads as a claim/lease fault. Time is lost diagnosing the wrong thing, and a hand-retitle is a manual mutation of coordination state that nothing audits.\n\n## Required work\n\nAccept an optional `issue` / `Issue` token before the number, OR emit a refusal that quotes the offending title and states the exact accepted form. Prefer accepting it -- a parser that rejects the obvious phrasing will keep costing sessions.\n\nProve the fix against a known-bad title before trusting it; a green run on a well-formed title proves nothing.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 120\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-08T00:48:35Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T22:03:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2344,"title":"Claim title parser accepts only 'CLAIM: #N', silently refusing 'CLAIM: issue #N'","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:21:16Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2344"},
{"body":"## Outcome\n\nMake batched, transient-tolerant GitHub reads permanent across every governed gate, so a single spurious API failure can never again stall production promotion, guarded merge, collision checks, or preview reconciliation.\n\nFollow-on from the production-gate repair (three production-apply runs `33920952504`, `33921168245`, `33921406952` each failed naming a *different* existing file — the signature of a transient read, not a real fault).\n\n## Evidence: this is systemic, not a one-off\n\nSurvey of `origin/main` @ `f462a411`:\n\n- **Eight independently hand-rolled `gh` wrappers exist. Exactly two have retries.**\n- `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py:97` scopes retries by a string match on the endpoint path:\n  ```\n  retry_transport = \"/issues/comments/\" in endpoint\n  effective_attempts = attempts if retry_transport else 1\n  ```\n  so every governed evidence read is single-attempt and fail-closed.\n- `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py:825` — `PREVIEW_PRODUCER_PATHS` is **56 entries**, two `blob_sha()` calls each, up to **112** sequential Contents calls per gate run, any one of which fails the promotion.\n- Same per-file-in-a-loop pattern: `check-dispatch-collision.mjs:569` (open PRs x migration files), `check-migration-pr-lease.mjs:82`, `check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:1113` and `:1160`.\n- No retry at all in: `check-dispatch-collision.mjs:479`, `check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:988`, `check-orchestrator-marker.mjs:354`, `check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:171`, `check-exact-head-approval.mjs:259`, `check-migration-pr-lease.mjs:69`, `check-pr-source-collisions.mjs:20`, `update-required-checks.mjs:70`.\n- Other pipelines that stall on one transient error: `guarded-migration-merge.yml:64,67,77,100,103` (two of them **under the merge lock**); `pr-object-collision.yml`; `preview-ledger-orphan-reconciliation.yml:155-162` (seven bare `gh api` calls under `set -euo pipefail`).\n\n## No existing check would have caught it — and one test pins the defect\n\n`scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py:113`\n```\ndef test_non_comment_evidence_read_never_retries(self):\n    ...\n    self.assertEqual(len(calls),1)\n```\n**This test must be rewritten, never deleted**, or it blocks the fix. There is no lint rule, no shared-transport conformance test, and no per-ref call budget for the Python gate.\n\nNo documented rule about batching GitHub reads or transient handling exists in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/`, or any `plan_*.md`. The nearest prior lesson argues the opposite (`AGENTS.md:997`, a retry wrapper that turned a failure into a slower named failure) — which is why the primary fix here is **batching**, not retrying.\n\n## Required work\n\n1. One shared GitHub transport module: retry on transient *transport* failures only, never on semantic failures. Reuse the existing classifier shape at `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:852`, which deliberately excludes 404 — note the production gate's failures WERE spurious 404s, so the classifier needs evidence-based revision, not a blind widening.\n2. Resolve blob SHAs from the single recursive tree read `tracked_paths_at()` already performs, instead of per-file Contents calls. Apply the same batching to the four `.mjs` collision/lease checks.\n3. A conformance test that FAILS if any file under `scripts/` or `.github/workflows/` invokes `gh api` outside the shared transport.\n4. As the immediate half-measure: a test asserting no gate makes more than one Contents call per ref.\n5. Rewrite `test_non_comment_evidence_read_never_retries` to assert the new intended behaviour.\n\n## Non-negotiable\n\nNothing any gate verifies may be relaxed. A gate that fails open is worse than one that fails closed. Every new guard must be proven against a known-dirty case before it is trusted — a green run on clean input proves nothing.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 240\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-06T21:54:03Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T21:39:12Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2342,"title":"Governed gates: one shared GitHub transport, batched evidence reads, and a conformance check","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:21:17Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2342"},
{"body":"#1090 structural successor: licensing source authority and relationship decisions\r\n\r\nThe durable `plm.source_resolution` entity-decision home is live. This successor adds only its missing Licensor/Franchise vocabulary, source scope, and direct relationship-decision contracts. Browser candidate and review APIs are a separate successor.\r\n\r\nRequired result:\r\n\r\n- extend the live entity-resolution vocabulary for Licensor and Franchise without weakening its audited setter;\r\n- add source-purpose-aware authorized scope with explicit permitted entity and relationship kinds;\r\n- add audited direct relationship decisions that preserve ambiguity and provenance;\r\n- preview, independent exact-head review, guarded merge, bounded production apply, and live catalog proof.\r\n\r\nNo resolution decisions, scope rows, or curated licensing rows are authorized.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 122\r\ndepends_on: 2333, 2334\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table plm.source_resolution\r\n  - function plm.set_source_resolution\r\n  - function api.set_source_resolution\r\n  - table plm.licensing_source_scope\r\n  - table plm.licensing_relationship_resolution\r\n  - index plm.licensing_relationship_resolution_asset_idx\r\n  - index plm.licensing_relationship_resolution_property_idx\r\n  - index plm.licensing_relationship_resolution_status_idx\r\n  - policy licensing_relationship_resolution_authenticated_read on plm.licensing_relationship_resolution\r\n  - policy licensing_source_scope_authenticated_read on plm.licensing_source_scope\r\nreads:\r\n  - table core.licensor\r\n  - table core.property\r\n  - table core.character\r\n  - table core.style_guide\r\n  - table core.franchise\r\n  - table dam.asset\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T06:16:25Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T21:24:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Finding\n\n`scripts/check-pr-source-collisions.mjs` hardcodes `PROTECTED_SOURCE_PATHS = new Set(['scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs'])` and intersects it with each PR's changed-file list. Any second open non-draft PR touching that file fails \"Cross-PR object collision\" with:\n\n```\nERROR: another ready open pull request edits the same protected coordination source.\n```\n\nThat is the guard working correctly. The consequence is that the file is a strictly single-writer resource, and **five** open PRs currently contend for it:\n\n- #2281 expired-claim atomic recovery (blocked by #2266)\n- #2266 reviewer replacement vs unrelated lease (green, behind main)\n- #2303 preview gate self-referential status (blocked)\n- #2245 unreadable reviewer verdict state (draft)\n- #2237 governed reinstatement for false terminal-unavailable (draft)\n\n## Why this matters now\n\nFour migration claims are deadlocked in a state neither `--renew-claim` nor `--expand-active-claim-from-pr` can clear: the PR writes objects the claim does not cover (so renewal refuses), and the lease is expired (so expansion refuses). Claims #2184/#2175/PR #2185, #2182/#2177/PR #2183, #2226/#2159/PR #2228, #2195/#2172/PR #2200. The fix for exactly that deadlock is PR #2281 — which cannot land until #2266 lands.\n\nSo a single protected file serialises the repair of the lane manager by the lane manager, and every stalled author lane waits behind it.\n\n## Orchestrator decision (marker #2330)\n\nMerge order for the protected file, one at a time, each brought current with main immediately before its review and merge: **#2266 → #2303 → #2281**, then the two drafts. Recorded here so a successor does not re-derive it or start a second contender.\n\n## What is worth changing\n\nThe guard is right to refuse concurrent edits to the coordination source. What is missing is a queue: nothing records who is next, so each contender discovers the collision independently and stalls. Consider an explicit ordered wait on the protected path, the same shape as the reviewer reservation waits.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 60\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-11T12:41:36Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T21:20:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2332,"title":"Protected coordination source serialises five open PRs with no queue","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:21:26Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2332"},

{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\nreturn_to: popcre/ai-devops\npriority: 3\n```\n\nBranch `claude/ai-glm-doctor-pin-fallback` in `popcre/ai-devops` carries two pushed commits and **no pull request**:\n\n- `62ac60f7` `bin/ai-glm` — doctor read the pinned binary path from the old launcher only; the launcher now execs an `opencode-ai-devops` wrapper, so doctor reported a version mismatch against a correctly pinned 1.18.12 install and blocked every governed review drawing glm. Added a fallback.\n- `644341f5` `bin/ai-codex-review` — the wrapper validated its own verdict section but printed only the report path to stdout, so shared-db's governed runner refused it for \"no recordable terminal verdict\" every time. This is why codex reads as a dead provider here. Added an **opt-in** terminal verdict line behind `AI_CODEX_REVIEW_STDOUT_VERDICT=1`, restating the already-validated verdict. `BLOCKED` deliberately unmapped.\n\n**The codex fix did not take effect when tested** (see the #2237 issue): either the env var is not forwarded by the governed runner, or a different copy of the wrapper is resolved. Diagnose where the wrapper resolves from before concluding anything about the provider.\n\nOutcome needed: open and merge the pull request in `popcre/ai-devops`, and prove the codex wrapper produces a recordable verdict in a real governed run.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-10T01:24:43Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T16:28:29Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. The fix must preserve every claim, version reservation, branch, pull request, worktree, and collision guard while freeing only the numerical author-capacity slot on durable evidence. It must add recovery metadata, stale-work retirement tombstones, independent capacity/preview outcomes, and read-only alerting. It authorizes no migration or database write.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\n```\n\nRequired outcome: a fresh implementation session can execute the checked-in plan without chat context; no expiry-only release, automatic PR closure, worktree deletion/cleaning, ref deletion, unsafe merge, or stale retired-work resurrection is possible.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-16T03:00:52Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T14:54:06Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"```machine\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\nreturn_to: none\nobjects: none\n```\n\n## What happened\n\nDrawn as the reviewer for PR #2298 at head `017eb079` (sequence 1288, slot 1), `codex-gpt-5.6-sol` via wrapper `ai-codex-review` produced a report whose Result section reads: the read-only sandbox rejected every permitted attempt to read the required manifest, so the bound change evidence could not be inspected, and no evidence-based findings are possible. Its verdict section is the single word `BLOCKED`.\n\nTwo separate defects, both reproduced live:\n\n1. **The sandbox cannot read the review packet manifest.** The reviewer never sees the diff, so it cannot produce a code review at all.\n2. **The wrapper prints no verdict line.** With `2>&1` captured, stdout carried exactly one line: the report file path. `run-governed-review.mjs` therefore refuses with `review wrapper did not produce a recordable terminal verdict (exit 0)` and the failure reads as a reviewer fault rather than a tooling fault. A `BLOCKED` verdict is also not one of the three words the recorder accepts, and it carries no head SHA.\n\nThis was invoked in the wrapper's documented shape (`ai-codex-review diff-review`, no prompt file, `AI_CODEX_REVIEW_CALLER=claude`), from a fresh clone at the exact PR head with a current local `main`, so the base resolved to the current main tip. The invocation shape is not the cause.\n\nThis is the same failure recorded during #2216/#2217 on 2026-09-03, so it is durable, not noise.\n\n## Cost\n\nEvery draw of this reviewer spends a rotation turn and forces a `--replace-failed-reviewer` round trip. On PR #2298 that cost one wasted assignment plus a replacement draw before `grok-4.6` could review.\n\n## Asked for\n\nEither repair the sandbox's access to the packet manifest and make the wrapper emit `VERDICT: <WORD> <40-hex head sha>` as its final stdout line, or remove `codex-gpt-5.6-sol` from the active rotation in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` until both are fixed. Do not leave it drawable in its current state.\n\nNot orchestrator work: it changes no database object. It belongs to an independent repository session, with the wrapper fix living in `ai-devops`.\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 3\n```\n\nClassified by the orchestrator on 2026-09-05 under AGENTS.md 0.0-C. Body text above is unchanged.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-08T00:20:42Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T14:18:29Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"The DesignFlow **sandbox-albert** database (the Supabase project named by secret `DB_HOST_SANDBOX` in `lithe-breaker-323913`, NOT the project the Supabase MCP is bound to) has drifted in two ways that together stop the tracking service from booting and stop Sample Tracking work.\n\n## 1. Startup-fatal: three `dflow` tables are gone\n\n`popcre-albert-tracking-sandbox` revision 00185 exits 1 during startup with:\n\n```\n{\"code\":\"42P01\",\"event\":\"application_startup_fatal\",\"message\":\"relation \\\"dflow.LicenseFeedBacks\\\" does not exist\"}\n```\n\nIn that database `dflow` no longer contains `LicenseFeedBacks`, `LicensingTime` or `FactoryTime`. Identical tables (28 / 14 / 0 rows) exist in schema `plm` in the same database. Revision 00183 (2026-09-02 20:10) booted fine against the same host secret version (v2, created 19:56 the same evening), so the tables were present that evening and are not now. designflow-tracking has cached all three at startup since March 2026, so this is environment drift, not an app change.\n\nEvery sandbox tracking deploy now fails at the Cloud Run health check; the service is serving the 2026-09-02 revision.\n\n## 2. The #2136 widening is not in this database\n\n`dflow.sample_workflow_valid_flow_path` there still reads:\n\n```\n(workflow_type = 'nyo_factory_make_request' AND business_path IN ('factory_ningbo_nyo','factory_ningbo_customer'))\n```\n\n`factory_customer` is absent from the `business_path` CHECK. The database also has no `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` table, so it is not receiving the governed migration stream at all.\n\n## Ask\n\nDecide and apply the correct governed fix for the sandbox database: restore the three `dflow` tables (or state that the app must now read them from `plm`), and bring `dflow.sample_workflow` and `dflow.validate_sample_path_revision()` up to `20260903083204_sample_workflow_factory_customer_direct_path.sql`.\n\nThe matching application change is already pushed to `designflow-tracking` `sandbox-albert` (`9da26e0`) and `designflow-frontend` `sandbox-albert` (`470deefc`); it is correct against production and cannot be verified in sandbox until the above is fixed.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 500\ntarget: sandbox-albert supabase project (DB_HOST_SANDBOX)\nschemas: dflow\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-04T14:22:41Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T13:53:54Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2299,"title":"sandbox-albert database drift: three dflow tables missing (tracking will not boot) and #2136 not applied","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:22:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2299"},

{"body":"Split out of #2274, whose fail-open half landed in https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/pull/2276. The pagination half did not, and is still open on main.\n\n`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs` reads `commits/{sha}/status` and `commits/{sha}/check-runs` with a bare `per_page=100` and no pagination. This repository already reports seventeen checks on a head, and a re-run **adds** a report rather than replacing one. Past a hundred reports, a required context that really did pass comes back absent, the pre-flight calls it \"never reported\", and the merge is refused for a reason nobody can act on. Safe direction, but an unexplainable block on the only merge path into `main`.\n\nFix: paginate both reads, flatten pages through a helper that refuses a non-list page rather than skipping it, and cross-check the flattened count against GitHub's own `total_count` so a short read is a loud refusal instead of a silent undercount.\n\nWork is already implemented in https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/pull/2275.\n\nroute: repo-maintenance","closedAt":"2026-09-04T07:46:41Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T06:56:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2282,"title":"Required-checks pre-flight: paginate both head reads","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:46:29Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2282"},
{"body":"Found while resuming structural issue #2177 under expired protected claim #2182.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 2\ndepends_on:\n```\n\nThe governed recovery commands deadlock when an expired claim's PR parser discovers legitimate child-column objects beneath already-claimed tables. `--renew-claim` refuses because the parsed columns are not individually recorded; `--expand-active-claim-from-pr` refuses because the lease is expired. The claim remains protected and must not be hand-edited or released.\n\nRequired outcome: an audited, append-only recovery path that can atomically validate and expand the expired protected claim from its existing PR, then renew it, without weakening collision checks. Add behavioural tests reproducing claim #2182 / issue #2177's two claimed tables plus eight parsed child columns. Return to active orchestrator marker #2269 when merged.","closedAt":"2026-09-07T23:56:43Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T05:28:51Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2280,"title":"HANDOVER: expired claim cannot expand from its existing PR before renewal","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:22:15Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2280"},
{"body":"The required-checks pre-flight landed in #2272 (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs`). Its governed review (muse-spark-1.2-contributor, APPROVE at `2738d435`) raised two non-blocking gaps. Neither warranted holding that merge; both are worth closing.\n\n## 1. A 200 with no `contexts` list passes with zero required checks\n\n```js\nprotection?.contexts ?? []\n```\n\nIf branch protection answers 200 but the payload carries no `contexts` array, the pre-flight computes an empty required list and passes, having checked nothing. A missing protection returns 404, which does fail closed — this is the 200-shaped case only. It should refuse instead, the same way `evaluatePreflight` already refuses a non-array required list.\n\n## 2. Both API reads are `per_page=100` with no pagination\n\n```\ncommits/{sha}/status?per_page=100\ncommits/{sha}/check-runs?per_page=100\n```\n\nPast 100 reports on one head, a required context that really did pass would appear \"never reported\" and the merge would be refused. That is the safe direction, but it is an unexplainable block on the only merge path, and this repository already runs 17 checks per head. Follow the `Link` header, or at least state in the code why 100 is enough.\n\n## Also worth pinning while there\n\nThe review noted these behaviours have no test, so a mutation of any of them stays green:\n\n- `neutral` and `skipped` counted as passing\n- an empty conclusion mapping to pending\n- the self-context filter being an exact `!==` and not a substring match\n- a commit status and a check run sharing one name (the cross-type tie-break)\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-04T05:06:32Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T03:56:36Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2274,"title":"Required-checks pre-flight: close the 200-with-no-contexts fail-open and the unpaginated reads","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:22:17Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2274"},

{"body":"Found while confirming the appearance-axis source for #2124 against the inventory, as that issue required.\n\n## What is wrong\n\n`api.source_capture_inventory` is the authoritative instrument for judging how much data a licensor capture actually holds. `docs/core-character-backfill-source-decision-20260902.md` §6 precondition 1 makes reading it mandatory before any curated Master Data load, precisely because counting a guessed table understated landed data by hundreds of thousands of rows on 2026-08-13.\n\nMeasured read-only against production on 2026-09-04:\n\n| Measure | Value |\n|---|---|\n| rows in the view | 392 |\n| rows with a non-null `retained_row_count` | **0** |\n| rows with a non-null `latest_complete_row_count` | **0** |\n\nBoth count columns are empty for every row in the view. The view still reports `count_basis` and `latest_complete_status` correctly, so it looks healthy at a glance.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThe documented rule is that a NULL count means the count cannot be derived and **does not mean zero**. That rule was written for the occasional gap. With every count NULL, the instrument gives no coverage signal at all while still appearing to answer, and the required precondition can be satisfied without learning anything. Any session that follows the rule literally will conclude nothing is derivable and either stall or fall back to the exact guessed-table counting the rule exists to prevent.\n\n## Scope\n\nFind why the count columns are unpopulated view-wide — whether the producing job stopped, the source of the counts moved, or the view's count expressions silently return NULL — and repair it so the view sizes the captures again. Do not remove the columns and do not change the documented NULL semantics as a substitute for the repair.\n\n**Control:** the whole-view count above was run deliberately alongside the character-table query, so this is a view-wide defect and not a character-specific gap.\n\nRead-only reproduction:\n\n```sql\nselect count(*) as rows,\n       count(retained_row_count) as retained_notnull,\n       count(latest_complete_row_count) as latest_notnull\nfrom api.source_capture_inventory;\n```\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads: api.source_capture_inventory\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-04T03:30:29Z","createdAt":"2026-09-04T02:17:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2263,"title":"api.source_capture_inventory reports no row counts at all (392 rows, zero non-null counts)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:22:20Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2263"},

{"body":"## Symptom\n\n`run-governed-review.mjs` invoking `ai-codex-review` refuses with\n\n```\nREFUSED: review wrapper did not produce a recordable terminal verdict (exit 0)\n```\n\neven though the wrapper exits 0 and publishes a complete, high-quality review report.\n\n## Cause — a contract mismatch, not a provider failure\n\nThe two sides disagree on how a verdict is spelled.\n\n- `run-governed-review.mjs` requires exactly one terminal line of the form `VERDICT: <APPROVE|REVISE|REJECT> <40-char head sha>`.\n- `ai-codex-review` enforces its own format: a final two-line section `## Verdict` followed by a bare `APPROVE` / `REJECT` / `BLOCKED`, with no SHA. Its report is written to `.ai/reviews/codex-<mode>-<runid>.md`, which the runner never reads.\n\n`ai-codex-review` also accepts no prompt: its usage is `ai-codex-review <plan-review|diff-review|security-review|visual-review|final-check> [--tests <cmd>]`. There is no way to hand it the runner's output-discipline instruction, so it can never be talked into the runner's format.\n\n## Evidence\n\nGoverned run against PR #2232 at head `1bee1f1382f2bc720dd7db2b14a34fea70fab246` (issue #2171), slot 1, sequence 1195. Wrapper `doctor` passes: `PASS provider=codex sandbox=read-only reasoning=explicit command=codex`. The run produced a substantive review with a High finding and a `## Verdict / REJECT` section, all of it unrecordable.\n\n## Consequence\n\n`codex-gpt-5.6-sol` is a **structurally dead slot** for every governed review, not an intermittently failing one. With `qwen-3.8-max`, `glm-5.2`, `deepseek-chat` and `kimi-k3` retired or paused, this leaves an effective pool of two. Every draw that lands on codex costs a wasted allocation, a terminal-failure replacement, and a fresh draw — and the review work itself is thrown away.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nTeach `run-governed-review.mjs` to read the wrapper's published report and accept the `## Verdict` two-line section, binding it to the head SHA the runner already knows and already pins. Do not relax the single-terminal-verdict rule, the extra-decision-word refusal, or the auto-void path — the head binding must come from the runner's own pinned SHA, never from reviewer text.\n\nDo not delete or exclude the reviewer as a substitute for the repair: the provider works, only the transcription is missing.\n\n```machine\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nwrites: scripts/run-governed-review.mjs\nreads:\n```\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 3\n```\n\nClassified by the orchestrator on 2026-09-05 under AGENTS.md 0.0-C. Body text above is unchanged.\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-08T19:39:30Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T22:23:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2244,"title":"Governed review runner cannot record a codex verdict: wrapper publishes '## Verdict / APPROVE', runner requires 'VERDICT: <x> <sha>'","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:22:30Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2244"},
{"body":"## Symptom\n\nMerging a documentation-only PR moved `main` from `fe822fef` to `73717cf1`. The net diff between those two tips is exactly two `.md` files. Yet `check-main-tip-freshness.mjs --contains` refused PR #2232 with a list of twenty non-documentation paths and \"Re-dispatch against the current tip.\"\n\n## Cause\n\nThe documentation allowlist is evaluated **per commit in the range**, not against the **net diff of the range**. The docs PR's history contained a `chore: update from main` merge commit (`6e1cdef5`). Diffed against its first parent, that merge introduces every file main had gained since the branch point — `.mjs`, `.py`, `.sql`, `.json`. None of it is new to `main`; all of it was already an ancestor of `fe822fef`.\n\n## Consequence\n\nEvery branch we update from `main` before merging produces such a merge commit. Once it lands on `main`, it makes the next docs-only merge look like a large code change to every other open PR. The exemption added for #2047/#2030 is therefore defeated in normal operation, and each PR must be re-updated and **re-reviewed** — burning a reviewer draw from a pool of five with two unavailable.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nCompute the changed-file set as the **net diff** `git diff --name-only <MAIN_SHA> <origin/main>` rather than the union of per-commit diffs, keeping the extension allowlist and every fail-closed refusal exactly as they are. A net diff cannot hide a code change: any file whose bytes differ between the two tips still appears.\n\nDo not widen the extension allowlist.\n\n```machine\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nobjects: scripts/check-main-tip-freshness.mjs\n```\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 3\n```\n\nClassified by the orchestrator on 2026-09-05 under AGENTS.md 0.0-C. Body text above is unchanged.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T23:59:05Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T22:17:49Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2243,"title":"check-main-tip-freshness: per-commit diffing makes every update-from-main merge look like a code change","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:22:32Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2243"},
{"body":"```machine\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nobjects: supabase/tests/popdam_effective_count_performance_contracts.sql\n```\n\nIndependent review of #2230 (grok-4.6, `VERDICT: APPROVE a1bc807b`) raised one Medium finding that was deliberately not fixed on that head, to avoid invalidating the verdict.\n\n`public.get_effective_filter_counts_unchecked_1703(jsonb)` now has **three** arms:\n- Arm 1 — no identity filter, `tagFilter` null\n- Arm 1T — no identity filter, `tagFilter` present; driven by `select distinct e.asset_id from public.asset_effective_tags e where e.tag = ...`, an index-only scan on `asset_effective_tags_tag_asset_idx (tag, asset_id)`\n- Arm 2 — identity filter present\n\nThe migration `20260903193135` pins that shape in an apply-time `DO` guard, but that guard runs exactly once and never again.\n\nThe durable test `supabase/tests/popdam_effective_count_performance_contracts.sql` still describes **two** matched arms, still matches `-- arm 1: no identity filter` as a prefix, and never mentions Arm 1T. A later `create or replace` could delete the tag-leading scan, keep the Arm 1 and Arm 2 comments, and this test would still pass — the performance regression would ship silently.\n\n**Wanted:** extend the durable contract test to pin Arm 1T specifically — the `distinct` subquery over `asset_effective_tags`, the primary-key join to `assets`, the `tagFilter is null` / `is not null` exclusivity pair, and the three-way `union all` count. Also add a case covering a tag present at two scopes (`asset` and `style_group`) for the same asset, which is what makes the `distinct` load-bearing; the existing parity test in `popdam_effective_asset_filter_contracts.sql` does not cover it.\n\nDo not weaken or delete the existing assertions.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 3\n```\n\nClassified by the orchestrator on 2026-09-05 under AGENTS.md 0.0-C. {"body":"## What is missing\n\n`plm.wb_property` has no `core_property_id` and no `resolution_status` column. Every other resolution-capable source landing table has them. The consequence is concrete: **once someone decides which `core.property` a Warner property maps to, there is nowhere to record the decision.** The answer is lost the moment the session that made it ends.\n\n## How this surfaced\n\nFound during the four-licensor reconciliation (#640, PR #2229, `docs/licensor-source-reconciliation-20260903.md`), read-only against production. That run also established:\n\n- All 1,901 rows across the three resolution-capable source tables are currently `unresolved` with a NULL `core_property_id` — so no resolution has ever been stored for any licensor, not just Warner.\n- Warner spans **three** `core.licensor` rows (WB / DC / HP), derived by cross-tab rather than assumed.\n- Warner reuses one UUID across two namespaces, so any resolution key must be `(source_system, source_namespace, source_id)` — namespace included. A `(source_system, source_id)` key is not sufficient here.\n\n## Scope\n\nAdd the two columns to `plm.wb_property` to match its sibling landing tables, with whatever FK/constraint shape those siblings already use. Derive that shape from the siblings rather than inventing one; if they disagree with each other, stop and report instead of picking.\n\nThis is the structural enabler only. {"body":"PopDAM issue: https://github.com/u2giants/popdam3/issues/107 Plan: `u2giants/popdam3/plan_popsg_production_readiness.md` sections 9.2–9.10.  ## Outcome  Provide the governed database shape for truthful, bounded PopSG crawl reconciliation; explicit lifecycle metrics; restart-safe PopSG PDF text extraction; and authorized server-side search/filter/facet pagination. The existing unbounded cleanup and blocking aggregate refresh timed out during an ordinary production crawl while the run was still marked completed.  The application session owns app code and later reversible row reconciliation. This issue owns structure only. No licensed paths, filenames, or row exports are included here.  ## Required contract  - Preview stale candidates without mutation, then reconcile deterministically in bounded idempotent batches by root and accepted crawl ID. - Persist explicit ingest/reconcile/refresh/completed/failed/attention-required state and lifecycle counters. A run is never completed before reconciliation and aggregate freshness succeed. - Guard empty, inaccessible, and suspicious low-nonzero crawls without inactivating current rows. - The existing `public.deactivate_stale_sg_files(text,uuid)` is `SECURITY DEFINER` and currently executable by `authenticated`; revoke execution from `authenticated` and `public`, and make every replacement continuation RPC service-role-only. - Maintain guide/folder aggregates incrementally or with a preview-proven nonblocking bounded strategy. - Store and claim/complete dedicated PopSG PDF extraction keyed to active `style_guide_files`, invalidating safely on content identity change. - Maintain incremental PopSG search documents and expose one authorized RPC covering active path/name/guide metadata/tags/PDF text, required filters, stable ranking/pagination, exact total, and matching facets. - Prove representative-volume plans, interruption/resume, reactivation, least privilege, RLS/authorization, and stable paging in preview before guarded merge/promotion.  ```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 100\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table public.style_guide_crawl_runs\r\n  - table public.style_guide_files\r\n  - materialized view public.style_guide_file_groups\r\n  - materialized view public.style_guide_folders\r\n  - function public.deactivate_stale_sg_files\r\n  - function public.preview_stale_sg_files\r\n  - function public.reconcile_stale_sg_files_batch\r\n  - function public.refresh_style_guide_matviews\r\n  - table public.style_guide_pdf_text\r\n  - function public.claim_style_guide_pdf_text\r\n  - function public.complete_style_guide_pdf_text\r\n  - table public.style_guide_search_documents\r\n  - function public.search_style_guide_library\r\n  - index public.sgfolders_licensor_property_uidx\n  - index public.idx_sgf_reconcile_root_active_run_id\n  - index public.idx_sg_pdf_text_claimable\n  - index public.idx_sg_search_documents_search_vector\n  - index public.idx_sg_search_documents_filters\n  - index public.idx_sg_search_documents_stable_page\nreads:\n```  The migration author may refine new-object signatures before claim acquisition, but must update this block atomically through the lane manager and claim every exact final object before authoring. Preserve all existing rows and compatibility; the migration must not perform a bulk backfill or full aggregate rebuild. {"body":"## What happened\n\nOn PR #2145 (issue #2123), slot 1 (glm-5.3, replacement seq 1083) reached a durable\n\\`VERDICT: APPROVE\\` for head \\`61c1460d09ee609103cad748c4d9344cbb9abf46\\` before slot 2\nwas ever drawn. Every subsequent attempt to draw slot 2 for that same head — including\na first-time draw, not just a replacement — was refused.\n\n## Root cause\n\nTraced to \\`hasVerdictForHead\\` in \\`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs\\`: once ANY\nslot has a recorded verdict for a head, the tool refuses every further reviewer\nassignment for that head, with no distinction between \"assign a fresh slot\" and\n\"replace an already-assigned slot.\" The working pattern this tool actually requires —\nconfirmed against an earlier head in this same PR's history — is to draw BOTH slots\nbefore EITHER review runs to completion. If one reviewer finishes first (the normal\ncase; reviewers are asynchronous and vary widely in speed), the other slot becomes\npermanently undrawable for that head.\n\n## Impact\n\nThis is not specific to PR #2145. Any migration where one reviewer finishes\nmeaningfully faster than the other hits this. The only documented recovery is\nproducing a new head (discarding the already-obtained verdict) and drawing both slots\ntogether before either completes — an workaround, not a fix, and it burns a review\nround and reviewer-pool capacity every time it happens.\n\n## Fix needed\n\n\\`hasVerdictForHead\\` (or its caller) should refuse a *replacement* of an\nalready-verdicted slot, but must not refuse a genuine first-time draw of a\nstill-empty slot at the same head just because a sibling slot already completed.\n\n## Work type\n\nTooling defect in reviewer-assignment orchestration, not a database structural\nchange. REPO-SESSION per AGENTS.md 0.0-C — not an orchestrator migration-author-lane\nitem.\n\nFiled by the shared-db orchestrator session while unblocking PR #2145.","closedAt":"2026-09-03T22:51:48Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T14:22:35Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2208,"title":"Reviewer assignment refuses a first-time draw of slot 2 once slot 1 has a recorded verdict for the same head","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:46:43Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2208"},
{"body":"## What happened\n\nDuring the governed review of PR #2139 (issue #2130), `scripts/run-governed-review.mjs`\nrefused to record a completed review with:\n\n```\nreview findings carry 1 line(s) a downstream verdict parser would read as a\ndecision besides the terminal verdict line\n```\n\nThe reviewer had done the work and produced three correct, load-bearing findings.\nThe refusal discarded all of it: nothing was posted to the PR, no verdict artifact\nwas recorded, and the reviewer's slot had already been spent. The findings survived\nonly because the wrapper keeps its own transcript and I could read them back out of\nit by hand. Nothing in the governed path would have told a successor session that a\nreal review had happened, or what it said.\n\n## Why this is a defect and not just a strict rule\n\nThe rule itself is right — a stray decision word in the body is exactly what\n#2075 and a-comment-can-become-a-verdict describe, and it must not be recorded.\nThe defect is the **disposal**. A review that is unrecordable *as a verdict* is\nstill valuable *as findings*, and the current path throws both away together at the\nlast step, after every expensive part is finished.\n\nThree consequences, each independent:\n\n1. **The cost falls on the wrong side.** The reviewer slot is consumed, the lease is\n   held, and the round produced no artifact — so the PR looks unreviewed while the\n   pool looks busy (a-dead-lane-reads-as-a-busy-one).\n2. **The recovery is out-of-band.** Reading the wrapper transcript is not part of the\n   governed path; a session that did not know the wrapper name would have lost the\n   content outright.\n3. **Nothing warns the reviewer in advance.** The prompt the runner sends does not\n   state the constraint, so a reviewer writing normal prose — \"REVISE. The direction\n   of the change is right, but ...\" — trips it by writing in the ordinary way. The\n   round only succeeded on the retry because I added the prohibition to the prompt\n   text by hand.\n\n## What a fix looks like\n\nAny of these closes it; the first is the smallest:\n\n- Persist the raw reviewer output before the decision-word scan runs, so a refused\n  round leaves a readable record of what the reviewer said and which line tripped it.\n- Have the runner state the constraint in the brief it sends every reviewer, so this\n  is prevented rather than caught.\n- Distinguish \"cannot be recorded as a verdict\" from \"cannot be recorded at all\":\n  post the findings, withhold the verdict, and let the round be retried without\n  spending a fresh reviewer.\n\nDo not relax the scan itself. A body that can be read as a decision must never\nbecome one.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- PR #2139, round 2, reviewer glm-5.3. The refused round and the successful retry are\n  both in that PR's history; the retry differs only in the prompt's output-format\n  section.\n- Related but not the same: #2075 (prose read AS a verdict), #2157 (an unreadable\n  verdict reported as absent), #2117 (a wrapper that cannot be briefed at all).\n\n```machine\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\nobjects: none\n```\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 3\n```\n\nClassified by the orchestrator on 2026-09-05 under AGENTS.md 0.0-C. Body text above is unchanged.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T23:51:14Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T14:19:41Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2207,"title":"A decision word in a review body discards the whole review, after the reviewer slot is already spent","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:23:00Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2207"},
{"body":"## Goal\n\nComplete the workflow-action contract needed for reliable repeated Sales/Sourcing handoffs, stale-write rejection, and zero-recipient rollback.\n\n## Gaps in #1987\n\nThe current `record_item_workflow_action` function:\n\n- finds the earliest reverse-direction action rather than linking a return to the corresponding open Sales-to-Sourcing handoff;\n- accepts no expected prior step/version, so a stale browser can overwrite a newer transition after the item lock is acquired;\n- can commit the RFQ step/action with zero notifications when the destination function has no active assignee;\n- carries fallback/review facts only as free JSON and has no durable source-action relationship for audit/read APIs.\n\nThese violate the approved behavior in `popcre/designflow-backend#81`: return to the actual original requester for that pricing cycle, reject stale transitions, and never silently complete a required handoff with no recipient.\n\n## Required contract\n\n- Add an explicit self-FK such as `source_action_id` / `return_of_action_id` from a return action to its originating handoff action.\n- Define an unambiguous open/closed handoff rule that supports multiple pricing cycles for one RFQ item and prevents one source handoff from being returned twice unless an explicit reversal rule allows it.\n- Add expected-prior-step (or equivalent version) input and reject stale transitions before any write.\n- For recipient-required transitions, raise and roll back when no eligible active recipient resolves.\n- Preserve immutable original actor even when the application uses a labeled inactive-requester or legacy fallback; make fallback reason/admin-review state queryable and testable.\n- Preserve correlation-key retry idempotence and reject reuse by a different action/actor.\n- Add real-DML tests for repeated cycles, stale concurrent transitions, duplicate returns, missing owner, inactive original requester, fallback, retry, and total rollback.\n\nExact names/signatures may follow the canonical objects produced by #2202. Do not edit the applied #1987 migration.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 100\ndepends_on: 2202\nwrites:\n  - table dflow.item_workflow_action\n  - function dflow.record_item_workflow_action\nreads:\n  - table dflow.item_user_assignment\n  - table plm.RFQItem\n  - table plm.RFQStep\n  - table dflow.users\n  - table app.user_notification\n```\n\nDatabase package 2 of 3 for `popcre/designflow-backend#81`.\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-05T07:25:54Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T12:14:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2203,"title":"DesignFlow workflow actions: source handoff, stale-write, and zero-recipient integrity","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:23:04Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2203"},
{"body":"## Goal  Add a forward migration that makes the DesignFlow item-assignment, workflow-action, and linked-notification contract from #1987 operate on the canonical tables used by the multi-schema DesignFlow application.  ## Confirmed defect  Migration `20260901221310_designflow_item_assignment_action_history.sql` from PR #1989 creates both new history tables in `dflow`, references `dflow.\"RFQItem\"` and `dflow.\"RFQStep\"`, and alters `dflow.user_notification`.  The current DesignFlow backend table map and the live production catalog use:  - `plm.\"RFQItem\"` and `plm.\"RFQStep\"` for operational RFQ data; - `dflow.users` for DesignFlow staff identity; - `app.user_notification` for notification list/count/read APIs.  Read-only live-catalog inspection on 2026-09-03 proved both legacy and canonical copies coexist. `dflow.item_user_assignment` and `dflow.item_workflow_action` exist, and only `dflow.user_notification` has #1987's `workflow_action_id` / `idempotency_key`; `app.user_notification` lacks both. Therefore #1987 can update the legacy RFQ copy and create a notification the running application does not read.  ## Required forward fix  - Never edit or reuse migration `20260901221310`. - Establish canonical assignment/action tables whose FKs reference `plm.\"RFQItem\"`, `plm.\"RFQStep\"`, and `dflow.users`. A safe forward-copy/rename/view strategy is implementer judgment, but there must be one unambiguous application authority. - Add action/idempotency linkage to `app.user_notification`; do not make the new application path write `dflow.user_notification`. - Replace the two write functions so the RFQ step, action, assignment, and notifications affect only canonical objects atomically. - Preserve server-attributed actors, effective-dated assignment history, idempotency, duplicate-recipient protection, and append-only action history. - Keep legacy rows/copies intact for rollback; do not destructively move or guess application data in this structural migration. - Add contract tests proving `plm.\"RFQItem\"` changes, canonical history is written, `app.user_notification` receives the notification, and legacy copies are untouched by the new path. - Rehearse on shared preview and attach exact catalog/readback evidence.  ## Package boundary  This is database package 1 of 3 for `popcre/designflow-backend#81`. Follow-ups #2203 and #2204 are declared now and depend on this canonical-location repair.  ```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 100\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table dflow.item_user_assignment\r\n  - table dflow.item_workflow_action\r\n  - table app.user_notification\n  - column app.user_notification.workflow_action_id\n  - column app.user_notification.idempotency_key\r\n  - index app.user_notification_action_recipient\r\n  - index app.user_notification_idempotency_key\r\n  - function dflow.set_item_user_assignment\r\n  - function dflow.record_item_workflow_action\r\nreads:\r\n  - table plm.\"RFQItem\"\r\n  - table plm.\"RFQStep\"\r\n  - table dflow.users\r\n  - table dflow.user_notification\r\n```  Found while beginning application implementation after #1987 was reported complete. \r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-04T17:30:41Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T12:10:32Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2202,"title":"HANDOVER: #1987 workflow contract targets legacy DesignFlow schemas","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:23:06Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2202"},

{"body":"## Goal\n\nLower `fillfactor` on `public.dam_search_documents` so its lease/retry/error updates can go HOT.\n\nSplit out of #1966 as the one actionable, non-frozen piece of that issue. The index-drop half of #1966 stays frozen until its observation window closes on 2026-09-17 and is **out of scope here**.\n\n## Why this table and only this table\n\nCause-(2) analysis on #1966 ([comment](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/1966#issuecomment-5525453029)) checked all four high-churn tables against their real update statements and their live index definitions:\n\n| table | verdict |\n|---|---|\n| `public.style_guide_files` | every update path writes an indexed column or a partial-index predicate column. HOT is impossible regardless of fillfactor. **No change.** |\n| `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` | the `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` in `plm.refresh_style_tracker_item_bridge` sets seven indexed columns, incl. `sku` feeding an `upper(sku)` expression index. **No change.** |\n| `public.assets` | already 46.2% HOT, 2 GB heap, 35 indexes. Weakest case. **No change.** |\n| `public.dam_search_documents` | **the only candidate.** Only the completion write touches `embedding`. The claim/lease, error and reset writes touch `embedding_lease_token`, `embedding_lease_owner`, `embedding_lease_expires_at`, `embedding_attempts`, `embedding_error*` and `embedding_next_retry_at` — none of which is indexed on this table. That is most of 3.27M updates, HOT-eligible by column, yet still only 6.6% HOT. The blocker is page space, not column choice. |\n\n`reloptions` is null on all four tables, so every one sits at the default fillfactor 100 with no free space reserved for an updated row to stay on its page.\n\n## The cost, which is real and must be measured not assumed\n\nRows are roughly 1.9 KB (the 384-dimension vector is stored inline), so only about 4 rows fit per 8 KB page. Buying even one free slot per page therefore means roughly `fillfactor = 75`, implying about 30% heap growth on a currently 271 MB table.\n\n**Do not copy the usual 85-90 advice.** At 4 rows per page, 90 and 85 both round to zero reserved slots and would change nothing while still being recorded as a fix. Derive the value from the actual live row width and page occupancy, and state in the PR what free-slot count the chosen value actually buys.\n\n## Scope\n\nStructural, metadata-only. `alter table public.dam_search_documents set (fillfactor = N)` takes no rewrite, affects only pages written afterwards, and is reversible. It does **not** shrink the already-bloated heap; reclaiming existing bloat is not part of this issue.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- The chosen fillfactor is justified by a measured row width and resulting free-slot count, not by convention.\n- The migration is metadata-only and reversible.\n- No index is dropped, created or altered.\n- No statistics counters are reset (the #1966 observation window is open until 2026-09-17 and must not be disturbed).\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 100\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table public.dam_search_documents\nreads:\n```\n\nSplit from #1966.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-05T11:05:00Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T12:05:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2196,"title":"Lower fillfactor on public.dam_search_documents so its lease/retry updates can go HOT","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:23:10Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2196"},

{"body":"## Routing\n\n**Repo-maintenance, NOT orchestrator work.** This changes one script (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`) and possibly `AGENTS.md`. It does not change the shape of the database, no migration is involved, and no claim or version reservation is needed. It belongs to a repo session, not to the orchestrator lane. Labelled `db-work` (unclassified intake, grants no orchestrator ownership) and `bug`.\n\n## Summary\n\n`--supersede-active-claim-version` (alias `--reversion-active-claim`) refuses on any claim whose issue **title** omits the `#` before the issue number. Since claim titles are neither validated at creation time nor documented as needing that form, an unknown number of open claims cannot be superseded at all. Separately, the refusal message names six things that are all fine and stays silent about the seventh, which is the one that actually failed.\n\n## Two faults\n\n**1. Undocumented, unenforced title-format requirement.**\n\n`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:3158` gates the supersession on:\n\n```js\n!new RegExp(`#${request.issue}(?:\\D|$)`).test(before.title ?? '')\n```\n\nThe claim title must contain `#<issue>`. Nothing creates claim titles in that form as a guarantee, nothing validates it when a claim is opened, and `AGENTS.md` does not state it. Claim #2153 was titled `CLAIM: 2146 restore core.character foreign keys on the three Tier-1 plm character tables` — correct in every respect except the missing `#` — and was therefore un-supersedable.\n\n**2. The refusal does not say which term failed.**\n\nThe exact text, verbatim:\n\n```\nREFUSED: claim issue, owner, lease, version, branch, or worktree changed\n```\n\nThat message lists six candidate causes. The title check is `&&`-ed into the same condition but is not named in the message at all, so the one term that actually failed is the one term the operator is not told about. Worse, the message asserts something \"changed\" when nothing had changed — the title had been that way since the claim was opened.\n\n## How the cause was proved\n\nDiagnosing this took a full investigation rather than a read of the message:\n\n1. Ran the command with every argument taken from the claim body verbatim; got the refusal above.\n2. Parsed claim #2153's lease with the script's own exported `parseAuthorLease`, and compared every field named in the message against the arguments passed. All six matched exactly: owner `claude-lane-2146-tier1-fk`, branch `claude/2146-tier1-character-fk`, worktree `C:/repos/shared-db/.claude/worktrees/shared-db-2146-tier1-character-fk`, version `20260903014958`, claim open, lease `active` and unexpired.\n3. Read line 3158 and found the unnamed seventh term.\n4. Evaluated the regex directly against the live title: `new RegExp(\"#2146(?:\\D|$)\").test(title)` returned `false`. Sole cause confirmed.\n\n## Suggested fix (for the repo session; deliberately not applied here)\n\n- Split the composite condition so the refusal names the specific term that failed — the guard already knows which one it is.\n- Either validate the claim-title form at claim creation, or state the `#<issue>` requirement in `AGENTS.md` next to the claim format, or relax the check to accept a bare issue number when it is unambiguous. Whichever is chosen, creation-time and supersession-time expectations should agree.\n- Consider auditing existing open `db-claim` issues for titles that would fail this check today.\n\n## Note\n\nThe immediate blocker was cleared under orchestrator authorization by a title-only correction on #2153 (adding the `#`; the claim already named and belonged to #2146). That unblocked PR #2156 and is recorded on #2153. It does not fix this defect for any other claim.\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 3\n```\n\nClassified by the orchestrator on 2026-09-05 under AGENTS.md 0.0-C. {"body":"Split out of #2177 on 2026-09-03. The owner ruled on `/salespersons` and `/customers` (#2081 comment 5519623574) and those moved to #2177 as ready work. **`/vendors` and `/seasons` were not part of that ruling and still need one.** Structure only; no row loads.\n\n## The decision the owner must make\n\n| feed | live fields (2026-09-02 census) | stored, excluding provenance | undisposed |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `/vendors` | 29 | 10 | 19 |\n| `/seasons` | 13 | 6 | 7 |\n\n`/seasons` adds `seasonDesc, startDate, endDate, shipStartDate, shipEndDate, active` beyond what is stored.\n\nOwner decision **D5** rejects a per-row raw archive. There is no stored copy of the payload, so **a field left out now is unrecoverable without re-pulling the feed.** Each undisposed property needs an explicit ingest or ignore ruling. `docs/coldlion-field-decisions-20260819.csv` has `vendors` rows that predate the current payload and **no `seasons` rows at all**.\n\nNeither feed has raised a personal-data concern; both look like ordinary business reference data. The ruling is still the owner's, because under D5 the omission is permanent either way.\n\n## Then, and only then\n\nAdd the approved missing typed fields to `coldlion.vendor` and `coldlion.season` by forward migration — never by editing applied migrations `20260825023430` or `20260902054548`. Ignored fields map nowhere; a sampled field with no disposition must make the loader fail loudly.\n\n`/api-docs` types both feeds as a bare `{\"type\":\"object\"}`, so the disposition list must be built from live sampling and re-sampled at authoring time. No field values, customer identifiers or licensed data belong in this public repository; the sanitized field-name census is on #2081.\n\n## Gate\n\nEvery sampled property of both feeds has a recorded ingest/ignore ruling; approved fields map once; RLS/grant posture unchanged; replay idempotent; the same season code in different divisions stays distinct.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 3\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table coldlion.vendor\n  - table coldlion.season\nreads:\n```\n\nblocker: owner ingest/ignore ruling required for 26 undisposed live properties across `/vendors` (19) and `/seasons` (7). The 2026-09-03 ruling covered `/salespersons` and `/customers` only. D5 makes every omission permanent.\n\nTracker: #2081. {"body":"ColdLion's `GET /EhpApi/pickticket` returns HTTP 500 with an empty body whenever the request is not narrowed, and both `/pickticket` and `/receiving` report zero rows for every window we can successfully query. This blocks the Step 6b landing tables in `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md`: we have never observed a row from either feed, so we cannot state their fields or their grain.\n\n**This issue is not structural and must not take a migration-author lane.** It is vendor liaison. It stays open until ColdLion answers.\n\n### The defect, precisely\n\nFailure depends on breadth of match, not on a missing parameter:\n\n- `minTransactionNo=999999` (matches nothing) → HTTP 200\n- `minTransactionNo=0` and `minTransactionNo=1` (match everything) → HTTP 500, empty body\n- no parameters at all → HTTP 500, empty body\n- any date narrowing (`createdFrom`, `createdFrom`+`createdTo`, `transactionDate`) → HTTP 200\n- `createdTo` alone, and `sort=transactionNo&size=1` → connection dropped before response\n\nReproducible: three consecutive `?size=1` calls returned dropped-connection, 500, 500. Never once succeeded unnarrowed.\n\n`/receiving` has an identical parameter signature in `/v2/api-docs` and handles every one of those calls correctly, returning a well-formed empty page. Same key, same session, same minute — so this is not our credentials, our client, or rate limiting. `/divisions`, `/orderHistory` and `/prodHistory` all returned data on that key at the same time.\n\n### The entanglement worth remembering\n\nThe `/pickticket` requests that fail are exactly the broad ones that would show whether data exists. So we **cannot** conclude the pick-ticket feed is empty — only that the narrow windows we are permitted to ask are empty. Do not let \"0 rows\" harden into \"no data\" in any later summary.\n\n### State\n\n- Vendor problem report drafted with the full request/response table, the `/receiving` contrast, and the reproducibility evidence. Sent to Albert to forward to ColdLion; not yet sent to the vendor.\n- Corrections posted to #2081 (comment 5519596972), superseding the coarser §8 claim in the census that `/pickticket` was unconditionally broken and `/receiving` merely empty.\n\n### Done when\n\n1. ColdLion acknowledges and fixes the 500, or gives a workaround.\n2. ColdLion answers whether pick-ticket and receiving transactions should be visible to our API key.\n3. At least one row is observed from each feed, so field names and grain can be censused.\n4. Unit 6b is then unblocked and can be split into structural issues normally.\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: source-data\nroute: source-data-session\npriority: 3\nreturn_to: u2giants/shared-db\n```\n\nClassified by the orchestrator on 2026-09-05 under AGENTS.md 0.0-C. Vendor liaison, not structural: it cannot take a migration-author lane and it has no repository return address, because the answer must come from ColdLion. It stays open until the vendor replies.\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-06T22:48:50Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T02:51:36Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2178,"title":"ColdLion vendor defect: /pickticket returns HTTP 500 unnarrowed, and both /pickticket and /receiving show zero rows (blocks Step 6b)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:23:31Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2178"},
{"body":"Part of the ColdLion landing split from §9 Step 1 of `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md`. Structure only; no row loads.\n\n**Revised 2026-09-03: the owner has ruled, and this unit is ready.** The authority is #2081 comment 5519623574 (Albert Hazan, 2026-09-03). `/vendors` and `/seasons` still have no ruling and were moved to their own issue.\n\n## What this unit builds\n\nAdd the owner-approved missing typed fields to `coldlion.customer` and `coldlion.salesperson` by **forward migration** — never by editing applied migrations `20260825023430` or `20260902054548`.\n\n### `coldlion.salesperson` — a deliberately narrow projection\n\nIngest **name, code, company, and active status. Nothing else.**\n\nEvery other property on `/salespersons` is **DECLINED** — not pending, not deferred, not awaiting anything. That explicitly includes email, phone, home address, commission and quota. They are personal data about named people with no established business use, and they must not appear in this table, in any `writes:` list, or in any follow-up issue.\n\nTwo sessions independently recommended a projection here and they differed; the owner chose the narrower one. The discarded wider recommendation is not the decision.\n\n**Widening this projection requires a NEW owner ruling recorded the same way as #2081 comment 5519623574.** Under D5 there is no raw archive, so an omission is permanent — but permanence is not a reason to over-ingest, and no session may widen this by inference, by \"it was in the feed anyway\", or by a later convenience argument.\n\nNote the casing trap: `/salespersons` returns `uDF01`/`uDF02` where every other feed uses `udf01`.\n\n### `coldlion.customer` — ingest everything\n\nThe owner ruled ingest-everything for `/customers`: company-level business data, no personal-data concern. The live feed returned 39 fields against 7 stored columns at the 2026-09-02 census; re-sample immediately before authoring and map every sampled property.\n\n## Sampling, not the spec\n\n`/api-docs` types both feeds as a bare `{\"type\":\"object\"}` — 14 of 16 GET feeds are untyped, and where the spec does type a feed it is wrong. Build the column list from a live sample and key the loader's unknown-field refusal to that **sampled shape**, never to `/api-docs`. A newly appearing property with no ruling must make the loader fail loudly rather than land silently — that is how the declined `/salespersons` fields stay out.\n\n## Gate\n\nThe four approved `/salespersons` fields land and no others; every sampled `/customers` property maps once; RLS/grant posture unchanged (no application-facing policy); replay idempotent. Extend `coldlion_master_landing_contracts.sql`, and add an assertion that `coldlion.salesperson` has no email, phone, address, commission or quota column.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 3\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table coldlion.customer\n  - table coldlion.salesperson\nreads:\n```\n\nTracker: #2081. Owner ruling: #2081 comment 5519623574.
