This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2177,"title":"ColdLion landing: customer and salesperson field projections (owner ruling recorded)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:23:33Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2177"},
{"body":"Unit 5a of the ColdLion landing split, from §9 Step 6 of `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md`. Structure only; no row loads.\n\n**Revised 2026-09-02.** Filed as one blocked \"remainder tables\" issue; the live field census on #2081 (comment 5519573718) proved two of the seven endpoints authorable now and four not sampleable at all, so it was split. This is the authorable half. The other four feeds are in the 5b issue.\n\n## What this unit builds\n\nLanding tables for the two remainder endpoints whose grain and fields are proven from live sampling.\n\n- **`coldlion.inventory`** — `/inventory`, paged envelope, 12 fields: `colorCode, dimCode, divisionCode, inventoryCost, inventoryQty, itemNo, itemPkey, labelCode, prepackCode, sizeCode, warehouseCode, warehouseSku`.\n- **`coldlion.prod_tracking`** — `/prodtracking`, 52 fields, purchase-order grain keyed on `prodOrderNo`. Returns a **bare array with no page envelope**; its filter parameters are date-based only.\n\nWhere the vendor exposes no stable line/event identity, use a surrogate row UUID plus a uniqueness contract over the smallest **proven** source identity and the source hash. Never label a guessed key as natural. Child tables for any repeated group must be added to the `writes:` list before dispatch.\n\nRe-sample both endpoints immediately before authoring and confirm the field lists and grain; these counts are today's measurement, not a contract.\n\n## Correction to plan Step 6 as written\n\nStep 6 asks for a grain proof from the spec. `/api-docs` types **both** of these feeds as a bare `{\"type\":\"object\"}` — 14 of 16 GET feeds are untyped, and where the spec does type a feed it is wrong (both history feeds declare raw arrays but live-return a Spring `Page` envelope). Grain and disposition come from **live sampling only**, and unknown-field refusal must be keyed to a sampled shape, never to `/api-docs`.\n\nPaging is not uniform across this API: `/inventory` is enveloped, `/prodtracking` is a bare array. Do not assume one envelope shape.\n\nNo image-content table under any circumstances; image bytes are rejected by owner decision and PopDAM remains the image source.\n\n## Gate (plan §9 Step 6)\n\nEach endpoint has a documented grain proof from live sampling, a complete field disposition, an idempotent replay test, and no unexplained duplicate collapse. Test: `coldlion_remainder_landing_contracts.sql`.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 4\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table coldlion.inventory\n  - table coldlion.prod_tracking\nreads:\n```\n\nTracker: #2081. Plan: `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md` §9 Step 6.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-05T12:11:18Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T02:48:58Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2175,"title":"ColdLion landing unit 5a: inventory and production-tracking landing tables","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:23:37Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2175"},
{"body":"Unit 4 of six, split out of tracker #2081 by §9 Step 1 of `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md`. Structure only; no row loads under this issue.\r\n\r\n## What this unit builds\r\n\r\nStep 5 of the plan — redesign production history using the same parent-version pattern as sales history.\r\n\r\n- `prod_history_line` — parent purchase line/version, storing the **returned** `stageCode` and asserting it equals the **requested** stage. A returned/requested mismatch aborts.\r\n- `prod_history_component` — mandatory parent FK plus component-level prepack facts.\r\n- `prod_history_last_lookup` — mandatory parent FK; `lastProdCost` must never be exposed as current-order cost.\r\n- `salesOrderNo = 0` means no link.\r\n- Retention is a separate restartable maintenance operation: partition by full source identity, order newest by a deterministic observation/version timestamp plus a stable tie-breaker, retain the newest three, and **refuse** to prune when ordering or identity is ambiguous. Initial backfill writes one baseline version and is never mistaken for reconstructed change history.\r\n\r\nThis is where objection **U13** is answered: every seven-day window is fetched separately for `ISS`, `INTRAN` and `REC`, and each request is paged to completion through the repaired ledger from unit 3. A no-stage request is incomplete.\r\n\r\nThe three tables already exist on `origin/main` (`20260825023430`) and are empty; this is a forward migration, never an edit to the applied one.\r\n\r\n## Why this is now ready (revised 2026-09-02)\r\n\r\nFiled blocked; **unblocked by the live field census** on #2081 (comment 5519573718).\r\n\r\n- **U13 CONFIRMED with a positive control.** Over one seven-day window on `companyCode=EDGEHOME`: a stage-less `/prodHistory` call returned **3 rows, all `ISS`**, while an independent `stageCode=INTRAN` call returned **3 INTRAN rows for that same window** and `REC` returned 0. The no-stage call is not merely incomplete — it looks like a complete answer. The three-stage loop is mandatory.\r\n- **The returned-vs-requested stage assertion is enforceable**: returned `stageCode` equalled requested in every probe. The spec enum is exactly `[\"ISS\",\"INTRAN\",\"REC\"]` — no fourth stage.\r\n- **`ProdHistory` property count re-derived from the live spec: 105.** Per plan §9 Step 5, do not copy that number into the migration — re-derive it again at authoring time.\r\n- A `fromDate`/`toDate` span wider than seven days returns **HTTP 400**. The fixed grid is mandatory.\r\n\r\n`depends_on: 2173` is a **hard prerequisite, not a note**: `coldlion.window_ledger` currently has no `stage_code`, no division scope and no page number, so it cannot express a stage-scoped multi-page window at all. #2173 builds that identity and the page ledger.\r\n\r\nOwner field disposition for the newer `prodHistory` properties still has to be recorded before columns are written; unlike `/salespersons` this feed carries no personal data, so it is authorable alongside the census rather than behind an owner ruling.\r\n\r\n## Gate (plan §9 Step 5)\r\n\r\nMulti-line orders remain distinct; all three stage-specific windows and every page land; a returned-stage mismatch aborts; component quantity assertions pass; cost tests prove `extCost` and `lastProdCost` cannot be confused; a four-version fixture prunes only the oldest and a one-version backfill fixture is untouched. Tests: `coldlion_prod_history_contracts.sql`, `coldlion-history-retention.test.mjs`.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 3\r\ndepends_on: 2173\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table coldlion.prod_history_line\r\n  - table coldlion.prod_history_component\r\n  - table coldlion.prod_history_last_lookup\r\nreads:\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\nTracker: #2081 (holds the U1-U20 reviewer objection ledger). {"body":"Unit 3 of six, split out of tracker #2081 by §9 Step 1 of `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md`. Structure only; no row loads under this issue.\r\n\r\n## What this unit builds\r\n\r\nStep 4 of the plan — repair history completion evidence, then redesign sales history.\r\n\r\n**1. Completion evidence (this is the structural answer to objection U6).**\r\n- Extend `coldlion.window_ledger` identity with `stage_code` and a nullable division scope.\r\n- Add `coldlion.history_page_ledger`, keyed by endpoint, company, division scope, stage scope, window and page number. It stores page row count, reported totals, `last`, run, state and error.\r\n- Every nullable identity constraint uses PostgreSQL `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`, so replaying an unscoped null stage/division cannot duplicate a page or a window.\r\n- A window may become loaded only when pages are contiguous from zero through the witnessed last page, every page succeeded, and summed page counts equal the window/API totals. One `sync_run` row never proves a multi-page window complete.\r\n\r\n**2. Sales history tables**, replacing the obsolete empty ones by forward migration:\r\n- `order_history_line` — `id uuid` primary key, company, order number, line number, master item number, line-grain facts, line hash, run/fetch provenance; unique on order + line number + master item + line hash. Order + line alone is **not** business identity.\r\n- `order_history_component` — parent `line_id` FK, master item, component item, per-design quantities/prices, component taxonomy/descriptions, component hash; unique on parent + component identity + hash.\r\n- `order_history_invoice_ref` — parent/component ownership as proven by the payload, ordinal, invoice-number token as text, aligned date token only where alignment is provable.\r\n- `order_history_pick_ticket_ref` — parent/component ownership as proven by the payload, ordinal, pick-ticket token as text.\r\n\r\nNeither sales-history table may carry a foreign key to `coldlion.item_header`: discontinued historical items may be absent from the current item master. Retention follows the deterministic newest-three contract; initial backfill retains its single baseline version.\r\n\r\n## Why this is ready\r\n\r\nThe three facts that previously held Step 4 unsplit are all settled in the merged plan:\r\n\r\n- **Natural key** — `(salesOrderNo, salesOrderLineNo, itemNo, subItemNo)`, verified in `docs/business-rules-erp-data.md` §10 (plan §6.2). The old `(salesOrderNo, itemNo, labelCode)` design is superseded.\r\n- **Flat vs split** — settled in plan §8: keep split grains, add a surrogate parent-version UUID and a mandatory child FK.\r\n- **D2 prepack scope** — narrowed by D14 (2026-09-01): D2 applies to non-prepack rows only; `merchGroup01`-`06` are KEPT on prepack component rows because they vary per component.\r\n\r\nOwner field dispositions for `orderHistory` (59 rows) are already in `docs/coldlion-field-decisions-20260819.csv`.\r\n\r\n**Naming note for the author:** the write list claims the existing table names. Plan §9 Step 4 permits a clean `_v2` name instead of preserving the old names. If the author chooses `_v2` names, amend this issue's `writes:` list before dispatch — a claim must name the exact object it creates.\r\n\r\n## Census confirmations (2026-09-02, #2081 comment 5519573718)\r\n\r\n- **U6 CONFIRMED empirically.** `GET /orderHistory?...&size=2000&page=0` returned `size=200` in the envelope, with no error. The requested page size is silently replaced. The page ledger in this unit is the fix and stands exactly as written.\r\n- **The envelope is a Spring `Page`**, not the raw array `/api-docs` declares: `content, first, last, number, numberOfElements, size, sort, totalElements, totalPages`. Treat the spec as stale documentation; key unknown-field refusal to a sampled shape.\r\n- **`coldlion.window_ledger` today has `endpoint, company_code, window_from, window_to, state, attempt_count, last_run_id, row_count` and no `stage_code`, no division scope and no page number.** It cannot express a stage-scoped or multi-page window. That is why this unit is a hard prerequisite for production history (#2174), not a sibling task.\r\n- **`coldlion.order_history_line` has no `sales_order_line_no` column**, as the plan states.\r\n- A `fromDate`/`toDate` span wider than seven days returns **HTTP 400**, not a truncated result. The fixed seven-day grid is mandatory, not an optimisation.\r\n- `OrderHistory` carries `merchGroup01`-`merchGroup06` only. The 14-slot rule in plan §8 is **item-side only** and must not be applied to sales history; the existing `order_history_component` already models six.\r\n\r\n## Gate (plan §9 Step 4)\r\n\r\nZero four-part component-key collisions on the `docs/business-rules-erp-data.md` §10 corpus procedure; every component has exactly one parent version; repeated line fields pass full-group constancy checks; per-design quantities reconcile; document-list tokens survive round-trip; a forced 201st row proves page 1 is recorded and the window cannot complete with page 0 alone. Tests: `coldlion_order_history_contracts.sql`, `coldlion_history_page_ledger_contracts.sql`.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 3\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table coldlion.window_ledger\r\n  - table coldlion.history_page_ledger\r\n  - table coldlion.order_history_line\r\n  - table coldlion.order_history_component\r\n  - table coldlion.order_history_invoice_ref\r\n  - table coldlion.order_history_pick_ticket_ref\r\n  - column coldlion.history_page_ledger.is_last_page\r\n  - column coldlion.history_page_ledger.page_row_count\r\n  - column coldlion.history_page_ledger.requested_page_size\r\n  - column coldlion.history_page_ledger.returned_page_size\r\n  - column coldlion.order_history_component.document_list_cardinality_mismatch\r\n  - column coldlion.order_history_component.invoice_no_string\r\n  - column coldlion.order_history_component.order_qty\r\n  - column coldlion.order_history_line.brand_assurance_no\r\n  - column coldlion.order_history_line.line_qty\r\n  - column coldlion.order_history_line.sales_order_line_no\r\n  - column coldlion.window_ledger.division_code\r\n  - column coldlion.window_ledger.last_page_number\r\n  - column coldlion.window_ledger.reported_total_elements\r\n  - column coldlion.window_ledger.stage_code\r\n  - function coldlion.history_page_ledger_immutable_when_loaded\r\n  - function coldlion.history_page_ledger_scope_guard\r\n  - function coldlion.window_ledger_completion_guard\n  - function coldlion.window_ledger_scope_immutable_with_pages\r\n  - index coldlion.coldlion_history_page_ledger_run_idx\n  - index coldlion.coldlion_order_history_line_run_idx\n  - index coldlion.coldlion_order_history_component_run_idx\n  - index coldlion.coldlion_order_history_invoice_ref_run_idx\n  - index coldlion.coldlion_order_history_pick_ticket_ref_run_idx\r\n  - index coldlion.coldlion_history_page_ledger_state_idx\r\n  - index coldlion.coldlion_history_page_ledger_window_idx\r\n  - index coldlion.coldlion_order_history_component_line_idx\r\n  - index coldlion.coldlion_order_history_invoice_ref_component_idx\r\n  - index coldlion.coldlion_order_history_invoice_ref_line_idx\r\n  - index coldlion.coldlion_order_history_pick_ticket_ref_component_idx\r\n  - {"body":"Unit 2 of six, split out of tracker #2081 by §9 Step 1 of `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md`. Structure only; no row loads under this issue.\r\n\r\n## What this unit builds\r\n\r\nStep 3 of the plan — correct the item landing structures by **forward migration** against the current live `ItemHeader` / `ItemDetail` definitions and owner decisions D14-D17.\r\n\r\n- One `coldlion.item_header` row per company + division + item number. Two identical item numbers in different divisions must survive as separate rows.\r\n- One `coldlion.item_detail` row per stable vendor `itemPkey` under its parent item, retaining the parent FK — unless live evidence proves `itemPkey` is not stable.\r\n- `coldlion.item_merch_group` stores merchandise groups **as rows** (all 14 slots), and a cleared slot is reconciled transactionally, i.e. it disappears.\r\n- No item-level taxonomy copied onto component designs as a fallback. Descriptions are stored inline only where approved; they are evidence, never keys.\r\n- Never edit the applied migration `20260825023430`; this is a new forward migration.\r\n\r\n## Why this is ready\r\n\r\n- The three tables already exist on `origin/main` (`20260825023430`), so the write surface is exact and complete.\r\n- Owner field dispositions for `items` (132 rows) and `itemDetails` (118 rows) are already in `docs/coldlion-field-decisions-20260819.csv`.\r\n- D14-D17 are merged (PR #2068).\r\n- #2081 records that steps 2 and 3 are \"unaffected by every open objection\". U6 (silent 200-row page cap) and U13 (three-stage ISS/INTRAN/REC loop) are history-endpoint defects and land in units 3 and 4, not here.\r\n\r\nAny live field that appears in the current `/api-docs` and carries no disposition must make the loader **fail loudly** rather than be silently dropped (D5 makes an omission permanent).\r\n\r\n## Census confirmations (2026-09-02, #2081 comment 5519573718)\r\n\r\n`ItemHeader` (146 properties) and `ItemDetail` (133) are two of only ten definitions `/api-docs` actually types, so unlike the master and remainder feeds a spec comparison is possible here — but the spec is proven stale elsewhere (both history feeds declare raw arrays and live-return a Spring `Page` envelope). Re-sample live before authoring and key unknown-field refusal to the **sampled** shape, not to `/api-docs`.\r\n\r\n`ItemHeader`, `ItemDetail` and `ProdHistory` carry merchandise-group slots `01`-`14`; the plan §8 14-slot rule is item-side and production-side only. `OrderHistory` carries `01`-`06` and must not be widened to 14.\r\n\r\n## Gate (plan §9 Step 3)\r\n\r\nTwo identical item numbers in different divisions survive; a cleared slot disappears; every approved live field maps once; ignored fields map nowhere; an unknown field causes refusal. Test file: `coldlion_item_landing_contracts.sql`.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 3\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table coldlion.item_header\r\n  - table coldlion.item_detail\r\n  - table coldlion.item_merch_group\r\nreads:\r\n```\r\n\r\nTracker: #2081 (holds the U1-U20 reviewer objection ledger). {"body":"Unit 1 of the ColdLion landing split, from §9 Step 1 of `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md`. Structure only; no row loads.\n\n**Revised 2026-09-02** after the live `/api-docs` field census on #2081 (comment 5519573718). Two changes: this unit is now **ready** and narrowed to `coldlion.division` alone; the four master field projections that need an owner ruling were carved out into their own issue.\n\n## What this unit builds\n\nAdd `coldlion.division` for the `/divisions` feed, keyed on the vendor's stable company + division identity (plan §8: do not hardcode a durable division dictionary in loaders). Forward migration under `supabase/migrations/`; extend `coldlion_master_landing_contracts.sql`.\n\nLive shape measured 2026-09-02: 26 fields — `accDivCode, active, address1, address2, city, companyCode, countryCode, createdTime, createdUser, currencyCode, divisionCode, divisionDesc, dunsNo, ediDivisionCode, faxNo, generalLedgerCode, itemNoCode, manuFacturerCode, modTime, modUser, phoneNo, state, upcCurrent, upcEnd, upcStart, zipCode`. Ten divisions across three company codes. Re-sample immediately before authoring; do not treat this list as a contract.\n\n## Correction to plan Step 2 as written\n\nPlan §9 Step 2 says to compare live `/divisions` **definitions** with production columns. **That is not executable.** The census found `/api-docs` types 14 of its 16 GET feeds — including `/divisions` and every master feed — as a bare `{\"type\":\"object\"}`. There is no schema to compare against. Field disposition must come from **live sampling**, and the loader's unknown-field refusal must be keyed to a **sampled shape**, never to `/api-docs`. Where the spec does type a feed it is wrong: both history feeds declare raw arrays but live-return a Spring `Page` envelope.\n\nTwo projection traps from the same census: `/merchGroupDetails` returns a bare array with no page envelope, unlike every other master feed, so paging is not uniform; and `/salespersons` returns `uDF01`/`uDF02` where every other feed uses `udf01`.\n\n## Explicitly out of scope — do not recreate\n\n- `coldlion.merch_group_header` (8 live fields, 8 stored) and `coldlion.merch_group_detail` (13 live, 13 stored) are **field-complete**. They appear in no write list.\n- `coldlion.customer`, `coldlion.vendor`, `coldlion.season`, `coldlion.salesperson` moved to the owner-decision issue below; their fields must not be added here.\n\n## Gate (plan §9 Step 2)\n\nEvery sampled `/divisions` property has a disposition; natural-key replay is idempotent; the same code in different divisions stays distinct; RLS enabled with no application-facing policy.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 3\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table coldlion.division\nreads:\n```\n\nTracker: #2081. {"body":"Governed review needs two reviewers per pull request head. The pool is nominally five. Two cannot be used:\n\n- `codex-gpt-5.6-sol` — structurally unusable. Fixed subcommands, no `--prompt-file`, so it can never be told the head SHA that its verdict line must carry. Tracked at #2117 and popcre/ai-devops#217. A codex draw should be treated as an immediate `wrapper_terminal_failure` replacement rather than a long wasted run.\n- `kimi-k3` — out on a genuine 7-day provider quota (`403 You've reached your weekly (7-day) usage limit`), expected back around 2026-09-08. `ai-kimi doctor` still reports `auth OK` because doctor does not test quota, so a passing doctor is not evidence the reviewer can run.\n\nUsable pool is therefore `glm-5.3`, `grok-4.6`, `muse-spark-1.2-contributor`. **Review one pull request at a time** — two concurrent PRs exhaust it, and a reviewer that cannot be replaced jams the head (see #2123 / PR #2145).\n\nTwo operational rules that came out of this and are not written down anywhere in the repo:\n\n1. **Draw every reviewer slot BEFORE running any review.** `hasVerdictForHead` is head-wide, not slot-wide, so the first recorded verdict permanently blocks drawing *or* replacing the second slot at that head.\n2. **`ai-kimi` inlines the whole `--prompt-file` as an argv element.** A 36 KB prompt gives exit 126 `Argument list too long`, surfaced by the runner as the generic \"review wrapper did not produce a recordable terminal verdict (exit 1)\". Keep review prompts under ~8 KB and tell the reviewer to take the diff from the checkout it is already in. Always read the newest job's `stream.jsonl.err` before recording any reviewer as failed — the runner's refusal string never names the cause.\n\nDetail: `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-03T0235Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-2121-closeout.md` sections 7 and 9.\n\n```db-work-scope\nkind: repo-maintenance\nobjects: scripts/run-governed-review.mjs\nstatus: blocked\nblocking: true\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:56:38Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T02:22:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2162,"title":"HANDOVER: governed reviewer pool is down to three usable reviewers","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:47:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2162"},
{"body":"Found by the #2147 author while clearing a CI refusal on PR #2158. Detail: `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-03T0235Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-2121-closeout.md` section 8.  `scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs` deliberately exempts temporary tables from object extraction — session-local scratch is not a shared object, and emitting it would flag unrelated migrations against each other. The exemption is written into the **create table** pattern only. The **drop table** pattern matches any name, temp or not.  So an author who writes `create temporary table probe …` (exempt) and then tidies up with `drop table probe` (not exempt) gets `REFUSED: migration writes undeclared objects: table probe`. The refusal names the claim, not the drop, so the obvious-but-wrong fix is to widen the claim to cover a scratch name.  Fix: add `temp|temporary` to the drop-table pattern's optional prefixes so the exemption is symmetric.  ```db-work-scope work_type: repo-maintenance objects: scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs status: ready route: repo-maintenance\npriority: 0\ndepends_on: ```   \r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T23:18:10Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T02:22:58Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"`plm.source_resolution`'s `source_system` allowlist accepts Warner rows through a `LIKE 'warner:%'` pattern. `%` matches **zero** characters, so the bare string `'warner:'` — a Warner row with an **empty namespace** — is accepted today.\n\nFound on `main` while authoring the WildBrain vocabulary addition (#2147, PR #2158). The author's first draft listed `'warner:'` among the values that should be refused; the behavioural verification block correctly failed, which is how the gap surfaced. It was then moved to the accepted list, because narrowing an existing value inside that claim would have been exactly the silent narrowing the block exists to forbid. So this is pre-existing on `main`, not introduced by #2158.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThe `warner:` prefix exists because `plm.wb_property` keys identity on `(source_namespace, source_id)` and `20260814233423` writes `'warner:' || p.source_namespace` — the namespace is part of durable identity. A row with an empty namespace therefore carries a resolution decision that names no source namespace at all, while still passing every constraint. It is unresolvable back to a capture, and it sorts and groups alongside genuine Warner values.\n\nNo such rows are known to exist. This is a constraint that does not enforce what it was written to enforce, ahead of the promotion load.\n\n## Scope\n\nTighten the pattern so at least one namespace character is required — `warner:_%` is the obvious form, but derive the right shape from `20260814233423` and from the actual `plm.wb_property.source_namespace` values rather than assuming, and check whether any other value in the allowlist has the same zero-length hole.\n\nBefore tightening, prove no existing row would be invalidated; if any exists, that is a data finding to report, not something to silently exclude.\n\nVerification must be behavioural — real inserts in rolled-back subtransactions asserting SQLSTATE 23514 — and must prove all three: a genuine `warner:<namespace>` value is still accepted, the bare `warner:` value is now refused, and every other previously-accepted value is still accepted. Mutation-test it.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 300\ndepends_on: 2147\nwrites:\n  - table plm.source_resolution\nreads:\n  - table plm.wb_property\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-05T11:38:39Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T02:10:41Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2159,"title":"plm.source_resolution accepts a Warner value with an empty namespace ('warner:'), because % matches zero characters","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:23:56Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2159"},
{"body":"`reviewerCapacityReport` reports `verdictPresent: false` for a lease whose verdict is **unreadable**, because the probe is wrapped in a bare `catch` that discards the error:  `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2528`  ```js let verdictPresent=false try{verdictPresent=hasVerdictForHead(record.lease.issue,record.lease.pr,record.lease.headSha,io)}catch{verdictPresent=false} ```  \"I could not read it\" and \"there is no verdict\" are collapsed into the same value, with empty stderr. That is the **fail-OPEN** direction: a recorded verdict is the thing that forbids drawing or replacing a second reviewer slot at a head, so a false negative here understates how locked a head is and invites an operator to attempt an action the mutex will then refuse — or, worse, to reason about reclaiming a lease from a report that silently could not see the evidence.  ## Observed  Found while fixing #2152. On `origin/main` (pager broken, so every `hasVerdictForHead` call threw) `--reviewer-capacity` printed `verdictPresent: false` for **every** held lease with no error output at all. On the #2152 branch the same command reports `true` for three of them.  No reclaim decision is known to have flipped as a result, and #2152 removes today's cause of the throw. This issue is about the swallow itself, which is independent of what made the read fail.  Note that `classification` does not currently consume `verdictPresent`, so the automatic classifier was not misled — the hazard is to the reader of the report, which is how reviewer-slot decisions are actually taken in this repo.  ## Scope  Distinguish the three states in the report rather than two. A lease whose verdict could not be read should say so — a third value (e.g. `unknown`) or an accompanying error field — and the command should surface the underlying error text rather than discarding it. Decide deliberately whether an unreadable verdict should also push `classification` to `unknown`; state the reasoning either way.  Do **not** fix this by making the whole command throw on the first unreadable lease: one bad lease should not blind the operator to the other four. And do not remove the guard — the command has to keep working when a single lease is unreadable.  Verification: prove with a fake IO that a throwing `hasVerdictForHead` produces the unreadable state and not `false`, that a genuinely absent verdict still produces `false`, and that the error text reaches the output. Prove the old code fails that test.  ```db-work-scope\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nobjects: scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs\nstatus: ready\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\n```   \r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T13:31:06Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T01:56:58Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2157,"title":"reviewer-capacity reports an UNREADABLE verdict as 'no verdict' — a bare catch fails open","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:23:58Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2157"},

{"body":"## Impact — the governed review system is DOWN\n\nEvery `--assign-reviewer` and `--replace-failed-reviewer` call now refuses with:\n\n```\nREFUSED: active reviewer leases are unreadable; reviewer assignment refused before mutex acquisition\n```\n\nThe underlying error is:\n\n```\nrefs/db-review-verdict exceeded 6 pages of 100 refs; refusing a possibly truncated reviewer audit\n```\n\nNo reviewer can be drawn for any PR. PR #2149 (issue #2136) and PR #2150 (issue #2138) are both blocked at fresh heads with no way to start a review.\n\n## Root cause — NOT ref growth\n\n`listReviewRefsPaged` (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`) walks explicit pages:\n\n```js\nconst chunk=ghJson(['api',`repos/${REPO}/git/matching-refs/${short}?per_page=100&page=${page}`])\n...\nif(chunk.length<100)return rows\n```\n\n**GitHub's `git/matching-refs` endpoint ignores the `page` query parameter.** It honours `per_page` and Link-header pagination only. Measured today against this repository:\n\n```\npage 1: 100\npage 2: 100\npage 3: 100\npage 4: 100\npage 5: 100\npage 6: 100\npage 7: 100\n```\n\n…while the namespace holds exactly **100 refs in total** (53 `db-review-verdicts` + 47 `db-review-verdict-replacements`, both matched by the shared string prefix `db-review-verdict`). Page 3 was sampled and returns the same 100 rows as page 1.\n\n`gh api ... --paginate` on the same prefix correctly returns 100 rows, and returns 726 for `db-review-assignments`.\n\nSo the loop never sees a short page, never terminates early, and always hits `REVIEW_REF_PAGE_LIMIT` and refuses.\n\n## Why it appeared only now\n\nThe `chunk.length<100` early return masked the fault while a namespace held **fewer than 100** refs: page 1 came back short and the loop exited with a correct answer. The verdict namespace crossed 100 refs today, and the endpoint's repeated page 1 turned an always-wrong pager into a hard outage.\n\nThe same latent fault sits under every other namespace read this way. `db-review-assignments` (726), `db-review-replacements` (229) and `db-review-failures` (235) are all past 100, so any audit path that lists them is affected identically — and if the page ceiling were merely raised, those paths would silently accumulate **duplicated** rows rather than refuse.\n\n## Do NOT fix this by raising REVIEW_REF_PAGE_LIMIT\n\nThe constant's own comment is explicit that the page count is not the real ceiling — the 25-request wire budget is, and the two namespaces share it. Raising the constant converts a loud refusal into `reviewer operation request budget exhausted`, and for namespaces over 100 refs it would return a list with repeated entries. The pager is wrong, not too small.\n\n## Required fix\n\nReplace the manual `page=N` walk with Link-header pagination (the mechanism `ghPaginated` already uses via `--paginate`), while preserving the two properties `listReviewRefsPaged` exists to guarantee:\n\n1. **Never return a partial or duplicated list** — a short list reads as \"no verdict\", which is the fail-OPEN direction for release and replacement.\n2. **Refuse loudly** past a bounded ceiling, and keep every request countable by the reviewer wire budget.\n\nA row-count ceiling with a loud refusal is the natural replacement for the page ceiling. Note that inside a wire budget `ghPaginated` deliberately refuses at 100 rows and does a single unpaginated request, so it cannot be used as-is here — the budget accounting for a Link-header walk needs to be settled deliberately, not by reusing that helper unchanged.\n\nAlso verify whether the assignment/replacement/failure audit paths ever received duplicated rows from this pager before the refusal threshold, and whether any decision was taken on such a list.\n\n## Verification requirement\n\nThe fix must be proved against a namespace that genuinely exceeds one page. `db-review-verdict` (100 refs) and `db-review-assignments` (726 refs) are live examples. A test that only exercises a sub-100 namespace cannot distinguish the broken pager from a correct one — that is exactly why this shipped.\n\n```db-work-scope\nkind: repo-maintenance\nobjects: scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs\nstatus: ready\nblocking: true\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T08:50:33Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T01:44:18Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2152,"title":"Reviewer assignment is fully blocked: git/matching-refs ignores page=N, so listReviewRefsPaged loops on page 1 and refuses","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:47:11Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2152"},
{"body":"#2138 reported two regressions together: `filter_effective_assets` timing out on every call, and the tag facet count falling from 7-of-8 passing to 0-of-8. The row-fetch half is fixed in PR #2150 (issue #2138). **The facet half may not be, and it is on a different object.**\n\nThe facet counts come from `get_effective_filter_counts_unchecked_1703`, which duplicates the same predicates inline and never calls `filter_effective_assets`. It was outside #2138's object claim and was not touched.\n\n## What the lane found\n\nOn a fixture carrying the production RLS policies, indexes and entitlement functions at production-shaped volume (144,944 assets / 134,704 live), the count helper was **fast and correct** — unfiltered 136 ms, tag-filtered 62 / 30 ms. The production failure did not reproduce there, so its cause is not established.\n\nThe row-fetch defect was a bound-parameter generic plan that could not fold the identity predicates and rescanned the whole live-asset identity set once per output row. Whether the count helper suffers the same thing is **unknown, not ruled out** — it shares the predicate shapes but not the self-join that caused the row defect.\n\n## Scope\n\n1. Re-measure the tag facet count against production, read-only, with a real `authenticated` JWT, AFTER PR #2150 merges and reaches production. If the DAM derives its facets from the row RPC, #2150 may already have fixed this and there is nothing to do — check that first and close this if so.\n2. If it is still failing, diagnose the count helper on its own terms. Do not assume the row-fetch cause transfers; a refutation of one story does not validate the next. Start the replacement cause at zero evidence and prove it with a plan.\n3. Any fix is a structural migration on `get_effective_filter_counts_unchecked_1703` and needs its own object claim.\n\nRaised out of #2138 by the migration-author lane that fixed the row half.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 600\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function public.get_effective_filter_counts_unchecked_1703\nreads:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-11T12:41:41Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T00:50:39Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2151,"title":"The tag facet half of #2138 is unfixed and lives on a different function","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:03Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2151"},
{"body":"`docs/core-character-backfill-source-decision-20260902.md` §3 states that the Tier-1 tables `plm.opa_character`, `plm.nbcu_character` and `plm.pmt_character` all refuse a resolution that carries no resolver and no timestamp.\n\nReading the creating migrations, **only `plm.opa_character` does** (`20260814040000`). `plm.pmt_character` and `plm.nbcu_character` carry only a target-coherence check — a resolved row on either can be written with no resolver and no `resolved_at`.\n\nIndependently confirmed by two reviewers during PR #2145 (issue #2123), which copied the stronger OPA shape onto the Tier-2 tables and said so in its header.\n\n## Scope\n\nDocumentation only: correct §3 to say which table enforces what, and note that the OPA shape is the one being propagated. Do not change any constraint here.\n\nA separate question this raises, and deliberately does NOT decide: whether `pmt_character` and `nbcu_character` should be tightened to the OPA shape. Both are empty of resolutions, so it would be cheap now and expensive later — but that is a structural change on a different claim and needs its own issue if the answer is yes.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 200\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:37:00Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T00:42:06Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2148,"title":"Decision document §3 overstates what the Tier-1 character tables enforce","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2148"},
{"body":"`plm.source_resolution` — the durable, capture-independent home for character resolution decisions, rebuilt by `20260902024541` — constrains `source_system` to an explicit allowlist (`paramount`, `nbcu`, `disney_opa`, … `twentieth_century_dcpvault`, plus `warner:%`). **WildBrain is not in that vocabulary.**\n\n## Why it blocks a WildBrain promotion\n\n`plm.wildbrain_character` is per-capture: its primary key is `(capture_id, character_source_id)` (`20260819014639:405`). A resolution recorded on one capture's row therefore does not carry forward to the next capture's rows. The cross-capture record has to live in `plm.source_resolution`, and today that table would refuse the insert.\n\nWarner is already anticipated by the `warner:%` pattern, so #2123's other Tier-2 table is unaffected.\n\n## Scope\n\nAdd the WildBrain `source_system` value to the allowlist CHECK on `plm.source_resolution`, matching the naming shape the existing values use — derive that shape from `20260902024541` rather than assuming it, and check whether WildBrain needs a namespaced form (as Warner does) or a plain one. Verification block must fail unless the value is accepted and an off-vocabulary value is still refused. No rows loaded.\n\nRaised by `glm-5.3` while approving PR #2145 (issue #2123). Correctly kept out of that migration — different object, different claim.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 350\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table plm.source_resolution\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T08:50:36Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T00:42:05Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2147,"title":"plm.source_resolution's source vocabulary has no WildBrain value, so a WildBrain character promotion cannot be recorded","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:07Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2147"},
{"body":"`plm.nbcu_character`, `plm.opa_character` and `plm.pmt_character` each keep a `core_character_id` column, but none of them has a foreign key to `core.character` any more.\n\n`20260823133150_drop_empty_universe_a_character_tables.sql:122-126` dropped `nbcu_character_core_character_id_fkey`, `opa_character_core_character_id_fkey` and `pmt_character_core_character_id_fkey` because it was about to `drop table core.character restrict`. That was correct at the time.\n\n`20260829004145_separate_property_and_character.sql` recreated `core.character` and restored the referential contract for the neighbours it touched — `core.property_character_associations` and `plm.item_character_associations` both carry `references core.character(id) on update cascade on delete restrict`. The three `plm.*_character` Tier-1 tables were not included.\n\nVerified on `origin/main` at `bd00aaa7`: those three constraint names appear in exactly one file in the whole migration history — the one that dropped them.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThese are the Tier-1 tables named as the promotion source in `docs/core-character-backfill-source-decision-20260902.md` §3. When a character promotion actually runs, a `core_character_id` written into any of them will not be checked against `core.character` at all, and a `core.character` row can be deleted out from under a resolved source row without the `on delete restrict` refusing it. The column reads as a governed resolution pointer and currently is not one.\n\nThe tables are empty of resolutions today (the retirement migration proved that before dropping the constraints), so this is a correctness gap ahead of the load, not live corruption.\n\n## Scope\n\nRestore the three foreign keys with the same shape the surviving tables carry: `foreign key (core_character_id) references core.character(id) on update cascade on delete restrict`, keeping the original constraint names. Verify against the creating migrations rather than assuming the shape; add a verification block that fails unless all three exist afterwards. No rows are loaded.\n\nFound during the governed review preparation for #2123, which adds the same contract to the Tier-2 tables and correctly declared its FK on its own two tables only.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 450\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table plm.nbcu_character\n  - table plm.opa_character\n  - table plm.pmt_character\nreads:\n  - table core.character\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T08:50:38Z","createdAt":"2026-09-03T00:36:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2146,"title":"Tier-1 character tables lost their core.character foreign key in #1684 and never got it back","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:09Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2146"},

{"body":"Two non-blocking residuals that `glm-5.3` named while approving #2139. Both are false negatives, so the guard stays safe to keep on while they are open.\n\n1. **`reindex` is not a read context.** `reindex table plm.big` and `reindex (verbose) index plm.big_idx` rebuild production-size indexes inside the apply transaction — the same cost class as the `vacuum` and `cluster` entries added in #2139 — and nothing matches them. Note the optional `TABLE` / `INDEX` keyword, the same shape that hid `truncate table` in #2130.\n2. **A quoted language name is not recognised as a `DO` block.** `DO_LEAD` accepts `do language plpgsql $verify$` but its identifier class is `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, so `do language \"plpgsql\" $verify$` is not read as a verification block at all and the body is never inspected.\n\nWhoever takes this: the pattern from #2130 and #2139 is that each fix needs a test *proven* to fail without it — revert the one line in a scratch copy and watch the fixture go from refused to passing — plus a fixture-mode run over every existing migration to show the widened rule adds no false positive.\n\nRaised from the review of #2139 (merged as `d4071e715f23bbf05f55cef4ad395afd26a62e33`).\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 350\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-04T00:20:51Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T23:29:36Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2141,"title":"Verify-cost guard: two residuals named by the #2139 review","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:16Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2141"},
{"body":"Split out of #2118, which is closed because its stated problem no longer exists. This is the one real finding that survived it.\r\n\r\n## The gap\r\n\r\nA batch rehearsed on preview with `merged_preview_source_pr_map` files its binding under **only the map's last PR** — `shared-supabase-migrations.yml:389` (`MAP_LAST_PR`).\r\n\r\n`prove_bound_mainline_post_merge_original` in `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py:1056-1067` compares the binding against **each version's own authoring PR**.\r\n\r\nThose two disagree for every version in such a batch except the last one. So a multi-PR rehearsed batch can never be recovered per version on the historical lane: the gate refuses each version whose authoring PR is not the map's last, and it is right to, because the binding genuinely does not name it.\r\n\r\n## Why it did not bite this time\r\n\r\nThe nine versions #2118 was about reached production by another route and are applied ([run 33691168861](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/actions/runs/33691168861) reports NO ACTIONABLE DRIFT). Nothing is blocked today. This is a latent trap for the next multi-PR batch that needs per-version recovery.\r\n\r\n## What the fix must NOT be\r\n\r\nDo not widen the comparison in `prove_bound_mainline_post_merge_original`, and do not relax the producer pin. The precedented safe shape is a fully pinned governed exception in the manner of `GOVERNED_ORIGINAL_RECONCILIATION` (`production_business_risk_gate.py:886-935`) — naming the run id, the head, the artifact id and the artifact digest — so that the exception cannot be reused for anything else.\r\n\r\nThe alternative, and probably better, fix is at the producing end: have the rehearsal file a binding under **every** PR in the map rather than only the last, so no exception is needed at all. That should be evaluated first.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\r\nroute: repo-maintenance\r\npriority: 300\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\nreads:\r\n```\r\n\r\nNote for the lane: this touches `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml` and `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py`, not database objects, so the writes/reads lists are empty by design.\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-04T05:42:08Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T23:01:52Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2140,"title":"Multi-PR rehearsed batches file their binding under only the last PR, so per-version historical recovery can never pass","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:17Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2140"},
{"body":"## Summary\n\n#2054's own target is fixed — the licensor/property identity count is now fast and reliable. But `filter_effective_assets` has regressed **worse than before #1945**: it now times out for *every* call, including five rows with no filter and no count. The tag facet count has gone from 7-of-8 passing to 0-of-8.\n\nThis did not come from #2054's migration. `20260902042548` only touches the facet-count path. The row regression traces to `20260901130428` / `20260901142825`, which redefined `filter_effective_assets`.\n\nRead-only measurement, production, real `authenticated` JWT (PopDAM viewer test account, 1Password `vibe_coding`), 2026-09-02. Target proof: `https://qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai.supabase.co`; ledger shows `20260902042548`.\n\n## Fixed — the identity count, and it is a big win\n\n`get_filter_counts {\"licensorId\":\"154bf54b-…\"}`, 8 consecutive calls: **8 passed, 0 failed**, 0.11–0.43 s. Previously 4 of 8 failed at up to 8.1 s. The predicate rewrite worked exactly as hoped.\n\n## Regressed — 1. row fetching now always times out\n\n`POST /rest/v1/rpc/filter_effective_assets?select=id`, `{\"p_filters\":{}}`, **no count header**, 3 calls each:\n\n| range | after #1945 | now |\n|---|---|---|\n| `0-4` | — | **0 passed, 3 failed** — 8.10 / 8.13 / 8.09 s |\n| `0-24` | 200 @ 0.94 s | **0 passed, 3 failed** — 8.11 / 8.09 / 8.15 s |\n| `0-199` | 200 @ 0.99 s | **0 passed, 3 failed** — 8.12 / 8.10 / 8.09 s |\n\nFive rows, one column, no filter, no count — still 8 s. This is not selectivity and not the count.\n\n## Regressed — 2. the tag facet count now always fails\n\n`get_filter_counts {\"tagFilter\": …}`, 3 calls per tag:\n\n| tag | result |\n|---|---|\n| `front view` | 0 passed, 3 failed — 8.07 / 8.12 / 8.11 s |\n| `blue` | 0 passed, 3 failed — 8.11 / 8.07 / 8.16 s |\n| `tech pack` | 0 passed, 3 failed — 8.15 / 8.09 / 8.09 s |\n| `design asset` | 0 passed, 8 failed |\n\nPreviously 7 of 8 passed. `get_effective_filter_counts {\"tagFilter\":\"blue\"}` direct → 500 @ 8.11 s, while `{\"licensorId\":…}` direct → 200 @ 0.47 s. The tag path is now the slow one and the identity path is the fast one — the reverse of before.\n\n## Still outstanding from #2054\n\n`count=exact` over `filter_effective_assets` never completes: 500 @ ~8.1 s at every range tried. Unchanged.\n\n## Likely cause\n\n`20260901130428_popdam_ranked_filter_parity.sql` and `20260901142825_popdam_effective_count_performance.sql` both redefine the function as:\n\n```sql\ncreate or replace function public.filter_effective_assets(p_filters jsonb default '{}'::jsonb)\nreturns setof public.assets\nlanguage sql stable security invoker\nas $$\n  with authorized as materialized (select public.require_dam_access() ok)\n  select a.* from authorized cross join public.assets a ...\n```\n\n`WITH … AS MATERIALIZED` is an explicit optimization barrier. A SQL function whose body contains one cannot be inlined, so PostgREST's `LIMIT` cannot push down and the full `assets ⋈ style_groups` result is built on every call — the same class of failure as the original `set search_path`, reintroduced by a different route. The constant ~8 s regardless of range, filter, or column list matches that exactly.\n\nThe entitlement check clearly needs to run once rather than per row, which is presumably why `MATERIALIZED` was chosen. Worth exploring whether `require_dam_access()` can be enforced without a barrier in the body — for example as a `SECURITY DEFINER` wrapper that checks entitlement and then calls an inlinable inner function, so the barrier sits outside the hot path.\n\n**Hypothesis, not a prescription** — I cannot run `EXPLAIN` as `authenticated`.\n\n## What would close this for PopDAM\n\n1. `filter_effective_assets` returning rows inside the ceiling again (it did after #1945).\n2. The tag facet count passing consistently, as the identity count now does.\n3. A list total obtainable inside the ceiling — either `count=exact` working, or `get_filter_counts.total` being reliable for every effective filter, which the app would use instead.\n\nPlease measure each over several consecutive calls and record the timings. Single warm calls have passed at every stage of this while the real shapes failed.\n\n## PopDAM state\n\nWiring stays gated off behind `EFFECTIVE_SCOPE_CONTRACT_READY = false` in `src/hooks/useAssets.ts`. No application change has been shipped against this contract at any point.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 850\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function public.filter_effective_assets\nreads:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-11T12:41:43Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T22:57:29Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2138,"title":"REGRESSION after #2054: filter_effective_assets times out on every call (5 rows, no filter, no count); tag facet count now 0/8. Likely the MATERIALIZED entitlement CTE added in 20260901130428/142825","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:19Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2138"},
{"body":"## What is needed\n\nThe owner confirmed on 2026-09-02 that a sample a factory is asked to MAKE can ship\nstraight from the factory — to New York, or to the customer — without passing through\nNingbo. The database currently forbids both.\n\nTwo changes to the Sample Tracking flow/path contract in schema `dflow`:\n\n1. Add `factory_customer` to the allowed `business_path` value list.\n2. Allow `nyo_factory_make_request` to use `factory_nyo` and `factory_customer` in\n   addition to its current `factory_ningbo_nyo` and `factory_ningbo_customer`.\n\nThe `factory_to_customer` ROUTE LEG already exists and needs no change\n(`20260724040000_sample_shipment_line_route_legs_explicit.sql`).\n\n## Exact objects\n\nCurrent definitions come from\n`supabase/migrations/20260818024441_sample_tracking_release_a_catalog_reconciliation.sql`:\n\n- `dflow.sample_workflow` — `business_path` CHECK (add `factory_customer`)\n- `dflow.sample_workflow` — CONSTRAINT `sample_workflow_valid_flow_path`\n  (widen the `nyo_factory_make_request` arm)\n- `dflow.sample_path_revision` — `business_path` CHECK (add `factory_customer`)\n- `dflow.validate_sample_path_revision()` — the same widened matrix inside the trigger\n\nThe table CHECK and the trigger must stay identical; they are two copies of one rule\ntoday and a change to one alone would let a path revision take a value the table\nrefuses, or the reverse.\n\n## Why it must be governed\n\nBoth the CHECK constraint and the trigger enforce the flow/path matrix independently of\nthe application, so no application-side change can deliver this.\n\n## Nothing else changes\n\nNo new route leg, no new location, no data migration. No existing row can violate the\nwidened rule, since widening only permits more.\n\n## Application side (owned by this session, blocked on the above)\n\n`popcre/designflow-tracking` `config/sampleVocabulary.js` — `BUSINESS_PATHS`,\n`VALID_FLOW_PATHS`, `PATH_ROUTE_LEGS` — plus the frontend path wording. Those mirror the\ndatabase and will be updated to match once this lands, not before.\n\n## Requested by\n\nDesignFlow PLM Sample Tracking session, 2026-09-02, on the owner's instruction.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 500\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table dflow.sample_workflow\n  - table dflow.sample_path_revision\n  - function dflow.validate_sample_path_revision\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T08:50:40Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T22:44:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2136,"title":"dflow: allow a make-request sample to ship direct from the factory (add business_path factory_customer)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:20Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2136"},

{"body":"## What is missing\n\nThe Warner Submissions catalogue and the Warner Creative/Art-Assets catalogue both carry\nthe property **Mortal Kombat II (2026)**, under the same Warner source identity\n`e01f0a1f-0ca6-42ac-8e9d-8e5e50421631`:\n\n- `plm.wb_property` id `fce7424a-f157-40df-8be9-7c8fb321da5c`, `source_namespace = warner_product_catalogue`\n- `plm.wb_property` id `9dd513ee-6cd8-4990-81a4-f999a6ce5831`, `source_namespace = warner_art_assets`\n\nA shared source identity across the two namespaces is direct source evidence of\nCreative-to-Submissions equivalence, not a name-similarity inference.\n\n`core.property` has no row for it. Under licensor `WARNER BROS`\n(`88313675-0089-4072-87be-5b989df8a3fc`) the only Mortal Kombat row is code `MB`\n`MORTAL KOMBAT` (`c0873079-36a4-4ab1-9aa0-1e8bedc6b274`), which is the franchise-level\nrow imported from DesignFlow PLM on 2026-06-25. All 41 Warner rows came from that one\nimport and all carry a DesignFlow PLM code.\n\nWarner's own catalogue already distinguishes dated titles at this level — `THE NUN 2018`\nversus `THE NUN 2 2023`, `IT 2017` versus `IT CHAPTER TWO 2019` — so a separate row is\nthe established shape here, not a new pattern.\n\nOwner instruction, 2026-09-02: if the Submissions site has it, our system needs it too,\nor submissions cannot be filed correctly.\n\n## The structural blocker\n\n`core.property` carries `property_licensor_id_code_key UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (licensor_id, code)`.\n\n`code` is nullable, but `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` means a NULL code counts as a value, so **at\nmost one code-less property can exist per licensor**. There are zero code-less rows in the\ntable today, so nobody has hit this.\n\nThe codes on `core.property` are DesignFlow PLM merch-group codes. A property that exists\nin a licensor portal but not yet in DesignFlow PLM legitimately has no code, and there is\nmore than one of them for Warner alone (see \"Also missing\" below). One NULL slot per\nlicensor is therefore not enough.\n\nThis is also a latent import defect. `plm.import_master_data` matches an incoming property\nby source ref, then code, then case-insensitive name, and inserts when none match. A second\ncode-less insert for the same licensor raises `unique_violation`; the handler then re-looks-up\nby code or name, finds nothing, leaves `core_property_id` NULL, and the following\n`core.taxonomy_source_ref` insert fails on NOT NULL. The constraint converts a normal\ncondition into an import abort.\n\n## The change\n\n1. Replace `property_licensor_id_code_key` with `UNIQUE NULLS DISTINCT (licensor_id, code)`,\n   so a licensor may hold more than one property whose code is not yet known. Non-NULL codes\n   stay unique per licensor exactly as today.\n2. Insert one `core.property` row: licensor `88313675-0089-4072-87be-5b989df8a3fc`,\n   name `Mortal Kombat II (2026)`, `code` NULL, `status` `active`, metadata recording that\n   the row is curated from the Warner source extracts and must not be treated as\n   import-owned.\n3. Insert one `core.taxonomy_source_ref` row binding the new property to the Warner source\n   identity: `source_system = warner_product_catalogue`, `source_table = plm.wb_property`,\n   `source_id = e01f0a1f-0ca6-42ac-8e9d-8e5e50421631`, `confidence = verified`. This matches\n   the five Warner refs created by #640 exactly. Those refs key on the Warner source identity,\n   not on the `plm.wb_property` primary key, so the single row covers both namespaces --\n   `core.taxonomy_source_ref` also carries `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (source_system,\n   source_table, source_id)`, and no `warner_art_assets` ref row exists for any property.\n   Do not invent a second one.\n\nConvergence is already handled: when DesignFlow PLM eventually publishes this property, the\nimporter's name fallback matches the curated row and `code = coalesce(v_source_code, code)`\nfills the code in. No duplicate is created.\n\n## Also missing, not in scope here\n\n`Mortal Kombat (2021)` and `Mortal Kombat Core: Video Game` are in the Warner extracts and\nabsent from `core.property` on the same footing. Their source evidence has not been checked\nto the same standard as this one and they are deliberately left out. They are the reason the\nuniqueness relaxation is needed rather than a single NULL slot.\n\n## Lane\n\nAuthor lane claim: #2133. Reserved migration version `20260902222649`.\n\n## Related\n\nInstance of the \"present in source but not in our data\" class in #640.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 800\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table core.property\n  - table core.taxonomy_source_ref\nreads:\n  - table plm.wb_property\n  - table core.licensor\n```\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T00:17:42Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T22:26:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2132,"title":"core.property cannot hold a second code-less property, so Mortal Kombat II (2026) cannot be created","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:23Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2132"},

{"body":"The verification cost guard (`scripts/check-migration-verify-cost.mjs`, merged in #1954) is a static text scanner. Its own document already records the general limits; external review of #1954 named five specific shapes it cannot see today, and they are worth closing or explicitly accepting one at a time:\n\n1. `execute E'...'` and `format(E'...')` — the dynamic-SQL lead check does not account for the `E` prefix, so an escaped string handed to `execute` is blanked instead of scanned.\n2. A file-scope `set search_path ... plm` outside any inspected `DO` body. The in-block form is refused; the file-scope form is not seen.\n3. `truncate table <object>` — the read-context list matches `truncate` followed directly by the name, so the optional `table` keyword slips past.\n4. The 200-character window used to find the `DO` lead before a dollar tag. A longer comment or clause between them hides the block.\n5. The unresolvable-base seam: a verification block reaching a prohibited object through a name it cannot resolve statically.\n\nEach is a false negative, not a false positive, so the guard stays safe to keep on while these are open. Nothing here is urgent.\n\nRaised during the close-out of #2104.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-02T23:29:19Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T22:03:18Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2130,"title":"Verify-cost guard: five named blind spots from the #1954 review","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:47:14Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2130"},

{"body":"## What is broken\n\nWith **zero open orchestrator markers**, no pull request in this repository can draw a reviewer, so no pull request can merge. This is repository-wide, not specific to any one PR.\n\nReproduced 2026-09-02T17:26Z:\n\n```\n$ node scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --assign-reviewer \\\n    --issue 1224 --pr 1957 --head-sha a1ee43fc95f92208ced1a4fa066b870d04d5826a\nREFUSED: live orchestrator engine could not be resolved\n  (Command failed: node scripts/check-orchestrator-marker.mjs --resolve --json)\n\n$ node scripts/check-orchestrator-marker.mjs --resolve --json ; echo \"exit=$?\"\n{ \"state\": \"none\", \"routing\": null,\n  \"message\": \"NO ACTIVE ORCHESTRATOR: zero open markers. ...\" }\nexit=3\n```\n\n## Mechanism\n\n`resolveOrchestratorEngine` in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:1281` runs the marker resolver through `execFileSync` and treats a **non-zero exit as an unreadable answer**:\n\n```js\ntry { resolved = JSON.parse(execFileSync(process.execPath,\n  ['scripts/check-orchestrator-marker.mjs','--resolve','--json'], {encoding:'utf8'})) }\ncatch (error) { throw new LaneError(`live orchestrator engine could not be resolved (${error.message})`) }\nconst engine = resolved?.state === 'declared' ? resolved.routing?.engine : null\nif (!engine) throw new LaneError('live orchestrator engine is unreadable; reviewer assignment refused')\n```\n\n`--resolve` exits **3** for `state: none`, so the `catch` fires and the second, more accurate refusal is never reached. The reported cause is therefore wrong in a way that matters: *\"could not be resolved\"* reads as a broken resolver or a local fault, when the resolver in fact answered correctly and completely — **there is no orchestrator**.\n\nThe engine is needed only to **exclude the live orchestrator's own engine** from the reviewer rotation (Codex cannot review while Codex orchestrates; Claude cannot review while Claude orchestrates). With no orchestrator running, there is nothing to exclude — yet the allocator fails closed and blocks every draw.\n\n## Why this is worth an issue rather than a note\n\n1. **It is a repository-wide stop, and it is invisible.** Nothing announces it. A session discovers it only by attempting a draw, and the message it gets points at the wrong thing. Compare the sibling defect recorded in `docs/agents/` where a wrapper's missing CALLER variable was reported as a local dependency fault — same failure shape, same wasted diagnosis.\n2. **It is coupled to an unrelated event.** Closing an orchestrator marker is a *normal, correct* end-of-session action. It should not silently disable merging for the whole repository until someone volunteers to open a new one.\n3. **It creates a bad incentive.** The cheapest way out is for a maintenance session to open an orchestrator marker it should not hold, purely to unblock a reviewer draw. That is exactly the collision the marker guard exists to prevent.\n4. **The fail-closed direction is not obviously right here.** Failing closed on an *ambiguous* marker (two orchestrators) is clearly correct. Failing closed on `state: none` protects nothing: the exclusion list is empty, and the rotation is safe.\n\n## Live impact right now\n\nSix pull requests from the #2104 sweep are conflict-free, fully green (13 checks pass / 0 fail on the two that were rebuilt) and blocked on nothing except this:\n\n| PR | Head | Closes |\n|----|------|--------|\n| #1935 Centralize pending migration classification | `f0fab188` | #1690 |\n| #1946 Fix production lane acquisition order | `bbec3793` | #1689 |\n| #1957 Close preview rehearsal coverage gaps | `a1ee43fc` | #1224 |\n| #1956 Preserve owner ruling catalog in empty replay | `eb04488e` | #1258 |\n| #1954 Block expensive migration verification reads | `d527759e` | #1285 |\n| #1951 Add rollback-only preview performance rehearsals | `a454276b` | #1356 |\n\nReviewer capacity is **not** the constraint: `--reviewer-capacity` reports 5 total, 2 free, 3 stale-reclaimable, 0 live.\n\n## Two decisions needed\n\n**(a) Should `state: none` still refuse a reviewer draw?**\n\n- *Option A — allow the draw.* When there is no orchestrator, exclude nothing and rotate normally. The exclusion is a same-engine conflict guard; with no live engine there is no conflict. `state: ambiguous` and `state: invalid` keep refusing.\n- *Option B — keep refusing, but say so honestly.* Preserve the current stop and only fix the message, so a session is told *\"no orchestrator marker is open; open one or wait for a successor\"* instead of *\"could not be resolved\"*. This keeps a deliberate hard gate on all merging whenever no orchestrator is running — which should then be **written down as a rule**, because today it is an accident of an exit code, not a stated policy.\n\n**(b) Regardless of (a), fix the misreported cause.** Distinguish \"the resolver exited non-zero because it has a real answer\" from \"the resolver crashed\". Exit 3 with parseable JSON is an answer.\n\n## Suggested fix for (b)\n\nRead the resolver's stdout on the non-zero path before deciding it failed, and let the existing `state`-aware branch produce the accurate message:\n\n```js\nlet raw\ntry { raw = execFileSync(process.execPath, [...], {encoding:'utf8'}) }\ncatch (error) {\n  raw = error?.stdout ?? ''\n  if (!raw.trim()) throw new LaneError(`live orchestrator marker resolver could not be run (${error.message})`)\n}\n```\n\nThen branch on `state`: `declared` returns the engine; `none` says no marker is open and names the decision from (a); `ambiguous` / `invalid` refuse as they do now. Add a test that asserts a `state: none` resolver produces the *no-marker* message and never the *could-not-be-resolved* message — the current wording is the defect being fixed, so the test has to name it.\n\n## Not doing\n\nThis session is a repository-maintenance session for #2104 and was instructed not to open an orchestrator marker. It has not opened one and has not worked around the refusal. The six PRs above stay open and ready.\n\nRelated: #2104 (the sweep this surfaced from), and the reviewer-allocation limits already recorded in `docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md`.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T12:52:30Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T19:30:00Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2127,"title":"Reviewer assignment is frozen repository-wide when no orchestrator marker is open, and the refusal misreports its own cause","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:26Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2127"},
{"body":"## What I need\n\nReview and merge PR #2122 (`feat/dcp-match-ui` -> `main`, head `e53670f0c236b8fbf743ed78461a5f64a52cfcff`).\n\nIt is BLOCKED only on the required status `Migration guarded merge authorization`, which is posted solely by a `Guarded Merge` workflow_dispatch. That workflow runs `check-exact-head-approval.mjs`, which needs a rotation reviewer assignment (`manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --assign-reviewer --issue <this issue> --pr 2122 --head-sha e53670f0...`) and an APPROVE tied to that exact head. Only the orchestrator can draw that rotation; I am the PR author and cannot self-approve.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nPR #2122 realigns the DB Data Admin **Property Matches** screen with the RPC contract that actually shipped in `20260902053756_property_match_review_rpcs.sql` (issue #2008).\n\nThe UI merged earlier in #2006 was written against the proposed spec, not the shipped one. PostgREST binds RPC arguments **by name**, and the shipped function takes `p_decision_reason` / `p_client_request_id`, not `p_reason` / `p_operation_id`. As merged, **every reviewer decision on that screen fails**. The screen is live on data.designflow.app today.\n\n#2122 also: reads candidates as `{licensed_property_id, member_ordinal}` and looks names up from `api.opa_property_reconciliation`; sends no members on a rejection (the database raises `invalid_parameter_value` otherwise); holds one `p_client_request_id` per row for idempotent retry; and updates `docs/db-data-admin-property-match-review.md` to the shipped signatures.\n\n## Scope\n\nApplication code and docs only. **No migration, no schema change, no data.** Four files under `apps/db-data-admin/` plus one doc.\n\n## Verification already done on the head\n\n- `npx vitest run src/PropertyMatchReview.test.tsx` — 15 passed\n- `npm test` — 20 files, 133 passed\n- `npm run lint` — clean\n- `npm run build` — succeeded\n\nEvery other check on the PR reports pass or skipping; none are pending.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-02T19:33:55Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T18:24:32Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2126,"title":"HANDOVER: review and merge PR #2122 (Property Matches screen vs shipped RPC contract)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:47:20Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2126"},
