{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 900\ndepends_on:\n```\n\nThe production business-risk gate compares the wrong two things, and the comparison it makes gets **permanently** harder to satisfy as `main` moves. Right now it blocks every production promotion.\n\n## What happened\n\nThe owner authorized a production promotion in chat on 2026-09-02 at main tip `912419b4fee0dbb4077e657aae0fb120f69b908a`. The first version in the batch, `20260901142825` (from PR #2057), was refused. Two apply attempts, runs `33646585228` (15:08Z) and `33647019780` (15:12Z), both failed at the same step with the same message:\n\n```\nProduction business-risk gate rejected evidence: original apply run 33640550973\ndispatched at 912419b4fee0dbb4077e657aae0fb120f69b908a produced evidence with a\ndifferent scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs than the merge commit\n21d120fe187985f6ff46964c9914e6d358731b62 of the pull request that authored\n20260901142825\n```\n\nThe batch stopped there. **Nothing was promoted.** Preview proof (`33646808518`) and review evidence (`33646993519`) were both green; only this gate refused.\n\n## Why it can never pass again\n\nThe gate requires the lane-management script as it existed at the *evidence-run dispatch SHA* to be byte-identical to the same script at the *merge commit that authored the migration*. Those two commits are necessarily different whenever `main` has moved since the migration merged — and `main` always moves.\n\nMeasured on 2026-09-02: **14 commits** have changed `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` between `21d120fe` and current `main`, most of them the reviewer-pool repairs (#2075, #2079, #2102). Every one of those made this version less promotable, and none of them touched the migration, the evidence, or the database.\n\nSo this is not a transient failure to retry. Re-dispatching produces the identical refusal, which is what the two runs above already demonstrate.\n\n## What the gate presumably meant to check\n\nThat the evidence was produced by the *governance rules in force*, so an old evidence artifact cannot be replayed under rules that have since tightened. That is a legitimate thing to want. Pinning it to byte-equality of an unrelated orchestration script is not a way to get it: the script changes for reasons that have nothing to do with the migration being promoted, and the check has no way to tell a rules change from a typo fix.\n\n## What is needed\n\n1. Decide what the gate is actually asserting, and assert *that*. If it is \"the evidence was generated under the current governance contract\", compare a contract version or a digest of the governing rules, not the whole script file.\n2. Whatever replaces it, **prove it can fail** before trusting it — feed it a known-bad evidence artifact and confirm a red result. A gate that only ever passes and a gate that only ever fails look the same from the outside until you test both directions.\n3. Do not weaken it into a no-op to unblock the promotion. The promotion can wait; a silently-permissive production gate cannot be undone.\n\n## Blast radius\n\n**All production promotion is blocked** until this is resolved. Nine versions were queued behind it. That is the highest-consequence open item in the repository right now.\n\n## Classification note\n\nThis fails the AGENTS.md §0.0-C shape test — it changes a workflow and a Python gate, not the database — so it is `repo-maintenance` and routes away from the orchestrator, even though what it blocks is orchestrator work. Filed here so the route is recorded, not to claim it.\n\nFound during orchestrator marker #2109.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-02T23:01:33Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T17:09:40Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2118,"title":"HANDOVER: production promotion is permanently blocked — the business-risk gate pins an unrelated script's bytes","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:33Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2118"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority:\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\n## What is wrong\n\n`scripts/run-governed-review.mjs` passes every wrapper the same invocation shape after `--`:\n\n```\nnew <session-name> --prompt-file <path>\n```\n\n`ai-codex-review` does not accept that. Its only usage is:\n\n```\nai-codex-review <plan-review|diff-review|security-review|visual-review|final-check> [--tests <command>]\nai-codex-review doctor\n```\n\nIt takes **no prompt file at all** — it reviews the working tree itself. Given the standard shape it\nprints its usage text and exits non-zero, which the runner reports as:\n\n```\nREFUSED: review wrapper did not produce a recordable terminal verdict (exit 2)\n```\n\n## Why it has stayed hidden\n\nThe runner suppresses wrapper stdout, so the usage text never reaches the operator. The refusal is\nindistinguishable from a reviewer that genuinely said nothing. `ai-codex-review doctor` returns\n`PASS`, so every health check says the reviewer is fine.\n\nThis is almost certainly the true cause of the long-standing \"codex-review never returns a verdict\"\nfolklore recorded across several previous sessions. It is a **harness** fault, not a provider fault,\nand every rotation that drew this reviewer has been spent for nothing.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- A drawn `codex-gpt-5.6-sol` costs a rotation and produces no review.\n- Even in its supported form the wrapper cannot be given the PR-specific brief the other wrappers\n  receive, so it cannot be told which head SHA to bind its verdict to — and a verdict line without\n  the head SHA is discarded by `verdictFromOutput`.\n\n## Suggested direction\n\n1. Give the runner a per-wrapper invocation template instead of one hard-coded shape, and refuse at\n   dispatch time when the drawn wrapper has no template.\n2. Surface the wrapper's own stderr/usage text in the refusal, so a shape mismatch never again reads\n   as a silent reviewer.\n3. Decide whether `codex-gpt-5.6-sol` can be briefed at all; if it cannot bind a head SHA, it should\n   leave the rotation rather than keep consuming draws.\n\nScope: repository plumbing, no database SHAPE change — **REPO-SESSION** under `AGENTS.md` §0.0-C.\n\nFound 2026-09-02 under orchestrator marker #2109 while reviewing PR #2114.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:28:24Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T15:50:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2117,"title":"One reviewer wrapper takes no prompt file, so the governed runner can never brief it","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:34Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2117"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority:\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\n## What happened\n\nDuring orchestrator #2109 a nine-version batch was promoted to production (apply run 33647723083). The promotion freezes the merge lane, and freezing it revoked the **Migration guarded merge authorization** check on the head of *every* open pull request — including PRs that had nothing to do with the promotion.\n\nWhen the promotion finished, nothing restored it. Each affected PR had to be refreshed from the new main tip and re-authorized by hand before `guarded-migration-merge.yml` would run.\n\n## Why it matters\n\n- The revocation is invisible from the PR page until a guarded merge is attempted and refused.\n- A lane that was mid-flight when a promotion starts looks exactly like a lane whose review went stale — the operator cannot tell \"your authorization was taken by a freeze\" from \"your head moved\".\n- The freeze is bounded; the revocation is not. Nothing in the promotion path is responsible for putting the authorizations back.\n\n## Scope\n\nRepository plumbing only — no database SHAPE changes. This is a **REPO-SESSION** item under `AGENTS.md` §0.0-C, not a migration-author lane.\n\n## Suggested direction\n\nEither (a) make the freeze scope its revocation to PRs that actually collide with the promoted allowlist, or (b) make the end of the promotion restore what the freeze took, or (c) at minimum have the refusal message say the authorization was revoked by production freeze run `<id>` and name the exact re-authorization command.\n\nObserved 2026-09-02, orchestrator marker #2109.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-04T08:14:28Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T15:43:28Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2116,"title":"A production apply revokes guarded-merge authorization on every open PR head and never restores it","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:36Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2116"},
{"body":"The post-apply production catalog verifier reports every behavioural contract as `MISSING` when its query fails, which reads as \"the contract is absent from the database\" and is actually \"the check never ran\".\n\nFound live during the production promotion of nine merged migrations on 2026-09-02: apply run `33647723083` applied all nine successfully and then failed only on its \"Post-apply catalog verification\" step. An independent production ledger-drift run (`33648130412`) confirmed all nine are applied and reported no actionable drift, so the database is correct and the verifier is wrong.\n\nCause: in `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py`, two `position(...)` search needles were written with Python-escaped double quotes, so PostgreSQL received double-quoted identifiers instead of string literals and rejected the statement. All seven behavioural contracts are built into one `union all`, so a single rejected branch aborts the whole query and every contract comes back with no row.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\n```\n\nFix is in PR #2114: correct the quoting, and make the report distinguish \"the query errored, this is not evidence of absence\" from a genuine missing row.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-02T16:22:17Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T15:38:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2115,"title":"Post-apply catalog verifier reports MISSING when its query fails","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:24:37Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2115"},

{"body":"Step 2 of the ColdLion raw-landing plan, split out of the #2081 tracker so it is a single dispatchable unit with an exact write surface.\n\nBuild the six master landing tables described in `docs/coldlion-raw-landing-schema-design.md` §3.1, in a new `coldlion` schema. Current-state behaviour: each table carries the common landing columns plus `first_seen_at` / `last_seen_at` and `source_hash` computed over the complete fetched record before projection. No foreign keys into `core.*` or any curated table — this layer never interprets.\n\nNatural keys, exactly as designed:\n\n| Table | Natural key |\n|---|---|\n| `coldlion.customer` | company_code, customer_code |\n| `coldlion.vendor` | company_code, vendor_code |\n| `coldlion.merch_group_header` | company_code, division_code, mg_type_code |\n| `coldlion.merch_group_detail` | company_code, division_code, mg_type_code, mg_code |\n| `coldlion.season` | company_code, division_code, season_code |\n| `coldlion.salesperson` | company_code, salesperson_code |\n\nThe four-part key on `merch_group_detail` is mandatory: `mgCode` collides across types inside one division (`1P` is both a licensor and a property in CW001).\n\nNone of the open reviewer objections U1-U20 touches these six tables — U6 (silent 200-row page cap) and U13 (three-stage `prodHistory` loop) are history-endpoint problems and land in Steps 4 and 5. That is why this step is separable and ready while #2081 stays blocked.\n\nStructure only. No row loads under this issue.\n\nTracker: #2081. Design: `docs/coldlion-raw-landing-schema-design.md`. Plan: `docs/plan_coldlion-landing-phases-2-6.md`.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 3\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - schema coldlion\n  - table coldlion.customer\n  - table coldlion.vendor\n  - table coldlion.merch_group_header\n  - table coldlion.merch_group_detail\n  - table coldlion.season\n  - table coldlion.salesperson\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-02T06:17:53Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T05:44:58Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Summary\n\n`20260902024541` (PR #1939, merged as `e947f3c8`) delivered the durable source-to-POP resolution home: `plm.source_resolution`, the `plm.set_source_resolution` setter, the 26 immutability triggers, and the four `api.*` consumer views.\n\nOne piece of #1609 was deliberately left out of that migration and is not yet delivered: **there is no `api.set_source_resolution` wrapper**, so a browser client holding an `authenticated` JWT cannot record a resolution. Only `service_role` paths can write today. This was verified against production during #1609 and recorded there before that issue was closed out.\n\n## What to build\n\n`api.set_source_resolution`, a thin wrapper over `plm.set_source_resolution`:\n\n- `SECURITY DEFINER`\n- `set search_path to pg_catalog`\n- `revoke all` from `public` and `anon`\n- `grant execute` to `authenticated, service_role`\n- same argument list and same raise codes as the `plm` setter; no additional privilege beyond what the setter already enforces\n\nAdd a contract test asserting anon is denied and `authenticated` succeeds.\n\n## Provenance\n\nSplit out of #1609 at closeout so the obligation is not lost. Nothing here changes what `20260902024541` already applied.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1\nwrites:\n  - function api.set_source_resolution\nreads:\n  - function plm.set_source_resolution\n  - table plm.source_resolution\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-02T04:01:27Z","createdAt":"2026-09-02T03:16:23Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2085,"title":"FOLLOW-UP to #1609: browser clients still cannot record a source resolution — api.set_source_resolution wrapper is missing","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:25:10Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2085"},

{"body":"The ColdLion raw-landing plan (`docs/plan_coldlion-landing-phases-2-6.md`) is now documented, reviewed and settled through owner decisions D1-D17, but **none of steps 2-6 has been built**. This is the tracker for building them.\n\n## State as of 2026-09-01\n\n- Plan, prepack model, business rules and owner decisions D14-D17 are all merged to `main` (last: PR #2068, merge 373a46ad).\n- Steps 2 and 3 (merch groups, items) are unaffected by every open objection and are safe to start now.\n- Step 4 (sales history) must be re-designed before it is built: corrected natural key, flat-vs-split table decision, and D2's scope on prepack rows.\n- Step 5 (production history) needs its field count re-derived from the live spec.\n\n## Open reviewer objections\n\nA structured critique of the plan and of its 2026-09-01 review produced an **unresolved-objection ledger U1-U20**. None has been addressed. The two flagged most serious:\n\n- **U6** - the paging defect's severity may be understated. Both history endpoints silently cap a page at 200 rows and return no error, so a loader that does not loop until `last` is true will believe a partial pull is complete.\n- **U13** - `prodHistory` probably needs a three-stage ISS/INTRAN/REC loop rather than a single pull; the plan assumes one pass.\n\nThe full ledger is NOT in this repository (it may quote customer identifiers, and this repo is public). It is recoverable two ways:\n- `AI_MUSE_CALLER=claude ai-muse transcript coldlion-plan-review-2065`\n- a saved copy on EDGE-DEV at `C:\\Users\\ahazan\\.claude\\projects\\C--repos-shared-db\\artifacts\\2026-09-01-muse-coldlion-plan-review-2065-U1-U20.txt`\n\n## Definition of done\n\nSteps 2-6 built and loaded, with U1-U20 each either implemented, refuted in writing, or escalated to the owner.\n\nRelated: #1031 (chunked historical puller), #2066, #2069, #2071 (all closed docs lanes).\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 3\ndepends_on: 2094\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\nReclassified by the orchestrator on 2026-09-02. Each buildable step gets its own structural issue\nwith an exact write surface; this one tracks them and carries the U1-U20 objection ledger.\n\n- Step 2 (six master tables) is split out as #2094 and is ready now.\n- Steps 3-6 stay unsplit: Step 4 needs its natural key, flat-vs-split decision and D2 prepack scope\n  settled first, and Step 5 needs its field count re-derived from the live spec. U6 (silent 200-row\n  page cap) and U13 (three-stage ISS/INTRAN/REC loop) would both change what gets built.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T21:10:31Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T23:54:04Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"`deepseek-chat` produced a complete, confidently formatted, well-ranked review of\nPR #1989 describing code that does not exist, and the governed pipeline recorded\nit as a durable verdict artifact bound to the exact head.\n\n**Durable artifact:** `refs/db-review-verdicts/1987-1989-fe810d47b643e986d0357a5af0fe1b3a9f2d0d27`\n(reviewer `deepseek-chat`, slot 1, verdict REVISE).\n\n**What it reviewed.** A file `20260901221310_add_designflow_item_assignment_action_history.sql`\n(the real file is `20260901221310_designflow_item_assignment_action_history.sql`),\ncontaining functions `notify_designflow_item_assignment`,\n`notify_bulk_designflow_item_assignment`, `log_designflow_item_assignment_action`,\n`get_designflow_assignment_action_history`, `handle_designflow_assignment_change`,\ntables `designflow_item_assignment_action_history` and\n`designflow_item_assignment_actions`, and `user_notification` columns\n`designflow_action_id` and `assignment_action_seq`.\n\n**Verified independently:** `git grep` for those identifiers across the branch\nreturns zero files. None of them exist. It also placed the objects in `public`\n(they are in `dflow`), stated \"no GRANT statements are present\" (there are eight\nexplicit REVOKE/GRANT statements), and stated the migration sets\n`SET search_path = ''` at the top (it does not).\n\n**Root cause.** `ai-deepseek-agent` is a conversational API wrapper with no\nrepository access — no filesystem, no diff, no tools. Unlike `ai-grok-review` and\n`ai-codex-review`, which run in read-only sandboxes over a real checkout, it sees\nonly the text of the brief. Given a brief that describes what a change *claims* to\ndo, it will produce a plausible review of the described change rather than the\nactual one. The `--worktree` argument to `run-governed-review.mjs` sets the spawn\ncwd; for this wrapper that is inert.\n\n**Why this is worse than a bad review.** Nothing in the gate distinguishes a\nreviewer that read the code from one that could not. The same run could have\nemitted `VERDICT: APPROVE` and produced a durable approval artifact over a change\nno reviewer ever saw — a green merge gate on unreviewed SQL. The verdict's\n*format* is the only thing checked.\n\n**Required fixes:**\n1. Remove `deepseek-chat` from the reviewer rotation, or restrict it to\n   non-code roles. It must not be drawable for an exact-head code review.\n2. Make the rotation record, per reviewer, whether the wrapper actually reads the\n   repository, and refuse to record a code-review verdict from one that does not.\n3. Consider requiring the reviewer to quote at least one verbatim line from the\n   diff under review, checked against the real diff before the artifact is\n   recorded. A reviewer that cannot read the code cannot satisfy this; one that\n   can, satisfies it for free.\n\n**Prove the guard can fail before trusting the fix:** feed the new check a known\nconfabulated review (this one is preserved in the artifact above) and show it is\nrefused, then show a genuine review still records.\n\nRelated: this is the same family as #2075 (verdict detection reading PR prose).\nBoth are the gate trusting a *shape* instead of a fact.\n\n```queue-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\n```\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:18:34Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T22:45:40Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2078,"title":"A reviewer with no repository access recorded a durable verdict on code it never saw","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:25:15Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2078"},
{"body":"`--exclude-reviewer` applied to a reviewer that already holds the current head's\ndurable assignment ref releases its lease but leaves the assignment ref pointing\nat the now-excluded reviewer. Every later `--assign-reviewer` for that head then\nthrows:\n\n```\ndurable assignment reviewer <name> is excluded for this PR (<reason>); it was not returned or re-leased\n```\n\nThere is no command to return the reviewer. `--replace-failed-reviewer` is the\nonly replacement route and it demands a `TERMINAL_FAILURE_CODES` value, which is\nuntrue when the reviewer did not fail — it was excluded for `already-reviewed`\nindependence. Assigning a different slot does not help either:\n`assertDurableReviewApproval` requires a durable APPROVE for **every** slot's\nlatest exact-head assignment, so slot 1 stays permanently unsatisfiable and the\nPR becomes unmergeable at that head.\n\n**Live instance:** issue #1999 / PR #2002, head `0f139c0dafe6542b4395f571310ac3c65bdea32d`,\nreviewer `muse-spark-1.2-contributor`, exclusion ref\n`refs/db-review-exclusions/1999-2002-muse-spark-1.2-contributor`.\n\nThis is the same family as the recorded \"a lease cannot be handed back\" defect:\nthe only release path also draws a successor, so a slot becomes unreturnable at\nexactly the moment it must be returned.\n\n**The fix must repair the capability, not remove the guard.** An excluded\nreviewer must still never be drawn again for that PR, and a slot with no APPROVE\nmust still refuse. Excluding a reviewer that holds the current head's assignment\nmust additionally record a durable *return* of that assignment so a fresh,\nindependent reviewer can be drawn for the same head.\n\n**Prove the guard can still fail before trusting the fix.** Required proofs:\n1. the deadlock reproduces against the pre-fix code;\n2. after the fix, assignment for that head succeeds and draws a different reviewer;\n3. the excluded reviewer is still never drawn for that PR;\n4. `assertDurableReviewApproval` still refuses when a live (non-returned) slot has no APPROVE.\n\n```queue-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\n```\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:28:10Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T22:12:22Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2076,"title":"Reviewer exclusion after assignment is unreturnable: the PR becomes permanently unmergeable","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:25:17Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2076"},
{"body":"## What happened\n\nOrchestrator marker #2074, 2026-09-01. While recovering a stalled GLM reviewer session for PR #1939, I posted a PR comment whose **first paragraph said, in capitals, that it was NOT a governed verdict**, and which quoted the reviewer's prose analysis. That analysis contained the word `APPROVE` and the exact head SHA.\n\nThe very next command — `--release-failed-reviewer` — was refused with:\n\n```\nREFUSED: an existing verdict for the exact head forbids reviewer release\n```\n\nThere was no verdict. `git ls-remote origin 'refs/db-review-verdict*'` showed no verdict ref for the tuple. My own explicitly-non-authorizing comment had been counted **as the verdict**. Deleting the comment made the refusal disappear and the release succeed.\n\n## The defect\n\n`hasVerdictForHead` / `anyVerdictFor` (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:1814`) decide \"this review is finished\" from the *text* of any issue comment, PR comment, or PR review that mentions a decision word near the head SHA. It checks:\n\n- not **who** wrote it,\n- not whether it is in the machine-recordable `VERDICT: APPROVE <sha>` terminal form that `run-governed-review.mjs:13` requires,\n- not whether a durable create-only verdict artifact exists under `refs/db-review-verdicts/`,\n- not the explicit disclaimer sitting directly above it.\n\nThe comment above `anyVerdictFor` says a verdict exists when a comment \"carries a decision\". Prose carries a decision to a regex.\n\n## Why this is more than an annoyance\n\nThis is the **third recorded sighting** of \"a comment becomes a verdict\" in this repository. The previous two were near-misses in the other direction. This one is worse in one specific way and better in another:\n\n- **Better:** here it produced a *refusal*, which is fail-closed. Nothing was authorized that should not have been.\n- **Worse:** the same predicate gates `assertReviewLeaseStillStale` and the busy-reviewer probe, and the same text would read as APPROVE there too. Any person or agent who pastes a reviewer's prose — a summary, a quote, a handoff excerpt, a \"here is what the last reviewer said\" comment — onto a PR at its exact head can silently manufacture the *appearance* of a completed review. The recorded design intent (the comment at line 1810) is that both places must mean the same thing; they do, and what they both mean is wrong.\n\n## Required outcome\n\nMake \"a verdict exists\" mean **a durable create-only verdict artifact exists under the `refs/db-review-verdicts/` prefix for the exact tuple**, and nothing else. Comment text is evidence a human can read; it must not be evidence a gate can read.\n\nIf a text fallback must be retained for a transition period, it must at minimum require the machine terminal form (`^VERDICT: (APPROVE|REVISE|REJECT) <40-hex>$` as the final line) **and** an author check, and it must be reported as `unverified-text-verdict`, never as a verdict.\n\nProve the fix by feeding the checker a known-dirty case first: a comment that says APPROVE and the head SHA inside an explicit non-authorizing disclaimer must classify as **no verdict**.\n\n## Where the evidence is\n\nPR #1939, head `f8ee002d58d85d7378004b9ab7efe7803ddeb479`. The offending comment was `5501000870`; it has been deleted, and the GLM reservation was then released as `wrapper_terminal_failure` (failure SHA `8242e65a3cf8a00d1ea7a099181e4f1026798204`). The GLM analysis it quoted is preserved in that session's wrapper transcript, not on the PR, precisely because posting it is unsafe today.\n\n## Related but separate\n\nThe GLM wrapper session `shared-db-1609-seq854` reached a conclusion, but its poller stopped at `2026-09-01T20:17:58Z` while its metadata still read `status: active`, so the governed harness never captured a recordable verdict line. That is a **cross-repository wrapper defect** and belongs to `ai-devops` under parent #159, not here. It is recorded here only so the two are not confused.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:28:08Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T22:01:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2075,"title":"Verdict detection reads PR prose: an explicitly non-authorizing comment counted as a recorded verdict","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:25:20Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2075"},

{"body":"## Application owner and dependency\n\nDesignFlow backend issue popcre/designflow-backend#79, plan Steps 4 and 6. The production HTS RAG contract from migrations 20260831234750 and 20260901011306 is live and Step 2 application models now mirror it.\n\n## Structural gap\n\nThe current hts_rag_determinations table can store method, proposed HTS, state, hashes, and a comparison key, but it has no immutable comparison category/details or idempotent completion/session identity. The current extraction job/precedent contract stores hashes and an error code but has no protected durable raw provider-response/parse artifact. Step 6 also requires ordered multi-turn provider responses persisted before HTTP release and an incomplete/review-needed sweep. These requirements cannot be implemented honestly by application code without new canonical structure.\n\n## Required governed outcome\n\nPlease bound and author the minimum additive, privacy-protected contract for: (1) immutable determination comparison taxonomy/details and completion idempotency; (2) durable raw structured extraction and legacy provider-response artifacts with parse/enrichment state; (3) ordered multi-turn linkage to determination/session; (4) bounded retry/incomplete/dead-letter visibility; and (5) RLS/grants/indexes/assertions preserving service-only writes and authorized admin review. Do not store customer descriptions in logs or public evidence.\n\n## Safety constraints\n\nLegacy AI/CROSS remains operative. Shadow mode remains mandatory. Authoritative rate lookups remain the only rate source. Auto-recommend remains off. Schema is additive and application startup DDL is forbidden. This issue must be independently routed by the current shared-db orchestrator; it does not inherit issue #2004's claim or lane.\n\n## Routing\n\nRouted by the DesignFlow backend application session on 2026-09-01 after resolving the live\norchestrator marker (#2061). This issue does not inherit #2004's claim, lane, or reserved version.\nThe object list below is the maximum write surface requested; the authoring agent bounds the\nfinal minimum additive design within it.\n\n```machine\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nobjects: table public.hts_rag_determinations, table public.hts_rag_provider_responses, table public.hts_rag_extraction_jobs, policy hts_rag_provider_responses_backend_all on public.hts_rag_provider_responses, policy hts_rag_provider_responses_backend_read on public.hts_rag_provider_responses, index public.hts_rag_determinations_comparison_category_idx, index public.hts_rag_provider_responses_determination_idx\n```\n\n\nClassified by orchestrator marker #2074 (2026-09-01): genuinely structural (new tables, columns, indexes, RLS policies and grants). Admitted to the shared-db orchestrator queue. Held `blocked` until the exact object set is bounded, because a migration-author lane claim requires an exact, parseable object list and this issue currently states outcomes rather than objects. Bounding is the next orchestrator action; it does not inherit #2004's claim, lane or objects.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 2\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table public.hts_rag_determinations\n  - table public.hts_rag_provider_responses\n  - table public.hts_rag_extraction_jobs\n  - policy hts_rag_provider_responses_backend_all on public.hts_rag_provider_responses\n  - policy hts_rag_provider_responses_backend_read on public.hts_rag_provider_responses\n  - index public.hts_rag_determinations_comparison_category_idx\n  - index public.hts_rag_provider_responses_determination_idx\nreads:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-02T06:42:59Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T19:25:03Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"# Outcome needed\n\nRepair the reviewer-capacity registry so finished, failed, stale-head, closed-issue, and otherwise orphaned reviewer leases cannot report the whole pool busy when no reviewer process is running. Provide a guarded reconciliation command and saturation regression tests; do not manually delete coordination refs.\n\nThe full orchestrator briefing will be committed at [`HANDOFF.d/2026-09-01T1630Z-edge-dev-codex-reviewer-capacity-deadlock.md`](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/blob/main/HANDOFF.d/2026-09-01T1630Z-edge-dev-codex-reviewer-capacity-deadlock.md).\n\n## What happened\n\nDuring marker #2051, structural PRs #1939 (#1609), #2002 (#1999), and #2057 (#2054) reached exact-head review. The live `refs/db-review-active/*` index showed all six providers occupied while the live Codex worker tree showed zero active reviewer workers after GLM sequence 813 timed out and was aborted.\n\nActive records at 2026-09-01 16:14 UTC were: Codex sequence 797 (#2035), DeepSeek 808 (#1609), GLM 813 (#2054), Grok 809 (#1999), Kimi 747 (#1824), and Muse 801 (#1987).\n\n## Actually completed\n\n- Local incident `20260901T155739Z-edge-dev-reviewer-coordination-2741130` was recorded under `C:/repos/ai-devops/.ai/reviewer-issues/`.\n- DeepSeek 808 ended with an evidence-boundary block but no confirmed Critical/High code defect.\n- Grok 809 exhausted its turn limit with no verdict.\n- GLM 813 exceeded its documented 30-minute limit (34m41s), produced no verdict/findings, and was aborted.\n- No reviewer refs were manually deleted or bypassed.\n\n## Preview and production\n\nThis repository-maintenance incident applied nothing to preview or production. Separately, marker #2051 completed issue #2031 through production in workflow run 33519224144.\n\n## Half-finished / ownership\n\nNo repair branch or code exists for this incident. The open structural branches/worktrees remain owned by their existing claims: #1609/#1939, #1999/#2002, #1987/#1989, and #2054/#2057.\n\n## Next action\n\nStart a fresh repository-maintenance session. Reproduce the saturated-index state from immutable refs, implement atomic terminal-result release before replacement selection, reconcile stale records with compare-and-swap ownership proof, and add a six-slots-full recovery test. Success means #1609 and #1999 can obtain governed replacement reviewers without manual ref deletion.\n\n## Blockers\n\nThis is outside the structural orchestrator by owner ruling 2026-08-21. It must be handled by a separate repository-maintenance session.\n\n## What did not work\n\n- `--replace-failed-reviewer` for DeepSeek sequence 808 and Grok sequence 809 refused because every provider appeared occupied.\n- Posting a machine-recognizable `REVISE` verdict for GLM sequence 810 did not make replacement capacity available to the two other PRs.\n- Waiting did not help: finished or failed assignments remained in the bounded active index.\n\n## Facts that may go stale\n\nThe six active refs, PR heads, and exact pool state are a 2026-09-01 16:14 UTC snapshot. Re-read live refs and PR heads before repair.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 0\nwrites: []\nreads: []\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-01T19:42:54Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T16:31:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2058,"title":"HANDOVER: reviewer-capacity index reports six busy reviewers while none are running","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:25:35Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2058"},

{"body":"## Problem\n\n`--resume-author-lease` excludes the claim being resumed but still passes that claim's own open PR into `assertLaneAvailable`, so the PR is reported as a competing object owner. This blocks a safe refresh of #1987 / claim #1988 / PR #1989 after capacity was relinquished.\n\nRenewal already filters the target PR before the same collision check; resume needs the equivalent self-PR exclusion plus regression coverage. No claim, branch, PR, or database mutation was made after the refusal.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-01T18:46:46Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T13:52:22Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2055,"title":"resume-author-lease falsely collides with its own protected PR","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:25:38Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2055"},
{"body":"## Summary\r\n\r\n`20260831044913` fixed the row-fetch half of #1945 — that part is genuinely solved and fast. **Counting is not.** The facet-count path for an effective filter sits on the 8-second ceiling and flaps, so the PopDAM filter sidebar still errors for users, now intermittently instead of constantly. And `count=exact` over `filter_effective_assets` never completes, which is the shape the library list query needs for pagination.\r\n\r\nI have made no change to the shared database. All measurements below are read-only, production, real `authenticated` JWT (PopDAM viewer test account, 1Password `vibe_coding`), 2026-08-31.\r\n\r\n**Target proof:** `https://qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai.supabase.co`; `supabase migration list --linked` shows `20260831044913` in the Remote column.\r\n\r\n## Fixed — thank you, this is a real improvement\r\n\r\n| call | before | now |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| `filter_effective_assets`, 200 rows, no count | 500 @ 8.15 s | **200 @ 0.99 s** |\r\n| `filter_effective_assets`, 25 rows, no count | — | **200 @ 0.94 s** |\r\n| `get_filter_counts {}` (legacy path, warm) | 6.31 s | **200 @ 0.54 s** |\r\n\r\nThe inlining problem is gone.\r\n\r\n## Not fixed — 1. exact count over the contract never completes\r\n\r\n`POST /rest/v1/rpc/filter_effective_assets?select=*` with `Prefer: count=exact`:\r\n\r\n| range | count | result |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| `0-24` | none | 200 @ 0.94 s |\r\n| `0-24` | **exact** | **500 @ 8.07 s** |\r\n| `0-24` | planned | 200 @ 0.76 s |\r\n| `0-199` | none | 200 @ 0.99 s |\r\n| `0-199` | **exact** | **500 @ 8.07 s** |\r\n\r\nRow limit is irrelevant; `count=exact` alone decides it. This matters because `useAssets` needs a total for pagination. The 25-row bounded calls in the acceptance comment did not carry an exact count, which is why they passed.\r\n\r\n## Not fixed — 2. the delegating facet count flaps on the ceiling\r\n\r\n`get_filter_counts`, 8 consecutive calls each:\r\n\r\n| filter | passed | failed | observed times |\r\n|---|---|---|---|\r\n| `{\"licensorId\":\"154bf54b-…\"}` | 4 | **4** | 8.11, 8.06, 4.40, 8.10, 2.01, 4.34, 8.09, 2.94 |\r\n| `{\"tagFilter\":\"design asset\"}` | 7 | **1** | 5.13, 8.06, 5.88, 3.05, 0.84, 1.09, 1.51, 0.66 |\r\n\r\nFailures are `57014 canceling statement due to statement timeout`. A user filtering by licensor gets an error roughly half the time. This is the live regression from #1945 — narrowed, not closed.\r\n\r\n## A pointer that may explain the remaining cost\r\n\r\nAdding a filter makes counting **slower**, which is backwards:\r\n\r\n- `get_effective_filter_counts {}` → 200 @ 3.26 s\r\n- `get_effective_filter_counts {\"licensorId\":…}` → 500 @ 8.07 s\r\n\r\nAnd the tag filter, which resolves through the indexed `asset_effective_tags` projection via `exists (…)`, is consistently the faster of the two (0.66–1.5 s on most calls) while licensor is the slow one.\r\n\r\nThat is what I would expect if the identity predicate is unindexable. `filter_effective_assets` expresses it as:\r\n\r\n```sql\r\ncase when a.style_group_id is null then a.licensor_id else sg.licensor_id end = (p_filters ->> 'licensorId')::uuid\r\n```\r\n\r\nA `CASE` over two tables cannot use an index on either column, so it forces the full 135k-row join before counting. Rewriting it as a disjunction the planner can index —\r\n\r\n```sql\r\n(a.style_group_id is null and a.licensor_id = X)\r\nor (a.style_group_id is not null and sg.licensor_id = X)\r\n```\r\n\r\n— would let `assets(licensor_id)` and `style_groups(licensor_id)` be used. Same for `propertyId`. **Hypothesis, not a prescription** — I cannot run `EXPLAIN` as `authenticated`.\r\n\r\n## What would close this from PopDAM's side\r\n\r\n1. `count=exact` over `filter_effective_assets` completing inside the ceiling, **or** an agreed alternative for the list total (for example `get_effective_filter_counts` returning `total` reliably and fast, which the app would use instead of `count=exact`).\r\n2. `get_filter_counts` with an effective filter passing consistently, not 50% of the time. Please measure repeatedly rather than once — a single warm call passes.\r\n\r\nPlease record the measured `authenticated` timings and the pass rate over several consecutive calls so I can re-verify rather than assume.\r\n\r\n## PopDAM state\r\n\r\nUnchanged: the Step 7 wiring stays gated off behind `EFFECTIVE_SCOPE_CONTRACT_READY = false` in `src/hooks/useAssets.ts`. I will not enable it while the list total cannot be obtained and the sidebar count is intermittent.\r\n\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 0\r\ndepends_on: 2031\r\nwrites:\r\n  - function public.filter_effective_assets\r\n  - function public.get_effective_filter_counts\r\n  - function public.get_filter_counts\n  - function public.get_effective_filter_counts_unchecked_1703\r\nreads:\r\n  - table public.assets\r\n  - table public.style_groups\r\n  - table public.asset_effective_tags\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-02T05:21:59Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T13:45:33Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## The question for Albert\n\nYou asked, during the #1703 promotion on 2026-08-31: *\"Another session keeps landing docs commits on main — is there a way we can avoid/prevent this going forward?\"*\n\nThe answer is yes, and it is a small change. It was never built, because the promotion took the rest of the session. **Do you want it built?**\n\n## What is actually happening\n\nToday, when anything at all lands on `main`, a pull request in flight has to re-sync and re-run its checks. That is correct and necessary when the landing commit touches database code — the in-flight change may no longer be safe. It is pure waste when the landing commit only edits prose, because a Markdown file cannot change what a migration does.\n\nBecause handover documents and notes land on `main` constantly, in-flight database work keeps getting bounced for reasons that have nothing to do with it.\n\n## Proposed change\n\nMake the re-sync requirement conditional on **what the landing commits touched**: force it when they touch migrations, scripts, or workflows; skip it when every changed file is documentation.\n\nThis narrows a gate rather than removing one. That is why it is being asked rather than just done: the safe default is the current behaviour, and anything that makes a gate fire less often deserves a deliberate decision.\n\n## What is not being proposed\n\nBlocking or discouraging other sessions from landing documentation on `main`. Docs-only pull requests are merged promptly by design (`AGENTS.md` §5) and that should not change.\n\n## Where the detail is\n\n`HANDOFF.d/2026-09-01T1059Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-2026-path-b.md` §4.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-01T11:38:24Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T11:01:26Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2047,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] should the merge gate stop bouncing in-flight work for docs-only commits on main?","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:25:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2047"},
{"body":"Three reviewer-wrapper defects hit during the #1703 / #2004 promotion (marker #2026). Each cost a full reviewer rotation. None is a shared-db structural change; this is repo/tooling maintenance, filed here so it is not lost.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\n1. **`ai-deepseek-agent` hits an argv length limit on Windows.** A review packet large enough to be useful exceeds it. The wrapper should read the message from a file rather than the command line.\n2. **`muse-spark-1.2-contributor` returns HTTP 404.** The reviewer is in the durable round robin and is currently unusable, so every assignment that lands on it burns a rotation slot and needs `--replace-failed-reviewer`. Either fix the endpoint or take it out of the pool.\n3. **`.ai/deepseek-sessions/` is not in `.gitignore`.** `.gitignore` covers `.ai/reviews/*` but not this sibling directory, so DeepSeek review transcripts show up as untracked noise in every session that runs one. Add the ignore entry.\n\nRelated, already open: #1833 (rotation cannot express \"unusable for this PR\", only \"failed\") — item 2 is a live instance of exactly that gap.\n\n## Where the detail is\n\n`HANDOFF.d/2026-09-01T1059Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-2026-path-b.md` §8, items 11 and §5.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T21:35:35Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T11:01:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Two schema observations recorded while promoting the HTS RAG durable precedent contract (#2004/#2009, live on production as `20260831234750` + `20260901011306`). Neither blocked the promotion; both are real and neither has an owner.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\n1. **`hts_rag_determinations.precedent_id` has a foreign key with no supporting index.** Every delete or update on the parent table has to scan the child. Decide whether the access pattern justifies an index and, if so, ship one.\n\n2. **`operative_eligible` does not require a `proposed_hts`.** A row can be marked operative-eligible while carrying no proposed classification, which is very likely not the intended contract. Confirm the intent with whoever owns the RAG determination flow, then either add the constraint or record explicitly that the permissive form is deliberate.\n\nItem 2 is the one with real consequences — it is a data-integrity gap in a contract that is already live, so the longer it stands the more rows may need reconciling.\n\n## Where the detail is\n\n`HANDOFF.d/2026-09-01T1059Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-2026-path-b.md`, and the merged bodies of `supabase/migrations/20260831234750_*.sql` and `20260901011306_*.sql`.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table public.hts_rag_determinations\nreads:\n  - table public.hts_rag_precedents\n```\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T12:59:56Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T11:01:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Production catalog verification was repaired in PR #2042 (merged as `92cba695`) so it understands a `DROP INDEX` that removes an index created earlier in the same ordered batch. Two gaps were left open deliberately at that time, because closing them was not needed to unblock the frozen #1703/#2004 promotion.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\n1. **Pin the real batch in CI.** The two tests added in PR #2042 use a synthetic single-file fixture. Nothing in CI exercises the actual two-file batch (`20260831234750` + `20260901011306`) that motivated the repair. A regression that re-broke the batch case would pass the suite.\n2. **Add absence assertions.** The verifier only asserts that expected objects are *present*. It has no way to assert that a dropped object is genuinely *gone*. An index that survives a legitimate `DROP INDEX` therefore passes silently. This is pre-existing, not introduced by #2042, but the drop-index work is what exposed it.\n\n## Where the detail is\n\n`HANDOFF.d/2026-09-01T1059Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-2026-path-b.md` §10, and the merged diff of PR #2042.\n\nRelevant files: `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py` (`DROP_INDEX_RE`, `derive_targets`), `scripts/test_production_catalog_verification.py`.\n\nNote that `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json` pins a sha256 of the detector source. Any change to the detector must regenerate that digest, and the regeneration must be justified by proving the marker inventory unchanged — not simply overwritten.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-04T06:07:21Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T11:01:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## What happened\n\n`supabase/migrations/20260831234750_hts_rag_durable_precedent_contract.sql` was applied to preview by run 33454217961 at 2026-09-01T00:19Z, from PR #2009 head `bb77fdd4`.\n\nAt 00:27Z a second session pushed commit `461d40ec` to the same PR, which **edited that same migration file**: two CHECK regexes widened, four constraints added, one index dropped, two grants widened, a column-scoped UPDATE grant added, and one `FOR ALL` policy split into three. PR #2009 then merged as `30221c0b`.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nAGENTS.md is explicit: *never edit a migration that has already been applied anywhere*. A version can be applied only once, so:\n\n- preview permanently holds the **pre-edit** body of `20260831234750`;\n- `main` holds the **post-edit** body;\n- the preview rehearsal pinned to run 33454217961 therefore rehearsed SQL that no longer exists, and must not be cited as evidence for the production promotion of this version.\n\nThere was also a duplicate-orchestrator condition at the time: the marker resolved solely to route `local_356c2f5c-…` (issue #2026), and the session that pushed `461d40ec` held no marker.\n\n## Remedy in progress\n\nA forward alignment migration at a newly reserved version, written to be a no-op where the merged shape already exists, so preview and production converge on the same shape. Production promotion of `20260831234750` will disclose that its own preview rehearsal ran an earlier body rather than reusing that evidence as if it were current.\n\n## Governance gap to close\n\nNothing refuses a push that modifies a migration file already present in the preview ledger. That check is mechanical and belongs in the pull-request guards.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-08T14:57:31Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T01:14:10Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2037,"title":"Incident: migration 20260831234750 was edited AFTER it had been applied to preview (AGENTS.md 6.x rule 4)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:25:58Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2037"},

{"body":"Follow-on to #2004 (PR #2009, merged as `30221c0b669fe3954a874d584db94d9e09d756ae`).\n\n## The problem, proven from both ends\n\nPreview applied `20260831234750` in run `33454217961` from PR #2009 commit `bb77fdd49fe032c985dc93c907f5d4d93a2456a1` — the body **before** the two High review findings were fixed.\n\n- Preview content manifest records `20260831234750` = `2931391a44f512ec80fe468b00c3b92c277397418e5fda25fa98907dad6559cb`\n- Exact main carries `356e2c4d1ac4e64e3a47ff70ec4e97132c3ca52dbdacbe66af4442242994d470`\n\nConsequences, both verified in code:\n\n1. `production_business_risk_gate.prove_preview_migration_contents` (\"BIND THE BYTES, NOT THE COMMIT\") refuses promotion: *preview rehearsed different bytes than exact main*.\n2. `production_migration_guard.validate_candidates` refuses a second preview apply of the same version (run `33456937617`: `BLOCKED: already applied on production: 20260831234750`, which for a preview target means already applied on preview).\n3. `preview_ledger_orphan_reconcile.py` mode `rehearsal_reset` does **not** fit: it requires the live preview ledger statements to equal the merged file's statements (they differ), and it deletes only a ledger row, leaving the seven tables in place.\n\nSo the seven `hts_rag_*` tables exist on preview from the superseded body. Any route that re-runs `create table` on preview fails.\n\n## The route\n\nFix forward with an ALTER-level delta, and make main's `20260831234750` tell the truth about what every database actually ran.\n\n1. **Restore** `supabase/migrations/20260831234750_hts_rag_durable_precedent_contract.sql` to the exact bytes preview applied (`bb77fdd4`, sha256 `2931391a…`). This is a code-truth restoration in the sense of `scripts/historical-migration-restorations.mjs` (see its existing `20260824150630` `previewProject` entry), not an edit that changes any database. Register it there; the current validator assumes a single-statement file and must be extended to multi-statement restorations without weakening any digest check.\n2. **Add a new reserved version** carrying the corrective delta, exactly reproducing the merged contract:\n   - `hts_rag_precedents` and `hts_rag_determinations`: drop and re-add the `proposed_hts` check as `^[0-9]{4}([.][0-9]{2}){0,3}$`\n   - add `hts_rag_determinations_shadow_precedent_chk`\n   - add `hts_rag_extraction_jobs_pending_unclaimed_chk`, `_active_claim_chk`, `_success_result_chk`\n   - drop index `hts_rag_product_family_allowlist_enabled_idx`\n   - `grant select` on `hts_rag_extraction_jobs` and `hts_rag_product_family_allowlist` to `authenticated`\n   - `grant update (comparison_review_state) on public.hts_rag_determinations to service_role`\n   - drop policy `hts_rag_determinations_backend_all`; create `_backend_read`, `_backend_insert`, `_backend_review`\n   - update the `hts_rag_determinations` table comment\n3. Carry the merged contract test `supabase/tests/hts_rag_durable_precedent_contract.sql` forward unchanged — it already asserts the *final* state and so is the acceptance test for the delta.\n\n## Promotion plan (two sequential single-version production runs)\n\n- `20260831234750` promotes on the existing preview evidence (run `33454217961`, artifact `9780872485`), which after step 1 matches main byte for byte.\n- The delta version promotes on its own fresh preview run.\n- Order is fixed: `20260831234750` first.\n\n## Constraints\n\n- Do not weaken any guard, digest check, or threshold to make this pass.\n- Do not drop or recreate the seven tables on preview.\n- Final production schema must be byte-equivalent in effect to the merged `30221c0b` contract.\n\n```machine\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nobjects: table public.hts_rag_precedents, table public.hts_rag_determinations, table public.hts_rag_extraction_jobs, table public.hts_rag_product_family_allowlist, policy hts_rag_determinations_backend_all on public.hts_rag_determinations, policy hts_rag_determinations_backend_read on public.hts_rag_determinations, policy hts_rag_determinations_backend_insert on public.hts_rag_determinations, policy hts_rag_determinations_backend_review on public.hts_rag_determinations, index public.hts_rag_product_family_allowlist_enabled_idx\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-01T03:07:18Z","createdAt":"2026-09-01T01:12:35Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2035,"title":"HTS RAG precedent contract: reconcile preview rehearsal with merged body (follow-on to #2004)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:47:38Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2035"},
{"body":"## Application\n\nPopDAM (`u2giants/popdam3`) follow-up to PopDAM #97 and shared-db #1703.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe production `public.search_dam_documents(text,jsonb,integer,integer,text[],vector,real)` contract now provides authorization-safe ranked pagination, counts, facets, and Style Group rollup. However, its `p_filters` implementation does not yet cover the full active PopDAM library filter contract, so the app cannot safely activate ranked pagination without applying some filters after pagination.\n\nMissing/currently incompatible filters:\n\n- canonical `customerId` UUID, matched to `assets.customer_id` / `style_groups.customer_id`; the current `customer` key is legacy path-derived text\n- `contentType`\n- `productMaterial`\n- `fileStatus` (`has_preview`, `no_preview_renderable`, `no_pdf_compat`, `no_preview_unsupported`)\n- `productCategory` (the app's existing folder-path category semantics)\n\n## Required structural change\n\nExtend the ranked-search filter contract to accept the keys above and apply them before ranking, offset, limit, `total_count`, `has_more`, and facet calculation. Preserve all existing #1703 filters and behavior. Avoid changing the legacy `customer` meaning unless compatibility is explicitly proven; add `customerId` as the canonical key.\n\nKeep `filter_effective_assets` / filter-count behavior compatible with canonical customer IDs where the same payload is accepted.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- Authenticated DAM caller: each new filter independently and in combination returns only matching rows.\n- Canonical `customerId` uses the UUID relationship, not legacy customer text.\n- Ranked page 1/page 2 have no duplicates and concatenate to the same ordering as a larger equivalent call.\n- `total_count`, `has_more`, and returned facets remain in parity with the filtered population.\n- Asset results and Style Group rollups both obey applicable filters.\n- Non-DAM authenticated caller remains denied.\n- Cold production runtime remains under eight seconds with headroom for a representative filtered ranked query.\n- Evidence is privacy-safe: timings/counts/booleans only, no row values.\n\n## Routing\n\nStructural shared-database work. Preview first; production only after preview acceptance and the active production freeze is lifted by the owner/orchestrator.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function public.search_dam_documents\n  - function public.filter_effective_assets\n  - function public.get_effective_filter_counts\nreads:\n  - table public.assets\n  - table public.style_groups\n```\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-01T14:27:02Z","createdAt":"2026-08-31T23:58:31Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2031,"title":"Complete PopDAM ranked-search filter parity","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:26:01Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2031"},
{"body":"The historical preview recovery record embeds `mainSha`, and `production_business_risk_gate.py` re-derives the record at the CURRENT main and refuses on any difference (`historical preview source proof does not match current governed evidence`).\n\nDuring the #1703 promotion this voided the evidence twice in twenty minutes. Both invalidating commits were documentation-only (#2027 and #2028) and touched no SQL, no migration, and nothing the recovery record actually proves. Each time, the full chain had to be regenerated — review evidence, recovery evidence, then apply — roughly ten minutes per cycle. A repository with several active sessions can invalidate a promotion faster than the promotion can complete, and nothing in the lane model stops it: the exclusive production lock does not freeze merges to main.\n\nTwo things are worth separating here. The gate is right to bind evidence to exact content. It is not obviously right to bind it to exact main when the content it proves is a fixed set of migration files, whose bytes could be pinned directly.\n\nScope block:\n```\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\n```\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:21:29Z","createdAt":"2026-08-31T23:46:10Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2030,"title":"Historical preview recovery evidence is pinned to main, so any unrelated commit voids it mid-promotion","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:26:03Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2030"},
{"body":"During the #1703 promotion (run `33451271767`) the ordered batch `20260831184547, 20260831212757, 20260831221607` applied correctly, but the post-apply catalog verification failed the job.\n\nEvery migration's sidecar contract is asserted against the FINAL database state. Forward 6's contract `popdam_ranked_search_private_keyed_visibility_v2` asserts strings from forward 6's own `search_dam_documents` body — a body that forwards 7 and 8 deliberately replace later in the same batch. Forward 7's and forward 8's contracts both PASSED; only the superseded intermediate one failed.\n\nSo the gate reports a red job for a correct promotion, and the operator has to read three contract rows to tell a real failure from a designed supersession. Worse, a genuine failure now looks like the benign case.\n\nThe verifier needs to know that a contract belongs to a version later versions in the SAME allowlist supersede — either by only asserting the last contract that touches each object, or by letting a sidecar declare the version that supersedes it.\n\nScope block:\n```\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\n```\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-04T06:07:19Z","createdAt":"2026-08-31T23:46:00Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2029,"title":"Production catalog verification fails a superseded intermediate contract in a multi-version batch","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:26:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2029"},

{"body":"Issue #1703 exposed that the from-empty pass-2 routine restorer preserves `pg_get_functiondef` but loses default `SECURITY INVOKER` and empty `proconfig` state when an older migration overwrites a later routine. That can make the rebuilt catalog differ from the real ordered end state and can silently disable SQL-function inlining.\n\nSeveral attempted corrections revealed why this needs its own repository-maintenance change and real database coverage rather than more generator substring assertions:\n\n- literal backslash-n output became an invalid psql command;\n- reconstructing `search_path=public, extensions` as one quoted value broke vector operator lookup;\n- unconditional `RESET ALL` failed when the replayed migration dropped a snapshotted overload;\n- combined contract diagnostics obscured which catalog invariant failed.\n\nImplement the smallest generic algorithm:\n\n1. Snapshot every exact live overload for a colliding function/procedure using schema, name, full identity arguments, and `prokind`.\n2. After replaying the older migration, reset configuration only when that exact routine still exists.\n3. Replay PostgreSQL's own `pg_get_functiondef` output so PostgreSQL owns all `SET` syntax, including multi-schema search paths.\n4. Explicitly restore saved `SECURITY INVOKER` or `SECURITY DEFINER` after creation because default invoker is omitted from `pg_get_functiondef`.\n5. Skip only the unnecessary reset for an absent overload; its saved definition must recreate it or fail. Do not swallow errors, reconstruct `SET` from `proconfig`, quarantine failures, or weaken catalog assertions.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n\n- Add a live ephemeral-PostgreSQL test, not only Python string tests.\n- Prove configured predecessor to invoker plus `proconfig IS NULL`.\n- Prove `SET search_path = public, extensions` and the vector `<=>` operator survive restoration.\n- Prove two overloads where the replay drops one: the existing overload resets, the dropped one is recreated, and identities do not cross.\n- Prove procedure handling and real newline-separated executable SQL.\n- Prove unexpected reset/create/security errors still fail the job.\n- Keep the generator unit tests as smoke coverage.\n- Merge this independently before issue #1703's structural PR relies on the final catalog result.\n\nThis is repository-maintenance work. It is not a database structure or data change and must be implemented in a fresh isolated repository-maintenance session, outside the structural orchestrator.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites: scripts/check_pass2_routine_supersession.py, scripts/test_check_pass2_routine_supersession.py, .github/workflows/database-contract-tests.yml\nreads: supabase/migrations/, supabase/tests/\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-04T02:35:13Z","createdAt":"2026-08-31T20:21:17Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2014,"title":"Prove pass-2 routine restoration in live PostgreSQL","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:26:17Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2014"},
{"body":"Addressed to the running shared-db orchestrator. Albert confirmed on 2026-08-31 that an orchestrator session is live in Codex; direct `codex-reply` dispatch to the address declared by marker #2000 (route_id `01a058e1-1004-79b1-a31d-9705c5c38fab`) returns \"Session not found for thread_id\", so this issue is the delivery channel instead. See #2000 for the failed-dispatch note.\n\n## What I need\n\nTwo pieces of structural work, **in this order**. Both are already specified; this issue exists to get them picked up, not to restate them.\n\n### 1. #1999 — Marvel tie-breaker amendment (do first)\n\nAmend the fail-closed rule introduced by `supabase/migrations/20260830130345_opa_authority_for_dcp_creative.sql` so that `contract_asserted_studio_code = 'marvel'` against `opa_studio_code = 'disney'` is **not** treated as `contract_opa_conflict`.\n\n### 2. #2007 — the review queue itself (depends on #1999)\n\n- `api.db_data_admin_property_match_queue(p_search text, p_cursor text, p_page_size int)`\n- `api.db_data_admin_decide_property_match(p_resolution_id uuid, p_decision text, p_licensed_property_ids bigint[], p_reason text, p_operation_id uuid)`\n- Load the pending `decision_version = 1` rows into `plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution` and `plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member`\n\nFull column contract, return shapes, and the constraint list are in **#2007**. Candidate data source is the private repo `u2giants/licensor-source-data`, `reconciliation/opa-contract-match-20260831/` — read it there; no licensed rows appear in any issue.\n\n## Why it is ordered that way\n\nIf #2007 lands first, every Marvel property approved through the new screen still presents as a conflict, because OPA has no `marvel` branch to agree with. The reviewers would be making correct decisions that the site then contradicts. #1999 has to be in place before the queue is populated.\n\n## Why the work exists at all\n\nOPA carries only two creation branches, `disney` (1,445 Properties) and `lucasfilm` (74). When Disney moved Marvel product submissions off ASGARD into OPA, Marvel was folded into the `disney` branch instead of getting its own the way Lucasfilm did. I verified there is no hidden back-end separator: sample Marvel and Disney Properties are identical on region, line of business, product type, template and workflow, and `plm.opa_property_scope_membership` holds only the two branches.\n\nOwner ruling, Albert Hazan, 2026-08-31 — merged in #1991, `docs/business-rules/licensing-master-data.md`, section \"OPA cannot separate Marvel from Disney\" — makes the signed K2557 contract schedule controlling for that split. A controlling contract requires a recorded, per-Property, human decision, which is what this queue is.\n\nToday every DCP Vault Property on data.designflow.app reads `DCP Creative - unresolved authority`, because `plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution` has zero rows. That is not a pending human review — it is unfinished wiring. This work is what finishes it.\n\n## What is already done, so it is not repeated\n\n- #1991 — the business rule, merged\n- #2006 — the reviewer UI, merged (`apps/db-data-admin/src/PropertyMatchReview.tsx`, documented at `docs/db-data-admin-property-match-review.md`). It detects the missing RPCs (`PGRST202` / `42883`) and shows \"not enabled on this database yet\", so it is safe in production right now and lights up on its own the moment the RPCs exist. No app change is needed after your work — just the migration.\n- The contract-to-OPA-to-Vault-to-ASGARD name crosswalk, in the private repo above: 148 contract clauses matched against 1,519 OPA Properties, 325 DCP Vault names and 75 ASGARD guides, with 53 rows flagged for human decision.\n\n## What I need back\n\nAn acknowledgement on this issue that it has been picked up — a prior dispatch was lost to silent non-delivery and nothing reported it.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-31T20:57:30Z","createdAt":"2026-08-31T20:14:27Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":2013,"title":"DISPATCH: build the property-match review queue (#1999 then #2007) — orchestrator pickup requested","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:47:41Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/2013"},

{"body":"DesignFlow Step 1 has completed the required pilot-first schema-bounding slice. The privacy-safe evidence is in popcre/designflow-backend commit `0c17d75`, `docs/verification/hts-rag/pilot/20260831T173059Z/schema-bounding-summary.md`; raw provider output and CBP bodies remain private.\n\nOutcome: land the minimum additive shared Supabase contract needed for structured ruling extraction, precedent evidence, immutable RAG-versus-legacy comparisons, review history, database-backed extraction jobs, and disabled-by-default family allowlisting. Do not add embeddings in this change: `vector` is installed, but no representative retrieval benchmark has selected it.\n\nPilot-bounded requirements:\n\n- Permit incomplete HTS headings with an explicit needs-more-facts state; never require or invent a 10-digit code.\n- Store positive attributes, negative attributes, exclusions, missing critical facts, and conflicts separately from a confidence number.\n- Keep the classifier's provisional citation claim distinct from the final reviewed relationship. Final relationship values are exactly `relied_on`, `supporting`, `contrasting`, or `background`.\n- Keep ruling existence, source lifecycle/status, verifier relevance, and final relationship distinct. Unknown source status stays unknown; model opinion cannot promote it to active.\n- Distinguish decision-card candidacy from eligibility for an operative classification.\n- Preserve immutable comparison history plus append-only review events.\n- Persist prompt/model/extraction versions and fixture/input/full-text/raw-result hashes for idempotency and reproducibility.\n- Use a database-backed extraction job because the measured classifier slice took about two minutes; required audit work cannot be untracked fire-and-forget processing.\n- Backend-only runtime writes and authorized admin read/review. No direct browser writes to these tables.\n- Additive and backward-compatible with existing `public.hts_rag_rulings`; legacy AI/CROSS remains operative and auto-recommend remains off.\n- Include migration assertions covering columns, constraints, policies, grants, indexes, idempotency, append-only behavior, and rollback on assertion failure.\n\nThe author must finalize concrete columns from this evidence, remove speculative fields, update generated types through the standard generator, apply/verify preview first, obtain exact-head review, merge through the guarded path, promote through the governed production gate, and prove the exact production catalog/ledger without reading application rows.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 92\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  -
