{"body":"## What  Amend the Disney-family authority expression in `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text, text, integer)` so that, **for the Disney-versus-Marvel split only**, a contract-asserted studio code of `marvel` against an OPA scope studio code of `disney` is **not** treated as `contract_opa_conflict`.  Function last changed by `supabase/migrations/20260830130345_opa_authority_for_dcp_creative.sql` (issue #1658, production-live 2026-08-30).  ## Why  Owner ruling, Albert Hazan, 2026-08-31, already merged into `docs/business-rules/licensing-master-data.md` (PR #1991, merge commit `eece8554261a92dde1428dca3965d4d47ab683b2`), section **\"OPA cannot separate Marvel from Disney\"**.  When Disney moved Marvel product submissions out of ASGARD into OPA, Marvel was merged into the Disney creation branch rather than given its own branch. Lucasfilm / Star Wars kept its own branch. Verified against captured production data, not assumed: `plm.opa_property_scope_membership` contains exactly two branch values, `disney` (1,445 Properties) and `lucasfilm` (74). Marvel Properties (Avengers 709, Black Panther Movie - No Likeness 1069, Deadpool Classic 1108) sit under `disney` and are identical to non-Marvel Disney Properties (Muppets 333, Mickey Mouse 372, Frozen 777) on every other captured axis — region, line of business, product type, template, workflow.  Consequence: OPA branch membership can prove a Property is *not* Lucasfilm, but can never distinguish Marvel from Disney. Under the current expression, every Marvel Property that ever gets a resolution row will read `contract_opa_conflict` forever, because OPA will always say `disney`. That is a permanent false conflict, not a real disagreement.  ## Exact change requested  In the authority `case` expression, the branch  ```sql when r.contract_asserted_studio_code is not null   and o.opa_studio_code is not null   and r.contract_asserted_studio_code <> o.opa_studio_code   then 'contract_opa_conflict' ```  must not fire when `r.contract_asserted_studio_code = 'marvel'` and `o.opa_studio_code = 'disney'`. In that one combination the contract wins and the result is `direct_marvel`.  Everything else is unchanged:  - `opa_scope_conflict` (more than one OPA scope) still fires first and still wins. - Lucasfilm / Star Wars keeps the existing agree-or-stop rule. A contract   assertion of `lucasfilm` against an OPA scope of `disney` (or the reverse)   remains `contract_opa_conflict`. - Pixar is unchanged. - Where there is no contract assertion, direct OPA scope still places the   Property exactly as it does today. - Marvel Creative Asset authority is unchanged and remains ASGARD.  ## Objects touched  - `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text, text, integer)` — replace in place,   same signature, via `pg_get_functiondef` + targeted `replace()` as the   2026-08-30 migration did.  No table, column, constraint, index, or policy changes. No data changes. `plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution` and `plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member` are both still empty in production, so this migration cannot change any currently displayed row — it only removes a false conflict that would otherwise appear the moment the first Marvel resolution row is approved.  ## Requested by  Working session on `u2giants/licensor-source-data`, branch `claude/dcp-creative-authority-decision-5c4328`. The supporting contract-to-OPA name crosswalk that will eventually populate the resolution table is committed there under `reconciliation/opa-contract-match-20260831/` (private repo; no licensed rows are reproduced in this issue). \n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 0\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties\nreads:\n  - table plm.opa_property_scope_membership\n  - table plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution\n  - table plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-02T04:17:23Z","createdAt":"2026-08-31T17:25:57Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1999,"title":"Marvel/Disney tie-breaker: contract wins over OPA branch in scraped-properties authority","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:26:30Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1999"},

{"body":"# HANDOVER: DesignFlow item ownership and action history for reliable notifications\n\nDesignFlow needs production-safe workflow notifications. Today an RFQ step change can notify every user whose `users.level` matches the step, while the item does not reliably retain the specific user who sent it to a department. The legacy frontend also persists the step separately from the notification call, so actor and handoff history are not a trustworthy routing source.\n\n## Required business behavior\n\n- An item can have one or more named users assigned for each business function/department involved in that item.\n- Every workflow action records the authenticated acting user on the server, the item, the action/step transition, and time.\n- When Sales changes an RFQ item to `@sourcing`, notify the assigned Sourcing user(s), not every Sourcing account.\n- When Sourcing changes it to `px sent to sales`, notify the Sales user who originally handed that item to Sourcing. Preserve the historical sender even if current assignments later change.\n- Support reassignment and multiple participating functions without adding a new column for every department.\n- Keep notification creation and the step/action write atomic or otherwise idempotent so retries do not duplicate alerts and failures do not leave a changed step with no corresponding event.\n- Existing RFQ rows must remain valid. Define a safe backfill/fallback policy without guessing ownership from ambiguous history.\n\n## Proposed structural direction\n\nPlease design the canonical shared-db contract for:\n\n1. item-to-user functional assignments, with item identity, function/department key, user identity, active/effective history, assignor, and timestamps;\n2. immutable item workflow actions, with authenticated actor, prior/new step, routing context/correlation key, and timestamp;\n3. notification linkage/idempotency needed to trace each notification to its action and recipient.\n\nThe exact table/RPC names are the orchestrator's design decision. Prefer normalized relationships and server-owned actor identity. Do not rely on client-supplied user IDs or overwrite history.\n\n## Existing objects and application follow-up\n\n- Existing RFQ item: `dflow.\"RFQItem\"`\n- Existing users: `dflow.users`\n- Existing steps: `dflow.\"RFQStep\"`\n- Existing notifications: `dflow.user_notification`\n- Existing generic audit history: `dflow.\"AuditLog\"` (inspect for compatibility; do not assume it is sufficient)\n- After the shared contract lands, the DesignFlow backend/frontend session will replace broad department fan-out, record transitions server-side, add assignment management, tests, and end-to-end browser proof.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 90\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table dflow.item_user_assignment\n  - table dflow.item_workflow_action\n  - table dflow.user_notification\n  - column dflow.user_notification.workflow_action_id\n  - column dflow.user_notification.idempotency_key\n  - function dflow.current_designflow_user_id\n  - function dflow.record_item_workflow_action\n  - function dflow.set_item_user_assignment\n  - function dflow.reject_item_assignment_history_rewrite\n  - function dflow.reject_item_workflow_action_rewrite\n  - trigger item_user_assignment_immutable_history on dflow.item_user_assignment\n  - trigger item_workflow_action_immutable on dflow.item_workflow_action\n  - index dflow.item_user_assignment_one_active\n  - index dflow.item_user_assignment_active_lookup\n  - index dflow.item_workflow_action_item_time\n  - index dflow.user_notification_action_recipient\n  - index dflow.user_notification_idempotency_key\nreads:\n  - table dflow.RFQItem\n  - table dflow.RFQStep\n  - table dflow.users\n  - table dflow.AuditLog\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-02T03:16:34Z","createdAt":"2026-08-31T15:08:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1987,"title":"HANDOVER: DesignFlow item ownership and action history for reliable notifications","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:26:44Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1987"},

{"body":"PR #1853 is exact-current-base and all checks are green, but governed DeepSeek sequence 718 correctly returned BLOCKED because the Windows review launch could not carry the complete full-range evidence packet. The migration and focused test fit, but adding both complete authoritative base migrations exceeded the Windows process argument-list limit. The reviewer therefore could not independently prove faithful full-body re-derivation.\n\nThis is a repository-maintenance transport defect, not a structural defect in #1772/#1863 and not permission to reduce review coverage. {"body":"After three terminal reviewer providers on PR #1899, the next governed `--replace-failed-reviewer` call refuses before mutex acquisition:\n\n`reviewer operation cannot fit 11 remaining requests inside the 22-request budget; refused before mutex acquisition`\n\nThis is not unavoidable per-call spend. The first replacement path is tested at 8 pre-mutex requests. Each prior replacement row currently adds two more wire reads because `readReviewRecords` lists matching refs without their commit messages, then the replacement path separately reads each replacement commit and its failure ref. With two prior replacements, pre-mutex spend grows to 12, so the fixed 11-request mutex reserve can never fit.\n\nClosed issue #1911 / PR #1918 fixed the same refusal for merged-head target/evidence rereads, but did not address linear growth across a terminal-provider replacement chain. Live issue and PR history was searched before filing; no open issue covers this chain-growth defect.\n\nPreserve the 22-request ceiling, 11-request mutex reserve, every failure/verdict/exact-head/ref ownership guard, and immutable chain evidence. Batch or cache only immutable replacement/failure records; mutable issue, PR, lease, mutex, cursor, and exact-head state must still be re-read where currently required. {"body":"## Structural prerequisite\n\nDB Data Admin needs a narrow authenticated API function to set `core.property.status` between `active` and `inactive` without bypassing the existing licensing write-authority trigger.\n\nCurrent main has no Property-update RPC. Direct updates are correctly refused unless an exact transaction-bound authorization is created and consumed. The function must preserve that guard, create only the bounded authorization needed for this one Property/status change, consume it in the same transaction, and retain auditable evidence. It must not load the 66 ColdLion rows or implement the UI; those remain issue #1322 repo-session/curated work.\n\nNo licensed row values are included.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_set_property_status\nreads:\n  - table core.property\n  - function app.enforce_licensing_write_authority\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-31T03:51:06Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T22:30:41Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Summary\n\n`20260830110517_popdam_effective_asset_filters.sql` is in production, and the contract it ships **cannot run inside the 8-second `authenticated` ceiling**. Acceptance criterion 6 of #1645 is not met.\n\nWorse, this is not only a \"cannot wire it yet\" problem. `get_filter_counts` was replaced by the same migration and now delegates whenever an effective filter is present, so **the PopDAM library returns 500 today, with no application change, for any user who filters by licensor, property, or tag.** That path is reachable from the normal filter sidebar.\n\nI have made no change to the shared database. Everything below is read-only measurement against production.\n\n## Target proof\n\n`https://qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai.supabase.co` (production). `supabase migration list --linked` against `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` lists `20260830110517` in the Remote column.\n\n## How measured\n\nReal `authenticated` JWT (PopDAM viewer test account, credentials in 1Password `vibe_coding`), PostgREST, production, 2026-08-30. Not `postgres`, not preview.\n\n## Evidence — `get_filter_counts`\n\n| call | HTTP | time |\n|---|---|---|\n| `{}` (legacy covering-index path) | 200 | **6.31 s** |\n| `{\"fileType\":[\"psd\"]}` (legacy path) | 200 | 0.77 s |\n| `{\"licensorId\":\"154bf54b-…\"}` (delegates) | **500** | **8.10 s** |\n| `{\"tagFilter\":\"design asset\"}` (delegates) | **500** | **8.09 s** |\n\nBoth failures return `{\"code\":\"57014\",\"message\":\"canceling statement due to statement timeout\"}`.\n\nNote the first row as well: the legacy no-filter path is at **6.31 s** against an 8 s ceiling. That was ~260 ms when `idx_assets_facet_counts` was introduced. Whether or not it is related to this migration, it has very little headroom left.\n\n## Evidence — `filter_effective_assets`\n\n`POST /rest/v1/rpc/filter_effective_assets?select=id&limit=200`, `Range: 0-199`, `Prefer: count=exact`:\n\n| payload | HTTP | time (3 runs) |\n|---|---|---|\n| `{\"licensorId\":\"154bf54b-…\"}` | 500 | 8.11 / 8.09 / 8.06 s |\n| `{\"tagFilter\":\"design asset\"}` | 500 | 8.06 / 8.07 / 8.07 s |\n| both | 500 | 8.07 / 8.06 / 8.07 s |\n| **`{}` — no filter at all** | **500** | **8.15 s** |\n\nThe empty-payload row is the important one: it is not a selectivity problem. The function cannot return the **first 200 rows** of the library within 8 s even when nothing is being filtered.\n\n## Likely root cause\n\n`filter_effective_assets` is `language sql`, `stable`, `returns setof public.assets` — which would normally be inlined, letting PostgREST's `LIMIT 200` push down into the scan. But it also carries `set search_path = public`. **A SQL function with a `SET` clause cannot be inlined by PostgreSQL.** So every call materialises the full `assets ⋈ style_groups` result — 135,451 assets — before the outer limit is applied. That matches the observed behaviour exactly: constant ~8 s regardless of filter selectivity, including with no filter.\n\n`get_effective_filter_counts` then wraps the same function in a `with base as materialized (...)`, so it inherits the same cost.\n\nIf that diagnosis is right, the fix is small: drop the `SET search_path` from `filter_effective_assets` so it can inline (schema-qualifying every reference inside the body instead), and re-measure. Please treat that as a hypothesis to test, not a prescription — I could not run `EXPLAIN` as `authenticated`.\n\n## Scale context (production, read-only)\n\n`assets` 135,451 · `asset_effective_tags` 1,022,852 · `asset_tags` 2,172,534 · `style_groups` 13,050 · `style_group_tags` **0**.\n\n`style_group_tags` being empty matters: no group tag exists in production yet, because the PopDAM group-profiling pilot has not run. So these timings are the **best case** — the effective join has no group-tag rows to resolve at all, and it still times out.\n\n## What I am asking for\n\n1. Treat the `get_filter_counts` delegation as a live production regression and decide quickly whether to restore the previous behaviour for that entry point while the performance work is done. PopDAM users are hitting 500s on the filter sidebar now.\n2. Re-open the acceptance-criterion-6 gate on #1645: cold `authenticated` timing was named as the next step on 2026-08-27 and 2026-08-27T21:54, but no comment on the issue ever recorded it. The catalog-presence and ledger evidence is thorough; the timing evidence is absent.\n3. When it is fixed, please record the measured `authenticated` timings so I can re-verify rather than assume.\n\n## PopDAM state\n\nThe application half of #96 Step 7 is deployed and unaffected — the detail panels read `get_effective_asset_metadata` and do not touch this contract. I have written and tested the wiring for `filter_effective_assets` but I am **not** shipping it, because it would convert every tag/licensor/property filter into a 500. It will land once this is fixed and re-measured.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 2900\ndepends_on: 1645\nwrites:\n  - function public.filter_effective_assets\n  - function public.get_effective_filter_counts\n  - function public.get_filter_counts\nreads:\n  - table public.assets\n  - table public.style_groups\n  - table public.asset_effective_tags\n  - table public.asset_tags\n  - table public.style_group_tags\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-31T05:59:11Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T21:45:15Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1945,"title":"PRODUCTION REGRESSION: 20260830110517 effective filters exceed the 8s authenticated ceiling; get_filter_counts now 500s on licensor/property/tag","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:27:11Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1945"},

{"body":"# Production incident\n\nAlbert reported that **Scraped Properties** on `https://data.designflow.app` fails with `canceling statement due to statement timeout`.\n\nRead-only production evidence confirms the exact failure on project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`:\n\n- 2026-08-30 21:24:03 UTC: authenticated `POST /rpc/db_data_admin_scraped_properties` returned HTTP 500.\n- PostgreSQL SQLSTATE `57014`, command `SELECT`, application `PostgREST 14.5`.\n- The timed-out statement is the current `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text,text,integer)` body, including the source unions and Creative-to-Submissions/contract-resolution joins added through #1669 and #1872.\n- The app requests the first bounded page with `p_page_size = 1000`; it times out before returning that first page.\n\n## Required outcome\n\nRestore the production Scraped Properties page while preserving its complete reviewed capability:\n\n1. Reproduce and measure the current first-page call on preview using the Licensing Manager execution path.\n2. Re-derive from the current production/main function after migrations `20260830172356` and `20260830202243`; do not restore an older body or drop any source, mapping, contract-status, unresolved/conflict visibility, privacy restriction, grant, or authorization check.\n3. Make the bounded first page and subsequent cursor pages complete within the normal PostgREST statement timeout. Prefer a permanent query/indexing correction over raising or disabling the timeout.\n4. Add a regression check that exercises the representative populated path and proves pagination remains stable and complete.\n5. Follow preview, review, merge, production apply, and authenticated live UI verification. The incident is complete only when the visible tab loads and the original data/mapping capability still works.\n\nNo licensed row values are included in this issue.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 3000\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties\n  - index plm.idx_dcp_asset_property_obs_property_asset\n  - index plm.idx_lucasfilm_dcp_asset_property_obs_property_asset\n  - table plm.dcp_asset_property_observation\n  - table plm.lucasfilm_dcp_asset_property_observation\nreads:\n  - table plm.opa_property\n  - table plm.dcp_property\n  - table plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property\n  - table plm.marvel_dcp_property\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_style_guide\n  - table plm.twentieth_century_dcp_property\n  - table plm.pmt_property\n  - table plm.wb_property\n  - table plm.nbcu_property\n  - table plm.wildbrain_era\n  - table plm.sega_submission_property\n  - table plm.sega_property\n  - table plm.creative_submission_property_resolution\n  - table plm.creative_submission_contract_resolution\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-31T03:02:47Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T21:28:17Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Outcome\n\nAdd explicit active/withdrawn lifecycle to the two durable Disney OPA entity tables that already have stable source identities and first/last-seen timestamps in production: `plm.opa_property` and `plm.opa_character`.\n\nOPA does not currently retain a trustworthy entity-level modification signal or a dedicated capture-run table. This bounded successor is therefore presence-only: add active/withdrawn status, first withdrawal time, and a structural invariant that status and withdrawal time agree. Preserve original first-seen history when a source entity disappears and later reappears.\n\n## Explicit exclusions\n\n- Do not invent first/last capture IDs, a change signal, or a capture-run baseline object.\n- `plm.opa_property_character` and scope-membership/resolution tables are excluded. Whether relationship rows have their own withdrawal lifecycle remains unresolved in #1275.\n- No loader or data load is included.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- Existing rows remain active and keep their current first/last-seen timestamps.\n- Withdrawn status and withdrawal time are structurally consistent.\n- Reappearance can restore active status without changing original first-seen time.\n- Contract tests cover withdrawal, reappearance, and unchanged rows.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 578\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table plm.opa_property\n  - table plm.opa_character\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T20:54:50Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T14:47:44Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1883,"title":"Disney OPA: durable property and character lifecycle","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:27:49Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1883"},
{"body":"## Outcome\r\n\r\nComplete durable active/withdrawn lifecycle on Warner STARLABS entity tables that already have stable cross-run identity and first/last-seen timestamps in production.\r\n\r\nLive production catalog proof on 2026-08-30 shows the current entity names are `plm.wb_asset_normalized`, `plm.wb_character_normalized`, `plm.wb_property`, and `plm.wb_style_guide_normalized` (the older umbrella names were stale). Each already has a durable primary identity, stable source-key uniqueness, and first/last-seen timestamps.\r\n\r\nAdd explicit active/withdrawn status, immutable first withdrawal time, and a consistency invariant across all five peer entity tables including `plm.wb_franchise`. Preserve first-seen and first-withdrawal history when an entity disappears and later reappears. Store only a deterministic opaque change signal derived from already-retained source metadata/hash; do not expose licensed values.\r\n\r\nExtend the existing `plm.sync_wb_normalized_target` body in place so complete entity snapshots withdraw missing identities and reactivate present identities, including unchanged hashes. Filter inferred relationship views to active entity endpoints while preserving the relationship evidence history. Make the canonical-edge writer derive active state from the entity table instead of accepting caller assertions, and keep the candidates view active-only.\r\n\r\n## Explicit exclusions\r\n\r\n- `plm.wb_capture` is chunk-addressed by `(capture_id, chunk_number)`. Baseline-run and delta-count structure is excluded until the header/chunk lifecycle is decided in #1275.\r\n- Relationship and evidence tables retain their own history and are not deleted or lifecycle-mutated here.\r\n- No loader run or data load is included.\r\n\r\n## Acceptance\r\n\r\n- Existing rows remain active and preserve their original first-seen timestamps.\r\n- Withdrawn status and withdrawal time are structurally consistent; `first_withdrawn_at` is immutable once set.\r\n- Reappearance restores active status without losing original first-seen or first-withdrawal history, even when the retained source hash is unchanged.\r\n- The change signal is deterministic and opaque.\r\n- Inferred views and canonical candidates exclude inactive endpoints without deleting relationship history.\r\n- The canonical-edge writer refuses caller-controlled lifecycle and derives current source activity from the relevant entity table.\r\n- Contract tests cover real-table capture behavior, withdrawal, reappearance, unchanged rows, foreign keys, trigger, grants, RLS, active filtering, and writer semantics.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 579\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table plm.wb_asset_normalized\r\n  - table plm.wb_character_normalized\r\n  - table plm.wb_property\r\n  - table plm.wb_style_guide_normalized\r\n  - table plm.wb_franchise\r\n  - function plm.sync_wb_normalized_target\r\n  - function plm.sync_wb_canonical_relationship_edges\r\n  - view api.wb_inferred_franchise_property\r\n  - view api.wb_inferred_franchise_style_guide\r\n  - view api.wb_inferred_franchise_character\r\n  - view api.wb_inferred_style_guide_property\r\n  - view api.wb_inferred_property_character\r\n  - view api.wb_inferred_style_guide_character\r\n  - view api.wb_canonical_relationship_candidates\r\n  - view api.wb_durable_entity_lifecycle_verification\n  - table api.wb_durable_entity_lifecycle_verification\r\nreads:\r\n  - table plm.wb_capture\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T19:42:03Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T14:47:31Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1881,"title":"Warner STARLABS: durable entity lifecycle for incremental capture","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:27:50Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1881"},
{"body":"## Outcome\n\nComplete incremental row lifecycle for the two DCP Vault entity tables whose live production identity and observation model are already unambiguous: assets and style guides.\n\nProduction catalog proof on 2026-08-30 shows both are durable cross-run entities with stable unique source keys and existing first/last crawl references:\n\n- `plm.dcp_asset`: unique `(source_system, source_path)`, with `first_seen_crawl_id` and `last_seen_crawl_id`.\n- `plm.dcp_style_guide`: unique `(source_system, source_path)` plus a partial unique source-guide ID, with `first_seen_crawl_id` and `last_seen_crawl_id`.\n\nAdd an explicit active/withdrawn lifecycle, the first withdrawal time, and an invariant that withdrawn status and withdrawal time agree. DCP publishes no trustworthy modification signal, so this successor is presence-only and must not invent one. A later sighting must be able to reactivate a temporarily withdrawn entity without losing first-seen history.\n\nAlso make `plm.dcp_crawl` delta-aware with full/incremental run kind, an optional complete baseline crawl, and privacy-safe aggregate delta counts. A failed or partial crawl must never qualify as a baseline. Preserve the existing coverage/authentication safeguards and do not infer mass withdrawal from an incomplete crawl.\n\n## Explicit exclusions\n\n- `plm.dcp_property` and `plm.dcp_character` are excluded because their first/last references point to metadata runs, not crawls; the umbrella issue retains that unresolved lifecycle boundary.\n- Observation/join tables are excluded. Their row lifecycle semantics remain unresolved in #1275.\n- No loader or data load is included.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- Existing rows remain active and retain first/last crawl history.\n- Complete-baseline enforcement cannot be bypassed by a failed or partial crawl.\n- Status/withdrawal consistency is enforced structurally.\n- A reappearing source entity can return to active without changing its original first-seen crawl.\n- Contract tests cover withdrawal, reappearance, invalid baseline, and incomplete-crawl refusal.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 580\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table plm.dcp_asset\n  - table plm.dcp_style_guide\n  - table plm.dcp_crawl\n  - function plm.validate_dcp_incremental_baseline\nreads:\n  - table plm.dcp_crawl_section\n  - table plm.dcp_crawl_gap\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T20:16:50Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T14:47:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1880,"title":"DCP Vault: durable asset and style-guide lifecycle for incremental capture","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:27:52Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1880"},

{"body":"DB Data Admin needs a privacy-safe read contract for the already-loaded Creative-to-Submissions decisions and signed-contract Property evidence. The current `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text,text,integer)` response exposes source rows but no authoritative Submissions members and no contract-entitlement/evidence status. The underlying decision and contract tables are intentionally service-only, so the browser must not query them directly.\n\nRequired behavior:\n\n- For every Creative-purpose row already returned by the RPC, expose a sanitized decision state (`mapped`, `conflict`, or `unmapped`) and zero or more authoritative Submissions display labels/identities from the latest non-superseded exact-source decision.\n- Expose a sanitized contract status suitable for the admin grid: entitled/evidenced, not evidenced, incomplete chain, conflict, or unknown. Do not expose contract text, document identity, filenames, hashes, page/schedule locators, terms, restrictions, personal data, or private paths.\n- Do not infer contract entitlement from normalized-name similarity. If the existing exact Creative/Submissions decision does not provide an authoritative route to contract evidence, add a private service-only exact-identity link/decision object and keep unresolved rows unknown.\n- Preserve every unmapped Creative row in the result. The application will style those rows red.\n- Keep the existing Licensing Manager gate and pagination contract.\n\nAcceptance:\n\n- Contract tests cover mapped, one-to-many, conflict, unmapped, incomplete-chain, and no-contract-evidence cases.\n- The public RPC response contains only the sanitized fields needed by the grid.\n- No licensed row values appear in migrations, tests, issues, logs, commit messages, or PR text.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 2100\ndepends_on: 1669\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties\n  - table plm.creative_submission_contract_resolution\nreads:\n  - table plm.creative_submission_property_resolution\n  - table plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member\n  - table plm.contract_property_capture\n  - table plm.contract_property\n  - table plm.contract_property_evidence\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T20:39:09Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T14:25:26Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"The shared checkout at `C:\\repos\\shared-db` was measured **~30 commits behind `origin/main`** on 2026-08-30, and silently so. Anything read from its working tree — a migration file, a sidecar pin, a digest, an object list — is quietly the wrong version, and nothing about the read announces it.  This is dangerous because the checkout is *shared*: many sessions run from it and nobody owns keeping it current. It compounds with rapid supersession — on issue #1658 the reserved migration version moved **five** times, so a stale tree can hold a version that no longer exists anywhere on `main`.  **Interim rule already in use:** derive versions and object names from the merge commit's own file list on `origin/main`, through a temporary detached worktree — never from a working tree, an issue title, or a PR title.  **Wanted:** either something that keeps the shared checkout current, or a guard that refuses a verification read taken from a stale tree. {"body":"Run 33308654166 exposed a false-pass hole in `.github/workflows/database-contract-tests.yml`.\n\nPass 1 applies migrations from empty and records failures. After the captured baseline is applied, pass 2 appends only those failures to the already-applied successful migrations. An older failed migration can therefore replace a function already installed by a later successful migration.\n\nObserved: `20260810010000_popdam_order_list_contract.sql` fails from empty because `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` is a pre-adoption table supplied only by the baseline. In pass 2 it then replaces the four OrderList routines after newer migration `20260830111545_popdam_orderlist_input_only_write_contract.sql`, leaving the older definitions active and making downstream tests judge superseded code.\n\nRepair the harness so pass 2 cannot silently leave an older definition over a later-stamped definition. Add regression coverage for the exact older-fails/later-succeeds/redeclares-same-routine case. Do not edit the applied 20260810010000 migration. A forward migration cannot make an earlier migration succeed during pass 1, so this is repository-maintenance work and authorizes no database change.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 5\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T13:43:48Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T13:28:51Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1858,"title":"Fix pass-2 migration replay supersession ordering","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:12Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1858"},
{"body":"## What happened  Mid-review on PR #1823 (sequence 537), continuing an existing session to put measurements back to the reviewer:  ``` ai-review-sandbox: refusing to refresh /c/Users/.../review-sandboxes/kimi-claude-pr1823-seq537b-...:   it is outside managed review storage. ai-kimi: error: could not refresh the recorded private review snapshot ```  The recorded snapshot path and the managed-storage root differ only in the case of the drive letter (`/c/...` recorded, `/C/...` expected). The containment check is a string comparison, so it rejects a path that is in fact inside managed storage.  ## Why it matters more than its size suggests  The check itself is right to exist and right to fail closed — a review snapshot outside managed storage is a real hazard. The defect is that it cannot tell a genuine escape from its own path formatting.  It fires on **continuation**, which is exactly the moment continuity is most valuable. The turn it blocked was a rebuttal: the reviewer had produced a blocking finding it admitted it could not compute, I had executed the measurement, and I needed to put the numbers back to the same reviewer in the same session so its withdrawal or persistence would mean something.  Losing the session forced a restart with the prior findings restated in the new brief. That works, but it is strictly weaker evidence. A reviewer re-reading its own conclusions handed to it by the author is in a different position from one holding them in its own context, and the author is the interested party doing the restating.  ## Asks  1. Normalise the drive letter (and any other path spelling that varies on Windows) on both sides before the containment comparison, or compare resolved real paths rather than strings. 2. Do not weaken or remove the containment check — this should stay fail-closed. 3. Add a regression case with a mixed-case drive letter, since the two spellings are produced by different parts of the toolchain and will drift back.  \n\n ```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: application-data\nroute: application-session\npriority: 1000\nreturn_to: u2giants/ai-devops\nwrites:\nreads:\n``` \n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:14:10Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T12:33:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1857,"title":"Review snapshot containment check rejects its own path on a drive-letter case mismatch, breaking session continuation","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:14Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1857"},
{"body":"## The defect  A reviewer wrapper can silently deliver less than the change it was asked to review, and still return a fluent, confident verdict. Nothing downstream can distinguish that artifact from a real review. The verdict is treated as evidence by the merge machinery, so the failure is not \"a review was inconvenient\" — it is that **a verdict can mean nothing while the machinery still counts it**.  We have no receipt anywhere in the pipeline proving a reviewer received what we believe we sent. Every gate we have checks the change; none checks the reviewer's input.  ## The mechanism that exposed it  The Kimi CLI has no prompt-file or stdin path in headless mode, so the wrapper passes the entire brief through `-p` on the command line. Packet capacity is therefore set by an operating-system argument limit, not by anything the review contract knows about.  Commissioning review sequence 537 on PR #1823, the packet was a ~630-line brief with the diff embedded verbatim. The provider process died at exit 126 before reading anything:  ``` ai-kimi: line 651: .../kimi: Argument list too long ```  The wrapper correctly wrote an `INCOMPLETE — NO VERDICT` recovery artifact with terminal reason `provider-process-failed`, so nothing false was recorded. That part worked, and this instance was loud.  The loud case is not the concern. It is evidence that delivery capacity is governed by the operating system rather than by the contract, and a delivery path bounded by something the contract cannot see is one where context can go missing without the loss appearing anywhere in the verdict. Raising the limit does not fix that; it only moves the threshold at which the quiet version starts happening.  ## Workaround used  Re-issued as a path-based brief naming the seven changed files for the reviewer to read from its own snapshot, ~2.8KB instead of ~30KB. That worked and the review was substantive. But it changes the instrument: a file-reading review is not a sealed-patch review, and which one we get should be a deliberate choice, not the residue of an argument limit.  ## Asks  1. **A receipt, first.** Have the reviewer restate a hash or a length of what it actually received, and check it against what was sent. This is the ask that addresses the defect; without it, an unread packet stays invisible in the artifact. 2. Give the wrapper a delivery path that is not the command line — a file the provider reads, or chunked delivery — so brief size is a contract decision rather than an OS accident. 3. Until then, have the wrapper refuse up front with a clear message when a brief exceeds a safe threshold, instead of letting the provider die on invocation.  Note the ordering: 2 and 3 are the mechanism, and fixing them alone would leave the defect intact at a higher threshold.  \n\n ```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: application-data\nroute: application-session\npriority: 1000\nreturn_to: u2giants/ai-devops\nwrites:\nreads:\n``` \n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:14:14Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T12:33:00Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1856,"title":"A wrapper that silently drops the diff still returns a confident verdict, and no gate can tell","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:15Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1856"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope status: ready work_type: repo-maintenance route: repo-maintenance objects: none ```  ## The defect, stated plainly  **Reviewer verdict evidence in this repository is read from unauthenticated comment text.** A comment body containing a verdict word anywhere near the head SHA is treated as a recorded reviewer decision, with **no author check and no permission check**. Anyone who can comment on an issue or PR can write one.  It runs in **both directions**, and both are live:  - **It can lock a head nobody reviewed.** Prose that merely *mentions* a verdict registers as one, and that head then refuses reviewer assignment and reviewer replacement. The head becomes unmergeable with no comment-shaped symptom — the refusal names a verdict that does not exist. - **It can satisfy a gate nobody passed.** The same permissiveness in the approving direction means ordinary prose can score as the approval a merge gate is waiting for.  **This is the second sighting, not bad luck.** The first was a comment stating that an approval was *missing*, which scored **as an approval**. The second is recorded below. Two independent sightings in opposite directions is the design behaving as written, not a pair of formatting accidents.  Read this as *unauthenticated evidence in a merge gate*. The tempting framing — \"a comment accidentally tripped a parser\" — is wrong and dangerous, because it sizes the problem as a formatting nuisance and invites a fix that only tightens the pattern. Tightening the pattern narrows the accident. It does not close the forgery, because nothing anywhere asks **who wrote this**.  ## What happened   While shepherding PR #1818 I posted an ordinary governance comment on the PR. It reported a reviewer's verdict and named the current head SHA. That comment then **blocked reviewer assignment and reviewer replacement at that head**, with these refusals:  ``` REFUSED: an existing verdict for the exact head forbids reviewer replacement REFUSED: review assignment issue, PR head, or verdict changed after mutex acquisition ```  No verdict had been recorded at that head. My prose *was* the verdict.  ## Root cause  `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2202` (and `hasVerdictForHead`, the same rule) decide whether a head already carries a verdict with:  ```js const body = String(row.body ?? ''), tied = row.commit_id === request.headSha || body.includes(request.headSha) return tied && (/\\b(?:APPROVE|REVISE|REQUEST_CHANGES)\\b/i.test(body) || ['APPROVED','CHANGES_REQUESTED'].includes(String(row.state ?? '').toUpperCase())) ```  Two problems, both of them the same shape:  1. **The verdict word matches anywhere in the body.** Any sentence containing the word, including a report *about* a verdict, a quotation of one, or a design discussion of the parser itself, scores as a recorded verdict. 2. **There is no author, association or permission check.** The rows come straight from issue and PR comments. Anyone who can comment can create or destroy a verdict signal at a head.  Combined with the body-wide SHA tie, ordinary prose near a 40-character SHA is indistinguishable from a reviewer's recorded decision.  ## Why this is worth fixing rather than working around  PR #1818 fixes exactly this for the **merge** gate: `scripts/check-exact-head-approval.mjs` requires the verdict word to **open its line** (markdown emphasis and quoting stripped first), which is how the reviewer wrappers emit it and is not how anyone writes a status update. That gate correctly did **not** read my comment as a verdict. The lanes file's assignment and replacement paths were simply never given the same treatment, so the repository now has two different answers to \"is this text a verdict?\" in two files that gate the same workflow.  The workaround I had to use is itself evidence of the problem: I had to **edit a truthful governance comment to remove a SHA** so the tooling would stop mistaking it for a decision. That is backwards — the record should not have to be degraded to keep the machinery working.  ## Suggested fix  Export the line-anchored verdict predicate from `scripts/check-exact-head-approval.mjs` (`stripVerdictLabel` + the `APPROVE` / `REFUSAL` patterns) and use that single implementation in `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` for `hasVerdictForHead` and the pre-replacement check at :2202, so the two files cannot drift into disagreeing about what a verdict is. Add a regression test feeding a known-dirty case: a comment that reports a verdict and names the head must NOT score as a verdict.  **Separately, and larger:** neither implementation checks authorship. Line-anchoring narrows the accident; it does not close the forgery. Authenticated verdict provenance is a real gap and is documented as such in `docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md` as of #1818.  ## Repro  Comment on any open PR with a body containing the current head SHA and a sentence using the word REVISE, then run `--assign-reviewer` at that head.   \n\n ```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n``` \n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T15:29:36Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T11:26:33Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1855,"title":"Unauthenticated comment text is trusted as reviewer verdict evidence","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:17Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1855"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1\n```\n\n## Summary\n\n`node scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --cleanup-stale` closes a protected\nmigration-author claim on nothing more than an expired lease, without checking whether\nthat claim still owes a **preview rehearsal** or a **production promotion**. When it does,\nthe lane is stranded with **no sanctioned exit**.\n\nThis is the same family as the defects already on file — a terminal state rendered as an\nordinary one (#1847 counts an expired lane as active; #1517 is a merged-but-never-rehearsed\nmigration that became unrecoverable through its original file). Here the inversion is:\n*\"the author stopped typing\"* is being read as *\"the work is finished\"*.\n\n## Why this is a real defect, not a tidy-up preference\n\n**Expiry deliberately does NOT release the object locks.** The claim body says so in its\nown words:\n\n> Expiry is an audit warning, not an automatic release. The migration version is permanent\n> and is never reused.\n\nThat is correct and intentional: collision protection must outlive the authoring session,\nbecause another session may still write the same objects long after the author's lease\nlapses. But `--cleanup-stale` then **closes the claim issue**, and the open claim is the\nonly record that says downstream work is still owed. Closing it throws away exactly the\nsignal that expiry was careful to preserve.\n\nThree states are not two. **Merged**, **applied-to-preview**, and **applied-to-production**\nare distinct, and a claim can be finished in the first while still owing the second and\nthird. Nothing in the cleanup path distinguishes them.\n\n## The strand is permanent, not merely inconvenient\n\nThe permanent version reservation `refs/db-claims/<version>` **survives** the cleanup, by\ndesign — the version can never be reused. That is what converts an inconvenience into a\ndead end:\n\n- The rehearsal must apply **the version that actually merged**, so a new version is wrong.\n- `--reissue-merged-stranded-claim` only mints a *later* version, so it is the wrong tool.\n- `--recover-same-owner-split` is hard-pinned to claims #1058/#1063 and refuses anything else.\n- There is no other command that returns a cleanup-closed claim to `open`.\n\nSo the version is spent, the claim is closed, and `--prepare-preview-dispatch` refuses\nforever. The lane cannot be recovered by any governed command that exists today.\n\n## Reproducing case (this instance)\n\n- Work issue: **#1684** — merged to `main` as `20ec217fa0f4d3777cf245b9fd2414d53bb1a456` (PR #1712).\n- Migration version: `20260829004145`.\n- Protected claim: **#1711**, owner `codex-agent issue_1684_phase2`,\n  branch `codex/issue-1684-character-separation`, lease expired `2026-08-29T03:57:34Z`.\n- Closed **2026-08-30T11:01:55Z** with the guarded-cleanup comment\n  \"Expired migration-author lease closed by guarded cleanup. Its migration version remains unavailable.\"\n- At that moment #1684 had **never been applied to preview or production**, and its own\n  acceptance test is a *production* verification.\n- Result now, at `origin/main` 75a6e35e:\n\n      $ node scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --prepare-preview-dispatch 1684\n      REFUSED: work issue #1684 must have exactly one live protected claim\n\n- `refs/db-claims/20260829004145` is still present (reservation `2b68e7e2…`), so the\n  version stays spent and the strand is permanent.\n\nNote that the merged-PR half of the flow is healthy: `deriveLivePreviewCandidate` already\nfalls back to the merged pull request on the claim branch (`branchPulls` +\n`mergeCommitInMain`) and would have driven `POST_MERGE_REHEARSAL` normally. The **only**\nmissing precondition is the claim the cleanup closed.\n\nThe preview route itself is fine — derived READY / POST_MERGE_REHEARSAL against the live\nledger, with a positive control proving the selector can still refuse. Evidence is on\n#1684. Nothing about this defect is a route or ordering problem.\n\n## What a fix has to do\n\n1. **`--cleanup-stale` must not close a claim that still owes preview or production.**\n   An expired lease may relinquish *author capacity*; it must not retire the claim while a\n   downstream obligation is unmet. Leave it open and name it in the audit instead.\n2. **The obligation must be readable.** Cleanup needs a way to ask \"has this version been\n   applied to preview? to production?\" — the preview ledger and production ledger already\n   answer both.\n3. **A sanctioned, narrow recovery** for a claim already stranded this way, so the fix does\n   not require the strand to be repaired by hand.\n\nWhatever lands must be non-vacuous and proven: a test that goes red when the guard is\nremoved, then green.\n\n## Out of scope\n\nNot a schema change. No database object is claimed or altered by this issue.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T15:40:20Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T11:19:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1852,"title":"cleanup-stale closes claims that still owe a preview rehearsal or production promotion, stranding the lane permanently","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:18Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1852"},
{"body":"## Reviewer pool exhausted — the review stage is the bottleneck for every lane\n\nRecording this as a condition, not as one PR's local obstacle. At 2026-08-30 ~11:15Z all six reviewers hold a live active lease:\n\n| reviewer | PR | issue | lease head |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| codex-gpt-5.6-sol | #1823 | 505 | `ab4acbe4` |\n| kimi-k3 | #1823 (slot 3) | 505 | `ab4acbe4` |\n| glm-5.3 | #1823 (replacement for deepseek-chat, insufficient_quota) | 505 | `ab4acbe4` |\n| deepseek-chat | #1749 (slot 2) | 1645 | `fe614334` |\n| muse-spark-1.2-contributor | #1749 | 1645 | `fe614334` |\n| grok-4.6 | #1818 (replacement for deepseek-chat, insufficient_quota) | 1816 | `d0660c10` |\n\n**None of these are stale.** All three PRs are open and each lease head matches its PR's current head exactly, so there is nothing abandoned to reclaim — this is genuine saturation, not leaked leases. `--assign-reviewer` correctly refuses with `no reviewer is available`.\n\nTwo things worth noting beyond the count:\n\n- **Three of the six leases are consumed by one PR** (#1823), across slots plus a replacement. A multi-slot review plus a failure replacement can take half the roster on its own.\n- **deepseek-chat's billing failure is amplifying the shortage.** It failed `insufficient_quota` on #1823 and #1818, and each failure drew a *replacement* from the same roster — so an unusable provider is still consuming a lease of its own on #1749 while having cost two more elsewhere.\n\nConsequence: any lane needing a fresh review waits on another lane finishing, and the wait is invisible unless something is actively watching. PR #1829 is in that queue now.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:21:59Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T11:18:34Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1851,"title":"reviewer pool exhausted: all six reviewers leased across three PRs, no lane can commission","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:20Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1851"},
{"body":"## The defect  `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` verifies that the reviewed inventory is **complete and correctly positioned**. It does not verify, and cannot verify, that a site's recorded disposition still describes the line it names.  The inventory is keyed by `path:line`. `run()` checks the discovered site count and a sha256 over the discovered list, then requires exactly one `enriched`/`excluded` disposition per site with a reason of at least 20 characters. Every one of those checks is satisfied by a mechanical renumber.  So after any edit to a covered file, a script can re-attach each old disposition and reason to whatever line now occupies that number, and the guard passes — identically to how it passes after a genuine re-review. **There is no difference in the output.** The green tick is evidence the inventory is complete; it is not evidence that it is true.  That makes this a silent failure. Nothing warns, nothing degrades, and no reviewer downstream can tell the two cases apart from the artifact.  ## Why it matters more than the churn  The churn is already recorded on #1822: line-keying means any edit to a shared file drifts every recorded site below it, forcing a regeneration commit that voids the review in progress. That is expensive but visible.  This is the other half, and it is worse: the regeneration the churn forces is exactly the operation the guard cannot audit. The mechanism that makes the guard noisy is the same mechanism that makes it unenforceable.  ## Suggested direction  Key the inventory by a hash of the **matched line text** rather than its position. Then a site needs re-review only when its text actually changes, movement alone produces no drift and no regeneration commit, and a mechanical renumber cannot manufacture a pass because there is no number to renumber.  ## Provenance  Found by glm-5.3 (sequence 524) reviewing PR #1829, and confirmed against the guard source. Deliberately not fixed in #1829 to keep that PR to its own subject. Recorded here rather than only in PR comments, because a comment on a merged PR is not a work item anyone finds later.  \n\n ```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n``` \n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T15:38:39Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T11:17:51Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1850,"title":"truth-audit guard cannot tell a real re-review from a mechanical renumber (silent)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:22Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1850"},

{"body":"## What happens\n\n`--queue-audit` shows a lane as `active` whether the claim holding it is being worked or was abandoned days ago. Today, four of the five occupied author lanes were held by claims whose leases had expired — sessions that stopped on 2026-08-28 and 2026-08-29 — with real work queued behind each of them:\n\n```\nlane 3  active 1711 (owner codex-agent issue_1684_phase2, 2026-08-29)  queued: 1684, 1780\nlane 4  active 1659 (owner codex-agent issue-1658-1649,   2026-08-28)  queued: 1658, 1781\nlane 5  active 1656 (owner codex-agent issue-1645-1649,   2026-08-28)  queued: 1645, 1782\n```\n\nThe information exists — `--audit` prints `5/8 active-author leases occupied; ... 4 expired lease(s) remain locked` — but it is in a *different command*, as a count with no issue numbers, and `--queue-audit` never mentions it. So the queue view, which is the one an orchestrator reads to decide what to dispatch, presents a dead lane and a working lane identically.\n\nThe consequence is not a stalled lane, it is a **stalled lane that reads as healthy**. Three of the assigned issues (#1658, #1645, #1684) sat queued behind their own abandoned claims, and #1703 sat blocked behind #1645, while the audit reported no dispatchable work and three empty lanes. Everything looked correct.\n\n## Why the current design is right and still insufficient\n\nExpiry deliberately does **not** release the object locks — collision protection must outlive the session, and that is correct. And a claim with a live PR behind it must never be auto-released, because releasing it certifies unfinished work as finished. Neither rule should change.\n\nWhat is missing is that nobody is *told*. An expired lease is not a safe state to leave alone; it is a piece of work with no one on it.\n\n## Suggested directions (none prescribed)\n\n- Have `--queue-audit` mark each occupied lane with its lease state and age, and list expired-lease claims by number with the PR state behind each one. Occupancy and liveness are different facts and should not share one field.\n- Distinguish the three real cases in the report, since they need different actions: expired with an **open** PR (take the lease over), expired with a **merged** PR (close out and free the lane), expired with **no** PR (likely nothing was written).\n- Consider making an expired lease with queued work an audit failure rather than a silent count, in the same way `EMPTY LANE NOT PROVEN` already fails.\n\nWhatever is built, drive it against a known-expired claim and watch it report before trusting a clean run.\n\nRelated: #1840 (finished work reads as dispatchable) and #1845 (an abandoned preview version blocks the lane forever) are the same shape — a terminal state that the tooling renders as an ordinary one.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T15:46:00Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T10:59:28Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1847,"title":"Queue audit shows an abandoned author lane as active: expired leases are counted in a different command and never named","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:26Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1847"},
{"body":"## What happens\n\nA preview-only version that will never merge blocks **every** later version's preview route, permanently.\n\n`scripts/orchestrator-flow/preview-graph.mjs` builds one edge per (preview-only blocker, later version not yet on preview):\n\n```\nfor(const blocker of previewOnly)\n  for(const target of [...nodes.keys()].filter((v)=>v>blocker&&!preview.has(v)))\n    edges.push({from:blocker,to:target,reason:'preview-ledger-predecessor-not-on-main'})\n```\n\n`select-preview-route.mjs` then returns `WAITING` for anything with such an edge. There is no notion of an **abandoned or superseded** preview version, so the blocker never ages out. Because migration versions are timestamps, \"later\" means every version authored from that moment on, forever.\n\nLive instance today: `20260828113920` (issue #1722, claim #1747, source PR #1748) was applied to preview and then superseded — PR #1748 merged as `20260830013942`. Verified: the replacement is on `main`, the orphan is not, and never will be.\n\n```\ngit ls-tree origin/main --name-only supabase/migrations/ | grep -E \"20260828113920|20260830013942\"\n-> supabase/migrations/20260830013942_orderlist_bridge_covering_index.sql\n```\n\nThat single row is currently blocking the whole preview lane, not just its own issue.\n\n## Why the escape hatch does not scale\n\n`.github/workflows/preview-ledger-orphan-reconciliation.yml` is the only sanctioned way to clear one, and its `case \"$ISSUE:$CLAIM:$SOURCE_PR:$ORPHAN:$REPLACEMENT\"` allowlist is hard-coded. It has grown to eight entries. Every orphan therefore costs a reviewed, CI-gated, merged code change to the workflow **before** the lane can move at all — while the lane is stopped.\n\nThe allowlist is doing real safety work and should not simply be deleted. But an unbounded, permanently-blocking failure mode whose only remedy is a merged PR per instance is a queue that halts on its own routine exhaust. Eight entries is the evidence: this is not an exceptional event.\n\n## Suggested directions (none prescribed)\n\n- Let the graph carry a **superseded** marker: an orphan whose replacement is provably on `main`, under the same claim, is not a predecessor of anything.\n- Make the allowlist data rather than source — a signed/reviewed manifest the workflow reads — so clearing an orphan is still gated but is not a source change to a workflow file.\n- At minimum, make `--queue-audit` report an orphan the moment it appears, naming every version it will block, instead of surfacing it only when some unrelated issue's route turns `WAITING`.\n\nAny check or marker built here must be driven against a known-orphaned ledger and watched to go red **before** it is trusted.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 600\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-31T08:03:55Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T10:54:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1845,"title":"Preview lane: an abandoned preview version blocks every later version forever, and the only remedy is a merged workflow edit","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:28Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1845"},
{"body":"The CI check named **PII forward guard** scans added diff lines for **email-shaped strings only**. Ruling 6.14 forbids an email address, a full name, a phone number, a home address, *\"or any other personal identifier\"* — roughly one of five categories is implemented.\n\n**It has already failed in production use.** The licensing reviewer's first name was written into two source files under PR #1825; the guard went green, because it was never capable of catching it. The breach is fixed in #1842.\n\n## Why this is worse than a missing check\n\nA missing check is a known gap. This is a **partial implementation behind a green tick that reads as full coverage**, and the check's *name* is doing work its code does not do. Anyone reading the checks list on #1825 would reasonably conclude 6.14 was verified — the check is named for the exact ruling that was being violated at that moment. A guard that reports success on the case it was created to prevent is worse than no guard, because it is believed.\n\nSame family as #1841, one step further on: there, unauthenticated prose counted as evidence; here, a check's name counts as its coverage.\n\n## What the fix has to handle\n\nWidening this is not mechanical, and the hard part is real: **legitimate name-as-data.** The evidence CSVs are full of real personal names that are the business value, and 6.14 explicitly protects that use. A guard that fires on every capitalised word pair will be disabled within a week, which returns us to no coverage with extra noise. Design for the distinction between a person named *as source data* and a person named *incidentally in code, comments, filenames or commit messages* before widening the pattern.\n\nInterim, and cheap: **stop the name from over-claiming.** Either rename the check to what it does, or make it declare its own partial coverage in its output, so a green tick stops asserting 6.14 was verified.\n\n## Standing requirement\n\nDrive any widened guard against the known breach — the two comments fixed in #1842 are a ready-made fixture — and watch it go **red** before trusting it. A guard that has never been shown to fire is not evidence.\n\n## Related\n\n- #1842 — the fix and the round-2 guard that was missing\n- #1841, #1837, #1840, #1843\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T15:55:22Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T10:47:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1844,"title":"SECURITY: 'PII forward guard' checks email shapes only, but is named for ruling 6.14 and reads as full coverage","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:30Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1844"},
{"body":"Found during the round-6 review-cutover repair on PR #1799 (kimi-k3, sequence 519, non-blocking finding F1). Filed as a follow-up rather than changed there, which was the right call — it does not weaken that fix.\n\n## The defect\n\nAt two places the cutover encounters a record whose **commit message disagrees with its ref name** and **silently skips it**. The replacement path then proceeds to lease the *failed* reviewer — precisely the outcome the activation exists to prevent. The mechanism inverts the guard rather than merely bypassing it.\n\nReaching it needs durable-state corruption, so the probability is low. That is a reason to file it, not a reason to shrug: the states that produce disagreement between a ref name and its commit message are exactly the states where the ledger is already untrustworthy, and that is when a guard has to hold.\n\n## Why it is clearly wrong rather than arguably wrong\n\n**Every neighbouring parse failure refuses. These two skip.** The inconsistency is the argument — there is no design rationale under which a corrupt record deserves gentler handling than a malformed one, and the odd one out is the pair that keeps going.\n\n## Direction\n\nRefuse, matching the neighbours. A skip that silently continues into leasing a disqualified reviewer is the worst available shape: it produces a confident, wrong assignment with no announcement.\n\nDrive whatever check is added against a deliberately corrupted record — a ref whose commit message names a different reviewer — and watch it refuse **before** trusting it. A guard that has never been shown to fire is not evidence.\n\n## Related\n\n- #1837 — a lease naming the wrong head. Same family: the ledger being wrong about what it authorises.\n- #1841 — unauthenticated prose counting as review evidence.\n- #1833, #1840.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T15:51:00Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T10:46:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1843,"title":"Reviewer cutover silently SKIPS a record whose commit message disagrees with its ref name","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:31Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1843"},
{"body":"**A comment I wrote explaining that an APPROVE was missing is read by the gate as an APPROVE.**\n\nProven, not inferred, by the lane investigating #1769. The verdict detector's evidence set includes GitHub issue comments with **no author check and no provenance check**. My own comment on #1769 (id `5465923925`) contains a full 40-character head SHA and the word APPROVE — in a sentence saying no APPROVE exists. Direct probe: `sha: true, APPROVE: true`, with a control probe returning `true/false` correctly, so the instrument was shown capable of a negative before the positive was believed.\n\n## Both directions are broken, and the second is the dangerous one\n\n**Direction 1 (today, visible):** `--assign-reviewer --issue 1769 --pr 1809 --head-sha 8d3c31ac…` refuses with *\"review assignment issue, PR head, or verdict changed after mutex acquisition\"*. The gate sees prose as a verdict and blocks a legitimate assignment. Annoying, and self-announcing.\n\n**Direction 2 (latent, silent):** `previewGateProof` builds its evidence from the identical set. It fails today only because no assignment names `8d3c31ac`. **The moment anyone creates that assignment — which is exactly the repair the situation calls for — the prose comment satisfies \"an independent APPROVE tied to the exact head.\"** The remedy for a missing approval manufactures a counterfeit one, and nothing announces it.\n\n## Why the obvious fix is the wrong one\n\nEditing the comment to break the SHA/APPROVE pairing unblocks the immediate case, and I am authorising that as a stopgap. But it implies a rule no one can follow: *never write a full commit SHA near the word APPROVE in any comment on a work issue.* Orchestrators explain missing approvals for a living. A gate that can be defeated — or satisfied — by ordinary prose is not a gate.\n\n## Required shape of the real fix\n\nReview evidence must be **authenticated and provenanced**: the artifact, its author, and the head it was produced against, bound together and written by the review path itself. A comment body is not evidence of anything. Do not fix this by tightening the regex; a cleverer parser of untrusted prose is the same defect with more steps.\n\nWhatever is built must be driven against a known-counterfeit comment — this exact one is a ready-made fixture — and watched to **reject** it before being trusted.\n\n## Distinct from #1837\n\n#1837 is a lease naming the wrong head: a real review, mispinned. This is **non-review prose counting as a review at all**. Different premise, different fix, different harm. Folding them loses the second.\n\nRelated: #1833, #1837, #1840. Same family — a premise read once, from a source that was never authorised to supply it.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T15:29:37Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T10:39:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1841,"title":"SECURITY: the verdict detector accepts unauthenticated issue-comment prose as review evidence","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:33Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1841"},
{"body":"`--queue-audit` printed `REFILL REQUIRED NOW: dispatch issue(s) #1769` for work that was already authored, reviewed-badly, and **merged to `main`** four days earlier under a different claim (#1805, PR #1809, migration `20260828232207_wwe_licensor_capture_tables.sql`).\n\nActing on that, I claimed an author lane (#1839) and burned a reserved migration version (`20260830102829`, now permanently unavailable). The only thing that stopped a duplicate definition of 26 tables reaching a PR was the author reading `main` before writing and refusing on its own initiative. **That is a human-shaped safety net under a machine-shaped instruction**, and it will not hold every time.\n\n## The gap\n\nThe audit classifies an issue from its own scope block — `status: ready`, `work_type: structural`, `route: shared-db-orchestrator` — and from whether a live claim holds its objects. All three were true and no claim was live, because the claim that did the work (#1805) is closed. **Nothing asks whether the objects the issue proposes to create already exist on `main`.** An issue is dispatchable if nobody is currently working on it; \"already finished\" is not a state the classifier can represent.\n\nNote the failure is worst exactly where it matters: the claim being closed is what makes the issue look free, and a merged claim is closed. The more completely the work was finished, the more dispatchable it looks.\n\n## Suggested direction (not prescribed)\n\nBefore reporting an issue dispatchable, resolve its declared objects against current `main` and refuse — or at minimum warn loudly — when they already exist. The declared objects are already parsed for collision detection, so the input is in hand; what is missing is the comparison against the merged tree rather than against live claims.\n\nWhatever check is built here must be driven against a known-already-merged issue and watched to go red **before** it is trusted, per the standing rule — a checker that cannot fail is not evidence.\n\n## Related\n\n- #1769 is re-scoped in a comment there: what remains is a post-merge independent approval bound to head `8d3c31ac`, not authoring.\n- Same family as #1833 and #1837 — a premise read once and never re-read after it can move.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T16:08:35Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T10:32:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1840,"title":"queue-audit reports an issue dispatchable when its objects already exist on main","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:34Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1840"},
