{"body":"## Summary\n\nFor the entire time the accepted review of #1813 ran at `f41ed226`, the ledger entry authorising it named `fe627a23`. That is a record which proves the rotation was followed while being wrong about what was reviewed — and it is worse than a missing record, because it will be believed.\n\nNothing noticed. Not the assignment path, not the verdict-acceptance path, not any gate. The reviewer read the right tree and returned a sound verdict; the audit trail that is supposed to attest to that names a tree the reviewer never saw.\n\n## What happened\n\n1. Reviewer lease `sequence=513 reviewer=muse-spark-1.2-contributor issue=1812 pr=1813 head=fe627a2392b938be5bb5dc59bc95b3b05888dba5 slot=2` was created against head `fe627a23`.\n2. The PR head then moved to `f41ed226b18c8c8b58fba5793b6da45855907579`.\n3. The review was resumed and completed at `f41ed226`. Citations were verified byte-for-byte against that tree, and the verdict body was checked against its token.\n4. The lease was never re-pinned and never invalidated. Its `head=` field still named `fe627a23` at the moment the verdict was accepted and the PR merged (`2a0d357f4db10d7d8167d68edb4306b55cc151cd`).\n\nThe merge was correct. The record of why it was correct is not.\n\n## A lease is not a lock\n\nA second finding from the same episode, which I did not initially register as one.\n\nLease 513 is now gone from `refs/db-review-active/muse-spark-1.2-contributor`. It was not released. It was **overwritten** by the next taker — the ref now holds `sequence=514 reviewer=muse-spark-1.2-contributor issue=1722 pr=1748`.\n\nSo a reviewer lease is not a lock. It is the current value of a ref. A stale binding does not persist until someone decides it is finished; it vanishes the moment anyone else claims that reviewer, taking the evidence of the mispinning with it. There is no tombstone and no history anyone reads. I only caught the `fe627a23`/`f41ed226` disagreement because I went looking before the overwrite happened — had I looked an hour later, the wrong record would have been silently replaced by an unrelated correct-looking one, and the audit trail would have shown nothing amiss at any point.\n\nThis also means the ledger cannot answer \"what was assigned when\" after the fact. It can only answer \"what is assigned now.\"\n\n## Why this is not #1833\n\nSame axis as #1833 — nothing re-reads its premise after the premise can move — but a different defect, and it must not be folded in.\n\n- #1833 is about the rotation making a **wrong assignment**. This is about the **record of an assignment** disagreeing with the tree actually reviewed.\n- Different consumer: #1833's consumer is the lane picking a reviewer. This one's consumer is anyone later auditing whether review governance was followed.\n- Different harm: #1833 wastes a reviewer. This one produces false attestation.\n- Deciding point: **different fix.** #1833 re-samples a reviewer. This one re-pins or invalidates a ledger entry. Folded together, the second fix gets closed by the first, and the loser is the audit trail.\n\nCross-reference, do not merge: #1833.\n\n## Suggested direction\n\nNot prescribing an implementation, but the shape:\n\n- On head movement, a lease bound to the retired head should be re-pinned or explicitly invalidated — one or the other, never left silently stale.\n- Verdict acceptance should compare the reviewed head against the authorising lease's `head=` and refuse, or at minimum record the divergence, when they disagree. Today nothing performs this comparison.\n- Lease overwrite should leave something behind. A binding that disappears without anyone deciding it should is not an audit trail.\n\nAny check built here must be **proven able to fail** — run it against a known-divergent lease and watch it go red — before it is trusted. On this subsystem we have repeatedly mistaken an instrument that cannot fail for an instrument that passed.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- Accepted review head: `f41ed226b18c8c8b58fba5793b6da45855907579`\n- Authorising lease head field: `fe627a2392b938be5bb5dc59bc95b3b05888dba5`\n- Merge: `2a0d357f4db10d7d8167d68edb4306b55cc151cd` (#1813, closed #1812)\n- Overwriting lease now on the ref: `sequence=514 ... issue=1722 pr=1748 head=8ce3e13d3fed0164a8a4ef9ed0aef5075b29923c`\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T16:05:39Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T10:02:11Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1837,"title":"A reviewer lease can name a head the reviewer never read, and the record is believed anyway","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:37Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1837"},
{"body":"## Summary\n\nThree assertion failure messages in `scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py`\non `main` contain `PREVIE\\w_PRODUCER_PATHS` and `PREVIE\\w_RUNTIME_DATA_EXEMPTIONS`\n— a literal backslash-w where the constant name belongs.\n\n```\n1487:  f\"The docs entry in PREVIE\\w_RUNTIME_DATA_EXEMPTIONS claims no \"\n1489:  f\"docs in PREVIE\\w_PRODUCER_PATHS or rewrite the reason -- do \"\n1502:  \"is false and docs must be pinned in PREVIE\\w_PRODUCER_PATHS.\",\n```\n\nThe real constants are `PREVIEW_PRODUCER_PATHS` and\n`PREVIEW_RUNTIME_DATA_EXEMPTIONS`, both imported at line 15 and used correctly\nin the executable code (lines 373, 403, 438, 764).\n\n## Why this is worth fixing rather than ignoring\n\nThese are **failure messages**. They reach a reader at the exact moment the gate\nhas fired and that reader is trying to find the mechanism — and they name a\nconstant that does not exist. Someone who greps `PREVIE\\w_PRODUCER_PATHS` after\na failure finds nothing and concludes the message is stale or the constant was\nrenamed. A wrong name in a failure message is worse than no name, because it\nstops the reader looking at exactly the thing the message is about.\n\nIn Python, `\\w` in a non-raw string is not a recognised escape, so it survives\nas a literal backslash rather than erroring. It fails silently and renders\nwrong. Newer Python versions raise a `SyntaxWarning` for invalid escape\nsequences, so this will start emitting warnings on upgrade.\n\n## How it was found, which is the part I would keep\n\nI introduced a **fourth** copy of this corruption in PR #1813, in a comment I\nwrote immediately adjacent to this code, and I did it by copying the shape of\nthe surrounding lines. I have fixed mine in that PR and deliberately left these\nthree alone rather than widening the PR's scope.\n\nThat is the finding: **a corrupted name in code is a template.** The next person\nwriting nearby prose matches the local style, and the error propagates by\nimitation rather than by copy-paste. Mine was caught only because an independent\nreviewer's claim that the file's prose named the constant correctly turned out\nto be checkable, and checking it surfaced the neighbours.\n\nWorth noting the reviewer looked directly at this file, asserted the prose named\nthe constant correctly, and was wrong — these three lines were in front of it. A\nreviewer confirming a name is correct is not the same as a reviewer having\ngrepped for the name.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nCorrect the three names. Then consider a cheap guard: a test asserting every\n`PREVIEW_`-prefixed identifier appearing in this file's message strings is a\nreal module attribute. Prove it fails against the current file before trusting\nit — the corruption is present today, so the check should go red immediately if\nit is doing anything at all.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:41:35Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T09:49:49Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1836,"title":"Corrupted constant names in three risk-gate assertion failure messages on main","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:38Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1836"},
{"body":"Deferred deliberately from PR #1829 with a decision, a reason, and a named home.\nThis is a coverage gap, not a live defect. **The shipped code is correct today.**\n\n## The exact gap\n\n`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, `gateAuthorizes` — the fail-open\npreview gate's authorization decision, the single place in this repository that\ncan **authorize a database migration**:\n\n```js\nexport function gateAuthorizes(evidence,headSha,bundleId,readAssignments){\n  return (evidence??[]).some((row)=>isApprovalFor(row,headSha)&&(\n    String(row?.body??'').includes(bundleId)||\n    (readAssignments?.()??[]).some((assignment)=>assignment?.headSha===headSha)))\n}\n```\n\n**The swap: `isApprovalFor` -> `isVerdictFor`.** One identifier.\n\n`isVerdictFor` is true for a REFUSAL as well as an approval — that is its whole\npurpose, since the fail-closed assignment guards need \"any decision exists here\".\nMaking the gate use it would mean **a `REVISE` or `REJECT` tied to the head\nauthorizes the migration it was written to stop.** The strongest possible refusal\nbecomes the authorization. That is precisely the inversion #1822 exists to\nprevent, one layer up from the prose-matching bug it fixed.\n\n**No gate-level test goes red on that swap.** The predicate tests cover the\napproval/refusal asymmetry thoroughly, but every test in the gate block feeds it\nan APPROVE-shaped row. There is no gate test whose evidence is a `REVISE` or\n`REJECT`. The seam between \"the predicate knows the difference\" and \"the gate\nasks the right one\" is untested.\n\nFound by `grok-4.6` (governed assignment sequence 511) reviewing #1829 at head\n`63dc8d76ac164803bc2dbdf641eff7144310fb71`.\n\n## Two smaller residuals from the same review, fix together\n\n1. `findPrReviewAssignments` returning `null` — the new `??[]` is untested.\n2. Dropping the optional-call `?.()` or the `assignment?.` guard leaves the\n   current tests green.\n\n## The fix\n\nAdd gate-level tests that go red on the swap:\n\n- a `REVISE` row tied to the exact head, carrying the bundle id, must NOT\n  authorize (this is the one that catches it);\n- the same for `REJECT` and a structured `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review state;\n- `readAssignments` returning `null` and returning rows without `headSha`.\n\nThen add the swap itself to the mutation set as a named mutation and confirm it\ngoes red. Standard discipline: pristine baseline, one mutation at a time, and\nconfirm the test actually reaches the mutated path under the shipped\nconfiguration before crediting either result.\n\n## Why this was deferred rather than fixed in #1829\n\nFixing it would have moved #1829's head, which voids an independent APPROVE that\npassed the authenticity check on all six of its citations — and the reviewer pool\ncould not have replaced it. `grok-4.6` is spent on this PR, `muse-spark-1.2` is\ncommitted to #1813, `kimi-k3` is disqualified there by its own findings,\n`deepseek-chat` is out of quota at three separate heads, and `codex-gpt-5.6-sol`\nwas refused elsewhere for wrong scope. A head move would have cost a reviewer\nthat does not exist, to protect against an edit nobody has made.\n\n## Where this must be closed\n\n**As part of the coordination-script work that follows #1813's merge.** That file\nis already being opened for #1833 and #1834, so the head move is free at that\nmoment and costs no reviewer. Do not let it slide past that window — the whole\njustification for deferring is that a cheaper moment is already scheduled.\n\nCross-reference: PR #1829, issue #1822. Related coordination-script work: #1831,\n#1833, #1834.\n\nThis is a considered deferral with a named home, not an oversight. Deferring a\nknown gap with an owner and a moment is legitimate; deferring it into silence is\nnot, and the difference is that this issue exists.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:47:01Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T06:24:23Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1835,"title":"gateAuthorizes: swapping isApprovalFor for isVerdictFor would let a REFUSAL authorize a migration, and no test goes red","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:40Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1835"},
{"body":"## Summary\n\n`--assign-reviewer --review-slot 2` cannot succeed for a pull request whose slot 1\nhas no replacement record. It is refused deterministically by the request-budget\nguard, before the mutex, every time. This is arithmetic, not contention.\n\n## Measurement\n\n`REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT` is 19. `assignNextReviewerOperation` calls\n`requireReviewWireCapacity(13)` after its preflight. On the slot-2 path the\npreflight spends **9** requests, because slot 2 additionally calls\n`resolveSlotOneReviewer` before the capacity check, and that is not counted in\nthe 13.\n\n9 + 13 = 22 > 19. Refused.\n\nMeasured directly by driving `assignNextReviewer` inside `withReviewRequestBudget`\nand reading the budget counter at the point of refusal. Three consecutive runs:\n\n```\nslot 2: spent=9 limit=19 -> reviewer operation cannot fit 13 remaining requests\nslot 2: spent=9 limit=19 -> reviewer operation cannot fit 13 remaining requests\nslot 2: spent=9 limit=19 -> reviewer operation cannot fit 13 remaining requests\n```\n\nIdentical every run. Slot 1 on the same tuple takes the idempotent replay path and\nreturns without refusal, so the defect is specific to slot 2.\n\n## What it is NOT\n\nI first diagnosed this as contention — too many live reviewer leases inflating the\npre-mutex lease snapshot. **That was wrong**, and I am recording the wrong\ndiagnosis because it cost another lane real work: a reviewer lease was released on\nmy analysis, the live lease count went from six to five, and the refusal did not\nmove. The lease snapshot is batched, so its cost is roughly constant in the number\nof leases. Freeing leases cannot help and no one should be asked to free one for\nthis reason again.\n\nNote that slot 2 *has* succeeded elsewhere (three slot-2 assignments exist on\n1812-1813). I do not have a confirmed explanation for why those fit, and I am\ndeliberately not guessing at one here — the reproducible measurement above is what\nI can actually stand behind.\n\n## Impact\n\nThe second reviewer slot is the only governed route to an independent reviewer when\nslot 1 is disqualified — for example when slot 1 would be grading repairs its own\nfindings produced, which is findings-only and never a verdict. With slot 2\nunavailable, such a pull request has no route to an independent verdict at all,\nand the pressure is to merge on a verdict that should not count. That is the real\ncost.\n\nCurrently blocking `u2giants/shared-db#1823`.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nEither count `resolveSlotOneReviewer`'s spend inside the reserved 13 rather than\noutside it, or move the slot-1 resolution to after the capacity reservation, or\nraise the limit for the slot-2 path by the measured difference. I have not made\nthe change: it is shared coordination tooling, it is adjacent to work in flight on\n#1799, and it does not belong inside an unrelated two-row data migration.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T10:01:05Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T06:05:00Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1834,"title":"Reviewer slot 2 is unreachable: preflight spend plus reserved capacity exceeds the request budget","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:47:44Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1834"},
{"body":"## Summary\n\nThe reviewer rotation models exactly one reason a reviewer might be unsuitable: it is\n`busy` (holding a live lease). It has no concept of a reviewer being **unusable for\nthis specific pull request** — already having reviewed this exact change, or being\nknown-dead at this exact head. So it hands back reviewers that cannot legitimately be\nused, and the only levers that would move it require writing something false.\n\nTwo lanes hit this from opposite directions within a few hours of each other.\n\n## Instance 1 — the rotation re-offered a reviewer that had already reviewed the change\n\nPR #1748 (issue #1722).\n\n- Sequence 494 assigned `glm-5.3`. It ran and returned findings on this change.\n- Sequence 502 assigned `deepseek-chat`. It died with HTTP 402 `Insufficient Balance`\n  and produced no output at all — a genuinely failed reviewer.\n- That failure was recorded honestly through `--replace-failed-reviewer`\n  (`insufficient_quota`, no verdict, no artifact).\n- The replacement, sequence 506, was `glm-5.3` — the reviewer that had already\n  reviewed this same change at the same head.\n\n`glm-5.3` was free precisely *because* the failure had just been recorded correctly.\nRecording a real failure shrinks the free pool, and the rotation then returns the one\nreviewer whose second look adds the least independence.\n\nThere is no governed lever to redirect it:\n\n- There is no `--reviewer` override on `--assign-reviewer`; the flag exists but is\n  consumed only by `--reviewer-preflight`.\n- Slot 2 excludes slot 1's provider, but slot 2 is unreachable at the current request\n  ceiling (#1812 / PR #1813).\n- `--replace-failed-reviewer` on sequence 506 would require declaring `glm-5.3` failed.\n  It never ran. That record would be a lie and would sit in the ledger permanently.\n\nThe correct action was to stop and wait for a human to name a reviewer. That is the\nright outcome, but it means the governed route has no answer for a routine situation.\n\n## Instance 2 — the rotation re-offered a reviewer already known dead at the previous head\n\nPR #1813 (issue #1812), slot 2.\n\n- Slot 2 drew `deepseek-chat` at one head; it was out of quota.\n- The head moved; slot 2 drew `deepseek-chat` again at the successive head\n  (sequence 508 at `7572a5a2`); still out of quota.\n- Per #1832 there is no governed route to replace a failed **slot-2** reviewer at all.\n\nSo the rotation re-offered a reviewer already proven dead minutes earlier, and the only\nescape is to push a commit to move the head — the exact ungoverned head-moving behaviour\nthe assignment refs exist to prevent.\n\n## Why these are one defect\n\nBoth are the same missing distinction: **failed** (a global, recorded state) versus\n**unusable for this PR** (a local, per-change property). The rotation knows the first\nand is blind to the second. A reviewer that has already reviewed this change and a\nreviewer that was dead thirty minutes ago at the previous head are both perfectly\n\"available\" as far as `notTaken` is concerned:\n\n```\nconst notTaken = (row) => eligibleNames.has(row.name) && !busy.has(row.name) && row.name !== excludedProvider\n```\n\n`excludedProvider` is populated only for slot >= 2, and only with slot 1's provider for\nthat exact head.\n\n## What would fix it\n\nNot a workaround — a rotation that can express \"skip this reviewer for this PR\" without\nrequiring a false failure record. Two candidate rules, either or both:\n\n1. **Skip a reviewer that already holds a recorded assignment or verdict for the same\n   (issue, pr) at any head**, not just the same head and not just slot 1. Reviewing the\n   same change twice is a real independence loss, and the second pass is the one most\n   likely to defer to its own earlier reasoning.\n2. **Skip a reviewer with a recent terminal failure record**, scoped by provider and a\n   short window, so a known-dead provider is not re-offered at the next head. `insufficient_quota`\n   in particular does not resolve in minutes.\n\nBoth are additive to the existing busy exclusion, not a replacement for it. Neither should\nbe able to empty the roster silently — if every reviewer is excluded, refuse loudly and\nname why, the way slot 2 already does.\n\n## Cross-references\n\n- #1832 — `--replace-failed-reviewer` cannot replace a failed slot-2 reviewer. That is the\n  narrower mechanical gap; this issue is the reason the gap keeps being reached.\n- #1812 / PR #1813 — the request-ceiling defect that makes slot 2 unreachable, removing the\n  one existing exclusion that would have helped instance 1.\n\n## Evidence\n\nLive reviewer leases at the time of writing, all six occupied:\n\n```\nseq 496 muse-spark-1.2-contributor  issue 1822 pr 1829 head 24b22855\nseq 499 grok-4.6                    issue 1812 pr 1813 head 5115b0dc   (PR since moved to 7572a5a2)\nseq 501 codex-gpt-5.6-sol           issue  505 pr 1823 head 760d4aa3\nseq 506 glm-5.3                     issue 1722 pr 1748 head cc67e3fa   (replacement for failed 502; unrun, unusable)\nseq 507 kimi-k3                     issue 1812 pr 1813 head 7572a5a2\nseq 508 deepseek-chat               issue 1812 pr 1813 head 7572a5a2 slot 2   (out of quota)\n```\n\nTwo of the six leases are held by reviewers that cannot produce a usable verdict, and\nneither can be released without either a false failure record or an ungoverned head move.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:59:15Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T06:02:29Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1833,"title":"Reviewer rotation cannot express \"unusable for this PR\", only \"failed\"","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:42Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1833"},
{"body":"## What happened\n\nOn PR #1813, slot 2 was assigned `deepseek-chat` (sequence 498). That provider is out of\nquota (HTTP 402, \"Insufficient Balance\") and the wrapper confirmed `conversation was not\ncreated`, so there was verifiably no verdict and no artifact — the textbook case for the\ngoverned replacement route.\n\nThe governed route refused:\n\n```\nnode scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --replace-failed-reviewer \\\n  --issue 1812 --pr 1813 --head-sha <head> --failed-sequence 498 \\\n  --failure-code insufficient_quota --confirm-no-verdict --confirm-no-artifact\nREFUSED: durable reviewer assignment or replacement does not match the replacement request\n```\n\n## Cause\n\n`--replace-failed-reviewer` is not slot-aware. It only looks in slot 1's ref namespace.\nThis is already known and written down in the source, at the comment above\n`resolveSlotOneReviewer`:\n\n> `--replace-failed-reviewer`, which is not slot-aware and only ever touches slot 1's own\n> ref namespace\n\nSlot 2 records its assignment under a `-slot2` suffix\n(`refs/db-review-assignments/<issue>-<pr>-<head>-slot2`), which the replacement path never\nreads.\n\n## Consequence\n\nA slot-2 reviewer that fails for a genuine provider-side reason has **no governed\nreplacement route at all**. The slot is stuck on a dead provider until the PR head moves,\nwhich only happens if the author pushes. That is an incentive to push a no-op commit purely\nto escape the deadlock — the exact ungoverned behaviour the assignment refs exist to prevent.\n\nThe refusal message also misdescribes the situation. It says the assignment \"does not match\nthe replacement request\", which reads as a currency or identity mismatch and sends the\noperator looking for a moved head. The assignment matched perfectly; it was simply in a\nnamespace this code path does not look at.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\n1. Make `--replace-failed-reviewer` accept `--review-slot` and apply the same `-slot<N>`\n   suffix that `assignNextReviewerOperation` uses when building `assignmentRef` and\n   `replacementBase`.\n2. Until then, make the refusal say so: if a `-slot<N>` assignment exists for this exact\n   issue/pr/head/sequence, refuse with a message naming the real reason rather than a\n   generic mismatch. A tool that declines for a stated reason is recoverable; one that\n   declines for the wrong stated reason costs an investigation.\n\nPoint 2 is worth doing even if point 1 lands, on the general principle that a confidently\nwrong diagnosis is more expensive than a refusal.\n\n## Not in scope here\n\nFiled separately rather than folded into #1813, which is a budget-ceiling repair and should\nnot grow a second subject.","closedAt":"2026-08-30T10:16:48Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T02:30:57Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1832,"title":"--replace-failed-reviewer cannot replace a failed slot-2 reviewer","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:47:48Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1832"},
{"body":"Found while delivering #1822 as PR #1829.\n\n## The gap\n\n`acquireAuthorLane` locks **database objects** and reserves an irreversible 14-digit migration version. `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` is a source file and touches no database object, so a change to it is not lane-eligible — `--queue-audit` correctly lists such work under `NOT ORCHESTRATOR WORK`.\n\nThe result is an inversion worth stating plainly: **the file that implements every lane, every reviewer assignment, and every merge gate is the one file the lane system cannot protect.** Concurrency on it is arbitrated by nothing but git's own conflict detection at merge time, plus whatever a human or agent notices beforehand.\n\n## Why this is not merely theoretical\n\nAt the time of filing there were three open PRs against that single file — #1813 (one constant), #1799 (new constants and a new io method), and #1829 (a shared predicate replacing eight longhand copies plus one variant). Nothing in the tooling knew that. The non-overlap finding that made #1829 safe to write was produced by an agent reading three diffs by hand and reporting the result in chat.\n\nThat is the current control: **an agent checks by hand and reports.** It is exactly the class of control this repository has spent the week concluding is not a control — a rule that depends on an actor stopping itself will fail at some rate, and the rate does not depend on how well the actor understands it.\n\n## The trap to avoid\n\nDo **not** fix this by making lane acquisition accept source files. Taking a lane for a code-only change consumes a permanently unreusable migration version to obtain a lock over a resource the change does not use — a real, irreversible cost paid for no protection. Whatever the fix is, it needs a lock whose unit is the file, not the database object, and whose cost is not a burnt version number.\n\nPossible directions, none of them decided:\n\n- A lightweight advisory ref keyed on high-traffic source paths, with no version reservation.\n- A merge-gate check that refuses when another open PR touches the same declared regions of the coordination script.\n- Accepting the gap explicitly for this file, but making the hand check a required, recorded step rather than an informal one.\n\n## Not in scope for #1829\n\n#1829 is deliberately not fixing this. It is filed separately so the fix is not smuggled into a change that is already load-bearing.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-31T08:21:21Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T02:24:27Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1831,"title":"The coordination script every lane depends on is the one file lanes cannot protect","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:44Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1831"},
{"body":"## Summary\n\n`requireReviewWireCapacity(n)` is called before mutex acquisition to guarantee an\noperation can still complete and release a mutex it is about to take. There are\nthree such reserves in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, and they do\nnot agree:\n\n```\nline 1661  requireReviewWireCapacity(REVIEW_MUTEX_RELEASE_RESERVE)   // 13, re-derived in #1812\nline 2035  requireReviewWireCapacity(10);  acquireReviewMutex(...)   // untouched\nline 2140  requireReviewWireCapacity(11);  acquireReviewMutex(...)   // untouched\n```\n\nPR #1813 re-derived the first one against the real pre-mutex cost of the\nassignment path, after issue #1812 showed the surrounding budget had been sized\nfor a caller that no longer matched. **The other two were derived the same way,\nby hand, and have not been re-checked.** If 13 was wrong for its path, 10 and 11\nare suspect for theirs for exactly the same reason.\n\n## Why this is worth checking rather than assuming\n\nThe two failure directions are not symmetric, and the dangerous one is the quiet\none:\n\n- A **ceiling** that is too small refuses early. It fails closed. That is what\n  #1812 was, and it announced itself as a clean `REFUSED`.\n- A **reserve** that is too small does not fail closed. The operation passes the\n  pre-mutex check, **acquires the mutex**, and can then exhaust the budget\n  partway through releasing it — leaving the mutex held with no owner running.\n  Recovery is the guarded `recover-author-mutex.yml` procedure, not a retry.\n\nSo an under-sized reserve converts a budget shortfall into a stranded\ncoordination lock. That is the failure the reserve exists to prevent.\n\n## What needs doing\n\nFor each of the two untouched sites, count the actual wire requests on the path\nbetween mutex acquisition and release — the same exercise #1812 did for the\nassignment path — and confirm the reserve covers the worst case, including any\npath that costs one extra request per recorded replacement row. Then either\ncorrect the number or record the derivation so the next reader does not have to\nredo it.\n\nNote that both remaining literals sit next to `acquireReviewMutex` on the same\nline, so correcting them need not shift line numbers. That matters: this file\nholds 19 of the 223 call sites recorded by line number in\n`docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json`, and adding lines\nto it drags that inventory into the change and makes it conflict on every move\nof `main`. Keeping edits in place avoids that entirely.\n\n## Provenance, stated plainly\n\nThis was raised by the reviewer of PR #1813 and **I could not verify it** — those\ntwo call sites are outside that PR's delta and I did not measure their paths.\nIt is filed as a question to be checked, not a defect I have confirmed. It may\nturn out that 10 and 11 are correct and simply undocumented.\n\nRelated: #1812, PR #1813.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:54:36Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T02:21:05Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1830,"title":"Re-derive the two untouched mutex-release reserves (10 and 11); an undersized reserve strands the mutex rather than failing closed","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:45Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1830"},
{"body":"## The conflict\n\n`AGENTS.md` states that curated Master Data exits by **FORK** and that it forks\n\"because it must not occupy a migration-author lane,\" and the route table records\n`curated-master-data` / `curated-master-data-governance` as \"§6.4 governance, **never a\nlane**.\"\n\nThe required check **`Migration author lease`** refuses any pull request that changes a\nfile under `supabase/migrations/` unless the branch holds exactly one active\nref-backed claim:\n\n```\nREFUSED: migration PR branch <branch> must have exactly one active ref-backed claim; found 0\n```\n\nThe only governed apply path in this repository is a migration\n(`shared-supabase-migrations.yml` / `guarded-migration-merge.yml`). So a\ncurated-Master-Data fork whose change ships as a migration file is **structurally\nunmergeable** under the routing rule as written. The two rules cannot both be honoured.\n\n## The decision taken, so the next session does not rediscover this\n\nEncountered on issue #505 / PR #1823. Resolved by the shared-db orchestrator on\n2026-08-29 in favour of **claiming the lane**, with this reasoning:\n\n- The \"curated Master Data must not occupy a migration-author lane\" rule is a\n  **throughput** rule. The lane cap is throughput, never isolation.\n- The lease gate is a **safety** mechanism: atomic version reservation plus\n  exact-object collision locking.\n- A change that ships a migration file genuinely needs both. **Overriding a throughput\n  preference to satisfy a safety gate is the right direction; the reverse never is.**\n\nThe safety value was demonstrated immediately: the claim attempt refused on an object\ncollision with live claim #1656 (issue #1645) over `public.assets`, which correctly\nforced #505 to narrow its scope rather than contend for a held object.\n\n## What this issue asks for\n\nReconcile the written rule with the gate so the next curated-Master-Data fork does not\nstall. Options, not a recommendation:\n\n1. Amend the routing text to say curated Master Data does not *normally* occupy a lane,\n   but **must** claim one when its change ships as a migration file, citing the\n   throughput-vs-safety reasoning above.\n2. Give curated Master Data a non-migration governed apply path, so the rule as written\n   becomes achievable.\n3. Exempt `curated-master-data` from the lease check — **explicitly not recommended**,\n   since it would drop atomic version reservation and object-collision locking for\n   exactly the changes that write curated data.\n\n## Note\n\nThis issue records a repository-rule conflict. It authorises **no** database change.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 200\ndepends_on:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T16:01:33Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T01:57:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1827,"title":"Routing rule and migration-author lease gate disagree for curated Master Data shipping a migration","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1827"},

{"body":"Spec only. No implementation here, and I am not touching `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` while #1813 and #1799 are open on it.\n\n## Why\n\nThe review path emits an assignment and then relies on the session that ran the review to write the outcome down by hand. Seen twice in two days, two pull requests, two lanes, neither careless:\n\n- #1821 — review genuinely ran; the verdict survives only as post-merge prose citing a seven-character SHA. Under #1818's rule that fails twice: the verdict does not open its line, and a short SHA is not an exact-head pin.\n- #1813 — rounds 3 and 4 genuinely ran; the output existed only as local files on one machine (background job output in the session's task directory, evidence packets under a local review-sandbox path). Nothing was posted to the PR or the issue, nothing went through the governed reviewer path, so no ref recorded any of it.\n\nBoth were honest sessions reporting real outcomes. That is the finding: **truthfulness is not the failure mode, durability is.** A verdict that lives in a context window dies with it, and the merge gate cannot act on a memory.\n\nThis blocks #1818. An enforced exact-head approval gate with no artifact for it to read refuses every merge through the guarded lane, indefinitely. Ordering is therefore **#1819 → this → #1818 → #1822**. Recorded in #1816 as data points 5 and 6.\n\n## What the review path must emit\n\nOne ref per verdict, create-only:\n\n```\nrefs/db-review-verdicts/<issue>-<pr>-<headSha>[-slot<N>]\n```\n\nSame naming grammar as `refs/db-review-assignments` so `parseAssignmentRef` in `scripts/check-exact-head-approval.mjs` extends to it without a second parser. Slot suffix and a replacement namespace (`refs/db-review-verdict-replacements/...`) mirror the assignment side exactly — a replaced reviewer's verdict must be recordable, and a replacement replaces silence, never a verdict.\n\nThe ref points at a commit whose message carries the payload, following the existing `makeOwnerCommit` pattern used for `db-preview-ready`:\n\n| field | rule |\n|---|---|\n| `verdict` | exactly one of `APPROVE`, `REVISE`, `REJECT`. No free text in this field, ever. |\n| `head_sha` | full 40 characters. A short SHA is a validation error, not a warning. |\n| `issue`, `pr`, `slot` | integers, must match the ref name. |\n| `reviewer` | must equal the reviewer named in the assignment this verdict answers. |\n| `assignment_sha` | the object SHA of the assignment ref being answered. |\n| `findings_digest` | sha256 of the reviewer's raw output. |\n| `findings_ref` | where that raw output was posted, so a human can read it. |\n\nRendering to a PR comment stays, for humans. It stops being the record.\n\n## Where it lives\n\nThe same object, read by both sides. Today the assigner writes refs and `previewGateProof` reads comments — two representations that can disagree, and did. After this there is one:\n\n- the assigner writes the assignment ref;\n- the review path writes the verdict ref as its terminal step, before returning anything to the caller;\n- `check-exact-head-approval.mjs` reads the verdict ref;\n- `previewGateProof` reads the verdict ref.\n\n`previewGateProof` currently regex-matches `/\\bAPPROVE\\b/i` anywhere in a comment body. That is the same trap as #1822 and it must move to the ref, not be re-patched.\n\n## How a session is prevented from writing it by hand\n\nThis is the part that matters, and I want to be exact rather than reassuring: **a session with repository write access can forge any ref.** Nothing here makes forgery impossible. What it can do is remove the ordinary route, and make the extraordinary one leave a mark.\n\n1. **Create-only, never force-updated.** The review path writes the verdict before the session sees the outcome. A later hand-write finds the ref occupied. Use the existing `createRefWithReadback`; forbid `updateRef` on this namespace.\n2. **The verdict commit is a child of the assignment commit.** Parent it to `assignment_sha`. A hand-rolled verdict has the wrong parent chain, and the chain is cheap to verify.\n3. **Written under the reviewer lease.** The verdict may only be created while `refs/db-review-active/<reviewer>` is held for that assignment. The lease is released when the run ends, so a verdict written afterwards is written without one and is refusable on that basis alone.\n4. **The gate cross-checks identity.** Reject any verdict whose `reviewer` did not hold the assignment or its replacement. A session cannot approve its own change by naming someone else.\n5. **`findings_digest` must match `findings_ref`.** A verdict with no readable findings behind it is not a verdict.\n\nRules 1–3 mean a forged verdict requires a deliberate, differently-shaped act that leaves evidence, rather than being the path of least resistance — which is what it is today. That is tamper-evidence, not tamper-proofness, and it should be written down as tamper-evidence so nobody later mistakes it for more.\n\n## Tests I would want before believing it\n\nOrdinary coverage will pass on day one and prove little. Per #1816's second mechanical rule:\n\n- Drive the **adapter** with real GitHub payload shapes, not hand-built objects. Both defects of this class in the last week were a conversion layer whose test shape diverged from its production shape while the suite stayed green.\n- Mutation-check it: break the verdict enum, drop the parent check, drop the lease check, drop the reviewer-identity check. Each must fail at least one test. If any mutation stays green, that rule is decorative.\n- Cover the honest-but-undurable case directly: a review that ran, returned a real verdict, and wrote no ref must be **refused at merge**. That is the case that produced this issue, and it currently passes.\n\n## Not in scope\n\nBackfilling verdicts for merges that already happened. Those are logged in #1816 and stay logged; inventing artifacts for them retroactively would be the exact thing this issue exists to prevent.\n\ncc #1816 #1818 #1822\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-01T17:18:04Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T01:46:50Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1824,"title":"The review path emits no durable verdict artifact, so every verdict is one context window from never having happened","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:50Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1824"},
{"body":"Found live by the orchestrator session on 2026-08-29.\n\nA lane wrote an ordinary progress comment on its own PR that named the exact head SHA and contained the word REVISE. The tooling treats any comment pairing a head SHA with a verdict word as a recorded verdict, so the note read as a refusal and permanently blocked review assignment at that head. The lane locked its own PR with its own status update. It recovered by editing the comment to break the pairing.\n\nTwo things make this worse than an inconvenience:\n\n1. **The symptom is not comment-shaped.** It surfaces as an unexplained review-assignment refusal. Nobody looks at their own progress note.\n2. **Under #1818 a self-locked head is unmergeable**, not merely awkward — the enforced gate refuses a head carrying an unanswered refusal.\n\n#1818 now narrows its own reading: a verdict must OPEN its line (markdown emphasis and quoting allowed), which is how the reviewer wrappers emit verdicts and is not how anyone writes a status update. The rule is symmetric, so prose cannot grant an approval either. That fixes the merge gate's exposure.\n\n**It does not fix the review-assignment path**, which does its own pairing check and is where the lane actually got stuck. That path should adopt the same lead-the-line rule so the two cannot disagree about what counts as a verdict — a gate and an assigner with different definitions is its own bug. Filing separately rather than widening #1818 beyond its review.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T12:01:46Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T01:38:11Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1822,"title":"A progress comment naming a head SHA and a verdict word silently locks that head","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:51Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1822"},
{"body":"Discovered while remediating #1769. `plm.wwe_*` merged to main (PR #1809, merge commit `2b68e7e2a93dc38391a653726209fa290d9e7d62`) at head `8d3c31accd5b21ea669e65f5ae53f5f95cc57337` with **no approval at that head** — the sole assignment ref `refs/db-review-assignments/1769-1809-b494401028464ef8b2e67fe0b5b1836839b2be36` is an earlier head that grok-4.6 REJECTed. Obtaining the missing exact-head APPROVE retroactively is currently **impossible**, because reviewer assignment refuses on any merged PR.\n\nReproduced live:\n\n```\n$ node scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --assign-reviewer --issue 1769 --pr 1809 \\\n    --head-sha 8d3c31accd5b21ea669e65f5ae53f5f95cc57337\nREFUSED: review assignment issue, PR head, or verdict changed after mutex acquisition\n```\n\nRoot cause is the post-mutex freshness check in `assignNextReviewerOperation` (~line 1688):\n\n```js\nif(fresh?.issue?.state!=='open'||fresh?.pr?.state!=='open'||fresh?.pr?.head?.sha!==request.headSha||freshVerdict)\n  throw new LaneError('review assignment issue, PR head, or verdict changed after mutex acquisition')\n```\n\n`fresh.pr.state` is `closed` for a merged PR, so the guard fires unconditionally. The head SHA itself is still correct and still readable on a merged PR — only the openness predicate blocks. The same `state==='open'` predicate also gates active-lease creation at ~lines 1644 and 1655, so even if the refusal were lifted there the reviewer would be assigned without a serializing lease.\n\nThis is the reviewer-rotation counterpart of the preview-dispatch merged-PR blindness being fixed separately in #1815, and it is a distinct defect on a distinct code path. AGENTS.md §4 rule 2 is merge-first, so post-merge remediation is a legitimate, expected state that this tooling must support.\n\n**Fix direction:** treat a *merged* PR as an eligible assignment target — permit `pr.state==='open'` **or** (`pr.merged===true` and its merge commit is in main history, via the existing `mergeCommitInMain`). Keep every other guard exactly as-is: issue still open, exact head SHA still required, existing-verdict-for-head still refuses. A **closed-but-unmerged** PR must stay refused — an abandoned branch has no claim on a reviewer. Extend the lease-creation predicate at ~1644/1655 identically so merged-PR assignments are serialized like any other.\n\nRegression tests must cover: merged PR assigned at its merged head; closed-unmerged PR still refused; merged PR whose merge commit is absent from main still refused; and a merged PR that already has a verdict for that head still refused.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 500\nobjects: scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs (assignNextReviewerOperation)\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T02:01:24Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T01:14:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1817,"title":"Reviewer assignment refuses merged PRs, making post-merge exact-head approval impossible","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:53Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1817"},
{"body":"## Machine block\n\n```\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-session\n```\n\n## Gate gap\n\nPR #1809 merged as `2b68e7e2a93dc38391a653726209fa290d9e7d62` at head `8d3c31accd5b21ea669e65f5ae53f5f95cc57337` with **zero approvals tied to that head**.\n\nThe only assignment ref was `refs/db-review-assignments/1769-1809-b494401028464ef8b2e67fe0b5b1836839b2be36` (grok-4.6), pinned to an **earlier** head. Grok returned REJECT. Commit `8d3c31a` was then pushed to answer those findings, and the PR merged at that new head with no re-review.\n\nResult: `plm.wwe_*` structures are live on main with bytes that were never independently approved.\n\n## Why this is a gate gap, not a one-off\n\nThe guarded-merge path is supposed to make an exact-head independent APPROVE a precondition of merging. It did not refuse here. Any PR that answers a REJECT with a new commit and then merges can reproduce this. The exact-head evidence rule is enforced by convention in the orchestrator's instructions but evidently not by the merge gate itself.\n\n## Asks\n\n1. Determine why guarded-migration-merge did not refuse the unapproved head — missing check, or a check that passed on a stale/mismatched ref.\n2. Close the gap so a merge is refused unless a non-stale APPROVE exists for the exact head being merged.\n3. Add a regression test covering the REJECT-then-new-commit-then-merge sequence.\n\nRemediation of #1769's own missing approval is being handled separately under claim #1805; this issue covers only the gate.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T15:18:45Z","createdAt":"2026-08-30T01:11:05Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1816,"title":"Guarded merge allowed a head with no review approval (PR #1809 / issue #1769)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:28:54Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1816"},

{"body":"```db-claim\nversion: none\nobjects:\n  # none yet — repair issue, no migration required\n```\n\n## Problem\n\n`assignNextReviewerOperation` in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` reserves\n`requireReviewWireCapacity(13)` before acquiring the review mutex (line ~1585/1613 area).\nThis 13-request reserve, together with `REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT = 19`, leaves only\n6 requests of headroom for everything called before that point in the same operation:\n`reviewersForOrchestrator()`, `resolveSlotOneReviewer()` (for slot >= 2), and\n`findBusyReviewers(io)`.\n\n`findBusyReviewers` is O(existing reviewer-lease refs): it has to read each\n`refs/db-review-active/<reviewer>` ref, fetch that PR's state, and check evidence/verdicts\nto decide whether the lease is stale. With all 6 reviewer providers carrying a lease\nrecord (live or stale-but-still-present), this alone costs well more than 6 requests.\n\nResult: **`--review-slot 2` deterministically fails** with\n`REFUSED: reviewer operation cannot fit 13 remaining requests inside the 19-request budget`\nwhenever the shared review system has been busy recently — independent of whether the\nleases are actually live or already stale. Reproduced 57 consecutive times over about an\nhour against PR #1748 / issue #1722, including after two of the six busy leases' PRs\n(#1712, #1811) merged and should have freed capacity — the failure persisted because\n`findBusyReviewers` still has to *read and evaluate* every existing lease ref, live or\nstale, before it can report which providers are actually free.\n\nThis blocks every migration lane needing two reviewers (see #1722), which is the whole\npopulation of structural work in this repository, whenever there's realistic concurrent\nreview activity (i.e. always, at this repo's current throughput).\n\n## Fix\n\nRe-size the budget so slot >= 2 can actually complete under realistic lease-ref counts.\nOptions for whoever picks this up (pick whichever fits the existing design cleanly):\n\n- Raise `REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT` (and/or `REVIEW_QUOTA_RESERVE`) enough that\n  `findBusyReviewers` over all `ACTIVE_REVIEWERS` plus the mandatory 13-request mutex\n  reserve always fits, with a documented worst-case calculation (number of reviewers ×\n  calls-per-lease-check + fixed overhead), not a guessed constant.\n- Or reduce `findBusyReviewers`'s per-lease cost (e.g. batch the PR/evidence lookups it\n  already caches via `reviewOperationIo`'s proxy, or skip evidence-fetching for leases\n  whose PR is already closed/merged before checking verdicts).\n- Or make the 13-request reserve tighter/lazier so slot-2's actual downstream request\n  count is measured rather than a flat worst-case constant.\n\nWhatever the mechanism, add a test that exercises `--review-slot 2` (or the exported\n`assignNextReviewer`/`assignNextReviewerOperation` function directly) with all 6\n`ACTIVE_REVIEWERS` holding lease refs (mix of live and stale) and asserts it succeeds\nwithin the budget, so this regresses loudly next time.\n\n## Evidence\n\nSee issue #1722 / PR #1748 comment thread for the full reproduction, including the\n`refs/db-review-active/*` and `refs/db-review-assignments/*` states observed on\n2026-08-28/29 and the exact repeated error text.\n\nClose this issue when the fix merges to `main` and #1722's slot-2 assignment succeeds.","closedAt":"2026-08-30T09:56:29Z","createdAt":"2026-08-29T01:53:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1812,"title":"Fix --review-slot 2 request-budget sizing bug in manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:47:52Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1812"},

{"body":"## Bug\n\n\\`githubIo.readActiveReviewLeases()\\` (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs ~line 706) queries:\n\n\\`\\`\\`graphql\nrefs(refPrefix:\"refs/db-review-active/\", first:10){ nodes{ name target{oid ... on Commit{message}} } }\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nGitHub's GraphQL API only supports listing refs under \\`refs/heads/\\` and \\`refs/tags/\\` via \\`refPrefix\\` — arbitrary custom ref namespaces (like \\`refs/db-review-active/*\\`) always return an empty \\`nodes\\` array, even when the refs exist. Confirmed directly:\n\n\\`\\`\\`\n$ gh api graphql -f query='query($owner:String!,$name:String!){repository(owner:$owner,name:$name){refs(refPrefix:\"refs/db-review-active/\",first:10){nodes{name}}}}}' -F owner=u2giants -F name=shared-db\n{\"data\":{\"repository\":{\"refs\":{\"nodes\":[]}}}}\n$ git ls-remote https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db.git 'refs/db-review-active/kimi-k3'\nf5f659b77cc7712224d94627fb56c4e8ee60c1d1\trefs/db-review-active/kimi-k3\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n## Effect\n\n\\`findBusyReviewers\\` always sees an empty lease snapshot, so every reviewer looks unassigned/free. \\`--assign-reviewer\\` then picks a reviewer whose lease ref already exists (stale or live) and issues \\`--force-with-lease=refs/db-review-active/<name>:\\` (empty = expects the ref to be absent). The push is correctly rejected by git every time with \\`(stale info)\\`, so **every reviewer assignment in the repository is currently blocked**, indistinguishable from real optimistic-concurrency contention.\n\n## Fix direction\n\nReplace the \\`refPrefix\\` listing with per-ref \\`ref(qualifiedName: \\\"refs/db-review-active/<name>\\\")\\` lookups (one per entry in \\`ACTIVE_REVIEWERS\\`/\\`OVERFLOW_REVIEWERS\\`), the same pattern already used correctly in \\`readReviewRefs\\`. Batch them in one GraphQL query by aliasing, same style as \\`readReviewStates\\`.\n\n## Scope\n\n\\`\\`\\`db-work\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nstatus: ready\nobjects: scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs (readActiveReviewLeases)\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThis blocks every open PR in the repo from getting a reviewer assigned. Treat as a priority repair.","closedAt":"2026-08-28T23:47:50Z","createdAt":"2026-08-28T23:20:48Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1803,"title":"Reviewer allocator: readActiveReviewLeases always returns empty (GraphQL refPrefix does not list custom refs)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:47:55Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1803"},
{"body":"PR #1777 (`fix: harden bounded reviewer allocation`, commit 74a6e00) added a hard fail-closed gate in `findBusyReviewers`:\n\n```js\ntry{cutover=io.readRef(REVIEW_ACTIVE_CUTOVER_REF)}catch{return null}\nif(!cutover)throw new LaneError('active reviewer lease cutover is incomplete; assignment refused')\n```\n\n`REVIEW_ACTIVE_CUTOVER_REF` (`refs/db-coordination/reviewer-index-cutover`) is never written by any code path. That means every call to `--assign-reviewer` against the real repository refuses outright with `active reviewer lease cutover is incomplete`, repo-wide, until someone manually creates that ref by hand with no audit of in-flight reviews. The hardening in #1777 shipped without its own activation step.\n\n## Fix\n\nAdds `--activate-review-cutover`, a one-time governed activation operation in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`:\n\n- Bounded live audit of every currently open pull request's durable assignment refs, to find any review that was already live before cutover existed.\n- Backfills the `refs/db-review-active/<reviewer>` lease for any such live review, under the existing reviewer mutex, before the cutover ref is created — so `findBusyReviewers` never loses visibility into a review already in flight the moment cutover flips on.\n- Creates `REVIEW_ACTIVE_CUTOVER_REF` via the existing atomic createRef-with-readback pattern.\n- Fails closed on any unproven step of the audit (unreadable PR head, unreadable assignment ref, unrecognized reviewer) — no cutover ref is written unless the whole audit succeeded.\n- Idempotent on retry: if the cutover ref already exists, it returns immediately with no writes.\n\nAlso whitelists the new mutex owner-commit message in `recoverStaleAuthorMutex`'s recognized-lock regex, and regenerates the throughput-guard truth-audit inventory for the shifted line numbers.\n\nTests added in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`. Full suite (769 tests) passes.\n\nPer the shared-db orchestrator's own written instruction, the new command was built and tested only — it was not run against the live repository. Someone with authority over shared-db coordination refs still needs to run `--activate-review-cutover` once against production to actually lift the repo-wide block.\n\nFixes the gap left by #1777.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T10:47:41Z","createdAt":"2026-08-28T23:06:28Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1798,"title":"PR #1777 gated reviewer assignment on a cutover ref that nothing creates","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:29:00Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1798"},
{"body":"## Summary\n\nPR #1777 (\\\"harden bounded reviewer allocation\\\") added a hard gate in\n\\`findBusyReviewers(io)\\` in \\`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs\\`:\n\n\\`\\`\\`js\nif(!io.readRef(REVIEW_ACTIVE_CUTOVER_REF))throw new LaneError('active reviewer lease cutover is incomplete; assignment refused')\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nwhere \\`REVIEW_ACTIVE_CUTOVER_REF = 'refs/db-coordination/reviewer-index-cutover'\\`.\n\nThat ref was never actually written to the repository. As a result every\n\\`--assign-reviewer\\` invocation now fails repo-wide with:\n\n> active reviewer lease cutover is incomplete; assignment refused\n\n## Root cause\n\nThe verification doc for PR #1777,\n\\`docs/verification/reviewer-assignment-api-budget-2026-08-28.md\\`, documents a\n\"Cutover audit\" (a bounded GraphQL read that found five open PRs, zero\nGitHub review verdicts, and zero active reviewer refs) and concludes \"no\npre-cutover active lease needed creation.\" That audit was real, but nothing\nin the merged code or the PR ever executed the corresponding write: creating\n\\`REVIEW_ACTIVE_CUTOVER_REF\\` itself. The plan (\\`plan_reviewer_assignment_api_budget.md\\`,\naround line 172 and the \"Cutover misses a review already in flight\" risk at\nline 311) explicitly calls for an activation step that creates any needed\nactive refs for live pre-cutover reviews and then flips the cutover ref on.\nThat step was described but never built or run.\n\n## Fix\n\nAdds a governed \\`--activate-review-cutover\\` CLI operation to\n\\`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs\\` that:\n\n1. Re-audits every currently open pull request's assignment ref at its exact\n   current head (bounded by open-PR count).\n2. Backfills the active lease (\\`refs/db-review-active/<reviewer>\\`) for any\n   assignment that is still genuinely live (PR open, head unchanged, no\n   verdict), under the existing coordination mutex.\n3. Only then creates \\`refs/db-coordination/reviewer-index-cutover\\` via the\n   established atomic-ref-with-readback pattern.\n4. Fails closed if any part of the audit can't be proven, and is a safe\n   no-op if the ref already exists.\n\nThe existing gate in \\`findBusyReviewers\\` is left untouched. This must be run\ndeliberately against the live repository (not as part of this PR) with the\nrest of the fleet quiesced, since it mutates shared coordination refs.","closedAt":"2026-08-28T23:08:13Z","createdAt":"2026-08-28T23:05:34Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1797,"title":"Reviewer-index cutover ref was never created after PR #1777, blocking all --assign-reviewer calls","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:48:02Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1797"},
{"body":"## What\n\nAdd a governed second-reviewer slot to `assignNextReviewer` in\n`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, so a migration PR can get a\ngenuinely independent SECOND reviewer bound to the same (issue, PR, head SHA)\ntuple, per AGENTS.md's \"migrations ... still need two [independent reviewers]\"\nrule.\n\n## Why this is blocking real work\n\nPR #1748 (issue #1722) has one valid APPROVE at its exact head and no\ngoverned way to get a second independent reviewer -- `assignNextReviewer` is\nintentionally idempotent per (issue, pr, headSha) and just returns the same\nfirst reviewer again, and `--replace-failed-reviewer` is correctly gated on a\ngenuine failure and must not be repurposed to fabricate a second reviewer\nafter a clean APPROVE. The same gap will block #1658, #1684, and #1645.\n\n## Scope\n\nTooling/scripts only. No `supabase/migrations/*.sql` file is created or\ntouched, and no migration-author lane is claimed.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-29T00:11:12Z","createdAt":"2026-08-28T22:38:07Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1792,"title":"tools: add second-reviewer slot to assignNextReviewer","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:29:02Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1792"},

{"body":"## Outcome\n\nEnforce the Google OrderList input-versus-automatic contract in PopDAM's database RPCs so browser/API callers cannot change calculated, lookup, tracking-feed, canonical Master Data, diagnostic, or helper fields.\n\n## Routing\n\n\n\n## Source-grounded business rule\n\nLive Google workbook `1i1da5J0qy5a0EvsO1CvfyQ6Xijn4678LG7TFqbwxwUk`, tab `Order` (`gid=0`), was inspected on 2026-08-28. Blue header columns are human inputs. Light gray columns are automatic lookup/calculation/tracking values (several explicitly say `This is an automatic column`). Dark gray columns are derived PO-writing helpers. PopDAM must visually mirror this and the RPC must reject writes to non-input fields.\n\nGoogle blue input columns:\n\n- J Order Person\n- K Order Type\n- L Customer\n- N Customer PO #\n- O Assortment ID\n- P Style #\n- R Order Depth\n- U Quantity\n- V Case Pack\n- X Ship To\n- Y Start Ship Date\n- Z Cancel Date\n\nSpecial handling:\n\n- B Import PO # is yellow and is needed to create an order, but must be immutable after creation.\n- Customer is stored as canonical `company_id`, never copied customer text.\n- `voided` and `void_reason` remain valid correction controls.\n- `source_style_type` is automatic matching evidence in Google. Preserve a safe way to resolve a genuinely ambiguous Licensed/Generic Style # without making other derived fields writable.\n- Service ingestion/import paths must retain their capabilities. Do not solve this by weakening or disabling the existing source feeds.\n\n## Required enforcement\n\n1. `public.create_dam_order` accepts only creation identity plus user-input fields and the minimum safe matching discriminator.\n2. `public.update_dam_order` accepts only the blue user-input fields, canonical `company_id`, and void/restore controls; it rejects automatic fields with the existing `42501` contract.\n3. Automatic fields currently accepted by the RPC (status, dates/tracking fields, suffix, cases, cargo forecast, helper/status fields, etc.) become non-writable through these user RPCs.\n4. Add contract tests proving every allowed key succeeds and every automatic/derived key fails.\n5. Preview-test, independently review, merge, promote to production through the governed lane, and return the exact production proof to PopDAM before its dependent UI ships.\n\n## PopDAM follow-up\n\nAfter production enforcement lands, PopDAM will mark input columns blue, automatic/linked/helper columns gray with clear tooltips, remove automatic fields from the edit dialog and cell editing, add the canonical Customer picker if required, test, deploy, and verify signed in.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 900\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function public.create_dam_order\n  - function public.update_dam_order\n  - function plm.dam_order_allowed_header_keys\n  - function plm.dam_order_allowed_line_keys\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-31T07:31:10Z","createdAt":"2026-08-28T17:14:57Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1772,"title":"Enforce OrderList input-only write contract from Google color rules","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:29:18Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1772"},
{"body":"Create the `plm.wwe_*` table family in the `plm` schema to hold the WWE licensor\ncapture — the submissions portal (Dependable Solutions) and the creative\nstyle-guide portal (Frontify).\n\nFull spec, including observed row counts and example values, lives in the\nprivate repo `u2giants/licensor-source-data` at `wwe/docs/wwe-shared-db-table-spec.md`.\nNo licensor data is reproduced here by design.\n\n## Shape\n\nModelled directly on the existing `plm.sega_*` family — same platform on the\nsubmissions side — plus a new creative-portal side. Every table carries\n`capture_id uuid` and `raw jsonb`, so a load is fully re-derivable from its\ncapture. Sits alongside the existing `plm.contract_property*` tables.\n\n### Capture headers\n- `wwe_submission_capture` — columns as `sega_submission_capture`.\n- `wwe_creative_capture` — columns as `sega_capture`, plus `portal_base_url`,\n  `brand_paging_terminal`, `folder_paging_terminal`, `asset_paging_terminal`,\n  and a `guidelines_visible` / `guidelines_reported` pair so the\n  account-visibility gap stays auditable.\n\n### Submissions side (authoritative for property identity)\n- `wwe_contract` — `contract_source_id`, `contract_label`\n- `wwe_property` — `property_source_id`, `property_label`,\n  `parent_property_source_id`, `license_type_label`, `source_url`, `source_hash`\n- `wwe_contract_property` — contract to property grant\n- `wwe_product_entitlement` — `product_label`, `category_label`,\n  `sub_category_label`, `article_label`, `contract_source_id`,\n  `property_source_id`\n- `wwe_submission` — `submission_number`, `submission_code`, `licensor_label`,\n  `contract_label`, `company_label`, `sku`, `submission_type`, `samples`,\n  `date_submitted`, `response_date`, `submitted_by`, `status`, `source_url`\n- `wwe_submission_ip` — `submission_number`, `ip_ordinal`, `ip_label`,\n  `normalized_ip_label` (the multi-valued free-text IP field, split)\n- `wwe_submission_stage` — `stage_label`, `stage_ordinal`, `revision_number`,\n  `stage_status`\n- `wwe_submission_image` — `image_source_id`, `stage`\n- `wwe_submission_comment` — `stage`, `posted_on`, `author`, `body`,\n  `comment_hash`\n\n### Creative side\n- `wwe_creative_brand` — `brand_source_id`, `brand_label`\n- `wwe_style_guide` — `guideline_source_id`, `brand_source_id`,\n  `guideline_label`, `page_count`, `source_url`\n- `wwe_style_guide_page` — `page_source_id`, `page_title`, `page_ordinal`\n- `wwe_asset_library` — `library_source_id`, `brand_source_id`,\n  `library_label`, `library_kind`, `asset_count`\n- `wwe_asset_folder` — self-parented tree: `folder_source_id`,\n  `parent_folder_source_id`, `folder_label`, `folder_path`, `folder_depth`\n- `wwe_asset` — `asset_source_id`, `library_source_id`, `title`, `file_name`,\n  `extension`, `asset_kind`, `width`, `height`, `source_status`,\n  `source_created_at`, `source_modified_at`, `creator_label`,\n  `copyright_status`, `copyright_notice`, `source_hash`\n- `wwe_asset_folder_member` — asset to folder, many-to-many\n- `wwe_asset_tag` — `asset_source_id`, `tag_source_key`, `tag_value`,\n  `tag_source` (the portal flags each tag as manually entered or\n  machine-generated; both are kept and the flag must survive the load)\n- `wwe_tag` — deduplicated tag dimension\n\n### Derived / inference tables\nMirroring the Sega `*_candidate` / `*_inferred` pattern. Nothing here is\nlicensor truth; every row carries `match_method`, `rule_version`, `confidence`,\n`relationship_truth`.\n- `wwe_character_candidate` — `character_candidate_key`, `candidate_label`,\n  `normalized_candidate_label`, `inference_method`, `rule_version`\n- `wwe_character_evidence`\n- `wwe_character_property_inferred`\n- `wwe_asset_property_inferred`\n- `wwe_style_guide_property_inferred`\n- `wwe_asset_style_guide_inferred`\n\n## Relationships\n\n```\nwwe_contract -< wwe_contract_property >- wwe_property\nwwe_contract -< wwe_product_entitlement\nwwe_property -< wwe_submission -< wwe_submission_ip\n                              |-< wwe_submission_stage\n                              |-< wwe_submission_image\n                              \\-< wwe_submission_comment\n\nwwe_creative_brand -< wwe_style_guide -< wwe_style_guide_page\nwwe_creative_brand -< wwe_asset_library -< wwe_asset_folder (self-parented)\nwwe_asset_library  -< wwe_asset -< wwe_asset_tag >- wwe_tag\nwwe_asset >- wwe_asset_folder_member -< wwe_asset_folder\n\nwwe_character_candidate   <- fed by wwe_submission_ip, wwe_asset_folder, wwe_asset_tag\nwwe_character_candidate  -< wwe_character_evidence\nwwe_character_candidate  -< wwe_character_property_inferred   >- wwe_property\nwwe_asset                -< wwe_asset_property_inferred       >- wwe_property\nwwe_style_guide          -< wwe_style_guide_property_inferred >- wwe_property\nwwe_asset                -< wwe_asset_style_guide_inferred    >- wwe_style_guide\n```\n\n## Constraints the load must respect\n\n- The submissions side is canonical for property identity. Creative-portal\n  labels may only be added *below* that level — never rename, split, or merge a\n  submissions-derived property.\n- The submissions portal exposes a single property and no child IPs;\n  character-level detail exists only as free text on submission detail pages,\n  and reflects what this licensee submitted, not the licensor's full vocabulary.\n- The creative portal shows this account fewer style guides than it reports as\n  existing. Both counts must be stored, not reconciled away.\n- Structure only. No row data is loaded from this issue; the capture in the\n  private repo is the source.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - schema plm\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T16:18:12Z","createdAt":"2026-08-28T16:13:05Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. It reports `pull request removes a file; split recovery refuses it`, even though the PR removes no migration.\n\nLive evidence from #1684 / claim #1711: the check in `migrationVersions(files)` rejects any `status=removed` file before restricting the list to `supabase/migrations/`. The command failed before mutation: claim #1711 still owns `20260827224649`, the permanent reservation remains, no supersession ref exists, and PR #1712 head `95e298f538f3243fe1f0dae89d277ef7ec55f186` is clean.\n\n## Required outcome\n\nRepair and test the manager so split/atomic supersession still refuses removal of a migration file, but does not reject unrelated removed files.
