{"body":"Follow-up to #1657 (merged, verified). Both indexes from #1657 are live in production and they worked — but the measurement afterwards shows one remaining term worth removing, and it is the dominant one.\n\n## Request\n\nWiden the bridge index from #1657 into a covering index:\n\n```sql\ncreate index concurrently if not exists style_tracker_item_bridge_plm_item_cover_idx\n  on plm.style_tracker_item_bridge (plm_item_id)\n  include (id, style_tracker_row_id, tracker_type);\n\ndrop index concurrently if exists plm.style_tracker_item_bridge_plm_item_idx;\n```\n\nThe `include` columns are exactly the three columns `api.dam_order_list` projects from the bridge (`20260810010000_popdam_order_list_contract.sql:534-537`), plus the join key.\n\n## Measured state after #1657 (production, `set role authenticated`, 2026-08-27)\n\nConfirmed both indexes exist and are used. Warm count went **161 ms → 77-86 ms**. Cold shared-buffer reads went **24,835 → 4,707 (~194 MB → ~37 MB)**.\n\nBut a cold `explain (analyze, buffers)` run still took **1,481 ms**, and the reason is visible in the plan:\n\n```\n->  Memoize  (Hits: 17941  Misses: 6069)\n      Buffers: shared hit=14328 read=3910\n      ->  Index Scan using style_tracker_item_bridge_plm_item_idx on style_tracker_item_bridge\n            Buffers: shared hit=14328 read=3910\n```\n\n**3,910 of the 4,707 remaining cold reads — 83% — are random heap fetches into `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge`.** The plain index finds the row but must then visit the heap for `id`, `style_tracker_row_id` and `tracker_type`, and that heap is 132 MB for ~24 MB of live data (15,619 rows, ~5x bloat). Random reads into a bloated heap are the worst remaining case: fewer buffers than the old seq scan, but no prefetch.\n\n## Why the covering index closes it\n\n`relallvisible = relpages = 16943` — the table is **100% all-visible**, so an index-only scan will do essentially zero heap fetches. Validated with `hypopg` on production (hypothetical only, nothing created):\n\n- with the plain index (current production): plan cost **7,129**\n- with the covering index: bridge becomes an **Index Only Scan**, plan cost **3,128**\n\nRemaining cold reads would fall from ~4,707 to roughly **~800 (~6 MB)** — the residue is two small seq scans on `production_order` (224) and `production_order_line_source_ref` (375).\n\nIt also helps the **row** queries, not just the count: a 100-row grid block with the bridge columns selected also plans as an Index Only Scan on the bridge under the covering index. Those run on every scroll.\n\n## Scope / risk\n\n- Additive, then a drop of the now-redundant narrower index; both `concurrently`, no write lock.\n- The covering index supersedes `style_tracker_item_bridge_plm_item_idx` completely (same leading column), so index count does not grow. Create first, drop second.\n- Slightly wider index (three extra columns: uuid, uuid, text).\n- Rollback: recreate the narrow index, drop the covering one.\n- No view, RLS, grant, function or column touched. No app-side contract change.\n\n## Also worth noting (not requested here)\n\n`plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` is ~5x bloated (132 MB heap, ~24 MB live, `n_dead_tup = 0`, so autovacuum cannot reclaim it — it needs a repack). The covering index makes that non-urgent for PopDAM, but the table is now carrying 108 MB of empty space that every scan and every backup pays for.\n\n## Verification asked for\n\n```sql\nset role authenticated;\nexplain (analyze, buffers) select count(*) from api.dam_order_list;\n```\n\nExpect an **Index Only Scan** on `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` with near-zero `Heap Fetches`, and total cold `read=` under ~1,000 buffers.\n\nRequester: PopDAM session, worktree `issue-100-4a0376`, for `u2giants/popdam3#100`.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on: 1657\nwrites:\n  - index plm.style_tracker_item_bridge_plm_item_cover_idx\n  - index plm.style_tracker_item_bridge_plm_item_idx\n  - table plm.style_tracker_item_bridge\nreads:\n  - view api.dam_order_list\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T10:24:34Z","createdAt":"2026-08-28T01:16:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1722,"title":"OrderList count, follow-up to #1657: make the bridge lookup index-only (covering index) — 83% of remaining cold IO (popdam3#100)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:29:48Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1722"},
{"body":"## Outcome\n\nChange only `core.licensor` code uniqueness so multiple licensors whose owner-confirmed code is unknown (`code IS NULL`) can coexist, while every non-null licensor code remains unique. This is the minimal structural dependency blocking curated Master Data issue #1719.\n\nThe current `licensor_code_key` is `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (code)`, which permits only one null-coded row. The intended contract is ordinary PostgreSQL null-distinct uniqueness: unknown is not an identity and must not force unrelated licensors to collide. Do not invent or backfill codes, and do not change any existing row.\n\nPrivacy boundary: use synthetic test rows only. No licensed Property names, source evidence, or private contract data may enter this issue, migration, tests, logs, commit, or pull request.\n\nAcceptance:\n- replace only `core.licensor.licensor_code_key` with unique `(code)` using default `NULLS DISTINCT` semantics;\n- two synthetic rows with different names and `code IS NULL` can coexist;\n- duplicate identical non-null codes are still rejected;\n- existing licensor rows and codes are unchanged;\n- all existing foreign keys, write-authority guards, RLS, grants, triggers, and downstream code-based lookups remain intact;\n- preview verification and governed independent non-Kimi review pass before merge;\n- production promotion is limited to this exact constraint change and is verified before #1719 resumes.\n\nBlocks #1719. After production verification, dispatch #1719 again under `curated-master-data-governance`; its exact-name matched-row abstention remains mandatory.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table core.licensor\n  - constraint licensor_code_key on core.licensor\n```\n## Author-ready implementation brief (read-only derivation, 2026-08-27)\n\n### Exact current shape and blast radius\n\n- Main defines `core.licensor.code text` and `licensor_code_key UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (code)` in `20260621150815_app_core.sql`.\n- The replacement must keep the same constraint name and column and change only `pg_index.indnullsnotdistinct` from true to false.\n- Repository migrations contain 24 previously live-audited foreign keys to `core.licensor`; they reference `core.licensor(id)`, not `code`. Dropping/recreating `licensor_code_key` therefore does not detach an FK. Re-prove this from `pg_constraint.confkey` on preview and production before promotion.\n- The backing unique B-tree index is owned by the constraint and will be replaced with it. No separate index should be added.\n- Downstream code-based resolution uses equality on non-null codes (not the constraint/index OID), including the item-taxonomy resolver, PLM import matching, DAM canonical cutover, and remaining-source resolution. Default null-distinct uniqueness preserves the one-row guarantee for each non-null code and leaves these lookups unchanged.\n\n### Migration shape\n\nUse one new timestamped migration, one transaction, and a guarded `DO` block modeled on `20260810060000_popdam_order_list_source_pair_nulls_distinct.sql`:\n\n1. Find the unique constraint on exactly `core.licensor(code)` by joining `pg_constraint` to `pg_index` and `pg_attribute`.\n2. Refuse if none exists or if its name is not `licensor_code_key`; do not silently create a second unique surface.\n3. If `indnullsnotdistinct` is true, atomically `ALTER TABLE core.licensor DROP CONSTRAINT licensor_code_key`, then `ADD CONSTRAINT licensor_code_key UNIQUE NULLS DISTINCT (code)`.\n4. If it is already false, verify the same name/one-column definition and no-op.\n5. Add a privacy-safe constraint comment: null means unknown/no canonical code, multiple nulls may coexist, and known codes remain unique.\n\nThe transaction is rollback-safe: the stronger old constraint guarantees there cannot already be duplicate non-null codes, and any failure while rebuilding restores the old constraint. Do not use `DROP ... CASCADE`, `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, a partial index, data backfill, generated codes, or any DML in the migration.\n\n### Synthetic rollback-only contract test\n\nAdd a dedicated SQL contract test wrapped in `BEGIN`/`ROLLBACK`. Use synthetic names and synthetic non-null codes only. Because the licensing write guard consumes one exact transaction-bound authorization per protected write, create a fresh `licensing_review_create` authorization for each attempted insert, bound to the current backend/transaction, `core.licensor`, protected columns `name,code,status`, a synthetic plan UUID/hash, and a short expiry.\n\n- Insert two synthetic licensors with different names and `code NULL`; assert both exist inside the test transaction.\n- Insert one synthetic licensor with a non-null synthetic code.\n- With a fresh authorization, attempt a second row with the same non-null code; catch only `unique_violation` and fail if it succeeds.\n- Assert the constraint name remains `licensor_code_key`, it is validated, covers only `code`, and `indnullsnotdistinct = false`.\n- `ROLLBACK`; assert through the test runner that no fixture or authorization/audit row persists. Do not use real licensors, Properties, private source references, or licensed evidence.\n\n### Preview/production catalog verification\n\nImmediately prove the target before each apply or verification. Record:\n\n- `pg_get_constraintdef(...) = UNIQUE NULLS DISTINCT (code)` (format may include `NULLS DISTINCT` explicitly);\n- `contype = 'u'`, `convalidated = true`, exact `conkey` resolves only to `code`, and `indnullsnotdistinct = false`;\n- exactly one unique constraint/index backs `core.licensor(code)` and it is named `licensor_code_key`;\n- all FKs referencing `core.licensor` still resolve to its `id` key and have unchanged count/actions;\n- pre/post hashes and counts of existing `core.licensor` rows, IDs, names, codes, statuses, and metadata are identical;\n- synthetic rollback-only behavior test passes, duplicate non-null rejection is SQLSTATE 23505, and no synthetic rows remain.\n\nAfter exact-head preview evidence and a governed independent non-Kimi review, merge normally. Production promotion must be bounded to this one migration, re-prove the production target immediately before it, repeat catalog and unchanged-row verification, then release the claim and resume #1719.\n\n### Current collision status\n\nLatest live queue audit at derivation time: `emptyLanes: 0`, `dispatchable: []`. No claim was attempted, no migration/worktree was created, and production was not touched. Re-run the audit and atomically claim only when a lane genuinely frees.","closedAt":"2026-08-28T11:16:13Z","createdAt":"2026-08-28T00:57:52Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1720,"title":"Allow multiple unknown licensor codes without weakening known-code uniqueness","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:29:50Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1720"},

{"body":"## Outcome\n\nAdd a private, source-neutral structural landing contract for reviewed Creative-to-Submissions Property mappings. This unblocks #1669 without publishing licensed mapping rows or coupling the public repository to private source files.\n\nThe structure records exact source identities and sanitized decision state only. A separately owned private loader will populate it after production promotion.\n\n## Required structure\n\nCreate immutable, versioned `plm.creative_submission_property_resolution` decision headers keyed by exact Creative source system, source table, source ID, and decision version. Allowed states are `mapped`, `conflict`, and `unmapped`.\n\nCreate `plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member` with zero or more exact Submissions source identities per decision. Preserve both source identities exactly; never merge, normalize, fuzzy-match, or rewrite them.\n\nThe tables may retain opaque reviewed-batch identifiers or digests and approval metadata. They must not contain source labels, contract text, file paths, private repository locations, licensed payloads, or human-readable evidence.\n\n## Integrity and access\n\n- Both tables are append-only through owner-bypass-safe row mutation triggers and statement-level TRUNCATE rejection triggers.\n- One deterministic decision version exists per exact Creative identity.\n- A superseded decision has at most one direct successor.\n- Duplicate members within one decision are forbidden.\n- `mapped` requires at least one member; `unmapped` requires zero; `conflict` remains fail-closed.\n- Cross-table member rules are enforced transactionally with deferred constraint triggers.\n- Enable RLS; revoke all privileges from `public`, `anon`, and `authenticated`.\n- Grant `service_role` only `SELECT` and `INSERT`; add no authenticated read policy.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. Synthetic SQL tests prove mapped, conflict, unmapped, supersession, duplicate rejection, and deterministic latest-decision lookup.\n2. Tests prove updates, deletes, and truncation are unavailable or rejected, including the owner path.\n3. Public, anonymous, and authenticated roles cannot read or write either table.\n4. `service_role` can insert and read, but cannot update, delete, or truncate.\n5. No labels, paths, contract wording, private evidence references, licensed payload columns, mapping rows, or licensed values appear in public artifacts.\n6. The private loader remains separately owned and writes only after production promotion and exact target proof.\n7. Normal review, CI, preview, merge, production, and catalog-verification gates pass.\n\nThis issue provides only the private structural landing layer. It does not modify `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties`, UI code, browser tests, or licensed data. Final #1669 remains blocked on #1658 production completion, this structure's production promotion, sanitized private-loader completion evidence, production-backed source coverage, and #1676 only where contract-backed evidence is presented.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 2100\nwrites:\n  - table plm.creative_submission_property_resolution\n  - table plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member\n  - function plm.reject_creative_submission_property_resolution_mutation\n  - function plm.enforce_creative_submission_property_resolution_members\n  - trigger creative_submission_property_resolution_immutable on plm.creative_submission_property_resolution\n  - trigger creative_submission_property_resolution_member_immutable on plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member\n  - trigger creative_submission_property_resolution_no_truncate on plm.creative_submission_property_resolution\n  - trigger creative_submission_property_resolution_member_no_truncate on plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member\n  - trigger creative_submission_property_resolution_members_check on plm.creative_submission_property_resolution\n  - trigger creative_submission_property_resolution_member_header_check on plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member\n  - index plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_latest_idx\n  - index plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_supersedes_uidx\n  - index plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member_identity_uidx\n  - index plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member_submission_idx\nreads:\n  - table plm.creative_submission_property_resolution\n  - table plm.creative_submission_property_resolution_member\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T03:13:09Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T23:13:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## What was found\n\nWhile diagnosing why the shared preview branch showed `MIGRATIONS_FAILED`, a peer session established that the Supabase GitHub integration's **\"Deploy to production\"** switch was ON for project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` (production), and that the repository feeding it was **`u2giants/popdam3`**, not `u2giants/shared-db`.\n\nThat means production schema changes could be applied from a repository that is **not** governed by the shared-db branch-and-PR workflow, the allowlist, the review-evidence chain, or the business-risk gate.\n\nAlbert authorized that peer session in chat to turn the switch off, and it did. Verified after reload: \"Deploy to production\" OFF; automatic branching, branch limit 3, and \"Supabase changes only\" untouched; the integration itself was NOT disabled.\n\n## What is still open — needs Albert\n\nNobody has audited what is actually in `u2giants/popdam3`'s `supabase/` directory, or whether anything from it was ever applied to production. Until that audit happens we do not know whether production carries schema that shared-db has no record of.\n\n**The ask:** confirm whether `u2giants/popdam3` should keep a `supabase/` directory at all, and authorize a read-only audit of it plus a comparison against production's actual schema.\n\n**Recommendation:** yes to the audit; and `popdam3` should not carry migrations that touch the shared database — those belong in `shared-db`.\n\n## Related\n\n- #1663 — the MIGRATIONS_FAILED investigation this came out of.\n- #1675 — migration ledger drift.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: security-settings\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 500\ndepends_on:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:24:53Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T20:25:36Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1693,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] audit u2giants/popdam3's supabase directory — it was the repo wired to auto-deploy to PRODUCTION","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:30:12Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1693"},
{"body":"## Summary  Two migrations are permanently stranded before production by a correct-but-unescapable guard. This is a systemic trap, not a one-off, and it will strand the next migration the same way.  `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py::prove_historical_original_apply_runs` pins BOTH the original preview run's dispatch ref (`head_sha`) AND the artifact-named checkout commit to the **merge commit of the PR that authored the version**, and compares every file in `PREVIEW_PRODUCER_PATHS` (line 432) byte-for-byte via `prove_preview_producer_matches_main` (line 647).  ## Why that strands work  1. A branch rehearses its migration on preview at time T. 2. An unrelated PR then lands on `main` that touches a pinned producer path. PR #1677 did exactly this to `scripts/production_migration_guard.py`, which IS a pinned producer path because it executes inside the preview job. 3. The branch merges `main` (as it must), so its merge commit now carries the NEW producer bytes. 4. Production apply refuses: *\"original apply run … dispatched at … produced evidence with a different scripts/production_migration_guard.py than the merge commit … of the pull request that authored …\"*  There is no escape:  - A **historical preview recovery** cannot substitute — the same function refuses recovery-of-a-recovery: *\"original apply run … is itself a historical recovery; a recovery is only ever bound to a run that actually applied bytes\"* (observed on runs 33109639903, 33109940566, 33110202832). - A **fresh real rehearsal** is impossible because preview already holds the version in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`, so the apply is a no-op that produces no bytes-applied evidence.  ## Confirmed NOT the cause  This is not the main-SHA race. `main` was stable at `254f0db` across the last three refusals.  ## Affected right now  - `20260827183106` (issue #1467) — remedy exists: `rehearsal_reset` via PR #1687, merged at `466ffbc091c4b883732c74fc030aec42e1f3444e`. - `20260827183011` (issue #1645) — **cannot** use `rehearsal_reset`; see that issue.  ## What is wanted  A designed way for a migration to be re-rehearsed at exact current `main` after an unrelated producer-path change, without weakening the producer pin and without relaxing the transaction-control refusal in `load_replacement()`. `rehearsal_reset` is today's manual, per-tuple, allowlisted workaround; it does not scale and it does not cover migrations that create objects.  ```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 2500\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - file scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs\n  - file scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs\n  - file scripts/production_migration_guard.py\n  - file scripts/test_production_migration_guard.py\nreads:\n  - issue 1645\n  - claim 1656\n  - pull-request 1664\n``` ","closedAt":"2026-08-28T11:35:45Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T20:25:23Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1692,"title":"SYSTEMIC: the producer-path pin strands any migration whose rehearsal predates an unrelated producer-path change","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:30:13Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1692"},
{"body":"## db-work-scope\n\n- **Class:** repository maintenance / tooling correctness. **No database change**: no migration, no preview apply, no production apply, no data load.\n- **Surfaces:** `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs`, `scripts/post_batch_app_verification.py`, `scripts/production_migration_guard.py`, `scripts/test_post_batch_app_verification.py`.\n- **Blast radius:** how a human or agent answers \"is this unapplied migration deliberate?\". No schema, no data.\n\n## The gap\n\nA migration present in the repo but absent from the ledger is classified by consulting five separate registries spread across two languages:\n\n- `RETIRED_VERSION_REASONS` / `RETIRED_VERSIONS` — `scripts/post_batch_app_verification.py:343`, `:407`\n- `HELD_VERSIONS` — `scripts/post_batch_app_verification.py:410`\n- `HARD_BLOCKED` — `scripts/production_migration_guard.py:66`\n- `PREVIEW_ONLY_HISTORICAL_RESTORATIONS` — `scripts/production_migration_guard.py:190`\n- `FR_HELD_20260803` / `FR_SHIP_SET_HOLD` — `scripts/production_migration_guard.py:241`, `:289`\n\n`scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs` re-decides the classification in JavaScript (`classifyPendingWithRules`, line 147) by reading those raw Python sets, rather than asking Python for the answer.\n\nTwo concrete costs already paid:\n\n1. **A reviewer got it wrong.** On 2026-08-27 a session reported `20260817150944` and `20260824150630` as unregistered drift. They are in `PREVIEW_ONLY_HISTORICAL_RESTORATIONS` and are correctly excluded. An independent Grok review reached the same conclusion and identified the registry split as the cause of the misread — the answer requires knowing all five sets exist and which the checker actually consults.\n2. **One registry is already stale and unreferenced.** `HELD_VERSIONS` is not imported by the drift checker, yet `scripts/test_post_batch_app_verification.py:779` asserts its contents, so the test passes while the set influences nothing.\n\n## Suggested direction (not a decision)\n\nA single `classify_pending_version(version)` in Python returning one kind, with every registry behind it, and the JS drift checker calling it rather than reimplementing the rules. That makes the classification answerable in one place and removes the class of error above.\n\n## Evidence\n\n`.ai/reviews/grok-shared-db-migrations-failed-freeze-20260827T194237Z-2021807.md`.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:15:20Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T20:06:23Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1690,"title":"Migration pending-status is decided by five registries across two languages","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:48:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1690"},
{"body":"## db-work-scope\n\n- **Class:** CI workflow correctness. **No database change**: no migration, no preview apply, no production apply, no data load.\n- **Surfaces:** `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml`.\n- **Blast radius:** the production apply lane's own SHA pinning. No schema, no data.\n\n## The gap\n\nIn the production apply job, the exclusive production lane is acquired **after** the `main` SHA is verified, not before:\n\n- `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml:1249` — `Verify exact main commit` asserts `git rev-parse origin/main` equals the requested SHA.\n- `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml:1257` — `Acquire the exclusive production lane and freeze merges` runs next.\n\nBetween those two steps nothing holds `main` still. A merge that lands in that window moves `origin/main` after the equality check has already passed, so the job proceeds believing it is pinned to a SHA that is no longer head. The same verify step also appears at lines 890 and 1074 ahead of their own lanes.\n\nThis is a time-of-check / time-of-use ordering bug, and it is the mechanism *inside* the workflow that corresponds to the policy gap in #1688. #1688 asks for a surface a merge can see; this asks for the lane to be taken before the check that depends on it.\n\n## Suggested direction (not a decision)\n\nAcquire the production lane first, then verify the exact `main` commit while holding it, and fail closed if the SHA moved. That makes the pin meaningful without depending on every concurrent session having read a chat message.\n\n## Evidence\n\nIndependent review of the 2026-08-27 apply attempts: `.ai/reviews/grok-shared-db-migrations-failed-freeze-20260827T194237Z-2021807.md`.\n\n## Related\n\n- #1688 — the same failure seen from the merge-policy side.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 900\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:18:32Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T20:06:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1689,"title":"Production apply lane is acquired after the exact-main-SHA check, not before","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:48:08Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1689"},
{"body":"## db-work-scope\n\n- **Class:** repository maintenance / CI policy. **No database change**: no migration, no preview apply, no production apply, no data load.\n- **Surfaces:** `.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml`, branch protection settings, `AGENTS.md` §5.\n- **Blast radius:** merge policy on `main`. No schema, no data.\n\n## What happened\n\nOn 2026-08-27, session `shared-db.orch` declared a merge freeze on `main` while running a bounded production apply whose gate pins an exact `main` SHA. Five apply attempts were burned by `main` moving underneath it (`a343b11` → `058c51a` → `172d2bb` → `a288137` → `254f0db`). Two of those commits (#1679 and #1682) were mine — documentation-only PRs that I merged without knowing a freeze existed.\n\n## Why no mechanism stopped it\n\nReported by session `shared-db-orchestrator-3925aa-e5` from an independent Grok review, and consistent with what I observed:\n\n1. `migration-author-lease.yml` **auto-passes** the required \"Migration guarded merge authorization\" check for any PR containing no migration files.\n2. `required_status_checks.strict` is **false** by owner ruling (#1286), so a PR need not be up to date with `main` to merge.\n\nTogether, a documentation PR merges cleanly through both a chat-declared freeze and an active production apply lock. **There was no mechanism that could have stopped it.** The freeze existed only as text in a session conversation.\n\n## The gap\n\nA production apply lock is real state, and merges to `main` invalidate it — but the lock is invisible to the merge path for exactly the class of PR least likely to think about it. \"Do not merge\" currently depends on every concurrent session having read a chat message.\n\n## Suggested direction (not a decision)\n\nGive the freeze a surface a merge can see. Options, cheapest first:\n\n1. A repository-level flag (a file, a label, or a GitHub Environment) that a lightweight required check reads and fails on while set — applying to **all** PRs, not only those with migration files, since docs PRs are the ones that slip through.\n2. Turning on `required_status_checks.strict` for the duration of an apply, so any merge must first update against the pinned SHA. Note #1286 turned this off deliberately; reversing it needs the owner.\n3. Having the production apply lane itself take and release the flag, so it is never left set by a dead session.\n\nWhichever is chosen, it must **fail closed and be self-releasing**: a freeze that outlives the session holding it becomes the next blocker.\n\n## Related\n\n- Owner ruling on `strict: false`: #1286\n- Plan on issue lead time and guard truth: #1680 (this is a instance of the same class — a real constraint with no enforcement surface)\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 900\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-02T18:12:06Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T19:59:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1688,"title":"A declared merge freeze has no enforcement surface: docs-only PRs merge straight through it","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:48:11Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1688"},
{"body":"Albert's owner ruling in the current chat: `core.properties_and_characters` must no longer exist. Properties and characters are distinct datasets and must not share a typed table. Drop the combined table and create the separate `core.character` table. `core.property` already exists and remains the property dataset.\n\n## Why\n\nThe current combined table encodes two different business entities behind a `type` column. Production currently contains 10,132 rows: 510 `PROPERTY` and 9,622 `CHARACTER`. This contradicts the established model that a Property and a Character have different identities, attributes, lifecycles, and relationships. The database should express that distinction structurally:\n\n- Properties live in `core.property`.\n- Characters live in `core.character`.\n- Property-to-character membership remains an explicit relationship, not co-location in one table.\n- `core.properties_and_characters` is removed completely; no compatibility table or permanent view under that name.\n\n## Required safety and migration work\n\nThe 10,132 rows in this combined table are disposable. Their authoritative information already exists in the normalized licensor-scrape tables, so do not back up, preserve, or migrate these combined rows. Rebuild future canonical Property and Character data from those normalized sources. Inventory every application/database dependency, and repoint or deliberately retire all dependent foreign keys and routines in the same governed change. Do not use `CASCADE` as a substitute for explicitly handling dependencies.\n\nDo not copy either the 9,622 `CHARACTER` rows or the 510 `PROPERTY` rows out of the combined table. `core.character` must be created as a distinct dataset and populated only from normalized source evidence through the governed curated Master Data process. `core.property` remains separate; this issue does not authorize overwriting it.\n\nLive production dependency inventory at filing time:\n\n- `core.property_character_associations` has both property and character foreign keys to the combined table.\n- `plm.item_character_associations` has its character foreign key to the combined table.\n- Three Warner canonical-property edge tables reference the combined table.\n- `api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree(...)` reads the combined table.\n- `plm.sync_wb_canonical_relationship_edges(...)` validates against it.\n- The combined table owns five indexes that disappear with it.\n\nThe migration must follow the normal isolated branch, exact-object claim, preview rehearsal, independent review, guarded merge, and separately authorized production promotion. Verify the exact production target immediately before every write and verify afterward that `core.properties_and_characters` is absent while `core.property` and `core.character` are present with the intended contracts.\n\n## Immediate Phase 1 — EOL staging\n\nDo this first, as a separately verifiable migration before the final drop:\n\n1. Add an explicit catalog comment that the table is EOL, must receive no new dependencies, and will be removed by this issue.\n2. Add a reversible fail-closed write guard covering INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and TRUNCATE. Existing reads remain available during consumer cutover.\n3. Add repository enforcement that rejects new runtime or migration references to `core.properties_and_characters`, with an exact allowlist only for the EOL/drop migration and existing historical migrations.\n4. Prove on preview that reads still work and every write verb is rejected; then follow the normal reviewed promotion path and verify production.\n\nDo not copy, salvage, or migrate the current combined rows during this stage. The normalized scrape tables remain authoritative.\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table core.properties_and_characters\n  - function core.reject_properties_and_characters_write\n  - trigger properties_and_characters_eol_write_guard on core.properties_and_characters\n  - table core.character\n  - table core.property_character_associations\n  - table plm.item_character_associations\n  - table plm.wb_asset_canonical_property_edge\n  - table plm.wb_character_canonical_property_edge\n  - table plm.wb_style_guide_canonical_property_edge\n  - function api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree\n  - function plm.sync_wb_canonical_relationship_edges\n  - index core.idx_properties_licensor_id\n  - index core.idx_properties_name\n  - index core.properties_and_characters_pkey\n  - index core.unique_character_entity\n  - index core.unique_property_entity\n  - index core.character_licensor_code_key\n  - index core.character_licensor_id_idx\n  - index core.character_name_idx\n  - index core.property_character_associations_character_id_idx\n  - policy shared_read on core.character\n  - policy shared_read on core.property_character_associations\n  - trigger set_updated_at on core.character\n  - trigger set_updated_at on core.property_character_associations\n  - table api.wb_canonical_relationship_candidates\n  - view api.wb_canonical_relationship_candidates\nreads:\n  - table core.property\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T19:07:13Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T19:26:40Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1684,"title":"Drop core.properties_and_characters and restore separate core.character table","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:30:15Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1684"},
{"body":"Phase A gates and step C1 of the `age_group` Cloud SQL -> Supabase cutover are complete and recorded in\n[`docs/verification/age-group-cutover-phase-a-and-c1-20260827.md`](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/blob/main/docs/verification/age-group-cutover-phase-a-and-c1-20260827.md)\n(merged as `b49a5665060fcc9a100f12a096460ea44a30451c`).\n\nThis issue tracks the remainder.\n\n## What is done\n- **A1/A2/A3 — PASS.** `core.age_group` holds exactly `1 = Adult`, `2 = Juvenile`, both active. Zero foreign keys, views, matviews or functions reference it. The DesignFlow finding that no screen reads `age_group` was re-confirmed against current code.\n- **C1 — implemented and deployed to sandbox.** `designflow-backend` `models/db/AgeGroup.js` gained `schema: 'core'` (commit `1506639`). Read target proved by capturing the generated SQL with `process.env.schema` deliberately set to `dflow` — it still emits `FROM \"core\".\"age_group\"`. Cloud Build `a12b46f0-329c-40ac-8027-f9bd3781989a` SUCCESS; ready revision `popcre-albert-core-sandbox-00173-8ff`.\n\n## What remains\n1. **C2 — develop and staging.** Blocked on review of https://github.com/popcre/designflow-backend/pull/75. DesignFlow policy forbids self-merge, so this waits on a human/AI reviewer.\n2. **C3 — grade the plan's §7 claims.** Write after C2 lands. At least one row will be NOT PROVED (see finding below).\n3. **Not tested:** an authenticated `GET /api/admin/getAgeGroups` round-trip. The endpoint is behind `authRole([...])` and returned 403 without a session token — proving the service is up, not that the response is correct.\n\n## The finding that changes the grading\n`dflow.art_piece.age_group_id` holds ids in the **3760–3810** range; `core.age_group` holds ids **1 and 2**. **Zero of 1,116 art pieces reference the table.** The \"Age Group\" dropdown in the UI is fed from merch groups, not from this list. The move is therefore safer than the plan assumed and a weaker rehearsal than it hoped — it does not prove the harder Phase D moves.\n\n## Owner decisions pending\n- **A design question for the PR #75 reviewer.** `createAgeGroup` / `updateAgeGroup` / `deleteAgeGroup` now target `core` too. They are unreachable from the UI, but if wired up an application write would land in the shared `core` schema. Decide whether this model should be read-only from DesignFlow's side. Recommendation: make it read-only.\n- **Phase D (production) remains NOT APPROVED and NOT SCHEDULED.** It additionally needs production Cloud SQL reads — `dflow_prod` cannot substitute, as `dflow_prod.age_group` and `dflow_prod.art_piece` are both empty shells from `20260824011750_create_dflow_prod_and_audit_archive`.\n\n## Note for future least-privilege work\nThere are no role grants on `core.age_group` at all. The backend reads it through the Supabase pooler as `postgres.<ref>`, which maps to `postgres`. It works by role privilege, not by explicit grant.\n\nRelated: #1663 (migration ledger drift, separate workstream).\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: application-data\nroute: application-session\nreturn_to: popcre/designflow-backend\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: #75\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T01:37:54Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T19:16:10Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1681,"title":"age_group cutover: finish C2 (develop/staging) and C3 (grading)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:30:17Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1681"},
{"body":"Tracking issue for `plan_orchestrator_throughput_guard_truth.md`. Read its STATUS table first.\n\n```db-work-scope\nclass: repository-maintenance\nstructure_change: none\ndata_change: none\nmigrations: none\npreview_apply: no\nproduction_apply: no\ndatabase_access: read-only (existing Management API path, read_only:true)\nobjects: none\n```\n\n## Locked design\n\n- Extend the existing version-keyed, migration-hash-bound verification sidecars; do not create a second manifest.\n- The mechanical presence guard requires a reviewed disposition for changed dynamic-SQL risk markers but never classifies execution, infers targets, or decides durability.\n- Sidecar and catalog data never feed migration acceptance, `created_objects()`, `available`, or `preflight_batch()`.\n- Report migration-file, ledger, preview, and production states independently. Requested unavailable evidence is `UNVERIFIABLE`, exit 2.\n- Use immutable per-incident blocker files, an executable false-alarm corpus, and one-command triage.\n- Reviewer replacement requires no verdict plus no progress or an explicit transport/coverage failure; it never lowers coverage or replaces `REVISE`.\n\n## Target\n\nZero known false-alarm recurrence; every diagnosis has a rerunnable proof command; publish causal improvement only when at least 20 comparable evidenced entries exist. {"body":"## Owner request\r\n\r\nCreate a private, service-only landing family for exact Property names that appear in signed licence-contract evidence, grouped by licensor. This owner instruction supersedes the property-list portion of ruling 6.16 for this isolated evidence family only. Contract financial terms, territory, restrictions, personal data, filenames, and text remain excluded.\r\n\r\n## Required design\r\n\r\n- One normalized family, not one physical table per licensor.\r\n- Preserve exact licensor identity, exact Property text, opaque evidence identity, document SHA-256, page/schedule locator, signature status, decision authority, evidence date, and controlling-chain completeness.\r\n- No fuzzy matching, no promotion into portal Submissions/Creative vocabularies, and no writes to core.property.\r\n- Service-role only; licensed rows never enter this public repository, issue, migration, PR, logs, or tests.\r\n- Private loader and values remain owned by u2giants/licensor-source-data.\r\n\r\n## Acceptance\r\n\r\n- Additive migration creates the capture, evidence-document, Property, and Property-to-document evidence tables with licensor-scoped exact identity and append-only provenance.\r\n- Constraints reject blank identities, invalid SHA-256 values, cross-capture evidence, and duplicate exact Property identities within the same licensor capture.\r\n- RLS/grants deny public, anon, and authenticated access; service_role has only the permissions required by the private loader.\r\n- Preview, independent review, guarded merge, production promotion, and exact production catalog verification complete.\r\n\r\n```yaml db-work-scope\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\nobjects:\r\n  - plm.contract_property_capture\r\n  - plm.contract_property_document\r\n  - plm.contract_property\r\n  - plm.contract_property_evidence\r\n  - plm.contract_property_capture_licensor_idx\r\n  - plm.contract_property_document_sha256_uq\r\n  - plm.contract_property_licensor_identity_uq\r\n  - plm.contract_property_evidence_document_idx\r\n```\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table plm.contract_property_capture\n  - table plm.contract_property_document\n  - table plm.contract_property\n  - table plm.contract_property_evidence\n  - index plm.contract_property_capture_licensor_idx\n  - index plm.contract_property_document_sha256_uq\n  - index plm.contract_property_licensor_identity_uq\n  - index plm.contract_property_evidence_document_idx\nreads:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-27T23:37:38Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T18:41:04Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1676,"title":"Contract Property evidence landing tables by licensor","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:30:19Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1676"},
{"body":"The scheduled `Migration ledger drift` run failed against **production**.\n\nEither migrations are **merged to `main` and not applied**, or the ledger holds a\nrow with **no file on `main`**, or the check **could not run at all**.\n\n**Read the run before drawing any conclusion about the schema:**\nhttps://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/actions/runs/33100671768\n\n⚠️ **The live catalog is NOT proof that work was never done.** A merged-but-unapplied\nmigration is invisible in `information_schema` and looks exactly like work nobody\never wrote. That mistake was reported to the owner on 2026-08-13 (issue #892).\n\nCheck by hand:\n\n    SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=... node scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs --target production\n\n**Close this issue by hand once resolved.** It is throttled: while it is open, no\nfurther alarm issues are filed.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-28T23:18:21Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T17:53:11Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Authorized outcome  Apply the already-merged migration `20260817150944_sync_dflow_columns_onto_plm_designflow_copies.sql` only to the non-production database target(s) actually serving DesignFlow develop and staging, then return exact apply and catalog evidence so popcre/designflow-backend PR #70 can complete E2E verification.  Owner authorization in the originating task is conditional on independent approval. GLM 5.3 approved the exact PR head and migration on 2026-08-27:  > APPROVE: safe to apply migration 20260817150944 to develop/staging and continue PR #70 E2E  The GLM review found no Critical or High PR-code findings. It classified the migration as additive and ledger-idempotent DDL with a bounded one-shot backfill. Source PR: https://github.com/popcre/designflow-backend/pull/70 at exact head `a4f7fa001ef8798287c46c81f6f31ca7005e1116`. Sanitized deployment and E2E evidence is at https://github.com/popcre/designflow-backend/pull/70#issuecomment-5442371772.  ## Safety boundary  - Do not apply to production, change production configuration or traffic, or merge DesignFlow PR #70. - Resolve the live develop/staging database bindings rather than assuming environment names imply separate Supabase projects. If either binding is the protected shared production project, stop and return the target conflict; this authorization is non-production only. - Use the governed shared-db promotion path and prove the target immediately before every write. - Apply exactly the existing migration once through the ledger. Never replay its UPDATE blocks manually after PLM E2E writes begin.  ## Required preflight from GLM 5.3  1. Confirm `dflow.\"itemDetail\"` already has `coldlion_synced_at`, `compan_code_fk`, `div_code_fk`, and `item_num_id`, and confirm the prerequisite ledger state. 2. Confirm primary-key parity for the `dflow` and `plm` copies of `RFQItem`, `GridViewState`, and `itemDetail`. 3. Check for long-running transactions that could block the three target tables. 4. Confirm an environment restore point is available before apply.  ## Required post-apply evidence  1. Ledger contains version `20260817150944` and all 21 destination columns exist. 2. {"body":"## Owner ruling\n\nAlbert Hazan ruled on 2026-08-27:\n\n`mgCategory` is determined only by MG01, and it applies only to items created on or after May 14, 2025. Historical items created on or before May 13, 2025 must return no `mgCategory` until they have been reclassified under the new MG01+MG02+MG03 methodology.\n\nThe date restriction is intentionally temporary. Mark it clearly as obsolete and remove it only after a separately verified project has reclassified every historical item to the new methodology. Do not infer completion from partial analysis, proposed workbook values, or elapsed time.\n\n## Required implementation\n\n1. Add a governed item-level read contract that resolves `mgCategory` solely from the item's division-qualified MG01 definition.\n2. For items created before May 14, 2025, return no category unless and until the temporary cutoff is retired by a later governed migration after complete historical reclassification is proved.\n3. MG02 and MG03 must never affect the category.\n4. Document the cutoff beside the implementation as temporary/obsolete-after-reclassification, with the exact retirement gate.\n5. Update the Settled merchandise-taxonomy business rule and add tests for both sides of the date boundary, division-qualified MG01 resolution, missing MG01, and proof that MG02/MG03 cannot change the result.\n6. Do not write categories onto item rows and do not apply proposed historical classifications.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- 2025-05-13 item: no `mgCategory`.\n- 2025-05-14 item with a valid division-qualified MG01: exactly its mapped category.\n- Same MG01 with different MG02/MG03: same category.\n- Missing or unresolvable MG01: no category.\n- The temporary cutoff cannot disappear without a later migration and verified complete historical reclassification evidence.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function api.resolve_item_mg_category\nreads:\n  - table dflow.itemHeader\n  - table core.merchGroup\n  - table core.mg_category_merch_group\n  - table core.mg_category\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-27T22:17:59Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T14:18:26Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1662,"title":"HANDOVER: enforce mgCategory only for post-May-13-2025 items","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:30:30Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1662"},
{"body":"Requested by Albert 2026-08-27 in chat, as a required part of the `dflow_prod` migration (#1352).\n\n## Ask\n\nCompare what ColdLion's API feed currently serves against what DesignFlow actually holds in **Cloud SQL production** (`designflow`), and reconcile the differences, before production data is moved into `dflow_prod` on Supabase.\n\nRationale: migrating unreconciled data carries every existing discrepancy into the new schema, where it becomes far more expensive to correct. Reconcile at the source first.\n\n## Scope\n\n1. Establish the ColdLion API feed's authoritative endpoint, auth and record set. Prove the exact source before reading.\n2. Read the corresponding entities from **Cloud SQL production** `designflow` — not Supabase `dflow`, which is dev/staging/sandbox only (owner correction on #1353).\n3. Produce a field-level and row-level difference report: present in feed only, present in DB only, present in both but divergent.\n4. Classify each class of difference: ColdLion is right, DesignFlow is right, or owner decision required.\n5. Escalate only the owner-decision class to Albert. Do not guess.\n\n## Constraints\n\n- Read-only until the difference report exists and its correction classes are agreed.\n- Do NOT use an AI-generated mapping as an input — see the standing ruling that AI merch-group mappings are drafts only.\n- Prove the target database immediately before every read and every write.\n- No bulk load into curated Master Data outside the governed shared-db branch-and-PR route.\n\n## Depends on / relates to\n\n- #1352 fresh-empty-schema `dflow_prod` cutover (parent effort)\n- #1315 primary-key / sequence audit\n- #771 timed cutover rehearsal\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: source-data\nroute: source-data-session\nreturn_to: u2giants/licensor-source-data\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: #1352\nwrites:\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T01:37:57Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T14:14:36Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1661,"title":"Reconcile ColdLion API feed against dflow in Cloud SQL production, as part of the dflow_prod migration","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:30:32Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1661"},

{"body":"## Owner correction\n\nAuthority is assertion-specific. Signed agreements and schedules govern POP entitlement and any explicit Property-to-Licensor relationship they state. Direct captured OPA evidence governs submissions-system Property scope and relationships. DCP Vault and ASGARD Creative placement are Creative evidence only. The current Scraped Properties contract incorrectly describes competing rows as “DCP Vault decisions” and conflates authoritative contract/OPA assertions with non-authoritative canonical ownership, normalized names, source titles, and landing families.\n\nRead-only production evidence showed that the current review example covers 791 assets across 10 style guides. The page must name the relevant style guides and explain the actual cross-source conflict; it must not imply DCP made ownership decisions.\n\n## Required structural correction\n\n1. Add an explicit, append-only, versioned DCP-source-identity to OPA-Property-ID resolution contract. It must support zero, one, or multiple approved OPA Property members for one exact DCP source identity, with supersession and approval provenance. Candidate generation never establishes ownership.\n2. Derive DCP Creative presentation studio only through explicit signed-contract assertions and/or resolved OPA `licensed_property_id` members with direct latest-approved `plm.opa_property_scope_membership`. Missing authoritative evidence remains unresolved. If explicit contract and direct OPA evidence disagree, fail closed and expose the concrete conflict for Licensing review.\n3. Stop using `plm.dcp_property_licensor_resolution` as blanket current authority. Preserve its append-only history. Only explicit signed-contract assertions may contribute contract authority. Name, core ownership, source-label, landing-family, DCP, and ASGARD evidence never establish ownership.\n4. Expose authorized source context for each DCP review row: exact style-guide display names and aggregate asset/style-guide counts. Do not expose raw paths, account data, private authority references, or unrelated licensed rows.\n5. Replace “DCP Vault decision” language. Unresolved wording must say DCP supplied Creative metadata but no approved authoritative link exists. Conflicts must describe the actual contract-versus-OPA or OPA-scope conflict and name the relevant style guides.\n6. Keep Review reason, Evidence basis, and Decision guidance blank when no problem exists. Preserve the two-line cells and full-text tooltips delivered by #1654/#1655.\n7. Update `docs/business-rules/licensing-master-data.md` as Settled with this assertion-specific authority rule.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- Sanitized tests prove no name, core ownership, source-label, landing-family, DCP, or ASGARD fallback.\n- Authenticated production UI names every implicated style guide for the review example without exposing raw asset paths.\n- Aggregate-only verification proves clean rows have blank review fields and every DCP studio placement traces to compatible explicit signed-contract authority, direct OPA Property-ID scope, or both; disagreement fails closed.\n- Preserve all existing RLS/EXECUTE restrictions and fail-closed behavior.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 2000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution\n  - table plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties\n  - policy \"dcp_opa_property_resolution_read\" on plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution\n  - policy \"dcp_opa_property_resolution_member_read\" on plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member\n  - function plm.reject_dcp_opa_resolution_mutation\n  - trigger dcp_opa_property_resolution_append_only on plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution\n  - trigger dcp_opa_property_resolution_member_append_only on plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member\nreads:\n  - table plm.opa_property\n  - table plm.opa_property_scope_membership\n  - table plm.dcp_property_licensor_resolution\n  - table plm.dcp_property\n  - table plm.dcp_asset_property_observation\n  - table plm.dcp_asset\n  - table plm.dcp_style_guide\n  - table plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property\n  - table plm.lucasfilm_dcp_asset_property_observation\n  - table plm.lucasfilm_dcp_asset\n  - table plm.lucasfilm_dcp_style_guide\n  - table plm.marvel_dcp_property\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T16:49:50Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T13:40:02Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1658,"title":"HANDOVER: reconcile contract and OPA authority for DCP Creative studio scope","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:30:35Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1658"},
{"body":"## Request\r\n\r\nAdd two btree indexes so `api.dam_order_list` can be counted without two cold sequential scans.\r\n\r\n```sql\r\ncreate index concurrently if not exists style_tracker_item_bridge_plm_item_idx\r\n  on plm.style_tracker_item_bridge (plm_item_id);\r\n\r\ncreate index concurrently if not exists production_order_line_count_cover_idx\r\n  on plm.production_order_line (production_order_id, item_id, id);\r\n```\r\n\r\nBoth are additive index-only changes. No view, RLS, grant, function or column is touched.\r\n\r\n## Why\r\n\r\nPopDAM `u2giants/popdam3#100`: `/orders` intermittently dies with `canceling statement due to statement timeout` because the unfiltered exact total on `api.dam_order_list` was measured at 3.4 s against the 8 s `authenticated` ceiling, and it grows with the table.\r\n\r\nThe popdam issue assumed RLS re-checking was the cost. Measured on production (`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, read-only, as `set role authenticated`) on 2026-08-27, that is **not** the cause — every policy on the joined tables is `using (true)` and folds away, and a warm count is 161 ms. The cost is **cold-cache sequential IO**:\r\n\r\n`explain (analyze, buffers) select count(*) from api.dam_order_list` — 24,486 rows, **24,835 shared buffers (~194 MB), all `read`, 922 ms on an already-busy cache**:\r\n\r\n| node | buffers |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| Seq Scan `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` | 16,943 (132 MB) |\r\n| Seq Scan `plm.production_order_line` | 7,290 (57 MB) |\r\n| Seq Scan `production_order_line_source_ref` | 375 |\r\n| Seq Scan `plm.production_order` | 224 |\r\n\r\n`plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` has **no index on `plm_item_id`**, which is the column `api.dam_order_list` joins it on (`20260810010000_popdam_order_list_contract.sql:516`). The join cannot be pruned by the planner because the bridge is not unique on `plm_item_id` — it genuinely fans out (24,010 order lines → 24,486 view rows) — so every count pays a full scan of a 132 MB table that holds only ~24 MB of live data (15,619 rows; ~5x bloat, `last_autovacuum` 2026-08-26).\r\n\r\n## Evidence the fix works\r\n\r\nValidated with `hypopg` on production (hypothetical indexes only — nothing was created):\r\n\r\n- baseline: two seq scans as above\r\n- with `style_tracker_item_bridge (plm_item_id)`: bridge seq scan replaced by a Memoize + index scan; total cost 13,929\r\n- with both indexes: `production_order_line` becomes an **Index Only Scan** (7,530 → 730); total cost **7,129**\r\n\r\nCold buffer reads drop from ~24,800 to roughly ~2,000 — about 90% less IO on the query that is closing on the timeout. The bridge index also helps the per-block row queries, which use the same join.\r\n\r\n## Scope / risk\r\n\r\n- Additive only; both are `create index concurrently`, so they take no write lock (must run outside a transaction — see `AGENTS.md` on non-transactional migrations).\r\n- Write cost: two more index maintenance targets on tables that are written by importers, not by browser traffic.\r\n- Rollback is `drop index concurrently`.\r\n- No app-side contract change; PopDAM needs no regenerated types.\r\n- Separately worth considering (NOT requested here): `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` is ~5x bloated and would benefit from a repack. The indexes make that non-urgent.\r\n\r\n## Verification asked for\r\n\r\nAfter preview + production apply, re-run as `authenticated` and report:\r\n\r\n```sql\r\nexplain (analyze, buffers) select count(*) from api.dam_order_list;\r\n```\r\n\r\nExpect no seq scan on `plm.style_tracker_item_bridge` and an index-only scan on `plm.production_order_line`.\r\n\r\nRequester: PopDAM session, worktree `issue-100-4a0376`, for `u2giants/popdam3#100`.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - index plm.style_tracker_item_bridge_plm_item_idx\n  - index plm.production_order_line_count_cover_idx\nreads:\n  - table plm.style_tracker_item_bridge\n  - table plm.production_order_line\n  - view api.dam_order_list\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T01:13:52Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T13:23:39Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1657,"title":"OrderList exact count: add plm.style_tracker_item_bridge(plm_item_id) + production_order_line count-cover index (popdam3#100)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:30:37Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1657"},

{"body":"## What is needed\n\nPopDAM's library filters cannot express **effective** metadata, and the application half of issue [u2giants/popdam3#96](https://github.com/u2giants/popdam3/issues/96) Step 7 has now shipped without them. Two filters are affected:\n\n1. **Tag filter.** `useAssets.ts` filters `assets.tags @> [tag]` (PostgREST `.contains`). `assets.tags` is a compatibility array of that asset's **own active** rows only. Style Group tags are deliberately **never** copied onto members — that separation is the entire point of #96 — so filtering by a shared product tag returns nothing today.\n2. **Licensor / property filter.** `useAssets.ts` filters `assets.licensor_id` / `assets.property_id` directly. Those columns used to be null-filled on every sibling by the legacy tag-propagation job. That job was removed in popdam3 `72b07e23`, so for a grouped asset the identity now lives on `style_groups`, and the asset column may be null.\n\nThe read contract `public.get_effective_asset_metadata(uuid)` already resolves both correctly, but it is per-asset and therefore cannot drive a list filter or a facet count.\n\n## Why this needs shared-db rather than app code\n\n- A group tag is structurally absent from `assets.tags`, so `@>` cannot express it at any cost.\n- Resolving matching `style_group_id`s in the client and passing them back as `IN (...)` is unbounded — a common product tag can span thousands of groups — and gives no facet-count parity.\n- `dam_search_documents.search_text` already unions group tags, but it is a tokenised full-text blob: it is correct for ranked search and wrong for an exact tag facet.\n\n## Constraints that must hold\n\n- **Cold 8s `authenticated` ceiling.** `AGENTS.md` (popdam3) \"Library list/facet queries must beat the 8s `authenticated` timeout (2026-06-19)\": the browser runs as `authenticated` with a Supavisor-enforced `statement_timeout=8s` that `SET LOCAL` cannot raise. Size everything cold as `authenticated` on production-scale preview fixtures, never as `postgres`.\n- **`get_filter_counts` covering-index contract.** It was 14s (5 table scans) and was brought to ~260ms by one materialised scan plus the index-only `idx_assets_facet_counts ON public.assets (is_deleted) INCLUDE (file_type, status, workflow_status, stage, is_licensed, modified_at, file_created_at, thumbnail_url, style_group_id) WHERE is_deleted = false`. Keep it reading only columns in that index, **or** deliberately extend the index and re-prove the cold timing. Silently widening the read set will regress the incident this index was created for.\n- **Facet-count parity.** Counts must be computed over the same effective scope as the list query, or the sidebar will disagree with the grid.\n- **Candidate vs active must be distinguishable.** #96 promotes an AI group fact to `active` only at >= 0.85 confidence with two distinct member files; everything else stays `candidate`, and rejected rows are durable tombstones. Only `active` rows may make an asset match, but the contract should expose the distinction so parity is testable.\n- **Authorization-safe.** Results must respect whatever the `authenticated` role may already see; this must not become a way to enumerate rows a user cannot otherwise read.\n- Soft-deleted assets (`assets.is_deleted = true`) must never match.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. Filtering the library by a tag that exists **only** on the Style Group returns every non-deleted member of that group.\n2. Filtering by a tag that exists only on one file returns that file and **not** its siblings.\n3. A `candidate` or `rejected` tag never causes a match at either scope.\n4. Filtering by licensor or property returns grouped assets by their **group's** identity and ungrouped assets by their **own** identity, with no column on `assets` being written to achieve it.\n5. Facet counts for the same filter set equal the list total, at both scopes.\n6. Every path above completes under the 8s `authenticated` ceiling cold, on production-scale preview fixtures, with headroom stated in the evidence.\n7. `get_filter_counts` either still reads only `idx_assets_facet_counts` columns, or the index is deliberately extended and the cold timing re-proven and cited.\n\n## Suggested shape — design authority is the orchestrator's, not mine\n\n**Recommended: a maintained projection plus effective identity.**\n\n- `public.asset_effective_tags(asset_id uuid, tag text, scope text)` — one row per (asset, active tag) from either scope, maintained by triggers on `asset_tags`, `style_group_tags`, and on `assets.style_group_id` changes (a regrouped asset must gain and lose group rows). Indexed on `(tag, asset_id)` and `(asset_id)`. This lets PostgREST keep the existing query builder intact via an embedded `!inner` filter, and makes exact counts cheap.\n- Effective identity exposed so it is filterable and indexable without copying values onto `assets` — a maintained column pair, a generated expression, or a view the API layer can filter, whichever the orchestrator judges safest against the covering-index contract.\n\n**Alternative:** a dedicated `public.filter_effective_assets(...)` / `public.get_effective_filter_counts(...)` RPC pair. This keeps everything inside `SECURITY DEFINER` functions and avoids trigger maintenance cost on every tag write, but it means PopDAM rewrites its list query instead of extending it, and pagination/ordering parity has to be rebuilt.\n\nTrade-off worth an explicit decision: the projection adds write amplification on tag writes (the AI tagger writes in batches), while the RPC adds read cost and an app rewrite. I lean to the projection because it preserves facet parity almost for free, but I do not own that call.\n\n## What is already true in production\n\n- popdam3 `main` at `70e0f8d2` — Step 7 application half is deployed. Both detail panels read `get_effective_asset_metadata` and display Style Group facts separately from file facts, so the **display** side is already correct; only **filtering and counting** are wrong.\n- popdam3 `72b07e23` — legacy tag propagation is gone; nothing null-fills sibling identity any more.\n- Shared-db migrations `20260825010603`, `20260825031841`, `20260825082910`, `20260825165139` provide `asset_tags`, `style_group_tags`, `get_effective_asset_metadata`, `replace_asset_ai_tag_result`, `replace_style_group_ai_profile`, and the `dam_search_documents` refresh functions this work builds on.\n\n## Requesting session\n\nPopDAM application session (claude, hetz), working popdam3 issue #96. I have made **no** change to the shared database and hold no lane. Read-only inspection only, per Rule 0. Happy to take the app-side wiring, generated types, and the parity/performance tests once the contract lands — just tell me the final shape.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table public.asset_effective_tags\n  - table public.assets\n  - table public.asset_tags\n  - table public.style_group_tags\n  - function public.filter_effective_assets\n  - function public.get_effective_filter_counts\n  - function public.get_filter_counts\n  - function public.sync_asset_effective_tags\n  - function public.assets_thumbnail_min_date\n  - trigger asset_tags_effective_tags_sync on public.asset_tags\n  - trigger style_group_tags_effective_tags_sync on public.style_group_tags\n  - trigger assets_effective_tags_sync on public.assets\n  - index public.asset_effective_tags_tag_asset_idx\n  - index public.asset_effective_tags_asset_tag_scope_uidx\n  - policy \"Authenticated read asset_effective_tags\" on public.asset_effective_tags\nreads:\n  - table public.style_groups\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T17:12:57Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T11:06:47Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1645,"title":"PopDAM #96 Step 7: effective-tag and grouped-identity filtering with facet-count parity","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:30:46Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1645"},

{"body":"## Source finding\n\nThe completed 75-guide ASGARD crawl proved that one source original-file UUID can legitimately appear on multiple visible file cards with different exact filenames. This occurs within a single page, so it is not pagination overlap or crawler duplication. No licensed filenames or values are included here.\n\nThe production landing contract currently makes original_file_id globally unique and stores one exact_filename on the asset row. That cannot preserve the source truth. The loader would either reject valid rows or discard visible filenames.\n\n## Required correction\n\nPreserve the stable source UUID as the asset/group identity and add a lossless file-card/file-observation identity for every visible exact filename. Preserve guide/node/page/order provenance and attach character, typed term, and likeness evidence at the most specific source-observation level without inventing identities. Exact replay must remain idempotent; conflicting replay must fail closed. Update guarded begin/load/finalize functions, count reconciliation, tests, and private read contracts as needed. Do not expose licensed values publicly.\n\nThe source-data loader and normalizer will be updated against the accepted contract, then the full verified capture will be loaded and audited.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 2000\nreturn_repo: u2giants/licensor-source-data\nwrites:\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_asset\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_node_asset_observation\n  - function plm.load_marvel_asgard_chunk\n  - function plm.finalize_marvel_asgard_capture\nreads:\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_capture\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-27T11:07:44Z","createdAt":"2026-08-27T08:43:09Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1640,"title":"Marvel ASGARD: preserve multiple filename observations sharing one source UUID","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:30:51Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1640"},

{"body":"## What's wrong  `api.crm_update_customer` uses `coalesce(p_domain, c.domain)` for every field, so `null` means \"leave unchanged\". That is the right contract for an update RPC, but it leaves no way to express \"clear this field\". POP CRM's Domain editor therefore clears a customer's domain by writing an **empty string** instead of `null`.  ```sql -- api.crm_update_customer, current domain = coalesce(p_domain, c.domain), ```  No production rows are affected today (`core.customer` currently holds 93 real domains, 733 nulls, **0 empty strings**) — nobody has cleared a domain since the Domain field became editable on 2026-08-25. So this is a latent contract flaw, not an active data problem.  ## Why it's worth fixing anyway  `core.customer` is shared with PM/PIM, DAM and PLM. Verified inside popcrm-web, `''` behaves exactly like `null` everywhere it is read:  - `core.match_customer` step 2 uses `nullif(btrim(...))` on the probe and   `domain is not null`, so `''` never matches — correct behaviour, by luck rather   than design. - The worker's contains-ilike domain matching never matches an empty stored value. - Every frontend check is falsy-based (`domain ? … : '—'`).  What is **not** verified is the other apps. Any consumer that does `where domain is not null` and then uses the value would treat `''` as a real domain. That is the failure this prevents, and it cannot be checked from the CRM repo alone.  ## Requested change  Follow the precedent already set for contacts by `20260623024500_crm_update_contact_clear_relationship_fields.sql`, which added explicit `p_clear_*` flags for exactly this reason:  ``` api.crm_update_customer(   ...,   p_clear_domain boolean default false ) ```  - when `p_clear_domain` is true, set `domain = null` regardless of `p_domain` - otherwise keep the current `coalesce(p_domain, c.domain)` behaviour - existing callers that omit the flag must be unaffected  Optionally the same treatment for the other nullable text fields on that RPC (`chain_type`, `routing_aliases`, `so_patterns`) if the reviewer thinks it is worth doing once rather than per-field later. Domain is the only one the CRM can clear from the UI today.  Please also normalise as a one-time step, so the two representations never coexist:  ```sql update core.customer set domain = null where domain = ''; ```  (Zero rows today; the statement is there so it stays zero if any land before the RPC change ships.)  ## App-side follow-up (popcrm-web, not this repo)  `DomainField` in `src/features/crm/components/CustomerDrawer.tsx` will pass `p_clear_domain: true` when the box is emptied, instead of sending `''`. I'll do that once this lands.  ## Provenance  Raised by GLM 5.3 in an independent review of the 2026-08-25 popcrm-web domain curation work, and confirmed by reading every consumer reachable from that repo. Deliberately deferred at the time as not worth a shared-db change on its own; Albert asked on 2026-08-26 for it to be filed so it isn't lost. \n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 50\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function api.crm_update_customer\nreads:\n  - table core.customer\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-27T11:15:22Z","createdAt":"2026-08-26T18:37:12Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1615,"title":"api.crm_update_customer has no way to clear a domain: add p_clear_domain instead of writing an empty string","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:31:10Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1615"},
