{"body":"## Machine scope\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 99\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function dflow.validate_sample_approval_event\n  - trigger sample_approval_event_validate on dflow.sample_approval_event\n```\n\n## Production-backed failure\n\nDesignFlow Sample Tracking issue popcre/designflow-frontend#157 Flow 3 is deployed and production-backed. The assigned factory posts the first photo event as pending with `qc_required=false`, because vendors are explicitly forbidden from deciding whether QC is required. NYO then approves the photo with `qc_required=true`. Production rejects the legal business transition with: `QC requirement cannot change within an approval history`.\n\n## Required contract\n\nPreserve append-only approval history and every existing transition guard. Permit `qc_required` to change only for a photo transition from pending to approved, because that is the NYO decision point. Keep vendor photo submissions pending with false; keep rejected-to-pending rework from silently changing QC; keep every QC event true and dependent on a currently approved photo whose `qc_required` is true. Add focused pgTAP coverage for allowed false-to-true photo approval and all forbidden changes.\n\n## Evidence and rollout gate\n\nLive failure is on Supabase project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` after migration `20260826010223` / completed #1520. Application consumers must not be changed to bypass this constraint. Preview, exact-head review, governed merge, production promotion, and production function-definition proof are required before Flow 3 live QA resumes.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-26T19:48:11Z","createdAt":"2026-08-26T17:18:12Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Recording a durable source-to-POP decision is unsupported, and both migrations that would have provided it are permanently retired  ## What is missing  There is no way to record \"this licensor's source record means this POP record\" so that the decision survives the next capture. Landing rows are immutable per-capture snapshots; a decision written onto one disappears from the current read path when the next scrape lands. That was the whole point of issues #963 and #999, and neither shipped.  Both are closed, and both of their migrations are now **retired and hard-blocked** — they can never run:  - `20260814224937_source_resolution_durable_home` — creates `plm.source_resolution`. Retired: it declares a foreign key to `core.character`, which `20260823133150` (issue #1374) dropped from production. - `20260814233423_remaining_source_resolution_durable_home` — backfills and guards that table. Retired: its first reference to `plm.source_resolution` (the conflict-gate join, line 152) fails 42P01 without the above, and no replacement can rescue it because every replacement sorts *above* it in version order.  Verified read-only against production 2026-08-25: `to_regclass('plm.source_resolution')` is NULL. The capability does not exist anywhere.  ## Why this is not urgent but must not be dropped  No decisions have been lost, because none exist yet: zero resolved rows in `plm.opa_property`, `plm.opa_character`, `plm.opa_property_character` and `plm.wb_property_character_normalized`. The exposure is that the guard rails are absent, so the **first** human decision anyone records can still be written onto a capture snapshot and silently erased by the next scrape.  The reason for filing rather than leaving it in a document: this requirement has now been described correctly in `plan_curated-decisions-survive-syncs.md`, `plan_licensing_master_data_implementation.md` and `docs/verification/unapplied-20260814-migrations-audit-20260823.md`, and still has no owner and no ticket. Issue #1459's second half was lost the same way when that issue closed as superseded.  ## What a replacement must decide, not repeat  1. **Do not edit or revive the retired files.** Author fresh, additively. Both are hard-blocked, and editing merged SQL is the anti-pattern this repo's own Warner dependency audit names. 2. **`core_character_id`: keep as a plain uuid, no foreign key.** That is the settled pattern from `20260823133150`, which kept the `core_character_id` columns on `plm.nbcu_character`, `plm.opa_character` and `plm.pmt_character` and dropped only their constraints. 3. **⚠️ `core_property_id` has the same disease one ruling later.** The retired table also declares `core_property_id uuid references core.property(id)`, and under AGENTS.md §6.15 `core.property` (Universe A) is itself slated for deletion. A replacement that keys to it breaks again the same way, and every stored property decision dangles. **This is an owner question the implementing session must ask, not decide silently:** plain uuids with no canonical foreign keys and target validity enforced by the write function, versus foreign keys only where the target's survival is settled (`dam.asset`; `core.style_guide` is at least under no deletion ruling). 4. Keep the design intent that made the original correct: loaders never write the decision table; the only write path is a single guarded function; landing rows stay immutable evidence.  Useful prior art, for content only — never for the version numbers or the FK shape: `supabase/migrations/20260814224937_*.sql` and `20260814233423_*.sql` on `main`, and `plan_curated-decisions-survive-syncs.md`.  ## Related  - #1374 / `20260823133150` — dropped `core.character`, the change that stranded the original. - #1459 (closed) and #1608 — the promotion-coherence gap surfaced by the same audit. - `docs/verification/unapplied-20260814-migrations-audit-20260823.md` — the measurements above.  ```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 400\ndepends_on: 1684\nwrites:\n  - column plm.source_resolution.updated_at\n  - table plm.source_resolution\n  - function plm.set_source_resolution\n  - view api.source_resolution\n  - view api.pmt_properties\n  - view api.pmt_characters\n  - view api.opa_property_reconciliation\n  - table api.source_resolution\n  - policy source_resolution_authenticated_read on plm.source_resolution\n  - function plm.source_resolution_target_missing\n  - function plm.reject_legacy_landing_resolution_write\n  - trigger pmt_property_resolution_immutable on plm.pmt_property\n  - trigger pmt_character_resolution_immutable on plm.pmt_character\n  - trigger nbcu_property_resolution_immutable on plm.nbcu_property\n  - trigger nbcu_character_resolution_immutable on plm.nbcu_character\n  - trigger nbcu_style_guide_resolution_immutable on plm.nbcu_style_guide\n  - trigger nbcu_asset_resolution_immutable on plm.nbcu_asset\n  - trigger opa_property_character_resolution_immutable on plm.opa_property_character\n  - trigger opa_property_resolution_immutable on plm.opa_property\n  - trigger opa_character_resolution_immutable on plm.opa_character\n  - trigger dcp_portal_tile_resolution_immutable on plm.dcp_portal_tile\n  - trigger dcp_style_guide_resolution_immutable on plm.dcp_style_guide\n  - trigger dcp_property_resolution_immutable on plm.dcp_property\n  - trigger dcp_character_resolution_immutable on plm.dcp_character\n  - trigger lucasfilm_dcp_portal_tile_resolution_immutable on plm.lucasfilm_dcp_portal_tile\n  - trigger lucasfilm_dcp_style_guide_resolution_immutable on plm.lucasfilm_dcp_style_guide\n  - trigger lucasfilm_dcp_property_resolution_immutable on plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property\n  - trigger lucasfilm_dcp_character_resolution_immutable on plm.lucasfilm_dcp_character\n  - trigger marvel_dcp_portal_tile_resolution_immutable on plm.marvel_dcp_portal_tile\n  - {"body":"A migration can be promoted to a database that lacks the base it was derived from, and nothing refuses it\n\n## The gap\n\nEvery loader-style migration in this repo is authored as a **full re-derivation of the then-current body on `main`** — the header of `20260814193351` states that rule explicitly, and `20260824135515` and `20260825094455` both name the exact base they re-derived from.\n\nThat makes each such migration silently dependent on its base being present **in the target database**. Nothing checks it. `parse_allowlist` validates version syntax, hold/retirement membership and bundle composition; the post-apply catalog verification confirms the named objects exist afterwards. Neither asks the only question that matters for a re-derived body: **is the base this file was derived from actually in the target ledger?**\n\n## It already happened, and cost three retirements\n\n`20260824135515` states in its own header that it is \"a full re-derivation of the CURRENT function body on main (20260814223552, the third rewrite)\". It was promoted **alone** to production under its own owner authorization (issue #1418, run 32793586633) while none of the three 2026-08-14 rewrites were applied there.\n\nProduction was left with a `plm.load_pmt_capture_chunk` that inserted into `plm.pmt_metadata_element` (absent → 42P01) and no longer wrote two columns still `NOT NULL` there (→ 23502). Measured read-only 2026-08-25; recorded in `docs/verification/unapplied-20260814-migrations-audit-20260823.md` and issue #1459.\n\nEvery individual step was correct and evidenced. The promotion passed every gate it was asked to pass. The combination was incoherent, and no gate was looking at the combination.\n\nThe same episode produced two further retirements for adjacent reasons — `20260814223552` (\"unpromotable byte binding, merged unrehearsed\") and `20260825094455` (\"only preview apply ran on a squash-orphaned commit\"). Different symptoms; the same underlying shape, which is a migration whose proof does not match what the target database actually holds.\n\n## What is asked\n\n1. **A machine check, not prose.** Where a migration declares the base it was re-derived from, refuse to promote it if that base is absent from the target ledger — or require an explicit, recorded override naming the resulting state. The declaration needs a parseable form; today it exists only as English in a header comment, which is why no tool can read it.\n2. Decide whether that declaration should be **mandatory** for any migration containing `create or replace function` / `create or replace view` over an object an earlier merged-but-unapplied migration also rewrites. That is the exact population at risk.\n3. Make the failure mode visible in the drift report: a version whose declared base is unapplied in the target is not the same risk as an ordinary pending version, and today they are indistinguishable.\n\nThis must not be satisfied by a documentation line. Issue #1459's own history is the argument: its finding was correct, was written into three documents, and was still nearly acted on wrongly twice — a supersession route that inverted the required order (caught by an independent Grok 4.6 review), and a bare three-version allowlist the guard would have accepted.\n\n## Related, not duplicate\n\n- #1182 — supersession leaves **stale version references** in the guard, un-gating a held migration. Adjacent: both are \"the guard's view of reality drifted from reality\", but that one is about renamed versions, this one is about absent prerequisites.\n- #1223 — 32 guards in the promotion-evidence chain have no test that fails when disabled. A new gate here needs such a test, or it joins them.\n- #1459 (closed, superseded) — this is the second half of that issue. The first half, the Paramount four-version window, is done and verified; this half travelled nowhere when the issue closed.\n- #1344, #1321 — promotion-lane exclusivity and post-merge rehearsal evidence.\n\n## Scope note\n\nNo database object changes. This is guard/tooling work on `scripts/production_migration_guard.py`, `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs` and their tests, plus whatever declaration format is chosen for migration headers.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-26T18:58:16Z","createdAt":"2026-08-26T16:30:06Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1608,"title":"A migration can be promoted to a database that lacks the base it was derived from, and nothing refuses it","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:31:16Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1608"},
{"body":"DesignFlow Sample Tracking issue popcre/designflow-frontend#157 is ready for Release E structure. Implement the single governed Flow 4 remote-request family described in `plan_sample_tracking_full_restructure.md` step 9.\r\n\r\nRequired contract:\r\n\r\n- One request header supports `photo`, `china_warehouse`, and `ningbo_inventory` sources and persists the selected source and valid business path.\r\n- Request items progress independently through append-only history: requested, awaiting Ningbo, awaiting QC, confirmed, not found, declined, in transit to Ningbo, received, reserved for the general Ningbo next-box queue, packed into the actual box, and shipped onward.\r\n- Request creation posts no movement. Confirmation of existing Ningbo stock never duplicates custody. Reservation changes neither custody nor box membership. Packing atomically consumes one reservation and creates box membership/shipment intent.\r\n- Wrong-role, skipped-state, duplicate reservation, and concurrent retry/packing attempts fail closed. Idempotent replay must not duplicate request items, history, reservations, membership, intent, or movement, and a retry after the original transaction commits must return the same successful result rather than a false business rejection.\r\n- Preserve `dflow.sample_movement` as sole physical-custody authority and integrate with the existing sample, workflow, box, shipment-item, and shipment-line identities.\r\n- Provide focused migration contract tests for both confirmation branches, not-found/declined, mixed-source items, genuine two-session idempotent concurrency ordering, competing packing behavior, and no false office inventory.\r\n\r\nThe application session will implement API/models/UI only after this governed structure is previewed and production-live. Do not place application code in shared-db.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: blocked\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 95\r\ndepends_on:\r\nobjects:\r\n  - table dflow.sample_remote_request\r\n  - table dflow.sample_remote_request_item\r\n  - table dflow.sample_remote_request_history\r\n  - table dflow.sample_reservation\r\n  - function dflow.post_sample_remote_request_event\r\n  - function dflow.reserve_sample_remote_request_item\r\n  - function dflow.pack_sample_reservation\r\n```\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-27T13:15:07Z","createdAt":"2026-08-26T16:22:49Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1607,"title":"HANDOVER: DesignFlow Sample Tracking Flow 4 remote requests and reservations","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:31:17Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1607"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 80\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n## Problem\n\nA session determines the sole shared-db orchestrator from the open `orchestrator-marker` issue. The marker proves an orchestrator **exists**; it does not carry a **routable address**. Marker #1602 records machine, session slug, predecessor and startup proof — and nothing another session can send work to.\n\nConsequence, observed: an authorized structural request was delegated back to an orchestrator session that had already closed, because the delegating session fell back to conversation history / an old handoff for the routing target.\n\n`scripts/check-orchestrator-marker.mjs` counts markers. It never reads the body, so a marker with no routing information, or a successor that copied its predecessor's target, passes.\n\n## Prior art — extend, do not duplicate\n\n- **#1366 / `plan_multi_agent_database_coordination_hardening.md`** — complete. Steps 1-6, 8A, 9 merged. It hardened claims, dependencies, work contracts, coordination events and exclusive leases. It did not address orchestrator **discovery/routing**.\n- **`plan_orchestrator-workflow-gaps.md` §B1/B1a/B1b** — built the marker guard. Its three recorded failure modes (label rename, eventually-consistent server-side filter, empty `gh` output) and the UNKNOWN-never-means-none rule are preserved verbatim by this change.\n- **`plan_orchestrator-workflow-gaps.md` §C** — recorded \"there is no mechanism that reaches a running session, and this plan should not pretend to invent one.\" That was accurate when written. Two mechanisms now exist: Claude cross-session messaging, and Codex `codex-reply` by thread id. This issue does **not** invent a push channel; it publishes the address those existing mechanisms need. §C's conclusion is extended, not relitigated.\n\n## Outcome\n\nEvery open orchestrator marker carries a machine-readable routing block recording: fixed identifier `shared-db.orch`, engine, routable session/thread id, stable owner identity, machine, start time, originating handover issue and briefing, and an explicit active status.\n\nThe guard enforces, fail-closed:\n\n- Missing or malformed routing block or id fails. Placeholders are not ids.\n- Exactly one open marker is required before a session treats an orchestrator as active.\n- Zero markers means **no active orchestrator** — work queues until a successor starts. It is not a licence to start dispatching.\n- Two or more markers are ambiguous and unsafe.\n- A successor that reuses its predecessor's routable id fails.\n- Unreadable GitHub stays UNKNOWN, never \"none open\".\n\nA `--resolve` mode returns the delegation destination from the current open marker only, so no session resolves routing from conversation history or an old handoff. Closing or handing over a marker therefore invalidates the old target by construction.\n\n## Scope boundary\n\nRepository maintenance and governance. **No** migration-author lane, **no** version reservation, **no** database change, **no** structural-orchestrator dispatch. Owner ruling 2026-08-21 (#1366): the orchestrator's only job is database structure; a normal repository-maintenance session owns this.\n\nSkill sources of truth in `u2giants/ai-devops` (`skills/shared/shared-db-orchestrator`, `skills/shared/shared-db-handover`) are updated in a companion PR.","closedAt":"2026-08-26T16:16:05Z","createdAt":"2026-08-26T15:29:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1605,"title":"Orchestrator marker must publish a routable, fail-closed delegation target","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:31:19Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1605"},

{"body":"## Business outcome\n\nMake DB Data Admin's Scraped Properties results explain both the source's business purpose and why a row needs Licensing review, without treating a landing-table family as licensor authority.\n\nAlbert authorized this exact structural/UI-data-contract outcome on 2026-08-26. No additional production approval is required after the normal independent review, preview, guarded merge, dry-run, evidence, and production gates pass.\n\n## Required structural contract\n\nUpdate `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text,text,integer)` so each returned row/group carries user-facing source-purpose grouping plus detailed review explanation/evidence fields sufficient for Licensing to resolve OPA ambiguous/unresolved and DCP authority-conflict/unresolved states.\n\nExact business presentation:\n\n- Disney / Marvel / Lucasfilm-Star Wars / Pixar — Submissions (OPA).\n- Disney and Lucasfilm-Star Wars — Creative (DCP Vault).\n- Marvel Creative is ASGARD only.\n- DCP Vault rows tagged Marvel are non-authoritative mixed-guide noise. Exclude them from Marvel Creative presentation while retaining raw landing evidence.\n- Never use a DCP landing-table family as licensor authority; authority conflicts fail closed.\n- Expose the existing per-row OPA `resolution_reason` now, plus review reason, evidence basis, and candidate/decision guidance without leaking licensed bulk rows.\n- The current OPA extract proves Property -> Character only. It does not establish that no direct Licensor/Studio -> Property selector exists in the live source. The API must remain able to consume direct hierarchy evidence after the private capture is expanded; never join `brandPropertyID` to `licensedPropertyID`, interpret constant `optionSourceID=1007`, or encode absence as a business fact.\n- Authenticated aggregate-only source inspection now proves separate North America Disney and Lucas creation branches. Direct branch/route membership is authoritative licensor/studio scope evidence; landing-table family and property-name keywords are not. Marvel submissions remain under Disney OPA by settled business rule.\n- The governed structure must support append-only OPA Property scope/source membership keyed by `licensed_property_id` plus stable route identity (region, branch, LOB, product type, template, workflow, and capture), including legitimate membership of one Property in multiple scopes. Current presentation must prefer direct latest-approved scope evidence and fail closed when evidence conflicts or is absent.\n- Star Wars-like source names move only through evidence-backed, owner-approved semantic/source-name resolution; no table-family fallback or fuzzy guess.\n\n## Governed DCP decision supersession\n\nPreserve every prior decision and bind each supersession to exact source identity plus evidence/approval metadata. Current presentation must deterministically select only the latest approved decision and fail closed on ambiguity/conflict. Add truthful evidence status `supported_owner_source_label` (or an equally explicit reviewed name) for owner-approved source-title-family declarations, distinct from OPA-exact evidence. Preserve the SELECT/INSERT-only loader posture unless a narrower reviewed mechanism proves necessary; do not grant general service-role UPDATE.\n\nThe private replacement payload is prepared and loaded only after the structure is verified in production.\n\n## New direct OPA scope evidence (aggregate only)\n\nRead-only DOM inspection on 2026-08-26 found Disney Home Standard (`templateId=21`, `workflowId=49`, `lob=200`) and Lucas Home Standard (`templateId=462`, `workflowId=50`, `lob=200`) as separate source branches. Disney exposed 1,451 unique Property IDs; Lucas exposed 74; exactly one ID overlapped. The prior private canonical-properties capture had 1,445 unique IDs, all currently present in Disney, and contained only the single overlapping Lucas ID. Therefore 73 directly Lucas-scoped Properties were absent from that capture. These are aggregate coverage facts only; licensed identifiers and names stay private.\n\nThis evidence supersedes any inference that the older Disney-route capture covered Lucas/Star Wars. The migration must define the append-only structural contract; private route-membership capture/loading remains downstream and occurs only after production structure verification.\n\n## Coordination boundary\n\nThe shared-db migration owns the API function/result contract and governed decision-history structure. The DB Data Admin UI consumer update is coordinated against the finalized API shape and verified authenticated-live. Keep licensed source rows and names out of this public repository, issue, PR, review prompts, and logs; use only sanitized contract fixtures and aggregate evidence.\n\nUpdate the canonical Licensing Master Data rules in the same reviewed change: OPA = Submissions; DCP Vault = Disney/Lucasfilm Creative only; Marvel Creative = ASGARD only; mixed-guide DCP Marvel tags remain raw evidence but are excluded from licensor presentation; landing family is never authority.\n\n## Completion evidence\n\nReport issue, claim, migration, PR, exact-head independent review, preview run/digest, production dry-run, immutable review evidence, production run/digest, direct catalog/function verification, authenticated live UI proof, and private downstream hand-back to source task `01a03a84-ce14-74d3-bdfe-de69a894d32b`.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1800\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties\n  - table plm.dcp_property_licensor_resolution\n  - table plm.opa_property_scope_membership\nreads:\n  - table plm.opa_property_studio_resolution\n  - table plm.dcp_property\n  - table plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property\n  - table plm.marvel_dcp_property\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-26T22:29:11Z","createdAt":"2026-08-26T14:22:39Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1599,"title":"HANDOVER: add source-purpose and review evidence contract to Scraped Properties","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:31:25Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1599"},

{"body":"Follow-up to production-complete shared-db #1427, discovered during GLM's independent review of PopDAM issue #96.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1700\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - function public.propagate_group_tags_batch\n```\n\n## Problem\n\nProduction `public.asset_tags.category` and `status` are NOT NULL with no defaults after #1427. The existing `public.propagate_group_tags_batch` function still performs `INSERT INTO asset_tags (asset_id, tag, source)`, so every genuinely new propagated tag fails with SQLSTATE 23502. This breaks the existing Propagate Group Tags operation before its planned safe replacement in PopDAM #96 Step 6.\n\n## Required governed correction\n\n1. Replace only `public.propagate_group_tags_batch` through a new timestamped migration; do not edit applied migrations.\n2. Preserve the existing public signature, batching/cursor behavior, permissions, and capability.\n3. Include explicit `category='legacy_unscoped'` and `status='active'` for copied legacy AI rows, matching #1427's transition classification. Do not infer scope from tag text and do not promote copied rows to group facts.\n4. Preserve manual rows, rejected tombstones, and unrelated assets; keep conflict handling non-destructive.\n5. Add transaction-rolled-back preview tests proving a new propagated tag succeeds with required fields, an existing manual/rejected collision survives, rerun is idempotent, and unrelated groups are untouched.\n6. Cross-link [PopDAM #96](https://github.com/u2giants/popdam3/issues/96) and shared-db #1427. Merge and promote through the active orchestrator with ledger and live function evidence.\n\nThis is an urgent compatibility repair for the existing capability. {"body":"## Outcome\r\n\r\nCorrect the DCP Vault portion of DB Data Admin Scraped Properties so presentation licensor is evidence-backed rather than inferred from the landing-table family. Disney, Marvel, and Star Wars remain distinct licensors. Every DCP row remains visible; rows without sufficient evidence or with conflicting authorities appear in explicit review groups instead of being falsely assigned.\r\n\r\nThe private source-data session has completed and committed the signed K2557 schedule extraction and conservative reconciliation. No licensed property names or contract text belong in this public issue, migration, PR, tests, or logs.\r\n\r\n## Current production failure proof\r\n\r\nThe existing function blanket-labels `plm.dcp_property` as Disney, `plm.marvel_dcp_property` as Marvel, and `plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property` as Star Wars. Private exact-evidence reconciliation proves those source-table families contain cross-licensor records. Portal/table provenance is therefore not licensor ownership evidence.\r\n\r\nAggregate private evidence only:\r\n- 325 DCP property identities reviewed.\r\n- 145 currently supported by signed contract, canonical core ownership, or exact owner-approved OPA evidence.\r\n- 1 authority conflict and 179 unresolved; these must fail closed and remain visible.\r\n\r\n## Required structural contract\r\n\r\n1. Add private table `plm.dcp_property_licensor_resolution`, keyed by `(source_system, source_property_id)`.\r\n2. Store nullable presentation licensor key/name, resolution status, authority/provenance reference, evidence reference, source hash, and timestamps. Allowed presentation licensors are Disney, Marvel, and Star Wars. Allowed statuses must include the current evidence outcomes plus explicit conflict and unresolved states.\r\n3. RLS/direct grants must keep the mapping private; service-role application data loading is allowed, authenticated users receive no direct table access.\r\n4. Update `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text,text,integer)` to join all three DCP property tables to the resolution table. Supported rows group under Disney, Marvel, or Star Wars. Conflict and unresolved rows group under clearly named DCP Vault review headings. Never fall back to table-family ownership.\r\n5. Preserve source system, source table, source ID, readable display label, capture marker, search, pagination, licensing-manager authorization, and exact-once coverage.\r\n6. The migration creates no licensed-data rows. The private source-data session will load the 325 mappings only after exact production target proof.\r\n\r\n## Scope block\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 1\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - table plm.dcp_property_licensor_resolution\r\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties\r\n  - trigger set_updated_at on plm.dcp_property_licensor_resolution\n  - policy dcp_property_licensor_resolution_read on plm.dcp_property_licensor_resolution\r\nreads:\r\n  - table plm.dcp_property\r\n  - table plm.marvel_dcp_property\r\n  - table plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property\r\n\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n1. All 325 current DCP properties appear exactly once after the private mapping load.\r\n2. No DCP row is assigned a licensor from its source table alone.\r\n3. Supported rows group separately under Disney, Marvel, and Star Wars.\r\n4. Conflicts and unresolved rows remain visible in explicit review groups.\r\n5. No licensed property name or contract clause is committed to this public repository or printed in CI.\r\n6. Contract tests cover each licensor, conflict, unresolved, missing-mapping fail-closed behavior, exact-once coverage, pagination, search, and authorization.\r\n7. Preview, guarded merge, production promotion, private production data load, and authenticated live browser verification pass.\r\n\r\n## Owner authorization\r\n\r\nAlbert Hazan explicitly directed this work to continue without stopping until 100% complete in the current conversation on 2026-08-26. This authorizes the scoped structural correction through production and the subsequent private 325-row resolution load, subject to exact-target proof and all governed safety gates.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-26T14:01:14Z","createdAt":"2026-08-26T12:36:26Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Outcome\n\nUpdate the production DB Data Admin Scraped Properties feed so Disney OPA rows use the completed owner-reviewed studio resolutions instead of appearing as one Disney OPA (unsplit) group.\n\nRequired OPA review groups: Disney OPA, Marvel OPA, Lucasfilm / Star Wars OPA, Pixar OPA, Disney OPA - ambiguous crossover, and Disney OPA - unresolved.\n\nKeep Disney, Marvel, and Star Wars DCP Vault rows as separate source-preserving groups. Do not change `plm.opa_property` or `plm.opa_property_studio_resolution` rows.\n\n## Live failure proof\n\nAuthenticated production `https://data.designflow.app/` build `5356de9` showed Disney OPA (unsplit) with all 1,445 properties. Marvel examples remained inside that section. Existing Disney and Marvel headings represented DCP Vault data, not the completed OPA classification.\n\nProduction resolution coverage was reconciled at 1,445/1,445 with no orphan or missing resolutions.\n\n## Business rule\n\nSettled rule in `docs/business-rules/licensing-master-data.md`: Marvel submissions and approvals are performed through Disney OPA. ASGARD is authoritative only for Marvel creative assets. Preserve source provenance and leave unresolved mappings explicit.\n\n## Scope block\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text,text,integer)\nreads:\n  - table plm.opa_property\n  - table plm.opa_property_studio_resolution\nreturn_to: n/a\n```\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. All 1,445 OPA properties appear exactly once.\n2. No Disney OPA (unsplit) heading remains.\n3. Canonical classifications create Disney OPA, Marvel OPA, Lucasfilm / Star Wars OPA, and Pixar OPA groups.\n4. `ambiguous_crossover` and `unresolved` rows remain visible in explicit review groups.\n5. DCP Vault groups and other feeds remain unchanged.\n6. Pagination, search, Licensing Manager authorization, provenance, source IDs, and read-only behavior remain intact.\n7. Contract tests cover all six outcomes and exact-once coverage.\n8. Preview, guarded merge, production promotion, and authenticated live browser verification pass.\n\n## Owner production authorization\n\nAlbert Hazan authorized this exact production change in the current conversation on 2026-08-26 after being told the outcome: remove Disney OPA (unsplit) and expose the completed OPA classifications on the production Scraped Properties tab for Licensing review.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-26T13:10:26Z","createdAt":"2026-08-26T12:26:17Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1589,"title":"Split Disney OPA classifications in Scraped Properties","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:31:37Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1589"},

{"body":"## Outcome\n\nAdd a private, capture-versioned landing model for Marvel ASGARD Creative Asset metadata: guide categories, style guides, nested guide nodes, asset files, Characters, source terms/facets, likeness, and their direct source relationships.\n\n## Business boundary\n\n- Disney OPA is authoritative for current Marvel submissions and submission-side vocabulary, effective December 2025.\n- ASGARD is authoritative for Marvel Creative Assets.\n- ASGARD guide and Character labels must not be automatically promoted or fuzzy-matched to OPA Property or Character identities.\n- The existing DCP Vault Marvel-tag slice came from one mixed guide whose assets were indiscriminately tagged Disney, Lucas, and Marvel. It must not seed these tables or establish direct Marvel relationships.\n- Licensed filenames and labels remain private and are intentionally omitted from this issue.\n\n## Required structure\n\nCreate capture/completeness tables, an arbitrary-depth guide-node hierarchy, stable asset identity with all three currently observed source identifier fields, capture-versioned node/asset placement, Character relationships, generic typed facet terms, asset-level likeness, and explicit reviewed OPA resolution tables.\n\nSource term kinds must initially support character action, artwork type, image coloration, descriptive keyword, and iteration. Descriptive-keyword combined values must retain raw evidence while loaders also create individual source terms.\n\nUse guarded begin, chunk-load, finalize, and abort RPCs. Finalization must reconcile checkpoints and gaps. Incomplete captures cannot withdraw rows. No source row is hard-deleted. Store no artwork bytes, preview/download URLs, signed URLs, tokens, or account identity.\n\n## Proven live shape\n\n- categories -> style guides -> nested nodes, with up to 12 hierarchy tiers supported by the portal;\n- paginated asset lists at leaf nodes;\n- application-side asset identifiers for style-guide asset, asset, and original file;\n- filename, file size, and display order;\n- many-to-many facets for Character Name, Character Action, Artwork Type, Image Coloration, descriptive keywords, optional Iteration, and asset-level Actor Likeness;\n- asset-search responses include records plus facet counts;\n- no direct Property relationship was observed in the inspected guide.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- a 12-level guide tree and paginated node assets load and reconcile;\n- duplicate observation of one source asset does not duplicate asset identity;\n- asset-to-Character and asset-to-term relationships are many-to-many and capture-versioned;\n- likeness is asset-level tri-state only;\n- replay is idempotent and conflicting source identifiers fail closed;\n- incomplete captures cannot deactivate prior evidence;\n- OPA resolutions require an explicit confirmed decision with authority/evidence;\n- DCP mixed-guide rows cannot populate ASGARD tables;\n- licensed rows remain private under RLS and raw source JSON is retained privately;\n- aggregate tests reconcile capture, guide, node, page, asset, Character, and term-kind totals.\n\nThe full licensed-source-side specification is in the private `u2giants/licensor-source-data` repository at `marvel-asgard/SHARED-DB-SCHEMA-SPEC.md`.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 950\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_capture\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_capture_checkpoint\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_capture_gap\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_guide_category\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_style_guide\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_guide_node\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_asset\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_node_asset_observation\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_character\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_asset_character_observation\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_term\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_asset_term_observation\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_asset_likeness_observation\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_character_opa_resolution\n  - table plm.marvel_asgard_guide_opa_property_resolution\n  - function plm.begin_marvel_asgard_capture\n  - function plm.load_marvel_asgard_chunk\n  - function plm.finalize_marvel_asgard_capture\n  - function plm.abort_marvel_asgard_capture\n  - index plm.marvel_asgard_asset_asset_id_uidx\n  - index plm.marvel_asgard_asset_original_file_uidx\n  - index plm.marvel_asgard_asset_style_guide_asset_uidx\n  - index plm.marvel_asgard_category_source_key_uidx\n  - index plm.marvel_asgard_character_one_confirmed_opa_idx\n  - {"body":"## Result required\n\nDisney OPA properties must no longer be consumed as though every row belongs to the Disney studio/licensor. Preserve the raw OPA submission capture, but provide governed separation for Disney, Marvel, and Lucasfilm/Star Wars.\n\nThis is a bounded successor from the current licensing architecture and issue #640. Do not dispatch the stale umbrella issue #1090.\n\n## Current evidence\n\n- Production target was proved read-only as the shared POP database before inspection.\n- `plm.opa_property` contains 1,445 property identities and has no studio/licensor discriminator.\n- `plm.opa_property_character` contains 10,262 direct OPA property-character links.\n- Separate DCP property tables exist for Marvel and Lucasfilm, but OPA is the canonical submissions vocabulary and DCP is secondary evidence.\n- The private OPA capture includes substantial Marvel coverage.\n- Only a small residual set of Star Wars-labelled OPA options is visible; it is dominated by retired/do-not-use and crossover/co-brand options. Do not infer that the active Lucasfilm catalogue was captured by OPA.\n- The existing private ColdLion reconciliation uses name patterns and ColdLion title-family matching to route combined OPA candidates. That is inferred operational matching, not direct OPA studio assertion.\n\nNo licensed property names or source IDs are included in this issue.\n\n## Required structural contract\n\n1. Keep `plm.opa_property`, `plm.opa_character`, and `plm.opa_property_character` as immutable/raw source identities and direct relationships. Do not rewrite source labels or IDs.\n2. Add a governed OPA property-to-studio resolution layer with explicit provenance and resolution status. It must distinguish at least direct source assertion, owner-reviewed resolution, inferred candidate, ambiguous/crossover, and unresolved.\n3. Do not force one owning studio when a submission option spans Disney, Pixar, Marvel, and/or Star Wars. The structure must support multi-studio evidence or an explicit ambiguous/crossover state without promoting it as direct ownership.\n4. Expose consumable separated results for Disney, Marvel, and Lucasfilm/Star Wars that exclude unresolved and merely inferred candidates from canonical ownership by default.\n5. Preserve the distinction between the portal operator/source system (Disney OPA) and the resolved licensor/studio. `source_system = Disney OPA` must not imply `licensor = Disney`.\n6. The loader must fail closed when a canonical studio resolution is missing or unrecognized; no silent Disney default.\n7. Add regression tests proving Marvel rows do not appear in the Disney canonical view, Lucasfilm/Star Wars rows do not appear in Disney or Marvel, crossover/ambiguous rows are not forced, and raw OPA counts/IDs/links survive unchanged.\n8. Keep licensed row mappings in the private `u2giants/licensor-source-data` repository. Public migrations, issue text, tests, and PR descriptions may contain only structure, synthetic fixtures, counts, and provenance rules.\n\n## Data follow-up after structure\n\nThe licensor-source-data session will build/review the private resolution rows. Name-pattern and DCP/ColdLion matches may create candidates, but only direct source evidence or explicit owner review may promote canonical studio ownership. Unresolved rows stay unresolved.\n\n## Acceptance gates\n\n- Preview migration and tests pass against the exact current shared-db main.\n- Raw OPA property and property-character counts reconcile before and after the change.\n- Separated views have no cross-studio leakage under synthetic regression fixtures.\n- A count-only private reconciliation reports canonical, inferred, ambiguous/crossover, and unresolved totals per studio without publishing licensed rows.\n- Production requires a fresh exact-change owner authorization after preview proof; this issue is not production approval.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 850\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table plm.opa_property_studio_resolution\n  - view api.opa_disney_property\n  - view api.opa_marvel_property\n  - view api.opa_lucasfilm_property\n  - table api.opa_disney_property\n  - table api.opa_marvel_property\n  - table api.opa_lucasfilm_property\n  - function plm.sync_opa_property_studio_resolution\nreads:\n  - table plm.opa_property\n  - table plm.opa_character\n  - table plm.opa_property_character\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T22:19:54Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T20:05:58Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1547,"title":"HANDOVER: separate Disney OPA properties into Disney, Marvel, and Lucasfilm resolution","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:32:10Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1547"},
{"body":"# Fix DCP Vault Property display labels in DB Data Admin\n\nAlbert reported that the production **Scraped Properties** tab shows DCP Vault rows as `[Unlabeled source ID: dcpvault:properties/…]` for Disney, Marvel, and Star Wars. The capture contains a stable source ID whose final segment is a readable Property slug, but no separate source-declared display-name field.\n\n## Required outcome\n\nUpdate `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties` so DCP Vault Property rows for all three presentation Licensors receive a clean human-readable `display_label` derived deterministically from the terminal `source_id` slug when `display_name` is null or blank.\n\n- Apply to `plm.dcp_property`, `plm.marvel_dcp_property`, and `plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property` / Star Wars presentation rows.\n- Preserve `source_property_id` and source provenance exactly; do not update licensed landing rows.\n- Prefer a nonblank source `display_name` if a future capture supplies one.\n- Derive only from the terminal path segment after the final `/`; do not reinterpret other path segments, infer relationships, or fuzzy-match curated Master Data.\n- Convert hyphen/underscore separators to spaces and produce readable capitalization. Handle common connector words and apostrophe forms conservatively where deterministic; never use a bespoke list of licensed Property names.\n- If the terminal segment is missing or cannot yield a meaningful label, retain the existing explicit unlabeled fallback.\n- Do not change Disney/Marvel/Star Wars grouping or Lucasfilm source provenance.\n- Add SQL contract tests covering all three DCP studios, a future nonblank `display_name`, malformed/empty terminal IDs, multiword slugs, and the unchanged non-DCP fallback.\n- Rehearse on preview, review, merge, promote, and verify representative production results without copying licensed row values into this public issue, PR, logs, or test fixtures.\n\nRoot cause confirmed in migration `20260825175339`: each DCP arm passes nullable `p.display_name`; the final JSON uses the generic `[Unlabeled source ID: …]` fallback. The private capture contract confirms `properties[]` contains DCP IDs, not a separate official display-name field, so this must remain a presentation derivation rather than a source-data rewrite.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 903\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties\nreads:\n  - table plm.dcp_property\n  - table plm.marvel_dcp_property\n  - table plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property\n  - function app.require_licensing_manager_access\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T23:33:06Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T20:02:56Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1546,"title":"Fix DCP Vault Property display names in Scraped Properties","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:32:12Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1546"},
{"body":"## Outcome\n\nPOP CRM users need to rename the customer label shown throughout CRM. Customer-serving code deliberately shows `coalesce(display_name, name)`, but the guarded browser RPC `api.crm_update_customer` currently accepts only `p_name`; for rows with `display_name`, changing `name` appears to do nothing.\n\nExtend the existing guarded RPC so CRM can update `core.customer.display_name` without direct table access.\n\n## Requested structural change\n\nReplace the current seven-argument `api.crm_update_customer` signature with a backward-compatible eight-argument contract that appends:\n\n```sql\np_display_name text default null\n```\n\nThe function should continue to:\n\n- require `app.has_app_access('crm')`;\n- update the existing customer row only;\n- preserve all existing named arguments and their behavior;\n- use `display_name = coalesce(p_display_name, c.display_name)`;\n- remain executable by `authenticated` with no new direct grants on `core.customer`.\n\nDrop the old signature after creating/replacing the new contract so PostgREST does not face ambiguous overloads. Existing callers omit `p_display_name`, so the appended default preserves them.\n\n## Business boundary\n\nThis is a label change on the same Customer identity. It must not create a customer, change CRM classification, change ERP linkage, or derive customer status. The canonical business topic is `docs/business-rules/customers-contacts-and-organizations.md`.\n\n## App follow-up\n\nAfter the migration reaches production, `popcrm-web` will add a Rename control in `CustomerDrawer` and pass `p_display_name`. The UI will reject a blank label.\n\n## Verification\n\n- CRM-authorized authenticated user can update `display_name` through the RPC.\n- User without CRM access receives `insufficient_privilege`.\n- An existing call that omits `p_display_name` still succeeds.\n- The old seven-argument signature is absent and the new eight-argument signature is exposed without overload ambiguity.\n- No direct `core.customer` grant is added.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 850\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function api.crm_update_customer\nreads:\n  - table core.customer\n  - function app.has_app_access\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-26T01:17:01Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T19:00:51Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1544,"title":"Allow CRM to rename the displayed customer name","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:32:14Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1544"},

{"body":"# Add the Scraped Properties tab to DB Data Admin\n\nAlbert requested a new **Scraped Properties** tab on `data.designflow.app` showing every source-declared Property retained from authorized licensor scrapes, grouped by Licensor. Disney, Marvel, and Star Wars must be separate groups.\n\nThis application work is blocked on structural issue #1533. Start only after `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties` is merged and production-live.\n\n## Required outcome\n\n- Add a `Scraped Properties` tab alongside the existing `Properties` tab.\n- Load only through `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties`; do not query licensed landing tables directly from the browser.\n- Show all returned rows, organized by presentation Licensor, with Disney, Marvel, and Star Wars as distinct headings.\n- Display source provenance separately, including Lucasfilm provenance for Star Wars-presented rows where the governed contract supports that mapping.\n- Keep the screen read-only.\n- Reuse the existing RevoGrid and `FilterHeader` multi-filter conventions; do not create a second filter implementation.\n- Add unit tests plus browser assertions for tab presence/navigation, complete row handling, grouping, access denial, and distinct Disney/Marvel/Star Wars headings.\n- Visually verify the deployed screen before closing this issue.\n\nLikely files: `apps/db-data-admin/src/DataAdmin.tsx`, a new `ScrapedPropertiesTable.tsx`, `apps/db-data-admin/src/lib/data-admin.ts`, component/unit tests, and `apps/db-data-admin/tests/browser/grid.spec.ts` / `shell.spec.ts`.\n\nThe application will read `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties` after dependency #1533 is production-live. This prose dependency is not a database-object claim for the structural orchestrator.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 902\ndepends_on: 1533\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T19:33:31Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T17:16:34Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"# HANDOVER: add read-only Scraped Properties feed for DB Data Admin\n\nAlbert requested a new **Scraped Properties** tab on `data.designflow.app` that shows every source-declared Property retained from authorized licensor scrapes, organized by Licensor. Disney, Marvel, and Star Wars must appear as three separate Licensors.\n\nThe existing `api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree` is not sufficient: it represents curated `core.licensor` / `core.property`, not the complete retained source vocabularies. This task needs a separate, read-only API contract. The application tab will be implemented against that contract after it is available.\n\n## Required outcome\n\n1. Add `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties()` (or an equivalently safe paged contract) that returns one stable row per source Property identity with:\n   - presentation Licensor key/name\n   - source system and table\n   - stable source Property ID\n   - source-declared Property name, nullable\n   - source status when explicitly available, nullable\n   - provenance kind\n   - latest-seen/capture marker when reliably available\n2. Include only source-declared Property vocabularies. Do not reinterpret creative groups, guides, art programs, brands, or sub-brands as Properties.\n3. Preserve source provenance and never fuzzy-deduplicate names across portals. Deduplicate capture-scoped repeats only by stable source identity. If a source has no display name, return an explicitly unlabeled source ID rather than inventing a name.\n4. Present Disney, Marvel, and Star Wars separately. For Star Wars rows sourced from `lucasfilm_dcpvault`, keep Lucasfilm as provenance. Do not blanket-map Lucasfilm rows to Star Wars if the current source can contain non-Star-Wars Properties; use only an authoritative row-level mapping in that case.\n5. Expose selected vocabulary columns only. Never return raw payloads, source URLs, licensed assets, or unrelated metadata. Use the existing DB Data Admin authorization gate, revoke `public` and `anon`, and grant execute only to `authenticated`.\n6. Add SQL/contract tests for exact union membership, grants, absence of raw fields, capture deduplication, null-label handling, multi-Licensor Sega rows, and distinct Disney/Marvel/Star Wars groups.\n7. After the function is production-live, implement the application tab in a fresh repository-maintenance/app session using the existing RevoGrid and multi-filter conventions. {"body":"DesignFlow Sample Tracking plan step 8 needs durable, separate photo approval and optional QC approval facts for Flow 3. The current production schema has `sample_attachment` and `sample_workflow`, but no approval/history structure; overloading sample status would lose who decided what and would make rejected photos destructive or ambiguous.\n\nPlease author and promote a governed forward migration for:\n\n- append-only `dflow.sample_approval_event`, keyed to sample and optional attachment, with approval type (`photo` or `qc`), state (`pending`, `approved`, `rejected`), whether QC is required, optional destination type/id, reason, actor user/role, idempotency key/request hash, and timestamp;\n- `dflow.sample_approval_current`, the deterministic latest event per sample and approval type;\n- `dflow.post_sample_approval_event(...)`, an idempotent transition RPC that serializes per sample, rejects invalid/skipped transitions, requires an approved photo before QC decisions, preserves rejected/rework history, and never posts inventory movement.\n\nThe application will enforce authenticated role/capability boundaries; the RPC must still enforce state consistency and idempotency. Add indexes/constraints required for latest-per-sample reads and exact-key replay. Add regression SQL for approved photo with QC not required, QC pending/approved/rejected, rejection followed by rework, invalid skipped states, idempotent replay/conflict, and zero sample movements from approval events.\n\nThis is structural shared-db work. Application code stays in the DesignFlow repos and no DDL will be added there.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 85\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - table dflow.sample_approval_event\n  - view dflow.sample_approval_current\n  - function dflow.post_sample_approval_event\n```\n\nReturn to: popcre/designflow-frontend issue #157 / Sample Tracking step 8.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-26T03:01:55Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T14:55:44Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"`supabase/migrations/20260814170749_wb_retire_legacy_capture_paths.sql` (authored under #958, PR #979, merged 2026-08-14) is applied to **neither preview nor production**. It cannot be promoted through its original file, and the reason is structural rather than anything wrong with the SQL.\n\n## Why it cannot be promoted as-is\n\nThe production business-risk gate (`scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py`, `prove_preview_producer_matches_main`) requires the preview-apply evidence to come from commits carrying the **same producer files as the merge commit of the PR that authored the version**:\n\n```\nPR #979 merge commit 5d17cbe  .github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml -> d40f3c2a3fbb424654c566aeef29a2a88e85f00d\nexact main today             .github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml -> 1721b9d618888afce1e2db81adfdf35171802978\n```\n\nDifferent bytes, so a rehearsal run today produces evidence the gate must refuse — the same refusal that stopped `20260814223552` on #679.\n\n**Rehearsing at the authoring commit is impossible, not merely disallowed.** The workflow at `5d17cbe` hard-codes `PREVIEW_PROJECT_REF: rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` and asserts it on its first step. That project was **deleted on 2026-08-18** and replaced; current `main` reads the ref from a repository variable precisely because of that deletion. Authoring-era machinery has no live database to write to.\n\n**Do not rehearse this version at current main.** `20260814223552` is unrecoverable specifically because its one preview apply happened at a non-qualifying commit and *an applied version can never re-apply to preview*. `20260814170749` is still `[GENUINELY-PENDING]` on preview, so its one chance is unspent. Spending it on non-qualifying evidence strands it permanently.\n\n## What the migration does\n\nFinishes retiring the first-generation Warner (STARLABS) tables. Drops 8 tables, 18 functions and 2 API views. **Destructive, but only of empty objects** — verified read-only on production 2026-08-25: all eight tables hold 0 rows, the 4,158 real relationships live in `plm.wb_property_character_normalized`, and no legacy capture is in flight. Its own preflight refuses to run if either changes.\n\nIndependently reviewed by Muse Spark 1.2 (session `wb-legacy-cleanup-safety`): safe to apply, zero consumers of the dropped views, no conflict from `20260816045120` or `20260823175638` (both read only the normalized tables). It added one required follow-up: `types/database.types.ts:28883` carries the legacy table definition, so **`types/` must be regenerated in the same window**.\n\n## Impact if it never lands\n\n**Nothing is broken in production today.** Two API views return zero rows from emptied tables, so an ad-hoc query through them is silently wrong; no application code reads them. Sixteen retired loader functions remain callable and the capture guard still accepts retired target names, so a stale script could land a fresh Warner scrape into tables nothing reads. Latent risk, not an outage.\n\n## The decision needed\n\n**OWNER RULING RECORDED 2026-08-25:** Reissue under a fresh version. Hard-block the original. Reconcile the stranded-version exception in the existing production procedure. Ship no replacement API view. Preview rehearsal and production promotion remain separate owner-authorized actions. Full plan: `plan_warner-legacy-cleanup-reissue.md` at `main` commit `0efc34913a8350416fdaaccacd7ee0611039f0b7` (PR #1528).\n\nPrecedents: `20260816045130` → `20260816110750`, and `20260814223552` → `20260825124200` on #679.\n\nFull analysis: `docs/verification/unapplied-20260814-migrations-status-20260825.md` §2, and #949 comments of 2026-08-25.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function plm.begin_wb_capture\n  - function plm.begin_wb_capture_legacy\n  - function plm.finalize_wb_capture\n  - function plm.finalize_wb_capture_legacy\n  - function plm.sync_wb_asset\n  - function plm.sync_wb_asset_character\n  - function plm.sync_wb_asset_franchise_property\n  - function plm.sync_wb_asset_style_guide\n  - function plm.sync_wb_character\n  - function plm.sync_wb_franchise_property\n  - function plm.sync_wb_property_character\n  - function plm.sync_wb_style_guide\n  - function plm.wb_validate_normalized_row\n  - function public.sync_wb_asset\n  - function public.sync_wb_asset_character\n  - function public.sync_wb_asset_franchise_property\n  - function public.sync_wb_asset_style_guide\n  - function public.sync_wb_character\n  - function public.sync_wb_franchise_property\n  - function public.sync_wb_property_character\n  - function public.sync_wb_style_guide\n  - table plm.wb_asset\n  - table plm.wb_asset_character\n  - table plm.wb_asset_character_normalized\n  - table plm.wb_asset_franchise\n  - table plm.wb_asset_franchise_property\n  - table plm.wb_asset_normalized\n  - table plm.wb_asset_property\n  - table plm.wb_asset_style_guide\n  - table plm.wb_asset_style_guide_normalized\n  - table plm.wb_capture\n  - table plm.wb_character\n  - table plm.wb_character_normalized\n  - {"body":"## What is broken  Classifying a domain on the POP CRM **Customers → Triage** tab fails in the browser with:  ``` permission denied for table ingested_domain Hint: Grant the required privileges to the current role with: GRANT UPDATE ON crm.ingested_domain TO authenticated; (42501) ```  Reported by the owner on 2026-08-25 against production. The Triage tab is therefore read-only in practice: a human can see ingested domains but cannot classify one as Active Customer / Potential Customer / Not a Customer.  ## Why the app cannot fix this itself  `popcrm-web` writes the classification with a direct table update (`src/features/crm/api.ts` → `updateRow('ingested_domain', …)` against schema `crm`). `authenticated` holds no grants at all on `crm.ingested_domain` (`information_schema.role_table_grants` returns zero rows for that table), and the browser contract for these apps is \"read the `api` schema, write through `api` RPCs\" — every other CRM write already goes through one (`api.crm_update_customer`, `api.crm_update_contact`, …).  **Please do not solve this with `GRANT UPDATE … TO authenticated`.** That would be the first browser-writable `crm` table and would bypass the `app.has_app_access('crm')` check every other write enforces.  ## Requested change  Add a `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC in the `api` schema, matching the shape of `api.crm_update_customer`:  ``` api.crm_update_ingested_domain(   p_ingested_domain_id uuid,   p_status text default null ) returns crm.ingested_domain ```  - raise `insufficient_privilege` unless `app.has_app_access('crm')` - `coalesce(p_status, d.status)` so null means \"leave unchanged\", consistent   with the other CRM update RPCs - constrain `p_status` to the values the Triage UI offers   (`ACTIVE_CUSTOMER`, `POTENTIAL_CUSTOMER`, `OTHER`, plus whatever   `crm.ingested_domain.status` already accepts — `new` is the default today) - `grant execute` to `authenticated`, and no new table grants  Ingested domains stay triage-only: this RPC must not create, link to, or update `core.customer` in any way (promotion was dropped by `20260629034600` and must stay dropped).  ## App-side follow-up (popcrm-web, not this repo)  `updateIngestedDomain()` will switch from the direct table update to the new RPC, and the generated types will be regenerated. I will do that in popcrm-web once this lands — no coordination needed beyond the function name and argument names above.  ## Verification asked for  - as an `authenticated` user holding `crm` app access: classifying a domain   succeeds - as an `authenticated` user without `crm` access: raises `insufficient_privilege` - `crm.ingested_domain` still has zero direct grants to `authenticated`  ## Context  Filed from the popcrm-web session that fixed the worker paging bug — the Triage list grew from 96 to 457 domains once contact-sync could see the whole mailbox, which is why this long-standing permission gap is now blocking real work.  \n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 850\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function api.crm_update_ingested_domain\nreads:\n  - table crm.ingested_domain\n  - function app.has_app_access\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T22:38:02Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T14:15:35Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Request\n\nRepair the production-live Flow 1 skipped-check-in factory-return trigger introduced for issue #1422. The canonical application and shipment vocabulary stores the Ningbo office as `Ningbo`, but `dflow.validate_sample_movement_shipment_identity()` currently requires the return shipment destination id to equal lowercase `ningbo`. A valid return shipment created by the live tracking API is therefore rejected with SQLSTATE `23514`, surfaced as HTTP 422.\n\nThis must be a forward migration in `u2giants/shared-db`; do not edit applied migration `20260824172136` and do not place DDL in either DesignFlow application repository.\n\n## Live evidence\n\n- Production target was proved immediately before the attempted write: Supabase project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\n- Controlled durable Flow 1 fixture: sample 24, factory visit 3, outbound shipment 1.\n- The visit is legitimately `shipped`; custody is exactly one unit at `in_transit/1`.\n- The live API created canonical outbound data successfully, then `POST /sample/24/factory-visits/3/return` returned HTTP 422 with no partial write.\n- Trigger source in applied migration `20260824172136_sample_tracking_piece_split_and_transit_return.sql` compares `v_line.destination_location_id IS DISTINCT FROM 'ningbo'`, while the application creates the canonical return destination as `Ningbo` and existing office custody uses `Ningbo`.\n\n## Required repair and proof\n\n1. Preserve the existing exact visit/sample/shipment/factory identity checks and transit-to-transit conservation.\n2. Make the Ningbo endpoint comparison conform to the canonical office vocabulary without weakening unrelated endpoint validation.\n3. Add a contract test using the canonical `Ningbo` shipment destination.\n4. Rehearse on preview, obtain the required reviewer verdict, and promote only through the governed bounded production lane.\n5. Verify the exact production function definition after promotion.\n6. Notify `popcre/designflow-frontend#157` so the same controlled fixture can retry the original UI action and prove return transit, Ningbo receipt, and no duplicate custody.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 560\ndepends_on: #1422\nobjects:\n  - function dflow.validate_sample_movement_shipment_identity\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T13:51:10Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T11:58:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1502,"title":"Sample Tracking Step 5: canonical Ningbo case rejects skipped-check-in return","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:32:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1502"},
{"body":"Follow-up to production-complete shared-db #1427, discovered by independent Grok review of PopDAM issue #96 app integration.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1100\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - function public.replace_asset_ai_tag_result\n```\n\n## Problem\n\nThe production function `public.replace_asset_ai_tag_result(uuid,text,text,jsonb)` deletes only rows matching source + model. Historical AI rows use `source='ai'`, `category='legacy_unscoped'`, and `model IS NULL`, so a new model-scoped replacement does not remove them. Because `asset_tags` uniqueness is `(asset_id, tag)`, a legacy row can block the newly typed row and silently retain stale category/provenance.\n\nThe current `ON CONFLICT` predicate can also update a same-source/same-model rejected tombstone back to active, violating #1427's durable-rejection contract.\n\n## Required governed correction\n\n1. Change only the canonical RPC through a new timestamped migration; do not edit applied migrations.\n2. On a new file-AI result, replace AI-owned active/candidate rows for that asset across prior model/null-model legacy representations while preserving all manual/created-by rows and every rejected tombstone.\n3. On normalized-tag conflict with an existing rejected tombstone, do not resurrect or overwrite it; the proposal remains absent from active compatibility/search data.\n4. Preserve service-role-only access, validation, bounded search refresh, grants, and the public signature used by PopDAM.\n5. Add preview fixture tests proving null-model legacy collision is upgraded/replaced, stale AI rows disappear, manual collision survives unchanged, rejected same-model and legacy tombstones survive and remain excluded, rerun is idempotent, and unrelated assets are untouched.\n6. Cross-link [PopDAM #96](https://github.com/u2giants/popdam3/issues/96) and shared-db #1427. Merge and apply through the active orchestrator, with production ledger and live function-definition evidence.\n\nPopDAM application rollout remains blocked until this correction is production-complete. No embedding backfill should run against an intermediate corpus.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T17:22:42Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T11:19:50Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1498,"title":"Fix asset AI replacement legacy collision and rejected tombstones","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:32:49Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1498"},
{"body":"# DesignFlow multi-schema adoption: users, roles, permissions, and comments contract\n\nIssue #1439 deliberately split Factory/Artist identity bridging from the higher-risk authentication and application-support cutover. This successor owns the remaining coordinated structural design for users, roles, permissions, and comments.\n\n## Required outcome\n\n- Preserve every `dflow` integer identity, FK, login/JWT, and workflow contract during develop/staging adoption.\n- Reconcile `dflow.users`, `dflow.\"Roles\"`, `dflow.\"RolePermissions\"`, `dflow.\"UIElements\"`, and `dflow.comments` against `app.profile`, `app.role`, `app.users`, `app.\"RolePermissions\"`, `app.\"UIElements\"`, and `app.comment` from current live catalogs and current `main`.\n- Keep `office_location` and `preferred_language` authoritative on `dflow.users` until user/auth authority moves as one verified contract.\n- Provide exactly one writable authority throughout. Do not add trigger mirroring, dual-writable replicas, manual synchronization, or deletion-based reconciliation.\n- Keep `dflow` compatibility until backend issue popcre/designflow-backend#71 passes password login, Microsoft SSO, `/api/user/me`, language, photo, Manage Users, impersonation, mentions, roles/permissions, and threaded item-comment CRUD in develop/staging.\n- Production Cloud SQL remains unchanged during this adoption.\n\n## Required discovery\n\nInventory all columns, integer sequences, incoming/outgoing FKs, grants, RLS, triggers, views, and functions touching the listed objects. Bind every mapping to direct evidence and leave ambiguous identities unresolved.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 949\nwrites:\n  - table dflow.\"Roles\"\n  - table dflow.comments\n  - table dflow.users\n  - table app.role\n  - table app.comment\n  - table app.profile\nreads:\n  - table dflow.\"RolePermissions\"\n  - table dflow.\"UIElements\"\n  - table app.users\n  - table app.\"RolePermissions\"\n  - table app.\"UIElements\"\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T14:59:26Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T10:53:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1496,"title":"HANDOVER: DesignFlow users, roles, permissions and comments coordinated transition","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:32:51Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1496"},

{"body":"## Outcome\n\nComplete #1427 after production prerequisite A (#1474) is live. Reconcile existing `public.asset_tags` rows in separately timed top-level batches, install and validate the complete PopDAM AI metadata/search contract, then remove the two recovery-only indexes while retaining the final active-only index.\n\n## Production starting state\n\nMigration `20260825041343` is live and verified. The eight new `asset_tags` columns are nullable, the legacy compatibility trigger remains enabled, and the forward/pending/active indexes provide a safe explicit pending state. No scoped AI/search capability is activated by A.\n\n## Required recovery B\n\n- Use monotonic keyset batches as separate top-level statements so each receives its own statement-timeout budget.\n- Do not repeat an unbatched insert, window dedupe, normalization loop, or compatibility-array rebuild inside a trailing `DO`/`EXECUTE` block.\n- Preserve transaction and failure semantics appropriate to each bounded step; every committed intermediate state must remain safe and explicit.\n- Validate completeness before late `NOT NULL`, constraints, functions/RPCs, triggers, policies, and final activation.\n- Drop `asset_tags_forward_asset_id_idx` after the rebuild and `asset_tags_pending_metadata_normalization_idx` after normalization; retain `asset_tags_active_asset_idx`.\n- Preserve the complete #1427 capability. No removal, bypass, or weakened contract is acceptable.\n- Keep prior failed versions permanently retired/hard-blocked.\n\n## Reviewer findings to carry\n\nUnify the migration/test contract-complete probes, update the historical tests when B removes the pending accelerator, and keep verification fail-closed. The production promotion must use the exact ordered version and immutable review/preview evidence.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on: 1474\nwrites:\n  - {"body":"Follow-up to #1427 after two production attempts rolled back cleanly at the unchanged 10-minute statement timeout. Review proved that resetting the timeout between statements does not release PostgreSQL table locks inside one transaction.\n\nThis issue now owns prerequisite A only. It is a short, independently safe migration that adds nullable asset_tags metadata columns plus the indexes required by the later bounded reconciliation, verifies an existing compatibility trigger remains enabled, and commits. It performs no reconciliation and does not activate the final #1427 contract. The pending state preserves current PopDAM behavior and is explicitly marked until a separately governed dependent B migration completes normalization, final constraints, triggers, RPCs, and search capability.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1200\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table public.asset_tags\n  - index public.asset_tags_active_asset_idx\n  - index public.asset_tags_forward_asset_id_idx\n  - index public.asset_tags_pending_metadata_normalization_idx\nreads:\n  - trigger trg_sync_asset_tags on public.asset_tags\n  - trigger asset_tags_sync_assets_tags on public.asset_tags\n```\n\nHistorical merged versions 20260825010603, 20260825025154, and 20260825031841 remain retired and production-hard-blocked. Rejected draft 20260825034915 never merged and remains permanently reserved against reuse.\n\nAcceptance: exact-head review; preview apply; guarded merge; production apply; ledger/catalog proof; then release #1475 and open the dependent B lane.
