{"body":"Production's Paramount loader was repaired against a body production does not have, and applying the trio now would silently revert that repair\r\n\r\n## What is true in production right now (measured 2026-08-25, read-only)\r\n\r\n`20260824135515_pmt_loader_raw_value_json_null_normalization` is applied to production. Its header states plainly that it is \"a full re-derivation of the CURRENT function body on main (20260814223552, the third rewrite)\". But **none of the three rewrites it derives from are applied to production** — `20260814193351`, `20260814213043` and `20260814223552` are still merged-but-not-applied, exactly as recorded in `docs/verification/unapplied-20260814-migrations-audit-20260823.md`.\r\n\r\nSo production now runs a Paramount loader that:\r\n\r\n- inserts into `plm.pmt_metadata_element`, which **does not exist in production** (`to_regclass` → NULL) → 42P01;\r\n- **no longer writes** `plm.pmt_authorized_title_property.paramount_property_name` or `plm.pmt_property_capture_log.property_name`, both of which are still **NOT NULL** in production (`is_nullable = 'NO'`, because `20260814193351` never applied) → 23502.\r\n\r\nMeasured:\r\n\r\n```\r\nfn_refs_element      = true      -- loader references pmt_metadata_element\r\nfn_writes_dupname    = false     -- loader no longer writes the duplicate-name columns\r\nelement_table        = null      -- pmt_metadata_element absent in production\r\natp_name_nullable    = NO\r\nlog_name_nullable    = NO\r\n```\r\n\r\nThis is **fail-closed**, not corrupting: a production Paramount capture aborts on its first chunk. Preview is unaffected — the trio is applied there and the 2026-08-24 preview capture (`037d73e3-185d-48b0-9e11-a16cbdd3418a`) succeeded on that state.\r\n\r\n## The second problem: applying the trio now reverts the repair\r\n\r\n`20260814223552` rewrites `plm.load_pmt_capture_chunk` and sorts **below** `20260824135515`, which is already in the ledger and will not re-run. So a production window that applies the trio in version order ends with the 08-14 body — i.e. **the JSON-null repair silently disappears**, and the exact bug issue #1418 fixed comes back. Nothing in the apply path warns about this: the function exists either way, so catalog verification passes.\r\n\r\n## What this needs\r\n\r\n1. A decision on the production Paramount window that accounts for the ordering: apply the trio **and** re-apply the JSON-null normalization as a new forward migration above it, in the same bounded set. Applying the trio alone is not safe.\r\n2. Consideration of whether the promote-a-repair-alone path should be blocked when the repair's own header names a base version that is not in the target ledger. This is the generic defect: #1418's repair was correct for preview and became incoherent the moment it was promoted alone. Related process issues: #1344, #1321.\r\n\r\nNo production Paramount data capture has been authorized or performed; this issue asks for no data action.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 850\r\ndepends_on:\r\nwrites:\r\n  - function plm.load_pmt_capture_chunk\r\nreads:\r\n  - table plm.pmt_metadata_element\r\n  - table plm.pmt_authorized_title_property\r\n  - table plm.pmt_property_capture_log\r\n  - table plm.pmt_asset_metadata_value\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Scope note for the orchestrator\r\n\r\nThe deliverable is ONE new forward migration re-applying the JSON-null normalization\r\n(`nullif(r->'raw_value', 'null'::jsonb)`) on top of the `20260814223552` loader body, so the\r\nproduction window can carry four versions in order: `20260814193351`, `20260814213043`,\r\n`20260814223552`, then this new one. It writes exactly one object, `plm.load_pmt_capture_chunk`,\r\nand must be a full re-derivation of the then-current body on `main` — never a copy of an older\r\nfile (the header of `20260814193351` states that rule).\r\n\r\nIt does not conflict with lane 2's `api.source_capture_inventory` work: different object, no overlap.\r\n\r\nThis issue asks for authoring plus a preview rehearsal of the four-version set only. **Production\r\npromotion is a separate owner-authorized step and is not requested here.** The owner has authorized\r\npreparation up to proven preview evidence (2026-08-25).\r\n\r\n\n\n## Historical evidence recovery stage\n\nFirst sequential prerequisite supersession only: reproduce the SQL bytes of 20260814193351_pmt_duplicate_name_columns_deprecated.sql under fresh governed version 20260825102727. Hold/exclude the original version after proving byte equality. The remaining two prerequisite supersessions follow only after this PR is previewed, merged, and its claim released. Migration 20260825094455 remains unchanged and last in the eventual production allowlist.\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T11:44:48Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T01:46:51Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1459,"title":"Production's Paramount loader was repaired against a body production does not have; applying the trio now would silently revert that repair","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:33:24Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1459"},

{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 80\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table dflow.\"itemattachment\"\n  - index dflow.itemattachment_item_num_id_fk_idx\nreads:\n```  ## Business problem  DesignFlow Item Library loads attachments for each bounded page with one Sequelize `separate: true` query using `item_num_id_fk IN (...)` and ordering by `item_num_id_fk, attachment_display_name`. The table has 194,624 estimated rows and is 69,853,184 bytes, but production has only the primary-key index on `item_attachment_id`.  ## Shared Supabase evidence (read-only, 2026-08-25 UTC)  - Proven database target for this structural finding: shared Supabase project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`. Live Cloud Run `db_ready` telemetry separately proves DesignFlow production still uses Cloud SQL/schema `designflow`; sandbox-Albert, develop, and staging use this Supabase pooler/schema `dflow`. The counters below therefore prove the migrated Supabase workload, not current production Cloud SQL pressure. - `extensions.pg_stat_statements` fingerprint `-5029970611856841487`: 3 calls, 1,648.16 ms total, 549.39 ms mean, 2,928 rows, 23,796 shared-buffer reads. - `pg_stat_user_tables`: 22 sequential scans and 1 index scan for `dflow.itemAttachment`. - Plain `EXPLAIN` (no execution) for the same filter/order shape selects a parallel sequential scan plus sort, total cost 10,522.58. - Separately, current Cloud SQL production request logs for `popcre-item-prod` show `/lib/getAllitems` at 110 calls, 1,169.5 ms average and 2,617.8 ms p95 in the 12-hour window beginning 2026-08-24 12:00 UTC. This proves the endpoint is materially slow but is not joined to the Supabase statement counters; the attachment statement is a proven migrated-Supabase structural defect, not asserted to be the entire production endpoint latency.  ## Requested governed outcome  Design and preview-verify the smallest index beginning with `item_num_id_fk`. Include `attachment_display_name` only if representative plans show the ordering benefit justifies the extra index width/write cost. Inspect open claims and canonical naming before selecting an index name.  Do not alter Item Library behavior, row data, or production infrastructure. Do not apply to production without the normal owner approval and promotion gates.  ## Verification  - Preview fixtures representative of 194k+ attachments and realistic page-sized `IN` lists. - Safe preview `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` for the attachment query. - Confirm indexed/bitmap access, lower buffers and latency, and stable order. - Run Item Library page tests and browser verification with attachments present and absent. - Return migration/PR and before-after evidence to `popcre/designflow-backend#72`.  ","closedAt":"2026-08-26T18:21:11Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T01:13:18Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1453,"title":"HANDOVER: index DesignFlow Item Library attachment page lookups","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:33:29Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1453"},
{"body":"```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 80\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table dflow.user_notification\n  - index dflow.user_notification_unread_user_created_idx\nreads:\n```  ## Business problem  DesignFlow's notification badge preserves a 30-second visible-tab refresh. Its unread count and notification-list queries filter `dflow.user_notification` by `user_id_fk` and `unread`; the table has 104,345 estimated rows but only the primary-key index.  ## Shared Supabase evidence (read-only, 2026-08-25 UTC)  - Proven database target for this structural finding: shared Supabase project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`. Live Cloud Run `db_ready` telemetry separately proves DesignFlow production still uses Cloud SQL/schema `designflow`; sandbox-Albert, develop, and staging use this Supabase pooler/schema `dflow`. The counters below therefore prove the migrated Supabase workload, not current production Cloud SQL pressure. - `extensions.pg_stat_statements` fingerprint `473917481045255957`: 1,812 count calls, 47,731.34 ms total, 26.34 ms mean, 2,452,292 shared-buffer hits, and 142,492 shared-buffer reads. The statistics reset timestamp is unavailable, so these are cumulative evidence, not a bounded incident window. - `pg_stat_user_tables`: 1,840 sequential scans and 3 index scans for `dflow.user_notification`. - Plain `EXPLAIN` (no execution) for `count(*) where user_id_fk = 0 and unread = true` selects a sequential scan with total cost 2736.33. - Separately, current Cloud SQL production request logs show 6,082 `/api/notifications/count` requests in the 12-hour window beginning 2026-08-24 12:00 UTC. This proves the application polling frequency but is not joined to the Supabase statement counters. The application-side hidden-tab polling repair is tracked in `popcre/designflow-backend#72` and does not remove the visible badge capability.  ## Requested governed outcome  Design and preview-verify the smallest index that supports both active queries without adding write-heavy redundant structure. A likely candidate is a partial index beginning with `user_id_fk` and scoped to unread rows; include `created_date DESC` only if representative plans prove it benefits the bounded notification-list query. Inspect existing/open claims before choosing the exact index name.  Do not change application polling, production infrastructure, or row data in this work item. Do not apply to production without the normal owner approval and promotion gates.  ## Verification  - Preview fixtures representative of 100k+ notifications. - Plain and safe preview `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` for the count and ordered/limited list. - Confirm indexed/bitmap access and materially fewer buffers. - Confirm notification inserts, mark-one-read, mark-all-read, list, and count still work. - Return the migration/PR and before-after evidence to `popcre/designflow-backend#72`.  ","closedAt":"2026-08-28T17:41:53Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T01:12:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Outcome\n\nAdd append-only Sega submission-vocabulary evidence and inferred Property relationships for style-guide and character candidates. This complements #1276, which owns inferred asset-to-Property links.\n\nNo licensed names or source rows appear in this issue. All facts below are aggregate counts and field requirements.\n\n## Why this is needed\n\nProduction currently contains the complete Sega asset-side capture:\n\n- 110 registry Properties\n- 7,000 assets\n- 37 inferred style-guide candidates\n- 176 inferred character candidates supported by 417 evidence rows\n- 0 direct asset-to-Property links\n\nA later read-only new Product Approval capture found a contract-specific canonical vocabulary of **6 Properties**. Production has no table recording that submission-side vocabulary and no Property relationship columns or tables for style-guide or character candidates.\n\nFolder-path evidence can currently associate:\n\n- 7,000 of 7,000 assets to at least one of the six canonical Properties, producing 7,113 assignments — owned by #1276\n- 19 of 37 style-guide candidates to one of the six\n- 78 of 176 unique character candidates to one of the six, supported by 250 of 417 evidence rows\n\nAll guide and character relationships remain inferred. The portal declares no style-guide flags in this capture and offers no Character picker or canonical Property-to-Character link.\n\n## Requested structure\n\n### `plm.sega_submission_capture`\n\nAppend-only identity and completeness record for a read-only Product Approval vocabulary capture. Include capture key, source commit, source hash, source URL, capture/load timestamps, status, selected contract source ID, expected/observed counts, `save_clicked`, submission-list-before hash, submission-list-after hash, and an explicit no-submission-created result.\n\nRequire `save_clicked = false` and equal before/after list hashes for a complete capture.\n\n### `plm.sega_submission_property`\n\nExact source IDs and labels offered by the selected contract's new Product Approval picker.\n\n- Composite identity scoped to the submission capture.\n- Foreign key to `plm.sega_submission_capture`.\n- Preserve exact source label, source URL and raw evidence.\n- Do not copy these rows into `core.*` and do not mark the other registry Properties deleted.\n\n### `plm.sega_style_guide_property_inferred`\n\nLink an existing capture-scoped style-guide candidate to an existing capture-scoped registry Property using folder-path evidence.\n\nRequire capture-scoped foreign keys to the candidate, Property and evidence catalog; evidence key; match method; rule version; confidence; raw evidence; and `relationship_truth = 'inferred'`.\n\n### `plm.sega_character_property_inferred`\n\nLink an existing capture-scoped character candidate to an existing capture-scoped registry Property using character evidence paths.\n\nRequire capture-scoped foreign keys to the character candidate, Property and supporting character evidence; evidence key; match method; rule version; confidence; raw evidence; and `relationship_truth = 'inferred'`.\n\n## Integrity and access\n\n- Never relax `plm.sega_asset_property`; it remains direct-only.\n- Allow more than one Property per asset, guide or character when separate source paths support it.\n- Pin every inferred relationship to `relationship_truth = 'inferred'` and confidence between 0 and 1.\n- Reject relationships whose endpoints come from different asset-side captures.\n- Use explicit `service_role` SELECT and INSERT grants only, matching the other append-only Sega landing tables; no update or delete.\n- Extend the appropriate Sega finalization checks and `api.source_capture_inventory` without changing another licensor's result.\n\n## Private application work after structure lands\n\nThe private `u2giants/licensor-source-data` repository will add loader support and invented-fixture tests after these database objects are merged. Licensed labels and relationship rows stay out of this public repository and public issue.\n\n## Verification\n\n- Preview accepts a complete six-row invented submission capture only when Save is false and the before/after hashes match.\n- Preview rejects mismatched counts, cross-capture relationship endpoints, non-inferred truth values and confidence outside 0..1.\n- Multiple Properties for one entity succeed when separate evidence supports them.\n- Inventory reporting includes the new Sega objects and no other licensor changes.\n- Production promotion remains a separate governed step.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 545\ndepends_on: 1276\nobjects:\n  - table plm.sega_submission_capture\n  - table plm.sega_submission_property\n  - table plm.sega_style_guide_property_inferred\n  - table plm.sega_character_property_inferred\n  - function plm.begin_sega_submission_capture\n  - function plm.finalize_sega_submission_capture\n  - function plm.finalize_sega_capture\n  - view api.source_capture_inventory\n  - function api.source_capture_inventory_exact\n  - policy sega_submission_capture_service_read on plm.sega_submission_capture\n  - policy sega_submission_capture_plm_read on plm.sega_submission_capture\n  - policy sega_submission_property_service_read on plm.sega_submission_property\n  - policy sega_submission_property_plm_read on plm.sega_submission_property\n  - policy sega_style_guide_property_inferred_service_read on plm.sega_style_guide_property_inferred\n  - policy sega_style_guide_property_inferred_plm_read on plm.sega_style_guide_property_inferred\n  - policy sega_character_property_inferred_service_read on plm.sega_character_property_inferred\n  - policy sega_character_property_inferred_plm_read on plm.sega_character_property_inferred\n  - index plm.idx_sega_submission_capture_status_captured\n  - index plm.idx_sega_style_guide_property_inferred_property\n  - index plm.idx_sega_style_guide_property_inferred_evidence_catalog\n  - index plm.idx_sega_character_property_inferred_property\n  - index plm.idx_sega_character_property_inferred_evidence\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T04:49:14Z","createdAt":"2026-08-25T01:02:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1451,"title":"Add Sega canonical submission vocabulary and inferred guide/character Property links","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:33:31Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1451"},

{"body":"# DesignFlow multi-schema adoption — governed bridge/cutover contract\n\nUma's requested application outcome is verified in `popcre/designflow-backend#71` at commit `af267ff9850028b94b02749970dca2586c8bfcbb`. Rebuild from that outcome; do not revive obsolete PR #1365.\n\n## Governing decisions\n\n- Preserve current DesignFlow integer identities and workflows during develop/staging adoption.\n- Do not create writable replicas, trigger mirroring, manual sync, or deletion-based reconciliation.\n- Keep `dflow` compatibility until every affected application workflow passes.\n- Production Cloud SQL remains unchanged during this adoption.\n- Unresolved or ambiguous canonical mappings remain unresolved; never force name-only matches.\n\n## Current bounded structural slice\n\nThis issue's first migration covers Factory and Artist identity only:\n\n- Factory uses existing `core.factory_source_ref` as the sole mapping authority and exposes a read-only compatibility view. It does not create a second mapping field.\n- Artist gains a nullable, reviewed UUID bridge to `core.artist`; the migration does not populate it.\n- Legacy rows, integer IDs, attributes, and write authority remain unchanged.\n\nUsers, roles, permissions, and comments require a separate coordinated successor because authentication, JWT identity, permissions, and comment ownership cannot be safely cut over piecemeal.\n\n## Verification gates\n\n- Preview-first migration and contract tests.\n- Exact row/ID conservation and no orphaned dependent FKs.\n- Exactly one writable authority per business record.\n- Factory/RFQ/vendor and Artist CRUD workflows remain on `dflow` until the application explicitly adopts the bridges.\n- No production Cloud SQL DDL or runtime switch.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 950\nwrites:\n  - table dflow.\"Factory\"\n  - table dflow.artists\n  - table dflow.\"Roles\"\n  - table dflow.comments\n  - table dflow.users\n  - view dflow.factory_canonical_identity\n  - table core.factory\n  - table core.artist\n  - table app.role\n  - table app.comment\n  - table app.profile\nreads:\n  - table core.factory_source_ref\n  - table dflow.vendor\n  - table dflow.\"RFQVendor\"\n  - table dflow.\"RolePermissions\"\n  - table dflow.\"UIElements\"\n  - table dflow.artist_types\n  - table dflow.art_types\n  - table app.users\n  - table app.\"RolePermissions\"\n  - table app.\"UIElements\"\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T13:31:47Z","createdAt":"2026-08-24T23:54:02Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1439,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] Uma's factory work (PR #1365) — get his intent, then rebuild it properly","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:33:46Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1439"},
{"body":"Opened by orchestrator marker #1419 on 2026-08-24, at Albert's explicit direction (\"yes, propose both\"). Two proposals, one cheap and one not. The evidence is a single day's measured cost.\n\n## Problem 1 — the merge race\n\nStructural work funnels through one `main` and one ordered migration-version sequence. Losing a race is not a retry; it is expensive and asymmetric.\n\n**Measured on PR #1406 (issue #1400), 2026-08-24. THREE governed version supersessions in one day:**\n\n| # | Version | Killed by |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `20260824002041` | `20260824135515` (PR #1421) merged while #1406 waited |\n| 2 | `20260824151714` | `20260824172136` (PR #1424) merged while #1406 waited |\n| 3 | `20260824181600` | survived — merged at 18:50Z |\n\nEach loss cost a supersession, a branch update, and a **full external re-review** (glm-5.3 sequences 287, 293, 296). Four merge attempts. Roughly six hours wall-clock for a change that was approved at the first attempt.\n\n**The asymmetry is the defect.** The competing merges were unattended agent sessions that merge in seconds. This session had to stop for a human permission click each time, and a change that pauses can never win against one that does not. It was mitigated mid-session by granting the orchestrator direct permission to dispatch `guarded-migration-merge.yml` — that removed the pause but not the race.\n\n**Proposal: adopt GitHub's native merge queue on `main`.** The queue serialises entry, auto-updates each PR against the tip, runs required checks against the *post-merge* state, and merges one at a time. Nobody loses a race because there is no race — and the backdating that forces supersession largely stops occurring, because the queue updates the branch immediately before merging rather than hours later.\n\nOpen questions for whoever implements it:\n- Interaction with `guarded-migration-merge.yml`, which asserts `git merge-base HEAD origin/main == origin/main` and mints its own required status. The queue must not bypass that guard; ideally the guard runs inside the queue's merge-candidate build.\n- Interaction with the object-claim and lease checks — those are correctness gates and must remain required.\n- Whether the reserved-version rule still needs to precede the file, or can become reserve-before-merge with the queue doing the ordering. See the human-contributor discussion on #1414.\n\n## Problem 2 — one shared preview database\n\nEvery migration rehearses against a single shared preview project, so one session's leftover blocks everyone.\n\n**Measured the same day.** PR #1424 applied `20260824150630` to preview, then superseded that version to `20260824172136`. The file went away; the applied ledger row did not. Preview then failed closed for **every** session with `Remote migration versions not found in local migrations directory`. Three runs died on it within four minutes — 32764765789, 32764907289 (that lane's own rehearsal), and 32765053613 (this lane's). The suggested remedy in the error text, `supabase migration repair --status reverted`, is forbidden by AGENTS.md §4 rule 1, so nobody could clear it except the owning lane, using evidence only that lane had. Preview stayed wedged roughly 20 minutes until the reconciliation workflow ran.\n\n**Proposal: give each PR its own throwaway preview database.** This is already written up and deferred as **#1391 (\"Pilot isolated Supabase per-PR branches\")**. Today is the argument for un-deferring it: an orphaned ledger row in an isolated database is one PR's problem and dies with the database. In the shared one it is everyone's outage.\n\nCosts to weigh honestly: per-PR databases are slower to provision, cost more, and the seeding/teardown story is real work (#1356 covers repeatable seed/teardown). They also do NOT remove the need for the shared rehearsal before production — they change what an early rehearsal is *for*.\n\n## Recommended order\n\n1. **Merge queue first.** Cheaper, self-contained, and it addresses the failure that actually cost the most today. Albert reports the same merge-race pattern across several repos, so the benefit is not limited to this one.\n2. **Then reopen #1391** with today's outage attached as evidence.\n\nNeither is urgent enough to interrupt live work, and neither should be done as a drive-by. Both need their own governed issue and review when picked up.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 700\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:25:04Z","createdAt":"2026-08-24T23:53:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1438,"title":"Adopt a GitHub merge queue and per-PR preview databases — today cost 3 version supersessions and wedged preview for every session","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:33:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1438"},
{"body":"Opened by orchestrator marker #1419 on 2026-08-24, at Albert's direction. This does not replace #1391 — it supplies the incident evidence for un-deferring it.\n\n## What happened today, 2026-08-24\n\nPR #1424 (issue #1422, Sample Tracking) applied migration `20260824150630` to the **shared preview** database. It then re-reserved that version as `20260824172136` (commit `f5d6a2d`), which deleted the file but left the applied row on the preview ledger.\n\nFrom that moment, **every** push to preview failed closed for **every** session:\n\n```\nRemote migration versions not found in local migrations directory.\nsupabase migration repair --status reverted 20260824150630\n```\n\nWedged within four minutes of each other:\n\n- Run 32764765789 (18:51Z) — production apply review, `20260824172136` — the orphan's own lane\n- Run 32764907289 (18:52Z) — preview apply, `20260824172136` — the orphan's own lane\n- Run 32765053613 (18:54Z) — preview rehearsal for PR #1406, orchestrator marker #1419 — **an unrelated lane**\n\nPR #1406 merged cleanly at 18:50Z after a full day of work and a passing external review, and then **could not be rehearsed at all** because of a different session's leftover. Its claim #1405 remains open and issue #1400 remains unclosed rather than recording a delivery that did not happen.\n\nThe suggested repair command is forbidden by AGENTS.md §4 rule 1 — it rewrites ledger rows representing applied work. The governed remedy (`preview-ledger-orphan-reconciliation.yml`) requires immutable evidence of the replacement's successful preview apply, which is owned by the orphan's lane. So the blocked lane **cannot** clear its own blocker: it must wait for another session to act. Blocking is transitive, and recovery is not self-service.\n\n## Why this is structural, not bad luck\n\nOne shared preview database means one shared failure domain. Every session's rehearsal correctness depends on every other session having cleaned up after itself. Version supersession — which is itself a *sanctioned, routine* operation, used three times today on PR #1406 alone — creates exactly this orphan class whenever it happens after a preview apply. So the failure mode is not an accident; it is a predictable consequence of two sanctioned mechanisms interacting.\n\n## Proposal\n\nUn-defer **#1391 (Pilot isolated Supabase per-PR branches)** and treat this incident as its justification.\n\nWith a throwaway database per PR:\n- An orphan is confined to that PR's own database and dies with it.\n- No session can wedge another session's rehearsal.\n- The orphan-reconciliation workflow becomes a rare recovery tool instead of a shared-fate dependency.\n- The \"rehearse with nothing merged in between\" constraint (AGENTS.md §4 rule 2) relaxes, because the rehearsal no longer competes for one database.\n\nPoints to settle in the pilot:\n1. Cost and provisioning time per PR, and whether it is acceptable at current PR volume.\n2. Whether a per-PR database faithfully reproduces the shared preview's state, or whether some class of defect only appears against a long-lived database that has accumulated real history.\n3. Teardown discipline — a per-PR database that is never deleted is a new leak.\n4. What still needs a shared long-lived preview afterwards (performance rehearsals, #1356's seed/teardown work).\n\nPoint 2 is the one that could invalidate the approach and should be tested first.\n\n## Related\n\n- **#1391** — the deferred pilot this asks to revive; the design work lives there.\n- Companion proposal: adopt a GitHub merge queue (sibling issue opened alongside this one) — that addresses the merge race; this addresses the shared-preview failure domain. They are independent and both were hit today.\n- **#1356** — repeatable preview seed/teardown, relevant to point 4.\n- **#1422 / #1424** — the lane that must reconcile today's orphan.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1200\ndepends_on: 1391\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:41:12Z","createdAt":"2026-08-24T19:06:52Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1436,"title":"Un-defer isolated per-PR preview databases (#1391): one session's ledger orphan wedged preview for every session today","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:33:49Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1436"},
{"body":"Opened by orchestrator marker #1419 on 2026-08-24, at Albert's direction, with today's costs as the evidence.\n\n## The problem, stated precisely\n\nMerges into `main` are first-come-first-served. Any PR that pauses — for a human permission click, for a review, for anything — loses to a session that does not pause. Losing is not free:\n\n1. The branch goes stale, so the guarded merge refuses it (`guarded-migration-merge.yml` asserts `git merge-base HEAD origin/main == origin/main`).\n2. Updating the branch moves the head SHA, which **voids the external review**, because review evidence is pinned to an exact head.\n3. If a competing merge took a later migration version, Guard B backdating fails, which forces a **governed version supersession** and a new reserved version.\n4. Then a fresh external review at the new head. Then repeat, if you lose again.\n\nThe asymmetry is the core defect: **attended sessions lose to unattended ones, structurally.** An agent merging without a human in the loop wins every race against one that stops for approval.\n\n## Measured cost, PR #1406 (issue #1400), 2026-08-24\n\nOne change — securing `api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree` — took the whole day:\n\n| Attempt | Head | Version | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `e1bc5792` | `20260824002041` | Pre-merge preview impossible (35 commits behind); branch update voided glm-5.3 seq 272 |\n| 2 | `27b2a44` | `20260824002041` | Guard B backdating: `20260824135515` landed meanwhile. **Supersession #1** |\n| 3 | `8f178a9` | `20260824151714` | glm-5.3 seq 287 APPROVE. Lost race to #1432 (17:14Z) and #1424 (17:29Z) |\n| 4 | `ca79c738` | `20260824151714` | glm-5.3 seq 293 APPROVE. Guard B failed again — #1424 took `20260824172136`. **Supersession #2** |\n| 5 | `bc96881` | `20260824181600` | glm-5.3 seq 296 APPROVE. **Merged** as `1c86ebc` at 18:50Z |\n\n**Three reserved migration versions permanently burned. Four external reviews paid for. Roughly nine hours of wall clock for a one-expression security change that was approved, unchanged, on the first review.** The function body never changed after the first approval — every re-review re-reviewed identical SQL.\n\n## Why the existing machinery does not solve this\n\nAGENTS.md §4 rule 1 says preview, merges and production promotion are one at a time. That is only enforceable if every session voluntarily serialises. Today two Claude sessions confirmed they were not merging here, and the merges came from an unattended Codex session. A rule that depends on unattended agents choosing to wait is not a lock.\n\n## Proposal\n\nAdopt a **GitHub merge queue** on `main`. Each PR enters a queue; GitHub updates it to the queue tip, runs required checks against that exact combination, and merges strictly one at a time. Nobody loses a race, because there is no race.\n\nPoints requiring design work before adoption — do not treat this as a drop-in:\n\n1. **Review-pin interaction.** Review evidence is pinned to an exact head SHA. If the queue updates the branch, does the pinned approval survive? Either the review must pin to the *content* of the claimed objects rather than the tree SHA, or the queue must be configured so migration PRs merge without a content-changing update.\n2. **Guard B and version reservation.** The queue removes the merge race but not version ordering. Consider whether the reserved version should be assigned *at queue entry* rather than at claim time, which would make backdating structurally impossible instead of a repeated failure.\n3. **The guarded merge workflow.** `guarded-migration-merge.yml` currently both validates and merges. In a queue world it should validate and let the queue merge, or the queue should be the only merger.\n4. **The post-merge rehearsal window.** AGENTS.md §4 rule 2 requires the preview rehearsal to run with nothing merged in between. A queue that merges several PRs back to back breaks that discriminator. Sequence rehearsals into the queue, or make the recovery lane tolerate intervening merges.\n\nPoint 4 is the hard one and must be solved before adoption, not after.\n\n## Related\n\n- Companion proposal: isolated per-PR preview databases (see the sibling issue opened alongside this one, and existing #1391).\n- The permission asymmetry was partially mitigated on 2026-08-24 by allowing this session to dispatch the guarded merge without a per-merge human click. That reduces the odds of losing; it does not remove the race.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1200\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:22:09Z","createdAt":"2026-08-24T19:06:22Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1435,"title":"Adopt a GitHub merge queue: the merge race cost three version supersessions and three external reviews in one day","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:33:51Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1435"},
{"body":"Opened by orchestrator marker #1419 on 2026-08-24, from a Low finding raised in glm-5.3 review sequence 293 on PR #1406 (issue #1400).\n\n## The finding\n\nPR #1406 secures `api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree` with a `SECURITY DEFINER` gate calling `app.require_licensing_manager_access`. That gate is correctly implemented and the review confirmed it: `search_path` pinned, no dynamic SQL, ACL unchanged, refusal proven behaviorally rather than textually.\n\n**But the three Universe B `core.*` tables it reads carry no row-level security and are already readable by `authenticated`.** So the gate protects the RPC route, not the underlying data. Anyone able to query the tables directly bypasses it entirely.\n\n## Scope and severity\n\n- **Pre-existing posture, not a regression.** PR #1406 did not introduce this and did not make it worse. It was outside that PR's object claim, which is why it was correctly not fixed there.\n- The immediate defect this issue must fix is smaller and unambiguous: **the migration header comment on `20260824151714` overstates what is protected.** Leaving a comment in the tree that claims more protection than exists is how a future session concludes the data is guarded when it is not.\n\n## Required outcome\n\n1. Correct the migration comment (or the function comment on current main, whichever carries the overstatement) so it states plainly that the gate protects the RPC and that the underlying tables are not RLS-protected.\n2. Separately assess whether RLS belongs on `core.\"licenseList\"`, `core.properties_and_characters`, and `core.property_character_associations`. That is a shared-contract decision affecting every app that reads them — do NOT enable RLS on curated Master Data tables as a drive-by fix. Measure which apps and roles read them first, then propose.\n3. If the assessment concludes RLS is warranted, open a bounded successor with the exact objects; do not widen this issue into the implementation.\n\nDo not weaken, drop, or bypass the existing RPC gate as part of any of the above.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 900\ndepends_on: 1400\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree\nreads:\n  - table core.\"licenseList\"\n  - table core.properties_and_characters\n  - table core.property_character_associations\n  - function app.require_licensing_manager_access\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-25T16:48:46Z","createdAt":"2026-08-24T17:41:18Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1434,"title":"Universe B core licensor/property tables have no RLS; the RPC gate protects the route, not the data","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:33:52Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1434"},

{"body":"# ColdLion licensor/property synchronization must honor merchandise-group active status\n\nAlbert confirmed that the merchandise-group records used for licensors and properties now expose an `active` flag through `/merchGroupDetails`. The current sync captures the raw payload but its typed mirrors and guarded promotion still implement the obsolete rule that ColdLion has no active/inactive flag.\n\nRequired outcome:\n\n1. Preserve the source active value as a typed, validated field for both ColdLion licensor and property mirrors.\n2. Make recurring synchronization apply the ColdLion value to canonical licensor/property lifecycle status for ColdLion-governed identities, without overriding a more authoritative signed entitlement schedule or unresolved/ambiguous identity.\n3. Define deterministic behavior for duplicate division rows and conflicting source flags; never force an ambiguous status.\n4. Add behavioral database contracts and runner tests proving active-to-inactive and inactive-to-active transitions, unchanged runs, invalid/missing values, ambiguity abstention, and preservation of higher-authority decisions.\n5. Correct the ColdLion question register and every current authoritative document that still says the flag is absent.\n\nOwner answer, 2026-08-24: merchandise groups—the fields holding licensors and properties—now have and expose active/inactive flags in the API. This closes open question 2.6; do not ask JamieLynn again.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1100\nwrites:\n  - table plm.erp_licensor\n  - table plm.erp_property\n  - table core.licensor\n  - table core.property\n  - function plm.sync_coldlion_licensors_properties\n  - function public.sync_coldlion_licensors_properties\n  - function plm.promote_coldlion_source_owned\n  - function public.promote_coldlion_source_owned\n  - function app.enforce_licensing_write_authority\nreads:\n  - table core.taxonomy_source_ref\n  - table core.taxonomy_owner_ruling\n  - table plm.licensing_write_authorization\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T00:33:23Z","createdAt":"2026-08-24T15:54:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1429,"title":"ColdLion licensor/property sync must honor merchandise-group active status","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:33:58Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1429"},

{"body":"PopDAM issues [#96](https://github.com/u2giants/popdam3/issues/96) and [#97](https://github.com/u2giants/popdam3/issues/97) require one coordinated structural delivery. This issue owns the database shape only; PopDAM owns application code and later application-data pilots/backfills.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1100\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - table public.style_group_tags\n  - table public.asset_tags\n  - index public.asset_tags_pending_metadata_normalization_idx\n  - table public.style_groups\n  - table public.dam_search_documents\n  - function public.replace_style_group_ai_profile\n  - function public.replace_asset_ai_tag_result\n  - function public.get_effective_asset_metadata\n  - function public.refresh_dam_search_asset_document\n  - function public.refresh_dam_search_style_group_document\n  - function public.refresh_dam_search_documents_batch\n  - function public.claim_dam_search_embedding_documents\n  - function public.upsert_dam_search_embedding\n  - function public.mark_dam_search_embedding_error\n  - function public.get_dam_search_embedding_status\n  - function public.reset_dam_search_embedding_errors\n  - trigger asset_tags_sync_assets_tags on public.asset_tags\n  - trigger asset_tags_dam_search_refresh on public.asset_tags\n  - trigger style_group_tags_dam_search_refresh on public.style_group_tags\n  - trigger asset_characters_dam_search_refresh on public.asset_characters\n```\n\n## Outcome\n\nStore shared product/artwork facts once on the Style Group and file-specific visual facts on the asset; preserve manual authority and durable AI rejection; expose effective metadata without copying group rows; and create one deterministic tag/character search corpus with lease-safe embedding primitives.\n\nRequired delivery order:\n\n1. Scoped tag/status/provenance objects and legacy reconciliation.\n2. One final deterministic search/maintenance definition containing active asset tags, active Style Group tags, and canonical character names.\n3. No embedding backfill in this issue. PopDAM runs exactly one later application-owned backfill after the final corpus is promoted and its separate approval gate passes.\n\n## Contract\n\n- Create `public.style_group_tags`: UUID PK, cascading Style Group FK, normalized tag, controlled category/source, `active|candidate|rejected` status, confidence `0..1`, model, evidence, creator/audit timestamps, and uniqueness/history rules that preserve manual authority.\n- Extend `public.asset_tags` with controlled category/status, confidence, model, evidence, rejection audit, and updated timestamp. Preserve existing creator and `(asset_id, tag)` compatibility.\n- Reconcile in this exact order before any next `assets.tags` rebuild: insert missing normalized `assets.tags` entries as active manual/other rows without overwriting existing provenance; then rewrite current AI rows to active `legacy_unscoped`. Do not infer scope/category from legacy text.\n- Make the `assets.tags` compatibility trigger aggregate active asset rows only. Rejected tombstones and Style Group tags never enter that array.\n- Add `style_groups.group_ai_description`, its source/model/tagged-at fields, and evidence asset IDs without altering authoritative `item_description`.\n- Add narrow service-role atomic replacement RPCs for group profiles and asset AI results. Preserve manual rows and rejected tombstones; replace only the calling AI source/model; validate scope/category/status/confidence/evidence; refresh search; and make retries idempotent.\n- Add an RLS-compatible effective-metadata read contract returning group and asset tags with scope/category/source/status/confidence/manual ownership plus effective identity. Grouped assets resolve licensor/property from the current Style Group; ungrouped assets may use asset columns. Never copy group identity to members.\n- Deterministically include active asset tags, active Style Group tags, and canonical character names in asset and Style Group search documents. Candidate/rejected tags stay out of ordinary search.\n- Maintain tag/character changes with bounded deduplicated old/new asset and Style Group refresh, using transition tables or a durable stale queue based on preview measurement. No row-level repeated full refresh and no unbounded group trigger transaction.\n- Replace destructive refresh and pseudo-claim behavior with bounded incremental refresh, real embedding leases, expiry/recovery, bounded categorized retries, lease-and-hash checked writes, status, and admin-only reset/requeue.\n- Preserve least privilege/RLS/grants. Do not expose the private `dam` schema. Do not remove or rewrite `propagate_group_tags_batch` in the first migration.\n- The production-timeout recovery may add only the reserved prerequisite partial index needed to make the already-merged bounded normalization complete within the unchanged timeout. It must not weaken the timeout, edit the merged migration, or reduce any delivered capability.\n\n## Verification required\n\n- `scripts/check-sql.sh` green.\n- Preview target proof immediately before every write.\n- Transaction-rolled-back fixtures for manual wins, idempotent legacy reconciliation, rejected/candidate exclusion from `assets.tags` and search, active group tag member matching, asset-only isolation, canonical character matching, group reassignment, bounded refresh, RLS/service-role access, deterministic hashes, unchanged embedding retention, changed embedding invalidation, lease exclusivity/expiry, stale-hash refusal, retry exhaustion, and grants.\n- Cross-link both PopDAM issues in PR and canonical migration note.\n- Merge and promotion through current orchestrator locks/gates only; record exact ledger and production object evidence.\n- Do not run the hybrid corpus embedding backfill against an intermediate definition.\n\n## Application baseline\n\nPopDAM Step 1 is complete at `ae029a53ade761d7d989fd6f188eb8631915019a`. Aggregate production evidence is committed under `verification/ai-tagging-scope/2026-08-24T1533Z/baseline.md`; it contains no licensed row content. The ordinary `/worksp/shared-db` checkout was stale, so this request deliberately leaves branch, worktree, version, preview, merge, and promotion to the active orchestrator.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T09:41:58Z","createdAt":"2026-08-24T15:35:07Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Request\r\n\r\nFinish the two missing structural contracts required by Sample Tracking Step 5. Release B issue #1307 added factory-visit plans and piece lineage, but real application integration proved that the movement contract cannot yet express two required physical operations without falsifying custody or quantity.\r\n\r\n### 1. Conserved parent-to-child piece split\r\n\r\nAdd one governed RPC, proposed as `dflow.post_sample_piece_split`, that atomically transfers a positive quantity from one existing parent sample at one proven custody location into one or more already-created child sample records linked through `dflow.sample_piece_lineage`.\r\n\r\nThe operation must:\r\n\r\n- reduce the parent balance at the exact source location;\r\n- create equal child balance at that same source location;\r\n- conserve total active quantity across parent plus children;\r\n- be idempotent and reject the same key with a different request;\r\n- never classify the parent as disposed, lost, delivered, returned, or complete merely because quantity moved into child identities;\r\n- refuse children whose workflow is not the same Flow 1 business identity or whose lineage root is wrong;\r\n- write only through a database-owned function, never direct application inserts into the immutable movement ledger.\r\n\r\nThe orchestrator owns the exact shape. A narrow lifecycle action and terminal pair such as `split_out` / `split_in` is acceptable only if all balance and global-status views explicitly treat them as an identity transfer rather than completed custody.\r\n\r\n### 2. Factory return when factory check-in was skipped\r\n\r\nRelease B deliberately allows `shipped -> returning` and direct return completion because factory check-in is optional. The current movement guard accepts only shipment origin -> transit and transit -> shipment destination. It rejects the honest transition from outbound transit to return transit, so the application would have to invent a factory receipt.\r\n\r\nExtend the canonical movement contract to allow one idempotent, conserved reroute from the outbound shipment identity to the return shipment identity for the same sample and matching Flow 1 visit. It must not create a false factory-receipt movement, must require both shipment lines to match the visit/sample/factory endpoints, and must leave one custody location after the operation.\r\n\r\n## Evidence\r\n\r\n- GLM 5.3 review: `popcre/designflow-tracking/.ai/reviews/glm-sample-tracking-full-restructure-20260824T145104Z.md`, findings F2 and F3.\r\n- `dflow.sample_movement_transit_location_identity_check` requires `in_transit.location_id = coalesce(box_id_fk, sample_shipment_id)`.\r\n- `dflow.validate_sample_movement_shipment_identity` currently rejects transit-to-transit reroutes.\r\n- `helpers/sampleFactoryVisit.requiresSplitBeforeShipping` correctly identifies the split, but the current RPC vocabulary cannot transfer custody between sample identities.\r\n\r\n## Required proof\r\n\r\n1. Split one quantity-3 Flow 1 sample into three quantity-1 siblings at Ningbo; total active quantity remains 3 and each child has exactly one custody location.\r\n2. Ship the three siblings to three factories concurrently; the lineage root remains common.\r\n3. Replay the split with the same key: no duplicate children or movements. Reuse the key with different children/quantity: reject.\r\n4. Start a Flow 1 return from outbound transit without a factory-receipt movement; custody moves once to return transit and later once to Ningbo.\r\n5. Wrong sample, wrong visit, wrong line, wrong factory, or already-consumed transit is rejected.\r\n6. Existing movement, balance, discrepancy, shipment, and global-status contracts remain green.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 525\r\ndepends_on: #1307\r\nobjects:\r\n  - function dflow.post_sample_piece_split\r\n  - function dflow.post_sample_movement\n  - function dflow.sample_movement_guard\r\n  - function dflow.validate_sample_movement_shipment_identity\r\n  - table dflow.sample_movement\r\n  - table dflow.sample_global_status\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-24T19:39:41Z","createdAt":"2026-08-24T14:54:01Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1422,"title":"Sample Tracking Step 5: conserved piece split and check-in-free factory return movement","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:34:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1422"},

{"body":"## Outcome needed\n\nRepair `plm.load_pmt_capture_chunk` so a valid Paramount metadata-value row whose optional `raw_value` is JSON `null` is stored as SQL NULL and continues to satisfy `pmt_amv_raw_value_shape_chk`.\n\n## Sanitized preview evidence\n\n- Target was proven as preview project `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs`; production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` was not contacted.\n- Required Paramount versions `20260814193351`, `20260814213043`, and `20260814223552` are applied.\n- Retired versions `20260814233342` and `20260814233423` are absent.\n- The private full capture passes its completeness validator and the public sync tool passes 70/70 focused tests.\n- A new preview capture reached `pmt_metadata_element`, then failed closed on the first `pmt_asset_metadata_value` chunk with `pmt_amv_raw_value_shape_chk`.\n- Failed capture ID: `58cfc82c-571e-4bc9-b9d5-327ea9379782`. It was marked `failed` and preserved for diagnosis.\n\n## Root cause\n\nThe private builder correctly represents an absent optional nested remainder as JSON `null`. The database loader currently selects `r->'raw_value'`. For a present JSON-null key, PostgreSQL returns JSONB `null`, not SQL NULL. The constraint allows SQL NULL or a safe JSON object, so JSONB `null` is rejected.\n\nThe durable repair should normalize JSONB `null` to SQL NULL at the loader boundary, for example with `nullif(r->'raw_value', 'null'::jsonb)`, while preserving the existing object-shape and forbidden-key constraint. Do not drop, weaken, disable, or bypass the constraint, and do not omit the normalized metadata target.\n\nAdd a focused positive test that loads a value row with JSON-null `raw_value` and a negative test proving an unsafe/non-object value is still rejected. Rehearse only on preview. After the migration is applied, return control to the `licensor-source-data` session to run a brand-new full capture and complete the business verification. Production is explicitly forbidden without separate owner authorization.\n\nNo licensed Paramount names, values, source rows, or allowlists are included here.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n- function plm.load_pmt_capture_chunk\nreads:\n- table plm.pmt_asset_metadata_value\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-24T14:30:08Z","createdAt":"2026-08-24T12:31:03Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1418,"title":"Repair Paramount JSON-null metadata load on preview","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:34:10Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1418"},

{"body":"# Handover: decide handling of licensed Paramount metadata in a private Codex transcript\n\nDuring the authorized Paramount preview verification, one overly broad local search emitted one raw private Paramount metadata record into Codex task transcript `01a02ea5-11b6-7ab2-a886-ff03271a754b`.\n\nFull context is in `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-24T1204Z-edge-dev-codex-orchestrator-closeout.md`.\n\n1. **Purpose:** obtain Albert's decision on whether the private task transcript needs deletion, restricted retention, or another containment action.\n2. **Actually done:** confirmed no credential, cookie, authorization header, token, or secret was emitted; nothing was posted to GitHub or a public repository.\n3. **Database writes:** none for this incident.\n4. **Half-finished:** transcript disposition has not been decided.\n5. **Ownership:** owner-only security/privacy decision; no code branch or PR.\n6. **Next:** Albert chooses the transcript handling; then an authorized session performs that exact action.\n7. **Blocker:** owner decision.\n8. **What did not work:** the local search scope was too broad and printed a licensed record before later filtering could protect it. {"body":"# Handover: repair Paramount preview loader JSON-null handling\n\nThe authorized Paramount preview rehearsal completed its three schema migrations, then a real private-source capture failed safely. The source data is valid; the loader writes an explicit JSON `null` for an absent `raw_value`, while the preview database accepts SQL NULL or a JSON object.\n\nFull orchestration context and evidence are in `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-24T1204Z-edge-dev-codex-orchestrator-closeout.md`.\n\n1. **Purpose:** repair the private Paramount loader and repeat the real preview capture.\n2. **Actually done:** preview migrations `20260814193351`, `20260814213043`, `20260814223552` applied in run `32721695779`; database contract verification passed.\n3. **Database writes:** preview only. Failed capture `379cbf7b-8e55-4e0d-b34a-89a7bd22a289` retained 33,862 asset rows and seven headings, zero metadata-value rows, and is marked failed. Production was untouched.\n4. **Half-finished:** no loader fix exists and the successful real capture has not been repeated.\n5. **Ownership:** private source/loader belongs to `u2giants/licensor-source-data`; no shared-db branch or PR owns the fix.\n6. **Next:** make absent `raw_value` omit the key (preferred) or otherwise bind SQL NULL, add regression coverage, then repeat the preview capture and verify it reaches complete.\n7. **Blocker:** loader implementation defect only; credentials and approved private source were available.\n8. **What did not work:** sending `raw_value: null` looked equivalent to absence but PostgreSQL receives JSON null, which violates `pmt_amv_raw_value_shape_chk`. Do not change licensed source rows to bypass the check.\n9. **Possibly stale:** capture counts and current preview state were checked on 2026-08-24; re-query before cleanup or retry.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: source-data\nroute: source-data-session\npriority: 1000\nreturn_to: u2giants/licensor-source-data\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-24T12:06:25Z","createdAt":"2026-08-24T12:05:37Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1412,"title":"HANDOVER: repair Paramount preview loader JSON-null handling","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:34:18Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1412"},

{"body":"Successor to #1358 and PR #1379 after independent review found that browser-side licensing-manager validation could be bypassed by direct authenticated reads of `core` tables.\n\nReplace the existing `api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree(text, boolean, text, integer)` body rather than adding a parallel endpoint. The function must enforce `app.require_licensing_manager_access()` internally before reading, remain `SECURITY DEFINER`, preserve its existing JSON response contract and grants, and read Universe B only:\n\n- licensors from `core.\"licenseList\"`;\n- properties from `core.properties_and_characters` where `type='PROPERTY'`;\n- parent relationship only through integer `licensor_id -> licenseList_id`;\n- character counts aggregated server-side from `core.property_character_associations`;\n- stable keyset order by normalized title and integer id;\n- complete orphan collection;\n- no name/code joins to the disjoint `core.licensor` catalogue.\n\nAdd SQL contract coverage with more than 1,000 associations proving exact aggregate counts, stable entity pagination, access refusal, and no duplicate/skip behavior. Preserve the current revoke-public/grant-authenticated posture.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1050\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - function api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree\nreads:\n  - table core.\"licenseList\"\n  - table core.properties_and_characters\n  - table core.property_character_associations\n  - function app.require_licensing_manager_access\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-24T23:52:50Z","createdAt":"2026-08-23T23:49:09Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This blocks issue #1315 because the real sequence `dflow.\"itemHeader_item_num_id_pk _seq\"` contains a space, while the SQL collision parser already preserves quoted identifier whitespace.\n\nRequired outcome: allow exact schema-qualified quoted identifiers in claim and issue-scope object lists, canonicalize them consistently with the SQL collision parser, preserve existing case-insensitive comparison behavior for ordinary unquoted identifiers, and add regression tests covering mixed-case quoted names and a quoted name containing a space. Do not weaken exact-object validation or accept unqualified/broad free-form names.\n\nThis is a prerequisite for safely claiming all 18 evidence-backed #1315 sequence objects.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 1200\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-23T23:36:58Z","createdAt":"2026-08-23T23:21:31Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Deferred from [#1366](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/1366) on 2026-08-23. Steps 7 and 8B of `plan_multi_agent_database_coordination_hardening.md`, retained verbatim there.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 10\ndepends_on:\n```\n\n## Why this was split out\n\nIt prevents no failure mode listed in §1 of that plan. Isolated per-PR database testing is a **product experiment**, not a coordination fix — and it was the only thing that could have held #1366 open indefinitely while waiting for a suitable real migration that may never appear.\n\nThe core coordination rollout (Steps 1-6, 8A, 9) is complete and live without it. Evidence: [`docs/verification/multi-agent-coordination-hardening-2026-08-23.md`](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/blob/main/docs/verification/multi-agent-coordination-hardening-2026-08-23.md).\n\n## What it would involve\n\n**Step 7 — pilot one opt-in Supabase pull-request branch.** Write a read-only readiness report first: is Supabase Branching available, is the GitHub integration installed, what check name does it emit, how are branch refs obtained, what is the billing impact, can historical migrations replay? Then a label, a repository variable defaulting to false, and a workflow that runs only for a migration PR carrying the label.\n\n**Step 8B — decide expansion** only after a real pilot produces committed evidence.\n\n## Hard constraints\n\n- **No purchase and no plan upgrade is authorized.** If Branching costs money or is unavailable, the correct outcome is a committed readiness report and a blocked pilot — not a spend.\n- Pick a genuinely additive, low-risk migration whose prerequisites are already on `main`. Do not use a destructive migration, a historical out-of-order one, a bulk load, or one that depends on production-only rows. **Do not invent a migration to test with.**\n- No licensed data and no secret values in any branch seed.\n- The shared preview remains the **final** integration rehearsal. This supplements it and never replaces it.\n- Blocked until a suitable real migration appears. Waiting is a legitimate state; say so rather than forcing it.\n\nRead plan Steps 7 and 8B for the full specification before starting.\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:22:07Z","createdAt":"2026-08-23T22:29:10Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"# Warner reconciliation relationship bridge onto surviving Universe B\n\nThe completed private Warner/STARLABS reconciliation needs a safe database contract for loading its relationship evidence. This is the bounded current successor to the Warner portion of #1090. It deliberately does not revive that tracker's stale Universe A architecture.\n\nOutcome:\n\n- retain direct Asset-to-Property evidence separately from inferred Style-Guide/Character evidence;\n- target the surviving `core.properties_and_characters` Universe B rows;\n- preserve inactive or out-of-contract evidence without presenting it as promotable;\n- reject unknown endpoints, invalid target kinds, and assertion-type mixing;\n- provide an idempotent guarded loader and a read-only candidate view;\n- use synthetic test fixtures only. Licensed rows and labels remain in the private source-data repository.\n\nThis issue governs structure only. After deployment, ordinary writes into the new `plm` evidence tables belong to the Warner scrape session. Any later promotion into curated core Master Data must be separately governed.\n\nAcceptance requirements:\n\n1. Every canonical target must be a `type='PROPERTY'` row in `core.properties_and_characters`.\n2. Direct and inferred evidence remain distinguishable and can coexist without one overwriting the other.\n3. Inactive/out-of-entitlement evidence remains retained but is excluded from promotable candidates.\n4. Inferred asset co-occurrence never creates or masquerades as a direct source relationship.\n5. Repeated loads are idempotent; unknown endpoints and invalid assertion labels are refused.\n6. Grants/RLS follow the existing Warner read gate and direct writes are refused in favor of the guarded function.\n7. No migration in this issue writes to or depends on retired `core.property`, `core.character`, or `core.property_character`.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - table plm.wb_asset_canonical_property_edge\n  - table plm.wb_style_guide_canonical_property_edge\n  - table plm.wb_character_canonical_property_edge\n  - function plm.sync_wb_canonical_relationship_edges\n  - view api.wb_canonical_relationship_candidates\n  - table api.wb_canonical_relationship_candidates\n  - policy wb_asset_canonical_property_edge_read on plm.wb_asset_canonical_property_edge\n  - policy wb_style_guide_canonical_property_edge_read on plm.wb_style_guide_canonical_property_edge\n  - policy wb_character_canonical_property_edge_read on plm.wb_character_canonical_property_edge\n```\n\nParent completion tracker: #1090.\nWarner requirement evidence: #1090 comment dated 2026-08-23.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-23T18:47:34Z","createdAt":"2026-08-23T17:56:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"This is the deliberately narrow, early portion of #1238. The completed blast-radius and salvage evidence on #1238 is authoritative and must not be redone.\r\n\r\nOutcome: remove the two empty Universe A character tables now, without touching `core.property` or `core.licensor` and without waiting for the larger property cutover.\r\n\r\nCurrent facts to re-check immediately before authoring and again before promotion:\r\n- `core.character` and `core.property_character` are empty.\r\n- No populated foreign-key referrer exists.\r\n- The two DB Data Admin RPCs name `core.character`; preserve their current non-character behavior while removing that dependency.\r\n- Remove only the now-obsolete foreign keys from the named empty/reference landing tables. Do not delete their rows or retire the tables themselves.\r\n- Correct contract tests and generated schema expectations in this repository. {"body":"Closeout of orchestrator marker **#1355** (session `claude-20260820-2345Z`, edge-dev), 2026-08-21T12:50Z.\n\n**Full briefing:** `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-21T1250Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`. Read §7 (\"what did NOT work\") before repeating anything.\n\n## Delivered to production and verified\n\nThe **FRIENDS TV erasure and the five migrations it held** are applied to production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` as one bounded event, exactly as owner ruling §6.5 requires:\n\n`20260802170000` → `20260817124545` → `20260817225127` → `20260818174350` → `20260819151527` → `20260820183334`\n\nProduction apply run **32483394133**, from merge commit `080cf00df958ef47ec93df30160ba0dd9dabf5d1`. Verified behaviourally, not from job status: both rows gone by id and by code, licensors 26 → 25, properties 256 → 255, ledger 475 → **481**. Nothing over-deleted.\n\nAlso closed: **#1188** (preview outage — preview proven healthy), **#1339**, **#1350**, and claim **#1345**.\n\n## Outstanding — each already has its own open issue\n\n| Item | Issue | Next action |\n|---|---|---|\n| Sample Tracking release B | **#1307** / PR **#1360** | review → merge → rehearse in the same breath → production. Lane #1357 live to 2026-08-22T01:54Z. |\n| Reviewer-assignment keying | **#1351** / PR **#1359** | merge it — the reason it was held is gone. Re-check merge cleanliness first: #1361 and #1362 have since landed in the same file. Also `u2giants/ai-devops` PR **#60**. |\n| Universe A deletion | **#1238** | three gates: #1358, find the `core.property` writer, retire remaining read sites. `core.character` and `core.property_character` can go first, independently. |\n| Rebuild the two Data Admin screens | **#1358** | app work in `apps/db-data-admin/`, in this repo. Gates #1238. |\n| grok reviewer hangs indefinitely | **ai-devops#61** | its wait timeout never fires; cost this repo a working day. |\n| Preview seed/teardown | **#1356** | so clearing fixtures never means rebuilding the branch. |\n| Waiting on Albert | **#1352, #1353, #1291, #1204, #778** | unchanged; not re-asked. |\n| Carried forward | **#1344, #1315, #1287** | unaddressed by me. |\n\n## ⛔ Do NOT dispatch #1090 as written\n\n`--queue-audit` lists it as dispatchable. It is not. Its object list is stale and names tables ruled for deletion; not one object on it exists in production. See its 2026-08-20 comment.\n\n## The three things most likely to bite the next session\n\n1. **`grok-4.6` hangs silently.** 11h32m, zero output, and `AI_GROK_WAIT_TIMEOUT` never fired — a second stuck run sat on the same machine for 17h. A 0-byte output file looks exactly like healthy work. **Prefer `glm-5.3` via `ai-glm`**, which registers its session at start and is monitorable.\n2. **Never pre-acquire an exclusive lane.** The merge and preview workflows acquire their own locks; taking one first makes the job refuse `refs/db-coordination/… is occupied`.\n3. **Claiming a table does NOT claim its triggers and indexes.** Every object must be named, and a claim renewal validates against the *work issue's* scope block — so an expanded claim cannot be renewed until that block is expanded to match.\n\n## One correction to the record\n\nEarlier documents said the five held migrations were already in production. **They were not.** Production held 475 ledger entries before this promotion and 481 after. **#1225 was closed on 2026-08-20 partly on that belief** — not reopened blind, because the two sets may not be the same five, but whoever revisits it must re-measure rather than trust either document.\n\nMarker #1355 closed. Three stale `HANDOFF.d/` files retired in the same PR as this closeout, all with CLOSED contract issues.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 200\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:25:21Z","createdAt":"2026-08-21T13:59:52Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"**Owner ruling, 2026-08-20 (Albert Hazan), recorded on #1238.** Asked whether deleting Universe A could take away the Licensor Tree and Property Table screens on `data.designflow.app`, his answer was: **rebuild them on the good list first, then delete.** He uses both screens and they must keep working.\n\n## What is wrong today\n\nThose two screens read `core.property` and its companions — that is, they *are* Universe A, the list that owner ruling `AGENTS.md` §6.15 orders deleted. §6.15 says there should be exactly two kinds of property list: the direct results of scrapes from the licensor websites, and the list that comes in from the ColdLion API. Universe A is neither, and it is the last thing holding these screens up.\n\n## What is needed\n\nRepoint both screens at **Universe B** — `core.properties_and_characters` (10,122 rows) and `core.property_character_associations` (9,622 rows) — which is the licensor-portal scrape list and survives. `core.licensor` also survives and is unchanged, so the licensor side of the tree does not move.\n\n**This is application work, and DB Data Admin lives IN THIS REPOSITORY at `apps/db-data-admin/` (AGENTS.md §0.2) — so it stays here. It is NOT a shared-db migration and it does not need a lane, a version or a claim.** No schema change is required: every table it needs already exists.\n\n## Facts the implementer needs, from the blast-radius analysis on #1238\n\n- **Universe B is the licensor-PORTAL scrape list, not the ColdLion list.** This surprised the analysis and it will surprise you. Zero of the 40 name-matched Universe A rows share a source id with Universe B.\n- **Nothing is being migrated into Universe B for you.** Of the 256 Universe A rows: 59 are redundant, 14 are recoverable with a real portal ID, 183 have no portal identity at all, and 0 are considered lost. The screens read Universe B's own rows; they do not read moved Universe A rows.\n- **Do not carry the grain mistake forward.** 35 Universe A rows name-match a Universe B character and 19 of those are character-only — rows stored at CHARACTER grain inside a table called `property`. The rebuilt Property Table must not reproduce that.\n- `public.assets` keeps denormalised `property_code`/`property_name` on about 96% of tagged rows, so the human-readable tag survives independently of `core.property`.\n\n## Definition of done\n\nBoth screens work at `data.designflow.app` against Universe B, verified visually against the requirement — served and screenshotted, not assumed. Then say so on #1238, because this is one of the three gates on the Universe A deletion.\n\n## Blocks\n\n**#1238** (Universe A deletion) cannot reach its DROP migration until this lands. The other two gates are: finding and stopping the DesignFlow writer that populates `core.property`, and retiring the remaining Universe A read sites (nine views, seven PostgREST-exposed; popdam3's fourteen read sites, one of them reached through a runtime variable that a text search misses).\n\nRelated: #1238, #640, #974.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 420\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-27T19:58:01Z","createdAt":"2026-08-21T01:03:32Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1358,"title":"Rebuild the DB Data Admin Licensor Tree and Property Table screens on Universe B, so Universe A can be deleted","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:34:46Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1358"},

{"body":"Carried forward from #1188, which is closed because the preview outage it describes is resolved.\n\n## The problem\n\nOn 2026-08-18 the only available way to clear ~100,500 performance-fixture rows (`AI-PERF-20260818-inventory-*` in `dflow.sample` and `dflow.sample_movement`, from #1181) was to rebuild the whole preview branch from scratch. That rebuild got stuck for hours, deleted the existing preview branch in the process, and took preview down for every session and every application until a new branch came up on a different project ref — which then required a code change of its own, because the old ref was hard-coded.\n\n**Rebuilding the branch is far too blunt an instrument for \"delete some test rows\", and it is currently the only one.**\n\n## What is needed\n\nAgree and document a repeatable way to seed and tear down fixture data on preview that does not touch the branch itself. Options worth evaluating:\n\n- a disposable branch-off-a-branch for each rehearsal, discarded afterwards\n- a fixture namespace convention plus a teardown script that deletes by that convention, with a hard refusal if it is ever pointed at production\n- a transaction-scoped or savepoint-scoped rehearsal where the data never commits\n\nWhichever is chosen, it must prove which database it is connected to before deleting anything (AGENTS.md §4.2) and must refuse to run against `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\n\n## Why it matters now\n\n#1181's structural fix for `dflow.sample_inventory` still needs working preview to re-verify, and the next performance rehearsal will face exactly the same choice.\n\nRelated: #1188 (closed), #1181, #901, #880.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 300\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:18:30Z","createdAt":"2026-08-21T00:00:28Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1356,"title":"Preview needs a repeatable seed/teardown for performance rehearsals, so clearing fixtures never means rebuilding the branch","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:34:49Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1356"},
