{"body":"# Handover: dev, staging and sandbox share the same Supabase project and schema\n\nVerified directly on 2026-08-20: DesignFlow dev, staging and sandbox use the same Supabase project, database and `dflow` schema. They are not separate Supabase branches. Today that mixes non-production data. Without #1352's isolated `dflow_prod` cutover, redirecting production to the same schema would let sandbox/dev writes reach live business data.\n\n1. **Purpose:** keep production isolated from non-production before any Cloud SQL cutover.\n2. **Actually done:** #1352 structural foundation is live: isolated `dflow_prod` and `dflow_archive` exist. Four app preparation PRs and infrastructure runbook work were green during marker #1370.\n3. **Database writes:** structure only from #1352; no business-row copy or service cutover occurred.\n4. **Half-finished:** real rows are not copied and production services/secrets are not redirected.\n5. **Ownership:** production data copy belongs to the application/cutover session; secret and Cloud Run changes belong to `popcre/infrastructure`.\n6. **Next:** complete timed rehearsal #771, present exact live resources/actions and rollback, obtain Albert's current-chat authorization, then run the coordinated Sunday cutover.\n7. **Blocker:** Albert must authorize the exact production data copy, secret rebinding and Cloud Run switch.\n8. **What did not work:** treating dev/staging/sandbox names as separate environments was false; they pointed to one project/schema. Do not build a second structural solution before using the already-live `dflow_prod` foundation.\n9. **Possibly stale:** secret versions, service revisions and writer activity must be re-proven immediately before cutover.\n\nOwner rulings already recorded: use `dflow_prod`; keep 24 months of AuditLog live and archive older history indefinitely; Sunday is preferred but is not blanket production authorization.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: security-settings\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 200\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:15:22Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T23:17:12Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1353,"title":"HANDOVER: DesignFlow dev/staging/sandbox share one non-production Supabase project — production is separate (Cloud SQL)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:34:52Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1353"},
{"body":"Opened by orchestrator marker #1338 at closeout, 2026-08-20T23:15Z. Evidence: the read-only reassessment recorded on #770, and `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T2315Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`.\n\n## Albert's proposal, 2026-08-20\n\n> \"so we just have to make an empty copy of the schema/structure (once we've nailed it down) and point production at that. Is that easy to do?\"\n\n**This is a better plan than the one of record, and it should replace it.**\n\n## Why it is better\n\nThe largest risk in #770 is that production Cloud SQL `designflow` and Supabase `dflow` have been issuing **overlapping primary keys** for months — the defect that re-issued live ids on 2026-07-29 and that #1315 is still auditing. The plan of record copies production data into the existing `dflow` schema, which already holds dev/staging/sandbox rows in the same id space, and then has to manage that collision.\n\n**An empty schema has nothing to collide with.** The risk is removed rather than managed.\n\nIt also solves #1353 for free: production gets the fresh schema, dev/staging/sandbox keep the existing one, and the two stop sharing a database without any extra work.\n\n## Measured 2026-08-20 — the schema is nearly free-standing\n\nRead against production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` (target proved via `get_project_url` first):\n\n- **Foreign keys INTO `dflow` from other schemas: 0**\n- **Foreign keys OUT of `dflow` into other schemas: 0**\n- **Views or functions outside `dflow` that reference it: exactly 1** — `public.style_tracker_rows_with_bridge`\n\nSo the cutover surface is one view, not a web of cross-schema dependencies.\n\n## What still has to be decided or done\n\n1. **Nail the structure down first** — Albert's own sequencing, and correct: the structure is the expensive thing to change after data lands.\n2. **Name the new schema.** It cannot be `dflow` (in use by non-production) and it must not be `designflow` — that name is already taken on Supabase by an empty 7-table orphan, which #778 exists to delete and which is currently blocked. **Two schemas with nearly the same name during a cutover is how the wrong one gets dropped.**\n3. **Decide the `AuditLog`.** ~400 MB of the 542 MB — three-quarters of the migration's weight. Copy, archive, or move separately. Documented trap: any delta cutoff must key on `id`, never `actionDate` (32,823 rows run backwards).\n4. **Flip the code guard.** `designflow-backend/config/database-connection-contract.js` hard-fails any production service whose `DB_PROVIDER` is not `cloud-sql` on port 5432 over private VPC. Cutover is a **code change**, not just a settings change — six repos plus every prod trigger's substitutions.\n5. **Size the connection budget.** Production Supabase: `max_connections` = 90, 34 already in use. Cloud SQL: 500. Four production services × up to 10 Cloud Run instances each.\n6. **Run the timed rehearsal (#771)** — never done. Until it runs, every downtime figure is invented. **#1315 should complete first** even under this plan: the sequences must start above Cloud SQL's live maxima or the same collision reappears the first time the app inserts.\n7. **Rollback plan.** Nothing writes production data into Supabase today; after cutover, going back means replaying everything written since.\n\n## Not yet known\n\n**Live row counts in Cloud SQL production were never read** — every row figure in circulation is a planner estimate. The 2026-08-10 capture deliberately read zero rows. Also unread: `designflow_dev` (708 MB, larger than production).\n\nAlso unverified since **2026-08-11**: the claim that the two schemas diverge by only three objects (one unique constraint, two indexes). Nine days of migrations have landed on Supabase since.\n\n## Related\n\n#770 (umbrella — see the 2026-08-20 reassessment comment), #771, #1315, #778, #1353, #696, #1327.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1150\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - {"body":"Opened by orchestrator marker #1338 at closeout, 2026-08-20T23:15Z. Evidence in `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T2315Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md` §7.2.\n\n**This blocks every migration in the repository, not just the one that hit it.** No migration can merge without an independent verdict, and today the round robin could neither produce one nor record its own failure.\n\n## Defect 1 — `ai-muse` cannot run in this repository at all\n\n```\nai-muse: error: refusing Muse reports: .ai/reviews contains tracked files.\n```\n\n`.ai/reviews` **always** contains tracked files here, by design: 25 review reports are deliberate named exceptions in `.gitignore` because they are cited BY PATH from a migration header and four permanent documents (#1304 — already resolved, do not \"fix\" it again; PR #1348 tried and was correctly failed by `tools/gitignore-tracked-contradiction.test.mjs`).\n\n**`ai-muse doctor` reports all five checks PASS.** This is not an environment fault — it is a repo-state assertion that is too broad. The wrapper should probe whether **its own new report path** is ignored, which `.gitignore` guarantees and which the third test in `tools/gitignore-tracked-contradiction.test.mjs` pins, rather than asserting the whole directory is untracked.\n\n**Effect:** one reviewer in three is unusable. It blocked PR #1347's assigned reviewer (sequence 243) today. **Fix belongs in `u2giants/ai-devops`.**\n\n## Defect 2 — the failure cannot be recorded, because the assignment was never durably written\n\nTrying to reassign after defect 1:\n\n1. `--failure-code local_dependency_unavailable` → refused, requires `--failing-check` naming an exact doctor check. **Naming one would be a lie** — doctor passes. (The refusal itself is correct behaviour, and is what #1287 is about.)\n2. `--failure-code wrapper_terminal_failure` → refused, needs `--confirm-no-verdict --confirm-no-artifact`. Supplied.\n3. With both confirmations → **`REFUSED: original durable reviewer assignment is missing`**, preceded by five `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)` lines.\n\n**The durable assignment record from `--assign-reviewer` is not actually being written.** The same 404 lines appeared during assignment for **both** #1335 (seq 242) and #1347 (seq 243), and were mistaken for harmless noise at the time. `--assign-reviewer` returns a clean JSON result and exits 0 while its readback 404s, so the failure is invisible until you try to use the record.\n\n**Effect:** the replacement path is unusable, and the round robin's durable history may be incomplete for every assignment made today. A reviewer must be assigned fresh each time.\n\n## What is needed\n\n1. Fix `ai-muse`'s probe in `ai-devops` so it works against a repository with named `.gitignore` exceptions.\n2. Find out why `--assign-reviewer`'s durable write 404s, and make it **fail loudly** rather than returning success — a record that silently is not written is worse than one that errors.\n3. Consider whether `--replace-failed-reviewer` should have a path for \"the wrapper refused for a repository-state reason\", which is neither a local dependency fault nor a provider fault. The three existing codes are `local_dependency_unavailable`, `provider_unavailable`, `wrapper_terminal_failure`.\n\n## Related\n\n#1287 (named failing check + the `local_dependency_unavailable` code), #1303 (owner asked whether to fix the wrappers before the next promotion batch — **still unanswered, and this is the concrete cost of leaving it**), #1304 (resolved, do not reopen), #1297, ai-devops#56, ai-devops#45.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 900\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:35:54Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T23:16:29Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1351,"title":"HANDOVER: the reviewer round robin is broken two ways — Muse cannot run here, and assignments are not durably recorded","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:34:55Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1351"},
{"body":"Opened by orchestrator marker #1338 at closeout, 2026-08-20T23:15Z. Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T2315Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md` — read §4 and §7 first.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nTake **PR #1347** (the FRIENDS TV / FRIDA KAHLO erasure, issue #1339) from \"written and green\" to \"applied in production and verified\". It is 90% done.\n\n## State at 2026-08-20T23:12Z — re-derive, do not reuse\n\n- PR **#1347**, head **`5d5bacf385792aaf02d22c9ce6ce847b705c31b9`**, MERGEABLE, **all 12 required checks pass**\n- Branch `feat/issue-1339-fr-removal`; worktree `C:\\repos\\shared-db-worktrees\\issue-1339-fr-removal` — **LIVE and clean, do not retire**\n- Claim **#1345**, version `20260820183334`, 8 objects\n- `origin/main` was `0cef120bec0d04e7ca7a8693c629ba9ea7209ce9`\n\n## The only blocker: no reviewer verdict, and the tooling refuses\n\nDo NOT try `--replace-failed-reviewer` first — it was tried and it fails (see #1351). **Assign a reviewer fresh**, and pick `ai-glm` or `ai-grok-review`: `ai-muse` cannot run in this repository at all right now.\n\n## Why this one deserves a hard review\n\n1. **It extends a security guard to DELETE.** A mistake changes what the guard permits for every future write, not just these two rows.\n2. **It edits four pre-existing contract tests** that its own change broke. Legitimate — and also exactly how a real regression gets normalised. Judge each edit on whether it still proves what it was written to prove.\n3. **Permanent consequence:** afterwards no `core.licensor` or `core.property` row is deletable by anything except the two named rows.\n\n## Then, in this order\n\n1. Reviewer verdict on the exact head. Require a coverage statement; never accept a bare verdict.\n2. Guarded merge via `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml`. Re-derive `origin/main` first.\n3. **Preview rehearsal IMMEDIATELY after the merge, in the same breath** — from merged main, `merged_preview_source_pr`. This is not fussiness: see #1321 and §7.4 of the handoff. A rehearsal delayed past another PR's merge becomes unrecoverable.\n4. Production promotion. Expect the refusals in #1344 if anything merges mid-flight.\n5. Verify behaviourally: both rows gone, dependants handled, and the `core.taxonomy_owner_ruling` record readable — after this migration that record is the ONLY surviving explanation of why either row vanished.\n\n## What it releases\n\nRegistering `20260820183334` in `FR_REMOVAL_VERSIONS` **unblocks five merged-but-unapplied migrations**: `20260802170000`, `20260817124545`, `20260817225127`, `20260818174350`, `20260819151527`. Promote the bundle as one bounded event in dependency order — **never `20260818174350` alone**, which would leave production at `FR = inactive`, a state the owner explicitly did not want, with no undo.\n\n## Owner input needed\n\n**None.** Both rulings are recorded on #1339. Do not re-ask, and do not ask Albert to sign off on technical risk.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 950\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - table core.licensor\n  - table core.property\n  - table core.taxonomy_owner_ruling\n  - table plm.licensing_write_authorization\n  - table plm.licensing_write_guard_audit\n  - function app.enforce_licensing_write_authority\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-21T12:48:08Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T23:16:06Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Found by orchestrator marker #1338 while promoting `20260820165926` (PR #1335) on 2026-08-20. **Three promotion attempts were refused, all correctly, all for the same underlying reason: an unrelated pull request merged while the promotion was in flight.** No database write occurred at any point — every refusal happened at a gate.\n\n## The gap in one sentence\n\nProduction promotion is described as a single exclusive lane, but **nothing actually stops an unrelated PR merging into `main` in the middle of one**, and every piece of promotion evidence is pinned to an exact `main` SHA — so an unrelated merge silently invalidates evidence that was valid when it was produced.\n\n## What happened, in order\n\n| Time | Event | Result |\n|---|---|---|\n| 18:10 | Guarded merge of #1335 -> `1247d125` | ok |\n| 18:14 | Preview rehearsal from merged main `1247d125`, run 32402123930 | SUCCESS |\n| 18:16 | Immutable review evidence recorded at `1247d125`, run 32402288523 | SUCCESS |\n| ~18:17 | **PR #1340 merged by another session** -> main `65dae349`, changing `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` | — |\n| 18:17 | Production apply | **REFUSED** — `review run has wrong head_sha: expected 65dae349…` |\n| 18:19 | Re-recorded review evidence at `65dae349`, run 32402471268 | SUCCESS |\n| 18:20 | Production apply | **REFUSED** — `preview run checked out at 1247d125… produced evidence with a different scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs than exact main` |\n| 18:21 | Re-run preview rehearsal at `65dae349` | **REFUSED** — `BLOCKED: already applied on production: 20260820165926` (preview's ledger — the #1321 strand) |\n| 18:23 | Historical recovery lane, run 32402833543 | SUCCESS — see #1321 |\n| 18:25 | Production apply, run 32402996954 | SUCCESS |\n\nTwo full evidence re-runs and one recovery-lane run, caused by one unrelated documentation-and-tooling merge. Had #1340 landed thirty seconds later, none of it would have happened.\n\n## Why each refusal was correct — do not weaken any of them\n\n1. **Review evidence pinned to exact main** (#1213 lineage). Without it, approval of one commit could be replayed against different code.\n2. **Producer-file pin on preview evidence.** Without it, someone who can dispatch the workflow could produce evidence from a branch whose copy performs no database write.\n\nThe gates are right. **The defect is that the promotion lane is not actually exclusive**, so correct gates fire against a target that moved for reasons unrelated to the promotion.\n\n## Why it will recur, and get worse\n\n- shared-db now runs up to three concurrent migration authors plus documentation and tooling sessions. Merges to `main` are frequent and mostly unrelated to whatever is being promoted.\n- The exposure window is the whole promotion: merge -> rehearse -> seal review evidence -> apply. Minutes at best, and much longer whenever an owner decision or a reviewer sits in the middle.\n- It composes badly with #1321: an unrelated merge during the window can strand a migration outright (already applied on preview, evidence no longer accepted). Today that was recovered; on 2026-08-20 the same class caused `20260819011639` to be superseded and re-reviewed at real cost.\n- The failure is *silent until the gate fires*. Nothing warns the promoting session that its evidence just went stale.\n\n## What a fix probably looks like\n\nNot prescribing the implementation. Options, roughly in order of preference:\n\n1. **Make the promotion lane genuinely exclusive.** A GitHub-backed promotion lock that the guarded merge lane checks and refuses against, the way the merge and preview locks already work. Unrelated merges queue for the duration of a promotion. Cheap to hold, and promotions are short when nothing blocks.\n2. **Make evidence tolerant of provably irrelevant merges** — accept a `main` that is a descendant of the evidence commit when no producer file and no migration file changed between the two. Narrower than option 1 and does not stall other work, but the \"irrelevant\" test must be exact and is itself security-sensitive.\n3. **At minimum, fail fast and loudly at the START of the promotion** rather than three steps in: re-derive `main` before each stage and refuse immediately with \"main moved from X to Y, re-seal\", so no one burns a rehearsal discovering it.\n\nOption 1 plus option 3 is probably the honest answer: hold the lane, and if it is lost anyway, say so at once.\n\n## Related\n\n- #1321 — the recovery-lane gap this composes with. See the comment recording that the recovery lane DOES work when the rehearsal ran at the authoring merge commit.\n- #1286 — \"require branches up to date\" is OFF on main, which is what allows unrelated merges to land without rebasing.\n- #1182 — version supersession leaving stale references, same family of moving-target problem.\n- #1213 — why the producer-file pin exists. Do not remove it.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:43:29Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T18:33:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1344,"title":"Production promotion is not actually an exclusive lane — an unrelated merge mid-promotion invalidates evidence three different ways","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:00Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1344"},
{"body":"Opened by orchestrator marker #1338 from a read-only ground-truth assessment of #1090 (2026-08-20T18:15Z). **This phase currently has no open issue owning it** — that is why it is invisible and why five merged migrations are stuck.\n\n## The problem in one paragraph\n\nAlbert ruled on 2026-08-03 that `FRIENDS TV` (`FR`) was never a real licensor and must be **removed**, not merely marked inactive. The production migration guard holds a bundle of FR-related migrations and refuses to release them until the removal migration travels with them — via the version set `FR_REMOVAL_VERSIONS` in `scripts/production_migration_guard.py`, **which is still empty**. Nobody ever authored the removal. Five finished, reviewed, merged migrations therefore cannot reach production.\n\nThe issue that carried this (#553, via #902) was closed COMPLETED on 2026-08-18 during triage of #1166, on the grounds that \"the underlying migration was superseded\". The superseded migration was `20260802171000`; the FR **removal** sequence in #553's body was not superseded and was never done. `FR` is still `status = 'active'` in production today.\n\n## Ground truth (production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, target proved before reading)\n\nEverything the FR bundle needs is merged; none of it is applied:\n\n| Version | File | Merged | Applied in production |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `20260802170000` | plm_import_preserve_curated_licensor_property_status | yes | no — held |\n| `20260802171000` | owner_ruling_friends_tv_frida_kahlo | yes | no — permanently retired, superseded by `20260818174350` (AGENTS.md 6.5) |\n| `20260817124545` | licensing_write_authority_guard | yes | no |\n| `20260817225127` | fr_owner_ruling_guard_compatibility | yes | no — held |\n| `20260818174350` | fr_owner_ruling_guarded_forward | yes | no — held |\n| `20260819151527` | fr_owner_ruling_transaction_bound_authorization | yes | no — blocked on #901 |\n| FR removal | — | **does not exist** | — |\n\n**Blast radius, measured live — six rows in total:** `core.property` 1, `assets` 2, `style_groups` 1, `plm.licensor_import` 1, `plm.property_import` 1. Every other one of the 24 FK referrers of `core.licensor` is 0.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nOne new forward migration that removes `FR` `FRIENDS TV` from `core.licensor` (id `2b2caddf-4fb0-4fc3-8245-ccd8f8177e48`), re-homing or retiring its dependants first, executing through a one-use transaction-bound authorization consumed via `app.enforce_licensing_write_authority`, recording the ruling in `core.taxonomy_owner_ruling`, and leaving immutable audit evidence — **and** registering its version in `FR_REMOVAL_VERSIONS` in `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` in the SAME commit, with the hold-set file-existence test extended to cover it.\n\n## Blocked on one owner answer\n\n**Does `FRIENDS TV` disappear entirely, or remain as a retired record?** #553 says \"remove `FR` entirely (not merely mark it inactive)\" but the exact SQL shape was never authored, and the owner's 2026-08-03 wording is no more specific. Asked 2026-08-20. Do not author until answered — the two shapes are not interchangeable and the migration is forward-only.\n\nSecond, smaller: the one FR-parented `core.property` row. #553 says \"re-home anything currently under FR\", but that predates owner ruling AGENTS.md 6.15 (2026-08-19) by 16 days, and that row is a Universe A row on #1238's deletion path. **Recommendation: leave it to #1238 rather than re-home it**, and do NOT claim `core.property` here — claiming it collides with #1238 and #1177.\n\n## Traps for the authoring session\n\n1. **The guard triggers are `before insert or update` only.** A `DELETE` of the `FR` row is NOT covered by the existing guard. The migration must either add DELETE coverage or use an update-to-removed path — decide deliberately and state which in the header.\n2. **`FR_REMOVAL_VERSIONS` unblocks by DATA, not policy.** Never edit the guard's co-presence check to release the held migrations.\n3. **Never promote `20260818174350` alone.** It leaves production at `FR = inactive` — a state the owner explicitly did not want, with no undo. The only legal event is ONE bounded apply carrying `20260802170000`, `20260817225127`, `20260818174350`, the removal members and (ordering permitting) `20260819151527`, in dependency order.\n4. **`ci_authorize_licensing_contract_test()` pre-issues 100 blanket authorizations (#1262)**, so a new guard contract test will pass while proving nothing. Clear those rows and assert an empty baseline first. PR #1256 deliberately did not fix the helper.\n5. **Version strings in the guard, its test and AGENTS.md 6.5 are safety controls, not a file index (#1182).** If the lane tool re-reserves this version, all three change in the same commit.\n6. **The supersession readback race (#1164): every attempt permanently burns a version reservation.** `20260818142815` and `20260818142855` are already spent. Never retry in a loop.\n7. Preview is `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs`. `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` is DELETED — the plan doc and older AGENTS.md sections still name the dead one.\n\n## Exact object claim when this is dispatched\n\n```\nobjects:\n  - function app.enforce_licensing_write_authority\n  - table core.licensor\n  - table core.taxonomy_owner_ruling\n  - table plm.licensing_write_authorization\n  - table plm.licensing_write_guard_audit\n  - trigger licensor_licensing_write_guard on core.licensor\n  - table core.property\n  - trigger property_licensing_write_guard on core.property\n```\n\nSame lock #1143/#1164 used. Deliberately excludes `core.property`, `dam.*` and the rest of #1090's declared list.\n\n## Related\n\n#1090 (tracker), #1164, #1143, #1140, #1258, #1259, #1262, #1182, #901, #1238, #553 (wrongly closed), #902.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 900\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - function app.enforce_licensing_write_authority\n  - table core.licensor\n  - table core.taxonomy_owner_ruling\n  - table plm.licensing_write_authorization\n  - table plm.licensing_write_guard_audit\n  - trigger licensor_licensing_write_guard on core.licensor\n  - table core.property\n  - trigger property_licensing_write_guard on core.property\n```\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-21T12:48:11Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T18:12:54Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Started: 2026-08-20T20:15Z\nMachine: edge-dev\nSession: claude-20260820-2015Z\nPredecessor marker: #1333 (closed on takeover; that session stopped mid-workstream, Albert authorised takeover in chat)\n\n## Adopted work\n\nPR #1335 / claim #1334 — restore `dflow.art_piece` ids 1024/1025 to the Batman artwork (owner answer B on #1326).\nAdopted unchanged: lane claim held, reserved version `20260820165926`, branch `fix/restore-art-piece-1024-1025`, head `25a4f7de`.\nFull context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T1750Z-edge-dev-claude-pr-1335-restore-batman-ids.md`.\n\nRemaining on that workstream: one reviewer verdict -> guarded merge -> preview rehearsal -> production promotion -> behavioural verification -> close out.\n\n## Startup audit (2026-08-20T20:15Z)\n\n- `origin/main` = `85c71a2` (re-derived before every dispatch/rehearsal/promotion; never reused from a document)\n- Lanes 1/3 occupied (#1334), 0 expired claims\n- Open PRs: #1335 (this work), #1212 (docs)\n- #1171 confirmed DELIVERED to production (`20260820142402`); #1199 is stale and closed on that evidence\n\n## Standing constraints carried forward\n\n- Preview `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs`; production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`. {"body":"Started: 2026-08-20T15:50:00Z\nMachine: C--repos-shared-db (edge-dev)\nSession: claude-20260820-155000Z\nPredecessor marker: #1308 (closed cleanly earlier today; no marker was open at start)\n\nPurpose: sole orchestrator, opened to execute ONE owner decision.\n\n## Scope — deliberately narrow\n\n**Albert answered #1326 with option B on 2026-08-20:** renumber the two test records that\noccupy `dflow.art_piece` ids 1024 and 1025, and let the real Batman artwork take those ids\nback.\n\nThat is the entire scope of this session. It exists because the previous marker was already\nclosed when the answer arrived, and executing a migration requires an open marker.\n\n## What the answer actually requires, measured before designing\n\n| Fact | Value |\n|---|---|\n| `dflow.art_piece` ids 1024/1025 | the two test records |\n| `designflow.art_piece` ids 1024/1025 | the real Batman artwork |\n| `dflow.art_piece_attachment` rows pointing at 1024/1025 | **0** — renumbering breaks nothing there |\n| `plm.art_piece_attachment` rows pointing at 1024/1025 | 4, and that table has **no FK** to art_piece |\n| Batman `art_number`s already present in dflow | **0** — no unique collision |\n| ids 10001/10002 in use | **0** |\n\n**The finding that shapes the migration:** `art_number` is not free text. Across **all 1,114\nrows, with zero nulls and zero exceptions**, it ends with `-<5-digit zero-padded id>`\n(`PDCBM-01023` for id 1023). Renumbering a row without updating its `art_number` would break\nan invariant that currently holds universally. So option B is a **two-part** change:\n\n1. move the test records to fresh ids **and** correct their `art_number` suffix;\n2. insert the Batman rows at 1024/1025 — their `art_number`s (`PDCBM-01024`, `PDCBM-01025`)\n   already satisfy the invariant.\n\nNew ids will be allocated with `nextval` rather than hard-coded, so the sequence itself hands\nthem out and no future insert can collide with them.\n\n## Standing constraints carried forward\n\n- Preview `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs`; production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`. Prove the target\n  immediately before every write.\n- Re-derive `origin/main` immediately before every dispatch, rehearsal and promotion input.\n- Never pre-hold the preview or production coordination refs.\n- A `do $$` block disqualifies a pure-data `catalog-verification: no-op` declaration, and the\n  token is read from prose as well as code (#1317).\n- Never accept a bare verdict; require a coverage statement; read the raw provider stream\n  before recording any reviewer failure.\n- Clone from GitHub, never a local path, to isolate a review (#1296).\n- Never rename a backdated migration by hand — use `--supersede-active-claim-version`.\n- The historical-recovery lane cannot recover a post-merge rehearsal (#1321). Promote promptly\n  after merging so the evidence stays usable.\n- `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` stays retired and unwritten.\n\nStartup audit (2026-08-20T15:50Z): `origin/main` = `9fb240c`; lanes 0/3, no expired claims;\n`--queue-audit` fullyAudited true; 7 handoff files, zero stale.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T17:58:54Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T16:59:16Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACu_OSRw","name":"orchestrator-marker","description":"Marks the one active orchestrator session (see shared-db-orchestrator step 0)","color":"0E8A16"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1333,"title":"ORCHESTRATOR MARKER: session claude-20260820-155000Z (edge-dev)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:06Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1333"},
{"body":"## The numbers\n\nMeasured against `origin/main` on 2026-08-20:\n\n| File | Size | Its own stated limit |\n|---|---|---|\n| `AGENTS.md` | **234,259 bytes (229 KB)** | soft 60 KB, **hard 80 KB** |\n| `HANDOFF.md` | 440,183 bytes (430 KB) | ~1 KB static pointer |\n\n`AGENTS.md` is loaded in full at the start of every session. At 229 KB that is roughly **57,000 tokens, about 29% of a 200k context window**, spent before any work begins — on every session, in every repo that reads it.\n\nThe rule it breaks is written in the session-docs skill and was learned from `designflow-frontend/AGENTS.md`, which reached 151 KB by 2026-08 because 87 sessions each appended a quirk and nothing ever moved out. It was split on 2026-08-18. This file is **55% larger than that one was**.\n\n## Why nobody has noticed\n\nThe rule says to check `wc -c AGENTS.md` before appending. Sessions append without checking, and each individual addition looks small and justified. This session added one line to it and only measured because the closing checklist demanded the number.\n\n## What this is NOT\n\n**Do not delete history to make room.** The rule is explicit: move it, never delete it. Sections that grow one entry per session belong in `docs/` from the start — `docs/idiosyncrasies.md`, `docs/incident-log.md`, `docs/pending-work.md` — each with a one-line index entry left behind in the router.\n\n## Why this session did not just do it\n\nThree reasons, all worth respecting:\n\n1. A 229 KB refactor of the file every other session reads is not a safe end-of-session action. Other sessions were actively working this checkout today.\n2. Splitting requires repointing `§N` cross-references from other docs. Those references are load-bearing — several skills and workflows cite `AGENTS.md §5.2`, `§6.4`, `§6.15`, `§6.16`, `§2.1-H` by number. A split that breaks them is worse than the size.\n3. It needs a plan, not an afternoon.\n\n## Suggested approach\n\n1. Measure first: which sections are largest, and which grow per-session rather than being stable routing.\n2. Move the per-session growers out, leaving a pointer plus a one-line title index.\n3. Repoint every `§N` cross-reference in docs, skills and workflow comments — grep for them before and verify after.\n4. Target the 60 KB soft ceiling, not 79 KB.\n\n## Related\n\n`HANDOFF.md` at 430 KB with no `handoff-pointer: v1` marker is a **separate, already-tracked problem** — see #1083. Do not fold the two together; the handoff migration has its own rules.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-20T18:06:45Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T16:47:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1331,"title":"AGENTS.md is 234 KB — nearly 3x its own hard ceiling, and every session pays for it","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:07Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1331"},
{"body":"Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T1530Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`. Orchestrator marker #1308.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nMove the **2,276 rows** in `plm.art_piece_attachment` to wherever PLM wants them to live, then drop that table.\n\n**This is now ordinary data work with no blockers.** Every prerequisite landed on 2026-08-20.\n\n## What was blocking it, and is not any more\n\n`plm.art_piece_attachment` holds real image links — full-size and thumbnail pairs in the DigitalOcean bucket, Feb–Jul 2026. **266 of them pointed at art pieces that existed only in the leftover `designflow` schema**, so they could not be rehomed.\n\n`20260820145950` (#1314) backfilled those 133 art pieces into `dflow.art_piece`. Verified from production immediately afterwards:\n\n```\nplm.art_piece_attachment STILL STRANDED     0     (was 266)\nplm.art_piece_attachment now resolving   2276\ndflow.art_piece total                    1114     (was 981)\n```\n\n**All 2,276 rows now resolve to a parent in `dflow`**, the schema the live application actually reads.\n\n## Why this is NOT shared-db's job\n\nUnder the owner ruling in `AGENTS.md` §0.0-B, rows an application creates, edits or moves in the normal course of its work belong to the session working on that application. **No shared-db issue, no dispatch, no migration.** This issue exists only so the item is not lost, and so #778 has something to point at.\n\n**Two carve-outs that would change that**, worth checking before you run it:\n\n1. If any part becomes a **bulk or ad-hoc load of outside-sourced content into curated Master Data** — `core.licensor`, `core.property`, `core.character`, `core.customer`, `core.factory` or their `*_ext` tables — that part is the §6.4 carve-out and routes to `curated-master-data-governance`.\n2. **Dropping the table is structural** and comes back to shared-db as a migration. Moving the rows is yours; removing the table is not.\n\n## The state of the data, measured 2026-08-20\n\n| Fact | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Rows in `plm.art_piece_attachment` | **2,276**, all with a non-null `art_piece_id` |\n| Distinct parents referenced | **1,114** |\n| Rows failing a `dflow.art_piece` lookup | **0** |\n| Rows in `dflow.art_piece_attachment` (the live table) | 2,006, parents 1..1023 |\n\nNote the live `dflow.art_piece_attachment` **already exists** and holds 2,006 rows with parents up to id 1023. So this is a merge into an existing table, not a fresh landing — decide how duplicates are treated before you start.\n\n## One wrinkle you must know about: ids 1024 and 1025\n\n**Four of the 2,276 rows point at ids 1024 and 1025, and those two ids mean different things in the two schemas:**\n\n| id | `dflow.art_piece` (live) | `designflow.art_piece` (orphan) |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1024 | `Testing Art Piece` | `Batman and Catwoman in a dynamic…` |\n| 1025 | `Testing again for autocomplete` | `Batman running in a dynamic pose…` |\n\nThe live app issued those two ids on 2026-07-29 because the sequence was never advanced after the schemas split. `20260820133058` fixed the sequence so it cannot recur, but **deliberately did not renumber the two rows that already collided** — renumbering live rows from inside a schema migration is exactly the invisible change this repository exists to prevent.\n\n**So those four attachment rows currently resolve to test records rather than the Batman artwork.** Moving them as-is would carry that wrongness across. That decision is #1326.\n\n## Verification when done\n\n- `select count(*) from plm.\"art_piece_attachment\"` → 0, or the table is gone.\n- Every moved row resolves to a parent in whatever table it now lives in.\n- The four rows pointing at 1024/1025 were handled according to the #1326 decision, not silently.\n- Then #778 can proceed to its next step.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: application-data\nroute: application-session\nreturn_to: popcre/designflow-item-master\npriority: 640\ndepends_on: #1326\nobjects:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T22:54:06Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T15:27:11Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1327,"title":"HANDOVER: move the 2,276 plm.art_piece_attachment rows into dflow, then drop the table","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:09Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1327"},
{"body":"Orchestrator marker #1308. Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T1530Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`.\n\n## Albert — one decision, and it is genuinely yours\n\n**Two art records in the live app are wrong, and I deliberately did not fix them automatically. What should happen to them?**\n\n| id | What the live app shows now | What it should almost certainly be |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1024 | `Testing Art Piece` | `Batman and Catwoman in a dynamic…` |\n| 1025 | `Testing again for autocomplete` | `Batman running in a dynamic pose…` |\n\n- **Option A — leave them.** They are two test records. The real Batman artwork still exists in the old copy and in live DesignFlow production, so nothing is lost. Four image links stay pointed at test records.\n- **Option B — renumber the two test records** onto fresh ids (10001, 10002) and let the Batman artwork take back 1024 and 1025.\n- **Option C — delete the two test records** and let the Batman artwork take the ids.\n\n**My recommendation: B.** It keeps everything, puts the artwork back where its image links already point, and moves the two throwaway test records out of the way. But this touches live application data, so it is your call and the app team's, not mine.\n\n**One word answers it: A, B, or C.**\n\n## How this happened, in plain terms\n\nThe live app and an old leftover copy of the same data were split apart, and **the counter that hands out new ID numbers was never moved forward**. So on 29 July the app created two test records and gave them numbers that already belonged to two real Batman artworks in the old copy. Four image links now point at the test records instead of the art.\n\n**It cannot happen again.** `20260820133058` advanced that counter past every number in use anywhere, and it is applied to production.\n\n## Why I did not just fix it\n\nRenumbering live records from inside a database migration is silent and invisible. Nothing in the app would announce it, and anyone looking later would have no way to tell what changed or why. The repository has a standing rule against exactly that, and it exists because invisible changes are how the next incident starts.\n\n**Advancing the counter stopped the bleeding. Healing what already bled is a deliberate decision, which is why it is in front of you rather than done quietly.**\n\n## What is blocked on this\n\n**Not much, and nothing urgent.** #1326 — moving 2,276 image links out of `plm.art_piece_attachment` — should know the answer first, because four of those rows are the affected ones and moving them as-is would carry the wrongness across. Everything else is unaffected.\n\n## Evidence, measured read-only against production 2026-08-20\n\n```\ndflow.art_piece      id 1024 = \"Testing Art Piece\",              created 2026-07-29\n                     id 1025 = \"Testing again for autocomplete\", created 2026-07-29\ndesignflow.art_piece id 1024 = \"Batman and Catwoman in a dynamic…\"\n                     id 1025 = \"Batman running in a dynamic pose…\"\n\nplm.art_piece_attachment rows pointing at 1024/1025: 4\ndflow.art_piece_id_seq: 10000  (next id 10001 — collision cannot recur)\n```\n\nThose were the only two ids the app issued after the split, so the damage is exactly two records and four links. It is not a growing problem.\n\n## Not to be re-asked\n\nThe counter fix itself is done and needs nothing from you (#1312, applied to production). The 133-record backfill is done and needed nothing further after your approval (#1314).\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 620\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T18:27:46Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T15:27:10Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1326,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] two art records show test data where Batman artwork should be — leave, renumber, or delete?","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:10Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1326"},
{"body":"## The ruling\n\n**Albert Hazan, 2026-08-20:** admit all **66** unmatched ColdLion property codes, including the **51** still marked active in ColdLion. Paired with a requirement that is **not optional**:\n\n> `data.designflow.app` must gain a control to mark a property **inactive on our side.**\n\n## Why the pairing matters\n\nColdLion has **no licence expiry flag and never will**. That is the single reason admitting these 66 rows was resisted for months: a blanket admission resurrects lapsed licences, including `EX` (THE EXORCIST) and `LB` (THE LOST BOYS).\n\nThe ruling answers that by **owning the flag ourselves** rather than refusing the rows. Admitting the 66 without shipping the control would recreate exactly the problem everyone was avoiding, so the two must land together or the admission waits.\n\n## No schema change is required\n\nVerified read-only against production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` on 2026-08-20:\n\n```\ncore.property.status  ->  USER-DEFINED, enum entity_status\nentity_status values  ->  active, inactive, archived, deleted, potential\ncore.property         ->  256 rows, all currently 'active'\n```\n\nThe column already accepts `inactive`. **This is app work, not structural database work — do not route it to the shared-db orchestrator or write a migration for it.**\n\n## What to build\n\n1. A control in the DB Data Admin app (`apps/db-data-admin`) to set a Property's `status` between `active` and `inactive`.\n2. Whatever permission guard decides who may flip it. Note the standing rule that Master Data open writes are intentional — see AGENTS.md §0.4 — so do not invent a restriction that contradicts it without asking.\n3. Make inactive properties visibly distinct, and decide with evidence whether they should be filtered out of pickers by default. State the choice rather than leaving it implicit.\n4. The 66-row admission itself is data work on rows the app owns; it does not need a migration. Confirm which side runs it.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `docs/coldlion-unmatched-properties-by-licensor-20260731.md` — the 66 codes and their licensors\n- `docs/coldlion-open-questions.md` §4 and §5 — the ruling as recorded\n- Do **not** re-ask Laura about these codes; she already answered\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 300\ndepends_on: 1952\nwrites:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-08T19:06:43Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T14:32:49Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1322,"title":"data.designflow.app: let a user mark a Property inactive on our side (owner ruling 2026-08-20)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:12Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1322"},
{"body":"Hit on 2026-08-20 while promoting `20260819011639` (#1171), which was blocking a live money leak. Orchestrator marker #1308.\n\n## The gap, in one sentence\n\n**The historical-recovery lane cannot recover a rehearsal produced by the workflow this repository mandates.**\n\n## The refusal\n\n```\nProduction business-risk gate rejected evidence: original apply run 32250275467\ndispatched at b8390fe7ff4eb0cc441c2f490cfb9777bebb6f2b produced evidence with a\ndifferent .github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml than the merge commit\n51e7764f34394a3bf903f5aa5d05ebc147c03be1 of the pull request that authored\n20260819011639\n```\n\nNo database write occurred — it failed at the gate, before the apply job.\n\n## Why the two rules collide\n\n`AGENTS.md` pins the original run's producer files to **the authoring pull request's MERGE COMMIT**, and explains why: pinning to today's main would refuse every genuine recovery, because an older commit necessarily carries older producer files.\n\nThat reasoning holds for a **pre-merge** rehearsal, which is what the lane was built for — the #1194/#1208 trap, where a migration was rehearsed before its PR merged and stranded.\n\nBut the repository now mandates the opposite order:\n\n> **ALWAYS merge first, then rehearse on preview from merged main, then promote.**\n\nA post-merge rehearsal runs from a main tip that is **later** than the authoring merge commit — often much later, because other pull requests merge in between. Here, ten producer files changed between `51e7764` (the authoring merge) and `b8390fe` (the main tip the rehearsal ran from), including `production_business_risk_gate.py`, `preview_instance_binding.py` and their tests, some of which **did not exist at the merge commit at all**.\n\n`AGENTS.md` already anticipates the \"file absent on one side\" case and says it is **refused**, because a file present on one side only is *\"a real difference in the machinery that ran\"*. That is correct as written — and it means the newer, mandated workflow reliably produces evidence the recovery lane must reject.\n\n**So the safer rehearsal order produces the less recoverable evidence.** Any migration rehearsed post-merge, whose promotion is then delayed past a producer-file change, lands in this state.\n\n## Why this is not rare, and will recur\n\n- **Producer files change often.** They changed ten times between one merge and one rehearsal in the same 24 hours.\n- **The gap only has to open once.** Once a promotion is delayed past a producer change — a blocked prerequisite, a busy reviewer, an owner decision, a weekend — the migration is stuck, permanently, in the lane built to unstick exactly this.\n- Two of the three migrations promoted on 2026-08-20 needed the recovery lane at all. This is the normal path now, not an exception.\n\n## What was done in the meantime, and what was NOT done\n\n**The refusal was accepted. No guard was weakened, and no `if:` condition or artifact name was edited.**\n\n`20260819011639` was superseded by `20260820142402` (PR #1320) — **byte-identical executable SQL**, proven by diff with and without blank lines, taking the ordinary path: fresh preview rehearsal from current main, independent review, guarded merge, promotion. That unblocks the money leak today without touching the gate.\n\n**That is a workaround with a real cost and should not become the pattern:** it burns a migration version, re-issues 1,328 lines, and requires a fresh review round for content that had already passed six.\n\n## What a fix probably looks like\n\nNot prescribing the implementation, but the shape of the question:\n\n1. **Accept a rehearsal commit that exact main contains**, not only one matching the authoring merge commit — the security property that matters is that the run's checkout and dispatch ref both carry *genuine repository code*, and a commit main contains satisfies that at least as well as a PR commit does.\n2. If (1) is too loose, **compare producer files against the rehearsal's own commit rather than the merge commit**, and require that commit to be an ancestor of exact main.\n3. Whatever is chosen, `AGENTS.md` must say plainly **which rehearsal orders are recoverable and which are not**, because today it mandates one order and its recovery lane only supports the other.\n\n**Do not \"fix\" this by removing the producer-file pin.** #1213 established why it exists: without it, someone who can dispatch the workflow could push a branch whose copy performs no database write, hand-write a ledger delta and content manifest, name that run as the original apply, and promote bytes preview never executed.\n\n## Related\n\n- **#1171 / PR #1176 / PR #1320** — the migration this blocked, and the supersede.\n- **#1288** — the first migration through the recovery lane; it succeeded because its rehearsal predated only a workflow change, not a producer-file divergence of this shape.\n- **#1200** — the pre-merge rehearsal trap the lane was originally built for.\n- **#1213** — the round of hardening that introduced the two-commit producer pin.\n- **#1317** — a second undocumented-mechanism gap found the same day (`-- catalog-verification: no-op`).\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 880\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T11:30:04Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T14:26:28Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1321,"title":"The historical-recovery lane cannot recover a POST-MERGE rehearsal — i.e. evidence produced by the order AGENTS.md mandates","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:13Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1321"},

{"body":"Found the hard way on 2026-08-20: migration `20260820133058` reached production correctly and its run still went **red**, because of a mechanism that exists in the guard and **nowhere in the documentation**. Orchestrator marker #1308.\n\n## What happens\n\nThe **Post-apply catalog verification** step fails, *after* the migration has already committed, with:\n\n> *the allowlisted migrations named no catalog object this lexer can read. That may be legal (a pure-data migration), but it means **THIS STEP PROVED NOTHING**, so enforcing mode fails rather than letting a green tick stand in for evidence it never gathered. A genuine no-op declares itself in the migration with a `-- catalog-verification: no-op <reason>` line.*\n\n**The guard is right and must not be weakened.** A migration that asserts nothing should not show a green tick. The problem is purely that nobody is told the declaration exists until they have already shipped without it.\n\n## Why this is worse than an ordinary missing-doc\n\n**A migration is immutable once applied** under the forward-only rule. So the moment you hit this, you cannot fix the file — the declaration can never be added to that migration, and its run stays permanently red in the history. The only remedies are a superseding migration (absurd for a comment) or, as here, a written explanation attached to the issue.\n\n**The failure also lands at the worst possible moment**: after a successful production apply. The operator sees a red production run and must work out, under pressure, whether production is broken. In this case it was not — the SQL and its ledger row commit in one transaction per file, that transaction succeeded, and production was verified correct by reading its own ledger and sequence state directly. But that is several minutes of investigation the declaration would have avoided entirely.\n\n## Evidence that nobody knows about it\n\n```\n$ grep -rn \"catalog-verification: no-op\" supabase/migrations/*.sql\n(no matches)\n\n$ grep -rn \"catalog-verification\" AGENTS.md\n1357:  ...one passing mention, in an unrelated sentence about phases\n```\n\n**No migration in the repository has ever used the declaration**, and `AGENTS.md` — the authoritative rulebook, and the thing an author actually reads — never explains it. `20260820133058` is the first pure-state migration to reach the gate, so this has simply never fired before.\n\n## What to add, and where\n\nIn `AGENTS.md`, in the section that tells authors what a migration must contain, state plainly:\n\n1. **The catalog verifier derives its targets by lexing the migration text.** It reads `create table/view/function/index`, `grant`, `revoke` and `alter default privileges`. It does **not** see objects named only through `execute format(...)`, quoted or mixed-case identifiers, or search_path-relative names.\n2. **If your migration names no readable catalog object, the step fails in enforcing mode** — deliberately, because it proved nothing.\n3. **Declare it:** add a `-- catalog-verification: no-op <reason>` line to the migration.\n4. **The cases that need it**, so authors recognise themselves: pure data migrations, sequence-state changes (`setval`), and anything whose entire body lives inside `do $$ ... $$` blocks.\n5. **Add it BEFORE the migration merges.** After it applies, the file is immutable and the red run is permanent.\n\nWorth stating the reasoning too, not just the rule — the guard's behaviour is a good example of the repository's own standard that an absent check must never be displayed as a passing one.\n\n## Cheap hardening worth considering separately\n\n`scripts/check-sql.sh` could **warn at authoring time** when a migration's lexed target list is empty and no `-- catalog-verification: no-op` line is present. That moves the discovery from \"red production run, file now immutable\" to \"local check before the PR\", which is where it belongs. Not required to close this issue, and it should be a warning rather than a hard failure until the pattern is understood.\n\n## Related\n\n- **#1312 / PR #1313** — the migration that hit this. Production is correct; see the closing comment there for the verified state.\n- **#1315** — the sibling-sequence audit, which will produce more pure-sequence migrations and would hit this identically.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 600\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:30:26Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T14:16:27Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1317,"title":"AGENTS.md never mentions '-- catalog-verification: no-op', so a pure-state migration goes RED after a correct production apply","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:18Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1317"},
{"body":"Raised by glm-5.3 (reviewer sequence 236) while reviewing PR #1313, as finding 3. Orchestrator marker #1308.\n\nIts words: *\"the class deserves a follow-up issue rather than silence.\"*\n\n## The class of exposure\n\n`dflow.art_piece_id_seq` was found sitting at **1025** while a leftover `designflow.art_piece` had already issued ids up to **1163**, and live Cloud SQL DesignFlow production up to **1465**. The two Supabase schemas were split from a common ancestor and **the sequence was never advanced**, so the live app re-issued ids that already meant something else. It happened twice on 2026-07-29 and would have recurred on every new art piece. PR #1313 fixes that one sequence.\n\n**Every other `dflow.*_id_seq` reconciled from the same `20260710135950_reconcile_dflow_baseline.sql` carries the identical theoretical exposure**, because they were all split the same way at the same time. `dflow.art_piece_attachment_id_seq` (baseline line 1641) is the one the reviewer named explicitly.\n\n## Why this is NOT urgent, stated honestly\n\nThe reviewer found **no observed damage path** for the siblings, and neither did I:\n\n- `art_piece` was damaging because **other data joins on its id** — `plm.art_piece_attachment.art_piece_id` and `dflow.art_piece_attachment.art_piece_id` both carry `art_piece` ids as references. A re-issued `art_piece.id` therefore silently re-points real image links at unrelated records.\n- `dflow.art_piece_attachment` rows are joined **by `art_piece_id`, not by their own id**. A duplicated attachment id has nowhere to leak to.\n\nSo the question for each sibling is narrow: **is this table's own id used as a reference anywhere else — another table, an application, an export, a URL?** Where the answer is no, a duplicated id is untidy but inert. Where it is yes, it is the `art_piece` bug again.\n\n## What this issue is asking for\n\n1. **Enumerate every sequence in `dflow` reconciled from the 2026-07-10 baseline**, with its current `last_value` and its table's `max(id)`.\n2. **For each, compare against every other copy of that table's id space** — the leftover `designflow` schema on Supabase, and live Cloud SQL `designflow` (read-only credentials exist; `albert_read_only` on `creatiflow-database`, 1Password item `tcaf3o3u2cx52g6ivvczxbhola`). **Cloud SQL is the one that matters most and is the one most likely to be skipped**, because it is a different database and easy to forget. It is also the largest id space: `art_piece` there was at 1465 versus the orphan's 1163.\n3. **Establish, per table, whether its own id is referenced anywhere** — foreign keys, application code, exports, URLs.\n4. **Advance only those sequences that can actually cause a collision**, in one migration, using the same shape as `20260820133058`: forward only, `greatest(floor, max(id))`, `to_regclass`-guarded, and a `to_regclass`-guarded assert against the orphan ceiling.\n\n**Do not blanket-bump every sequence without step 3.** A sequence jump is cheap but not free: it is a permanent, visible discontinuity in a live table's id space, and doing it without a reason makes the next person wonder what incident they missed.\n\n## Precedent to copy\n\n`supabase/migrations/20260820133058_dflow_art_piece_seq_clear_all_id_spaces.sql` (PR #1313) is the worked example, including the two corrections that mattered:\n\n- **A row count is not a maximum id.** The original report proposed advancing to 1114, which is the row count of `designflow.art_piece`; its max id is 1163. That would have left ids 1115-1163 still colliding and looked fixed.\n- **Clear every id space, not just the nearest one.** Stopping above the orphan would still have collided with Cloud SQL, whose data #770 plans to move into this database — re-creating the same bug, larger, on the day #770 lands.\n\n`10000` was chosen for `art_piece` to clear all three with years of headroom and to give a diagnostic boundary: below it means pre-split, at or above means issued afterwards. **Pick each sibling's floor on its own evidence rather than reusing 10000 by habit** — a floor below a table's real ceiling is worse than no change, because it looks like a fix.\n\n## Related\n\n- **PR #1313** — the `art_piece` fix and the worked precedent.\n- **#1314** — owner decision on the 133 missing art pieces (waiting on Albert).\n- **#778** — the leftover `designflow` schema; still blocked, now on rehoming 270 image links rather than on the question it originally asked.\n- **#770 / #771** — the Cloud SQL move that makes the third id space live rather than theoretical.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1100\ndepends_on: #1313\nobjects:\n  - sequence dflow.\"AuditLog_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"Factory_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"MerchGroup_mg_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"ProdOrderHeader_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"RFQContainer_RFQContainer_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"RFQGroup_RFQGroup_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"RFQItem_rfqItem_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"RFQVendor_RFQVendor_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"StandardizedGroup_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"StandardizedSize_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.customers_customers_id_seq\n  - sequence dflow.\"externalCustomer_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"externalVendor_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"licensingStatus_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.\"user_notification_id_seq\"\n  - sequence dflow.users_id_seq\n  - sequence dflow.vendor_vendor_id_seq\n  - sequence dflow.\"itemHeader_item_num_id_pk _seq\"\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-24T00:20:49Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T13:45:48Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1315,"title":"Audit every other dflow.*_id_seq for the same never-advanced split exposure that broke art_piece","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:19Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1315"},
{"body":"Orchestrator marker #1308. Raised from the `plm.art_piece_attachment` investigation on #778.\n\n## Albert — one decision\n\n**133 art pieces exist in the leftover `designflow` copy but not in the live `dflow` one. Should they be brought into the live app, or written off?**\n\n- **Bring them in** — the 270 orphaned image links then reconnect to real artwork, and nothing from Feb–Jul 2026 is lost.\n- **Write them off** — simpler, and the artwork still exists in DesignFlow production on Cloud SQL. The 270 links are then discarded with the leftover copy.\n\n**My recommendation: hold this decision until #770 is scheduled.** Reasoning below — it may make itself moot.\n\n## Why you are being asked\n\nA separate session found that `plm.art_piece_attachment` holds **2,276 real image links** (full-size plus thumbnail pairs in the DigitalOcean bucket, Feb–Jul 2026). The data is genuine. **270 of those rows point at art pieces the live app does not have.** They cannot be moved until it is decided whether those parent records should exist.\n\nAll figures below were re-measured read-only against production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` on 2026-08-20 and every one matched the original report.\n\n## What is already being fixed, and needs nothing from you\n\nThe same investigation exposed a **live bug**: the live app has been handing out ID numbers that were already used by the leftover copy. It has already happened twice — on 2026-07-29 the app created two test records that took the numbers of two real Batman artworks, so those artworks' image links now point at test records.\n\n**That is a structural fault and it is mine.** PR #1313 advances the counter past every number in use anywhere, which stops it recurring. **It does not require this decision** and is not waiting on you.\n\nOne thing worth knowing: it does **not** renumber the two records that already collided. Silently renumbering live records from a database migration is exactly the sort of invisible change that causes the next incident. If you want those two repaired, that is a separate, deliberate piece of work.\n\n## Why I recommend waiting\n\nThe live DesignFlow production database on Google Cloud SQL — the real one, not either Supabase copy — **already holds 1,408 art pieces**, more than either. It is very likely that all 133 exist there too.\n\n**#770 is the plan to move that entire database into Supabase.** If it goes ahead, the 133 arrive as part of it and a separate backfill is wasted work. If #770 is shelved or delayed a long time, the backfill becomes worth doing on its own.\n\nSo the useful question is not really \"backfill or write off\" — it is **\"is #770 happening, and roughly when?\"** That is genuinely your call and nobody else's.\n\nNote #770 is currently gated behind **#771**, which cannot run as written: it targets a preview project that was deleted on 2026-08-18. That is being corrected separately.\n\n## What is blocked on this, and what is not\n\n| Item | Waiting on you? |\n|---|---|\n| PR #1313, the counter fix | **No.** Proceeding. |\n| Moving the 270 image links | **Yes** — they need parent records, or a decision that they have none. |\n| Dropping `plm.art_piece_attachment` | **Yes** — it follows the move. |\n| #778, deleting the leftover `designflow` schema | **Yes** — and it was already blocked; see below. |\n\n## This also settles a question left open on #778\n\n#778 asked whether `plm.art_piece_attachment` was a live feature or dead weight. **The answer is neither, and it is the more useful third option:** the data is real, but the copy is an orphan — no view, function, or application code reads it. The only application that uses that table, `designflow-item-master`, is pointed at the `dflow` schema at deploy time through its `SCHEMA` environment variable.\n\nSo the leftover `designflow` schema still **cannot be dropped**, but the reason has moved on: it is no longer \"something live depends on it\", it is \"270 real image links have not been rehomed yet\". That is a sequencing problem with a clear end, not a blocker without a plan.\n\n**Recorded, unchanged: the verified pre-deletion backup of the whole orphan schema is in 1Password (`vibe_coding`, item `zepc66j5xajdg4novzttmmrtg4`), retrieved and confirmed byte-identical. Production has no point-in-time recovery, so that logical dump remains the only surgical recovery path.**\n\n## Evidence\n\n| Fact | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Art pieces in `designflow` but not `dflow` | **133** |\n| `plm.art_piece_attachment` rows total | **2,276**, all with a non-null parent |\n| ...that fail the live `dflow` foreign key | **266** |\n| ...pointing at the two collided ids | **4** (266 + 4 = the 270) |\n| Colliding ids | **1024, 1025**, both created 2026-07-29 |\n| `dflow.art_piece` | 981 rows, max id 1025 |\n| `designflow.art_piece` | 1114 rows, **max id 1163** |\n| Cloud SQL `designflow.art_piece` (live) | 1408 rows, **max id 1465**, still growing |\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: application-data\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 760\ndepends_on: #1313\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T15:17:27Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T13:33:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1314,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] backfill the 133 art pieces now — recommendation CHANGED after Muse challenged it and the data proved identical","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:21Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1314"},
