{"body":"Started: 2026-08-20T11:30:00Z\nMachine: C--repos-shared-db (edge-dev)\nSession: claude-20260820-113000Z\nPredecessor marker: #1293 (closed cleanly; no marker was open at start)\n\nPurpose: sole orchestrator.\n\nOwner instruction this session: *\"look into #770, #771, and #778 - i want to get the tables set up to accept the Cloud Sql migration.\"* Plus: check whether the reviewer wrappers were fixed (#1303), and whether #1302 needs anything.\n\n## Findings that shape the plan\n\n- **#778 is the actual prerequisite for #770.** The orphan `designflow` schema on production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` occupies the exact schema name the Cloud SQL migration needs. It was never created by any migration in this repo (verified by grep), so nothing manages it. **Albert approved backup-then-delete on 2026-08-19** and the approval is recorded on the issue. No branch, no PR, nothing in flight.\n- **#771 is unexecutable as written.** It names preview `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` as its rehearsal target. That project was deleted 2026-08-18 and rebuilt as `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs`. Its 2026-08-11 baseline measurements are also 9 days stale by its own terms.\n- **AGENTS.md contradicts itself on the preview ref.** Section 4.2's \"compare against these characters\" block still names the DEAD `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` as preview, while lines 862 and 982 correctly say it was deleted. A session following 4.2 literally would reject the real preview as wrong.\n- **#1302 (mgCategory) needs nothing** — ready, route proven by #1288, no collision with the designflow work.\n- **Reviewer wrappers (#1303): 3 of 5 defects now fixed** by another session, verified against current code, not commit messages. Grok's artifact suppression, Muse's silent return, and ai-devops#45 are fixed. **#1298 (GLM liveness) and #1297 (stranded replacement) are NOT.**\n\n## Priority order\n\n1. **AGENTS.md preview-ref contradiction** — cheap, and it is actively misleading guidance in the authoritative rulebook.\n2. **#771** — re-point at the live preview so the rehearsal becomes runnable at all.\n3. **#778** — orphan schema: fresh inventory, verified private backup outside this public repo, then delete, then prove. Owner-approved.\n4. **#1302** — mgCategory promotion through the historical-recovery lane.\n\n## Standing constraints carried forward\n\n- Preview is `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs`. Production is `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`. Prove the target immediately before every write.\n- Re-derive `origin/main` immediately before every dispatch, rehearsal and promotion input.\n- Never pre-hold `refs/db-coordination/preview` or `/production` — the workflow acquires them itself.\n- For any \"what does the database currently do\" question, read the CURRENT object definition across ALL migrations plus the production ledger.\n- A verify block inside a migration is production code.\n- Never accept a bare verdict as review evidence; require a coverage statement.\n- Never ask Albert to sign off on technical risk. Genuine business judgements still go to him.\n- `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` stays retired and unwritten.\n- **Every destructive action must be recoverable before it is taken.** #778 deletes a production schema; the verified private backup comes first, and its restore path must be proven, not assumed.\n\nStartup audit (2026-08-20T11:30Z): `origin/main` = `76aba9e`; lanes 0/3, no expired claims; `--queue-audit` fullyAudited true; 7 handoff files, zero stale.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T15:39:25Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T11:42:56Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACu_OSRw","name":"orchestrator-marker","description":"Marks the one active orchestrator session (see shared-db-orchestrator step 0)","color":"0E8A16"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1308,"title":"ORCHESTRATOR MARKER: session claude-20260820-113000Z (edge-dev)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:24Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1308"},
{"body":"## Request\n\nImplement **Sample Tracking release B: Flow 1 factory visits** in `dflow`. Structure only,\nadditive only. This is the second of the release slices planned in\n`popcre/designflow-frontend/plan_sample_tracking_full_restructure.md` (step 5). Release A\n(#975, merged `46b01e3c`, production-applied) is the sole dependency and is already in place.\n\n## Scope boundary\n\n**In scope — Flow 1 (`workflow_type = 'nyo_purchased_factory_reference'`) only:**\n\n- an ordered, append-only-audited plan of factory visits per physical sample\n- provenance of each visit: requested by NYO versus added later by Ningbo\n- visit state through ship / optional factory check-in / return / Ningbo receipt\n- the lineage record that links separately tracked physical pieces back to one parent\n  sample when identical pieces diverge to different factories\n- a read view the API and UI can query for current / completed / remaining visits\n\n**Explicitly OUT of scope, do not mix in:** Flow 3 photo or QC approvals (step 8), Flow 4\nremote-inventory requests (step 9), spreadsheet import (step 11), legacy retirement (step 12).\nThose get their own issues.\n\n**No new route legs are needed.** Release A already added `ningbo_to_factory` and\n`factory_return_to_ningbo` to the `sample_shipment_line.route_leg` allow-list and they are\nalready in the tracking vocabulary. Please confirm rather than re-add.\n\n## Application coordination\n\n- Consumer repos: `popcre/designflow-tracking` (API commands) and `popcre/designflow-frontend` (step 6 UI)\n- App branch `sandbox-albert`; PR base `develop`; Uma (`devopswithkube`) merges app PRs\n- Canonical plan: `popcre/designflow-frontend/plan_sample_tracking_full_restructure.md` step 5\n- Business specification: `popcre/designflow-frontend/docs/sample-tracking-restructure-spec.md` §5 Flow 1\n- Release B must land in preview before the tracking API commands can be integration-proven,\n  and in production before any consumer deploy.\n\n## Why this cannot be modelled with what release A already has\n\n1. **`dflow.sample_workflow.sample_id_fk` is UNIQUE.** One sample has at most one business\n   identity, and `POST /sample/guided-create` returns 409 rather than give a sample a second\n   one. So when identical pieces are split to travel to different factories, each child piece\n   must be its own `dflow.sample` row with its own `sample_workflow` row. **The shared parent\n   relationship therefore has nowhere to live today** — it must be carried by a new lineage\n   record, not by reusing one workflow across pieces.\n2. **`dflow.sample_movement` is custody truth and must stay that way.** It records where a\n   quantity physically is. It cannot express *intent* — \"NYO asked for factories A, B and C in\n   that order, and Ningbo later added D\". A plan is not custody, and custody is not a plan.\n3. **`dflow.sample_shipment` is one leg.** It cannot say which planned visit a leg belongs to,\n   nor that a visit is still open because the factory has not returned the piece.\n\n## Proposed objects\n\nNames and shapes below are a proposal from the consuming application; the orchestrator owns the\nfinal DDL, the version (claim it through `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --claim`; do not\npick one from a directory listing), the branch, preview proof, tests, generated types, PR and\nmerge. Everything is additive; nothing in release A changes.\n\n### 1. `dflow.sample_piece_lineage` — the shared-parent relationship\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE dflow.sample_piece_lineage (\n  sample_piece_lineage_id bigint GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,\n  sample_id_fk          integer NOT NULL UNIQUE\n                          REFERENCES dflow.sample(sample_id_pk) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n  parent_sample_id_fk   integer NOT NULL\n                          REFERENCES dflow.sample(sample_id_pk) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n  root_sample_id_fk     integer NOT NULL\n                          REFERENCES dflow.sample(sample_id_pk) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n  piece_quantity        integer NOT NULL CHECK (piece_quantity > 0),\n  split_reason          text    NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(split_reason) <> ''),\n  split_by_user         text    NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(split_by_user) <> ''),\n  split_by_role         text    NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(split_by_role) <> ''),\n  idempotency_key       text    NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(idempotency_key) <> ''),\n  request_hash          text    NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(request_hash) <> ''),\n  created_at            timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\n  CHECK (sample_id_fk <> parent_sample_id_fk),\n  CHECK (sample_id_fk <> root_sample_id_fk),\n  UNIQUE (split_by_user, idempotency_key)\n);\nCREATE INDEX sample_piece_lineage_root_idx ON dflow.sample_piece_lineage (root_sample_id_fk, sample_id_fk);\n```\n\n- One row per **child** piece. The original sample has no row; it is its own root.\n- `root_sample_id_fk` is denormalised deliberately so \"show me every piece of this sample\" is\n  one indexed read, not a recursive walk. A trigger must enforce that the root of a child equals\n  the root of its parent (or the parent itself when the parent has no lineage row), so the\n  denormalisation cannot drift.\n- Splitting does **not** move quantity. Quantity conservation stays entirely in\n  `dflow.sample_movement`; the split command in the API posts the movements.\n\n### 2. `dflow.sample_factory_visit` — the plan\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE dflow.sample_factory_visit (\n  sample_factory_visit_id bigint GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,\n  sample_id_fk        integer NOT NULL\n                        REFERENCES dflow.sample(sample_id_pk) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n  factory_id          integer NOT NULL,\n  visit_order         integer NOT NULL CHECK (visit_order > 0),\n  provenance          text NOT NULL CHECK (provenance IN ('nyo_requested','ningbo_added')),\n  state               text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'planned' CHECK (state IN (\n                        'planned','shipped','at_factory','returning','returned',\n                        'cancelled','not_returned')),\n  outbound_shipment_id bigint REFERENCES dflow.sample_shipment(sample_shipment_id)\n                        ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n  return_shipment_id  bigint REFERENCES dflow.sample_shipment(sample_shipment_id)\n                        ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n  requested_by_user   text NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(requested_by_user) <> ''),\n  requested_by_role   text NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(requested_by_role) <> ''),\n  shipped_at          timestamptz,\n  factory_received_at timestamptz,\n  returned_at         timestamptz,\n  closed_at           timestamptz,\n  idempotency_key     text NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(idempotency_key) <> ''),\n  request_hash        text NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(request_hash) <> ''),\n  created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\n  updated_at          timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\n  UNIQUE (requested_by_user, idempotency_key),\n  CHECK (state NOT IN ('shipped','at_factory','returning','returned') OR outbound_shipment_id IS NOT NULL),\n  CHECK (state NOT IN ('shipped','at_factory','returning','returned') OR shipped_at IS NOT NULL),\n  CHECK (state <> 'returned' OR (return_shipment_id IS NOT NULL AND returned_at IS NOT NULL)),\n  CHECK (factory_received_at IS NULL OR shipped_at IS NOT NULL),\n  CHECK ((closed_at IS NOT NULL) = (state IN ('returned','cancelled','not_returned')))\n);\n```\n\nIndexes and the two rules that matter most:\n\n```sql\n-- A physical piece can be at only one factory at a time.\nCREATE UNIQUE INDEX sample_factory_visit_one_active_uniq\n  ON dflow.sample_factory_visit (sample_id_fk)\n  WHERE state IN ('shipped','at_factory','returning');\n\n-- Order is unique among visits that are still live. Cancelled visits free their slot,\n-- which is what makes reorder possible without renumbering history.\nCREATE UNIQUE INDEX sample_factory_visit_order_uniq\n  ON dflow.sample_factory_visit (sample_id_fk, visit_order)\n  WHERE state <> 'cancelled';\n\nCREATE INDEX sample_factory_visit_factory_queue_idx\n  ON dflow.sample_factory_visit (factory_id, state, visit_order);\n```\n\n`factory_id` intentionally carries no foreign key, matching `dflow.sample.factory_id_fk`, which\nis also an unconstrained integer in this schema. **Please confirm that is still the right call**\nrather than silently copying it — if a canonical factory table is reachable from `dflow`, a real\nFK is better and we will adapt the API.\n\nA trigger must reject a visit whose sample is not Flow 1:\n\n```\nsample_factory_visit.sample_id_fk must have a dflow.sample_workflow row with\nworkflow_type = 'nyo_purchased_factory_reference', else ERRCODE 23514.\n```\n\nAnd a trigger must enforce the legal state graph, since a CHECK cannot see the old row:\n\n```\nplanned    -> shipped | cancelled\nshipped    -> at_factory | returning | not_returned\nat_factory -> returning | not_returned\nreturning  -> returned | not_returned\nreturned / cancelled / not_returned -> terminal\n```\n\n`at_factory` is reachable but never required — factory check-in is optional in Flow 1 and must\nnever be able to strand the return. `returning -> returned` must be reachable directly from\n`shipped` as well, which the graph above already allows via `shipped -> returning`.\n\n### 3. `dflow.sample_factory_visit_event` — append-only history\n\nSame shape and discipline as release A's `dflow.sample_path_revision`: monotonic `revision` per\nvisit enforced by a BEFORE INSERT trigger, and a second trigger that raises on any UPDATE or\nDELETE so the table is provably append-only.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE dflow.sample_factory_visit_event (\n  sample_factory_visit_event_id bigint GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,\n  sample_factory_visit_id bigint NOT NULL\n      REFERENCES dflow.sample_factory_visit(sample_factory_visit_id) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n  revision      integer NOT NULL CHECK (revision > 0),\n  event_type    text NOT NULL CHECK (event_type IN (\n                  'planned','reordered','shipped','factory_received','return_started',\n                  'returned','cancelled','marked_not_returned','factory_changed')),\n  from_state    text,\n  to_state      text,\n  from_visit_order integer,\n  to_visit_order   integer,\n  sample_shipment_id bigint REFERENCES dflow.sample_shipment(sample_shipment_id)\n                  ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n  reason        text NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(reason) <> ''),\n  changed_by_user text NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(changed_by_user) <> ''),\n  changed_by_role text NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(changed_by_role) <> ''),\n  changed_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\n  UNIQUE (sample_factory_visit_id, revision)\n);\n```\n\nEvery state change on `sample_factory_visit` must require a matching event row, in the same way\nrelease A's `require_sample_path_revision` guards `sample_workflow.business_path`. History that\nthe application can forget to write is not history.\n\n### 4. `dflow.sample_visit_plan` — read view\n\nOne row per sample carrying: root sample, piece count, ordered planned factories with\nprovenance, the currently active visit (if any), completed visit count, remaining visit count,\ncurrent custody derived from `dflow.sample_movement`, and the outbound/return tracking numbers\nper visit.\n\n**Performance warning, learned the hard way:** release A's `dflow.sample_inventory` view cannot\nuse any index because of CASE-wrapped predicates plus an OR self-join, and it degrades about\nn^1.57 — that is open as #1181 and must land before step 10. Please do not repeat that shape\nhere. The view should be index-usable on `sample_id_fk` and on `(factory_id, state)`, and the\n`EXPLAIN` proof should be part of this issue's evidence.\n\n## Non-negotiable behaviour this schema has to make impossible\n\n1. One physical piece record has **no overlapping active visits**. Two pieces of the same parent\n   may be at two different factories at the same time — that is the whole point of the lineage\n   table.\n2. NYO-requested and Ningbo-added visits stay distinguishable **forever**, including after\n   reorder and cancellation.\n3. Ningbo receipt closes the active visit; returning the quantity to Ningbo inventory is a\n   `dflow.sample_movement`, not a column on the visit.\n4. Factory check-in is optional and must never block or strand a return.\n5. The visit table is **not** custody truth. Nothing in it may contradict\n   `dflow.sample_movement`, and nothing may write around `dflow.post_sample_movement`.\n6. `sample.status` and the other legacy strings remain compatibility data only.\n\n## Tests requested\n\nPreview SQL tests, in the style of the existing `supabase/tests/` contract files:\n\n1. A second active visit on the same piece is rejected; the same two states on two sibling\n   pieces of one root are accepted.\n2. Full happy path: plan three factories, ship, factory receives, return, Ningbo receives, next\n   visit becomes active. Then the same path with factory check-in skipped entirely.\n3. Reorder among `planned` visits succeeds and writes a `reordered` event; reordering a shipped\n   or returned visit is rejected.\n4. Cancelling a `planned` visit frees its order slot; cancelling a `shipped` visit is rejected.\n5. A `not_returned` visit is terminal and does not block the piece from being marked as such,\n   but does block a new visit on the same piece.\n6. A direct `UPDATE` or `DELETE` on `sample_factory_visit_event` raises.\n7. A state change on `sample_factory_visit` with no matching event row raises.\n8. A visit on a sample whose `workflow_type` is not `nyo_purchased_factory_reference` raises.\n9. Lineage: a child whose `root_sample_id_fk` disagrees with its parent's root raises.\n10. `EXPLAIN` on `dflow.sample_visit_plan` filtered by `sample_id_fk` and by\n    `(factory_id, state)` shows index use, with the plan captured in the issue.\n\n## Gotchas the last slice paid for\n\n- **`NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` columns break Sequelize consumers.** Release A shipped four tables\n  whose timestamp columns the tracking service declared `allowNull: false` with no model\n  default. Sequelize runs its own notNull validation *before* the statement reaches Postgres, so\n  the database default never applied and every write returned a 500. It was found only by a\n  browser run, because the unit tests mock Sequelize. The tracking repo now has a generic guard\n  (`tests/unit/releaseATimestampDefaults.test.js`) that walks every Release A model — we will\n  extend it to Release B models. No change is needed on the database side; this is flagged so\n  the shape is a known, handled hazard rather than a fresh surprise.\n- **Never reuse a migration version.** The ledger keys on the version alone, so a duplicate makes\n  one migration silently skip.\n- **Preview may be unavailable.** #1188 reports the `shared-db-schema-rehearsal` branch stuck in\n  RESTORING / MIGRATIONS_FAILED. If that is still true, this issue cannot be preview-proven and\n  should be queued behind it rather than promoted on file inspection alone.\n\n## Definition of done for this issue\n\nMigration merged to `main`, preview-proven with the SQL tests above green, generated types\nregenerated, production promotion proposed through the normal approval lane (owner approval\nrequired — do not self-promote), and the version and object list reported back here so the\ntracking API work in step 5's second half can start against real tables.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 520\ndepends_on: #975\nobjects:\n  - function dflow.apply_sample_factory_visit_event\n  - function dflow.reject_sample_factory_visit_event_mutation\n  - function dflow.require_sample_factory_visit_event\n  - function dflow.touch_sample_factory_visit_updated_at\n  - function dflow.validate_sample_factory_visit\n  - function dflow.validate_sample_factory_visit_event\n  - function dflow.validate_sample_piece_lineage\n  - table dflow.sample_factory_visit\n  - table dflow.sample_factory_visit_event\n  - table dflow.sample_piece_lineage\n  - view dflow.sample_visit_plan\n  - index dflow.sample_factory_visit_event_visit_idx\n  - index dflow.sample_factory_visit_factory_queue_idx\n  - index dflow.sample_factory_visit_one_active_uniq\n  - index dflow.sample_factory_visit_order_uniq\n  - index dflow.sample_factory_visit_sample_state_idx\n  - index dflow.sample_piece_lineage_parent_idx\n  - index dflow.sample_piece_lineage_root_idx\n  - trigger sample_factory_visit_event_apply on dflow.sample_factory_visit_event\n  - trigger sample_factory_visit_event_immutable on dflow.sample_factory_visit_event\n  - trigger sample_factory_visit_event_required on dflow.sample_factory_visit\n  - trigger sample_factory_visit_event_validate on dflow.sample_factory_visit_event\n  - trigger sample_factory_visit_touch on dflow.sample_factory_visit\n  - trigger sample_factory_visit_validate on dflow.sample_factory_visit\n  - trigger sample_piece_lineage_validate on dflow.sample_piece_lineage\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-24T12:05:53Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T11:36:13Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1307,"title":"Sample Tracking release B: Flow 1 factory visit plan, piece lineage, and visit history","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:26Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1307"},
{"body":"## What is needed\n\nIncremental (change-only) licensor captures are being rolled out. The repo-side baselines now exist for Paramount and Warner, but no delta can ever be loaded into the database because the landing tables have nowhere to record what the delta means.\n\nEvery `plm.*` licensor landing table family needs:\n\n| Column | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `first_seen_at timestamptz` | the run that first indexed this key |\n| `last_seen_at timestamptz` | the most recent run that still saw it |\n| `status text` | `active` or `withdrawn` |\n| `withdrawn_at timestamptz` | when it stopped appearing |\n\nPlus **uniqueness on the licensor's own source key**, which the upsert depends on.\n\n## Table families in scope\n\n`plm.pmt_*` (Paramount), `plm.wb_*` (Warner STARLABS), `plm.nbcu_*`, `plm.opa_*` (Disney OPA), `plm.dcp_*` (Disney DCP Vault), `plm.wildbrain_*`, `plm.peanuts_*`, Sega, and Sesame's landing tables.\n\n## Design notes that matter\n\n- **Withdrawn is marked, never deleted** (owner ruling 2026-08-19). Product may already have been made from art a licensor later pulls, and withdrawals are frequently temporary. A key that reappears goes back to `active` and keeps its original `first_seen_at`.\n- **Source keys are text, not numbers.** Paramount already learned this the hard way (migration `20260811030000_pmt_lossless_source_ids_and_asset_metadata_value.sql`): storing an opaque identifier as `bigint` silently destroys a leading zero.\n- **Warner keys must be namespace-qualified.** STARLABS publishes two namespaces and the same real-world entity appears in both, so a bare source id is not unique. Its style guides publish no source id at all and key on a natural key.\n- **Loads are upserts on the source key, never truncate-and-reload.** A reload would destroy `first_seen_at` and any local curation.\n- Paramount's landing tables carry an immutability guard that freezes rows once a capture is marked `complete`. Adding these columns must not fight that guard: incremental bookkeeping columns are OURS and need to stay writable after completion, the same carve-out `plm.pmt_property` and `plm.pmt_character` already have for their reconciliation columns.\n\n## Context\n\nOwner approved 2026-08-20. Repo-side work and per-licensor detail is tracked in `u2giants/licensor-source-data` issue #27.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 580\ndepends_on: #1275\nobjects:\n  - table plm.nbcu_asset\n  - table plm.nbcu_property\n  - table plm.nbcu_character\n  - table plm.nbcu_style_guide\n  - table plm.dcp_asset\n  - table plm.dcp_property\n  - table plm.dcp_character\n  - table plm.dcp_style_guide\n  - table plm.opa_property\n  - table plm.opa_character\n  - table plm.wb_asset\n  - table plm.wb_property\n  - table plm.wb_character\n  - table plm.wb_style_guide\n  - table plm.wildbrain_asset\n  - table plm.wildbrain_character\n  - table plm.wildbrain_guide\n  - table plm.peanuts_asset\n  - table plm.peanuts_character\n  - table plm.peanuts_style_guide\n  - table plm.peanuts_art_program\n  - table plm.sesame_asset\n  - table plm.sesame_character\n  - table plm.sesame_style_guide\n  - table plm.sesame_brand\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:23:33Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T11:36:02Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1306,"title":"Add incremental-capture columns to every plm.* licensor landing table family","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:27Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1306"},
{"body":"Found during orchestrator session `claude-20260820-030000Z` (marker #1293) while measuring the `git check-ignore` behaviour behind #1296. Recorded there as a comment; promoted to its own issue because it is a real decision that will otherwise be made by accident.\n\n## The contradiction\n\n`.gitignore` line 48 says `.ai/reviews/`, and the comment immediately above it says a review *\"is session scratch and must never be committable.\"*\n\n**25 review files are tracked in the repository anyway:**\n\n```\n$ git ls-files .ai/reviews/ | wc -l\n25\n$ git log --oneline -1 -- .ai/reviews/\ne0b18a6 Add immutable production review evidence gate\n```\n\nThey were committed **before** the ignore rule was added, and `.gitignore` does not untrack what is already tracked. So the repository simultaneously holds a rule declaring reviews disposable and 25 committed reviews, several added by the commit that introduced the immutable production review evidence gate.\n\n## This does not affect the wrapper bug in #1296\n\n`git check-ignore` still resolves the rule correctly for *new* files (`rc=0` for an untracked path), so the false-negative warning has a different cause and the same fix. **The two are unrelated; do not fix them together.**\n\n## Why it needs deciding rather than leaving\n\n**Because the next person to act on the stated rule will delete evidence.**\n\nI did exactly that. While measuring `check-ignore` I ran `rm -rf .ai` — reasoning, from the rule, that the directory was disposable scratch. It deleted 25 tracked files. I restored them immediately with `git checkout -- .ai/reviews/` and the working tree is clean and matches `origin/main`, so nothing was lost. **But the only thing standing between that rule and a real deletion was noticing `git status`.**\n\nA cleanup script, a `git clean`, or any session reasoning from the `.gitignore` comment would do the same thing and might not notice.\n\n## The decision\n\n**Which is true — are these files durable evidence, or scratch?**\n\n- **If durable:** they should not be sitting under a path the repo declares disposable. Move them somewhere the rule does not contradict, or carve out an exception in `.gitignore` with a comment saying why these 25 are tracked deliberately.\n- **If scratch:** untrack them (`git rm --cached`) so the rule and reality agree, accepting that the text stays only in git history.\n\n**This is a judgement about what counts as durable review evidence in this repository, and it should not be settled as a side effect of a wrapper investigation** — which is precisely why I did not settle it myself. Note that at least some of the 25 relate to the production review evidence gate, which argues for \"durable\", but I did not audit all 25 and that audit is part of the work.\n\n## What must be true when it is done\n\n- `.gitignore` and the actual tracked state agree, in whichever direction is chosen.\n- The `.gitignore` comment no longer says something that is false about the files sitting next to it.\n- `git status --porcelain` is empty afterwards.\n- If any file is untracked or moved, the decision and the reasoning are recorded — these are review artifacts and a future session must be able to tell why they went.\n\n**You'll know it worked when:** a session reading only `.gitignore` and its comment would reach the correct conclusion about whether `.ai/reviews/` can be deleted.\n\n## Facts that may be stale\n\nCounts and SHAs read **2026-08-20T11:2xZ** against `origin/main` = `e4ea901`. Re-run `git ls-files .ai/reviews/ | wc -l` before acting; another session may have added or removed files.\n\n## Related\n\n- **#1296** — the `check-ignore` false negative and the evidence-packet collision. This was found while investigating it and is explicitly *not* the same bug.\n- `ai-devops/docs/reviewer-result-delivery-defects-2026-08-20.md` — the three-reviewer result-delivery analysis.\n- **PR #1300** (`918ba31`) — separate, already merged: `.ai-review/` (the packet directory) was ignored only by machine-local `.git/info/exclude` and is now ignored in-repo.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 480\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T18:57:28Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T11:21:36Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1304,"title":"25 review files under .ai/reviews/ are TRACKED while .gitignore declares them disposable scratch","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:29Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1304"},
{"body":"Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T0314Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`, section 0. Orchestrator marker #1293.\n\n## Albert — one question, one word answers it\n\n**Should a session spend a short focused pass fixing the four reviewer-wrapper defects before the next batch of production promotions?**\n\n- **Recommended: yes.** Each fix is small. Together they remove a cost paid on every single review from here on.\n- **Also fine: later.** Nothing is blocked today — every promotion this session still completed.\n\nThat is the whole decision. Everything below is why, and you do not need to read it to answer.\n\n## What you are being asked about, in plain terms\n\nThe independent reviewers are the outside check on database changes before they reach production. There are three of them in rotation.\n\n**On 2026-08-20 all three did their job correctly and all three then told us the wrong thing about their own result.** Not one of them failed at reviewing. They failed at *reporting*.\n\n| Reviewer | What we saw | What was actually true |\n|---|---|---|\n| GLM | Looked frozen and dead | Working correctly the whole time |\n| Muse | Returned nothing at all | A complete, excellent review saved on disk |\n| Grok | Warned it could not save its report | It could; the warning is wrong |\n\n## What it cost, measured, not estimated\n\n- **A complete, correct review was destroyed.** I judged GLM dead from its own status display and stopped it. It had already read the entire migration and found things nobody asked it to look for. All of it was thrown away and the work had to be redone with a different reviewer.\n- **About forty minutes of this session.**\n- **GLM was benched for two days** (2026-08-18 to 2026-08-20) as an unreliable provider, on a diagnosis that was wrong. You paid for that in review capacity: for most of 2026-08-19 the rotation was effectively one reviewer, and twice that day a second reviewer overturned the first's conclusion. A rotation of one is not a rotation.\n- **The best review of this session nearly went in the bin.** Muse returned zero bytes. It looked like a dead reviewer. Its 10 KB review was sitting in a file the whole time, and it is the review that cleared the Sesame migration for production.\n\n**Nothing bad reached the database.** The standing rule you set — never accept a bare verdict, read the raw output — caught all three. It was load-bearing three separate times in one session. Without it: two reviewers falsely marked as broken, and one review recorded against the wrong version of the code, all looking perfectly normal in the record.\n\n## Why it is worth a deliberate decision rather than just doing it\n\nTwo reasons it is not automatic:\n\n1. **The fixes live in `ai-devops`, not in the database repo**, and `ai-devops` currently has a lot of uncommitted work from another session across nearly every wrapper file. Landing these means coordinating with that work rather than dropping changes on top of it.\n2. **It is a detour.** There are real database promotions queued (#1302 mgCategory, and the four licensor promotions #678/#679/#680/#681). This pass buys reliability, not features, and it competes with those for a session.\n\nMy view: **do it first.** The next promotion batch is bigger than this one, every promotion needs an independent review, and each review currently carries a chance of a false failure that costs a reviewer or a redone review.\n\n## What \"a short focused pass\" actually covers\n\nFour items, all already written up with root causes and suggested fixes:\n\n- **#1298** — GLM reports itself idle while working. The field it uses is only updated *after* a review finishes, so it can never move during one.\n- **#1296** — Grok's warning that it cannot save its report is false, and it silently discards the report. Also: running two reviewers in the same folder makes them overwrite each other's input.\n- **#1297** — a failed reviewer can be left with no replacement available.\n- **ai-devops#45** — a reviewer should say plainly when the problem is on this machine rather than at the provider. That is what caused the two-day GLM bench.\n\nFull analysis with the exact code paths and proposed fixes:\n[`ai-devops/docs/reviewer-result-delivery-defects-2026-08-20.md`](https://github.com/u2giants/ai-devops/blob/main/docs/reviewer-result-delivery-defects-2026-08-20.md) (merged as `bb79c4c`).\n\n## Nothing else in this session needs you\n\nAll three priorities you set were completed with no owner decision required, and no technical risk was put to you. **#1291 still holds your three existing items and I did not add to it or re-ask them.**\n\n## Already settled — please do not let anyone re-ask these\n\n| Settled | When |\n|---|---|\n| Stop Kimi, restore GLM, use Muse, hold Gemini | 2026-08-19 — **implemented and merged**, `cef67d6` |\n| You are never asked to sign off on technical/SQL risk | 2026-08-18 — retired |\n| Act without per-step approval | standing |\n| Scrape data visible to Licensing users | 2026-08-19 — **now live in production** |\n| Withdrawn assets are marked, never deleted | 2026-08-19 |\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T18:57:37Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T11:21:07Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1303,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] one question — fix the reviewer wrappers before the next promotion batch, yes or later?","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:30Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1303"},
{"body":"Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T0314Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`, sections 5.1 and 6 item 1. Orchestrator marker #1293.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nPromote **`20260818203751`** — the mgCategory taxonomy migration (#1163, PR #1175) — to production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, through the **historical-recovery lane**.\n\n## This supersedes the \"unrecoverable\" claim on #1200\n\n**#1200 states that `20260818203751` is stranded and that the evidence \"cannot be regenerated\". That is no longer true, and this session proved it.**\n\n#1200's reasoning was correct at the time: a migration rehearsed on preview *before* its PR merged cannot satisfy a gate that requires the rehearsal to have run from the promoted commit, an applied version can never be re-applied to preview, the preview lane wants a live author claim that the merge released, and the branch is gone.\n\nWhat it did not account for is the **historical-recovery lane** (`historical_preview_source_pr` + `historical_preview_original_run_map`), which exists for exactly this shape and **performs no database write**. It re-proves provenance rather than re-running the rehearsal.\n\n**On 2026-08-20 that lane took `20260819151510` — refused by the business-risk gate for materially the same reason — all the way into production** (#1288, apply run `32326682504`). The gate passed twice, on evidence produced by the pipeline currently on main, and **no guard, `if:` condition or artifact name was edited**.\n\n`20260818203751` is the same shape. It should go the same way.\n\n## The exact chain that worked, to copy\n\nEvery input must be re-derived immediately before use. Main moved **six times** during the session that ran this.\n\n1. **Read production's ledger directly** — production dry-run with `production_allowlist=20260818203751`. Confirm the version shows local-only (second column empty) and that its prerequisites are applied. Do not trust any document for this.\n2. **Historical recovery** — `target=preview`, `mode=apply`, with:\n   - `preview_allowlist=20260818203751`\n   - `historical_preview_source_pr=1175`\n   - `historical_preview_original_run_map=20260818203751:<the run id that ORIGINALLY applied it to preview>` — find it in Actions history as the successful `apply` run whose artifact is `preview-migration-apply-<sha>` for that batch. **This input is required and the gate byte-compares the digest that run recorded against the file on exact main.**\n   - `commit_sha=<current main tip>`\n   Record the uploaded artifact digest from the run log.\n3. **Immutable review evidence** — `production-apply-review-evidence.yml` with `reviewed_main_sha=<same main tip>`, `ordered_allowlist=20260818203751`, `verdict=APPROVE`, and a `reviewer_label` naming the reviewer. Record its artifact digest.\n4. **Production dry-run** with the full evidence chain (`review_run_id`, `review_artifact_digest`, `source_pr`, `preview_run_id`, `preview_artifact_digest`).\n5. **Production apply**, same inputs, `confirmation=APPLY <sha>`.\n\n**You'll know it worked when:** production's own `supabase migration list`, read in the apply run's \"Capture production migration record (after)\" step, shows `20260818203751 | 20260818203751`. Both columns populated. **Do not accept the workflow's summary as proof.**\n\n## Two traps that each cost a full cycle last time\n\n1. **Do NOT pre-hold `refs/db-coordination/production` or the preview ref.** The workflow acquires both itself; a manual hold refuses the run with `REFUSED: refs/db-coordination/... is occupied`. This happened on the preview lane and then again on production. **No database write occurred either time** — both failed before touching anything — but each cost a cycle.\n2. **Check whether the rehearsal evidence is genuinely stale before assuming it is.** One command decides it:\n   ```bash\n   git diff <rehearsal-commit> origin/main -- .github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml\n   ```\n   If it is empty, the workflow that produced the evidence is byte-identical to the one on main and the original rehearsal is still valid — no recovery needed at all. That check saved a full cycle on `20260819212002` (#1289).\n\n## Still true from #1200, and still important\n\n**Do NOT merge PR #1194.** An independent review showed it is the wrong fix: it pins `run.head_sha` when the rehearsal actually applies from `claim_head_sha`, it adds no preview-instance binding, and its five tests stay green through an inverted compare. It is parked as a draft deliberately.\n\n## Independent review required\n\nThis is a production promotion, so it needs an independent reviewer with a **coverage statement** — a bare verdict is not evidence. Brief it on the apply-time cost question specifically: a `verify` block inside a migration is production code, and `20260819151536` became permanently unappliable because its block was cheap on an empty preview and prohibitive on full production. Assert shape from the catalogue; count rows only inside your own tables.\n\n**Before recording any reviewer failure, read the raw provider stream.** All three active reviewers currently misreport their results in different ways — see #1296, #1297, #1298 and `ai-devops/docs/reviewer-result-delivery-defects-2026-08-20.md`.\n\n## Facts that may be stale\n\n`origin/main` was `e4ea901` and the maximum migration on main was `20260820004338`, both checked **2026-08-20T11:18Z**. Re-derive both. The migration file is `20260818203751_core_mg_category_taxonomy_and_mg01_mapping.sql`; it creates `core.mg_category` and `core.mg_category_merch_group`, verified by reading the file on main rather than from any document. Its source PR **#1175** is confirmed MERGED and did add that file. The original preview apply run id is **not** recorded here deliberately — find it in the Actions history rather than trusting a number copied between documents.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 900\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - table core.mg_category\n  - table core.mg_category_merch_group\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T13:14:41Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T11:20:29Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1302,"title":"HANDOVER: promote 20260818203751 (mgCategory) via the historical-recovery lane — it is NOT unrecoverable, #1200 is superseded","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:32Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1302"},
{"body":"Observed in orchestrator session claude-20260820-030000Z (marker #1293), 2026-08-20. **I aborted a live, correct review because of this.** Recording it so nobody repeats it.\n\n## What happened\n\n`ai-glm new promo-20260819151510` was started to review a production promotion. For **25 minutes**:\n\n- `ai-glm show promo-20260819151510` reported `\"last_activity_at\": \"2026-08-20T02:39:44Z\"` — **identical to `created_at`, never moving.**\n- `status: active`.\n- The wrapper had written nothing to stdout beyond its two startup lines.\n\nEvery observable signal matched the documented \"session that never produced a turn\" failure — the exact signature that caused GLM's false two-day pause on 2026-08-18. On that evidence I aborted it.\n\n**`ai-glm transcript` showed it had been working the whole time**, and working well:\n\n- It had read all 364 lines of the migration.\n- It had confirmed the house read predicate is **character-identical** to the Sega one at `20260819015333:1297-1298`.\n- It had confirmed **no migration after `20260819151510` alters those 28 tables' policies or grants** — i.e. it did the forward-only current-definition check correctly, which is the check this repository got wrong on 2026-08-19.\n- It had independently spotted the evidence-packet mismatch now filed as #1296, unprompted.\n\nIt had not yet reached a verdict, so **none of that is usable as review evidence.** The work was thrown away.\n\n## The defect\n\n`last_activity_at` is written at session creation and apparently not updated while a turn is in progress. A long turn — and a thorough review is a long turn — therefore looks exactly like a session that never started. **The wrapper's own status output cannot distinguish its healthiest behaviour from its worst.**\n\nThis is very likely a large part of why GLM acquired a reputation for producing dead sessions. It compounds the #1287 problem: a pause needs no evidence, and the cheapest available evidence is a status field that lies about long work.\n\n## What to fix (in ai-devops — provider machinery does not live in this repository)\n\n1. **Update `last_activity_at` on every streamed event**, not only at creation. Then elapsed-since-last-activity becomes a real liveness signal.\n2. Failing that, have `show` report the transcript's own last event time and event count, so `show` alone answers \"is it working?\".\n3. Consider emitting a heartbeat line to stdout during a long turn.\n\n## Interim rule, effective now — this is the important part\n\n**Never judge a GLM session dead from `ai-glm show`. Read `ai-glm transcript` first.** This is the same standing rule that already applies to Muse (\"it saves its output — read the saved artifact before recording a failure\") and it is now the rule for GLM too.\n\nMore generally, and this is the shared-db rule: **never record a reviewer failure from a wrapper's summary or status field. Read the raw provider stream.** A wrapper's status is a claim about the provider, not an observation of it.\n\n## Related\n\n- #1287 — a pause must name the failing check; `local_dependency_unavailable` as a distinct code.\n- #1290 / PR #1295 — the roster change restoring GLM. Its health check **passed** this time and it still looked dead, which is precisely the case #1287 says must be recorded explicitly rather than guessed.\n- #1296 — the concurrent-review evidence-packet collision, which GLM found on its own.\n- ai-devops#45 — wrappers self-checking their local dependencies.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 710\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-20T13:05:24Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T02:45:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1298,"title":"ai-glm's last_activity_at does not move during a live turn, so a working review is indistinguishable from a dead session","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:33Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1298"},
{"body":"Found by grok-4.6 (reviewer sequence 235) reviewing PR #1295. Orchestrator marker #1293.\n\n## The defect\n\n`replaceFailedReviewer` in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` selects the replacement as:\n\n```js\nconst sequence = cursor.sequence + 1\nconst reviewer = ACTIVE_REVIEWERS[(sequence - 1) % ACTIVE_REVIEWERS.length]\nif (reviewer.name === original.reviewer) throw new LaneError('next durable reviewer is the same failed provider; replacement refuses to retry it')\n```\n\nThe refusal is **correct and fail-closed** — retrying a provider that just died is worse than refusing. But it means **a failed review can have no replacement at all**, and the operator is stuck until someone assigns unrelated work to move the cursor.\n\n## When it fires\n\nWhenever there have been **N-1 assignments since the failure**, for any roster size N. It is not a property of even-vs-odd length. PR #1295 originally claimed a three-name rotation removed the trap; that claim was false and has been withdrawn from the code comment and the test.\n\n- **N = 2**: one intervening assignment strands it.\n- **N = 3** (the roster after #1290): **two** intervening assignments strand it — and two is the *natural rest point of a three-name parallel dispatch*. Grok takes a PR and holds `ai-grok-review`'s per-repository in-flight lock, GLM takes the next, Muse takes the third, the cursor lands on a multiple of three. A Grok failure then computes back to Grok and is refused.\n- **N = 1**: every replacement is stranded, always.\n\nSo growing the roster buys **capacity**, not freedom from this.\n\n## The fix\n\nSelect the next active reviewer that is **not** the failed provider, rather than refusing when the modulo happens to land on it. Advance the cursor past it. Refuse only when there is genuinely no other active reviewer (N = 1, or every other name already failed on this same head).\n\n## Why this needs its own change, not a hitchhike\n\n`replaceFailedReviewer` is a governed function with **immutability and idempotency guarantees**: a repeated call with the same `failedSequence` must return byte-identical results, replacement chains are recorded in permanent coordination refs, and the durable cursor must never be rewritten. A selection change has to preserve all of that, and the existing chained-replacement tests (`two consecutive terminal no-verdict failures form an immutable idempotent chain`) are the ones that will catch a mistake. It deserves its own review round rather than riding a roster edit.\n\n## Tests that already exist and must keep passing\n\n- `one intervening assignment gives a failed reviewer a named replacement` — pins the successor by name.\n- `N-1 intervening assignments still strand a replacement on the failed provider` — **this test asserts the CURRENT behaviour and is expected to change when this issue is fixed.** Rewrite it to assert the skip, do not delete it.\n- `terminal provider failure advances exactly once and retry is idempotent`\n- `two consecutive terminal no-verdict failures form an immutable idempotent chain`\n- `chained replacement rejects mismatch, exact-head drift, and a verdict at every depth`\n\n## Related\n\n- #1290 / PR #1295 — the roster change that surfaced this.\n- #1287 — the other two reviewer-rotation bookkeeping items (a distinct `local_dependency_unavailable` failure code, and a pause naming its failing check).\n- Note the standing constraint from the same review lane: `--replace-failed-reviewer` REFUSES outright when the PR is merged (*\"requires the exact open PR head\"*), which is every production promotion. A failed reviewer on a promotion already cannot be repaired through this tool at all. Worth considering in the same pass.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 720\ndepends_on: #1290\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-20T13:35:43Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T02:43:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1297,"title":"replaceFailedReviewer strands a replacement whenever the cursor wraps onto the failed provider — skip it instead of refusing","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:35Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1297"},
{"body":"Observed live in orchestrator session claude-20260820-030000Z (marker #1293) on 2026-08-20.\n\n## What happened\n\nTwo independent reviews were started concurrently from the SAME checkout `C:/repos/shared-db`:\n\n1. `ai-grok-review new review-1295-roster` — evidence packet `/c/repos/shared-db/.ai-review (base 55f0eb726108, head 938870d3cb2a, sha 2963e610ebbf)`\n2. `ai-glm new promo-20260819151510` — evidence packet `/c/repos/shared-db/.ai-review (base 55f0eb726108, head 938870d3cb2a, sha fbb67518c8ca)`\n\n**Same directory. The second write landed on top of the first**, while the first reviewer was still working, and the `sha` line shows the packet contents changed underneath it.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThe evidence packet is what the reviewer reads to know *what it is reviewing*. A reviewer whose packet is swapped mid-review can produce a verdict about a different change than the one it was asked about — and nothing in the output would say so. That is worse than a failed review, because the verdict looks normal.\n\nNote the second symptom in the line above: **GLM's packet was built against PR #1295's head**, because the checkout happened to be on that branch, even though GLM was asked to review a migration file for a production promotion unrelated to #1295. The packet framing follows the working tree, not the brief.\n\n## Not the same as the known defect\n\nai-devops PR #44 documents a four-wrapper `.ai/reviews` defect. This is a different failure: not where a wrapper *saves* its output, but that the per-run **input** packet has a fixed per-repository path with no per-session isolation and no in-flight lock.\n\n`ai-grok-review` holds a per-repository in-flight lock for *Grok*. That lock does not exclude `ai-glm`, `ai-kimi`, `ai-qwen` or `ai-muse`, so nothing stops a cross-wrapper collision.\n\n## Why this is getting worse, not better\n\n#1290 takes the rotation from two active reviewers to three, precisely so reviews can proceed in parallel and a failed reviewer has somewhere to go. **Parallel reviews are now the expected case**, so a shared mutable packet path is a defect that will fire more often from here.\n\n## What a fix looks like\n\nThe substantive fix belongs in `ai-devops` (per the standing rule that provider-specific machinery does not live in this repository): each wrapper writes its packet to a per-session path, or takes a cross-wrapper lock on the checkout. **This issue exists to record the observation and its evidence**, and to make sure the orchestrator rule below is written down somewhere durable.\n\n## Interim orchestrator rule, effective now\n\n**Do not run two reviewers concurrently from the same checkout.** Either serialise them, or give the second one its own self-contained copy via `ai-review-sandbox ensure`. Never hand any wrapper a linked git worktree.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-20T16:23:05Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T02:40:22Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1296,"title":"Two reviewers running at once in one checkout share .ai-review and overwrite each other's evidence packet","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:36Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1296"},
