{"body":"Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T0200Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`, section 0. Orchestrator marker #1229.\n\n**Nothing here is blocking. This is the short list of things only Albert can answer, gathered so the next orchestrator does not have to reconstruct it — and so he is not asked the same thing twice.**\n\n## 1. Queue triage — #1166\n\n**96 open `db-work` issues.** Only Albert can say which of his own business items are still live. Several date back weeks. This is the single biggest source of noise for an incoming orchestrator: `--queue-audit` reports honestly on all of them, and most of the reading is spent on items that may already be dead.\n\nNot urgent, and it has not blocked anything. But it has now been outstanding across at least three sessions.\n\n## 2. ColdLion phases 2-6 — #1204 / #1226\n\nThe **plan** landed today (PR #1263, merged `5a88061`) — a 13-section implementation plan, a 532-row field-decisions CSV, and two owner rulings. **The implementation has not started**, deliberately: it is roughly 25 tables plus a seven-year backfill, which is its own workstream rather than something to squeeze into a session's tail.\n\nThe next orchestrator can start it whenever Albert wants it started. It does not need a decision to begin; it needs a decision about *priority*.\n\n## 3. Two questions ALREADY ANSWERED — do not re-ask\n\nRecorded here because both were answered today and both are the kind of thing a fresh session re-asks:\n\n- **\"Should scrape data be visible to Licensing?\"** — **Yes.** Answered 2026-08-19: *\"scrape data should be visible to Licensing department users.\"* Implemented (#1249), merged, proven behaviourally. **Not yet in production** — that is #1288, and it is the most valuable outstanding item.\n- **\"Should Disney scrape data be restricted?\"** — **Yes, and it already was.** He answered *\"restrict Disney to match every other licensor\"*, and it turned out that had been true since 2026-08-07 (`20260807190000`, applied to production). **That question should never have reached him**; it was raised on a stale reading of the migration that first created the policy rather than the one that superseded it. Closed as already-done (#1251). The lesson is recorded in section 9 of the handoff.\n\n## 4. Not a question, but he should know\n\n**`20260819151510` — his own Licensing ruling — is merged and proven but NOT in production**, blocked on a technicality: its preview rehearsal predates a workflow change, so the safety gate correctly refuses the evidence. It needs the historical-recovery lane. Tracked as **#1288**. If he asks \"did my Licensing change go live?\", the honest answer is: it works, it is proven, and it is one governed step short of production.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 300\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-26T11:58:54Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T02:01:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1291,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] three items waiting on you — queue triage, ColdLion phases 2-6 priority, and two questions already answered","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:39Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1291"},
{"body":"Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T0200Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`, section 7. Orchestrator marker #1229.\n\n## The owner has decided; the code change has NOT been made\n\nAlbert, 2026-08-19, after being shown a measured failure count: **\"Stop Kimi. Restore GLM. And start using Gemini and Muse and tell me (and document in ai-devops) if they're helpful.\"**\n\nThe trial is done and written up (**ai-devops PR #44**). **The roster edit itself was never made** — that is this issue, and it is the reason it is titled HANDOVER rather than closed.\n\n## The measurements behind it\n\n| Reviewer | Result |\n|---|---|\n| **kimi-k3** | **11 terminal failures vs 5 successes in one session.** Three modes: findings discarded above the verdict heading (1); usage-limit exhaustion (1); nine consecutive 6-second `exit 127` deaths. Reviewer issue `20260820T004602Z-edge-dev-kimi-k3-385556`. |\n| **glm-5.3** | **Works. Its pause was a false diagnosis** — `ai-glm doctor` showed every check passing except `health endpoint answers`, because its local `opencode` server was not running. `opencode-glm-launch` fixed it, and it produced a full 10 KB review with a coverage statement first time. |\n| **muse-spark-1.2-contributor** | **Good reviewer, broken verdict detection.** Complete seven-point review ending in `VERDICT: APPROVE`; the wrapper failed to detect it and wrote *\"This is not a review result\"* over correct work. **It SAVES the output**, so the review was fully recoverable. Reviewer issue `20260820T013646Z-edge-dev-muse-spark-1.2-contributor-394599`. |\n| **gemini-3.7-flash-high** | **Not usable on this evidence.** Two attempts: `no usable Gemini verdict`, then a bare `PASS` with an **empty report**. `ai-gemini doctor` passes, so the install is sound. |\n| **grok-4.6** | 19 successes, 1 failure (a 20-turn cancellation on an oversized brief). Carried the session. |\n\nAll four reviewed **the same PR, from the same self-contained copy, on the same brief**, independently.\n\n## The change needed\n\nIn `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`:\n\n1. **Add `kimi-k3` to `RETIRED_REVIEWERS`.**\n2. **Remove `glm-5.3` from `RETIRED_REVIEWERS`.**\n3. **Do NOT add `gemini` to the registry yet.** Two attempts is thin evidence; retry after someone establishes why its report comes back empty.\n4. **Muse is a candidate but is not in `REVIEWERS` at all**, so adding it is a registry change, not an un-pause. Adding it is reasonable once its verdict detection is fixed, or immediately if the caller is willing to read the saved artifact on every \"incomplete\" result.\n\n**Do not delete any name from `REVIEWERS`.** Reviewer names are read back out of permanent coordination refs, one of those lookups is not null-guarded, and a missing name is a crash rather than a graceful miss. Pause by adding to `RETIRED_REVIEWERS`; the historical verdicts must stay readable forever.\n\n**Mind the rotation slot comment.** `glm-5.3` occupies the same slot `glm-5.2` held so `ACTIVE_REVIEWERS` keeps its length and order and the round robin does not skip a turn. Removing Kimi changes that length — check the comment block's reasoning still holds and update it.\n\n## Capacity warning, which is why this matters\n\nWith Qwen and GLM both paused and Kimi failing, the rotation was **effectively down to Grok alone** for most of 2026-08-19. That is not a theoretical weakness: **twice that day a second reviewer overturned the first's conclusion**, and on one of those occasions the second reviewer refuted an author's design rationale using the author's own test fixture. A rotation of one is not a rotation.\n\n## Related\n\n- **ai-devops#45** — the primary fix for the GLM-style false pause: a wrapper must not report `provider_unavailable` when its own LOCAL dependency is down.\n- **#1287** — the two caller-side items that stay in this repository: a distinct `local_dependency_unavailable` failure code, and a rule that a pause must NAME the failing check.\n- This issue supersedes the narrower framing of **#1203** (\"register Gemini in the reviewer rotation\"); on today's evidence Gemini is the one candidate that should NOT be registered yet.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 800\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T03:08:17Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T02:00:56Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1290,"title":"HANDOVER: make the reviewer roster change Albert decided — pause Kimi, restore GLM, hold Gemini, consider Muse","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:41Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1290"},
{"body":"Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T0200Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`, section 6 item 1. Orchestrator marker #1229.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nPromote **`20260819212002`** — the Sesame Workshop (NetX) source landing schema — to production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\n\n**There is no known blocker.** It is merged (`41b8f74`, PR #1274), it is rehearsed on preview (dry-run `32309845668`, apply `32309958178`, digest `sha256:501f516177c85918763d683da50b49233bcc14165a4eb86f18e767b8f8805b3c`), and unlike the other outstanding promotions nothing is standing in its way. **It simply ran out of session.**\n\nNote the rehearsal ran at main `41b8f74b5fb7179e3d314b3b121eaba88b30d161`, which is AFTER PR #1265 changed `shared-supabase-migrations.yml` — so it does not have the stale-workflow problem that blocks #1288.\n\n## What it is\n\n19 `plm.sesame_*` tables, `begin_sesame_capture`, `complete_sesame_capture`, `latest_sesame_capture`, 19 indexes, 38 RLS policies. It creates only new objects and does not extend `api.source_capture_inventory` (deliberately — that is #1283).\n\n## Review history worth knowing before you promote\n\nThree rounds, and the middle one matters. The author added an exclusion-honesty gate the spec did not ask for, to enforce the spec's own promise that ambiguous character links are *\"excluded, not guessed\"*.\n\n- **Round 1 (Medium):** the gate rejected a truthful zero and rubber-stamped any fabricated nonzero. The author's own fixture demonstrated it — a multi-guide asset with no character rows, and the passing call reporting `4`.\n- **Round 2 (High):** the fix then accepted **every integer between 1 and the true count**, so a capture skipping 1,165 rows could report `1` and publish. The reviewer refuted the author's justification using the author's own fixture.\n- **Round 3:** equality pinned under three named codes; APPROVE, no findings.\n\nThe author then explained why its own testing could not have caught it: it had mutated the guard's BRANCHES and never its STRICTNESS, and its fixture had one excludable row so the under-report mutant was **not expressible**. It rebuilt the fixture with two rows and added an assertion preventing anyone shrinking it back.\n\n## Standing requirements\n\nFollow the normal lane: re-derive `origin/main` immediately before every input, rehearse-then-review-then-evidence-then-dry-run-then-apply, and **verify the result by reading production's own `supabase migration list`, not the workflow's word.**\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 900\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - table plm.sesame_capture\n  - table plm.sesame_asset\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T03:08:06Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T02:00:28Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1289,"title":"HANDOVER: promote 20260819212002 (Sesame Workshop landing) to production — rehearsed, no blocker, ran out of session","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:42Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1289"},
{"body":"Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-20T0200Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`, section 6 item 1. Orchestrator marker #1229.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\n**`20260819151510` — the Licensing read access migration — is merged, proven, and NOT in production.** It is the implementation of an owner ruling and it is the single most valuable outstanding item on the board.\n\nAlbert ruled, verbatim (2026-08-19): *\"scrape data should be visible to Licensing department users.\"* The migration grants `authenticated` SELECT plus a house-predicate `_plm_read` policy on the 11 `plm.wildbrain_*` and 17 `plm.nbcu_*` tables, which previously granted nobody. Merged as `d00812e` (PR #1255) after three review rounds, and **proved behaviourally against a real from-empty database**: `B: 54 passed / 0 failed` — licensing, sales, administrator and a `plm` app-access principal each read both landing schemas; vendor, viewer and a role-less principal read nothing; `anon` refused at the grant; `service_role` still reads.\n\n## Why it is blocked, exactly\n\nIts preview rehearsal (run `32289307005`) ran at main `b660e08998d59eb5259e7726f0f63dd4b493f574` — **before PR #1265 changed `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml`.** The production business-risk gate correctly refuses:\n\n```\nProduction business-risk gate rejected evidence: preview run checked out at\nb660e08998d59eb5259e7726f0f63dd4b493f574 produced evidence with a different\n.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml than exact main\n```\n\n**That refusal is correct.** The rehearsal was produced by a different pipeline than the one now on main, so it does not prove what the current lane would do.\n\n## Why it cannot simply be re-rehearsed\n\n`20260819151510` is **already applied to preview**. The post-merge apply lane refuses a version already in the preview ledger — a rehearsal runs ONCE. Re-running it is not available.\n\n**Its route is therefore the historical-recovery lane** (`historical_preview_source_pr` / `historical_preview_original_run_map`), which exists for exactly this shape: a migration whose preview application is real but whose provenance must be re-proved. That lane was hardened substantially in #1213. Read `AGENTS.md` on it before dispatching, and note the residual recorded there: it deliberately does not bind the original run to today's `PREVIEW_PROJECT_REF`, because that would refuse 100% of existing recoveries.\n\n## What to verify before trusting any of this\n\n- Re-derive `origin/main`; it moved about ten times during the session that wrote this.\n- Confirm `20260819151510` is still absent from production and still present on preview by reading the ledger in a fresh production dry-run, not from this issue.\n- The preview evidence digest recorded at the time was `sha256:fee5105923a774ed084d0dfd400880d04684d64dc599a5e0bf8584be77bb68e7`. Re-verify rather than reusing it.\n\n## Related\n\n`20260819151527` (FR authorization) is blocked differently — preview is missing its prerequisite `20260817124545` (#901). `20260819212002` (Sesame) is rehearsed and has no known blocker; it simply ran out of session.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 950\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - table plm.wildbrain_capture\n  - table plm.nbcu_capture\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T03:03:45Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T02:00:06Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1288,"title":"HANDOVER: promote 20260819151510 (Licensing read access) — its rehearsal predates PR #1265, so it needs the historical-recovery lane","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:44Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1288"},
{"body":"Raised after GLM 5.3 was restored on 2026-08-20 and found to have been working the whole time. Orchestrator marker #1229. Owner asked directly: *\"how do we prevent this from ever happening again?\"* This is the answer.\n\n## What happened\n\n`glm-5.3` was paused on 2026-08-18 after three consecutive `provider_unavailable` failures — rotation sequences 161, 164 and 167 — each creating a session that never produced a turn, each costing a governed reviewer replacement. The pause note in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` reads, reasonably: *\"Pausing stops the rotation handing work to a dead provider.\"*\n\n**The provider was not dead.** `ai-glm doctor` passes every check except one:\n\n```\nFAIL  health endpoint answers\n1 check(s) FAILED.\n```\n\nIts local `opencode` server was simply not running on this machine. `opencode-glm-launch` started it; every check then passed, and GLM produced a full 10 KB review with a coverage statement on the first attempt.\n\nA working reviewer was out of the rotation for two days because a background process on one machine had stopped. During that window the rotation was down to two, and after Kimi's failures, effectively down to one.\n\n## The mechanical cause — and it is already in this file\n\n`reviewerExecutionPreflight` checks:\n\n- the reviewer is approved and the wrapper matches\n- the head SHA is exactly 40 hex characters and a worktree is named\n- **`io.commandAvailable(wrapper)`** — the wrapper binary is on PATH\n- the worktree is at the exact head and is clean\n\n**It verifies the wrapper EXISTS. It never verifies the provider ANSWERS.**\n\nThat is precisely the gap. `ai-glm` was on PATH, so the preflight passed, and every review then died at provider execution with a generic `provider_unavailable` — a message about the provider that was actually about a stopped local service.\n\n## The second, deeper problem: an evidence asymmetry\n\nRead the two paths side by side:\n\n- **Pausing** a reviewer requires no evidence about *why* it failed. Three `provider_unavailable` codes are enough, and `provider_unavailable` is exactly the code a stopped local service produces.\n- **Restoring** it requires a probe — the note says *\"restore it by deleting 'glm-5.3' from this list once the provider answers a probe.\"*\n\nSo a provider can be benched on a symptom and stays benched until somebody happens to probe it. Nobody did, for two days. **The cheap check is required only on the path nobody is in a hurry to take.**\n\n## Proposed fix\n\n**1. Make the preflight probe the provider, not just the binary.** Every wrapper has a `doctor` subcommand — `ai-glm doctor`, `ai-gemini doctor`, `ai-grok-review doctor`, `ai-kimi doctor`. The preflight should run it and refuse with a NAMED error when a check fails, quoting the failing check verbatim:\n\n```\nREFUSED: reviewer preflight: ai-glm doctor reports \"FAIL health endpoint answers\"\n  -- this is a LOCAL SERVICE fault on this machine, not a provider fault.\n  Try: opencode-glm-launch\n```\n\nThat single change converts *\"provider unavailable, pause the reviewer\"* into *\"your local server is down, start it\"* — a fixable instruction instead of a wrong verdict about a model.\n\n**2. Require the same evidence to pause as to restore.** A pause should record WHICH doctor check was failing at the time, or state explicitly that doctor passed and the failure was elsewhere. A pause note that cannot name the failing check is a guess, and this one was.\n\n**3. Distinguish the failure codes.** `provider_unavailable` currently covers both \"the remote provider is down\" and \"a local dependency of the wrapper is not running\". Those need different responses — the first waits, the second is a thirty-second fix. Consider a distinct `local_dependency_unavailable`.\n\n**4. Fold the doctor probe into the restore path too**, so restoring is a mechanical check rather than a research project. That is already the intent of the existing note; making it a command closes the loop.\n\n## Why this is worth doing properly\n\nThe rotation exists to give an independent second opinion. On 2026-08-19 that mattered twice: a second reviewer overturned the first's conclusion, and on one of those occasions refuted an author's design rationale using the author's own test fixture. **Silently losing a reviewer to a stopped background process degrades the safety property the rotation is for**, and it does so invisibly — everything still looks like it is working, because the remaining reviewers keep returning verdicts.\n\nRelated: reviewer issues `20260820T004602Z-edge-dev-kimi-k3-385556` and `20260820T013646Z-edge-dev-muse-spark-1.2-contributor-394599`; ai-devops PR #44 (the 2026-08-19 trial write-up); #1220.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-20T18:57:15Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T01:51:03Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1287,"title":"Reviewer pause needs a named failing check, and a local_dependency_unavailable code — primary fix is ai-devops#45","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:45Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1287"},
{"body":"## What changed and why\n\n**2026-08-19, owner-authorized (Albert Hazan, in chat).** Branch protection on `main` no longer requires a branch to be up to date with `main` before merging.\n\n```\nstrict: true  ->  false\n```\n\n**Unchanged:** all 9 required status checks, and `enforce_admins: true`. Nothing was weakened except the up-to-date requirement.\n\nThe prior settings are recoverable from this issue: the 9 contexts are `Promotion contract tests (offline)`, `Cross-PR object collision`, `Tools offline tests`, `SQL migration guards`, `Domain ownership`, `Intake pointer guard`, `Handoff contract`, `Migration author lease`, `Migration guarded merge authorization`. To revert: `gh api -X PUT repos/u2giants/shared-db/branches/main/protection` with `required_status_checks.strict = true` and those contexts.\n\n## The problem it solves\n\nMany concurrent AI sessions merge into `main`. With `strict: true`, **every merge reset every other waiting PR to \"behind\"** and restarted its 9 checks (~4 min). On 2026-08-19 this cost one session ~35 minutes on PR #1243 and ~25 more on #1263 — roughly 50 minutes of pure queue-reset, with no check ever actually failing.\n\n## What to watch for — the real risk\n\nA **semantic conflict**: two PRs that each pass every check independently but break `main` when combined. The textbook shape is one PR adding a call to a function while another renames it. No text conflict, both green, `main` red.\n\nMitigating factors already present:\n- These guards scan **repo-wide**, not just the diff, so most collisions still get caught on the next run.\n- `Cross-PR object collision` already watches the highest-risk version (two PRs claiming the same database objects).\n- `Migration author lease` serialises migration work.\n\n**If `main` goes red after a merge and the failure names something the merging PR did not touch, suspect this change first.** Note the cost is a red `main` and a forward fix, not data loss.\n\n## Revert criteria\n\nRevert to `strict: true` if semantic conflicts break `main` more than **twice in two weeks**. Below that, the ~50 min/day of queue-reset is the larger cost.\n\n## Deliberately NOT done: path filters\n\nThe companion proposal — let docs-only PRs skip the database checks — was **rejected on investigation**. This repo already forbids `paths:` filters on repo-wide guards, in AGENTS.md §5.2 and in explicit comments in `shared-supabase-migrations.yml`, `tools-offline-tests.yml` and `coldlion-promotion-contract-tests.yml`. Two documented failure modes:\n\n1. A path-filtered workflow creates **no check run at all** on a PR that misses its paths, so a required context stays pending forever and can never block a merge (PRs #328/#307).\n2. A guard that scans more than its trigger watches reports **stale verdicts** — the 2026-07-31 domain-ownership incident, where fixing `HANDOFF.md` did not re-run the check and `main` stayed red on an already-corrected failure.\n\nBoth apply directly here: `check-domain-ownership.mjs` enumerates every tracked text file including `docs/**`, so a docs-only PR is exactly the case that must still be scanned.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 600\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:17:48Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T01:39:02Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1286,"title":"CI throughput: 'require branches up to date' is now OFF on main — watch for semantic conflicts","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1286"},
{"body":"Raised by the #1280 author, unprompted, when asked whether its own fix was guarded. Orchestrator marker #1229.\n\n## The gap, stated plainly\n\n`20260819151536` could not apply to production because its in-file verify block counted rows across every `plm` table and hit the statement timeout (#1280). Its replacement `20260820004338` asserts the same end state from the catalogue instead — reading no `plm` table at all, measured at 14 ms.\n\n**Nothing prevents the next author reintroducing the expensive form.** The 14 ms measurement is evidence about one run on one cluster. It is not a guard. No test in this repository fails if someone drops a `count(*)` over every `plm` table into a verify block tomorrow.\n\n## Three approaches considered and REJECTED, with reasons\n\nRecorded so this is a known gap with a rationale, not an oversight, and so nobody re-proposes them.\n\n1. **A `pg_proc.prosrc` catalogue check cannot work.** That technique guards `plm.finalize_wildbrain_capture` because a stored function's source lives in the catalogue. A verify block is an anonymous `DO` block — PostgreSQL stores nothing about it, before, during or after execution. There is no catalogue row to inspect.\n2. **A self-timing assertion would be theatre.** Measuring `clock_timestamp()` across the block and failing past a budget passes on every CI run and every preview apply, because on an almost-empty database the expensive statement is *also* fast. It fires only on production, at apply time — **the exact preview/production divergence that created #1280.** It would turn a timeout into a clearer message and guard nothing. Wrapping the block in a short `set local statement_timeout` has the same objection, plus the hazard that `set local` sets absolutely and could RAISE a lower session timeout.\n3. Raising `statement_timeout` was already rejected in #1280 as the weaker option; noted here for completeness.\n\n## The only real guard: a static check in CI\n\nA check over migration text — **no verify block may read `api.source_capture_inventory` or any `plm.*` table** — fails on the pull request, on an empty database, which is where it needs to fail.\n\n`scripts/check-sql.sh` already performs exactly this class of content assertion (for example `grep -qF \"create or replace view api.pm_product_board\" …`), so there is precedent and a natural home.\n\n**It needs honest design, not a grep bolted on.** At minimum it must:\n- handle dynamic SQL, which a naive text scan will miss;\n- stay maintainable as the set of expensive objects grows, rather than hard-coding a list that goes stale — the staleness trap that has bitten three separate tests in this repo in one day;\n- have its **false-negative surface written down**, so the next reader knows what it does NOT catch rather than discovering it during an incident;\n- have a test that fails when the guard is disabled, per the standing rule that an unfalsifiable guard is not a guard.\n\n## Why this is worth doing\n\nA verify block is production code that runs inside the apply transaction. The failure mode is unusually bad: the rehearsal passes, the review passes, every check is green, and the migration is simply unappliable to production — discovered only at the promotion, by which time it is merged and applied to preview and therefore uneditable under §4.\n\nThat is exactly what happened today, and it cost a stranded migration plus a full replacement cycle.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 580\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:15:19Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T01:08:32Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1285,"title":"No guard stops an expensive statement being added to a migration's verify block","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:49Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1285"},
{"body":"Found by the #1280 author while diagnosing why that migration's verify block timed out on production. Orchestrator marker #1229.  ## The problem  `api.source_capture_inventory` performs an **exact `count(*)` on every `plm` table, on every single read**, through a `query_to_xml` subquery.  `query_to_xml` is `VOLATILE`. **The planner therefore cannot push a `where table_name like …` qualifier under the subquery**, so the per-table counts run for *every* `plm` table before any filter applies. Adding a restriction to the outer query does not reduce the work — which is exactly why `20260819151536`'s verify block already carried `like` filters on all eleven of its queries and still hit the statement timeout on production (#1280).  ## Why this matters beyond that one migration  - **Every consumer of the view pays this**, not just verify blocks. It is a live production cost on an ordinary read. - **It grows with every landing schema.** The `plm` schema gained 19 Sesame tables today (#1216), on top of WildBrain, Sega, Peanuts, NBCU, Paramount, Warner and both Disney schemas. Each new licensor makes every read of this view slower. - **It has already caused one unappliable migration.** #1280 records the full evidence: two apply attempts, both cancelled by the statement timeout, both rolled back cleanly.  ## What needs deciding  Someone has to work out what this view is actually for and price it accordingly. Sketch of the options, in no particular order:  1. **Drop the exact counts from the view** and expose them separately for callers that genuinely need them — most consumers appear to want classification, basis and status, not a live row count. 2. **Use `pg_class.reltuples` estimates** in the view, with the note column saying plainly that the count is an estimate. Exact counts then move to an explicit function a caller opts into. 3. **Materialise it**, refreshed when a capture completes rather than recomputed on every read. 4. **Keep it exact but scope it**, if a formulation exists that the planner CAN push a qualifier through — note the `VOLATILE` finding above says the obvious formulations do not.  **Do not \"fix\" this by raising `statement_timeout`.** That limit exists to stop a query holding production, and the query is the thing that is wrong.  ## Constraint on whoever takes it  That view has been replaced six times and is live in production. Its lineage is `20260814030000 → 20260814233342 → 20260819015333 → 20260819125713 → 20260819151536 → 20260820004338`, with #1283 (Sesame classification) likely to add another. **Re-derive from the current body on main at authoring time and say which one you used.** A stale derivation silently reverts every classification added after it — the single most dangerous mistake available in this file, and the reason every recent review of it has been asked to check exactly that.  Every pre-existing source must keep its classification, counting rule, basis, status and note, and the output column list must not change unless that is the explicit point of the change.\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 560\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - view api.source_capture_inventory\n  - table api.source_capture_inventory\n  - function api.source_capture_inventory_exact\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-25T02:36:12Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T01:08:01Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1284,"title":"api.source_capture_inventory does an exact count(*) per plm table on EVERY read, and the filter cannot be pushed down","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:50Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1284"},
{"body":"Found by the #1280 author while re-deriving the inventory view. Orchestrator marker #1229.\n\n## The problem\n\n`20260819212002_sesame_workshop_netx_source_landing.sql` created 19 `plm.sesame_*` tables and **never extended `api.source_capture_inventory`**, so they fall through to `source_system = 'other'` with `count_basis = 'retained_only'`.\n\n**This is the identical defect #1239 fixed for WildBrain.** Same shape, same consequence: the view answers, and the answer misleads.\n\n## Why it happened, and why the author was right\n\nThe Sesame author deliberately did not extend the view: it was outside its object claim, and it recorded that decision in the migration and in its PR rather than reaching past the claim. That was correct — the alternative is one author quietly adopting another's objects, which is what the object guard exists to prevent.\n\nIt also correctly observed that NOT extending the view keeps Sega's F1 classification tripwire green, since that tripwile treats an unmapped prefix as `other`.\n\nSo this is not an oversight to criticise. It is the predictable cost of per-claim isolation, and it now has a name.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nExtend `api.source_capture_inventory` additively so the 19 `plm.sesame_*` tables are classified with the correct counting rule, basis, status and note.\n\n**Re-derive from the CURRENT body on main at authoring time.** That lineage is now `20260814030000 → 20260814233342 → 20260819015333 (Sega) → 20260819125713 (Peanuts) → 20260819151536 → 20260820004338` (#1280). A `create or replace` built from a stale body would silently revert everything after it. Say in the PR which body you derived from and why.\n\nEvery pre-existing source must keep its classification, counting rule, `count_basis`, `latest_complete_status` and `count_note` unchanged, and the ten output columns must not change. Assert both.\n\n**Add the `v_map` row** to Sega's F1 tripwire and the equivalent in the Peanuts suite, exactly as #1239 did — the mechanism now tells you what to add when it fires.\n\n## Do NOT reintroduce the cost defect\n\n`20260819151536` could not apply to production because its verify block counted rows across every `plm` table and hit the statement timeout (#1280). Its replacement asserts the end state **from the catalogue** — `pg_class`, `pg_get_viewdef`, `pg_attribute`, ACL lookups — reading no `plm` table at all, measured at 14 ms.\n\n**Follow that pattern.** A verify block is production code that runs inside the apply transaction; one that is cheap on an empty preview and expensive on a full production database turns a passing rehearsal into an unappliable migration.\n\n## Related, and worth doing at the same time if the claim allows\n\nThe #1280 author also observed that **`api.source_capture_inventory` is expensive for ordinary readers**, not just for verify blocks: it performs an exact `count(*)` per `plm` table on every single read, via a `VOLATILE` `query_to_xml` subquery whose qualifier the planner cannot push down. That is a live cost paid by every consumer of the view, and it will grow with every landing schema. Recorded separately as its own concern; noted here because whoever opens this file should know.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 620\ndepends_on: #1280\nobjects:\n  - view api.source_capture_inventory\n  - table api.source_capture_inventory\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-25T01:14:53Z","createdAt":"2026-08-20T01:07:40Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1283,"title":"Sesame landing is unclassified in api.source_capture_inventory (same defect as #1239)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:52Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1283"},

Close when the work merges or is abandoned.","color":"B60205"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1281,"title":"CLAIM: #1280 supersede 20260819151536 - WildBrain classification and extra-key sweep with a production-cheap verify","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:54Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1281"},
{"body":"Found while promoting the licensor set. Orchestrator marker #1229. **Production is UNCHANGED and safe — both attempts rolled back cleanly.**\n\n## What happens\n\n`20260819151536_wildbrain_inventory_classification_and_finalize_extra_key_sweep.sql` applies to production and then **its own in-file verification block is cancelled by the statement timeout**:\n\n```\nERROR: canceling statement due to statement timeout (SQLSTATE 57014)\n```\n\nThe whole apply rolls back. Production's ledger reads the same before and after, both times:\n\n```\n   20260819151536 |                | 2026-08-19 15:15:36\n```\n\nBlank remote column = not applied. Verified on runs `32311544882` and `32312000123`, and again by an independent production dry-run (`success`, ledger re-read).\n\n**Reproducible, not transient.** Two apply attempts, same failure, same step.\n\n## Why it passes preview and fails production\n\nThe verify block counts rows across the `plm` tables to prove the classification took. Preview holds almost no licensor data. **Production holds the real NBCU, Paramount, Disney, Warner, WildBrain, Sega and Peanuts captures**, so the same `count(*)` sweep is orders of magnitude more expensive there and exceeds the statement timeout.\n\nThis is a **preview/production behavioural divergence**, the class of problem `AGENTS.md` warns about and #880 records: a preview rehearsal does not prove a production outcome. The rehearsal genuinely passed. The production apply genuinely cannot complete. Both are true.\n\nWorth noting the promotion review (Grok 4.6, sequence 235) **did flag the cost** — it described the verify step as taking \"the same shared-read cost Peanuts already paid today\" — and judged it acceptable because Peanuts had just succeeded. Peanuts got away with it; this one did not. The difference is that Peanuts ran before Sesame's 19 tables and this one after, but the honest reading is that the sweep was always close to the limit and nobody measured it against production.\n\n## Why this is awkward to fix\n\n- The migration is **merged to main** and **already applied to preview**, so `AGENTS.md` §4 forbids editing it. An applied migration is history.\n- It **cannot be applied to production as written**, so it is stranded: preview has it, production cannot take it.\n- A plain forward migration does not help on its own, because `20260819151536` itself must apply first for the ledger to advance.\n\n## What needs deciding\n\nSomeone has to choose between, roughly:\n\n1. **A superseding migration** that performs the same two changes (WildBrain classification in `api.source_capture_inventory`, and the extra-key sweep in `plm.finalize_wildbrain_capture`) with a verification that is cheap on production — scope the count to `plm.wildbrain_*` only, use `pg_class.reltuples` estimates, or drop the row count and assert the catalogue shape instead — plus a governed decision about `20260819151536`'s ledger state.\n2. **An agreed `statement_timeout` for the production apply session.** This is the tempting one and it is the weaker one: it widens a limit that exists to stop a migration holding production, in order to accommodate a verification that did not need to be expensive.\n\n**Recommendation: option 1.** The verify block is the thing that is wrong. It proves classification by counting rows when it could prove it from the catalogue, and it sweeps every `plm` table when it only needs the eleven WildBrain ones.\n\n## Lesson worth recording beyond this migration\n\n**Every in-file verification block is production code that runs inside the apply transaction.** A verify that is cheap on an empty preview and expensive on a full production database converts a passing rehearsal into an unappliable migration. Future landing and classification migrations should assert shape from the catalogue, and count rows only within their own tables.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 900\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - view api.source_capture_inventory\n  - table api.source_capture_inventory\n  - function plm.finalize_wildbrain_capture\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-20T01:50:00Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T23:13:50Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1280,"title":"20260819151536 CANNOT APPLY TO PRODUCTION: its own verify block hits the statement timeout","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:55Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1280"},
{"body":"## What is needed\n\nOne new table in `plm` to hold **inferred** Sega asset-to-property links, derived from\nfolder containment, kept strictly separate from the direct table that already exists.\n\nNo licensed value appears in this issue. All examples below are invented.\n\n## Why the existing table cannot hold this\n\n`plm.sega_asset_property` was added by #1196 (migration\n`20260819015333_sega_dsi_source_landing.sql`) and is correct as it stands:\n\n```\nCHECK (evidence_type = 'source_asset_ip_association')\n```\n\nThat constraint is deliberate and should NOT be relaxed. That table is for what the\nlicensor declares. Writing a folder-derived guess into it would make an inference\nindistinguishable from a portal fact, which is the exact failure the Sega landing design\nwas built to prevent.\n\n## Background: why an inference is needed at all\n\nThe first complete Sega capture loaded on 2026-08-19 (capture `sega-2026-08-19-full-v2`,\n7,000 assets). It found **zero** direct asset-to-property links. The portal was then\nsearched in full:\n\n- The file-listing method takes no property parameter. Its own client script enumerates\n  every parameter it accepts, and invented property parameters return identical counts.\n- The property dropdown on the library page is hidden and sits in a container named\n  `associationInput`. It authors an association; it does not filter by one. The feature\n  exists in the vendor product and this licensor has not populated it.\n- Six property-related page methods return HTTP 401 to a licensee account.\n- The product-approval area carries Licensor and Contract, but no Property.\n- Property registry rows have no detail view.\n\nSo the link is genuinely not published. Every asset does sit in at least one folder, and\nfolder names match property names once both sides are normalized. Measured on the loaded\ncapture: **77% of assets (5,377 of 7,000) become attributable, across 37 of 110\nproperties.** Matching raw labels without normalization reaches only 2%, so the\nnormalization rule is load-bearing and its version must be recorded per row.\n\n## Proposed table\n\n```\nplm.sega_asset_property_inferred\n  capture_id            uuid    not null\n  asset_source_id       text    not null\n  property_source_id    text    not null\n  evidence_key          text    not null   -- dedupes repeated evidence for one pair\n  catalog_source_id     text    not null   -- the folder that produced the match\n  match_method          text    not null\n  matched_property_key  text    not null   -- normalized form that matched, for audit\n  matched_catalog_key   text    not null\n  rule_version          text    not null\n  confidence            numeric not null\n  relationship_truth    text    not null default 'inferred'\n  raw                   jsonb   not null\n```\n\n### Keys and integrity\n\n- Primary key `(capture_id, evidence_key)`.\n- Composite foreign keys including `capture_id`, matching the pattern already used by the\n  #1196 tables so a relationship can never cross two captures:\n  - `(capture_id, asset_source_id)` → `plm.sega_asset`\n  - `(capture_id, property_source_id)` → `plm.sega_property`\n  - `(capture_id, catalog_source_id)` → `plm.sega_catalog`\n- Unique `(capture_id, asset_source_id, property_source_id, catalog_source_id)`.\n- Indexes on `(capture_id, asset_source_id)` and `(capture_id, property_source_id)`.\n\n### Constraints requested\n\n- `relationship_truth = 'inferred'` — pinned, exactly as `sega_character_evidence` does.\n- `confidence >= 0 and confidence <= 1`.\n- `match_method` in `('exact_label', 'normalized_label', 'subtree_of_match')` — the loader\n  needs to say whether a row came from an exact folder-name match, a match after\n  normalization, or inheritance from an ancestor folder that matched.\n- Non-empty `btrim()` checks on every text column, per the existing Sega tables.\n- `jsonb_typeof(raw) = 'object'`.\n\n### An asset legitimately gets MORE THAN ONE property\n\nPlease do not add a uniqueness constraint on `(capture_id, asset_source_id)`. Roughly 2% of\nattributed assets match two properties, and those are correct: this licensor's registry\nmixes platform-level and title-level properties, so one file can belong to both a platform\nentry and a title entry. Collapsing them to one winner would discard a true relationship.\n\n## Also needed\n\n1. `plm.finalize_sega_capture` should gain `asset_properties_inferred` in its\n   expected/observed count pairs and its orphaned-endpoint checks, matching how every other\n   Sega entity is gated. The count-pair array and the endpoint checks are the two places to\n   touch.\n2. `api.source_capture_inventory` should classify the new table under the Sega source, as\n   #1196 did for the others. Purely additive; do not move any other source's expression.\n3. Grants matching the other `plm.sega_*` tables: `service_role` gets SELECT and INSERT and\n   deliberately NOT update or delete. Please write the grants and RLS as explicit\n   per-table statements. #1196's first revision hid them behind a `DO` loop with\n   `execute format('… plm.%I …')`, which defeated the object guard and hid the privilege\n   model from readers; it was rewritten before merge.\n\n## Not requested\n\n- No change to `plm.sega_asset_property`. Leave its constraint alone.\n- No promotion into `core.*`. Canonical resolution is separate and out of scope here.\n- No change to any other licensor's tables.\n\n## Loader side\n\nThe loader lives in the private repository `u2giants/licensor-source-data` at\n`sega/loader/`. It already refuses a capture whose counts disagree with the tables, and it\nruns as `service_role`. Once this lands I will add the inferred rows to it, behind the same\nbegin/finalize gate, with tests against invented fixtures.\n\n## Verification\n\n- Migration applies cleanly to preview and every named object exists.\n- Inserting an inferred row for an asset and property from two different captures fails.\n- Inserting two properties for one asset in the same capture succeeds.\n- `relationship_truth` other than `inferred` is rejected; `confidence` outside 0..1 is\n  rejected; a `match_method` outside the three values is rejected.\n- A capture finalizes complete only when the inferred counts agree three ways, and is\n  rejected when they do not.\n- `api.source_capture_inventory` lists the new table under the Sega source and no other\n  source's row changes.\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 540\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - table plm.sega_asset_property_inferred\n  - column plm.sega_asset_property_inferred.relationship_truth\n  - index plm.idx_sega_asset_property_inferred_asset\n  - index plm.idx_sega_asset_property_inferred_property\n  - policy sega_asset_property_inferred_plm_read on plm.sega_asset_property_inferred\n  - policy sega_asset_property_inferred_service_read on plm.sega_asset_property_inferred\n  - function plm.finalize_sega_capture\n  - view api.source_capture_inventory\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T04:12:17Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T21:54:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1276,"title":"Add plm.sega_asset_property_inferred: folder-derived asset-to-property links, kept out of the direct table","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:35:57Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1276"},

{"body":"Found in passing while fixing #1218, and deliberately not fixed there.\n\n## The symptom\n\n`python scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py` fails one test on a developer machine:\n\n```\nFAIL: test_preview_producer_paths_cover_runtime_read_data_files\n```\n\nwith a message listing files under `supabase/.temp/` — `gotrue-version`, `linked-project.json`, `pooler-url`, `postgres-version`, `project-ref`, `rest-version`, `storage-migration`, `storage-version` — as *\"neither pinned in `PREVIEW_PRODUCER_PATHS` nor given a written reason in `PREVIEW_RUNTIME_DATA_EXEMPTIONS`\"*.\n\n## The cause\n\nThose files are written by the `supabase` CLI when a project is linked. They are gitignored, so they never reach CI — which is why the check is green there and red locally. The test scans the working directory rather than the tracked tree, so it sees whatever the local CLI happened to leave behind.\n\n**Confirmed pre-existing:** it fails identically on unmodified `main` with the change stashed.\n\n## Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating\n\nThe suite is otherwise 103 tests of the last gate before a production write. A suite that is *expected* to be one-red locally trains everyone to skim the summary line instead of reading it, and the next genuine local failure gets waved past as \"oh, that's just the temp thing\". That is the same habit #1186 and #1266 are about.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nRestrict the scan to tracked files (`git ls-files`), or exempt `supabase/.temp/` explicitly with a written reason, as the exemption mechanism already supports. Prefer whichever keeps the check's real purpose intact: it exists to catch a producer-surface file that a preview job could read but that nobody pinned — and `supabase/.temp/` genuinely is on that surface, so an exemption should say why it cannot matter rather than simply hiding it.\n\nLow priority. Nothing is unsafe; the check does the right thing in CI.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 200\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-28T23:21:25Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T19:18:03Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACoQNUrw","name":"bug","description":"Something isn't working","color":"d73a4a"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1268,"title":"scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py fails on any machine that has run the supabase CLI","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:02Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1268"},
{"body":"**Two commits of real work have no pull request and live on exactly one branch. This issue exists so they are not lost.**\n\n## What is orphaned\n\nBranch: **`claude/review-evidence-coverage-rule`**\n\n| commit | subject |\n|---|---|\n| `33b030c` | docs: implementation plan for ColdLion landing phases 2-6, with the owner's per-field decisions |\n| `de4e21a` | docs: correct the ColdLion plan after Grok review — component merch groups are NOT dropped, itemDetails keys on itemPkey, orderHistory line key is unresolved |\n\nThree files:\n\n- `docs/plan_coldlion-landing-phases-2-6.md`\n- `docs/coldlion-field-decisions-20260819.csv`\n- `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-19T1500Z-al8960ofc-claude-coldlion-phases-2-6-plan.md`\n\n## How it got there\n\nA concurrent session pushed those two commits onto a branch that belonged to unrelated work (the #1220 review-evidence rule). The branch owner did **not** rewrite the branch. My own commit was cherry-picked onto a clean branch instead and merged as #1264, and PR #1260 was left open with its branch intact precisely so these two commits survive.\n\n## Verified: this is the only copy\n\n- PR #1263 (`plan-coldlion-landing-phases-2-6`) contains only `docs/business-rules/merchandise-and-product-taxonomy.md` and `docs/coldlion-raw-landing-schema-design.md`. **None of the three files above.**\n- None of the three files exist on `main`.\n\n**Do not delete branch `claude/review-evidence-coverage-rule` or close PR #1260 until this work is claimed.**\n\n## Why it matters\n\nAlbert authorized ColdLion phases 2-6 in full on 2026-08-19 (see #1204: *\"Build all of phases 2-6, then backfill\"*). This plan is the first execution artifact of that decision. Phase 2 alone covers the biggest gap — 13 of 19 ColdLion feeds currently have nowhere to land.\n\n## What to do\n\nWhoever owns this work: open a pull request from `claude/review-evidence-coverage-rule`, or cherry-pick `33b030c` and `de4e21a` onto a branch of your own. Then the branch can be retired and PR #1260 closed.\n\n## A blocker you will hit\n\nThe **PII forward guard** fails on this work. `docs/plan_coldlion-landing-phases-2-6.md:513` carries a `postgresql://…@aws-1-us-east-1.pooler.supabase.com:6543/postgres` connection string, and the guard reads the Supabase pooler username as an email address.\n\n**No credential is exposed** — the URL was checked and carries a username only, no password. So this is a false positive on a service connection string, not a leak. But the guard is a required check, so it needs either the domain added to the allowlist in `.github/workflows/pii-forward-guard.yml` or the `pii-guard-allow` label. Make that call deliberately rather than reflexively.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 700\ndepends_on: 1204\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-19T20:10:31Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T19:18:02Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1267,"title":"ORPHANED WORK: the ColdLion phases 2-6 plan exists only on branch claude/review-evidence-coverage-rule, with no pull request","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:03Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1267"},
{"body":"## What happened\n\nOn 2026-08-19, PR #1264 (a 26-line docs change) could not merge because the required check **SQL migration guards** sat `in_progress` for **42 minutes**. The job was stuck on one step:\n\n```yaml\n- name: Install SQL check dependencies\n  run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y ripgrep\n```\n\nCancelling and re-running it made the same job complete in **51 seconds**, all steps green. So it was a transient package-mirror stall, not a defect in anything being tested.\n\nA second run, 32274680584, stalled the same way at the same step and had to be cancelled by hand.\n\n## The gap\n\n`grep -n \"timeout-minutes\" .github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml` returns **nothing**. Not one of its five jobs — `validate`, `preview`, `production-dry-run`, `production-apply-review`, `production-apply` — sets a timeout, so every one of them inherits GitHub's default of **360 minutes**.\n\nA required check that can hang for six hours is not a gate, it is a hostage situation. And it is worse than ordinary flakiness, for the same reason #1186 gave: an operator cannot distinguish a stall from a slow run without opening the log, so the learned response becomes \"cancel and re-run\" — which is exactly the reflex that eventually waves a real failure through.\n\n## This is the second instance today\n\n#1186 covered the identical shape in `db-data-admin.yml`, where `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` hung ~28 minutes. That one is fixed in PR #1244: bounded at `timeout-minutes: 6` with a single retry and a `::warning::` naming it. **The same treatment is wanted here** — the pattern, not just the one step.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\n1. Give every job in `shared-supabase-migrations.yml` a `timeout-minutes` sized to its real work. `validate` completes in about a minute, so a small number is generous.\n2. Bound the dependency-install steps specifically, and retry once, matching the shape merged in #1244. There are **six** such steps across the workflows that currently have no bound:\n   - `shared-supabase-migrations.yml:117` (`ripgrep`) — the one that stalled\n   - `shared-supabase-migrations.yml:437`, `:764`, `:902`, `:1100` (`postgresql-client`)\n   - `guarded-migration-merge.yml:37` (`ripgrep`)\n   - `database-contract-tests.yml:125` and `preview-ledger-orphan-reconciliation.yml:53` (`postgresql-client`)\n3. **Care required on the production jobs.** `production-apply` and `production-apply-review` write to production. A timeout there must fail closed and must not be able to interrupt a job mid-apply in a way that leaves a half-applied batch — see #870, which already covers the guard being silent when production rests inside a half-applied atomic batch. Size those timeouts generously and say in the PR why the chosen number cannot truncate real work.\n\n## Why this is not urgent but should not be dropped\n\nNothing is unsafe: a stalled job blocks a merge, it does not promote anything. The cost is entirely operator time and the habit it teaches. But it has now cost two manual interventions in one day.\n\nNot a database change. No migration, no schema, no RLS.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-19T22:02:08Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T19:17:34Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACoQNUrw","name":"bug","description":"Something isn't working","color":"d73a4a"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1266,"title":"No job in shared-supabase-migrations.yml has a timeout, so a stalled apt-get blocks merges for hours (observed: 42 minutes)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1266"},
{"body":"Found by the #1140 author (PR #1256) when its own guard contract passed for the wrong reason. Orchestrator marker #1229.\n\n## The defect\n\n`ci_authorize_licensing_contract_test()` pre-issues **100 blanket `canonical_merge` authorizations, for every column subset, inside each test's own transaction.**\n\nThe consequence is the worst kind: **it silently authorizes exactly the writes a guard contract needs refused.** A licensing-guard test that does not explicitly clear those rows first is not testing its guard. It is testing a database in which the guard has already been told to permit everything, and it passes.\n\nThis is the same failure class the repo has been closing all week — a check that returns green for a reason unrelated to the thing it claims to prove — except here it sits in shared test scaffolding, so it can invalidate any number of suites at once rather than one.\n\n## How it surfaced\n\nThe #1140 author's first contract run went green. On investigation the guard was not being exercised at all; the pre-issued authorizations were satisfying it. Its file now **clears them and proves the empty baseline** before asserting anything, and only then did the contract become a real test. That was the first CI failure on PR #1256 and the author recorded it as a genuine defect in its own test rather than working around it.\n\n## Why this needs its own issue and its own review\n\nThe helper is used by other test files. Changing it could turn other suites red for reasons unrelated to whoever touches it, and some of those suites may be passing today only because of it. **That is the thing to find out, and it should not be discovered by surprise inside an unrelated PR.** PR #1256 deliberately does not touch the helper.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\n1. **Enumerate every test file that calls `ci_authorize_licensing_contract_test()`** and, for each, determine whether it is currently proving what it claims. Expect some to be passing vacuously.\n2. Decide the correct design. Options, roughly in order of preference:\n   - the helper issues nothing by default and callers request exactly the authorizations they need;\n   - or it keeps the blanket behaviour behind an explicit opt-in with a name that says what it does;\n   - or every guard contract is required to clear and prove the empty baseline first, enforced by a check rather than by convention.\n3. Whichever is chosen, **there must be a test that fails if the pre-issued rows come back.** A convention that guard contracts \"should\" clear them is not enforcement.\n\n## Related\n\n- #1140 / PR #1256 — where it was found. It clears the rows in its own file; that is the correct scope for that PR.\n- #1223 — 32 guards in the promotion-evidence chain with no test that fails when they are disabled. Same underlying theme: a guard nobody has falsified is not known to be a guard.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 680\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:11:49Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T16:31:23Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1262,"title":"SYSTEMIC: ci_authorize_licensing_contract_test() pre-issues 100 blanket authorizations, so a guard contract can pass while testing nothing","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:07Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1262"},
{"body":"Hit three times in one afternoon while three migration authors worked in parallel. Orchestrator marker #1229.\n\n## What happens\n\n`supabase/tests against an ephemeral database` hits the workflow's 45-minute ceiling while still on the **`Install psql`** step — an `apt-get` stall on the hosted runner. Every step after it is marked **skipped**: `Start an empty ephemeral database`, the migration replay, and `Run every supabase/tests/*.sql`. **Not one line of SQL executes.**\n\nObserved on PR #1256 (run `32270255274`), with PRs #1255 and #1257 having launched the same job within four minutes. This is the hosted-runner starvation mode already described in `AGENTS.md` §5.2-A.\n\n## Why it matters more than it looks\n\n**It reports as a red X on the PR.** A red `supabase/tests against an ephemeral database` is indistinguishable, at a glance, from a genuine contract-test failure — and this is the single check that runs contract files against a real from-empty database, so it is the one nobody may wave through. Today it cost an author a full diagnostic round to establish that its own SQL had never run.\n\nThe failure mode also gets worse exactly when the orchestrator is working correctly: three migration-author lanes running concurrently is the designed state, and it is what triggers this.\n\n## What a fix should do\n\n1. **Distinguish infrastructure failure from test failure.** A timeout during `Install psql`, before the database even starts, must not surface as the same signal as a contract test that ran and failed. Fail with a distinct, named message — `::error::CI INFRASTRUCTURE: psql install did not complete; no test executed` — so nobody has to read the log to tell the two apart. This is the same principle as the repo's rule that a silent failure must alert loudly.\n2. **Stop paying for the install.** Use a container image or a runner that already has the client, or cache it. Installing a PostgreSQL client from `apt` on every run of a 45-minute job is the fragile part.\n3. **Consider serialising or staggering** the job across concurrent PRs, or raising the ceiling — but only after (1) and (2), because a longer ceiling on a starved runner just fails later.\n\n## Not a fix\n\nDo not \"fix\" this by making the job non-required or by treating a red result as advisory. It is the only executed proof in the pipeline.\n\n## Cross-reference\n\nRelated but distinct: #1258 (a from-empty replay leaves `core.taxonomy_owner_ruling` absent). Both are about the fidelity and reliability of the from-empty replay, which several safety guards now depend on.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 620\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-19T21:03:56Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T16:15:56Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1261,"title":"The ephemeral-database suite times out on 'Install psql' when several PRs run it at once, and reports as a test failure","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:08Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1261"},
{"body":"Three Low findings from the exact-head review of PR #1256 (Kimi K3, rotation sequence 212, issue #1140). Orchestrator marker #1229. **None blocked that merge** — they are recorded here so they are not lost.\n\n## 1. Low — `supersedes` is admitted but its value is never bound\n\n`supabase/migrations/20260819151527_*.sql:234` admits `supersedes` in the allowed metadata key set but never binds its VALUE, and admits it even when `ruling_migration = '20260802171000'`, whose historical statement (`20260802171000:261-268`) carries no `supersedes` key at all.\n\nSo the contract's promise of \"ONLY that exact statement\" is slightly overstated for the metadata provenance payload: a planted authorization could record an arbitrary `supersedes` pointer into immutable metadata and audit evidence.\n\nExploitation requires a privileged authorization insert, and the row, column, status and ordering bindings are all unaffected — which is why it is a Low and not a High. But immutable evidence that can carry an arbitrary pointer is worth tightening: either bind the value, or refuse the key under the ruling migration that has no such key.\n\n## 2. Low — the \"exactly one outstanding\" check ignores expiry\n\n`20260819151527_*.sql:255-262`. A committed-but-abandoned FR authorization — say from a migration that inserted the row and then failed before writing — **blocks all future FR writes until a superuser cleans it up by hand.**\n\nThis fails CLOSED and matches the stated design intent (\"none may be left behind unconsumed\"), so it is not a security problem. It is a permanent-latch operational property, and **it must be written into the FR bundle runbook** so that whoever hits it recognises it instead of debugging the guard.\n\n## 3. Low — the contract test cannot run against preview\n\n`supabase/tests/fr_owner_ruling_transaction_bound_authorization_contracts.sql:73` inserts `code = 'FR'`, which violates `core.licensor`'s `unique nulls not distinct (code)` (`20260621150815:188`) on any database where the real FR row already exists.\n\nIt fails loudly — red, never silently green — and the test's own header scopes it to the from-empty CI database. But the in-file comment \"On preview it already exists\" could mislead someone into running it there and reading the resulting failure as a defect in the guard. Reword it to say plainly that the file is CI-only and why.\n\n## Context for whoever picks this up\n\nPR #1256 closed a real and live hole: `20260817225127` widened the `write_kind` CHECK to admit `owner_ruling_fr_inactivation` and taught the guard function nothing, making that write_kind the widest authorization in the system. These three items are polish on the contract that closed it, not a reopening of it.\n\nRelated: #1258 (the from-empty replay leaves `core.taxonomy_owner_ruling` absent — the review confirmed the guard fails CLOSED in that case, raising 42P01 and aborting the write).\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 400\ndepends_on: #1140\nobjects:\n  - table plm.licensing_write_authorization\n  - function app.enforce_licensing_write_authority\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-28T17:40:54Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T16:08:17Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1259,"title":"FR authorization follow-ups: an unbound supersedes value, an expiry-blind latch, and a test that cannot run on preview","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:10Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1259"},
{"body":"Found by the #1140 author while building the transaction-bound authorization contract (PR #1256). Orchestrator marker #1229.\r\n\r\n## The problem\r\n\r\nIn a **from-empty replay** — which is what the `supabase/tests against an ephemeral database` CI job does, and what any rebuild of preview does — both `20260802171000` and `20260818174350` abort on `select ... into strict` for the FR and FK rows.\r\n\r\nThe consequence: **`core.taxonomy_owner_ruling` does not exist on the CI database at all.** The #1140 contract test has to create it as scaffolding inside its own rolled-back transaction just to have something to test against.\r\n\r\n## Why this matters beyond a test inconvenience\r\n\r\n1. **Whoever assembles the FR bundle cannot assume the table is there.** The guard in PR #1256 READS `core.taxonomy_owner_ruling` to prove ordering — that read is precisely what makes a standalone status flip impossible. If the table is absent in a given environment, that ordering proof cannot run.\r\n2. **This is the same class of problem as the preview rebuild on 2026-08-18.** When preview was rebuilt from empty, migrations that assume prior data behave differently from migrations replayed onto an existing database. A from-empty replay is not a theoretical scenario here; it has already happened once this month.\r\n3. It means the CI suite is not exercising the FR path against a realistic catalog, so a defect in that path would not turn CI red.\r\n\r\n## What needs deciding\r\n\r\nWhether the from-empty replay SHOULD produce `core.taxonomy_owner_ruling`, and if so how — a seed, a conditional creation, a `ci-bootstrap` baseline entry, or an explicit documented statement that the FR path is not replayable from empty and why that is acceptable.\r\n\r\nDo not \"fix\" this by loosening the `select ... into strict`. Those statements are refusing to guess, which is correct behaviour; the question is what the environment should contain, not whether the migration should tolerate its absence.\r\n\r\n## Related\r\n\r\n- #1140 / PR #1256 — the contract that surfaced it. It does NOT fix this and does not need to.\r\n- AGENTS.md §6.5 — records that `20260802171000` is permanently retired from production, superseded by `20260818174350`.\r\n- #949 (migration ledger drift) and #901 (preview behind production) are adjacent replay-fidelity issues.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\r\nroute: repo-maintenance\r\npriority: 550\r\ndepends_on: #1143\r\nwrites:`nreads:\r\n```\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T19:41:43Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T15:43:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1258,"title":"core.taxonomy_owner_ruling does not exist in a from-empty replay — both FR migrations abort on select..into strict","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:12Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1258"},
