{"body":"Found while implementing owner ruling #1249 (\"scrape data should be visible to Licensing department users\"). Orchestrator marker #1229.\n\n## The finding\n\n`plm.opa_property_character` — the Disney OPA scrape landing table — has this read policy (`20260807170000_...:189-196`):\n\n```sql\nusing (true)\n```\n\nThat is not \"Licensing can read it\". That is **every signed-in account can read it**, including roles named `vendor` and `viewer`. Every other landing schema restricts reads to administrators, Licensing, Sales and PLM-app users.\n\nWarner's landing had the identical defect and was fixed on 2026-08-10 (`20260810110000`), whose own header says the original state meant \"every signed-in account… can read Warner's confidential STARLABS data.\" Disney was not fixed at the same time. `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md:462-472` already describes this shape as \"definitively wide open.\"\n\nTo be precise about the exposure: `plm` is not PostgREST-exposed, so this is reachable over a direct SQL connection rather than from the web app. It is not an open door to the internet. It is still the wrong permission on business-confidential data held under a commercial licensing relationship.\n\n## Why this is a separate issue and not folded into #1249\n\nAlbert ruled that Licensing SHOULD see scrape data. He did not rule that vendors should stop seeing it. Removing access from a group is a business change, not an implementation detail of his ruling, so it gets its own decision, its own review and its own promotion. #1249 deliberately only ADDS access, to WildBrain and NBCU.\n\n## The question for Albert — one question, plain\n\n**Should outside vendors be able to read raw Disney scrape data?**\n\n- **No, restrict it** (recommended) — bring Disney OPA in line with every other licensor: administrators, Licensing, Sales and PLM-app users only. This is what Warner already does.\n- Yes, leave it open to everyone signed in.\n\nIf the answer is \"no, restrict it\", nothing else is needed from him and this becomes ordinary structural work.\n\n## Before implementing, check whether anything actually relies on the open policy\n\nA vendor-facing or viewer-facing feature reading this table would break. `plm` is not on the API, so a breaking caller would be a direct-SQL job rather than a screen. Prove it either way before promoting, the same way the NBCU gate promotion was proved against its live loader.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - policy opa_property_character_read on plm.opa_property_character\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-19T15:30:37Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T15:15:00Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1251,"title":"[ALBERT] Disney OPA scrape data is readable by ANY signed-in account, including vendors","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:18Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1251"},
{"body":"**OWNER RULING (Albert Hazan, in chat, 2026-08-19).** Verbatim:\r\n\r\n> \"scrape data should be visible to Licensing department users.\"\r\n\r\n## This is implementable with an existing mechanism. No new concept is needed.\r\n\r\n`licensing` is already first class in this database:\r\n\r\n- a value of the `app.app_role` enum (`20260621150714_foundation.sql:19` — `administrator, sales, licensing, designer, viewer, vendor`)\r\n- a seeded row in `app.role` (`20260621150815_app_core.sql:338-348`)\r\n- assignable per user through `app.user_role` (`:26-34`)\r\n- testable in RLS with `app.has_role('licensing')` / `app.has_any_role(...)` (`:365-397`), which resolves through EITHER a live `app.user_role` row OR a JWT `app_metadata.roles` entry\r\n\r\n## CORRECTION to the original report on this issue\r\n\r\nI originally wrote that the Sega landing \"grants `authenticated` SELECT on its licensed tables\", implying every signed-in user can read them. **That was wrong and I am correcting it rather than leaving it to mislead.** The `grant select ... to authenticated` is required plumbing; the RLS policy is what decides, and Sega's is:\r\n\r\n```sql\r\ncreate policy <t>_plm_read on plm.<t>\r\n  for select to authenticated using (\r\n    app.has_app_access('plm')\r\n    or app.has_role('administrator')\r\n    or app.has_any_role(array['sales', 'licensing']::app.app_role[])\r\n  );\r\n```\r\n\r\nSo Sega and Peanuts **already satisfy the ruling.** The problem is narrower and different from what I described.\r\n\r\n## The actual state across every landing schema\r\n\r\n| Schema | SELECT granted to | RLS predicate for `authenticated` | Satisfies the ruling? |\r\n|---|---|---|---|\r\n| `plm.sega_*` | authenticated, service_role | house pattern (admin / plm-access / sales+licensing) | YES |\r\n| `plm.peanuts_*` | authenticated, service_role | house pattern | YES |\r\n| `plm.dcp_*` (DCP Vault) | authenticated, service_role | house pattern | YES |\r\n| `plm.wb_*` (Warner) | authenticated, service_role | house pattern | YES |\r\n| `plm.pmt_*` (Paramount) | authenticated, service_role | `admin / sales / licensing / designer` — no plm-access | YES |\r\n| **`plm.wildbrain_*`** | **service_role ONLY** | **none** | **NO — Licensing cannot read it** |\r\n| **`plm.nbcu_*`** | **service_role ONLY** | **none** | **NO — Licensing cannot read it** |\r\n| **`plm.opa_property_character` (Disney)** | authenticated, service_role | **`using (true)`** | over-broad, see #NEW |\r\n\r\n## What this issue now does\r\n\r\nBring **WildBrain** and **NBCU** up to the established house predicate so Licensing can read them, exactly as Sega, Peanuts, DCP and Warner already do:\r\n\r\n```sql\r\ngrant select on plm.<t> to authenticated;\r\ncreate policy <t>_plm_read on plm.<t>\r\n  for select to authenticated using (\r\n    app.has_app_access('plm')\r\n    or app.has_role('administrator')\r\n    or app.has_any_role(array['sales', 'licensing']::app.app_role[])\r\n  );\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Deliberately NOT narrowing anything.** Albert ruled that Licensing SHOULD see this data. He did not rule that Sales or PLM-app users should stop seeing it, and removing access nobody asked to remove is a scope expansion, not an implementation. Paramount's extra `designer` and missing `has_app_access('plm')` are likewise left alone — changing them removes access from designers.\r\n\r\nThe one genuinely over-broad case, Disney OPA's `using (true)`, is split into its own issue because removing vendor and viewer access from confidential licensor data IS a business change and deserves its own decision and its own review.\r\n\r\n## Two facts the owner should know, neither of which blocks this work\r\n\r\n1. **`plm` is NOT PostgREST-exposed.** Production `pgrst.db_schemas` is `public, graphql_public, api, crm, pim, core, app` (`AGENTS.md` §8.1). So this grant is reachable only over a direct SQL connection, not from any web app. If \"visible to Licensing users\" is meant to mean visible in a screen, that needs a separate `api.*` view, which `docs/licensor-source-shape-decisions-20260811.md:526` explicitly defers as a separate access decision. **This issue makes the database permission correct; it does not put the data on a screen.**\r\n2. **A missing role grant is silent.** Per `docs/popdam-access-provisioning.md`, a user with no `app.user_role` row gets HTTP 200 and an empty array, not an error. Whether the actual Licensing staff hold the `licensing` role today is a DATA question, not a schema one, and is not answerable from this repo — no user-to-role assignments are committed. Someone should verify real Licensing accounts actually carry it, or the ruling will be satisfied on paper and not in practice.\r\n\r\n## Requirements\r\n\r\n- Match the house predicate character for character. Do not retype it — copy it from `20260819015333`.\r\n- Explicit per-table statements. No `DO` loop with `execute format`, which defeats the object guard and hides the privilege model.\r\n- The `service_read` policies already present must be left intact.\r\n- Tests must prove, behaviourally: a `licensing` user CAN read; an `administrator` CAN; a user with `plm` app access CAN; a `vendor` and a `viewer` and a role-less authenticated user CANNOT; `anon` CANNOT. Prove it for both schemas, and prove it fails without the change.\r\n- An RLS policy is not a grant and a grant is not a policy (AGENTS.md §11). Both are required, and both must be asserted.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 800\r\ndepends_on:\r\nobjects:\r\n  - table plm.wildbrain_asset\r\n  - policy wildbrain_asset_plm_read on plm.wildbrain_asset\r\n  - table plm.wildbrain_asset_category\r\n  - policy wildbrain_asset_category_plm_read on plm.wildbrain_asset_category\r\n  - table plm.wildbrain_asset_character\r\n  - policy wildbrain_asset_character_plm_read on plm.wildbrain_asset_character\r\n  - table plm.wildbrain_asset_guide\r\n  - policy wildbrain_asset_guide_plm_read on plm.wildbrain_asset_guide\r\n  - table plm.wildbrain_asset_nature\r\n  - policy wildbrain_asset_nature_plm_read on plm.wildbrain_asset_nature\r\n  - table plm.wildbrain_capture\r\n  - policy wildbrain_capture_plm_read on plm.wildbrain_capture\r\n  - table plm.wildbrain_character\r\n  - policy wildbrain_character_plm_read on plm.wildbrain_character\r\n  - table plm.wildbrain_creative_group\r\n  - policy wildbrain_creative_group_plm_read on plm.wildbrain_creative_group\r\n  - table plm.wildbrain_era\r\n  - policy wildbrain_era_plm_read on plm.wildbrain_era\r\n  - table plm.wildbrain_guide\r\n  - policy wildbrain_guide_plm_read on plm.wildbrain_guide\r\n  - table plm.wildbrain_guide_alias\r\n  - policy wildbrain_guide_alias_plm_read on plm.wildbrain_guide_alias\r\n  - table plm.nbcu_asset\r\n  - policy nbcu_asset_plm_read on plm.nbcu_asset\r\n  - table plm.nbcu_asset_character\r\n  - policy nbcu_asset_character_plm_read on plm.nbcu_asset_character\r\n  - table plm.nbcu_asset_ip_family\r\n  - policy nbcu_asset_ip_family_plm_read on plm.nbcu_asset_ip_family\r\n  - table plm.nbcu_asset_metadata_value\r\n  - policy nbcu_asset_metadata_value_plm_read on plm.nbcu_asset_metadata_value\r\n  - table plm.nbcu_asset_property\r\n  - {"body":"Owner ruling **`AGENTS.md` §6.16** (Albert Hazan, 2026-08-19, PR #1241):\n\n> \"this system has no connection to license term or territory. remove any and every record of that from this system for all licensors\"\n\nand:\n\n> \"you're not supposed to be referring to or using the contracts. the data scrapes + coldlion api feed are canonical.\"\n\nThis issue is the removal work. It replaces #732, which is closed as void.\n\n## 1. Drop `plm.nbcu_right`\n\nCreated by `20260810070000_nbcu_creative_asset_factory_landing.sql` lines 167-193. Its entire content is contract-derived and there is nothing left in it once contracts stop being a source:\n\n| column | why it goes |\n|---|---|\n| `business_title` | transcribed from Schedule \"B\" |\n| `rights_scope` (`title` / `franchise` / `all_related`) | a contract classification |\n| `restriction_text` | contract restrictions |\n| `global_rule_applied` | contract section (c) |\n| `source_document` | names the contract |\n\n**Nothing has ever been loaded into it.** #732 recorded that `restriction_text` and `global_rule_applied` are empty and no load has run, so the drop costs no data.\n\nKnown dependants to handle in the same change — do not drop the table and leave these dangling:\n- `20260811070000_nbcu_asset_ip_family_relationship.sql:371` — `select count(*) into v_n from plm.nbcu_right where capture_id = p_capture_id;`\n- `20260810080000_nbcu_revoke_default_granted_write_privileges.sql:61` and `20260810180000_plm_default_privilege_hole_and_pg17_maintain_revokes.sql:200,289` — `nbcu_right` appears in the revoke table lists.\n- Any capture-publication or completeness gate that counts rights rows. **A gate that silently passes because its subject table vanished is worse than the table.** Check before dropping, and make the gate fail loudly or be removed deliberately.\n\n## 2. Sweep every other licensor for the same thing\n\nThe ruling says **all** licensors, not just NBCU. Search every licensor landing schema — Disney/OPA, DCP Vault, Warner/STARLABS, Paramount, Peanuts, Sesame, WildBrain, Sega — for any column or stored value expressing:\n\n- licence term, start date, end date, expiry, renewal\n- territory, region, or geographic limitation\n- rights scope, restriction text, or permitted-use language\n\nReport what you find before dropping anything beyond `plm.nbcu_right`. Some of these words appear innocently (a portal's own `region` facet on an asset is portal-scraped data, not a licence territory) — **the test is whether the value came from a contract or from a scrape.** Scraped values stay.\n\n## 3. Documentation\n\n`nbcu/SUPABASE-IMPORT-SPEC.md` (private repo) cites the contract as source of record. That framing is now wrong repo-wide. Correct it to name the portal scrape, and demote any contract reference to a superseded note.\n\n## Process\n\nStructural change to production tables: branch, PR, preview rehearsal, guarded merge, production evidence chain. §4.2 applies — prove which database you are connected to before any DROP and quote the proof.\n\nRelated: #732 (closed as void), `AGENTS.md` §6.15 and §6.16.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - table plm.nbcu_right\n  - table plm.wb_property_character\n  - view api.wb_property_character\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-25T16:13:47Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T12:38:33Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1242,"title":"Drop plm.nbcu_right and sweep licence term/territory records for every licensor (owner ruling AGENTS.md §6.16)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:21Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1242"},
{"body":"Recommended by the #1221 / #1222 author (PR #1236) and deliberately left out of that PR. Orchestrator marker #1229.\n\n## The asymmetry\n\n`plm.finalize_sega_capture` sweeps `expected_counts` for keys it does not recognise and applies the full type / non-negative-integer / range rule to them. `plm.finalize_wildbrain_capture` has no such sweep at all.\n\nThe two schemas were written from the same template days apart, so this reads as an oversight rather than a decision — and the next person to read both will assume the WildBrain gate refuses things it does not.\n\n## Why it was not fixed in PR #1236\n\nRight call by that author: #1221 does not ask for it, and adding it would change refusal behaviour beyond the two issues that PR closes. A gate that starts refusing new shapes is a behaviour change and deserves its own review.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nDecide whether the WildBrain gate should sweep unrecognised `expected_counts` keys, and if so add it with the same rule Sega uses, plus tests that fail without it. If the answer is that WildBrain should NOT sweep, write the reason into a comment in the function so the asymmetry stops looking accidental.\n\nDo not start this until #1221 / #1222 (PR #1236) has merged — it rewrites the same function body.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: #1221, #1222\nobjects:\n  - function plm.finalize_wildbrain_capture\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:23:32Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T12:09:28Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Found by the Peanuts landing author (#1217 / PR #1234) while extending the same view. Orchestrator marker #1229.\n\n## The problem\n\nThe WildBrain DAM landing migration `20260819014639` created `plm.wildbrain_*` but never extended `api.source_capture_inventory`. Every sibling landing schema classifies itself there; WildBrain does not. It therefore falls through to `source_system = 'other'` with `count_basis = 'retained_only'`, which is silently wrong rather than absent — the view answers, and the answer is misleading.\n\nSega (`20260819015333`) DID extend the view in-file, which is why the omission was not obvious.\n\n## Why it was not fixed in PR #1234\n\nCorrectly refused by that author: fixing it there means one author's migration adopting another author's tables, which is exactly the cross-author overwrite the object guard exists to prevent. It needs its own claim. It is recorded in a comment block in `20260819112505` and in PR #1234.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nExtend `api.source_capture_inventory` additively so `plm.wildbrain_*` is classified with the correct counting rule, basis, status and note. Every pre-existing source must keep its classification unchanged, and the ten output columns must not change — assert both in tests. Re-derive from the CURRENT body on main at authoring time, not from `20260819015333`: PR #1234 also rewrites this view, so whichever merges second must re-derive rather than resolve the `create or replace` conflict mechanically.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 640\ndepends_on: #1217\nobjects:\n  - view api.source_capture_inventory\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:23:32Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T12:09:27Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1239,"title":"WildBrain landing is unclassified in api.source_capture_inventory (falls through to 'other'/'retained_only')","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:24Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1239"},
{"body":"Owner ruling **`AGENTS.md` §6.15** (Albert Hazan, 2026-08-19, recorded in PR #1237) settles that \"list A\" is deleted. This issue is the WORK. The ruling deliberately did not authorize the drop on its own authority.\n\nHis words:\n\n> \"Delete list A completely. There should be 2 types of lists: the lists that are the direct results of scrapes from the licensor websites, and the list that comes in from the Coldlion api.\"\n\n## What is in scope\n\n| object | rows | note |\n|---|---|---|\n| `core.property` | 256 | uuid keys, **no source-ID columns at all** |\n| `core.character` | 0 | empty |\n| `core.property_character` | 0 | empty |\n| `core.licensor` | 26 | **conditional** — only if it proves unused; it mixes licensors, brands and franchises and is referenced by more than the property tables |\n\n`core.property_licensor_id_fkey → core.licensor(id)` binds them.\n\n## Explicitly NOT in scope — do not touch\n\n`core.properties_and_characters` (10,122 rows), `core.property_character_associations` (9,622 rows), `core.\"licenseList\"`. This is Universe B and it survives.\n\n## The order of work — none of it is optional\n\n1. **Blast radius.** Prove which applications read each of the four objects: DesignFlow, PopDAM, PopPIM, PopCRM, DB Data Admin, and any view, function, RPC, trigger or RLS policy in this database. `core.licensor` most likely has readers the property tables do not; if so it stays and only its three companions go.\n2. **Salvage.** Anything genuinely worth keeping out of the 256 `core.property` rows must be moved into a surviving list FIRST, **with its licensor source ID attached**. Without a source ID it cannot live in Universe B and it is gone. 16 of the 256 rows are stored at CHARACTER grain inside a table named `property` — do not carry that mistake forward.\n3. **Compatibility.** If any app still reads these, either move that app first or land a temporary view and register it on #974 (mandatory-cleanup tracker), so the shim cannot become permanent.\n4. **Migration.** Normal shared-db process — branch, PR, preview rehearsal, guarded merge, production evidence chain. §4.2 applies: prove which database you are connected to before any destructive statement, and quote the proof.\n\n## Why this must not be rushed\n\nThese are DROPs on production master-data tables. Nothing in step 1 is a formality — a wrong blast-radius read here breaks applications silently, and there is no undo once the rows are gone. If step 1 cannot be completed with evidence, stop and say so rather than dropping.\n\nRelated: #640 (re-scoped to Universe B by the same ruling), #865 (closed by it), #974.\n\n## Current dispatch gate — 2026-08-25\n\nDo not dispatch a DROP yet. `core.character` and `core.property_character` were already removed; `core.licensor` explicitly stays. The only possible remaining structural write is `core.property`, and it remains blocked until #1358 / PR #1379 is merged and live, the DesignFlow writer is found and stopped, and all remaining database/application reads are retired or deliberately adapted.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table core.property\nreads:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:27:32Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T11:52:49Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1238,"title":"Delete Universe A (core.property, core.character, core.property_character, core.licensor) per owner ruling AGENTS.md §6.15","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:26Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1238"},
{"body":"Split out of #1219 (orchestrator marker #1229) so it cannot redden `main`.\n\n## Why this is its own issue\n\n#1219 step 3 asks for a repo-wide static rule in `scripts/check-sql.sh` banning the bare `?`-then-raw-cast expected-count test. Adding it today turns CI red on `main`, because the WildBrain and Sega instances of the same defect are still unmerged (#1221 / #1222, PR pending). The rule is correct; only its timing is wrong.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nAfter #1219, #1221 and #1222 have all merged, add a static check to `scripts/check-sql.sh` that fails any new migration containing the defective shape, so the pattern cannot be reintroduced by the next landing schema written from the same template.\n\nThe shape has THREE forms, all found on 2026-08-19:\n1. a JSON-null expected count silently skipping the capture publication gate;\n2. a raw cast that wedges the capture on a float or an oversized count;\n3. a numeric-looking JSON *string* (`\"12\"`) casting cleanly through `->>` and being accepted as a count — a silent wrong answer, not a crash.\n\nThe guard must have a test that fails when the guard is disabled.\n\n## Verified scope (do not re-derive)\n\nAffected: NBCU (`plm.finalize_nbcu_capture`, `plm.begin_nbcu_capture`), WildBrain, Sega.\nNOT affected: `plm.finalize_wb_capture` (typed `expected_row_count integer`, and `begin_wb_capture` already refuses null and `<= 0`), `plm.finalize_pmt_capture`, and both Disney schemas — none use a jsonb `expected_counts` map. `plm.finalize_warner_capture` does not exist.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: #1219, #1221, #1222\nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:35:42Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T11:40:30Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1235,"title":"Static guard in check-sql.sh for the bare-`?` expected-count test (deferred half of #1219)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:28Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1235"},

{"body":"Full context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-19T0810Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`, section 0.\n\nNothing here blocks any current workstream. This issue exists so the three items waiting on Albert are in the queue rather than only in prose — the 2026-07-31 failure, where a fresh orchestrator reported \"there is no pending work\" over a twenty-item backlog, happened because outstanding items lived only in a handover narrative.\n\n## 1. #1166 — which of ~90 open `db-work` issues are still live?\n\nThe queue audits clean, so nothing is malformed or unroutable. But it holds roughly ninety open issues, many of them business items Albert raised over past months. **Only he can say which are still real work.** An orchestrator cannot retire someone else's business request by guessing it has gone stale.\n\nA useful shape for the answer is a pass through the list marking each as still-wanted, superseded, or done-elsewhere. It does not need to happen in one sitting.\n\n## 2. #1204 — Coldlion phases 2-6, and the seven-year backfill\n\nPhase 1 (the landing spine, `20260818232639`) is merged. Phases 2-6 are roughly 25 more tables and are **deliberately unstarted** — that was the previous session's decision and this session did not revisit it.\n\nThe backfill is its own job and is not part of any phase. The settled rulings from 2026-08-18 stand and should not be re-asked: history from 2019-01-01 on one seven-day grid; no image bytes at all; retention of the three most recent versions with **forward-only** versioning, so the backfill lands one version per row and writes no `change_log` rows.\n\nNothing here needs a decision today. It needs someone to do it, when Albert wants it done.\n\n## 3. #1195 — Coldlion spine follow-ups\n\nTwo Mediums on the merged phase 1. One is **free** because of Albert's own 2019 ruling. The other **breaks CI repo-wide the day phase 2 lands**, so it is cheap now and expensive later.\n\nNeither needs a decision — only doing. Flagged here so it is not discovered by a red build.\n\n## Explicitly NOT waiting on Albert\n\nRecorded so nobody sends him a technical question dressed as a business one:\n\n- **The promotion gate.** #1208 is merged; #1225 carries the first real promotion. No sign-off is owed. The owner-decision approval ritual for technical risk stays retired (ruling 2026-08-18) — never ask Albert to accept a risk flag he cannot evaluate.\n- **#1219, #1221, #1222, #1223, #1224, #1220, #1218.** All engineering, all filed with their own scope blocks.\n- **Whether to bypass the safety gate.** Asked and answered this session; see section 0 of the handoff.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 200\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T12:32:21Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T08:15:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake.
