{"body":"Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-19T0810Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md`. Read section 6 first, then section 9 (\"what did NOT work\").\n\n## Outcome needed\n\n**Nothing has ever used the new preview-rehearsal lane.** #1208 merged as `f975518` at the very end of the 2026-08-19 session, minutes before closeout, so the path it creates is unexercised. Its first real run is the next piece of work, and it will surface things no test could.\n\nFive migrations are now merged and present in **neither** preview nor production:\n\n| Version | What | Issue |\n|---|---|---|\n| `20260818203751` | mgCategory | #1196-era, stranded 2026-08-18 |\n| `20260818232639` | Coldlion landing spine | #1198 |\n| `20260819011639` | PopDAM bulk-operation lease | #1199 / #1171 |\n| `20260819014639` | WildBrain DAM landing | #1197 |\n| `20260819015333` | Sega DSI landing | #1196 |\n\n## Start with the Coldlion spine (#1198), and do it in this exact order\n\nThe merge-first order is now executable. It was not, for the whole of the previous session — that is what #1208 fixed.\n\n1. Rehearse on preview **from merged `main`**, through the new `preview-rehearsal` lane (`merged_preview_source_pr`). Note the run id and its artifact digest.\n2. Record review evidence via `production-apply-review-evidence.yml`.\n3. Production dry-run, then apply, supplying **both** digests in canonical `sha256:<64 hex>` form.\n4. Verify by direct query against `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, not by the workflow's word.\n\n**`20260818203751` is the awkward one.** It is already applied to preview, so the post-merge apply lane cannot re-apply it; its route is the historical-recovery lane. That lane was hardened substantially in #1213 and its original apply run (`32184240106`) was verified during that work to still carry a readable, unexpired artifact whose digest matches exact main. Re-verify before relying on it.\n\n## What to expect, and what NOT to do about it\n\nThe gate is pedantic on purpose and refuses on a missing `sha256:` prefix, an omitted digest, a re-run producing two artifacts, and a rehearsal whose run did not move preview's ledger. **Every one of those refusals is correct.** A rehearsal runs ONCE — see the \"do not re-run it, recover it\" section added to `AGENTS.md` by #1213.\n\nIf the new lane refuses something that looks legitimate, the answer is a fix that is reviewed, never an `if:` edited to force it through. #1194 is the cautionary tale: it was closed as superseded precisely because its central line was the defect.\n\n## Before any licensor capture is loaded\n\n#1219, #1221 and #1222 must be closed first. They are not blockers for promoting the schema; they are blockers for trusting the data that lands in it.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 950\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - schema coldlion\n  - table coldlion.sync_run\n  - table coldlion.window_ledger\n  - table coldlion.change_log\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T18:01:08Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T08:14:29Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1225,"title":"HANDOVER: run the FIRST production promotion through the new preview-rehearsal lane","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:38Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1225"},
{"body":"Three Lows from the independent review of PR #1213 (Kimi K3, sequence 200, head `b7ea4be6`), which returned **APPROVE**. None is Critical or High, so they did not block the merge of the preview-rehearsal path.\n\n## Low 1 — the eleventh instance of the recurring shape, inside a function this PR rewrote\n`preview_applied_commit` in `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py`.\n\n```python\nif artifact.get(\"expired\") is not False or artifact.get(\"workflow_run\", {}).get(\"id\") != run_id\n```\n\nTwo operands, and **only the second has a negative test** (`\"another run\"`). Every stub in the suite sets `\"expired\": False`; nothing sets `expired: True`, and nothing omits the key — which `is not False` also refuses. **Deleting the first operand leaves all 677 tests green.**\n\nThe same line crashes with `AttributeError` rather than refusing if GitHub returns `\"workflow_run\": null`.\n\nImpact is genuinely small: GitHub physically deletes expired artifacts, so the download fails closed downstream. But this is the eleventh instance of \"a check that can be made a no-op while the suite stays green\", and it is inside the function this PR rewrote and claimed to have per-condition swept — which is the point worth recording.\n\n**Fix:** one test case with `\"expired\": True`, one with the key missing, both asserting the refusal message; plus an `isinstance(artifact.get(\"workflow_run\"), dict)` guard.\n\n## Low 2 — the round-9 \"no line-number citations remain\" claim needs rescoping\nThe author stated no line-number citation remains in any file this PR touches. This PR touches `AGENTS.md`, and it still carries them: the `db-data-admin.yml` path-filter citations (`:5-12`, `:15-22`), `domain-ownership.yml` (`:26`), `20260724030000_coldlion_licensor_property_phase1_mirror_schema.sql` (\"lines 71-72\"), `admin.router.js:87`, and `20260621150815_app_core.sql:200` / `:188`.\n\n**The 8 conversions themselves are true** — the reviewer verified the `capture-postgres-schema.sql` READ ONLY statement and the two-`EXCLUSIVE_REFS`-cross-checks description against the code, and both match exactly. The defect is the scope of the claim, which is the same defect class as the 24 untrue enforcement claims found over rounds 4-9: **a statement believed because it was written down.**\n\n**Fix:** either convert the remaining citations, or rescope the claim to \"in the sections this PR edited\". Prefer converting.\n\n## Low 3 — the new merged-rehearsal workflow YAML is asserted by no test\nWorkflow-text tests exist for the historical lane (`test_workflow_refuses_both_historical_forms_at_once`, `test_every_historical_condition_tests_both_forms`), but **nothing references** `merged_preview_source_pr`, the `preview-rehearsal` lock kind, the checkout ref expression, the binding step's `if: success() && inputs.mode == 'apply'`, or the `--preview-project-ref` plumbing.\n\nThe reviewer traced each failure mode — dropping the ref-expression clause, weakening the binding step's `if:`, dropping the CLI argument, the wrong lock kind — and **each fails closed at runtime** (the `HEAD == MAIN_SHA` test, the gate's required argument, the run-conclusion shape check, the live-claim requirement). So this is a coverage gap, not an open hole. It is still surface this PR claims to have made falsifiable.\n\n**Fix:** workflow-text assertions for the merged-rehearsal lane, mirroring the historical ones.\n\n## Sequencing\nBefore the first production promotion runs through the new lane. Low 1 and Low 3 are on the promotion path; Low 2 is documentation hygiene but belongs to the same claim-verification discipline as #1219 and #1223.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: #1208\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:21:01Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T08:04:16Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1224,"title":"Preview-rehearsal follow-ups: an eleventh untested operand, a rescoped citation claim, and untested workflow YAML","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:40Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1224"},
{"body":"While closing round 8 of #1213, the author ran a mechanical mutation sweep of `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py` and its neighbours: every guard whose body raises was replaced one at a time with `if False:`, and the full 664-test offline suite was re-run against each.\n\n**117 guards. 41 survived — the test suite stayed green with the guard disabled.**\n\nOne survivor was hand-verified to confirm the tooling was honest rather than broken.\n\n## What was already fixed on #1213\n\nNine, chosen because they sit in that PR's blast radius — seven inside `prove_preview`, the function #1213 rewrites:\n\n- the run's four-key shape check\n- the post-download hash re-check\n- the unreadable-record refusal\n- the unreadable-source-map refusal\n- the whole-record re-derivation compare\n- the recovery-must-run-at-exact-main rule\n- `prove_pr_and_checks`' three guards\n- `classify_sql`'s file-count guard\n\n**None were introduced by #1213.** They are pre-existing, and seven rounds of careful human-style reading never surfaced them.\n\n## What this issue is for\n\n**The other 32.** They are in code #1213 does not touch, and folding a full coverage-hardening pass into an eighth-round review of the last gate before a production write is exactly the scope creep that makes a change unreviewable. They are recorded here instead of being quietly carried.\n\nAsk:\n1. Re-run the sweep on current `main` to re-derive the list — it will have moved.\n2. For each survivor, decide: write the missing test, or delete the guard as genuinely unreachable. **A guard nothing can falsify is either untested or dead, and both are worth knowing.**\n3. Prioritise anything in the production-promotion evidence chain over everything else.\n\n## The wider lesson, which is the real point\n\nEight review rounds on #1213 found eight real defects by reading. **A single mechanical sweep found 41 more in an afternoon**, including several the reading had walked past repeatedly. Three of the eight rounds' findings were the same shape — a check that silently passes while its tests stay green — and that shape is exactly what mutation testing detects and reading does not.\n\nWorth considering whether a sweep of this kind belongs in CI for the promotion-gate scripts specifically, rather than being run once by hand. That would be a separate change; noting it here so the idea is not lost.\n\n## Method notes, so the next run does not repeat them\n\nAn early sweep timed out and left a file mutated, which silently poisoned the next two sweeps' baselines. **Every sweep must assert a green baseline before it starts**, and only assertion-passing runs may be reported. The author caught this and re-ran; a less careful run would have reported confident nonsense.\n\nSeparately, installing the optional `tzdata` package cleared the environmental `test_post_batch_app_verification` failure that had been carried since round 6, so the offline suite is now green with no standing exception. Worth adding to the machine setup notes.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 550\ndepends_on: #1208\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-05T07:44:02Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T06:31:45Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1223,"title":"32 guards in the promotion-evidence chain have no test that fails when they are disabled","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:41Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1223"},
{"body":"From the independent review of PR #1215 (Grok 4.6, sequence 189, head `47f87937`), which returned **APPROVE** — neither finding is Critical or High, so they did not block the merge.\n\n**Finding 1 is the SAME defect as #1221's Medium 1 on the WildBrain landing**, found by the same reviewer on a different schema the same night. Both were written from the same template. It should be fixed in both, together with the #1219 audit of the older landings.\n\n## Medium — a float or oversized count dies as a raw cast, not a named refusal, and wedges the capture\n`supabase/migrations/20260819015333_sega_dsi_source_landing.sql:1024-1033` and `1046-1055` (`finalize_sega_capture`); `begin_` at 803-810 lets the same values in.\n\nThe type check and the whole-non-negative-number check are correctly separated now, so `null`, `\"7\"`, `true`, `{}`, `[]`, `1.5` and `-1` no longer skip the gate. But finalize then does:\n\n```sql\nv_want := (v_exp ->> v_key)::bigint;\n```\n\nwhich casts the **text** of the JSON number, not the number.\n\n- `{\"assets\": 1.0}` (or `0.0`, `2.00`) is a JSON number and `1.0 = trunc(1.0)`, so the range check accepts it — then `'1.0'::bigint` raises `invalid input syntax for type bigint`.\n- `{\"assets\": 9223372036854775808}` or `1e20` is a whole non-negative number, stored by `begin_`, and finalize raises `bigint out of range`.\n\n**Neither publishes a short capture — this is the opposite failure direction from the original High.** But the call dies with a raw cast error, `error_summary` is never written, the status stays `loading`, and a retry with the same JSON dies identically. The capture is wedged, and the operator gets a Postgres cast error instead of the named refusal the design promises.\n\n`1.0` is not exotic. Any loader arithmetic producing a numeric rather than an integer emits it.\n\n**Fix:** after the numeric integer check, assign through numeric (`::numeric::bigint`), and if the value does not fit a bigint append a named code — `expected_count_not_a_nonnegative_integer` / `reported_count_not_a_nonnegative_integer`, or a dedicated out-of-range code — and reject. Cover `1.0` and a past-bigint value in E2N (ii) and (iii).\n\n## Low — the extra-key sweep is type-only\nSame file, lines 1064-1078; test E2N (iv) only uses `{\"zztest_future_entity\": null}`.\n\nAn extra key whose value is `-1` or `1.5` is a JSON number, so the sweep ignores it. That cannot skip an entity count, so it is not a publication hole — but it does not match the claim that every key outside the eleven is covered.\n\n**Fix:** apply the same integer/range rule to extra keys, or state that the sweep is type-only and test a float extra key as explicitly allowed.\n\n## Sequencing\nBefore the first real Sega capture is loaded. Do it in the same pass as #1221 and the #1219 audit — one fix, three or more schemas.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 650\ndepends_on: #1196\nobjects:\n  - function plm.finalize_sega_capture\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T14:08:25Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T02:57:22Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1222,"title":"Sega landing follow-ups: a float or oversized count wedges a capture with a raw cast error (same defect as #1221)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:43Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1222"},
{"body":"Four findings from the independent review of PR #1214 (Grok 4.6, sequence 187, head `a299234b`). The review returned **APPROVE** — none is Critical or High — so they did not block the merge.\n\n**One of them is a live functional defect and MUST be closed before the first real WildBrain load.** Doing so is cheap; discovering it during a load is not.\n\n## Medium 1 — a float expected count wedges a capture in `loading` forever\n`supabase/migrations/20260819014639_wildbrain_dam_source_landing.sql:1066`\n\nAfter accepting a JSON number that is a mathematical integer, finalize does `v_want := (v_exp ->> v_key)::bigint`. But jsonb `->>` of `1.0` yields the text `'1.0'`, and `'1.0'::bigint` **raises**. Same for any value above bigint.\n\nThat is a raw cast error, not a named refusal, and it aborts **before the reject row is written** — so the capture never becomes `rejected` and never becomes `complete`. It stays `loading` indefinitely.\n\nConcrete: `expected_counts.assets = 1.0` with one landed asset. `begin_` accepts it (its check is numeric truncation), `finalize` raises, and the capture is stuck.\n\n`1.0` is not an exotic input. Any loader arithmetic that produces a numeric rather than an integer emits it.\n\n**Fix:** assign from numeric — `(v_exp ->> v_key)::numeric::bigint` — and refuse out-of-range values with a named code, the way nulls are now refused.\n\n## Medium 2 — the gate's \"one root\" check is not the same fact as its reachability walk\n`…20260819014639…sql:1189-1220`\n\nG2 counts `is_root`. G3 starts from `parent_era_source_id is null`. That these are the same set is guaranteed only by the table CHECK `wildbrain_era_root_matches_parent_chk`, which the gate never re-asserts.\n\nDrop that one CHECK and a second parent-null row with `is_root = false` publishes as a second tree: G2 still sees one root, G3 reaches every parent-null subtree. Concretely — root `R` (`is_root` true), parent-null `S` (`is_root` false), a child of `S`, matching `expected_counts` — and finalize publishes two disjoint era trees as one licensed property.\n\nThis is the same shape as the two Highs already fixed on this PR and as #1219: **a guard that holds only because a separate constraint happens to be present.** The gate should not be able to be defeated by deleting a CHECK somewhere else in the file.\n\n**Fix:** at the gate, treat a root as `parent_era_source_id is null` (and/or re-assert `is_root = (parent is null)`), so dropping the CHECK still refuses a second tree.\n\n## Low 1 — the interesting cycle-termination case is untested\n`supabase/tests/wildbrain_landing_contracts.sql:1225-1247`\n\nF9 lands a no-root cycle, so the recursive branch never runs. The genuinely interesting shape — a reachable root **plus** a disjoint unreachable loop — is not exercised. The reviewer confirmed the code handles it; the test does not prove it. That is a weak proof of termination, not a hole.\n\n## Low 2 — no contract test for a JSON-null `observed_counts` value\n`…20260819014639…sql:1083-1087`\n\nThe author closed this trap in code, unprompted, when fixing the expected-counts side. But no test ever passes `p_observed_counts` with a present null, so **a future edit can reopen it with no red test.** Given #1219 exists precisely because this defect class kept being reintroduced by copying, the missing test matters more than usual.\n\n## Sequencing\n\nMedium 1 and Medium 2 before the first real WildBrain capture is loaded. The two Lows with them, since they are test-only and cheap once the file is open.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 650\ndepends_on: #1197\nobjects:\n  - function plm.finalize_wildbrain_capture\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T14:08:23Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T02:48:27Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1221,"title":"WildBrain landing follow-ups: a float count wedges a capture in loading, and the one-root gate leans on a deletable CHECK","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:45Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1221"},
{"body":"Twice tonight a review wrapper exited **0** having produced no findings and no verdict, and in each case the run had genuinely done work. A caller that reads only the exit code, or only stdout, cannot distinguish this from a clean APPROVE.\n\n## Occurrence 1 — `ai-muse`, PR #1176 at head `3fc26778`\n\nExit 0. The report file recorded the model reading the migration and the contract tests and narrating four review steps, then stopped. No findings, no `VERDICT:` line.\n\n## Occurrence 2 — `ai-kimi`, PR #1214 at head `a299234b`, review sequence 186\n\nExit 0 after **637 seconds of provider time**. The job's `stream.jsonl` is 185 KB with 14 lines and exactly one assistant message:\n\n> \"I've read all four patch parts in full. Let me verify a couple of environmental facts before finalizing findings.\"\n\nThen nothing. The run ended before writing a single finding. The console output was telemetry only.\n\n## A third, different failure in the same family — `ai-kimi`, PR #1176 at head `3fc26778`, sequence 180\n\nThat run **did** complete a full, substantive review — five Low findings and a hand-traced coverage statement — but the wrapper printed only:\n\n```\n## Verdict\nVERDICT: APPROVE\n```\n\nThe entire review body was recoverable only from `stream.jsonl`. A caller quoting the wrapper's stdout as the review evidence would have posted a bare two-line APPROVE as the audit record for a change one step from a production write.\n\n## Why this is a defect and not an inconvenience\n\nIn this repository a review is a **merge gate**. The failure mode is silent and biased toward \"looks approved\": exit 0, no findings, no verdict. An orchestrator under time pressure that treats \"no findings\" as \"nothing found\" merges an unreviewed change. Tonight's rounds have each surfaced real Highs, so an unreviewed merge is not a theoretical loss.\n\n## What to fix\n\n1. **A review run that produces no `VERDICT:` line must exit non-zero**, with a message naming what was missing. Silence is not approval.\n2. **The wrapper must emit the full review body**, not just the tail. When the provider stream carries a complete review and the printed output does not, the wrapper has lost the evidence. Persist the reconstructed body to the report file and print its path.\n3. **Distinguish \"provider ended mid-run\" from \"reviewer found nothing\"** in the exit status, so `--replace-failed-reviewer … --failure-code wrapper_terminal_failure` is reachable automatically rather than by an operator noticing.\n4. Do the same audit for `ai-glm`, `ai-qwen` and `ai-gemini`; this is a wrapper-contract problem, not a model problem.\n\nRelated operational note already worked around here: `ai-kimi new --base main` fails inside the review sandbox with `the requested base 'main' does not exist`; pass the base as an explicit SHA.\n\n## Repository-side follow-up\n\nThe orchestrator must never accept a bare verdict with no coverage statement as review evidence. Both recovered reviews were posted to their PRs in full, with the recovery method stated, so the audit trail records what was actually checked rather than the wrapper's summary of it.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 600\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T15:01:48Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T02:36:32Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1220,"title":"Review wrappers exit 0 with no verdict, and one truncated a full review to two lines — silence must never read as APPROVE","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1220"},
{"body":"The same defect has now been found in **three independent capture-landing schemas tonight**, by two different reviewers, each of whom had to rediscover it from scratch:\r\n\r\n- WildBrain `plm.finalize_wildbrain_capture` (#1197 / PR #1214, review sequence 183)\r\n- Sega `plm.finalize_sega_capture` (#1196 / PR #1215, review sequence 185)\r\n- and the sibling `observed_counts` comparison two lines away in WildBrain, which the author found itself after being told about the first\r\n\r\n## The defect\r\n\r\nA capture's publication gate checks that every expected entity count matches what actually landed. The check is written as:\r\n\r\n```sql\r\nif v_exp ? v_key then\r\n  ...\r\n  if v_n <> v_want then   -- record count_mismatch\r\n```\r\n\r\n`jsonb ? key` is **true for a key whose value is JSON `null`**. `v_want` then becomes SQL `NULL`, `v_n <> NULL` evaluates to UNKNOWN, and the `IF` never fires. The mismatch is silently skipped.\r\n\r\nA missing key is correctly rejected. A present-but-null key is not.\r\n\r\n## Why it matters\r\n\r\nThis is not a theoretical shape. `jsonb_build_object('assets', v_unset)` stores `\"assets\": null`, not an omitted key, so an ordinary loader bug produces it. Combined with otherwise-publishable flags, `finalize` sets `status = 'complete'` on a capture that landed a fraction of the data — and `api.source_capture_inventory` then reports that capture as latest-complete.\r\n\r\nFor WildBrain this is worse than generic: **the portal's API accepts and silently ignores every offset parameter**, returning page one forever with HTTP 200. The count gate is the *only* thing standing between a broken pager and a published 200-row capture. That is the exact disaster `pagination_verified` and the expected counts exist to prevent.\r\n\r\n## Why a per-schema fix is not enough\r\n\r\nThree schemas, three separate rediscoveries, and the existing NBCU and Warner landings were written from the same template and have not been checked. The next licensor landing will be written by copying one of these files.\r\n\r\n## What this issue asks for\r\n\r\n1. **Audit every existing capture-landing `finalize_*` function** — NBCU, Warner/STARLABS, Paramount, Disney, and any other — for this exact pattern, and for the same trap in any loader-supplied `observed_counts` comparison. Report which are affected before changing anything.\r\n2. **Fix each affected one** to refuse a non-number at `begin_` *and* re-check the stored object at `finalize_` (an owner `UPDATE` can reach the stored value, so trusting `begin_` ran is not sufficient). JSON `null`, string, bool, object, array, float and negative must each produce a NAMED rejection, not a skipped check.\r\n3. **Add a shared contract test** — or a static guard in `scripts/check-sql.sh` — that fails when a new `finalize_*` uses `?` alone to decide a count key was supplied. The point is that the next landing schema cannot reintroduce this by copying.\r\n\r\n## Implementation note learned the hard way\r\n\r\n**SQL does not promise to short-circuit `or`.** A single combined predicate can cast a JSON string and die with a raw cast error instead of the intended named message. Split the guard into separate `exists` checks. The WildBrain author hit this and documented it.\r\n\r\nReference implementation: `supabase/migrations/20260819014639_wildbrain_dam_source_landing.sql` on branch `claude/issue-1197-wildbrain-landing`, around lines 813-829 (`begin_`) and 1056-1087 (`finalize`).\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 700\r\ndepends_on:\r\nobjects:\r\n  - function plm.finalize_nbcu_capture\r\n  - function plm.begin_nbcu_capture\r\n```\r\n\r\n*(The object list is provisional and must be narrowed to what the audit in step 1 actually finds, before a claim is taken.)*\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n**ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION (2026-08-19, marker #1229).** The object list above was wrong on one line and is now fixed.\r\n\r\n- `plm.finalize_warner_capture` **does not exist.** The real Warner object is `plm.finalize_wb_capture`, and it is **NOT affected**: Warner uses a typed `expected_row_count integer` column rather than a jsonb map, and `plm.begin_wb_capture` already refuses null and `<= 0`. It has been removed from the claim.\r\n- `plm.begin_nbcu_capture` has been **added**, so the argument-time refusal this issue asks for can be authored under the same claim (#1230).\r\n- Audit result, verified against a throwaway PostgreSQL 18 cluster: only **NBCU** carries the defect. Paramount (`plm.finalize_pmt_capture`) and both Disney schemas have no jsonb `expected_counts` at all. WildBrain and Sega do, and are being fixed under #1221 / #1222.\r\n- A **third** shape was found that this issue did not name: a numeric-looking JSON *string* (`\"12\"`) casts cleanly through `->>` and was accepted as a count — a silent wrong answer, not a crash.\r\n- Step 3 of this issue (a static guard in `scripts/check-sql.sh`) is **deliberately deferred to its own issue**: a repo-wide ban would turn CI red on `main` today, because the WildBrain and Sega fixes are still unmerged. It must land after they merge.\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T14:08:21Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T02:30:46Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1219,"title":"SYSTEMIC: a JSON-null expected count silently skips the capture publication gate in every landing schema","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:48Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1219"},
{"body":"Found by independent review (Kimi K3, sequence 182) of PR #1213 and filed separately at the reviewer's and the orchestrator's direction. **This is a pre-existing pattern, not introduced by #1213.** It was deliberately NOT fixed there, because widening an exception clause on the last gate before a production write deserves its own review rather than riding along on an unrelated change.\r\n\r\n## The defect\r\n\r\n`scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py` `main()` catches only:\r\n\r\n```python\r\n(RiskGateError, OSError, ValueError, CalledProcessError, BadZipFile)\r\n```\r\n\r\nSeveral gate paths can raise types outside that set when the GitHub API returns a well-formed response of an unexpected *shape*:\r\n\r\nLine numbers are given at the commit the review ran against (`ee44cc82`) **and** at the current branch tip `f294f8e3`, because #1213 added lines above them afterwards.\r\n\r\n* `api(...).get(\"check_runs\", [])` raises `AttributeError` if the endpoint returned a JSON **list** rather than an object — `production_business_risk_gate.py:611` at `ee44cc82`, **`:673` at `f294f8e3`**.\r\n* `pr[\"merge_commit_sha\"]` raises `KeyError` if the key is absent from the pull-request payload — `production_business_risk_gate.py:608` at `ee44cc82`, **`:670` at `f294f8e3`**.\r\n* The same `pr[\"merge_commit_sha\"]` subscript appears again at **`:686` at `f294f8e3`**, which is why the fix must sweep rather than patch two lines.\r\n\r\nThe same shape assumption very likely appears elsewhere in the file; the fix should sweep for it rather than patch these two lines (`AGENTS.md`: when you find one silent-failure pattern, sweep the codebase for the same pattern).\r\n\r\n## Why it matters, and why it is Low\r\n\r\nIt is **still fail-closed at the workflow level**: the uncaught exception exits non-zero, so no production write happens. The harm is to the *operator*, not to safety:\r\n\r\n* the run dies with a raw Python traceback instead of the deliberate `::error::` refusal message every other gate path emits;\r\n* the refusal therefore does not name what was missing, which is the standard this gate holds itself to everywhere else;\r\n* an operator reading a traceback is far likelier to conclude \"the gate is broken\" and reach for a workaround than one reading \"REFUSED: the pull-request payload had no merge_commit_sha\".\r\n\r\n## What a fix should do\r\n\r\nNot simply widen the `except` tuple — that would convert a crash into a refusal but still lose the *specific* message. Prefer normalising the API-shape assumptions at the read site so each one raises a `RiskGateError` that names the endpoint and the field that was missing or the wrong type. Add tests that feed each affected call a list-where-object-expected and an object-missing-the-key, and assert the `::error::` refusal text rather than the exception type alone.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\r\nroute: repo-maintenance\r\npriority: 200\r\ndepends_on:\r\nobjects:\r\n```\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T15:09:59Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T02:15:57Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1218,"title":"production_business_risk_gate: malformed GitHub shapes crash with a traceback instead of a named ::error:: refusal","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:36:50Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1218"},
{"body":"## Outcome required\r\n\r\nAdd an append-only, capture-scoped **Peanuts** landing schema. It must accept the private `u2giants/licensor-source-data` Peanuts scraper output (`peanuts/scraper/peanuts-scrape.mjs`) without putting licensed rows in this public repository, normalize every relationship the portal actually declares, keep the licensor's master vocabularies as first-class rows rather than deriving them from assets, preserve raw evidence, and keep anything we reconstructed strictly separate from facts the portal states.\r\n\r\nThis is schema only. No Peanuts art-program, style-guide, character, initiative, holiday, animation-title, asset-type, filename, title, keyword or raw payload value may appear in this public issue, in migrations, in tests, in CI output, or in commit messages. Tests must use invented values.\r\n\r\nPer-licensor landing tables, per the standing owner ruling in `AGENTS.md` §6.13.1. Do not extend an existing licensor's tables and do not add a shared multi-licensor table.\r\n\r\nThis issue must not write canonical `core.*` or `dam.*` rows. Every reconciliation column ships NULL and unresolved by design.\r\n\r\n## Why this portal needs its own shape\r\n\r\nThe source is a **Tenovos DAM** (v3.5.0) fronted by an AWS AppSync GraphQL API. Five properties drive the design, and three of them would corrupt a load if the schema ignored them.\r\n\r\n1. **There is no hierarchy above the asset.** Unlike NetX (a 427-node category tree) or the Disney DAM (a path that encodes guide identity), Tenovos stores one flat metadata document per asset plus a set of controlled vocabularies. There is no style-guide entity, no character roster, no property/franchise tree, and no folder path. Every axis is a vocabulary value stamped on the asset. A schema that expects a parent table to hang assets from will have nothing to put in it.\r\n\r\n2. **The internal field name and the portal label disagree on the two most important fields.** The field internally named `property` is labelled **\"Art Program\"** in the UI, and the field internally named `program` is labelled **\"Initiative\"**. Neither is a \"property\" in our master-data sense — the entire portal is a single franchise, and the art-program axis is an art-style/era bucket. Every table and column here must be named after the **label**, with the internal field name recorded alongside it, or this mismatch becomes permanent. This has already cost this scrape one wrong turn: a search filter built from the internal name is **silently ignored** by the API and returns the unfiltered total, so a mis-named filter produces a capture that looks complete and is not.\r\n\r\n3. **Vocabulary values exist that no asset uses, and they are licensed content we are entitled to.** The gap is not small:\r\n\r\n   | Axis | Values in the master vocabulary | Values actually on an asset |\r\n   |---|---:|---:|\r\n   | Style Guide | 528 | 255 |\r\n   | Character | 77 | 64 |\r\n   | Art Program | 19 | 5 |\r\n\r\n   Deriving the master lists from `distinct(value)` over assets — the obvious loader shortcut — silently discards **273 style guides and 13 characters**. The vocabularies are pulled from their own API (`getControlledVocabularyByIds`) and must land in their own tables, with the asset-usage count stored as an attribute rather than as the source of existence.\r\n\r\n4. **A style guide has no source ID; an asset does.** The vocabulary returns a `valueId` per value, but it is a vocabulary-row identifier, not a stable licensor style-guide number, and nothing else in the portal references it. Style-guide identity is therefore a normalized label generated by us, exactly as in the Sesame landing. **Assets are the opposite case**: every asset carries a real source-issued UUID (`objectId`), so asset identity is the licensor's, not ours, and must not be re-keyed on filename. Filenames are not unique in this portal.\r\n\r\n5. **The search API has a hard 10,000-row deep-paging wall.** `from + size > 10000` returns zero hits with HTTP 200 — the same silent-truncation failure mode that truncated the Disney crawl. The scraper works around it by crawling the sort key in both directions (2 × 10k, no overlap) and then partitioning by vocabulary term. The portal reports **22,461** assets; the capture reaches **22,425** and converges short. That shortfall is real, is not an error, and must be recorded on the capture rather than rounded away.\r\n\r\n## Which relationships are portal-declared\r\n\r\nRecorded explicitly so this load does not repeat the Disney DCP Vault mistake, where two independent arrays on one asset were paired and fabricated links.\r\n\r\n**Declared by the portal, safe to store as fact:**\r\n\r\n- Every controlled vocabulary and its values.\r\n- Every value stamped on an asset: asset to art program, style guide, character, asset type, comic-strip type, initiative, holiday, animation title, era, licensing status, keywords, creator.\r\n- **Asset to asset parent/child.** This is the one true hierarchy and it is explicit, returned by `getRelationshipByObjectId` with a `linkType` of `child` and a stated parent (`primaryId`) and child (`secondaryId`). In practice the parent is a style-guide document asset and the children are the art files cut from it. Verified end to end on a sample: a parent whose asset type is the style-guide type, a child whose asset type is an art type, both carrying the same style-guide value. This is a genuine licensor-asserted edge and must land as fact, with the `linkType` preserved rather than assumed.\r\n\r\n**Reconstructed by us, must stay separated:**\r\n\r\n- **Style guide to character.** Safe to derive here, and safely more than at Sesame, because the style-guide field is **single-select** (`isMultipleSelect = false`): an asset either has exactly one style guide or none. There is no ambiguity to split, so no exclusions are needed. It still lands as `relationship_truth = 'derived'` — the portal does not publish a character roster per guide, and 17,557 of 22,425 assets carry no style guide at all, so the derivation covers only the 4,868 that do.\r\n- **Style guide to art program.** Derived, and it must be **many-to-many**: seven style guides in this capture appear under two different art programs. A one-art-program-per-guide column would be wrong on the data we already hold.\r\n\r\n**Refused outright:**\r\n\r\n- **Art program to character.** The art-program field is multi-select, so an asset carrying two art programs and four characters states nothing about which character belongs to which program. Pairing them is precisely the DCP Vault error. **No table in this schema may hold an art-program-to-character link**, derived or otherwise. The co-occurrence counts stay in the private repo's `derived/` output as analysis, not as a stored relationship.\r\n\r\n## Shape facts the schema must tolerate\r\n\r\n- **78% of assets carry no style guide** (17,557 of 22,425). They are overwhelmingly comic strips, which are a first-class asset type here rather than style-guide art. Style guide must be nullable on the asset, and any promotion that assumes an asset belongs to a guide will drop three quarters of this licensor.\r\n- 2,418 assets carry no character; 22 carry no art program.\r\n- Only 196 assets are style-guide documents themselves — the parents of the explicit graph.\r\n- The asset metadata document contains nested repeating groups (creator information, asset-type/comic-type cascade, character-angle cascade, archive information, notes). These are not flat scalars and must not be flattened lossily into the asset row; they belong in the raw payload plus purpose-built child tables where they carry meaning.\r\n\r\n## Exact schema contract\r\n\r\nAll tables are in `plm`. All source tables are append-only snapshots keyed by `capture_id`; a refresh **adds** a snapshot and never overwrites or deletes a previous one. Every raw payload column must enforce `jsonb_typeof(raw) = 'object'`. All text identifiers and labels require `btrim(value) <> ''`. Every count or size is non-negative. All timestamps are `timestamptz`.\r\n\r\nImmutability is delivered by **privilege separation**, matching the NBCU, WildBrain and Sesame landings: `service_role` gets `select` + `insert` and **not** `update`/`delete` on the snapshot tables, and `select` only on `plm.peanuts_capture`. No triggers. Retry safety is `on conflict do nothing`.\r\n\r\n### `plm.peanuts_capture`\r\n\r\n- `id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()`\r\n- `capture_key text not null unique`\r\n- `source_repository text not null`\r\n- `source_commit_sha text not null`, exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters\r\n- `read_commit_sha text null`, same format when present\r\n- `source_manifest_sha256 text not null`, exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters\r\n- `portal_base_url text not null`\r\n- `api_endpoint text not null`\r\n- `source_customer_id text not null`\r\n- `source_captured_at timestamptz not null`\r\n- `load_started_at timestamptz not null default now()`\r\n- `load_completed_at timestamptz null`\r\n- `status text not null default 'loading'`, limited to `loading`, `complete`, `rejected`, `abandoned`\r\n- `expected_counts jsonb not null`\r\n- `observed_counts jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb`\r\n- `media_downloaded integer not null default 0`, constrained to zero\r\n- `portal_reported_asset_total integer not null check (portal_reported_asset_total >= 0)`\r\n- `assets_captured integer not null check (assets_captured >= 0)`\r\n- `assets_unreachable integer not null check (assets_unreachable >= 0)`\r\n- `deep_paging_partitioned boolean not null default false`\r\n- `vocabularies_loaded_from_source boolean not null default false`\r\n- `relationship_graph_walked boolean not null default false`\r\n- `error_summary jsonb not null default '[]'::jsonb`\r\n- `raw_summary jsonb not null`\r\n- `created_by text not null`\r\n\r\n`complete` requires a completion time, `deep_paging_partitioned = true`, `vocabularies_loaded_from_source = true`, zero media downloads, no validation errors, and `assets_captured + assets_unreachable = portal_reported_asset_total`. A rejected capture remains immutable evidence and never replaces the latest complete capture.\r\n\r\n`assets_unreachable` is not a fudge column. It is the arithmetic proof that the 10,000-row paging wall was accounted for rather than hidden. A capture claiming `assets_unreachable = 0` while `assets_captured` is below the portal total must be rejected.\r\n\r\n`vocabularies_loaded_from_source` is set only after the loader proves the vocabulary tables were populated from the vocabulary API and not from `distinct()` over assets. It is the guard against the 273-style-guide data loss described above.\r\n\r\n### Vocabulary tables — the axes with no usable source ID\r\n\r\nEight tables share one shape. Identity is `value_key`, a normalized label generated by us. `source_value_id` is kept because the vocabulary API does return one, but it is **nullable and non-identifying** and nothing may join on it.\r\n\r\nCommon columns:\r\n\r\n- `capture_id uuid not null references plm.peanuts_capture(id) on delete restrict`\r\n- `value_key text not null` — case-folded, whitespace-collapsed label\r\n- `value_label text not null` — the licensor's own spelling, verbatim\r\n- `source_value_id text null` — the vocabulary row id, recorded only as evidence\r\n- `source_field_name text not null` — the internal metadata field name\r\n- `source_field_label text not null` — the label the portal UI shows\r\n- `is_multi_select boolean not null`\r\n- `asset_count integer not null check (asset_count >= 0)` — **zero is legal and meaningful**\r\n- `raw jsonb not null`\r\n- Primary key `(capture_id, value_key)`\r\n- Index on `(capture_id, asset_count)`\r\n\r\nNote the deliberate difference from the Sesame landing: `asset_count` here is `>= 0`, not `> 0`. A vocabulary value with zero assets is exactly the content that the naive loader loses, and it must be storable.\r\n\r\nThe tables, with rows for this capture:\r\n\r\n| Table | Axis | Cardinality on the asset | Values |\r\n|---|---|---|---:|\r\n| `plm.peanuts_art_program` | art program | multi | 19 |\r\n| `plm.peanuts_style_guide` | style guide | **single** | 528 |\r\n| `plm.peanuts_character` | character | multi | 77 |\r\n| `plm.peanuts_asset_type` | asset type | single | 28 |\r\n| `plm.peanuts_initiative` | initiative | single | 24 |\r\n| `plm.peanuts_holiday` | holiday | multi | 13 |\r\n| `plm.peanuts_animation_title` | animation title | multi | 5 |\r\n| `plm.peanuts_licensing_status` | licensing status | single | 3 |\r\n\r\nComic-strip type (2 values) is a sub-axis of asset type and lands as a column on the asset, not as its own table.\r\n\r\n### `plm.peanuts_metadata_field`\r\n\r\nThe field dictionary, because the label/name mismatch in §2 is the single most dangerous thing about this portal and it must be stored, not remembered.\r\n\r\n- `capture_id uuid not null references plm.peanuts_capture(id) on delete restrict`\r\n- `source_field_name text not null` — internal key\r\n- `source_field_label text not null` — portal UI label\r\n- `source_definition_id text not null`\r\n- `source_vocabulary_id text null`\r\n- `is_multi_select boolean not null`\r\n- `is_facetable boolean not null`\r\n- `field_type text not null`\r\n- `raw jsonb not null`\r\n- Primary key `(capture_id, source_field_name)`\r\n- Unique `(capture_id, source_field_label)`\r\n\r\n### `plm.peanuts_asset`\r\n\r\nAsset identity is the licensor's `objectId`. Filename is **not** unique and must not be treated as a key.\r\n\r\n- `capture_id uuid not null references plm.peanuts_capture(id) on delete restrict`\r\n- `source_object_id text not null` — the portal UUID\r\n- `source_file_id text null`\r\n- `file_name text not null`\r\n- `file_ext text null` — lowercased, no dot\r\n- `file_size_bytes bigint null check (file_size_bytes >= 0)`\r\n- `content_type text null`\r\n- `checksum text null`\r\n- `object_type text null`\r\n- `version_number integer null`\r\n- `is_current_version boolean null`\r\n- `style_guide_key text null` — **nullable by design**, 78% of rows are null\r\n- `asset_type_key text null`\r\n- `comic_strip_type text null`\r\n- `initiative_key text null`\r\n- `era_label text null`\r\n- `licensing_status_key text null`\r\n- `title text null`\r\n- `description text null`\r\n- `publication_date_text text null` — **text, not date**; the portal puts free text here\r\n- `source_created_at timestamptz null`\r\n- `source_updated_at timestamptz null`\r\n- `metadata_template_id text null`\r\n- `rendition_base_url text null`\r\n- `raw jsonb not null` — the entire metadata document, including every nested repeating group\r\n- Primary key `(capture_id, source_object_id)`\r\n- Index on `(capture_id, style_guide_key)`, `(capture_id, asset_type_key)`, `(capture_id, lower(file_name))`\r\n\r\n`style_guide_key`, `asset_type_key`, `initiative_key` and `licensing_status_key` are the normalized `value_key`s and carry composite foreign keys to their vocabulary tables on `(capture_id, value_key)`.\r\n\r\n### Multi-value link tables\r\n\r\nThree, one per multi-select axis, all portal-declared:\r\n\r\n- `plm.peanuts_asset_art_program` — `(capture_id, source_object_id, art_program_key)`\r\n- `plm.peanuts_asset_character` — `(capture_id, source_object_id, character_key)`\r\n- `plm.peanuts_asset_holiday` — `(capture_id, source_object_id, holiday_key)`\r\n\r\nEach is primary-keyed on its full triple, carries composite foreign keys to `plm.peanuts_asset` and to the relevant vocabulary table, and carries `raw jsonb not null`. Animation title is multi-select as well and gets `plm.peanuts_asset_animation_title` on the same shape.\r\n\r\nKeywords are multi-select and high-cardinality; they land as `plm.peanuts_asset_keyword` with the same shape but no vocabulary foreign key, because the keyword vocabulary is open and partly unvalidated (the portal carries a separate free-text unvalidated-keywords field, which stays in `raw`).\r\n\r\n### `plm.peanuts_asset_relationship` — the one declared hierarchy\r\n\r\n- `capture_id uuid not null references plm.peanuts_capture(id) on delete restrict`\r\n- `source_relationship_id text not null`\r\n- `parent_object_id text not null`\r\n- `child_object_id text not null`\r\n- `link_type text not null` — stored verbatim, never assumed\r\n- `raw jsonb not null`\r\n- Primary key `(capture_id, source_relationship_id)`\r\n- Index on `(capture_id, parent_object_id)` and `(capture_id, child_object_id)`\r\n- Check `parent_object_id <> child_object_id`\r\n\r\nBoth endpoints carry composite foreign keys to `plm.peanuts_asset`. This table is the reason `relationship_graph_walked` exists on the capture: it is populated by a per-asset call, it is the slowest part of the capture, and a partial walk must be visible rather than silently short.\r\n\r\n### `plm.peanuts_style_guide_character` — derived, and labelled as such\r\n\r\n- `capture_id uuid not null references plm.peanuts_capture(id) on delete restrict`\r\n- `style_guide_key text not null`\r\n- `character_key text not null`\r\n- `asset_count integer not null check (asset_count > 0)`\r\n- `relationship_truth text not null check (relationship_truth = 'derived')`\r\n- `derivation_note text not null`\r\n- Primary key `(capture_id, style_guide_key, character_key)`\r\n\r\nThe single-value constraint on the style-guide field is what makes this derivation clean, and `derivation_note` must say so. The column is constrained to `'derived'` rather than defaulted to it, so no later migration can quietly promote these rows to fact.\r\n\r\n### `plm.peanuts_style_guide_art_program` — derived, many-to-many\r\n\r\nSame shape, keyed `(capture_id, style_guide_key, art_program_key)`, same `relationship_truth = 'derived'` constraint. Many-to-many is mandatory: seven guides in this capture already violate a one-program assumption.\r\n\r\n## What this issue explicitly does not do\r\n\r\n- No `core.*` or `dam.*` writes. No promotion. No reconciliation.\r\n- No art-program-to-character table, in any form.\r\n- No media. `media_downloaded` is constrained to zero; only metadata and rendition URLs land.\r\n- No merging of the vocabulary style-guide values with the style-guide **document assets**. They are related through the declared parent/child graph and through `style_guide_key`, and that is the only link that exists. Any \"one row per style guide, with its PDF attached\" convenience view is a later, separate ruling.\r\n\r\n## Source of these facts\r\n\r\nCaptured 2026-08-19 from the live portal under POP Creations' licensee access. The scraper, the raw vocabularies, the field dictionary and the derived maps are in the private `u2giants/licensor-source-data` repository under `peanuts/`. Operating knowledge, including the label/name trap, the paging wall and the filter-is-silently-ignored behaviour, is in the `peanuts-scrape` skill.\r\n\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Orchestrator classification, 2026-08-19 (marker #1207)\r\n\r\nClassified structural and routed to the orchestrator. Objects taken from the schema contract above.\r\n\r\n**Two things the author must carry in from tonight**, because both were found the hard way on the sibling WildBrain (#1197) and Sega (#1196) landings, which merged a few hours ago:\r\n\r\n1. **The capture publication gate must not be defeatable by a JSON `null`.** `jsonb ? key` is TRUE for a key whose value is `null`, so `v_want` becomes SQL NULL, the mismatch comparison evaluates UNKNOWN, and a short capture publishes as `complete`. See #1219. Validate at `begin_` AND re-validate the STORED object at `finalize_`, because an owner `UPDATE` reaches it without the function. Keep the type test and the range test as SEPARATE statements — SQL does not promise to short-circuit `or`, so a combined predicate dies with a raw cast error instead of your named message.\r\n2. **Do not then assign with `(… ->> key)::bigint`.** That casts the TEXT of the JSON number, so `1.0` raises `invalid input syntax for type bigint` and a value past bigint raises out-of-range — wedging the capture in `loading` with an unnamed crash. See #1221 and #1222. Assign through `::numeric::bigint` and refuse out-of-range with a named code.\r\n\r\nReference implementations on main: `supabase/migrations/20260819014639_wildbrain_dam_source_landing.sql` and `20260819015333_sega_dsi_source_landing.sql`.\r\n\r\nAlso carry: privileges must be **static and schema-qualified**, one statement per table — a `DO` loop with `execute format('… plm.%I …')` hides the privilege model from the object guard and from any human reader, and was rejected on #1196. And contract tests must pin `constraint_name`, not accept a bare `check_violation`; a test that would stay green with its constraint deleted is itself a defect.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 100\r\ndepends_on:\r\nobjects:\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_capture\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_art_program\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_style_guide\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_character\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_animation_title\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_holiday\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_initiative\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_asset_type\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_licensing_status\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_metadata_field\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_asset\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_asset_art_program\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_asset_character\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_asset_animation_title\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_asset_holiday\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_asset_keyword\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_asset_relationship\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_style_guide_character\r\n  - table plm.peanuts_style_guide_art_program\r\n  - function plm.begin_peanuts_capture\r\n  - function plm.finalize_peanuts_capture\r\n  - view api.source_capture_inventory\r\n  - index plm.peanuts_animation_title_usage_idx\r\n  - index plm.peanuts_art_program_usage_idx\r\n  - index plm.peanuts_asset_animation_title_value_idx\r\n  - index plm.peanuts_asset_asset_type_idx\r\n  - table api.source_capture_inventory\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n**ORCHESTRATOR SCOPE EXTENSION (2026-08-19, marker #1229).** Three objects added to the claim after the first authoring pass (PR #1234) proved the original scope produces an inert schema.\r\n\r\n- `plm.begin_peanuts_capture` and `plm.finalize_peanuts_capture`. Without them no capture row can be created — `service_role` holds SELECT only on `plm.peanuts_capture`, and every snapshot table has a foreign key to it. The failure is immediate and visible, never silent. It must **not** be \"fixed\" by granting INSERT on the capture root. Both functions must carry the #1219 / #1221 / #1222 lessons: no jsonb-null expected count silently skipping the publication gate, no raw cast that wedges on a float or oversized count, no numeric-looking JSON *string* accepted as a count, and no bare `exception when others` in the tests.\r\n- `view api.source_capture_inventory`, extended additively to classify `plm.peanuts_*`. Every sibling landing schema appears there; without this Peanuts is invisible to it.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n**ORCHESTRATOR SCOPE EXTENSION 2 (2026-08-19, marker #1229).** The `Migration author lease` guard refused PR #1234 because a claim must declare EVERY object a migration writes, not just its tables and functions. The 56 objects above — 17 indexes, 38 RLS policies, and `api.source_capture_inventory` under the name the guard uses for it — are all objects this migration already creates on the `plm.peanuts_*` tables it owns. Nothing new is being authorised; the declaration is being completed so it matches what the SQL actually does. The guard was right to refuse.\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T14:43:44Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T02:03:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Outcome required\r\n\r\nAdd an append-only, capture-scoped **Sesame Workshop** landing schema. It must accept the private `u2giants/licensor-source-data` Sesame scraper output (`sesame/scrape.py` + `sesame/analyze.py`) without putting licensed rows in this public repository, normalize every relationship the portal actually declares, deduplicate the licensor's own duplicate field generations, preserve raw evidence, and keep anything we reconstructed strictly separate from facts the portal states.\r\n\r\nThis is schema only. No Sesame brand, sub-brand, character, style-guide, art-style, theme, category, asset, filename, or raw payload value may appear in this public issue, in migrations, in tests, in CI output, or in commit messages. Tests must use invented values.\r\n\r\nPer-licensor landing tables, per the standing owner ruling in `AGENTS.md` §6.13.1. Do not extend an existing licensor's tables and do not add a shared multi-licensor table.\r\n\r\nThis issue must not write canonical `core.*` or `dam.*` rows. Every reconciliation column ships NULL and unresolved by design.\r\n\r\n## Why this portal needs its own shape\r\n\r\nThe source is a **NetX DAM** (`sesameworkshop.netx.net`, portal \"TheLetterA\"). Four properties of it drive the design, and three of them have burned a licensor load before:\r\n\r\n1. **The portal carries two live generations of the same field.** Brand, SubBrand, Character, Theme, Language, Territory and several others each exist twice: a legacy lowercase free-text version and a curated proper-cased version, both populated on the same asset, with different value sets and different cardinalities (legacy character list: 111 values; curated: 104). A schema that keeps only one generation destroys evidence; a schema that merges them fabricates identity. Both must land, in separate tables, explicitly labelled which generation they are.\r\n\r\n2. **Vocabulary values are the only identity there is.** NetX exposes numeric IDs for *categories* and *assets*, but the brand, character, style-guide, art-style, asset-type and theme values arrive as **strings on the asset** with no ID of their own, and the portal's `getChoiceList` API returns empty for every one of them. Identity for those axes is therefore a normalized label, generated by us, and the schema must say so rather than pretending a source ID exists.\r\n\r\n3. **Multi-valued fields arrive as one CSV-quoted string** (`\"A\",\"B\",\"C\"`), while a single value arrives bare with no quotes. A loader that splits on commas unconditionally shatters single values that legitimately contain commas; a loader that never splits collapses every multi-valued asset to one bogus value. The parsed cardinality is part of the contract and must be validated against the counts below.\r\n\r\n4. **A style guide exists in two incompatible forms at once**: as a folder in the category tree (47 at guide level) and as a value in the asset's Style Guide field (130 distinct values, lowercase, 52 of them colon-nested as `family:variant`). Only 13 field values match a folder name exactly. These are **not** the same object and must not be merged. Both land; the correspondence is left unresolved for a human ruling.\r\n\r\n## Which relationships are portal-declared\r\n\r\nRecorded explicitly so this load does not repeat the Disney DCP Vault mistake, where two independent arrays on one asset were paired and fabricated links.\r\n\r\n**Declared by the portal, safe to store as fact:**\r\n\r\n- category to parent category (a real 427-node tree, with `path` and `ancestors` stated by the API)\r\n- asset to category (many-to-many: 1,263 assets sit in more than one)\r\n- asset to brand, sub-brand, character, style guide, art style, asset type, theme, holiday, audience, territory, language, usage rights and restriction type — every one of these is a field on the asset record\r\n\r\n**Reconstructed by us, must stay separated:**\r\n\r\n- **style guide to character.** Derived only from assets carrying **exactly one** style guide, where every character on that asset is unambiguously filed under that guide. 1,752 assets carry two or more guides at once and cannot be split; the 1,165 character rows behind them are excluded, not guessed. This lands as `relationship_truth = 'derived'` with the exclusion count recorded on the capture.\r\n\r\n**Refused outright:**\r\n\r\n- **brand to character.** The portal never states which characters belong to which brand, and 3,599 assets carry no character at all while 1,044 carry no brand. Pairing the two fields on a shared asset is exactly the DCP Vault error. **No table in this schema may hold a brand-to-character link**, derived or otherwise. If that roster is ever needed it is a business ruling made against the asset evidence, not a stored fact.\r\n\r\n## Scope limit that the schema must enforce\r\n\r\nThe licensee account sees 10,220 assets across 427 categories, of which **18 categories sit outside the licensee portal entirely** (the DAM's own internal folders: onboarding material, CMS content, watermarks). Those 18 land — they are needed to resolve parent IDs on the tree and to prove the scope limit was real — but they must be flagged `in_licensee_portal = false` and must never be treated as licensing content.\r\n\r\nUnlike the WildBrain capture, this account is **not** limited to one property: 25 distinct brands appear, being the flagship plus its international co-productions. 8,938 of the 9,176 branded assets carry the flagship brand alone. All 25 are licensed visibility and all 25 load.\r\n\r\n## Exact schema contract\r\n\r\nAll tables are in `plm`. All source tables are append-only snapshots keyed by `capture_id`; a refresh **adds** a snapshot and never overwrites or deletes a previous one. Every raw payload column must enforce `jsonb_typeof(raw) = 'object'`. All text identifiers and labels require `btrim(value) <> ''`. Every count or size is non-negative. All timestamps are `timestamptz`.\r\n\r\nImmutability is delivered by **privilege separation**, matching the NBCU and WildBrain landings: `service_role` gets `select` + `insert` and **not** `update`/`delete` on the snapshot tables, and `select` only on `plm.sesame_capture`. No triggers. Retry safety is `on conflict do nothing`.\r\n\r\n### `plm.sesame_capture`\r\n\r\n- `id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()`\r\n- `capture_key text not null unique`\r\n- `source_repository text not null`\r\n- `source_commit_sha text not null`, exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters\r\n- `read_commit_sha text null`, same format when present\r\n- `source_manifest_sha256 text not null`, exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters\r\n- `portal_base_url text not null`\r\n- `portal_slug text not null`\r\n- `source_captured_at timestamptz not null`\r\n- `load_started_at timestamptz not null default now()`\r\n- `load_completed_at timestamptz null`\r\n- `status text not null default 'loading'`, limited to `loading`, `complete`, `rejected`, `abandoned`\r\n- `expected_counts jsonb not null`\r\n- `observed_counts jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb`\r\n- `media_downloaded integer not null default 0`, constrained to zero\r\n- `category_tree_walked boolean not null default false`\r\n- `categories_visited integer not null check (categories_visited >= 0)`\r\n- `pagination_verified boolean not null default false`\r\n- `multivalue_parse_verified boolean not null default false`\r\n- `guide_character_rows_excluded integer not null default 0 check (guide_character_rows_excluded >= 0)`\r\n- `error_summary jsonb not null default '[]'::jsonb`\r\n- `raw_summary jsonb not null`\r\n- `created_by text not null`\r\n\r\n`complete` requires a completion time, `category_tree_walked = true`, `pagination_verified = true`, `multivalue_parse_verified = true`, zero media downloads, and no validation errors. A rejected capture remains immutable evidence and never replaces the latest complete capture.\r\n\r\n`category_tree_walked` is not ceremony. **The portal's `facetedSearch` is not recursive**: asking a parent folder for its assets returns `size: 0` with HTTP 200 even when its children hold thousands of assets. A crawler that queries only the top folders therefore produces an empty-looking but entirely successful capture. The flag is set only after every one of the 427 nodes has been queried individually, and `categories_visited` must equal the loaded category count.\r\n\r\n`multivalue_parse_verified` is set only after the loader has proved, on the capture it is loading, that at least one asset in each multi-valued dimension parsed to more than one value. It catches a regression where the CSV quoting is passed through unparsed.\r\n\r\n### Vocabulary tables — the axes with no source ID\r\n\r\nSix tables share one shape, because six axes in this portal are label-only. **In every one of them, identity is `value_key`, a normalized label generated by us, and there is no source-ID column, because the portal does not issue one.**\r\n\r\nCommon columns:\r\n\r\n- `capture_id uuid not null references plm.sesame_capture(id) on delete restrict`\r\n- `value_key text not null` — case-folded, whitespace-collapsed, quote-stripped label\r\n- `value_label text not null` — the licensor's own spelling, verbatim\r\n- `field_generation text not null check (field_generation in ('current','legacy'))`\r\n- `asset_count integer not null check (asset_count > 0)`\r\n- `raw jsonb not null`\r\n- Primary key `(capture_id, field_generation, value_key)`\r\n- Index on `(capture_id, value_key)`\r\n\r\nThe tables:\r\n\r\n| Table | Axis | Rows this capture (current / legacy) |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| `plm.sesame_brand` | the property | 25 / 24 |\r\n| `plm.sesame_sub_brand` | sub-property | 2 / 3 |\r\n| `plm.sesame_character` | character | 104 / 111 |\r\n| `plm.sesame_art_style` | visual family | 24 / — |\r\n| `plm.sesame_asset_type` | what the file is | 36 / — |\r\n| `plm.sesame_theme` | subject matter | 35 / 115 |\r\n\r\n`field_generation` is inside the primary key on purpose: the two generations of the same axis hold values that case-fold onto each other while meaning different curation states, and collapsing them would silently pick a winner. Nothing in this schema may join the two generations together; that mapping is a business ruling.\r\n\r\n**34 of the 36 asset-type values and several theme values are colon-nested** (`Parent: Child`, and one is three levels deep). Store the label verbatim. Do **not** split it into a parent link here — the portal states no parent object, only a string, and inventing the hierarchy is out of scope.\r\n\r\n### `plm.sesame_style_guide` — the field-value form\r\n\r\nSame shape as the vocabulary tables above, plus:\r\n\r\n- `guide_family text null` — the segment before the first colon, where the label is colon-nested, stored as evidence only\r\n- `is_colon_nested boolean not null`\r\n\r\n130 rows this capture, 52 of them colon-nested. `field_generation` is always `current`; this field has no legacy twin.\r\n\r\n### `plm.sesame_category` — the declared tree\r\n\r\n- `capture_id uuid not null`\r\n- `category_source_id integer not null` — a real portal ID\r\n- `parent_category_source_id integer null`\r\n- `category_label text not null`\r\n- `category_path text not null` — the portal's own path string\r\n- `depth integer not null check (depth >= 0)`\r\n- `in_licensee_portal boolean not null`\r\n- `is_guide_level boolean not null`\r\n- `child_count integer not null check (child_count >= 0)`\r\n- `raw jsonb not null`\r\n- Primary key `(capture_id, category_source_id)`\r\n- Unique `(capture_id, category_path)`\r\n- Self-referencing composite foreign key `(capture_id, parent_category_source_id)` to `(capture_id, category_source_id)`, deferrable initially deferred\r\n- Check that a category cannot parent itself\r\n\r\n427 rows, 18 with `in_licensee_portal = false`, 47 with `is_guide_level = true`.\r\n\r\nThis is the one axis in the portal with genuine declared identity and a genuine declared hierarchy. **`is_guide_level = true` marks a folder that is an individual style guide.** It is deliberately *not* a foreign key to `plm.sesame_style_guide`: only 13 of the 130 field values match a folder name, and asserting the other correspondences is a human ruling.\r\n\r\n### `plm.sesame_asset`\r\n\r\n- `capture_id uuid not null`\r\n- `asset_source_id integer not null` — a real portal ID\r\n- `asset_name text not null`\r\n- `original_file_name text null`\r\n- `file_type_label text null`\r\n- `file_size_bytes bigint null check (file_size_bytes >= 0)`\r\n- `pixel_width integer null check (pixel_width >= 0)`\r\n- `pixel_height integer null check (pixel_height >= 0)`\r\n- `title text null`\r\n- `description text null`\r\n- `raw_keyword_text text null`\r\n- `usage_rights_label text null`\r\n- `usage_terms text null`\r\n- `asset_status_label text null`\r\n- `copyright_notice text null`\r\n- `source_created_at timestamptz null`\r\n- `source_modified_at timestamptz null`\r\n- `source_imported_at timestamptz null`\r\n- `source_md5 text null`, 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters when present\r\n- `source_hash text not null`\r\n- `raw jsonb not null`\r\n- Primary key `(capture_id, asset_source_id)`\r\n\r\n10,220 rows. `source_md5` is nullable because 12 assets in this capture carry none.\r\n\r\n**No brand, character, style-guide, art-style or theme column may exist on this table.** Every one of those is multi-valued in the source and belongs only in the link tables below. A denormalized convenience column would be a lie on the 1,752 assets carrying several style guides, and on the 1,561 carrying several characters.\r\n\r\nNo media byte, base64, thumbnail, preview URL, or download-path column is allowed.\r\n\r\n### `plm.sesame_asset_category` — portal-declared\r\n\r\n- `capture_id uuid not null`\r\n- `asset_source_id integer not null`\r\n- `category_source_id integer not null`\r\n- `relationship_truth text not null default 'declared' check (relationship_truth = 'declared')`\r\n- `raw jsonb not null`\r\n- Primary key `(capture_id, asset_source_id, category_source_id)`\r\n- Composite foreign keys to `plm.sesame_asset` and `plm.sesame_category`\r\n\r\n11,506 rows over 10,220 assets: 1,263 assets are filed in more than one folder, so this is genuinely many-to-many and must not be flattened onto the asset.\r\n\r\n### Asset-to-vocabulary link tables — portal-declared\r\n\r\nSeven tables, one per axis, all the same shape:\r\n\r\n- `capture_id uuid not null`\r\n- `asset_source_id integer not null`\r\n- `value_key text not null`\r\n- `field_generation text not null check (field_generation in ('current','legacy'))`\r\n- `value_ordinal smallint not null check (value_ordinal >= 0)`\r\n- `relationship_truth text not null default 'declared' check (relationship_truth = 'declared')`\r\n- `raw jsonb not null`\r\n- Primary key `(capture_id, asset_source_id, field_generation, value_key)`\r\n- Composite foreign keys to `plm.sesame_asset` and to the matching vocabulary table on `(capture_id, field_generation, value_key)`\r\n\r\nThe primary key is the deduplication: an asset listing the same value twice collapses to one row. `value_ordinal` preserves the order the licensor listed them in, which is lost otherwise and is not recoverable from a set.\r\n\r\n| Table | Rows this capture (current generation) |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| `plm.sesame_asset_brand` | 9,361 |\r\n| `plm.sesame_asset_sub_brand` | 29 |\r\n| `plm.sesame_asset_character` | 12,054 |\r\n| `plm.sesame_asset_style_guide` | 11,225 |\r\n| `plm.sesame_asset_art_style` | 10,344 |\r\n| `plm.sesame_asset_asset_type` | 9,572 |\r\n| `plm.sesame_asset_theme` | 181 |\r\n\r\nLegacy-generation rows load into the same tables under `field_generation = 'legacy'`; their counts are supplied through `expected_counts` and are not repeated here.\r\n\r\n### `plm.sesame_style_guide_character` — derived, with a stated exclusion\r\n\r\n- `capture_id uuid not null`\r\n- `guide_value_key text not null`\r\n- `character_value_key text not null`\r\n- `asset_count integer not null check (asset_count > 0)`\r\n- `derivation_method text not null default 'single_guide_asset' check (derivation_method = 'single_guide_asset')`\r\n- `relationship_truth text not null default 'derived' check (relationship_truth = 'derived')`\r\n- `rule_version text not null`\r\n- `raw jsonb not null`\r\n- Primary key `(capture_id, guide_value_key, character_value_key)`\r\n- Composite foreign keys to `plm.sesame_style_guide` and to `plm.sesame_character` on its `current` generation\r\n\r\n1,234 rows, built from the 5,680 assets that carry exactly one style guide and at least one character. The 1,165 character rows on multi-guide assets are excluded by construction and their count is recorded on the capture in `guide_character_rows_excluded`, so the gap is auditable rather than invisible.\r\n\r\nThis is the **only** derived relationship table in the schema, and it is the only one whose `relationship_truth` is not `declared`. Any future derived link needs its own issue and its own justification.\r\n\r\n## Expected counts for this capture\r\n\r\nDrift checks supplied through `expected_counts`, not hard-coded constraints:\r\n\r\n| Table | Rows |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| `sesame_category` | 427 (18 outside the portal, 47 guide-level) |\r\n| `sesame_brand` | 25 current, 24 legacy |\r\n| `sesame_sub_brand` | 2 current, 3 legacy |\r\n| `sesame_character` | 104 current, 111 legacy |\r\n| `sesame_style_guide` | 130 |\r\n| `sesame_art_style` | 24 |\r\n| `sesame_asset_type` | 36 |\r\n| `sesame_theme` | 35 current, 115 legacy |\r\n| `sesame_asset` | 10,220 |\r\n| `sesame_asset_category` | 11,506 |\r\n| `sesame_asset_brand` | 9,361 |\r\n| `sesame_asset_sub_brand` | 29 |\r\n| `sesame_asset_character` | 12,054 |\r\n| `sesame_asset_style_guide` | 11,225 |\r\n| `sesame_asset_art_style` | 10,344 |\r\n| `sesame_asset_asset_type` | 9,572 |\r\n| `sesame_asset_theme` | 181 |\r\n| `sesame_style_guide_character` | 1,234 |\r\n\r\nSparse axes that must not fail validation: 1,044 assets carry no brand, 838 no style guide, 3,599 no character, 1,736 no art style. Only 29 assets in the whole capture carry a sub-brand, and only 1 asset carries the portal's separate human-character field — that field is deliberately **not** given a table here; one row does not justify one, and it stays in the asset's `raw` payload until it earns one.\r\n\r\n## Functions\r\n\r\n### `plm.begin_sesame_capture(...) returns uuid`\r\n\r\nSecurity definer, fixed `search_path`, executable only by `service_role`. Accepts the capture identity, provenance SHAs, portal base URL and slug, source capture time, and `expected_counts`; inserts a `loading` row; returns its id. Rejects a duplicate `capture_key`.\r\n\r\n### `plm.complete_sesame_capture(...) returns void`\r\n\r\nSecurity definer, fixed `search_path`, executable only by `service_role`. Takes the capture id, `observed_counts`, `categories_visited`, and the three verification flags. Sets `status = 'complete'` only if every gate above passes and `observed_counts` matches `expected_counts` on every key; otherwise sets `status = 'rejected'` and records why in `error_summary`. **It must never raise instead of recording** — a rejected capture is evidence.\r\n\r\n### `plm.latest_sesame_capture() returns uuid`\r\n\r\nThe most recent `complete` capture. Every consumer view reads through this rather than picking a capture by date, so a rejected or in-flight load can never be read as current.\r\n\r\n## Out of scope for this issue\r\n\r\n- Any `core.*` or `dam.*` write, and any reconciliation of these labels against canonical licensor, property, or character rows.\r\n- Merging the `current` and `legacy` field generations.\r\n- Mapping the 130 style-guide field values onto the 47 style-guide folders.\r\n- Splitting colon-nested asset-type and theme labels into a hierarchy.\r\n- Any brand-to-character relationship, in any form.\r\n\r\nEach of those is a business ruling. None of them belongs in a landing schema.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: ready\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 100\r\ndepends_on:\r\nobjects:\r\n  - {"body":"Two Low findings from the independent review of PR #1176 (Grok 4.6, review sequence 179, head `8810a927`). Neither blocks the merge — the reviewer confirmed neither is a working unprivileged exploit and returned APPROVE — but both are real and should be closed before the PopDAM worker is written against this contract.\n\n## Low 1 — the batch-id branch is not gated on the one proof definition\n\n`supabase/migrations/20260819011639_popdam_bulk_operation_revision_lease.sql` (was `20260818223054_…`), lines ~672-678 vs ~307-310.\n\nThe migration header states that every pointer guard is gated on `v_proven`. Introducing `provider_batch_id` is not: it allows `p_submission_owner is not null and v_stored_owner is null` even when `v_stored_proof` is already set. `v_proven` additionally requires `v_stored_proof is null`.\n\nThe reviewer could not reach \"proof without owner\" through these functions today — a claim always stamps both, and neither the legacy nor the batch path can plant lease fields — so this is not currently exploitable. It is a drift hazard: two definitions of \"proven\" that are equal by accident rather than by construction.\n\n**Fix:** gate that branch on `v_proven` so it cannot drift from the single proof definition.\n\n## Low 2 — a test comment contradicts the production path and will mislead the worker author\n\n`supabase/tests/popdam_bulk_operation_revision_lease_contracts.sql`, lines ~1674-1688.\n\nSection 14b plants an expired lease with **no** digest, then asserts that a later claim **does** issue a receipt, and its comment calls that \"reconciliation\". Section 17 — the real production path, a genuine claim followed by a lapse — asserts the opposite: no remint once a digest exists.\n\nThe assertion is correct; it is exercising the `v_stored_proof is null` branch. The **comment** is wrong about production. A PopDAM worker author who copies 14b will expect a receipt they will not get.\n\n**Fix:** state in 14b that it covers the no-digest branch only, and that section 17 is production reconciliation.\n\n## Related\n\nThe coordination debt for the PopDAM app team is tracked on #1199 and in `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-19T0050Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md` section 7.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on: #1171\nobjects:\n  - function public.update_bulk_operation\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-24T01:37:27Z","createdAt":"2026-08-19T01:17:37Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake.
