{"body":"## What happened\n\nRebuilding the preview branch from scratch (fixture cleanup after #1181's Sample Tracking measurement — see that issue for the fixture data this was meant to clear: ~40,200 `dflow.sample` rows and ~60,300 `dflow.sample_movement` rows named `AI-PERF-20260818-inventory-*`).\n\nSequence tried, in order, against project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` (parent) / preview branch `shared-db-schema-rehearsal`:\n\n1. `POST /v1/branches/{id}/reset` on the original branch (`rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`, `persistent: true`) — returned `{\"workflow_run_id\":..., \"message\":\"ok\"}` but nothing happened after 13 minutes (postmaster start time and row counts unchanged, branch status never left `FUNCTIONS_DEPLOYED`).\n2. `PATCH /v1/branches/{id}` to set `persistent: false`, then retried reset — this time branch status changed to `MIGRATIONS_FAILED` after ~10 minutes, but the underlying database was untouched (same postmaster start time, same row counts). No data loss from this step.\n3. With Albert's explicit approval, deleted the branch (`DELETE /v1/branches/{id}?force=true` — succeeded once `persistent` was false) and recreated it via `POST /v1/projects/qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai/branches` with `{\"branch_name\":\"shared-db-schema-rehearsal\",\"persistent\":true,\"with_data\":true}`.\n4. New branch: id `0903fc16-8c76-441d-aa1b-613497333a94`, project ref `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs`. Went `CREATING_PROJECT` → `RUNNING_MIGRATIONS` → `MIGRATIONS_FAILED` over about 7 minutes. `preview_project_status` has shown `RESTORING` continuously since creation (19:24 UTC). Over 30+ minutes of polling since, nothing has changed: `updated_at` on the branch record is frozen at creation time, and every query against `https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs/database/query` returns:\n   ```\n   FATAL: 57P03: the database system is not accepting connections\n   DETAIL: Hot standby mode is disabled.\n   ```\n\n## Current state\n\n- **Old preview branch is gone.** `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` no longer exists — it was deleted as part of this rebuild.\n- **New preview branch is unusable.** Project ref `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs` exists but its database has never come up. No app or session can use shared-db preview right now.\n- The fixture data that motivated this (see #1181) is gone along with the old branch, so that specific problem is resolved — but preview itself is currently down.\n\n## Likely relevant context\n\n- #901 and #880 already documented preview/production migration-ledger drift on the old branch. That drift may be why a from-scratch migration replay against current `main` is failing to complete, though the direct symptom here (stuck in `RESTORING`, DB refusing connections) looks more like a Supabase platform-side provisioning fault than a SQL/migration error — no actual migration error text was ever surfaced, just a stuck state.\n\n## What's needed\n\n- Someone with Supabase support access (or deeper Management API/dashboard visibility than the plain PAT calls used here) should check why project `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs` is stuck in `RESTORING` and either unstick it or confirm it needs to be deleted and retried.\n- Once preview is healthy again, verify: migration ledger has all entries currently on `main` (main had 469 including `20260814130000`, `20260814193402`, `20260818024441` at the time of this rebuild), and the Sample Tracking Release A objects exist (`sample_creation_batch`, `sample_workflow`, `sample_path_revision`, `sample_carrier`, `sample_shipment`, `sample_inventory` view).\n- Whoever picks up #1181's structural fix for `dflow.sample_inventory` will need working preview to re-verify — flagging that this blocks that work too.\n- Worth a follow-up: agree a repeatable seed/teardown approach for preview performance rehearsals (e.g. a disposable branch-off-a-branch) so a stuck full rebuild isn't the only way to clear fixture data next time.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 800\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-21T00:00:34Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T19:43:29Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2kDg","name":"blocked","description":"Blocked on something other than the owner: another item, an upstream system, or a machine.","color":"B60205"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1188,"title":"Preview branch rebuild stuck: new shared-db-schema-rehearsal (mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs) never leaves RESTORING / MIGRATIONS_FAILED","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:22Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1188"},
{"body":"Follow-ups from the sequence-171 independent review (Kimi K3) of PR #1175 at head `d2a9d918`. That review returned **APPROVE** — none of these blocked the merge, and none is a correctness bug on today's data. Recorded so they are not lost.\n\nOrdered by how much they could actually cost.\n\n## 1. The category upsert contradicts its own comments\n\n`supabase/migrations/20260818154748_...sql:288-291` upserts `core.mg_category` on `code`, so a **deliberate display-name rewording is silently reverted** on any replay. The comments at `:169-170` and `:204-206` say the opposite.\n\nCode and comment disagreeing is the defect, independent of which behaviour is right. Decide which is intended: the display name is authoritative-from-migration and reverting is correct (then fix the comments), or it is a business-editable label (then the upsert must not touch it). **Do not leave them disagreeing** — the next reader will trust the comment.\n\n## 2. `dupes` check groups by a case-sensitive label\n\n`:530-540` groups by `division_label` rather than `division_key`. Two rows differing only in the case of their division code would not be seen as duplicates of each other. The contract test's total-count assertion backstops this on a populated database, so it is not currently exploitable — but the backstop is in a different file from the check.\n\n## 3. The empty gate cannot tell \"no MG01 rows\" from \"all MG01 rows inactive\"\n\n`:434-436` vs `:588-596`. A database whose MG01 rows all exist but are inactive (or carry a NULL `is_active`) takes the empty branch and commits with only a notice. That is arguably correct — there is nothing live to map — but it is indistinguishable in the log from a genuinely empty database, and those two situations warrant very different human reactions.\n\nSuggest: make the notice state which case it is, with the counts that decided it.\n\n## 4. Declaration narrowing is undetectable when the row is also absent\n\n`:309-341`, `:465-471`. `expected_divisions` is the sole authority for scope, so someone \"fixing\" a failure by narrowing a declaration instead of fixing the data produces a silently smaller grid. The file explicitly warns against this in a comment, which is the honest mitigation available without a second source of truth — but it is a comment, not a control.\n\nWorth considering whether the declared scope can be cross-checked against something independent once the workbook is machine-readable.\n\n## 5. Test nits\n\n- the test file header understates the privileges section D needs (its fixtures insert into `core.\"merchGroup\"`)\n- `service_role` is asserted to have SELECT but its **write** grant is never asserted (`supabase/tests/mg_category_taxonomy_contracts.sql:195-200`)\n- D2 duplicates D1's constraint coverage and adds no new rule\n\n## Context\n\nThe reviewer confirmed as genuinely fixed: the HIGH partial-seed bug (a product type resolving in 2 of 3 divisions now raises and names the division), the renamed unique constraint matching what it actually enforces, the negative tests exercising constraints for real on an empty database via rolled-back fixtures, and the documents.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 200\ndepends_on: 1163\nobjects:\n  - table core.mg_category\n  - table core.mg_category_merch_group\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-26T04:44:17Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T19:14:58Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1187,"title":"mgCategory follow-ups: upsert contradicts its comments, case-sensitive duplicate check, and three smaller gaps","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:24Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1187"},
{"body":"## Symptom\n\nThe required check `verify` (DB Data Admin) fails intermittently on unrelated pull requests. On 2026-08-18, on branch `codex/issue-1143-fr-ruling-forward` with **zero changes under `apps/`** (`git diff --stat e922cce HEAD -- apps/` is empty), the same commit produced: one hang, one failure, one pass.\n\n## Root cause\n\n`npm test` in `apps/db-data-admin` exits non-zero while **all 16 test files and all 104 tests PASS**.\n\nThe non-zero exit comes from a single unhandled async error: `@revolist/revogrid`'s debounced resize handler fires **after jsdom teardown** and throws\n\n```\nFailed to execute 'dispatchEvent' on 'EventTarget'\n```\n\noriginating in `src/DataAdmin.environment-label.test.tsx`. Nothing is actually broken — the component works; a third-party grid's timer simply outlives the DOM the test built for it.\n\nSeparately, some runs stall for 25+ minutes on `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`. That is a runner/package-mirror problem, not this defect, but it compounds it: an operator sees a long-running `verify` and cannot tell a stall from a real failure without opening the log.\n\n## Why this matters more than a flake usually does\n\n`verify` is a **required** status check, so it gates merges on a repository whose entire discipline is evidence-based. A required check that is a coin flip teaches every session and every person to hit re-run instead of reading the failure. That is precisely how a real failure eventually gets waved through — and this repo governs the shared production database for roughly nine applications.\n\nIt also silently punishes correct work: three database pull requests today were reported as failing for a reason that had nothing to do with them.\n\n## Suggested fix (for whoever owns the DB Data Admin frontend)\n\nEither:\n\n- cancel or await revogrid's debounced resize in an `afterEach` for the affected suite, so no timer survives teardown; or\n- register a Vitest `onUnhandledError` filter scoped to exactly this error and this library, so a genuine unhandled error still fails the run.\n\nPrefer the first. The second must be narrow — a broad filter would hide real unhandled errors and trade a visible flake for an invisible one.\n\nAlso worth doing: make `npx playwright install` failures fail fast rather than hang, so a stalled run is distinguishable from a slow one.\n\n## What this issue is NOT\n\nNot a database change. Not shared-db structural work. No migration, no schema, no RLS. It needs no author lane and no migration version — it is application-repository maintenance surfaced here because it blocks this repository's required checks.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- run 32169499936 — hung ~28 min on `playwright install`, cancelled\n- immediate re-run — failed in 27s, 104/104 tests passing, exit code from the unhandled error above\n- second re-run — passed, 3m14s\n- earlier the same day on the same branch — passed twice (3m47s, 5m57s)\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T13:18:19Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T19:11:32Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1186,"title":"Required check 'verify' (DB Data Admin) is a coin flip: revogrid resize throws after jsdom teardown","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:25Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1186"},
{"body":"## What and why\n\nColdlion ERP data must land in a schema built to receive it **raw, directly from the Coldlion API**. DesignFlow PLM is not in this path (owner direction, Albert Hazan, 2026-08-18). No application ever reads these tables. How the data then reaches `core.*` or app tables is a separate decision, made per feed, after the raw data exists.\n\nToday only **1 of 19** Coldlion feeds has a correctly built landing table (`ingest.coldlion_product_size_landing`). Customers and vendors land in the generic `ingest.raw_record` bucket, which keys on a single text column and keeps only the latest version. The `plm.erp_*` mirrors are a staging-and-matching layer, not landing — they carry curation on the same row. Thirteen feeds, including both history endpoints, have nowhere to land at all.\n\n## Spec\n\n`docs/coldlion-raw-landing-schema-design.md` (on `main`) is the full grain-by-grain design and is the spec for this issue. It carries the table list, keys, the two table behaviours, the data rules, and the disposition of what exists today.\n\nVerified companions that constrain the work: `docs/coldlion-erp-api-reference.md`, `docs/coldlion-history-endpoints-shape.md`, `docs/merch-group-taxonomy-architecture.md`.\n\n## One issue, not six (owner direction 2026-08-18)\n\n1,182 issues created, 78 open. Splitting sequential work on one schema into six tickets adds clutter without preventing any collision — this is one schema, one loader family, built in order. The phases below are a checklist inside this issue, not separate issues.\n\n## Phases\n\n- [ ] **1. Spine** — schema `coldlion`, plus `sync_run`, `window_ledger`, `change_log`.\n- [ ] **2. History feeds** — `prod_history_line`, `prod_history_component`, `prod_history_last_lookup`, `order_history_line`, `order_history_component`. Biggest gap; nothing exists today.\n- [ ] **3. Items** — `item_header`, `item_merch_group`, `item_detail`.\n- [ ] **4. Merch groups** — `merch_group_header`, `merch_group_detail`; migrate rows off `ingest.coldlion_product_size_landing`, then retire it.\n- [ ] **5. Customers and vendors** — `customer`, `vendor`; re-land out of `ingest.raw_record`. `plm.erp_*` becomes a consumer of `coldlion.*`.\n- [ ] **6. Remainder** — `item_image`, `item_image_content`, `inventory_snapshot`, `prepack_component`, `season`, `salesperson`, `pickticket_line`, `receiving_line`, `prod_order_detail`, `prod_tracking_event`.\n\nThe seven-year history **backfill run** is deliberately excluded. It is a long background job with its own failure modes and belongs in its own issue once the tables exist and the depth question is answered. See #1031, which covers the chunked historical puller and should be reconciled against phase 2 rather than duplicated.\n\n## Non-negotiables for whoever implements this\n\n- No foreign keys into `core.*`. No resolution or matching columns. No grants to application roles.\n- No invented structure. Coldlion has no licensor-to-property link and no active flag; do not model one here.\n- Every row keeps the complete original payload in `raw` alongside typed columns.\n- Merch-group keys are four-part `(company, division, mg_type_code, mg_code)`. `mgCode` collides across types inside one division (`1P` is both a licensor and a property in CW001). Never hardcode `05` = Licensor.\n- `1900-01-01` is Coldlion's empty-date marker (owner-confirmed 2026-08-14). Store NULL in typed columns; keep the original in `raw`.\n- History row identity is `(prodOrderNo, prodLineSeq, prepackItemNo)`. Distinct `prodLineSeq` means distinct real purchases — never merge them. The seven `last*` fields are a separate lookup, not part of the purchase; `lastProdCost` must never reach a cost report.\n\n## Open owner questions (non-blocking for phases 1 to 5)\n\n1. History depth: backfill everything from 2019 (about 740 requests), or start from a chosen date?\n2. Image bytes: store base64 content in the database, or metadata plus `has_image` only? (Affects phase 6 only.)\n3. Retention: keep every version of append-only history forever, or roll off?\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 600\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - schema coldlion\n  - table coldlion.sync_run\n  - table coldlion.window_ledger\n  - table coldlion.change_log\n  - table coldlion.customer\n  - table coldlion.vendor\n  - table coldlion.merch_group_header\n  - table coldlion.merch_group_detail\n  - table coldlion.season\n  - table coldlion.salesperson\n  - table coldlion.item_header\n  - table coldlion.item_merch_group\n  - table coldlion.item_detail\n  - table coldlion.item_image\n  - table coldlion.item_image_content\n  - table coldlion.prepack_component\n  - table coldlion.inventory_snapshot\n  - table coldlion.pickticket_line\n  - table coldlion.receiving_line\n  - table coldlion.prod_order_detail\n  - table coldlion.prod_tracking_event\n  - table coldlion.prod_history_line\n  - table coldlion.prod_history_component\n  - table coldlion.prod_history_last_lookup\n  - table coldlion.order_history_line\n  - table coldlion.order_history_component\n  - table ingest.coldlion_product_size_landing\n  - table ingest.coldlion_product_size_run\n```\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T02:47:44Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T18:47:54Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1184,"title":"Coldlion raw landing layer: a coldlion schema that receives the API feeds directly (no DesignFlow in the path)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:27Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1184"},
{"body":"## What happened\n\nToday `--supersede-active-claim-version` renamed PR #1145's migration from `20260817232425` to `20260818174350`. The rename itself was correct and fully evidenced (`refs/db-claim-supersessions/1144-20260817232425`).\n\nBut **a migration version is not only a filename.** That version was also a value inside the production safety gate:\n\n```python\n# scripts/production_migration_guard.py:148\nFR_HELD_20260803 = {\n    \"20260802170000\",\n    \"20260817232425\",   # <- now names a file that does not exist\n}\n```\n\nand it appears four more times in `scripts/production_migration_guard.py`, once in `scripts/test_production_migration_guard.py`, and four times in `AGENTS.md` §6.5.\n\nAfter the rename, `20260817232425` names nothing, and the file that actually exists — `20260818174350` — is in **no hold set at all**. It is not in `FR_HELD_20260803`, not in `HARD_BLOCKED`, not in `FR_COMPATIBILITY_VERSIONS`.\n\n## The consequence\n\nAn allowlist of `20260818174350` passes `parse_allowlist` unchallenged, reaches production, sets `core.licensor` `FR` to inactive, and leaves production at rest in exactly the state AGENTS.md §6.5 forbids. That is the same cornering that stopped `20260817124545` being promoted alone, re-created silently by a rename.\n\nThe tests lock the hole in: `scripts/test_production_migration_guard.py:336` asserts the phantom version, and nothing asserts that the real one is refused. `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:147` would classify it `genuinely-pending` rather than `deliberately-held`.\n\nFound by Grok 4.6 in the sequence-166 independent review of #1145. The merge is stopped; the immediate repair is tracked on that PR. **Production was never at risk** — nothing was promoted.\n\n## Why this is a tooling defect, not just a PR defect\n\nThe supersession tool moved a value that the repository uses as an identifier in at least three non-filename places, and reported success without mentioning it. Any future supersession of any held or gated migration will do this again. The next one may not have an independent reviewer who reads the production gate.\n\n## Required fix\n\n`supersedeActiveClaimVersion` must, before it reports success, scan the repository for the old version string outside the migration filename it just renamed — at minimum `scripts/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `.github/workflows/**`, and `supabase/tests/**`.\n\nThen either:\n\n- **refuse** the supersession when the old version appears in a decision-making set (`FR_HELD_*`, `HARD_BLOCKED`, `FR_COMPATIBILITY_VERSIONS`, any allowlist constant), telling the operator exactly which files must be updated first; or\n- **rename it everywhere in the same atomic operation** and prove the readback, the same way it proves the file rename.\n\nRefusing is the safer default. A rename that silently un-gates a held migration is worse than a rename that fails.\n\nA pure-documentation mention (a `HANDOFF.d/` file recording history) must NOT block — those are historical records and are correct to keep the old number. Distinguish decision-making references from historical prose.\n\n## Tests this needs\n\n- supersession refuses when the old version is in a guard's hold set, naming the file and line\n- supersession succeeds when the old version appears only in historical handoff prose\n- a guard test asserting every member of every hold set exists as a real migration file (today `test_every_member_is_a_real_migration_file` covers only atomic batches — extend it to `FR_HELD_20260803` and every other set)\n\n## Related\n\nSame class as #1165 (a supersession failure mode found the hard way). #1165 was about the rename failing loudly; this is about it succeeding quietly and taking a safety property with it.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 950\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:16:58Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T17:59:34Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1182,"title":"Version supersession silently un-gates a held migration by leaving stale version references in the production guard","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:28Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1182"},
{"body":"## Request\n\n`dflow.sample_inventory` cannot use any index and degrades super-linearly with movement volume. It is the read behind the Sample Tracking inventory screens (NY Office / Ningbo / China Warehouse, newest first, one-month default with Show All), so it is on the path of the module's most-used screen. Please consider a structural fix.\n\nThis is a **structure** request, so it belongs here rather than in the app repo. I have made no schema change anywhere.\n\n## Where this came from\n\nPlan step 3 of the Sample Tracking restructure (`designflow-frontend/plan_sample_tracking_full_restructure.md`) has a verification gate requiring an `EXPLAIN` proof that the Release A reads use their intended indexes. Every other Release A index passed. This one did not, so I seeded preview and measured it.\n\n## Measured evidence (preview `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`)\n\nQuery under test — the actual inventory screen read:\n\n```sql\nSELECT sample_id_fk, product_location_type, product_location_id, quantity,\n       available_since, is_boxed, is_in_transit, is_eligible\nFROM dflow.sample_inventory\nWHERE product_location_type = 'office' AND product_location_id = 'nyc'\n  AND available_since >= now() - interval '1 month'\nORDER BY available_since DESC, sample_id_fk DESC\nLIMIT 100;\n```\n\n`EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`, second run of each, after `ANALYZE`:\n\n| `sample_movement` rows | Execution time | Rows discarded to return 100 | Seq scans | Nested loops |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 30,302 | **100.2 ms** | 50,506 | 3 | 1 |\n| 60,302 | **296.3 ms** | 73,706 | 3 | 1 |\n\nControls at the same two volumes, same predicate shape:\n\n| Query | 30k | 60k |\n|---|---|---|\n| Raw `sample_movement` read on `sample_movement_inventory_idx` | 0.123 ms | 0.174 ms |\n| `sample_balance_by_location` (the view this one is built on) | 0.414 ms | 0.572 ms |\n| `/sample/list` page scan | 0.091 ms | 0.134 ms |\n\n**Doubling the data roughly tripled the time** (1.99x rows → 2.96x time, ≈ n^1.57), while the indexed control grew sub-linearly. At 60k movements the view is ~520x slower than the balance view it wraps and ~1700x slower than the equivalent indexed read.\n\nExtrapolating that exponent — and it is an extrapolation, not a measurement — ~240k movements lands near 2.7s and ~1M movements near 25s. The BFF proxy times out at 30s (`designflow-bff/routes/api.js` `PROXY_TIMEOUT_MS`). This is the same failure shape as incident SAMPLE-LIST-001, where a slow sample read surfaced to users as \"Failed to load samples\".\n\n## Why no index can help as written\n\nTwo things in the view definition, both structural:\n\n1. **The filter columns are `CASE` expressions.** The view rewrites `to_location_type` / `to_location_id` into `product_location_type` / `product_location_id` to fold the `terminal/nyc_office_inventory` and `terminal/ningbo_office_inventory` leftover buckets into `office/nyc` and `office/ningbo`. A plain column index cannot match a predicate on a `CASE` result, which is why `sample_movement_inventory_idx` is never chosen even with `enable_seqscan = off`.\n\n2. **`available_since` needs an OR self-join.** The view LEFT JOINs `sample_movement` back onto itself with `(m.to_location_* = b.location_*) OR (m.from_location_* = b.location_*)` to find `max(occurred_at)`. An OR across two column pairs is not indexable, so the plan becomes a nested loop over aggregated movement rows. That join is what discards 73,706 rows to return 100.\n\n## Possible directions (the orchestrator's call, not mine)\n\nI am not proposing a specific migration — the shape of the fix is your decision. Options that seem open:\n\n- Expression indexes on `sample_movement` matching the view's exact `CASE` predicates.\n- Rewrite `available_since` as a `UNION ALL` of the to-side and from-side instead of an OR join, so each branch can use `sample_movement_destination_idx` / `sample_movement_source_idx` (both already exist and both are chosen when the OR is removed).\n- Materialize or incrementally maintain `available_since` per (sample, location).\n- A different projection that keeps the leftover-bucket folding without wrapping the filter columns.\n\nRelated: the step-1 contract in the app-side plan specifies an inventory index on `(location_type, location_id, available_since desc, sample_id)`. No index with that shape exists; `sample_movement_inventory_idx (to_location_type, to_location_id, occurred_at DESC, sample_id_fk)` shipped instead. Worth reconciling either the contract text or the structure.\n\n## Not urgent, and why\n\nNothing consumes this view in production yet. The inventory UI is plan step 10, still unstarted. So this can be scheduled properly rather than rushed. It should land before step 10 ships.\n\n## Reproducing\n\nPreview now holds tagged fixture data from this measurement: **~40,200 `dflow.sample` rows and ~60,300 `dflow.sample_movement` rows**, all named / stamped `AI-PERF-20260818-inventory-*`.\n\nI could not remove them. `sample_movement_immutable_trigger` correctly blocks `DELETE` on the movement ledger, and I did not verify that before seeding — that is my error, recorded rather than hidden. Two consequences worth knowing:\n\n- Preview planner statistics for `dflow.sample` and `dflow.sample_movement` are now shaped by this fixture data, so another session measuring something else in preview may get skewed numbers until the branch is rebuilt.\n- Fixture movements were written through `dflow.post_sample_movement()`, never by direct insert, so the ledger's own rules were respected throughout.\n\nEvery fixture write proved the target immediately beforehand per `AGENTS.md` §4.2 and refused to proceed unless the live session identity named `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`; production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` was never connected to.\n\nThe seed and measurement harness is small and I can attach or re-run it on request.\n\n\n---\n\n## Orchestrator classification, 2026-08-19 (marker #1207)\n\nClassified as structural and routed to the orchestrator. The exact remedy — index-backed view rewrite, a materialized read model, or an index on the underlying movement table — is the author's design decision, so the object claim below covers all three candidates and must be narrowed by the author before their claim is taken.\n\n**Note on the evidence:** the measurements above were taken on preview `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`, which was DELETED and rebuilt on 2026-08-18 (#1188). The replacement is `mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs` and it does not carry that seeded data. The measurements remain valid as evidence of the shape of the problem; they cannot be reproduced by re-running against preview without re-seeding.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 400\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - view dflow.sample_inventory\n  - table dflow.sample_movement\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-26T01:48:29Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T17:26:48Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1181,"title":"dflow.sample_inventory cannot use an index and degrades super-linearly (measured: 100ms at 30k movements, 296ms at 60k)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:30Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1181"},

{"body":"## Request\n\nImplement the shared-database prerequisite for u2giants/popdam3 issue #92 and plan_openrouter_batch_restart_recovery.md Step 1.\n\n## Required contract\n\nExtend public.update_bulk_operation through a new timestamped canonical migration. Preserve existing callers while adding a guarded compare-and-swap path that:\n\n- compares the stored operation state_revision with the caller expected revision;\n- atomically claims submission_owner and lease_expires_at;\n- returns the saved operation row/state so the worker can prove the expected revision, owner, and provider batch ID were stored;\n- refuses stale writes that could overwrite Stop, a newer revision, or a live or ambiguous external_job;\n- makes an expired submission lease without a saved batch ID ambiguous instead of allowing automatic resubmission;\n- keeps p_only_if_status equals running protection;\n- remains backward-compatible only where legacy callers cannot clobber protected external-job state.\n\nThe current canonical definition is present in supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql. Inspection found no existing migration-level compare-and-swap or lease equivalent on current origin/main.\n\n## Required proof\n\n- Dedicated shared-db branch and new unique migration timestamp.\n- SQL behavior tests proving only one worker can claim a revision/lease.\n- Tests proving expired lease without batch ID becomes ambiguity.\n- Tests proving old callers remain compatible but cannot overwrite protected state.\n- Preview dry-run and apply against rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel.\n- PR merged by the shared-db coordinator and production promotion status recorded.\n\n## Dependency\n\nPopDAM application implementation must not begin until this contract has landed as required by its approved plan. Link the merged PR and applied migration back to u2giants/popdam3#92.\n\n---\n\n## Orchestrator classification (2026-08-18)\n\nVerified on `origin/main`: bulk-operation state is **not** a table. It is a single JSONB value in `public.admin_config` under key `BULK_OPERATIONS`, written by `public.update_bulk_operation` and by `public.update_bulk_operations_batch` (`supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:6324` and `:6367`). There is no `state_revision`, `submission_owner`, or `lease_expires_at` anywhere on that path today.\n\nThe batch function is claimed too: it writes the same key and is exactly the legacy caller that could clobber protected external-job state, so the author must prove it cannot.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 700\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - function public.update_bulk_operation\n  - function public.update_bulk_operations_batch\n  - table public.admin_config\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T14:55:35Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T14:52:30Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1171,"title":"HANDOVER: Guard PopDAM bulk-operation state with revision and submission lease","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:37Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1171"},
{"body":"Started: 2026-08-18T14:50:00Z\nMachine: al8960ofc\nSession: claude-20260818-145000Z\nPredecessor marker: #1152 (closed)\nIngested: HANDOFF.d/2026-08-18T1435Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-closeout.md, issue #1164.\n\nPurpose: sole orchestrator. Resume #1090 (issue #1143 / claim #1144 / PR #1145 / handover #1164) — the single live structural workstream. It is blocked on the version-supersession readback race (#1165), not on the migration itself. {"body":"**This needs Albert, and it is a business-triage question, not a technical one.**\n\nThe `db-work` queue holds ~90 open issues. A full classified audit on 2026-08-18 found:\n\n| work type | count |\n|---|---|\n| repo-maintenance | 55 |\n| source-data | 9 |\n| documentation | 8 |\n| curated-master-data | 8 |\n| application-data | 2 |\n| security-settings | 1 |\n| **structural (this repo's actual job)** | **1** |\n\nThat single structural item is #555, and it is blocked.\n\nSo shared-db is carrying a large backlog that mostly belongs to other routes — scraping sessions, documentation, application data, and general maintenance. Those never consume a migration-author lane, and they should not be triaged by the database orchestrator either.\n\n**The risk is not the count.** It is that a fresh orchestrator opening this repo sees ~90 open issues and cannot tell, without a full re-audit, that only one is its work. That has already caused a wrong \"there is no pending work\" report once in this repo's history, in the opposite direction.\n\n## The question for Albert\n\nWhich of these do you actually still want done? Most look like they were filed as \"worth recording\" rather than \"please do this\", and several are 2+ months old.\n\nA one-hour pass with you closing the dead ones would leave a queue that means something. Nobody but you can decide which of your own business items are still live.\n\nThe orchestrator can then route the survivors to their correct sessions.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 400\nobjects: []\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T12:32:03Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T14:34:01Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"`supersedeActiveClaimVersion` in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` renames the migration, pushes the commit, then re-reads the pull request's file list through the GitHub API to confirm the rename landed. When the API has not yet caught up with the commit just pushed, the readback disagrees and the tool rolls the rename back with:\n\n```\nREFUSED: PR did not expose exactly the new reserved migration\n```\n\nRolling back on an unproven readback is CORRECT and must not change. The defect is that the readback has no bounded retry, so a transient lag is treated as a permanent failure.\n\n**The cost is not just a retry.** Every attempt permanently burns a migration version reservation, because reservations are never reused by design. Two versions — `20260818142815` and `20260818142855` — were consumed this way on 2026-08-18 while trying to unblock #1090, and they are gone forever.\n\nThis repo already has the right pattern in several places: bounded retry with exact readback, retrying only transient transport failures while semantic failures still stop immediately. `readRefAfterWrite` and the production owner-comment read both do this.\n\nObserved 2026-08-18 on PR #1145. The same tool succeeded on the first attempt for #1126 and #1117 the same day, which is what identifies it as a race rather than a logic error.\n\n## Fix\n\nApply bounded retry with exact readback to the PR-file readback specifically. Do not widen it to semantic mismatches — a genuinely wrong file list must still refuse immediately and roll back.\n\n## Test\n\nA readback that returns a stale file list once and the correct one on retry must succeed without burning a second reservation; a readback that stays wrong must still refuse and roll back.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 800\nobjects: []\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-18T17:39:59Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T14:33:48Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1165,"title":"Version supersession burns a permanent reservation on a transient GitHub readback lag","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:41Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1165"},
{"body":"Sample Tracking Release A and #1115 are both live in production. The remaining structural workstream is #1090, and it is blocked on a tooling race, not on the migration.\n\n## State, verified 2026-08-18T14:32Z\n\n- `origin/main` = `12b1ef7ffc0e2adedb5989620325fd4963d5a925`\n- PR #1145, branch `codex/issue-1143-fr-ruling-forward`, worktree `C:\\repos\\shared-db-worktrees\\issue-1143-fr-ruling-forward` (clean, LIVE, do not retire)\n- Claim #1144 renewed, expires `2026-08-18T22:28Z`, version still `20260817232425`\n- All checks green EXCEPT `SQL migration guards` and `Migration author lease`\n\n## The blocker\n\nMain now carries `20260818141220`, so `20260817232425` is backdated and the guard refuses it. The version must be re-reserved, and `--supersede-active-claim-version` fails repeatedly:\n\n```\nREFUSED: PR did not expose exactly the new reserved migration\n```\n\nThe branch shows it renaming forward and then rolling itself back:\n\n```\n3cbc028 migration: re-reserve 20260818142855 as 20260817232425   <- rollback\n66cbf1d migration: re-reserve 20260817232425 as 20260818142855   <- rename\n```\n\nThe rename lands, the tool re-reads the PR file list through the GitHub API to confirm it, the API has not caught up with the commit it just pushed, and the tool correctly rolls back rather than proceed on an unproven readback.\n\n**This is a race, not a defect in the migration.** The same tool succeeded first time on #1126 and #1117 earlier today.\n\n## Why I stopped instead of retrying\n\nEvery attempt permanently burns a version reservation. `20260818142815` and `20260818142855` are now spent and can never be reused. A retry loop would burn more of a finite resource against a timing problem.\n\n## Next steps\n\n1. Retry the supersession once, after a pause. If it succeeds, continue from step 2.\n2. If it fails again, add bounded retry-with-exact-readback to the PR-file readback in `supersedeActiveClaimVersion` — the same pattern this repo already uses for other GitHub reads. That is a real tooling gap and should be its own issue.\n3. Fresh exact-head independent review of #1145. **The interrupted sequences 154, 155 and 157 are NOT approval.**\n4. Guarded merge, then the remaining FR removal and strict-cleanup phase under fresh claims.\n5. Promote the complete ordered package in ONE bounded event. Never `20260817124545` alone — a production review found that alone would block held migration `20260802171000` and make the settled FR removal sequence impossible.\n\n## Held migrations\n\n`20260802170000` and `20260802171000` remain deliberately unapplied. Their interaction with #1090 is the entire reason the forward-compatibility package exists.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 1000\ndepends_on: 1143\nobjects:\n  - function app.enforce_licensing_write_authority\n  - table core.licensor\n  - table core.taxonomy_owner_ruling\n  - table plm.licensing_write_authorization\n  - table plm.licensing_write_guard_audit\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-26T02:42:34Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T14:33:34Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1164,"title":"HANDOVER: finish #1090 licensing package — blocked on a version-supersession race","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:43Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1164"},
{"body":"Albert requested a permanent `core.*` table for `mgCategory`, using the first column of `docs/verification/item-mg-reclassification-20260814/data/MerchGroup_Rework.xlsx` as the controlling business logic.\n\n## Required outcome\n\nCreate a normalized category list and an explicit relationship from each category to the real MG01 product types. Do not treat the existing free-text `mgCategory` columns on `core.\"merchGroup\"` and `core.\"merchGroupMaster\"` as the category master.\n\nRecommended structure for the migration author to validate against current naming and key conventions:\n\n- `core.mg_category`: one row per product category, with a stable key, display name, active status, and ordering.\n- `core.mg_category_merch_group`: the explicit relationship from a category to the applicable MG01 merchandise-group/product-type row(s). Preserve division/company scope through the referenced merchandise-group identity. Do not rely only on a globally unique MG01 code unless the live keys prove that assumption.\n\nThe workbook's category-to-MG01 mapping is:\n\n| Category | MG01 product types |\n|---|---|\n| Wall | A Stretched/Box; B Framed; C Plaque; D Functional; E Other Wall |\n| Tabletop | F Block; G Box; H Photo Frames; J Object; K Other Tabletop |\n| Clock | M Clocks |\n| Storage | N Soft Storage; P Hard Storage; R Other storage |\n| Workspace | S Stationery org; T Desk Acc; U Other workspace |\n| Floor | V Floor coverings |\n| Garden | W Garden |\n\nThe category is a hidden grouping used to constrain downstream logic, not another MG hierarchy level. The workbook labels column A `Prod Category- (no one sees this)` and columns B/C `MG01 code` / `MG01 - Product Type`. The `Sizes` tab independently confirms category groupings by MG01 code, including A-E Wall, F-K Tabletop, and S-U Workspace.\n\n## Existing state verified live on 2026-08-18\n\n- Supabase production project: `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\n- There is no table named `mgCategory` or `mg_category`.\n- `core.\"merchGroup\"` and `core.\"merchGroupMaster\"` each have a nullable free-text `mgCategory` column.\n- No database writes, migration files, branches, worktrees, commits, preview applies, or production applies were made by the requesting session.\n\n## Acceptance checks\n\n1. The seven categories exist exactly once.\n2. Every mapped MG01 product type above resolves to the correct category.\n3. A product type cannot be assigned to two categories unless an explicit business rule permits it.\n4. Relationships remain correct across company/division-specific merchandise-group rows.\n5. The design exposes a clear read contract for applications needing category, MG01 code, and MG01 product-type name.\n6. Migration tests cover all 19 category-to-MG01 mappings and reject invalid or duplicate mappings.\n7. Preview is proven before merge; production promotion follows the governed path.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 900\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - table core.mg_category\n  - table core.mg_category_merch_group\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T00:13:03Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T14:14:37Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1163,"title":"REQUEST: create core mgCategory taxonomy and MG01 product-type mapping","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:44Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1163"},
{"body":"Found by GLM 5.3 during independent review of #1160.\n\n`prove_preview_migration_contents` historical branch in `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py` checks migration name presence and ledger stability. It never compares digests. The byte-binding added by #1157 exists only on the ordinary apply path.\n\nSo a version whose bytes changed after preview applied it passes both the v1 and v2 historical proofs. That is not hypothetical: it is exactly Sample Tracking Release A `20260814130000`, which was applied to preview from an intermediate file that later changed before merge.\n\nPre-existing and not introduced by #1160, but #1160 is its first real consumer, so it should no longer be implicit.\n\nConsider binding the historical proof to bytes as well, or stating in the evidence record itself that the proof is ledger-and-authorship only so no future reader over-trusts it.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 600\nobjects: []\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:16:04Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T13:04:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1161,"title":"Historical preview proof is filename-based, not byte-based","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:46Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1161"},
{"body":"Found by GLM 5.3 during independent review of #1157.\n\n`prove_preview_migration_contents` compares the preview content manifest digest (raw bytes, from `compute_content_manifest`) against the atomic policy hash computed by `canonical_sha256` (CRLF normalised to LF) in `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py`. For any atomic migration authored with CRLF line endings the two can never agree, so the version can never be promoted through the atomic path.\n\nFail-closed, so it is not a safety hole. It is a permanent false reject, and it contradicts the rule stated in `manifest_sha256`: both sides of a digest comparison must use the same function.\n\nPre-existing; deliberately NOT widened into #1157, which was already changing a production safety gate.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 300\nobjects: []\n```","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:16:03Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T11:26:26Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1158,"title":"Atomic migration path mixes raw-byte and CRLF-normalised digests, so a CRLF atomic migration can never pass","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1158"},
{"body":"The production business-risk gate proves a rehearsal happened by comparing **commit identity**, not by comparing what was rehearsed. `prove_preview()` requires the preview run's `head_sha` to equal the source PR head. That proxy fails in both directions.\n\n**Too strict.** Any commit landing after a successful preview apply permanently strands the promotion. The rehearsal cannot be repeated, because `validate_candidates()` in `production_migration_guard.py` refuses to re-apply a version already in the preview ledger — in dry-run as well as apply. So a single follow-up commit is unrecoverable.\n\nThis is not hypothetical, and it is not an edge case: it fires on the repository's own required workflow. Generated types must be produced **from** the repaired preview, so the types commit necessarily lands **after** the preview apply. Doing the required thing breaks the gate. It blocked Sample Tracking Release A (#1149) on 2026-08-18.\n\n**Not strict enough.** For non-atomic migrations the same function checks only that the migration *filename* appears in the preview output. A file whose bytes changed under the same version number was never compared on that path. Byte comparison exists only for versions named in `config/atomic-migration-allowlist.json`.\n\n**The proof is already collected and unused.** `compute_content_manifest()` writes a SHA-256 of every migration file, the preview workflow uploads it as `migration-content-manifest.json`, and the atomic path already consults it. Non-atomic versions ignore it.\n\nIndependent design review by Grok (grok-4.6) recommended replacing commit identity with provenance plus content binding, and explicitly rejected the alternatives: freezing the branch after preview (fights generated types and squash merges, and will be bypassed), re-applying an already-applied version (that is a second real write, not a rehearsal), and routing this through the owner-decision hatch (it is an evidence-validity problem, not a business risk).\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 900\nobjects: []\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-18T12:06:46Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T11:13:04Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1156,"title":"Production gate proves rehearsals by commit identity, which is both too strict and too weak","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:49Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1156"},
{"body":"The durable reviewer registry in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` lists the GLM reviewer as `glm-5.2`, but the approved wrapper `ai-devops/bin/ai-glm` has pinned `MODEL=glm-5.3`, and its own doctor reports `model glm-5.3 available`.\n\nSo the model in use was already correct. The **label** was wrong, and the label is what gets written into permanent review evidence and review artifacts. Past GLM reviews are therefore attributed to a model that did not perform them.\n\nFound while assigning review sequence 158 for #1115. Reported by Albert, who asked for it corrected at the source rather than worked around.\n\nThe fix must not simply rename the entry: reviewer names are read back out of permanent coordination refs (`parseReviewCursor` then `REVIEWERS.find(...)`), and that lookup at line 457 is not null-guarded, so removing `glm-5.2` would turn every historical GLM review record into a crash. The retired name stays readable; only the active rotation changes, keeping the same slot so the round robin does not skip a turn.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 500\nobjects: []\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-18T14:03:50Z","createdAt":"2026-08-18T02:12:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1153,"title":"Reviewer registry records GLM as glm-5.2 while ai-glm actually runs glm-5.3","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:37:50Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1153"},

{"body":"Tracking issue for the remaining division-code work. Full detail: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-17T2146Z-al8960ofc-claude-division-code-qa.md` and `docs/division-code-round2-answers-and-reference-check-20260817.md`.\r\n\r\nQ&A with Uma is complete over two rounds and the `itemHeader` reference check he required has been run over all 363 unclean `core.\"merchGroup\"` rows. **The database has not been touched.** No migration exists yet.\r\n\r\n## BLOCKED ON THE OWNER — the only real blocker\r\n\r\n**78% of item history sits in DesignFlow division `2`**: 15,185 of 19,463 item headers, none active. Two rules contradict each other:\r\n\r\n- `plm.\"divisionCode\"` says id `2`'s `external_divisoncode` **is** `CW001`.\r\n- The agreed rule says id `2` is dead and must never be accepted as a division code.\r\n\r\nUntil Albert rules, `public.erp_items_current.division_code` (17,703 NULL rows) must not be backfilled. Options, recommendation first: treat them as `CW001`/POP Lic (what the bridge table says, preserves history, none are active); leave blank; or exclude from the item key.\r\n\r\n## Ready to build (each needs its own migration)\r\n\r\n1. Set `divisionCode_id_fk = 1` on `mg_id` 3120, 3121, 3580, 3581, 3582 — they are POP Lic (348 item references vs 4). Do **not** rewrite their text to `SP001`; that rule is withdrawn.\r\n2. Set `is_divcode_active = false` on `plm.\"divisionCode\"` ids `2` and `7`. Approved outright.\r\n3. Normalise `itemHeader.compan_code_fk` NULL/`2` to EDGEHOME. Approved outright. DesignFlow-owned table — confirm ownership first.\r\n\r\n## Blocked, with reasons\r\n\r\n4. The 217-row Block A fix — 142 are referenced by division-2 items, **and** the update creates 142 duplicate rows with no unique constraint to stop it.\r\n5. Deleting the 4 empty rows — 3 of them (`mg_id` 2, 3, 4) hold **573** item references between them.\r\n6. The `erp_items_current` backfill — blocked on the decision above.\r\n7. A `CHECK` constraint on division shape — last; 363 rows violate it today.\r\n\r\n## Ready with a caveat\r\n\r\n8. Delete the 178 unreferenced rows — safe against `itemHeader` **only**. RFQs, art pieces, style guides and PopDAM were not checked.\r\n\r\n## Other repo\r\n\r\n9. Remove the hardcoded division map from `designflow-data-syncing/helpers/utility.js`; read `plm.\"divisionCode\"` instead. Agreed by Uma. Belongs to the DesignFlow repos, not here.\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\r\nstatus: blocked\r\nwork_type: structural\r\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\r\npriority: 500\r\ndepends_on:\r\nobjects:\r\n  - table core.merchgroup\r\n  - table plm.divisioncode\r\n  - table plm.itemheader\r\n  - table public.erp_items_current\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T14:34:06Z","createdAt":"2026-08-17T21:53:35Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Problem\n\nThe required Cross-PR object collision guard fails closed when GitHub's Compare REST endpoint returns a transport failure. On 2026-08-17 GitHub returned HTTP 404 for every comparison tested, including shared-db main...main and public cli/cli trunk...trunk, while commit and branch endpoints remained available. This blocks otherwise safe pull requests.\n\n## Required permanent fix\n\nKeep fail-closed behavior and complete collision coverage. Use authenticated pull-request file lists and commit/tree data as a fallback only when Compare transport fails. Bind the fallback to the exact base and head. Detect pagination, truncation, incomplete history, and mismatches. Validate both sources when Compare works.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- Compare remains the primary source.\n- Fallback runs only for a Compare transport failure.\n- Exact base/head identity is verified.\n- Pagination and truncation fail closed.\n- Any Compare/fallback mismatch fails closed.\n- Regression tests cover Compare 404, complete fallback, identity mismatch, truncation, and a real object collision.\n- No database contact or schema change.","closedAt":"2026-08-17T17:12:24Z","createdAt":"2026-08-17T13:42:10Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1121,"title":"Make Cross-PR collision guard resilient to Compare API failures","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:48:21Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1121"},
{"body":"The protected production workflow verifies immutable owner-decision evidence twice, including a live read of the authenticated GitHub issue comment. {"body":"Requested from the PopDAM app repo for u2giants/popdam3#91, which owns the remaining\nOrderList application work after #853 closed. This asks for **one small structural\naddition** and nothing else. The item row load, the bridge refresh call, the evidence\nartifact and the `/orders` page are application-owned and stay in popdam3.\n\n## What is requested\n\nA set-based bulk relink function, e.g.:\n\n```\npublic.relink_dam_order_lines_bulk(p_limit int default null) returns jsonb\n```\n\nIt must apply **exactly the eligibility rule already enforced by\n`public.link_dam_order_line`** (migration `20260810100000`) — count DISTINCT\n`plm.style_tracker_item_bridge.plm_item_id` joined to `public.style_tracker_rows`,\nwhere `b.tracker_type = l.source_style_type` and\n`nullif(btrim(lower(r.sku)),'') = l.sku_normalized`; trim + case-fold only, nothing\nfuzzy — and write `plm.production_order_line.item_id` only where that count is exactly 1.\n\nRequired behavior:\n\n- only rows with `item_id is null`; never overwrite an existing link\n- never touch a line whose `master_data_match_status = 'manual'`\n- a SKU resolving to more than one item is left unlinked and visibly unresolved; the\n  automatic path must never break a tie (same rule the per-line RPC raises `23514` for)\n- rows with no candidate, and rows with no SKU (`not_applicable`), are left alone\n- stamp provenance in `metadata` the way the per-line RPC does\n  (`last_relinked_by` as a system actor, `last_relinked_at`, `link_candidate_item_count`),\n  and preserve the pre-existing `master_data_match_status` in metadata so a row that was\n  historically `ambiguous` and is now uniquely resolvable does not lose that history\n- return counts only (per-status before/after, linked, ties left, no-candidate), so the\n  caller can commit a counts-only artifact without reading row values\n- idempotent: a second run links nothing further and changes no business rows\n- `SECURITY DEFINER`, `search_path` set, execute revoked from `public`/`anon`\n\n**Whether the 436 currently `ambiguous` rows should be auto-linked once they resolve to\nexactly one item is the one semantic decision in this request.** Evidence below says all\n436 now resolve uniquely. Our recommendation is to link them and record the prior status\nin metadata, but the orchestrator owns that call.\n\n## Why this cannot be done from the application\n\nBoth blockers were verified live today against production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`:\n\n1. `public.link_dam_order_line` raises `authentication required` when `auth.uid()` is\n   null, so a service-role script or the Railway worker cannot call it. Driving it with a\n   copied browser token is banned in the PopDAM repo.\n2. The `plm` schema is not exposed through PostgREST: a service-role request with\n   `Accept-Profile: plm` returns **406** for both a table read and an RPC call. The\n   worker only speaks PostgREST.\n\nA direct `UPDATE plm.production_order_line SET item_id = …` from app code would bypass\nthe eligibility proof and actor stamping that `20260810100000` deliberately centralized.\nWe are not doing that.\n\n## Evidence, read-only, preview `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`\n\nMeasured with the shipped safe-forward bridge body live (`20260816110750`; function body\nmd5 `ef757a56e6e5de4fff488b29c4c21ab8`, **identical on preview and production**, ledger\nchecked on both) and `plm.item` populated on preview (19,315 rows):\n\n| Current status | Exactly one candidate | Ties (>1) | No candidate | Total |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| `unmatched` | 23,519 | 0 | 41 | 23,560 |\n| `ambiguous` | 436 | 0 | 0 | 436 |\n| `not_applicable` | 0 | 0 | 13 | 13 |\n\nPlus 1 line already linked manually through the existing per-line RPC during app\nverification. Total lines 24,010.\n\nProduction currently has `plm.item` = 0 rows, `plm.item_import` = 0 rows and\n`style_tracker_item_bridge` with 15,619 rows and 0 canonical links, so the production\ndispositions cannot be measured until the app-owned ColdLion item load runs there. The\nfunction is expected to be merged and preview-proven first; PopDAM will run it on preview\nimmediately after its item load and post the counts back here before any production use.\n\n## Not requested\n\n- No change to `api.dam_order_list`, the order tables, the bridge, or `plm.item`.\n- No change to `public.link_dam_order_line`; the human path stays exactly as it is.\n- No data load. The 19,315 ColdLion rows are application-owned and load through\n  `plm.import_item_master_data` from popdam3.\n\n## Related\n\n- u2giants/popdam3#91 (owns the remaining application work)\n- u2giants/shared-db#853, #868 (closed; structural half complete in production)\n- `shared-db/docs/verification/popdam-item-identity-reconciliation-20260816/README.md`\n- `shared-db/plan_popdam_order_list.md` — note its **open question 2** (all four OrderList\n  tables are `USING (true)` readable by every authenticated account) is still undecided\n  and becomes staff-visible when `/orders` deploys. Not part of this request, but it is\n  the same workstream and should not be lost.\n\n## Housekeeping observed from the app side\n\nThe `shared-db/` mirror vendored into `u2giants/popdam3` is stale: its newest migration is\n`20260816063532`, so `20260816110750` is absent there even though it is live in both\ndatabases. A sync commit would prevent the next reader from drawing the wrong conclusion.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n  - function public.relink_dam_order_lines_bulk\n  - table plm.production_order_line\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-18T14:23:53Z","createdAt":"2026-08-17T13:16:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1115,"title":"Add a set-based bulk relink RPC for PopDAM OrderList lines (public.relink_dam_order_lines_bulk)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:38:18Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1115"},

{"body":"# Owner ruling: establish the official licensing Master Data structure\n\nAlbert is ready to establish the official Supabase structure for:\n\n- Licensor\n- Property\n- Character\n- Style Guide\n- Asset metadata\n- Franchise\n\nThis issue must first update the canonical design contract in detail, then implement the reviewed structure through the normal preview-first migration process. Do not use the one stale DesignFlow-to-Supabase pull as authority.\n\n## Machine routing block\n\n```yaml\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\nowner_decision_recorded: true\nobjects:\n  - core.licensor\n  - core.property\n  - core.character\n  - core.style_guide\n  - core.franchise\n  - core.taxonomy_source_ref\n  - canonical licensing asset metadata table selected after current-schema audit\n  - canonical character/property relationship table selected after current-schema audit\n  - canonical style-guide/character relationship table selected after current-schema audit\n  - canonical asset/property relationship table selected after current-schema audit\n  - canonical asset/character relationship table selected after current-schema audit\n  - canonical asset/style-guide relationship table selected after current-schema audit\n  - canonical asset/franchise relationship table selected after current-schema audit\n```\n\nNames listed as “selected after current-schema audit” are deliberately not invented here. The author must inspect the current schema and merged-but-not-applied migrations, then reuse the correct existing canonical object or claim the exact new object before authoring.\n\n## Owner decisions, 2026-08-16\n\n### 1. Licensed-source scrapes are canonical for identity\n\nFor every licensor whose authorized portal we scrape, that scrape is authoritative for:\n\n- which licensor a property belongs to;\n- the official spelling of the property name;\n- the characters, style guides, asset metadata, franchises, and source-published relationships it actually exposes.\n\nFour licensed sources have been undertaken so far: Disney, NBCUniversal, Paramount, and Warner Bros. The same rule applies to additional licensed-source scrapes added later.\n\nWhere a licensed-source scrape conflicts with DesignFlow, the old Supabase DesignFlow mirror, ColdLion, or another internal record, the licensed-source scrape wins for property spelling and property-to-licensor ownership. Keep conflicting internal wording only as an alias or source reference when useful. It must never remain the canonical name.\n\n### 2. Disregard the one stale DesignFlow pull\n\nThe single stale DesignFlow import must not seed, overwrite, arbitrate, or validate the official licensing Master Data structure or its canonical values.\n\nRemove the contrary language in `docs/core-master-data-consolidation-aim.md` that says the property-to-licensor edge is seeded from DesignFlow where no scrape covers it. Do not carry that rule forward into code, migrations, loaders, documentation, tests, or review queues.\n\nHistorical DesignFlow values may be retained only as non-authoritative evidence, aliases, or source references. They cannot win a conflict and cannot create a canonical relationship merely because a portal has not yet been scraped.\n\n### 3. ColdLion controls Active versus Inactive only\n\nColdLion supplies the operational list of properties currently used by the business.\n\n- A canonical property present in the current successful ColdLion API set is `active`.\n- A canonical property absent from that current successful ColdLion API set is `inactive`.\n- Absence means inactive, never deleted.\n- A short, failed, incomplete, or suspicious ColdLion pull must not mass-deactivate properties. Existing completeness and shrink guards remain mandatory.\n- ColdLion does not decide the canonical property spelling or the owning licensor when an authorized licensor scrape covers that property.\n\nThis replaces older wording that treated status as manually curated after mapping. The computed status must remain reviewable and auditable, but ColdLion membership is the business rule.\n\n### 4. ColdLion and DesignFlow have no authority for characters, style guides, or assets\n\nColdLion and DesignFlow do not provide complete lists of characters, style guides, or assets. They must never create a complete-universe claim for those entities.\n\nFor the licensed sources we scrape, the authorized scrapes are the only canonical feed for those lists and their source-published relationships. Do not fabricate a relationship from co-occurrence. Preserve the distinction already documented for Paramount, where property/franchise co-occurrence on an asset is evidence, not a direct relationship.\n\n### 5. Weekly refresh is required\n\nEvery authorized licensor scrape must run weekly.\n\nEach weekly cycle must:\n\n1. capture the source faithfully into its source-specific landing tables;\n2. retain source identifiers and capture history;\n3. reconcile into the canonical licensing tables without creating duplicates;\n4. update canonical spelling and source-published relationships when the authoritative source changes;\n5. never delete canonical records merely because they disappear from a later scrape;\n6. mark missing source records for review and preserve their last-seen history;\n7. apply ColdLion membership separately to calculate Property Active/Inactive;\n8. produce a visible success/failure record and alert loudly on a failed, partial, or suspicious run.\n\nWeekly scheduling belongs to the scraper/application runtime, not to a migration alone. The database structure must support freshness, last-seen state, provenance, audit, and safe idempotent reruns.\n\n## Required canonical model\n\n### Licensor\n\nOne row per licensing company or separately administered licensing entity. Portal source references and aliases attach to that row. A licensor is not inferred from stale DesignFlow data.\n\n### Property\n\nOne row per real property/title. It carries one canonical licensor relationship unless a future authoritative source proves the business model genuinely requires more. The canonical name and owning licensor come from the applicable licensor scrape. ColdLion membership alone determines Active/Inactive.\n\n### Character\n\nOne row per real character. A character may belong to multiple properties, per the owner decision already recorded on issue #503. The relationship must therefore not be stored as a single `property_id` column on Character.\n\n### Style Guide\n\nOne row per source-defined style guide or collection that truly functions as a style guide. Preserve source terminology and identifiers. Style Guide to Character is many-to-many. A style guide may contain many characters and a character may appear in many style guides.\n\n### Asset\n\nCanonical metadata only, not the licensed artwork files themselves. Keep source identity, filename/path or source locator, timestamps, checksum where available, and source-published links to Property, Character, Style Guide, and Franchise. Relationships are many-to-many wherever the source permits more than one value.\n\n### Franchise\n\nOne row per source-defined franchise or equivalent family. Preserve source-specific terms such as NBCU IP Family. Store only direct source relationships as canonical relationships. Co-occurrence is evidence and must remain clearly labelled as such.\n\n### Provenance and aliases\n\nEvery canonical entity must retain all contributing source references without treating a short code as globally unique. Aliases preserve alternate/internal spellings. The source-specific composite identity must prevent cross-licensor and cross-division collisions.\n\n## Documentation changes required before migration authoring\n\nUpdate at minimum:\n\n- `docs/core-master-data-consolidation-aim.md`\n- the short routing statement near the top of `AGENTS.md`\n- any active plan or contract that says DesignFlow seeds the canonical parent edge, that ColdLion controls canonical spelling/ownership, or that Active/Inactive is independent of ColdLion membership\n\nAdd an authority matrix showing, for each entity and field, which source wins and what happens on absence or conflict. Add the relationship diagram and weekly-refresh contract. Link this issue as the owner-decision evidence.\n\n## Structural acceptance criteria\n\n- The six official entity types have one documented canonical home each.\n- No competing canonical licensing table is introduced.\n- Property spelling and property-to-licensor ownership follow the applicable licensed-source scrape.\n- The stale DesignFlow pull has no authority in consolidation logic.\n- Property Active/Inactive is derived from a guarded current ColdLion set.\n- Characters can link to multiple properties.\n- Style Guides can link to multiple Characters and vice versa.\n- Franchise relationships distinguish direct source statements from co-occurrence evidence.\n- Asset metadata can link to every relevant licensing entity without storing licensed files in this public repository.\n- All canonical rows retain source references, aliases, capture dates, first-seen/last-seen facts, and audit history.\n- Missing records are never hard-deleted by refreshes.\n- Weekly jobs are idempotent, guarded against partial pulls, observable, and alert on failure.\n- Existing source-specific landing tables remain faithful mirrors and are not mistaken for canonical tables.\n- Documentation, migration tests, API contracts, and DB Data Admin behavior agree.\n\n## Safety boundaries\n\n- Licensed row data and artwork files must never be copied into this public repository, issue, PR, logs, or outside review prompts.\n- Structure is implemented through branch, reserved migration version, isolated worktree, preview proof, independent review, PR, guarded merge, and the production business-risk gate.\n- Curated data consolidation is a separate governed data operation after the structure is ready.\n- No production write is authorized by this issue or by the owner decisions recorded here.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T22:27:50Z","createdAt":"2026-08-16T22:25:31Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":1086,"title":"Official licensing Master Data: canonical Licensor, Property, Character, Style Guide, Asset, Franchise structure","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:48:39Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/1086"},

{"body":"## Outcome\n\nExpose every Warner relationship that can be derived from shared asset evidence without misrepresenting it as a direct Warner assertion.\n\nCreate six read models:\n\n- `api.wb_inferred_franchise_property`\n- `api.wb_inferred_franchise_style_guide`\n- `api.wb_inferred_franchise_character`\n- `api.wb_inferred_style_guide_property`\n- `api.wb_inferred_property_character`\n- `api.wb_inferred_style_guide_character`\n\n## Required contract\n\nEach view must derive pairs only through the existing normalized Warner asset relationship tables. It must never insert inferred rows into direct relationship tables.\n\nEach view must expose both source identities plus:\n\n- `via_asset_count`\n- a support ratio suitable for distinguishing universal, strong, and weak evidence\n- first-seen and last-seen evidence timestamps available from the Warner landing records\n- `evidence_type = 'inferred_asset_cooccurrence'`\n- `is_direct = false`\n\nRules:\n\n1. Preserve many-to-many results. Never force one parent.\n2. Preserve exact source namespaces and IDs. Never merge identities by label.\n3. One-asset evidence remains available but visibly weak.\n4. Direct Product Property-to-Character relationships remain separate and authoritative as direct source evidence. The inferred Property-to-Character view describes asset depiction/co-occurrence only.\n5. Franchise-to-Property is a human-assignment suggestion for DB Data Admin, never automatic parentage.\n6. Views must update automatically when Warner landing rows refresh.\n7. Do not expose raw licensed row payloads or asset names/paths.\n8. Use security-invoker behavior and the existing Warner API access pattern.\n9. Add synthetic, Warner-free contract tests for pair counts, support counts, ratios, namespace isolation, multiple-right-side relationships, weak one-asset evidence, and direct/inferred separation.\n10. Add aggregate-only verification queries. Never place Warner labels or licensed rows in this public repository, PR, CI logs, or review prompts.\n\n## Delivery\n\nFollow the shared-db author-lane, object-claim, reserved-version, isolated-worktree, preview-lock, external-review, guarded-merge, and production-promotion procedures. Verify all six views on preview and production against live aggregate counts. Production promotion is part of completion unless the governed business-risk gate requires an owner decision.\n\nRelated source and prior specification: #588. The Warner landing tables already exist; re-derive current schema and ledger state before implementation.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstate: eligible\npriority: 350\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - view api.wb_inferred_franchise_property\n  - view api.wb_inferred_franchise_style_guide\n  - view api.wb_inferred_franchise_character\n  - view api.wb_inferred_style_guide_property\n  - view api.wb_inferred_property_character\n  - view api.wb_inferred_style_guide_character\n```","closedAt":"2026-08-16T20:03:23Z","createdAt":"2026-08-16T01:50:36Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake.
