{"body":"**Shape work is done and merged** (#1020, #1028, #1030). This issue tracks the two open actions.\n\nRead [`docs/coldlion-history-endpoints-shape.md`](../blob/main/docs/coldlion-history-endpoints-shape.md) and `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-14T2236Z-al8960ofc-claude-coldlion-history-endpoints.md` first. Do not re-probe the endpoints — seven one-month windows spanning 2019-2026 were already sampled (5,874 `orderHistory` rows, 3,411 `prodHistory` rows).\n\n### 1. Albert: send the questions to ColdLion\n`docs/_drafts/coldlion-history-endpoints-questions.md` is a complete, unsent draft. Only Q1 (a production-order line number) is a true blocker. An AI session must not send it; it goes from Albert.\n\n### 2. Build the chunked puller\nNot started, no code exists. Confirm scope with Albert before writing — in particular **how far back the history should go**, which is still unknown (earliest probed is 2019-06 and it returned data; no earlier boundary was searched).\n\nRequirements, all evidence-backed in the shape doc:\n\n- Chunk by **date window only** — there is no paging, and `page`/`size` are accepted and silently ignored.\n- **One request at a time, never parallel.** Response times ranged from under 1s to 51s unpredictably; the owner's stated constraint is not to disrupt ERP users.\n- Per-request timeout ≥120s; ~3s pause between requests.\n- Run as a **background task writing each chunk to disk**, so a stall loses one window rather than the run.\n- Implement the §4.3 dedupe rule and **alert loudly** on the ambiguous case (identical quantities) rather than guessing — collapsing wrongly erases real purchases, keeping wrongly double-counts them.\n- Unit tests, per the `tools/*.test.mjs` pattern. `tools/coldlion-sync-common.mjs` has reusable API-key handling, but **its `fetchPaged` is wrong for these endpoints** (it assumes paging).\n\n### Still unknown\n1. How far back the history goes — determines the size of the pull. **Settle before building.**\n2. Whether repeated calls for the same window return the same rows — matters for the recurring sync, not the one-time load.\n3. `stageCode` (`prodHistory`) and `divisionCode` / `salesOrderNo` (`orderHistory`) filters exist in the spec but were never exercised; the latter two are a possible second chunking axis.\n\n### Note on scope\nAny Supabase tables for this data are a **structural change** and must go through the orchestrator workflow. The shape work deliberately produced zero schema.\n\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-09-07T12:28:19Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T22:42:31Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Owner ruling\nThe orchestrator must keep all three migration-author slots continuously productive whenever eligible open work exists. Each slot has its own automatic queue grouped by exact database-object overlap, not by arbitrary issue order.\n\n## Required SOP\n- Maintain three concurrent author lanes.\n- Build each lane queue from open `db-work` issues after reading exact object scope, current claims, open PRs, blockers, and dependencies.\n- Never run overlapping database objects or full-body functions concurrently.\n- When a claim releases, automatically select and dispatch the highest-priority eligible non-overlapping issue in the same turn. Do not wait for Albert to ask for status or to say start.\n- Ask Albert only for a genuine business decision or exact production approval.\n- Skip blocked/owner-decision/data-only/non-structural issues without consuming an author lane.\n- Keep preview and merge globally serialized.\n- If no eligible issue exists for a slot, record the complete audit evidence; otherwise an empty slot is an orchestrator failure.\n- While an author waits for preview/review/CI, continue safe local work or prepare the next queued issue without creating overlapping migration files.\n- Recompute queues after every merge because object shapes, versions and priorities change.\n\n## Durable locations\nUpdate shared-db AGENTS.md, queue/claim tooling and tests, canonical ai-devops shared-db-orchestrator skill/reference/metadata, installed machine copy, and forward-test evidence. No database migration or preview/production call belongs in this SOP change.","closedAt":"2026-08-14T23:51:58Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T21:28:41Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Outcome needed\n\nAllow the guarded Warner normalized loader to load the verified source snapshot without inventing rows or replacing valid missing values.\n\n## Proven blockers\n\n1. `links-franchise-property-evidence.csv` correctly contains zero rows because STARLABS exposes no direct Franchise-to-Property relationship. `tools/sync-warner-starlabs.mjs` currently requires all eleven files to contain at least one row, so it refuses this truthful empty relationship stream.\n2. `assets-normalized.csv` has valid blank values for nullable asset fields. The CSV reader includes every header as an empty string, while `plm.wb_validate_normalized_row` and `plm.sync_wb_normalized_target` cast present empty date/size strings directly. Valid nullable source values therefore fail instead of landing as SQL NULL.\n\n## Required behavior\n\n- Keep the ten evidence-bearing Warner streams non-empty and fail closed on unexpected emptiness.\n- Permit the direct Franchise-to-Property evidence stream to be header-only when its declared row count is zero, without treating that as an extract failure.\n- Convert blank optional asset values to NULL before validation/casts. Continue requiring Asset namespace, source ID, file name, source path, and source URL.\n- Preserve all existing project-ref proof, pinned-commit, capture, shrink, privilege, and repeat-run guards.\n- Add synthetic tests for the truthful empty evidence stream and blank nullable asset fields.\n\nNo licensed Warner values or examples are included in this request.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-14T21:11:39Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T20:11:15Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":995,"title":"Allow truthful empty Warner evidence and nullable asset fields","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:49:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/995"},

{"body":"## Owner ruling\nAlbert approved replacing the single migration-author rule with safe concurrent authoring on 2026-08-14.\n\n## Required outcome\n- Allow up to three agents to author unrelated migrations simultaneously in isolated worktrees.\n- Centrally reserve unique migration versions before any migration file is created.\n- Require parseable exact object claims and reject overlaps or unreadable claims.\n- Keep preview application, pull-request merge, and production promotion serialized one at a time.\n- Require every waiting branch to update from newly merged main and re-run collision/version checks before preview or merge.\n- Preserve applied-migration immutability and all existing SQL/cross-PR guards.\n- Update canonical shared-db rules, dispatch tooling/tests, and the canonical ai-devops orchestrator skill so future sessions use the new rule.\n\n## Safety boundary\nThis issue changes coordination rules and tooling only. It must not create or apply a database migration and must not touch preview or production.","closedAt":"2026-08-14T17:58:02Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T16:47:02Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"```db-claim\nversion: 20260814130000\nobjects:\n  - function dflow.apply_sample_path_revision\n  - function dflow.post_sample_movement\n  - function dflow.reject_sample_path_revision_mutation\n  - function dflow.require_sample_path_revision\n  - function dflow.validate_sample_path_revision\n  - function dflow.validate_sample_shipment_line_header\n  - index dflow.sample_box_active_name_custody_uniq\n  - index dflow.sample_movement_inventory_idx\n  - index dflow.sample_shipment_active_tracking_uniq\n  - index dflow.sample_shipment_line_header_idx\n  - index dflow.sample_workflow_queue_idx\n  - table dflow.sample_box\n  - table dflow.sample_carrier\n  - table dflow.sample_creation_batch\n  - table dflow.sample_movement\n  - table dflow.sample_path_revision\n  - table dflow.sample_shipment\n  - table dflow.sample_shipment_line\n  - table dflow.sample_workflow\n  - trigger sample_path_revision_apply on dflow.sample_path_revision\n  - trigger sample_path_revision_immutable on dflow.sample_path_revision\n  - trigger sample_path_revision_validate on dflow.sample_path_revision\n  - trigger sample_shipment_line_header_route on dflow.sample_shipment_line\n  - trigger sample_workflow_path_revision_required on dflow.sample_workflow\n  - view dflow.sample_inventory\n```\n\n```db-author-lease\nowner: orchestrator:/root/issue_975_resume\nbranch: codex/issue-975-release-a\nworktree: C:/repos/shared-db/.claude/worktrees/issue-975-release-a\nexpires_at: 2026-08-15T07:30:35.5746181Z\n```\n\nAdopted into the ref-backed lease system without changing the already-applied preview migration or its version.\n\n## Request\nImplement Sample Tracking release A exactly from the frozen application contract below.\n\n## Scope boundary\nStructure only. The shared-db orchestrator owns branch, migration, preview proof, SQL tests, generated types, PR, merge, and any separately approved production promotion. Do not include later Flow 1 visit, Flow 3 approval, or Flow 4 request tables.\n\n## Application coordination\n- Consumer repos: popcre/designflow-tracking and popcre/designflow-frontend\n- App branch: sandbox-albert; PR base: develop; Uma merges app PRs\n- Canonical plan: popcre/designflow-frontend/plan_sample_tracking_full_restructure.md\n- Release A must land before any consumer deploy\n\n### Technical contract frozen on 2026-08-14\n\nThis contract is the step-1 exit artifact. It is based on the current `sandbox-albert` source in\nfrontend `25c2a658`, tracking `59b80f4`, backend `21d8355`, the canonical 20260721-20260724 Sample\nTracking migrations/tests, and the live shared-db work queue inspected on 2026-08-14. The database\nproposal remains additive and belongs to the shared-db orchestrator. Application repositories must\nnot add schema SQL.\n\n#### Current contract to approved requirement matrix\n\n| Requirement | Current contract | Frozen change |\n|---|---|---|\n| Four flows and nine paths | `sample.origin`, `direction`, status state machine, eight route legs | Add stable `workflow_type` and `business_path` identities plus append-only path revisions. Keep route legs as shipment segments. |\n| Single/group creation | `Sample.create` creates one sample; imports confirm rows separately; `sample_factory_group` requires factory ownership | Add neutral `sample_creation_batch`; one atomic guided-create command owns single, repeated-entry, inventory-selection, and import-confirm creation. |\n| Physical custody and quantity | Immutable `sample_movement`, `post_sample_movement`, balances, closeouts | Preserve unchanged as sole truth. Workflow, reservation, status, box, and shipment records never substitute for movements. |\n| Boxes | `sample_box`, membership, shipment item/line, vendor ownership checks | Reuse. Add active-name uniqueness by normalized name and current custody location. Box creation plus membership is one transaction. |\n| Shipments and tracking | Shipment lines are intent; courier/tracking also live as mutable sample/box strings | Add shipment header with stable carrier ID and tracking number. Boxed and unboxed lines share it. Keep old strings as compatibility projections. |\n| Carrier choices | Frontend hard-codes UPS/FedEx/DHL/USPS; no carrier table/API found anywhere in the six apps or shared-db | Add one canonical active carrier table. Seed only those four proven values. No automated delivery in this redesign. |\n| Five locations | Movement supports factory, office, customer, in_transit, terminal; offices are `nyc`/`ningbo`; no warehouse location | Add `warehouse` movement location and canonical `china_warehouse` ID. Display names are NY Office, Ningbo Office, Factory, China Warehouse, Customer. |\n| Inventory | Balance view plus office leftover buckets `terminal/{office}_office_inventory`; client list is bounded and filtered locally | Add a server inventory read model that unions ordinary balances and parked leftovers, exposes boxed/reserved/in-transit eligibility, accepts `since` or Show All, and preserves browser-visible selection. |\n| Factory visits | No visit-plan entity; route legs and events only | Release B adds ordered visit plans/items with requested-versus-Ningbo-added provenance and append-only state history. Diverging identical pieces get child physical-piece samples tied to one parent/batch. |\n| Flow 3 approvals | Photos/comments exist; no durable photo/QC approval state | Release D adds per-sample approval requirements, decisions, actor/time/note history, and a separate QC capability. |\n| Flow 4 | No remote request, physical-confirmation, reservation, or packing-queue entity | Release E adds request header/items, append-only state history, reservations, expiry, and Ningbo packing queue. Requests create no movement. |\n| Languages | Typed English/Chinese module dictionary and saved profile language exist | Extend the same dictionary; parity-test every new key. |\n| Hidden selection | Visible-node action policy exists on the client-side grid | Preserve client-side loaded rows through releases A-E. Server date filtering changes the row set, never selection ownership. |\n| Legacy rows | Old origin/direction/status fields remain authoritative to old UI | Display `legacy_unclassified`; never infer flow/path. New reads expose both legacy fields and nullable workflow contracts. |\n\n#### People, access, and command matrix\n\n| Actor | Real identity contract | Server-enforced capability | Commands |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| NYO | Internal JWT role in `admin`, `production`, or `sourcing_manager`; profile `office_location='nyc'` | `sample_nyo` derived from internal write role plus office | Create Flows 1/3/4, manage NY inventory/boxes, approve Flow 3 photos, request remote stock, ship/check in NY work. |\n| Ningbo | Same internal write roles; profile `office_location='ningbo'` | `sample_ningbo` derived from internal write role plus office | Check in, confirm Ningbo stock, manage boxes/packing queue, add visits, ship, receive factory returns. |\n| Vendor | JWT `role='vendor'` plus authenticated `factoryId`; existing actor resolver fails closed when factory is absent | `sample_vendor` scoped to exactly that factory | Create/list/update own Flow 2 offers, see assigned requests, add details/photos, pack/ship own samples. No office or other-factory inventory. |\n| QC | Internal authenticated user plus assignable `sample_qc` permission | New user-level capability returned by the profile/permission contract; initial data assignments are `dhuang`, `wchen`, `emmali`, never code constants | Confirm/decline warehouse pulls, mark not found, ship warehouse stock to Ningbo, perform required Flow 3 QC approval. |\n| Customer | Specific canonical customer ID on destination; no Sample Tracking login role | None | No check-in. Delivery remains carrier-linked/manual evidence until a supported integration exists. |\n\n`designer` and `sales` remain read-only where current reads allow them. Existing route-level role arrays\nare too coarse for the new commands; every command also checks office, capability, workflow state, and\nfactory/customer scope. The Vendor UI is a separate `/apps/sample-offers` route with only My Offers and\nassigned-work data. The current internal Sample Tracking menu remains unavailable to Vendor.\n\n#### Stable IDs and valid combinations\n\n- Flows: `nyo_purchased_factory_reference`, `vendor_unsolicited_offer`,\n  `nyo_factory_make_request`, `nyo_remote_china_inventory_request`.\n- Paths: `factory_ningbo_nyo`, `factory_ningbo_customer`, `factory_nyo`,\n  `china_warehouse_ningbo_nyo`, `china_warehouse_ningbo_customer`, `nyo_factory`,\n  `nyo_ningbo`, `ningbo_nyo`, `ningbo_customer`.\n- Product locations: `ny_office`, `ningbo_office`, `factory`, `china_warehouse`, `customer`.\n- Flow 1 permits `nyo_ningbo` and `nyo_factory`; its later factory circulation is the visit plan.\n- Flow 2 permits `factory_ningbo_nyo` and `factory_nyo`.\n- Flow 3 permits `factory_ningbo_nyo` and `factory_ningbo_customer`.\n- Flow 4 permits `china_warehouse_ningbo_nyo`, `china_warehouse_ningbo_customer`, `ningbo_nyo`, and\n  `ningbo_customer`.\n\n#### Product location and required route-leg map\n\n| Product location | Movement identity |\n|---|---|\n| NY Office | `office/nyc` |\n| Ningbo Office | `office/ningbo` |\n| Factory | `factory/<core factory id>` |\n| China Warehouse | `warehouse/china_warehouse` |\n| Customer | `customer/<core customer id>` |\n\nKeep the eight existing legs and add `ningbo_to_factory`, `factory_return_to_ningbo`, and\n`warehouse_to_ningbo`. Ordered path expansion is: factory-Ningbo-NYO = `factory_to_ningbo`,\n`ningbo_to_nyc`; factory-Ningbo-customer = `factory_to_ningbo`, `ningbo_to_customer`; factory-NYO =\n`factory_to_nyc`; warehouse-Ningbo-NYO = `warehouse_to_ningbo`, `ningbo_to_nyc`; warehouse-Ningbo-\ncustomer = `warehouse_to_ningbo`, `ningbo_to_customer`; NYO-factory = `nyc_to_factory`; NYO-Ningbo =\n`nyc_to_ningbo`; Ningbo-NYO = `ningbo_to_nyc`; Ningbo-customer = `ningbo_to_customer`.\n\n#### Additive schema proposal\n\nRelease A adds `sample_creation_batch`, nullable workflow/path identity on new workflow rows, append-only\n`sample_path_revision`, canonical `sample_carrier`, `sample_shipment` header, shipment-to-line relation,\nwarehouse movement support, the three missing route legs, and inventory/query indexes. The shipment\nheader stores `carrier_id`, `tracking_number`, origin/destination identity, ship time, state, actor, and\nidempotency key. Tracking identity is unique per active carrier/tracking shipment, not per sample.\n\nLater releases add only when consumed: `sample_factory_visit_plan/item/history` in B;\n`sample_approval_requirement/decision` plus the assignable QC permission in D; and\n`sample_remote_request/item/history` plus `sample_reservation` in E. Request and workflow history tables\nare append-only. Master factory/customer records are referenced, never copied.\n\nRequired indexes cover `(workflow_type, workflow_state, updated_at desc)`, inventory\n`(location_type, location_id, available_since desc, sample_id)`, eligible boxes by normalized active name\nand custody, shipment carrier/tracking, visit next-work, approval queue, remote-request queue, and active\nreservation uniqueness. Inventory pages are newest-first with stable sample-ID tie-breakers and a\nserver `since` filter; Show All omits `since`.\n\n#### Frozen state machines\n\n- Shipment: `draft -> packed -> shipped -> received`; customer-bound work uses `delivered_reported` or\n  `delivery_exception` after shipped. Only ship/receive posts movements. Cancel is allowed before ship.\n- Factory visit: `planned -> ready -> in_transit_to_factory -> at_factory -> returning -> returned ->\n  completed`, with `cancelled` before dispatch. Every transition records actor/time/note.\n- Approval: `required -> pending -> approved|rejected`; a superseding photo creates a new revision rather\n  than rewriting the decision.\n- Remote request item: `requested -> awaiting_ningbo_confirmation|awaiting_qc_confirmation ->\n  confirmed|not_found|declined`; warehouse items continue `in_transit_to_ningbo -> checked_in_ningbo`;\n  confirmed Ningbo custody continues `reserved_next_box -> added_to_box -> shipped_onward`. Reservation\n  expiry returns confirmed stock to eligible inventory and retains history.\n\n#### Legacy and duplicate-action compatibility\n\nLegacy rows have null workflow/path and display `Legacy / needs classification`. There is no inferred\nbackfill. For new rows, compatibility writes are: Flow 1 `origin='usa_bought'`, outbound direction,\nstatus reflecting the current real shipment/receipt; Flow 2 `origin='factory_offer'`, inbound direction;\nFlow 3 `origin='factory_request'`, inbound direction; Flow 4 uses a new neutral compatibility origin\n`remote_inventory_request` only after the shared constraint accepts it. `office_location` is a display\nprojection only; new custody screens read balances.\n\n| Active workflow state | Check In/Out | Ship | Qty Movement | Legacy status action |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Draft/request/offer/awaiting approval or confirmation | Disabled | Disabled | Disabled | Disabled; use workflow command |\n| Confirmed physical stock at actor's location | Reroute to receive/allocate command | Allowed through shipment command | Reroute to allocate/reconcile command | Disabled |\n| Packed, not shipped | Disabled | Reroute to shipment command | Disabled except explicit unpack/reconcile | Disabled |\n| In transit | Reroute to matching receive command for office | Disabled | Disabled except discrepancy workflow | Disabled |\n| At factory/office with active visit or approval | Reroute to workflow receive/return | Reroute to next approved leg | Reroute to workflow allocation | Disabled |\n| Legacy unclassified row with no new workflow | Existing actions remain under current server rules | Existing action remains | Existing action remains | Existing action remains |\n\n#### Endpoint contracts\n\n- `GET /api/tracking/sample/metadata` returns flows, paths, valid combinations, locations, route legs,\n  active carriers, actor capabilities, and contract version.\n- `POST /api/tracking/sample/guided-create` accepts contract version, idempotency key, single/group mode,\n  entry method, flow/path, placement/request action, batch details, sample rows or existing sample IDs,\n  and optional box/shipment details. It returns batch, samples, workflow, placement/request, box, and\n  warnings. The transaction is all-or-nothing.\n- `GET /api/tracking/sample/inventory` accepts location, `since`, Show All, eligibility, cursor, and\n  bounded limit; returns custody-derived rows with box, reservation, transit, and eligibility reasons.\n- `POST /api/tracking/sample/shipments` and `/shipments/:id/receive` own boxed/unboxed movement and\n  require idempotency keys.\n- Later release endpoints are `/factory-visits`, `/approvals`, `/remote-requests`, and\n  `/remote-requests/:id/items/:itemId/transitions`; each response includes current state and append-only\n  history. Vendor list is `/api/tracking/sample/offers/mine` and is factory-scoped server-side.\n\n#### Explicit gap proofs and decisions\n\n- Repository-wide search found no canonical carrier table, model, ID, list endpoint, or shared-db\n  migration. The only list is hard-coded in Angular and tracking links switch on strings. Release A\n  therefore creates the canonical carrier source.\n- Backend exposes JWT roles, `office_location`, per-user/role UI permissions, and Vendor factory\n  identity, but no QC role/capability. Use an assignable user permission, not another global JWT role.\n- Current movement constraints contain no `warehouse` type and no `china_warehouse` ID. Warehouse\n  custody needs the additive mapping above. No existing physical warehouse rows can be represented\n  honestly; do not reclassify existing office/terminal rows by guess.\n- The leftover trigger can remain unchanged. Its `terminal/*_office_inventory` balances are projected\n  into normal location inventory and use the same eligibility/date rules; movement history stays intact.\n- Vendor tenancy checks are already strong enough to reuse, but the current internal route/menu exposes\n  the wrong surface. A separate narrow route and factory-scoped endpoints are required.\n- One-month/Show All is a server date filter over the loaded result. The grid remains client-side and\n  every selection action still derives only visible loaded nodes, so hidden-selection safety remains\n  valid.\n- `sample_factory_group` has required factory ownership/lifecycle fields and cannot represent a neutral\n  creation group. Use `sample_creation_batch`.\n- Active box-name uniqueness is normalized name plus current custody location among non-closed boxes.\n  A collision returns 409 and the UI requires a different name; there is no silent disambiguation.\n- Carrier automation is explicitly deferred. This release stores a linkable carrier identity and\n  honest manual status only.\n\n#### Acceptance-criteria trace\n\nCriteria 1-5 map to metadata plus guided-create/batch; 6 to Vendor capability and My Offers; 7 to visit\nplans and child physical pieces; 8 to Flow 2, shipment, and receipt movements; 9 to approvals; 10 and\n14-15 to remote requests/confirmation/reservation; 11-12 to shipment carrier identity and honest\ndelivery evidence; 13 to inventory `since`/Show All; 16 to separate movement, box, reservation,\nworkflow, path, approval, and history contracts; 17 to nullable legacy compatibility; 18 to the typed\nbilingual dictionary; and 19-20 to steps 13-14. No acceptance criterion depends on an unknown contract.\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-17T17:54:01Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T16:09:07Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvGcdSA","name":"db-claim","description":"An agent is dispatched and holds these DB objects. Close when the work merges or is abandoned.","color":"B60205"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"# Albert: choose where Master Data matching decisions are reviewed\n\nThis issue is pinned above the normal Issues list. It asks one business question only.\n\n## What the review workflow does\n\nWhen an imported Disney, Paramount, NBCU, Warner, ColdLion or other source record does not match POP's existing Master Data with certainty, a person needs a screen where they can:\n\n- compare the source record with possible existing matches;\n- select the correct existing Master Data record;\n- approve creating a new Master Data record;\n- mark the source record unresolved when the evidence is insufficient;\n- see who made the decision and why.\n\nYou have already ruled that imports cannot create permanent Master Data automatically. This review screen is where the required human approval will happen.\n\n## Option A: DB Data Admin owns the review workflow\n\nDB Data Admin is the application at `data.designflow.app` used to administer the shared database and Master Data.\n\n- One matching process serves every POP application.\n- Decisions are not owned by whichever application happened to import the source.\n- Avoids building the same review tools in DAM, CRM, PIM and DesignFlow separately.\n\n## Option B: another application owns the review workflow\n\nChoose this only if the team should perform all matching decisions inside a different existing application. Your answer must name that application.\n\n- The chosen application becomes responsible for shared decisions used by every other application.\n- Additional integration will be required so the rest of the applications can see those decisions.\n\n## Recommendation\n\n**Choose A: DB Data Admin.** It already owns shared-data administration and provides one neutral place for decisions used by every application.\n\n## Acceptable answers\n\n- `A - DB Data Admin`\n- `B - another application: <application name>`\n\nNo production database change is authorized by answering this issue.\n\nSource workstream: #912. Orchestrator marker: #960.","closedAt":"2026-08-14T16:06:31Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T16:04:45Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":973,"title":"🚨 ALBERT ACTION REQUIRED: where should Master Data matching be reviewed?","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:49:10Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/973"},
{"body":"# Albert: one Master Data decision is needed now\n\nThis issue is pinned above the normal Issues list. It asks one business question only.\n\n## The situation\n\nPOP receives source records from systems such as Disney, Paramount, NBCU, Warner and ColdLion. A source may contain a licensor, property, character, style guide, customer or vendor that does not yet exist in POP's reviewed Master Data.\n\nThe system must decide what happens when it cannot match that source record to an existing Master Data record.\n\n## Option A: require a person to approve every new Master Data record\n\nThe import may prepare a proposed record, but it cannot create the permanent Master Data entry until a person reviews and approves it.\n\n- Lower risk of duplicate or incorrectly named records.\n- Slower when many genuinely new records arrive.\n- Uncertain records wait safely instead of being guessed.\n\n## Option B: allow automatic creation after technical checks\n\nThe system creates the permanent Master Data record automatically when required fields and technical validation pass.\n\n- Faster imports.\n- A source naming difference or source mistake can create a duplicate or incorrect permanent record.\n- Technical checks cannot determine whether two differently named properties are legally or commercially the same property.\n\n## Recommendation\n\n**Choose A: require human approval.**\n\nThis is the safer rule until the matching-review screen and its audit history have operated reliably. Automation can be reconsidered later using real review results.\n\n## Acceptable answers\n\n- `A - require human approval`\n- `B - allow automatic creation after technical checks`\n\nNo production database change is authorized by answering this issue.\n\nSource workstream: #912. Orchestrator marker: #960.","closedAt":"2026-08-14T16:04:44Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T16:00:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":972,"title":"🚨 ALBERT ACTION REQUIRED: may source imports create new Master Data automatically?","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:49:13Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/972"},

{"body":"# Albert: one decision is needed now\n\nThis issue is pinned above the normal Issues list. It asks for one business decision only.\n\n## What exists today\n\nThe old licensing system contains **19 license-agreement records** that need to be connected to the correct legal licensor.\n\nThese are not disposable rows. Each agreement has an existing ID that other records may depend on, so the safe approach is to preserve every agreement and identify its legal owner.\n\nA private evidence review found:\n\n- 10 agreements have one plausible licensor candidate;\n- 1 agreement has more than one plausible candidate;\n- 8 agreements have no reliable match;\n- a matching or similar name is not sufficient proof.\n\nThe agreement names and licensor choices are private licensed business data. They must not be copied into this public GitHub issue.\n\n## What approval means\n\nIf you approve, the coordinator will create a **private local review page** containing the 19 agreements.\n\nFor each agreement, you will choose:\n\n- one approved licensor; or\n- **Uncertain**, when the correct legal licensor cannot be proven.\n\nNothing will be assigned automatically. Existing agreement IDs will be retained. No production database change is authorized by this answer.\n\n## Acceptable answers\n\n- **A. Proceed with the private one-by-one review.** Build the private review page and preserve unresolved agreements as Uncertain.\n- **B. Defer the review.** Make no change; the licensing normalization work remains blocked.\n\n## Recommendation\n\n**Choose A.** It preserves every agreement, avoids guessing legal ownership, and lets genuinely uncertain records remain unresolved safely.\n\n## Reply\n\nComment with either:\n\n`A - proceed with the private review`\n\nor\n\n`B - defer`\n\nSource workstream: #912. Orchestrator marker: #960.","closedAt":"2026-08-14T15:54:55Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T15:35:31Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":968,"title":"🚨 ALBERT ACTION REQUIRED: approve private review of 19 license agreements","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:49:23Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/968"},

{"body":"Tracking issue for the four follow-ups left by the 2026-08-14 scrape-normalization\r\nsession. Full background, measured evidence and ready-to-send prompts are in\r\n`HANDOFF.d/2026-08-14T1346Z-al8960ofc-claude-scrape-schema-normalization.md` §6.\r\n\r\nThis issue closes when all four are done.\r\n\r\n- [ ] **1. Warner legacy cleanup.** Warner has two generations of landing tables live at\r\n  once. The retired set (`plm.wb_property_character`, `plm.wb_character`,\r\n  `plm.wb_franchise_property`, `plm.wb_asset*` legacy) is empty but still present, with\r\n  live functions pointing at it (`plm.sync_wb_property_character`,\r\n  `plm.begin_wb_capture_legacy`, `plm.finalize_wb_capture_legacy`). Send the prompt in\r\n  handoff §6 step 1 to the Warner workstream; do **not** drop those tables from outside it.\r\n\r\n- [x] **2. Tell the Disney session how to close #953.** The issue body explains the loader\r\n  change but never states the closing condition. Post the comment in handoff §6 step 2.\r\n  #953 closes when the OPA loader writes names to `plm.opa_property` / `plm.opa_character`\r\n  and has stopped writing `property_name`, `character_name` and `property_id` on the link\r\n  table. Those three columns are dropped only after they confirm.\r\n\r\n- [x] **3. Update the `nbcu-creative-assets-scrape` skill.** Migration `20260814050000`\r\n  made `property_label` and `character_label` on `plm.nbcu_property_character` nullable so\r\n  the loader can stop writing them. The skill still describes the old shape. Update both\r\n  the machine copy and `skills/shared/` in `u2giants/ai-devops`. NBCU has no issue of its\r\n  own for the eventual column drop — consider opening one.\r\n\r\n- [x] **4. Audit the Paramount schema.** Owner asked for it directly. Paramount is being\r\n  treated as the model the other three are moved toward, on the strength of a single\r\n  passing observation, and has never actually been audited. It has 33,862 assets in the latest complete capture. The older 119,304 figure incorrectly summed all four retained captures, including two failed captures, so audit and report **before** changing anything. The seven checks are in\r\n  handoff §6 step 4.\r\n\r\nContext for anyone picking this up cold: on 2026-08-13/14 Disney's OPA capture was\r\nnormalized (`plm.opa_property` 1,445 rows, `plm.opa_character` 9,613, link table 10,262),\r\nNBCU's duplicated link labels were deprecated, and `api.source_capture_inventory` was added\r\nso no session ever again guesses which table a loader writes to. That view exists because a\r\nsession reported \"Disney landed zero rows\" while 156,644 Disney assets sat in\r\n`plm.dcp_asset`.\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-14T19:07:08Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T13:53:58Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":958,"title":"Complete Warner legacy cleanup; Disney, NBCU and Paramount follow-ups are done","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:49:41Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/958"},
{"body":"## For the Disney scrape session: the OPA loader must change\n\n`plm.opa_property_character` is no longer a flat table. It was normalized on\nproduction on 2026-08-14 by migration\n`20260814040000_opa_property_character_normalize.sql`. **The next OPA load will write\ninto the new shape, so the loader has to be updated before it runs again.**\n\n### What changed\n\n| Before | After |\n|---|---|\n| one flat table, property name + character name repeated on all 10,262 rows | three tables |\n| no character entity table at all | `plm.opa_character` — 9,613 rows |\n| property identity implicit | `plm.opa_property` — 1,445 rows |\n| — | `plm.opa_property_character` is now the LINK table (10,262 rows) |\n\nRow counts verified on production after apply. Nothing was lost.\n\n### What the loader must do now\n\n- Write display names to the **entity** tables: `plm.opa_property.property_name` keyed by\n  `licensed_property_id`, `plm.opa_character.character_name` keyed by `character_id`.\n- Write to `plm.opa_property_character` **only** the ID pair plus `brand_property_id`.\n- **Stop writing** `property_name`, `character_name` and `property_id` on the link table.\n  They still exist and are marked DEPRECATED in column comments precisely so this loader\n  does not break today, but they are duplicates and will be dropped once you have stopped\n  writing them. Tell us when that lands and we will drop them.\n- Both entity tables have FK constraints from the link table, so **insert entities before\n  links** or the load fails.\n- Resolution to `core.*` now belongs on the entity tables (`core_property_id`,\n  `core_character_id`), not on the link row.\n\n### Three facts the old shape let you get wrong\n\nMeasured on the 2026-08-06 snapshot, on production:\n\n1. **Names are not identity.** 1,445 property IDs carry 1,444 distinct names and 9,613\n   character IDs carry 9,591 — two properties and 22 characters legitimately collide by\n   name. Every ID maps to exactly one name, so the ID is the key. Never deduplicate on a\n   display name.\n2. **A character is not owned by one property.** **609 character IDs appear under more than\n   one property.** The skill previously said character identity is \"scoped by Property\",\n   which invites a per-property character row; that is wrong, and the relationship is\n   many-to-many. This is also why `plm.opa_property_character` **must never be deleted** —\n   those 609 characters' extra parents exist nowhere else.\n3. **`brand_property_id` belongs to the pair, not the property.** 24 properties carry more\n   than one, so it stays on the link row.\n\n### Skill already updated\n\nThe shared `disney-source-data-scrape` skill is updated in `u2giants/ai-devops`\n(`e773fcd`): the landing section now names the three tables and the field split, and the\n\"OPA facts and limits\" section carries the three corrections above. Re-sync your skills\nbefore the next capture.\n\n### Not in scope here\n\nThe DCP side is untouched. `plm.dcp_property` and `plm.dcp_character` remain empty and are\na separate question — Disney's property/character universe currently comes from OPA.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-14T21:22:41Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T11:45:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":953,"title":"FOR THE DISNEY SCRAPE SESSION: OPA loader must write the new normalized tables","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:49:44Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/953"},

{"body":"Phase A of `plan_dispatch-collision-hardening.md` merged on 2026-08-07. **Phase B has never been started**, and its step 5b is the last open row of that plan's STATUS table:\r\n\r\n> | 5b | Release object refs on merge (CI) + a staleness rule for abandoned holds | B | open |\r\n\r\n**Why it matters.** The collision tooling now reserves schema objects so two sessions cannot write the same table at once. Nothing releases a reservation when the pull request merges, and nothing expires one whose session died. Held-forever reservations turn the guard into a permanent block on healthy work — the same failure shape as issue #658, where cleanup depended on a session that was already gone.\r\n\r\n**Read first, and not alone:**\r\n- `plan_dispatch-collision-hardening.md` — the STATUS table, then §14 \"DRIFT AFTER PHASE A\"\r\n- `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-07T0212Z-t16-claude-dispatch-collision-phase-a-done.md` — what Phase A actually changed, and §4's twelve dead ends, which are still in force\r\n\r\n**This issue owns that handoff file.** When Phase B lands, retire `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-07T0212Z-t16-claude-dispatch-collision-phase-a-done.md` in the same pull request. The handoff contract guard added in #658 will ask for it.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 250\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:09:54Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T03:42:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## What is needed\r\n\r\nAdd notification and upstream-fix state to `plm.taxonomy_resolution_review` so a\r\nfinding of the form *\"the source system is wrong and a human must correct it\r\nthere\"* can be tracked to closure.\r\n\r\nStructure change on a table owned by the ColdLion cutover workstream, so it is\r\norchestrator work rather than something a session adds ad hoc. Opened by a\r\nnon-orchestrator session per `AGENTS.md` §0.0.\r\n\r\nOwner ruling, Albert Hazan, 2026-08-13: when we establish that a source system is\r\nwrong, correcting our canonical row is only half the job — a human who can edit\r\nthat source has to be notified so the error is fixed where it originates.\r\nOtherwise every future pull re-presents the bad value, every reconciliation\r\nre-raises the same finding, and the canonical correction has to be defended\r\nforever. Recorded as `docs/core-master-data-consolidation-aim.md` §6a (PR #940).\r\n\r\n## What already exists\r\n\r\n`plm.taxonomy_resolution_review` models the finding well: composite source key\r\n(`company_code`, `division_code`, `mg_type_code`, `mg_code`), `entity_type`,\r\n`finding_scope`, `reason`, `evidence`, `confidence`, and a `conflict` value in both\r\nthe `status` and `resolution` CHECK constraints. That is the right home.\r\n\r\nWhat it has no notion of: **which system owns the fix**, **who was told and when**,\r\nand **whether the source has since been corrected**.\r\n\r\n## Proposed columns\r\n\r\n- `fix_owner_system` — text, CHECK in (`coldlion`, `designflow`, `licensor_portal`,\r\n  `canonical`). Not derivable from `source_name`; see the routing note below.\r\n- `notified_at` — timestamptz, null until sent.\r\n- `notified_to` — text; a role or profile reference, **not** a personal email\r\n  address (`AGENTS.md` §6.14, and this repo is public — the PII forward guard will\r\n  fail a PR that adds one).\r\n- `notified_note` — text, optional; how it was sent.\r\n- `upstream_corrected_at` — timestamptz, set only when a **fresh pull** shows the\r\n  source agreeing.\r\n- `upstream_verified_run_id` — reference to the sync run that proved it.\r\n\r\nConstraint to enforce the discipline: `upstream_corrected_at` may not be set unless\r\n`notified_at` is set, and a finding may not close on notification alone. Sending the\r\nmessage is not the fix.\r\n\r\n## Routing note — do not derive the owner from the source\r\n\r\nVerified against the live ColdLion API on 2026-08-13: `merchGroupDetails` returns\r\nonly `createdTime, createdUser, modTime, modUser, companyCode, divisionCode,\r\nmgTypeCode, mgCode, mgDesc, itemNoCode, mgCategory, mgCode2`, and the published\r\nendpoint list (`/customers`, `/inventory`, `/itemDetails`, `/itemImages`, `/items`,\r\n`/merchGroupDetails`, `/merchGroupHeaders`, `/order`, `/pickticket`,\r\n`/prepackDetail`, `/proddetails`, `/prodtracking`, `/receiving`, `/salespersons`,\r\n`/seasons`, `/vendors`) contains **no relationship, parent or hierarchy endpoint**.\r\n`designflow-data-syncing` declares `parent_id` on its `merchGroup` model but never\r\nwrites it from any sync path.\r\n\r\nSo a wrong **parent** is a DesignFlow record even though the row's other fields come\r\nfrom ColdLion. Name and code corrections go to ColdLion. `fix_owner_system` must\r\ntherefore be set per finding, not inferred.\r\n\r\n## First item to load once the columns exist\r\n\r\n| Field | Value |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| entity | property `CC` (COCO) |\r\n| keys | `EDGEHOME/CW001/06/CC` and `EDGEHOME/SP001/06/CC` |\r\n| source says | parent `ZZ` (DTR - NO LICENSE) |\r\n| correct value | parent `DY` (DISNEY) — owner ruling 2026-08-13 |\r\n| `fix_owner_system` | `designflow` |\r\n| canonical action | **none** — `core.property` already says `DY` and is correct |\r\n\r\n## Out of scope\r\n\r\nChanging `core.property` for COCO. It is already right.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstate: blocked\npriority: 200\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n  - table plm.taxonomy_resolution_review\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T12:17:07Z","createdAt":"2026-08-14T03:33:17Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":941,"title":"HANDOVER: track upstream source corrections (notification + upstream-fix state on taxonomy_resolution_review)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:49:53Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/941"},

{"body":"## What is needed\n\nWire the existing `licensing` role into DB Data Admin so a licensing manager can\noperate the ColdLion -> canonical property mapping screen **without being granted\n`administrator`**.\n\nOwner ruling, Albert Hazan, 2026-08-13: the person who runs the mapping screen is\na licensing manager, not a company-wide administrator. Do not grant\n`administrator` to `app.profile` `8f383a14-f303-4890-90a2-80306a2d4665` as a\nshortcut.\n\nStructure change (a new gate function plus RPC gating), so it is orchestrator\nwork. Opened by a non-orchestrator session per `AGENTS.md` §0.0.\n\n## What already exists\n\nVerified read-only on production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, 2026-08-13:\n\n- `app.role` already contains **`Licensing`** (`1da12588-4e71-4492-a682-260d5086d92d`),\n  slug `licensing`.\n- The `app_role` enum already contains `licensing`\n  (`admin,administrator,user,sales,licensing,designer,viewer,vendor`).\n- `app.has_role('licensing')` therefore already works.\n\nThe role is simply wired to nothing in DB Data Admin. Nothing needs to be invented.\n\n## The problem with the current gate\n\n```sql\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION app.require_db_data_admin_access() ...\n  if not (app.has_role('administrator') and app.has_explicit_app_access('admin'))\n```\n\nIt is one all-or-nothing gate for every DB Data Admin RPC. Satisfying it to reach\nthe mapping screen also grants Customers, Vendors, merges, product depth, and every\nother surface gated on `app.has_role('administrator')` across the shared database.\nThat is precisely what the ruling forbids.\n\n## Proposed shape\n\n1. **New narrower gate**, e.g. `app.require_licensing_manager_access()`: satisfied by\n   `administrator` **or** `licensing`, plus explicit application access. Same\n   `SECURITY DEFINER` / `search_path` shape and same `insufficient_privilege`\n   errcode as the existing function.\n2. **New `app_name` enum value** for the licensing surface (current values:\n   `dam,popdam,crm,styleguides,pm,plm,admin`), so a licensing manager never needs\n   the blanket `admin` grant. Adding an enum value is additive and safe; it must be\n   its own migration step because Postgres will not let a new enum value be used in\n   the same transaction that adds it.\n3. **Re-gate only the licensing RPCs** onto the narrower function:\n   `api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree`, the mapping/review RPCs when they are\n   built, and the grid-state and audit RPCs scoped to those entities. Leave\n   `db_data_admin_customer_*`, `db_data_admin_vendor_*`, all merge RPCs, and\n   `db_data_admin_*_product_depth*` on the administrator gate, unchanged.\n4. **Front end** (`apps/db-data-admin/`): render only the permitted tabs. The tab\n   strip is a convenience — the server gate stays the real boundary, per the\n   existing \"the denial is scoped to the panel, the tab strip stays\" behaviour in\n   `DataAdmin.tsx`.\n5. **Tests**: a licensing manager reaches the tree and mapping RPCs and is refused\n   on customers, vendors, merges and product depth; an administrator is unaffected;\n   a profile with neither role is refused everywhere. Add to `supabase/tests`.\n\n## Grants to apply after the gate ships\n\nFor `app.profile` `8f383a14-f303-4890-90a2-80306a2d4665` (currently active,\n`Designer` role, `crm` access only):\n\n- `app.user_role` -> the `Licensing` role\n- `app.app_access` -> the new licensing application value\n\nBoth are ordinary row writes once the structure exists. Record them in the DB Data\nAdmin audit store. Do **not** add `administrator` or `admin`.\n\n## Context\n\nTarget state and the mapping screen this gate protects:\n`docs/core-master-data-consolidation-aim.md` §4 and §5 (PR #932, refined in #934).\nRelated data reconciliation: #933.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-14T03:41:12Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T22:01:03Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## What is needed\r\n\r\nReconcile the canonical licensor -> property edge in `core.property.licensor_id`\r\nagainst the DesignFlow mirror, which is the owner of that edge. Five properties\r\nare missing and one parent disagrees.\r\n\r\nThis is a **curated Master Data** load into `core.property`, so it falls under the\r\n`AGENTS.md` §6.4 carve-out (matched-row abstention included) rather than the\r\n\"application session owns its own rows\" rule in §0.0-B. Opened by a\r\nnon-orchestrator session per §0.0.\r\n\r\n## Design finding — no schema change is needed\r\n\r\nThe edge is already stored in the correct normalized form. Measured on production\r\n`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, read-only, 2026-08-13:\r\n\r\n```sql\r\nselect count(*), count(distinct p.mg_code)\r\nfrom dflow.\"merchGroup\" p join dflow.\"merchGroup\" l on l.mg_id = p.parent_id\r\nwhere p.\"mgTypeCode\" = '06';\r\n-- 503 edges over 261 distinct property codes\r\n```\r\n\r\nEvery parent is `mgTypeCode` 05 (a licensor), and **zero** property codes resolve\r\nto more than one licensor across the four divisions. The relationship is a true\r\none-to-many, so the existing `core.property.licensor_id` foreign key\r\n(`NOT NULL`, `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, shipped in `20260724030000`) is the correct\r\nmodel. **Do not introduce a `core.licensor_property` junction table** — that\r\nwould be denormalization, and it would let the same property acquire two parents,\r\nwhich the source data does not support.\r\n\r\n`core.property_character` is the separate many-to-many and is unrelated to this.\r\n\r\n## The data gaps\r\n\r\nMissing from `core.property` entirely (present in the DesignFlow mirror with a parent):\r\n\r\n| Property code | DesignFlow parent licensor |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| `CHR` | `VM` |\r\n| `EX`  | `WB` |\r\n| `GW`  | `WB` |\r\n| `LB`  | `WB` |\r\n| `SGT` | `WB` |\r\n\r\nNote `CHR` (CHEERS), `EX` (THE EXORCIST), `LB` (THE LOST BOYS) and `SGT`\r\n(SUPERGIRL THEATRICAL 2026) also exist in the live ColdLion API; `GW` does not.\r\n\r\nOne disagreement:\r\n\r\n| Property | canonical `core` parent | DesignFlow parent |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| `CC` (COCO) | `DY` (DISNEY) | `ZZ` (DTR - NO LICENSE) |\r\n\r\n`core` currently says `CC` -> `DY`. `COCO` is a Disney/Pixar title, so the\r\ncanonical value looks like the deliberate curated correction and `ZZ` looks like\r\nthe ERP placeholder. **This one needs an owner decision before it is touched**;\r\ndo not flip it just to make the two sides agree.\r\n\r\nThere are no canonical properties whose parent is missing from the DesignFlow\r\nmirror, and no orphan rows (`licensor_id is null` = 0).\r\n\r\n## Constraints\r\n\r\n- `core.property.licensor_id` is `NOT NULL`, so each of the five new rows needs\r\n  its licensor resolved in the same statement. All five parents (`VM`, `WB`)\r\n  already exist in `core.licensor`.\r\n- Each new row needs a `core.taxonomy_source_ref` entry with\r\n  `source_system = 'designflow_plm'`, `source_table = 'merchGroup'`, matching the\r\n  37 licensor / 468 property refs already recorded.\r\n- Prove the target before writing (§4.2) and quote the proof.\r\n\r\n## Why this surfaced\r\n\r\nThe Licensors and Properties tabs on `https://data.designflow.app` read\r\n`core.licensor` / `core.property` through\r\n`api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree`. That function reports\r\n`feeder_available: false` on every load: `ingest.sync_run` has **no**\r\n`designflow_plm` rows and `plm.licensor_import` / `plm.property_import` are\r\nempty, so the tabs serve a one-time June 2026 snapshot. Wider context and the\r\ntarget state are in `docs/core-master-data-consolidation-aim.md`\r\n(PR #932).\r\n\r\n## Out of scope for this issue\r\n\r\nThe ColdLion source cutover, which already has a plan and a STATUS table in\r\n`fix_coldlion_licensor_property_cutover.md` and\r\n`plan_coldlion_licensor_property_accelerated_cutover.md`. Do not restart it here.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: curated-master-data\nroute: curated-master-data-governance\npriority: 300\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T01:48:16Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T21:41:07Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":933,"title":"HANDOVER: reconcile core.property licensor edge against the DesignFlow mirror (5 missing, 1 conflict)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:40:27Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/933"},
{"body":"## Owner ruling, 2026-08-13\n\nDCP Vault hosts several licensors or studios in one portal, but their captured source data must not share landing tables.\n\nRequired storage boundaries:\n- Disney data in Disney-only landing tables.\n- Lucasfilm data in Lucasfilm-only landing tables.\n- Marvel data in Marvel-only landing tables.\n- 20th Century data in 20th Century-only landing tables.\n\nThe separation must cover crawl history, sections and gaps, asset and style-guide identities, portal-tile observations, crawl membership, chunk proof, exceptions, and later metadata landing. Guarded loader functions must reject a payload whose studio does not match its target table family.\n\nExisting Disney rows must remain intact. The change needs a safe migration and a clear compatibility plan for the current plm.dcp_* objects. Do not place licensed source rows or names in this repository or issue.\n\nCurrent application-side fact: Disney-only rows were loaded before the crawler reached Lucasfilm. A later local checkpoint contains Lucasfilm capture data, but no Lucasfilm rows have been written to Supabase.","closedAt":"2026-08-14T00:04:00Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T21:37:23Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"**A process finding, not a bug.** Recorded because it cost real time on 2026-08-13 and the correction is cheap.\n\n## What happened, three times in one session\n\n1. I read the live catalog, saw Disney had 1 landing table where Paramount had 20, and **told the owner Disney's model was missing**. It was not — 17 tables existed as reviewed, merged SQL that had never been applied (#892).\n2. I told the owner a **security lockdown had been unapplied since 2026-07-29**, \"over two weeks exposed\". Wrong. `20260729120000` is **RETIRED**: its end state is already on production via `20260729130000` and `20260729180000`, and applying it now would **regress** production. `scripts/production_migration_guard.py:91` blocks it and explains exactly this.\n3. I told the owner an **owner ruling had never reached the database** and implied neglect. It is held back by **another owner ruling** (AGENTS.md 6.5, 2026-08-03) pending the FR removal work (#902).\n\nEach time a guard was right and I was wrong. Each time the correction was already written down in the repo.\n\n## The rule\n\n**\"Merged but not applied\" has at least three causes, and only one is neglect:**\n\n| cause | example | what to do |\n|---|---|---|\n| genuinely pending | the Disney landing migrations | apply through the gated workflow |\n| **retired** — end state already live by another route | `20260729120000` | **never apply; applying regresses production** |\n| **deliberately held** by a ruling or dependency | `20260802170000` / `20260802171000` | build the dependency first |\n\nSo: **run the drift check, then READ WHY each pending version is pending** before reporting a gap or pushing to apply. `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` carries a written reason for every block, and `RETIRED_VERSIONS` in `scripts/post_batch_app_verification.py` names the retired ones.\n\n```\nnode scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs --target production\n```\n\nExit 0 = no drift, 1 = drift, **2 = could not check, which is never \"no drift\"**.\n\n## Already done\n- `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs` + workflow + tests, merged in #893.\n- `AGENTS.md` carries a warning block above section 0 where a session orients.\n\n## What is NOT yet done, and is the ask here\n**The drift report lists pending versions but does not say WHY each is pending.** It would have prevented all three of my errors if it printed, next to each version, whether it is blocked by `production_migration_guard.py` and the reason string that guard already holds. That is a small change to an existing script and both data sources are already in the repo.\n\nRelated: #892, #902, #893.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-13T18:04:34Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T15:34:54Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":907,"title":"HANDOVER: make the drift report say WHY each migration is pending — 'not applied' was misread as 'forgotten' three times in one session","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:50:15Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/907"},
{"body":"**Waiting on Albert. This was asked badly once and needs re-asking cleanly.**\n\nOn 2026-08-13 I put two unrelated things to the owner as a single numbered item: the scope of the PopPIM grant fix, and this. He replied *\"that's a meaningless question\"* — which was a fair response to a question with no context attached. **The PopPIM half was then answered separately and is done (#866). This half was never actually answered.**\n\n## The finding\n\nThe ColdLion ERP base URL is plain **HTTP**, not HTTPS:\n\n```\nhttp://x5.coldlion.com/EhpApi\n```\n\nThe `X-API-Key` header therefore crosses the wire **in clear text on every request**, along with the entire response payload.\n\n## What is exposed\n- The API key itself, to anyone able to observe the network path.\n- The full merchandising taxonomy: licensor codes, property codes and names, and the audit fields (`createdUser`, `modUser`).\n\n## Why it matters now\nThis is the feed being prepared to run **on a schedule** against the shared database. Every scheduled run repeats the exposure, and the key is a long-lived shared credential rather than a per-run token. Once the mirror is scheduled the exposure becomes continuous rather than occasional.\n\n## The three things to establish\n\n1. **Does ColdLion expose an HTTPS endpoint**, on the same host or another? If so this is a one-line config change.\n2. **If it does not, is the traffic confined to a private network path**, or does it cross the public internet?\n3. **Can the key be rotated, and who owns that?**\n\n## Constraints\n- **Do not rotate the existing credential without owner approval.**\n- **Do not change the endpoint until HTTPS is confirmed to work** — a silent failure here stops the feed rather than securing it.\n\n## Related, and part of why this is urgent\nThe same investigation established that ColdLion has **no active/inactive/deleted concept of any kind**, so a property removed upstream vanishes with no tombstone. That is an argument for starting the scheduled mirror soon — which is exactly what makes the plain-HTTP exposure continuous.\n\nSupersedes the ambiguous framing in #875, which stays open as the original record.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: security-settings\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 600\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T11:42:57Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T15:34:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":906,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] re-ask cleanly — does ColdLion have an HTTPS endpoint? (the first ask was bundled and got no real answer)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:40:45Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/906"},
{"body":"Full context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-13T1535Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-disney-live-and-guard-lessons.md` §4.\n\nBoth PRs were independently reviewed on 2026-08-13 and **deliberately held**. Neither carries a migration. Neither is urgent. Full findings are posted as comments on each PR.\n\n## PR #864 — DO NOT MERGE as-is\n\n**Blocking:** the armed production preflight runs `sync-coldlion-licensors-properties.mjs` with **no `COLDLION_API_KEY` in the step env** (`coldlion-licensor-property-production.yml:539-545`; the production lane supplies it at `:296-297`). Without it, `readColdlionApiKey()` falls back to `op read`, and **the 1Password CLI does not exist on a GitHub runner**. The step dies at exit 1 under `set -euo pipefail` and the five lanes it exists to prove are all skipped.\n\nThe PR's \"all six runners verified locally to exit 0\" is true only on a machine with `op` installed. **The safety net looks armed and is not there at all.**\n\nAlso worth fixing in the same pass: `DEDUPE_DEFAULT_LOOKUP_LIMIT = 100` while the repo has 109 open issues, so `lookupExistingAlertIssues` never returns `exhaustive: true` and **every normal alert prints `DEDUPE CHECK FAILED`**. No alert is suppressed, but the alarm reserved for a real dedupe breakage fires constantly.\n\nWhat checks out: the read-only guarantee is **structural, not intentional** — no credential, no session, no `environment: production`.\n\n## PR #874 — mergeable, but fix two findings first\n\n**The atomic version reservation (#670) is genuinely atomic and Guard B2 (#651) is sound.**\n\nBut `extractOperations` (`check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:644-646`) strips every `$$…$$` body, which also strips `DO $$` blocks — **this repo's dominant idempotent-DDL idiom**. Measured against the real corpus: **60 literal DDL statements inside `DO` blocks**, none of them dynamic. Example: `20260722221100_dflow_sample_shipment_item_membership_uniqueness.sql` alters `dflow.sample_shipment_item` and `dispatchObjectKeys()` returns `[]`.\n\nThat is precisely the failure #563 exists to fix — a migration reported as touching NO OBJECTS, which reads as a clear.\n\nWorse, the anti-regression test applies **the identical strip** before counting verbs, so the test built to catch a blind class is structurally blind to this one.\n\nAlso: the documented superset invariant at `:616-620` is **false** on 21 of 440 migrations. Delete or correct it — a future session will rely on it.\n\n## Merge mechanics\nStrict mode: each merge flips the other PR to BEHIND and requires `gh pr update-branch` plus a full re-run. Auto-merge is off. **One at a time.**\n\nRelated: #876, #563, #670, #651, #551, #548.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-13T18:11:46Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T15:34:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":904,"title":"HANDOVER: PRs #874 and #864 are held on real defects — what each needs before merge","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:50:18Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/904"},
{"body":"**Waiting on Albert.** He asked for enough detail to take this to Uma, the DesignFlow PLM developer. The briefing is written and merged.\n\n## The briefing\n**`docs/division-code-questions-for-uma.md`** — 8 specific questions, each answerable with one fact, each paired with what breaks if the answer is wrong, plus a table of what we already verified so Uma is not asked those.\n\n## Why it matters\n\n`public.erp_items_current.division_code` is **NULL on all 17,703 rows**. The `plm.item` key is `company_code | division_code | item_no`, so every derived key is currently NULL. **This blocks #853 and makes the Phase 3/4 plan merged in #867 non-executable as written.**\n\nThe owner's answer was that divisions come from ColdLion and that DesignFlow also has them. Verified live, those are **two different encodings of the same real-world divisions**:\n\n- `plm.\"divisionCode\"` maps DesignFlow ids to ColdLion codes **many-to-one** — ids **1, 2 and 7 all map to `CW001`**. DesignFlow to ColdLion is decidable; ColdLion to DesignFlow is a guess between three answers.\n- ColdLion's fourth division **`EP001` has no DesignFlow row at all**, and in `EP001` the ColdLion type codes mean Product Line / Product Type rather than licensor / property.\n- **271 of the 3,553 fully-populated rows in `core.\"merchGroup\"` already contradict themselves**: 217 say `EH001` while their integer means `CW001`; 54 say `CW001` while their integer means `SP001`.\n\n## The questions that matter most\n- **Q1** — is `plm.\"divisionCode\".\"external_divisoncode\"` maintained by a process, or hand-entered once? It is the only bridge between the two code spaces anywhere in our data.\n- **Q2** — which of ids 1, 2, 7 are actually live?\n- **Q5** — which column is authoritative in DesignFlow, the text one or the integer one? This is the 271-row contradiction.\n\nNothing should be backfilled until Q1, Q2 and Q5 are answered. A wrong answer produces **wrong** keys, not missing ones, so nothing errors and items quietly merge or split.\n\n## Not yet done\nThe DesignFlow-side sync code under `C:\\repos\\dflow plm` was **not read**. Q1, Q6 and Q8 may be partly answerable from that code without troubling Uma at all. That is a cheap next step for whoever picks this up.\n\nRelated: #868, #853, #867.\n\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: application-data\nroute: application-session\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T11:57:27Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T15:34:18Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":903,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] the division-code questions for Uma are written and ready to ask","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:40:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/903"},
{"body":"Full context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-13T1535Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-disney-live-and-guard-lessons.md` §5.\r\n\r\n## The block\r\n\r\nTwo migrations are merged to `main` and cannot reach production:\r\n\r\n- `20260802170000_plm_import_preserve_curated_licensor_property_status.sql`\r\n- `20260802171000_owner_ruling_friends_tv_frida_kahlo.sql`\r\n\r\n`scripts/production_migration_guard.py` refuses any allowlist containing them, citing **AGENTS.md 6.5, OWNER RULING 2026-08-03**: neither may reach production by any route until the FR `FRIENDS TV` removal work ships **with them, as ONE bounded apply, in dependency order**.\r\n\r\n**No FR removal migration exists yet**, so that combined change cannot be assembled. Register their versions in `FR_REMOVAL_VERSIONS` in `scripts/production_migration_guard.py`.\r\n3. Apply all of them together as one bounded batch.\r\n\r\n⛔ **Do NOT edit the guard to unblock the two existing migrations on their own.** The guard message says this explicitly. The whole point of the owner's ruling is that a partial apply leaves the taxonomy half-changed with no undo.\r\n\r\n## Why this is worth flagging clearly\r\n\r\n`20260802171000` **encodes an owner ruling**. From outside the database, a ruling that was made, written into SQL, reviewed, merged, and never applied is indistinguishable from a ruling that was never made. Compare #769, which asks whether the 'R5' ruling was ever actually made because it exists in no file — this is the same failure mode from the other end.\r\n\r\nAnyone auditing whether the Friends/Frida Kahlo decision took effect will find it has NOT, and should not conclude the decision was forgotten.\r\n\r\nRelated: #892, #769.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstate: blocked\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T01:32:04Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T15:33:48Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Corrected state\r\n\r\nThe original title and body were wrong. Loaders do exist, and several licensors have substantial landed data. The mistake came from counting guessed entity tables instead of the authoritative capture inventory.\r\n\r\nThe Warner loader exists at `tools/sync-warner-starlabs.mjs` and was committed in `696dc42`. What remains true is narrower:\r\n\r\n- Warner has landed zero source rows.\r\n- Warner currently has both legacy and normalized landing structures; cleanup is tracked by #958 and #946.\r\n- Disney, NBCU and Paramount have landed source data. Never report their state from one guessed table.\r\n\r\n## Authoritative check\r\n\r\nUse:\r\n\r\n```sql\r\nselect * from api.source_capture_inventory order by source_system, row_count desc;\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe inventory currently raw-sums retained captures, including failed captures. A separate follow-up must correct it to show latest-complete counts clearly.\r\n\r\n## Current owner\r\n\r\n- Warner legacy and loader cleanup: #958, protected by object claim #967.\r\n- Warner normalized-schema follow-ups: #946.\r\n- Capture inventory count semantics: separate db-work issue opened by orchestrator #960.\r\n\r\nDo not delete Warner tables or run the loader outside those coordinated workstreams. No production action is authorized by this correction.\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: source-data\nroute: source-data-session\npriority: 300\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-18T14:59:50Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T15:33:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Raised by an independent **Grok 4.6** review of #866 (session `pim-grant-scope-866`). The owner ruled \"fix all 21\", 18 tables were widened to INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and that is now **live on production** (migration `20260813180000`, run `31714556376`). This issue records the risk that came with it.\n\n**The three tables held narrow were the safe part. The extra risk is inside the 18.**\n\nPopPIM today only writes `checklist_item`, `product_assignee`, `product_submission`, `product_sample` and `revision_request`. The other 13 widened tables are **read-only in the current app** and were widened because the ruling said all of them.\n\n## Three specific concerns\n\n### 1. `pim.stage` now has DELETE, and it quietly guts the audit log\n\nProducts store their stage as **text, not a foreign key** (`20260621151024_domain_tables.sql:467`). So deleting a stage row does not block on any product. But it **does** null `stage_history.from_stage_id` and `to_stage_id` (same file, 498-500).\n\nThe result: `stage_history` was deliberately kept INSERT-only so nobody can rewrite the trail, and a `stage` delete blanks it out through the side door.\n\n### 2. `pim.product_update` and `pim.product_time_entry` look like imported ClickUp history\n\nBoth carry `external_source`/`external_id` with a unique constraint, the signature of imported records. **DELETE lets any staff user erase that history.** Same class of risk as `stage_history`, but they landed in the 18 rather than being held narrow.\n\n### 3. The write policy does not require PM app access\n\nRead on these tables requires `has_app_access('pm')`. **Write does not** — compare `20260621151155:345` (the read policy) with `:349` (the write policy). The write policy only excludes `viewer` and `vendor`.\n\nSo a **CRM salesperson with the `sales` role and no PopPIM access at all** can write every widened `pim` table by calling PostgREST directly. That was true in intent before this change; it is now true in effect, because the missing grants that made the policy inert are gone.\n\n## What is NOT a problem, checked\n\n- **No TRUNCATE** was granted anywhere. TRUNCATE bypasses row rules; test D asserts its absence.\n- **No append-only table was touched.** That set is `plm.coldlion_promotion_audit`, `plm.coldlion_promotion_quarantine`, `dam.popsg_property_resolution` and `core.property_alias` (`20260812020000`), and the migration checks it explicitly.\n- **`pim.product` UPDATE was already broad** before this change. The client could already change name, status, stage, company, licensor and the whole `metadata` blob.\n\n## The decision\n\nThree options, none urgent, all owner calls:\n\n1. **Leave as ruled.** The roles are staff-only and the blast radius is accepted.\n2. **Revoke DELETE from `stage`, `product_update` and `product_time_entry`** — the three where deletion destroys history rather than a working record. Cheapest and highest value.\n3. **Add `has_app_access('pm')` to the write policy** so PM writes need PM access, matching the read policy.\n\nOption 2 is the recommendation. It is a small forward migration and it does not disturb anything PopPIM actually does.\n\nRelated: #866, #892.\n\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n  - table pim.stage\n  - table pim.product_update\n  - table pim.product_time_entry\n```\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-17T04:41:09Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T15:19:52Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":898,"title":"DELETE is now live on pim.stage and two ClickUp-history tables — review whether it should be","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:40:53Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/898"},
{"body":"```db-claim\nversion: none\nobjects:\n  - pim.checklist_item\n  - pim.customer_order\n  - pim.design\n  - pim.design_asset\n  - pim.design_collection\n  - pim.product_assignee\n  - pim.product_field\n  - pim.product_file\n  - pim.product_link\n  - pim.product_sample\n  - pim.product_style_group\n  - pim.product_submission\n  - pim.product_tag\n  - pim.product_time_entry\n  - pim.product_update\n  - pim.project\n  - pim.revision_request\n  - pim.stage\n```\n\nClaim for #866, implemented in PR #896. Grant-only change (no schema, no policy\nchange): the `pm_write` RLS policy on these tables is inert because\n`authenticated` was only ever granted SELECT.
