{"body":"Found 2026-08-13 while investigating why Disney has only one landing table. **The Disney model is not missing. It was written, reviewed and merged, and then never applied.**\n\n## The gap, verified two ways\n\nCompared the migration FILES on `origin/main` against `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` on production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\n\nThe applied ledger jumps straight from `20260810180000` to `20260812010000`. **Six merged migrations in between are absent:**\n\n| version | what it creates |\n|---|---|\n| `20260810190000_dcp_vault_source_landing` | `dcp_crawl`, `dcp_portal_tile`, `dcp_style_guide`, `dcp_asset`, `dcp_crawl_section`, `dcp_crawl_gap`, `dcp_asset_crawl`, `dcp_load_exception`, `dcp_asset_tile_observation` |\n| `20260810190100_dcp_vault_chunked_loader` | loader |\n| `20260811030000_pmt_lossless_source_ids_and_asset_metadata_value` | Paramount lossless IDs + `pmt_asset_metadata_value` |\n| `20260811050000_dcp_vault_metadata_landing` | `dcp_metadata_run`, `dcp_metadata_asset`, `dcp_property`, `dcp_character`, `dcp_term`, `dcp_asset_property_observation`, `dcp_asset_character_observation`, `dcp_asset_term_observation` |\n| `20260811060000_dcp_vault_metadata_chunked_loader` | loader |\n| `20260811070000_nbcu_asset_ip_family_relationship` | `nbcu_asset_ip_family` |\n\nConfirmed independently against `information_schema.tables`:\n- tables in `plm` starting `dcp_`: **0**\n- `plm.nbcu_asset_ip_family`: **absent**\n- `plm.pmt_asset_metadata_value`: **absent**\n\n**17 Disney tables exist only as unapplied SQL.**\n\n## Why this matters — it produced a false conclusion\n\nEarlier in this same session I reported to the owner that \"Disney has 1 landing table where Paramount has 20\", and framed it as a schema gap. That was wrong, and I only found out by digging further. **Reading the live catalog alone makes a merged-but-unapplied migration look like work that was never done.** Anyone comparing licensor coverage will reach the same false conclusion.\n\n## Disney is two portals, not one — and that part IS a real doc gap\n\n- **OPA** (`opa.disney.com`) → `plm.opa_property_character`. One table is the CORRECT shape here; OPA genuinely returns only `property, licensedPropertyID, optionSourceID, character, characterID, brandPropertyID`. Documented at `docs/verification/opa-source-of-truth-20260807/README.md:641` (\"OPA has no style-guide concept\").\n- **DCP Vault** (`dcpvault.disney.com`) → the 17 `dcp_*` tables. ~40k assets, 1,208 style-guide folders, portal tiles, regions, classification terms, use restrictions, and three observation link tables.\n\n`docs/licensor-portal-scrape-source-schema-20260807.md` §1 lists Disney's landing namespace as **only** `plm.opa_*` and marks it \"built\". **DCP Vault is absent from that table entirely.** The doc is dated 2026-08-07; the DCP migrations landed 2026-08-10/11 and it was never updated. That is the omission — not the one-table OPA model.\n\nNo document, comment or issue anywhere justifies Disney having less coverage than the other three, because none was intended.\n\n## Landing-table coverage, corrected\n\n| Licensor | capture entities | tables designed | live | gap |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Warner | 4 entities + 4 link files | 9 `wb_*` | 9 | none |\n| NBCU | 6 entities + 6 link files | 16 `nbcu_*` | 15 | 1 unapplied |\n| Paramount | 7 entities + 10 link files | 17 `pmt_*` | 16 | 1 unapplied |\n| Disney OPA | 1 pair file | 1 | 1 | none (correct) |\n| **Disney DCP Vault** | asset, style guide, property, character, term, tile, crawl provenance + 3 observation files | **17** | **0** | **everything** |\n\nEvery landing table that IS live holds **0 rows**. The loaders were never run either.\n\n## Two more merged-but-unapplied, added today\n`20260813020000` (#862 search_path) and `20260813030000` (#861 null-permissive guards). Both are security fixes and both need applying. **That makes eight pending in total.**\n\n## What needs deciding\nApplying migrations to production needs owner approval of an exact package. This issue exists to make the gap visible and get that package built. Nothing has been applied.\n\n## Do not pair these two\nTwo Disney documents warn that DCP Vault's `properties[]` must never be paired with its `character[]` — that relationship is only valid from OPA. Whoever writes the loaders needs to know this before they start.\n\nRelated: #878 (the DCP crawl stopped at 3 of 22 portal sections, so the capture itself is incomplete), #865.","closedAt":"2026-08-13T17:50:03Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T03:47:58Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":892,"title":"SIX merged migrations were never applied to production — all four Disney DCP Vault tables among them","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:50:24Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/892"},

Verified NOT on `origin/main` by comparing file content, not by `git cherry` — that command falsely reports squash-merged branches as unlanded. {"body":"From orchestrator session 44090f (marker #855). Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-13T0015Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-orderlist-and-licensor-truth.md` §7.\r\n\r\nThree of the five app repos were inspected: `popdam3`, `poppim-web`, `popcrm-web` — all present under `C:\\repos\\`. **`hiclaw` and `monitor` are NOT checked out on this machine**, and there is no second drive here either. They were not guessed at. #512 goes from 4 unknown repos to 2.\r\n\r\n**Correction to #512's body:** it says `popcrm-web` was already read but `popdam3` and `poppim-web` were not. On this machine **all three are readable**, including the one that matters most.\r\n\r\n**What was found.** popdam3 calls **57 distinct RPCs** against the shared database, including `refresh_style_tracker_item_bridge`, `upsert_style_tracker_value_resolution`, `search_style_tracker_link_candidates` and `execute_readonly_query`. Heaviest table dependencies by reference count: `admin_config` (213), `assets` (124), `agent_registrations` (54), `style_groups` (39), `render_queue` (38), `characters` (34), `embeddings` (28).\r\n\r\npopcrm-web depends on the `crm_*` RPC family and five tables. poppim-web is the thinnest consumer — `current_user_profile` beyond boilerplate, plus eleven `pim` tables.\r\n\r\n**The finding that is the actual point of #512:** hard-coded UUID literals in application source, which **no catalog query can ever see** — popdam3 1,048, poppim-web 555, popcrm-web 513. These are raw counts including test fixtures, so they are a **ceiling, not a coupling count**. Each needs triage. UNVERIFIED how many are live production keys.\r\n\r\n**Caveat stated rather than buried:** the table-reference counts include vendored `@supabase/supabase-js` test fixtures (`avatars`, `countries`, `instruments`, `orchestral_sections`) that appear identically in all three repos and are library artefacts, not shared-db tables. Discount those rows.\r\n\r\nAlso: the `desc-cleaner.ts` file that #512 cites as its example of ~150 hard-coded strings **does not exist in popdam3** under that name. It must live in one of the two unreachable repos, or has been renamed. UNVERIFIED.\r\n\r\n**Cross-link:** the five `SECURITY DEFINER` functions with a mutable `search_path` in issue #862 are all popdam3 callers, so that fix has a real consumer to regression-test against.\r\n\r\n**To close this issue:** check out `u2giants/hiclaw` and `u2giants/monitor` on a machine and re-run the sweep.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 300\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:45:48Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T00:16:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":883,"title":"HANDOVER: #512 app blast-radius narrowed to 2 repos, not closed — hiclaw and monitor absent from this machine","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:41:01Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/883"},
{"body":"From orchestrator session 44090f (marker #855). Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-13T0015Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-orderlist-and-licensor-truth.md` §0 and §7.\n\nThis issue exists so the corrections are not lost in a handover file.\n\n**1. The \"86 object assertions and 38 behavior assertions\" preview rehearsal DOES NOT EXIST.** Exhaustively searched: it appears in exactly two prose locations and nowhere else. No artifact, no run ID, no date. The only primary source (`HANDOFF.d/2026-08-10T0030Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-nine-agent-fan-out.md:436`) says **86 object tests and 33 behaviour tests** — 33, not 38 — describing tests written in PR #635 on 2026-08-10, not a preview rehearsal on 2026-08-12. It was a misquotation of different work on a different date, restated until it read as fact. **Struck from the plan and the approval package this session.**\n\n**2. Issue #788's premise is stale.** It says four migrations \"sit in no batch and appear in no approved allowlist\". They do — `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` §5A defines batch B10 and names all four. Item 3 of that issue is already done. Re-scope or close it rather than working it as written.\n\n**3. Paramount's bigint→text conversion is future-proofing, not a fix for observed data loss.** A full scan of all 22 Paramount CSVs found **zero** leading zeros, **zero** values above 2^53, and non-numeric values only in `asset_id`, which is already `text`. The conversion is right for a lossless landing zone and should still be promoted — but presenting it as fixing real corruption is inaccurate.\n\n**The general lesson:** a number restated across documents is not corroborated; it is copied. Check provenance before quoting any figure in this repo.\n\nTwo mechanical traps found the same way, both worth knowing: `gh issue view --comments` returns **silent empty output** on this machine (the plain form works), and the DCP crawl's `gaps: []` field looked like proof of completeness while being silent about 10 sections never attempted. **Empty is not none.**\n","closedAt":"2026-08-13T18:19:15Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T00:16:15Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"From orchestrator session 44090f (marker #855). PR #869 is **merged**. Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-13T0015Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-orderlist-and-licensor-truth.md` §7.\n\n**The behaviour change anyone promoting to production must know.** The co-presence rule now fires when the \"create\" migration is in the **production ledger**, not only when it is in the allowlist. So an allowlist that repairs only *part* of an applied create's outstanding fixes is now **refused**.\n\nConcrete: with Warner's `20260810030000` applied, an allowlist of `[20260810110000]` alone used to pass — leaving production with the wrong read claim and `service_role` still able to INSERT. It is now refused. `[20260810110000, 20260810120000]` is accepted. **Completing a repair is always legal; only stopping short is refused.**\n\nAn independent adversarial review enumerated every newly-failing allowlist and found **no false positive** — every refusal is satisfiable by completing the batch, and the rule still demands the fixes and never the create.\n\nAlso landed: #784 and #819 enforcement (previously prose-only), #609 F5 (verified to change no existing verdict across all 437 migrations), #805 item 1. Tests 276 → 484.\n\n**Two follow-ups the reviewer raised, not blockers:**\n1. A latent false-REJECT in the drop object-list scanner: `drop function plm.f(plm.mytype);` records `plm.mytype` as dropped. Zero occurrences today; direction is always REJECT, never ACCEPT. One-line fix: stop the object list at `(` as well as `;`.\n2. `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` §5A.8 still says B10c is enforced by nothing and #784 is open. **Both sentences are now false** and it is the text an operator reads under pressure.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-13T18:19:12Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T00:16:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":881,"title":"HANDOVER: guard hardening changed a PASS into a FAIL — partial batch repairs are now refused","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:50:31Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/881"},
{"body":"From orchestrator session 44090f (marker #855). Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-13T0015Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-orderlist-and-licensor-truth.md` §1. This supersedes the framing in issue #818, which is now answerable.\r\n\r\n**Preview's ledger was fully enumerated for the first time this session.** Preview `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`: **430 applied**, max `20260812211000`. Production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`: **426 applied**, max `20260812020000`. **No orphan ledger rows on either.**\r\n\r\n⚠️ **Preview is NOT a superset of production.** `20260810140000` and `20260810180000` are on **production but NOT preview**; six others are on preview but not production. So preview is simultaneously ahead and behind.\r\n\r\n**The consequence, which is the whole point of this issue: \"we rehearsed it on preview\" is not evidence about production.** Every existing rehearsal claim in this repo should be read with that in mind, and any new rehearsal should state which of the two databases it actually ran against and what the delta was at the time.\r\n\r\n**Still UNVERIFIED:** only the *ledger* was enumerated. No object-level drift diff was run inside schemas, so hand-made non-migration objects on preview are not ruled out. Settled by a catalog-level diff of the two databases.\r\n\r\nRelated standing fact: the Supabase MCP is bound to PRODUCTION and takes no project parameter, so preview work needs psql (pooler `aws-0-us-east-1`, port **5432** — the 6543 transaction-mode port breaks single-transaction work). There is no WSL on this machine.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 350\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:09:10Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T00:16:13Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"From orchestrator session 44090f (marker #855). Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-13T0015Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-orderlist-and-licensor-truth.md` §5. The live ColdLion API was queried read-only on 2026-08-12 with the owner's explicit authorisation.\r\n\r\n**ColdLion returns 300 distinct properties.** Not the 258 that several repo documents still state, and not the 285 snapshot sitting on preview from 2026-07-31. The list is actively growing — 59 of the 300 were created in 2026.\r\n\r\n**Joined on CODE: 252 agree on code AND name with `core.property`, with ZERO disagreements.** 4 of ours are absent from ColdLion; 48 ColdLion codes are unmatched. 252+4=256 and 252+48=300 — the arithmetic closes exactly. **`core.property` is not similar to ColdLion's list; it IS ColdLion's list, 48 rows stale.**\r\n\r\n⚠️ **Issue #539 asks Albert to rule on \"33 unmatched codes\". The real number is 48.** I have commented there. **Re-scope it to 48 before putting it to him.**\r\n\r\n**Recommendation on record:** keep `core.property` canonical; ColdLion is the **feed**, not the list. ColdLion has no parent field, **no active/inactive/expiry concept of any kind**, and 642 codes reused across division/type slots (17 are both a licensor and a property inside `CW001` alone). Adopting it as canonical would resurrect lapsed licences across all four applications.\r\n\r\n**A consequence worth acting on:** because ColdLion carries no tombstone, a deleted property is indistinguishable from a bad pull. The only way to ever detect a deletion is to run the mirror on a schedule and diff snapshots forward — so every day without the feed is a day of undetectable loss.\r\n\r\n**UNVERIFIED:** only 4 divisions were queried (`CW001,SP001,EH001,EP001`) because the API exposes no division-listing endpoint. If a fifth licensed division exists, its properties are invisible to us.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: curated-master-data\nroute: curated-master-data-governance\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T21:03:07Z","createdAt":"2026-08-13T00:15:32Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":879,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] ColdLion sends 300 properties and IS core.property — 48 unmatched, not 33","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:41:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/879"},
{"body":"From orchestrator session 44090f (marker #855). Full briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-13T0015Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-orderlist-and-licensor-truth.md` §7 (last agent block).\r\n\r\n**Correcting a wrong recommendation this session made.** I told the owner Disney DCP Vault needed an expensive re-scrape. **That was wrong.** The capture holds 156,644 file paths, which is genuinely useful; the missing per-asset fields (stable ID, file size, checksum, `collectionDmcId`, property/character arrays) come from a **documented per-asset endpoint at ~3 KB and ~125 ms per asset** (`C:\\repos\\ai-devops\\memory\\shared-db\\dcpvault-metadata-json-endpoint.md`).\r\n\r\n**Migration `20260811050000` already creates the enrichment tables that expect exactly those fields.** Somebody designed a two-step landing: a path crawl, then an enrichment pass. **The second step has never been executed** — grep for `dam:sha1`, `dam:size`, `collectionDmcId`, `source_uuid` across every branch of `u2giants/licensor-source-data` returns hits only in markdown, never in a data file.\r\n\r\nSo the correct ask is an **additive enrichment over an existing path list**, not a re-scrape. Scope it that way.\r\n\r\n**Separately and still true: the crawl is incomplete.** It stopped at job 23 of 34; 10 of 22 portal tiles have zero rows. {"body":"Found by the live ColdLion query (orchestrator #855, 2026-08-12).\r\n\r\n## The finding\r\nThe ColdLion ERP base URL is plain **HTTP**, not HTTPS:\r\n\r\n```\r\nhttp://x5.coldlion.com/EhpApi\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe `X-API-Key` header is therefore transmitted **in clear text** on every request, along with the entire response payload.\r\n\r\n## What is exposed\r\n- The API key itself, to anyone able to observe the network path.\r\n- The full merchandising taxonomy: licensor codes, property codes and names, and the audit fields (`createdUser`, `modUser`).\r\n\r\n## Why it matters here\r\nThis is the feed we are preparing to run on a schedule against the shared database. Every scheduled run repeats the exposure, and the key is a long-lived shared credential rather than a per-run token.\r\n\r\n## What to establish (not to change unilaterally)\r\n1. Does ColdLion expose an HTTPS endpoint on the same host or another? If so, switching is a one-line config change.\r\n2. If it does not, is the traffic confined to a private network path, or does it cross the public internet?\r\n3. Whether the key can be rotated, and who owns that.\r\n\r\n**Do not rotate the existing credential without owner approval.** Do not change the endpoint until HTTPS is confirmed to work — a silent failure here stops the feed rather than securing it.\r\n\r\n## Related\r\nThe same session established that ColdLion has **no active/inactive/deleted concept of any kind**, so a property removed upstream vanishes with no tombstone. That is an argument for starting the scheduled mirror soon and diffing snapshots forward — but it also means the exposure above becomes continuous rather than occasional.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: security-settings\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T21:03:03Z","createdAt":"2026-08-12T23:04:31Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":875,"title":"[ALBERT] ColdLion ERP is plain HTTP — the API key crosses the wire in clear text on every call","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:41:08Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/875"},
{"body":"OWNER RULING 2026-08-12 (Albert, in session, orchestrator #855).\n\n**The approved populated-row count for the OrderList production import is 12,354.** The owner is content to approve against the current count and does NOT require the five changed rows to be itemised first.\n\n## What this closes\nThe earlier owner question — \"why did the sheet shrink by five rows (12,328 -> 12,323), and what were those five rows?\" — is **answered by decision, not by investigation.** It is no longer a gate on the import.\n\n## What remains true and must not be re-mislabelled\nThe record previously explained the gap as a counting-definition artefact. **That explanation is incomplete.** Investigation found:\n- 12,323 was measured on workbook files `b9b282dc...` (10,690,991 bytes) and `904b2cb9...`.\n- The approved workbook is `68c9b03a...` (10,679,199 bytes).\n- **12,323 was never measured on the approved workbook at all.** Two independent exports agreed at 12,323, so the sheet genuinely changed between 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-11. It was a real human edit, not purely a definitional change.\n- The 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-12 profiles also disagree on direct-only rows (8,412 vs 8,438).\n\nWhich five rows changed **cannot be recovered from this repository**. The workbook is licensed data and was correctly never committed, and none of the three export files was retained. Only the Google Sheets revision history for spreadsheet `1i1da5J0qy5a0EvsO1CvfyQ6Xijn4678LG7TFqbwxwUk` tab `Order` could answer it.\n\n## Effect on the importer\n`--expected-populated-rows 12354` is the approved value. The importer requires this to be stated explicitly (no default) and, since PR #860's rework, asserts it **before** any write — a wrong count now refuses with nothing written.\n\nRecorded so a future session does not reopen this as an unresolved blocker, and does not repeat the incomplete \"purely a counting definition\" explanation.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-13T17:50:00Z","createdAt":"2026-08-12T22:24:20Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Found during the #784/#819 guard-hardening sweep (orchestrator #855, PR #869). Reported, deliberately NOT fixed, because the fix is a policy call the owner should make.\r\n\r\n## The gap\r\n`assert_atomic_batches` is silent when production is **already resting inside** an atomic batch and the proposed allowlist touches none of that batch.\r\n\r\nReproduced: with half of B9 applied, an allowlist of `['20260811030000']` is **accepted**. The guard checks whether the allowlist itself is a legal batch shape; it does not check whether production is currently in an illegal resting state that the allowlist ignores.\r\n\r\n## Why it was not fixed in PR #869\r\nThe obvious fix — refuse any promotion while any atomic batch sits half-applied — would refuse every unrelated promotion for as long as that state persists. That could wedge the production lane entirely, which may be worse than the gap it closes.\r\n\r\nThat is a trade-off between two failure modes, not a code defect with an obvious correct answer, so it needs an owner or an explicit design decision rather than an agent's judgement.\r\n\r\n## The options\r\n1. **Refuse everything while any batch rests illegally.** Safest, but can wedge the lane.\r\n2. **Warn loudly and require an explicit acknowledgement flag** to proceed with an unrelated promotion. Keeps the lane moving, makes the state impossible to miss.\r\n3. **Refuse only promotions that share objects with the half-applied batch.** Narrowest, but needs object-level analysis the guard may not have.\r\n\r\nOption 2 matches this repo's stated preference that a fallback must alert loudly rather than pass quietly.\r\n\r\n## Related\r\n- PR #869 closed the declared-shape half of this for #784 and #819.\r\n- `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` §5A.8 still says B10c is enforced by nothing and that #784 is open. **Both sentences are now stale** and need a docs pass — noting it here so it is not lost.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: security-settings\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 250\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T21:35:33Z","createdAt":"2026-08-12T22:18:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":870,"title":"Guard is silent when production already rests inside a half-applied atomic batch","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:41:10Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/870"},
{"body":"Found while authoring the `fix_schema_for_api.md` Phase 3/4 plan (orchestrator #855, PR #867). **This blocks Phase 3 and the PopDAM `/orders` deployment, and the parent plan does not anticipate it.**\r\n\r\n## The two key spaces cannot be joined\r\nThe shipped resolver `plm.import_item_master_data()` builds:\r\n\r\n```\r\nplm.item.source_id = companyCode | divisionCode | itemNo\r\n```\r\n\r\nBut `public.erp_items_current.external_id` is a **bare item number**. Measured on live data: **0 of 17,703 rows contain a pipe character.** And `erp_items_current` has **no `company_code` column at all**.\r\n\r\nSo there is no direct join between the legacy mirror and the canonical `plm.item` key. The Phase 4 bridge repoint cannot be done until an explicit derived mapping exists, **proven both unique and total** across all 17,703 items.\r\n\r\n## Why this is dangerous rather than merely inconvenient\r\n`plm.style_tracker_item_bridge.erp_item_id` is FK'd to `public.erp_items_current(id)` with `ON DELETE SET NULL` — confirmed from the catalog, not from a document. Those `id` values are random `gen_random_uuid()` values that do not survive a truncate-and-re-pull.\r\n\r\nA cutover that guesses at the mapping **silently NULLs bridge links and raises nothing**. No error, no failed migration, and bridge row counts stay identical — so a count-based check passes while the links are gone.\r\n\r\n## Current baseline (preview, verified)\r\n```\r\nerp_items_current = 17,703 | plm.item = 0 | plm.item_import = 0\r\nbridge rows = 15,533 | bridge linked = 13,701\r\n```\r\n\r\n## What must happen before Phase 4\r\n1. Derive the mapping from `external_id` to `companyCode|divisionCode|itemNo` explicitly.\r\n2. Prove it is **unique** (no two legacy rows map to one canonical item) and **total** (every non-dismissed item maps).\r\n3. Prove **zero orphaned or NULLed bridge rows** before AND after the repoint — by comparing the linked-row set, not the row count.\r\n\r\n## Owner decision embedded here (D3)\r\nIs `company_code` genuinely the constant `EDGEHOME`? **If that assumption is wrong, every canonical key is wrong**, and it would not be discovered until after the backfill.\r\n\r\n## Related recommendation (D4)\r\nThe new bridge FK should be `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, not `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so a future mistake fails loudly instead of silently blanking links.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-17T03:09:19Z","createdAt":"2026-08-12T22:15:26Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":868,"title":"ENGINEERING BLOCKER: prove complete ColdLion item mapping before bridge repoint","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:41:12Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/868"},
{"body":"Found by the #720 review (orchestrator #855), verified live from the production catalog. **#720 understates this: the gap is 21 tables, not 5, and PopPIM is broken at 11 call sites today.**\n\n## The root cause — one commit, proven\n`supabase/migrations/20260621151155_api_rls_realtime.sql`:\n- **line 349** creates the `pm_write` policy: `create policy pm_write on %s for all to authenticated using (app.has_role('administrator') or app.has_any_role(array['licensing','designer','sales']))` with a matching `with check`.\n- **line 471** grants only `grant select on all tables in schema pim to authenticated;`\n\nThe write **policy** was authored. The write **grant** never was. RLS and table privileges are independent gates, so the policy is inert.\n\nConfirmed live: **21 of 24 `pim` tables carry a `pm_write ALL/authenticated` policy while `authenticated` lacks INSERT.** Only `saved_view`, `stage_history` and `view_pref` have working grants.\n\n## PopPIM genuinely writes as `authenticated` — not service_role, not a definer path\n`C:\\repos\\poppim-web\\src\\lib\\supabase.ts` builds a single browser client with `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` + Azure OAuth. No service-role key, no server-side proxy. Writes are direct PostgREST table calls:\n- `src/features/board/collab.ts` — `checklist_item` insert (:67), update (:74), delete (:79), insert (:94); `product_assignee` insert (:122), delete (:136)\n- `src/features/workflow/api.ts` — `product_submission` insert (:123)/update (:138); `product_sample` insert (:128)/update (:143); `revision_request` insert (:133)/update (:149)\n\nAll 11 fail at the grant gate.\n\n## Precedent already set twice by the owner\n`20260727013100_poppim_atomic_contract_dml_grants.sql` header states the reasoning exactly: *\"RLS policies already restrict PM writes... PostgreSQL table privileges are an independent gate: grant only the DML required...\"*. Also `20260727213000_poppim_saved_view_crud_grants.sql`. Existing grants are deliberately verb-surgical (`product` = UPDATE only, `stage_history` = INSERT only, `view_pref` = no DELETE), so a blanket `grant all` would depart from the established pattern.\n\n## Owner decision needed on SCOPE\nFix the 5 named in #720, the 9 PopPIM actually writes, or all 21 mismatches? UNVERIFIED which of the other 12 have live consumers — settle by grepping popcrm-web / popdam3 / db-data-admin for `pim` writes.\n\nThis is a production access change and therefore an owner decision. No agent should widen grants on its own initiative.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-13T14:46:34Z","createdAt":"2026-08-12T22:09:55Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":866,"title":"[ALBERT] 21 pim tables have write policies but no write grants — PopPIM is broken at 11 call sites (widens #720)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:50:44Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/866"},
{"body":"Found by the #640 reconciliation review (orchestrator #855), verified live against production. **This blocks #640 and needs an owner ruling before any licensor reconciliation is run.**\n\n## There are two disjoint property universes in `core`, and #640 names the smaller one\n\n| | Universe A (what #640 names) | Universe B |\n|---|---|---|\n| licensor table | `core.licensor` (uuid), 26 rows | `core.\"licenseList\"` (integer), 19+ rows |\n| entity table | `core.property` (uuid), **256** rows | `core.properties_and_characters` (integer), **10,122** rows |\n| link table | `core.property_character` — **0 rows** | `core.property_character_associations` — **9,622 rows** |\n| source-ID columns | none | `source_licensed_property_id`, `source_character_id` |\n\n**There is no foreign key between them.** `pg_constraint` confirms: `property_licensor_id_fkey → core.licensor(id)` and `properties_and_characters_licensor_id_fkey → core.\"licenseList\"(\"licenseList_id\")`. Two separate trees.\n\n## Universe B is already loaded from the licensor portals — proven by source-ID membership, not inferred\n- `licenseList` 1 (`DS`, 1,221 rows) and 3 (`MV`, 3,878 rows): 112 sampled `source_character_id` values, **112/112 present in Disney OPA `characterID`**. Zero unmatched.\n- `licenseList` 2 (`WB`, 4,244 rows): IDs are UUIDs; **6/6 sampled present in Warner STARLABS `characters.csv:source_id`**.\n- `licenseList` 10 (`NU`, NBCUniversal): 123 rows. 17 (`VM`): 34 rows.\n- `licenseList` 13 (`CC`): synthetic hand-made IDs (`COKE-CHAR-00n`), NOT portal-derived.\n\nBreakdown: 9,622 rows typed `CHARACTER`, 500 typed `PROPERTY`.\n\n## Why this matters\nA reconciliation run against Universe A (256 rows, **no source IDs at all**) would report enormous, meaningless gaps while ignoring 10,122 rows that already carry the licensors' own primary keys and are joinable exactly.\n\n## The owner decision\nWhich is the intended reconciliation target — Universe A, Universe B, or must the two be reconciled to each other first? Both exist, both are populated differently, and neither references the other.\n\n## A second owner decision inside #640\n`core.licensor`'s 26 rows are **not licensor-grained** — they mix licensors, brands and franchises. Disney is split across three codes (`DY` 40, `MV` 29, `SW` 28), Warner across four (`WB` 41, `DC` 14, `HP` 12, `FR` 1), Paramount across two (`VM` 18, `PP` 8), NBCU one (`NB` 31). Six `X-*` codes hold zero properties. Grouping these into four portal licensors is a business judgement, not a fact — every number in the #640 review is conditional on an assumed grouping.\n\n## Related grain problem, recorded so it is not rediscovered\n16 `core.property` rows match a licensor's **character** list and no property list. Whole licensor groups are stored at character grain (`SW` and `HP` almost entirely individual characters; `PP` and much of `VM` likewise), while `core.character` and `core.property_character` are **both empty**. The extracts supply a property/character separation with source IDs that Universe A structurally cannot hold.\n\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: curated-master-data\nroute: curated-master-data-governance\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T11:52:31Z","createdAt":"2026-08-12T22:09:54Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":865,"title":"[ALBERT] core has TWO disjoint property universes — #640 reconciliation targets the smaller one (256 rows vs 10,122)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:41:13Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/865"},
{"body":"Found during the OrderList production approval verification (orchestrator #855). **This must be decided before the OrderList production import, not after.**\n\n## The finding\nFour RLS policies on the OrderList tables are `USING (true)` for the `authenticated` role, on **both** preview and production:\n\n- `plm.production_order.production_order_popdam_read` [SELECT]\n- `plm.production_order_line.production_order_line_popdam_read` [SELECT]\n- `plm.production_order_source_ref.production_order_source_ref_read` [SELECT]\n- `plm.production_order_line_source_ref.production_order_line_source_ref_read` [SELECT]\n\nPostgres OR-s policies together. So these permissive `true` policies **fully subsume** the restrictive `plm_read` policy that sits alongside them. The net effect today: **every authenticated account can read all four OrderList tables in full.**\n\nThis is identical on both databases, so it is not drift — it was written this way.\n\n## Why it is not urgent today, and why it becomes urgent\nAll four tables currently hold **zero rows** in production (verified). The exposure is theoretical while they are empty.\n\nThe pending OrderList production import would insert **3,212 orders and 24,010 order lines** — customer, factory, PO, quantity and pricing data. At that moment the exposure becomes real.\n\n## The owner decision\nEither:\n- **(a)** tighten the four policies to match the restrictive `plm_read` intent before the import, or\n- **(b)** accept that every authenticated user can read the full order list.\n\nThis is a production access-control change and therefore an owner decision. No agent should change it on its own initiative.\n\n## Notes for whoever implements (a)\n- Needs a forward migration. Do not edit the applied migrations.\n- Objects written: the four policies above. File a `db-claim` first.\n- Related: `20260810110000` already sets `api.dam_order_list` to `security_invoker`, so the view correctly defers to these table policies — which is exactly why the table policies matter.\n- Verify the behaviour, not the ledger row: assert what a plain `authenticated` session can actually SELECT, before and after.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T22:24:18Z","createdAt":"2026-08-12T22:06:04Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":863,"title":"[ALBERT] Every authenticated user can read all four OrderList tables — decide before the production import","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:50:47Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/863"},
{"body":"Found by the #546 SECURITY DEFINER audit.\n\nFive `SECURITY DEFINER` functions run as `postgres` with **no `search_path` pinned** (`proconfig` has no `search_path=`):\n\n- `public.bulk_insert_pdf_text_samples`\n- `public.claim_pdf_backfill_batch`\n- `public.count_pdf_backfill_remaining`\n- `public.find_ai_pdf_duplicates`\n- `public.get_ai_sentinel_stats`\n\n`anon` cannot execute them, which caps the severity.\n\n**Not academic — all five have a live consumer.** They are called from `popdam3`: `supabase/functions/admin-api/index.ts`, `supabase/functions/agent-api/index.ts`, `_shared/admin-handlers/ai-duplicate-handlers.ts`, `_shared/admin-handlers/ai-sentinel-handlers.ts`. So the fix has something real to regression-test against.\n\nFix is cheap and isolated: `alter function ... set search_path = public, pg_catalog` in a forward migration. Test that each still works from its popdam3 caller.\n\nObjects written: the five functions above. File a `db-claim` before dispatching.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-13T02:52:58Z","createdAt":"2026-08-12T22:05:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":862,"title":"SECURITY: five SECURITY DEFINER functions have a mutable search_path, all called by PopDAM","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:50:50Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/862"},
{"body":"Found by the #546 SECURITY DEFINER audit, verified against live `pg_proc.prosrc` on production (not just the files).\n\n## The defect\nFour live `SECURITY DEFINER` functions, all owned by `postgres`, all carrying `authenticated=X/postgres`, use the null-permissive guard shape:\n\n```sql\nif not (app.has_role('administrator') or auth.role() = 'service_role') then\n```\n\nWhen `auth.role()` is NULL: `NULL = 'service_role'` is NULL, `false or NULL` is NULL, `not NULL` is NULL, and `IF NULL` is not true. **The `raise` is skipped and the function proceeds.** The guard reads strict and behaves open.\n\n| function | source |\n|---|---|\n| `public.propose_popsg_property_resolution` | `supabase/migrations/20260731150000_popsg_property_resolution_contracts.sql:414` |\n| `public.activate_popsg_property_decision_batch` | `20260731150000_popsg_property_resolution_contracts.sql:478` |\n| `public.promote_property_alias_batch` | `20260731150000_popsg_property_resolution_contracts.sql:569` |\n| `public.approve_licensor_alias` | `20260731210000_core_licensor_alias.sql:382` |\n\n## Why these four survived\nThe repo already knows this trap and documents it in three places. Every migration written afterwards uses the correct positive-match form. **These four original callers were simply never corrected.** They are the only live instances of the shape; every other match in the tree is a comment warning against it.\n\n## Honest bound on exploitability\nNot reachable from a normal PostgREST call: an `authenticated` JWT sets the `role` claim, so `auth.role()` returns `'authenticated'` and the guard does fire. The NULL path is a session with no JWT claims — direct/pooler connections, migration context, and any JWT reaching PostgREST without a `role` claim. `anon` has no EXECUTE on these four, which is what keeps this HIGH rather than CRITICAL.\n\n## The fix\nThe correct pattern already exists in this repo: `plm.assert_taxonomy_alert_ack_authority()` and `ingest.assert_coldlion_product_size_authority()`. Require a non-null role AND a positive match, and **test the NULL case** — a test that only covers a wrong role will pass against the broken form.\n\n## Dispatch notes\n- Needs a forward migration. Do not edit the applied migrations — the ledger already records those versions, so the CLI will never re-run them; editing changes nothing in the database and desynchronises file from ledger.\n- Objects written: the four functions above. File a `db-claim` before dispatching.\n- Preview first, then owner approval for production.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-13T02:59:51Z","createdAt":"2026-08-12T22:05:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":861,"title":"SECURITY: four live SECURITY DEFINER functions use the null-permissive guard and admit the call","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:50:54Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/861"},

{"body":"## The outage\n\nDesignFlow on `https://alsand.designflow.app` cannot be logged into at all, by any method, as of\n2026-08-12. This is not a backlog item; the app is down.\n\n- Password login returns: `Find User Login Info failed (SYS-030). Technical details: column \"office_location\" does not exist.`\n- Microsoft SSO returns: `HTTP 401; URL: https://api.alsand.designflow.app/api/core/auth/azure.`\n\nBoth are the same fault. `designflow-backend/services/auth.service.js:66` does\n`sql.users.findOne({ where: { email } })` with no attribute list, so Sequelize selects every column\ndeclared in `models/db/users.js` — including `office_location` and `preferred_language`\n(`models/db/users.js:63-70`). `services/user.service.js:33` names them explicitly as well. The\nstatement errors in the database, password login surfaces SYS-030, and the Azure route turns the\nsame throw into a bare 401.\n\n## Root cause\n\n`supabase/migrations/20260810160000_dflow_users_office_location_preferred_language.sql` is merged to\n`main` (PR #694, issue #690, claim #692) but **has never been applied to production**\n(`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`). Verified 2026-08-12 against the live catalog:\n\n```sql\nselect table_schema, column_name\nfrom information_schema.columns\nwhere table_name = 'users'\n  and column_name in ('office_location','preferred_language');\n-- 0 rows. dflow.users has 21 columns and neither of these.\n```\n\nThe ledger confirms it: `20260810140000` and `20260810180000` are applied, `20260810160000` is not.\nThat is the out-of-order apply already described in #773.\n\nMeanwhile the backend code that reads the columns is live on `sandbox-albert`. Code shipped, schema\ndid not.\n\n## What is needed\n\nApply atomic batch **B9**, all 14 versions, none of which are in the production ledger today:\n\n```\n20260810010000,20260810020000,20260810030000,20260810050000,20260810060000,20260810070000,20260810080000,20260810090000,20260810100000,20260810110000,20260810120000,20260810130000,20260810160000,20260810170000\n```\n\n`20260810160000` **cannot go alone**. `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` encodes B9 as an\n`ATOMIC_BATCHES` member, and `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` section 5 declares\nit atomic. A single-file allowlist is refused by the preflight, and resting inside B9 leaves eight\ntables of confidential Warner STARLABS data readable by every authenticated account.\n\n### Dispatch inputs (`Shared Supabase Migrations`)\n\n| input | value |\n|---|---|\n| `target` | `production` |\n| `mode` | `apply` (a `dry-run` first is welcome) |\n| `commit_sha` | `0f42555c9dca23574a23fc6fe992cd0a716c5991` (`origin/main` at time of writing) |\n| `confirmation` | `APPLY 0f42555c9dca23574a23fc6fe992cd0a716c5991` |\n| `production_allowlist` | the 14 versions above |\n| `review_reference` | the Claude Code review link, or a path under `.ai/reviews/` |\n\nThen Albert approves the `production` environment gate.\n\n## Verification\n\n1. `information_schema.columns` returns both `dflow.users.office_location` and\n   `dflow.users.preferred_language`, type `text`.\n2. `pg_constraint` holds `users_office_location_check` and `users_preferred_language_check`.\n3. The ledger gains exactly those 14 versions and nothing else.\n4. Log into `https://alsand.designflow.app` with a password AND with Microsoft SSO. Both must reach\n   the app. This is the acceptance test; a green ledger alone does not close this issue.\n\n## Relationship to existing issues\n\n- **#696** covers these exact columns but frames them as a **Cloud SQL** problem owned by Uma, and\n  states the sandbox/Supabase side is already handled. That premise is now false — see #763. The\n  sandbox IS Supabase, and it does not have the columns. #696 does not cover this outage.\n- **#809** asks for the promotion sequence B3 → B4 → B6 → B7 → B8 → B9. The fix is the last file of\n  the last batch there. If that sequence runs in full, this closes with it.\n- **#773** is the ledger-drift handover (out-of-order applies, B3..B9 unapproved). This issue is the\n  first user-visible consequence of that drift.\n\n43 merged migrations are unapplied in total. That is #773's scope, not this issue's. This issue asks\nonly for B9.\n\n## What was deliberately NOT done\n\n- **No band-aid.** Removing the two columns from the Sequelize model would restore login in minutes\n  and hide the drift. {"body":"Follow-up from the review of #794 (merged as `eaacaa5`). Two unrelated-sized items in one issue because they are both \"next time this file is open\" work, and the first one has an owner attached to it.\r\n\r\n## 1. Narrow the top-level data-statement allowance in `read_noop_declaration`\r\n\r\n**These are LATENT, not currently exploitable. Read the mitigations section before deciding this is urgent — and before deciding it can be ignored.**\r\n\r\n### What the code does today\r\n\r\n`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py` lets a migration declare itself a pure-data no-op with a `-- catalog-verification: no-op <reason>` line. The claim is checked: every statement in the file must be a data statement. \"Data statement\" is decided by `DATA_STATEMENT_RE`, which matches on the **head keyword only** and never looks at the target:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nDATA_STATEMENT_RE = re.compile(\r\n    r\"^\\s*(insert|update|delete|merge|with|select|values|set|reset|analyze)\\b\"\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\nThree shapes therefore pass the claim check today. Reproduced against `eaacaa5`, each prefixed with a valid declaration line:\r\n\r\n| statement | verdict | why it matters |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| `update pg_class set relacl = null where relname='t';` | ACCEPTED | writing `relacl` **is** a privilege change, by effect |\r\n| `select dblink_exec('revoke all on t from public');` | ACCEPTED | a revoke, executed through a function call |\r\n| `set role service_role;` | ACCEPTED | changes the executing principal |\r\n\r\nTo reproduce:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nimport sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts')\r\nimport production_catalog_verification as m\r\nD = \"-- catalog-verification: no-op a sufficiently long stated reason here\\n\"\r\nm.read_noop_declaration(D + \"update pg_class set relacl = null where relname='t';\", \"20260101000000\")[\"accepted\"]\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Why this is not currently exploitable — and why that is exactly the reason to fix it\r\n\r\nChecked read-only against production (`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`):\r\n\r\n```\r\npostgres_is_superuser        = false\r\npostgres_can_update_pg_class = false\r\ndblink_installed             = 0      (available = 1, but not installed)\r\n```\r\n\r\n- The `pg_class` write **cannot execute**. The migration role is not superuser and lacks UPDATE on `pg_catalog.pg_class`, so it dies at apply time with a permission error.\r\n- `dblink_exec` **does not exist** — the extension is not installed, and a migration could not install it either, because `create extension` is rejected by this same check.\r\n- `set role` on its own creates no catalog object, so declaring it a no-op is not a false claim. Every other statement in the file is still judged individually, so it cannot launder anything sitting beside it. This one is arguably not a defect at all — it is listed because `reset role` should be handled consistently with it either way.\r\n\r\n**Every one of those mitigations is environmental.** None of them lives in this repository, none is asserted by a test, and none would announce itself if it changed. Someone installing `dblink` for an unrelated feature, or a future platform change to what the migration role may write, silently converts a theoretical gap into a real one — with no diff, no review, and no failing check anywhere in this repo to notice it. That is the whole argument for closing it: not that it is dangerous today, but that its safety is currently being provided by something nobody here controls or watches.\r\n\r\n### What to change\r\n\r\n- **A target check on data statements.** A statement whose head is `update`/`delete`/`insert`/`merge` and whose target is in `pg_catalog` is not a data statement for the purposes of this claim. It should be rejected with a reason naming the catalog table.\r\n- **`reset role` handled alongside `set role`.** `PRINCIPAL_CHANGE_RE` currently matches `set role` and `set session authorization` but not `reset role`, which restores the session's original (higher) principal. Whichever way the decision goes, the two should agree.\r\n- Tests for each rejection, in the style of the existing ones in `scripts/test_production_catalog_verification.py`.\r\n\r\n### Who should own this\r\n\r\n**Whoever picks up draft PR #804.** That PR is redesigning the `do`-block accept path in this same function after three rounds of bypasses, and it will be touching `read_noop_declaration`, `DATA_STATEMENT_RE` and `is_data_statement` directly. Doing this narrowing separately would mean two people editing the same accept-path logic at once. It belongs in that work.\r\n\r\n**Do not treat this as a reason to delay #804 or to widen anything.** The accept path as merged in #794 is fail-closed: the `do`-block accept path was reverted out entirely, and the real `20260807030000` currently fails verification as the accepted cost of that split.\r\n\r\n## 2. Stale comment in the model-review workflow step\r\n\r\n`.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml`, in the `SHARED_DB_REVIEW_MODEL` env block on the \"Automatic model review\" step, still says:\r\n\r\n> unset, the script uses its own DEFAULT_MODEL, which is a real, working id\r\n\r\nThere is no `DEFAULT_MODEL` in `scripts/production_apply_model_review.py` any more. After #803 (merged as `4645191`), an unset `SHARED_DB_REVIEW_MODEL` resolves the **newest member of `DEFAULT_MODEL_FAMILY` from the live `GET /v1/models` listing**, and an unreachable listing or an empty family is fatal rather than a guess. The comment predates the better behaviour and now describes something that does not exist.\r\n\r\nOne line, next time that file is open. Nothing depends on it, but it is the kind of comment that sends someone looking for a constant that isn't there.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\nFiled by the review sub-agent for orchestrator session fcc2a1 (marker #793), after merging #794, #799, #800 and #803. No code was changed for this issue and no database was written to; the one production query above was read-only, with `get_project_url` called first.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstate: non-structural\npriority: 250\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T17:11:26Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T23:08:52Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":805,"title":"verify: narrow the top-level data-statement allowance in the no-op claim check (latent, not currently exploitable) + one stale workflow comment","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:51:33Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/805"},
{"body":"Filed by a non-orchestrator session on `al8960ofc`, worktree\n`C:\\repos\\shared-db-worktrees\\github-issues-dedup-review-ba4fde`, branch\n`claude/github-issues-dedup-review-ba4fde`, 2026-08-11. Orchestrator marker #793 was open at\nthe time; this session was not it and did no dispatched work.\n\n**Nothing was written to any database.** No migration authored, no preview push, no\nproduction apply, no DML, no schema read beyond none at all. The only mutation anywhere was\nclosing one GitHub issue.\n\n## 1. What this session was doing, and why\n\nAlbert asked, in plain terms: *read through all the GitHub issues in this repo and tell me if\nyou see any duplicated issues, or two or more issues that should logically be combined into\none.* The repo had **119 open issues**, a large share of them `HANDOVER:` write-ups filed by\nsuccessive orchestrator sessions. The exercise was triage, not engineering.\n\n## 2. What was actually DONE\n\n- Read every open issue title (119) plus the full bodies of 23 candidates.\n- **Closed #766** as a verbatim duplicate of #764 (`gh issue close 766 --reason \"not planned\"`,\n  with a comment naming #764). This is the ONLY state change this session made anywhere.\n- Ran a second-opinion review through GLM 5.2 (`ai-glm` session\n  `github-issue-dedup-consolidation`, model `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2`). GLM read\n  `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` and\n  `scripts/production_apply_model_review.py` directly and confirmed two live defects there.\n- Verified GLM's two most load-bearing claims against `gh` rather than trusting them.\n\nNo commits. No branches pushed. No PRs opened. `git log -1` on this worktree is `37fec74`,\nidentical to `origin/main` as of 2026-08-11T21:45Z.\n\n## 3. Applied to preview / production\n\n**Nothing to either.** Preview `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` was never touched, connected to, or\nread. Production was never touched, connected to, or read. No Supabase MCP call was made in\nthis session at all.\n\n## 4. What is half-finished\n\n**The consolidation itself.** A reviewed, revised plan exists (below) and Albert has NOT\napproved it. Nine issue closures are proposed and zero have been executed beyond #766.\n\n## 5. What this session owns\n\n- Worktree `C:\\repos\\shared-db-worktrees\\github-issues-dedup-review-ba4fde` on branch\n  `claude/github-issues-dedup-review-ba4fde`. **Clean except for one untracked file** (below).\n  Safe to retire once this issue is read; the branch has no commits of its own.\n- **One untracked file, declared so it is not a mystery:**\n  `.ai/reviews/glm-github-issue-dedup-consolidation-20260811T213853Z.md` — the GLM review\n  transcript, written automatically by the `ai-glm` wrapper. Its substance is reproduced in\n  this issue. Delete it with the worktree; it does not need committing.\n- GLM session `github-issue-dedup-consolidation` is still active and warm. Continue it with\n  `ai-glm ask github-issue-dedup-consolidation` rather than re-briefing from scratch — it has\n  all 23 issue bodies in cached context.\n\n## 6. What it was about to do next — THE PLAN, awaiting Albert's go\n\n**One exact duplicate, already handled:** #764 and #766 were identical in title and body.\n#766 is closed. Note the same double-filing produced #765/#767, another identical pair, both\nalready closed. **Something double-filed issues on 2026-08-11 and it is worth finding out\nwhat** — nobody has looked.\n\nThe nine remaining actions, after GLM's corrections were folded in:\n\n| # | Action | Note |\n|---|---|---|\n| #710 | Close as **superseded by #773** | NOT \"done\" — it covered B2..B9 and only B2 ran. GLM's correction to my wording; the closing comment matters. |\n| #730 | Close as done | B2 is applied, ledger 376 per #773. |\n| #773 | **Keep open** | The single live \"promote B3..B10\" tracker. |\n| #784, #788 | **Keep open, separate** | Real guard/review gaps, not promotion tasks. Point them at #773. |\n| #676 | Close, but **copy two facts into #774 FIRST** | See the warning in section 9. |\n| #503 | Close **only after** its four decisions are added to #736 | See the warning in section 9. |\n| #711, #516 | Close, folded into #736 | Both already indexed there; verified. |\n| #785 + #737 | Combine into one script-defect issue | Both are live defects in `scripts/production_apply_model_review.py`; GLM confirmed both against the file. |\n| #682 + #528 | Combine | Both are \"retire done worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`\". |\n| #523 | Fold into #539 | #523 is the prerequisite analysis for #539's question. |\n\n**Left deliberately open, as decisions and not oversights** — #689, #557, #526, #551, #536,\n#444. Reasons in section 9.\n\n## 7. Blocked on\n\n**Albert.** He was given the revised plan and said \"wrap up\" instead of \"go\". Nothing may be\nclosed on the strength of this issue alone. He also has one open question of his own, surfaced\nbelow in section 9, that gates the #503 half.\n\n## 8. What was tried that did NOT work — MANDATORY\n\n- **`ai-glm` from the Bash tool fails** with `command not found`. The wrapper resolves through\n  a Windows shim; it must be called from PowerShell on this machine. The skill says this; it is\n  restated here because the failure looks like a missing install and is not.\n- **A GLM review session has no `bash` tool and cannot run `gh`.** Briefing it with \"read the\n  issues with gh\" would have produced a confident answer built on nothing. The 23 issue bodies\n  had to be dumped to a file and pasted into the prompt. Budget for this: the brief was 62KB.\n- **My first pass got three of six groupings wrong**, and all three errors were the same\n  mistake — assuming that issues which *look* alike are the same *kind* of work. Specifically:\n  I treated a data-rescue task (#689), a root-cause investigation (#557), a live incident with\n  a data-state precondition (#444) and an unrelated licensing-answers task (#526) as ordinary\n  members of tidy-up groups. **If you re-run this exercise, that is the failure mode to watch\n  for.** Title similarity is not task similarity.\n- **GLM was wrong about one thing.** It flagged #721 as a dangling dependency of #730 and said\n  to check it during closure. #721 is already CLOSED. Verified with `gh issue view 721`. Do not\n  spend time on it.\n\n## 9. Facts that may already be stale, and the traps\n\n**Re-derive all of these before acting. Every count here was read once, on 2026-08-11.**\n\n- 119 open issues; `origin/main` at `37fec74`; marker #793 open. All checked ~21:45Z.\n- The production ledger figures (376 applied / 53 unapplied) are **quoted from #773, not\n  measured by this session.** Four different figures for this circulated on 2026-08-10 and all\n  four were wrong. Re-derive from the live ledger.\n\n**Three traps that will bite whoever executes the plan:**\n\n1. **#503 is NOT indexed by #736**, despite #736 declaring itself the index of every open\n   owner decision. I verified this: #736 references #515, #516, #521, #531, #539, #541, #551,\n   #582, #618, #643, #644, #665, #675, #676, #696, #705, #711, #714, #719, #723, #732, #733 —\n   and **#503 is absent**. Closing #503 without first copying its four decisions into #736\n   silently drops them off the tracker. One of the four is dangerous on its own: *does the\n   ColdLion \"follow deletions\" rule apply to licensors and properties?* — **92,173\n   `public.assets` rows carry a `core.licensor` id with `ON DELETE SET NULL`.** Albert was\n   asked on 2026-08-07 and dismissed the question without answering it. A dismissal is not an\n   answer, and this is a live path to blanking 92k rows.\n2. **#676 holds two operating constraints that #774 does not repeat**: the asset count is\n   **frozen permanently at finalize and cannot be corrected** (a bad load stays as history),\n   and it **must be observed the same day as the load**. Copy both onto #774 before closing\n   #676, or they are lost.\n3. **#539 carries a do-not-re-litigate trap** that must survive absorbing #523: *do NOT re-ask\n   `EX` / `LB` / `JL` — Laura answered those in round 1, and `JL` is Laura's question, not\n   Albert's.*\n\n**Why six issues were left open deliberately** (each is a decision, not an oversight):\n\n- **#689** — four commits on one hetz VPS disk, on no remote, no backup. This is rescue, not\n  cleanup. Folded into a sweep it reads as optional tidying and gets skipped.\n- **#557** — the shared checkout broke twice and the root cause was never established. The\n  symptom may be gone (#689 reports `/worksp/shared-db` clean on `main` at `bc29d36`, itself\n  unverified here); the investigation is the point.\n- **#526** — records round-3 **licensing answers**, not property codes. Carries its own\n  warning: extract ref→answer only, do NOT commit the workbook (third-party name and a real\n  POP item number), and the validator has a global-match defect that would miss a\n  wrong-licensor CC.\n- **#444** — a live incident with 18 named alert rows that must be acknowledged in\n  `plm.taxonomy_sync_alert` before it can close. That precondition dies in a merge.\n- **#551 / #536** — related but not the same defect, and #536 is explicitly ON HOLD.\n  Cross-reference them; do not merge.\n\n**One structural observation, offered and not acted on:** ~45 of the 119 open issues are\ntitled `HANDOVER:`. Those are session logs, not tasks. Separately, #551 records that the\nhourly ColdLion alert monitor opens a GitHub issue **unconditionally, every run** — it is\nitself a duplicate-issue factory, and #444 is one of its outputs. Any serious attempt to get\nthis tracker under control has to stop that first.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T21:56:46Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T21:42:22Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Summary\n\nBatch **B9 — the licensor landing batch** (the Paramount, NBCU and Warner landing tables) is **impossible to apply by any allowlist string** at `main`. This is a guard deadlock, not a data problem. It blocks the owner's current priority.\n\nRecording it here so it is on the record independent of the fix PR.\n\n## The deadlock\n\nTwo rules in `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` contradict each other:\n\n1. `CO_PRESENCE_RULES` requires `20260810180000` in **any** allowlist containing `20260810020000` (Paramount) or `20260810070000` (NBCU). Both are in B9.\n2. `validate_candidates` refuses **any** allowlist naming a version already applied on production.\n\nAnd `20260810180000` **is already applied on production**. It was promoted early and alone on 2026-08-11, and it sorts *above* B9's own end version `20260810170000`. Verified read-only against project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\n\n| Allowlist | Result |\n|---|---|\n| B9's 14 versions | REFUSED — `co-presence rule: 20260810020000 may not be promoted without 20260810180000` |\n| B9's 14 + `20260810180000` | REFUSED — `already applied on production: 20260810180000` |\n\nThere is no third string. Every entry point (`prepare`, `preflight`, `verify-dry-run`, `assert-bounded`) routes through `parse_allowlist`, so no subcommand escapes it.\n\nB9's 14 versions:\n`20260810010000`, `20260810020000`, `20260810030000`, `20260810050000`, `20260810060000`, `20260810070000`, `20260810080000`, `20260810090000`, `20260810100000`, `20260810110000`, `20260810120000`, `20260810130000`, `20260810160000`, `20260810170000`\n\n## Root cause\n\n`ATOMIC_BATCHES` was **deliberately** made ledger-aware (`members - already_applied`) for exactly this resume scenario, and its header explains at length why a ledger-blind version would be unsatisfiable rather than strict.\n\n`CO_PRESENCE_RULES` was left **ledger-blind**. That asymmetry was harmless right up until a required *fix* was promoted early and alone. Then it stopped being strictness and became a lock with no key — and the only escape is editing a safety guard under time pressure, which is the precise failure mode both headers were written to prevent.\n\n## The fix\n\nSubtract the production ledger from the required-fix set before comparing, exactly as `assert_atomic_batches` already does.\n\nThis must **not** weaken the rule, and the distinction is the whole point:\n\n- An **already-applied** fix satisfies the rule, because the property the rule protects — production must never hold the create without the fix — is already true and stays true.\n- A **missing** fix (neither applied nor in the allowlist) must still REFUSE. That is exactly the exposed state.\n- The rule stays **one-directional**: `20260810020000` without `20260810090000` stays REFUSED; `20260810090000` alone stays ALLOWED, as the only legal recovery path from a run that died between them.\n\n## Related\n\n`verify-dry-run` had no way to be given a ledger at all, so it would have re-introduced the deadlock at the lane's last gate even after `prepare` and `preflight` accepted the same allowlist. It needs an optional `--remote-ledger`; omitting it keeps the stricter ledger-blind behaviour, which fails closed.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T21:55:33Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T21:42:05Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":796,"title":"B9 (licensor landing batch) is unshippable: ledger-blind co-presence rule deadlocks against validate_candidates","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:51:39Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/796"},

{"body":"## Orchestrator handover — session `shared-db-orchestrator-1067a1`, round 2, 2026-08-11\r\n\r\n**Full briefing:** [`HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T2036Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-first-gated-production-apply.md`](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/blob/main/HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T2036Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-first-gated-production-apply.md) (PR #791).\r\n\r\n**Read the earlier one first:** [`HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T1850Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-production-lane-made-real.md`](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/blob/main/HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T1850Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-production-lane-made-real.md) (PR #786). Proven two ways: ledger 376 → 377 by per-version set membership, and `pg_default_acl` for `(plm, postgres, 'r')` narrowed from `{service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres}` to `{service_role=arwd/postgres}` — the uppercase `D` (TRUNCATE) is gone. Nothing built, no database touched, ready to dispatch.\r\n- Four PRs merged earlier in the session (#779, #780, #781, #783) plus #787 and the two handover PRs.\r\n\r\n### ⚠️ The two things most likely to be got wrong next\r\n1. **The apply's job shows a red X and the apply SUCCEEDED.** The post-apply catalog verifier refused to report green because its lexer cannot read `alter default privileges` migrations — its own caveat says so. **That is correct behaviour. Do not weaken enforcing mode, do not add a bypass, do not special-case a migration id.** Fix **#790** instead. **It will recur for every privilege-only migration in B3–B10.**\r\n2. **Production's ledger is applied OUT OF ORDER** — unapplied versions sort below the max applied. **Never reason from the high-water mark**; use per-version set membership only.\r\n\r\n### Outstanding — all tracked, nothing lives only in prose\r\n**Waiting on Albert:** #778 (preserve `art_piece.id = 790`, then name the exact schema and action for a drop) · #727 (the reversed source ruling and the unbudgeted re-profile it forces) · the 23 open `needs-albert` issues, indexed **imperfectly** by #736 — **#736 is stale and incomplete, do not rely on it**.\r\n\r\n**Ready to dispatch, no decision needed:** **#790** (do this before the next promotions) · #788 (four unbatched leftovers, still unreviewed; the first real model review already returned CONCERNS on `20260811070000`) · #784 · #785 · #782 · #727 re-profile · #773 / #710 (batches B3–B10) · #682 (53 worktrees).\r\n\r\n### Recommended next promotion order\r\n`20260810180000` was only the first file of B10. **B5 next** (function-only, no DDL, no data, independent), then **B3 → B4** in that order (B4 aborts without B3), then B6, B7, B8, and **B9 last**.\r\n\r\n### State left behind, deliberately\r\n53 worktrees (#682, untouched). `issue-727-design` worktree is **LIVE** — branch `docs/727-orderlist-import-design` (`824eee5`), pushed, **no PR**, holds the #727 design; **do not delete**. {"body":"## What happened\nOn 2026-08-11 the owner approved the production apply of `20260810180000` (run [31532843298](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/actions/runs/31532843298)). **The apply succeeded** — ledger 376 → 377, and `pg_default_acl` for `(plm, postgres, 'r')` narrowed from `{service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres}` to `{service_role=arwd/postgres}`, with the uppercase `D` (TRUNCATE) removed exactly as intended.\n\n**The job still went red**, because the *Post-apply catalog verification* step exited 1:\n\n> the allowlisted migrations named no catalog object this lexer can read … it means THIS STEP PROVED NOTHING, so enforcing mode fails rather than letting a green tick stand in for evidence it never gathered.\n\nDerived targets: tables 0, views 0, functions 0, rls_relations 0, seeded 0.\n\n## Why\nThe step derives its target list with a **conservative lexer over the migration text**, and its own printed caveat says objects named through **`alter default privileges`** — along with `execute format(...)`, quoted or mixed-case identifiers, and search_path-relative names — are **\"NOT listed and NOT checked\"**. `20260810180000` is `alter default privileges` plus conditional revokes, so the lexer honestly found nothing.\n\n## ⚠️ Do NOT fix this by softening enforcing mode\nThe step behaved **correctly**. Refusing to show green on zero evidence is precisely the discipline built on 2026-08-11, after three stacked faults in the model-review lane were each hidden by a green tick that had been earned by nothing (see #617, PRs #779 / #783 / #787). Turning enforcement off, adding a bypass flag, or special-casing this migration id would restore the exact failure class the whole day was spent removing.\n\n**The fix is to make the lexer able to VERIFY this shape, not to excuse it.**\n\n## What is needed\n1. **Teach the target derivation to read privilege-shaped migrations.** Derive targets from `alter default privileges` (→ assert against `pg_default_acl`), and from `grant`/`revoke` on tables and functions (→ assert against `relacl` / `proacl`). The evidence exists in the catalog; only the derivation is missing.\n2. **Assert, do not merely print.** For a privilege migration the expected end state is knowable — `20260810180000` even asserts it internally (`D2 OK: plm default privileges for tables are now {service_role=arwd/postgres}`). The lane should be able to make the same assertion externally rather than leaving a human to read an ACL string. Note the existing caveat that privileges are currently \"EVIDENCE, not assertions\".\n3. **Handle the genuine no-op case honestly.** A pure-data migration really does name no catalog object. That case needs an explicit, recorded reason — not a silent pass.\n4. **Watch the related blind spot** the same caveat names: `acl_is_default = true` means `proacl` is NULL, which for a function is **`EXECUTE` to `PUBLIC`** — the state a missing revoke leaves behind, **not** \"no grants\". That reads as safe and is not.\n\n## This WILL recur\nAny grant / revoke / default-privilege-only migration hits the same wall. Several are queued in batches B3–B10. Each will fail a correct apply and force a human to distinguish a false negative from a real one under promotion pressure — which is when mistakes get made.\n\nRelated: #773 (production state and the apply record), #784 (non-atomic never-rest states unenforced), #785 (nothing proves the review model id is real), #788 (the four unreviewed leftovers).","closedAt":"2026-08-11T23:08:05Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T20:33:33Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":790,"title":"Post-apply catalog verification cannot read privilege-only migrations, so every one of them fails a correct apply","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:51:45Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/790"},
