{"body":"The four migrations merged after the nine-batch promotion plan was written — `20260811030000`, `20260811050000`, `20260811060000`, `20260811070000` — sit in **no batch** and appear in **no approved allowlist**. They were explicitly outside the Grok review brief on 2026-08-11, so **neither Grok nor the verifying agent looked at them.**\n\nRe-derive before acting:\n```bash\ngit ls-tree origin/main --name-only supabase/migrations/\ngh issue list --repo u2giants/shared-db --label db-work --state open\n```\n\n## Why this is now urgent rather than tidy\n\nOn 2026-08-11 the advisory model review ran **for the first time in this repo's history** (PR #779 made a non-running review fatal; #783 and #787 fixed a model id that did not exist and then moved it to `claude-opus-5`). Its very first real end-to-end run was against **`20260811070000`**, and it returned **VERDICT: CONCERNS** with substantive findings, not boilerplate:\n\n- The batch depends on `plm.nbcu_*` tables that **no file in the batch creates**.\n- The out-of-order apply **would break two lower-versioned count gates**. (Note this is the known trap: production's ledger is applied out of order — 48 unapplied versions sort below the max applied `20260810140000` — so version order is not apply order here.)\n- A `CREATE OR REPLACE finalize_nbcu_capture` **tightens the loader contract**.\n- **PG17-only `MAINTAIN` syntax** is used.\n\nThese are exactly the class of finding the review exists to surface, and they were found on the first migration it was ever pointed at. Treat that as a signal about the leftovers as a group, not as a verdict on one file.\n\n## What is needed\n\n1. **Review all four properly** — the same treatment B3–B10 received: read the real SQL, check order dependencies against the live ledger (per-version set membership, never the high-water mark), check for irreversible operations, locking, and whether they belong together.\n2. **Verify each CONCERNS finding above against the actual SQL** before acting on it OR dismissing it. A model verdict is a claim; the code is the fact. This repo has recorded second-opinion models being confidently wrong.\n3. **Decide their batch membership** and record it in `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` — the contract is the authority for batch membership, **never an issue body**. (On 2026-08-11 the batch lists in #710/#773 carried a B3/B4 overlap the contract did not have.)\n4. Only then can they be proposed for owner approval.\n\n## Do not skip this by promoting around them\n\nThey cannot be quietly left behind: they are on `origin/main`, so any future apply pinned to a `main` SHA will encounter them. Leaving them unclassified is how a partial fix ships.\n\nRelated: #773 (production state), #710 (batch plan), #785 (nothing proves the review model id is real), #784 (non-atomic never-rest states unenforced).","closedAt":"2026-08-13T00:17:47Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T19:03:36Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":788,"title":"The 4 unbatched leftover migrations are unreviewed, and the first real model review flagged 20260811070000","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:51:48Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/788"},
{"body":"### What happened on 2026-08-11\n\n`scripts/production_apply_model_review.py` pinned `MODEL = \"claude-opus-4-5-20260514\"`. **That model id has never existed.** It sat in the repo undetected because the review step had never actually run — no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` was configured, and before PR #779 a non-running review reported green anyway.\n\nThe moment the key was installed and the review ran for the first time, it returned `HTTP 404 not_found_error`. Because #779 correctly made a non-running review fatal, that kept the production apply lane RED with eight batches queued behind it.\n\nFixed in PR #783: corrected to `claude-opus-4-5-20251101`, moved behind the `SHARED_DB_REVIEW_MODEL` environment variable (per the standing rule that AI model choices must be configurable, never hard-coded), and a 404 now produces a message naming the model id and saying plainly that it is a CONFIGURATION problem, not a network one.\n\n### The gap that is still open\n\n**Nothing can prove the configured model id is real without calling the API.** PR #783 added 9 tests covering: the id is read from config with a default; the env var overrides; whitespace falls back; the default matches the documented constant and is shaped like an Anthropic id; the id lands in the request body; a 404 gives the CONFIGURATION message and is not retried; a 500 still is; the evidence records the model; the workflow wires the variable through.\n\n**They cannot catch a dead id.** The broken `claude-opus-4-5-20260514` passes every structural assertion in that file. Only a live call proves an id is real.\n\nThis matters more than it used to: because a failed review is now fatal, **the day the configured model retires, every production promotion blocks.** That blast radius did not exist when the code was always green.\n\n### Options — pick one, do not build both\n\n1. **Live pre-flight probe.** A `max_tokens: 1` call before the real review. Fails fast and precisely, on the run that would have failed anyway. Costs one tiny API call per production apply.\n2. **Weekly canary job.** Goes red if `DEFAULT_MODEL` stops resolving. Catches the retirement days before it blocks a promotion, and costs nothing at apply time — but only if someone reads the red.\n\nRecommended: (1), because it puts the failure where the operator already is. (2) is a reasonable addition, not a substitute.\n\n### Also in scope — a related weak test\n`test_there_is_no_bypass_env_var` (flagged Medium during the #779 review) is a **denylist of three literal strings**. A bypass flag named anything else passes it, and it does not assert the absence of an `if:` skip on the review step or job. The code has no bypass today — that was traced by hand during the review — but the regression net has holes. Rewrite it to assert the invariant rather than enumerate three names.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T01:01:04Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T18:47:11Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":785,"title":"Nothing proves the review model id is real until a production apply fails on it","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:51:51Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/785"},
{"body":"PR #781 (merged 2026-08-11) made `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` enforce the **four batches the contract labels ATOMIC** — B1, B3, B7, B9. A partial allowlist for any of those is now refused, with a message naming the batch, the members supplied and the members missing.\r\n\r\n**The hole that remains:** `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` §6 also forbids resting inside **B2, B5, B6 and B8**, but those batches are not labelled atomic, so nothing mechanically enforces them. A partial B2 allowlist still passes the guard today — and would ship the known-defective ClickUp importer.\r\n\r\nThis is faithful to the contract's own labelling, so it was correctly out of scope for #781. It is still a real gap in the production lane, and the failure mode is the one this repo keeps hitting: a rule that exists only in prose gets skipped by whoever is under pressure at 2am.\r\n\r\n### Two pieces of work\r\n\r\n**1. Enforce the §6 never-rest states for the non-atomic batches.** Decide the right shape first — these are not all-or-nothing like the atomic four, so the atomic mechanism may not fit. The contract states a legal resting point per batch; the check probably needs to be \"an allowlist may not stop at a version §6 forbids resting on\" rather than \"all members or none.\"\r\n\r\n**2. Tighten `test_membership_matches_the_contract_counts` to assert exact frozensets, not lengths.** It currently checks counts only. The exact membership was verified BY HAND during the #781 review (all four batches reconciled member-for-member against §5 counts and §6 lists), but nothing pins it for the next editor. A future edit could swap one version for another and the test would still pass.\r\n\r\n### Context worth carrying\r\nBatch membership drift is not hypothetical here. On 2026-08-11 the batch lists carried in issue text (#710 and #773) were found to contain a **B3/B4 overlap that the contract did not have** — two versions listed in both batches. The contract was right; the copies were wrong. See AGENTS.md §4.3, added the same day: documents point at the live reading, never carry the figure.\r\n\r\n**The contract file is the authority for batch membership. Never an issue body, including this one.**\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstate: non-structural\npriority: 250\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T05:44:30Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T18:47:09Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":784,"title":"Production lane: enforce the section 6 never-rest states for non-atomic batches (B2, B5, B6, B8)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:51:54Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/784"},
{"body":"# HANDOVER: PopCRM durable Outlook delta cursor contract\n\n## Requesting repo and plan\n\n- Consumer repo: `u2giants/popcrm-web`, local `/worksp/popcrm-web`, branch `main`\n- Plan: `/worksp/popcrm-web/plan_codebase_audit_remediation.md`, Session 6A\n- Current app commit: `5191d35`\n- Production must not be changed without Albert Hazan's exact approval in the active chat.\n\n## Business problem\n\nPopCRM's Outlook worker currently fetches a bounded newest-message window. A burst larger than that window can permanently skip older unseen mail. The permanent solution is Microsoft Graph delta pagination backed by a durable cursor that survives restarts and advances only after all fetched work succeeds.\n\n## Exact shared-db work requested\n\nCreate the smallest CRM-owned, service-role-only durable worker-state contract for the Outlook mailbox delta cursor. The contract must:\n\n1. Atomically load and save one opaque Microsoft Graph delta link for a named cursor purpose/mailbox or integration.\n2. Deny browser roles and prevent any browser-readable view or broad API exposure.\n3. Allow the PopCRM worker's service-role path to read and replace only the intended state.\n4. Record non-sensitive identity/purpose and safe update timestamps without logging or returning the cursor in verification output.\n5. Be additive, idempotent, documented, and delivered as a new unique timestamped migration.\n6. Include tests that prove unauthenticated and authenticated browser access is denied, service-role load/save works, replacement is atomic, and no unrelated CRM state is exposed.\n7. Be applied and verified on preview project `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` only at this stage.\n\nObject names and the exact RPC/table shape should follow current shared-db conventions. Likely object class is a CRM-owned worker-state table plus narrow functions, but the orchestrator and implementation agent must inspect current conventions and choose the final names before claiming objects.\n\n## Required workflow and review\n\nUse a fresh implementation sub-agent in an isolated shared-db worktree. Run the collision check with every object the migration writes. Create a branch and PR, run all SQL checks, perform preview dry-run/apply/verification, and record the project ref immediately before every preview write as required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.2.\n\nHave Kimi K3 review the complete database diff. Return every actionable Kimi comment to the same implementation agent until Kimi returns `APPROVE`. Record the review evidence and preview evidence on this issue or its linked PR.\n\nDo not apply to production and do not merge in a way that triggers production work. Stop at the preview-proven, Kimi-approved gate and report the exact branch, PR, migration filename, preview checks, and the exact production approval/action needed. PopCRM Phase 6B must not begin until the contract is approved, merged/applied as authorized, and available to the consumer.\n\n## Relevant app evidence\n\n- Current bounded fetch: `/worksp/popcrm-web/workers/crm-worker-supabase.mjs`, around lines 554-610.\n- Existing injectable but non-durable cursor-store seam: `/worksp/popcrm-web/workers/lib/worker-foundation.mjs`, around line 424.\n- Existing inserts are idempotent by `outlook_message_id`, but that prevents duplicates only. It does not prove complete discovery.\n- The Graph delta link is opaque and potentially sensitive. Never place a real value in logs, fixtures, issue text, PR text, commits, or handoffs.\n\n## Verification gate\n\nThis request is ready for PopCRM Phase 6B only when all of the following are true:\n\n- Unique migration and exact contract names are recorded.\n- Shared-db checks pass.\n- Preview dry-run lists only the intended migration.\n- Preview apply succeeds against `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` with target proof recorded immediately before the write.\n- Contract tests prove browser denial and narrow worker load/save behavior.\n- Kimi K3 says `APPROVE` after any findings are fixed by the same implementation agent.\n- The production status is stated explicitly. {"body":"> # ⛔ BLOCKED 2026-08-20 — DO NOT DELETE. The premise below is FALSE.\n>\n> Measured live against production on 2026-08-20: **two foreign keys point INTO `designflow` from live, migration-managed schemas** — `plm.art_piece_attachment` (**2,276 rows, every one of them**, resolving to all 1,114 `art_piece` rows) and `app.RolePermissions` (4 rows). The statement below that *\"no cross-schema foreign key was found using it\"* is **wrong**, and the owner approval recorded on 2026-08-19 was given on that false basis, so **it cannot carry the deletion as scoped.**\n>\n> A `DROP SCHEMA designflow CASCADE` would not refuse — it would **silently strip both constraints** and strand those rows.\n>\n> A **verified pre-deletion backup exists anyway**: 1Password vault `vibe_coding`, item `zepc66j5xajdg4novzttmmrtg4`, sha256 `916be84f…`, retrieved back and confirmed byte-identical. Production has **no PITR**, so that logical dump is the only surgical recovery path.\n>\n> **Read the 2026-08-20 comment for the full evidence and the three options before acting on anything below.**\n\n## Current conclusion\n\nThe `designflow` schema on production Supabase project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` is an unused, unmanaged leftover copy. It is not the live DesignFlow production database. Live DesignFlow production currently uses the separate `designflow` schema on Google Cloud SQL.\n\nThis issue remains separate from #770 and #771:\n\n- #770 is the eventual full move of live DesignFlow production from Cloud SQL to Supabase.\n- #771 is the timed rehearsal required before that move can be scheduled.\n- #778 is a same-name orphan cleanup that requires its own recovery proof and explicit owner approval.\n\nCombining them would increase the risk of deleting or inspecting the wrong same-named schema.\n\n## Read-only investigation completed\n\nThe full evidence is preserved in the existing investigation comment on this issue. In summary:\n\n- the orphan has seven populated tables plus any other schema objects that must be freshly inventoried before action;\n- nearly all investigated records were duplicated by the newer, larger Cloud SQL production system;\n- one art-record identity existed only in the orphan because it had later been deleted from live production;\n- the orphan appeared to be bulk-loaded once and then abandoned;\n- no deployed configuration, application traffic, or cross-schema foreign key was found using it;\n- no database change has been made.\n\nThe orphan is not an authority source for licensing, ColdLion, or the future migration.\n\n## Grok 4.6 independent review, 2026-08-19\n\nGrok 4.6 agreed that #778 should remain separate and that the future full Cloud SQL migration does not change the cleanup answer. It raised one material correction to the earlier recommendation:\n\n**Preserving only the one unique record is not enough to make deletion recoverable.** Before any deletion, preserve a private full backup of the entire orphan schema, keep the unique record private, and freshly prove the schema's complete object inventory and lack of use.\n\nGrok review cost: first broad attempt produced no verdict and cost $0.274907; the successful narrow review cost $0.11892962.\n\n## Recommended recoverable action\n\nOwner-approved successor action (2026-08-27): rename the schema to designflow_frozen_20260710, preserving all rows and inbound foreign keys. The earlier deletion plan below is retained as superseded history and is not authorized for execution:\n\n1. Prove the target is production Supabase project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, not Google Cloud SQL.\n2. Freshly inventory every object in the Supabase `designflow` schema and re-check dependencies and use.\n3. Create and verify a private full backup of the entire orphan schema outside this public repository.\n4. Preserve the one unique record inside that private backup. Do not restore it into live DesignFlow unless separately requested.\n5. Delete only schema `designflow` from Supabase project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\n6. Prove the orphan is gone and that live Cloud SQL DesignFlow and Supabase `dflow` are untouched.\n\n## Owner approval recorded\n\nAlbert Hazan approved the exact recommended action in chat on 2026-08-19: make a verified private backup of the unused `designflow` schema on production Supabase project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, including its one unique record, then delete that exact orphan schema. The approval does not cover Google Cloud SQL, the active Supabase `dflow` schema, or restoring the unique record into live DesignFlow.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 500\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - schema designflow\n  - schema designflow_frozen_20260710\nreads:\n```\n\n\n\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-31T05:26:43Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T15:57:21Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Two loose ends and one live worktree\n\nHousekeeping left by orchestrator session d152a272, recorded so the next session does not treat any of it as abandoned.\n\n### 1. A LIVE worktree with possibly uncommitted work\n\n**`.claude/worktrees/backlog-sweep`** — its agent was mid-way through the READY list when the session ended. It may hold uncommitted work. **CHECK IT BEFORE CLEANING ANYTHING.** Its earlier work merged as PR #747; anything beyond that is unlanded.\n\nEvery other worktree named in the handover file is finished with its PR merged and is safe to retire under the `cleanup-worktree` skill.\n\n### 2. Nothing was deleted this session, deliberately\n\n46 worktrees exist. Several belong to other sessions. Issues #682 and #528 ask for retirement and were **left alone on purpose** because agents were live inside worktrees for most of the session — and six agents were killed mid-run by a session limit, which is exactly the scenario where a tidy-up destroys the only copy of someone's work.\n\n**That was a decision, not an oversight.** Retirement is a quiet-window job.\n\n### 3. `audit.service.js` swallows write failures\n\nFound while proving `AuditLog` is append-only. `designflow-backend/services/audit.service.js` catches a failed audit write into a `console.error` and returns. **Audit rows can be silently lost.** Not blocking anything, and in a different repo, but it is a silent-failure path in the audit trail and the standing rule is that every fallback must alert loudly.\n\n### 4. Migration version `20260811040000` was allocated and never used\n\nReserved for PopDAM OrderList (#727); no migration proved necessary. **It is free for reallocation.** Recorded so nobody assumes it is taken and skips it, and so nobody assumes it is a gap that means something.\n\n### 5. Two machines still need a dotfiles sync\n\n`916` (was powered off) and `4837` (never checked). Only the owner can run it. It carries the orchestrator-marker fix — the marker query was missing `--repo`, so from any other repository it returned zero markers and **exited 0**, indistinguishable from a clear board. A second orchestrator could have started while one was live.\n\nFull briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T1516Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-fourteen-agent-session.md`. {"body":"## The Paramount load is blocked on one number that may not exist\n\nMigration `20260811030000` is merged and **applied to preview**, verified by object and behaviour. The private builder is written and proven, producing **150,430 metadata values**, deterministic across two runs, zero banned fields. Both halves fit — all 150,430 rows were fed through the real loader end to end.\n\n**The load has not run.** It requires `PMT_PORTAL_GLOBAL_ASSET_COUNT`.\n\n## What that field is\n\nThe loader header says it is \"an observation the operator made in the portal... NOT in the capture manifest and cannot be computed from the captured files. Deriving it from anything available here would mean inventing it.\"\n\n**It appears in exactly seven places, and every one of them stores or displays it.** It is checked as a non-negative integer, passed to `begin_pmt_capture`, held as an `integer not null` column with a `>= 0` check, and selected verbatim into `api.pmt_latest_capture`. It appears **nowhere** in `validate_pmt_capture`, `finalize_pmt_capture`, or any reconciliation, expectation or shrink check.\n\n**Definitively: a recorded observation with zero computational role.**\n\n## Why it is hard\n\nThe owner has used the portal and **has never seen a portal-wide asset total**. Facet screenshots show only per-brand and per-property counts.\n\n**Do not sum the brand facets.** The eight brand buckets add to 46,955, but the capture holds 25,983 asset-to-brand links across only 25,760 distinct assets — **223 assets carry more than one brand** — and there is an `undefined` bucket of 108. The sum is an upper bound at best and double-counted at worst. The Paramount capture skill says plainly: preserve per-label totals and overlaps, do not add result counts to claim a unique total.\n\n## The two ways to close it\n\n1. **Get the real figure.** On a results screen with **no filter of any kind** applied, the count sits on the line directly above the first row of thumbnails, in the wide centre column — not in the left facet panel. Confirm nothing is selected in the left panel first. Expect roughly 41,000 to 47,000; wildly outside that means something is still filtered.\n2. **Record it as not observed.** Redefine the field as `library_view_asset_count` and load with a documented placeholder plus a `PMT_NOTES` entry saying it was never captured. Honest, and costs nothing computationally.\n\n**Do not invent a plausible number.** The fact that nothing validates it makes fabrication invisible, which is exactly when the discipline matters.\n\n## Context that resolved a bigger question along the way\n\nThe account's library view is a genuine **superset** of the authorized scope. Two brands matched the capture exactly (Paramount Network 1,434 and Paramount 1,217), which proves the facet and the capture count the same library; Nickelodeon showed 41,740 against 21,445 captured, which is the rights boundary. **Zero unauthorized assets were captured** — the scary facet names appear only as co-tags, standalone count 0 for all 25 of them.\n\nFull briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T1516Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-fourteen-agent-session.md`. Filed by orchestrator session d152a272, marker #739.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T22:01:09Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T15:25:46Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. {"body":"## Where the production promotion stands after batch B2\n\nBatch B2 applied to production on 2026-08-11, owner-approved. **Ledger 373 to 376.** That is the only production write of the session.\n\n| Figure | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Applied | **376** |\n| Max applied version | `20260810140000` — **and the ledger is OUT OF ORDER**, so this does not mean everything below it is applied |\n| **Total unapplied** | **53** |\n| Unapplied within batches B3..B9 | **50** |\n| Unapplied belonging to NO batch | **3** |\n\n## B3 through B9 are unrun and unapproved\n\nThe owner's approval covered **batch B2 only**. Nothing beyond it may be applied without a fresh, explicit, per-run approval naming the exact project and action. \"Fix the feed\" or \"carry on\" is not approval.\n\n## The three that belong to no batch — the new B10\n\nThese postdate the nine-batch plan in `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` §5, so **completing B2 through B9 will not promote them**:\n\n- `20260810180000_plm_default_privilege_hole_and_pg17_maintain_revokes.sql`\n- `20260810190000_dcp_vault_source_landing.sql`\n- `20260810190100_dcp_vault_chunked_loader.sql`\n\n**Orchestrator ruling: these get a new B10, and `20260810180000` must come FIRST inside it.** The reason is load-bearing: two independent live `pg_default_acl` reads showed `plm` AND `ingest` both still read `{service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres}`, so **every table created before `20260810180000` lands is born holding TRUNCATE for `service_role`**. TRUNCATE fires no row triggers and voids every immutability guard. If `180000` lands after the DCP tables, there is a window in which the DCP migrations' own explicit revokes are the only thing standing.\n\nMigrations merged after that ruling (`20260811030000`, `20260811050000`, `20260811060000`, `20260811070000`) also belong in B10 or a successor — **check the real list, do not trust this one.**\n\n## Before the next batch runs\n\n- **Freeze merges first.** The SHA pin refused two approved runs this session because main moved between staging and the click.\n- The post-batch harness `scripts/post_batch_app_verification.py` is now trustworthy — its assertions were proven already-correct (PR #742) and its 141 tests now actually execute in CI (PR #741). Use it, and still verify by object and behaviour separately.\n- Expect the advisory model review to report NOT RUN. It is a permanent no-op without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (#709, #737).\n\n## Ordering dependency discovered this session\n\n`20260810050000` (admin `app_access` provisioning) grants access to screens that **B8 creates**. **B8 must apply first**, or a user is granted access to a Product Depth screen whose tables do not exist. This blocks both the Carlos provisioning (#607) and the DB Data Admin production launch (#729).\n\nFull briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T1516Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-fourteen-agent-session.md`. {"body":"## Four things this session found that `AGENTS.md` does not say\n\nEach has already misled at least one session or agent. They belong in the standing-facts section so the next session reads them first.\n\n### 1. Preview and production have diverged IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Neither predicts the other.\n\nVerified by object on 2026-08-11:\n\n- Preview `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` holds **all 23 `plm.pmt_*` tables**, with both prerequisite migrations genuinely applied.\n- Production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` holds **ZERO** of them.\n- And in the other direction: `20260810140000_production_lane_canary` **IS applied on production and is NOT applied on preview**.\n\n**Consequence:** any rehearsal claim resting on \"preview is production minus N migrations\" is wrong. A passing preview rehearsal means \"this behaved correctly on preview\", never \"this will behave correctly in production\". Post-apply verification against production objects and behaviour is not optional.\n\nBoth ledgers are also **applied OUT OF ORDER**, in different ways. A high max version does not mean everything below it is applied. This has misled at least three sessions.\n\n### 2. The advisory model review is a permanent silent no-op.\n\nThe `Production apply review (advisory model verdict + hard guards)` step reports **\"NOT RUN — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not configured on this repository\"** and is `continue-on-error`. No HTTP request is made.\n\n**A green production apply run does NOT mean a model reviewed the migrations.** Anyone reading one today would reasonably conclude otherwise. Tracked as #709 and #737.\n\n### 3. The migration history is not self-contained.\n\nReplaying all 429 migrations into an empty database **applies 363 and fails 66**, because this repo was adopted on top of an already-populated database. `public.assets`, the legacy popdam tables and the `dflow.*` mirrors exist in preview and production with no migration here creating them.\n\nA CI bootstrap now closes most of this (PR #759): quarantined contract files went **26 to 11**, passing tests **14 to 29**, replay failures **66 to 10**. It lives at `supabase/ci-bootstrap/` and is deliberately **not** a migration — a file at the front of an applied sequence cannot re-run, and a back-dated version is what Guard B exists to stop.\n\n### 4. Freeze merges before every production apply.\n\nThe production apply is pinned to an exact `origin/main` SHA. On 2026-08-11 that pin refused **two separately approved runs**, each because PRs merged between staging and the owner's click. Nothing was written either time — the guard worked — but two approvals were wasted and the third only landed under a deliberate merge freeze.\n\n**Make the freeze standard practice**, not an improvisation.\n\n## Why this is filed rather than done\n\n`AGENTS.md` is single-writer by rule and no agent owned it this session. Whoever picks this up takes that ownership first.\n\nFull briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T1516Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-fourteen-agent-session.md`. Filed by orchestrator session d152a272, marker #739.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T22:05:20Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T15:25:44Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":772,"title":"HANDOVER: four standing facts AGENTS.md does not say, and each has already misled a session","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:52:08Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/772"},
{"body":"## Purpose\n\nRun a current, timed rehearsal before anyone schedules the full Cloud SQL to Supabase move in #770. Every earlier duration was an estimate. The last database measurements were taken on 2026-08-11 and are stale until refreshed.\n\nThis issue remains separate from #770 because the output is a measured rehearsal report, not the production migration itself. #770 depends on this issue, not the other way around.\n\n## Current references to read first\n\n- #770, the umbrella Cloud SQL to Supabase migration decision\n- `docs/business-rules/licensing-master-data.md`\n- `plan_licensing_master_data_implementation.md`\n- `docs/plan_coldlion-landing-phases-2-6.md`\n- #1090, licensing implementation\n- #1184, ColdLion landing layer\n\nThe rehearsal must not change the settled direction:\n\n- ColdLion owns official Licensor names.\n- Scrapes own Property truth inside their authorized coverage.\n- ColdLion-only Property data under Licensors with no scrape data is canonical.\n- ColdLion owns Property Active/Inactive.\n- ColdLion feeds land in dedicated `coldlion.*` tables.\n- DesignFlow licensing data has no authority.\n\n## Step 0: refresh the baseline\n\nBefore timing anything, remeasure the current Cloud SQL and Supabase catalogs. Do not reuse the August 11 table count, size, index, constraint, sequence, or row-count figures as current facts. Record the exact source and destination and publish only counts, names, types, sizes, constraints, and definitions permitted by the production read rules.\n\nUpdate the rehearsal table list from that fresh inventory. Preserve the critical `AuditLog` rule: its delta cutoff uses `id`, never `actionDate`.\n\n## Rehearsal target and safety\n\nTarget preview Supabase project: `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`.\n\nUse a newly dated scratch schema, not the old `zz_rehearsal_cutover_20260811` name. The run must:\n\n- prove the target is preview and hard-stop otherwise;\n- use the exclusive preview lane and announce the heavy run;\n- create everything inside the one scratch schema;\n- set bounded lock, statement, and idle-transaction timeouts;\n- check free storage before loading;\n- leave production and shared infrastructure read-only;\n- preserve timings before teardown;\n- remove the scratch schema only after evidence is saved and its exact recoverability path is recorded.\n\n## Timed phases\n\n1. Create the scratch schema and timing table.\n2. Time representative heap loads using the freshly measured large-table list.\n3. Time index creation.\n4. Time primary keys, unique constraints, and foreign-key validation. Include the `productUserAssignment (item, role)` unique constraint unless the refreshed catalog proves it no longer applies.\n5. Time sequence maxima and sequence repair preparation.\n6. Time both validation choices: full ordered hashes for the bounded transactional set, and the cheaper `AuditLog` gate using count, `id` bounds, and a tail hash.\n7. Time `ANALYZE` on the scratch copies.\n8. Save all timings and failures.\n9. Tear down the exact scratch schema and prove it is gone.\n\n## Separate authorization boundary\n\nAn internal preview copy does not measure Cloud SQL network export and Supabase restore time. A direct `pg_dump` or table-data read from production Cloud SQL is outside the standing catalog-only permission and requires its own explicit approval. Do not silently add it to this rehearsal.\n\n## Required output\n\nUpdate #770 with:\n\n- refreshed database measurements;\n- every phase's actual time;\n- measured storage use;\n- the recommended validation gate;\n- the credible cutover window, including any still-unmeasured term;\n- whether the one-window plan remains viable;\n- any blocker, especially duplicate `(item, role)` pairs or a timeout.\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 450\ndepends_on:\nobjects:\n```\n","closedAt":"2026-09-05T00:31:19Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T15:24:28Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":771,"title":"Run timed Cloud SQL to Supabase rehearsal before scheduling #770","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:41:58Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/771"},
{"body":"## The question, in one line\r\n\r\n**Was the ruling cited everywhere as \"R5\" ever actually made?**\r\n\r\n## What R5 is claimed to say\r\n\r\nThat the shared Supabase `core.*` tables become the single source of truth for every application, and DesignFlow's private `dflow.*` copies get retired, table by table.\r\n\r\n## The problem\r\n\r\n**It exists in no file, no commit and no issue.** Searched on 2026-08-11 across the full working tree and the **full history** (`git log --all -S\"R5\" --pickaxe-all`), plus the retired `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` at three revisions. Six citations, zero sources.\r\n\r\nEvery other hit is unrelated: a review finding numbered R5, a smoke test named R5, a rejected option R5, and a ColdLion merch-group code `R5` (\"Specialty Fabric w Attachment\").\r\n\r\n**The two earliest citations were written FOUR MINUTES APART on 2026-08-03.** Everything since may descend from one afternoon.\r\n\r\n## What rests on it\r\n\r\nFour planning documents build their whole strategy on it. GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3 both independently refused to execute any plan resting on it until it exists in writing.\r\n\r\n## The reconstruction\r\n\r\n`docs/owner-ruling-r5-core-is-source-of-truth.md` (PR #743, merged) states it clause by clause, each tagged **[QUOTED]** or **[INFERRED]**, with file:line anchors. The \"table by table\" clause is **[INFERRED]** — no citation contains the phrase. The document is marked UNCONFIRMED and must not be cited as owner authority until it is confirmed.\r\n\r\n## The label is ambiguous and should be retired\r\n\r\n`AGENTS.md` §6.10 records five numbered owner rulings from 2026-08-06 and **its \"ruling 5\" is a completely different ruling** (\"STOP THE DATA LOSS FIRST\", `AGENTS.md:1603`). A third numbering exists at `AGENTS.md:1357`. **Three schemes, one label.** Whatever is decided, replace `R5` with a name — the reconstruction proposes \"the core-is-canonical ruling\".\r\n\r\n## What a \"no\" would mean\r\n\r\nFour plans are built on something never said, and need rewriting before anyone acts on them. That is a fine answer and worth having.\r\n\r\nFull briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T1516Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-fourteen-agent-session.md`. Filed by orchestrator session d152a272, marker #739.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T22:36:57Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T15:24:26Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## The question\r\n\r\n**Is DesignFlow already pointing at Supabase, in whole or in part?**\r\n\r\nAn application is definitely connected to Supabase `dflow` and writing to it right now (#763). It is recognisably DesignFlow's Node/Sequelize backend. **Nobody can tell whether it is production, the sandbox, or something else.**\r\n\r\n## Why it is the first question, not a detail\r\n\r\n- **If production is already partly there, this is not a migration project.** It is a half-finished one that nobody documented, and the correct next step is finding out what state it is in, not planning a cutover.\r\n- If it is the sandbox, the cutover plan stands but must not overwrite the sandbox's live rows.\r\n- Either way, `dflow` is the destination named in every migration plan, and something is already writing to it.\r\n\r\n## What is proven and what is not\r\n\r\n**Proven:** a Sequelize application is connected, writing to 28 tables, and running DDL on every boot. **Not proven:** which deployment. `pg_stat_statements` gives the queries, not the client identity.\r\n\r\n## How to answer it\r\n\r\nWhich database does the live DesignFlow at its production URL talk to — Google Cloud SQL, or Supabase? Same question for the sandbox.\r\n\r\nIf that is not known offhand, the next step is reading the deployed configuration for each DesignFlow environment rather than guessing from the database side.\r\n\r\nFull briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T1516Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-fourteen-agent-session.md`. Filed by orchestrator session d152a272, marker #739.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T22:36:55Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T15:24:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## The defect\n\n**DesignFlow's application runs DDL against the shared database on every boot.**\n\n`pg_stat_statements` on production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` shows ~30 distinct statements of the shape:\n\n- `ALTER TABLE \"dflow\".<table> ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ...`\n- `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \"dflow\".ai_cache_events`\n- `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \"dflow\".app_settings`\n\neach called **90 to 140 times**.\n\n## Why this is forbidden\n\nThis is the Sequelize startup-migration pattern the shared-db rules explicitly prohibit. It means `dflow`'s structure is being changed **from application code, outside shared-db, continuously** — no branch, no PR, no preview-first, no review, and no record in the migration ledger.\n\nThe shared database serves four applications. A structural change made this way is invisible to every guard this repo has built.\n\n## What needs to happen\n\n1. Identify which deployment is doing it — see the open question on whether DesignFlow already points at Supabase.\n2. Turn the startup sync off in the application.\n3. Re-author anything it has created as proper shared-db migrations, so the ledger matches reality.\n\n## It compounds a known problem\n\nObjects created this way exist in no migration. That is part of why a from-empty replay could not reproduce the database (#754): 66 of 429 migrations failed against an empty database because the repo was adopted on top of an already-populated one and things like this keep adding to the gap.\n\nFull briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T1516Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-fourteen-agent-session.md`. Filed by orchestrator session d152a272, marker #739.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T15:56:57Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T15:24:24Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":767,"title":"DesignFlow runs ALTER/CREATE DDL against dflow on every application boot — the forbidden Sequelize startup-migration pattern","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:52:12Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/767"},
{"body":"## Two sequences will collide on the very next insert\n\nFound while verifying the Cloud SQL migration premise. **These are live bugs today and have nothing to do with any migration.**\n\n| Table | Max id | Sequence value | Effect |\n|---|---:|---:|---|\n| `dflow.LicensingTime` | **24** | **2** | next insert collides immediately |\n| `dflow.properties_and_characters` | **10,458** | **never used (starts at 1)** | next insert collides immediately |\n\nAll other 63 sequence-backed tables in `dflow` are correctly positioned (sequence = max id, next value = max+1). 85 id columns are proper `GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY`; only 16 use the older `nextval` default, and **both broken ones are in that group.**\n\n## Why it has not been noticed\n\nPresumably nothing has inserted into either table recently. It will fail the moment something does.\n\n## What to do\n\nFix forward with a `setval` in a new migration authored in shared-db, preview-first. Do not hand-run it against production. Check whether any other schema has the same `nextval`-default pattern with a stale sequence — the sweep above covered `dflow` only.\n\nRelated: the cutover plan needs 97 `setval` fixes inside its window anyway, so this may fold into that work — but these two are broken NOW and should not wait for it.\n\nFull briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T1516Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-fourteen-agent-session.md`. {"body":"## The finding\n\n**Supabase `dflow` is NOT a stale copy of DesignFlow's database. It is a LIVE database with an application connected to it right now, writing to it.** Verified read-only against production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` on 2026-08-11.\n\nEvidence:\n- **193,591 inserts into `itemAttachment`** since the stats epoch (2026-07-02 restart), 206 into `AuditLog`, 105 updates on `RFQVendor`, 88 on `users`. **28 tables show write activity.**\n- `pg_stat_statements` shows **thousands of Sequelize-shaped ORM queries** — `grid_cell_notes` 5,833 calls, `INSERT INTO \"dflow\".\"AuditLog\"` 203 calls, `UPDATE \"dflow\".\"Factory\"` 91 calls. That is DesignFlow's Node backend.\n- Fresh rows: `sample_movement` 2026-08-10, `itemHeader` 2026-08-07, `AuditLog` 2026-08-07.\n- **No `pg_cron` job touches `dflow`** — all 9 cron jobs work on `public.*`. The writer is an application.\n\n## Why this matters\n\n**Every Cloud SQL migration plan written before 2026-08-11 assumed `dflow` was a dormant copy and involved loading Cloud SQL data into or over it.** All three plans considered this session — the copy-first plan, GLM 5.2's and Kimi K3's — would have **destroyed live data**.\n\n## The data is divergent, not stale\n\n`itemAttachment`: **214,058 rows on Supabase against ~20,384 on Cloud SQL — ten times.** That is a different dataset, not drift. The whole `sample_*` family is **0 bytes on Cloud SQL** and populated on Supabase.\n\n## Supabase-native — must NEVER be clobbered\n\nPer owner ruling #707, confirmed present and in use today. 5 tables (`sample_import_job`, `sample_import_row`, `sample_movement`, `sample_shipment_line`, `sample_stop_closeout`), 5 views, 4 functions, 3 triggers, 4 columns. `sample_movement` was written **yesterday**.\n\nKimi K3's proposed \"rename a fresh import over `dflow`\" would have quarantined all of it.\n\n## Also corrected\n\n**The three-object gap direction was BACKWARDS.** All three objects (`productUserAssignment_item_role_key`, `idx_dflow_rfqitem_style_number_normalized`, `RFQVendor_item_vendor_summary_idx`) **already exist on Supabase and are missing on Cloud SQL**. GLM built its step 1 on the opposite assumption.\n\nFull briefing: HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T1516Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-fourteen-agent-session.md (PR pending at handover). Filed by orchestrator session d152a272, marker #739.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T18:48:28Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T15:21:47Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## The outcome needed\n\nThe NBCU Creative Asset Factory landing schema is missing the **Asset-to-Franchise** relationship. NBCU calls Franchises \"IP Families\". The scrape already preserves the source values losslessly in `nbcu/assets.csv` column `ip_family_labels` and in `plm.nbcu_asset.ip_family_labels`, but nothing models those links in a relationship table.\n\nOwner-authored specification, issued 2026-08-11, relayed verbatim to the sub-agent.\n\n## Scope\n\nAdd `plm.nbcu_asset_ip_family` and replace `plm.finalize_nbcu_capture(uuid)` in ONE new additive migration. The NBCU table family goes from 16 to 17.\n\n**Nothing is loaded. No contract data is added. No canonical POP data is changed. Production remains unchanged.**\n\nExplicitly out of scope: contract terms, dates, territories, sales channels, account limits, approval rules, licence restrictions not from portal asset metadata, and canonical taxonomy changes.\n\n## The rule that protects the data\n\nOne row means: *the NBCU asset metadata explicitly listed this IP Family for this asset.* Links come only from the exact values in `assets.csv.ip_family_labels` — never from the search scope, folder paths, file names, a related Property, a Character namespace, label similarity, another asset, or any assumption about which titles belong to a Franchise. An empty array means zero links. A missing or ambiguous label must REJECT finalization, never be silently discarded.\n\nThe JSON array stays. The new table adds relationship integrity; it does not replace lossless source preservation.\n\n## Orchestrator allocations\n\n- Migration version **20260811070000**, allocated by the orchestrator. The agent must not choose its own.\n- Claim issue filed separately.\n- Collision gate run against 6 in-flight items: no overlap.\n\nDispatched as workstream \"NBCU asset-to-franchise relationship\" by orchestrator session d152a272 (marker #739).\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T15:11:04Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T13:38:39Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":757,"title":"WORKSTREAM: NBCU landing — add the missing Asset-to-Franchise (IP Family) relationship","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:52:25Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/757"},
{"body":"## The finding\n\nThe first-ever CI execution of `supabase/tests/` (PR #741, issue #731) established something nobody had measured: **replaying all 429 migrations into an empty database applies 363 and FAILS 66.**\n\n**This repository's migration history is not self-contained.** It was adopted on top of an already-populated database. So `public.assets`, the legacy popdam tables and the `dflow.*` mirrors exist in preview and production without any migration in this repo creating them.\n\n## What that costs today\n\n26 of the 40 contract test files are quarantined — they execute, their output is printed and uploaded as an artifact, and the list appears in the job summary every run, but they cannot pass:\n\n- **13 files** depend on objects no migration here creates (`dam_order_list_contract`, the `dflow.sample` tests, `core_licensor_alias_contracts`, and others).\n- **11 files** need seeded reference data an empty database cannot have — the `db_data_admin_*` suite needs active authenticated profiles.\n- **2 files** assert a property of a specific deployed environment by design (`taxonomy_baseline_pin_and_breaker_environment_contracts`, `owner_ruling_coco_is_a_disney_license_contracts`).\n\nSo the CI lane proves **the subset of the contract provable from the repository alone**. That is a real and worthwhile guarantee, and it is not the whole contract. Anyone reading a green run as \"the contracts hold\" is reading it wrong.\n\n## What would fix it\n\nTwo artifacts that do not exist:\n\n1. **A captured pre-adoption baseline migration** — the schema as it stood when this repo adopted the database, so a from-empty replay reaches the same starting point production did.\n2. **A test-fixture seed** — the reference data the `db_data_admin_*` suite and its siblings need, synthetic, with no licensed or personal rows.\n\nThe 2 environment-asserting files may never belong in a from-empty lane at all; that is a judgement to make when the other 24 are addressed.\n\n## Why this is worth doing\n\nEvery promotion decision in this repo currently rests on contract tests, and two thirds of them cannot run outside a populated database. That gap is invisible unless someone reads the quarantine list. Closing it turns the promotion checks from partly-enforced into enforced.\n\nNot blocking anything today. Filed by orchestrator session d152a272 (marker #739) from the #741 result.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T15:05:01Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T13:29:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":754,"title":"The migration history is not self-contained: a from-empty replay fails 66 of 429, quarantining 26 contract tests","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:52:28Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/754"},

{"body":"## The outcome needed\r\n\r\nExecute `IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN-dcp-vault-full-schema-redesign.md` (49 KB, written 2026-08-10, living in the PRIVATE repo `licensor-source-data-disney/disney-dcpvault/`). Albert asked on 2026-08-11 for this to become a tracked workstream. Until now the plan existed in a private repo with no issue and no agent — nothing in shared-db pointed at it.\r\n\r\n## Why this is separate from #665\r\n\r\n#665 is the owner-level instruction (\"stop keeping this in a repo, write it to Supabase\") and still carries `needs-albert`. THIS issue is the engineering execution of the redesign plan that followed it.\r\n\r\n## What already exists, and what it means\r\n\r\nThe DCP Vault landing schema was BUILT and MERGED (PR #726, claim #725 closed):\r\n- `20260810190000_dcp_vault_source_landing.sql` — 9 `plm.dcp_*` tables, 5 functions, 9 triggers, RLS, PG17 revokes\r\n- `20260810190100_dcp_vault_chunked_loader.sql` — `plm.dcp_chunk_ledger` plus 8 SECURITY DEFINER functions\r\n\r\n**Both are UNAPPLIED, and critically they belong to NO batch in the nine-batch promotion plan.** Completing B2 through B9 will NOT promote them. That is a real gap, first flagged in this session's triage (contradiction C3), and it needs resolving as part of this workstream.\r\n\r\n## Constraints carried forward from the merged work — do not re-litigate\r\n\r\n1. `plm.dcp_*`, NOT the design's `ingest.portal_*`.\r\n2. `api.*` views deliberately omitted; no application reads this data yet.\r\n3. The frozen row-hash specification is a **ONE-WAY DOOR** — once ~155,900 rows are hashed it cannot change without a full re-capture. Treat any redesign touching it with extreme care and say so explicitly.\r\n4. Property links and character links are **two independent sets per asset and must NEVER be joined**. Doing so fabricates relationships the licensor never asserted.\r\n5. The asset path is the unique key. File name is NOT unique. Style-guide source id is nullable text in two formats; a name must never be used as an id.\r\n6. Re-scrapes mark vanished rows gone; never hard-delete.\r\n\r\n## Outstanding and must not be skipped\r\n\r\n`supabase/tests/dcp_vault_landing_contracts.sql` has **NEVER been executed**. CI does not run `supabase/tests/` (#695, being fixed in PR #741). Green checks on PR #726 are not evidence that contract test passed.\r\n\r\n## Confidentiality\r\n\r\nThe plan and the source repo contain real licensor names and licensed rows. Nothing from them may reach this public repo, a GitHub issue, PR text, a test fixture, a log, a commit message, or an outside AI service. Counts and structure only.\r\n\r\nDispatched as workstream \"DCP Vault schema redesign\" by orchestrator session d152a272 (marker #739).\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-30T11:10:48Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T13:08:18Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Filed by orchestrator f3fbdd0a (marker #714) at handover, 2026-08-11. Found while fixing #709; deliberately left out of PR #715 as out of scope.\n\n`scripts/production_apply_model_review.py:92-101` makes a `urllib.request` POST with **no `User-Agent` header**, exactly like the bug that froze the production promotion for a day.\n\n## Why it is not failing today\n\nThat script targets `api.anthropic.com`. The #709 failure was **Cloudflare error 1010** in front of `api.supabase.com`, which bans the default `Python-urllib/3.x` browser signature at the edge before the origin ever sees the request. Anthropic's endpoint does not apply that rule, so the same defective code works.\n\nIt is the same latent bug class, one host away from firing. If Anthropic ever fronts that endpoint with a similar rule, this script starts returning 403 with no explanation.\n\n## The second half, which matters more\n\n`production_catalog_verification.py` had a companion defect: it printed only `str(exc)` and never read `HTTPError.read()`, so the Cloudflare response body was invisible in CI logs. That is why the real cause took a day to find — the logs said \"403 Forbidden\" and nothing else.\n\nCheck whether `production_apply_model_review.py` has the same blindness. If it does, fix it in the same change: include the status code and the response body (decoded defensively, so a read failure cannot mask the original error) in whatever it raises or prints.\n\n## What to do\n\n1. Send an explicit, descriptive `User-Agent` on every outgoing request the file makes.\n2. Make its HTTP errors truthful — status code plus response body.\n3. Unit test asserting the constructed request carries a non-default, non-empty `User-Agent`. Assert on the request object; do **not** make a live network call in the test.\n4. Sweep `scripts/` and `.github/` for any other `urllib` caller with no `User-Agent`. As of 2026-08-10 these two were the only ones, but that was a point-in-time check.\n\n**Do not weaken any hard-fail behaviour while doing this.** The precedent from #715: making a failure more *informative* is right; making it more *forgiving* is not.\n\nReference implementation: `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py` as merged in PR #715 (`6578935`) — `USER_AGENT` constant, `build_query_request()` split out so tests can inspect headers without a network call, and `read_error_body()` with a defensive decode.\n\nFull context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T0118Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-709-unblocked-disney-built.md` section 4, the #709 implementation block.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T01:01:06Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T01:26:36Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":737,"title":"production_apply_model_review.py has the same UA-less urllib POST that caused #709","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:52:31Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/737"},
{"body":"Filed by orchestrator f3fbdd0a (marker #714) at handover, 2026-08-11. A single index of everything currently waiting on an Albert decision, so the next orchestrator does not have to reconstruct it from thirteen issues.\n\n**This issue is an INDEX. It duplicates no detail.** Each item points at the issue that owns it. Close this one when the list is empty or superseded; do not answer decisions here.\n\n## Raised this session\n\n1. **#732 — NBCU amendment paperwork.** Scarface, Minions 3 and The Mummy Franchise rest on Albert's verbal statement alone, and are headed into tables designed around source-pinned immutability with no correction path.\n2. **#732 — the `rights_scope` classification** for all 58 NBCU Properties. A proposal exists; it is not a decision.\n3. **#732 — \"Lamp Chop\".** The contract spells entry 32 that way and the spec demands exact source text.\n4. **#732 — two restrictions with no contract basis** (An American Werewolf in London; Field of Dreams). Do not load them until the source is established.\n\n## Raised earlier, still unanswered — from #711\n\n5. **D2** — how long may a resting point persist between batches.\n6. **D5** — DesignFlow non-production drift: asset or hazard.\n7. **D6** — is `20260810170000`'s read-widening still wanted? It opens the item catalogue to every logged-in account and it rides **inside atomic batch B9**, so it ships with the licensors or not at all. Reversible by a later migration, but the data is visible in the meantime.\n\nD1, D3, D7 and #696 were answered on 2026-08-10 and are done.\n\n## Answered this session, recorded so nobody re-asks\n\n- **D7** (#711) — \"assign an ai agent to do the checks\". Built as PR #719, merged `0a5bf04`.\n- **#705** — \"ignore the 'read only is not read only' issue\", then, on an explicit follow-up, \"yes, use it to read production\". Recorded as `AGENTS.md` §0.1-A.1 (PR #723, merged `f3a2d7d`). Read-only and catalog-only; it authorises a read and nothing more.\n- **NBCU licensing** — \"assume if they made it available for us to download, we're licensed for it\". This voided a 7,071-asset exposure analysis. See #733.\n\n## Standing, inherited, not touched by me\n\n#675, #676, #643, #644, #618, #515, #516, #521, #531, #539, #541, #551, #582, #665.\n\nNote **#675 is now largely superseded by #732** — the \"75 vs 57\" question is answered (it was a grain mismatch, and the contract says 58), but its underlying counting-rule decision now lives in #732.\n\n## Standing ruling — do NOT re-ask\n\n**ColdLion key rotation is WITHDRAWN** (`HANDOFF.md:32-51`).\n\nFull context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T0118Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-709-unblocked-disney-built.md` sections 5 and 7.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-14T15:37:06Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T01:25:59Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":736,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] index of every open owner decision as of 2026-08-11","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:52:34Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/736"},
{"body":"Filed by orchestrator f3fbdd0a (marker #714) at handover, 2026-08-11. **Read this before touching PR #728.**\n\nAt 01:17Z, one minute before I began writing my handover, **PR #728** appeared in this repo:\n\n- **Title:** `docs(AGENTS): read-only inspection of the shared database is allowed from every app repo`\n- **Branch:** `claude/global-ai-database-rules-44090f`\n- **Worktree:** `C:/repos/shared-db-worktrees/global-ai-database-rules-44090f` — note this is **outside** `.claude/worktrees/`, which is why it does not appear in the usual worktree sweep alongside the others.\n- **Files:** `AGENTS.md` only\n- **State when I read it (01:18Z):** open, `BEHIND` main\n\n**I did not review it, did not merge it, and did not touch its branch or worktree.** It is not my work. The handover standard says a docs-only PR is merged by the session that wrote it, and that session appeared to still be running.\n\n## Why this needs care rather than a quick merge\n\n**#728 edits `AGENTS.md`. So did my PR #723**, merged this session as `f3a2d7d`, which added §0.1-A.1 — the bounded Cloud SQL read-gate exception carrying Albert's ruling.\n\n**#728 was cut BEHIND main**, so it may not contain §0.1-A.1 at all. Whoever merges it must confirm it does not clobber, contradict or silently revert that section. Branch protection has `strict` = true (require branches up to date before merging), which should force a rebase and surface the conflict — but confirm rather than assume.\n\nThere is a second-order risk worth naming. §0.1-A.1 is a **bounded** exception: it waives the read-only proof for one named credential on one named schema, and its closure rule explicitly keeps every other §0.1-A condition binding, including catalog-only SELECTs and no row contents. A PR whose whole subject is \"read-only inspection is allowed from every app repo\" is adjacent to that closure rule. If the two texts are merged carelessly, the result could read as a general permission where §0.1-A.1 deliberately grants a narrow one. **Read both texts together before merging.**\n\n## What the next orchestrator should do\n\n1. Claim the marker first. #714 is closed, so the board should be clear.\n2. Establish whether that session is still alive. If it is, coordinate and leave the PR alone — it belongs to whoever opened it.\n3. If it is dead, ingest #728 as a handover: verify its claims against the live repo (`git fetch --all`, `gh pr list`, `git worktree list`, the real migration maximum), rebase it onto current main, read it alongside §0.1-A.1, and only then merge.\n\n## The wider lesson, worth recording\n\nTwo sessions edited `AGENTS.md` on the same day without either knowing about the other. The single-writer rule for `AGENTS.md` did not catch it, because that session was never in my register — it was started outside the orchestrator and works in a worktree directory the standard sweep does not cover.\n\nThe orchestrator marker only protects against a second **orchestrator**. It does nothing about an ordinary session doing shared-db work directly. That gap is real and is not currently closed by anything mechanical.\n\nFull context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T0118Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-709-unblocked-disney-built.md` section 2.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T01:28:26Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T01:25:35Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":735,"title":"HANDOVER: PR #728 is another live session's work on AGENTS.md — do not merge blind","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:52:38Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/735"},
{"body":"Filed by orchestrator f3fbdd0a (marker #714) at handover, 2026-08-11.\r\n\r\nTwo documents give **opposite first instructions** for the Cloud SQL to Supabase move, and one of them does not exist as a file.\r\n\r\n**Doc A - `SUPABASE-MIGRATION.md`** in `popcre/designflow-backend` (347 lines, last touched 2026-07-10, commit `225bab92`). Self-declared \"canonical, workspace-wide operating contract\" for all six DesignFlow repos. Its Migration Order says: restore the Cloud SQL data into a Supabase sandbox, validate, then point each service at it. `dflow.*` is preserved; Sequelize models and schema stay unchanged.\r\n\r\n**Doc B - \"R5\"**, cited as an owner ruling in at least six places, says the opposite: `core.*` in Supabase becomes the source of truth for every application and the `dflow.*` tables get **retired**, table by table.\r\n\r\n**R5 exists in no file in this repo.** It survives only as second-hand quotes:\r\n- `docs/cloudsql-first-migration-candidate-20260803.md:53`\r\n- `docs/age-group-cloudsql-migration-plan-20260804.md:52-53`\r\n- `docs/licensor-property-cloudsql-cutover-plan-20260806.md:530`\r\n- `docs/dflow-parent-logic-and-curation-home-20260803.md:299,311`\r\n\r\nYou cannot reconcile against a quote. Any agent that reads the wrong document first does the wrong thing, and the two prescribe opposite opening moves: copy the whole database, versus move one list at a time and drop the copy.\r\n\r\n## Why this is now worth doing, when it was not before\r\n\r\nIt was previously blocked behind a measurement nobody had taken. **That measurement now exists.** PR #722 (merged `2e3ae23`) captured the DesignFlow production schema for the first time and the answer is much smaller than anyone assumed: **the real divergence is 3 objects**, not 18 migrations. One unique constraint (`productUserAssignment_item_role_key`) and two indexes on `RFQItem` and `RFQVendor`. Zero Cloud SQL-only tables. Every Supabase-only object is Sample Tracking, which #707 already ruled deliberate.\r\n\r\nA three-object divergence makes this a small, boring cutover rather than a large one - which is exactly the information needed to choose between the two shapes.\r\n\r\n## What this needs\r\n\r\n1. **Write R5 down** as a real document in this repo, e.g. `docs/owner-ruling-r5-core-is-source-of-truth.md`, sourced from Albert rather than from the quotes.\r\n2. **Reconcile it against Doc A.** Note the scope limit: `SUPABASE-MIGRATION.md` lives in a `popcre` org repo, so this means raising a supersession PR against `develop` there, never self-merged. An agent confined to `u2giants/shared-db` cannot edit it.\r\n3. Record which document wins, and add dated supersession pointers rather than rewriting either. The originals are the audit trail.\r\n\r\n## Related, from the same capture\r\n\r\n- **#696 is bigger than written.** The office/language columns are absent from Cloud SQL AND from Supabase production, because `20260810160000` is merged but unapplied everywhere.\r\n- **The age-group-first plan rests on a false premise.** `art_piece.age_group_id` has an enforced FK pointing at `merchGroup`, not `age_group`.\r\n- **Trap for the cutover:** Supabase production also has a schema named `designflow`, distinct from Cloud SQL's. Cloud SQL is `designflow`; Supabase DesignFlow lives in `dflow`; Supabase's own `designflow` is a decoy. Do not \"correct\" either name to the other.\r\n\r\nFull context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T0118Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-709-unblocked-disney-built.md` section 4, Cloud SQL blocks.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-18T14:59:49Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T01:25:34Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":734,"title":"HANDOVER: write R5 down and reconcile it against SUPABASE-MIGRATION.md — the capture now makes this decidable","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:42:18Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/734"},
{"body":"Filed by orchestrator f3fbdd0a (marker #714) at handover, 2026-08-11. **Not a shared-db change — recorded here because it gates the NBCU load into `plm.nbcu_*`.**\r\n\r\nThose tables are insert-only and immutable by design, so whatever gets loaded cannot be removed. Two capture problems must be settled first. Both live in the private scrape repo `u2giants/licensor-source-data`, under `nbcu/scripts/`.\r\n\r\n## 1. The reported exclusion count is a mislabelled silent failure\r\n\r\n`nbcu/capture-summary.json` reports `excluded_unlicensed_assets: 107`. That number does not mean what it says.\r\n\r\n`build-outputs.mjs:121-128` compares the count of parse FAILURES to a number in `raw/detail-clean-summary.json`, and when the two happen to be equal it relabels the failures as licence EXCLUSIONS and then **empties `failures.csv`** (now 54 bytes, header only). It infers cause from a coincidence of counts, then prints success.\r\n\r\nEstablished by reading `raw/details/*.ndjson` directly: **there were zero fetch failures.** All 108,026 detail records are `status: 200` with non-empty metadata. The 107 were **deliberate denylist removals** - 105 Casper files and 2 Minions files, both licensed Properties. Note the record schema has no `error` field at all, so `build-outputs.mjs:85`'s `r?.error` could never have populated anything even if a failure had existed.\r\n\r\nUnder Albert's ruling (\"assume if they made it available for us to download, we're licensed for it\"), that four-label denylist should not exist. Recovery: delete the `denied` Set and its guard in `clean-detail-checkpoints.mjs`, **delete `nbcu/raw/detail-clean-summary.json` first** (see item 2), re-fetch the 107 from the existing `asset-index.csv` rows, re-run `build-outputs.mjs`. Expect 108,026 to become 108,133 and exclusions to become 0. A recovery prompt with exact paths and detail-page forms has been handed to Albert for the scrape agent.\r\n\r\n## 2. Three silent drop points, none of which records a reason\r\n\r\nThis is the real defect and it matters more than the 107.\r\n\r\n- `clean-detail-checkpoints.mjs:19-20` - drops every non-200, empty-metadata or login-interstitial record with **no counter, no log, no output file**. It fired zero times this run, provable only by arithmetic luck. A single 403 would have vanished without trace, and the arithmetic that made the diagnosis above possible would have silently broken.\r\n- `clean-detail-checkpoints.mjs:32` - `Math.max(excluded, previous.excluded_unlicensed_assets ?? 0)`. The stored exclusion count can only ratchet **up**. **This will actively sabotage the recovery** unless the summary file is deleted first: it will keep reporting 107 forever.\r\n- `clean-detail-checkpoints.mjs:41-48` - `--replace` deletes the source checkpoints after filtering, and pre-clean checkpoints were never committed. This is why the question could only be answered by inference rather than by reading the record. **Unrecoverable.**\r\n\r\nAlso worth knowing: `build-outputs.mjs:38` builds `entitledPropertyLabels` and it **gates nothing** - it feeds only a cosmetic `unmatchedProperties` list. Anyone skimming that line would reasonably assume entitlement enforcement exists in this pipeline. It does not, and never did.\r\n\r\n**Minimum fix:** a single `dropped.csv` with `href, stage, reason` appended at EVERY `continue`, plus a non-zero exit when it is non-empty. The standing rule in this shop is that every fallback must alert loudly.\r\n\r\nFull context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T0118Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-709-unblocked-disney-built.md` sections 4 and 8.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: source-data\nroute: source-data-session\nreturn_to: u2giants/licensor-source-data\npriority: 450\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-20T22:54:15Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T01:24:48Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":733,"title":"HANDOVER: NBCU capture has three silent drop points and a mislabelled exclusion count","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:42:20Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/733"},
{"body":"Filed by orchestrator f3fbdd0a (marker #714) at handover, 2026-08-11. **Supersedes the \"75 vs 57\" framing of #675.**\n\nAlbert supplied the signed contract this session: Schedule \"B\" dated 2024-11-05 to the Master Merchandising License Agreement (Universal Studios Licensing LLC / Edge Home d/b/a Comicwalls, contract 201310576), plus three amendments he had missed.\n\n**The authoritative count is 58**, not 57 and not 56:\n- 55 Universal Properties in Schedule B section (b). The heading is literally \"UNIVERSAL PROPERTY\", which settles the vocabulary: they are **Properties**, not titles, and one Property may span many titles.\n- +1 Scarface (1983 live-action film only), +1 Minions 3, +1 The Mummy Franchise (four named works; **REPLACES** the entry typed at #56, not in addition to it).\n\nOrdinals become 1..58 and `right_key` becomes `rights-list:001`..`058`. The existing format check `^rights-list:[0-9]{3}$` at migration line 183 still passes. **No migration change is needed.**\n\n## NEEDS ALBERT\n\n1. **The amendment paperwork for Scarface, Minions 3 and The Mummy Franchise.** Three of the 58 currently rest on his verbal statement alone, and they are going into tables whose entire design is source-pinned immutability with an append-only capture and no correction path. Schedule B is a signed, DocuSigned instrument; these three are not in it.\n2. **The `rights_scope` classification** for all 58 (`title | franchise | all_related`). A proposal exists — 11 franchise, 10 all_related, 37 title — with reasoning for the non-obvious calls (Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town, Little Golden Books, Felix the Cat, Chucky). It is a proposal, not a decision.\n3. **\"Lamp Chop\".** The contract spells entry 32 that way. The spec requires `business_title` to be exact source text. Transcribe the typo and record an alias, or correct it?\n4. **Two restrictions with no contract basis.** \"An American Werewolf in London - restrictions apply\" and \"Field of Dreams - higher-end specialty accounts only\" appear NOWHERE in Schedule B. They may come from the Master Agreement (not seen) or from a business conversation. **Do not load either as contract restriction text until the source is established.**\n\n## Restrictions nobody had ever transcribed\n\n`plm.nbcu_right.restriction_text` and `global_rule_applied` are currently empty. The contract contains real content for both.\n\n**Global (section c):** all use is subject to Approval; no rights to any other derivative or ancillary work including sequels, prequels, spin-offs, publications, live shows or interactive games; performer name, voice or likeness needs prior Approval. **Term: 2025-01-01 to 2026-12-31.** The document is CONFIDENTIAL.\n\n**Per-Property, the ones that bind hardest:**\n- **Halloween II is \"US & Canada ONLY\"** - the only territorial limit in the contract, and it sits in the Property name itself.\n- Wicked excludes the stage play and Maguire's novel.\n- Little Golden Books is 18 enumerated storybook titles, not the imprint.\n- Felix the Cat excludes the Poindexter character and every motion picture, TV production, live/touring/Broadway show and virtual world.\n- Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town is limited to an enumerated character list and excludes Fred Astaire's name, voice and likeness.\n- Curious George (TV) excludes character images and audio clips carrying likeness or voice, and excludes the classic illustrated book property entirely.\n- Apollo 13 and Fast & Furious put third-party clearance on the licensee, expressly including automobile names and logos.\n- Casper (Harvey) and Hot Stuff are limited to the original Harvey comic depiction.\n\n**Schema gap worth a deliberate decision:** `plm.nbcu_right` has no term column and no territory column. The 2026-12-31 expiry and the Halloween II territory limit would have to live inside `restriction_text` as free text, making them unqueryable. That is a design choice, not a default.\n\n## Also required before any load\n\n`nbcu/SUPABASE-IMPORT-SPEC.md:83` currently reads \"57 documented title lines\" and names `LICENSED_SCOPE.md` as the source. Both wrong. It must name the contract as source of record, state 58 Properties (55 plus 3 amendments), demote `LICENSED_SCOPE.md` to a superseded working note, and say \"Property\" rather than \"title\" throughout sections 5 and 6.2.\n\nThe contract and the amendment record must be committed into the **private** repo `u2giants/licensor-source-data` - the loader pins `source_commit_sha` and cannot cite a PDF on a Desktop. That creates a new commit, so the capture needs a fresh `source_commit_sha`. Nothing is loaded yet, so this costs nothing today.\n\nFull context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-11T0118Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-709-unblocked-disney-built.md` sections 4 and 7.\n\n\n\n\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: source-data\nroute: source-data-session\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\n\n\n","closedAt":"2026-08-19T12:38:12Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T01:24:47Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":732,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] NBCU is 58 Properties, not 57 — plus contract restrictions nobody transcribed","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:42:22Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/732"},
