{"body":"## Owner request\n\nAlbert explicitly authorized proceeding to make DB Data Admin live at `https://data.designflow.app` on 2026-08-10/11.\n\n## Goal\n\nLaunch the existing DB Data Admin application from `apps/db-data-admin/` at its permanent production hostname, using the approved GitHub Actions -> GHCR -> Coolify path. Do not use SSH or direct VPS edits.\n\n## Verified starting state\n\n- Canonical repo `u2giants/shared-db` main was `0a5bf04104aaa093dfc2ec05b4a636cfe301afae` when this request was filed.\n- Development `https://data-dev.designflow.app/health` returns HTTP 200.\n- Development live build SHA is `f3a2d7d6bcf6df39f445d8818650a5e775c2372f`.\n- Production `https://data.designflow.app/health` returns HTTP 503 `no available server`.\n- `.github/workflows/db-data-admin.yml` currently verifies, builds, publishes an immutable GHCR image, and deploys only the development Coolify application.\n- Production hostname ownership is locked to DB Data Admin by `docs/db-data-admin-domain-ownership.md`.\n- Production Supabase/Entra callback is already documented as registered. Reverify it.\n\n## Required work\n\n1. Re-derive current main, open PRs/claims, production migration ledger, and relevant DB Data Admin gates. Do not trust dated counts.\n2. Confirm the application can be safely launched read-only if production write/admin grants are not yet approved. Do not silently enable production write gates, merge execution, PLM writes, or grant users beyond Albert's explicit authorization.\n3. Create or verify the production Coolify runtime for `data.designflow.app`, with Coolify owning domain, runtime configuration, health check, restart behavior, and immutable image target.\n4. Add the repository-driven production deployment path to `.github/workflows/db-data-admin.yml`. It must depend on verification and image publication and deploy the exact `sha-<commit>` image through Coolify.\n5. Update `docs/db-data-admin-deployment.md` with production identifiers, runtime settings ownership, trigger, and rollback.\n6. Run domain ownership, lint, unit, build, browser, and container checks.\n7. Use the shared-db branch + PR workflow, obtain all required checks, and merge according to repo rules.\n8. Deploy through GitHub Actions and Coolify only.\n9. Verify production `/health`, TLS, HTML `build-sha`, Microsoft sign-in routing, authorized/denied behavior, and rollback target. Record exact commit, workflow run, image tag, Coolify deployment, and live evidence.\n\n## Safety boundaries\n\n- No direct production database mutation outside the canonical promotion lane.\n- No enabling write/admin/PLM gates without their existing approvals and evidence.\n- No SSH, direct Docker, or manual VPS deployment.\n- Runtime secrets stay in Coolify or 1Password vault `vibe_coding`; never print or commit values.\n- Serialize all 1Password reads.\n- Preserve other active shared-db workstreams and use an isolated worktree.\n\n## Definition of done\n\n`https://data.designflow.app/health` returns HTTP 200, TLS is valid, live HTML reports the merged production commit, sign-in routing works, access denial is proven for an unapproved user, and the deployment is traceable through GitHub Actions, GHCR, and Coolify with a documented immutable rollback image.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T17:23:32Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T01:18:04Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. The NOT CHECKED classes (table, column, grant, index, schema) are what this touches, so the clear result rests on there being zero other migration writers at dispatch time.\n\nORCHESTRATOR RULING recorded here so it is not re-litigated: the design specified `ingest.portal_*` with licensor-generic names. Renamed to `plm.dcp_*`. Three reasons: (1) every prior licensor lands in `plm.<prefix>_*`; (2) `ingest` still carries the #649 default-privilege hole — `pg_default_acl` for `ingest` reads `{service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres}`, so tables created there are born with TRUNCATE, and TRUNCATE does not fire row triggers, which would void every immutability guarantee in the design; `20260810180000` narrowed `plm` only; (3) generic names in a shared schema squat the namespace for the next licensor, contradicting #665's own per-licensor direction.\n\nClose this issue when the work merges or is abandoned.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T01:18:19Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T00:22:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvGcdSA","name":"db-claim","description":"An agent is dispatched and holds these DB objects. {"body":"## Outcome needed\n\nIdentify the existing Supabase schema and tables intended to receive Paramount Creative Library source data, then perform a read-only fit review against the Paramount source contract.\n\n## Required source shape\n\nThe source layer must preserve exact Paramount identities and metadata for:\n- Brands\n- Franchises\n- Properties\n- Collections, which map to POP Style Guides\n- Characters\n- Assets\n- Capture runs, scope, pagination progress, reconciliation counts, and failures\n\nSource IDs must remain separate from POP canonical IDs. Known source identities include 40-character text asset IDs and numeric IDs stored as text for Properties, Collections, Characters, and Franchises.\n\nThe model must support explicit many-to-many links:\n- Franchise to Property\n- Property to Collection\n- Property to Character\n- Asset to Property\n- Asset to Collection\n- Asset to Character\n- Asset to Brand and other metadata facets\n\nDirect Property-to-Character and Property-to-Collection links come from full asset cascading metadata. Missing or malformed links must be stored as source anomalies and must not be inferred.\n\n## Review questions\n\n1. Which current schema and tables are intended for Paramount source data?\n2. Does the structure support every entity, source ID, exact label, metadata field, capture fact, anomaly, and relationship above?\n3. Are keys and uniqueness rules based on licensor plus source ID rather than display name?\n4. Can repeated, idempotent scrape loads preserve history and reconcile counts without duplicating records?\n5. What gaps or unsafe assumptions exist?\n6. If changes are needed, propose them in shared-db using the normal preview-first branch and PR flow. Do not mutate Supabase as part of the review.\n\n## Data boundary\n\nDo not copy licensed Paramount rows into this public issue. Inspect source shape and schema only.","closedAt":"2026-08-13T00:18:22Z","createdAt":"2026-08-11T00:18:47Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Found by the post-batch application verification harness (PR #719) on its first live read-only run against production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, 2026-08-10. Filed by orchestrator f3fbdd0a (marker #714).\n\n`docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` is the document the post-batch checks are derived from. Three of its claims no longer match reality. That matters more than the individual defects: the contract is now the input to an automated check that runs after every production batch, so a wrong claim in it becomes a wrong assertion in the harness, in both directions — a false alarm, or worse, a green light.\n\n**1. PopDAM's size picker is ALREADY running on its hardcoded fallback, silently.**\n`core.product_size` does not exist on production. `StylesPage.tsx` catches the resulting error and falls back to a hardcoded list, so the app looks fine and nobody is told. This is live right now, not a future risk. It is precisely the silent-failure shape the contract's own section 3.2 warns about, and it violates the standing rule that every fallback must alert loudly. The missing table is expected — it arrives with a queued migration — but the swallowed error is a defect regardless of when the table lands.\n\n**2. `core.product_material` has no reader at all.** The contract names it as read by an application. Against `origin/main`, nothing reads it. Either the reader was removed and the contract is stale, or the reader lives somewhere that was not searched.\n\n**3. `dam_character_catalog` is read from `public`, not `api`.** The contract says `api`. The code says `public`. One of them is wrong, and the harness asserts on whichever it is told.\n\n**What this issue needs.**\n1. Re-derive each of the three claims from code and from a live catalog read. Do not trust the contract, and do not trust this issue either — it is a report, not a fact.\n2. Correct `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` for whichever claims are genuinely stale, and update the harness assertions in `scripts/post_batch_app_verification.py` in the same change so the two cannot drift apart again.\n3. For item 1, fix the swallowed error in PopDAM (different repo) so the fallback alerts loudly instead of pretending to work. That is app-side and needs its own dispatch.\n4. Consider whether anything mechanically checks contract-versus-code drift. Today nothing does, which is how three claims went stale unnoticed. Related: #654 records the same class of gap for skills-versus-rulebook drift.\n\nBlocked on nothing. {"body":"Found by the post-batch application verification harness (PR #719) on its first live read-only run against production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, 2026-08-10. Filed by orchestrator f3fbdd0a (marker #714).\r\n\r\n**The defect.** The `authenticated` role holds SELECT and nothing else on these five tables:\r\n\r\n- `pim.checklist_item`\r\n- `pim.product_assignee`\r\n- `pim.product_sample`\r\n- `pim.product_submission`\r\n- `pim.revision_request`\r\n\r\nPopPIM's application code inserts, updates and deletes against all five.\r\n\r\n**Why this matters.** This predates every production batch — it is a pre-existing baseline gap, NOT damage caused by the B1 promotion. It is recorded here so it is not mistaken for batch fallout later, and so it is not silently absorbed into the post-batch check's noise floor. The harness reports it on every run and never suppresses it.\r\n\r\n**What needs establishing before anyone writes SQL:**\r\n1. Confirm the privilege state live from the catalog (`has_table_privilege` per role per verb), not from migration files.\r\n2. Confirm PopPIM genuinely performs those writes as `authenticated` and not through a service-role path or an RPC that is `security definer`. If the writes go through a definer function, the grant is correctly absent and this issue is a false alarm — say so and close it.\r\n3. Only then decide the fix: a grant, an RLS policy, or a definer RPC. Do not reflexively grant write to `authenticated` on a shared database used by four applications; the least-privilege shape may be an RPC.\r\n\r\n**Context.** PopPIM is in development, so live user impact is likely low right now. That is a reason to fix it before launch, not a reason to leave it.\r\n\r\nRelated: #706 records that there is no monitoring on PopDAM, PopCRM or PopPIM, so breakage is found by a user complaining. This is exactly the class of defect that gap hides.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstate: non-structural\npriority: 250\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T01:29:22Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T23:19:31Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":720,"title":"PopPIM writes to five pim.* tables that 'authenticated' has no write privilege on","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:00Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/720"},
{"body":"Filed by orchestrator f3fbdd0a (marker #714) on 2026-08-10, so a deliberately-scoped-out gap is not lost.\r\n\r\nWhile fixing #664 and #649, the implementation agent for PR #717 left `plm.erp_*` alone and flagged it rather than widening its own claim.\r\n\r\n**The gap.** PR #717 does two things: it revokes `truncate, references, trigger, maintain` from `service_role` on the 39 `plm.pmt_*` and `plm.nbcu_*` tables, and it closes the root cause by altering the `plm` schema default privileges so NEW tables are not born with those bits.\r\n\r\nThe default-privilege fix stops the recurrence. It does NOT retro-fix tables that already exist. #649 names `plm.erp_*` as still carrying the bits, and those tables are outside #664's 39 and outside claim #716.\r\n\r\n**Why it was left.** Correctly, in the orchestrator's view: a broad sweep across every pre-existing `plm` table would have collided with whatever else is in flight, and widening a claim mid-task is exactly how two agents end up writing the same objects. Scoping it out and flagging it is the right call. But it means anyone reading \"#664 is fixed\" could reasonably believe every plm table is clean, and that is not true.\r\n\r\n**What this issue needs.**\r\n1. Establish the real, current list of pre-existing `plm` tables carrying unintended `truncate`/`references`/`trigger`/`maintain` for `service_role` — read it live from the catalog, do not infer it from migration files.\r\n2. Decide per group whether the privilege is genuinely unintended or load-bearing for a loader. A revoke that breaks a loader at load time is worse than the grant.\r\n3. One forward migration, with an in-migration assertion and a vacuous-pass guard (fail if the table set is empty or smaller than expected).\r\n\r\n**Ordering note.** Unlike #664's 39 tables, `plm.erp_*` may already exist on production. Confirm before writing SQL: if it does, this is a live privilege change on a shared production database, not a pre-emptive correction, and it needs the full promotion path rather than riding a batch.\r\n\r\nBlocked on nothing. Do NOT dispatch this concurrently with any other agent writing to `supabase/migrations/` — single-writer rule.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: structural\nroute: shared-db-orchestrator\npriority: 500\ndepends_on:\nwrites:\n  - table plm.item\n  - table plm.item_detail\n  - table plm.item_attachment\n  - table plm.art_piece\n  - table plm.production_order\n  - table plm.production_order_line\n  - table plm.licensing_status\n  - table plm.licensing_feedback\n  - table plm.rfq_group\n  - table plm.rfq_item\n  - table plm.rfq_vendor\n  - table plm.reference_value\n  - table plm.customer_import\n  - table plm.licensor_import\n  - table plm.property_import\n  - table plm.art_piece_item\n  - table plm.erp_customer\n  - table plm.erp_vendor\n  - table plm.merch_group_header\n  - table plm.item_import_staging\n  - table plm.item_import\n  - table plm.item_import_unresolved\n  - table plm.item_taxonomy_disagreement\n  - table plm.vendor_exclusion\n  - table plm.vendor_quarantine\n  - table plm.erp_licensor\n  - table plm.erp_property\n  - table plm.taxonomy_resolution_review\n  - table plm.taxonomy_parallel_observation\n  - table plm.taxonomy_sync_alert\n  - table plm.taxonomy_circuit_breaker\n  - table plm.taxonomy_circuit_breaker_event\n  - table plm.taxonomy_baseline_pin\n  - table plm.taxonomy_baseline_activation\n  - table plm.deployment_environment\n  - table plm.production_order_source_ref\n  - table plm.production_order_line_source_ref\nreads:\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-05T11:09:27Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T23:03:15Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":718,"title":"32 pre-existing plm tables still carry the unintended MAINTAIN/TRUNCATE grants — scoped out of #664, needs its own sweep","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:42:25Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/718"},
{"body":"```db-claim\nversion: 20260810180000\nobjects:\n  - plm\n  - plm.pmt_tables_maintain_grant\n  - plm.nbcu_tables_maintain_grant\n```\n\nHeld by orchestrator f3fbdd0a (marker #714) on behalf of the implementation agent for #664 / #649.\n\nScope: ONE new forward migration revoking the unintended MAINTAIN (and related) grants on the 39 plm tables that the Paramount and NBCU revokes missed, plus the plm schema-wide default-privilege hole. Additive forward migration only; no existing migration is edited.\n\nCollision gate run before dispatch: exit 0, 0 in-flight items. {"body":"Three issues on this board are **stale in a way that would cause a fresh session to rebuild work that already exists**. Assessed 2026-08-10 by orchestrator session 511f124e (marker #684); anchored to the repo, not to the issue text.\n\nFull context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-10T2110Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-first-production-promotion.md` §3.\n\n---\n\n## #617 — the production apply path: **substantially BUILT AND MERGED**\n\nMerged as `ca2eea2`. A fresh session reading #617's text would rebuild what is already\nthere. Verified against `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml` and\n`scripts/production_migration_guard.py`:\n\n| #617 requirement | status |\n|---|---|\n| `apply` mode on the workflow | DONE (`:290`) |\n| `production` environment, Albert required reviewer | DONE (`:298`), and **verified live** — `required_reviewers: [u2giants]` |\n| Same allowlist, same typed confirmation | DONE (`:302-308`, requires `APPLY <sha>`) |\n| Fresh dry-run in the same run, matching the allowlist before apply | DONE (`:361-368`, write at `:370`) |\n| Automatic model review | DONE (`:272-278`) |\n| Model review never the only gate | DONE and hard-wired — always exits 0, `continue-on-error: true` |\n| TOCTOU — re-read the ledger immediately before push | DONE (`:326-333`, plus `assert-bounded` at `:357`) |\n| **Content drift — pin file digests** | **NOT DONE** — no `hashlib`/`sha256` anywhere in the guard; only version *names* are compared |\n\n**Recommended: close #617 as satisfied by `ca2eea2`, and open one narrow successor** for\ndigest pinning plus recording the digests in the apply artifact. Residual risk is low\nbecause checkout is by exact SHA and asserted equal to `origin/main`, but **an audit after\nthe fact cannot prove what SQL ran.**\n\nOne deliberate deviation worth recording rather than \"fixing\": the model verdict is posted\nto the job summary and artifact, not to a PR as #617's wording asks. That is arguably\nbetter — the approver reads it at the moment of approval.\n\n**And one thing #617 does not track but should:** the **advisory model review does not\nactually run.** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is not configured on the repo. To its credit it fails\nloudly and tells the approver to rely on the deterministic guard, but it means there is **no\nmodel review layer on production applies today**, and half of #617's \"reviewer gate plus\nautomatic model review\" shape is absent.\n\n---\n\n## #615 — the production rehearsal: the allowlist is OBSOLETE\n\nIts \"47-migration allowlist\" is wrong. The **live** production read on 2026-08-10\nestablished **63 behind** at that time (now 53, after the canary and B1). A 47-item list\nbuilt from that figure would either be rejected outright by `validate_candidates` or, worse,\npass while **silently omitting 16 migrations**.\n\nAlso, #615's own \"Blocked by the bounded `--include-all` issue\" line is stale: **#614 is\nclosed** and `prepare`/`assert-bounded` are live at `production_migration_guard.py:754` and\n`:779`.\n\nThe `verify_dry_run` trap #615 warns about was **real and is now resolved by evidence**: it\nhard-codes `\"Would push these migrations:\"` and is coupled to Supabase CLI 2.105.0, and it\nexecuted successfully for the **first time in this repo's history** during the canary\npromotion, then again for B1.\n\n**Recommended: rewrite #615 around the live figure, or close it** — the batch plan in\n`docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` now supersedes it.\n\n---\n\n## #616 — the whole-batch clone rehearsal: possibly OVER-SCOPED now\n\nNot started; nothing in the repo implements a clone or ledger-seeding step.\n\nIts trap is correctly stated and now sharper: the clone must carry\n`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` with the **exact interleaved ledger**, not just a\nrow count — production applied migrations **out of order** relative to `main`\n(`20260729130000` is applied while `20260729120000` is not).\n\nBut its premise has shifted. It was designed when the plan was one big push. With the canary\npromoted, B1 applied, and a nine-batch bounded plan in place, a single whole-63 rehearsal\nbuys less than it did — and it costs a temporary paid Supabase project plus a production\n`pg_dump`, which is itself a full read of every row **including the customer and vendor PII\nflagged in #645**. That is not obviously approved.\n\n**Recommended: an explicit decision on whether #616 is still the right shape**, rather than\nsilent execution or silent abandonment.\n\n---\n\n## Also worth knowing\n\n`plan_popdam_order_list.md`'s STATUS table still marks Steps 1 and 2 as open. **Both are\nmerged.** Issue #613 was closed on that basis today. Whoever owns that document should flip\nit, or the next reader will re-author the OrderList contract.\n\nRelated: #612, #614 (closed), #709, #710.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T18:48:29Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T21:15:07Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":712,"title":"HANDOVER: #617 is already built, #615's allowlist is obsolete, #616 may be over-scoped — reconcile before anyone rebuilds them","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:04Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/712"},
{"body":"Four of the seven owner decisions in `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` §8 are still unanswered. Three were answered on 2026-08-10 (see below). **D7 is the urgent one.**\r\n\r\nFull context: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-10T2110Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-first-production-promotion.md` §6.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## D7 — who runs the manual checklist, nine times? ⚠️ MOST URGENT\r\n\r\nD1 was answered \"yes, accepted\" (#706): the three exposed apps — **PopDAM, PopCRM,\r\nPopPIM** — have **no monitoring** that would catch a mid-promotion break, and discovery is a\r\nuser complaining.\r\n\r\nThat answer has a consequence that has not been arranged. **The manual checklist in §7 of\r\nthe contract is now the entire safety net**, and it needs a named person with three logins\r\nand SSH to the worker host, willing to run it after each of the nine batches.\r\n\r\n**Nobody ran it after B1.** That is not a criticism of anyone — it was never assigned. But\r\nthe pattern is now set, and an unassigned checklist does not get run.\r\n\r\nThe single most important check is after **B8**: PopDAM swallows a broken\r\n`core.product_size` / `core.product_material` into hardcoded fallback lists\r\n(`StylesPage.tsx:771,783-790`), so that breakage is **completely invisible** — the dropdown\r\nstill populates, with the wrong values.\r\n\r\n**What is needed:** a name, and confirmation they will actually do it. If the honest answer\r\nis \"nobody will\", say so — then the batches should be spaced so a real user would surface a\r\nproblem before the next one goes, which is a different plan from the current one.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## D2 — how long may a resting point persist?\r\n\r\nThe nine boundaries are safe by construction, but each is still a **half-promoted production\r\ndatabase** watched by three live apps. Minutes apart, or days? This changes whether the\r\nremaining eight batches are one evening's work or a fortnight's.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## D5 — DesignFlow non-production drift: asset or hazard?\r\n\r\nDesignFlow's develop, staging and both sandboxes are contractually bound to the shared\r\nSupabase pooler, while **production is bound to Cloud SQL** and the code refuses to start\r\notherwise. So every shared-db promotion hits DesignFlow's non-production environments\r\n**immediately, with no redeploy**, while production is untouched until the same DDL reaches\r\nCloud SQL.\r\n\r\nThat is a permanent gap, not something these batches create. It is arguably an **asset** —\r\nfree rehearsal of every batch against a real app — and the DesignFlow sandbox is currently\r\nunused. It is also a hazard, because the two halves drift further apart with every\r\npromotion.\r\n\r\nRelated: the Cloud SQL move (#508, #696, #705, #707).\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## D6 — is `20260810170000`'s widening still wanted?\r\n\r\nThat migration (the #653 Option A fix, merged today) opens the **entire item catalogue to\r\nevery authenticated account**. That cost was accepted when Option A was chosen.\r\n\r\nSince then one fact emerged: **`api.dam_order_list` has no deployed reader.** The name\r\nappears in `popdam3` only inside vendored docs. So the widening ships **ahead of** the\r\nfeature that needed it, and will sit on production in B9 before anything reads it.\r\n\r\nStill wanted as-is, or should it be narrowed (Option B — expose only the four columns\r\nthrough a definer helper) before B9 promotes it? It is already merged and on preview, so\r\nchanging course means a forward migration, not an edit.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Answered on 2026-08-10, recorded for the next session\r\n\r\n- **D1 — user-reported discovery: ACCEPTED.** \"we have to start shipping!\" → #706.\r\n- **D3 — all four destructive migrations: APPROVED** in advance, so the batches do not stop\r\n  four more times. None deletes business data.\r\n- **D4 — canary before #611 was discharged:** moot. The canary was promoted and #611 is now\r\n  discharged by an executed experiment.\r\n\r\nRelated: #612, #706, #709.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 600\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T22:36:05Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T21:14:32Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":711,"title":"HANDOVER: [ALBERT] four open owner decisions on the promotion — D7 (who runs the checks) is urgent","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:42:30Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/711"},
{"body":"**53 migrations remain. B1 is applied. B2 is blocked on #709.**\n\nFull detail: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-10T2110Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-first-production-promotion.md`\nThe batch plan: `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md` §5, §6.\n\n## State as of 2026-08-10T21:10Z — re-derive before acting\n\n- `main` `55b0d66`, max migration `20260810170000`, **zero** open PRs, **zero** open claims.\n- **Production ledger 373.** Was 361 at session start; the canary `20260810140000` took it\n  to 362; B1's eleven took it to 373.\n- **53 promotable remain.** (64 backlog at `53e1e47` − 1 canary − 11 B1 = 52 … recount from\n  the live ledger; four different figures circulated today and all were wrong.)\n\n## ⛔ Blocked on #709 first\n\nB1 applied cleanly but its run is marked FAILED because the post-apply catalog verification\nreturns **HTTP 403** from the Management API. **Fix that before B2**, or every remaining\nbatch finishes red with no evidence. Do **not** weaken the hard-fail to make the red go\naway — that undoes #697.\n\n## The batches\n\nBoundaries are **not** free choices. Only nine states in the whole backlog are safe to rest\non; everywhere else leaves the database actively wrong, not merely half-finished. §6 of the\ncontract lists the states that must NEVER be rested on.\n\n- **B1** — DONE, applied 2026-08-10.\n- **B2** — `20260728171500, 20260728174500, 20260728181500`\n- **B3** — `20260729230000`…`20260731200000` (10 files) — **ATOMIC, no internal boundary.**\n  Eight successive bodies of `plm.promote_coldlion_source_owned`; **only the eighth is safe\n  to rest on.** Earlier bodies leave a known ambiguous-column error, broken absence\n  detection, no serialization lock, or incomplete provenance (unrecoverable after the fact).\n- **B4** — `20260731210000, 20260731220000, 20260731150000, 20260731153000` (version order)\n- **B5** — `20260802140000`…`20260802160000`\n- **B6** — `20260803150000`…`20260804120100`\n- **B7** — `20260807030000`…`20260807200000` — **ATOMIC.** Contains the OPA view\n  drop-and-recreate (a genuine column-set change, so there is a window with **no view at\n  all**) and the three-version `sync_opa_property_character` chain.\n- **B8** — `20260809170000`…`20260809170500`\n- **B9** — `20260810010000`…`20260810130000` + `160000`, `170000` — **ATOMIC, 13+ files.**\n  Carries all three security co-presence pairs, the `dam_order_list` `security_invoker` fix\n  and both DAM function chains.\n\n## ⚠️ B2 carries the highest-probability abort in the entire backlog\n\n`20260728171500` reads the **live body** of\n`api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree(text,boolean,text,integer)` out of the catalog,\nstring-patches two anchors, and re-executes it. **One character of drift and it fails or\nsilently patches nothing.** It also references `plm.\"divisionCode\"`, which nothing in the\nbacklog creates. **Check the anchors in the dry-run output before approving B2.**\n\n## Never in any allowlist\n\n- `20260729120000` — **RETIRED.** It would regress a live security control. In a\n  full-backlog push it would succeed, which is why it is guard-blocked.\n- `20260802170000`, `20260802171000` — FR held pair; `FR_REMOVAL_VERSIONS` is empty, so the\n  legal combined event cannot be assembled.\n\n## The three security windows — never rest inside these\n\n- **Paramount** `20260810020000`→`090000`: 23 tables with `service_role` holding TRUNCATE.\n  TRUNCATE fires no row triggers, so **one statement bypasses all five immutability guards**.\n- **NBCU** `20260810070000`→`080000`: 16 tables directly rewritable, capture ledger directly\n  insertable, bypassing `begin_nbcu_capture`/`finalize_nbcu_capture`.\n- **Warner** `20260810030000`→`110000`+`120000`: 8 tables of confidential licensor data whose\n  read policies are **wide open to every authenticated account**. Resting between `110000`\n  and `120000` still leaves `service_role` able to INSERT.\n\nRoot cause: `20260710135975`'s schema-wide `alter default privileges … to service_role`\nfires at CREATE TABLE, making in-migration grants a no-op. Already applied; in force\nthroughout.\n\n## A trap the documents hide\n\n`20260810110000` is described everywhere as a Warner grants migration. Its SQL at `:183`\n**also flips `api.dam_order_list` to `security_invoker`** — the #653 fix. Batching from the\ndescription alone separates the fix from `20260810010000` and silently reopens that bug.\nThe guard deliberately does not encode this dependency, so **the batch plan is the only\nthing preventing it.**\n\n## Procedure per batch\n\n1. Dry-run: `target=production`, `mode=dry-run`, the batch's versions ascending, the exact\n   `origin/main` SHA, `confirmation=DRY-RUN <sha>`.\n2. Read the output. Confirm it would push **exactly** that batch.\n3. Apply: same, `mode=apply`, `confirmation=APPLY <sha>`. **Albert clicks the environment\n   gate.** Never self-approve — agent tokens are `u2giants`, an admin, and\n   `can_admins_bypass` is `true`.\n4. Read the catalog verification evidence. Confirm the ledger moved by exactly the batch size.\n5. **Run the manual checks in contract §7.** With D1 accepted (#706), that checklist is the\n   entire safety net. **D7 — who runs it — is unanswered.**\n\n**`main` moved eight times today, twice between a dry-run and its apply.** If it moves\nbetween yours, re-check whether any file under `supabase/migrations/` differs; if one does,\nre-run the dry-run rather than trusting the old one.\n\n**A mid-batch failure leaves the earlier files applied and ledgered** — settled by the #611\nexperiment. Recovery is \"the remaining ones alone\"; `validate_candidates` refuses any\nallowlist containing an already-applied version.\n\nRelated: #612, #709, #706, #697, #677.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T21:56:33Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T21:14:31Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":710,"title":"HANDOVER: run batches B2 through B9 — 53 migrations left, blocked on #709","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:08Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/710"},
{"body":"**Batch B1 applied successfully to production, but the run is marked FAILED because the new post-apply catalog verification could not authenticate.** Fix this before batch B2, or every remaining batch will finish red and the evidence will be worthless.\n\n## What actually happened\n\nRun https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/actions/runs/31430916078, head `55b0d66`, owner-approved at the gate.\n\nStep-by-step outcome of the `Production apply` job:\n\n| step | outcome |\n|---|---|\n| Check exact confirmation | success |\n| Verify exact main commit | success |\n| Capture production migration record | success |\n| Build bounded checkout | success |\n| **Fresh dry-run, then apply** | **success — the write happened** |\n| Capture production migration record (after) | success |\n| **Post-apply catalog verification** | **FAILURE** |\n| Save apply evidence | success |\n\n**The migrations are applied.** Verified from the `production-ledger-after.txt` artifact: **373 applied rows** (up from 362), and all eleven B1 versions are present with remote values — spot-checked `20260724060000`, `20260726030000`, `20260727230000`, `20260728134500`.\n\n## The failure\n\n```\n- catalog query failed: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden\n- row-count query failed (recorded, not fatal on its own): HTTP Error 403: Forbidden\n\nCATALOG VERIFICATION FAILURE: the catalog query produced NO evidence while there were\n6 relation(s), 34 function(s) and 1 seeded relation(s) to check. Absence of evidence is\nnot evidence.\n```\n\n`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py` queries the Supabase **Management API `database/query`** endpoint with `read_only: true`, using `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`. That token is accepted for `supabase db push` but is **403 Forbidden** on the Management API query endpoint.\n\n## This is the guard working, not misfiring\n\nThe step is designed to hard-fail when it produces **no evidence at all** while having something to check — issue #697 exists precisely because a green tick was once mistaken for evidence. It refused to pass silently. That is correct behaviour and should not be softened.\n\nBut the practical effect is that **B1 has no catalog evidence**: the derivation worked (6 relations, 34 functions, 1 seeded relation, listed in the job summary), and every query behind it returned 403.\n\n## What needs deciding and fixing\n\nThe token needs Management API query permission on project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, or the step needs a different access path. Options, roughly:\n\n1. **Grant/replace the token** so the existing `database/query` call works. Smallest change; the script is already written and reviewed.\n2. **Switch the step to a direct Postgres connection** (the same credential the apply uses) instead of the Management API. Removes a whole class of permission problem, but is a real change to reviewed code and needs its own review.\n3. Something else — but **do not** weaken the hard-fail to make the red go away. That converts this from \"we have no evidence\" into \"we think we have evidence\", which is worse than the state before #697.\n\nOption 1 is preferred if the permission can simply be granted.\n\n## What to do about B1 specifically\n\nB1's objects are on production and unverified by catalog. Once the permission is fixed, run the verification against B1's allowlist retrospectively — the script takes an allowlist and reads current state, so it does not need a re-apply. Its own limits still apply: it reads state after the fact and cannot attribute an object to a particular apply.\n\n**Do not re-run the B1 apply.** `validate_candidates` refuses any allowlist containing an already-applied version, and re-applying is neither possible nor desirable.\n\n## Derived targets, recorded here since the artifact has no evidence\n\n- **tables (6):** `core.style_guide`, `core.style_guide_character`, `plm.taxonomy_circuit_breaker`, `plm.taxonomy_circuit_breaker_event`, `plm.taxonomy_parallel_observation`, `plm.taxonomy_sync_alert`\n- **rls_relations (6):** the same six\n- **functions (34):** including `plm.sync_coldlion_licensors_properties` and `public.sync_coldlion_licensors_properties` (the destructive 2-arg → 3-arg replacement), the taxonomy circuit-breaker family, and the ColdLion link/guard family\n- **seeded (1):** `plm.taxonomy_circuit_breaker`\n- **roles probed (4):** `anon`, `authenticated`, `public`, `service_role`\n\nRelated: #697 (the step), #701 (the PR that added it), #612 (the batch plan).\n","closedAt":"2026-08-10T22:55:37Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T21:11:29Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":709,"title":"HANDOVER: BLOCKING B2 — catalog verification gets 403 from the Management API; B1 applied but is unverified","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:11Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/709"},
{"body":"**Owner ruling, 2026-08-10 — this is NOT a defect and no one should try to fix it.**\n\nHis words: *\"Sample Tracking doesn't exist in Cloud SQL. It is a feature in testing and i didn't want to go through all the trouble building it on Cloud SQL only to move it.\"*\n\n## What this settles\n\nToday's Cloud SQL assessment flagged that **thirteen migrations** — `20260721201500_restore_dflow_sample_tracking_tables.sql` through `20260724040000` — build the Sample Tracking schema on the shared Supabase side, and that none of them appear to have reached Cloud SQL. That was the largest single block in an estimated 18-migration divergence, and it was raised as a possible live production breakage.\n\n**It is intentional.** Sample Tracking is a feature in testing. It lives on the Supabase environments (develop, staging, sandbox) where it is being tested, and it was deliberately never built on Cloud SQL because the platform move would make that work disposable.\n\n## Consequences for the migration work\n\n1. **Remove Sample Tracking from the divergence backlog.** It is not drift to be reconciled; it is a feature that starts life on the destination platform. Any plan proposing to apply those thirteen migrations to Cloud SQL should be rejected on sight.\n2. **The real divergence count is smaller than 18.** Recount excluding the Sample Tracking block before quoting a figure to anyone.\n3. **This is an argument in favour of the move, not a risk of it.** Work is already being deliberately withheld from Cloud SQL to avoid throwing it away. The longer the move takes, the more features accumulate on one platform only.\n4. **DesignFlow production does not have Sample Tracking, by design.** Anyone reading the schema diff cold would call that a missing feature. It is not.\n\n## Still true, and still needs Uma\n\nThe other divergences remain real and unresolved — including `20260810160000`, the `dflow.users` office/language columns merged today for issue #690, which will not reach DesignFlow production until applied to Cloud SQL. That is tracked separately as **#696**, which Uma owns.\n\nRelated: #508, #696, #705.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T22:01:01Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T20:43:54Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":707,"title":"OWNER RULING: Sample Tracking is absent from Cloud SQL deliberately — not drift, do not reconcile","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:14Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/707"},
{"body":"**Owner decision, 2026-08-10: user-reported discovery is ACCEPTED for now.** His words: *\"yes, and add an issue to address it in the future. we have to start shipping!\"*\r\n\r\nThis issue exists so the accepted risk is written down rather than forgotten, and so it can be fixed deliberately later instead of after an incident.\r\n\r\n## What was accepted\r\n\r\nDecision D1 of `docs/production-promotion-app-tolerance-contract.md`. The three applications that read the shared Supabase production project — **PopDAM, PopCRM and PopPIM** — have **no monitoring that would catch a mid-promotion break.** If a production promotion breaks one of them, the way anyone finds out is a person complaining.\r\n\r\n(DesignFlow and monitor are unaffected: DesignFlow production runs on Cloud SQL, and monitor uses a different Supabase project entirely. Both verified from code.)\r\n\r\n## The specific gaps\r\n\r\n- **PopDAM** — no Sentry, no error boundary, no health endpoint anywhere in `src/` or `apps/`. Its admin diagnostics panel reads the database, so a schema break takes out the very screen meant to reveal it. Background workers and on-prem agents fail with no user-visible signal at all.\r\n- **PopPIM** — no monitoring, and the most silent by design. `src/lib/uiError.ts:13-16` `reportOptionalDataError` shows a dismissible toast saying the rest of the page still works, used across seven components. There is **no ErrorBoundary**, so an unguarded null becomes a white screen.\r\n- **PopCRM** — best behaved of the three, with explicit UI error states. Its worker exposes `GET /health` at `workers/crm-worker-supabase.mjs:871`, **but that endpoint returns `{ok:true}` without touching the database** — it would stay green through a total schema break. Worker failures are visible only in the systemd journal.\r\n\r\n## Why this is worth fixing later, not never\r\n\r\nThe failure mode that matters is not a crash. It is data quietly going missing while every screen still renders. Two worked examples already exist in this repo:\r\n\r\n- `api.dam_order_list` blanked item columns for PopDAM staff and was only found when a person reported it (#653, fixed 2026-08-10).\r\n- PopDAM swallows a broken `core.product_size` / `core.product_material` into hardcoded fallback lists (`StylesPage.tsx:771,783-790`), so that particular breakage is **completely invisible** — the dropdown still populates, with the wrong values.\r\n\r\nA health check that does not touch the database is worse than none, because it actively reassures.\r\n\r\n## What would actually close this\r\n\r\nRoughly in order of value per unit of effort:\r\n\r\n1. **Make PopCRM's `/health` touch the database** — a single trivial query. It already exists; it just does not prove anything.\r\n2. **A cheap external canary** that queries one row through PostgREST per exposed app and alerts on failure or on an unexpectedly empty result. **Empty must be treated as failure**, since empty-not-error is this codebase's characteristic failure shape.\r\n3. **An ErrorBoundary in PopPIM**, so a null does not become a white screen.\r\n4. **Error reporting (Sentry or equivalent) in all three**, so worker and background failures surface at all.\r\n5. Reconsider `reportOptionalDataError`: a toast the user dismisses is not a signal anyone acts on.\r\n\r\n## Scope note\r\n\r\nItems 1-5 are **application-repo work** (`popdam3`, `popcrm-web`, `poppim-web`), not shared-db work. This issue is the record of the accepted risk and the pointer; the fixes belong in those repos.\r\n\r\nRelated: #612 (the contract), #653 (the worked example), #697 (the equivalent gap on the database side, now closed — the promotion lane produces catalog evidence as of PR #701).\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: documentation\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 250\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:27:57Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T20:43:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":706,"title":"ACCEPTED RISK: no monitoring on PopDAM, PopCRM or PopPIM — breakage is found by a user complaining","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:42:32Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/706"},
{"body":"**The Cloud SQL account named `albert_read_only` is not read-only.** Found 2026-08-10 by orchestrator session 511f124e (marker #684) while attempting a read-only schema capture of DesignFlow production. The capture was **stopped** and never run.\n\n## The finding\n\n`albert_read_only` on instance `creatiflow-database` (PostgreSQL 17.9) carries:\n\n| attribute | value | should be |\n|---|---|---|\n| `rolsuper` | false | false ✅ |\n| `rolbypassrls` | false | false ✅ |\n| `rolcreatedb` | **true** | false ❌ |\n| `rolcreaterole` | **true** | false ❌ |\n| member of | **`cloudsqlsuperuser`** (with `inherit` and `set`) | no membership ❌ |\n\nPlus `CREATE` on database `postgres` and `CREATE` on schema `public`.\n\nSo an account whose **name promises read-only** can create databases, create and manage roles, and create objects in `public`. Those are writes against production infrastructure.\n\n## What it CANNOT do — the good news, stated precisely\n\nThis was checked rather than assumed, because the name of a role proves nothing:\n\n- **Zero** `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` on any table in the `designflow` schema. It holds `SELECT` on 296 relations and nothing more.\n- The only write privileges found anywhere were on `pg_catalog.pg_settings` and `pg_catalog.pg_largeobject` — Postgres' stock grants to `PUBLIC`, not something anyone granted here.\n- The `cloudsqlsuperuser` membership is **not** a back door into DesignFlow data. All 386 relations in `designflow` are owned by `postgres`, and `cloudsqlsuperuser` holds neither `USAGE` nor `CREATE` on that schema and zero table privileges in it. `SET ROLE cloudsqlsuperuser` yields no path to DesignFlow data or DDL.\n\nThe blocker is the account's own attributes, not a route to the data.\n\n## Why the capture stopped\n\nThe owner authorised a shared-db session to read Cloud SQL on one condition: **prove the credential is read-only before connecting with it.** It was not proven, so the session went no further than the privilege probe. No DDL, no DML, no write was attempted — the conclusion is reasoned purely from catalog privileges, deliberately, rather than by testing whether a write would be refused.\n\n## The fix — four statements, for whoever owns the instance\n\n```sql\nALTER ROLE albert_read_only NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE;\nREVOKE cloudsqlsuperuser FROM albert_read_only;\nREVOKE CREATE ON DATABASE postgres FROM albert_read_only;\nREVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM albert_read_only;\n```\n\n**Leave the existing `SELECT` grants on `designflow` alone** — they are correct, and they are what makes the capture possible once the attributes are fixed. After these four statements the capture can proceed immediately with no other change.\n\nNote this credential was already rotated once, after being emailed in plaintext (issue #517). Its privileges were evidently never narrowed to match its name.\n\n## Facts learned anyway, useful to the migration\n\n- Cloud SQL production holds **five** non-system schemas: `designflow`, `designflow_dev`, `designflow_sandbox`, `rfq_backoffice13_prod`, `public`. Only `designflow` is readable by this credential.\n- **The `dflow` schema does not exist in Cloud SQL at all.** The production schema is `designflow`. This resolves the ambiguity raised in #696.\n- `designflow` holds **386 relations**, all owned by `postgres`.\n- `shared_preload_libraries` carries eight Google-specific modules with **no Supabase equivalent**: `dbsecurity`, `google_app_stats`, `google_dataplex`, `google_dbheartbeat`, `google_insights`, `iamgroup_management`, `pg_stat_statements`, `password_validation`. Flag for the migration plan.\n- `search_path` is the stock `\"$user\", public`, so the app must be schema-qualifying or setting it per connection.\n- This machine's egress IP is already on the instance's authorized-networks allowlist — the connection worked first try.\n\n## Notes for the reusable capture script\n\n- The 1Password MCP rejects a vault **UUID** in `vaultId`; it accepts only the literal name `vibe_coding`, and the `op://` reference must use the vault name too.\n- The item's title contains parentheses, so `op://` must address it by **item ID**, and the password by **field ID** — `DB_PASSWORD` is a custom field, not the standard `credential` field.\n- `psql` is not on `PATH` on al8960ofc; it is at `C:\\Program Files\\PostgreSQL\\17\\bin\\psql.exe`.\n- A plain `SELECT ... FROM pg_namespace` returns **1,022 rows** on this instance, because Cloud SQL carries ~510 `pg_temp_*` / `pg_toast_temp_*` slots. The script must filter them or the output is unreadable.\n\nNo business data and no personal data was read. The credential value was never revealed into the transcript.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-10T23:48:47Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T20:42:48Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":705,"title":"The Cloud SQL account named albert_read_only can create roles and databases on production","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:16Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/705"},
{"body":"Two Low nits from the PR #701 review (#697), landed deliberately rather than blocking the merge. Both are about the report being *misread*, not about it being wrong.\n\n## 1. The two most consequential SQL lines are pinned only by loose substring assertions\n\n`scripts/test_production_catalog_verification.py:289` asserts that the string `acl_is_default` appears in the SQL — not the actual predicate `'acl_is_default', p.proacl is null`. So an edit that changes the predicate to something **wrong** still passes all 58 tests green.\n\nSame shape at `:296` for the PUBLIC grantee label, where three other occurrences of the same literal in the file keep the substring alive regardless.\n\nThese are the two lines the whole function-privilege verification rests on:\n\n- `proacl is null` means **default privileges = EXECUTE to PUBLIC**, i.e. exactly what a missing `revoke` leaves behind. Get this predicate wrong and a Paramount promotion whose revoke silently failed produces a report that reads clean.\n- The PUBLIC label is what makes a grant-to-everyone searchable in the artifact rather than rendering as a bare dash.\n\nOffline tests cannot execute SQL semantics — that limit is inherent and fine. But an exact-string assertion is the strongest available proxy and costs **one line each**.\n\n## 2. Default and explicitly-empty ACLs share the same cell text\n\nBoth render `_no explicit ACL entry_` in the grantee cell, distinguished only by the boolean `acl default` column beside them. The prose does tell the reader to read that column first, and the `execute_held_by` probe disambiguates independently — so the information IS present, in two places. But different text per case would remove the last chance of a misread:\n\n- `_default: EXECUTE to PUBLIC_`\n- `_explicitly empty_`\n\nGiven that the entire point of #697 is that a green tick was once mistaken for evidence, a report cell that can be misread the wrong way is worth the small edit.\n\n## Not urgent\n\nNeither blocks a promotion. The verification is correct as merged; these make it harder to break silently later and harder to misread under pressure. Cheap to do next time anyone is in that file.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T22:40:23Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T20:09:55Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":702,"title":"Tighten the two SQL assertions the function-privilege verification rests on (follow-up to #697)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:19Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/702"},

Writes NO database objects; it adds\nread-only verification queries whose output lands in the run artifact.\n\nThe collision gate's NOT-CHECKED classes are not a concern here — this task authors no DDL at\nall. Confirmed by the orchestrator, not assumed.\n\n**This agent owns `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` and the workflow for the duration.**\nNo other agent may write them until this claim closes.\n\nClose this issue when the work merges or is abandoned.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-10T20:09:54Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T19:37:51Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvGcdSA","name":"db-claim","description":"An agent is dispatched and holds these DB objects. Close when the work merges or is abandoned.","color":"B60205"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":699,"title":"CLAIM: #697 post-apply catalog verification in the production lane","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:42:33Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/699"},
{"body":"```db-claim\nversion: 20260810170000\nobjects:\n  - plm.item\n```\n\nDispatched by orchestrator session 511f124e (al8960ofc), marker #684, for issue #653.\n\n**Owner ruling 2026-08-10: Option A.** An additive `for select to authenticated using (true)`\npolicy on `plm.item`, matching the precedent already set for `plm.production_order` and\n`plm.production_order_line` in `20260810010000:302-312`.\n\nScope: one policy plus its comment. Nothing else. The fix must NOT revert\n`security_invoker = true` on `api.dam_order_list` — that setting was made deliberately by\n`20260810110000:183` and reverting it would silently re-expose `core.customer`, `core.factory`\nand `plm.item` to every authenticated account through the view.\n\nCollision gate exit 0 against 0 in-flight items. Policies ARE a checked class for this tool,\nso this is a real check, not a blind spot — but zero in-flight items means there was nothing\nto compare against, which the orchestrator notes rather than treats as clearance. No other\nclaim is open.\n\nClose this issue when the work merges or is abandoned. An open claim blocks other agents from\nbeing dispatched onto the same objects.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-10T19:52:47Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T19:37:50Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvGcdSA","name":"db-claim","description":"An agent is dispatched and holds these DB objects. Close when the work merges or is abandoned.","color":"B60205"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":698,"title":"CLAIM: #653 Option A — plm.item authenticated read policy (version 20260810170000)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:42:35Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/698"},
{"body":"**Do this BEFORE the first licensor batch goes to production.** Found by verifying the\ncanary apply (#677) rather than trusting its green tick.\n\n## The gap\n\n`supabase db push` **discards `RAISE NOTICE` and all DO-block output.** The only post-apply\nstep in `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml` is `supabase migration list\n--linked` — a **ledger read**. There is **no catalog verification step anywhere in the lane.**\n\nSo the lane can prove that it *wrote*. It cannot prove *what* it wrote.\n\nConcretely, after the canary apply, only **2 of 5** basic checks were provable from the\nartifacts:\n\n| Check | Status after a fully green run |\n|---|---|\n| Ledger moved 361 → 362 with the version present | CONFIRMED from artifacts |\n| The four roles hold no privileges | Confirmed only **by silence** — the assertions are fail-closed and print nothing; a raise would have aborted the transaction, so the ledger row's existence implies they passed |\n| The table exists (`to_regclass`) | INFERRED, never queried |\n| The table holds exactly 1 row | INFERRED — and `create table if not exists` means a pre-existing hand-created table would silently skip the create while the insert appended |\n| RLS enabled with **zero policies** | **NOT CONFIRMED at all.** Not asserted by the migration, not queried by the lane. The only basis is reading the SQL text — an argument about source code, not an observation of production |\n\n## Why this is blocking, not cosmetic\n\nFor a throwaway canary table this is tolerable. **It is not tolerable when this lane carries\nthe Disney, Paramount, NBCU and Warner grants and RLS policies.** In that run, \"the job went\ngreen\" is again the only artifact — and a self-asserting migration whose assertion is wrong,\nor simply absent, looks **identical** to one that is right.\n\nThis repo already has the scar: a migration installed cleanly whose `BEFORE` trigger read a\n`GENERATED … STORED` column that Postgres populates *after* before-triggers, so the value was\nalways NULL, the guard never fired, and **no error was ever raised**. The rule written down\nafterwards was: *assert the BEHAVIOUR, and verify the OBJECT exists (`to_regclass`,\n`pg_trigger`, `pg_get_viewdef`), never just the ledger row.* The production lane does not yet\nfollow the repo's own rule.\n\nThe privilege case is the sharpest. Three known grant/revoke pairs (Paramount\n`20260810020000`/`090000`, NBCU `20260810070000`/`080000`, Warner\n`20260810030000`/`110000`+`120000`) exist precisely because\n`20260710135975`'s `alter default privileges in schema plm grant all … to service_role` fires\nat CREATE TABLE and makes the narrower in-migration grants a no-op. Whether a revoke actually\ntook is a **catalog fact**, and the lane currently cannot report it. #664 (39 `plm` tables\ncarrying an unintended `MAINTAIN` grant) is exactly what happens when nobody can see.\n\n## What to build\n\nA post-apply step in `production-apply` that runs a handful of **read-only** queries and\nlands their output in the run artifact. At minimum, for every object named in the allowlist's\nmigrations:\n\n- `to_regclass` for each table/view created\n- `relrowsecurity` and the `pg_policies` count for each RLS-bearing table\n- `has_table_privilege` across all seven privilege bits (including **`MAINTAIN`** — PG 17.6,\n  and the trap the canary was specifically written to catch) for `public`, `anon`,\n  `authenticated`, `service_role`, **and any other role holding a grant**\n- `pg_get_functiondef` presence for each function created or replaced\n- the row count for anything seeded\n\nThat closes checks 1, 2 and 3 permanently, for every future promotion, not just this one.\n\n⚠️ **Note the canary's own assertion is NOT a general-purpose template.** Its `aclexplode`\nsweep flags leftovers only for four named grantees, and its `has_table_privilege` loop covers\nonly `anon`, `authenticated` and `service_role` (`public` is caught by `aclexplode` alone). A\ngrant to any **other** role passes both checks silently.\n\n## Related\n\n- **The advisory model review currently does NOT run** — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is not configured\n  on the repo. It fails loudly and tells the approver to rely on the deterministic guard, which\n  is the right behaviour, but it means there is **no model review layer** on production applies\n  today. Worth fixing before the licensor batches, or the \"reviewer gate plus automatic model\n  review\" shape from #617 is only half present.\n- #695 — nothing runs the 36 contract tests in `supabase/tests/` either. Same shape: evidence\n  that exists but is never mechanically produced.\n- #664, #649 — the privilege drift this step would make visible.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-10T20:09:52Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T19:30:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":697,"title":"BLOCKING before licensor batches: the production lane produces no in-database evidence, only a ledger read","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:22Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/697"},
{"body":"**Owner ruling, 2026-08-10: Uma owns the Cloud SQL side.**\r\n\r\n## The gap\r\n\r\nDesignFlow **production runs on Cloud SQL, not Supabase** (`AGENTS.md:96-104`; enforced in\r\n`designflow-backend/config/database-connection-contract.js:78-88`). The `dflow` schema in\r\nshared-db is DesignFlow's **develop/staging/sandbox** database only.\r\n\r\nSo any shared-db change to `dflow.*` reaches sandbox and never reaches the app your staff\r\nactually use. The feature works in sandbox and fails in production the moment the backend\r\nselects the new columns. This is not a shared-db bug and cannot be fixed from this repo —\r\n`popcre/infrastructure` owns Cloud SQL, which is outside shared-db's authority (`AGENTS.md`\r\n§0.1).\r\n\r\n## What needs applying to Cloud SQL right now\r\n\r\nFrom `20260810160000_dflow_users_office_location_preferred_language.sql` (merged to `main`\r\nas PR #694, issue #690, and verified on preview):\r\n\r\n```sql\r\nalter table dflow.users add column office_location text;\r\nalter table dflow.users add column preferred_language text;\r\nalter table dflow.users add constraint users_office_location_check\r\n  check (office_location is null or office_location in ('ningbo','nyc'));\r\nalter table dflow.users add constraint users_preferred_language_check\r\n  check (preferred_language is null or preferred_language in ('en','zh-CN'));\r\n```\r\n\r\n⚠️ Note the **schema name differs by environment**: in Cloud SQL the DesignFlow schema is\r\nnamed `designflow`, not `dflow`. Confirm the live name before running anything.\r\n\r\n⚠️ **Values are LOWERCASE** — `'ningbo'`/`'nyc'`. `'Ningbo'` and `'NYC'` are rejected by the\r\nconstraint. Display capitals belong in the UI. `preferred_language` is BCP-47: `'en'`,\r\n`'zh-CN'`.\r\n\r\n**No backfill.** Nobody's office may be guessed. Assignments come later through DesignFlow's\r\nManage Users workflow from an authoritative roster. Both columns are nullable with no\r\ndefault, and the resolution rule is: saved language wins; else `office_location = 'ningbo'`\r\n→ `'zh-CN'`; else `'en'`.\r\n\r\n## This is a recurring structural gap, not a one-off\r\n\r\nEvery future shared-db change to `dflow.*` has the same two-database problem, and nothing\r\nmechanical catches it — a shared-db PR can be fully green while the production database it\r\nis supposed to serve never receives the change. Worth a standing rule rather than\r\nrediscovering it per feature.\r\n\r\n## Standing constraint\r\n\r\nNothing here authorises a shared-db session to touch Cloud SQL. Production infrastructure is\r\nread-only to AI sessions by default, and this hand-off is to a person.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: owner-decision\nwork_type: security-settings\nroute: owner-only\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:23:07Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T19:01:16Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":696,"title":"Cloud SQL: DesignFlow production needs the #690 office/language columns — Uma owns this","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:42:37Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/696"},
{"body":"Found during the independent review of PR #694 (issue #690), orchestrator session 511f124e.\n\n**`supabase/tests/` is not wired into any CI workflow.** No file under `.github/workflows/`\nreferences that directory. Every contract test in it must be run **by hand** against\npreview, by whoever happens to remember.\n\nThis is **pre-existing and repo-wide**, not introduced by any one PR — it applies to all\n30+ files already in that directory.\n\n## Why this matters here specifically\n\nThe repo's own hard-won rules say the opposite of what this setup delivers:\n\n- *\"'It applied successfully' proves nothing.\"* A migration once installed cleanly whose\n  `BEFORE` trigger read a `GENERATED … STORED` column — which Postgres populates AFTER\n  before-triggers — so the value was always NULL, the guard never fired, and no error was\n  ever raised. The lesson recorded was: **assert the BEHAVIOUR**. These tests are how that\n  is done, and nothing runs them.\n- The `SQL migration guards` check enforces file-level rules (duplicate versions,\n  backdating). It does **not** execute a single contract test. A PR can therefore be fully\n  green while its behavioural assertions have never once been evaluated.\n- The gap is silent in the worst way: a test that is never run is indistinguishable from a\n  test that passes, right up until production.\n\n## The obvious objection, and why it is not the whole answer\n\nThese tests need a live database, so they cannot run in a plain offline job. But that is an\nargument about *where* they run, not about whether anything should enforce them. Options\nworth weighing:\n\n1. Run them in the existing `preview` job of `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml`\n   after a preview apply — the database is already connected there.\n2. A nightly job against preview that opens an issue on failure (the same shape recommended\n   for `check-skill-drift.mjs` in #654), rather than a required PR context.\n3. At minimum, a cheap **offline** guard that fails a PR which adds a migration touching an\n   object covered by an existing test file without that test having been updated — catching\n   the drift case, if not the behaviour case.\n\nOption 1 is the strongest, since it makes \"applied to preview\" and \"proved on preview\" the\nsame event instead of two things one person has to remember to do in order.\n\n## Not a blocker for #694\n\nThat PR's test was run against preview by hand as part of its dispatch, which is the current\nprocedure correctly followed. This issue is about the procedure depending on memory.\n\nRelated: #654 (skill-drift check exists but SKIPS in CI — same shape of defect: a check that\nis present but never actually enforces anything).\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T13:28:32Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T18:31:26Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":695,"title":"No CI runs supabase/tests/ — 30+ contract tests are enforced only by memory","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:25Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/695"},
