{"body":"# HANDOVER: DesignFlow staff office and preferred language for Sample Tracking\n\n## Business goal\n\nDesignFlow Sample Tracking is used daily by Emma and other Ningbo-office staff. The UI needs an explicit, maintainable way to default Ningbo users to Simplified Chinese while allowing each person to save an English or Chinese override. The application must not infer office or language from email, name, IP address, browser language, or time zone.\n\nCanonical frontend plan:\n\n- `popcre/designflow-frontend/plan_sample_tracking_guidance_mandarin.md`\n- Current plan commit on `sandbox-albert`: `d53d4ee763a741adbccf5aab05e8c7c56039d06e`\n\n## Requested shared contract\n\nPlease dispatch through the single shared-db orchestrator and identify the authoritative DesignFlow staff-user table before writing anything.\n\nAdd nullable, constrained profile fields equivalent to:\n\n- `office_location`: allowed values `Ningbo`, `NYC`, or null.\n- `preferred_language`: allowed values `en`, `zh-CN`, or null.\n\nUse canonical table and column naming conventions if they differ. The application rule is:\n\n1. Saved preferred language wins.\n2. Otherwise `office_location = Ningbo` defaults to `zh-CN`.\n3. Otherwise default to `en`.\n\nDo not guess or bulk-backfill users. Office assignments will be made through the DesignFlow Manage Users workflow from an authoritative roster supplied by Albert or an office administrator.\n\n## Required shape and safety\n\n- Additive, nullable, and backward-compatible.\n- New timestamp above the repository's current maximum. Never reuse a version.\n- Shared-db migration and contract tests only. No app-repo migration.\n- Preview-first through the orchestrator's normal procedure.\n- Do not apply or promote this change to production without Albert's separate explicit approval for that exact action.\n- Preserve existing staff and vendor authentication behavior.\n- Document the fields and constraints where the canonical user contract is documented.\n\n## Consumer work after this lands\n\n`popcre/designflow-backend` will expose both fields from `GET /api/user/me`, allow admins to set office/language, and allow a user to update only their own preferred language. `popcre/designflow-frontend` will use these fields for the Sample Tracking English/中文 switch and Ningbo default.\n\n## Verification requested\n\n- Valid values and null succeed in preview tests.\n- Unsupported office/language values fail.\n- Existing rows remain valid without a backfill.\n- The issue response identifies exact schema/table/column names and the migration/PR used, so consumer code does not guess.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-10T18:34:39Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T17:52:51Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":690,"title":"HANDOVER: DesignFlow staff office and preferred language for Sample Tracking","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:29Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/690"},
{"body":"Found during the #686 cleanup on hetz and deliberately left untouched, because they were\r\noutside that job's scope and hold work that exists nowhere else.\r\n\r\n**Two worktrees OUTSIDE `/worksp/shared-db` carry unpushed commits:**\r\n\r\n- `/worksp/shared-db-cloudsql-proof-VazcWK` — **1 commit ahead**\r\n- `/worksp/shared-db-cutover-P9GGFO` — **3 commits ahead**\r\n\r\nBoth sit on `codex/reference-cutover-*` branches. Unpushed commits on a single VPS are\r\nthe least durable form of work there is: one disk, no backup, no remote copy.\r\n\r\n**Do this, in this order:**\r\n1. Read all four commits and determine whether their content is unique or already\r\n   superseded by `main` (now well past where those branches forked).\r\n2. Push anything unique to a named remote branch on `u2giants/shared-db` so it survives\r\n   independently of that machine.\r\n3. Only then decide whether the worktrees can be retired.\r\n\r\n⚠️ Before any commit or push on hetz, confirm `git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT` reads\r\n`Albert Hazan <[redacted personal email]>`. Git silently invents an identity from\r\nthe OS account when none is configured, and that has already put 231 wrong-identity\r\ncommits into merged history across these repos. Fix it BEFORE committing — correcting it\r\nafterwards means rewriting shared history.\r\n\r\n**Do NOT** `git clean`, reset, or force-remove either worktree as housekeeping. Follow the\r\n`cleanup-worktree` skill.\r\n\r\n**Separately, and lower priority:** eleven worktrees remain under\r\n`/worksp/shared-db/.claude/worktrees/`. Every one was checked during the #686 cleanup —\r\nall clean, none ahead of main, none holding unique work. They can be retired whenever\r\nsomeone wants the tidiness; there is nothing to recover from them.\r\n\r\nContext: `/worksp/shared-db` itself is now clean, on `main` at `bc29d36`, with all its\r\nstashes recovered to `recovered/*` branches. See #686.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 250\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:46:54Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T17:45:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":689,"title":"Two hetz worktrees hold 4 unpushed commits that exist on no remote","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:42:41Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/689"},
{"body":"## `supabase --version` printing `2.105.0` does NOT prove you are on the pinned CLI\n\nFound while updating hetz's Supabase CLI from 2.98.2 to the 2.105.0 pin\n(orchestrator session 511f124e, marker #684).\n\n**The official `v2.105.0` release tarball ships TWO different binaries — `supabase`\nand `supabase-go` — which both report `2.105.0` and are different programs with\ndifferent behaviour.**\n\nWhy this is not trivia. Issue #611's gate, and `docs/verification/issue-611-run-brief.md`,\nboth establish the pin by asserting that `supabase --version` prints `2.105.0`. That\nassertion is **not sufficient**: two distinct programs satisfy it. And the coupling is\nreal — `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` (~805-821) parses the CLI's dry-run\noutput by matching the literal string `\"Would push these migrations:\"` plus a filename\nregex. If the other binary words its output even slightly differently, `verify_dry_run`\nfails and the failure presents as a migration fault rather than as a wrong-binary\nproblem. That parser has still never been exercised successfully.\n\nOn hetz this was handled correctly: the binary actually used by the #611 run was\nidentified, and the one installed to `/usr/local/bin/supabase` was checksum-matched to\nit (`0392066…`), so hetz now matches the gate's binary exactly, not merely its version\nstring.\n\n**What should change**\n\n1. The run brief (and anything else establishing the pin) should verify the CLI by\n   **checksum**, or at minimum name which of the two binaries is the correct one — not\n   by the `--version` string alone.\n2. Any future CLI update, on **any** machine, faces the same fork. Record the correct\n   binary's checksum somewhere durable so the next person does not have to rediscover\n   this.\n\n**Also found, harmless but confusing:** running `supabase --version` from inside a\ndirectory that itself contains a file named `supabase` makes the CLI crash with a\nmisleading error. It looks exactly like a broken install.\n\n**hetz state after the update** (production server, 24 containers, all still running):\n- Was `2.98.2` at `/usr/local/bin/supabase`, a plain dropped-in binary — not apt, not\n  npm, not snap, not a symlink — so replacing it creates no package-manager conflict.\n- Backup at `/root/supabase-cli-backup/supabase-2.98.2`, checksum-verified against the\n  original. Rollback is one line as root:\n  `mv /root/supabase-cli-backup/supabase-2.98.2 /usr/local/bin/supabase`\n- Now `2.105.0`, `which supabase` unchanged at `/usr/local/bin/supabase`.\n- No auto-update risk: the CLI has no self-update command, no cron job or systemd timer\n  touches it, and while `unattended-upgrades` is enabled it only manages apt packages —\n  this binary is not apt-owned, so nothing will drift it off the pin.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T15:07:55Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T17:43:14Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":688,"title":"Two different binaries both report Supabase CLI 2.105.0 — the version string does not establish the pin","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:31Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/688"},
{"body":"Found during a read-only verification of hetz as a host for the #611 experiment.\nOrchestrator session 511f124e (al8960ofc), marker #684. **Nothing was touched.**\n\n## The clone at `/worksp/shared-db` is dirty and holds possibly-unique work\n\n- Branch `docs/clickup-handoff`, HEAD `cac0c3e`, **9 commits behind origin**. Not main;\n  never a usable base for anything current.\n- **3 stashes** from earlier sessions, one of them from a `codex/dam-search-synonyms`\n  branch that is not represented anywhere else that we know of.\n- Untracked: `.ai/deepseek-sessions/` (4 files, dated Aug 3) and\n  `.ai/reviews/clickup-import-fixes-glm.md` (Jul 29). Owned by user `ai`.\n- A git worktree exists at\n  `/worksp/shared-db/.claude/worktrees/coordinator-handoff-intake-7e55cb`.\n\nPer the orchestrator skill, **a dirty worktree belonging to a dead agent is EVIDENCE**:\nit can hold the only copy of work no report ever mentioned. It must be READ before\nanything is retired, and it must not be cleaned as housekeeping.\n\n## Two long-lived AI sessions are holding that repo\n\n- A `claude remote-control` session (PID group 1493456), alive **~4 days 16 hours**.\n- A second session inside the worktree above, alive **~5 days**.\n- Also long-lived on the box: a `codex app-server` (12 days), an OpenCode/GLM launcher\n  under `op run` (6 days), and `claude remote-control` listeners for popcrm-web, dflow\n  and ai-devops.\n\nThey look like idle remote-control listeners rather than agents mid-task, but that was\ninferred from process age and command line, **not confirmed**. Nobody knows whether a\nsession resumes on stale context and starts writing.\n\n## What needs doing\n\n1. Read the 3 stashes and the untracked files, and determine whether any of it is work\n   that exists nowhere else. Preserve anything unique.\n2. Establish whether those sessions are genuinely idle, and shut down the dead ones.\n3. Decide the fate of the `docs/clickup-handoff` branch and the\n   `coordinator-handoff-intake-7e55cb` worktree.\n\n## Do NOT\n\n- Do not `git clean`, reset, drop a stash, or remove that worktree as housekeeping.\n- Do not use `/worksp/shared-db` as a working directory for any new task — it is held\n  by live processes and is 9 commits stale. Plan debated to convergence with DeepSeek v4 Pro. **Largest of the four.**\r\n\r\n**The closure is SIX migrations, not three:** `20260810010000`, `20260810030000`, `20260810060000`, `20260810100000`, `20260810110000`, `20260810120000`. The debate uncovered why: `20260810110000` is a COMBINED-scope migration — it also does `alter view api.dam_order_list set (security_invoker = true)`, and that view is created by `20260810010000`, which is itself corrected by `060000` and `100000`. Promoting \"the three Warner files\" would have FAILED on the day.\r\n\r\n**#612 does NOT bind.** Every object in the closure is brand new, including `api.dam_order_list` which does not exist on production, so no live app can observe an intermediate state. Read that doc first — it makes a distinction that matters: G8 is a compiled constant costing a reviewed migration, while G9 is a caller-supplied parameter (`p_max_shrink_fraction`) any caller can widen to 1.0 leaving no artefact. Conflating them and \"fixing\" G8 into a parameter DELETES the guard rather than solving it. G9 traceability is flagged as unaddressed.\r\n\r\n**Sequencing enforced mechanically:** `030000` without BOTH `110000` and `120000` is REFUSED. Without them `service_role` holds the complete unmitigated `plm` default including TRUNCATE, and the read policy is `using (true)`.\r\n\r\nScale: about 594,000 rows, about 150 MB. {"body":"From orchestrator 52cd0e78 (marker #660), 2026-08-10. Briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-10T1250Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-production-lane-runnable.md` section 6. Plan debated to convergence with DeepSeek v4 Pro.\r\n\r\nTwo migrations, both on main and proven on preview: `20260810070000` then `20260810080000`. One-directional co-presence enforced in `parse_allowlist`; `080000` ALONE is the legal recovery.\r\n\r\n**Blocked by:** the #611 gate (#674), the 75-versus-57 ruling (#675), AND an unverified question that must be Gate 0.\r\n\r\n**GATE 0, and nobody has checked it: `plm` is not PostgREST-exposed.** Per AGENTS.md 8.1, `pgrst.db_schemas` is `public, graphql_public, api, crm, pim, core, app` — `plm` is absent. The NBCU loader lives in a DIFFERENT, PRIVATE repo (`nbcu/scripts/load-supabase.mjs`) and no agent has been able to read it. **If it uses supabase-js it cannot insert into `plm.nbcu_*` or call the two capture functions AT ALL.** Establish its write transport, and whether its environment even has a direct connection string or only the Supabase URL plus service_role key, before planning anything else. This may be a provisioning change, not just a code change.\r\n\r\n**The schema has NO correction path BY DESIGN** — no views, no way to edit landed rows. A bad load that FAILS validation lands as `rejected` evidence and harms nothing. A bad load that PASSES is permanent: the only remedy is a new correct capture with a later `source_captured_at`. The supersede path does not exist yet and should be filed before the promotion.\r\n\r\nAlso rejected during the debate, recorded so it is not re-proposed: adding `public` SECURITY DEFINER wrappers in the same promotion. It puts new elevated-privilege surface into the shared API that five apps use — a different risk class, and speculative on an unread loader.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:39:24Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T12:53:20Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"From orchestrator 52cd0e78 (marker #660), 2026-08-10. Briefing: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-10T1250Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-production-lane-runnable.md` section 6. Plan debated to convergence with DeepSeek v4 Pro.\r\n\r\nTwo migrations, both already on main and proven on preview: `20260810020000` (landing schema) then `20260810090000` (loader target guard + TRUNCATE revoke).\r\n\r\n**Sequencing is enforced mechanically** by the one-directional co-presence rule in `parse_allowlist` (PR #667): `020000` without `090000` is REFUSED. Between them `service_role` holds TRUNCATE on 23 tables and TRUNCATE does not fire the row-level triggers those tables rely on. **`090000` ALONE is deliberately ALLOWED** — it is the only legal recovery from a run that dies between them.\r\n\r\n**Blocked by:** the #611 gate (#674), and the portal eyeball count (#676).\r\n\r\n**Never carried real data anywhere.** Only a dry run has been done (20 of 20 groups matched, 0 of 258 batches incomplete).\r\n\r\nKey recovery note for the implementation agent: immutability triggers freeze rows only once a capture is COMPLETE, and `service_role` deliberately KEEPS DELETE so an in-flight or failed capture stays cleanable. **Write the child-first deletion SQL as a checked-in script BEFORE the load runs, not during an incident.**\r\n\r\nR8 from the debate: the capture CONTENT correctness is unvalidated. The loader proves id-SETS match per batch; it is blind to a field-level shift where every id is right and every name is on the wrong id. Mitigations agreed: a 5-record human spot check before the load, plus three statistical post-load checks (empty/garbage titles, URL origin mismatch, non-unique ids) — a systematic shift drives one to near 100 percent.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-25T14:28:54Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T12:52:46Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"From the independent Codex review of PR #667 (merged as ca2eea2), 2026-08-10, verified against source by a second agent. None blocked the merge. Ranked by the reviewing agent AND the authoring agent as listed.\n\n**1. MEDIUM, rank FIRST — the one-directional co-presence rule does not COMPEL every outstanding fix.**\n`scripts/production_migration_guard.py:281-283` — `if create not in chosen: continue`. Once the CREATE is already applied, an allowlist naming only SOME of its fixes passes. Concretely: with `20260810030000` (Warner) applied, an allowlist of `[20260810110000]` ALONE passes, leaving `20260810120000` unapplied — production would hold the wrong read claim and `service_role` would keep INSERT. Recovery is still possible, so this is not \"lets an unsafe state through\" in the strong sense; the guard simply does not force the complete repair in one run.\n\nFix, and it must preserve the one-directional recovery design: make the rule LEDGER-AWARE in `preflight_batch` (which already holds `remote`) rather than in `parse_allowlist` (which does not). Rule shape: *if the create is applied OR selected, every fix not already applied must be selected.* Paramount and NBCU have one fix each so they are unaffected today; Warner has two, which is why it surfaced there.\n\n**2. LOW, latent not live — extend the archaic-body refusal to a bare `do '...'`.**\nThe lexer fix blanks non-regclass literals. `ARCHAIC_BODY_AS_RE` requires `\bas\\s+'` and `CREATE_ROUTINE_RE` requires a `create|alter function|procedure` header, so a bare `do 'BEGIN ... END'` matches NEITHER and its contents are invisible to preflight. A sweep of `supabase/migrations/` for `do '` returns ZERO occurrences, so this is latent. One-line extension of the existing refusal.\n\n**3. LOW, near-theoretical — tighten the `::regclass` literal parse.**\n`production_migration_guard.py:632` returns the whole literal to the general scanner when `::regclass` follows, so the kept text is scanned by `CREATE_RES` as well as `REFERENCE_RES`. A literal whose contents read like `create table a.b` would register a PHANTOM CREATION and suppress a real reference — the permissive direction. Exploiting it needs a live relation literally named something containing `create table`; the accidental version needs an object name containing `create table` or `from`. Real-world probability negligible. Fix: parse the regclass literal separately, validate against the identifier grammar, record the one dependency, then blank.\n\n**Confirmed NOT a hole, recorded so nobody re-raises it:** the regclass exception cannot hide a dependency by OMISSION — keeping a literal only ever ADDS matched text. The only permissive path is the phantom-CREATE above.\n\n**Also recorded:** the canary migration 20260810140000 now contains a `do $$ ... $$` self-check block, which is itself an instance of the documented preflight blind spot (§5.1-A). It is safe there — it references only the table created three statements earlier — but it is an example of the gap living inside the file that demonstrates the lane.\nFrom the independent Codex review of PR #667 (merged as ca2eea2), 2026-08-10, verified against source by a second agent. None blocked the merge. Ranked by the reviewing agent AND the authoring agent as listed.\n\n**1. MEDIUM, rank FIRST — the one-directional co-presence rule does not COMPEL every outstanding fix.**\n`scripts/production_migration_guard.py:281-283` — `if create not in chosen: continue`. Once the CREATE is already applied, an allowlist naming only SOME of its fixes passes. Concretely: with `20260810030000` (Warner) applied, an allowlist of `[20260810110000]` ALONE passes, leaving `20260810120000` unapplied — production would hold the wrong read claim and `service_role` would keep INSERT. Rule shape: *if the create is applied OR selected, every fix not already applied must be selected.* Paramount and NBCU have one fix each so they are unaffected today; Warner has two, which is why it surfaced there.\n\n**2. {"body":"From the independent Codex review of PR #668 (merged as 6a63af1), 2026-08-10. All three verified against source by a second agent. None blocked the merge; all three harden a loader whose stated contract is \"never a silent partial\".\n\n**1. MEDIUM — no CSV header validation anywhere.** `tools/sync-warner-starlabs.mjs:220-229`, `csvToObjects` takes row 0 as headers verbatim and never checks them. The only shape check is `if (!rows.length)`. A file with renamed, reordered, missing, duplicated or extra columns loads silently as objects with the wrong keys. Truncation is largely caught by the database `expected_row_count` assert and an LFS pointer would fail on row count, but COLUMN IDENTITY is unverified. Fix: an ordered expected-header list per file, checked before any database call.\n\n**2. MEDIUM — `git show` does not guarantee a regular blob.** `sync-warner-starlabs.mjs:326-338`. A symlink entry (mode 120000) returns the link TARGET TEXT; a tree returns a listing; a gitlink returns a commit rendering. Any of those could parse to one or more rows and pass. Fix: `git ls-tree -z` requiring exactly one result at mode 100644, then `git cat-file blob`. Note the clean-status and pinned-HEAD checks are not load-bearing here, since content comes from `git show <commit>:` regardless of worktree state.\n\n**3. LOW — replace refs.** `git show` honours `refs/replace/*`, which neither `git rev-parse HEAD` nor `git status` reveals. Requires write access to the private capture repo, so the threat model is narrow. One-word fix: set `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` in the `git()` helper env at lines 273-279.\n\nAlso recorded, cosmetic, in `buildChunks` (lines 350-388): `JSON.stringify(row).length` counts UTF-16 code units not UTF-8 bytes so non-ASCII licensor names undercount (use `Buffer.byteLength`); a single row larger than `maxBytes` is admitted because the byte test is guarded by `batch.length &&`; and the running counter overcounts by exactly one unit, conservatively. All three are harmless given the measurement proved there is no hard body ceiling to breach.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T13:38:00Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T12:34:42Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":671,"title":"Warner loader hardening: CSV header validation, git blob-mode check, and replace-ref suppression","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:49Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/671"},
{"body":"Recorded 2026-08-10 by orchestrator 52cd0e78 (marker #660), after a real near-miss caught by hand.\n\nTWO agents were dispatched in the same session and BOTH ended up authoring a migration at version 20260810130000. The orchestrator allocated it to one and forgot to allocate anything to the other, which then picked a sensible next number. Caught only because the orchestrator read the file list of an open PR.\n\nWhy nothing else would have caught it:\n\n- Guard A (duplicate versions, scripts/check-sql.sh) only ever sees ONE branch file list at a time. Both branches were green in isolation.\n- The `Cross-PR object collision` required check compares OBJECT names. The two migrations shared no objects, so it correctly passed.\n- `scripts/check-dispatch-collision.mjs` exited 0 for the same reason: it compares objects, not versions.\n\nSo version allocation is an axis NO current mechanical check covers across branches. It is enforced only by the orchestrator remembering, and the consequence of forgetting is the worst failure mode this repo has: Supabase keys its ledger on the 14-digit version ALONE, so two files sharing a version means one is NEVER APPLIED while the ledger reports success. It has already happened twice (20260722220000 and 20260728160000).\n\nNote that `--allocate-version` was withdrawn on 2026-08-07 precisely because it never reserved anything — it read versions in use and printed a suggestion, so two orchestrators in the same minute got the same number. Withdrawing it was right; it left the gap open.\n\nWhat would close it: an ATOMIC reservation. The obvious shape is that the collision checker acquires the version at the same moment it acquires the object claim, recording it in the claim issue, and refuses to hand out a version already recorded in any OPEN claim. That makes allocation fail-closed and survives the orchestrator forgetting, changing machine, or dying mid-session.\n\nUntil that exists, every dispatch brief that authorises a migration MUST state its version explicitly, and the orchestrator must check open PR file lists for duplicates before merge.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-13T18:11:39Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T12:24:11Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":670,"title":"No mechanical check covers migration-version allocation across branches — a real near-miss on 2026-08-10","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:52Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/670"},
{"body":"Found by a sub-agent during dispatch on 2026-08-10 (orchestrator 52cd0e78, marker #660).\n\nClaim issue #666 was created with the `db-claim` label and a human-readable body, but WITHOUT the fenced ```db-claim block that `scripts/check-dispatch-collision.mjs` parses. The result: the checker exited UNKNOWN and refused to clear ANY dispatch, rather than reporting no collision.\n\nThis is a silent-ish failure of the collision gate. A claim that looks correct in the GitHub UI — right label, right title, sensible body — can render the gate unusable for every subsequent dispatch until someone notices and hand-edits the issue body.\n\nTwo things worth doing:\n\n1. The orchestrator skill and AGENTS.md tell a dispatcher to file the claim using a command the tool PRINTS. That printed command is a bash heredoc which does not work in PowerShell, so dispatchers routinely re-type the claim by hand and lose the fenced block. Either make the tool acquire the claim itself, or make it emit a `--body-file`-friendly artifact that cannot lose the block.\n\n2. `check-dispatch-collision.mjs` should distinguish \"no db-claim block found in an issue LABELLED db-claim\" from a generic UNKNOWN, and say so loudly, naming the offending issue number. Right now the operator sees exit 2 with no clear pointer to which issue is malformed.\n\nExit 2 is correctly fail-closed and should stay fail-closed. The problem is diagnosability and the ease of creating a malformed claim, not the exit code.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T13:38:04Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T12:23:01Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":669,"title":"A claim issue without the fenced db-claim block makes the collision gate unusable, with no clear pointer to the offender","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:55Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/669"},

{"body":"## The outcome needed\n\nLicensor art-library extracts must land in the shared Supabase database instead of\nliving as CSV files in a private repo. The owner's instruction, 2026-08-10:\n\n> \"we have to start writing everything to the database in supabase.com, not keeping\n> it in a repo\"\n\nThis is a request for the orchestrator to decide the shape and dispatch it. No schema\nis proposed here.\n\n## Why now — the repo storage has actually broken\n\nThe current Disney DCP Vault extract is a single CSV that has just crossed **50 MB**\nand triggered GitHub's large-file warning. GitHub's hard limit is 100 MB.\n\n- The crawl is at **~157,000 rows and is not finished** (23 of 34 jobs).\n- Checkpoints are committed every ~25 minutes, so each one stores **another full\n  50 MB copy** in git history. That repo is already 40 MB packed and climbing fast.\n- Compressed the same file is 1.7 MB, so compression would buy time — but it is a\n  workaround for using git as a datastore, which is the actual problem.\n\nA row-store makes the size question disappear and makes the data queryable, which is\nthe point of collecting it.\n\n## Volumes and shape (no licensor data included — see confidentiality below)\n\n| Thing | Scale |\n|---|---|\n| Asset rows, one licensor, in progress | ~157,000 and rising |\n| Style-guide folders | ~1,300 observed so far |\n| A second licensor extract | already exists, separate session |\n| A third licensor extract | already exists, separate session |\n| Per-asset metadata phase | approved but **not started** — will add character and property link rows per asset |\n\nGrain that matters, established by evidence this week:\n\n- The asset path is the unique key. **File name is NOT unique** (collisions observed).\n- Style-guide source id is **nullable text** — a third of folders have no id at all,\n  and ids come in two different formats. A name must never be used as an id.\n- Property links and character links are **two independent sets per asset and must\n  never be joined to each other** for this licensor. Doing so fabricates\n  relationships the licensor never asserted (one asset carries 9 properties and 1\n  character). The property-to-character relationship legitimately comes from a\n  different portal, where it is explicitly asserted.\n- Re-scrapes are re-runnable: rows that vanish from a portal should be marked gone,\n  never hard-deleted.\n- Multiple licensors will land here, each with its own fields. Per-licensor source\n  tables were the prior direction rather than one shared table with a discriminator,\n  so that a bad re-scrape of one licensor cannot touch another's rows.\n\nThere is an existing draft design covering a two-layer model — scrapes land in an\ningest layer, promotion into curated core tables is separate and re-runnable. It\nlives in the private extract repo and **contains real licensor names, so it must be\nsanitised before any part of it comes here.**\n\n## Applications affected\n\nNone of the four apps read this data today, so nothing breaks on day one. The\nintended consumers are the design and product-approval workflows: finding licensed\nartwork, and reporting royalties against the right characters.\n\n## Blocking?\n\n**Not blocking right now.** The crawl continues to disk and the data is safe. It\nbecomes blocking when the CSV approaches 100 MB, which at the current rate is days,\nnot weeks. A decision on the target shape is worth having before the metadata phase\nruns, because that phase multiplies the row count.\n\n## What I know about the current schema, and how I know it\n\n**Second-hand, from documents, not read live.** I have made no database call of any\nkind this session. Prior session notes mention `core.style_guide` having room for\nonly one property per guide, which conflicts with what the portal actually shows\n(15.2% of assets appear under more than one property). Treat every schema statement\nin this issue as unverified and re-derive it.\n\n## What I have NOT done\n\nNo branch, no migration file, no `supabase` CLI, no Supabase MCP call, no psql, no\npush to preview or production, no background task chip. Nothing was created, altered\nor queried. This is a request, not a handover.\n\n## Confidentiality\n\nThe extracts are licensor confidential material held under commercial licensing\nagreements. They live in the **private** repo `u2giants/licensor-source-data`.\n`u2giants/shared-db` is intended to become public again, so **no licensor data may\nbe committed here** — no CSVs, no sample rows, no names in markdown, no PR\ndescriptions. This issue deliberately contains volumes and shapes only, and no\nproperty, character, style-guide or file names.\n\nWriting the data into the Supabase database is a different question from committing\nit to this repo, and that distinction is the whole point of the request.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T22:01:12Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T11:22:18Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":665,"title":"Land licensor art-library extracts in Supabase instead of repo CSVs (owner instruction; the 50MB CSV has hit GitHub's warning)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:53:57Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/665"},
{"body":"Found while hardening PR #663 (orchestrator 52cd0e78, marker #660), 2026-08-10.\n\nThe preview server is PostgreSQL 17.6, so the MAINTAIN privilege exists and `grant all` confers it. The standing `alter default privileges in schema plm grant all on tables to service_role` (20260710135975:14) therefore hands MAINTAIN to service_role on every new plm table.\n\nThe two revoke migrations in #663 predate that check and BOTH LEFT MAINTAIN BEHIND:\n\n- Paramount 20260810090000 revokes `truncate, trigger` only, on 23 tables.\n- NBCU 20260810080000 revokes `update, delete, truncate` only, on 16 tables. It also never revokes TRIGGER.\n\nOnly the Warner hardening migration 20260810110000 revokes MAINTAIN (and REFERENCES), on its 8 tables.\n\nSo after #663 merges, three adjacent plm landing families sit at three different privilege postures, and 39 tables carry a MAINTAIN grant nobody intended. This was out of scope for the agent that found it, which held claims on the Warner tables only.\n\nThis is more evidence for #649: the fix belongs at the schema level, once, not per family. Anyone writing that fix must read #663 first, because the baseline is uneven in three directions now (MAINTAIN, TRIGGER, REFERENCES), not one.\n\nAlso worth asserting in the general fix: NBCU 20260810080000:94 self-asserts only UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/SELECT/INSERT, so TRIGGER, REFERENCES and MAINTAIN pass unexamined and the migration proves less than it appears to.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-10T23:27:32Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T04:02:11Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":664,"title":"39 plm tables carry an unintended MAINTAIN grant: the Paramount and NBCU revokes predate the PG17 check","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:54:00Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/664"},

{"body":"## Outcome needed\n\nClose the schema-wide privilege hole in `plm`, and own the general fix — right now nobody does.\n\n`ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO service_role` means every table created in `plm` is handed UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE at CREATE TABLE time. `plm.erp_*` still carries them. Two agents fixed only their own tables.\n\n⚠️ TRUNCATE does not fire row triggers, so any immutability guarantee built on row triggers is bypassable by the exact role importers run as.\n\n**Detail:** `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-10T0030Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-nine-agent-fan-out.md` and `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-10T0130Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-addendum-late-findings.md`. The `admin_config` row it claims to fall back from has never existed, so this key has served every ColdLion call PopDAM has ever made.\n\n**Rotation order matters:**\n\n1. Create the missing `COLDLION_API_KEY` row in PopDAM's `admin_config`.\n2. Rotate the key at ColdLion.\n3. {"body":"## Why this is high priority\r\n\r\nWe now have completed source extracts from FOUR licensors — Disney OPA, Warner STARLABS, Paramount Creative Library and NBCU Creative Asset Factory. **Nobody has yet compared what those licensors say they own against what our database says.** That comparison has never been run.\r\n\r\nThis matters because licensor attribution drives royalty reporting. Until it is run we do not know whether our property-to-licensor assignments are correct, and we have no defensible number for how many are wrong.\r\n\r\n## What this workstream is NOT — read this before quoting any figure\r\n\r\nThree separate things have been conflated in conversation and must not be again:\r\n\r\n1. **The 9,973 figure is PopDAM asset rows, not ColdLion SKUs and not properties.** Rows in `public.assets` whose `licensor_id` FK disagrees with the `licensor_code` on the same row. Root cause is PopDAM deriving the licensor from a fixed folder position invalidated by a folder reorganisation (`_shared/metadata-derivation.ts:98-105`). PopDAM's bug, PopDAM's data. Tracked separately.\r\n2. **ColdLion cannot misattribute a property to a licensor, because it never attributes one.** Verified across all 614 mirrored records on 2026-08-09: the complete field set is `companyCode, createdTime, createdUser, divisionCode, itemNoCode, mgCategory, mgCode, mgCode2, mgDesc, mgTypeCode, modTime, modUser`. No owner field. `mgCategory` empty on every row. MG05 is a licensor code-to-name dictionary; MG06 is a property code-to-name dictionary; there is no link between them. This is already recorded in AGENTS.md 6.6.\r\n3. **The four scrapes have not been compared to anything.** No figure exists. Do not carry one forward.\r\n\r\n## The work\r\n\r\n1. Establish, per licensor, what the source extract asserts about property ownership, using only DIRECT source records. Inferred links (co-occurrence on a shared asset) are forbidden and are indistinguishable from real ones once loaded.\r\n2. Compare against `core.property` / `core.licensor`.\r\n3. Produce a per-licensor reconciliation: agrees, disagrees, present in source but not in our data, present in our data but not in source.\r\n4. Absence in a source is NOT a delete instruction and NOT proof of nonexistence. Each extract reflects POP Creations' licensed account view, not the licensor's worldwide catalogue.\r\n5. Every disagreement is an owner decision. Agents present evidence and decide nothing.\r\n\r\n## Blocked on\r\n\r\nAll four landing schemas must merge and be promoted before a full comparison is possible. Current state as of 2026-08-09:\r\n\r\n- **Disney OPA** — on main, loaded to preview. Five migrations NOT promoted to production (issue #579).\r\n- **Warner STARLABS** — PR #637, built and green, never applied to preview.\r\n- **Paramount** — PR #636, built, applied to preview.\r\n- **NBCU** — PR #634, built, proven on preview, 160 tests passing.\r\n\r\nAll four are caught in the merge-ordering deadlock described in `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-10T0030Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-nine-agent-fan-out.md`.\r\n\r\n## Traps that will bite whoever picks this up\r\n\r\n- **Warner exposes Franchise and Property as SEPARATE levels.** Only the Product Property-to-Character catalogue is a direct Warner record.\r\n- **Paramount publishes no direct property-to-franchise pair.** `plm.pmt_property_franchise_evidence` is co-occurrence only and is hard-checked so it can never claim otherwise.\r\n- **`core.property` has no Exorcist row at all** — zero rows with code `EX`, zero named like Exorcist. The gap may be wider than the mismatches.\r\n- Sub-licensors stay flat per AGENTS.md 6.13 ruling 5. Desperate and FanCreations are stored as ordinary licensors, so any report answering \"who is the licensor\" returns the sub-licensor, not the brand owner.\r\n\r\nFiled by orchestrator session 8b3f21c4, marker #622, on the owner's instruction 2026-08-09.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: curated-master-data\nroute: curated-master-data-governance\npriority: 700\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-09-03T20:22:23Z","createdAt":"2026-08-10T02:44:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":640,"title":"HIGH PRIORITY: reconcile the four licensor source extracts against core.property and core.licensor","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:43:08Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/640"},

{"body":"# Build-ready specification: Paramount Creative Library landing schema and complete metadata import\n\n## Goal\n\nCreate a permanent, capture-versioned landing area in Supabase for the complete Paramount Creative Library metadata capture held in the private `u2giants/licensor-source-data` repository.\n\nThis work must store every captured entity, relationship, scope decision, batch result, capture log, and malformed source value. It must not store creative file bytes, previews, PDFs, ZIP contents, images, videos, credentials, cookies, tokens, authorization headers, or signed download URLs.\n\n## Confidentiality boundary\n\nThis repository and this issue are public.\n\n- Put schema, loader code, views, functions, and invented contract fixtures in `shared-db`.\n- Keep every real Paramount title, property, entity name, source ID, asset ID, filename, and relationship row in the private source repository and Supabase only.\n- Do not include real source rows in migrations, tests, issue comments, PR descriptions, commit messages, or CI output.\n- Load real rows at runtime from the private repository.\n- The source reflects POP Creations' licensed account and current library view. It is not Paramount's worldwide catalogue.\n- Presence is evidence. Absence is not a delete instruction or proof of nonexistence.\n\n## Verified capture contract\n\nThe private manifest for the completed capture reports:\n\n| Population | Expected |\n| --- | ---: |\n| Licensed business titles | 26 |\n| Titles matched to current portal properties | 21 |\n| Titles absent from the current portal view | 5 |\n| Exact licensed Property selections | 33 |\n| Property search-result rows | 25,858 |\n| Unique authorized portal assets | 25,790 |\n| Full-metadata batches | 258 |\n| Properties found in full metadata | 60 |\n| Franchises | 18 |\n| Characters | 52 |\n| Collections / style guides | 426 |\n| Brands | 7 |\n| Asset-property links | 26,451 |\n| Asset-franchise links | 25,116 |\n| Asset-character links | 8,558 |\n| Asset-style-guide links | 27,880 |\n| Asset-brand links | 25,983 |\n| Explicit property-character links | 52 |\n| Explicit property-style-guide links | 426 |\n| Property-franchise co-occurrence findings | 51 |\n| Authorized-property search-context links | 25,858 |\n| Preserved malformed relationship values | 4 |\n\nThe portal-wide current-library count observed by the capture was 46,556 asset records. The authorized population is 25,790 unique asset records after deduplicating 68 overlaps between exact Property searches.\n\nExpected values must come from the private manifest at runtime. Do not hard-code this capture's counts into permanent database checks. Use these values as acceptance fixtures for this one import.\n\n## Architecture ruling\n\nAll raw Paramount source data belongs in dedicated `plm.pmt_*` tables.\n\nDo not load raw rows into:\n\n- `core.*`\n- Disney `plm.opa_*`\n- legacy `public.*`\n- a shared multi-licensor landing table\n\nThe completed capture now proves the deferred franchise, brand, collection, authorized-title, and asset-link structures exist. Build the complete structure below. Landing and reconciliation to `core.*` remain separate jobs.\n\n## Shared table rules\n\nEvery source-data and relationship table must:\n\n1. Carry `capture_id uuid not null`.\n2. Reference `plm.pmt_capture(capture_id)`.\n3. Preserve source strings exactly.\n4. Key and link by source IDs, never names.\n5. Use composite keys and composite foreign keys containing `capture_id`.\n6. Retain every completed capture permanently.\n7. Never overwrite an older capture with a refresh.\n8. Reject relationships whose endpoints are absent from the same capture.\n9. Carry `source_hash text not null` and `imported_at timestamptz not null default now()`.\n10. Use `raw jsonb` only for source fields not represented by typed columns.\n11. Make source fields immutable after capture completion.\n12. Use `bigint` for portal numeric IDs and byte sizes.\n13. Store asset IDs as lowercase 40-character hexadecimal text.\n14. Use `on delete restrict` for completed capture evidence. Do not cascade-delete completed captures.\n\n## Required tables\n\n### 1. `plm.pmt_capture`\n\nOne row per scrape.\n\nColumns:\n\n- `capture_id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()`\n- `status text not null`: `loading | validating | complete | failed | abandoned`\n- `capture_kind text not null`: `full | targeted | test`\n- `source_system text not null default 'paramount_creative_library'`\n- `source_url text not null`, origin only\n- `library_name text not null`\n- `started_at timestamptz not null`\n- `completed_at timestamptz null`\n- `captured_by text not null`\n- `private_source_commit text not null`\n- `manifest_sha256 text not null`\n- `portal_global_asset_count integer not null`\n- `licensed_title_count integer not null`\n- `licensed_property_selection_count integer not null`\n- `property_result_row_count integer not null`\n- `unique_asset_count integer not null`\n- `metadata_batch_count integer not null`\n- `failure_count integer not null`\n- `anomaly_count integer not null`\n- `notes text null`\n- `created_at timestamptz not null default now()`\n- `updated_at timestamptz not null default now()`\n\nChecks:\n\n- Counts are non-negative.\n- Complete requires `completed_at`, manifest hash, source commit, zero unresolved failures, and successful validation.\n- Failed, test, loading, abandoned, and targeted captures never become the latest complete full capture.\n\n### 2. `plm.pmt_capture_batch`\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `batch_number integer`\n- `expected_asset_count integer`\n- `returned_asset_count integer`\n- `first_asset_id text`\n- `last_asset_id text`\n- `http_status integer`\n- `content_was_json boolean`\n- `requested_ids_sha256 text`\n- `returned_ids_sha256 text`\n- `id_sets_matched boolean`\n- `complete boolean`\n- `failure_message text null`\n- `captured_at timestamptz`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, batch_number)`.\n\nA complete batch requires at most 100 requested IDs, HTTP 200, JSON, equal counts, and exact requested/returned ID-set equality.\n\n### 3. `plm.pmt_authorized_title`\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `authorized_title_key text`\n- `authorized_title_name text`\n- `capture_status text`: `captured | licensed_but_not_present_in_current_portal_view`\n- `resolved_property_count integer`\n- `unique_asset_count integer`\n- `full_metadata_count integer`\n- `notes text null`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, authorized_title_key)`.\n\nAll 26 rights-list titles must be rows. The five unavailable titles must remain present with zero counts and the portal-view warning. Their absence must not be interpreted as unlicensed.\n\n### 4. `plm.pmt_authorized_title_property`\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `authorized_title_key text`\n- `property_source_id bigint`\n- `paramount_property_name text`\n- `reported_asset_count integer`\n- `mapping_status text`\n- `notes text null`\n- `source_evidence text not null default 'exact_property_selection'`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, authorized_title_key, property_source_id)`.\n\nFK both endpoints within the same capture.\n\n### 5. `plm.pmt_property`\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `property_source_id bigint`\n- `property_name text`\n- `is_licensed_selection boolean`\n- `core_property_id uuid null references core.property(id) on delete restrict`\n- `resolution_status text default 'unresolved'`\n- `resolution_reason text null`\n- `resolved_at timestamptz null`\n- `resolved_by text null`\n- `raw jsonb`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, property_source_id)`.\n\nAllowed resolution values: `unresolved | matched | ambiguous | no_match | rejected`.\n\nStore all properties carried by authorized assets, not only the exact Property selections.\n\n### 6. `plm.pmt_franchise`\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `franchise_source_id bigint`\n- `franchise_name text`\n- `raw jsonb`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, franchise_source_id)`.\n\n### 7. `plm.pmt_character`\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `character_source_id bigint`\n- `character_name text`\n- `core_character_id uuid null references core.character(id) on delete restrict`\n- reconciliation fields matching property\n- `raw jsonb`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, character_source_id)`.\n\nThe completed capture found no character source ID assigned to multiple properties in the explicit cascading field. Key by source character ID, not property-character or name. Never merge by name.\n\n### 8. `plm.pmt_collection`\n\nStores the portal concept called Collection. These values represent named style guides and related creative collections.\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `collection_source_id bigint`\n- `collection_name text`\n- `paramount_term text`\n- `raw jsonb`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, collection_source_id)`.\n\nDo not duplicate these into a second source table named style guide. Provide a style-guide-named API view.\n\n### 9. `plm.pmt_brand`\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `brand_source_id bigint`\n- `brand_name text`\n- `raw jsonb`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, brand_source_id)`.\n\n### 10. `plm.pmt_asset`\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `asset_id text`\n- `asset_name text`\n- `date_imported timestamptz null`\n- `date_last_updated timestamptz null`\n- `content_size_bytes bigint not null`\n- `content_type text not null`\n- `mime_type text not null`\n- `asset_version integer not null`\n- `raw jsonb`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, asset_id)`.\n\nChecks:\n\n- `asset_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'`\n- size and version non-negative\n\nOne row means one portal asset record. A ZIP is one asset record. Do not store creative bytes.\n\n### 11. `plm.pmt_asset_property`\n\nColumns: `capture_id, asset_id, property_source_id, source_evidence, source_hash, imported_at`.\n\nPK: `(capture_id, asset_id, property_source_id)`.\n\nEvidence must be `full_asset_metadata`.\n\n### 12. `plm.pmt_asset_franchise`\n\nSame shape, with `franchise_source_id`.\n\nPK: `(capture_id, asset_id, franchise_source_id)`.\n\n### 13. `plm.pmt_asset_character`\n\nSame shape, with `character_source_id`.\n\nPK: `(capture_id, asset_id, character_source_id)`.\n\nThis answers which asset references a character.\n\n### 14. `plm.pmt_asset_collection`\n\nSame shape, with `collection_source_id`.\n\nPK: `(capture_id, asset_id, collection_source_id)`.\n\nThis is the direct asset-to-style-guide link.\n\n### 15. `plm.pmt_asset_brand`\n\nSame shape, with `brand_source_id`.\n\nPK: `(capture_id, asset_id, brand_source_id)`.\n\n### 16. `plm.pmt_property_character`\n\nExplicit cascading pairs only.\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `property_source_id bigint`\n- `character_source_id bigint`\n- `source_evidence text`\n- `evidence_asset_count integer`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, property_source_id, character_source_id)`.\n\nEvidence must be `explicit_cascading_pair`. Never manufacture this pair from separate metadata fields.\n\n### 17. `plm.pmt_property_collection`\n\nExplicit cascading property-to-collection/style-guide pairs only.\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `property_source_id bigint`\n- `collection_source_id bigint`\n- `source_evidence text`\n- `evidence_asset_count integer`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, property_source_id, collection_source_id)`.\n\nEvidence must be `explicit_cascading_pair`.\n\n### 18. `plm.pmt_property_franchise_evidence`\n\nCo-occurrence evidence only. Do not call this a direct relationship table.\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `property_source_id bigint`\n- `franchise_source_id bigint`\n- `evidence_kind text not null default 'asset_cooccurrence_not_direct_pair'`\n- `evidence_asset_count integer`\n- `is_direct_source_relationship boolean not null default false`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, property_source_id, franchise_source_id)`.\n\nHard checks must require the default evidence kind and `false`.\n\n### 19. `plm.pmt_authorized_property_asset`\n\nRecords exact Property-search context used to establish authorized scope.\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `licensed_property_source_id bigint`\n- `asset_id text`\n- `source_evidence text not null default 'exact_property_search_result'`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, licensed_property_source_id, asset_id)`.\n\nThis is intentionally separate from `pmt_asset_property`: one is exact search context, the other is full asset metadata.\n\n### 20. `plm.pmt_relationship_anomaly`\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `anomaly_id bigint generated always as identity`\n- `asset_id text`\n- `relationship_field text`\n- `raw_value text`\n- `action text`\n- `details text null`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, anomaly_id)`.\n\nPreserve malformed values. Never infer the missing endpoint or insert an excluded row into a valid link table.\n\n### 21. `plm.pmt_property_capture_log`\n\n- `capture_id uuid`\n- `property_source_id bigint`\n- `property_name text`\n- `reported_asset_count integer`\n- `captured_asset_count integer`\n- `page_count integer`\n- `complete boolean`\n- `failure_message text null`\n- common provenance fields\n\nPK: `(capture_id, property_source_id)`.\n\nA complete row requires reported and captured search rows to match, all pages captured, no failure, and full metadata for all deduplicated assets.\n\n## Foreign keys and indexes\n\nEvery relationship endpoint must use a same-capture composite FK.\n\nAdd reverse indexes for:\n\n- asset name, MIME type, content type, and import date\n- every entity name\n- every right-hand relationship ID\n- title/property reverse lookup\n- authorized-property/asset reverse lookup\n- capture status and completion\n- reconciliation status and nullable core IDs\n\nExact source storage remains authoritative. Search indexes must not alter source strings.\n\n## Loader\n\nCreate `tools/sync-paramount-creative-library.mjs`, following the existing private-source runtime import pattern.\n\nIt must:\n\n1. Require an explicit private source path and manifest.\n2. Hash files before connecting.\n3. Never print source rows or secrets.\n4. Begin a capture as `loading`.\n5. Stream bounded chunks.\n6. Load parents before links.\n7. Validate every chunk response.\n8. Record all metadata batches and Property capture logs.\n9. Run database-side validation.\n10. Mark complete only after exact validation.\n11. Leave failed work visible as `failed`.\n12. Safely resume the same incomplete capture.\n13. Refuse to change a completed capture when the manifest differs.\n14. Never write creative bytes.\n15. Never write `core.*`.\n\nLoad order:\n\n1. capture\n2. batches\n3. titles\n4. properties\n5. franchises\n6. characters\n7. collections\n8. brands\n9. assets\n10. title/property mappings\n11. asset links\n12. explicit property links\n13. franchise evidence\n14. authorized search context\n15. Property capture logs\n16. anomalies\n17. validation\n18. finalize\n\n## Required functions\n\n- `plm.begin_pmt_capture(...)`\n- bounded typed loaders or `plm.load_pmt_capture_chunk(...)`\n- `plm.validate_pmt_capture(uuid)`\n- `plm.finalize_pmt_capture(uuid)`\n- `plm.fail_pmt_capture(uuid, text)`\n\nUse an advisory lock so two Paramount imports cannot finalize together.\n\nRevoke execution from `public`, `anon`, and ordinary authenticated users. Grant import execution only to `service_role`.\n\n## Finalization checks\n\nFinalization must verify manifest expected versus actual counts for every population listed above, plus:\n\n- every link endpoint exists in the same capture\n- no asset lacks full metadata\n- no duplicate asset ID exists within a capture\n- all batches passed exact ID-set validation\n- all exact Property captures are complete\n- all rights-list titles remain represented, including unavailable rows\n- captured title unique counts equal full-metadata counts\n- search-result rows may exceed unique assets because Property scopes overlap\n- malformed pairs remain anomalies\n- no co-occurrence row becomes a direct relationship\n- no source row reached `core.*`\n- manifest hash matches loaded files\n\n## Refresh shrink guard\n\nCompare a future full capture only to the latest complete Paramount full capture.\n\nInitial refusal rules:\n\n- Rights-list count changes require owner approval.\n- Unique assets below 90% of prior complete capture fail.\n- Any relationship population below 85% fails.\n- A previously populated licensed title dropping to zero fails.\n- Missing batches fail.\n- Any entity population dropping to zero fails.\n- Increased anomalies are reported loudly.\n\nAn override requires reason, operator, time, old count, new count, approver, and audit row.\n\n## API views\n\nAll views use `security_invoker = true`.\n\nRequired:\n\n1. `api.pmt_latest_capture`: latest complete full capture only.\n2. `api.pmt_assets`: business-friendly asset metadata and relationships. Avoid a Cartesian-product join; use arrays or separate relationship views.\n3. `api.pmt_style_guides`: collection source IDs/names exposed with business style-guide wording, linked properties, asset count, character count, capture time.\n4. `api.pmt_properties`: licensed-selection flag, mapped business titles, asset/character/style-guide counts, franchise evidence, optional core reconciliation.\n5. `api.pmt_characters`: explicit properties, assets, style guides, optional core reconciliation.\n6. `api.pmt_authorized_title_summary`: all rights-list rows, including unavailable rows with zero counts.\n7. `api.pmt_capture_health`: expected/actual counts, failures, anomalies, shrink result, manifest hash, source commit, completion.\n8. `api.pmt_property_franchise_evidence`: always exposes non-direct evidence fields and never implies authority.\n\n## Security\n\nFor all `plm.pmt_*` tables:\n\n- Enable RLS.\n- Revoke all from `anon`.\n- Service role gets controlled import rights.\n- Approved authenticated sales/licensing/design/admin roles may read under the established shared-db policy.\n- Ordinary authenticated users cannot mutate raw landing data.\n- Prefer API views for application reads.\n- Never expose credentials, session data, signed URLs, or creative content.\n\nAdd table/view comments stating the entitlement scope, confidentiality, presence/absence semantics, and public-Git prohibition.\n\n## Canonical reconciliation boundary\n\nAllowed now:\n\n- nullable core property/character links\n- resolution state and notes\n- read-only reconciliation views\n\nForbidden during source import:\n\n- creating, renaming, merging, reparenting, deactivating, or deleting canonical records\n- changing licensor assignments\n- treating source absence as deletion\n- populating canonical relationship tables automatically\n\nCanonical promotion requires a separate reviewed workstream.\n\n## Contract tests\n\nUse invented rows only. Prove:\n\n1. All objects exist with correct keys.\n2. All relationship FKs are capture-scoped.\n3. Completed evidence does not cascade-delete.\n4. Anonymous users cannot read.\n5. Approved roles can read approved surfaces.\n6. Authenticated users cannot mutate landing tables.\n7. Service role can load an incomplete capture.\n8. Incomplete/failed/test captures never appear as latest.\n9. Orphan links cannot finalize.\n10. Manifest mismatch cannot finalize.\n11. Incomplete batches cannot finalize.\n12. Completed captures are immutable.\n13. New captures do not overwrite old ones.\n14. Unavailable rights rows remain visible with zero counts.\n15. Collections expose as style guides without duplication.\n16. Malformed values remain anomalies.\n17. Co-occurrence never becomes a direct relationship.\n18. Asset aggregation does not multiply relationship rows.\n19. No importer path writes `core.*`.\n20. No real source row appears in public migrations, fixtures, logs, commits, PRs, or issues.\n\n## Delivery gates\n\n1. Run the dispatch collision check before writing.\n2. Use new migration timestamps.\n3. Keep real data out of public Git.\n4. Build schema, functions, views, loader, and tests.\n5. Run SQL guards.\n6. Prove the live project ref immediately before every database-changing command.\n7. Apply and test schema on preview first.\n8. Use invented preview fixtures.\n9. Run contract tests.\n10. Follow the shared-db PR and merge protocol.\n11. Promote schema to production only through the approved bounded process.\n12. Verify production objects, not only the migration ledger.\n13. Run the private loader against production only after schema verification.\n14. Verify exact production counts and API results.\n15. Record capture UUID, manifest hash, private source commit, migration versions, project ref, and verification results without publishing source rows.\n\n## Definition of done\n\n- Production has one complete full Paramount capture.\n- Every manifest count matches exactly.\n- Every direct relationship is present.\n- Co-occurrence is clearly non-direct.\n- All malformed values remain preserved.\n- Every licensed-title row is represented, including unavailable rows.\n- Latest views use only the newest complete full capture.\n- No real Paramount source row exists in public Git or public logs.\n- No creative bytes are stored.\n- No source importer wrote `core.*`.\n- Security and contract tests pass.\n- The final report quotes the exact Supabase project reference observed immediately before production mutations.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T22:00:49Z","createdAt":"2026-08-09T23:23:07Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":623,"title":"BUILD: Complete Paramount Creative Library landing schema and private metadata import","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:54:35Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/623"},

{"body":"**Briefing:** `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-09T2243Z-al8960ofc-claude-orchestrator-production-lane-unblocked.md` §5C and §6 step 1. Read it; this issue is the pointer, not the detail.\n\n## Outcome needed\n\nThe `production-dry-run` job in `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml` must pass a **bounded** `--include-all` to the Supabase CLI. **This is the single thing blocking plan item A2**, and the production lane has never been proven end to end because of it.\n\n## Why this is safe, and say so in the PR\n\nThe bound is **the filesystem, not the flag**. `prepare()` in `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` keeps exactly `remote ∪ allowlist` on disk and **deletes everything else**, so `--include-all` can only sweep files already on the allowlist. **33 of the 50 missing migrations sort BELOW the ledger head and the CLI refuses them without it.**\n\n`AGENTS.md` §5.1(4) already licenses this. The plan's old constraint 4 said \"never\" and was **incomplete shorthand**; it has been corrected. Write the reasoning into the PR so a later reader does not mistake this for a relaxation.\n\n⚠️ **Do NOT weaken any guard to make a run pass.** Standing rule. It must not create parallel orders.\n- Coordinate any PLM item, order, line, or style-item bridge work with `fix_schema_for_api.md`.\n\n## Intended write set\n\n- `plm.production_order`\n- `plm.production_order_line`\n- `plm.production_order_source_ref`\n- `plm.production_order_line_source_ref`\n- `api.dam_order_list`\n- `public.create_dam_order`\n- `public.update_dam_order`\n- `public.link_dam_order_line`\n- `public.order_list_user_views`\n\n## Collision evidence from 2026-08-09\n\nThe required command exited 0 and found zero claims/open PR inputs, but explicitly reported that table, column, index, grant, and every ALTER form were NOT CHECKED. Open PR inspection returned no open PRs. This is evidence only, not clearance.\n\nThe coordinator must manually confirm the unchecked object classes, file the `db-claim`, choose a unique migration timestamp, and begin Step 1 from current `origin/main` at or after `2162e95`.\n\n## Source-profile facts that affect schema\n\n- 12,328 populated Google business rows\n- 8,412 direct-SKU rows and 3,899 assortment-only rows\n- valid assortment rows expand to 15,816 components\n- 130 blank-PO rows must remain separate\n- 449 direct/component item matches are ambiguous\n- header conflicts must be quarantined, never resolved by first/majority value\n- all 48 columns are mapped in the completed audit\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T00:54:52Z","createdAt":"2026-08-09T22:43:18Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## The gap\n\nPromoting the ~47-migration backlog to production moves the database through **46 intermediate states**. Five live applications — PopDAM, PopCRM, DesignFlow PLM, PopPIM and monitor — are reading it the whole time.\n\n**Every artifact produced so far reasons about the DATABASE's consistency. None reasons about the APPLICATIONS' tolerance of those intermediate states.** Found by Codex during the PR #610 debate and accepted as genuinely new.\n\n## Why it matters more than it sounds\n\nThe two candidate strategies both depend on the answer, in opposite directions:\n\n- **One big push** — a single short window where the database is half-updated. Shortest exposure, but no chosen resting point.\n- **Sub-batching** — deliberately creates **several sanctioned half-promoted resting points, potentially hours apart**, each watched by five live apps. This is why sub-batching was downgraded from \"mitigation\" to \"conditional, and the condition is expensive\": it must not be adopted unless **every boundary is proven app-compatible BEFORE production work begins**. That is a precondition, not a follow-up.\n\nWithout a declared contract there is no way to judge either option, and \"it applied cleanly\" would say nothing about whether an app broke.\n\n## What is needed\n\nFor each of the five applications, a plain statement of what it can tolerate mid-promotion: a new column it does not know about, a view whose shape changed, a function replaced under it, a table that exists but is not yet populated, a value it reads going inactive.\n\nThen: which intermediate states are safe resting points, and which must never be one.\n\n## Note\n\nThis is partly a business question about what breakage is acceptable and for how long, not purely a technical one. Expect at least one part of it to need an owner decision.\n\nRelated: #609, and the canary issue on ledger transactionality. Filed by orchestrator `5e1ab3af` (marker #601).\n","closedAt":"2026-08-10T20:40:49Z","createdAt":"2026-08-09T19:06:03Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":612,"title":"Declare a safe intermediate-state contract for the five apps before any batch promotion","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:54:54Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/612"},
{"body":"## The assumption\n\nEvery recovery plan for a half-finished production promotion rests on this: **`supabase db push` writes the migration's SQL and its `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` ledger row in ONE transaction.** If true, a batch that dies at file 45 leaves a ledger that exactly describes what landed, and resuming is safe. If false, the ledger can claim a file that did not fully apply, or omit one that did, and **the 2am recovery procedure is built on sand.**\n\n## Why this is filed\n\n**Nobody has proven it.** Codex conceded the point directly: *\"'Each file is transactional' does not prove that the migration SQL and ledger update share one transaction.\"*\n\nThis repo asserts it in `docs/production-migration-lane-design-20260802.md` §3.3 and §8 **with no test, no reading of the CLI source, and no version pin.** Grok's resume procedure and Codex's own resume step both depend on it. It is the single load-bearing assumption under the entire partial-promotion story, and it is unevidenced.\n\n## What to do\n\nA **destructive canary on a disposable database** — never preview `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` (shared, mutable, holds other sessions' work) and never production:\n\n1. Stand up a disposable database whose ledger is seeded to a known state.\n2. Push a small batch whose **last file deliberately fails part-way**, after at least one successful statement.\n3. Read the ledger. Does it contain a row for the failed file? Is the partial DDL present?\n4. **Pin the exact Supabase CLI version tested**, and record it. This behaviour can change between CLI releases, so the answer has a shelf life and the version is part of the finding.\n\n## Deliverable\n\nA committed note under `docs/verification/` stating what was observed, the CLI version, and whether the resume procedure stands as written. **If the assumption is false, say so loudly** — the recovery procedure then has to be redesigned before any production apply, not after.\n\nRelated: #609. Filed by orchestrator `5e1ab3af` (marker #601) from the Codex debate on PR #610.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-10T18:30:17Z","createdAt":"2026-08-09T19:06:02Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":611,"title":"Prove (or disprove) that db push writes migration SQL and its ledger row in ONE transaction","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:54:56Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/611"},
{"body":"Three verified-but-latent defects in the SQL lexer / preflight behind `scripts/production_migration_guard.py`. Found by Grok 4.5 reviewing PR #608, reproduced and measured by a sub-agent of orchestrator session `5e1ab3af` (marker issue #601).\r\n\r\n**Do not fix these in PR #608.** They are recorded here so the guard can merge without carrying unrelated lexer work.\r\n\r\n## Why this is not urgent\r\n\r\nAll three fail in the **false-ACCEPT** direction (the guard lets something through it should question, rather than blocking something safe), and **all three have zero live exposure across all 411 migration files on `main`**. The measurements are below.\r\n\r\n## F1 — `$$` inside an unquoted identifier. High. False ACCEPT.\r\n\r\n`DOLLAR_OPEN_RE` matches the `$$` inside an identifier such as `my$$col`, latches onto the next genuine `$$`, and blanks everything between. A real hard reference silently disappears.\r\n\r\nReproduction:\r\n\r\n```\r\nbaseline (mycol):   created={plm.t, plm.f}   refs=[(plm.missing_dep,'alter table')]\r\nwith    (my$$col):  created={plm.t}          refs=[]        <- hard ref silently lost\r\n```\r\n\r\nExposure: the pattern `[A-Za-z0-9_]\\$\\$` matches **0 of 411** files.\r\n\r\nProposed fix: only treat `$tag$` as a dollar-quote opener at a token boundary, i.e. not when preceded by `[A-Za-z0-9_]`.\r\n\r\n## F2 — CREATE text inside a kept string literal. High. False ACCEPT.\r\n\r\nString literals are deliberately **kept** by `strip_sql` so that `'plm.t_id_seq'::regclass` still resolves. But `created_objects` then scans them, so CREATE text inside a literal registers a phantom object in `available`, which can satisfy a later file's dependency that production cannot actually meet.\r\n\r\nReproduction:\r\n\r\n```\r\nselect 'create table plm.ghost (id uuid)';   ->  created_objects == {plm.ghost}\r\n```\r\n\r\nExposure: **2 of 411** files contain a `'create function'` literal, but both are `command_tag` strings with no `schema.object`, so **0 phantom objects** are produced today. Both files correctly return `{public.lock_down_new_public_function_execute}`.\r\n\r\nProposed fix: blank string *contents* for the CREATE scan, and match `regclass` in a separate pass over the unblanked literals.\r\n\r\n## F5 — `available` never shrinks on DROP/RENAME. Medium. False ACCEPT.\r\n\r\n`drop table plm.old` in file N yields `created_objects == {}`, so a later `alter table plm.old` is still satisfied from the remote ledger.\r\n\r\nThis is an **architectural limit of the preflight**, not a lexer bug: the preflight models object *creation* only. Fixing it means tracking removals as negative entries against `available`, which is a design change, not a regex change.\r\n\r\n## Recorded so nobody re-proposes them\r\n\r\nTwo other findings from the same review were **withdrawn or downgraded**. Do not reopen them:\r\n\r\n- **F3 — typed literals ending in `e`, e.g. `date'2026-01-01'`.** Grok rated it Medium; it was measured working and Grok conceded it to **theoretical**. `strip_sql(\"select date'2026-01-01'; create table plm.after (id uuid);\")` is unchanged and `created_objects` correctly returns `{plm.after}`. The `E'...'` path only diverges when a backslash appears inside the literal, and a `date`/`time` constant cannot legally contain one under `standard_conforming_strings=on`.\r\n- **F4 — widening the dollar-tag regex for digit-leading tags like `$1$`.** **Withdrawn as wrong.** Dollar-quote tags follow unquoted-identifier rules and cannot start with a digit. The current `\\$([A-Za-z_]\\w*)?\\$` matches the real Postgres lexer. **Do not widen it.**\r\n\r\n## Source\r\n\r\n`.ai/reviews/20260809-pr608-apply-set-grok45.md` (committed on branch `a2-rebuild-apply-set-and-rehearsal`, PR #608).\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstate: non-structural\npriority: 250\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-16T05:44:32Z","createdAt":"2026-08-09T18:50:13Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":609,"title":"Guard lexer: three verified-but-latent false-ACCEPT defects (F1, F2, F5) - zero live exposure","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:54:59Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/609"},
