{"body":"# HANDOVER: Product Size and Product Depth Phase 1\r\n\r\n## Requested outcome\r\n\r\nComplete Phase 1 of `/worksp/popdam/plan_master_data_designflow_reference_cutover.md`: shared Product Size from the direct ColdLion MG04 feed, and shared Product Depth populated from authoritative DesignFlow `itemDepth`, including the DB Data Admin editor and safe consumer contracts.\r\n\r\n## Owner decisions already made\r\n\r\n1. Product Depth maintenance is allowed for administrators and the shared Designer role used by Carlos Corral.\r\n2. Inactive MG04 Size values remain visible on existing items but are excluded from new selections.\r\n3. DB Data Admin is the only place to add, rename, activate, or deactivate Product Depth values. The old DesignFlow editor must be retired or redirected.\r\n4. Phase 2 Packaging Type, Creative Designer, and Vendor/Factory ambiguity does not block Phase 1.\r\n\r\n## Completed evidence\r\n\r\n- Comparison evidence is on shared-db main under `docs/verification/master-data-designflow-reference-cutover-20260807/`.\r\n- Cloud SQL `designflow.\\\"itemDepth\\\"`: 121 rows; exact match with the Supabase mirror; snapshot SHA-256 `6a8dd274e380bbb12fd997d916858a75d5f6ae61872be02a92432f2a1f92c1ce`.\r\n- Direct ColdLion MG04 Size feed: 37/37 headers, one page, 530 current Size rows.\r\n- Eight historical inactive Size rows must be retained: CW001 `5B`, `8H`, `TT`; EH001 `5B`, `8T`, `ET`, `M8`, `TT`.\r\n- Nine EP001 values are Pages, not Size, and must be excluded: `114,144,168,192,288,360,504,576,672`.\r\n- Stable MG04 key: `(companyCode, divisionCode, mgTypeCode, mgCode)`. Never resolve by code alone.\r\n- Production currently has no `core.product_size`, `core.product_depth`, `api.product_size_list`, or `api.product_depth_list`.\r\n\r\n## Required database scope\r\n\r\n- Add canonical Product Size and Product Depth tables with stable UUIDs, preserved legacy source IDs/labels, lifecycle status, source references, audit history, and timestamps.\r\n- Populate Depth from all 121 authoritative `itemDepth` rows without changing legacy IDs or labels.\r\n- Build a guarded MG04 importer. Default dry-run, explicit apply, advisory lock, full pagination, count/payload/delete guards, idempotency, and loud failure.\r\n- Seed the 530 current Size rows plus the eight historical inactive Size rows. Exclude EP001 Pages.\r\n- Add picker contracts where inactive values are allowed only when already selected.\r\n- Add protected DB Data Admin mutations for Product Depth, restricted to admin and Designer, with optimistic concurrency and immutable audit evidence.\r\n- Add stable Product Size/Depth links to the PLM item contract while retaining compatibility fields until parity and rollback checks pass.\r\n- Add SQL/tool tests for permission, uniqueness, source refs, inactive behavior, importer guards/idempotency, audit, and rollback compatibility.\r\n\r\n## Workflow gates\r\n\r\n- Run the collision check and claim every written object before editing.\r\n- Use a dedicated shared-db branch and unique timestamped migrations.\r\n- Apply and prove on preview `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` first.\r\n- Open PR, pass all checks, merge it, then apply and verify production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\r\n- Return migration versions, commit SHA, PR URL, preview evidence, and production object/row-count evidence.\r\n\r\n## Consumer dependency\r\n\r\nPopDAM and DesignFlow app changes must not switch consumers until these contracts are merged and production verified. DesignFlow remains on `sandbox-albert`/`albert-2sandbox`, PRs to `develop`, Uma merges.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-18T14:59:44Z","createdAt":"2026-08-09T13:19:52Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":597,"title":"HANDOVER: Product Size and Product Depth Phase 1","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:43:27Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/597"},
{"body":"Follow-up to PR #591 (issue #581). **PR #591 wires ONE call site: the production target gate in `coldlion-licensor-property-production.yml`. Everything below is still on the old single-file check.**\n\n## Why this matters\n\n`supabase/.temp/` holds **three** files that can each name a project:\n\n| File | Names a ref how | Written by `supabase link`? |\n|---|---|---|\n| `project-ref` | bare ref | **yes** |\n| `pooler-url` | inside the **username**, as `postgres.<ref>` | **yes** |\n| `linked-project.json` | `{\"ref\": ...}` | **NO** — different tool |\n\nMeasured 2026-08-07 on a real checkout: `project-ref` said **preview** while `linked-project.json` said **production**.\n\nDirect measurement (three experiments, recorded in `docs/verification/opa-preview-load-20260807/`) established that **`project-ref` is what the CLI follows**, so `cat supabase/.temp/project-ref` is not wrong about the CLI. The real hazard is **cross-tool**: the Supabase MCP / editor extension reads `linked-project.json`, and on the affected machine that MCP was bound to **production** while the CLI was on preview. `supabase link` never writes or refreshes that JSON file, so **no re-link can ever correct it**.\n\nA single-file check cannot see that split.\n\n## Remaining call sites (14)\n\n**Workflows (2)**\n- `.github/workflows/coldlion-licensor-property-alert-monitor.yml`\n- `.github/workflows/coldlion-licensor-property-phase6-parallel.yml`\n\n**Tools (11)**\n- `tools/check-coldlion-designflow-sync-health.mjs`\n- `tools/compare-coldlion-designflow-daily.mjs`\n- `tools/dispatch-coldlion-taxonomy-alerts.mjs`\n- `tools/evaluate-coldlion-licensor-property-cutover-readiness.mjs`\n- `tools/promote-coldlion-source-owned.mjs`\n- `tools/rehearse-coldlion-cutover-sequence.mjs`\n- `tools/rehearse-coldlion-recurring-cycles.mjs`\n- `tools/run-coldlion-licensor-property-phase4.mjs`\n- `tools/sync-clickup-tasks.mjs`\n- `tools/sync-coldlion-licensors-properties.mjs`\n- `tools/sync-plm-master-data.mjs`\n\n**Docs (1, two places)**\n- `AGENTS.md` — still teaches `cat supabase/.temp/project-ref` as *the* safety check. Should teach the checker instead, and record that `project-ref` is authoritative for the CLI while `linked-project.json` can silently disagree for other tools.\n\n## The API to use\n\n`tools/check-supabase-link-state.mjs` (added in #591):\n\n```\nnode tools/check-supabase-link-state.mjs --expect-ref=<ref> [--root=<checkout>]\n```\n\nOr import `evaluateLinkState({ projectRefRaw, linkedProjectRaw, poolerUrlRaw, expectedRef })`.\n\nNotes for whoever picks this up:\n- The expected ref is **required and has no default** — that is deliberate.\n- `--root` matters in this repo's worktree-per-agent model: without it the checker validates the checkout containing the *script*, not the one you are working in.\n- The pooler URL is a connection string that **can carry the database password**. Never echo it; the checker deliberately never does.\n- 39 offline tests exist and are auto-run by `tools-offline-tests.yml`.\n\n## Not yet established\n\nWhether a **valid** `pooler-url` naming a different project can actually redirect the CLI. Testing that would have required pointing a connection at production, so it was not done. The checker rejects a mismatched `pooler-url` regardless, as defence in depth.","closedAt":"2026-08-11T13:37:58Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T23:28:34Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":593,"title":"Wire check-supabase-link-state.mjs into the remaining 14 call sites of the single-file project-ref check","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:55:05Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/593"},

{"body":"## What exists now\r\n\r\nThe completed Warner STARLABS source extract is in the PRIVATE repository\r\n`u2giants/licensor-source-data`, under `warner-bros/`.\r\n\r\n- **Stable source snapshot:** `main` commit `9092c51afc42c080f199e5784451425810c39316`.\r\n  Pin to this commit; do not read a moving `main`.\r\n- **Local path on al8960ofc:** `C:\\repos\\licensor-source-data-warner\\warner-bros`\r\n\r\nIt includes assets, style guides, characters, asset relationships, and the direct\r\nProduct Property-to-Character catalogue.\r\n\r\n## Required reading before loading anything\r\n\r\n1. `warner-bros/README.md` in the source-data repo.\r\n2. `shared-db/docs/licensor-portal-scrape-source-schema-20260807.md` — follow it.\r\n\r\n## The modelling trap (read this twice)\r\n\r\n**Warner exposes Franchise and Property as SEPARATE levels.** The current extract\r\nstores Franchise labels in `assets.csv` → `franchise_labels`.\r\n\r\n- Do **not** treat `franchise-properties.csv` or `links-asset-franchise-property.csv`\r\n  as proof that Franchise and Property are the same level. They are not.\r\n- Do **not** create direct Franchise-to-Property, Style-Guide-to-Property, or\r\n  Style-Guide-to-Character links from asset co-occurrence. Two things appearing on\r\n  the same asset is not a Warner record that they are linked. Those links would be\r\n  **inferred**, not direct, and inferred links are indistinguishable from real ones\r\n  once loaded.\r\n\r\nOnly the Product Property-to-Character catalogue is a direct Warner record.\r\n\r\n## Data-handling rule\r\n\r\nKeep **all** raw Warner files in the private source-data repo. Do **not** copy\r\nlicensed raw data into `shared-db` git history. `shared-db` is public.\r\n\r\n## Related open work\r\n\r\n- #583 — HANDOVER: Warner has no source tables and two competing unmerged PRs.\r\n  Those two PRs (in `licensor-source-data`) have different row counts and one must\r\n  be ruled authoritative before or alongside this work.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: source-data\nroute: source-data-session\npriority: 300\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-18T14:59:42Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T23:05:05Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"## Small, verified, low-severity items left deliberately\r\n\r\n### 1. `verify` check fails on every PR, unrelated to the PR\r\n\r\n`npm audit --audit-level=high` trips on `nanoid <3.3.17` (GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8). It fails on PRs touching no JavaScript, and it fails on `main`. **It is NOT one of the six required checks**, so it does not block merges — but it reads as a failure on unrelated work and trains people to ignore a red check, which is exactly how a real failure gets missed. Bump it or exclude it deliberately.\r\n\r\n### 2. Two deferred value-echo paths in the OPA loader\r\n\r\nBoth judged low and left on purpose, both recorded:\r\n- **G6 can echo a single field value on numeric overflow.** A JSON number too large for `bigint` passes every `jsonb_typeof` check, then fails the `::bigint` cast, and `int8in`'s error text includes the offending value. Needs a malformed oversized number; leaks one field, not a row. Same shape in G7.\r\n- The runner no longer prints response bodies at all, so the CI-log path is closed.\r\n\r\n### 3. One Disney property name remains in a public file\r\n\r\n`docs/verification/opa-characters-20260806/README.md` line 372 quotes a single Disney property name inside an owner ruling. **No ID values.** Raised with Albert; he did not rule. Left rather than widening a security task unilaterally. Keep or paraphrase — one-line decision.\r\n\r\n### 4. The dispatch-collision checker is blind to most DDL\r\n\r\n`AGENTS.md` §4 states it cannot see `create table`, `alter table`, `create index`, `grant`, `comment on` or `create type`. For a table-only change — such as the entire Paramount design — **a clean gate result is close to meaningless**. It is a second pair of eyes, not the orchestrator. Judge by hand and say you did.\r\n\r\n### 5. Two environment traps worth fixing at source\r\n\r\n- **The shared checkout's Supabase link state is internally inconsistent**: `supabase/.temp/project-ref` and `pooler-url` say **preview** while `linked-project.json` in the same directory says **production**. The `cat supabase/.temp/project-ref` check prescribed across every brief and skill in this repo **passes while the same directory names production**. Every agent this session bypassed it by naming the ref in the URL. This should be fixed or the prescribed check should be changed.\r\n- **`gh api .../contents/<file>` silently returns an empty body for files over 1 MB.** The Disney CSV hits this. Anyone re-fetching without `Accept: application/vnd.github.raw` analyses zero rows and does not notice.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: ready\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 250\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-18T14:53:27Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T22:27:53Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":584,"title":"HANDOVER: five small verified items left deliberately (nanoid check, G6 echo, one Disney name, collision-checker blindness, two env traps)","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:43:33Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/584"},
{"body":"## Two loose ends from the licensor/property workstream\r\n\r\n### 1. Warner has nothing built, and its data is in two competing unmerged PRs\r\n\r\n`u2giants/licensor-source-data` has **two open PRs from the same session, same folder, different row counts**: PR #2 (`codex/warner-starlabs-20260807-pr`) and PR #3 (`codex/warner-starlabs-20260807`). Neither merged. Only `disney-opa/` is on that repo's `main`.\r\n\r\n**There are also no Warner source tables in `shared-db` at all** — verified by grep across `supabase/migrations`. **Paramount is the SECOND licensor to be built, not the third.**\r\n\r\nAlbert's ruling 2026-08-07: **\"Leave Warner for now.\"** Filed so it is not lost. Somebody must eventually decide which Warner PR is authoritative before a third licensor lands.\r\n\r\nNote Warner's captured data has **no property→character link at all** — the relationship Disney and Paramount both provide. If Warner is ever landed it needs a third shape.\r\n\r\n### 2. The ColdLion gap grew during the session, and the sub-licensor ruling shapes it\r\n\r\nThe ColdLion-vs-Supabase mapping gap was **47 rows in the morning and 66 by evening**. **19 brand-new records appeared during the session**, all ending `- DESPERATE`: 5 licensors and 14 properties, all beer and car brands.\r\n\r\n**Albert established what they are:** Desperate is a **sub-licensor**, not the brand owner. POP does not hold the brand relationship; Desperate does. POP reports sales to Desperate broken down by ultimate licensor, and Desperate files royalties upward. **FanCreations is the same shape** for NCAA and NFL, which sit as `potential` because sampling has not started — unlike Ford, where it has.\r\n\r\n⚠️ **`ANHEUSER BUSCH - DESPERATE` and the existing `potential` `Anheuser Busch` record are NOT duplicates.** They are the brand owner and the sub-licensed route. **A future dedupe pass must not merge them.** An earlier report in this session wrongly flagged them as a duplicate-identity hazard; that was corrected.\r\n\r\n**Albert ruled: keep it FLAT for now.** `core.licensor` will not model the sub-licensor relationship. Consequence, recorded so it is not discovered by surprise: any report answering \"who is the licensor\" for those 14 properties returns **Desperate**, not the ultimate brand owner. The royalty chain is real in the business and absent from the data. Changing this is an owner decision, not an engineering one.\r\n\r\nAlso stale: `AGENTS.md` §6.9's \"33 codes\" figure is now **47**. And `CW001` / `SP001` are **no longer byte-identical** — CW001 returns 27 licensors / 299 properties against SP001's 22 / 285, contradicting a doc that says they match.\r\n\r\nFull ruling record: `docs/verification/owner-rulings-20260807/README.md` and `AGENTS.md` §6.13.\r\n\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:42:16Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T22:27:52Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":583,"title":"HANDOVER: Warner has no source tables and two competing unmerged PRs; ColdLion gap grew 47 to 66 with the DESPERATE sub-licensor records","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:43:35Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/583"},
{"body":"## The question\n\nWhere should the OPA extract's **selector parameters** live now that `OPA_SOURCE_URL` refuses them?\n\n## Background\n\n`tools/sync-opa-property-character.mjs` stores `source_url` verbatim as provenance on **every one of ~10,262 rows**. To stop a session token being written into all of them, the credential guard now **refuses any URL carrying a query string or fragment** outright, rather than scanning for secret-shaped words. That was a deliberate contract change, made because a blocklist guarding a value persisted ten thousand times is the wrong shape.\n\n## The cost, found on first contact with the real file\n\nThe real Disney OPA page URL carries a query string, and those parameters are **not decoration — they select the extract**:\n\n- `lob` — line of business\n- `regionName`\n- `templateId`\n- `workflowId`\n\nStripping them makes provenance say *which page*, not *which slice*. **Two different LOB extracts would store an identical `source_url`.**\n\n`line_of_business` is captured separately on the row. **`regionName`, `templateId` and `workflowId` are captured nowhere.**\n\nNo session token was present in the observed URL, but that is one observation.\n\n## Options\n\n1. Add explicit provenance columns for the selectors, keeping `source_url` clean and refusing query strings as now.\n2. Allow an allow-listed set of query parameters through the guard, refusing everything else.\n3. Accept the loss and record the selectors in the capture README only.\n\nOption 1 preserves the security property and the provenance. Recommending it, **not deciding it**.\n\nDetail: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-07T2222Z-al8960ofc-orchestrator-opa-build-and-paramount-design.md` §4, agent `opa-dry-run`.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T22:01:05Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T22:27:20Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. Do not act without a fresh answer in the current chat.","color":"D93F0B"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":582,"title":"HANDOVER: where do the OPA extract selectors (lob, regionName, templateId, workflowId) live now that source_url refuses query strings?","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:55:08Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/582"},
{"body":"## What is needed\n\nLoad Disney's OPA extract into **preview**. The tables exist and are empty.\n\n`plm.opa_property_character` = **0 rows** (measured). `core.character`, `core.style_guide`, `core.style_guide_character`, `core.property_character` are all **0 rows** too.\n\n## What is already proven\n\n- The loader `tools/sync-opa-property-character.mjs` has **45 tests, 28 mutants killed**.\n- A **dry run against the REAL Disney extract PASSES**, unmodified. 1,069,881 bytes / 10,262 data rows fetched and verified. Every predicted figure reproduced: 1,445 property IDs, 9,613 character IDs, 10,240 name pairs, 22 collisions. Cross-checked with a **separately written RFC4180 tokenizer** — two independent parsers agreeing.\n- The ID-pair key `(licensedPropertyID, characterID)` is unique across all rows. The **name** pair is not.\n\n## What is NOT proven\n\n**The `--apply` path has only ever run against invented fixtures.** The wrong-target gate and the shrink band are proven by unit tests, not by a real load.\n\n## Required invocation\n\nBoth are **mandatory with no defaults** — the run aborts without them:\n- `OPA_EXPECTED_PROJECT_REF` (or `--expect-ref=`) — compared against the ref parsed from `SUPABASE_URL`, refuses to send on mismatch.\n- `OPA_MIN_ROWS` — the first-load floor. The database shrink band only fires once rows exist, so the first import into an empty mirror has no other protection.\n\n⚠️ **Preview is `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`.** Do NOT rely on CLI link state — `supabase/.temp/project-ref` says preview while `linked-project.json` in the same directory says **production**. Name the ref explicitly.\n\n## Two known snags\n\n1. **`OPA_SOURCE_URL` refuses the natural provenance URL.** The credential guard rejects any URL carrying a query string or fragment. The real OPA page URL has one — and those parameters (`lob`, `regionName`, `templateId`, `workflowId`) are what **select** the extract, not decoration. Stripping them makes provenance say *which page*, not *which slice*: two different LOB extracts would store an identical `source_url`. **Needs an owner decision on where those selectors live.** See the separate issue.\n\n2. **The strict CSV parser's bare-quote rule never fired, and that is luck.** Disney's exporter quotes every field unconditionally and the file has zero embedded quotes. A future extract that quotes selectively is untested. **Re-run the dry run on every refresh** — it contacts no database.\n\n## Fetching the file\n\n`u2giants/licensor-source-data`, path `disney-opa/opa-characters.csv`. ⚠️ `gh api .../contents/...` returns an **empty body** for files over 1 MB — pass `Accept: application/vnd.github.raw`. On Windows a checked-out copy has CRLF and will not match the blob; use `git cat-file blob`.\n\n**Never commit the CSV into `shared-db`. It is PUBLIC.**\n\nDetail: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-07T2222Z-al8960ofc-orchestrator-opa-build-and-paramount-design.md` §4, agent `opa-dry-run`.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-08T00:01:56Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T22:27:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":581,"title":"HANDOVER: load the Disney OPA extract into preview — tables exist, 0 rows, dry run PASSES","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:55:13Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/581"},
{"body":"## What is needed\n\nBuild the Paramount (Nickelodeon/Viacom) source layer. **Design is FINAL, independently reviewed, and revised twice. Nothing is built.**\n\n## HELD — do not start yet\n\nAlbert ruled the build waits for the **full Paramount capture** to return. A capture prompt is on his Desktop (`paramount-full-capture-prompt.md`).\n\n## Release 1 = FIVE tables (owner ruling)\n\n```\ntable    plm.pmt_capture\ntable    plm.pmt_property\ntable    plm.pmt_character\ntable    plm.pmt_property_character\ntable    plm.pmt_asset\nfunction plm.pmt_loader_privilege_ok(text, text)\nfunction plm.sync_paramount_capture(jsonb, text, numeric)\nfunction public.sync_paramount_capture(jsonb, text, numeric)\npolicy   one read policy per table (5)\nview     api.pmt_property_character\n```\n\nDeferred to release 2+: `pmt_brand`, `pmt_franchise`, `pmt_franchise_property`, `pmt_collection`, `pmt_property_collection`, `pmt_asset_collection`, `pmt_asset_property`, `pmt_asset_character`, `pmt_authorized_title`, `pmt_authorized_title_match`, four views.\n\n## The rule that must not be lost\n\n**A property filter does NOT prove a property→character relationship.** Measured across 3 property filters and 5 assets: a character surfaced under all three filters while Paramount's explicit combined value named ONE property every time. Inferring from the filter would have produced roughly **two-thirds wrong edges**.\n\n`plm.pmt_property_character` may be populated **only** from the explicit `<property_id>^<character_id>` value in full asset metadata. The importer must have no code path that constructs an ownership row without it. The same trap is **assumed present** for property→collection and has not been separately tested.\n\n## Design decisions worth preserving\n\n- Surrogate `uuid` PK on every entity table, natural key as `unique (source_domain, source_id)`. Not a mix.\n- **Capture is PROVENANCE, never identity** — so a second capture updates in place and duplicates nothing.\n- All source IDs stored as **text**. Paramount's character field is `CHAR(50)` at source.\n- The four confidential Paramount domain strings **never enter this repo** — they are runner env gates (`PMT_EXPECTED_*_DOMAIN`), not migration constants. This also means the one unknown domain string does **not** block the build.\n- `^` rule: refuse anything that is not exactly one separator. Now observation-backed.\n- Never infer identity from a filename. An observed asset had a character-count field populated with both its character ID and combined value empty.\n- **The runner archives everything it observes, loads only what has a table** — so the deferred tables are backfilled later without a re-scrape.\n\n## Carry every Disney guard\n\nNULL-rejecting `p_max_shrink_fraction` (validate the **parameter**; an outer `coalesce()` returns `1` and does NOT fix the hole); `pg_temp.`-qualified staging dropped before creation; errors reporting ordinal and failing check, never row content; runner expected-project-ref gate; first-load floor; privilege predicate using `session_user`, returning FALSE on NULL. RLS: the corrected `erp_` predicate, policy **and** grant, `security_invoker = true` on views.\n\n## Note for the dispatch gate\n\n`check-dispatch-collision.mjs` is **blind to `create table`, `create index`, `grant`, `comment on`** — essentially this entire design. A clean automated result here is close to meaningless. **Judge the collision by hand.**\n\nDetail: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-07T2222Z-al8960ofc-orchestrator-opa-build-and-paramount-design.md` §3 and §4.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-12T22:00:48Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T22:26:52Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAAC2L_V2g","name":"non-orchestrator","description":"Does not change database structure: not orchestrator work","color":"FBCA04"}],"number":580,"title":"HANDOVER: BUILD the Paramount source layer — five tables, designed and reviewed, HELD until the capture returns","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T16:55:16Z","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/issues/580"},
{"body":"## The five migrations are on `main` and applied to PREVIEW. NONE is promoted to production.\n\nPromotion list, **in dependency order, all five, by exact 14-digit version**:\n\n```\n20260807170000_opa_property_character_landing.sql\n20260807170100_opa_property_character_importer.sql\n20260807180000_opa_sync_reentrancy_fix.sql\n20260807190000_opa_security_and_view_corrections.sql\n20260807200000_opa_comment_corrections.sql\n```\n\n⚠️ **Anything without `20260807190000` ships a read policy that lets EVERY authenticated account — including `vendor` and `viewer` — read the entire confidential Disney extract.** The landing migration originally shipped `using (true)` under a comment falsely claiming it matched the `plm.erp_*` precedent; the precedent actually role-gates. `20260807190000` is a **security fix, not optional**.\n\n⚠️ `20260807180000` must be promoted **before** `20260807190000`.\n\nAlso unpromoted from the previous session: `20260807030000_owner_ruling_coco_is_a_disney_license.sql`.\n\n## The bigger problem: nobody knows production's real position\n\nMeasured across **281 workflow runs**: the `production-dry-run` job was **skipped 142 times, failed once, and succeeded ZERO times**. The workflow's first step is literally \"Refuse production apply\". **No migration has ever reached production through this workflow.**\n\nConsequences:\n- `core.property_character` and `plm.opa_property_character` **certainly do not exist on production**. Any design assuming they do is wrong.\n- Production's true migration position **is not known by measurement**. Establishing it requires an approved window and is a task in its own right.\n- If anyone believes the production dry-runs are providing ongoing safety coverage, **they are not running at all**.\n\n## Preconditions before any promotion\n\n1. Establish production's real position by measurement, in an approved window.\n2. Albert must name the exact project and the exact action. \"Fix the feed\" is not approval.\n3. Note preview and production are **legitimately divergent** — preview carries `core.licensor` `FR` as `inactive`, which AGENTS.md says must not exist on production standalone. Do not \"reconcile\" it.\n\nDetail: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-07T2222Z-al8960ofc-orchestrator-opa-build-and-paramount-design.md` §5.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-11T01:43:45Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T22:26:33Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. This label never grants orchestrator ownership.","color":"1D76DB"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wmg","name":"needs-albert","description":"Blocked on an owner decision. {"body":"## What is needed\n\nScrub Disney's confidential material from `shared-db` git history. This is step (c) of R-SEC-1; steps (a) and (b) are DONE.\n\n## Why it is still open\n\nThe repo was PUBLIC from 2026-06-20 to 2026-08-07 ~15:10 UTC while holding Disney's property/character extract. It was made private, then **made PUBLIC again at ~17:11 UTC** (PR #494). The files have been removed from `main` but remain reachable in history.\n\nTwo blobs:\n- `docs/verification/opa-characters-20260806/opa-characters.csv` — 10,262 rows, Disney's own internal IDs. Removed from `main` by PR #495.\n- `docs/verification/opa-characters-20260806/DESIGN.md` — 937 lines quoting real Disney names and IDs. Removed by PR #500.\n\nBoth now live in the private repo `u2giants/licensor-source-data` under `disney-opa/`, hashes verified identical before deletion.\n\n## Measured blast radius\n\nThe CSV is reachable from **67 commits** and **13 refs** — every remote branch in the repo. A scrub rewrites all of them and **breaks every existing clone and worktree**.\n\n## Scope — owner ruling, do not widen\n\nAlbert ruled on 2026-08-07: **Disney material ONLY.** POP's own large committed CSVs — including a 29 MB, 111,012-row `docs/verification/popsg-property-reconciliation-20260726/property-relationships-accepted.csv`, which is 27x larger than Disney's and was public just as long — are **explicitly out of scope**.\n\n## Preconditions\n\n- A quiet window. No agents dispatched, no open PRs, no live worktrees.\n- Albert's explicit go-ahead in the current chat.\n\n## Not provable — do not claim otherwise\n\nWhether anyone fetched the data while public. Forks and stars were 0 at the flip, but an anonymous clone or a crawler leaves no trace. **Never report \"no one took it.\"**\n\n## Separate, unanswered, and not engineering's call\n\nWhether Disney or Warner require breach notification for the seven-week window.\n\nDetail: `HANDOFF.d/2026-08-07T2222Z-al8960ofc-orchestrator-opa-build-and-paramount-design.md` §2.\n","closedAt":"2026-08-07T22:35:15Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T22:26:19Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"Found 2026-08-07 when Albert asked why three skills carry `shared-db` in the name and none says \"coordinator\".\n\n## What was wrong\n\n`skills/claude/shared-db-change/SKILL.md` in `u2giants/ai-devops` — a portable summary of the migration discipline — had drifted from `AGENTS.md`, which is the live rulebook.\n\n**Rule 1 said: \"DDL via MCP `apply_migration` only.\"**\n\n`AGENTS.md` standing fact 6 says the Supabase MCP **may be bound to PRODUCTION and takes no project parameter — there is no way to aim it at preview.** So a session following that rule literally could apply DDL straight to production while believing it was doing the safe, documented thing.\n\nThe same skill also still described filing requests into `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md`, retired earlier the same day.\n\n**Both fixed** in `ai-devops` commit `019483e`, with a standing note that `AGENTS.md` wins wherever the portable summary disagrees.\n\n## Why this is an issue and not just a fix\n\n**Nothing systematically checks a skill against the rulebook it summarises.** This one drifted, was not noticed by three separate model reviews of the surrounding work, and was only caught because the owner asked an unrelated question about naming.\n\nThe other skills that carry `shared-db` rules — `shared-db-orchestrator`, `shared-db-handover`, and the `AGENTS.md` summaries embedded in other repos' skills — have never been audited against `AGENTS.md`.\n\n## What to do\n\n1. Read each `shared-db-*` skill against the current `AGENTS.md` and list every disagreement.\n2. For each: correct the skill, or correct `AGENTS.md` if the skill turns out to be right.\n3. Decide whether a mechanical check is worth it. A skill lives in a different repository from the rulebook it summarises, so CI in neither repo sees both. That is the actual root cause and it will recur.\n\n⚠️ Do **not** simply delete the summaries. They exist because they load into sessions that never open `shared-db` at all.\n\n## Not done\n\nNo other skill has been checked. This is the report.","closedAt":"2026-08-09T23:44:46Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T21:43:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"**Found while merging an unrelated PR on 2026-08-07.** Not caused by that change — it fails on any PR touching this repo right now.\n\n## What is happening\n\n`.github/workflows/db-data-admin.yml`, the `verify` job, runs `npm audit --audit-level=high` and exits 1:\n\n```\nnanoid  <3.3.17\nSeverity: high\nnanoid: custom generators can loop indefinitely when size is zero\nhttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8\nfix available via `npm audit fix`\n```\n\n## Why it matters more than it looks\n\n`verify` is **not** a required status check, so it does not block merges. That is the problem: it is now **permanently red on every pull request**, and a check that is always red is a check nobody reads. The next genuine failure in that job will be invisible.\n\nThis repo has been here before — see `AGENTS.md` §5.2 on false verdicts, and backlog B2, which exists because a guard could be tripped by a file it did not watch and could not be un-tripped.\n\n## What to do\n\n`npm audit fix` in `apps/db-data-admin`, confirm the lockfile change is the nanoid bump and nothing else, and check the app still builds. Small and self-contained.\n\nIf the fix turns out to be a breaking major bump, say so rather than pinning an exception — an unexplained audit exception is the same silent-failure pattern.\n\n## Not done\n\nNothing changed. This is a report; the finding was read from a CI log, not reproduced locally.","closedAt":"2026-08-07T22:40:20Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T21:32:08Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"> Migrated from `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` (WI-58) as of commit `17d25b66ab7d0b7d196b8b2e95a12b2f488b5094`.\n> Source: `## REQUEST QUEUE` line 2963.\n\n## The request, verbatim\n\nA summary loses the reasoning, and in this queue the reasoning — the traps, the\n\"do NOT re-litigate this\" lines — is the expensive part.\n\n### REQUEST — fix the backlog/queue CI guard, which currently reports false passes — 2026-08-05 — session: outgoing coordinator (hetz)\n\n**1. What outcome is needed, and why.** The required status check **\"Backlog /\nqueue sync\"** (`scripts/check-backlog-queue-sync.mjs`) reports green on\nconditions that are false. It searches a whole section's body for the bare\npattern `\\bB(\\d{1,3})\\b`, so **any passing mention of a backlog number in prose\nsatisfies the requirement for that item.** Right now it prints \"OK B8 — found in\n`## REQUEST QUEUE`\" for B8, B13 and B14, all three of which have **no entry in\nthat section at all**; their real entries live in `## COMPLETED`. It is matching\na parenthetical in the section preamble. The outcome needed: the guard must\nrequire the real heading form it already prescribes in its own error message\n(`### REQUEST — Backlog B<n>`), so a genuinely missing entry can no longer be\nmasked by an unrelated sentence. Detail and the exact offending lines:\n`HANDOFF.d/2026-08-05T1827Z-hetz-coordinator-handover-20260805.md` §5.1.\n\n**2. Which application(s) depend on this.** None directly. This is repository\nprocess safety for `shared-db` itself, but it is a **required** check, so it\ncurrently carries authority it has not earned across every pull request.\n\n**3. Is it blocking anything, and how urgently?** Not blocking. It is a\nfalse-confidence defect: nothing is stopped, but a real gap can slip through\nunnoticed at any time.\n\n**4. Deadline, if any.** None.\n\n**5. What I already know about the current schema.** N/A — no schema is\ninvolved. The defect was proven by **running** the script, not by reading it:\n`node scripts/check-backlog-queue-sync.mjs` at 2026-08-05 18:20 UTC printed the\nthree false OK lines quoted above. ⚠️ When fixing it, keep the existing\n`no-queue-entry-needed:` opt-out marker working, and afterwards confirm B8, B13\nand B14 are reported against `## COMPLETED`. ⚠️ **Coverage itself is already\ncomplete — do not seed any `B<n>` entry.** Eleven live entries (B1–B7, B9–B12)\nsit in `## REQUEST QUEUE`; B8, B13 and B14 are correctly filed in\n`## COMPLETED`.\n\n**6. Confirmation of what I have NOT done. [MANDATORY]** The script was **run\nread-only** and **not modified**. No branch created beyond this session's own,\nno migration file written, no push to preview or production, no `supabase` CLI\ncommand, no Supabase MCP call, no psql, no background task chip.\n\n---\n\n---\n\n*This issue replaces a block in `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md`. {"body":"> Migrated from `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` (WI-57) as of commit `17d25b66ab7d0b7d196b8b2e95a12b2f488b5094`.\r\n> Source: `## REQUEST QUEUE` line 2919.\r\n\r\n## The request, verbatim\r\n\r\nA summary loses the reasoning, and in this queue the reasoning — the traps, the\r\n\"do NOT re-litigate this\" lines — is the expensive part.\r\n\r\n### REQUEST — close the two remaining branch-protection gaps on `main` — 2026-08-05 — session: outgoing coordinator (hetz)\r\n\r\n**1. What outcome is needed, and why.** Branch protection on `main` is **already\r\nON** (`AGENTS.md` §6.7, done by Albert 2026-08-04 12:00 UTC) with six required\r\nchecks, `enforce_admins: true`, force-pushes and deletions off. **Two gaps\r\nremain.** First, `required_status_checks.strict` is **false**, which lets a pull\r\nrequest merge while its base is out of date with `main`. That is a real hazard\r\nhere because migrations use `CREATE OR REPLACE`, which is last-writer-wins: two\r\nchanges to the same function, each merged from a stale base, silently lose one\r\nof the two with no error anywhere. Second, `required_pull_request_reviews` is\r\nabsent. **Recommendation: turn `strict` on; leave required reviews off** — with\r\nagents doing most of the work, a forced reviewer adds a blocking human step\r\nwithout adding real safety. Full measured configuration and reasoning:\r\n`HANDOFF.d/2026-08-05T1827Z-hetz-coordinator-handover-20260805.md` §3.4 and\r\n§9.1 decision 1.\r\n\r\n**2. Which application(s) depend on this.** All of them, indirectly. This\r\nprotects the shared migration lane that popdam3, popcrm-web, poppim-web,\r\nDesignFlow (dflow), the monitor and DB Data Admin all read from.\r\n\r\n**3. Is it blocking anything, and how urgently?** Not blocking. It is a\r\ncorrectness guard against a silent failure mode, so it should be done before the\r\nnext batch of concurrent migration work, not after.\r\n\r\n**4. Deadline, if any.** None.\r\n\r\n**5. What I already know about the current schema.** N/A — no schema is\r\ninvolved. The protection configuration was read live from\r\n`repos/u2giants/shared-db/branches/main/protection` on 2026-08-05 at 18:18 UTC\r\nand is recorded in the handover above. ⚠️ The first read of that endpoint came\r\nback reformatted by a display layer and looked like drift; it was **not**. Any\r\nfollow-up must re-query narrowly (`--jq`) before recording a discrepancy.\r\n⚠️ Note also that the B6 queue block still carries an obsolete caveat saying the\r\ncollision guard is \"ADVISORY only, because `main` has NO branch protection\" —\r\nthat sentence is now false. **Do not edit or delete the B6 block** to fix it.\r\n\r\n**6. Confirmation of what I have NOT done. [MANDATORY]** No change was made to\r\nbranch protection. No branch created beyond this session's own\r\n`docs/coordinator-handover-20260805`, no migration file written, no push to\r\npreview or production, no `supabase` CLI command, no Supabase MCP call, no psql,\r\nno background task chip.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n*This issue replaces a block in `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md`. Closing them first just lets the monitor\r\nrecreate them.\r\n\r\n**2. Which application(s) depend on this.** The ColdLion taxonomy sync lane and\r\nanyone reading this repo's issue list.\r\n\r\n**3. Is it blocking anything, and how urgently?** Not blocking work, but it is\r\nactively generating noise every hour and burying real issues.\r\n\r\n**4. Deadline, if any.** None.\r\n\r\n**5. What I already know about the current schema.** `COLDLION_ALERT_MONITOR_ENABLED`\r\nis a **GitHub repository variable**, read by\r\n`.github/workflows/coldlion-licensor-property-alert-monitor.yml`. {"body":"> Migrated from `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` (WI-31) as of commit `17d25b66ab7d0b7d196b8b2e95a12b2f488b5094`.\r\n> Source: `## REQUEST QUEUE` line 1865.\r\n>\r\n> **Blocked:** The app-side half lives in C:/repos/dflow, a different repo.\r\n\r\n## The request, verbatim\r\n\r\nA summary loses the reasoning, and in this queue the reasoning — the traps, the\r\n\"do NOT re-litigate this\" lines — is the expensive part.\r\n\r\n### REQUEST — Let DesignFlow show an item's UPCs on the item detail page — 2026-08-03 — requester: Albert Hazan (via Claude session on t16, `C:/repos/dflow`)\r\n\r\n**1. What outcome is needed, and why.** Albert wants the UPC(s) for an item\r\nvisible on the DesignFlow item detail page (Second tab). Today the UPC data we\r\nalready pull from ColdLion is stored but unreachable: nothing in the app can\r\nconnect a UPC record to the item a user is looking at, so no screen can display\r\nit and the data has never been seen by a user. The outcome needed is simply\r\n\"open an item, see its UPCs\". A style has several UPCs — one per colour/size\r\nSKU — so all of them need to be reachable, not just one. I am deliberately not\r\nprescribing the design; the missing piece is that our stored ColdLion item-detail\r\nrecords carry no way to identify which item they belong to.\r\n\r\n**2. Which application(s) depend on this.** DesignFlow (dflow) only — frontend,\r\nBFF, item-master and data-syncing services. I did not find another application\r\nreading `dflow.\"itemDetail\"`; nothing at all currently reads it, which is part of\r\nthe problem. Treat my \"no other consumer\" claim as unverified across the other\r\napps — I only checked the six DesignFlow repos.\r\n\r\n**3. Is it blocking anything, and how urgently?** Blocking, but only this one\r\nfeature and only Albert's request from today. Nobody is sitting idle; no\r\nproduction behaviour is affected. LOW-to-MEDIUM. All the app-side work in the\r\nDesignFlow repos is stopped until the shape of the fix is decided here, because\r\nthe query the app would run depends entirely on that decision.\r\n\r\n**4. Deadline, if any.** None.\r\n\r\n**5. What I already know about the current schema.** All of the following I read\r\nlive today (2026-08-03) against project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` with read-only\r\n`select` statements through the Supabase MCP, not from any document:\r\n\r\n- `dflow.\"itemDetail\"` holds 21,841 rows, 10,774 of which have a non-empty\r\n  `\"UPC\"`. It also has `\"EAN\"`, `\"GTIN\"`, `color_code_fk` and `size_code_fk`,\r\n  all populated.\r\n- Its only key is `item_pk`, which is ColdLion's own `itemPkey`. It has **no\r\n  item-number column and no foreign key to `dflow.\"itemHeader\"`** — I searched\r\n  `information_schema.columns` across the whole `dflow` schema for any bridge\r\n  between `item_pk` and an item number and found none. That is the gap.\r\n- `dflow.\"itemHeader\"` carries the item number as `item_num_id`.\r\n- Separately, and read live from the ColdLion API itself\r\n  (`GET http://x5.coldlion.com/EhpApi/itemDetails?itemNo=…`): ColdLion's\r\n  item-detail payload **does** include `itemNo` alongside `itemPkey`, plus\r\n  `companyCode`, `divisionCode`, `colorCode` and `sizeCode`. Our sync in\r\n  `designflow-data-syncing/helpers/utility.js` (`remapItemDetail`) simply never\r\n  mapped `itemNo`. So the identifying value exists upstream and is being\r\n  discarded on the way in; it is not lost.\r\n- One thing the coordinator should know before choosing a design: that sync\r\n  writes with `bulkCreate(..., { ignoreDuplicates: true })`, so existing rows are\r\n  never updated — a UPC that changes in ColdLion never reaches us. Whatever is\r\n  done about identification, backfilling the 21,841 existing rows will not happen\r\n  by itself. The sync route (`GET /getItemDetailFromCL/`) also appears to be\r\n  manually triggered; I found it on no scheduler.\r\n\r\n**6. Confirmation of what I have NOT done. [MANDATORY]** No branch created, no\r\nmigration file written, no DDL of any kind, no push to preview or production, no\r\n`supabase` CLI command, no psql, no background task chip, and no app-repo code\r\nchanges in the DesignFlow repos.\r\n\r\nI must disclose one thing rather than claim a clean \"no Supabase MCP call\": I\r\n**did** make Supabase MCP calls, all of them **read-only `execute_sql` `select`\r\nstatements** (the row counts, the sample rows, and the `information_schema`\r\nsearch quoted in point 5). I made them while establishing what the data looked\r\nlike, before I had read this file. No `apply_migration`, no DDL, and nothing\r\nwritten. Flagging it so the coordinator can judge it rather than discover it.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n*This issue replaces a block in `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md`. Do not re-file work into\r\nthat file — it is being retired. Open an issue instead.*\r\n\n\n\r\n```db-work-scope\nstatus: blocked\nwork_type: repo-maintenance\nroute: repo-maintenance\npriority: 500\ndepends_on: \nobjects:\n```\r\n\n\r\n","closedAt":"2026-08-28T22:28:28Z","createdAt":"2026-08-07T19:03:25Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTAehpM8AAAACvU2Wcw","name":"db-work","description":"Unclassified shared-db intake. {"body":"> Migrated from `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` (WI-26) as of commit `17d25b66ab7d0b7d196b8b2e95a12b2f488b5094`.\r\n> Source: `## REQUEST QUEUE` line 1648, `## REQUEST QUEUE` line 3205.\r\n\r\n## The request, verbatim\r\n\r\nA summary loses the reasoning, and in this queue the reasoning — the traps, the\r\n\"do NOT re-litigate this\" lines — is the expensive part.\r\n\r\n### From `## REQUEST QUEUE`, line 1648\r\n\r\n### REQUEST — Fix a stale 1Password vault ID recorded in the `shared-db-orchestrator` skill (file lives OUTSIDE this repo) — 2026-08-06 — session: sub-agent `stale-sweep`\r\n\r\n**1. What outcome is needed, and why.** The `shared-db-orchestrator` skill file\r\nrecords a **1Password vault ID for `vibe_coding` that has changed.** The **live ID\r\nobserved 2026-08-06 is `pimcaogmxxzoafh7lsluj6uxkq`.** A session following the\r\nstale ID gets a lookup failure that reads like a permissions or token problem.\r\n\r\n⚠️ **The skill file is NOT in this repository and was NOT edited by this session.**\r\nIt is installed under the user profile Claude Code loads — on `al8960ofc` that is\r\n**`C:\\Users\\ahazan2\\.claude\\skills\\shared-db-orchestrator\\SKILL.md`** — and the\r\n**source of truth is the `ai-devops` hub repo** (`C:\\repos\\ai-devops` on this\r\nmachine), from which `sync-dotfiles` installs it. **Fix it at the source in\r\n`ai-devops` and re-sync**, or the next `sync-dotfiles` overwrites any local edit.\r\n\r\n⚠️ **Standing trap, already recorded in memory:** 1Password vault and item IDs\r\n**can be re-keyed within a single session** (MCP reconnect). The durable fix is to\r\n**look the vault up by TITLE (`vibe_coding`), not by a hard-coded ID.** Prefer\r\nremoving the hard-coded ID over updating it — a hard-coded ID is guaranteed to go\r\nstale again. Nothing hard-coded that should be configurable (global rule 12).\r\n\r\n**2. Which application(s) depend on this.** None — AI session tooling. What outcome is needed, and why.** The validator this repo **mandates** for\nevery returned licensing sheet (*\"Never accept a returned sheet on its\nanswered-count alone\"*, `fix_characters_style_guides.md`) decides whether an\nanswered code is usable by running:\n\n```sql\nselect p.code, p.name, l.name as licensor\n  from core.property p\n  left join core.licensor l on l.id = p.licensor_id\n where p.code = any($1)\n```\n\nthen building its \"present\" set from **`p.code` alone**\n(`tools/validate-licensing-answers.mjs:86-96`). **There is no licensor scope.** A\ncode that exists only under the *wrong* licensor is reported as present and\nusable. It even selects `l.name as licensor` and then never uses it.\n\nThis is wrong under the `(licensor_id, code)` model and it is exactly the defect\nclass that would have waved `A005`/`CC` through. The outcome needed: the validator\ncompares against the licensor the sheet row belongs to, and reports\n\"present-but-under-a-different-licensor\" as its own distinct problem class rather\nthan as a pass. **Add negative-path tests that prove it REFUSES** (backlog B7\nstandard).\n\n**2. Which application(s) depend on this.** None directly — repo tooling — but it\ngates what enters `core.property` mappings that all four apps read.\n\n**3. Is it blocking anything, and how urgently?** Not blocking. **MEDIUM.** The\nlicensing question stream is now closed, so nothing is queued behind it today;\nfix it before the next licensing round or reuse of the tool.\n\n**4. Deadline, if any.** None.\n\n**5. What I already know about the current schema.** `core.property` is\n`unique nulls not distinct (licensor_id, code)`;\n`core.licensor` is `unique nulls not distinct (code)`\n(`supabase/migrations/20260621150815_app_core.sql:188`, `:200`). Read from the\nmigration file, **not** verified live.\n\n**6. Confirmation of what I have NOT done. [MANDATORY]** No code changed, no test\nwritten, no branch beyond this session's own docs branch, no migration, no\ndatabase call of any kind, no background task chip.\n\n---\n\n---\n\n*This issue replaces a block in `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md`. {"body":"> Migrated from `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` (WI-20) as of commit `17d25b66ab7d0b7d196b8b2e95a12b2f488b5094`.\n> Source: `## REQUEST QUEUE` line 1404.\n\n## The request, verbatim\n\nA summary loses the reasoning, and in this queue the reasoning — the traps, the\n\"do NOT re-litigate this\" lines — is the expensive part.\n\n### ⛔ QUESTION TO RESOLVE — which `CC` property row should the Disney `Coco` style guide point at? — 2026-08-06 — session: sub-agent `stale-sweep`\n\n> **This is a QUESTION, not a defined change. Do NOT queue, plan, or implement it\n> as \"re-parent `CC` under Disney\" — that instruction is meaningless here.**\n> Follows the owner ruling *\"Coco IS a Disney license\"* (Albert Hazan, 2026-08-06),\n> which closed the old *\"is `Coco` correctly under NO LICENSE?\"* request (now in\n> `## COMPLETED`).\n\n**1. What outcome is needed, and why.** Albert has ruled that **Coco is a Disney\nlicense**, and Laura has confirmed (round-3 `A005`, 2026-08-06) that **`CC`** is\nthe property code POP used for Coco. The Disney `Coco` style guide must end up\npointing at the right `core.property` row. **Which row that is, is unknown.**\n\n⚠️ **The thing that makes this a question and not a task:** **property codes are\nNOT globally unique.** Licensor → Property is a parent-child relationship and the\n*same* code can exist as separate property rows under many different licensors at\nonce — there could be a `CC` under twenty licensors. (Albert, 2026-08-06. The\nschema already models this: `supabase/migrations/20260621150815_app_core.sql:200`\ndeclares `core.property … unique nulls not distinct (licensor_id, code)`. Note\n`core.licensor` at `:188` **is** `unique (code)` — licensor codes are global,\nproperty codes are not. The two are routinely confused.)\n\n**Three things to establish, read-only, before anyone proposes a change:**\n\n- **(i)** Does a `CC` property row **already exist under the Disney licensor**,\n  separately from the one under `ZZ` (`DTR - NO LICENSE`)? Query by\n  `(licensor_id, code)` — never by `code` alone.\n- **(ii)** **Which licensor's `CC` did Laura's answer refer to?** Her note cites a\n  specific POP item number as evidence that POP shipped product under `CC`. **That\n  item number is deliberately not written into this repository** — it is a real\n  internal POP item identifier and the workbook carrying it is deliberately\n  uncommitted. The coordinator holds it out of band; ask for it when this is\n  dispatched.\n- **(iii)** Is the correct fix **(a)** point the Coco style guide at an existing\n  Disney `CC`, **(b)** create a `CC` property under the Disney licensor, or\n  **(c)** something else entirely — including that the Disney-side Coco property\n  carries a code other than `CC`, or that the `ZZ` row is a legitimately distinct\n  row that simply is not the one this style guide should use?\n\n**⛔ Do NOT decide between (a), (b) and (c) from documents.** No committed artifact\nin this repo enumerates `core.property` by `(licensor, code)`; it needs a live\nread. Guessing would corrupt curated Master Data, which `AGENTS.md` §6.4 forbids.\n\n**2. Which application(s) depend on this.** Every app reading the licensor →\nproperty hierarchy — PopDAM, poppim-web, popcrm-web, DesignFlow; royalty\nreporting most of all.\n\n**3. Is it blocking anything, and how urgently?** Not blocking. It is a\ndata-quality item that should be settled before the licensor/property move, and\nit is on the path of the characters/style-guides Phase 3 backfill.\n\n**4. Deadline, if any.** None.\n\n**5. What I already know about the current schema.** `core.property` is keyed\n`(licensor_id, code)` — read from the migration file, **not** verified live. The\n`Coco`-under-`ZZ` observation came from PR #402 (2026-08-02) and has **not** been\nre-verified since. Authoritative narrative:\n`fix_characters_style_guides.md` § *\"8-OWNER. OWNER RULINGS — 2026-08-06\"*.\n\n**6. Confirmation of what I have NOT done. [MANDATORY]** No database call of any\nkind, no `supabase` CLI, no Supabase MCP call, no psql, no migration file written\nor edited, no preview or production write, no background task chip. Docs only.\n\n---\n\n---\n\n*This issue replaces a block in `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md`. Do not re-file work into\nthat file — it is being retired. {"body":"> Migrated from `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` (WI-12) as of commit `17d25b66ab7d0b7d196b8b2e95a12b2f488b5094`.\n> Source: `## REQUEST QUEUE` line 1001.\n\n## The request, verbatim\n\nA summary loses the reasoning, and in this queue the reasoning — the traps, the\n\"do NOT re-litigate this\" lines — is the expensive part.\n\n### REQUEST — `AGENTS.md` §6.7 is STALE on branch protection (verified live), plus fresh evidence the shared checkout is still colliding, plus a CI trap — 2026-08-06 — session: opa-scrape (t16)\n\nThree findings from one session. Full detail:\n`HANDOFF.d/2026-08-06T1755Z-t16-claude-opa-character-extract.md` §5, §6, §7.\n\n**1. What outcome is needed, and why.**\n\n**(a) `AGENTS.md` §6.7 no longer describes reality.** Verified live 2026-08-06\n~17:45Z with `gh api repos/u2giants/shared-db/branches/main/protection`:\n\n| Fact | §6.7 / this queue says | **Live** |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Required checks | **ONE** (`Promotion contract tests (offline)`), because three workflows all exposed a check named `verify` | **ALL SIX** — `Promotion contract tests (offline)`, `Backlog / queue sync`, `Cross-PR object collision`, `Tools offline tests`, `SQL migration guards`, `Domain ownership` |\n| `strict` | `false` | **`true`** |\n| `enforce_admins` | `true` | `true` |\n\nThe `ci-check-names` work has evidently landed. Two consequences: the documented\ncaveat that \"a check can pass against a `main` that has since moved\" is largely\n**closed** by `strict: true` and should stop being repeated unexamined; and\n**every open PR must now be current with `main` to merge**, which with ~15 open\nbranches will bite.\n\n**This session did NOT edit `AGENTS.md`** — it is single-writer and the live\nsession behind PR #467 is editing it right now (commit `60dcec3` touches it).\nHanding it over rather than causing a conflict.\n\n**(b) The shared checkout is STILL colliding — fresh evidence, today.** Mid-session\nanother session switched `C:\\repos\\shared-db` from this session's branch to\n`docs/plan-dispatch-collision-hardening` and committed on top. A commit landed on\nthe wrong branch and was pushed there before it was noticed. It was recovered\n**non-destructively** (cherry-picked to the right branch through a temporary\nworktree; their branch was never rewritten, reverted or force-pushed).\n\n⚠️ **Residual damage needing a decision: [PR #467](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/pull/467) currently contains all four of this session's OPA files**, because its branch was cut from this one.\n**The clean fix is to merge PR #466 FIRST** — once those files are on `main` they\ndrop out of #467's diff by themselves. **No history rewriting, no risk to the\nother session's work.** Do that before anyone attempts to rebase or force-push\n#467.\n\nThe queue already carries items about this checkout being unsafe. This is\nevidence they are still live. The durable fix is that **no session works directly\nin the shared checkout — worktrees only.**\n\n**(c) A CI trap worth documenting next to `AGENTS.md` §5.2.** `Cross-PR object\ncollision` on PR #466 went **red after 44 minutes without ever running**. The\nannotation: *\"The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after\nmultiple attempts.\"* That is **GitHub hosted-runner starvation, not a collision.**\n`gh run rerun --failed` cleared it. This is a second, distinct flavour of the\nfalse-verdict problem §5.2 already covers for `paths:` filters. **Before believing\na red X, check the job annotations for that runner message.**\n\n**2. Which application(s) depend on this.** None directly — this is repo/CI\nhygiene. It affects every session that merges anything.\n\n**3. Is it blocking anything, and how urgently?** (a) and (c) are documentation\nonly, not blocking. (b) blocks a clean merge of PR #467 until PR #466 merges.\n\n**4. Deadline, if any.** None.\n\n**5. What I already know about the current schema.** Nothing — no database call\nwas made by this session.\n\n**6. Confirmation of what I have NOT done. [MANDATORY]** No migration, no preview\nor production push, no `supabase` CLI, no Supabase MCP call, no `psql`, no chip,\n**no edit to `AGENTS.md`**, and no rewrite/revert/force-push of any other\nsession's branch. Only `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, my own\n`HANDOFF.d/` file and the two files under\n`docs/verification/opa-characters-20260806/`, all on branch\n`request/opa-character-lookup` (PR #466).\n\n---\n\n*This issue replaces a block in `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md`. {"body":"> **Split, 2026-08-30 (owner ruling).** The one discrete, dispatchable piece of this programme — promoting the merged-but-held migration `20260802171000_owner_ruling_friends_tv_frida_kahlo` — is now tracked separately as **#1848**. That issue is `ready`; it needs the preview and promotion leases, NOT an author lane, because the migration is already merged.\n>\n> This issue remains the **programme umbrella**: it is non-ready, it names no database objects of its own, and it is not dispatchable. Nothing below is superseded.\n\n> Migrated from `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` (WI-07) as of commit `17d25b66ab7d0b7d196b8b2e95a12b2f488b5094`.\r\n> Source: `## REQUEST QUEUE` line 887, `## REQUEST QUEUE` line 1308, `## REQUEST QUEUE` line 2694, `## INTAKE QUEUE` line 4553.\r\n\r\n## What is still outstanding\r\n\r\n- From the licensor/property taxonomy intake: **PR #408 is MERGED to `main` but is NOT promoted to production.** It must ship as one change with the `FR` removal work (`AGENTS.md` §6.5).\r\n- The unmatched ColdLion property codes and the broken PLM sync described in that intake block are still open, and are inputs to this work item.\r\n\r\n## The request, verbatim\r\n\r\nA summary loses the reasoning, and in this queue the reasoning — the traps, the\r\n\"do NOT re-litigate this\" lines — is the expensive part.\r\n\r\n### From `## REQUEST QUEUE`, line 887\r\n\r\n### REQUEST — ColdLion as the source for Supabase: the 47-row decision sheet — 2026-08-07\r\n\r\n**Outcome:** Albert asked *\"what is needed to have ColdLion API as the source for\r\nour Supabase without breaking anything?\"* Full answer, measured against\r\nproduction and the live ColdLion API on 2026-08-07:\r\n`docs/verification/coldlion-as-source-20260807/README.md` (merged PR #484). It\r\n**extends** the existing \"Move Licensors and Properties off Cloud SQL\" request\r\nbelow rather than replacing it — read both.\r\n\r\n**The headline: there is no name-mapping problem.** Across all **271** entities\r\nin both systems (19 licensors, 252 properties) **not one name differs**. The\r\ndisagreement is about which rows exist, not what they are called. **The mapping is\r\n47 rows:** 33 ColdLion-only properties, 4 Supabase-only properties, 3\r\nColdLion-only licensors, 7 Supabase-only licensors. A decision-sheet CSV of those\r\n47 was generated for Albert locally on 2026-08-07 and **deliberately not\r\ncommitted** (see R-SEC-1); regenerate it from §2.6 of that doc.\r\n\r\n⚠️ **The 33/4/3/7 figures are code-only matches.** `core.property` is really keyed\r\n`(licensor_id, code)` and property codes are **not** globally unique. The diff is\r\nexact *today* only because production's copy is crippled to one row per code.\r\n**Re-derive by full typed identity at the time of the work.**\r\n\r\n⚠️ **15 of ColdLion's 22 licensor codes are also ColdLion property codes**\r\n(`1P CB CC DC DY FK HP MV PN PP SE SM SS SW WW`). A code-keyed mapping is\r\nguaranteed to corrupt this.\r\n\r\nOther measured findings: ColdLion licensor/property has **never reached\r\nproduction at all** (`plm.erp_licensor` 0, `plm.erp_property` 0, promotion\r\nfunctions absent, `core.taxonomy_source_ref` 100% `designflow_plm`); production is\r\n**39 merged migrations behind `main`**; the famous **\"111 unparented properties\"\r\nis NOT a Supabase condition** — Supabase has **zero** orphans, they are in\r\nDesignFlow's Cloud SQL, and every document repeating it reads as ours.\r\n\r\n**Blockers: two closed, nine still open, three newly discovered.** The count went\r\nup. Verdict, unsoftened: still the **hardest** table set to move; `age_group`\r\n(PR #435) should still be the two-row rehearsal first. ColdLion-as-source makes\r\nthe mapping far easier but makes the human curation screen **mandatory rather\r\nthan optional** — ColdLion cannot supply a parent and `core.property.licensor_id`\r\nis `NOT NULL`.\r\n\r\n**Confirmation:** nothing moved, no migration, no database write.\r\n\r\n### From `## REQUEST QUEUE`, line 1308\r\n\r\n### REQUEST — Execute the licensor/property cutover plan — blockers 5 and 6 MUST precede blocker 2 — 2026-08-06 — session: outgoing coordinator (al8960ofc)\r\n\r\n**1. What outcome is needed, and why.** An ordered plan now exists where none did (an\r\naudit found 2 of 9 blockers designed, 2 scoped, 2 fragments, 1 a stub, 2 empty, and **no\r\ndependency graph anywhere**). It is a 6-phase sequence, reviewed across a 3-turn debate\r\nwith Grok 4.5. ⚠️ **The order is load-bearing:** the dead PLM sync is currently the\r\n**only** thing protecting curated data, so doing blocker 2 before 5 and 6 removes the\r\nprotection with nothing in its place.\r\n\r\n**2. Which application(s) depend on this.** DesignFlow, DB Data Admin, ColdLion.\r\n\r\n**3. Is it blocking anything, and how urgently?** It IS Albert's stated top priority.\r\nHIGH — but gated on the ownerless-property answer above.\r\n\r\n**4. Deadline, if any.** None stated.\r\n\r\n**5. What I already know about the current schema.** Detail:\r\n`docs/licensor-property-cloudsql-cutover-plan-20260806.md` (824 lines). Also note the\r\n`age_group` rehearsal (PRs #435/#446) is **documentation only** and its own §6.1 argues\r\nit does **not** de-risk this move — do not cite it as cover.\r\n\r\n**6. Confirmation of what I have NOT done. [MANDATORY]** **No migration authored.** No\r\nbranch beyond the docs branch, no database write, no CLI, no MCP call, no psql, no chip.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### From `## REQUEST QUEUE`, line 2694\r\n\r\n### REQUEST — Move Licensors and Properties off Cloud SQL — ALBERT'S STATED TOP PRIORITY — 2026-08-03 — requester: Albert Hazan\r\n\r\n**1. What outcome is needed, and why.** Albert, 2026-08-03: *\"I REALLY want to\r\nmove Licensors and Properties over. the current setup has so many problems and\r\nbandaids all over it.\"* The outcome is that licensor and property data lives in\r\nthe shared Supabase database rather than DesignFlow's Cloud SQL production\r\ninstance, with one curated source of truth instead of the current patchwork.\r\n\r\n**2. Which application(s) depend on this.** PopDAM, poppim-web, popcrm-web and\r\nDesignFlow — this is the **hub** table set for three live applications at once.\r\n\r\n**3. Is it blocking anything, and how urgently?** It is the owner's stated\r\npriority. **But be honest with him: it is the HARDEST candidate to move, not the\r\neasiest.** Nine blockers must be closed first — the dead PLM sync (silent since\r\n2026-07-08), 111 unparented properties (51 active), no curation path anywhere,\r\n`plm.import_master_data()` still overwriting `licensor_id` in production, three\r\nfurther overwrite paths, 9 properties under the wrong licensor, an unvalidated\r\nDesignFlow write endpoint open to 5 roles, and a promotion lane that aborts at\r\nfile 3 of 14. **The recommendation to put back to Albert: keep `age_group`\r\n(PR #435) as the first move — it is the two-row, zero-risk REHEARSAL that proves\r\nthe promotion mechanism — then move licensor/property with a proven lane.**\r\n`age_group` is not a detour from his priority; it is the safety rehearsal for it.\r\n\r\n**4. Deadline, if any.** None stated.\r\n\r\n**5. What I already know about the current schema.** Measured live by PR #433:\r\n**614 properties, 519 active, 111 unparented (18%), 51 of those ACTIVE and\r\nunparented**. **DesignFlow is Cloud SQL in PRODUCTION ONLY** — dev, staging and\r\nsandbox already run on Supabase (PR #435), so a table move can be rehearsed in\r\nthree real environments first.\r\n\r\n**6. Confirmation of what I have NOT done. [MANDATORY]** Nothing moved, no branch,\r\nno migration, no preview or production write, no `supabase` CLI, no Supabase MCP\r\ncall, no psql, no background task chip.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## The handover briefing stays a file\r\n\r\nIt is not reproduced here: a ten-page briefing pasted into an issue is a ten-page\r\nbriefing nobody reads. Read it at its source.\r\n\r\n```\r\ngit show 17d25b66ab7d0b7d196b8b2e95a12b2f488b5094:COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md | sed -n '4553,4834p'\r\n```\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n*This issue replaces a block in `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md`. {"body":"> Migrated from `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` (WI-04) as of commit `17d25b66ab7d0b7d196b8b2e95a12b2f488b5094`.\r\n> Source: `## REQUEST QUEUE` line 819.\r\n\r\n## The request, verbatim\r\n\r\nA summary loses the reasoning, and in this queue the reasoning — the traps, the\r\n\"do NOT re-litigate this\" lines — is the expensive part.\r\n\r\n### REQUEST — Execute the DS→DY-at-source plan (Albert's ruling: no hard-coding) — 2026-08-07\r\n\r\n**Outcome:** Albert ruled *\"don't hard-code DS to DY, change DS to DY at its\r\nsource.\"* Full chain-of-custody, blast radius and executable plan are in\r\n`docs/verification/ds-to-dy-at-source-20260807/README.md` (merged PR #483).\r\n\r\nKey established facts: \"at its source\" **is** the `public.licensors` row\r\n(`10a445bc-cdb8-4384-ad6f-a46fd029f2bc`) — nothing upstream writes it, no\r\nmigration seeds it, the only live writer is a human PopDAM admin via RLS policy\r\n`Admin write licensors`. The hard-code survives in exactly **one** live object,\r\nthe view `public.dam_character_catalog`, and degrades to a pass-through. Applied\r\nmigration `20260723113000` never needs editing.\r\n\r\n⚠️ **The trap that would have corrupted data:** 30 `public.assets` and 6\r\n`public.style_groups` rows carry `licensor_code = 'DS'` that is **NOT Disney** —\r\nthe letters are a substring of the item SKU (`MCZ6X**DS**PT01`). All have\r\n`licensor_name IS NULL` and `is_licensed = false`. A blanket sweep would label 30\r\nunlicensed products as Disney. Use the `licensor_name` discriminator.\r\n\r\n⛔ **ONE HONEST BLOCKER: `popdam3` is not checked out on this machine and was\r\nNOT read.** It owns the only live write path. **Read it before executing.**\r\n\r\n**Rider:** the `WWE`/`WW` twin is the identical shape and undocumented. No `WWF`\r\nexists in `core.licensor`, so there is no company conflation; the doc recommends\r\nit rides along.
