{"body":"Closes #3353\nRelated #2678\nRelated #2457\nRelated #2549\nRelated #3313\nRelated #2448\nRelated #3319\nRelated #2998\nRelated #3343\nRelated #2836\nRelated #2824\nRelated #3050\n\n## Why this pull request exists\n\nTen contributing pull requests all edited `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`. `Cross-PR object collision` serialises them by design, and `pr-content-equivalence.mjs` correctly voids every other pull request's approval each time that file changes on `main`. Landing them one at a time costs a fresh review and a fresh check round per merge — quadratic, against a GitHub rate limit this account tripped twice on 2026-09-20.\n\nThis branch is the **union** of all ten, built by MERGING each contributing branch from current `main` in the landing order published on #3346. Every implementation and test commit is preserved; superseded evidence-only tails remain on their original branches. No branch was rebased, rewritten or force-pushed. Neither gate was weakened: this is one review of the combined content, not no review.\n\n## Pull requests absorbed, and what each one fixes\n\n| PR | issue | one line |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| #3314 | #2678 | Pass each reviewer wrapper its own `AI_*_CALLER` before the doctor probe, so a healthy reviewer stops being refused as a local dependency fault. |\n| #3316 | #2457 | A lagging mutex readback no longer refuses a draw that actually succeeded, and a refused release still reports the completed assignment. |\n| #3334 | #2549 | Separate workflow-dispatch identity from applied-checkout identity in preview evidence. |\n| #3317 | #3313 | Fix lifecycle dispatch timestamp ordering and recover the affected outcome records. |\n| #3322 | #2448 | Refuse an ambiguous second issue reference in a claim title before a version is spent; order-insensitive `--claim --objects`; accept an ordinary claim apply against its proven claim head (#3125, #2491). |\n| #3325 | #3319 | Preserve protected claims while resolving proven legacy relation aliases. |\n| #3338 | #2998 | Fail fast before a reviewer draw is spent on a draft pull request, and front-load the readiness assertions (#2915, #2923). |\n| #3344 | #3343 | Allow verified merged completion for typed maintenance work. |\n| #3315 | #2836 | Stop the same-repo `return_to` loop that minted a new returned copy every generation. |\n| #3326 | #2824, #3050 | Sanctioned scope-status writer, and a wrong-owner refusal that still refuses and says why. |\n\n## Deliberately NOT absorbed\n\n- **#3308** — independently merged at faed5557 and integrated through main, preserving its behavior.\n- **#3330** — merged to `main` on its own at 17:10:58Z while this work was in progress. Its content arrives through the base, so **issue #2832 is not closed here** and #3330 is not listed above.\n\n## Conflicts, and how each was resolved\n\nEvery conflict was resolved as a faithful union of all sides, never by choosing a winner:\n\n- `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` — the merged-main rehearsal rejection from #3334/#3317 and #2491's `provenClaimApply` acceptance are both kept, and `appliedCommit` honours all four accepting conditions. The `--status` flag from #3326 and `--reviewer-allowlist` from the reviewer work are both admitted.\n- `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` — every contributed test block and every added import symbol from all ten branches is retained.\n- `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json` — #3338 added one new call site and recorded its reviewed disposition in the aggregate; #3330 then partitioned those dispositions per source file and froze the aggregate as historical evidence that must stay equivalent to the partitions. #3338's reviewed row remains in its per-source catalogue; recovery restores the frozen aggregate and corrects the historical/current-inventory test distinction.\n\n## Validation and independent review\n\nCurrent head: 8c953ff954adcf3c9155cdfc0f472bffd32b4262. Current main: 20641bc6bbcd4e6e8fe1e2211126837456c045ab. Implementation: a0099e0a. Immutable prospective contract generation4 and exact keyed completion evidence validate.\n\n- Five exact required Node commands: 1265 passed, zero failures/skips/cancellations/todos. Python producer suite:187 passed. All rerun after the final documentation-only main refresh. Truth audit:311 call sites,69 sources,digest871e1ed90397. Whitespace and keyed Git evidence pass.\n- Actual governed Muse APPROVE at a4f268d9e63b763010bfb9fc0d2144d461e5a1a7: durable verdict ea325263e2616f6e83b01010cb447b9d1929e1bc. The sanctioned exact-head gate verified content-bound carryforward to the current head, implementation digest0f807eea390f8e4be712b5635a8c70289ccf5e72eb10e9ec96e3dbe7b6603119. Required hosted checks and guarded merge still apply.\n- Earlier broad diagnostic at98f4fc0f:3576 total,3575 pass,1 failure at scripts/check-issue-505-licensor-code-forward-repair.test.mjs:36. The same failure reproduced on then-mainf1fef457. This historical diagnostic is not claimed as a current full-suite pass.\n\n## Recovery corrections\n\nAll ten implementation/test sets are retained. The frozen historical aggregate is restored; the exact reviewed partition-test correction from32d0fc3906139605d6d117328edba92429439f1a distinguishes frozen history from current inventory. Current dispositions remain in their per-source catalogues.\n\nThe OPEN issue3050 handoff (106 lines) is restored exactly: its deletion in absorbed3326 was unsupported by completed-outcome evidence. The final main refresh removed only seven unrelated old handoffs. Keyed resolution/base-binding/tail semantics retain landed3323 behavior (30 focused regressions passed).\n\nThe producer gate now pins its runtime-read incident configuration; the existing same-failure test passes without weakening it. Grok's preserved nonauthorizing findings5752087623 exposed a later-repair refusal. The corrected selector sends absent-URL and already-repaired/nonpristine valid-pin cases through generic repair while validating explicit incident pins first. New regressions fail on old source and pass now, proving later duplicate repair with/without reused URL, unchanged original comments, nonrace-gap refusal and tamper refusal. Muse subsequently reviewed and approved the complete corrected union.\n\nOnly3353 is a closing reference. Absorbed original pull requests are superseded with branches/commits preserved; original issue completion remains separately evidence-gated. Root owns guarded merge and completion reconciliation.\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n\nPosted by Codex chat 01a0bf00-fa7b-73d1-b447-fc4c89c50b96 on one combined merge for the ten serialised manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs pull requests (#3353)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3354"},
{"body":"## Problem and result\n\nObserved 2026-09-15 on PRs #2980 and #2981: sessions waited for a full green CI run before requesting the governed review that must approve the merge, then pushed once per review finding, rerunning the whole matrix each time (the Windows jobs alone are ~30 minutes). That roughly doubles wall-clock per pull request.\n\nThe cause is structural rather than carelessness: review evidence binds to the exact head SHA, so any fix pushed after a review voids that review, and sessions learn to \"spend\" only one review.\n\n**AGENTS.md 5.0-C** now states the rule: start the governed review as soon as a head is pushed, in parallel with CI; batch every review finding *and* every CI failure into a single new head; hold both waits inside the turn with the bounded event-aware waiter. `scripts/check-review-parallelism-brief.mjs` holds the brief in place in the tools-offline check.\n\nTooling and workflow only. No database component, no migration, no production action. **Non-orchestrator** repository-maintenance work.\n\n## Nothing was weakened, and one proposal is refused\n\nIssue #3002 raised three proposals. Two are adopted. **The third — accepting a review bound to a head whose only later change is test or evidence files — is REFUSED**, in the brief and in the guard. Tests are code: a changed test changes what the change proves, and a reviewer who never saw it never reviewed it. Widening equivalence past the narrow, already-enforced #2758 rule (`scripts/lib/pr-content-equivalence.mjs`, `.agent/` evidence only) would be reviewing *less*, not faster.\n\nThe exact-head APPROVE requirement is untouched, no required check becomes optional, no gate is skipped and no reviewer requirement is dropped. The guard actively refuses a future edit that would make a required check optional, skip the review, accept a stale approval, or widen equivalence past `.agent/`.\n\n## Request volume: this must not mean hammering the API harder\n\nToday this fleet ran ~14 agents concurrently and repeatedly exhausted the GitHub budget — `API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 55610577`, `GitHub API rate limit exceeded (host-wide latch)`, `API rate limit exceeded for installation`. Five required checks on this very pull request failed on that limit rather than on its content.\n\n**This change lowers request volume rather than raising it.** It adds no API client, no polling loop and no workflow trigger. Its two effects both cut requests:\n\n- Batching every review finding and every CI failure into one new head removes the per-finding re-push, and with it a full extra matrix run and a full extra reviewer round per finding. That is the single largest source of redundant requests in the old pattern.\n- The brief mandates the repository's existing bounded, event-aware waiter for both waits, rather than a hand-written polling loop — explicitly, and as a guarded clause.\n\nOverlapping the review with CI does not add calls: the same one review and the same one matrix run happen either way, just concurrently instead of end to end.\n\nThe only executable code added is `scripts/check-review-parallelism-brief.mjs`, which reads one local file and makes zero network calls.\n\n## Conflict resolution note\n\nRefreshed from `main` by **merging, not rebasing**, to preserve the ancestry the #2758 approval-carry rule depends on. One conflict, in `scripts/throughput-guard/check-throughput-truth-audit.test.mjs`: `main` had since rewritten that test into a stricter, self-contained form (`historical_disposition_loader_preserves_review_records`, plus two new tests). **Main's version was taken in full** — it supersedes the looser version this branch carried and preserves the other session's improvement. Because that genuinely changed this pull request's own diff, the earlier APPROVE correctly stopped carrying and a fresh exact-head review was taken. That is the rule working, not a cost to be avoided.\n\n## Regression tests — verified to fail first\n\n`an AGENTS.md without the brief is refused` was run against `origin/main`'s AGENTS.md before this change and failed exactly as intended:\n\n```\nAGENTS.md is missing the review-parallelism brief: ### 5.0-C Run CI and the governed review in PARALLEL, and batch fixes into ONE head\n```\n\n`dropping any single required instruction is refused` removes each of the eight required clauses in turn from the live brief and asserts the guard names the dropped clause — verified to fail when a clause pattern is absent.\n\n`editing the brief into a weaker gate is refused` inserts each of the four weakening sentences into the live brief and asserts the guard refuses with \"parallelise, do not delete\".\n\n## Validation\n\n- `node scripts/check-review-parallelism-brief.mjs` → `review-parallelism brief OK: 8 required clauses present, 4 weakening patterns absent`\n- `node --test scripts/check-review-parallelism-brief.test.mjs scripts/throughput-guard/*.test.mjs` → 64 passing, 0 failing.\n- `node scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` → `truth audit OK: call_sites=311 sources=70`. The new guard script adds exactly one call site, which carries its own hand-written disposition — one new file, not a global recount, which is the #2832 partition doing its job.\n- Task gate declared `reviewer-safety`; re-checked before review and ship.\n\n## Coordination\n\nStacked on #3330 (issue #2832), now merged. Issue #3002 also appears in the overlap map of the concurrently open planning PR #3318 (tracker #3306); this change takes the decision that plan defers, and takes it in the safety-preserving direction.\n\nCloses #3002\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-20T17:14:03Z","files":[{"path":".agent/work/3002/3/completion.json","additions":61,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".agent/work/3002/3/contract.json","additions":55,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".github/workflows/tools-offline-tests.yml","additions":12,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"AGENTS.md","additions":46,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/.github~workflows~tools-offline-tests.yml.json","additions":28,"deletions":20,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~check-review-parallelism-brief.mjs.json","additions":13,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/check-review-parallelism-brief.mjs","additions":67,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/check-review-parallelism-brief.test.mjs","additions":65,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"2c819be4875e0f103d3374a3e8b126059e5d218d","mergedAt":"2026-09-25T19:47:39Z","number":3352,"title":"fix(#3002): run CI and the governed review in parallel, and batch fixes into one head","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3352"},

{"body":"Closes #3342 (non-orchestrator repository-maintenance).\n\nDesignFlow's column-acceptance producer needs a database credential it does not have. This adds a fixed read-only catalog observation producer in shared-db using its existing management route. Backend PR102 authenticates the original archive against GitHub's digest, validates the pinned producer and exact application commit, and generates application acceptance artifacts. No lifecycle validator changes or database writes.\n\nManual execution on main alone can query the fixed production catalog; pull requests run hermetic tests. Inputs cannot select a query or target. Failed requests, redirects, unexpected columns and stale output refuse evidence. The credential is scoped to the query step; the artifact contains metadata only.\n\nRefreshed against main18c2610526e9b34a9d5af3818853cf1fb63e8979. The historical audit test correction is already on main, leaving eight owned files. Validation:28 focused tests pass,0 failures/skips; truth audit312 call sites/70 sources passes; contract and Git evidence pass. Governed Grok4.6 review sequence3456 APPROVE951435c57a0ad6f97ea7b9d94f2f812c45e09470; durable verdict4ea61b4fd24ed57cd65fcba3e72dd23c303ef11c. {"body":"Closes #3331.\n\n## The failure this fixes, proven first\n\nOn clean `origin/main` (`b1d4be2e`), before this change, `node --test scripts/orchestrator-snapshot.test.mjs` is **red — 5 failing tests**. I ran it in a worktree checked out at `origin/main` with no edits and captured the output:\n\n```\n✖ issue 3148 only a request the queue audit itself would admit alarms after 30 minutes\n✖ only trusted, well-formed outcome events are read\n✖ successor reconstructs the exact active map from the live snapshot and verifies it fresh\n✖ unchanged state produces zero output and no report; each transition wakes exactly once\n✖ events on a claim thread about an unowned issue are dropped\n```\n\nVerbatim assertion:\n\n```\n✖ only trusted, well-formed outcome events are read (0.3973ms)\n  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:\n  + actual - expected\n  + []\n  - [ 'dispatched' ]\n```\n\nAfter this change the same file is **green: tests 18, pass 18, fail 0**. So the test verifiably fails against the unfixed tree and passes after.\n\n## Cause\n\n`scripts/orchestrator-snapshot.test.mjs` built its trusted fixture comment with a hardcoded `author_association: 'OWNER'`. Since the `popcre` transfer (#2530, commit `bf0744f6`), `expectedOperatorAssociation()` correctly returns `MEMBER` for any repository whose owner is not `u2giants`, and `trustedOutcomeComments` defaults to `currentRepository()` — `popcre/shared-db`. Every fixture event was therefore discarded and each assertion saw an empty list. The failure is deterministic and environment-independent.\n\n## What is NOT wrong\n\nProduction trust is correct and is **not touched by this PR**. A live read of `repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/3081/comments` returns `{\"assoc\":\"MEMBER\",\"user\":\"u2giants\"}` — exactly what `isTrustedOperatorComment` now expects. No gate is disabled, weakened or bypassed here; the stale thing was the fixture, and the repair is in the fixture.\n\nThe untrusted cases still reject on the **author login** (`mallory`), and the `NONE`-association and malformed-block cases are unchanged, so the test keeps proving everything it proved before.\n\n## Scope\n\nOne test file, 7 insertions, 1 deletion. No production code, no workflow, no configuration, no database, no migration, no schema change.\n\nContract published at `refs/db-contracts/3331/1` (sha256 `d259d57f2c8eaaffd01e4a0fffab94f9d0259a1d3e54cf3f8d0258e3652f4b76`).\n\n## Checks run locally\n\n- `node --test scripts/orchestrator-snapshot.test.mjs` → tests 18, pass 18, fail 0\n- `node --test scripts/lib/repository-identity.test.mjs` plus `no-progress-alarm`, `hold-reason`, `reviewer-start-watch`, `db-coordination-events`, `admission-outcome` → tests 141, pass 141, fail 0\n- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` → clean\n\nFound while verifying #3081 and #3048, both of which were already delivered on `main` and are now closed with evidence.\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-20T15:41:34Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":19,"deletions":89,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":22,"deletions":31,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-snapshot.test.mjs","additions":7,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"469474749bde2606b672c5b920cde293f617cf99","mergedAt":"2026-09-20T18:05:33Z","number":3333,"title":"fix(#3331): derive the trusted fixture association instead of hardcoding the pre-transfer OWNER","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3333"},
{"body":"## Problem and result\n\nOne throughput bottleneck, tooling only. No database component, no migration, no production action. Issue #3002 is the sibling of this work and ships separately, stacked on this change.\n\n**#2832 — the truth audit was a global bottleneck.** `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json` carried one repo-wide `call_site_count` and one `call_site_sha256` over every discovered call site. Any pull request that added or removed a line matching the tracked pattern had to edit that one file, so two unrelated lanes could never both be correct — whichever landed second was forced to recompute. On 2026-09-11 eight open pull requests were queued on it.\n\nReviewed dispositions now live one JSON catalogue per source file under `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/`, named by an injective source-path mapping. The global count and digest are **derived and reported** by the checker on every run instead of being stored in a shared artifact an author must edit. The pre-partition aggregate is retained as historical evidence and is no longer read.\n\nAll 310 existing hand-written dispositions were migrated losslessly — identities, line hashes, verdicts and reasons byte-identical.\n\n## Nothing was weakened — this is the important part\n\n- Every call site still needs its own hand-written disposition with a substantive reason. There is still **no** bulk regenerate or `--update` flag, deliberately.\n- Unknown, stale, retired, duplicate, short-reason and uncatalogued sites all still fail, and so do smuggled, traversing, out-of-root and case-aliased catalogue filenames.\n\n## Regression tests — each verified to fail first\n\n`independent_source_dispositions_merge_without_global_edit` builds two lanes that each add a call site to a *different* source file and merges them. Run against the unfixed `origin/main` checker and its global aggregate, this reproduces verbatim:\n\n```\nCONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json\nAutomatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.\n```\n\nWith the partition it merges cleanly and the checker passes (`call_sites=4 sources=2`).\n\nAlso added and verified: `disposition_unknown_site_refuses`, `disposition_deleted_site_requires_retirement`, `disposition_path_rename_preserves_review`, `disposition_duplicate_identity_refuses`, `disposition_empty_reason_refuses`, `disposition_partition_complete_equivalence`, catalogue-filename smuggling, and \"an aggregate count and digest are no longer an input\".\n\n## Validation\n\n- `node scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` → `truth audit OK: call_sites=310 sources=69`\n- `node --test scripts/throughput-guard/*.test.mjs` → 59 passing, 0 failing.\n- `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → 1900 tests, 1894 passing, 6 failing. Those same 6 fail identically on `origin/main` before this branch (independently re-run at `b1d4be2e`: 1900 tests, 1894 pass, 6 fail, same names). They are pre-existing and unrelated.\n- Task gate declared `reviewer-safety`; re-checked before review.\n\n## Coordination\n\nIssue #2832 is also Step 2 of the concurrently open planning PR #3318 (tracker #3306). This implementation deliberately follows that plan's design — per-source-file partition, identity not bound to line numbers, derived global counts, lossless migration with an equivalence report, historical artifact retained, no bulk-update authority — rather than inventing a competing shape. No implementation work had started on #3306. Rebased onto current `origin/main` (`b1d4be2e`).\n\nThis is **non-orchestrator** repository-maintenance work: no database structure changes.\n\nCloses #2832\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude {"body":"Closes #2708\n\nIssue #2845 is fixed by the same change — the same `.agent` evidence mechanism, one coherent PR. It is deliberately NOT auto-closed here: the reviewer-assignment gate requires a pull request to close exactly one work issue, so #2845 is closed by hand against this merge commit.\n\nWork issue #2708 (and #2845 — one mechanism, one change).\n\n## #2708 — disjoint, generation-keyed evidence paths\n\nEvery agent-authored pull request wrote its own private work evidence into the same\ntwo fixed paths, `.agent/contract.json` and `.agent/completion.json`. The contents\nare per-pull-request; the paths were shared. So any merge to `main` put every other\nopen pull request into conflict on files that had nothing to do with it, and because\na governed review is pinned to an exact head, resolving that conflict voided every\ndurable verdict and forced a full re-review. One unrelated merge cost every other\nopen pull request a re-review round.\n\nEvidence now lives at:\n\n```\n.agent/work/<work_issue>/<generation>/contract.json\n.agent/work/<work_issue>/<generation>/completion.json\n```\n\nmirroring `refs/db-contracts/<work_issue>/<generation>`. Two pull requests can only\ncollide there if they claim the same issue **and** the same generation, which is the\none case where a collision is real information.\n\nThe validating checks moved with it: the gate resolves the pair from the pull\nrequest's own changed-file list, the tail after the implementation head must be\n*this* pull request's own two files (another pull request's keyed pair is refused),\nand a pull request carrying two pairs fails closed rather than the gate picking one.\nNothing about the standard changed — this is the filename, never the standard. No\n`main` freeze, no relaxed exact-head rule, no `.agent` conflict exemption.\n\n## #2845 — evidence rebound to the head under review\n\nA branch refreshed from `main` after its pair was written kept the OLD `base_sha` and\n`head_sha` while its recorded check results stayed presented as current. Nothing\nrefused it.\n\nThe published contract is immutable, so the current merge base is recorded by the\n**completion report**, which is regenerated at every refresh anyway.\n`verifyGitEvidence` now refuses when the evidence base is not the pull request's\nmerge base with `main`, and `scripts/refresh-code-pr-branch.mjs` rebinds both\n`base_sha` and `head_sha` and re-runs the checks. A report carrying no `base_sha` is\njudged on its contract's `base_sha`, so a branch that never refreshed passes exactly\nas before.\n\nThe files_changed comparison now runs from the merge base rather than the raw PR base\nSHA, which is what the report was always meant to describe and is strictly more\ntolerant of `main` moving.\n\n## The approval carry-forward rule is preserved\n\nAGENTS.md: \"Refreshing from main keeps the APPROVE ... ignoring only `.agent/`\nevidence files.\" That exclusion is `':(top,exclude).agent/'` in\n`scripts/lib/pr-content-equivalence.mjs` — the whole `.agent/` tree, by prefix — so it\nalready covers `.agent/work/<work_issue>/<generation>/` with no change. AGENTS.md now\nsays so explicitly. `check-main-tip-freshness.mjs`'s production-inert rule matched\n`.agent/*.json` only at the top level and has been widened to follow the pair down\nthe tree, for the same unchanged reason: no production step reads `.agent/` at all.\n\n## What existing open pull requests must do to adapt\n\n**Nothing, to keep passing.** The legacy pair stays valid, deliberately: forcing every\nopen pull request to rewrite its evidence would have caused exactly the re-review\nstorm this change exists to stop.\n\nTwo things to know:\n\n1. A pull request that **refreshes from main** after this lands must regenerate its\n   completion report at the new head — `node scripts/refresh-code-pr-branch.mjs\n   --issue <n> --pr <n>` does it, and now writes `base_sha`. A branch that does not\n   refresh is untouched.\n2. New work should use the keyed path. Mixing both pairs in one pull request is\n   refused.\n\n## Checks\n\n- `node --test` on every changed test file: 64 pass, 0 fail.\n- Each regression test fails on the pre-change code and passes after, for both issues\n  (`#2708:` and `#2845:` prefixed tests in\n  `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.test.mjs`,\n  `scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.test.mjs`,\n  `scripts/refresh-code-pr-branch.test.mjs`).\n- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: exit 0, no output.\n\n## Known limit, recorded not hidden\n\n`verifyMergedPrIssueBinding` in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` still\nreads the legacy `.agent/completion.json` at a merged head. That file carries another\nsession's uncommitted issue #2678 work in the worktree this session was handed, so it\nwas left untouched rather than entangled. The gap fails CLOSED — an operator-invoked\nrecovery binding on a keyed-path pull request refuses with \"unreadable\" rather than\nbinding wrongly — and is tracked as its own follow-up issue.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n","createdAt":"2026-09-20T15:29:44Z","files":[{"path":".agent/work/2708/3/completion.json","additions":44,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".agent/work/2708/3/contract.json","additions":64,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml","additions":23,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"AGENTS.md","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/agents/agent-work-contract-repo-maintenance-evidence.md","additions":44,"deletions":5,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs","additions":45,"deletions":11,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.test.mjs","additions":51,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-live-proof-probe.mjs","additions":6,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-main-tip-freshness.mjs","additions":5,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs","additions":107,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.test.mjs","additions":51,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/refresh-code-pr-branch.mjs","additions":50,"deletions":14,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/refresh-code-pr-branch.test.mjs","additions":39,"deletions":5,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"397a404eee1834fb2655a8a29b08760207da03e3","mergedAt":"2026-09-20T17:24:01Z","number":3323,"title":"fix(evidence): disjoint generation-keyed agent evidence paths (#2708) bound to the head under review (#2845)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3323"},
{"body":"Closes #3001 (deferred from #2728 / PR #2980). Repo-maintenance; no migration lane, no db claim, no database write.\n\n**Sidecar registry: already delivered, verified, not rebuilt.** The single sidecar declaration registry #3001 asks for landed on main under #3028 as commit `1eac6a8227c0c3b7741335bb8f3cf10cbfd3ab02` (\"feat: single sidecar declaration registry bound to delivery preflight\"), which `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms is an ancestor of current main. `config/production-verification-sidecar-registry.json` is now the only declaration point (60 sidecars), read by `load_sidecar_registry` in `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py` and pinned into `PREVIEW_PRODUCER_PATHS`; an undeclared sidecar file and a declaration without its file are both refused by `check_production_verification_sidecars.py`. Rewriting working code was not in scope.\n\n**Ownership check.** PR #2970, which owned `production_business_risk_gate.py` when #3001 was filed, is merged (`dae4becb79ae`). None of the 23 currently open pull requests touches `production_business_risk_gate.py`, `delivery-preflight*`, or `check_pass2_routine_supersession.py`, so the file is no longer contended.\n\n**The two edge cases named in #2728 now have direct tests.**\n\n1. `test_multiword_type_arguments_keep_both_words_in_the_guard` — `double precision`, `character varying` and `timestamp with time zone` keep both words, so the leading word is read as part of the TYPE and never stripped as a parameter name.\n2. `test_procedure_drop_keeps_out_arguments_in_the_guard` — `drop procedure f(in p text, out r int)` keeps the OUT argument type, because OUT arguments are part of a PROCEDURE's identity though not a FUNCTION's.\n\nBoth describe behaviour that was already correct but untested, so both pass against the pre-change code. That is stated plainly rather than dressed up as a regression: they are the coverage #2728 recorded as missing.\n\n**One real defect repaired, with a test that fails first.** `test_drop_routine_with_out_arguments_guards_both_candidate_signatures` FAILS on the unfixed code. Verified by removing only the implementation change and re-running; verbatim failure line:\n\n```\nAssertionError: \"to_regprocedure('public.deactivate_stale_sg_files(text, int)') is null\" not found in \"... where to_regprocedure('public.deactivate_stale_sg_files(text)') is null) r order by ord, s, f, a, stmt;\"\n```\n\n`DROP ROUTINE` names neither FUNCTION nor PROCEDURE, so when the target declares OUT arguments the statement is ambiguous. The old `_lookup_signature` always stripped them, so the guard could never resolve a procedure and the drop replayed over a procedure a later migration had re-created. `_lookup_signatures` now returns both candidate forms and `_drop_row` requires BOTH to be absent before the drop replays.\n\n**No refusal is narrowed.** The change adds a conjunct to an existing `WHERE` guard, so the drop-replay condition is strictly stricter than before — a replay that happened before can stop happening, never the reverse. No gate, refusal path, fail-closed branch, or blocked reason was removed or relaxed, and the sidecar registry was not altered at all.\n\n**Checks:** `git diff --check` clean; `python -m unittest scripts.test_check_pass2_routine_supersession` 42 passed (39 before); `node --test scripts/orchestrator-flow/delivery-preflight-gate.test.mjs scripts/orchestrator-flow/delivery-preflight.test.mjs` 31 passed; `python -m unittest scripts.test_production_business_risk_gate` 187 passed; `python scripts/check_production_verification_sidecars.py` `{\"status\":\"OK\",\"sidecars\":60}`.\n\nWork contract published at `refs/db-contracts/3001/1` (sha256 `d033327102902ca027cd52928ebed01b2ea5a74ff082c148930ac0668b7a9b8e`).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n","createdAt":"2026-09-20T15:29:09Z","files":[{"path":".agent/work/3001/2/completion.json","additions":42,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".agent/work/3001/2/contract.json","additions":46,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/check_pass2_routine_supersession.py","additions":15,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_check_pass2_routine_supersession.py","additions":112,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"067a9031f4624a7725b2d63b41e74e831383a508","mergedAt":"2026-09-20T20:24:57Z","number":3321,"title":"fix(#3001): guard ambiguous DROP ROUTINE on both candidate signatures; test the two deferred preflight edge cases","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3321"},

{"body":"Resolves #2876.\n\n## What was wrong\n\nThe post-apply production catalog verifier built its row-count report as:\n\n```\nselect jsonb_agg(x order by x->>'name') as report from (...) x\n```\n\n`x` is a derived-table alias — a PostgreSQL **composite record**, not JSON — so `x->>'name'` fails with SQLSTATE `42883` (`operator does not exist: record ->> unknown`). In production workflow run 34807646359 the migration applied successfully and this step then recorded a row-count **failure** instead of producing the intended report.\n\n## The repair\n\nOne expression: order by the composite field `x.name`. Deterministic `name` ordering is preserved and PostgreSQL accepts it for composite rows.\n\nNothing else changes. The complete catalog verification path — enforcement mode, object checks, privilege checks, sidecar checks and failure reporting — is untouched. Nothing is disabled, skipped, softened or replaced.\n\n## The regression is NOT vacuous — it was falsified explicitly\n\n`test_row_count_sql_orders_composite_rows_by_their_name_field` was run against the **unfixed** code on current `main`: the one-line `ORDER BY` was reverted to `x->>'name'` with the test left in place, and the test **failed**:\n\n```\nRan 1 test in 0.002s\nFAILED (failures=2)\nAssertionError: 'jsonb_agg(x order by x.name) as report' not found in\n\"select jsonb_agg(x order by x->>'name') as report from (select 'plm.b'::text as name, ... ) x\"\n```\n\nBoth subtests (one row-count target, and multiple) failed. The fix was then restored and the test passes. Exit code 1 before, 0 after.\n\n## Other evidence\n\n- Full suite: `python -m unittest scripts.test_production_catalog_verification` — `Ran 194 tests`, `OK`.\n- `node scripts/check-production-verification-sidecars.mjs --base origin/main` — `status OK` across 60 sidecars. The reviewed detector baseline is rebound because it pins the verifier's exact bytes; only `detector_source_sha256` changed, the historical marker inventory and the enforced-version set are byte-identical, and the guard still fails closed on any later unreviewed verifier edit.\n- `node --test scripts/throughput-guard/check-production-verification-sidecars.test.mjs` — 4 pass, 0 fail.\n- `git diff --check` — clean. `ai-task-gates start --class code` / `check --before review` — allowed.\n\nNo database read or write, no migration, no preview or production dispatch, and run 34807646359 was not replayed.\n\nEvidence pair is at the generation-keyed path `.agent/work/2876/9/` per #3323; the legacy `.agent` pair is left exactly as `main` has it.\n\nSupersedes the stale PR #2877 (last updated 2026-09-14, unmergeable), which is being closed in favour of this one.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\nPosted by Claude chat ${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-unknown} on 916-alien","createdAt":"2026-09-20T15:18:10Z","files":[{"path":".agent/work/2876/11/completion.json","additions":51,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".agent/work/2876/11/contract.json","additions":51,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_catalog_verification.py","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_production_catalog_verification.py","additions":12,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"3e5eaa42b311577f3f455fb9dae7d8b0d2bf03e7","mergedAt":"2026-09-24T17:43:58Z","number":3311,"title":"fix: order post-apply catalog row counts by composite field (#2876)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3311"},
{"body":"Prose-only. Resolves #2538 and #2450 together.\n\n## #2538 — HANDOFF.d hygiene\n\nRetired the handoff files whose issue is closed and which **no open issue cites**. The list was derived from a fresh local run of `scripts/report-stale-handoffs.mjs`, not from the issue body (last refreshed 2026-09-14, now superseded — the current run reports 47 files, 3 safely retirable, 33 still cited):\n\n| File | Issue | Owner (session gone) |\n|---|---|---|\n| `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-11T1152Z-edge-dev-codex-production-queue-closeout.md` | #2704 (closed) | `shared-db.orch/01a08eaa-8c89-7061-8f29-7b39095383cd` |\n| `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-16T0730Z-edge-dev-2-claude-orch-3004-closeout.md` | #3026 (closed) | `claude/orch-3004-closeout` |\n| `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-17T1305Z-edge-dev-claude-orch-3106-handover.md` | #3106 (closed) | `claude/orch-3106-handover` |\n\nEach issue's CLOSED state was re-verified with `gh issue view` immediately before removal. Per **AGENTS.md §2.1-H**, a non-owning session may retire a file only when the owning session is genuinely gone and it says so in the PR body with the evidence — that is this paragraph. The 33 files whose closed issue is still cited by an open issue were **left untouched**.\n\n## #2450 — documentation correction only\n\nVerified what the issue still asks for. Its code work was forked out before this PR: finding 1 (repoint the item list at `plm.item`) became **#2466, closed**; findings 3 and 4 (consolidation contract, missing link tables) are carried by the structural successors named in `plan_licensing_master_data_implementation.md` (#2333–#2336, #2355–#2358); findings 2 and 5 were routed with #2449, closed. Its own `db-work-scope` fence declares `work_type: documentation`.\n\nWhat was left was request 3, the documentation correction, made here in `docs/master-data-cutover-scoreboard.md`: a dated staleness banner over every row count on the page, the three counts #2450 recorded as moved, the corrections that `core.franchise` exists and `plm.item` is not empty, and a restatement of the landing-vs-canonical misreading trap that #2450 was itself originally filed on and withdrawn for. No code was guessed at.\n\n## Merge basis\n\n`git diff --name-only origin/main` is four files: three deleted Markdown handoffs and one Markdown doc. No code, test, script, workflow or configuration file is touched, so this merges under the documentation-only rule without waiting on checks.\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-20T15:17:40Z","files":[{"path":"HANDOFF.d/2026-09-11T1152Z-edge-dev-codex-production-queue-closeout.md","additions":0,"deletions":205,"changeType":"DELETED"},{"path":"HANDOFF.d/2026-09-16T0730Z-edge-dev-2-claude-orch-3004-closeout.md","additions":0,"deletions":109,"changeType":"DELETED"},{"path":"HANDOFF.d/2026-09-17T1305Z-edge-dev-claude-orch-3106-handover.md","additions":0,"deletions":51,"changeType":"DELETED"},{"path":"docs/master-data-cutover-scoreboard.md","additions":20,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"fb1788ae46caff624fc976c13235124b2d10b466","mergedAt":"2026-09-20T15:33:46Z","number":3310,"title":"docs: retire 3 stale HANDOFF.d files (#2538) and correct stale master-data counts (#2450)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3310"},

{"body":"Fixes #3295.\n\nThe scheduled master load timed out in the `item_header` audit insert because each changed item independently scanned that table's change history for its newest prior raw row. {"body":"Closes #3280\n\n## What this is\n\nIssue #2530 Phase C Step 7 (issue #3280): merge-queue trigger support across every required-check emitter, plus a dual-mode guarded merge lane. **Rebuilt from current `main` (`7d98876e`)** — the previous head `045be5c6` was conflicting and carried an unanswered `VERDICT: REVISE d6370dfeae26a8b4ca9a83cb575f5f5e1987ae67`. That old head is superseded, not lost; its contract generation `refs/db-contracts/3280/1` is left immutable.\n\nThis lands the implementation only. **Activating the live merge queue is a separate owner-authorized step and is not performed here.**\n\n## The REVISE finding, answered as a class\n\nThe reviewer's point: on a `merge_group` run the checkout action is handed the queue group commit **SHA**, so no `origin/<branch>` remote-tracking ref is created *even at `fetch-depth: 0`* — the ancestor objects are present, the ref is not. Any guard that resolves a base ref **by name** therefore hard-fails on every queue run.\n\nRather than patch the one job named, the whole class is fixed:\n\n1. **`scripts/check-sql.sh` — issue #1684 EOL guard.** It resolved `origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF:-main}` and returned `2` if absent. It now fetches the base branch explicitly and falls back to `FETCH_HEAD`, the pattern Guard B in the same file already used. It still **fails closed** (`return 2`) when nothing resolves — never skipped, never downgraded to a warning.\n2. **`scripts/check-production-verification-sidecars.mjs` — `resolveBase()`.** Same explicit-fetch fallback, same unchanged `UNVERIFIABLE` failure when no base resolves.\n3. **Directory-wide sweep test.** `scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs` now enumerates *every* workflow in `.github/workflows/` that triggers on `merge_group`, and fails any that invokes a base-ref consumer without an explicit fetch. It matches invocations, not mentions, so a comment naming a guard or a run of its `*.test.mjs` is not a false positive. A future `merge_group` workflow cannot reintroduce the defect silently.\n4. **Real regression coverage.** New tests build a git repository, push to a local `origin`, then check out detached at the SHA with every `refs/remotes/origin/*` deleted — the exact `merge_group` shape — and prove (a) the guard resolves its base via the fetch, and (b) with the remote removed it still fails closed with its original message.\n\nAudit result: those two scripts are the **only** base-ref-by-name consumers in the repository. The other `merge_group` workflows that touch a base (`cancelled-work-guard`, `handoff-contract-guard`, `shared-supabase-migrations`, `merge-queue-gate`) already fetch explicitly; `agent-work-contract` and `pr-object-collision` resolve SHAs, not refs, so they are outside the class.\n\n## `.agent` evidence\n\nRegenerated with the repository's own tooling — nothing hand-written:\n\n```\nnode scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs --validate-contract   --contract-file .agent/contract.json\nnode scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs --publish-contract    --contract-file .agent/contract.json\nnode scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs --validate-completion --report-file .agent/completion.json --contract-file .agent/contract.json --expected-pr 3279 --expected-head-sha 262638c57ce0a51ec4ea65e337559ca4cee91fc9\n```\n\nPublished immutable contract: `refs/db-contracts/3280/2` (`d552703e`, hash `6ce8059e…`). This also resolves the `.agent` conflict that made the PR `CONFLICTING`; see issue #2708 for the shared-path collision being fixed in parallel.\n\n## Checks run locally at this head\n\n| command | result |\n| --- | --- |\n| `node --test scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs` | 11 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped |\n| `node --test scripts/merge-queue-contract.test.mjs` | 15 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped |\n| `node --test scripts/configure-merge-queue.test.mjs` | 13 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped |\n| `node --test scripts/check-sql.test.mjs` | 58 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped |\n| `node --test scripts/throughput-guard/check-production-verification-sidecars.test.mjs` | 5 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped |\n\n## Safety\n\nNo required check is disabled, weakened, path-filtered or made optional; no guard is turned into a warning; the guarded lane keeps every safeguard and still never uses `--admin`. No SQL migration, no database change.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n\n","createdAt":"2026-09-18T19:15:14Z","files":[{"path":".agent/work/3280/6/completion.json","additions":123,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".agent/work/3280/6/contract.json","additions":118,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml","additions":27,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/cancelled-work-guard.yml","additions":5,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/coldlion-promotion-contract-tests.yml","additions":4,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/database-contract-tests.yml","additions":4,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/domain-ownership.yml","additions":4,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml","additions":31,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/handoff-contract-guard.yml","additions":34,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/intake-pointer-guard.yml","additions":4,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/merge-queue-gate.yml","additions":165,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml","additions":6,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/orchestrator-marker-guard.yml","additions":4,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/pr-object-collision.yml","additions":9,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/queue-sensitive-aggregate.yml","additions":9,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml","additions":45,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/tools-offline-tests.yml","additions":16,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/merge-queue-operation.md","additions":95,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughpu {"body":"## Outcome\n\nCloses #3273. A non-draft open PR editing `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` no longer precedes a newer PR when ALL of these hold:\n\n- **(a)** it has had no activity for 24+ hours (commits, reviews, labels, edits, ordinary comments — a stale-place nudge comment never counts as activity on the PR it was posted on);\n- **(b)** its latest checks are failing (latest run per check name) OR it conflicts with main (`mergeable === false` / `mergeable_state: dirty`);\n- **(c)** the newer PR's session has posted a dated nudge comment on it naming the stale state, using the machine-readable marker `stale-place-nudge: pr=#<newer> date=<YYYY-MM-DD> state=<...>`.\n\nThe predecessor **reclaims its place automatically** once refreshed and green — conditions (a)/(b) stop holding, no state is kept or reset. **Fail closed:** any unreadable signal (activity, checks, mergeability, comments) means no skip, and a nudge naming a different PR number yields the place to nobody.\n\n## Evidence (2026-09-18)\n\nPRs #3215, #3217 and #3228 sat 8+ hours ahead of #3247 in the protected-source queue tonight with no expiry — the only escape was waiting for a human to merge or close them.\n\n## Scope\n\nRepository maintenance: `scripts/check-pr-source-collisions.mjs` + its test only. No migration, no schema object, no database write. Contract published as `refs/db-contracts/3273/1` before the implementation commit.\n\n## Checks\n\n- `node --test scripts/check-pr-source-collisions.test.mjs` — 16 pass, 0 fail (nudge-gated skip, nudge gating, reclaim-after-refresh, green-recent-never-skipped, conflict-only condition (b), fail-closed, nudge-not-activity, marker parse/refuse, latest-checks, conflicts, gather wiring).\n- `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` (all 72 files, chunked locally) — zero regressions; the only failures reproduce identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout (pre-existing environment/fixture issues, cf. #3255).\n- `node scripts/check-cancelled-work.mjs` — OK.\n\n\n\n---\n\nRebased onto current `main` on 2026-09-20 by a landing session. The only conflict was the\n`.agent` work-contract evidence pair; this pull request's own pair was kept and republished\nas generation 4. No part of the stale-place implementation changed.\n\nScope note for review: this rule releases only the protected-source **queue slot**. It changes\nno review requirement and no check requirement — a stale predecessor simply stops serializing a\nnewer pull request; it is not merged, not approved, and not exempted from anything.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\nPosted by Claude chat 2e3c24d5-f6b8-44f8-b49f-3c67c1647d13 on 916-alien\n","createdAt":"2026-09-18T17:42:23Z","files":[{"path":".agent/work/3273/7/completion.json","additions":54,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".agent/work/3273/7/contract.json","additions":54,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"HANDOFF.d/2026-09-18T1806Z-edge-dev-kimi-3273-stale-place-mid-cycle.md","additions":0,"deletions":276,"changeType":"DELETED"},{"path":"scripts/check-pr-source-collisions.mjs","additions":173,"deletions":10,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-pr-source-collisions.test.mjs","additions":124,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/lib/open-pr-files.test.mjs","additions":14,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"46c548fa426de785748a4f3cf6df5550ce588027","mergedAt":"2026-09-25T11:26:57Z","number":3274,"title":"Stale-place rule: stale red/conflicted protected-source PRs yield the queue (#3273)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3274"},
{"body":"Closes #3271 (non-orchestrator work: no database structure change). Found while proving #3242, popcre/ai-devops#401 Step 7.\n\n## Why\nThe pass loop ran `node … > /tmp/pass.json` then `CODE=$?` under the step's `bash -e`, so a failing pass ended the step before its error JSON was printed, and the relay step was skipped. Live: leg 35342433808 reserved PR #3269's slot-2 reroute at 14:21:02Z, then ended with exit 1 and no JSON and no successor.\n\n## What\n- `|| CODE=$?` capture; a failed pass sets `failed=1` and the leg keeps watching (later passes resume the dispatch, bounded by `RESUME_ATTEMPT_LIMIT`); the leg exits `$failed`.\n- The relay step runs on `!cancelled()`, so a red leg still hands on.\n- Header comment updated. Checks: node tests 44 pass; guard pytest 275 passed; transport and identity conformance 0. A bash `-e` simulation of the loop printed all three passes and exited 1.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\nPosted by Claude chat e55a0f04-d3a0-4c38-b262-8214e273d1cf on edge-dev\n","createdAt":"2026-09-18T14:37:53Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":22,"deletions":19,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":23,"deletions":30,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/reviewer-start-watch.yml","additions":19,"deletions":6,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":9,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"415c59035a555a02a153c668bd3ff724b68b47da","mergedAt":"2026-09-18T20:45:48Z","number":3272,"title":"fix(#3271): reviewer start watch prints a failed pass and keeps relaying","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3272"},

{"body":"## Summary\nGuarded-lane merges push to main as `github-actions` using the workflow token. GitHub starts no `push` workflow for a push made with that token, so `sync.yml` (push-only trigger) never fired after a guarded merge — every consumer went stale. Evidence: #3254 merged as 2f204a48 started no sync run; #3263, merged by a human, started run 35351543065.\n\n- `sync.yml`: add `workflow_dispatch` alongside `push`.\n- `guarded-migration-merge.yml`: after the merge step proves success, dispatch `sync.yml` on `main` via `gh workflow run`, gated on that outcome so it never fires on a failed/skipped merge. Adds `actions: write`, scoped to this job only.\n- `scripts/check-guarded-merge-sync-dispatch.test.mjs`: offline shape tests for the trigger, the gating order, and the scoped permission.\n\nNo database, preview or production action. Repository-maintenance only; not routed to the shape orchestrator.\n\nCloses #3264\n\n## Test plan\n- [x] `node --test scripts/check-guarded-merge-sync-dispatch.test.mjs`\n- [x] `node --test scripts/check-lane-route-sync.test.mjs`\n- [x] `node --test scripts/lib/documents-only-change.test.mjs`\n- [x] `node scripts/check-github-transport-conformance.mjs`\n- [ ] Live proof after merge: a sync.yml run on the merge commit with all nine jobs successful (posted to #3264)\n\nPosted by Claude chat 3886eb83-7824-4477-a257-dd3adfd80d03 on edge-dev\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-18T13:56:43Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":26,"deletions":9,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":24,"deletions":13,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml","additions":12,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/sync.yml","additions":12,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-guarded-merge-sync-dispatch.test.mjs","additions":60,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"4382cb471da88e33f08e6dc340dbd6442986fb25","mergedAt":"2026-09-18T16:48:20Z","number":3268,"title":"fix(#3264): dispatch sync.yml after a guarded-lane merge lands","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3268"},

{"body":"Closes #3242 (non-orchestrator work: no database structure change). Programme popcre/ai-devops#401 Step 7. Follows #3243.\n\n## Why\nAfter #3243 merged, no scheduled run appeared. This public repository's crons fire every three to four hours whatever they ask for (the `*/10` alert monitor ran 00:03, 04:36, 09:11 on 2026-09-18), so a `*/5` schedule cannot meet the 10-minute start SLO.\n\n## What\n`.github/workflows/reviewer-start-watch.yml` only; the watcher script is unchanged.\n- An applying run is a **relay leg**: a watcher pass every `PASS_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (60) for `LEG_MINUTES` (330), then it dispatches the next leg with its own `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`actions: write`) and ends. Job timeout 355 minutes.\n- The cron is only the restart net: a scheduled run first checks for another live run of this workflow and starts a leg only when there is none, so cron firings never stack legs. Only a leg on `main` relays. Job-level concurrency keeps one leg running.\n- A failing pass exits non-zero at once and dispatches **no** successor, so a broken watcher is one red run waiting for the cron, not a stream.\n- Report-only dispatch (`apply=false`) is one pass, no relay. Report-only now also applies `DRAWN_SINCE`, so its decisions match an applying pass.\n- Step summary: full JSON only for passes that acted or failed; waiting, skipped and already-started leases count as quiet (one line).\n\n## Tests\n- 44 pass, 0 fail (reviewer-start-watch plus start-reroute); `test_production_migration_guard.py` 275 passed; transport and repository-identity conformance clean.\n- Loop step run locally in report-only mode: one pass, exit 0, summary line written.\n\nReview seq 3249 (REVISE) fixed as a class at the new head.\n\nPosted by Claude chat e55a0f04-d3a0-4c38-b262-8214e273d1cf on edge-dev\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-18T11:40:45Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":13,"deletions":13,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":9,"deletions":12,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/reviewer-start-watch.yml","additions":80,"deletions":25,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"d98572ed0c35c75adbb5e90d3bfc6bf8d62a1a34","mergedAt":"2026-09-18T12:00:04Z","number":3257,"title":"fix(#3242): keep the reviewer start watcher running as a self-dispatching relay","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3257"},

{"body":"Closes #3251 (repo-maintenance lane; source-data outcome on #3180).\n\nThe /proddetails reconciliation counted succeeded `sync_run` rows — correct during backfill (one run per key), wrong once the refresh regime re-reads answered orders. The first live refresh (2026-09-18, workflow run 35312282365) reported `keysDone=7016 / rowsFetchedTotal=28765` against 3,753 keys / 17,303 landed rows and **correctly failed its own agreement check** — the guard worked exactly as designed on a wrong input. The landed table was perfect throughout: `tableRows=17303=distinctPkey`, re-reads idempotent, zero collapse, `refusedKeys=8`.\n\nThe read now takes `distinct on (prod_order_no)` at the **latest** succeeded run per key: the rows that run fetched are the rows that run's upsert landed, so the sums are comparable again. The agreement predicate is untouched — it still detects a missing table row, a pkey collapse, and a zero-row key counted as landed. Regression test pins the distinct-on shape with the run reference.\n\nPart of #3180 (do not close it; the originating session owns closure).","createdAt":"2026-09-18T07:58:30Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":15,"deletions":10,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":16,"deletions":13,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"tools/coldlion-landing-prod-details.test.mjs","additions":11,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"tools/coldlion-landing/lib/prod-details.mjs","additions":15,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"6edb6dcb9726add30e2303693abe17e611cb3acf","mergedAt":"2026-09-18T09:47:06Z","number":3252,"title":"fix(#3251): count keys, not runs, in the /proddetails reconciliation","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3252"},
{"body":"Closes #3249 (repo-maintenance lane; source-data outcome on #3180).\n\nThe nightly ColdLion Landing Sync job's 90-minute ceiling no longer fits the work now that the prepack (#3179) and production-detail (#3180) refreshes ride it. Measured live on 2026-09-18 (dispatch run 35303647480, cancelled by the job timeout mid-prod-detail-refresh): setup + offline gate ~4 min, history ~2, masters ~4, prepack ~43 (2,577 codes at 1s), prod-detail up to ~63 (~1.9s/key over up to 2,000 recent orders) — ~116 min worst case.\n\nOne line changes: `timeout-minutes: 90` → `150`, with the dated arithmetic in a comment. The ceiling remains a real stall-killing budget (#1266); the concurrency group still serializes the lane; triggers, secrets, target declarations, offline-gate-before-write and loader limits are untouched.\n\nPart of #3180 (do not close it; the originating session owns closure).","createdAt":"2026-09-18T05:19:24Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":10,"deletions":19,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":21,"deletions":26,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/coldlion-landing-sync.yml","additions":7,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"e81264f21160379908c0b21f7d4fb6c1a4ce3330","mergedAt":"2026-09-18T05:48:20Z","number":3250,"title":"ci(#3249): raise the ColdLion Landing Sync job ceiling to 150 minutes","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3250"},
{"body":"## What this carries\n\nThis PR is **Step 0 of `plan_coldlion_order_intake.md`** (its docs-only and plan-registration items combined into one prose PR):\n\n1. **Business rules** (`docs/business-rules/erp-orders-and-source-meaning.md`, new intake section; `application-map.md`; `master-data-access.md`): the OrderList intake workflow (Adam/JamieLynn/Yuchen), the Settled automation ruling (intra-day unsealed current-window poll; JamieLynn's ERP entry stays manual), Order Type + Ship To as one `warehouseCode` routing code (POE vs DDP definitions; Forman Mills/Shoppers World are DDP), the 1:N sales-order→production-order ruling (placeholder + line-claim model), the forward-scan horizon ruling (\"API calls are cheap\"), `shipPortCode` as the FOB Ship To source, the superseded pre-2026-08-31 bare-list paging paragraph, and the poNumber-normalization / ERP-date / production-side-recovery join rules. Every ColdLion claim was verified live against the API on 2026-09-17.\n2. **The implementation plan** `plan_coldlion_order_intake.md` (v4.1) + its `AGENTS.md` registration + `HANDOFF.d/` entry. The plan was audited read-only three times (Qwen 3.8 Max → REJECT on v1; Grok 4.6 → \"not ready\" on v2; Muse → \"not ready\" on v3) with a Muse convergence turn returning **\"ready for a fresh implementing session\"** after the final tiebreak fix. Every load-bearing finding from all three audits was independently re-verified against this repository before incorporation — including one audit correcting another (sealed landing tables DO `grant all … to service_role`, `20260905105038:780-782`).\n\n## Review guidance\n\nRead the business-rules intake section first — the plan defers to it as authority and will not restate the rulings. The plan's STATUS table is the state marker (all open except C0, which is ✅ ruled). Audit reports remain local under the git-ignored `.ai/reviews/`.\n\nNo code, no migrations, no workflow changes in this PR — prose only.\n\nCloses #3262\n","createdAt":"2026-09-18T02:29:14Z","files":[{"path":".agent/work/3262/13/completion.json","additions":45,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".agent/work/3262/13/contract.json","additions":56,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"docs/agents/active-contracts-and-plans.md","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/business-rules/application-map.md","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/business-rules/erp-orders-and-source-meaning.md","additions":227,"deletions":6,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/business-rules/master-data-access.md","additions":3,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"plan_coldlion_order_intake.md","additions":782,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"cbdace8bcbeb4ba080f6768ea436033d59ca8570","mergedAt":"2026-09-25T22:45:00Z","number":3248,"title":"docs: ColdLion automatic order intake — settled rules and audited plan","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3248"},
{"body":"## Outcome\n\nCloses #3232. Enforces the owner's 2026-09-17 ruling — **\"I never want GLM reviewing GLM code\"** — in the reviewer draw: a GLM-engine (ZCode) orchestrator can now never draw the `glm` reviewers, exactly the way a Codex orchestrator never draws the Codex reviewer.\n\nRepository maintenance on scripts and tests only — no migration, no schema object, no database write.\n\n## What changed\n\n1. **`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`**\n   - The `glm-5.3` row and the retained `glm-5.2` label row now carry `orchestratorEngine:'glm'` (the precedent set by `codex-gpt-5.6-sol`).\n   - `reviewersForOrchestrator` maps the declared engine through the new exported `ENGINE_REVIEWER_EXCLUSION = { codex:'codex', claude:'claude', zcode:'glm' }` before comparing — the exclusion follows the **model engine behind the harness**, not the harness name. For codex and claude the mapping is the identity, so those orchestrations behave exactly as today; an unknown engine falls back to the raw string (pre-#3232 behaviour; the marker resolver rejects unknown engines long before this point).\n   - The map deliberately lives **beside the reviewer rows it filters, not as an import from `lib/orchestrator-routing.mjs`**: importing the routing module into the manager would pull it (and `orchestrator-admission.mjs`) into the manager's import closure and make every future routing edit a global evidence invalidator (`config/orchestrator-global-invalidators-v1.json`). The lane test suite instead asserts the routing engine vocabulary and this map agree key-for-key, so neither can drift alone.\n\n2. **`scripts/lib/orchestrator-routing.mjs`**\n   - `ENGINES` gains a `zcode` entry: session ids shaped `sess_<uuid>` (`ZCODE_SESSION_ID`), with an honest `howToReach` — the same headless `zcode --resume` `ai-blocker-watch` already uses to wake waiting zcode sessions. A ZCode orchestrator can now declare itself truthfully; previously the only valid marker paths were omitting the engine (reviewer assignment refused, fail closed) or misdeclaring `claude`/`codex` (excluded the wrong engine and left glm drawable).\n\n3. **`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`** — the three requested tests plus the coupling pin:\n   - (a) a glm-family/zcode orchestrator excludes **both** glm rows from the drawable set, draws a full cycle of everyone else, and the declared-marker path (`engine: zcode` → resolve → draw) chains the same way;\n   - (b) codex and claude orchestrations keep `glm-5.3` drawable and exclude only their own families — exactly as before;\n   - (c) a marker declaring no engine still refuses reviewer assignment;\n   - `ENGINE_REVIEWER_EXCLUSION` keys must equal `ENGINES` keys, and `zcode → glm` must match the family the glm rows carry.\n\n## Acceptance (read-only re-check, run against this head)\n\n- A synthetic marker declaring `engine: zcode` with a `sess_<uuid>` route id validates through the real `parseRoutingBlock`/`validateRouting`; `orchestratorEngineFromResolution` returns `zcode`; `reviewersForOrchestrator` returns a set **without** `glm-5.3` and `glm-5.2` (ACTIVE drawable: grok-4.6, kimi-k3, qwen-3.8-max, muse-spark-1.3-contributor, gemini-3.8-flash-high).\n- Lane test suite green: 607/607 in `manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`; the full CI coordination list (lease + collision jobs, incl. all `orchestrator-flow` suites) is 1450 pass / 0 fail; marker resolver and admission suites green.\n- **No reviewer's registration or rotation membership changes**: `ACTIVE_REVIEWERS`, `RETIRED_REVIEWERS` and `QUARANTINED_REVIEWERS` are name-for-name identical to `origin/main` (verified by importing both versions side by side).\n\n## Not in scope (unchanged)\n\nZCode is not added as a reviewer (permanently rejected by the same owner ruling); reviewer membership and rotation untouched; no migration or database write.\n\n\n\n---\nPosted by ZCode chat  on edge-dev\n","createdAt":"2026-09-18T02:23:45Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":15,"deletions":23,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":28,"deletions":45,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/lib/orchestrator-routing.mjs","additions":22,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":17,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":73,"deletions":12,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"d9a8720ec91f367f0a7385704edad35cbba0891c","mergedAt":"2026-09-18T14:51:07Z","number":3247,"title":"Reviewer independence: exclude glm reviewers for GLM-engine (ZCode) orchestrators (#3232)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3247"},
{"body":"## Outcome\n\nComplete the case-drift tolerance started in #3235 so the #3179 backfill can\nfinish: fold case in the key-coverage accounting, and collect each vendor row\nonce when two harvest spellings of one drifted key are both asked.\n\nCloses #3245. Refs #3179 (does NOT close it — the originating session owns\nclosure).\n\n## The live evidence\n\nThe re-dispatched final slice (Actions run 35294603177) passed the #3235\ncase-folded identity guard — the drift tolerance worked — and then aborted\nfail-closed on:\n\n```\nincomplete key coverage: the fetched rows do not account for every requested code\n```\n\nDiagnosis: the harvest holds BOTH spellings of the drifted key as distinct\ncodes (the vendor emitted `PPk133` through one feed and `PPK133` through\nanother), and both responses answer `PPK133`. The old cross-key arithmetic\n(two asked keys ≠ zero zero-rows + one distinct returned spelling) read that\nas a hole. This is exactly the residual the #3236 review named. Nothing was\nwritten; the failed run is recorded.\n\n## The change\n\n`collectPrepackDetail` in `tools/coldlion-landing/sync-prepack-detail.mjs`:\n\n1. **Per-key, case-folded coverage**: every asked code must be accounted for by\n   either its own zero-row response or returned rows answering it\n   case-insensitively. Cross-key arithmetic is gone. A row answering a code\n   unrelated to the request can never reach the count — the identity guard has\n   already refused it.\n2. **Collect each row once**: when two spellings of one key both return the\n   same vendor row (same grain, byte-identical), it is one row fetched twice,\n   not a duplicate — the duplicate-key refusal inside the projection would\n   otherwise abort the run. Rows that DIFFER for one grain still refuse loudly\n   (`conflicting rows for one natural key across two requested spellings`).\n3. `rowsFetched` keeps reporting the raw fetch count, so nothing landed is\n   hidden; the run notes and landed counts stay honest about both.\n\n## Verification\n\n`node --test tools/coldlion-landing-prepack.test.mjs` — 37/37 pass, with three\nnew pins: both spellings asked → one row, coverage holds; sibling-answered\nzero-row spelling accounted; differing bytes across spellings refuse.\n\n## Post-merge\n\nRe-dispatch the final bounded slice (777 pending) and reconcile.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-18T02:21:36Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":8,"deletions":11,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":13,"deletions":15,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"tools/coldlion-landing-prepack.test.mjs","additions":50,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"tools/coldlion-landing/sync-prepack-detail.mjs","additions":41,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"0270aada2e73e318ec889c467d939c53e596f0ec","mergedAt":"2026-09-18T02:49:17Z","number":3246,"title":"fix(#3245): account drifted key spellings per-key and collect each row once","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3246"},

{"body":"Closes #3242 (non-orchestrator work: no database structure change). Programme popcre/ai-devops#401 Step 7.\n\n## What\n- New `.github/workflows/reviewer-start-watch.yml`: runs `scripts/orchestrator-flow/reviewer-start-watch.mjs --apply --drawn-since $DRAWN_SINCE` every 5 minutes (plus `workflow_dispatch`, with a dry-run option). No push/PR trigger. One pass at a time, never cancelled mid-reroute. Runs the watcher's own tests first.\n- Watcher safety for unattended use:\n  - **Churn cap:** each (issue, PR, slot) gets at most `AUTO_REROUTES_PER_SLOT = 2` automatic reroutes; after that the lease stays on the ordinary two-hour silence path. An unreadable reroute history refuses the reroute.\n  - **Fail loudly:** a pass whose reroute or resumed dispatch failed exits 1 (was always 0).\n- `DRAWN_SINCE = 2026-09-18T02:00:00Z`: the current backlog of overdue leases is left alone; only leases drawn once this is live are rerouted.\n\n## Tests\n- `reviewer-start-watch.test.mjs` 21/21, `start-reroute.test.mjs` 23/23, `test_production_migration_guard.py` 275 passed, transport / repository-identity / throughput-truth conformance clean.\n\n## Live proof (after merge)\nFirst scheduled run, then one live unstarted reviewer rerouted automatically at the first pass after its 10-minute SLO while the other slot's lease stays intact; evidence goes on #3242.\n\nPosted by Claude chat e55a0f04-d3a0-4c38-b262-8214e273d1cf on edge-dev\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n","createdAt":"2026-09-18T01:54:00Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":21,"deletions":23,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":28,"deletions":40,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/reviewer-start-watch.yml","additions":101,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/reviewer-start-watch.mjs","additions":27,"deletions":6,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/reviewer-start-watch.test.mjs","additions":39,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"02bdf5193e96f022f3c28c0fcd9e8669309c4c30","mergedAt":"2026-09-18T11:15:08Z","number":3243,"title":"feat(#3242): run the reviewer start watcher unattended every 5 minutes","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3243"},

{"body":"## What\n\nAdds a **\"record the meaning, not only the answer\"** step to the business-rules collection process, plus the matching storage guard.\n\n- `How rules are collected` (new step 3): alongside the recorded answer, record under a clearly separated **\"What this changes\"** heading what the ruling changes about how existing rules are read, what it connects to across topics, and what it leaves open. Skipped only when the ruling connects to nothing — a one-line disposition needs no synthesis paragraph.\n- `How rules are stored` (new bullet): explanation lives in a clearly separated block and is never authority. Only the four statuses (Settled / Proposed / Historical / Unknown) carry authority, and a meaning note never changes a rule's status or upgrades it to Settled.\n\n## Why\n\nThe library's charter says topics hold *meanings* of business objects and relationships, but the collection procedure was transcription-shaped (\"Capture the exact business question… Record the answer…\"). Nothing asked a session to record interpretation, implications, or cross-topic connections, so sessions produced well-filed transcripts rather than explained rules — the documented failure mode of sessions re-deriving or misreading settled facts (e.g. `prodReferenceNo` ending `COS` is only safe to apply because its meaning layer is recorded with it: real cost, no customer revenue, so `salesOrderNo = 0` there is correct).\n\nThe authority boundary is deliberately tight: meaning is explanation, never authority — interpretations are marked as interpretation in text, and anything load-bearing takes Proposed or Unknown status through the existing mechanism.\n\n## Scope\n\nDocs-only change to `docs/business-rules/README.md`. The matching companion edits to the `pop-business-rules` Skill procedure (both copies, local skill files outside this repo) are applied in the same workstream.\n\nTask gate: class `prose`, required gate `repository-branch-and-pr` (satisfied by this PR).\n","createdAt":"2026-09-18T00:19:10Z","files":[{"path":"docs/business-rules/README.md","additions":11,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"5fdde4b19ac5d29c64cb2c777bdda67623ec5c34","mergedAt":"2026-09-18T00:29:34Z","number":3238,"title":"docs: record rule meaning, not only the answer, in the business-rules process","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3238"},
