{"body":"Step 7 of `plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md`, the completion step: full regression, live read-only proof of the finished lifecycle, the two fixes that proof demanded, the final STATUS and definition of done, and retirement of the plan's handoff.\n\n## What live verification found\n\nTwo defects that 980 passing unit tests could not see, because both need a real record written before the current conventions existed.\n\n**One legacy claim title silenced the whole hourly instrument.** The claim-identity read ran outside the per-domain failing legs of the flow snapshot. Live claim #2871 is titled `CLAIM: issue-2870-cutover-columns` and contains no `#<number>`, so the identity read threw out of the map and the snapshot came back empty: the hourly audit described none of the other seven lanes. The identity read is now its own failing leg. One unreadable claim is one unreadable row, reported as unverifiable in both the capacity and the preview domain, with the claim number in the message so an operator knows which claim to fix.\n\n**A refusal was announced as an expiry.** That refusal then fell through to the generic handler, which exits `2`. On `--abandonment-audit`, `2` already means \"an expired author lane was found\", so the scheduled run at main head `3fdd16ef` logged the refusal and then `##[error]Expired author lane(s) detected` — a report about lanes it had never read. A refusal on this command now exits `3`: an instrument that could not read is exactly the unverifiable case, and unverifiable already outranks expiry here. The `REFUSED` line is still printed in full, and every other command keeps the generic handler and keeps exiting `2`, which a test asserts directly.\n\nNeither change relaxes anything. The second narrows one command from a wrong exit code to the stricter correct one.\n\n## Proof\n\n- 653/653 across capacity-state, reconcile, lanes and migration-pr-lease; 57/57 exclusive-lease and coordination scenarios; 272 production-guard tests OK. Zero failed, cancelled, skipped or todo.\n- Live read-only `--abandonment-audit` at this head: `\"status\": \"UNVERIFIABLE\"`, `\"mutating\": false`, zero actions carrying `\"mutates\": true`, all eight lanes described, capacity 8 issues / 7 actions / 1 unverifiable, six `expired-unconfirmed-report` actions, exit `3`. It agrees with `--queue-audit`.\n- No database, preview, production or infrastructure write. No ref, branch or worktree deleted. The lifecycle was deliberately not applied to any live expired claim to demonstrate it.\n\n`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` is the repository's single protected coordination source; the nine open pull requests were checked against the collision rule before it was edited and none of them touches it.\n\nThe plan's handoff is retired here: with Step 7 landed there is no unfinished work for it to carry. Issue #2301 itself is closed by hand once this merge is verified on `main`, because a pull request may close exactly one work issue and that one is its own step issue.\n\nThe plan file stays as the durable record and now says plainly that it is complete and must not be restarted.\n\nCloses #3018.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-16T05:29:09Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":40,"deletions":39,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":47,"deletions":55,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"HANDOFF.d/2026-09-04T1453Z-edge-dev-codex-author-lane-lifecycle-plan.md","additions":0,"deletions":79,"changeType":"DELETED"},{"path":"plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md","additions":29,"deletions":19,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":30,"deletions":6,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":41,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"a64f233e9dbc2c6b387eb58ead84abc292404a76","mergedAt":"2026-09-16T06:26:20Z","number":3019,"title":"#2301 Step 7: full regression, live report proof, final STATUS, and plan completion","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3019"},
{"body":"Closes #3015. Part of #2301, Step 6 of `plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md`.\n\nSteps 1-5 changed how author lanes behave. The rules that tell an operator what to do still described the world before them.\n\n### Drift is not a cosmetic problem\n\nA rule that lives in five files becomes five rules the moment one of them is edited alone, and the reader who follows the stale copy has no way to know which one he read. So this change brings every venue up to the behaviour that actually landed, and adds static tests that turn the next divergence into a red build rather than a discovery made during an incident.\n\nThe tests assert **agreement, not wording**. Each names a fact that must appear wherever that fact is operative: the read-only command, all three exit codes, \"an expired lease is not an abandoned lane\", the four worktree states and who decides, the prohibition on mutating lane commands in scheduled jobs, every required field of the record, and both procedures written out rather than merely named. Prose can be rewritten freely; a promise cannot be deleted from one venue while the others still make it.\n\n### Two procedures, written out\n\n**Quarantine and recovery** keeps the pull request, the claim, the object locks, the version reservation, the branch and the worktree exactly as they are: capacity is relinquished against a durable audit issue and resumed atomically through every current collision, capacity and version check.\n\n**Terminal retirement** records the evidence, closes the pull request through the normal authenticated operator flow, and retires the claim with the tombstoning `--release-claim`, so a successor must take a fresh tuple and a fresh version. No ref, branch, claim or worktree is ever deleted to free a lane.\n\n### The authority boundary is recorded, not re-decided\n\nThe orchestrator may retire work whose worktree is `clean`, or `absent` with its absence proven and its durable branch and pull-request evidence complete — in both cases nothing unrecoverable is discarded. Albert alone decides whether potentially recoverable `dirty` or `remote` uncommitted work may be abandoned.\n\n### The record\n\nThe new issue template is the durable evidence, and it is privacy-safe by shape as well as by instruction: identifiers only, and its `db-work-scope` fence carries an empty `objects:` on purpose, because claiming the object would collide with the very claim the audit is investigating.\n\nThe canonical `popcre/ai-devops` orchestrator skill is the fifth venue and is synchronized in its own repository; `check-skill-drift.mjs` is the gate that covers it and still reports no contradictions.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-16T03:54:27Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":35,"deletions":20,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":40,"deletions":28,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/author-lane-abandonment.md","additions":106,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"AGENTS.md","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md","additions":121,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md","additions":4,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_production_migration_guard.py","additions":273,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"4f3f25b86a81d290467461ce53315a82ba389c72","mergedAt":"2026-09-16T05:07:40Z","number":3016,"title":"docs(#2301): synchronize the abandonment rules, record, and procedures","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3016"},
{"body":"Resolves the production-apply refusal for migration `20260916001944`\n(ColdLion prepack / production detail landing, issue #2863).\n\n## The refusal\n\n```\nProduction business-risk gate rejected evidence: original apply run 35047947727 dispatched at 0a11c42d3e373fe9b45e826a3015c93bb7cf4704 produced evidence with a different scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs than the merge commit 6c9b149d8747293cdb306a73262bd341873bc682 of the pull request that authored 20260916001944\n```\n\nThe evidence-producing lane script changed between the dispatch commit and PR #3008's merge commit. The original preview apply is immutable and cannot be replayed, so this uses the repository's registered historical restoration route (`validateHistoricalProductionProvenance`) to rebind that one exact apply.\n\n## What changed\n\n- One new frozen entry in `scripts/historical-migration-restorations.mjs` for `20260916001944`.\n- One verification doc, `docs/verification/issue-2863-historical-producer-restoration.md`, recording the evidence.\n\nEvery value is derived from real evidence: run 35047947727 (`workflow_dispatch`, attempt 1, success), its `head_sha` `0a11c42d3e373fe9b45e826a3015c93bb7cf4704`, the `appliedCommit` `1595aec05565b1a138b6f40e09bda8191fa40acf` from the run's own `preview-instance.json`, PR #3008 and merge commit `6c9b149d8747293cdb306a73262bd341873bc682`, and the file/statement hashes computed from the migration as it exists on `origin/main`. The registry `fileSha256` equals the run artifact's `migration-content-manifest.json` digest for this version.\n\n## Validator\n\n```\n$ node scripts/historical-migration-restorations.mjs --production-provenance supabase/migrations/20260916001944_coldlion_prepack_and_prod_detail_landing.sql '<gate evidence>'\n{\"version\":\"20260916001944\",\"fileSha256\":\"c79374a85369589e3a5ed6e5f58b5ccf495e0ba1ad420f9e589b7bd1dba6aec9\"}\n```\n\nNegative control (run id off by one digit) still refuses: `historical production provenance mismatch for previewApplyRun`.\n\nNo guard is weakened, bypassed, or special-cased. No workflow is dispatched and no database is changed by this PR.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n\nCloses #3017.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-16T03:41:19Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":21,"deletions":32,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":30,"deletions":47,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/issue-2863-historical-producer-restoration.md","additions":75,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/historical-migration-restorations.mjs","additions":25,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"bcc2587d6522dffca34099e2015769b7f5972014","mergedAt":"2026-09-16T04:19:39Z","number":3014,"title":"fix(#2863): register 20260916001944 as an exact historical restoration","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3014"},
{"body":"Closes #3012. Part of #2301, Step 5 of `plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md`.\n\nAn author claim carries a lease. When the lease runs out the claim stays locked and the lane stays occupied, and nothing reports it. The queue behind it is invisible until somebody tries to allocate and is refused, which can be days later — and the refusal names the lock, not the fact that the lock's author walked away. Step 4 built the report; this runs it every hour, and makes running it safe.\n\n### Read-only by construction, not by environment\n\n`reconcileFlow` decides whether to mutate from the live sole-orchestrator marker, and a hosted runner merely *happens* not to hold one. \"Happens not to\" stops holding the day a marker leaks into CI. `reportOnlyFlowIo` removes the capability instead of relying on its absence: the marker reads as gone and every mutation hook throws if it is reached at all, so a regression fails loudly rather than writing. The test proves the stronger property — the same fixture, through the mutating entry point, really does write all three transitions, and through `--abandonment-audit` writes none.\n\n### Three exit codes, not two\n\nExpiry needs a human decision. An unreadable or malformed state means the instrument is broken. An hourly job that reported both as one number would train its operator to ignore both, so they are `2` and `3`. Unverifiable outranks expiry: an audit that could not read everything is not trusted to have seen the expiry either. Anything the classifier does not recognise — a future schema, a result claiming to have mutated — is `3`, never `0`.\n\n### The workflow files nothing, and has no permission that could\n\n`contents`, `issues` and `pull-requests` are all `read`. This repository has already produced 25 duplicate issues from an unthrottled monitor; an hourly one would be worse. The failing run and its job summary are the report. No `push:` or `pull_request:` trigger, because expiry is created by time passing and changes no file.\n\n### Verification gate\n\nWorkflow-policy tests live in the canonical guard test and assert the **declaration**, not the intent: hourly schedule, dispatch, no commit-shaped trigger, an all-read permission set with no job-level override, a bounded timeout, concurrency cancellation, pinned actions and Node, the read-only command, and the absence of every mutating flag from **every** scheduled workflow in the directory — with a positive control asserting the scan found this workflow at all, and non-comment scanning so prose explaining why a trigger is absent is not read as a trigger.\n\nExpiry is not abandonment. Nothing here transitions a claim.\n\nThe orchestrator-skill half of this step is a separate synchronized change in `popcre/ai-devops` (PR 491), not a hand edit of the installed copy.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-16T02:35:09Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":35,"deletions":31,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":26,"deletions":20,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/author-lane-abandonment-audit.yml","additions":107,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":17,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/reconcile.mjs","additions":35,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/reconcile.test.mjs","additions":78,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_production_migration_guard.py","additions":144,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"b1f9bbc0f304ed52f9223c29c6310df2492d1f10","mergedAt":"2026-09-16T03:00:50Z","number":3013,"title":"#2301 Step 5 — hourly read-only detection of expired author lanes","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3013"},
{"body":"Closes #3011. Part of #2301, Step 4 of `plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md`. Base is the merged Step 3 head `1dcf196ea9b506ec14feb55e8465b53d9faf1706`.\n\n## What changes\n\n**Capacity and preview are separate truths.** The old `reconcileFlow` collapsed both domains into one status word, so a single undecipherable preview edge reported the whole run `UNVERIFIABLE` and hid every other lane's perfectly readable capacity answer behind it. The result now carries a `capacity` and a `preview` block, each with its own status, action count and unverifiable count.\n\nThe top-level `status` keeps its exact previous meaning. The only NEW way to reach `UNVERIFIABLE` is `capacity_error`, a field that did not exist before this change, so no run a consumer has already seen can be reclassified by it. Action ordering (relinquish, resume, ready) is unchanged, so the existing consumer assertion stays a true statement about the code rather than being rewritten to fit it.\n\n**An expired-unconfirmed lane is reported, with the facts needed to judge it:** owner, expiry, how long it has been expired, its pull request and that pull request's state and head, the durable blocker, and how many lanes are queued behind it. A `queued_behind` of `null` means UNKNOWN, never zero — \"nothing is waiting behind this lane\" is a reason not to act, and \"the queue was unreadable\" is not. The queued-behind computation is lazy and memoized, so only a snapshot with at least one expired lane pays for it.\n\n**Expiry is not abandonment.** An expired lease means a clock ran out. Abandonment is a separate fact that exists only if somebody wrote the evidence down. Only an exact abandonment-audit issue — open, classified `repo-maintenance`, naming the same claim, owner, pull request and head — is recognized as evidence, and even then the reconciliation does nothing but print the separate guarded command. Nothing transitions an expired claim automatically, with or without a live sole-orchestrator marker, because no automated caller can observe somebody else's disk. That refusal is pinned by a test rather than left as an accidental throw.\n\n`--reconcile-flow` now exits 2 if either domain is unverifiable, and 0 otherwise; an expired report is a report, not a failure.\n\n## Verification\n\nAll Step 4 gates from the plan are covered in `scripts/orchestrator-flow/reconcile.test.mjs`: multi-claim isolation in both directions, expired-without-evidence reports only, an ordinary dependency blocker never suggests a relinquishment, an exact audit yields only the suggested command, the command stays marker and mutex gated, the whole tuple is re-proved against a TOCTOU window, and exit codes are deterministic per domain. A further test asserts the suggested worktree-state list equals the list the command actually accepts, so the duplicated constant cannot drift into telling an operator to run a value the command refuses.\n\nSuites re-run at the implementation head: reconcile 26/26, author lanes 578/578, capacity-state 22/22, admission-outcome 70/70, coordination-scenarios 31/31, retirement tombstones 30/30.\n\nCloses nothing on its own; #2301 stays open for Steps 5 to 7.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-16T00:47:31Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":39,"deletions":43,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":31,"deletions":41,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":127,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/reconcile.mjs","additions":138,"deletions":6,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/reconcile.test.mjs","additions":253,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"c94a69ca93b1dc78b6753e740cfb4c575ec2c718","mergedAt":"2026-09-16T02:20:45Z","number":3010,"title":"feat(lanes): separate capacity truth from preview truth in reconciliation (#2301 Step 4)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3010"},
{"body":"Closes #2863. Split from #2179, tracker #2081, plan `plan_coldlion_landing_schema_completion.md` §9 Step 6. Author lane claim #3006, reserved migration version `20260916001944`.\n\n## What this creates\n\nExactly two tables, structure only — no rows, no loader:\n\n- `coldlion.prepack_detail` — `GET /prepackDetail`, prepack recipe lines\n- `coldlion.prod_detail` — `GET /proddetails`, production-order lines\n\n## Pre-dispatch gate\n\nBoth feeds were enumerated and sampled **live** on 2026-09-15 against `http://x5.coldlion.com/EhpApi`. Full evidence: `docs/coldlion-unit-5b-grain-proof-20260915.md`.\n\n**`/prepackDetail`** — 120 prepack codes harvested from `/inventory` and `/proddetails`, every one returning rows; 456 rows, 18-field union.\n`(companyCode, prePackCode, sequence)` is **456 distinct over 456 rows, 0 duplicate groups**. This feed emits no vendor row id, so that is the smallest proven *source* identity — not a guessed natural key. The descriptive tuple is also unique here but describes the row rather than identifying it.\n\n**`/proddetails`** — 45 production orders harvested from `/prodHistory` across seven windows, every one returning rows; 166 rows, 21-field union.\nTwo identities were proven independently, each **166 distinct over 166, 0 duplicate groups**: the real vendor row id `pkey` (primary key) and `(prodOrderNo, prodLineSeq)` (asserted as a unique constraint, so a future pull that breaks it fails visibly). A plausible-looking alternative, `(prodOrderNo, itemPkey)`, **does** collapse rows — 158 of 166 — and was rejected on measurement. The payload carries no `companyCode`, so it is stamped from the request and leads the primary key.\n\n**No unexplained duplicate collapse on either feed.**\n\n**Field disposition** — all 18 and all 21 sampled fields land, plus the request-stamped `company_code` on `prod_detail`. `docs/coldlion-field-decisions-20260819.csv` is the owner's field authority but covers neither of these feeds; the grain proof records that gap explicitly and nothing is dropped on our own judgement. ColdLion emits **both** `itemPrice` and `ItemPrice` on `/prepackDetail` — a genuine duplicate-cased property — so both land and neither is folded.\n\n## Verification\n\nApplied to a disposable PostgreSQL 18 cluster (never preview, never production — Supabase MCP is read-only here):\n\n- migration applies cleanly on the phase-1 spine\n- `supabase/tests/coldlion_prepack_prod_detail_landing_contracts.sql` passes: structural contracts (D5, no FK outside `coldlion`, `sync_run` attribution, exact column counts, both grains, RLS, no application grants) plus an **idempotent-replay behaviour block** proving a re-pulled line updates rather than duplicates, that company separation works, and that a differing payload on a proven key raises `unique_violation`\n- the test was **proven able to fail**: dropping the second identity constraint makes it stop with the expected error\n- the new catalog contract was proven able to fail: granting `anon` read flips it false\n\nLocal checks: `bash scripts/check-sql.sh` passed; `node scripts/check-production-verification-sidecars.mjs --base origin/main` → `{\"status\":\"OK\",\"sidecars\":55}`; `node --test scripts/check-sql.test.mjs` 56/56; `pytest scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py scripts/test_check_production_verification_sidecars.py` 167 passed; `pytest scripts/test_production_catalog_verification.py` 190 passed.\n\n## Also in this PR\n\nThe mandatory hash-bound sidecar `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260916001944.json` with its catalog contract `coldlion_unit_5b_landing_v1`, the sidecar path pinned in `PREVIEW_PRODUCER_PATHS`, and the reviewed detector baseline hash refreshed (required whenever `production_catalog_verification.py` changes).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-16T00:39:56Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":30,"deletions":57,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":49,"deletions":53,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/coldlion-unit-5b-grain-proof-20260915.md","additions":199,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260916001944.json","additions":13,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_catalog_verification.py","additions":65,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260916001944_coldlion_prepack_and_prod_detail_landing.sql","additions":224,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/coldlion_prepack_prod_detail_landing_contracts.sql","additions":335,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"fb46c1d62120ab12497c45578a0b74fb1f7ee03a","mergedAt":"2026-09-16T03:18:54Z","number":3008,"title":"feat(#2863): ColdLion landing unit 5b - prepack detail and production detail tables","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3008"},
{"body":"Closes #2988. Claim #3005. Reserved migration version 20260916001923.\n\n## Problem, measured on production\n\n`api.dam_order_list` joins `core.customer` and `core.factory` directly. Their `shared_read` policy qual calls `app.has_any_role(ARRAY[...])`, which is STABLE but takes no row-dependent argument, so PostgreSQL evaluates it **once per row** instead of folding it to a constant.\n\nTimed on production (read-only) under yzhou's own JWT claims — the identity with no `app.user_role` row:\n\n- 826 evaluations of the `core.customer` qual: **5,373 ms**, every one returning false.\n- The same `(id, name)` pairs read with no policy evaluation: **1.2 ms**.\n\nThat accounts for the ~3.44 s `core.customer` node and ~0.41 s `core.factory` node in the issue's plan, and for why the 500-row page hits the 8 s `authenticated` statement timeout.\n\n## Change\n\nTwo least-privilege `SECURITY DEFINER` set-returning functions in the `dam` schema — `dam.dam_order_list_customer_directory()` and `dam.dam_order_list_vendor_directory()` — each opening with the repo's standard guard (`auth.uid() is null or auth.role() is distinct from 'authenticated'` → `insufficient_privilege`), each returning only `(id, name)`. The view joins those in place of the base tables. PostgreSQL never inlines a definer SRF, so each runs **once per query** rather than once per row, and customer/vendor names stay non-null for every signed-in user.\n\nExpected effect: Yzhou's ~4.20 s page loses ~3.85 s of per-row policy evaluation, landing near Albert's ~1.03 s — far under 8 s.\n\n## Deliberately not changed\n\n- The view stays `security_invoker = true`. **It is not made SECURITY DEFINER — #2662 is untouched.**\n- No policy, grant, or column on `core.customer` / `core.factory` is modified; unrelated direct table access is unchanged.\n- No statement timeout raised, no full dataset loaded, no new index, matview, or job.\n- No dynamic `EXECUTE` anywhere, so no `marker_reviews` are required.\n\n## Governance note for the orchestrator\n\nClaim #3005 declares `view api.dam_order_list` only. This migration also creates the two `app.*` helper functions, which the issue's Structural route explicitly contemplates (\"the least-privilege supporting function/policy contract needed for its `core.customer` and `core.factory` joins\"). **The claim likely needs expanding to cover `function dam.dam_order_list_customer_directory()` and `function dam.dam_order_list_vendor_directory()` before the lease check will pass.**\n\n## Local checks\n\n- `scripts/check-sql.sh` — Static checks passed.\n- `node scripts/check-production-verification-sidecars.mjs --base origin/main` — `{\"status\":\"OK\",\"sidecars\":55}`, this migration scanning to zero dynamic-execution markers.\n- `node --test scripts/check-sql.test.mjs scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.test.mjs` — 91 pass, 0 fail.\n- `pytest scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py scripts/test_production_catalog_verification.py scripts/test_check_production_verification_sidecars.py` — 357 passed, 305 subtests passed.\n- `check-applied-migration-edit.mjs` returns UNKNOWN locally (no `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`); CI runs it with credentials.\n\nNothing has been applied to preview or production.\n\n\n## Review round 2 (governed REVISE on head b229b09b)\n\n**HIGH - contract registered after the `__main__` guard.** The new catalog contract sat below `if __name__ == \"__main__\": raise SystemExit(main())`, so script-mode runs - how the governed workflows invoke the verifier - exited before the registration line. Import-mode unit tests and the offline sidecar checker passed regardless, so live verification for this allowlisted migration would have errored on a missing key instead of enforcing anything. The block is now above the guard. Proof, executing the file with `__name__ == \"__main__\"`:\n\n```\nscript-mode registered: True | registry size 45\n```\n\nand the contract expression evaluated read-only against production returns `actual_count = 0` pre-apply (expected 1), so it is enforceable and not vacuously true.\n\n**MEDIUM - direct enumeration was real, and is now closed.** This project's PostgREST is configured with `pgrst.db_schemas = public, graphql_public, api, crm, pim, core, app`. The `app` schema **is** exposed, so as originally written any signed-in user could have called the two set-returning helpers as RPC and dumped all 826 customer names and 93 factory names outside the view. The helpers now live in the **`dam`** schema, which is not in that list; `authenticated` already holds USAGE on `dam` and `anon` does not, so they are reachable only through the view. The explicit authenticated guard inside each function is kept as a second layer. No change to query shape or cost.\n\nWhat a role-free user can see through the view is unchanged from the original design: the customer and vendor display names for the order lines the view returns to them - the same names an `administrator` already sees, and nothing else; the helpers return only `(id, name)`.\n\n**LOW (a) - view write grants.** Kept, with a verified justification. The live view's ACL on production today is `{postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres,authenticated=r/postgres}`, so re-asserting `grant select, insert, update, delete ... to service_role` reproduces existing state exactly; dropping it would be an unrelated privilege change outside this issue.\n\n**LOW (b) - contract coverage.** The contract now also pins each function's owner (`postgres`), its `search_path` (`pg_catalog, auth`), and its exact returned column list, in addition to definer/volatility/set-returning and the privilege posture.\n\n**LOW (c)** - timeout efficacy and hash bindings need the preview rehearsal; left for that.\n\n### Checks re-run on this head\n\n- `scripts/check-sql.sh` - Static checks passed.\n- `node scripts/check-production-verification-sidecars.mjs --base origin/main` - `OK`, 55 sidecars, this migration scanning to zero dynamic-execution markers.\n- `node --test scripts/check-sql.test.mjs scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.test.mjs` - tests 91, pass 91, fail 0.\n- `pytest` (gate, catalog verification, sidecar checker) - 357 passed, 305 subtests passed.\n\nSidecar `migration_sha256` and the detector baseline hash are refreshed for the new file contents. Nothing applied to preview or production.\n\n\n## Review round 3 (governed REVISE on head 48cb60eb)\n\n**HIGH - the previous shape broke every caller without an authenticated JWT. Confirmed and fixed.** The two SECURITY DEFINER helpers raised `insufficient_privilege`, and a LEFT JOIN does not swallow that, so `service_role` (role=service_role, no `sub`), a table-owner session and any no-JWT session got 42501 instead of the order list. Reproduced on a throwaway PostgreSQL 18 cluster with the old shape: both `service_role` and an owner session with no JWT aborted with `ERROR: Authenticated access required`.\n\nThe helpers are now narrow **views** in `dam`, owned by `postgres` and explicitly `security_invoker = false`. `core.customer` and `core.factory` are owned by `postgres` and do **not** have FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so the owner is not subject to their policies and the per-row qual is never evaluated - the same repair, with no failure mode. A view cannot raise, so it cannot abort the order list; a caller that may not read it gets a plain permission error on the view.\n\nProven on the same throwaway cluster, running the scenario from `supabase/tests/wb_grants_rls_and_dam_order_list_invoker.sql` lines 380-382 (`set role authenticated` with a JWT carrying neither `sub` nor `role`):\n\n| caller | result |\n| --- | --- |\n| authenticated, JWT with no `sub` and no `role` (the contract test) | 0 view rows, 0 `core.customer` rows, **no error** |\n| role-free authenticated with visible orders | all rows, **all names non-null** |\n| `service_role` | all rows, all names non-null |\n| owner session, no JWT | all rows, all names non-null |\n| `anon` reading a directory view directly | `permission denied for view` |\n| authenticated reading `core.customer` directly | 0 rows, unchanged |\n\nThe full `supabase/tests` suite needs the workflow's ephemeral Supabase stack; Docker is not available on this machine, so the fixture above reproduces that test's exact role/JWT/assertion shape instead. CI runs the real file.\n\n**MEDIUM 1 - contract now catches it.** The contract asserts `has_table_privilege('service_role','api.dam_order_list','SELECT')`, pins both directories as `postgres`-owned, non-invoker, exactly-two-column views whose definition contains no `has_any_role`, requires `core.customer` / `core.factory` to have RLS enabled and **not** forced, and requires that no helper of the abandoned function shape exists in `app` or `dam`.\n\n**MEDIUM 2 - corrected.** The stale header comment that still said `app` \"which PostgREST does not expose\" is gone; the header now describes the `dam` views and why they are views rather than functions.\n\n**MEDIUM 3 - stated plainly, because it cannot be closed without losing the fix.** `api.dam_order_list` must stay `security_invoker = true` (#2662), so the caller reads the directories under its own privileges and `authenticated` must hold SELECT on them. A session that already holds the `authenticated` role on a direct Postgres connection can therefore select all 826 customer name pairs and 93 factory name pairs - `(id, name)` only, no other column. That is not reachable by a PopDAM user: `dam` is not in `pgrst.db_schemas`, and the `authenticated` and `service_role` roles are **NOLOGIN** - they are only ever assumed by `authenticator` behind PostgREST. Closing it further would mean either a definer view over the whole order list (forbidden by #2662) or restoring the per-row policy evaluation that is the bug.\n\n### Checks re-run on this head\n\n- `scripts/check-sql.sh` - Static checks passed (verify-cost guard and #1684 EOL guard both passed).\n- `node scripts/check-production-verification-sidecars.mjs --base origin/main` - `OK`, 55 sidecars, zero dynamic-execution markers for this migration.\n- `node --test scripts/check-sql.test.mjs scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.test.mjs` - tests 91, pass 91, fail 0, skipped 0.\n- `pytest` (gate, catalog verification, sidecar checker) - 357 passed, 305 subtests passed.\n- Script-mode registration re-proved: `script-mode registered: True | registry size 45`; the contract evaluated read-only on production returns `actual_count = 0` pre-apply against an expected 1.\n\nSidecar `migration_sha256` is now `dc34e099b76b815fdf6a0b88cddb4c619c040d45007a237a5d21fc5a96c1ae2b` and the detector baseline hash is refreshed. Claim expansion now needs **`view dam.dam_order_list_customer_directory`** and **`view dam.dam_order_list_vendor_directory`** (no longer functions). Nothing applied to preview or production.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n## Round 4 — response to the round-3 REVISE (head `633e6aa6`)\n\n**MEDIUM — section C of `supabase/tests/wb_grants_rls_and_dam_order_list_invoker.sql`.** The zero-rows assertion is re-expressed, not deleted. Still asserted: `api.dam_order_list` is `security_invoker=true`, and a no-role authenticated principal reading `core.customer` **directly** still sees zero rows. Newly asserted: that principal must resolve the **full** customer and vendor directories through the owner-evaluated `dam` views (`v_dir_noRole = v_cust_owner`, `v_vdir_noRole = v_fact_owner`) — this is the assertion that carries the load on preview, where `plm.production_order_line` is empty, and it fails if either directory is flipped to invoker, has a role predicate reintroduced, or is replaced by a direct `core` join; and the view's row count must equal the principal's visible `production_order_line` count, proving the two `LEFT JOIN`s are name lookups and not filters. The section header and the file's own section-C summary are updated to match.\n\n**LOW 1 — idempotence.** `drop function if exists` for all four abandoned first-shape signatures (`dam.` and `app.` × customer/vendor) now precedes the directory-view creation, so a re-run or a partially applied environment converges instead of colliding on a name.\n\n**LOW 2 — unverifiable production-role claims.** The `relowner` / `relforcerowsecurity`, `pgrst.db_schemas` and NOLOGIN claims now cite the exact read-only queries and the date they were read from `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, and the comment states plainly that the last two are role settings that cannot be checked from the file itself. The first pair is additionally re-asserted by the production contract.\n\n**Agent work contract.** This PR now carries the required evidence pair: the contract is published immutably at `refs/db-contracts/2988/1` (sha256 `aba95e600e68fa6e52554eddbfeadbcbcba801e42c26a5d44b53ead02ae33e0d`), and `.agent/completion.json` binds to implementation head `3946f5413d50a67b3d2a70f72532fc50b1476137` with the two evidence files as the only commit above it. `origin/main` was merged in so the PR base is an ancestor of that head.\n\nChecks re-run at the implementation head: `check-sql.sh` — Static checks passed; sidecar checker — `OK`, 55 sidecars, version `20260916001923` markers `[]`, sidecar `true`; `node --test` — tests 91, pass 91, fail 0, skipped 0; pytest — 357 passed, 305 subtests passed. Sidecar `migration_sha256` is now `e8fbe0874fcb5289f1d60ec5a5c75c541fd234a3015458bb9d9ff26790ad65d0`. Claim #3005 still needs expansion to cover **`view dam.dam_order_list_customer_directory`** and **`view dam.dam_order_list_vendor_directory`**. The PRODUCTION DIAGNOSIS comment no longer names the reporting account by email address (AGENTS.md 6.14), which cleared the Email-address forward guard. Nothing applied to preview or production; nothing merged.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-16T00:31:52Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":39,"deletions":38,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":55,"deletions":49,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260916033914.json","additions":13,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":3,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_catalog_verification.py","additions":75,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260916033914_dam_order_list_role_free_party_names.sql","additions":257,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/wb_grants_rls_and_dam_order_list_invoker.sql","additions":76,"deletions":21,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"bac58c5f49687c7911d013e1f392fcf5c356e626","mergedAt":"2026-09-16T05:50:29Z","number":3007,"title":"fix(dam): open PopDAM OrderList for signed-in users with no role (#2988)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3007"},
{"body":"Closes #2999. Part of #2301, Step 3 of plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md.\n\nClosing a migration-author claim has never been terminal. Reopening the issue restored a lane whose work was over, and nothing recorded that it had ended. This adds a permanent, immutable tombstone under refs/db-claims-retired/<version> and makes every reactivation path read it.\n\n- --release-claim --retire validates the claim, pull request, exact head, worktree state and typed decision, then creates the tombstone BEFORE closing the issue. Create-first fails safe: a tombstone with a still-open claim refuses every mutation and is repaired by the identical, idempotent retry. Closing first would leave a closed claim with no terminal record, which is exactly the state a reopen resurrects.\n- An identical retry is idempotent, including when it loses the create race; a conflicting record refuses and never replaces what is already there. No code path deletes a retirement ref.\n- Acquire, resume, renew, expand (from PR and from issue) and same-owner split recovery all refuse a retired version, and a retired branch or worktree can never be reused, including under a different separator or letter case.\n- The migration lease gate refuses to merge a retired version and fails closed on an unreadable retirement ref.\n- --audit reports RETIRED-REOPENED for an open claim whose version is tombstoned, and the whole audit costs ONE bounded ref listing rather than a call per claim.\n- Retiring work from a dirty or remote worktree requires a dereferenceable owner-decision record, because that retirement destroys unmerged work.\n\nRetirement is opt-in: without --retire, --release-claim behaves exactly as before.\n\nNo schema, database or infrastructure change. No check, guard or refusal is weakened.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-15T23:23:31Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":62,"deletions":13,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":53,"deletions":23,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":9,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.mjs","additions":13,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.test.mjs","additions":14,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/coordination-scenarios.test.mjs","additions":4,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":292,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/migration-retirement-tombstones.test.mjs","additions":392,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission-outcome.test.mjs","additions":8,"deletions":8,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/capacity-state.test.mjs","additions":5,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test-fixtures/migration-lane-race-worker.mjs","additions":23,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"cd4aa51dd35d9c8d7cb828dd215f54d798f1b34c","mergedAt":"2026-09-16T00:32:41Z","number":3000,"title":"feat(#2999): terminal retirement tombstones for migration-author claims (#2301 Step 3)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3000"},

{"body":"Fixes #2987\n\nRepository-maintenance tooling; no database change.\n\n- New `--archive-old-review-verdicts` (read-only preview) and `--archive-old-review-verdicts --apply-recovery`. Under the review mutex, with compare-and-swap and readback, it moves verdict refs to `refs/db-review-archived-verdicts/<original name>` — never deletes. Only closed pull requests that were never merged, or were merged without touching `supabase/migrations/`, are archived. Open PRs, PRs named by an active reviewer lease, merged migration PRs (production promotion re-checks their approval), unknown PRs and unreadable merge commits are kept.\n- `findBusyReviewers` no longer swallows the verdict-namespace ceiling refusal into \"active reviewer leases are unreadable\"; it names the namespace, count and the archive command.\n- Live preview (2026-09-15): total 1000, archivable 546 (519 merged-no-migration, 27 closed-unmerged), kept 454.\n- Tests: manage-migration-author-lanes + check-exact-head-approval suites 628 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped; 5 new #2987 tests.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-15T21:01:11Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":12,"deletions":12,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":28,"deletions":25,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":132,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":92,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"be3cacbec01a1121e393b2508a671732bff5cfaa","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T22:38:26Z","number":2992,"title":"fix(reviewer): governed archive for old review verdicts (#2987)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2992"},
{"body":"Closes #2459.\n\n## Problem\nStale-mutex recovery only releases owner commits of allowlisted kinds. Five kinds that take the author mutex were absent, so a crash while holding one wedged every claim, release, renewal and supersession:\n- reviewer-exclusion-lock, reviewer-release-lock, merged-claim-reissue-lock (named in the issue)\n- reviewer-reinstatement-lock, reviewer-abandoned-lease-reap-lock (found by the audit below)\n\n## Fix\n- Add the five kinds to the recovery allowlist.\n- Per-kind test: strands an owner commit on MUTEX_REF and asserts recovery releases it.\n- Structural guard: a test scans the lanes script for every owner commit followed by acquireMutex/acquireReviewMutex and asserts recovery accepts that kind, so a new lock kind cannot be minted unrecoverable again.\n\n## Tests\n- Both new tests fail against origin/main's script (2/2 not ok) and pass with the fix.\n- Full suite scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs: 571 tests, 571 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.\n\nRepository coordination tooling only. {"body":"Closes #2982 (sub-issue). Refs #2729 (popcre/ai-devops#401 Steps 6-7). Follow-up to #2972; builds on main, independent of the still-open #2979.\n\n**Gap (a) - hash-bound claim-mode preview apply.** A pre-merge claim-mode preview apply whose versions are not in the historical restoration registry is now accepted only when its archived artifact verifies against the exact merge commit (the artifact manifest's migration sha256 must equal the merged files). Fail-closed: no verifier, a row mismatch, a content mismatch, or a receipt that does not bind the run/artifact/digest/versions each reject with a named condition, reported as `rejected candidates: run <id> (<lane>): <condition>`. The registry path is unchanged.\n\n**Gap (b) - migration train wired in.** New manager commands `--propose-train`, `--validate-train`, `--authorize-train`, `--dispatch-train`, `--close-train` (or failed with `--failed-applied-prefix`), and `--verify-train-dispatch`. Records are create-only immutable refs under `refs/db-migration-trains/`; authorize and dispatch re-prove every file hash on current main; a record read from a file must match its immutable digest and not be superseded. The Shared Supabase Migrations workflow gains an optional `migration_train_ref` input (25th) and the `validate` job, which every apply job needs, refuses a dispatch whose target, commit or allowlist is not the exact recorded train, and runs the train tests.\n\n**Tests:** manager + train suites 578 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped; workflow check tests 147 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped; truth audit OK; `git diff --check` clean.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-15T19:29:14Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":19,"deletions":15,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":37,"deletions":31,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml","additions":19,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":102,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":41,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/migration-train.mjs","additions":27,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/migration-train.test.mjs","additions":69,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"d296a33f58c8a3805565241509ddea6370b6cdc2","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T20:16:36Z","number":2981,"title":"feat(lanes): accept hash-bound claim applies and wire the migration train (#2729)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2981"},

Repo-maintenance; no migration lane, no db claim.\n\n- Delivery preflight gate now runs a static pass-2 rebuild check for any changed migration that drops or replaces a routine. Every older migration touching an affected routine is treated as a pass-2 file; if the repaired rebuild's routine set differs from a straight replay, `runDeliveryPreflightGate` and `assertDeliveryPreflightBeforeReview` refuse with `blocked by routine_rebuild` before any gate or reviewer draw. Proven by a failing PostgreSQL catalog test, now passing.\n- Sidecar declaration registry: not on main (sidecars are still listed one by one in `PREVIEW_PRODUCER_PATHS`). The plan assigns it to `production_business_risk_gate.py`, which #2970 is changing, so it is not implemented here.\n\nTests: python unittest test_check_pass2_routine_supersession 39 passed (incl. PostgreSQL catalog tests); node delivery-preflight(-gate) 31 passed; manage-migration-author-lanes preflight tests 12 passed. {"body":"Closes #2978.\n\nPart of #2728 (programme popcre/ai-devops#401 Step 5).\n\n## What this changes\n\n**Delivery preflight gets a real caller.**\n- `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --delivery-preflight` runs the composed preflight before author completion. It records `metadata.delivery_preflight` (the preflight id and input digest) in the evidence bundle.\n- When the head moves, the prior sealed record is reused only if `classify-invalidation.mjs` returns `INTEGRATION_REFRESH_ONLY`. Any other class re-runs every check.\n- `--assign-reviewer --delivery-preflight-record <file> --evidence-bundle <file>` refuses unless three things hold:\n  - the record is passing;\n  - the record is registered in the bundle;\n  - the record belongs to this issue and PR, with the bundle bound to the exact head.\n- That check runs before any GitHub access.\n- New module: `scripts/orchestrator-flow/delivery-preflight-gate.mjs`.\n\n**Review carry-forward.** An approval now carries across three kinds of commit:\n- evidence-only commits (`.agent/`);\n- diff-identical merges from main;\n- a re-pin of a registered stored script hash to the verified sha256 of its source at the same commit.\n\nHow the carry is kept safe:\n- The registry (`config/review-carry-forward-stored-hashes-v1.json`) is read from main only, so a PR cannot widen it.\n- A carried approval records `implementation_digest` (the approved implementation) and the new head.\n- Any other byte change voids approval. Every error fails closed.\n\n## Tests\n- Full manager suite, including `scripts/orchestrator-flow/*.test.mjs`: 1245 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.\n- `check-throughput-truth-audit`: OK, call_sites=295.\n\nNew cases:\n- an evidence-only commit keeps approval, with the same digest;\n- a diff-identical main refresh keeps approval;\n- a verified re-pin keeps approval;\n- a wrong pin voids it;\n- a one-line implementation change voids it;\n- a registry present only on the PR is ignored, and a malformed registry fails closed;\n- doc-only movement reuses the preflight with zero gate calls;\n- a blocked preflight refuses before review.\n\n## Out of scope\n- The pass-2 rebuild.\n- The sidecar registry.\n- Making the review-time preflight check mandatory. It is opt-in in this PR.\n\nContract: `refs/db-contracts/2728/3`. No database, migration, claim, preview or production work.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-15T17:31:50Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":26,"deletions":32,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":1,"deletions":61,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"config/review-carry-forward-stored-hashes-v1.json","additions":10,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/check-exact-head-approval.mjs","additions":7,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-exact-head-approval.test.mjs","additions":14,"deletions":5,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/lib/pr-content-equivalence.mjs","additions":113,"deletions":15,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/lib/pr-content-equivalence.test.mjs","additions":97,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":21,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":55,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/delivery-preflight-gate.mjs","additions":98,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/delivery-preflight-gate.test.mjs","additions":103,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":4,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"ced43bb4df3fd7a8dbcfcf4d36d6ee3fe4d85200","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T18:34:02Z","number":2974,"title":"orchestrator: wire delivery preflight and carry review over re-pins (#2728)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2974"},
{"body":"Closes #2977.\n\nPart of #2729 (programme popcre/ai-devops#401, Steps 6-7, code only). Contract: refs/db-contracts/2729/2.\n\n## Step 6 - workflow\n- A successful recovery run that sets historical_preview_source_pr now reaches Automatic production qualification and dispatch. It goes through the same activation, digest, main-freshness, guarded-merge, exact-head approval and admitted-issue gates as a merged run. It must also pass a proof bound to that PR, exact main, allowlist and a merge hash. That merge hash is re-read live from the PR and must be an ancestor of main.\n- Maps and doubly named sources still refuse.\n- No new production path; later steps read the guarded source PR output.\n- New offline test scripts/check-workflow-automatic-promotion-source.test.mjs runs the guard both ways, including a sabotage case. It is wired into the validate job.\n- Empty SHARED_DB_TEST_TOKEN: the script already exits 1. The logged BLOCKED line came from an offline unit test. That test now captures and asserts the message, and a new process-level test proves an empty token fails.\n\n## Step 7 - reviewer rerouting\n- start-reroute: turn_limit_cancelled is a terminal non-verdict eligible for same-head replacement. Another slot's verdict does not block it, but this assignment's own verdict does.\n  - One preflight_timeout gives retry-same-reviewer; a second gives governed-return-and-reroute.\n  - Liveness ignores session-metadata sources.\n- run-governed-review: a doctor timeout retries the same reviewer once and then refuses with a reroute decision. turn_limit_cancelled refuses with a same-head reroute decision. main prints a REROUTE line.\n\n## Deferred (manager, not edited here)\n- Replacement rule in manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs: allow a non-verdict terminal replacement when another slot has a verdict at the head (hasVerdictForHead slot scoping in isReviewAssignmentLive / assertReviewLeaseStillStale / release-and-replace).\n- Slot-draw independence: a slot-2 draw must not return slot 1's running assignment.\n- A durable adapter that persists lifecycle events (appendLifecycle and repairLocalService are optional hooks here).\n- The preview-evidence lookup in --prepare-preview-dispatch.\n\nNo database, claim, dispatch, reviewer draw or merge.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude {"body":"Closes #2976.\n\nPart of #2729 (programme popcre/ai-devops#401 Step 7, runner half). Authorization: https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/2729#issuecomment-5684812877\n\n## What this adds\n- `scripts/orchestrator-flow/runner-lanes.json`: the queue-sensitive job inventory (\"Tools offline tests\", \"Promotion contract tests (offline)\"), plus five free standard GitHub-hosted lanes: `ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-22.04`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `ubuntu-22.04-arm`. Every lane carries identical assertions. Cost evidence: GitHub docs say standard hosted runners are free and unlimited on public repositories.\n- `runner-lanes.mjs`: `qualifiedLanesFor()` feeds `runnerStartDecision`'s `qualified_lanes`, `replacementDispatchInputs()` builds the dispatch parameters, and `aggregateVerdict()` decides the aggregate check.\n- Both queue-sensitive workflows get a `lane` workflow_dispatch input. The default job name, and so the required context, is unchanged. A replacement run reports `<context> [lane <label>]`.\n- New stable check **Queue-sensitive checks (aggregate)**. It passes only when each assertion has exactly one successful run for the PR head, and refuses when an assertion is absent, duplicated, failed or on an unregistered lane. A superseded queued run must be cancelled before the aggregate accepts.\n\nNo run was dispatched and branch protection is unchanged. `shared-supabase-migrations.yml` is untouched, so \"SQL migration guards\" is not laned here.\n\n## Branch protection, admin follow-up\nAdd required status check context `Queue-sensitive checks (aggregate)` to `main`. Nothing is replaced for now. Once the aggregate has run green on main, the admin may remove \"Tools offline tests\" and \"Promotion contract tests (offline)\", because the aggregate covers both. Otherwise a lane replacement run cannot satisfy them.\n\n## Checks\n- `node --test scripts/orchestrator-flow/runner-lanes.test.mjs scripts/orchestrator-flow/start-reroute.test.mjs scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.test.mjs scripts/update-required-checks.test.mjs`: 98 pass, 0 fail\n- `node scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs`: OK, 295 call sites\n- `node scripts/check-github-transport-conformance.mjs`: OK\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-15T17:28:35Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":17,"deletions":27,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":55,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/coldlion-promotion-contract-tests.yml","additions":29,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/queue-sensitive-aggregate.yml","additions":38,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".github/workflows/tools-offline-tests.yml","additions":30,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/runner-lanes.json","additions":42,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/runner-lanes.mjs","additions":212,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/runner-lanes.test.mjs","additions":234,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"3eaf2112b174791fe02fd720b3ad1e853822494d","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T18:45:05Z","number":2972,"title":"ci: five free runner lanes and fail-closed aggregate for queue-sensitive checks (#2729)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2972"},
{"body":"Closes #2975.\n\nPart of #2728 (programme popcre/ai-devops#401, Step 4).\n\n## What\nNew read-only production caller `scripts/orchestrator-snapshot.mjs --orchestrator-snapshot` over the existing `scripts/orchestrator-flow/orchestrator-snapshot.mjs` library. It reads the live marker, open claims, open PR heads and check rollups, reviewer lease refs (`refs/db-review-active-v2/*`), exclusive stage lock refs (preview/merge/production), outcome events on owned issues, and the now/next queue, and prints a deterministic, sealed snapshot. It never writes to GitHub.\n\n- `stalled_outcomes`: minutes since each owned outcome's last stage transition (trusted OWNER outcome events, via `outcome-lifecycle.mjs`); flagged when idle > 120 minutes. `live_verified` closes an outcome.\n- `zero_closures_4h` alarm, plus `closures_in_window` and `closures_in_session`.\n- Transition-only output: with `--state-dir`, unchanged state prints nothing; each meaningful transition (snapshot change, newly stalled outcome, zero-closures alarm turning on) prints once. Snapshot events go through the library's compare-and-create publisher into a create-only local event store.\n\nNo edits to `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, `run-governed-review.mjs` or workflows. No database, claim, reviewer, preview or production action.\n\nThe canonical `shared-db-orchestrator` skill lives in popcre/ai-devops, not here; the transition-only reporting rule and alarm wording are left for ai-devops.\n\n## Tests\n`node --test scripts/orchestrator-snapshot.test.mjs scripts/orchestrator-flow/*.test.mjs scripts/check-orchestrator-marker.test.mjs`: tests 256, pass 256, fail 0, skipped 0, cancelled 0. Covers successor reconstruction + freshness verify, unchanged state gives zero output, one wake per transition, 121-minute idle stalls (120 does not), no report on unchanged state.\n`node scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs`: truth audit OK: call_sites=295. `git diff --check` clean.\n\n## Live read-only evidence (2026-09-15T17:22:45Z, redacted summary)\n```\nsnapshot_id  c0e0b4d048b945f6aa0ee9f15f8bd88798eb8cf9ea38bb3d654c08ad491788c2\nseal_digest  c042739a33944bed23b56141a143647bb7756c038d0c33872a899cce6969e105\nmarker #2927; claims 2745->2478, 2774->2769, 2816->2794, 2819->2611, 2834->2357, 2867->2866, 2871->2870\nopen_prs 11; reviewer_leases 34; stage_locks merge/preview/production free; outcome_events 6; eligible_queue 0\nnotification orchestrator_snapshot_created\nwakes state_changed, outcome_stalled#2866, outcome_stalled#2870, zero_closures_4h\nstalled_outcomes #2866 dispatched 2307 min; #2870 dispatched 2278 min\nactive_outcomes 2; closures_in_window 0; closures_in_session 0; zero_closures_4h true\nsecond run, same state dir: exit 0, 0 bytes output\n```\n\nContract: refs/db-contracts/2728/2.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-15T17:23:48Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":13,"deletions":17,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":17,"deletions":22,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-snapshot.mjs","additions":239,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-snapshot.test.mjs","additions":173,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"d47817c6d39dac868b67b64d458552a06099cf92","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T18:02:58Z","number":2971,"title":"Read-only --orchestrator-snapshot caller with stalled outcomes (#2728 Step 4)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2971"},
{"body":"Closes #2969.\n\nProduction run 34987389408 for migration 20260915130626 (#2934) was refused by `classify_sql`: its DROP rule reported \"existing production data may be lost or permanently altered\", matched only by `drop function if exists public.deactivate_stale_sg_files(text, uuid);`.\n\n- The DROP rule is now evaluated per statement. A statement consisting solely of `drop function|procedure [if exists] <name>(<args>)[, ...] [restrict]` is not reported: without CASCADE Postgres refuses the drop while any dependent object exists, so no rows are removed.\n- Still reported: any CASCADE (including after a stripped comment), name-only drops, quoted names, nested parentheses in args, DROP ROUTINE, and every other DROP. No other rule and not the preview-required check changed.\n\nTests: `python -m pytest -q scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py` 149 passed, 0 skipped, 169 subtests passed. The new no-finding test failed (4 subtests) on the old rule before the change. The real migration 20260915130626 now classifies to `[]`.\n\nNo database, preview, rehearsal or production work.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-15T15:24:41Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":27,"deletions":10,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":34,"deletions":19,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":87,"deletions":25,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":167,"deletions":37,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"d6b6484a452dae15e3e2c6d188f01e3cfc8b4b55","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T19:09:03Z","number":2970,"title":"fix(risk-gate): stop reporting a non-CASCADE DROP FUNCTION as data loss (#2969)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2970"},
{"body":"Closes #2967.\n\nPR #2958's guarded merge run 34985444563 refused with \"open claims seen (0): none\" in the exclusive merge lane, while the lease check in the same run (same `github.token`, same paginated open-issue read) verified claim #2957. Token, script version, filter, pagination, admission and the reviewer request budget are ruled out; a write-blocked local run of the exact `--acquire-merge` path sees all 9 open claims. The lane could not distinguish an empty or PR-only read from a genuine absence of claims.\n\n- The open-claim read refuses when the listing has no non-PR rows (or is unreadable).\n- A read with zero claims is cross-checked against GitHub search for open `db-claim` issues; disagreement or an unreadable search refuses, naming both counts.\n- The merge-lane refusal now reports rows, pull requests, unlabelled issues and claims the listing returned.\n\nTests: `node --test scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` 558/558; `node --test scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.test.mjs` 16/16; `git diff --check` clean.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-15T15:13:15Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":12,"deletions":44,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":19,"deletions":53,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":16,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":15,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"0e4837da2e8d7942140d9341e9690b65baf78b80","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T15:59:51Z","number":2968,"title":"Merge lane refuses an empty or PR-only open claim read","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2968"},

{"body":"Closes #2963.\n\nPR #2958's guarded merge refused three times although claim #2957 is open, labelled and binds its branch: GitHub's `labels=db-claim` filtered issue listing returned `[]` while the unfiltered listing and search both showed every claim.\n\n- Open claims (lane and lease re-check) are listed unfiltered and the `db-claim` label is filtered client-side.\n- Closed-claim history fails closed when its labels= listing is empty, so a GitHub fault can never make a consumed version or object look free.\n- The lane refusal names the open claims it saw (number, branch, active) and the PR head branch compared.\n\nTests: `node --test scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` 557/557; `node --test scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.test.mjs` 15/15.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-15T14:11:42Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":10,"deletions":8,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":15,"deletions":16,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.mjs","additions":4,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.test.mjs","additions":7,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":19,"deletions":8,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":37,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"269551a20a1944474daaa26232a885d16eef8937","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T14:50:19Z","number":2964,"title":"fix(lanes): stop trusting GitHub's labels= filtered claim listing (#2963)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2964"},

{"body":"Resolves #2429.\n\nAdds `scripts/check-supabase-ref-config.mjs`, a read-only checker that takes config files (JSON or KEY=VALUE) and/or env, extracts every Supabase project/branch ref, and classifies each key against the account's real inventory:\n\n- inventory = `supabase projects list` UNION `supabase branches list --project-ref <parent>` for every project (projects list alone omits preview branches, the trap in the issue comment);\n- verdicts LIVE / RETIRED (ref sits in a key whose name contains RETIRED) / UNKNOWN;\n- negative verdicts are only trusted when every branch listing succeeded and an optional `--control-ref` (a known-live branch) classifies LIVE; otherwise all non-LIVE verdicts downgrade to UNKNOWN and exit 2;\n- failures name source file and key plus where the authoritative value lives.\n\nNo database credential, no writes. CI runs the offline tests in the migrations workflow.\n\nProof: 7/7 offline tests pass; with branch enumeration sabotaged, 4 fail. Live run against the account: the deleted ref rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel => FAIL UNKNOWN (exit 1), rehearsal branch mvpkijzfmfcxhnzqogzs => LIVE.\n\nContract: refs/db-contracts/2429/1.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-15T12:03:12Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":11,"deletions":10,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":16,"deletions":15,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml","additions":4,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-supabase-ref-config.mjs","additions":184,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/check-supabase-ref-config.test.mjs","additions":92,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"196767ca0a4214399dc3825518482e95cf12543a","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T13:35:57Z","number":2953,"title":"feat(tools): verify Supabase ref config against the live account (#2429)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2953"},

{"body":"Closes #2390. Also settles the venue question in issue 2391, which is closed by hand after merge.\n\nRepo-maintenance fix.\n\n- #2390: the venue guard ran in no workflow, so PR #2340 merged eight flagged files with all checks green. It now runs on every pull request and every push to main as its own check, `Public data venue guard` (no paths filter).\n- #2391: the eight flagged files are PostgreSQL catalog statistics (index definitions, relation sizes, counters, placeholder-normalized statement text). The recorded independent assessment found no licensed or business data, and the object names already appear in public migrations. The guard now permits only the four capture names (`foreign-keys`, `indexes`, `pg-stat-statements-topN`, `relation-stats` `.csv`) directly inside `docs/verification/database-efficiency/<UTC timestamp>/runN/`. Any other name, depth, directory or spreadsheet format is still flagged, and a new test proves that.\n- Not changed: the `.json` twin rule (#2390 note). Applying the sensitive-path JSON rule to database-efficiency would flag the same non-sensitive statistics this PR permits.\n- Left for the owner: whether the published security-advisor JSON files in that capture should stay public. That is a security decision, not a venue-guard fix.\n\nEvidence: guard test 4 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. Planted `docs/planted-violation.csv` made the guard fail naming that file, then removed.\n\nAdmin follow-up: make `Public data venue guard` a required context.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-15T12:00:34Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":15,"deletions":13,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":28,"deletions":18,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/public-data-venue-guard.yml","additions":41,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/public-data-venue.test.mjs","additions":26,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"c33f54841c8dc917a36fce0e0c0085e99ec3e1be","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T12:26:52Z","number":2950,"title":"ci: run the public data venue guard and scope a structural-statistics exception","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2950"},

{"body":"Closes #2936\n\nRepository maintenance (CI guard), not a migration.  **Problem.** `scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.mjs` refuses an ADDED migration whose version is in the preview ledger. The governed flow applies an open PR's migration to preview before merge, so any later push turns the required check permanently red even when the file is unchanged. Live case: PR #2933, check run 34922885252 (`20260915023506 applied in: preview (added)`), guarded merge run 34923289466.  **Exception (narrowest).** Allowed only when ALL hold: the file is `added`; its version is in the preview ledger and NOT in production; and the file (CRLF-normalized) reproduces exactly, in order, the `statements` array preview's own `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` row recorded for that version. Only whitespace and `;` between statements are free, because both appliers store each statement trimmed and never execute separators. Evidence is the database's durable record of what it ran, not the branch.  **Fail closed.** Missing/unreadable row, API error, non-array, empty, blank or untrimmed statement, bare CR, unreadable file, or no reader -> refused. Production-applied versions never read statements and stay refused; modified/deleted/renamed files stay refused; any changed statement byte is refused (incident #2037 still caught). The statements reader refuses the production project ref and non-14-digit versions.  **Tests.** 7 new cases: identical body allowed (and CRLF), five modified-body variants refused, production refused, non-added kinds refused, eight unknown-evidence cases refused, reader input validation. `check-sql` + guard suites: 91/91 pass locally.  Does not touch PR #2933, claim #2931, issue #2792, preview or production.  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-15T03:08:14Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":17,"deletions":15,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":1,"deletions":34,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":9,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.mjs","additions":94,"deletions":5,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.test.mjs","additions":78,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"ea413f10f02fc51bae919d5ea4e95d5ce6dbd7c6","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T03:30:43Z","number":2935,"title":"fix(ci): allow a preview-only pre-merge apply proven identical by preview's ledger statements","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2935"},
{"body":"Closes #2792. Supersedes #2930 (closed unmerged).\n\n## What\n\nReissues the bounded PopSG stale reconcile at version **20260915023506** (claim #2931), with the `-- derived-from: 20260905104802` header present from the first commit.\n\n- `public.preview_stale_sg_files(text,uuid,numeric)`: single-pass count.\n- `public.reconcile_stale_sg_files_batch(text,uuid,integer,numeric)`:\n  - victims come from range scans on `idx_sgf_reconcile_root_active_run_id`, capped at 500 rows per call\n  - later calls use a fast ratio guard with a bounded probe, falling back to the exact preview when the guard is not proved\n- Preserved: ratio guard, advisory serialization, reversible inactivation, deterministic continuation, active search-document sync, counters, grants, signatures.\n- No timeout increase, no row delete or replay, and no change to the PDF backfill functions.\n\n## Orphan preview ledger row: 20260915015414\n\nPreview apply run 34920902290 applied 20260915015414 from unmerged #2930 head a119760e. That version has no file on main, so **preview's migration ledger holds an orphan row for it** until the follow-up PR lands. Preview's ledger is left untouched.\n\nThe follow-up PR restores the exact applied bytes (blob 133782d3), registers the restoration, adds the version to `HARD_BLOCKED`/`RETIRED_VERSION_REASONS`, and updates the pinned tests. It is claimed separately after this PR merges and claim #2931 is released, because the lane tool refuses a second open claim on these functions.\n\nThe orphan row is tolerable in the meantime: this PR's preview dry-run 34922134833 and apply 34922309051 both succeeded with it present.\n\n## Evidence\n\nPreview clone rehearsal (rolled back): 217,193 active and 4,137 stale rows.\n\n| Call | Before | After |\n|---|---|---|\n| preview | 0.40s | 1.07s |\n| batch of 1000 | 5.6s | 5.5s |\n| batch of 5000 | timed out at 8.0s | clamped to 500 |\n| 500 rows, first call / later calls | n/a | 2.6s / 1.8s |\n| final 137 rows | n/a | 1.1s |\n| retry after drain | n/a | 0.7s, 0 rows |\n\nThe drain took 7 calls, and 0 re-seen rows were inactivated.\n\nLocal checks:\n- `git diff --check` clean\n- `python -m pytest scripts`: 1158 passed, 8 skipped\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-15T02:40:24Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":13,"deletions":31,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":21,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260915023506_popsg_reconcile_bounded_under_statement_ceiling.sql","additions":367,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/popsg_reconcile_bounded_ceiling_contracts.sql","additions":295,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"2f861b0d037ac51b94823818fa70084e684bf578","mergedAt":"2026-09-15T03:42:41Z","number":2933,"title":"fix(popsg): bound stale SG reconcile under 8s ceiling (#2792, reissue 20260915023506)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2933"},
{"body":"Closes #2707. {"body":"Closes #2918. Follow-up to #2437.\n\nFollow-up to the two Medium findings in the governed GLM review of #2895 (verdict `refs/db-review-verdicts/2437-2895-48f883283d56a8b518763b4d404c764a6217f402`). Issue #2437.\n\n**1. Wider DROP classification.** Adds function, procedure, routine, aggregate, trigger, event trigger, policy, constraint, rule, role, user, group, type, domain, extension, sequence, owned by, publication, subscription, foreign table and server. Decision: all of these remove code, enforcement, access or dependent objects, so they need the same proposal as a table drop. `DROP DEFAULT` / `DROP NOT NULL` stay allowed.\n\n**2. Verified markers.** `-- destructive-proposal: #<n>` no longer silences a file on its own. CI reads every named issue (`gh api`, `issues: read`) and fails unless it exists, is an issue rather than a PR, carries `destructive-proposal`, and passes `checkProposalBody`. Lookup errors fail closed. {"body":"Closes #2906\n\n`--complete-outcome` re-derives live proof from an unexpired `shared-db-live-proof-<issue>-<sha>` artifact holding `db-live-proof.json`, but no workflow produced it, so an outcome returning to shared-db (live case #2848) could never write its completion record.\n\nAdds dispatch-only, main-only `Shared DB Live Proof`. {"body":"Closes #2883 (repo-maintenance).\n\nAutomatic production qualification uploads its review evidence, then refuses dispatch with \"automatic review evidence has no canonical artifact digest\" (runs 34869716305, 34872292289). `actions/upload-artifact@v4` reports `artifact-digest` as bare hex, but the dispatch check and the evidence verifier require `sha256:<hex>`, which is the form the preview digest already uses via the API. This PR adds the prefix to a bare 64-hex digest before the existing check. {"body":"Closes #2711.\n\n- New `--reap-abandoned-review-leases` on `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`. Without `--apply-recovery` it is a read-only preview. With it, under the review mutex, it re-proves and compare-and-swap deletes every `refs/db-review-active-v2/*` lease that `findBusyReviewers` already classifies stale (PR closed/merged, head moved, or verdict recorded).
