{"body":"Closes #2865 (work contract generation 4: `refs/db-contracts/2865/4`)\n\nAfter #2864 removed the EPIPE, runs 34803418431 and 34834257904 showed psql's real error: `item_detail_company_code_division_code_item_no_fkey`. A read-only pull of `/items` and `/itemDetails` on 2026-09-14 found 8 detail rows across 4 items (CW001 VSZM04BC, CW001 VSZM04DDS, EH001 CNVT01HY, EH001 YRN01V2) with no matching item header. One such row rolled back the whole master snapshot every night.\n\nFix: withhold only detail rows whose (company, division, item) header is absent from the same snapshot. They are never silent: the log line reports the withheld count, the `/itemDetails` sync_run records their identities in `request_params.orphanedWithoutItemHeader`, and the load raises `coldlion_sync_alert` in the same transaction. Their merchandise-group slots are withheld with them. {"body":"Closes #2865\n\nNightly ColdLion Landing Sync failed 2026-09-12 (run 34685660524) and 2026-09-13 (run 34751469115) with `psql could not be executed (EPIPE): spawnSync psql EPIPE` while saving the master snapshot (246,877 item slots).\n\nCause: the landing loader piped the whole SQL script into psql on stdin. When psql stops reading early, the pipe breaks and Node throws away psql's exit status and stderr.\n\nFix: write the script to a private temp file (mode 0600, removed afterwards) and run `psql -f <file>` with stdin ignored. No structure change, no behaviour weakened; ON_ERROR_STOP, timeout and client-fault classification unchanged. Two regression tests added; landing suites 97/97 pass.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-14T02:36:00Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":17,"deletions":10,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":34,"deletions":14,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"tools/coldlion-landing-masters.test.mjs","additions":32,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"tools/coldlion-landing/lib/db.mjs","additions":28,"deletions":10,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"6e40bcca3d4e818a94809da5257a8320fa75de54","mergedAt":"2026-09-14T03:40:18Z","number":2864,"title":"fix(coldlion-landing): pass psql script as a file so large master loads cannot EPIPE","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2864"},

{"body":"## Defect\n`automatic-production-promotion` declared `contents: read`, but its step *Re-prove current main, guarded merge, and durable exact-head verdict* runs `--resolve-admitted-issue-for-pr`, which POSTs a `db-coordination admission` commit object (and ref) via the Git data API. Run https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/actions/runs/34681414931 failed with `Resource not accessible by integration (HTTP 403)` after preview applied and before review evidence was written, so production was blocked by both the automatic and manual routes.\n\n## Fix\n- That job only: `contents: read` → `contents: write`. The top-level (line 106) and `production-apply-review` `contents: read` are unchanged.\n- The job still receives no database secret, so it still cannot write a database. `ENGINEER ACTION REQUIRED` fail-closed logic is untouched.\n- New test pins this job's exact permissions, the absence of `SUPABASE_*` credentials in the job, and the fail-closed text. Proven red against `contents: read`.\n\nRepository maintenance; no migration, no orchestrator lane.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\nCloses #2851\n","createdAt":"2026-09-14T01:37:11Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":20,"deletions":12,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":27,"deletions":22,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml","additions":3,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_production_owner_decision_evidence.py","additions":10,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"9425752894ca0d6fa955975e3aa0566d966b2d26","mergedAt":"2026-09-14T03:06:29Z","number":2856,"title":"fix(ci): let automatic production qualification write its admission commit","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2856"},
{"body":"Closes #2857\n\nRepository maintenance (not orchestrator work).\n\nAdds `review_target_superseded` to TERMINAL_FAILURE_CODES for leases stranded when the PR head moved mid-review.\n\n- Consumers found: terminal-failure validation, release (head guard + in-mutex recheck), replacement (failed-provider redraw exclusion), release-evidence parser, reinstatement/exclusion sets (not code-driven), quarantine (static list, not code-driven).\n- Release with this code must PROVE supersession (PR closed or open head differs); the normal exact-head guard is unchanged for every other code.\n- Replacement refuses the code, so the provider is never added to the failed-on-head set; no exclusion is written.\n- New test covers refusal at unchanged head, replacement refusal, successful release at moved head, no exclusion, retry idempotence.\n\nTests: 536 pass / 1 fail; the failing test (guarded merge derives and admits its one live linked structural issue) fails identically on untouched origin/main.\n\nThe stranded lease grok-4.6/2744-2818-4ad729ff was not touched.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-14T01:36:55Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":12,"deletions":30,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":21,"deletions":35,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":15,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":33,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"38467d9fba9ca73321659ba621dff011af6b6827","mergedAt":"2026-09-14T02:45:12Z","number":2855,"title":"fix(review-lanes): non-blaming review_target_superseded release code","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2855"},
{"body":"Fixes #2854.\n\nStructural admission refused #2818 (\"no statement-leading schema DDL\") because its migration rewrites a function from its catalog definition inside a do-block.\n\n- Admission-only recogniser: `pg_get_functiondef('schema.name(args)'::regprocedure) into v` followed by a statement `execute v;` inside a do-block → object `function schema.name` (same key normal DDL produces, so declared-writes matching still works).\n- Shared `inventoryDdlVerbs` / `dispatchObjectKeys` unchanged; truncated, filename-only and unmodelled-DDL refusals unchanged.\n- Tests: rewrite ADMITS; row-only do-block, no EXECUTE, EXECUTE of a different string, commented-out EXECUTE, unqualified name, and no do-block all REFUSE. Verified against the real #2818 migration at 93d35445 → `function api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties`.\n\nLocal: 136/136 pass (admission-outcome + check-dispatch-collision).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-14T01:35:14Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":20,"deletions":18,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":27,"deletions":29,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission-outcome.test.mjs","additions":27,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission.mjs","additions":26,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"3978cca25db3a8c579ee4aadae345f7008efcb2d","mergedAt":"2026-09-14T01:51:16Z","number":2853,"title":"fix(admission): recognise do-block function rewrites (pg_get_functiondef + EXECUTE)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2853"},
{"body":"Closeout handoff for orchestrator marker #2758.\n\nEight of the ten inherited issues closed to production. **#2482 and #2579 remain open**, both blocked on repairs that are not orchestrator work.\n\n- **#2744 / PR #2818** — the structural-admission gate refuses a valid migration. Evidence that this is a tool defect: the gate is one day old, 18 of 673 merged migrations already use the same pattern, the gate's tests never covered it, and the branch's own contract makes the pattern mandatory. Blast radius is this one PR.\n- **#2482** — the promotion job declares read-only repository access where it needs write, and dies before writing the review evidence the manual route also requires. {"body":"Closes #2847.\n\n## The defect\n\n`advanceOutcome` posted a lifecycle event and then **immediately** re-listed the issue's comments to verify it. GitHub comment listing is eventually consistent, so that verification raced its own successful write: the event landed and the run refused anyway.\n\nThe compounding harm is what wedged the queue. `assertOutcomeTransition` runs *before* the post and reads the same stale listing, so a retry did not see the earlier event and appended a **second** event with a different `event_id`. `outcomeHistory` dedupes by `event_id`, not `event_type`, so the duplicate escaped the duplicate check and instead tripped `index <= highest`, recording `<state> repeats or moves backward from <state>` and setting `history.valid = false`. `requireAdmission` throws on an invalid history before doing anything, so every later `--acquire-merge` on that issue refused forever. #2802 and #2848 are wedged exactly this way, each blocking an approved PR.\n\n## 1. Preventive — bounded-backoff re-read\n\n`advanceOutcome` no longer throws on the first failed read-back. It re-reads with bounded backoff (`[0, 250, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000]`ms, honouring the injectable `io.wait`) and refuses only once the event is genuinely absent after every attempt. This is the pattern the `--claim` dispatch path already uses for the same class of problem, extracted into `confirmOutcomeReadBack`. The refusal message is unchanged.\n\n**`event_id` was deliberately left non-deterministic.** Deriving it from `(issue, state)` so a re-post collapses would make `outcomeHistory` report `duplicate outcome event <id>` and push a problem — invalidating the very ledger this change repairs. That option breaks existing history parsing, so it was not taken.\n\n## 2. Curative — `--repair-outcome-history <issue>`\n\nA governed verb that frees an already-wedged ledger. It repairs **only by appending**: one event naming the exact earlier `event_id`s that no longer count (a new `supersedes` field, validated in `db-coordination-events.mjs`). `outcomeHistory` ignores every superseded event when replaying.\n\n- **No existing `db-coordination-event` comment is edited or deleted.** A test asserts every prior comment body is byte-identical after a repair.\n- Refuses unless the history is actually invalid (`already valid; repair refuses to append to a healthy ledger`).\n- Refuses any damage supersession cannot fix, rather than appending a useless event.\n- Supersedes the **smallest** set that restores validity, chosen from the exact offending events, and re-verifies validity on read-back.\n- Runs under the author mutex; requires `--owner` and `--reason`, both recorded in the event detail.\n\nNo guard was weakened, no reviewer/budget constant was touched, and no production command, migration apply, or workflow dispatch was run.\n\n## Tests — written red-first\n\nNew tests fail against the current behaviour. Verbatim failures:\n\n**The repair verb does not exist** (sources at `HEAD`, new tests present):\n\n```\nSyntaxError: The requested module './outcome-lifecycle.mjs' does not provide an export named 'repairOutcomeHistory'\n    at #asyncInstantiate (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:327:21)\nℹ tests 1\nℹ pass 0\nℹ fail 1\n```\n\n**The two advance tests, with only the backoff reverted to the single-shot read-back:**\n\n```\n✖ a lifecycle advance tolerates delayed visibility of its own event instead of wedging the ledger (issue #2847) (3.594ms)\n  Error: outcome dispatched event did not read back exactly\n      at advanceOutcome (.../scripts/orchestrator-flow/outcome-lifecycle.mjs:162:89)\n      at TestContext.<anonymous> (.../scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission-outcome.test.mjs:521:16)\n\n✖ a lifecycle advance still refuses only after every bounded read-back retry is exhausted (issue #2847) (1.1879ms)\n  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:\n\n  0 !== 5\n\n      at TestContext.<anonymous> (.../scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission-outcome.test.mjs:534:10)\n    actual: 0,\n    expected: 5,\n```\n\n### Green\n\n`node --test scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`\n\n```\nℹ tests 536\nℹ suites 0\nℹ pass 536\nℹ fail 0\nℹ cancelled 0\nℹ skipped 0\nℹ todo 0\n```\n\n`node --test scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission-outcome.test.mjs`\n\n```\nℹ tests 61\nℹ pass 61\nℹ fail 0\nℹ skipped 0\nℹ todo 0\n```\n\n`node --test scripts/db-coordination-events.test.mjs scripts/coordination-scenarios.test.mjs scripts/orchestrator-flow/coordination-audit.test.mjs`\n\n```\nℹ tests 49\nℹ pass 49\nℹ fail 0\nℹ skipped 0\nℹ todo 0\n```\n\n## Files changed\n\n- `scripts/orchestrator-flow/outcome-lifecycle.mjs` — backoff read-back, supersession-aware replay, `repairOutcomeHistory`\n- `scripts/db-coordination-events.mjs` — `supersedes` field and its validation\n- `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` — `--repair-outcome-history` verb\n- `scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission-outcome.test.mjs` — four new tests\n\n## Follow-up (not done here)\n\n#2802 and #2848 still need `--repair-outcome-history` actually run against them once this lands. That is a live operation on real issues and was left for an explicit authorised run.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-12T06:18:12Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":25,"deletions":17,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":35,"deletions":26,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":10,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/db-coordination-events.mjs","additions":25,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":16,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission-outcome.test.mjs","additions":146,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/outcome-lifecycle.mjs","additions":157,"deletions":20,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"f713fa85a0014898db4970b815bd28e933ca3ca4","mergedAt":"2026-09-14T02:13:08Z","number":2849,"title":"fix: stop the outcome ledger wedging on a raced read-back (#2847)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2849"},
{"body":"Closes #2478 work under existing claim **#2745** (reused, not re-opened).\n\n## Why a new version file\n\nClaim #2745's previous reserved version `20260911212849` merged to main via PR #2746 but was **never promoted to production**: the merge gate drew only one reviewer slot, so slot 2 was never drawn (#2837). That version string is permanently spent and its file stays in the tree unapplied, so re-adding it would be an empty diff. The claim was moved onto a fresh version by the governed tool.\n\n**Correction to the dispatch premise:** the dispatch stated #2478's dead version file was `20260911214438`. That is not #2478's file — `20260911214438_plm_factory_time_templates.sql` belongs to issue **#2724**. `20260911214438` is only the floor the new version must sort after. The conclusion (a new version is needed) holds; the stated reason did not.\n\n## What this actually changes\n\nReserved version **20260912030028** (atomic, via `--reissue-merged-stranded-claim`; retirement evidence `refs/db-claim-retirements/2745-20260911212849`). It sorts after both `20260911214438` and main's newest `20260911221304`.\n\nThe new file is byte-identical to the stranded `20260911212849` except exactly two hunks:\n\n1. the header names the new reserved version;\n2. `public.style_group_key_for_sku` is `CREATE OR REPLACE` rather than a bare `CREATE`, because `20260911212849` still applies first on any fresh or ephemeral database and a bare `CREATE` would fail with \"already exists\" there.\n\n`derived-from` stays `20260906035323` and `20260907031246`. `20260911212849` is deliberately **not** declared as a base: it will never be present in the production ledger, and a declared base absent from the target refuses promotion.\n\nNo behavior change. Consumers keep their signatures, settings, SECURITY DEFINER, owners, ACLs and results.\n\n## Checks — real exit codes, run unpiped\n\n| Check | Exit |\n| --- | --- |\n| `bash scripts/check-sql.sh` | **0** (Guard B: nothing sorts before base newest `20260911221304`) |\n| `node scripts/check-production-verification-sidecars.mjs --base origin/main` | **0** |\n| `node scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.mjs --base origin/main` | **0** (with a real `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`; it is exit **2 / UNKNOWN** without one) |\n| `node --test scripts/check-sql.test.mjs scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.test.mjs` | **0** |\n| `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` | **0** |\n| local PostgreSQL helper parity contracts | **DID NOT RUN** — see below |\n\nGuard B2 did not run: no ledger source is configured locally, and `check-sql.sh` says so itself.\n\nThe parity contracts (`supabase/tests/style_group_key_for_sku_contracts.sql`, `style_group_drift_reconciler_contracts.sql`) **did not run**. Applying the full migration history to a disposable local cluster fails at `20260702220336_ai_sentinel_stats_exact_match.sql` (`relation \"assets\" does not exist`) — roughly 200 migrations before this one, an unrelated Supabase-managed-schema gap in a plain Postgres fixture. Note that `check-sql.sh`'s `DATABASE_URL` path applies only four hardcoded foundation files, so it does **not** create these functions and cannot stand in for the contracts. Stubbing further would fabricate a schema that is not production's and risk a false pass, so this is reported as not run rather than worked around.\n\nNo production DDL, no database writes, no preview dispatch, no merge.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-12T03:10:15Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":22,"deletions":16,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":32,"deletions":26,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/live-proofs/2478.sql","additions":32,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260917112129_shared_style_group_sku_key.sql","additions":361,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"cfbb4b79ff0fceccdf3e9f7dabd40f52219c91f6","mergedAt":"2026-09-17T13:32:45Z","number":2846,"title":"feat(db): reissue #2478 shared style-group SKU key as 20260912030028","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2846"},
{"body":"## The defect\n\nEvery migration author lane in the fleet was blocked. A structural draw (reproduced on PR #2814, issue #2802) refused with:\n\n> REFUSED: GitHub command failed: reviewer operation 'reviewer-operation' exhausted its derived 25-request budget before request 24 (2 held back as the mutex-release reserve).\n\n`assignNextReviewerOperation` invokes the structural-admission gate inside the same `withReviewRequestBudget` wrapper as the reviewer draw, so admission's GitHub reads — the pull request, the linked work issue, the complete file list, file contents at the exact head and the closing-issue link — were billed against the reviewer operation's 25-request ceiling.\n\nThat ceiling was derived in `docs/verification/reviewer-assignment-api-budget-2026-08-28.md` for a draw that had **no** admission step. The admission gate (`scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission.mjs`) landed later, in e7bec2fe on 2026-09-11. The ceiling has never been charged for admission's cost and was never meant to be.\n\n## The ruling, and what changed\n\nAdmission is not reviewer work, and its request cost must not be charged against a reviewer mutex reserve. The fix moves admission **out of the reviewer operation's request accounting** — and nothing else:\n\n- `REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT` stays **25**. `REVIEW_MUTEX_SECTION_RESERVE` stays **15**. Nothing is widened, raised or relaxed, and the reserve is untouched. Weakening a guard to make a check pass is exactly what issue #2075 exists to prevent, and both constants are now asserted by the regression tests so the shortcut cannot be taken later.\n- Admission still **runs**, in the same place, in the same order, under the same held mutex — `requireOwnedRef(MUTEX_REF, mutexOwner, io)` is unchanged — and still **before** the draw proceeds.\n- Admission still **refuses identically**; only which budget its requests are counted against has moved.\n\nThe budget wrapper encloses the whole mutex section, so relocating the admission call site would have stripped its mutex-ownership proof. Suspending the reviewer budget across the gate (`withoutReviewRequestBudget`) implements the ruling without weakening that proof, and makes the reviewer path consistent with every other admission call site: `acquireAuthorLane`, the guarded merge gate and preview preparation all already invoke admission with no reviewer budget installed.\n\n## Verification\n\nTwo regression tests, both in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`, on a fixture that makes **real** wire requests (the pre-existing reviewer fixtures make none, which is why they never caught this):\n\n1. `#2802 the structural-admission gate is not charged to the reviewer request budget` — a structural draw whose admission gate alone makes more real requests than the entire reviewer ceiling allows completes successfully, the mutex is released, admission's reads are still observed on the wire, and both constants are asserted unchanged. **Fails before this change** with the exact production refusal (`exhausted its derived 25-request budget before request 18 (8 held back as the mutex-release reserve)` — 8 rather than 2 because the fixture has no atomic mutex release); passes after.\n2. `#2802 an inadmissible issue is still refused when admission is not charged to the reviewer budget` — a closed issue is still refused with `closed and cannot be admitted`, the mutex is not stranded, no sequence is consumed, and the refusal is proven to come from the gate actually running.\n\nNo assertion was deleted or re-pointed.\n\nSuites on the touched areas, run on the rebased tree:\n\n- `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` — tests 536, pass 536, fail 0, cancelled 0, **skipped 0**, todo 0 (534 before this change; the 2 new tests are the difference)\n- `scripts/orchestrator-flow/admission-outcome.test.mjs`, `scripts/coordination-scenarios.test.mjs`, `scripts/orchestrator-flow/reviewer-allocation.test.mjs` — tests 93, pass 93, fail 0, cancelled 0, **skipped 0**, todo 0\n\nThe derivation document records the change as a dated note: the ceiling is unchanged and nothing below it is re-derived, because the reviewer half of the operation costs exactly what it did.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n\nCloses #2843\n","createdAt":"2026-09-12T01:27:04Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":34,"deletions":32,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":34,"deletions":38,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/reviewer-assignment-api-budget-2026-08-28.md","additions":24,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":52,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":69,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"933e998b05b1e771a08911ea3d5296b35029b695","mergedAt":"2026-09-12T04:59:31Z","number":2842,"title":"fix: stop charging structural admission to the reviewer request budget (#2802)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2842"},

{"body":"Closes #2820.\n\n## The hazard\n\n`20260909121403_hts_rag_split_isolated_schema.sql` is merged on `main` but absent from the production ledger for a **legitimate** reason: its real target is the DesignFlow non-production Supabase project, not shared production. Nothing recorded that, so the drift checker listed it as ordinary promotable work — indistinguishable from a genuinely overdue migration. Acting on it would have applied schema to a database it was never reviewed against.\n\n## Target confirmed by reading, not assuming\n\n- **Issue #2403** titles it \"Create isolated `hts_rag_split` schema (9 tables) in the **DesignFlow non-prod Supabase project**\", reached via `DB_*_SANDBOX` in GCP `lithe-breaker-323913`, and states it is \"neither shared prod nor the `shared-db-schema-rehearsal` preview branch\".\n- **The migration's own header** says it was transcribed from the read-only structure dump of the live **DesignFlow non-production database** taken 2026-09-05.\n- Corroborated by `20260911210709`, which notes `20260909121403` is not applied on production.\n\nIt is **not** production-scoped, so this hides no real work.\n\n## The mechanism — a target model, not a skip\n\nThe gap was that the checker had **no concept of migration target**, so a one-off skip would leave the next cross-project migration in the same trap. Instead:\n\n- `FOREIGN_TARGET_MIGRATIONS` records each migration's **actual target** plus the issue establishing it. Exclusion is **derived** by comparing that target against the target being checked — a migration aimed at `preview` is still reported as outstanding on `preview`.\n- `classify_pending_version` now takes the target and returns the new `foreign-target` kind, remaining the single authoritative classifier. An unknown target is refused, never silently excluded.\n- `parse_allowlist` refuses such a version outright, in the one choke point every promotion subcommand must call, so it can never enter a production allowlist.\n- The checker reports these in a **separate, clearly-labelled `NOT IN SCOPE FOR THIS DATABASE` section** naming the real target and citing the issue. Never omitted silently — an invisible exclusion is its own hazard, and a reader must be able to challenge the claim.\n- Unregistered migrations stay in scope everywhere, so a forgotten entry can only **over-report**, never hide work.\n\n## Proof the exclusion can fail\n\nAn exclusion that silently swallows everything looks identical to one that works, so every exclusion test is paired with a positive control.\n\n**Live, production (exit 1):** promotable list 27 → 26. Still reported as promotable:\n\n```\n20260911210844  [GENUINELY-PENDING]\n20260911212849  [GENUINELY-PENDING]\n20260911213429  [GENUINELY-PENDING]\n20260911214438  [GENUINELY-PENDING]\n\nNOT IN SCOPE FOR THIS DATABASE — 1 version(s):\n  20260909121403  [FOREIGN-TARGET]  ... targets the DesignFlow consolidated\n  non-production Supabase project ... Recorded under issue #2403.\n```\n\n**Live, preview (exit 1):** 16 → 15, five genuinely-pending still reported, orphan ledger row `20260911221304` still surfaced.\n\nBoth targets still exit 1. Tests: `test_production_migration_guard.py` 247 OK; `check-migration-ledger-drift.test.mjs` 35/35.\n\nNo guard was weakened, no migration deleted, no version hard-coded as skipped.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:27:48Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":23,"deletions":73,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":32,"deletions":83,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":5,"deletions":5,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs","additions":48,"deletions":9,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.test.mjs","additions":90,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_migration_guard.py","additions":124,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_production_migration_guard.py","additions":83,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"570895d7369b243f13e05d0b7a5e3cd66787b1ff","mergedAt":"2026-09-12T01:22:42Z","number":2826,"title":"fix: give the drift checker a concept of migration target (#2820)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2826"},
{"body":"Closes #2796.\n\n## Reproduced first\n\nThe workflow's `mode` input is `required: true`, `default: dry-run`. The stored preview dispatch instruction said nothing about mode, so dispatching it **exactly as stored** dry-runs, applies nothing, and reports SUCCESS.\n\nVerbatim evidence:\n\n- Run **34633793571** — `conclusion: success`, head `120fb6125907386ce2b93bd9ae0a91de700fb738`, exactly one artifact: `preview-migration-dry-run-120fb6125907386ce2b93bd9ae0a91de700fb738` (42324 bytes, not expired).\n- The same manifest dispatched with `mode=apply` — run **34636081308** — produced `preview-migration-apply-153b7754155a22b8541349cc7fe372d14c4e4c96`.\n\nThe artifact name is the only thing that distinguishes the two runs after the fact, and nothing in the stored instruction chose between them.\n\n## Fixed at the store, not the call site\n\n`readyRecord` now attaches the route's required mode phases from one frozen `MODE_SEQUENCE`, and the producer emits the same value from the same source, so the two layers cannot drift. Ordinary and merged rehearsals name `['dry-run','apply']`; historical rebind names `['apply']` alone.\n\nPhase 2 is explicit that \"`mode` is a per-run phase, not part of ready identity or frozen-manifest equality\", so it is attached **after** both digests are taken. No `manifest_digest` or `ready_id` in existence changes and no fixture churn follows. It is derived from the route, never from the caller, so a candidate cannot smuggle in a mode its route forbids.\n\n## The silent case is now loud\n\n- The historical lane at `mode=dry-run` runs neither the recovery proof (gated on `mode == 'apply'`) nor \"Bounded dry-run\" (which excludes historical inputs) — it succeeds having proved nothing. It is now hard-refused before any work, naming the mode it was given.\n- The two production-gate `test -n` pairs died with a bare `Process completed with exit code 1`. They now name the missing preview evidence.\n\n## Proof it can still fail\n\n`scripts/check-workflow-preview-mode-guard.test.mjs` lifts the guard out of the YAML and runs it under real Git Bash, in **both** directions:\n\n- `dry-run` (the input's own default) is refused, and the step does not continue past the guard\n- an unset mode is refused, not treated as empty-and-therefore-fine\n- **`apply` still passes through** — a guard that refuses everything is as broken as one that refuses nothing\n- sabotage: inverting the predicate is caught from both sides\n- deleting the guard restores the pre-#2796 behaviour and fails the suite\n\nNo guard was weakened or bypassed. The merged lane's REQUIRED first dry-run stays dispatchable — a mode guard there was written and deliberately reverted, because it would have refused the mandated phase 1.\n\nLocal: new guard suite 8/8, reconciler 12/12, producer 522/522, Python 384 OK, map-parse 8/8.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:25:29Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":51,"deletions":13,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":57,"deletions":18,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml","additions":44,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":230,"deletions":216,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-workflow-preview-mode-guard.test.mjs","additions":135,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":21,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":16,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/reconcile.mjs","additions":32,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/orchestrator-flow/reconcile.test.mjs","additions":56,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"fb157e1c15a768571821f973844ca09ce5ad8d8a","mergedAt":"2026-09-12T04:10:30Z","number":2825,"title":"fix: stored preview instruction names its dispatch mode (#2796)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2825"},
{"body":"Closes #2611.\n\n## The claim was still true, but the issue's premise was not\n\nNo SQL anywhere implements the owner's prepack exclusion. A production scan of\nevery non-system function body, view and materialized view matching\n`prepack|pre_pack|assortment` returns only DAM-order objects and\n`api.plm_item_list`; none of them filters a missing-attribution population. (One\ndetail in the issue is inaccurate: the `pg_proc` scan does not return empty, it\nreturns unrelated matches. Same conclusion.)\n\nThe issue's **head source is wrong, not merely stale.**\n`public.erp_items_current` is a frozen DesignFlow snapshot (`source_system =\n'designflow'`, last synced 2026-05-21). Of its 1,454 prepack rows, **1,437 are\nlive prepack MEMBERS and exactly 1 is a live head.** Building the filter there\nwould have excluded the wrong items and missed nearly every real head. ColdLion\noutranks DesignFlow (ruling 2026-09-08) and `erp_items_current` is being retired\nby #2482, so this change does not reference it.\n\nThe live head test is `coldlion.prod_history_component.prepack_item_no`. Its\ngrain is the trap in this table: every head-bearing row is **self-referencing**\n(`sub_item_no = prepack_item_no`), so it is a flag meaning \"this ordered item is\na prepack head\", not a head-to-member explosion. Read as an explosion it invites\na confident but false \"the labels are inverted\" finding. Members come from\n`coldlion.item_detail.pre_pack_code`. Head codes and member codes are disjoint.\n\n## Re-scope: this is a member problem, not a head problem\n\n#2611 is framed entirely around heads. Within licensed divisions the exclusion\nremoves 1,770 rows, of which **heads are 7 and members are 1,763**. Almost every\napparent head (954 of 961) sits in EH001/EP001, which the non-licensed-division\nrule already removes first. Head coverage is not the problem. Both roles are\ntherefore excluded behind one function, and the regression guard covers both.\n\nThe re-derivation reproduced `unmapped-licensor-population.md`'s\nlicensed-division figure of **2,016 exactly** — an independent validation of that\ndocument. 246 rows remain afterwards, against 214 recorded on 2026-09-07, so the\npopulation has moved; that is a separate matter and is not addressed here.\n\n## What this adds\n\n- `plm.prepack_role(text, text, text)` — the single authoritative assortment\n  test, returning `head`, `member` or null, head winning. Security definer,\n  because the ColdLion landing is closed to application roles. Swapping the\n  source is a one-line change inside this function, as the issue asked; no\n  caller re-implements the test.\n- `plm.item_missing_attribution` — the population with the documented exclusions\n  already applied, so the ruling holds without anyone remembering it.\n- `scripts/check-prepack-exclusion.mjs` + test + workflow — the regression guard\n  the issue asked for. This repository's check scripts validate repository\n  artifacts offline and none opens a database connection, so this guards the\n  **definition**: if the filter is dropped, weakened, commented out, pointed back\n  at the retired snapshot, or reduced to heads only, it goes red. The test proves\n  the guard can fail by feeding it seven known-dirty variants, rather than\n  trusting a single green run.\n- Two corrections to `docs/business-rules/product-items-and-identifiers.md` that\n  this work disproved: the head/member table mislabelled\n  `erp_items_current.prepack_code` as heads, and a paragraph claimed an inventory\n  row's prepack code identifies an assortment head when\n  `coldlion.inventory.prepack_code` is empty on every production row.\n- `docs/verification/prepack-exclusion-20260911.md` recording every probe with\n  its query per AGENTS.md §4.3.\n\n## Reviewer: two judgement calls\n\n1. **The business-rules correction.** I am overturning a passage marked\n   \"Verified 2026-09-07\" on the strength of a re-derivation. Section 2 of the\n   verification note is the evidence.\n2. **The re-scope to both roles.** The owner ruling names heads. I read \"prepacks\n   must be excluded\" as covering members too, and the numbers say the ruling is\n   nearly inert otherwise. If you disagree, the fix is one branch of\n   `plm.prepack_role`.\n\nThe regression fixture is the seven heads that sit in a licensed division and are\nmissing attribution today. An EH001 head would prove nothing — the division rule\nexcludes it whether or not the prepack filter works.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:14:37Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":39,"deletions":12,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":64,"deletions":27,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/live-proofs/2611.sql","additions":32,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".github/workflows/prepack-exclusion.yml","additions":39,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"docs/business-rules/product-items-and-identifiers.md","additions":29,"deletions":13,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/prepack-exclusion-20260911.md","additions":160,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":79,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-prepack-exclusion.mjs","additions":215,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/check-prepack-exclusion.test.mjs","additions":144,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260917081048_prepack_exclusion.sql","additions":110,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"656bf9f48215ed04d2846aad9b23fbe9d0c4159c","mergedAt":"2026-09-17T10:17:06Z","number":2823,"title":"feat(plm): implement the prepack exclusion (#2611)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2823"},
{"body":"Closes #2817. Unblocks PR #2808 (#2797), whose required `SQL migration guards` check refuses `20260911221304 applied in: preview`.\n\nThe #2797 lane dispatched the preview apply before merging, so run `34655606553` wrote the version into the preview ledger from PR #2808 commit `916b8005`. Registering the version and its exact LF bytes in `HISTORICAL_RESTORATIONS` lets the applied-migration-edit guard tell \"the exact applied bytes\" from \"an edit to an applied version\", following the #2798 (for #2744) and #2768 (for #2535) precedent.\n\nEvery digest was recomputed independently from the file at `916b8005` before the entry was written, and each matched the values reported on the issue: `fileSha256 ecc847f6…`, `statementBytes 55149`, `statementSha256 a9171a60…`. The bytes are identical at the applied commit and at PR #2808 head `234647f3`.\n\nProduction producer provenance (`sourcePr`/`sourceMergeCommit`) is deliberately left unregistered, so this grants no production eligibility. No migration, preview or production change, no guard relaxed, and no entry added for any other version.\n\nTests: focused pin test (applied-commit bytes validate; one changed byte refuses; wrong path refuses; production provenance refuses), `check-applied-migration-edit` tests, `check-sql.sh`, agent work contract tests.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:10:27Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":24,"deletions":38,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":29,"deletions":42,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/historical-migration-restorations.mjs","additions":23,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/historical-migration-restorations.test.mjs","additions":47,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"a6790093a1973d72119c8d9c7f1d2fc9fc7b9d30","mergedAt":"2026-09-11T23:57:29Z","number":2822,"title":"fix(#2817): register #2797 preview apply 34655606553 as historical restoration","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2822"},
{"body":"Closes #2794. Migration author lane claim: #2816. Reserved migration version: `20260917081021`.\n\n## What this does\n\nRemoves the DesignFlow PLM master-data sync completely, including every runtime vestige.\n\n- **`supabase/migrations/20260917081021_remove_retired_designflow_plm_import.sql`** drops `plm.import_master_data(jsonb, jsonb)`.\n- Deletes the six vestige files named in the issue's `db-work-scope`: the import tool, its unit test, the host wrapper, and the three `systemd/plm-sync.*` units.\n\n## Why this is a DROP and not an ARCHIVE\n\nThe repository default for retirement is archive-never-drop, and that default exists to protect **data**. This object holds none. Since `20260817124545` (#1090 Step 1.0) the entire function body is a single `RAISE` that refuses every call. It owns no table, no rows, no history and no audit trail, so there is nothing to move into `archive`. Issue #2794 explicitly authorises the removal and conditions it on proof of no remaining callers.\n\n**No audit row, history row, or lock is deleted by this change.**\n\n## Proof that nothing still reads it (production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`)\n\n| check | result |\n|---|---|\n| function body | retirement `RAISE` only, no executable path |\n| `proacl` | `postgres=X/postgres` (EXECUTE revoked from public, anon, authenticated, service_role) |\n| referencing functions | 0 |\n| referencing views | 0 |\n| non-normal `pg_depend` rows | 0 |\n| **positive control** | **2** |\n\nThe positive control matters: the same predicate matches two real function bodies, so the zeros above are genuine absences rather than a silently broken query.\n\nThe migration is defensive in its own right. It returns quietly if the function is already gone, and **refuses** if the body is not the #1090 retirement stub or if any non-normal dependent exists — so it can never destroy a live replacement importer. The drop is deliberately **not** `CASCADE`. Post-drop assertions confirm the function is gone *and* that the unrelated licensing write-authority guard is fully intact (`plm.licensing_write_authorization`, `plm.licensing_write_guard_audit`, `app.enforce_licensing_write_authority()`, and both `*_licensing_write_guard` triggers).\n\n## Scope expansion — please adjudicate\n\nThe issue's `writes:` list names only the function and the six files. The following changes are **outside that literal list**, and I want them reviewed explicitly rather than assumed:\n\n1. **Forced, not optional** — deleting the tool and its test breaks `coldlion-licensor-property-phase6-parallel.yml`, which ran the deleted test file and invoked the deleted tool. Leaving it would land a red `main`.\n2. **Judgement call** — I also retired the `designflow` cron lane itself (`30 3 * * *`), its `workflow_dispatch` option, its `JOB=` case arm, and its entry in `tools/phase6-schedule-map.mjs`. The alternative was to keep a lane that dispatches to nothing. The issue says \"remove the DesignFlow PLM sync completely, including its vestiges\", so I took the coherent removal. Happy to be redirected.\n3. **Contract test** — `supabase/tests/licensing_write_authority_guard_contracts.sql` read the function's body via a `::regprocedure` cast, which hard-errors once the function is gone. That assertion is now an **absence** check -- strictly stronger than the previous \"body is the retirement stub\" -- but it is **conditioned on its precondition** rather than asserted flat. See \"CI finding\" below: the condition is not a softening, and \"present as the #1090 stub\" remains a hard failure. The `CREATE OR REPLACE` replay block is deliberately **retained**: it still proves that reviving the legacy importer cannot bypass the table-level guard.\n4. **Guard inverted, not deleted** — `coldlion-licensor-property-phase6.test.mjs` asserted the workflow *must* reference `DESIGNFLOW_API_KEY`. Rather than drop the assertion to go green, it is now `doesNotMatch`, so a silent revival of the lane fails the test.\n\nThe `compare-coldlion-designflow-*` and `check-coldlion-designflow-sync-health` tools are untouched — they read `ingest.sync_run` rows and are not the importer.\n\n## Docs\n\n`README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `docs/implementation/schema-implementation-notes.md` described the lane as active and are corrected. Historical evidence under `docs/verification/`, `docs/archive/` and `DB_Data_Admin.md` is preserved deliberately.\n\n## CI finding -- the replay harness resurrects dropped routines (filed as #2833)\n\nThe absence assertion failed on the from-empty ephemeral replay. **The cause was neither the migration nor its guard** -- the obvious reading is the wrong one, so it is worth stating plainly:\n\n- `20260917081021` applies cleanly in pass 1 and the function **is** genuinely dropped. It appears in neither the pass-1 nor the pass-2 failure list.\n- `20260723183000_step11_bounded_production_forward.sql` does not replay from empty, so it lands in **pass 2 -- which runs after every pass-1 migration** -- and its body redeclares `plm.import_master_data` with a pre-retirement body.\n- The pass-2 order repair cannot reverse that. `scripts/check_pass2_routine_supersession.py` snapshots and restores later routine **definitions**; a drop leaves **no definition to snapshot**, so absence is not expressible at all. It additionally classified this routine's later declarations as unproven, so nothing was snapshotted.\n\nThe resurrection is therefore a replay-harness artifact that no forward-only lane can reach. It is also a **general** gap -- any future migration retiring a routine by dropping it is silently reverted the same way -- so it is filed as **#2833** rather than patched around here. The harness is outside this issue's `allowed_paths`.\n\n**What the test asserts now**, following the precedent already set in `supabase/tests/fr_owner_ruling_forward_replay_contracts.sql` section 4:\n\n| state at test time | verdict |\n|---|---|\n| absent | **pass** -- the contract |\n| present, body is the #1090 retirement stub | **hard failure** -- `20260917081021` did not do its job |\n| present, pre-retirement body | **recorded with a loud notice** naming the pass-2 mechanism; must never appear on a forward-only database |\n\nThe guard was **not** loosened and the migration is **unchanged**. Suppressing the assertion, or relaxing the migration's refusal-on-unrecognised-body, would have faked the result -- that refusal is the exact safety property this issue asked for.\n\n## Verification\n\nAll three contract-required checks re-run on the merged tree, with exit codes observed **directly rather than through a pipe** (a pipe returns the last stage's status, so a failure can read as a clean pass):\n\n- `bash scripts/check-sql.sh` -- exit 0.\n- `node scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` -- exit 0; `call_sites=276`, re-derived rather than hand-edited (277 -> 276 is the one deleted call site).\n- `node --test tools/*.test.mjs` -- exit 0; **828 tests, 828 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped**, counts read from the runner summary rather than inferred from the exit code.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:08:50Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":62,"deletions":16,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":76,"deletions":27,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/live-proofs/2794.sql","additions":18,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":".github/workflows/coldlion-licensor-property-phase6-parallel.yml","additions":4,"deletions":22,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"AGENTS.md","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"README.md","additions":13,"deletions":14,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"config/production-verification-sidecar-registry.json","additions":4,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/implementation/schema-implementation-notes.md","additions":6,"deletions":5,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":99,"deletions":106,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260917102139.json","additions":19,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/production_catalog_verification.py","additions":8,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260917102139_remove_retired_designflow_plm_import.sql","additions":126,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/licensing_write_authority_guard_contracts.sql","additions":46,"deletions":23,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"systemd/plm-sync-alert.service","additions":0,"deletions":11,"changeType":"DELETED"},{"path":"systemd/plm-sync.service","additions":0,"deletions":13,"changeType":"DELETED"},{"path":"systemd/plm-sync.timer","additions":0,"deletions":11,"changeType":"DELETED"},{"path":"tools/coldlion-licensor-property-phase6.test.mjs","additions":4,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"tools/phase6-schedule-map.mjs","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"tools/phase6-schedule-map.test.mjs","additions":2,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"tools/run-plm-master-data-sync.sh","additions":0,"deletions":14,"changeType":"DELETED"},{"path":"tools/sync-plm-master-data.mjs","additions":0,"deletions":362,"changeType":"DELETED"},{"path":"tools/sync-plm-master-data.test.mjs","additions":0,"deletions":106,"changeType":"DELETED"}],"headRefOid":"189067fe8f3cc6601035391d553695f0ddb1e7cd","mergedAt":"2026-09-17T11:30:32Z","number":2821,"title":"feat(#2794): remove retired DesignFlow PLM sync and all runtime vestiges","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2821"},
{"body":"Closes #2744.\n\nNote: #2744 is only genuinely resolved once post-apply acceptance passes on production (five unfiltered default runs plus four targeted controls, as role authenticated, statement_timeout 8s). If merging auto-closes it before those numbers exist, it is reopened until they do.\n\r\n## What was slow\r\n\r\nThe unfiltered Scraped Properties listing regressed after `20260911170526`. Acceptance, measured as role `authenticated` with `statement_timeout='8s'` inside `begin; â€¦ rollback;`, produced **8400 ms (cancelled, 57014), 5966, 5367, 5196, 7083** against a **4275 ms** pre-apply baseline â€” slower than before the predecessor landed.\r\n\r\nRead-only `EXPLAIN (analyze, buffers)` on production shows the cost is **not** the ten-table union: the page limit pushes down and `ordered` completes in 132 ms. It is style-guide resolution. The page's retained `(property, asset)` pairs were hash-joined against the whole **61 MB** `plm.dcp_asset` heap (187,487 rows), and the build side spilled to temp.\r\n\r\n## The fix\r\n\r\nResolve style guides through a narrow `(id, style_guide_id)` asset map, so the hash build carries two columns instead of the full asset row, and evaluate each page's retained-asset set once instead of twice.\r\n\r\nStyle-guide **names** still resolve downstream from the page's own style ids, so the whole catalog is never materialized with folder names â€” the wide shape #2744 was filed against stays retired.\r\n\r\n## Measurements\r\n\r\nInterleaved on one session under identical live load, page size 500, role `authenticated`, inside `begin; â€¦ rollback;`:\r\n\r\n| | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 |\r\n|---|---|---|---|\r\n| before | 9991 ms | 4867 ms | 4466 ms |\r\n| after | **2671 ms** | **2525 ms** | **3273 ms** |\r\n\r\nThe baseline's 9991 ms tail is what produced the 8400 ms acceptance cancellation; the fixed statement's worst run was 3273 ms.\r\n\r\n**Parity proven:** the unfiltered default page is **1,311,298 bytes byte-identical** before and after, and Cinderella, Bambi, Cars 2 and Georgia Green Glass are byte-identical at page 100.\r\n\r\n**Small-page cost of the narrow map (accepted):** page size 1 unchanged (~99 ms); page size 100 unfiltered 263 â†’ 388 ms; targeted lookups 106â€“248 ms â†’ 116â€“314 ms. About 125 ms fixed cost to buy ~2 s on the broken path.\r\n\r\n## Refuted by measurement â€” recorded so they are not retried\r\n\r\n- **Removing the double evaluation alone bought nothing**: 4285 / 4226 / 4656 ms, on top of baseline. The obvious defect was not the cost driver.\r\n- **Raising `work_mem` 12Ã— bought nothing.** This refutes the theory named in claim #2791's own title; the reserved version was not spent on it.\r\n\r\n## Reviewer note â€” please scrutinise this\r\n\r\nThis change re-introduces a **whole-catalog materialization**, which is superficially what #2744 was filed against. It is narrower than the retired shape (two columns, names resolved downstream on ~5,900 rows, versus the retired CTE's asset row already joined to style-guide names), and Variant E above is the evidence that the narrow projection is the load-bearing part rather than a technicality.\r\n\r\nIt would have passed the existing contract test's `dcp_asset_context` ban purely because the new CTE has a different name. I did not want to win on that string technicality, so **the contract test is rewritten in this PR** to assert the real invariant â€” narrow projection present, names resolved from page rows only, and a new guard against the wide catalog-plus-style-guide join returning.\r\n\r\n## Residual\r\n\r\n`dcp_property_style_ids` still spills (`Batches: 4 (originally 1)`, `Memory Usage: 8825kB`). Headroom is roughly 2.5Ã— under the 8 s ceiling, not unlimited.\r\n\r\nNo timeout, role, `work_mem` or global setting is changed. Every probe ran inside `begin; â€¦ rollback;`; nothing was committed to any database.\r\n\r\n## Separate finding â€” the reported \"Product pipeline is down\" is NOT this function\r\n\r\nProduction log attribution of `57014` cancellations (18:00â€“23:00Z) and direct measurement identify `api.pm_pipeline_page('licensed', â€¦, limit 100)` at **8235 ms cold** as that outage. It reads `pim.product` and never touches `dcp_asset`, the observations, style guides or the OPA chain. **This PR will not repair that screen** â€” it needs its own issue. Detail posted on #2744.\r\n\r\nðŸ¤– Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-11T23:04:43Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":90,"deletions":14,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":77,"deletions":18,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json","additions":38,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260911222514.json","additions":25,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_catalog_verification.py","additions":46,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260911222514_scraped_properties_narrow_asset_style_map.sql","additions":91,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_properties_opa_groups.sql","additions":4,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/scraped_properties_page_asset_context_contracts.sql","additions":26,"deletions":5,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"3d562b8e38b07a9c1ac8607bf9efaf397cd61ea3","mergedAt":"2026-09-14T05:40:20Z","number":2818,"title":"perf(#2744): resolve Scraped Properties style guides through a narrow asset map","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2818"},
{"body":"Closes #2848. Part A of #2662 (parent stays open for the deferred views). Lane claim #2812, reserved migration version `20260911225108`.\n\n## What this changes\n\n`public.ai_sentinel_cleanup_log`, `public.dam_search_documents`, `public.dam_search_synonyms` and `public.scanner_ai_ignores` each have RLS **enabled with zero policies**, yet grant full `ALL` (`arwdDxtm`) to both `anon` and `authenticated`. This revokes both role grants and re-asserts RLS.\n\nToday every Data API read and write from those roles is denied — but only because an empty policy set denies all. The grant is the real control surface and it is wide open: one permissive policy added later for an unrelated reason would silently expose all four tables, full SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, to every browser caller including anonymous ones.\n\n## Why this is safe to apply\n\n**No behavioural change today.** Both roles are already denied by RLS, so this removes a grant that is currently unusable.\n\n`service_role` and `postgres` bypass RLS and keep their privileges untouched. That is measured, not assumed: production edge logs for the 24 hours to 2026-09-11 show the only live Data API traffic to any of these four tables is five successful inserts into `scanner_ai_ignores` from a Supabase Edge Function (`Deno/SupabaseEdgeRuntime`, `supabase-js-deno`). Those succeed against an RLS-enabled table with no policies, which is only possible by bypassing RLS — i.e. on the service role, which this migration does not touch. The other three tables saw no Data API traffic at all.\n\n## Evidence\n\n`docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260910T002917Z/api-access-matrix.md`, finding 1.\n\nRe-derived against production (`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`) on 2026-09-11 with `has_table_privilege` against `pg_class`. Note for reviewers: `information_schema.role_table_grants` is the **wrong** source here and silently reports no grants at all for these roles — a documented false negative.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis deliberately does **not** touch the definer views and materialized views in the same finding. Those can break live applications and carry a business judgement that belongs to Albert. They remain open under #2662 with a per-object plan and blast-radius analysis posted there, and are not applied here.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T22:56:44Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":49,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":53,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260914155226_revoke_api_role_grants_zero_policy_tables.sql","additions":75,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"c2ee8fd7448c70a676b42fc476d9aad48d60119e","mergedAt":"2026-09-14T16:20:57Z","number":2815,"title":"security(#2662): revoke anon/authenticated grants on four zero-policy tables","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2815"},
{"body":"Closes #2802. Author claim: #2811. Migration version `20260911224952`.\n\n## What this does\n\nAdds one nullable boolean column, `dam.style_guide_file.has_talent_likeness`.\n\n- `TRUE` — the source explicitly indicates talent likeness\n- `FALSE` — the source explicitly indicates no talent likeness\n- `NULL` — the source exposed no determination (never to be read as `FALSE`)\n\n## Scope discipline\n\n- **Structure only.** No data backfill is authorized by this intake; every existing row stays `NULL`, which is the correct \"no determination\" state.\n- **Stays nullable.** `NULL` is a distinct third answer, not a stand-in for `FALSE`.\n- **No filename inference.** The value is never derived from a filename, path or title. The raw source filename/label remains in the existing `title`, `relative_path`, `folder` and `metadata` columns, which this migration does not touch.\n- **Additive** per AGENTS.md §4 rule 3 — adding a nullable column cannot break any app already reading `dam.style_guide_file`.\n- Declares `-- derived-from: none` per §5.0-D: the file writes a new column from scratch and depends on no earlier object rewrite.\n\nDeclared scope: writes `table dam.style_guide_file`, reads `table core.style_guide`.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-11T22:54:52Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":28,"deletions":12,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":46,"deletions":18,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260914152758_dam_style_guide_file_has_talent_likeness.sql","additions":22,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"bf59b5ff0fd1dc458fb240ab1a45c1be606b45ba","mergedAt":"2026-09-14T15:39:39Z","number":2814,"title":"feat(dam): add nullable has_talent_likeness to dam.style_guide_file (#2802)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2814"},
{"body":"Fixes #2809.\n\n## The defect\n\n`scripts/production_migration_guard.py` booked an `alter table ... set schema ...` removal at the **start** of the statement. `hard_reference_events` records that same statement's own qualified table name at `match.start(1)` — **inside** the same match. `preflight_batch` sorts both streams by position, so the table was withdrawn from `available` before the guard reached the very reference that performs the move.\n\nResult: every archive-a-table migration self-flagged. It blocked the preview apply for #2482 (run 34653889672):\n\n```\n20260911210844 references missing public.erp_items_current (alter table); it was DROPPED\n(or renamed away) by 20260911210844 and not re-created\n```\n\nThe SQL is correct — the full set replays green from an empty database (run 34651929781).\n\n## The change\n\nBook the removal at `match.end()` and the new qualified name just after, so the statement's own name is judged while the object still exists. One ordering change; no rule is removed, relaxed, or bypassed.\n\n## Proof the capability survives\n\nTwo regression tests, alongside the existing 241:\n\n- `test_2809_archiving_a_table_does_not_self_flag` — an archive migration now passes preflight end to end.\n- `test_2809_the_OLD_name_after_a_move_is_still_REFUSED` — touching the former name after the move is still refused, with the same \"DROPPED (or renamed away)\" message.\n\nThe pre-existing dropped-object refusals (`test_f5_a_batch_referencing_a_DROPPED_object_is_REFUSED`, `..._APPLIED_LEDGER_...`) are untouched and still pass. Full suite: 241 before, 243 after, all green.\n\n## Note, not fixed here\n\nA plain `alter table x rename to y` shows the identical self-flag shape (`RENAME_RE` books its removal at `match.start()` too). It is left alone deliberately — out of this issue's scope, and no migration currently needs it. Worth its own issue.\n\n## Routing\n\n`repo-maintenance`, not structural: it ships no migration and changes no database shape, so it takes no migration lane or version.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T22:33:29Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":18,"deletions":23,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":30,"deletions":34,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":9,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_migration_guard.py","additions":9,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_production_migration_guard.py","additions":44,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"fbfc3004944ae61ed46993ca769aa9cd3d38e0a8","mergedAt":"2026-09-12T06:42:38Z","number":2810,"title":"fix(guard): book a schema move at the end of its own statement (#2809)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2810"},
{"body":"Closes #2797.\n\nAdds one read-only, Licensing-manager-gated, paged inventory RPC\n`api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory(text,text,text,integer)` over the raw\nscraped source vocabularies for Properties, Characters and Style Guides.\n\n- One entity kind per call (`property`, `character`, `style_guide`), with search\n  text, a deterministic base64 keyset cursor over `row_key collate \"C\"`, and a\n  page size clamped to 1..1000.\n- Rows carry source-declared identity only: licensor key/name decided by the\n  actual scrape route and source authority, source purpose normalized to exactly\n  `Creative` or `Submissions`, display label, source system/table/id/status, a\n  capture marker, and the existing mapped/unmapped indicator for Creative\n  Property rows only.\n- Disney, Marvel, Pixar and Lucasfilm / Star Wars stay separate licensors.\n  Retained copies of one source record across scrape routes are never\n  deduplicated, and identity is never inferred from names: every non-DCP identity\n  keeps its exact `source_table|source_system|source_id` copy key.\n- Matching controls, review reasons, evidence basis, review guidance, contract\n  status and authority-derived presentation buckets are absent, as are the Sega\n  and WWE inferred candidate tables, which are not source-declared facts.\n- `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties` is byte-for-byte unchanged and remains\n  the Property Matching contract. Nothing here touches #2744's performance repair.\n- `authenticated` only; `security definer` with `search_path` pinned to\n  `app, public`; the Licensing Manager gate is enforced before any read.\n\nClaim issue #2807, reserved migration version `20260911221304`.\n\n`supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql` proves the contract\nfrom the function definition and the catalog alone, so no licensed row content\nenters public CI evidence.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T22:14:56Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":41,"deletions":35,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":48,"deletions":45,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260911221304_db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql","additions":1154,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql","additions":198,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"929d1a022dc148f55c00c3c20a584937f5520778","mergedAt":"2026-09-12T01:51:30Z","number":2808,"title":"migration: DB Data Admin raw scraped source inventory API (#2797)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2808"},

{"body":"Closes #2744. Claim #2791, version 20260911170526, contract refs/db-contracts/2744/1.\n\n**Problem.** The signed-in Data Admin \"Scraped Properties\" default listing timed out (8s authenticated statement_timeout). EXPLAIN on production showed the page-context step materializing all of plm.dcp_asset joined to dcp_style_guide (187k rows, 8.7s) and then a 16.7s distinct join against it; the page's retained (property, asset) pairs (~435k rows) were also materialized, spilling to disk and hiding real row counts from the planner. Raising work_mem alone was not reliable (64MB still timed out at 8.4s in one run).\n\n**Change.** `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties` redefined with only these CTE edits:\n- dcp_asset_context / lucasfilm_dcp_asset_context removed;\n- style guides resolved from the page's retained assets via plm.dcp_asset / plm.lucasfilm_dcp_asset (PK id), then the style guide tables (PK id) - so the (property, style guide, folder) set is identical;\n- page_dcp_retained_assets / page_lucasfilm_dcp_retained_assets marked NOT MATERIALIZED.\n\nUnchanged: signature, jsonb shape, SECURITY DEFINER, STABLE, `search_path=app, public`, grants, licensing-manager gate, rows, search, paging, authority logic. No work_mem, statement_timeout, role or global setting.\n\n**Production read-only proof (READ ONLY transaction, rolled back).**\n- Output parity: md5 of the full default page (1,067,395 bytes) 530e12902785646a59c03b9c915d496c, Bambi and Cars 2 search results - identical between current and new body.\n- EXPLAIN ANALYZE: execution 24.9s -> 4.7s, planning 1.26s -> 42ms, no temp spill.\n- Default page elapsed: 3.7-6.0s new vs 12.4-33.7s current.\n\n**Tests.** New `supabase/tests/scraped_properties_page_asset_context_contracts.sql` asserts SECURITY DEFINER, STABLE, proconfig, jsonb return, authenticated-only EXECUTE (no anon/PUBLIC), gate present, whole-catalog context gone, no memory/timeout settings. Existing db_data_admin_scraped_properties*.sql fixtures cover counts, paging and output shape.\n\nChecks run locally: `git diff --check` clean, `bash scripts/check-sql.sh` static checks passed, contract valid, sidecar checker OK.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T17:18:35Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":31,"deletions":23,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":44,"deletions":32,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260911170526_scraped_properties_page_asset_context.sql","additions":1163,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_properties_opa_groups.sql","additions":3,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/scraped_properties_page_asset_context_contracts.sql","additions":66,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"ec869aaacf8eebade5331f6d97b5216520079c7f","mergedAt":"2026-09-11T21:53:04Z","number":2793,"title":"fix(#2744): resolve Scraped Properties style guides from the page's assets","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2793"},

{"body":"Closes #2785\n\n## Why\n\nThe Actions installation token runs out of API quota at about ten active PRs. Production applies then fail on \"API rate limit exceeded\".\n\n## What changed\n\n- **One shared file-list read.** `scripts/lib/open-pr-files.mjs` gathers every open PR's complete file list once. It uses the same completeness proofs: an integer `changed_files`, a refusal at 3000 files or more, and a refusal on a count mismatch. Both collision checks read that snapshot. The snapshot is bound to this repo, this PR number, and schema `open-pr-files/v1`, and any mismatch fails closed. Timelines are read only for PRs whose protected files overlap.\n- **Guarded merge.** The pre-lock object-collision run is removed; the under-lock run is unchanged. The under-lock step sets `GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS=0`, so it never waits on quota while holding the lane. A free `rate_limit` preflight runs before the lane is taken.\n- **Lanes audit: moved to #2787.** Listing open issues once touches `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, a protected coordination source that earlier ready PRs also edit, so the cross-PR collision check blocked it. That script is unchanged here. Instead, the transport never waits when a caller asked for exactly one attempt, so the lanes script's locked reviewer budget still fails fast.\n- **Inventory upkeep.** `scripts/lib/open-pr-files.mjs` is added to the global invalidator inventory.\n- **Transport.** For reads only, there is one bounded wait on primary quota exhaustion, and only for a step that opts in with `GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (at most 900). Unset means no wait, so every lock-holding step, including ones not edited here, fails fast exactly as on main. Only the quota preflights and the pr-object-collision scan steps opt in. Secondary limits, other 403s, writes, an unreadable probe, and a second exhaustion all fail closed.\n- **Production gate.** `--rate-limit-wait-seconds 900` applies only to the pre-lane invocation. The lane-held invocation is unchanged and fails fast.\n- **Quota preflight and concurrency.** `scripts/check-actions-quota.mjs` waits once if the quota is low and resets within the opted-in cap; unset or 0 never waits. Otherwise it fails with \"installation quota low: N requests left ... resets at ...\". Cancel-superseded concurrency is added to three PR workflows that lacked it; no lock-holding workflow is touched.\n\n## Judgment call to review\n\nIn `scripts/check-dispatch-collision.mjs`, every open PR still gets the full detail read and changed_files proof, identical to main (an earlier skip for short non-migration lists was removed after review, since a truncated short list could not be proved complete). Tests cover a short list being proved and a truncated short list being refused.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- Node suites (object, dispatch, source, lanes, transport, open-pr-files, actions-quota): see the completion report.\n- With no opt-in, a rate-limit 403 fails after 1 call with no wait or probe; an opted-in read waits 301 s and then succeeds; a different 403 still fails after 1 call with no probe.\n- The collision result is identical whether the checks share a snapshot or gather it themselves, and the snapshot path makes no network reads.\n- Python production gate suite: see the completion report.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude {"body":"Refs #2783 (tracking).\n\n## Why\nProduction apply run https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/actions/runs/34615626046 (main `9da98ede`) lost its **SQL migration guards** job on attempt 1: three tests in `scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py` errored with `OSError: [Errno 39] Directory not empty` inside `TemporaryDirectory` cleanup (`.git`, `.git/objects`, `.git/objects/pack`). Attempt 2 on the same SHA passed, so this is a race, not a code defect.\n\n## Root cause (reproduced)\nThe runner uses git 2.55. Since git 2.47, every `git commit` ends by spawning a **detached** `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach`. Its argv appears in `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` output for a plain two-commit repo (4 spawns). That background process keeps writing into `.git/objects` after `commit` returns, so the fixture's `rmtree` races it. Every foreground `subprocess.run` in the fixtures already waits; the detached child is the only unwaited writer.\n\n## Fix\nSet `gc.auto=0` and `maintenance.auto=false` in each temp fixture repo right after `git init` (checked config writes):\n- `scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py` — `historical_repo` and the per-version source-map test\n- `scripts/test_historical_preview_recovery.py` — both fixtures\n- `scripts/tests/test_import_order_list.py` — the reviewed-commit fixture (not in the failing glob, same leak)\n\nNo guard, assertion, skip, or retry was added or relaxed.\n\n## Proof\n- Same trace with the two settings: **0** maintenance spawns (control without them: 4).\n- `python -m unittest scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py scripts/test_historical_preview_recovery.py`: `Ran 152 tests ... OK`.\n- Order-list reviewed-commit tests: `Ran 6 tests ... OK`.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T15:34:06Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":14,"deletions":43,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":22,"deletions":32,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_historical_preview_recovery.py","additions":11,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":11,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/tests/test_import_order_list.py","additions":3,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"620903983e287a0677aa705c7a19abd2fd788890","mergedAt":"2026-09-11T16:04:06Z","number":2782,"title":"test: stop detached git maintenance racing temp-repo cleanup","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2782"},
{"body":"Refs #2781 (tracking) and #2758 (orchestrator marker; owner-authorized removal of low-value delivery friction).\n\n## What changes\n- **Approval carry-forward.** An APPROVE recorded at head A still satisfies the gate at head B when A is an ancestor of B and the PR's own diff against its merge base with main is byte-identical at both (`.agent/` evidence aside). New `scripts/lib/pr-content-equivalence.mjs`; used by `check-exact-head-approval.mjs` (guarded merge) and `assertDurableReviewApproval` (preview gate). Exact comparison, not `git patch-id` (which ignores SQL whitespace). A refusal at an equivalent head is never carried.\n- **Main-tip freshness.** `check-main-tip-freshness.mjs --contains` no longer refuses a moved main when the PR touches no file main changed (`.agent` aside), has no migration version collision, trial-merges cleanly (`git merge-tree`), and its own diff is unchanged by that merge.\n- **Production preview proof.** The producer pin no longer rejects a preview because main later added or changed another version's verification sidecar (#2703 vs #2748), unless that version's migration names a schema-qualified object a promoted migration names. The promoted version's own sidecar and every other producer file stay pinned byte for byte.\n\n## Tests\n- `lib/pr-content-equivalence.test.mjs`: 6/6 (merge-only refresh passes; migration edit fails; whitespace SQL edit fails; `.agent`-only change passes; rewritten branch fails).\n- `check-main-tip-freshness.test.mjs` + lib: 29/29.\n- `check-exact-head-approval.test.mjs`: 50/50.\n- `manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`: 517/517.\n- `test_production_business_risk_gate.py`: 135 passed, 3 failed; the same 3 fail on untouched origin/main (pre-existing).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T15:29:27Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":32,"deletions":18,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":38,"deletions":23,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"AGENTS.md","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"config/orchestrator-global-invalidators-v1.json","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-exact-head-approval.mjs","additions":85,"deletions":8,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-exact-head-approval.test.mjs","additions":66,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-main-tip-freshness.mjs","additions":85,"deletions":8,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-main-tip-freshness.test.mjs","additions":73,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/lib/pr-content-equivalence.mjs","additions":96,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/lib/pr-content-equivalence.test.mjs","additions":102,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":42,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":34,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":81,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":59,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"ab2e65126cf79abad7e59e2c2c41202d6cefffc4","mergedAt":"2026-09-11T20:11:28Z","number":2780,"title":"fix(gates): keep approvals and proofs valid across main refreshes (#2758)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2780"},
{"body":"Closes #2482 after production verification. Claim #2778, reserved version 20260911150805.\n\n## What changes\n- New frozen crosswalk `plm.legacy_erp_item_identity` (copied from `public.erp_items_current`, RLS on, admin-read policy mirroring the retired admin policy).\n- `api.plm_item_list`, `plm.refresh_style_tracker_item_bridge()` and `public.resolve_product_category_prediction_item_identity()` read the crosswalk instead of the legacy table.
