No other views, policies, publications or cron jobs; PopDAM app code has no references (only generated types in poppim-web).\n- View rewritten against the crosswalk: 19,362 rows, md5(id|source_id|division_code) `7f214c4a3178143a41d2741c8cad677a`, identical to the live view.\n\n## Tests\n- New `supabase/tests/erp_items_retirement_contracts.sql` (archive + revokes, no dependents, readers repointed, FK gone/column kept, column contract, legacy UUID resolution with a control).\n- Four existing tests repointed from the legacy table to the crosswalk.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T15:18:02Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":57,"deletions":26,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":68,"deletions":42,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"config/db-data-admin-property-source-coverage.json","additions":8,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260911210844_retire_erp_items_to_archive.sql","additions":625,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/erp_items_retirement_contracts.sql","additions":151,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/plm_item_import_phase2_contracts.sql","additions":18,"deletions":19,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/plm_item_list_repoint_contracts.sql","additions":2,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/popdam_item_bridge_additive_cutover_contract.sql","additions":28,"deletions":19,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/popdam_item_state_contracts.sql","additions":3,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"ff8cd9f5996e71134c7a07d73853a1863be506a0","mergedAt":"2026-09-11T22:14:03Z","number":2779,"title":"Retire erp_items_current/raw to archive schema (#2482)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2779"},
{"body":"Closes #2775. {"body":"Orchestrator marker #2758.\n\n## What changes\nA merged migration can go to production WITHOUT a shared-preview apply when the exact merged SQL passed the required check `supabase/tests against an ephemeral database` on the source PR head. Preview stays mandatory for SQL that is high-risk to live data.\n\n- `scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py`: new `preview_required_reasons` (conservative allowlist classifier), `prove_ephemeral_ci_evidence`, and exactly-one-route selection in `assess()`. New flag `--ephemeral-check-run-id`; the preview flags become optional, and mixing routes or supplying neither is refused.\n- `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml`: new input `ephemeral_check_run_id`, and both gate steps pick the route.\n- `.github/workflows/database-contract-tests.yml`: uploads `applied-migrations.txt`, the positive record of each migration that applied.\n- `AGENTS.md` rule 2: a short note on the exception.\n\n## High-risk (preview still required)\ninsert/update/delete/truncate/copy/merge/with, do/select/call, `create table ... as`, materialized views, any drop (except `drop trigger|policy if exists` recreated in the same file), lock/cluster/vacuum/reindex/refresh, a non-concurrent index on an existing table, any `alter table` on an existing table other than a nullable column with no default, `not valid` check/FK constraints, RLS enable/force, owner, or column default changes, plus unknown, empty or unparseable SQL.\n\n## Evidence the skip route requires\nThe job has the exact check name, is completed/success, and its head equals the PR head. Its run is the `database-contract-tests.yml` pull_request run on the same head, in this repo, and succeeded. There is exactly one unexpired `supabase-contract-test-logs` artifact whose downloaded bytes match its digest. Each migration is in `applied-migrations.txt` and not in `failed-migrations-pass2.txt`. The git blob at the PR head equals the file at exact main.\n\nUnchanged: exact-main pinning, required exact-head checks, review evidence, production target proof, lane lock and post-apply verification.\n\n## Tests\n- `test_production_preview_skip.py`: 22 passed (new)\n- `test_production_business_risk_gate.py`: 137 passed\n- `test_production_apply_review_evidence.py`: 15 passed\n- Related Node tests: 115 passed\n\nNote: runs of the contract workflow from before this merge lack `applied-migrations.txt`, so the skip route refuses them. A PR needs a contract run after this lands.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T13:14:54Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":22,"deletions":25,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":30,"deletions":30,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/database-contract-tests.yml","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml","additions":46,"deletions":14,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"AGENTS.md","additions":8,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":452,"deletions":11,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_production_preview_skip.py","additions":344,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"41112e1d5a0fbefc77fb5020e260730fed2ee982","mergedAt":"2026-09-11T20:53:32Z","number":2771,"title":"Promote low-risk migrations to production on ephemeral CI evidence, skipping preview (#2758)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2771"},

{"body":"Closes #2712 (author claim #2763). For popcre/designflow-backend#94.\n\n## What\n- New schema `hts_rag` with the ten-table HTS RAG contract, transcribed as explicit DDL (no `LIKE`), self-contained because 20260907/0908/0909 are not applied on production.\n- Every table has `source_environment` (`production` | `alsand`), NOT NULL, no default, not updatable. Provenance metadata only; no policy branches on it.\n- Four NOLOGIN roles: `designflow_hts_{prod,alsand}_{runtime,worker}`. No password anywhere.\n- Workers: SELECT/INSERT on all ten, column-bounded UPDATE, no DELETE/TRUNCATE. Immutable identity, hash and raw-artifact columns are never updatable; `promotion_gate_result` is set-once by trigger.\n- Runtime: SELECT only on precedents, precedent-ruling links and rulings; RLS limits rows to qualified operative precedents and the rulings they rely on.\n- Exact per-table, per-role policies (26), not broad all-table policies.\n- PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role: no privilege on schema, tables or function. Data API exposed schemas unchanged.\n- `public.hts_rag_*`, `hts_rag_split`, `dflow`, `dflow_prod`: untouched.\n\n## Verification\n- In-migration `do $verify$` block fails the apply on any posture drift.\n- `supabase/tests/hts_rag_shared_schema_contract.sql`: worker writes, bounded updates, delete/truncate refused, provenance required, gate immutability, runtime row visibility, browser roles refused.\n\n## Follow-up\nRoles are NOLOGIN; giving an application a login that can assume them is a separate credential step.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-11T13:01:48Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":45,"deletions":20,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":43,"deletions":27,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260911210709_hts_rag_shared_schema_least_privilege_roles.sql","additions":887,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/hts_rag_shared_schema_contract.sql","additions":296,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"6c363d1accb44822e2036713480ecc689fb345e4","mergedAt":"2026-09-11T21:18:07Z","number":2765,"title":"feat(hts_rag): shared HTS RAG schema and four least-privilege roles (#2712)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2765"},
{"body":"Refs #2662. Claim #2762 (version 20260911124746).\n\n## Change\n- `api.crm_customer_list`, `api.crm_account_list`: keep definer semantics, add the `app.has_app_access('crm')` gate `api.crm_contact_list` already applies. Plain security_invoker would break CRM: 8 active CRM profiles hold no role and `core.customer` RLS admits only role holders (preview: no-role CRM user reads 0 from core.customer, 862 via the view); the logo lookup reads admin-only `plm.customer_import`.\n- `api.crm_ingested_domain_list`, `api.crm_contact_segment_list`, `api.crm_contact_segment_counts`, `public.sg_archive_usage`: `security_invoker=true`; base RLS/grants express the same audience.\n- Columns, grants, comments unchanged. Sessions with no JWT (service_role scripts) now read 0 from the two gated views, same as crm_contact_list; no such consumer exists.\n\n## Consumers (popdam3, poppim-web, popcrm-web, dflow_plm, licensor-source-data)\n- crm_customer_list, crm_ingested_domain_list, crm_contact_segment_list/counts: popcrm-web browser (authenticated) only.\n- crm_account_list, sg_archive_usage: no app consumer. No PopDAM/PIM/DesignFlow/Data Admin consumer of any changed view.\n\n## Preview baseline (read-only, authenticated simulation, before apply)\n| identity | has crm | customer_list | account_list | domain_list | crm.ingested_domain | segment_list | contact_list | sg_archive_usage |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| CRM, no role | t | 862 | 862 | 96 | 96 | 8657 | 8657 | 774 |\n| CRM viewer | t | 862 | 862 | 96 | 96 | 8657 | 8657 | 774 |\n| DAM only | f | 862 | 862 | 96 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 774 |\nExpected after apply: CRM rows identical; DAM-only 0/0/0/0/0; sg_archive_usage 774 for all.\n\n## Excluded (reason)\n- crm_customer_picker_list, crm_factory_picker_list, pm_*_list, dam_*_list, opa_*_property: already caller-gated in-view; invoker would break.\n- api.source_capture_inventory: contract test requires authenticated SELECT; metadata only; separate decision.\n- public.style_tracker_rows_with_bridge: depends on api.plm_item_list (owned elsewhere) and ungranted dflow RFQ tables.\n- public.style_tracker_audit_log_with_user: invoker hides other users' names in PopDAM.\n- public.style_guide_folders / style_guide_file_groups: PopDAM browser reads; base already authenticated-readable; revoke would break PopSG.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-11T12:52:05Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":38,"deletions":25,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":45,"deletions":29,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260911124746_crm_definer_views_caller_gate.sql","additions":117,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/crm_definer_views_caller_gate_contracts.sql","additions":124,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"38687a605cf64ac5bbb4c3da9cd15e8d3647ab01","mergedAt":"2026-09-11T16:51:16Z","number":2764,"title":"fix(db): gate cross-app CRM definer views (#2662 batch 1)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2764"},

{"body":"Closes #2741. Standalone construction from the pre-2355 schema passed full database run34573081462, including exact catalog/row parity and original2355/C10. The replacement is therefore declared self-contained and the old version is not an execution prerequisite. Independent review and shared deployment remain pending.\r\n\r\nOriginal evidence: preview run `34066470075`, artifact `9999109871`, applied hash `67dc237a6968ad1a63a8d446e7bd0b1a2cb6efc52a9685dc9c5eb753008f204e`; final reviewed original hash `cb7bf087c6fd2eb2c21faaee786bdf8103ca8cf9f7bed37af0da2367f8c9d438`. {"body":"The production blue-tag facet and exact list count still exceed the existing eight-second viewer ceiling. Their tag-driven plan reads thousands of wide asset heap rows. {"body":"Closes #2579 context. Claim #2679; reserved migration version `20260910155753`.\n\n## What this does\n\nMigration `20260910155753`:\n\n1. Lands the Paramount TrackerPlus submission landing schema — an append-only capture root plus a Property child table, exact-label SHA-256 identity (`identity_method = 'exact-label-sha256'`), and three `security definer` loaders (begin / load chunk / finalize) that are idempotent on identical evidence and refuse changed evidence, duplicate labels, blank labels, a wrong local key, and any `property_source_id` / `source_id` / `portal_record_id`.\n2. Classifies the post-inventory `plm.marvel_*` and `plm.wwe_*` families in `api.source_capture_inventory`, which still reported them as `other`, and gives the TrackerPlus family its own latest-complete capture clock so it is never pinned to the Paramount Creative Library clock.\n3. Adds exactly three source groups to `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties`: Paramount Submissions (TrackerPlus), Coca-Cola Creative (Asset Library Property choices) and WWE Submissions. Paramount Creative stays a separate group.\n\nNo Property vocabulary is manufactured from inferred, folder, tag, guide, free-text or asset evidence: the migration's own fail-closed verification, the contract test and the catalog contract all require `plm.coke_approval_vocabulary_value` and the three `plm.wwe_*_inferred` tables to stay out of the reader.\n\n## The machine-readable authority\n\n`config/db-data-admin-property-source-coverage.json` records 35 families with an explicit disposition for every `plm.*` family, including the `marvel_asgard_*`, `wwe_*` and new `pmt_trackerplus_submission_*` families. `scripts/check-db-data-admin-property-source-coverage.mjs` is its fail-closed validator (unclassified table, duplicate family, unknown disposition, selector tie, exposed-without-source-table, refused evidence read by the migration), with 15 negative-path tests. Both are wired into the Shared Supabase Migrations workflow.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `bash scripts/check-sql.sh` — `Static checks passed.`\n- `node scripts/check-production-verification-sidecars.mjs --base origin/main` — `{\"status\":\"OK\",...,{\"version\":\"20260910155753\",\"markers\":[1083],\"sidecar\":true}]}`\n- `node scripts/check-db-data-admin-property-source-coverage.mjs` — `35 families, 15 exposed, 328 plm tables classified`\n- `node --test scripts/check-db-data-admin-property-source-coverage.test.mjs` — 15/15\n- `python -m pytest scripts/test_production_catalog_verification.py scripts/test_check_production_verification_sidecars.py scripts/test_migration_derivation.py scripts/test_production_business_risk_gate.py -q` — all passing\n\nThe single dynamic-execution marker is bound by `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260910155753.json` to catalog contract `all_licensor_property_source_coverage_v1`, a strict superset of `dcp_stable_identity_property_match_v1`.\n\nNothing here has been applied to preview or production. This repository is public and this migration is schema only: no licensed label, row, URL, contract or raw evidence appears in it, in the tests, in the manifest or in validator output.\n\nDo not merge without review.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude {"body":"Closes #2576. Claim #2673. Reserved migration version 20260910123636.\n\n## What changed\n\n`supabase/migrations/20260910123636_dcp_stable_identity_property_match.sql` — one migration, three function contracts, no data writes.\n\n- **`api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties`** now resolves `mapping_state` from the newest **terminal** (approved/rejected) decision across **every retained copy** of one stable DCP identity, instead of the exact `(source_system, source_table, source_property_id)` copy.\n- **`api.db_data_admin_property_match_queue`** presents one coherent review state per business identity (`identity_key`, `identity_decision_state`, `identity_resolution_id`, `identity_conflict`, `identity_copy_count`) while retaining full copy-level provenance and conflict evidence in `identity_copies`. Rows stay one-per-pending-copy, so `resolution_id`, the decide contract, evidence, candidates and keyset pagination are unchanged.\n- **`api.db_data_admin_decide_property_match`** returns the recorded decision under the same stable-identity/provenance contract (`identity_key`, `identity_decision_state`, `identity_copies`). No title-specific exception anywhere.\n\nSections 1 and 3 are text surgery on `pg_get_functiondef()` against exact anchors, each guarded by a `raise exception` if the current merged body is not the one this migration was derived from, plus a post-install check.\n\n## The defect, from production (ref `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`, read-only, 2026-09-10)\n\n```sql\nselect r.resolution_id, r.source_table, r.decision_version, r.approval_status,\n       r.creative_decision_state,\n       (select count(*) from plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member m\n          where m.resolution_id = r.resolution_id) as members\n  from plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution r\n where r.source_property_id = 'dcpvault:properties/ba/bambi'\n order by r.source_table, r.decision_version;\n```\n\n| source_table | v | approval_status | creative_decision_state | members |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| plm.dcp_property | 1 | approved | unmapped | 0 |\n| plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property | 1 | approved | unmapped | 0 |\n| plm.marvel_dcp_property | 1 | pending | (null) | 1 |\n| plm.marvel_dcp_property | 2 | approved | (null) | 1 |\n\nThe identity **is** mapped, yet the copy-keyed reader renders the Disney copy as unmapped.\n\n## The grouping is derived, not assumed\n\n```sql\nselect source_property_id, count(distinct source_table) as tables,\n       string_agg(distinct source_system||' / '||source_table, ' ; ')\n  from plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution\n group by 1 having count(distinct source_table) > 1;\n```\n\n- `dcpvault:properties/ba/bambi` → 3 tables: `disney_dcpvault / plm.dcp_property ; lucasfilm_dcpvault / plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property ; marvel_dcpvault / plm.marvel_dcp_property` — **same** business Creative (~17 other dcpvault ids behave identically).\n- `100`, `101`, `102`, `103` → 2 tables: `sega_dsi / plm.sega_property ; wildbrain_dam / source.wildbrain_era` — **different** businesses. Bare integer source ids collide between licensors and must never be grouped across systems.\n\n```sql\nselect (source_property_id like 'dcpvault:%'), source_system, source_table, count(*)\n  from plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution group by 1,2,3;\n-- true | disney_dcpvault    | plm.dcp_property            | 311\n-- true | lucasfilm_dcpvault | plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property  | 119\n-- true | marvel_dcpvault    | plm.marvel_dcp_property     |  32\n```\n\nAll 462 dcpvault-namespaced rows belong to exactly those three copies, and no other system emits that prefix. The stable key is therefore the id's **own emitted namespace** — never the landing-table family, never the non-authoritative Marvel tag (#2449), never a normalized name.\n\n## Fail-closed rule\n\nTwo or more retained copies terminally **mapped to different member sets** (compared by member fingerprint) is a genuine terminal disagreement: the identity resolves to `conflict`, serves **no** `resolution_id`, and stays reviewable. Nothing guesses a winner. A copy that merely *lacks* a mapping is not a competing authority, which is exactly what the issue's acceptance criterion requires.\n\n## Tests\n\n`supabase/tests/dcp_stable_identity_property_match_contracts.sql` — rollback-safe, entirely synthetic (no licensed values), covering:\n\n- an approved cross-copy mapping is not shown as unmapped because another retained copy lacks one;\n- a retained copy with no decision of its own inherits the identity state;\n- a newer pending proposal does not hide the latest terminal decision;\n- genuine terminal disagreement stays explicit and unresolved;\n- a bare, non-namespaced source id is never grouped across licensors, and its exact-copy contract still holds;\n- all three RPCs keep authentication, least-privilege grants, `security definer` + pinned `search_path`, gate refusal, append-only history, provenance and keyset pagination.\n\nThe fixture deliberately plants the **known-bad** input first (an approved, explicitly `unmapped`, member-less Disney copy) and asserts it is present before asserting the new behaviour, so no check can pass vacuously.\n\n## Verification run so far\n\n- **Local disposable PostgreSQL cluster (throwaway, `initdb` in a temp dir):** the new `api.db_data_admin_property_match_queue` body compiles and resolves every name against stub relations (`CREATE FUNCTION`), and the whole migration file parses (it stops exactly where expected, on the absent production function). The new identity block was then executed against a fixture reproducing all four acceptance cases and returned `shared → mapped`, `queued → mapped` (despite a later pending row), `conflict → conflict` with no mapping served, `bare` disney `→ unmapped` / marvel `→ mapped`.\n- **CI `database-contract-tests`** runs the full from-empty replay plus every `supabase/tests/*.sql` on this PR; that is the authoritative run.\n- **Not done, by instruction:** no preview or production apply, no workflow dispatch, no merge. No production writes were made — every production query above is read-only.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-10T12:53:06Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":65,"deletions":32,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":47,"deletions":36,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260910123636.json","additions":43,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_catalog_verification.py","additions":53,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260910123636_dcp_stable_identity_property_match.sql","additions":749,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/dcp_stable_identity_property_match_contracts.sql","additions":569,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"e5114758f9deb826a691b3d754bf685b6f0f8ff1","mergedAt":"2026-09-10T15:55:24Z","number":2676,"title":"feat(db): read DCP property matches by stable identity (#2576)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2676"},
{"body":"Closes #2670. Claim #2671, reserved version `20260910123601`. Blocks-clearing for #2439 and the forwarded appender `u2giants/popdam3#123`.\n\n## What was wrong\n\n`20260909202801` constrained `public.bulk_operation_runs.status` to `('succeeded','failed','interrupted','cancelled','stopped')`. That set came from the words the bulk-operation code *reads*, not the words the running system *writes*.\n\n## Evidence (read-only production, derived not assumed)\n\nProject ref proved first with the Supabase MCP `get_project_url` → `https://qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai.supabase.co`.\n\nQuery run against **every** operation key, not just the nightly rebuild:\n\n```sql\nselect op.key as operation_key,\n       op.value->>'status' as status,\n       op.value->>'run_id'  as run_id,\n       left(coalesce(op.value->>'result_message', op.value->>'message'),120) as msg\n  from public.admin_config c,\n       lateral jsonb_each(c.value) as op(key, value)\n where c.key = 'BULK_OPERATIONS'\n   and jsonb_typeof(op.value) = 'object'\n order by 1;\n```\n\n24 keys returned. The complete observed vocabulary was three words:\n\n| status | keys | notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `completed` | 11 | ai-tag-bakeoff, ai-tag-single-9bc0a30d, ai-tag-single-a4d9cc8c, ai-tag-untagged, erp-classify, erp-enrichment, propagate-group-tags, rebuild-style-groups, reconcile-style-group-stats, rich-pdf-extract, tag-popsg-files |\n| `interrupted` | 6 | ai-tag-all, ai-tag-groups, ai-tag-single-000370e0, ai-tag-single-34f71eee, embed-dam-search, reprocess-metadata |\n| `idle` | 7 | every one with `run_id = null` — a live state, not an outcome |\n\nThe #2670 row verbatim:\n\n```\nrebuild-style-groups | completed | 3a5cdfaa-ee88-4728-8641-05d4e22e9d37\n                     | \"Created 35974 style groups, assigned 98035 assets\"\n```\n\n**`succeeded` is emitted by nothing.** Second read, of the writers: neither `public.update_bulk_operation` nor `public.update_bulk_operations_batch` validates the status word — it is free text from PopDAM. The only vocabulary either knows is `c_stop_status = array['stop','stopping','stopped','stop_requested']`, of which only `stopped` is terminal.\n\n## Decision: widen, not map\n\nA mapping layer would put the appender in charge of translating a word the database cannot see, in a repo the database cannot check, for a vocabulary that is free text and gains a word whenever PopDAM adds an operation.\n\nBut a bare widen has a trap this migration closes in the same breath: `20260909202801` spells success as the literal `'succeeded'` in **both** the failures index (`where status <> 'succeeded'`) and the \"a failure must say why\" constraint. Adding `completed` alone would have counted every successful nightly run as a failure in the exact index alerting reads, and refused every successful append for not explaining a failure it did not have. So success stops being a spelling: a generated `succeeded` column classifies it once, and the index is rebuilt on that.\n\n`idle`, `running`, `stopping`, `stop_requested` stay refused — they are live states, not outcomes.\n\n## Making the rejection visible, not silent\n\n1. New `source_status` column keeps the raw admin_config word beside the classified one, so a normalised status can never quietly relabel a run.\n2. A bad status raises SQLSTATE 23514 on `bulk_operation_runs_status_is_terminal_outcome`, a constraint whose name states the rule; the column comment lists the accepted words.\n3. The append is the worker's own last statement in its own transaction, so a 23514 aborts and is reported as that run's failure — not absorbed by a scheduler that only measures the enqueue (cron job 7).\n\n## Tests\n\n`supabase/tests/bulk_operation_runs_contracts.sql` extended: the live `completed` shape inserts with no error and classifies as a success; `interrupted` inserts and does not; both legacy spellings still work; and six known-bad cases (`idle`, `running`, `stop_requested`, `stopping`, blank `source_status`, unexplained non-success) are each counted from inside their `check_violation` handler with a final `refusals <> 6` assertion — so the guard fails both if a rejection stops rejecting (bare `raise` escapes as P0001) and if a handler is ever widened to swallow everything.\n\n## Checks run locally\n\n- `bash scripts/check-sql.sh` — **passed** (Guard B ok; Guard B2 skipped, no ledger source configured locally).\n- `node scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.mjs` — **UNKNOWN**, `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` not set locally. Nothing was compared. No applied migration was edited by hand; this change is additive fix-forward.\n- Contract tests were **not** executed locally: no Docker/Postgres in this worktree. They run in CI (`database-contract-tests.yml`).\n\nNot applied to preview or production; no workflow dispatched.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-10T12:42:23Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":57,"deletions":12,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":58,"deletions":18,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260910123601_bulk_operation_runs_live_status_vocabulary.sql","additions":267,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/bulk_operation_runs_contracts.sql","additions":193,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"0d4777b4c19ebdf388a97f609763ef35e0046e01","mergedAt":"2026-09-10T14:55:21Z","number":2674,"title":"fix(bulk_operation_runs): accept the terminal status production actually writes (#2670)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2674"},
{"body":"Handoff for the session that closed #2307, #2308 and #2323 and delivered Step 2 of the database efficiency and Data API security program (#2326, merged as `59f7d2a7558a1359ef9e7a13c256ff23edf37c50`).\n\nDocuments-only: one new file under `HANDOFF.d/`.\n\nCarries the operational finding worth reading — `guarded-migration-merge.yml` requires a base equal to main's tip, and the rebase that satisfies it voids both durable reviewer verdicts, so a busy main can starve a PR indefinitely unless the rebase, both slot draws, both reviews and the dispatch are run back to back.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-10T12:36:49Z","files":[{"path":"HANDOFF.d/2026-09-10T0450Z-edge-dev-claude-five-oldest-issues.md","additions":81,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"108342c11d743b96e4f61b1880478c75e8240fe1","mergedAt":"2026-09-10T12:59:22Z","number":2672,"title":"docs: hand off the five-oldest-issues closeout","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2672"},

{"body":"Closes #2318.\n\n## The gap\n\nOn 2026-09-04 a DesignFlow application session hit a shared-db constraint defect, opened orchestrator marker #2312, and ran a structural repair. Albert had never authorized it.\n\nThe marker guard could not have caught it. #2312 was the **only** open marker and its routing block was **well-formed**, so every check passed. Routing answers \"where do I send work\". Nothing anywhere asked the earlier question: **was this session ever allowed to hold the role?**\n\nThe session did not lie to itself about any fact. It reasoned that delegated task traffic plus a genuine structural need added up to authority. The closeout finding is exact: *structural work need does not confer orchestrator authority; the marker itself was evidence of an unauthorized assumption, not evidence that authority existed.*\n\n## The change\n\n`authorization:` joins the `orchestrator-routing` block. Exactly two values are admissible:\n\n- `owner-current-chat <ISO-8601 instant>` — Albert authorized **this** session, in the conversation it is running in.\n- `owner-authorized-handover #<marker issue>` — direct succession, and it must cite the **same** issue the marker declares as `handover_issue:`, so a session cannot cite a handover it is not continuing.\n\nEvery inference that produced #2312 is refused **by name, with its reason quoted** — a `db-work` label, delegated task traffic, a structural need, a handoff document, plus the nearest neighbours of each. Naming them means the refusal argues back instead of saying \"invalid value\", which a session in that position would have read as a formatting problem and worked around. Unrecognised free text fails closed: free text is how \"the task needed it\" would have passed.\n\nA marker that cannot state admissible grounds resolves **INVALID, not NONE**. Per the AGENTS.md exit table those are opposite answers — NONE means nobody is running, INVALID means somebody may be running and unreachable. Neither is permission to dispatch and neither is permission to take the role. Path A either way.\n\n## What it deliberately does not do\n\nIt cannot **prevent** a marker being opened — markers are claimed outside any pull request, exactly as marker collisions are. It cannot prove Albert said the words; no repository check can. It converts a silent assumption into a written, refutable assertion, and makes the inferences that actually happened impossible to write down as valid.\n\n`authorization` is **not** added to `REQUIRED_FIELDS`. That would fail every marker opened before admission existed — including the live one, for a field nobody could have written. It has its own dated cutoff, `2026-09-10`, enforced only by `validateAdmission`, and grandfathering covers a **missing** field only: a pre-cutoff marker that writes a refused ground still fails, and an unreadable creation date is treated as in force. The renderer emits the field blank on a new marker rather than omitting it — and blank is refused, which is the intended outcome for a session with no grounds.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `node --test scripts/lib/orchestrator-admission.test.mjs scripts/check-orchestrator-marker.test.mjs scripts/lib/orchestrator-routing.test.mjs` — 60 pass, 0 fail (19 new admission tests, 6 new marker-guard tests).\n- `node --test scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` — 482 pass, 0 fail, unchanged.\n- Contract `refs/db-contracts/2318/1`.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-09T14:58:58Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":34,"deletions":39,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":53,"deletions":53,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/orchestrator-marker-guard.yml","additions":7,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"AGENTS.md","additions":64,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":62,"deletions":41,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-orchestrator-marker.mjs","additions":21,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-orchestrator-marker.test.mjs","additions":72,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/lib/orchestrator-admission.mjs","additions":249,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/lib/orchestrator-admission.test.mjs","additions":214,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/lib/orchestrator-routing.mjs","additions":9,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"4d5c01065c8f909630ed6d60f5d61be893862215","mergedAt":"2026-09-09T21:05:21Z","number":2636,"title":"feat(orchestrator): require admissible grounds to hold the orchestrator role (#2318)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2636"},

{"body":"Closes #2311.\n\n## What was wrong\nTwo refusals in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` named a menu of possible causes and left the operator to work out which one fired. Both cost real time during orchestrator session #2297:\n\n1. Assigning a reviewer for PR #2260 while work issue #2207 was **closed** was refused with *\"review assignment issue, PR head, or verdict changed after mutex acquisition\"* — pointing at a head change that had not happened. Reopening #2207 fixed it instantly.\n2. Passing an **orchestrator-marker** issue number as the work issue was refused with *\"reviewer does not hold the exact active lease\"*, which named neither the lease actually held nor the fix.\n\n## What changed\nTwo helpers now append the specific cause:\n\n- `reviewEligibilityCause` reports whichever of these is true: the work issue is closed while the PR is still open (with \"reopen it, or merge the PR first\", and the marker-vs-work-issue hint), the issue is closed and the PR is not proven merged into main, the PR head has moved (naming both SHAs), or — when neither holds — that the merge-eligibility check itself refused.\n- `reviewActiveLeaseCause` reports what the reviewer's active lease actually holds (issue, PR, head, parsed from the lease commit), against what the verdict claims, and says that differing issue numbers mean the wrong one was passed.\n\n**Neither helper issues a fresh wire read.** They use only the already-fetched issue, PR and requested head. The review request budget is fixed at 25, and a failing extra call from an error path would replace the real cause with its own.\n\nThe existing message prefixes are unchanged, so every prior assertion and any operator runbook still matches.\n\n## Verification\n- `node --test scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` — **486 pass, 0 fail** (482 before; 4 added).\n- The four added tests each assert the specific cause **and** that the misleading alternative is absent: the closed-issue case must not say the head moved, the moved-head case must not blame the issue, and the no-lease case must not name a different assignment.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-09T14:26:22Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":24,"deletions":51,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":41,"deletions":56,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":33,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":54,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"6f879343483df40d5de2f638bd9b3df2b45a2612","mergedAt":"2026-09-09T15:01:33Z","number":2633,"title":"fix(#2311): two lane-script refusals now name their own cause","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2633"},

{"body":"Mechanical closeout for orchestrator marker #2597 (`shared-db.orch EDGE-DEV-2`).\n\n**Docs-only.** Two prose files; no code, script, workflow, configuration, schema, or migration change. No database change of any kind was made by this session.\n\n**Do not merge this PR and do not close #2597** — Albert does both himself. The marker is deliberately left OPEN.\n\n## What is in it\n\n- `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-09T0620Z-EDGE-DEV-2-claude-orchestrator-2597-closeout.md` — the session handoff, with contract block `issue: 2597` / `status: OPEN`.\n- `docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md` — a dated supersession pointer recording that `--prepare-preview-dispatch` is a **mutating** command, not an instruction printer. The superseded wording is left in place on purpose; it is the audit trail.\n\n## Facts re-verified for this PR (UTC)\n\n- `origin/main` = `a7a5fa994ae5210f59e23492266d92d4eb4cbd42`, the merge of #2612 — checked 2026-09-09 06:15\n- Max migration version = `20260909005945_chain_style_group_counts_to_rebuild_completion.sql` — checked 2026-09-09 06:15\n- Marker #2597 OPEN — checked 2026-09-09 06:15\n\n## Preview — honest state\n\n**Not rehearsed for #2612.** `--prepare-preview-dispatch 2440` refuses while #2439 is open, and #2439 is still open (re-verified 06:16). No preview dispatch was issued. Closing #2439 releases it.\n\n## Sweep result\n\nClosed with dated evidence comments naming the merged PR: **#2535** (PR #2584), **#2440** (PR #2612). Deliberately left open: **#2439** (PR #2447 disclaimed closure) and **#2506** (PR #2542 only \"Tracks\" it). Nothing was deleted.\n\nThree briefed \"verified facts\" did not survive re-checking — #2610 is closed and correctly forwarded, #2588 is closed as completed, and the claimed #2466 owner ruling could not be found anywhere. Details in section 3 of the handoff. I did not write the unverified ruling into the issue.\n\nSecrets sweep: **swept, nothing new.** No worktree was retired — the reaper's own list is three too aggressive and the marker is still open; the safe list is recorded in the handoff for after the marker closes.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-09T06:27:56Z","files":[{"path":"HANDOFF.d/2026-09-09T0620Z-EDGE-DEV-2-claude-orchestrator-2597-closeout.md","additions":440,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md","additions":22,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/business-rules/product-items-and-identifiers.md","additions":8,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"33525d379852371f946ac0c03e13ce029d8fc0b5","mergedAt":"2026-09-09T06:37:12Z","number":2623,"title":"docs: orchestrator EDGE-DEV-2 closeout (marker #2597) — handoff + preview-dispatch supersession","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2623"},

{"body":"Closes the first of the two switches issue #1403 was opened to remember.\n\nEnforced mode for the agent work contract began 2026-09-07T21:26:45Z. The activation record says making `Agent work contract` a **required context** on `main` is a separate, later action, taken only after enforced mode has run green for a full day. That day closed at 21:26:45Z on 2026-09-08, and the live change was made after it.\n\n`scripts/update-required-checks.mjs --add \"Agent work contract\" --apply` made the change and rewrote the committed mirror from its own post-write readback:\n\n- twelve required contexts, no context removed, no context renamed\n- `strict` still `false` (owner ruling, #1286)\n\nThe mirror is what the guarded-merge pre-flight reads when the workflow token cannot read branch protection, so a stale mirror is a stale guard. `PINNED_REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` grows to match: the pin's only job is to make a SHRINKING mirror fail CI, so growth is recorded rather than resisted.\n\n**Switch 2 is deliberately untouched.** One open claim still uses `objects:`, with an active author lease. A legacy `objects:` claim is read as a **write**; retiring the alias while that claim is live would let a second writer start against work already in flight — the exact collision the lanes exist to prevent. Issue #1403 stays open for it.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-08T21:31:33Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":36,"deletions":65,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":30,"deletions":28,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/main-required-status-checks.json","additions":3,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":9,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs","additions":37,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.test.mjs","additions":58,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"1e82ca4e162482848533090cf7fb1cbd42e8f796","mergedAt":"2026-09-08T22:43:25Z","number":2613,"title":"chore(ci): require Agent work contract on main (#1403 Switch 1)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2613"},
{"body":"Closes #2440. Depends on #2439, merged to main as `03f917d0`.\n\nClaim [#2608](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/2608) reserves migration version `20260908204414` and the objects `function public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups` and `function public.refresh_style_group_counts_batch`.\n\n## The defect\n\n```\njobid 6   45 3 * * *   nightly-reconcile-sg-asset-counts\n                       SELECT public.refresh_style_group_counts_batch(array_agg(id)) FROM public.style_groups;\njobid 7   0  6 * * *   nightly-rebuild-style-groups\n                       SELECT public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups();\n```\n\nBoth UTC. Job 6 recomputes every style group's asset count **2 h 15 m before** the rebuild that decides which assets belong to which group. Every group whose membership moves in the nightly rebuild therefore carries a stale count for a full day, and the number is never wrong in a visible way - it is plausible, just old.\n\nJob 6 is also unbatched despite its name: `array_agg(id)` hands ~10.9k ids to one call of a function whose own `statement_timeout` is 30 s, measured at ~94.9 s average over 8 calls (#2214 evidence).\n\nMoving job 6 to a later hour does not fix it. The rebuild is asynchronous - job 7 only enqueues, a PopDAM worker drives it - and the 2026-09-06 run (`ba9ce32e-253f-45a9-ab4f-944cb260354c`, 135,300 processed) took 2 h 09 m, a duration that moves with data volume.\n\n## What changes\n\n1. **Job 6's schedule is deleted.** `nightly-reconcile-sg-asset-counts` is unscheduled; the reconcile no longer runs on a clock at all. This is #2440's stated outcome.\n2. **Job 7 becomes a 10-minute poll** (`*/10 * * * *`). Its jobname and its command are deliberately unchanged - #2439's evidence, the admin tooling and the runbooks all name that job. The function, not the schedule, now decides what happens.\n3. **`public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups()` becomes a three-armed driver.** At most one arm fires per invocation, and every arm is gated on state.\n\n| Arm | Fires when | Requirement |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Enqueue | not already running/queued, at or after 06:00 UTC, and not already enqueued this UTC day - the retired `0 6 * * *` behaviour expressed as state | - |\n| Chained reconcile | status is exactly `completed` **and** its `run_id` differs from the last reconciled run | 1 and 2 |\n| Floor | last reconcile older than 7 days, or never | 3 |\n\n`= 'completed'`, never \"the status changed\": an `interrupted` or `failed` run must not trigger a ~98 s recompute against membership the rebuild never finished touching. Keyed on `run_id`, never on status alone: a status left standing at `completed` would otherwise re-reconcile every ten minutes forever.\n\n**Requirement 4 - batching.** Both reconcile arms walk `public.style_groups` in ordered chunks of 500 and call `refresh_style_group_counts_batch` once per chunk. `statement_timeout` is enforced per statement, so the old single-array call was one statement racing a 30 s cap that a 94.9 s workload cannot win; each chunk now gets its own timer. It does not shorten the transaction, and no such claim is made.\n\n## The marker, and why it is not in the operation state\n\nIdempotence and the enqueue gate are keyed on a **separate top-level** key, `admin_config -> BULK_OPERATIONS -> 'style-group-counts-reconcile'`. It cannot live inside `'rebuild-style-groups'`: `public.update_bulk_operation` (20260819011639) replaces that object wholesale from the caller's payload on every write, so a marker stored there would be erased by the worker's next progress update - and an idempotency marker the thing it guards can delete is not a marker. No new table, column, type or index is created.\n\n## The detector (requirement 3, second half)\n\nThe failure mode this design **introduces** is silence: if the rebuild stops reaching `completed`, the counts simply stop refreshing and nothing says so - strictly worse than today's stale-but-running counts. Per #2437, a new failure mode does not ship without a detector. The floor bounds the silence at 7 days, and the marker records `last_reconciled_at`, `last_reconciled_run_id`, `last_reconcile_reason`, `last_reconcile_rows_written` and `last_reconcile_trigger_status`, so \"when did the counts last refresh, and why\" is one JSONB read instead of an inference from `cron.job_run_details` - which cannot answer it, because cron measures the enqueue and reports success for it. Wiring an alert on `last_reconciled_at` into PopDAM is application work and is **not** done here.\n\n## Costs stated plainly\n\n- **Advisory lock.** `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('BULK_OPERATIONS'))` is taken exactly as the baseline body took it and is transaction-scoped, so a reconcile arm holds it for ~98 s once per night and other BULK_OPERATIONS writers block for that window. It is what makes the `run_id` marker safe against two overlapping polls; releasing early would need a session lock and reopen the double-fire race. A separate advisory key would touch more objects than this claim holds.\n- **`admin_config`.** #2440's scope block lists it under reads. This function already **writes** that table today in the baseline body and continues to write exactly the same one row (`key = 'BULK_OPERATIONS'`). Named here rather than left to be discovered.\n- **`refresh_style_group_counts_batch`** is declared in the claim and deliberately **not** replaced. Requirement 4 is a call-site change, and that function's body already carries #2214's change predicate; re-issuing it would risk regressing it for no gain. Over-declaring a write is safe; under-declaring is not.\n- The **worker-signalled** variant (#2440 option A) remains the better long-term shape and is not foreclosed. It is PopDAM work in another repository; when the worker calls the reconcile as its final stage, the chained arm simply stops finding an unreconciled completed run and the floor keeps the net.\n\n`public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups` has no prior migration file; its body was re-derived line by line from `supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql`, not merged from a competing `CREATE OR REPLACE`.\n\n## Contracts\n\n`supabase/tests/chain_style_group_counts_to_rebuild_completion_contracts.sql` pins the catalog posture, that `nightly-reconcile-sg-asset-counts` is **gone** and job 7 polls on `*/10 * * * *`, that a failed run triggers nothing, that an already-reconciled `run_id` is not reconciled twice, that a new completed run reconciles once, and that the floor fires after 30 days without carrying the failed run forward as reconciled. Every behavioural step fails against the pre-#2440 body. The two positive steps run the full recompute and are guarded on `style_groups` size.\n\n## Local checks\n\n| Command | Exit | Evidence |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `bash scripts/check-sql.sh` | 0 | Guard B: nothing sorts before base newest `20260908195056`. Guard B2 skipped loudly - no live-ledger source configured; not claimed as clearance. |\n| `node scripts/check-production-verification-sidecars.mjs --base origin/main` | 0 | `{\"status\":\"OK\",\"sidecars\":43}` |\n| `git diff --check` | 0 | No whitespace errors. |\n| `node scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.mjs` | see completion report | Requires an open PR; run after this PR was created. |\n\nContract tests need a live database; no disposable-cluster run is claimed. Preview apply, review, merge and promotion belong to the orchestrator and were not performed.\n\nContract: `refs/db-contracts/2440/1`, sha256 `6689ea26710e44ffebd5e3f0b4889654154bc7e26a6d23c3d1fae2eacbec74d6`.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\n\n---\n\n## Review round 1 (slot 1, grok-4.6, REVISE) - what changed\n\n**HIGH, floor arm ran while the rebuild was in flight. Fixed in the function.**\nThe finding was right. `ARM 3` tested only `last_reconciled_at IS NULL OR older than 7 days`; `ARM 1` writes `last_enqueued_at` and returns without ever seeding `last_reconciled_at`. So the first poll at or after 06:00 UTC after this migration applies enqueued the rebuild, and the *next* poll - worker mid-run, marker still null - ran the full chunked recompute. That contradicts the header's own justification for the ~98s advisory-lock window, and a chunk cancelled by that contention aborts the driver without stamping the marker, so the next `*/10` poll retries it for the rest of a ~2h09m rebuild.\n\n`ARM 3` now also requires the operation not to be **in flight**: `status in ('running','queued')` **and** the operation's own `updated_at` (falling back to `started_at`, then `last_enqueued_at`) inside the floor window. The staleness half is not optional - without it, an operation abandoned at `queued` by a dead worker would suppress the floor **forever**, trading the reported bug for exactly the unbounded silence `ARM 3` exists to bound.\n\nThe other suggested remedy - seeding `last_reconciled_at` on `ARM 1` - is deliberately **not** taken. That field is the detector's answer to \"when did the counts last refresh\"; stamping it on an enqueue, which refreshes nothing, would make the detector lie. Gating the arm closes the window without corrupting the signal.\n\n**MEDIUM, `ARM 1` checked before `ARM 2`. Fixed in the same function.**\nContained change, so it is fixed rather than argued. `ARM 2`'s condition is now evaluated first. `ARM 1` replaces the `rebuild-style-groups` object wholesale with a fresh `queued` state and a new `run_id`, so a completed-but-unreconciled run met by the 06:00 enqueue lost the only record that it had completed and its membership changes went uncounted until the floor. The enqueue now simply happens on the next poll, at most ten minutes later. Header and `comment on function` both state the evaluation order 2, 1, 3.\n\n**LOW, the chunk walk is not one snapshot under READ COMMITTED. Accepted, not changed.**\nThis is the intended trade, not an oversight. Taking one repeatable-read snapshot for the whole walk reintroduces the long-lived transaction and the bloat that chunking exists to avoid, and it would hold a snapshot open across the same ~98s the review is rightly worried about. A style group whose membership changes mid-walk is picked up by the next completed-run reconcile - at most one rebuild later - and the 7-day floor is the backstop if that never comes. The reconcile has never claimed point-in-time consistency; it claims eventual convergence with a bounded lag, and the marker object makes that lag observable.\n\n**LOW, `authenticated` retains EXECUTE on a definer function that now reconciles. Left in place, disclosed.**\nThe grant is pre-existing baseline ACL, re-emitted unchanged, and the contract test pins the grant set. No caller can be proven absent: the consumer is PopDAM, a separate repository, so this repo cannot show the grant is unused, and revoking it here would be a change made blind. The reachable surface is also bounded by the arms themselves - every one of them is idempotent by `run_id` or by the floor, so an `authenticated` caller can force at most one recompute per completed run, which pg_cron would run anyway; it cannot be used to loop the recompute. Tightening it belongs with a PopDAM-side check of the actual callers, not with this migration.\n\n## Contracts added\n\nCovering the exact case the review said was never hit:\n\n- status `running` with `last_reconciled_at` **null** - nothing fires;\n- status `queued` with `last_reconciled_at` **null** - nothing fires;\n- a `queued` operation untouched for 30 days - the floor **does** fire (the suppression is bounded);\n- an unreconciled `completed` run is reconciled, not enqueued over (the MEDIUM).\n\nThe first two are negative steps and run unguarded, outside the `style_groups` size guard. The ordering step is honest about its limit: a contract test cannot move the clock, and `ARM 1` also needs UTC hour >= 6, so below 06:00 UTC the step emits an explicit `PARTIAL ... Not claimed as coverage of the ordering` notice rather than an unearned pass.\n\n**Positive control.** Running the new suite against the pre-fix function body taken from git produces `ERROR: CONTRACT (#2440 review HIGH): the floor arm fired (reason = floor) while the rebuild was \"running\" with last_reconciled_at still null`. The new test provably discriminates.\n\n**Rehearsal.** Disposable local PostgreSQL cluster, stubbed `admin_config` / `style_groups` (1200 rows) / `refresh_style_group_counts_batch`: all behaviour contracts pass; chunk walk 12 chunks, min 200, max 500, 4800 ids over 4 reconcile passes.\n\nNo previously disclosed caveat was removed and no guard was weakened.\n\nContract: `refs/db-contracts/2440/4`, sha256 `c613c5813a1283968ff7c9f58d99a9de7831bd442c74413caf4c5983ab3fa8dd`.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-08T20:57:57Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":56,"deletions":12,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":56,"deletions":32,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql","additions":0,"deletions":96,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260909005945_chain_style_group_counts_to_rebuild_completion.sql","additions":509,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/chain_style_group_counts_to_rebuild_completion_contracts.sql","additions":463,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"b294422da66210caac0a16c1c7f78a46be2c7a7f","mergedAt":"2026-09-09T06:06:52Z","number":2612,"title":"feat(db): chain style-group count reconcile to the rebuild completing (#2440)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2612"},
{"body":"Documentation-only. Captures findings from the 2026-09-06/07 \"Unmapped titles in Disney Creative Vault\" session that were never written down.\n\n## What is recorded\n\n**New `docs/business-rules/unmapped-licensor-population.md`**\n- The three different starting populations — 6,350 (all divisions), 2,016 (loader-unresolved, CW001 1,870 + SP001 146), 15,049 (live `/items` for the licensed divisions) — and why they answer different questions.\n- The authoritative live-feed chain 15,049 → 1,634 → 214 → 23, with the by-year split 2022:2 2023:6 2024:2 2025:7 2026:6, which is flat. The earlier \"getting worse every year\" claim is withdrawn.\n- What the 23 are: 14 ERP charge lines, 5 multi-license assortments, 2 uncleaned test rows, and exactly one genuinely routable product (`VSZ93SH01`, Shrek canvas, routes to NBCUniversal not Disney).\n- The superseded database-derived chain 2,016 → 2,011 → 608 → 288 → 31, marked Historical, each step with its exclusion rule and why it was legitimate, plus the reason the whole chain is void: it read `royaltyCode` as the Licensor when the published rule already said MG05 is Licensor.\n- Operational facts with no other home: `plm.item.style_number` is NULL on every row, `api.plm_item_list` has no reader in any application, and ColdLion exposes no licensor or property list endpoint.\n- The two ColdLion data faults that survived the vendor re-check.\n\n**Owner rulings, quoted verbatim, dated 2026-09-06, in their natural homes**\n- `merchandise-and-product-taxonomy.md` — EH001 and EP001 carry no licensed product; 100% unresolved is their expected state and they must be excluded from any missing-Licensor population.\n- `product-items-and-identifiers.md` — exclude items created 2021 and earlier, and obvious ERP artifacts, from any such population.\n\n**Correction that matters for prepack work in flight**\n- `plm.\"itemDetail\".prepack_code_fk` marks prepack MEMBERS (97.3% resolve a property); `public.erp_items_current.prepack_code` marks prepack HEADS (5.2%). Not interchangeable.\n\n## Venue\n\nshared-db is public. This adds business rules, counts, and a handful of named example SKUs — the pattern already used throughout `docs/`. No credentials and no licensor-confidential bulk data.\n\n## Checks\n\nEvery changed file is Markdown prose; no code, SQL, workflow or configuration is touched, so the merge does not wait on CI.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-08T20:47:38Z","files":[{"path":"docs/business-rules/application-map.md","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/business-rules/merchandise-and-product-taxonomy.md","additions":25,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/business-rules/product-items-and-identifiers.md","additions":35,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/business-rules/unmapped-licensor-population.md","additions":161,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"docs/coldlion-erp-api-reference.md","additions":8,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"5fbec8d1244511ee50759872bd3133cef0f897af","mergedAt":"2026-09-08T20:56:58Z","number":2609,"title":"docs: record the unmapped-licensor population analysis and its owner rulings","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2609"},

{"body":"Closes #1868.\n\n## The defect\n\n`scripts/reap-merged-worktrees.mjs` refused the **entire run** whenever any\n`orchestrator-marker` issue was open. A marker is open nearly all the time, so\nthe reap never ran. Issue #1868 reported 31 worktrees; the machine was at **81**\nwhen this branch started.\n\nThe refusal was right about the hazard and wrong about the remedy. Its stated\nreasoning — a clean worktree on a merged branch is indistinguishable from one a\nlive agent just pushed from — holds only if you look at git alone. The repo\nalready publishes positive liveness signals.\n\n## The repair\n\nThree positive signals replace the one blanket guess, and every one says **KEEP**:\n\n1. a worktree named by an open `db-claim` issue, matched on its exact `worktree:`\n   path **or** its `branch:` — with or without a marker;\n2. the worktree the reap is itself running inside;\n3. while a marker is open, any worktree touched inside the idle window (24h by\n   default), because dispatch and claim creation are not atomic.\n\n**Unknown counts as live.** A worktree whose activity cannot be measured is never\ncalled idle, and a failed read of the markers or of the claims never relaxes a\nguard — an unreadable marker list is treated as \"an orchestrator is live\".\n\nThe single remaining whole-run refusal is now about *missing evidence*: a live\norchestrator whose open claims could not be read at all, which would silently\ndowngrade the guard back to the guess it replaced.\n\n`--force` skips only the idle window. It cannot override a claim, uncommitted\nchanges, unpushed commits, a lock, a detached head, or an unmerged branch.\n\n## A measurement that changed the design\n\nThe git administrative *directory's* own mtime is deliberately not consulted. It\nread **0.0 hours for all 79 worktrees at once**, because any git command anywhere\nin the repository refreshes it for every worktree. Using it made the reap report\nzero candidates — the same do-nothing outcome as the old refusal.\n\n## Proof\n\n- `node --test scripts/reap-merged-worktrees.test.mjs` — **24 pass, 0 fail** (12\n  before). Every new signal has a known-dirty case, including `UNMEASURABLE\n  ACTIVITY COUNTS AS LIVE` across `undefined`, `null`, `NaN` and a non-number.\n- Dry run against the live repo, with orchestrator marker **#2597 open**: 79\n  worktrees, 8 claimed paths, 8 claimed branches, **9 retireable**. Each of the 9\n  was independently confirmed clean, pushed, on a merged branch, and last\n  committed 25 hours to 6 days ago.\n- `--apply` removed **9 of 9**. The reap ran for the first time since #1868 was\n  filed, alongside a live orchestrator, without `--force`.\n\nAgent work contract: `refs/db-contracts/1868/1`.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-08T19:53:10Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":79,"deletions":52,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":40,"deletions":55,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":16,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/reap-merged-worktrees.mjs","additions":217,"deletions":26,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/reap-merged-worktrees.test.mjs","additions":269,"deletions":6,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"4e4a8ddb9cd15cda62700ad0e527a3d7b7f8916f","mergedAt":"2026-09-08T22:24:45Z","number":2606,"title":"fix(#1868): reap merged worktrees on liveness evidence instead of a blanket refusal","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2606"},
{"body":"Closes #2244.\n\n## What was broken\n\n`ai-codex-review` exits 0 and publishes a complete, substantive review, but it spells its verdict as a final two-line `## Verdict` / `APPROVE` section inside the report file whose path it prints. The governed runner records only a terminal `VERDICT: <decision> <40-hex head>` line, and never read that file. Because the wrapper accepts no prompt argument, it cannot be talked into the runner's format the way `ai-gemini` can with `--governed-verdict`. Every reviewer draw that landed on codex was a structurally dead slot: the review was done, paid for, and discarded.\n\n## What changed\n\n`scripts/run-governed-review.mjs` now transcribes the published report into its own grammar. This is transcription, not relaxation:\n\n- The head still comes **only** from the runner's pinned `options.headSha`. The report can never supply it - it can only fail to match it.\n- The single-terminal-verdict rule, the extra-decision-word refusal and the auto-void path are untouched. Transcribed findings go through `extraVerdictLines` before anything is posted, so a codex review whose prose carries a stray decision word still takes the #2207 preservation path.\n- Two checks are **added**: the report must declare the same reviewed commit being recorded against, and the printed path must have the wrapper's own `.ai/reviews/codex-<mode>-<runid>.md` shape, because that path selects a file this process will read.\n- The wrapper's header table is left out of the posted body on purpose: its 64-character source digest opens with 40 hex characters that `unambiguouslyTiedToHead` would read as a foreign commit sha.\n- A failed wrapper run never reads a report, so a stale report from an earlier run cannot rescue it. `BLOCKED` is refused as unrecordable.\n\nThe reviewer is repaired, not removed or excluded.\n\n## Proof\n\n45/45 tests pass in `scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs`, 11 of them new. The known-dirty cases are exercised, not assumed: a report about a different commit, a missing or duplicated verdict section, `BLOCKED`, a non-decision word, empty findings, a missing result section, a path outside `.ai/reviews/`, a malformed basename, a failed run with a report on disk, and a findings body carrying a stray decision line.\n\nA positive control ran the **pre-fix** runner taken straight from `git archive HEAD` - never hand-reverted - against exactly what the wrapper emits:\n\n```\nBEFORE (git HEAD): review wrapper did not produce a recordable terminal verdict (exit 0): the wrapper supplied no recognized diagnostic\nAFTER  (this branch): recorded refs/db-review-verdicts/x verdict APPROVE\n```\n\nThat is the verbatim symptom reported in #2244.\n\n## Note on PR #2564\n\nThat PR takes the other approach - injecting `AI_CODEX_REVIEW_GOVERNED_VERDICT_SHA` - which is a no-op without a matching `ai-devops` wrapper change (issue #2307). This PR is self-contained in shared-db.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-08T19:18:33Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":24,"deletions":20,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":27,"deletions":25,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/run-governed-review.mjs","additions":89,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs","additions":134,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"51db03ccdb540d55b09e63ff58310214d56d6a16","mergedAt":"2026-09-08T19:38:41Z","number":2595,"title":"fix(#2244): transcribe the codex wrapper verdict into the governed grammar","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2595"},

{"body":"Closes #2591.\n\nA prose-only pull request currently cannot pass both gates. The reviewer documents-only lane exempts it, but the agent work contract gate demands two `.agent/*.json` files — and adding them makes the change no longer documents-only. Every prose handoff therefore pays a full code-review round.\n\nThis adds `scripts/check-documents-only-pull-request.mjs`, which classifies the pull request's own changed files with the existing `documents-only-change` classifier, and wires it into the contract workflow ahead of the enforced refusal.\n\nFail-closed by design: rulebook prose (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, plan_*.md, skills, agents, commands) is never a document, and an unreadable, empty or non-array file list is never documents-only. Paginated page arrays from `gh api --slurp` are flattened.\n\nThis pull request is code, so the exemption does not apply to itself; it carries a full evidence pair.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-08T18:29:18Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":32,"deletions":12,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":22,"deletions":15,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml","additions":31,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-documents-only-pull-request.mjs","additions":72,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/check-documents-only-pull-request.test.mjs","additions":76,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"24bca57c9a6de00a577af790733eed9d28f44138","mergedAt":"2026-09-08T18:57:18Z","number":2592,"title":"Exempt documents-only pull requests from the contract evidence pair (#2591)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2592"},
{"body":"Closes #2588.\n\nThe ColdLion history landing tables have been live since 2026-09-05 and every\none of them is empty, because nothing was ever written to fill them. This is the\nloader for the sales-order and production-order half of plan Step 7.\n\n## How it works\n\nOne 7-day grid window and one scope at a time, atomically: fetch every page,\nprove the pages are complete against the vendor's own totals, project the rows,\nthen write the rows, the page evidence, the `sync_run` record and the ledger\nstate in a single transaction. A window is fully loaded or not loaded at all, so\nthere is no partial state to reconcile by hand, and both entry points resume\nfrom that evidence rather than from a note somebody kept.\n\n- `sync-history.mjs` — scheduled, re-reads the most recent windows and skips\n  any already loaded. It trails more than one window on purpose: an order edited\n  days after it was written falls in an older window.\n- `backfill-history.mjs` — manual and resumable, walking the grid oldest-first\n  with a per-run limit so a multi-year backfill is a series of bounded runs\n  rather than one run racing a job timeout.\n\n## The vendor behaviours this is built around\n\nEach has a test that fails if the handling regresses.\n\n- **The page size is silently capped.** A request for 2000 returns 200 with no\n  error and no warning. The requested and returned sizes are stored separately\n  and completion is proven page by page.\n- **A refused request lies about its own status** — HTTP 400 on the wire while\n  the body claims 500. The wire status decides; both are stored. Believing the\n  body would mean retrying a permanent input error forever.\n- **Production history must be asked for one stage at a time.** A stage-less\n  request silently returns only ISS, so ISS/INTRAN/REC are three fetches, and a\n  returned stage disagreeing with the requested one aborts the window rather\n  than landing mislabelled rows.\n- **Parent totals repeat verbatim on exploded rows.** They are stored once and\n  never summed. The one quantity that is summed is checked against the parent\n  and, when it does not reconcile, the row lands without the assertion rather\n  than being quietly adjusted.\n\nA changed row is a new version, never an edit. The EP001 division is excluded\nand the exclusion is counted, so any gap between rows fetched and rows landed\nhas a stated cause.\n\n## Safety\n\n- No migration and no schema change; this ships tooling and two workflows only.\n- The target database is proved immediately before every write, and a target\n  with no `coldlion` schema is refused.\n- Both workflows are dispatch/schedule only — never a pull request or a push —\n  and they refuse to run without an explicitly named database target.\n- No real ColdLion values appear anywhere in the change. The fixtures are\n  synthetic and the loaders print counts, scopes and window dates only.\n\n## Tests\n\n`tools/coldlion-landing-history.test.mjs` adds 39 offline cases covering the\ngrid, the scopes, both vendor defects, both projections and the shape of the\ngenerated transaction. Full tools suite: 819 passing, 0 failing, 0 skipped.\n\n## Not in scope\n\n`sync-masters.mjs`, the masters half of Step 7. It remains open.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude
