{"body":"Documentation only — one file, `docs/owner-rulings.md`. No SQL, no migration, no workflow, no script.\n\nCorrects four inaccuracies in section 6.20 as merged by #2515, all found by an advisory second-opinion review and each verified against the repository before amending. The owner's ruling itself is unchanged; only claims made *around* it are fixed.\n\n1. **\"Every guide has one of each\" was false.** `era_source_id` is `not null` (`supabase/migrations/20260819014639_wildbrain_dam_source_landing.sql:448`); `creative_group_source_id` is nullable (`:449`) with a partial index on `is not null` (`:507-508`).\n2. **\"Equal standing\" contradicted that asymmetry.** Era is mandatory, creative group optional. Still orthogonal, still not a child of era.\n3. **Dangling citation.** The marked-never-deleted principle was cited as §6.5, which is the PR #408 hold. It is the 2026-08-19 owner ruling recorded on #1275 and is not in this file.\n4. **Overstated motivation.** In-place art replacement is one of three motivations #1275 lists, not the motivation.\n\nNo licensor values appear in the diff (§6.14).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-07T19:40:08Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":14,"deletions":8,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":23,"deletions":13,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/owner-rulings.md","additions":22,"deletions":7,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"01993873f9c50216e1ff9a9771aa38be6f4c3f55","mergedAt":"2026-09-07T21:02:17Z","number":2544,"title":"docs(#1275): correct four factual errors in owner ruling 6.20","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2544"},
{"body":"## Behavior\n\nPopSG v2 search exceeds the existing eight-second response budget on representative preview data. This forward migration narrows intermediate rows, selects the requested page before building response JSON, and aggregates exact guide facets once per complete guide identity. It preserves child-before-guide filtering, every response field, exact totals and facets, authorization, all four sorts, pagination, and v1. No indexes, grants, or application rows change.\n\nTracks #2506. Claim #2510 reserves forward version `20260908214749` (twice superseded from `20260907183041` -> `20260908195355` -> `20260908214749` as `main` merged later versions; durable supersession refs under `refs/db-claim-supersessions/2510-*`). Original migration `20260907131610` remains unchanged. Contract generation 10 is published at `refs/db-contracts/2506/10`, hash `1473dadf27d0b4a0e4f2bba30df43b0aa9d2dd85bcf1ead6c874fc1698c851ad`, bound to head `ca3a4ac2`; only the `.agent` evidence pair follows that head. Review must bind the final PR head and current base.\n\n## For the reviewer: the guides identity re-join and SQL NULL\n\nTwo earlier review rounds raised a Critical claiming that the guides-mode re-join, which matches children to their grouped identity on whole-array equality over `[root_label, licensor_name, property_folder, style_guide_folder, style_guide_name]`, drops identities containing SQL `NULL`. Please judge it independently. Three pieces of evidence are already in the tree so you do not have to re-derive them:\n\n1. **A contract test pins the behavior on a real database.** `supabase/tests/popsg_search_style_guide_library_v2_contracts.sql`, contract 8 (search for `contract 8:`), asserts that a guide whose licensor/property/style-guide folders are SQL `NULL` keeps its page row, keeps its re-joined child aggregates (`matched_file_count` 1, `file_extensions [\"pdf\"]`, `tag_names [\"null-tag\"]`), keeps its child-derived facets at count 2, and stays a *separate* identity from the same guide with empty-string folders. It executed against an ephemeral PostgreSQL database in the repository's own **Database Contract Tests** workflow, run [34285650340](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/actions/runs/34285650340), logging `issue #2506 PopSG v2 search contracts: all 9 checks passed`. The migration body is byte-identical since then.\n2. **Baseline and forward produce the identical digest on NULL-bearing volume data.** `scripts/benchmark_popsg_search_v2.py` builds a fixture whose EDGE data sets `property_folder` to SQL `NULL` for roughly a quarter of its rows. Both the unoptimized baseline and the forward function return guides digest `6b5ed84981bbb49f0a8f18252f367531` over 10,860 rows. If the re-join dropped NULL identities, those digests would differ.\n3. **The requested rewrite was implemented and measured, not argued away.** Rewriting the joins as per-column `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` defeats the hash join: the guides forward query went from 4.1s to past the unchanged 8s budget this migration exists to meet. It was reverted, and the reason is recorded in the migration file's own header comment (`supabase/migrations/20260908214749_popsg_search_v2_bounded_paging.sql`, lines 7-20) so the point is visible at the site of the code.\n\n## Validation\n\n- **Exact behavior:** `PASS: 160 exact full-JSON parity cases; 0 skipped.` Both modes, four sorts, two pages, child-only matches, tied dates, date boundaries, combined filters, repeated/null/empty tags, multi-value filters, inactive files, and null versus empty guide identities. Executed at head `ca0032a5` on a disposable local PostgreSQL 18.6 cluster via the script's `--database-url` option; the docker path is unchanged and still the default.\n- **Synthetic volume:** unchanged 8s budget. Files baseline timed out at 8,100 ms and files forward passed at 4,050 ms over 211,323 rows; guides baseline passed at 6,119 ms and guides forward at 3,162 ms over 10,860 rows, returning identical digests.\n- **Nine focused SQL contracts** ran green on an ephemeral database in CI (run 34285650340).\n- **Live preview diagnostics:** optimized read-only SELECT bodies completed in 6,419/6,955 ms over 217,193 active documents and 1,773 guides. These are not deployed optimized API measurements. Original actual API calls exceeded the eight-second client bound. [Evidence](https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/2506#issuecomment-5574442147).\n- **Offline guards at merged head `ca3a4ac2`:** static SQL guards pass (Guard B accepts the branch; Guard B2 live-ledger input intentionally absent, no shared write was performed), 42 derivation tests, 188 catalog verification tests, 10 focused throughput-guard tests, 44 sidecars OK against `origin/main`, truth audit OK for 269 call sites, and a clean `git diff --check`. The hash-bound sidecar verifies the exact installed function body, signature, security and privileges. None of this substitutes for business acceptance.\n\n## Release and acceptance\n\nProduction has v1 and lacks v2. After independent exact-head review, required checks, and coordinated guarded merge, rehearse the forward migration on preview from merged `main` and prove optimized authenticated preview API behavior within the same eight-second limit, including date/filter combinations and authorization.\n\nProduction requires the ordered batch of **both** `20260907131610` (PR #2512) and `20260908214749` (this PR). Bind actual apply-run maps for both versions into supported historical-preview evidence at the final release `main`; pin its digest and the independent production review digest. Use this PR as `source_pr` for the governed dry-run and ordered apply. No derivation override is needed.\n\nDatabase push is not atomic across files: the original may commit before the forward fails. Review this temporary slow-v2 state explicitly. Preserve v1 and prevent consumer rollout until acceptance. On failure, stop, inspect ledger/catalog, preserve applied bytes, and use governed forward-only recovery.\n\nClosure requires both production ledger rows, the optimized definition, authenticated API performance and business verification, and continued v1 behavior. Workflow success alone is insufficient.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-07T19:23:36Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":75,"deletions":41,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":71,"deletions":41,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json","additions":69,"deletions":62,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json","additions":43,"deletions":3,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/benchmark_popsg_search_v2.py","additions":64,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/historical-migration-restorations.mjs","additions":22,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/historical-migration-restorations.test.mjs","additions":35,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260908214749.json","additions":13,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_catalog_verification.py","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_production_catalog_verification.py","additions":14,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260908214749_popsg_search_v2_bounded_paging.sql","additions":391,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/popsg_search_style_guide_library_v2_contracts.sql","additions":105,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"725585e857ea222dca484255eaca76774bef3bdd","mergedAt":"2026-09-09T00:39:54Z","number":2542,"title":"perf: preserve exact PopSG v2 results within bounded response work","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2542"},
{"body":"Closes #2537.\n\n## The defect\n\nThe pass-2 ordering repair decided what counted as \"newer truth\" from migration **filenames** plus whatever the catalog happened to hold. In a from-empty replay that is not evidence. A later migration can fail in pass 1 and roll back again in pass 2, leaving the catalog holding the pre-adoption **baseline** body. The repair then snapshotted that obsolete body and restored it *over* the forward repair the pass-2 file had just made — silently, because both migrations reported success.\n\nRun 34142055022 failed PR #2527 / issue #2501 exactly this way: `20260902042548` and `20260904121037` both rolled back (\"filter count entry points no longer share the implementation\"), so `20260901142825`'s replacement helpers were reverted, and two effective-count contracts failed with a plan shape nothing in the diff explained.\n\n## The repair\n\nRestoration is bound to provenance **proven in this replay**:\n\n- Pass 1 and pass 2 each append a migration's basename to `applied-migrations.txt` the moment it really applies.\n- `check_pass2_routine_supersession.py` now requires `--applied-migrations` and snapshots a routine only when some later migration that declares it is on that record.\n- Routines whose later declarations all failed, have not run yet, or are otherwise unproven are reported and left alone, so the pass-2 file's own definition stands.\n- Overlapping routines are classified individually; a missing record is a refusal (exit 2), not an assumption of success.\n\nThe privilege half is unchanged and still restores schema-wide-revoked EXECUTE grants: it re-grants what the catalog holds right now and never writes a body, so it cannot resurrect an unproven definition.\n\n## Evidence\n\nAgainst the real `supabase/migrations` with an empty applied record, the script now refuses to restore `public.get_effective_filter_counts_unchecked_1703` (from the two rolled-back files) and `public.filter_effective_assets` (from `20260903075635`) — the defect the run reported. With those files marked applied, it emits the full definition snapshot as before.\n\n## Tests\n\n`scripts/test_check_pass2_routine_supersession.py` — 18 tests, all passing — adds the four focused cases from the issue: failed-later-migration must not resurrect, successful-later-migration still preserved, mixed outcomes classified one routine at a time, and grant restoration preserved without resurrecting unproven definitions. Case 1 keeps the pre-fix behaviour as an explicit control, so the test fails if the gating is removed.\n\nNo assertions were weakened, no quarantine added, no applied migration edited, no timeout raised, no RLS changed.\n\nAfter this lands the structural owner rebases #2527 through normal guarded recovery and reruns CI. Claim #2525 and PR #2527 are untouched.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-07T18:26:42Z","files":[{"path":".github/workflows/database-contract-tests.yml","additions":20,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check_pass2_routine_supersession.py","additions":98,"deletions":5,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/test_check_pass2_routine_supersession.py","additions":157,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"c2a8facbff357c126fc27529f7063e01c4fe6b1a","mergedAt":"2026-09-07T18:56:15Z","number":2540,"title":"fix(2537): bind pass-2 routine restoration to proven migration provenance","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2540"},

{"body":"Adds canonical Asset first/last-seen and missing/current facts while preserving established source identity, compatibility fields and historical rows.\n\nHistorical rows retain unknown timestamps and remain editable. {"body":"Records what we learned auditing the Item Master's Non Inventory Item flag on 2026-09-07.\n\n**Business rule (Settled, Albert Hazan, 2026-09-07)** — non-inventory covers fees and charges, raw materials and components consumed into products, sample/test placeholders, and never-stocked digital goods. Store fixtures we physically hold (racks, signage, PDQ, spinners, brackets) stay inventory. The test is whether we hold and count it as stock, not whether we sell it.\n\n**Source reliability** — the ColdLion flag meant to carry this is set on 15 of ~19,600 item records and blank on ~4,700, with at least 35 obvious non-products recorded as ordinary products and ~450 junk records in the file. A blank or \"product\" value therefore proves nothing, and no population may be taken straight from `/items` as a product catalogue.\n\nDocs-only change.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-07T15:03:32Z","files":[{"path":"docs/business-rules/application-map.md","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/business-rules/erp-orders-and-source-meaning.md","additions":31,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/business-rules/product-items-and-identifiers.md","additions":40,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/coldlion-erp-to-supabase-field-mapping.md","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"docs/coldlion.md","additions":8,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"886fe470de8106f2a6353b7cf00030193be68ce6","mergedAt":"2026-09-07T15:18:47Z","number":2516,"title":"docs: Non Inventory Item business rule and ColdLion flag reliability","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2516"},
{"body":"Records Albert's 2026-09-07 ruling on shared-db #1275 as `docs/owner-rulings.md` §6.20, plus the index row.\n\nThree things it captures:\n\n1. **Premise correction, repository-wide.** We collect asset **metadata** only - no art binary is downloaded by any capture. The incremental design therefore cannot detect art replaced in place under unchanged metadata, which was #1275's own stated motivation. Successors must not claim it does.\n2. **Peanuts** - `plm.peanuts_art_program` is the property-shaped entity. `plm.peanuts_initiative` is retailer- and period-bound, a secondary tag only. Note carried forward: an initiative vanishing at the end of its retail window is normal retirement, not withdrawal, so a naive lifecycle rule would false-alarm every season.\n3. **WildBrain** - `era` and `creative_group` are orthogonal axes, not alternatives. The 2026-08-20 framing on #1275 that pitted them against each other is withdrawn. `plm.wildbrain_asset` carries FKs to both, so the data already agreed.\n\nSesame is explicitly deferred: all five `plm.sesame_*` vocabulary tables are empty.\n\nNo licensor values appear in the file (§6.14, public repo). Docs only - no migration, no schema change.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-07T14:56:07Z","files":[{"path":"docs/owner-rulings.md","additions":78,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"5080c4ef53bfae6a5de348bf493ce972e0fa4567","mergedAt":"2026-09-07T15:03:58Z","number":2515,"title":"docs(#1275): owner ruling 6.20 - Peanuts art program is the property; WildBrain era and creative group are two axes","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2515"},

Both new tables ship readable but writable by nobody, pending a later governed write path.\n\nDesign note: the existing ten-argument setter is pinned by name, signature and body text by the production verification script, so it is untouched; a twelve-argument version sits beside it with every argument mandatory.\n\nKnown pinned limitation for the successor: `plm.source_resolution_target_missing()` and the `api.source_resolution` view are outside this claim, so a matched licensor/franchise decision reads as `target_missing = true` through that view. {"body":"Closes #2465.\n\n## Proven root cause\n\n`classifyMainTip` listed the changed files with:\n\n    git log --format= --name-only --no-renames -z -m <dispatched>..<origin/main>\n\n`-m` emits a diff against **each parent** of a merge commit. For a merge M with parents P1 (main) and P2 (the merged branch), M-vs-P1 is the branch's own change but M-vs-P2 is *everything main had gained since that branch forked*. In a repository where every change lands through a pull-request merge, that second diff dragged in unrelated files, so the documentation-only exemption could never fire.\n\nReproduced exactly against the SHAs in the issue:\n\n| command | result |\n| --- | --- |\n| `git log -m 8fa7408b..e82eec28` | `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md`, `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` |\n| `git diff 8fa7408b e82eec28` | `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md` |\n\nThe two script files the refusal named are the files PR #2461 changed. They are not files main moved.\n\n## Change\n\nOne command. A two-point `git diff <dispatched> <tip>` — the movement the refusal message already describes. It also answers what `-m` was reaching for: a plain `git log --name-only` shows *nothing* for a merge commit, so code could hide behind it, whereas a two-point diff cannot hide a file whose content differs between the two ends. `--no-renames` is unchanged and still load-bearing.\n\nThe staleness check is not relaxed: a tip on a different line of history, an unresolvable tip, an unreadable range and an advance reporting no changed file all still refuse exactly as before.\n\n## Tests\n\n- `a documentation-only advance that lands through a merge commit is accepted (#2465)` — **fails on the pre-fix code**, passes after. The documentation branch forks before the dispatched commit, so the merge's second parent is missing the code main gained in between: the exact shape that broke.\n- `POSITIVE CONTROL: a merge that lands code is still refused (#2465)`\n- `POSITIVE CONTROL: a rename from code to documentation is still refused (#2465)`\n\n`node --test scripts/check-main-tip-freshness.test.mjs` — 17 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-06T23:05:40Z","files":[{"path":"scripts/check-main-tip-freshness.mjs","additions":21,"deletions":4,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/check-main-tip-freshness.test.mjs","additions":71,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"df5aa6734bed6be7a0cacc2cf4b6f1f568cf1625","mergedAt":"2026-09-07T00:26:31Z","number":2480,"title":"fix(#2465): guarded-merge staleness check classifies what main moved by","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2480"},
{"body":"Closes #2430.\n\n## Root cause\n\nAfter a **confirmed** create, `recordReviewVerdict` read the ref back and refused permanently whenever the SHA differed. But a retried create writes a second commit object carrying the same verdict record under a different SHA — the commit has a timestamp, the record does not. On PR #2415 (head 0fab4ace) that discarded a completed, paid-for review and burned the tuple.\n\nThe other half of the issue — the runner voiding a findings comment whose digest an artifact had already recorded — was fixed separately by #2468 and is already on main.\n\n## Change\n\nThe readback now compares the **record** standing at the ref against the record this call intended to write, over sorted key/value pairs, so key order is not identity. An equivalent record that still validates as a full artifact is this verdict, and is a success. An unreadable commit, a genuinely different record, or an absent ref after a confirmed create is still a permanent refusal — and every refusal is still marked as created, so the runner never voids the findings comment.\n\nAlso restores `scripts/repair-voided-findings.mjs`: tuples burned before the #2468 fix still exist, and the void is a deterministic, invertible transform. It un-voids the live comment and proves the restoration by re-deriving the sha256 and requiring it to equal the digest the artifact already recorded. It writes no ref and records no verdict. Its test file is added to the required orchestrator-flow test list.\n\n## Tests\n\n- `an equivalent record under a different SHA is the same verdict (#2430)` — **fails on pre-fix code**\n- `the same record with its keys in another order is still the same record (#2430)` — **fails on pre-fix code**\n- `POSITIVE CONTROL: a genuinely different record under a different SHA is still refused (#2430)` — passes both ways, and still asserts the created-artifact marker\n- `scripts/repair-voided-findings.test.mjs` — 7 pass\n\nFull offline suite: 1260 pass, 1 fail — `licensed and internal data artifacts stay in the private source-data repository`, which fails identically on current main and is unrelated to these files.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-06T22:55:02Z","files":[{"path":".github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":27,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/record-review-verdict.test.mjs","additions":44,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/repair-voided-findings.mjs","additions":141,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/repair-voided-findings.test.mjs","additions":140,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"b5a504d93a23c5f2a71fbcb750f063f0522ccec9","mergedAt":"2026-09-07T02:11:41Z","number":2479,"title":"fix(#2430): an equivalent verdict record under a different SHA is a success","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2479"},
{"body":"Closes #2419. Claim issue #2473. Reserved migration version `20260906222019`.\n\n## What this adds\n\nOne object, exactly as claimed: `public.reconcile_style_group_drift(integer)`. It returns a single row of counts and writes nothing.\n\nIt answers three questions the nightly full rebuild currently answers only by doing the work:\n\n1. **Style-group assignment.** How many live assets whose path yields a SKU carry no group, the wrong group, or a SKU with no `style_groups` row yet — and, in the other direction, how many assets whose path yields **no** SKU still carry a group. That second direction is the one the pre-#2408 rebuild could not see at all, because it only ever *set* `style_group_id`; an asset stuck there keeps resolving the wrong licensor in the DAM libraries with nothing surfacing it.\n2. **Orphan references.** Group references pointing at rows that no longer exist.\n3. **Effective-tag projection.** Rows the triggers should have written and did not, and rows that exist with no live source — compared in both directions, over a sample whose size the caller controls, plus a drift *rate* for alerting.\n\n## It cannot grow a repair mode\n\n`LANGUAGE sql` + `STABLE`. PostgreSQL refuses DML in a non-volatile SQL function outright, so the read-only property is enforced by the engine, not by review. The contract test additionally proves it at runtime: `pg_current_xact_id_if_assigned()` is null before the call and still null after, with a control step proving that probe does fire on a real write — otherwise that assertion would prove nothing.\n\n## The SKU rule matches the rebuild\n\nThe issue is explicit that a reconciler deriving the SKU differently from `rebuild_style_groups_batch` reports rule mismatch dressed up as drift. The right shape is one shared derivation function — but extracting it means replacing `rebuild_style_groups_batch`, which is outside this branch's single-object claim and inside another author's collision boundary.\n\nSo the expression is copied verbatim and the agreement is enforced by CI instead: the contract test requires all five derivation tokens to be present in the **live** `pg_get_functiondef` of *both* routines. Changing the rule on either side without the other fails the test. The migration header records the debt.\n\n## Checks\n\n`bash scripts/check-sql.sh` passes on the current `origin/main` tip:\n\n```\nGuard B: no migration sorts before the base branch's newest version 20260906035323 (source: git:origin/main).\nIssue #1235 expected-count guard passed: added migrations validate JSON count types and avoid raw integer casts.\nVerify-cost guard passed: 1 added migration(s) contain no prohibited verification read.\nIssue #1684 EOL reference guard passed: no new dependency was introduced.\nStatic checks passed. Set DATABASE_URL to run migrations against a disposable database.\n```\n\nGuard B2 emitted its usual local warning (no ledger source configured). The contract test needs a database and there is no container runtime on this machine, so it runs for the first time in the `Database Contract Tests` workflow here — it is not quarantined.\n\nNot applied anywhere. Not merged.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-06T22:30:33Z","files":[{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260907031246_style_group_drift_reconciler.sql","additions":280,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/style_group_drift_reconciler_contracts.sql","additions":406,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"222ea52a68a62a9f8396319be95f36e2d209f957","mergedAt":"2026-09-07T05:32:04Z","number":2474,"title":"feat(#2419): read-only reconciler for style-group and effective-tag drift","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2474"},

{"body":"Fixes #2464.\n\n## Proven root cause\n\nThe create-only readback in `recordReviewVerdict` was asked exactly once, immediately after a successful `POST /git/refs`:\n\n    if(io.readRef(ref)!==sha)throw new LaneError('create-only verdict readback disagrees with the created object; this tuple is permanently refused')\n\nGitHub's custom refs are eventually consistent on that read — the exact behaviour this repo's own `readRefAfterWrite` was written for (\"GitHub's create-ref response can arrive before the new custom ref is visible to a following GET\"). A transient 404 was therefore reported as a disagreement for an artifact that HAD been created.\n\nEvidence: `refs/db-review-verdicts/2334-2409-283516930a02c223eda22c6e58252f58ed84d207-slot2` = `500e6ee6b92a3ed3b727bf9d8d30c7b541e13c1a` carries `{\"verdict\":\"APPROVE\",...,\"findings_ref\":\".../pull/2409#issuecomment-5561825191\"}` and was authored `2026-09-06T20:05:05Z`; the run that created it refused and posted `REVIEW RECORDING FAILED — ... Reason: create-only verdict readback disagrees with the created object` at `2026-09-06T20:05:06Z`, voiding comment `5561825191`.\n\nThat void is the destructive half: the artifact is immutable and records `findings_digest` = sha256 of that comment body. Editing the comment permanently invalidates a valid APPROVE. The re-run then hit the second half of the bug — the pre-existing artifact was validated against the NEW comment, giving `findings digest does not match the durable findings` (seen on the same PR at 19:39 and 20:01), which voided the new comment too. That cascade is what burned the tuple.\n\n## Changes (the guarantee is not weakened)\n\n- The readback uses `readRefAfterWrite`. A **different** SHA still fails closed on the first read; only absence is retried. Same check, asked until the API can answer it.\n- Any failure after the create carries `verdictArtifactCreated`, and `run-governed-review.mjs` refuses to run the void path when it sees that marker: it reports loudly, names the artifact and the confirming `gh api` command, and leaves the artifact and the findings comment untouched.\n- An existing artifact is validated against **its own** `findings_ref`, not the comment this round posted — matching what the create-race path already did.\n\n## Regression tests\n\n- `a create-only verdict survives a transient absent readback after a successful create (#2464)`\n- `a readback that never confirms still refuses, and names the created artifact (#2464)`\n- `an existing artifact is validated against its own findings comment, not this round's (#2464)`\n- `a failure AFTER the create-only artifact exists never edits the findings comment (#2464)`\n\nAll four fail on the pre-fix code and pass after.\n\n## Test counts\n\n- `scripts/record-review-verdict.test.mjs`: 9 pass, 0 fail (6 pass / 3 fail before the fix)\n- `scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs`: 32 pass, 0 fail (31 / 1 before)\n- `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`: 459 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped\n- `check-exact-head-approval` + `check-authenticated-review-verdict` + `coordination-scenarios`: 79 pass, 0 fail\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-06T20:26:58Z","files":[{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":76,"deletions":11,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/record-review-verdict.test.mjs","additions":159,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/run-governed-review.mjs","additions":27,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs","additions":63,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"a9959d2469cd5b77a9069f2991cb206ac7217eaf","mergedAt":"2026-09-07T00:13:33Z","number":2468,"title":"Fix #2464: never void a findings comment after the create-only verdict artifact exists","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2468"},
{"body":"Gemini is in the reviewer rotation and is being drawn, but a governed Gemini review could never record a verdict. `ai-gemini` asks Gemini to open its reply with a `## Verdict` heading and a bare decision word — which this runner voids as a stray decision line — and prints a `PASS session=...` summary instead of the review this runner reads from stdout.\n\npopcre/ai-devops#299 added `--governed-verdict <head>` to the wrapper: it switches the prompt contract and the wrapper's own verdict gate to the terminal `VERDICT: <DECISION> <head>` line and emits the review body on stdout. This change injects that flag from the head the review is actually recording against, so no caller has to remember it and a mismatched head is refused rather than silently accepted. Other wrappers are untouched.\n\nTests: `node --test scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs` — 27 pass, 0 fail (5 new).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-06T17:52:22Z","files":[{"path":"scripts/run-governed-review.mjs","additions":33,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs","additions":60,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"1adbbe34b43f1abd5153b8da3ee7a73f6c6261b2","mergedAt":"2026-09-06T18:37:54Z","number":2462,"title":"fix(review): give ai-gemini the governed verdict contract it needs","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2462"},
{"body":"Closes #2460.\n\n## Change\n\n`recoverExpiredClaimFromPr` now passes `allowClaimSuperset: true` to `renewalIssueScope` at both of its call sites, matching what `renewExpiredClaim` already does.\n\nTwo lines. Nothing else is touched: no other precondition is relaxed, the `--release-claim` guard is untouched, and no issue scope block or claim body was edited.\n\n## Premise verification\n\n1. **A claim-superset state is tool-produced and sanctioned.** `expandActiveClaimFromPr` never calls `renewalIssueScope`. It checks only that the work issue is open/ready/structural/orchestrator, then computes `uncovered` PR objects and writes `[...lease.objects, ...uncovered]` back into the claim via `replaceClaimObjects`. Nothing constrains the result to the issue's scope block. A claim exceeding its issue scope is therefore normal, not corruption.\n2. **The guarantee that matters is preserved.** The subset test `issueObjects.some(o => !claimObjects.includes(o))` runs unconditionally and is unaffected by the flag. Every object the work issue names must still be covered by the claim. Only the `issueObjects.length !== claimObjects.length` count equality is skipped.\n3. **No evidence the equality was deliberate.** `git log -S allowClaimSuperset` returns exactly one commit, `9c5eec4d` (\"fix: keep recovered claims maintainable\"), which introduced the flag and turned it on for `renewExpiredClaim` at both call sites while leaving `recoverExpiredClaimFromPr` on the default. There is no comment, test, or commit message asserting the equality as a safety property for recovery. No test in `manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` exercises the equality branch for the recovery path.\n\nOne note for the record: commit `9c5eec4d` paired renewal's superset allowance with an additional \"claim carries objects unsupported by its issue or pull request\" guard. That guard is deliberately **not** added here — it would refuse the very live case this issue exists to unblock (claim #2405's 93 objects against issue #2334's 21), and issue #2460 scopes the fix to the two flag arguments.\n\n## Test\n\nNew regression test builds an expired claim holding a strict superset of its work issue's scope objects, with uncovered objects on the PR, and asserts recovery succeeds, adds exactly the uncovered objects, and restores a live lease. It was run against the unfixed code first and failed with the exact refusal `renewal issue objects do not exactly match the permanent claim objects`. The same test also asserts the preserved subset guarantee: an object named by the work issue but absent from the claim is still refused, with zero writes.\n\n## Test results\n\n- `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs tools/*.test.mjs` — `tests 2008 / pass 2007 / fail 1 / skipped 0 / todo 0`\n- `python -m pytest scripts -q` — `1063 passed, 8 skipped, 5 warnings, 683 subtests passed`\n\nThe single node failure is the pre-existing `scripts/public-data-venue.test.mjs` case about licensed data artifacts (eight `docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260904T212459Z/**.csv` files). It is present on clean `origin/main` at `8fa7408b` and is unrelated to this change — the only files this branch touches are the two script files.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-06T16:47:47Z","files":[{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":2,"deletions":2,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":22,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"f3da884e97f7c72f0bc6882c4cbe7f9172d86b9e","mergedAt":"2026-09-06T18:23:39Z","number":2461,"title":"fix: allow expired claim recovery for legitimately expanded claims (#2460)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2461"},
{"body":"Closes #2454. Fixes the close-comment defect in #2448.\n\nUnblocks PR #2409, whose `Migration author lease` check refuses because branch `claude/issue-2334-canonical-bridges` carries two open claims.\n\n## New: `--release-duplicate-claim`\n\n```\nnode scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --release-duplicate-claim <duplicate-claim> --owner <exact-owner> --confirm-finished\n```\n\nIt refuses unless all of the following are proved from live GitHub state. There is no caller-supplied override flag, and the existing `--release-claim` guard is untouched.\n\n1. At least one **other** open non-legacy claim declares the same lease branch.\n2. That branch has exactly one open PR, and that PR changes at least one migration file.\n3. The claim being released does **not** hold a migration version the PR uses.\n4. Exactly one other open claim on that branch **does** hold such a version.\n5. The owner matches exactly, and the coordination mutex is held for the whole operation and re-proved immediately before the close.\n\n## Truthful close comments (#2448)\n\n`io.closeClaim()` now requires an exact stated reason. The three real paths say what actually ran — acquisition rollback after mutex loss, explicit owner-confirmed release, proved duplicate release — and none of them asserts an expiry sweep, which no code performs. The recovery check that previously verified the one hard-coded string now accepts the legacy string **and** the new explicit-release reason, so it does not start refusing valid closures.\n\n## Tests\n\nAdded to `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`: the duplicate releases with the truthful reason; the authority claim on the same branch is refused; a lone claim on a branch with an open PR is still refused by both paths; wrong owner, a PR with no migration, an unprovable version, and an attempted override flag are all refused; and every close reason is asserted free of the expiry claim.\n\n- `node --test` (migration-author-lease workflow suite): tests 799, pass 799, fail 0, skipped 0\n- `pytest scripts -q`: 1063 passed, 8 skipped, 683 subtests passed\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-06T15:45:18Z","files":[{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs","additions":78,"deletions":5,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs","additions":105,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"2143434da500942d300eca199ea631d14eeaa7b5","mergedAt":"2026-09-06T16:32:07Z","number":2455,"title":"Add a proved duplicate-claim release path and truthful claim-close reasons (#2454, #2448)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2455"},
{"body":"Tracks #2449. This recovery unifies the operative creative-to-submission source crosswalk while preserving canonical UUID source resolution as a separate authority.\n\nThe reader and approval writer use the same operative DCP crosswalk. Explicit mapped/unmapped/conflict states and deferred membership invariants preserve reviewed dispositions and one-to-many members. Existing DCP approvals remain intact; conflicting overlap or unsupported supersession history refuses migration. Overlapping non-mapped placeholders remain original archived evidence and cannot silently supersede operative decisions.\n\nBoth original generic tables become private immutable archives with their original row/audit contents and relation identities. Existing UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE refusals and new INSERT refusals protect history; narrow grants restore service insert/select and authorized legacy DCP reads without exposing generic private decisions. No historical archive is discarded. Migration transfer validates exact expected counts, including a valid empty baseline; it does not require a synthetic nonzero Warner population.\n\nClaim2451 and original owner shared-db.orch/agent-2449 remain protected. Guarded supersession reserved20260907200221 and retained old20260906145233. Prepared11-file patch provenance SHA256e623616daed59c4779b12be54fd10dfbe60d9d818068a8f98e88daeba4d45b68 is retained; final integration uses current mainb48f526f87369278e0b173ded6a2d97e729818d6. Immutable recovery contract refs/db-contracts/2449/3 records that inherited preparation preceded this prospective integration authority.\n\nVerification:229 Python tests; hash-bound sidecar inventory validation; static SQL guards (live-ledger GuardB2 not configured); disposable PostgreSQL17 focused SQL contracts including approval concurrency and4,000-group response regression. Empty and3-state populated migration rehearsals preserve exact archive row/audit hashes. Archive mutations refuse. Catalog contract positive repaired result1 and unchanged-baseline negative result0 demonstrate sensitivity. No shared database was written during author testing.\n\nPending: fresh exact-head CI, independently allocated review, governed preview/live API acceptance, guarded merge and production catalog/ledger/permission/behavior verification. Archive-protection functions remain in use and must not be treated as orphaned by a successor cleanup. This PR does not auto-close remaining application outcomes. No preview, production application or merge is claimed.\n\n\nCI privacy-test repair: the shared ledger deliberately has stricter legacy-row predicates than ordinary DCP tables. The corrected test asserts each complete predicate and actual role behavior: entitled legacy header/member reads remain, unentitled accounts and generic private rows are denied. Removing either privacy filter makes its negative control fail. Migration bytes are unchanged.\n\nThe cumulative10-file SQL scope passed. An overlapping disposable policy red-control initially deadlocked the4,000-group fixture; the two remaining files passed after serialization, and both changed permission tests passed again after negative-control rollback. Any drift re-quarantines it.\n2. A live review of merged commit `99fbefcb` returned a well-formed `VERDICT APPROVE 99fbefcb4cf3388a3d46e77a2fdddb1f06bd25a1` line above 3,137 characters of real analysis citing specific file lines.\n3. The empty-report mode is now caught rather than trusted: ai-devops `bin/ai-review-lifecycle` converts any APPROVE or REJECT whose report carries no substantive analysis into `BLOCKED` (`empty-report`), for every provider (popcre/ai-devops#285).\n\n**Rotation safety:** the name is APPENDED, so no existing slot moves and no in-flight sequence is reassigned out of order. {"body":"Closes nothing automatically; delivers issue #2403 under protected claim #2418.\n\n## Outcome\n\nCreates only schema `hts_rag_split` and nine empty, internally linked HTS RAG tables for the DesignFlow consolidated non-production Supabase target reached by `DB_*_SANDBOX` in GCP project `lithe-breaker-323913`.\n\nNo rows are copied. There is no `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` or `INSERT ... SELECT`. The migration’s verification fails if any split table contains a row.\n\n`public.hts_rag_*` is preserved. Executable SQL performs no alter, rename, drop, or row write there; it only uses read-only existence probes. Explicit DDL preserves all seven internal foreign keys that `LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL` would omit.\n\nThe nine split tables are closed to the Data API: RLS is enabled, browser grants are revoked, and `service_role` is granted access. The application uses PostgreSQL ownership on the named non-production target.\n\n## Governed version supersession\n\nOriginal reserved version `20260906040010` remains permanently protected. The claim manager reserved `20260908022407`, renamed only the migration filename, updated claim #2418, and published durable supersession ref `48b591b18702a30d42a2bf25be1f9f785a4e3a4f`. Both paths resolve to identical Git blob `3f2e7f44a6dfb30fc879449c684f260863c5fc10`; SQL bytes and semantics did not change.\n\n## Current evidence\n\nCurrent main `8d64a75812beec85d2f8b2c78669e5e17635359d` was merged normally. Implementation head is `1c928a09d55110228d3031cf9e6851b3a2fd648f`; exact evidence head is `c6805e243d3865e03084f0ece4a1c135c1fbb34f`. Immutable contract: `refs/db-contracts/2403/2` (`33ad74ce785d834ff06caf2afdbb6c3bf67527a7`).\n\nStatic SQL, sidecar, whitespace, contract, and Git-evidence checks passed. PostgreSQL 17 applied the migration and its catalog assertions on a disposable server: all nine split tables were empty afterward, while one positive-control row in each public table remained unchanged. Live-ledger Guard B2 did not run without configured credentials and is not clearance.\n\nThe DesignFlow owner task acknowledged the exact shared-db deployment route and target in issue comment `5577130097`; it will not deploy the database itself.\n\n## Still pending\n\nAutomatic exact-head CI, independent exact-head review, governed exact-target apply with immediate target proof, direct empty-schema/catalog/public-preservation verification, guarded merge, and production acceptance for this separately governed non-production target. No reviewer/provider call, database write, merge, claim release, issue closure, or inherited cleanup occurred during preparation.\n","createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:09:11Z","files":[{"path":".agent/completion.json","additions":73,"deletions":24,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":".agent/contract.json","additions":65,"deletions":35,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260909121403_hts_rag_split_isolated_schema.sql","additions":634,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"e5252b5b11e0cded4212129b78fda1f1d9dd869d","mergedAt":"2026-09-09T16:41:29Z","number":2425,"title":"Create empty isolated hts_rag_split schema (issue #2403)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2425"},
{"body":"Closes #2408. Author lane claim #2412, reserved migration version `20260906035323`. Umbrella #2209; guard shape follows #2213 and #2214.\n\n## Why\n\n`rebuild_style_groups_batch` had two defects.\n\nThe cheap one: it rewrote `style_group_id` on every asset in the batch on every run, whether or not the value changed, and upserted every style group unconditionally. That is write amplification through indexes and triggers on the whole table, nightly.\n\nThe one that matters: **there is no ungroup arm.** An asset whose folder is renamed so it no longer matches the SKU pattern keeps its old `style_group_id` forever. The DAM resolves licensor, property and customer through the style group, so that asset shows under the **wrong licensor**, indefinitely, with no error surfaced anywhere. `clear_style_group_batch` is on no cron schedule, so nothing else cleans it up. This is an attribution defect, not a performance one.\n\n## What changed\n\nOne migration, function body only. **No table is altered.**\n\n1. `assigned` gains `AND a.style_group_id IS DISTINCT FROM bg.id` — `IS DISTINCT FROM`, not `<>`, so a NULL-to-value transition still writes.\n2. New `ungrouped_assets` CTE sets `style_group_id = NULL` for batch rows whose folder yields no SKU, guarded by `AND a.style_group_id IS NOT NULL`. Its count is returned as a new output column `assets_ungrouped`.\n3. The `ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE` gains a `WHERE`, one `IS DISTINCT FROM` clause per `SET` column, matching the `COALESCE` semantics of each assignment exactly.\n\n### The interaction the issue warned about\n\n`ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... WHERE` suppresses the `RETURNING` row, not merely the write. So once change 3 lands, an implementation that keeps `assigned` joined to `upserted_groups` silently stops assigning any group whose upsert was a no-op — which, after this change, is nearly all of them. That would convert a performance fix into a much worse version of the very attribution bug this issue exists to close.\n\nA `batch_groups` CTE fixes it by `UNION`-ing the upsert's `RETURNING` with a direct read of `style_groups` joined on the batch's SKUs. Neither arm alone suffices: the snapshot read cannot see this statement's own inserts, and the `RETURNING` cannot see suppressed conflicts. `style_groups.sku` is unique, so a row present in both arms carries an identical `(id, sku)` pair and the `UNION` is exact.\n\n### Two data-modifying CTEs on the same table\n\n`assigned` draws from `grouped_assets` (`sku IS NOT NULL`) and `ungrouped_assets` from `ungroupable_assets` (`sku IS NULL`), over the same `asset_skus` rows. The row sets are provably disjoint, so PostgreSQL's unpredictable-results caveat for two modifications of one row cannot apply.\n\n### Return-value semantics\n\n`groups_created` and `assets_assigned` now mean \"rows actually written\" rather than \"rows examined\". The only caller in the fleet is `popdam3` `apps/worker/src/handlers/style-groups.ts`, which drives its loop purely on `done` and `next_cursor` and uses the counts only for a progress report. No caller could have been using `assets_assigned = 0` as a stop condition either: 37,593 of 135,251 live assets are already ungrouped, so zero-assignment batches occur today.\n\n## Verification\n\n- Production base proof: `pg_get_functiondef` for `public.rebuild_style_groups_batch` on the production project is byte-identical to the in-repo definition in `20260708150000_dam_strict_style_group_sku_regex.sql`, read through the approved read-only path. **The `sync_asset_effective_tags` repo-vs-production drift noted in #2408 does not touch this function**, and that drift already has a landed migration (`20260905143005`). No stop was warranted.\n- Grants restated to match the production ACL exactly: `authenticated`, `service_role`, `postgres`. `anon` deliberately not granted, and the contracts test asserts it did not gain EXECUTE.\n- `scripts/check-sql.sh` passes.\n- `supabase/tests/style_group_rebuild_guard_and_ungroup_contracts.sql` pins the signature, output column names, `SECURITY DEFINER`, `proconfig`, and grants; then runs a behavioural fixture that asserts: a converged batch writes 0/0/0; an already-correct asset's `ctid` does not move; an asset that no longer matches the SKU pattern **is** ungrouped; and — the central one — a run in which both upserts are suppressed (`groups_created = 0`) still assigns the asset. A control step proves a real update *does* move the `ctid`, so the no-rewrite assertions are not vacuous.\n\n## Not verified yet, and why\n\n**The behavioural half has not been executed.** `supabase link` to the shared preview project `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel` fails with `Resource has been removed`; the PAT is fine (`supabase projects list` works and shows six projects) but that project reference is not among them. Docker is not installed on this machine, so there is no local disposable Postgres either — and a local fixture would in any case miss the production triggers this test depends on. The contracts test is written and committed but needs a working preview to run.\n\n## Out of scope, deliberately\n\nRetiring `clear_style_group_batch` from scheduled paths, making the nightly run incremental, the generated SKU column, and the statement-level rewrite of `sync_asset_effective_tags` — all explicitly ruled out by the issue.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-06T04:07:29Z","files":[{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260906035323_style_group_rebuild_guard_and_ungroup.sql","additions":361,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/style_group_rebuild_guard_and_ungroup_contracts.sql","additions":337,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"b16c73a50892fc26bb07ddda1185ef7cb41314cd","mergedAt":"2026-09-06T13:26:24Z","number":2423,"title":"fix(#2408): guard the style-group assignment write and add the missing ungroup arm","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2423"},
{"body":"Closes #2355. Author lane claim #2410, reserved migration version `20260906034550`.\n\n## What this is for, in business terms\n\nThe same character is called different things by different licensors and portals.\nToday those are just unrelated strings, so a royalty or approval decision can rest on\na name coincidence. This change lets POP Creations hold every alternative name as an\nalias of one canonical character, and record which source said what.\n\nThe second half is provenance. Licensor source ids collide — Disney and Sega both\nnumber from small integers — so a bare source id is not an identity. This makes the\ndatabase refuse to record provenance without the licensor it belongs to.\n\n## What it does\n\n**`core.character_alias` (new).** An observed name resolving to a canonical\n`core.character`, with the source that used it. Uniqueness is scoped to the licensor:\nthe same name under two licensors is legitimate, while one normalized name resolving\nto two characters inside one licensor is refused. A guard trigger requires the alias's\n`licensor_id` to equal the parent character's, so a cross-licensor alias is\nunrepresentable. Normalization reuses `core.normalize_popsg_property_observation`\n(contract `popsg-property-observation-v1`), exactly as `core.franchise_alias` and\n`core.property_alias` do — no second, divergent normalizer.\n\n`core.franchise_alias` binds the equivalent field with a composite foreign key. That is\nnot available here: it would need a new unique index **on `core.character`**, which\n#2355 reads but does not own. A trigger is the strongest form available inside the\nclaim, and the difference is called out in the migration header.\n\n**`core.taxonomy_source_ref` (extended).**\n- `source_licensor_id` — derived from the entity the row points at, never trusted from\n  the caller, and refused when a caller supplies a contradicting value.\n- Kind-safe target integrity — `entity_id` is an untyped uuid, so nothing stopped it\n  naming a row of a different kind or no row at all. Now `entity_schema.entity_table`\n  must be a real table and `entity_id` must be a real row in it.\n- `first_seen_at`, `last_seen_at`, `missing_since`, and a generated `is_current`.\n  Absence is recorded, never deleted: a vanished source row is evidence.\n\n**The collision, closed.** Every importer in this repository upserts through\n`on conflict (source_system, source_table, source_id) do update set entity_id =\nexcluded.entity_id`, and that key is global. Two licensors reusing one small integer\nwould silently overwrite each other and the survivor would attribute one licensor's\ncharacter to the other. The existing unique constraint is deliberately **left intact** —\na dozen already-applied importer functions use it as their on-conflict target, and\nre-keying the table would break every one of them at runtime. Instead the guard refuses\nthe dangerous write: once a row's licensor is known, repointing it to another licensor\nraises. A silent misattribution becomes a loud failure, with no importer signature\nchanged.\n\n## Preservation\n\nAdditive. No rows seeded (#2355 authorizes structure only, and no licensed evidence).\nNo `UPDATE` is issued against `core.taxonomy_source_ref` — it already carries ColdLion\ncircuit-breaker triggers on insert, update and delete, and a backfill would be refused\nwhenever that breaker is tripped. The freshness presence rules are therefore declared\n`NOT VALID`, binding every new and modified row while leaving pre-existing rows exactly\nas they are. They must never be validated.\n\nNothing in `core.character`, `core.property`, `core.licensor` or `core.franchise` is\naltered, and the two pre-existing ColdLion breaker triggers are asserted still present.\n\n## Proof\n\n`supabase/tests/character_alias_and_source_provenance_contracts.sql` runs against the\nephemeral database in **Database Contract Tests** and asserts behaviour, not that a\nmigration applied:\n\n- objects confirmed via `to_regclass`, `pg_trigger`, `pg_constraint`,\n  `information_schema` — never the ledger row;\n- the pre-existing `UNIQUE (source_system, source_table, source_id)` still exists;\n- both ColdLion breaker triggers still exist;\n- one normalized name may not resolve to two characters inside one licensor;\n- the same name under two licensors is allowed;\n- an alias cannot be created on, or moved to, the wrong licensor;\n- a character with live aliases cannot be deleted;\n- **the collision**: two licensors both using source id `5` are refused when the\n  importer upsert pattern tries to merge them, and licensor A's row is proven untouched\n  afterwards;\n- provenance with a blank source id, a non-existent row, a non-existent kind, or a uuid\n  from a different kind is refused;\n- `missing_since` flips `is_current`, and `first_seen_at` cannot be moved forward;\n- pre-existing rows survive and the grandfathering constraints remain `NOT VALID`.\n\n`scripts/check-sql.sh` passes locally. This machine has no Docker or WSL, so no local\ndisposable database was available; the ephemeral-database run in CI is the behavioural\nevidence. No preview push has been made — that is not authorized yet.\n\n## Owner decisions deliberately NOT made\n\nWhich name is canonical and which alias is authoritative are business judgements. This\nchange only makes it possible to hold them and to tell the sources apart.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-06T03:56:21Z","files":[{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260906222338_core_character_alias_and_source_provenance.sql","additions":688,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/character_alias_and_source_provenance_contracts.sql","additions":912,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"2b95cd2b5be98037815b021f83f7400626da9f7b","mergedAt":"2026-09-07T02:55:08Z","number":2415,"title":"feat(#2355): character aliases and collision-proof source provenance","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2415"},
{"body":"Documentation only. One section added to `docs/business-rules/licensing-master-data.md`. No migration, no schema change, no code.\n\n## The ruling\n\nAlbert, 2026-09-05: \"If they appear in the OPA submissions system we have rights, regardless of the contract and we'll go by the submissions system.\"\n\n## Why it was needed\n\nThe K2557 crosswalk only ever created rows in `plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution` for contract-named Properties. 180 captured DCP Vault identities had **no row at all**. Because the authority gate requires an approved row, they presented as \"DCP Creative - unresolved authority\" permanently — and because the review queue lists only identities that already carry a *pending* row, they could never be reviewed either. Cinderella was the owner-reported example: matched to OPA Properties 115 and 959 by name, named by no clause.\n\n## Scope boundary this deliberately preserves\n\nThis is an **entitlement** ruling. The 2026-08-31 ruling that the signed contract is the controlling authority for the **Disney-versus-Marvel split** is untouched and explicitly restated as still binding — OPA branch membership still cannot distinguish Marvel from Disney.\n\n## Ledger consequence\n\nA null `contract_asserted_studio_code` now means \"authority is the submissions system\", not \"authority is missing\". 96 of the 180 resolved to exactly one OPA Property and were recorded as approved version-1 rows on that basis on 2026-09-05 (production ledger then 204 approved / 5 pending). The remaining 84 have no OPA Property, are not covered by this ruling, and stay an open question.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-06T03:53:20Z","files":[{"path":"docs/business-rules/licensing-master-data.md","additions":11,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"1c3c4c0668b4d5659c9617b8a4a19c982fcc56a2","mergedAt":"2026-09-06T12:31:41Z","number":2411,"title":"Record that OPA submissions presence is authority for entitlement","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2411"},
{"body":"Implements #2334 (structural successor to #1090). Claim issue #2405, reserved version `20260906033021`. Additive only; **no rows are seeded**.\n\n## What it adds\n\n**Five missing canonical bridges** — `core.property_style_guide`, `core.property_franchise`, `dam.asset_property`, `dam.asset_style_guide`, `dam.asset_franchise`.\n\n**Eight per-source support-edge tables**, one for every canonical licensing relationship, including the three whose bridges already existed.\n\nPlus `core.relationship_evidence_kind` and two guard functions.\n\n## Audit of `core.property_character_associations` (required by #2334)\n\nIt **is** the canonical application-facing Property/Character bridge, and it is correctly shaped:\n\n- endpoints are uuid `property_id` / `character_id`, PK `(property_id, character_id)`, no `licensor_id`;\n- **both FKs are already `ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT`**, so endpoint deletion already fails closed there;\n- it is read by exactly one live endpoint, `api.db_data_admin_licensor_property_tree`, purely as a per-property character count;\n- three contract-test assertions pin its shape, its emptiness, and its lack of INSERT privilege, and a fourth pins the api function to reference it literally.\n\n**Conclusion: no change to it is warranted or safe, and this PR makes none.** Its one real gap — it records no source and no evidence strength — is closed additively by `core.property_character_source_edge`, leaving the endpoint contract untouched.\n\n## Direct vs inferred vs co-occurrence\n\n`evidence_kind` is one of `direct_source_assertion` / `inferred` / `co_occurrence`. `is_direct_source_relationship` is a **generated** column — not a default, not caller-supplied — so an inferred row cannot relabel itself as direct. This strengthens the CHECK-pinned discipline of `plm.pmt_property_franchise_evidence` from \"cannot be overridden by an INSERT\" to \"cannot be written at all\".\n\n`core.require_direct_support_for_canonical_edge()` refuses any canonical edge without a **current** direct source assertion for that exact pair, so a table full of co-occurrence supports nothing.\n\n`licensor_id` is NOT NULL and part of the identity key, because integer source ids collide across licensors — a bare source-id join misattributes one licensor's relationship to another, which is a royalty error.\n\n## Fail-closed endpoint deletion\n\n- The five new bridges use `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, matching `core.property_character_associations`.\n- The three pre-existing bridges (`core.property_character_associations`, `core.style_guide_character`, `dam.asset_character`) use `ON DELETE CASCADE` and are **deliberately left unaltered** — rule 3, additive by default. `core.refuse_delete_of_current_support_edge()` aborts the cascade while current support remains, so endpoint deletion fails closed there too without changing a live table.\n- Superseded support (`is_current = false`) does **not** block, which is what #2334 asks for.\n\n## Proof\n\n`supabase/tests/canonical_licensing_relationship_bridges.sql` asserts behaviour against real rows on the Database Contract Tests ephemeral database: that an unsupported edge is refused; that inferred and co-occurrence evidence (at any volume/confidence) are refused; that a direct assertion is accepted; that direct support for another pair does not sustain this one; that the generated flag cannot be written; that current support cannot be deleted directly **or by cascade from a deleted endpoint**; and that superseded support can.\n\nLocal execution was not possible — this machine has no Postgres, no Docker and no WSL distro — so behavioural proof runs in CI's throwaway database, which is what that workflow exists for.\n\n## Not done here\n\nNo preview push, no merge, no production. Awaiting the orchestrator.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-06T03:43:49Z","files":[{"path":"scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260907030418.json","additions":27,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260907030418_canonical_licensing_relationship_bridges.sql","additions":1826,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/canonical_licensing_relationship_bridges.sql","additions":1050,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"03686677b0bc605f5522a1bddb7cde9d311a6bdd","mergedAt":"2026-09-07T05:15:54Z","number":2409,"title":"feat(#2334): canonical licensing relationship bridges and per-source support edges","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2409"},
