Adds the closeout handoff for orchestrator marker #2330.\n\nThe priority set is complete through to production: #2174/#2398, #2214/#2397 and #2213/#2399 were authored, independently reviewed, merged, rehearsed on preview from merged `main`, and applied to production.\n\nCloses #2400 bookkeeping context; outstanding items are tracked in #2401 and the owner-decision issues #2317, #2178, #2284, #2389, #2290.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-06T00:31:51Z","files":[{"path":"HANDOFF.d/2026-09-06T0030Z-edge-dev-claude-orchestrator-2330-closeout.md","additions":209,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"7fddf11462ab7e59d68e529f5f9a0d9303fb8670","mergedAt":"2026-09-06T00:38:19Z","number":2402,"title":"docs: orchestrator #2330 closeout handoff (#2400)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2402"},
{"body":"Implements issue #2213 (parent plan #2209). Claim: #2396. Reserved migration version `20260905143005`.\n\n## Why — the measured evidence\n\nFrom the #2209 Steps 1 & 3 read-only production evidence recorded on #2213 (https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/2213#issuecomment-5546883751), over a 7.556-day window:\n\n- `public.asset_effective_tags` took **6,762,623 deletes and 6,762,623 inserts** after its one-off backfill, and `n_live_tup` never moved off the backfill's own 2,045,705 rows. **Net change from 13,525,246 row versions: zero.**\n- All of it fires from one PostgREST statement shape, `UPDATE \"public\".\"assets\" SET \"style_group_id\" = ...`, **710,514 calls** — the only observed shape naming a column the `assets` trigger watches. 9.52 projection rows rewritten per firing.\n- The churn is **provably 100% no-op**: the `assets` branch re-derives from `public.asset_tags` (zero writes in the window) and `public.style_group_tags` (empty), so the re-derived set is identical to the set just deleted, whether or not `style_group_id` changed value.\n- Catalogue consequence: **261,433 dead tuples, 11.33%** of the table, 16 autovacuum cycles, on a projection whose content has not changed since backfill.\n- The reported 181-second population is the **one-off migration backfill** (`pg_stat_statements calls = 1`), not a recurring job.\n\n## What changed\n\nOne thing moves. The `assets` branch of `public.sync_asset_effective_tags()` stops being an unconditional delete-all-then-reinsert and becomes an **unchanged-set comparison**: delete only rows no longer derived, insert only rows newly derived. An unchanged input set now writes nothing at all.\n\nDeliberately **not** implemented, each ruled out on the same measurement: a supporting index (the delete already runs as an index scan on the `asset_id`-leading unique index — `idx_tup_fetch` 6,762,627 vs `n_tup_del` 6,762,623), statement-level transition handling, a durable changed-ID path, and staging/swap.\n\nPreserved exactly: signature, return type, volatility, `SECURITY DEFINER`, `search_path`, the F2 advisory-lock protocol from the #1664 review, all grants, and the `asset_tags` / `style_group_tags` branches (transcribed byte for byte from the live baseline `20260830110517_popdam_effective_asset_filters.sql`, which the evidence confirms is byte-identical to `pg_get_functiondef` in production). The three triggers are **not** redefined — they are outside this change's claimed objects and keep pointing at the function by name.\n\nTwo behaviours the old delete-all covered incidentally are kept explicitly: a `DELETE` or a soft delete still clears the asset's rows outright, and an `UPDATE` that moves the primary key still clears the old id's rows.\n\n## What the contract test proves\n\n`supabase/tests/effective_tag_sync_set_comparison_contracts.sql`. It **genuinely fails against the previous body** — the old body rewrote every row on every firing, so it fails Case A on all three assertions.\n\n- **Case A (unchanged set).** Fires the exact production statement shape and asserts **zero inserts, zero deletes** (`pg_stat_get_xact_tuples_inserted/deleted`) **and unchanged `ctid` identity** — no stored row version is even rewritten. Repeats it for duplicate delivery. It refuses to run if `track_counts` is off, so \"no writes\" can never be confused with \"no counting\".\n- **Case B.** The full set is still exactly correct after the no-op firings.\n- **Case C (changed set, including removal).** Reassignment to another style group asserts write volume is **exactly the difference** (1 insert, 2 deletes), that unchanged asset-scope rows keep their `ctid`, that the final set is exactly right, and explicitly that the previous group's tags are **gone**.\n- **Case D.** Ungrouping removes every style-group row and keeps the asset rows.\n- **Case E.** Soft delete clears the projection; restore rebuilds it exactly.\n- **Case F.** The untouched `asset_tags` and `style_group_tags` branches still add and remove exactly their own rows.\n- Plus catalogue guards: the function keeps its volatile `SECURITY DEFINER` posture, and all three triggers are still present and enabled — otherwise every \"zero writes\" assertion would pass for the wrong reason.\n\n## Verification status\n\n- `bash scripts/check-sql.sh` — passes (Guard B green; Guard B2 warns only because no ledger URL is configured locally; expected-count, verify-cost and EOL guards all green).\n- No local Postgres or Docker is available in this worktree, so the contract test is executed by the **Database Contract Tests** workflow against a from-empty ephemeral database with every migration applied. Its result is the execution proof.\n- **No preview or production apply, no merge, no promotion** is performed or authorized here.\n\n## Rollback\n\nA new forward migration restoring the function body verbatim from `supabase/migrations/20260830110517_popdam_effective_asset_filters.sql`. No index, trigger, table, policy or grant is added, altered or removed, so nothing else has to be restored.\n\nCloses #2213 on merge and promotion authorization.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-05T14:35:24Z","files":[{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260905143005_effective_tag_sync_set_comparison.sql","additions":227,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/effective_tag_sync_set_comparison_contracts.sql","additions":305,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"9dc6009a85c483d3dcd734c4f4992aec74c43b5e","mergedAt":"2026-09-05T16:12:39Z","number":2399,"title":"perf(db): effective-tag sync compares sets instead of delete-all-reinsert (#2213)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2399"},
{"body":"Closes #2174 (ColdLion landing unit 4). Claim #2394; reserved version `20260905142150`.\n\n## What changed\n\n`supabase/migrations/20260905142150_coldlion_prod_history_stage_agreement_and_retention.sql`\nrebuilds the three claimed landing tables — `coldlion.prod_history_line`,\n`coldlion.prod_history_component`, `coldlion.prod_history_last_lookup` — which the\n2026-09-02 census found empty. The migration refuses to run if any of them has been\npopulated in the meantime, so no evidence can be destroyed.\n\n**The stage is asserted, not stamped.** A stage-less `/prodHistory` request answers\nwith ISS rows only, no error and a plausible total, while INTRAN and REC rows exist\n(objection U13, re-confirmed live 2026-09-02 with a positive control). ColdLion began\nreturning `stageCode` on 2026-08-26, so the requested stage and the returned stage are\nboth stored and a mismatch aborts the row. Every window is fetched once per stage and\neach request is paged to completion through the ledger from #2173, which this migration\nrequires as a hard precondition.\n\n**A purchase line is one row.** `prodLineSeq` is part of the line identity, so the\n1,500-pack and 3,000-pack lines on one order stay two purchases. Parent totals live on\nthe parent and are never summed from components; `linePrice` is per component and lives\nthere.\n\n**Component quantities are evidence, not a flag.** A line may only claim its component\nquantities are proven when components exist, all carry a quantity, and they sum to the\nparent total — and that evidence is then immutable while the claim stands.\n\n**`lastProdCost` is structurally separated from this order's cost.** Of 98 duplicate\nkeys across two March-2021 windows, 98 differed only in the `last*` fields. Those seven\nfields now have their own table; no order-cost column name may exist on it (checked at\napply time); at most one copy per line may be marked selected, enforced by a partial\nunique index; and a selection with no recorded rule is refused. The 3.00/3.60 fan-out\nsurvives as two visible rows and is never aggregated.\n\n**Retention is a restartable maintenance operation.** A `before delete` guard keeps the\nnewest three versions per company/order/line/stage partition, allows only the oldest to\nbe pruned, one delete at a time, and refuses entirely when the ordering is not total or\nthe partition is flagged ambiguous — which is why a single backfill baseline is never\npruned.\n\n`salesOrderNo = 0` is surfaced as \"no link\" rather than a key, the `1900-01-01`\nempty-date marker is refused on every date column, and EP001 is refused. Closed landing\nposture throughout: RLS on, no application grants, no `raw` column, no FK to\n`item_header` (discontinued items are legitimately absent) and none into `core`.\n\n## What the contract test proves\n\n`supabase/tests/coldlion_prod_history_contracts.sql` fails if any of these is untrue:\na returned stage differing from the requested one is accepted; a fourth stage exists;\na component or lookup can be an orphan, or a parent FK does not cascade; two\n`prodLineSeq` values collapse into one row; a mismatched component sum is accepted, or\na matching one is refused, or asserted evidence can be rewritten; an order-cost column\nappears on the lookup table, or two copies can be selected, or one can be selected with\nno rule; `salesOrderNo = 0` reads as a link; `1900-01-01` or EP001 is stored; retention\nprunes the newest row, prunes below three, prunes a lone version, or prunes a partition\nflagged ambiguous; RLS is off or an application role holds a grant.\n\n`bash scripts/check-sql.sh` passes. No database was touched: nothing has been applied to\npreview or production.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-05T14:33:17Z","files":[{"path":"scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260905142150.json","additions":21,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260905142150_coldlion_prod_history_stage_agreement_and_retention.sql","additions":685,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/coldlion_prod_history_contracts.sql","additions":619,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/coldlion_raw_landing_phases_2_6_contracts.sql","additions":27,"deletions":14,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"616176e758dc88fd9aa3511fd5f6129dd574f26a","mergedAt":"2026-09-05T15:29:28Z","number":2398,"title":"feat(coldlion): production history with three-stage agreement and retention (#2174)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2398"},
{"body":"Closes part of #2214 (this PR implements the one function the evidence supports). Claim #2395, reserved version `20260905142725`. Parent plan #2209.\n\n## Evidence this is built on\n\nEntry-gate evidence comment on #2214 — https://github.com/u2giants/shared-db/issues/2214#issuecomment-5546883907 supersedes nothing; the decisive read is the 2026-09-05 read-only production measurement posted on that issue, taken as `supabase_read_only_user` against project ref `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\n\n- **10,864 of 10,868 style groups (99.96 %) already hold exactly the value `refresh_style_group_counts_batch` is about to write.** Zero groups have a wrong `asset_count`; four have a stale `latest_file_date`.\n- The nightly reconcile (`cron.job` 6, `45 3 * * *`) averaged **94,933 ms** per call — against this function's own **30 s** `statement_timeout`.\n- `public.style_groups` took **1,409,071 updates against 10,868 live rows** in a 7.5-day window (~130 updates per live row per week). `trg_dam_search_style_groups_refresh` keys on `updated_at` and `asset_count`, so every no-op write rebuilds that group's `dam_search_documents` row (3,521,227 updates, 732 MB).\n- **Removing `updated_at = now()` from the body would achieve nothing.** `style_groups` carries an unconditional `BEFORE UPDATE FOR EACH ROW` trigger (`update_style_groups_updated_at` → `update_updated_at_column()`, body `NEW.updated_at = now()`). The only change that removes the amplification is not issuing the `UPDATE` for unchanged rows, and no caller-side scheduling can substitute for it.\n\n## What changes\n\nOne added `WHERE` predicate on the `UPDATE` inside `public.refresh_style_group_counts_batch(uuid[])`. The `agg` CTE, the whole `SET` list, the `CASE` expressions that clear the primary-asset fields on an emptied group, and `updated_at = now()` are preserved verbatim.\n\nThe predicate is `IS DISTINCT FROM` (not `<>`) over every column the `SET` list can actually change: `asset_count`, `latest_file_date`, and the four `primary_*` columns in the `agg.asset_count = 0` branch only — the branch in which the `SET` list can change them. `<>` would return NULL for a NULL-to-value transition and silently stop correcting a stale row.\n\n**Preserved exactly:** signature including the argument name `p_group_ids`, `RETURNS integer`, `LANGUAGE sql`, `SECURITY DEFINER`, `search_path=public`, `statement_timeout=30s`, `lock_timeout=0`, and `EXECUTE` to `authenticated`, `service_role`, `postgres`. The return value still means \"rows written\"; it simply falls because fewer rows are written, and the evidence confirms no caller reads it.\n\n## Deliberately NOT changed\n\n- **No new index.** The read half is already index-driven; the evidence justifies none and none is added.\n- **`clear_style_group_batch` and `rebuild_style_groups_batch` are untouched.** Their write-side plans are recorded as NOT MEASURED (read-only identity is refused `EXPLAIN` on writes, SQLSTATE 42501), and the evidence states no database-side change to them can be justified. Claim #2395 covers only the counts function.\n- The 710,328 single-row PostgREST `style_group_id` updates are a **popdam3** N+1 and are out of scope here.\n\n## Contract test\n\n`supabase/tests/style_group_counts_change_predicate_contracts.sql` — it would fail against the pre-#2214 body:\n\n- Re-running the function over three already-correct rows must write **0** rows, proved twice over: the return value, and every row's `ctid` being byte-identical afterwards. The unconditional body returns 3 and moves all three `ctid`s. (`ctid`, not `xmin` or `updated_at` — the test runs in one transaction, where both of those are frozen.)\n- A **control** step proves `ctid` does move across a real `UPDATE`, so the no-rewrite assertions cannot pass vacuously.\n- Stale rows are still corrected: a wrong `asset_count`, a NULL `latest_file_date` (the exact case a `<>` predicate would skip), and leftover `primary_*` fields on an emptied group — each must write exactly 1 row and land the right value.\n- Catalog posture and all three `EXECUTE` grants are pinned.\n\n## Rollback\n\nA new forward migration restoring the baseline body — this file minus the added `WHERE` predicate. No index or grant is touched.\n\n## Checks\n\n`bash scripts/check-sql.sh` passes locally. **No preview or production apply, no promotion and no merge is authorized for this session** — it stops here with checks running.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-05T14:32:36Z","files":[{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260905142725_style_group_counts_change_predicate.sql","additions":136,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/style_group_counts_change_predicate_contracts.sql","additions":237,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"b0b56847f3b835f29edd7a96df30817cb35befdf","mergedAt":"2026-09-05T15:49:00Z","number":2397,"title":"feat(dam): skip unchanged rows in refresh_style_group_counts_batch (#2214)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2397"},
{"body":"Closes #2242.\n\n`public.get_effective_filter_counts_unchecked_1703(jsonb)` has three matched arms since 20260904121037, but the durable contract test still described two and pinned Arm 1 and Arm 2 by their comments alone. A later `create or replace` could delete the tag-leading Arm 1T, keep both pinned comments, and this file would still pass while the tag facet regressed to the ~8.1s whole-table scan #2151 removed. The migration's apply-time `DO` guard covers that shape exactly once and never again.\n\n**Test-only. No migration, no schema change, no DDL.** Two blocks are appended; not one existing assertion, guard or test was changed, weakened or removed.\n\n1. A durable copy of the apply-time guard. Arm 1T's comment exists and sits between Arm 1 and Arm 2; the seven `union all`s are counted; the `select distinct e.asset_id` subquery over `public.asset_effective_tags` and its primary-key join to `public.assets` are pinned as contiguous, whitespace-folded syntax; both halves of the `tagFilter is null` / `is not null` exclusivity pair are pinned; the identity arm keeps its `EXISTS` tag predicate; Arm 1T is not routed back through `identity_asset_ids`; and the no-tag arm does not scan the tag table.\n2. A data case in which one asset carries the same tag at both `'asset'` and `'style_group'` scope. That is what makes the `DISTINCT` load-bearing, and no existing test wrote two scopes for one asset — the parity test in `popdam_effective_asset_filter_contracts.sql` writes one.\n\n## Negative control — every new assertion was proved able to fail\n\nRun on a **local throwaway PostgreSQL 18 cluster** in the session scratchpad (database `arm1t`, port 54399, created and dropped for this purpose). No shared, preview or production database was contacted. The real function body was installed from 20260904121037, mutated, and restored.\n\n| mutation to the function body | new assertion fired |\n| --- | --- |\n| Arm 1T comment renamed | `effective count helper lost its tag-leading Arm 1T` |\n| `select distinct e.asset_id` → `select e.asset_id` | `lost a pinned Arm 1T property: from ( select distinct e.asset_id …` |\n| Arm 1T's `tagFilter … is not null` guard deleted | `lost a pinned Arm 1T property: … 'tagfilter', '') is not null and a.is_deleted = false` |\n| whole Arm 1T arm deleted | `effective count helper lost its tag-leading Arm 1T` |\n| Arm 1T joined back to `identity_asset_ids` | `tag-filtered facet counts were routed back through identity candidates` |\n\nFor the data case, on the same fixture (one asset tagged at two scopes, one at one scope, one untagged):\n\n- real function: `{\"total\": 2, \"fileType\": {\"ai\": 1, \"pdf\": 1}}` — block passes;\n- `DISTINCT` removed: `{\"total\": 3, \"fileType\": {\"ai\": 2, \"pdf\": 1}}` — block fails with `tag-filtered total 3 double-counts the asset tagged at two scopes (expected 2); Arm 1T lost its DISTINCT`;\n- body restored: passes again.\n\n`bash scripts/check-sql.sh` is green.\n\nAuthor lane: u2giants/shared-db#2392 (reserved version 20260905104858 is unused — this change ships no migration).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-05T10:54:34Z","files":[{"path":"supabase/tests/popdam_effective_count_performance_contracts.sql","additions":175,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefOid":"295b52de5ca724e910dc6035c8d2377573e89fab","mergedAt":"2026-09-05T12:45:11Z","number":2393,"title":"test: pin the tag-leading Arm 1T in the durable count-performance contract (#2242)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2393"},
{"body":"Closes #2333. Author-lane claim: #2387. Reserved version: `20260905083426`.\n\n## What this does\n\nCreates the canonical Franchise entity that the 2026-09-04 current-main/production reconciliation proved absent:\n\n- **`core.franchise`** — source-scoped identity, `app.entity_status` lifecycle, RLS with a `shared_read` SELECT policy, read-only grants for `authenticated`, `all` for `service_role`, and `created_at` / `updated_at` / `created_by` / `updated_by` audit fields with the standard `app.set_updated_at()` trigger.\n- **`core.franchise_alias`** — source-neutral normalization and Licensor-safe integrity.\n\n**Additive only.** No existing table, column, view, function, trigger, policy or grant is altered. `core.licensor`, `core.property`, `core.character`, the `*_ext` tables, shared provenance tables and every Asset table are untouched. **No rows are seeded** — #2333 authorizes no curated licensing data.\n\n## Design decisions worth reviewing\n\n**Identity is source-scoped, and Licensor is part of the key.** `(licensor_id, source_system, source_id)`. Integer source ids collide across licensors — Disney and Sega both number from small integers — so a bare source-id join attributes one licensor's franchise to another, which is a royalty error. Names are descriptive, never identity.\n\n**The code key is PARTIAL, not `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`.** `core.property` uses `unique nulls not distinct (licensor_id, code)`; that shape is not copied here. Because `code` is optional, `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` permits exactly **one** code-less franchise per licensor and refuses every later one. The contract test caught this against a live PostgreSQL before it reached review. Uniqueness of a real code is preserved.\n\n**Alias uniqueness is licensor-scoped, and cross-licensor aliases are unrepresentable.** `licensor_id` is carried on the alias row and bound to the parent by a composite foreign key `(franchise_id, licensor_id)` → `core.franchise (id, licensor_id)`. The same observed string under two licensors is legitimate; the same string resolving to two franchises of one licensor is refused at write time. `ON DELETE RESTRICT` on both licensor and franchise edges — no silent alias loss.\n\n**Normalization reuses the one frozen normalizer.** `core.normalize_popsg_property_observation` (contract `popsg-property-observation-v1`), rather than adding a second, divergent one. No change to that function.\n\n**Compatibility with source-specific Franchise evidence.** `plm.pmt_franchise` remains the raw Paramount landing record, capture-scoped and unchanged. The contract test asserts every distinct name there is representable in `core.franchise`, and that a bigint source key round-trips through the text `source_id`. Because that table is empty on an ephemeral database, the test falls back to the shape a real Paramount row has, so it cannot pass by having nothing to check.\n\n## Verification\n\nApplied against a disposable local PostgreSQL 18.6 cluster with the prerequisite objects present (`app.entity_status`, `app.set_updated_at`, `app.has_any_role`, `core.licensor`, `core.normalize_popsg_property_observation`, `plm.pmt_franchise`); the migration applied clean and `supabase/tests/core_franchise_canonical_entity_contracts.sql` printed `CONTRACT OK`.\n\n**Negative control:** replacing the composite `(franchise_id, licensor_id)` foreign key with a plain `franchise_id` reference made the test fail with `CONTRACT: core.franchise_alias accepted an alias whose licensor disagrees with its parent franchise.` The test can fail, and it fails on the guarantee it claims to hold.\n\n`scripts/check-sql.sh` — `Static checks passed.` Guard B: no migration sorts before the base branch's newest version `20260905063701`. Guard B2 did not run (no ledger source configured locally); CI runs it.\n\nA local fixture is not a production apply: it does not exercise the shared project's triggers, event triggers or role set. Preview rehearsal remains the real proof.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-05T08:39:49Z","files":[{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260905083426_core_franchise_canonical_entity.sql","additions":236,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/core_franchise_canonical_entity_contracts.sql","additions":307,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"85b7b0abbf17f5d9626de059102e2e1f7a26b97c","mergedAt":"2026-09-05T10:28:58Z","number":2388,"title":"feat(core): canonical Franchise entity and alias contract (#2333)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2388"},
{"body":"Closes #2204. Database package 3 of 3 for `popcre/designflow-backend#81`.\n\n## The two gaps this closes\n\n#2202 (migration `20260904143518`) already added `workflow_action_id`, `idempotency_key`, the FK to `dflow.item_workflow_action`, and the per-recipient / per-key unique indexes to `app.user_notification`. Live read-only production inspection on 2026-09-05 (`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`) confirms those are applied and that exactly two gaps remain:\n\n1. **`created_date` is `date`.** Two notifications created on the same day cannot be ordered against each other, so the frontend's newest-first list is arbitrary within a day.\n2. **The partial unread index is on the wrong table.** `20260827132637` indexed the legacy `dflow.user_notification`; the backend maps notification reads to `app.user_notification`, so the canonical unread list/count path is unindexed.\n\n## What the migration does\n\n- Adds `created_at timestamptz not null default now()`.\n- Backfills legacy rows to **UTC midnight of their own `created_date`**. That preserves the day each row records and deliberately refuses to invent a within-day order the source never held — same-day legacy rows tie, and the index's `id` tie-breaker resolves them deterministically. Production had 105,241 rows, 0 null dates, spanning 2022-03-29 to 2026-07-10; the `coalesce` to epoch is a deterministic floor so `SET NOT NULL` can never fail on an undated row, and can never make one look recent.\n- Adds `user_notification_unread_user_created_idx` on `(user_id_fk, created_at desc, id desc) where unread = true`.\n\n**Additive only.** `created_date` is not altered, retyped or dropped, so every existing reader, view and function keeps working, and all task/mention/legacy rows and their read state are preserved. No function body is changed — new rows pick up the timestamp from the column default, so there is no `CREATE OR REPLACE` conflict with #2202/#2203 and no new function overload.\n\n**No content duplicated.** `workflow_action_id` -> `dflow.item_workflow_action.rfq_item_id` already resolves the immutable RFQ item identity the deep link needs; a test asserts it. No price, customer-private text or note is copied into a notification row.\n\n## Tests\n\n`supabase/tests/canonical_notification_timestamp_and_unread_index_contracts.sql` — index definition and partial predicate; unread count and bounded newest-first list planning through the index with no sort; timestamptz precision and same-day ordering; same-instant `id` tie-breaking; mixed legacy/workflow rows keeping their dates, read state and relative order; per-recipient and idempotency-key uniqueness including the NULL-key partial case; FK integrity; RFQ deep-link resolution; and that `created_date` is still a `date`.\n\n## Checks\n\n`scripts/check-sql.sh` static checks passed (Guard B: no migration sorts before the base branch's newest version `20260905053422`).\n\nClaim: #2385 · Version: `20260905072856`\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-05T07:32:19Z","files":[{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260905072856_canonical_notification_timestamp_and_unread_index.sql","additions":76,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/canonical_notification_timestamp_and_unread_index_contracts.sql","additions":338,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"9c392bbbac56964a50ff1b63cd4c64fa51a93274","mergedAt":"2026-09-05T08:49:08Z","number":2386,"title":"feat(2204): canonical notification timestamp and unread index on app.user_notification","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2386"},
{"body":"Closes #2331. Author lane claim: #2383. Reserved version: `20260905063701`.\n\n## What changes\n\n`supabase/migrations/20260905063701_style_tracker_rows_realtime_publication.sql` adds **only** `public.style_tracker_rows` to the **existing** `supabase_realtime` publication.\n\n## Why\n\nIssue #810's live two-tab DAM Styles verification proved edits save (PATCH 204) but never propagate to a second open tab. Production catalog inspection returned zero `pg_publication_tables` rows for `public.style_tracker_rows`, so no `postgres_changes` subscription can receive its updates. Production target: `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`.\n\n## What is deliberately NOT changed\n\n- **Table, RLS policies, grants and indexes are untouched.** AGENTS.md §0.4 stands: `public.style_tracker_rows` writes stay open to every signed-in user. This PR neither widens nor narrows that, and a contract test now pins it.\n- **Replica identity is left at DEFAULT.** The table already has a primary key (`style_tracker_rows_pkey`), which is what `postgres_changes` needs. `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` would be a behaviour change outside the claimed objects and would grow the WAL for a hot, frequently-edited table.\n- No existing migration body was edited, and no guard or contract test was weakened.\n\n## Safety of the migration itself\n\nBoth guards follow the established pattern in `20260621151155_api_rls_realtime.sql`:\n\n- If the `supabase_realtime` publication does not exist (it is created by the Supabase platform, not by this migration history), the migration is a clean no-op instead of an error.\n- Membership is tested before the `alter publication`, so a re-apply cannot raise `already member of publication`.\n\n## Tests\n\n`supabase/tests/style_tracker_rows_realtime_publication_contracts.sql` (auto-globbed into `database-contract-tests.yml`) asserts, failing closed:\n\n1. `public.style_tracker_rows` exists and still has its primary key — the basis for using DEFAULT replica identity rather than FULL.\n2. RLS is still enabled and the open INSERT and UPDATE policies are still present.\n3. Where the `supabase_realtime` publication exists, `public.style_tracker_rows` is a member of it.\n\nIt also carries a **positive control**: the same membership predicate must return false for a table name that cannot exist. A checker that cannot answer \"no\" is not evidence.\n\n## Verbatim check results (local, at head)\n\n```\n$ bash scripts/check-sql.sh\nGuard B: no migration sorts before the base branch's newest version 20260905043023 (source: git:origin/main).\nWARNING: Guard B2 (backdated against a LIVE LEDGER) did not run -- no ledger\nsource configured. Guard B only compared this branch against the base branch,\nwhich is NOT what the databases have actually applied (issue #651).\nIssue #1235 expected-count guard passed: added migrations validate JSON count types and avoid raw integer casts.\nVerify-cost guard passed: 1 added migration(s) contain no prohibited verification read.\nIssue #1684 EOL reference guard passed: no new dependency was introduced.\nStatic checks passed. Set DATABASE_URL to run migrations against a disposable database.\n\n$ node scripts/check-cancelled-work.mjs\nOK — no cancelled instruction reintroduced (2 row(s) checked).\n\n$ node scripts/check-dispatch-collision.mjs --objects \"publication supabase_realtime,table public.style_tracker_rows\"\nChecked against 16 in-flight item(s).\nCollides with claim #2383  (this PR's own lane; no third-party collision)\n```\n\nBranch was updated from current `origin/main` (`03ec2a63`) and the checks re-run before handing back.\n\n## Next step (not done here, and not permitted here)\n\nPreview apply, publication-membership verification on preview and production, review assignment, merge and promotion all belong to the orchestrator. Issue #810 then ships the app-side subscription and repeats the live two-tab change/restore proof.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","createdAt":"2026-09-05T06:40:07Z","files":[{"path":"docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260905063701.json","additions":25,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"scripts/production_catalog_verification.py","additions":28,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260905063701_style_tracker_rows_realtime_publication.sql","additions":54,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/ci-quarantine.txt","additions":3,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/style_tracker_rows_realtime_publication_contracts.sql","additions":106,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"eb1d453ca7ba55251801aa30ce61e9f303afb08f","mergedAt":"2026-09-05T08:17:08Z","number":2384,"title":"feat(2331): publish public.style_tracker_rows for DAM realtime edits","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2384"},
{"body":"Closes the three integrity gaps issue #2203 names in the applied #1987/#2202 DesignFlow workflow-action contract.\n\nClaim: #2381 — reserved version `20260905053422`.\nDependency: #2202 (PR #2259, version `20260904143518`) is merged on main and applied on production.\n\n## What changes\n\n**1. A return now links to the handoff it actually answers.**\n`dflow.item_workflow_action` gains a `source_action_id` self-FK. The function previously matched the *earliest* reverse-direction action on the item, so on the second and every later pricing cycle a return went back to the *first* cycle's requester. It now selects the **latest still-open** handoff. \"Open\" means no other action already points at it, and a partial unique index (`item_workflow_action_one_return_per_source`) makes \"one handoff, one answer\" a database constraint rather than a convention — so a handoff can never be returned twice, by the function or by direct DML.\n\nThe rows are append-only (the #1987 trigger rejects every UPDATE and DELETE), which is why \"closed\" is modelled as a child row pointing back at its parent rather than a flag updated on the parent.\n\n**2. Stale transitions are rejected before any write.**\nNew reserved routing-context key `expected_prior_step_id`. Compared under the same `FOR UPDATE` item lock, before the insert; a mismatch raises SQLSTATE `40001` so the caller refetches and retries. Correlation-key retry idempotence is answered *first*, so a retried call still succeeds even though the item has moved past the step it was read at.\n\n**3. A required handoff can no longer commit with nobody told.**\nNew reserved routing-context key `require_recipient` (default true). The function counts the notifications it inserted; zero on a transition that names a destination function raises `P0002`, rolling back the action row, the item step change and the notification attempt together.\n\n**4. Fallback facts stop being free JSON.**\n`fallback_recipient_user_id`, `fallback_reason` and `requires_admin_review` are real, queryable, constrained columns — a fallback recipient without a reason is refused. The **original actor is never rewritten**: it is always read back through `source_action_id`, so a labeled inactive-requester or legacy fallback changes only who is notified, never who the record says asked.\n\n**5. `dflow.item_workflow_handoff`** exposes open/closed handoff state to the read APIs: one row per handoff with the return that closed it, `is_open`, and the fallback/admin-review state. Not reachable by `anon`.\n\n## Compatibility\n\n**The function signature does not change.** The four new inputs arrive as reserved keys inside the existing `p_routing_context` object — `expected_prior_step_id`, `require_recipient`, `fallback_recipient_user_id`, `fallback_reason` — each strictly type-checked (a malformed value raises `22023` rather than silently disabling a guard) and stripped before the routing context is stored, so the facts live in the typed columns and never as free JSON.\n\nAdding four defaulted parameters instead would create a second function whose first eleven parameter types are identical, making every existing eleven-argument call fail with `function is not unique`. Dropping the superseded signature does not rescue that under CI: the replay harness snapshots each routine's live definition, re-runs the earlier migration that declares it, and restores the snapshot — so a dropped overload is recreated and both exist again. One signature is the only shape that cannot break, and block A now asserts both \"exactly one function\" and \"still eleven parameters\".\n\nThe one intentional behavior change for existing callers is `require_recipient` defaulting to true, which is the point of the issue.\n\nThe applied #1987 migration is not edited.\n\n## Tests\n\n`supabase/tests/designflow_workflow_action_handoff_integrity_contracts.sql` — real DML, rolled back, no dependence on pre-existing rows. Blocks A–I cover: exactly one function overload; cycle 1 links and closes its handoff; **cycle 2 returns to its own requester, not cycle 1's** (the defect this issue exists for); duplicate return refused by both the function and the unique index; stale transition rejected *with a positive control* proving the guard does not reject everything; retry idempotence and correlation reuse; inactive-requester fallback with the original requester preserved and an unlabeled fallback refused; missing owner rolling back the action, the notification and the step change, with two positive controls (assignee present, and explicit opt-out).\n\nThe existing `designflow_item_assignment_action_history_contracts.sql` suite was read and stays green under the new function.\n\n## Checks run\n\n- `bash scripts/check-sql.sh` — **Static checks passed.** Guard B: no migration sorts before the base branch's newest version `20260905042713`. Guard B2 skipped (no ledger source configured locally). #1235, verify-cost and #1684 guards passed.\n- `node scripts/check-dispatch-collision.mjs` — collides only with this work's own claim #2381.\n- `node scripts/check-cancelled-work.mjs` — OK, no cancelled instruction reintroduced.\n\nReal-DML execution is left to CI's disposable-database replay: this machine has no local Postgres server and no Docker, so no local fixture result is claimed here.\n\n## Not done by this session\n\nNo preview apply, no reviewer assignment, no merge, no production promotion — this session holds none of those permissions.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-05T05:42:22Z","files":[{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260905053422_workflow_action_handoff_integrity.sql","additions":519,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"},{"path":"supabase/tests/designflow_workflow_action_handoff_integrity_contracts.sql","additions":551,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"9afbb04cdcb51a2426cf456bcb9c26ecb35de5be","mergedAt":"2026-09-05T07:12:46Z","number":2382,"title":"feat(dflow): workflow-action source handoff, stale-write, and zero-recipient integrity (#2203)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2382"},
{"body":"Closes #718. Author-lane claim #2379, reserved version `20260905042713`.\n\n## What this does\n\nRevokes `truncate`, `references`, `trigger` and `maintain` from `service_role` on the 37 pre-existing `plm` tables that `20260810180000` did not retro-fix.\n\n`20260710135975` ran `alter default privileges in schema plm grant all on tables to service_role`, so every `plm` table created while that rule stood was born with all eight privilege bits. `20260810180000` narrowed the schema default and retro-fixed the 39 `plm.pmt_*` / `plm.nbcu_*` landing tables of #664 — but a default-privilege change never touches tables that already exist. This is the retro-fix for the remaining set.\n\n## The population\n\nRead live, read-only, from production `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai` immediately before authoring. The catalog returns exactly 37 `plm` tables holding any of the four bits, and the set matches the list in #718's scope block exactly. It is closed: the default-privilege fix bounds it above, and no `plm` table created since holds any of the bits.\n\nReproduce it on any target with the read-only query in the migration header.\n\n## Why it is safe\n\nThese tables exist on production, so this is a live privilege change, not a pre-emptive correction. The owner resolved item 2 of #718 from a repository-wide loader audit: no application or loader code issues `TRUNCATE` against any of the 37 — the only matches are isolated database tests. `MAINTAIN`, `REFERENCES` and `TRIGGER` are DDL-adjacent and have no use for an importer role. `TRUNCATE` is the dangerous one: it does not fire row triggers, so it bypasses every trigger-based immutability guarantee in the schema.\n\n`service_role` keeps `insert`/`select`/`update`/`delete`; `authenticated` keeps its `SELECT`.\n\n## Guards in the migration\n\n- **Section A — vacuous-pass guard.** Fails if the list is not 37 entries, or if any of the 37 tables is absent. There is no \"some missing, carry on\" branch: a partial sweep would report success while leaving the privileges in place.\n- **Section C** re-asserts the #649 default-privilege fix from `pg_default_acl`, so this cannot pass on a database where the hole has been reopened.\n- **Section D** asserts the outcome in both directions — unwanted bits surviving *and* wanted bits over-revoked — so a revoke that did nothing cannot look identical to one that worked.\n\nRevokes are 37 explicit statements, not a dynamic loop, so the promotion preflight can model the objects.\n\n## Checks\n\n- `scripts/check-sql.sh` — static checks passed.\n- `scripts/test_migration_derivation.py` — 42 passed; header declares `-- derived-from: none`.\n- Cross-PR object collision runs on this PR in CI (it fails closed off-PR by design).\n- No preview apply, review assignment, merge or production promotion performed by this session.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","createdAt":"2026-09-05T04:31:05Z","files":[{"path":"supabase/migrations/20260905042713_plm_legacy_service_role_privilege_revoke.sql","additions":280,"deletions":0,"changeType":"ADDED"}],"headRefOid":"55099dfc8ab4e8ce96a559be946bf86602fa7c3b","mergedAt":"2026-09-05T05:25:27Z","number":2380,"title":"fix(plm): revoke service_role TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER/MAINTAIN on the 37 legacy plm tables (#718)","url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/2380"},
{"body":"Closes #2349. Claim #2359. Reserved version `20260905024139`.\n\n## Why\n\n`20260903200951_coldlion_division_reference_table.sql` (issue #2171, PR #2199) is merged, correct, and **permanently unpromotable**.\n\nVerbatim refusal from the production business-risk gate (run 33926573085):\n\n> Production business-risk gate rejected evidence: original apply run 33754529571 dispatched at 63d8441b37bf41fa7dd798ba313a58d666e2ea53 produced evidence with a different scripts/production_migration_guard.py than the merge commit 477ef03cd516c79188d81b6c21260575a43a9239 of the pull request that authored 20260903200951\n\n- Its only preview apply (run 33754529571) was a **pre-merge branch rehearsal**, applied under the superseded version 20260903115927.\n- `preview-ledger-orphan-reconciliation.yml` run 33821298999 renamed that ledger row to 20260903200951, so **preview already holds the version** and no fresh preview ledger delta can ever be produced for it.\n- 63d8441b **is** in main's history (`behind_by 0`), so this is producer-file drift, not the squash-orphan variant. The historical recovery lane refuses it correctly, and its own contract prescribes a new migration.\n\nThis is the documented `docs/production-promotion-procedure.md` §5.1-A route. **No gate is weakened, edited or bypassed.**\n\n## What changed\n\n- **New migration** `20260905024139_reissue_coldlion_division_reference_table.sql` — byte-identical to the original. Both sibling readers in this repo do, explicitly:\n- `scripts/check-dispatch-collision.mjs:573` — `if (files.length !== pr.changed_files) throw new Unknown(…)`\n- `scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.mjs:96` — `if(Number(pr.changed_files)!==apiFiles.length) throw new LeaseCheckError('incomplete PR pagination…')`\nA partial list reads as one migration and then mints a **permanent, never-releasable** reservation (`check-dispatch-collision.mjs:302-308`). `pr.changed_files` is already in hand from the `io.getPr(TARGET.pr)` call two lines above at `:32`, so this is a one-line fix. Note the script already obtains this same fact *with* the proof at `:44-45` via `io.prSources()`, which routes through `gatherOpenPrObjects` — it reads PR #3557's files twice, once proven and once not.\n**2. `scripts/recover-3539-reservation.mjs:36` — target-worktree proof is weaker than the canonical one.**\nThe repo's established routine for proving a substitute worktree is `rebindClaimWorktree`'s `verifyTarget` (`manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:~6320`), which requires **three** things plus path hygiene:\n```\nif(!io.localClean(request.targetWorktree))throw …\nif(io.localHead(request.targetWorktree)!==request.headSha)throw …\nif(typeof io.localBranch!=='function'||io.localBranch(request.targetWorktree)!==request.branch)throw new LaneError('target worktree is not on the claim branch')\n```\nand before it: `if(/[\\r\\n`]/.test(request.targetWorktree)||request.targetWorktree!==request.targetWorktree.trim())throw`, plus `normalizeWorktreePath(worktree)===normalizeWorktreePath(targetWorktree)` → refuse.\nThe new script checks only clean + exact head. It never calls `io.localBranch`, so a detached-HEAD checkout — or any other ref that happens to resolve to `headSha` — satisfies the guard. It performs no path validation on a fully operator-supplied argument that is then handed to `execFileSync('git',['-C',worktree,…])` (`:2873`, `:2880`). Because `--target-worktree` is the *substitute* for the unreachable recorded Windows worktree (contract assumption 1, `.agent/work/3574/5/contract.json:35`), this is precisely the proof that should not be weaker than its sibling.\n**3. The issue's required outcome is not delivered, and the explicitly-added second failure is unaddressed.**\n#3574 requires \"prove the original lease check passes at an exact reviewed head\", and the issue comment adds: *\"Recovery must renew it through the governed claim command after the reservation inconsistency is repaired, then re-run the exact-head lease check. Do not treat the missing ref as the only failure.\"*\nCreating `refs/db-claims/20260925223300` does **not** make the lease check pass. `validateMigrationLease` refuses earlier at `scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.mjs:38` — `if(!holder.lease.active) throw new LeaseCheckError('claim #3546 is expired')` — and `lease.active` is false: the author's own fixture sets `expires_at: 2026-09-26T05:48:20.047Z` against `NOW = 2026-09-28` (`recover-3539-reservation.test.mjs:6,10`), which `parseAuthorLease:1343` derives to `capacityState:'expired-unconfirmed'`. The recovery script never inspects `lease.active` or `lease.capacityState`.\nConsequently: `required_checks` (`.agent/work/3574/5/contract.json:29-33`) does not include the lease check, `completion.json` records no run of it, and no lease renewal is performed or evidenced. The PR body is honest that renewal is a later manual step — but that means the issue's stated outcome is deferred, not met.\nAlso unmet: *\"Determine how claim and PR version moved without a durable supersession reservation.\"* Neither the diff nor the supplied evidence records a root-cause determination. The PR body offers a hypothesis (\"out-of-band claim and pull-request rename\") with no supporting evidence, and `completion.json:33-36` `assumptions_resolved` restates the hypothesis as an assumption.\n### Should fix\n**4. Negative coverage is thin for a script whose entire value is guarded refusal.** `recover-3539-reservation.test.mjs` exercises 6 refusals out of roughly 18. Never exercised: `:29` old reservation missing (a *core* requirement of the issue — the fixture always seeds it), `:27` retired version, `:25`/`:26` claim identity, `:31` `renewalIssueScope`, `:35` migration count ≠ 1, `:40` empty main tree, `:42`/`:43` claim listing, `:45` parser source, `:48` lane collision, `:51` conflicting/stranded evidence pair, `:53` different identities, `:61` inputs changed under mutex, `:64`/`:66` create-or-readback failure, `:67` old ref changed mid-recovery. The PR body's claim \"foreign evidence refuses\" is tested only in its weakest form — case 6 (`test.mjs:37`) leaves the commit absent, so `evidence(undefined)` throws at `:15`; the `:53` different-identities branch, which is the actual foreign-evidence guard, is never reached.\n**5. `retirementSnapshotCache` is a module global with no per-`io` keying, and the script never resets it.** `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2006-2019`: `if (retirementSnapshotCache) return retirementSnapshotCache`, keyed on nothing. Test 1 populates an empty snapshot; every later invocation in the same process reuses it regardless of which `io` is passed. So the retired-version refusal at `:27` is untestable as written, and in any long-lived process importing this module it reads stale. Single-shot CLI use is unaffected, and siblings share the pattern (`renewExpiredClaim:8153`, `supersedeActiveClaimVersion:6266`) — but this is the only path that mints a reservation outside `--reserve-version`, so it is the one place where staleness has permanent consequences.\n**6. Two canonical private helpers are re-implemented, one more loosely.** `workstreamKey` (`:7708`) and `migrationVersions` (`:7713`) are module-private, so the script duplicates them at `:25` and `:9-12`. The duplication of `migrationVersions` is faithful. The title check is not: `/^CLAIM:\\s+(?:issue\\s+)?#?3539\\b/i` accepts `CLAIM: #3539/#9999 …` (`/` is a non-word char, so `\\b` matches), whereas `workstreamKey` canonicalizes that to `#3539/#9999` and `supersedeActiveClaimVersion:6264` would refuse it as not identifying exact issue #3539. Exporting and reusing both helpers removes the drift; the contract's \"do not edit the shared coordination source\" is a self-imposed constraint, not a repo rule.\n**7. The main-version predicate differs from the canonical one.** `:39` uses `^supabase\\/migrations\\/(\\d{14})_[^/]+\\.sql$`; `currentMainMaxVersion` (`:1834`, exported, and the manager's own ordering rule at `:6271`) uses `^supabase\\/migrations\\/(\\d{14})_` with no suffix constraint. Any main-tree entry under `supabase/migrations/` that is not `*.sql` would be invisible to `:39` and could make the ordering guard pass wrongly. **Not live today** — I enumerated `supabase/migrations/*`: all 709 entries are `.sql`, and the maximum is `20260925193145` (patterns `2026093*` and `20261*` return nothing). Still an unstated loose assumption; reusing `currentMainMaxVersion` would settle it.\n**8. `evidence()` is stricter than the manager's parser for the same record.** `:14` requires `old-ref=([0-9a-f]{40})`; `parseVersionSupersession` (`:6239`) accepts `[0-9a-f]{7,40}`. A supersession record the *manager* wrote with an abbreviated `old-ref` would make `:52` throw 'existing reservation evidence is unreadable' and permanently block the resume path. Fail-closed, but needlessly so — widening to `{7,40}` costs nothing and makes the two parsers agree on the ref they both read.\n### Worth noting\n**9. The idempotent/resume path is head-sensitive.** `:53` compares `prior.head!==headSha`. Once both refs exist, any later PR #3557 head movement makes a re-run refuse with 'existing supersession evidence names different identities' rather than reporting \"already complete\". The natural operator verification — run it again to confirm — therefore fails and looks like corruption. `supersedeActiveClaimVersion:6250` has the same coupling, so it is consistent; a message distinguishing \"already complete at head X, you passed Y\" from \"foreign evidence\" would avoid a needless escalation.\n**10. `:67` hides the state it leaves behind.** If the old ref changed *after* both new refs were created, the script throws 'old permanent reservation changed during recovery' with no mention that `refs/db-claims/20260925223300` and the supersession ref now exist permanently and are not rolled back. `:66` gets this right ('permanent reservation retained for retry'); `:67` does not. There is also no `requireOwnedRef` between `:66` and `:67`, unlike before each of the three mutations.\n**11. The ordering guard is a closing window.** `:40` requires `20260925223300 > max(main)`. Verified against this checkout: max is `20260925193145`, so it passes with roughly three hours of margin. Versions are UTC timestamps, so the first author who reserves ≥ `20260925223300` and merges permanently disables this utility — and the refusal text ('recovered version must be later than the current main migration maximum') does not tell the operator that the remedy is a fresh supersession of PR #3557, not a retry. The rule itself is correct: a version already behind main could never merge.\n**12. Draft PRs are accepted.** `:33` checks only `state==='open'`; `gatherOpenPrObjects` labels drafts `PR #3557 [DRAFT] \"…\"` (`check-dispatch-collision.mjs:595`), which the `:44` regex `^PR #3557(?:\\s|$)` still matches. Consistent with `supersedeActiveClaimVersion:6267`, so low.\n**13. Disposition reasons are copy-pasted across two semantically different sites.** `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~recover-3539-reservation.mjs.json` gives both `:29` (missing old reservation ref) and `:45` (missing/ambiguous PR parser source) the identical 152-character reason. The checker enforces only `reason.trim().length >= 20` (`check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:120`). `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/README.md` refuses a bulk-regenerate flag *\"deliberately: a bulk regenerate would let new call sites through unreviewed while the guard stays green\"* — hand-copying one reason across sites reproduces exactly that outcome. The `excluded` verdicts themselves are substantively correct.\n**14. Check evidence is paraphrased, not recorded.** `completion.json:29` says `\"truth audit OK with 326 call sites at implementation 6a7578ca\"`; the tool actually prints `truth audit OK: call_sites=N sources=M derived_digest=XXXXXXXXXXXX` (`check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:127`). Sibling `.agent/work/3573/1/completion.json:26` records it verbatim. Dropping `sources=` and `derived_digest=` weakens the record.\n**15. CLI ergonomics (`:72-75`).** A bad invocation throws an uncaught `LaneError` — stack trace, exit 1 — instead of the `console.error` + `process.exitCode` shape used by `check-migration-pr-lease.mjs:106` and `agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs`. No `--help`. Cosmetic.\n**16. Dead defensive branches.** `:39`'s `file.path??file.filename??''` and `:10`'s `row.path` fallback are unreachable for `githubIo`: `treeFiles` → `pathsAtRef` returns sorted path **strings** (`scripts/lib/github-tree.mjs:61`), and `getPrFiles` returns REST file objects. Harmless, but they imply an input shape that never occurs. A `null` entry in either list would raise `TypeError`, not `LaneError`.\n### Verified positives (checked, not assumed)\n- **All 12 imported symbols exist with matching call shapes**: `acquireMutex:3473`, `assertClaimNotRetired:2042`, `assertLaneAvailable:1348`, `githubIo:2147`, `LaneError:1272`, `MUTEX_REF:87`, `parseAuthorLease:1302`, `readRefAfterWrite:3437`, `releaseOwnedRef:3521`, `renewalIssueScope:8106`, `requireOwnedRef:3491`, `validateClaimObjects:1275`, plus `claimBody:1365` in the test. Every `githubIo` method called is defined: `makeOwnerCommit:2605`, `getIssue:2535`, `readRef:2641`, `getPr:2484`, `getPrFiles:2485`, `localClean:2880`, `localHead:2873`, `mainSha:2565`, `treeFiles:2523`, `openClaims:2399`, `prSources:2469`, `createRef:2630`, `getCommit:2595`. I traced all three tests line by line against these definitions; each is internally coherent and should pass.\n- **Old reservation and evidence are preserved.** No `io.deleteRef` call touches any `refs/db-claims/*`; the only release is `MUTEX_REF` in `finally:69`. Old-ref presence is required before any write (`:28-29`), re-asserted at `:61` and `:67`, and the test asserts preservation after *every* refusal (`test.mjs:39`). Honours `check-dispatch-collision.mjs:302-308` (\"RESERVATIONS ARE PERMANENT … Do not add rollback\") and the contract's `prohibited_actions`.\n- **Create-if-absent is preserved.** Refs are written via `io.createRef` (`:56`, `:64`, `:66`) → `createRefWithReadback:1522` → GitHub `POST /git/refs`, never `git push`, respecting the explicit prohibition at `check-dispatch-collision.mjs:296-300`. Every create is followed by `readRefAfterWrite`.\n- **Mutex discipline matches the manager**: `acquireMutex` outside the `try`, `requireOwnedRef` before each of the three mutations (`:55`, `:62`, `:65`), guarded release in `finally`. And a **stranded mutex left by this script is recoverable** — the owner-commit prefix at `:21` matches the `recoverStaleAuthorMutex` allowlist regex at `:3506` via its `claim-version-supersession` alternative.\n- **The written evidence is readable by the manager.** The `:63` message grammar is exactly `parseVersionSupersession`'s (`:6239`), and `evidenceRef` at `:8` is exactly `supersessionRef` at `:6246`, so `supersedeActiveClaimVersion`'s idempotent branch (`:6248-6251`) accepts the hand-written record.\n- **Pointing `refs/db-claims/<version>` at an owner commit breaks no reader.** Every consumer in the repo reads it for existence only, never parsing the message: `check-migration-pr-lease.mjs:100`, `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:6250, 6272, 6281, 7450, 8046, 8155, 8184, 8228, 8257, 8285, 8309, 8334, 8350, 8386, 8409`. It is nonetheless a shape deviation from `runReserveVersion`, which points it at `io.baseSha(repo)` (`check-dispatch-collision.mjs:861`) — worth recording in the retirement note.\n- **Creating the ref is exactly what unblocks the later renewal.** `renewExpiredClaim:8155` refuses with 'permanent version reservation is unreadable' when the ref is absent, so the recover-then-renew ordering in the PR body is correct and necessary.\n- **`treeFiles` is completeness-proven**: `treeAtRef` refuses `truncated === true` (`scripts/lib/github-tree.mjs:38-40`).\n- **Contract/evidence pair is coherent.** `contract_ref` = `contractRef(3574,5)` = `refs/db-contracts/3574/5`, matching the published ref and `contract_sha256`; `files_changed` (3) ⊆ `allowed_paths ∪ file_writes`, so `reconcileReportWithContract`'s outside-paths check (`agent-work-contract.mjs:219-221`) passes; the two `.agent/work/3574/5/*` files are exactly the tail `verifyGitEvidence` requires after `head_sha` (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:65-70`); `head_sha: 6a7578ca…` as the *implementation* head with the pair added by `ac912c7` matches the sibling convention in `.agent/work/3573/1/completion.json` and satisfies that function's ancestry and merge-base requirements. The on-disk `contract.json` is byte-identical to the copy published in the issue comment.\n- **Throughput catalogue is required, correctly named and correctly shaped**: `dispositionFileName('scripts/recover-3539-reservation.mjs')` = the committed filename; the test file is correctly excluded by `!/\\.test\\./` (`check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:66`); partitioning means no other catalogue is touched (issue #2832).\n- **New test file is not wired into CI — consistent with convention, not a new gap.** No workflow references `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` or `scripts/recover-3539-reservation.test.mjs`; `tools-offline-tests.yml` enumerates specific script tests and globs only `tools/*.test.mjs` (`:262`). Enforcement is therefore via the contract's self-reported `required_checks`, as for the manager's own 714-test suite.\n## The three mandatory checks\n**1. Index usage — NON-APPLICABLE, source-backed.** The change adds no SQL and no database object. Both evidence files declare `db_reads: []`, `db_writes: []` (`.agent/work/3574/5/contract.json:23-24`, `completion.json:17-18`) and `migration_versions: []` (`completion.json:6`); `scripts/recover-3539-reservation.mjs:4-5` imports only `node:url` and `./manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` and issues no query. No predicate or join is introduced, so no index can serve or fail to serve one. This is a source-backed conclusion, not an absence of evidence.\nApplying the *spirit* — does every lookup the change relies on have a read path that actually serves it, completely? — three of four are proven: `treeFiles` refuses a truncated tree (`github-tree.mjs:38`); `prSources` proves `files.length === pr.changed_files` per PR and refuses at the 3000-file limit (`check-dispatch-collision.mjs:571-573`); `openClaims` paginates with `--paginate --slurp`, validates every page, refuses an all-empty read and cross-checks via search when zero claims are found (`manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2399-2417`). **The one lookup with no completeness proof is `getPrFiles` at `recover-3539-reservation.mjs:34` — finding 1.** That is the direct analogue of \"an index that exists but cannot be used as written\": the guarantee is available, is enforced twice elsewhere in the repo, and is not used here.\n**2. Function volatility — NON-APPLICABLE, source-backed.** No PostgreSQL function is created, altered, or referenced; the strings `IMMUTABLE`, `STABLE` and `VOLATILE` do not appear in any of the five changed files, and no migration is touched (`migration_versions: []`). The JavaScript analogue is correct: `oneVersion` (`:9`) and `evidence` (`:13`) are pure; `recover3539Reservation` (`:19`) is intentionally effectful and takes injectable `now=new Date(), io=githubIo`, matching the sibling convention (`supersedeActiveClaimVersion:6245`, `renewExpiredClaim:8135`); the CLI body is guarded by `import.meta.url===pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href` (`:72`), so importing the module for tests produces no side effects — the same guard shape as `check-migration-pr-lease.mjs:106`.\n**3. Exact object checks — SUBSTANTIALLY SATISFIED, with three loosenesses.**\nSatisfied: a frozen exact identity tuple — issue 3539, claim 3546, PR 3557, owner string, branch string, recorded Windows worktree, both 14-digit versions (`:7`); 40-hex validation of `headSha` (`:20`) and `oldSha` (`:29`); exact ref names constructed from those literals rather than discovered (`:8`); the single claimed database object `function api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory` asserted by literal equality against the parsed lease (`:26`) *and* cross-checked against SQL-derived PR objects through `validateClaimObjects` (`:46`, which enforces schema-qualified `kind schema.name` form at `:1275-1300`); all seven supersession fields re-parsed from the durable commit and compared (`:52-53`); every imported symbol and every `githubIo` method verified present with a matching shape. Nothing in the change settles for \"a name exists\" where an identity is required — existence reads are always followed by identity comparison.\nLoose, in descending importance: the claim-title check bypasses canonical `workstreamKey` and accepts a combined workstream key (finding 6); the main-version predicate is narrower than `currentMainMaxVersion`'s (finding 7); `evidence()`'s `old-ref` width is narrower than the manager's, so it rejects records the manager accepts (finding 8).\n## Rollback and recovery assessment\nPartial-failure behaviour is sound and matches the repo's permanence rule. Failure before `:64` leaves nothing written. Failure at `:64` leaves nothing (create-or-readback refused). Failure at `:66` leaves the permanent reservation intentionally — stated in the message — and `:50-58` resumes it on a later run when the stranded commit's identities match exactly, which test 3 exercises. Failure at `:67` leaves both refs and reports it unhelpfully (finding 10). The mutex is released on every exit path. Old reservation and all prior evidence are never deleted. **No rollback of a created reservation exists, by design** (`check-dispatch-collision.mjs:302-308`) — so the correctness burden falls entirely on the pre-write guards, which is why findings 1 and 2 matter more than they would in a reversible change.\n## What would move this to APPROVE\nBatch into one head per AGENTS.md §5.0-C: assert `pr.changed_files === files.length` at `:34`; add `io.localBranch(targetWorktree) === TARGET.branch` plus the sibling's path-hygiene refusals at `:36`; widen `old-ref` to `{7,40}` at `:14`; reuse `workstreamKey`/`migrationVersions`/`currentMainMaxVersion` (or state why not); add negative tests for at least `:29`, `:53`, `:61` and `:67`; write distinct disposition reasons; record the audit output verbatim. `validatePullRequestCompletion:245-251` ✓. `.agent/work/3574/6/` is the only pair in the tree, so `resolveEvidencePair` returns `current`, not `conflicted` ✓.\n**One structural fact I could not establish, stated precisely rather than assumed.** `verifyGitEvidence:56-63` requires `report.files_changed` to equal `git diff --name-only mergeBase..report.head_sha` exactly, and `:66-72` requires `report.head_sha..prHeadSha` to be exactly the two `3574/6` files. `completion.json` names `head_sha: 5b5aaa23…` with three files. That is self-consistent **only if** the `3574/6` pair did not exist at `5b5aaa23` and was added whole by `5dc6151`. The packet exposes no per-commit structure (`.git/logs/HEAD` has one checkout entry; no `packed-refs`; git objects are compressed), and I have no shell. Two facts make this low-risk rather than unknown-and-ignored: `files_changed`/`head_sha` are meant to be derived, not typed (`deriveGitFacts`, `agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:120-133`, added by #2998 after five mismatches), and the condition is enforced by `agent-work-contract.yml:232` on every head. Settle it with:\n```\nnode scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs \\\n  --contract-file .agent/work/3574/6/contract.json \\\n  --report-file  .agent/work/3574/6/completion.json \\\n  --pr-base-sha  5f91f2f6582df8eb7774cf48aa1849e5891a0b02 \\\n  --pr-head-sha  5dc61519c3a26ff41e2e0fecee70dc6516a7287b\n```\nThe same limit applies to the two `line_sha256`/context digests and to `contract_sha256`: I verified their *structure*, *site numbers*, *counts* and *consistency*, not the hash preimages.\n## Repository repair readiness vs. the later, separately governed live work\nThese are distinct, and the distinction is legitimate — but the boundary should be stated plainly on the PR, because the issue text bundles them.\n**Delivered by this PR (repository repair readiness):** a guarded, auditable, tested one-time utility that can restore `refs/db-claims/20260925223300` and its supersession evidence, create-only, under the coordination mutex, preserving the old reservation and all prior evidence, refusing on any identity, collision, ordering, worktree or concurrency mismatch. Nothing in it weakens an existing check. Merging it changes no live state.\n**Not delivered, and correctly deferred:** the live recovery run, the lease renewal, and the lease-check re-run. I confirmed from source that this PR *cannot* make the original check pass: `validateMigrationLease` refuses at `check-migration-pr-lease.mjs:38` (`claim #3546 is expired`) **before** it reaches the reservation-existence refusal at `:59`, and the recovery script never inspects `lease.active` or `lease.capacityState`. The fixture's own expiry (`test.mjs:6,10`: `2026-09-26T05:48:20.047Z` against `NOW = 2026-09-28`) derives `capacityState: 'expired-unconfirmed'` via `parseAuthorLease:1341-1343`.\nTwo positives worth recording, both verified rather than assumed:\n- **The repair really is a prerequisite for renewal.** `renewExpiredClaim:8155` refuses with `'permanent version reservation is unreadable'` while the ref is absent, so recover-then-renew is the necessary order.\n- **No deadlock on the inaccessible worktree.** `renewExpiredClaim` (`:8133-8186`) never calls `localClean`/`localHead`/`localBranch`; it compares `lease.worktree` to `options.worktree` as strings only. So renewal does not need the recorded Windows path to be reachable, and `rebindClaimWorktree` — which *would* need it and additionally requires an **active** lease (`:6343`) — is not on the critical path. The sequence in the PR body is viable.\nAlso outside this diff and still open: the lease check is not in `required_checks`, so nothing in the evidence pair records its state at any head.\n## What I did not execute\nNo tests, no audit, no hash recomputation, no git graph query, no network read of `refs/db-contracts/3574/6`, `refs/db-claims/*` or `refs/db-claim-supersessions/*`, and no CI status at this head. The author's \"7 recovery / 714 manager / 70 throughput tests pass\" is not my result. I did trace all seven tests by hand against the real manager source and each is internally coherent: the retirement fixture satisfies `validateRetirementRecord` on every field (`schema_version` 1 = `RETIREMENT_SCHEMA_VERSION:102`; `worktree_state: 'clean'` ∈ `WORKTREE_STATES:84` and ∉ `RETIREMENT_OWNER_DECISION_STATES:110`, so no `owner_decision` needed; `decision: 'abandoned-worktree'` ∈ `RETIREMENT_DECISIONS:106`; `head_sha` 40-hex; `successor_issue: null`; no unknown keys), so `assertClaimNotRetired:2042-2047` produces the `terminally retired` text the test expects; the work-issue fixture satisfies `parseQueueScope:944-1027` including `structural` + `shared-db-orchestrator` + non-empty writes; and the `readRef` call-count fixtures line up with the exact read sequence at `:30`, `:53`, `:65`, `:71`. That is a reading, not a run.\n## What would move this to a clean pass\nOne batched head per AGENTS.md §5.0-C, plus one dispatcher action: add the `:57` different-identities negative test (finding C); record the root-cause determination, or state its deferral explicitly as was done for renewal (finding A); restate or implement the dry-run claim (finding B); fix the `:40` absent-vs-dirty message and wrap `localBranch` so a detached target yields its intended `LaneError` (finding F). Dispatcher side: publish a gen-7 contract whose `allowed_paths`/`file_writes` name `.agent/work/3574/6/*` and, if the suite is to be wired in, `.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml` (findings D, E). I checked the readers in `check-migration-pr-lease.mjs:59` and the manager's `refs/db-claims/*` reads — they test existence only — so nothing breaks today.\n5. REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### Findings and reasoning (everything the reviewer said before its verdict)\n\nI'll start with the evidence packet and then inspect the sealed diff and related source.Packet matches the requested head. Next I’ll read the sealed patch and the queue comparison helpers.Provisional lean is approve if exactness holds. I’ll now read the helpers, tests, and sibling stringify comparisons.I’ll compare the verification record to the required-check list, then inspect tests and any leftover stringify comparisons on the queue path.I’ll verify git ancestry for the completion SHA, run the tests, and read the evidence-pair rules plus the merge-queue plan.Shell is blocked in this profile, so I’ll read git metadata and the Step 8 plan from files instead.Reviewed sealed packet head `505d5e1be2b3fbf7b62247ffd6f92989b1855230` against base `d68be25cb86cb0546dc2b58602953d148c44faef`. Changed paths are the seven listed files: the comparison helper and both call sites, the two test files, the dated activation record, and the generation-2 work-contract pair. No SQL, migrations, grants, or workflow files are in the diff.\n\n## Findings\n\nNo blocking defect. Exactness of the queue-parameter gate is preserved, the sibling `queueRulesetMatches` path uses the same helper, and the activation record matches the committed sources of truth.\n\n### Comparison exactness\n\n`queueParametersEqual` in `scripts/merge-queue-contract.mjs` requires the same own-key set (sorted key arrays compared elementwise) and `===` on every value. That still refuses a changed value, an extra key, an absent key, and a retyped value (`1` vs `'1'`). Arrays, `null`, and non-objects return false.\n\n`QUEUE_RULE.parameters` is a frozen object of seven primitives. For that shape, key-order-independent `===` is at least as strict as the old `JSON.stringify` check: extra or missing keys still fail, and nested objects would fail closed on reference identity.\n\nBoth production call sites now use the helper:\n\n- `verifyReadback` in `scripts/configure-merge-queue.mjs`\n- `queueRulesetMatches` (used by `queueMode()`) in `scripts/merge-queue-contract.mjs`\n\nThe remaining `JSON.stringify` of parameters is the `verifyReadback` error text and the test fixture that asserts GitHub’s insertion order differs from `QUEUE_RULE`. Neither is a comparison. No other production `JSON.stringify` of ruleset parameters remains on the queue path (`configure-merge-queue.mjs`, `merge-queue-contract.mjs`, queue tests, `.github` workflows).\n\n### Tests (read, not executed)\n\n`scripts/merge-queue-contract.test.mjs` pins GitHub’s order with `assert.notEqual(JSON.stringify(GITHUB_ORDER_PARAMETERS), JSON.stringify(QUEUE_RULE.parameters))`, then accepts that object through `queueParametersEqual` and `queueRulesetMatches`, and refuses changed / extra / absent / retyped / `null` / `[]`.\n\n`scripts/configure-merge-queue.test.mjs` accepts the same GitHub-order object through `verifyReadback` (id `24024180`) and still throws on `grouping_strategy: 'HEADGREEN'`. Extra/absent/retyped coverage for read-back is through the shared helper.\n\nThis review profile could not run `node --test`; the packet also recorded no test run.\n\n### Verification record\n\n`docs/verification/merge-queue-activation-20260925.json` matches `QUEUE_RULE.parameters` on all seven values (GitHub key order). The 16 `requiredContexts` match `docs/verification/main-required-status-checks.json` in name, count, and order. `strict: false` matches that mirror and `docs/verification/main-required-status-checks-readback-20260925.json`. `enforce_admins: true` matches the transfer baseline (`enforceAdmins: true`) and owner-rulings; this review did not re-fetch live GitHub.\n\nRollback command `node scripts/configure-merge-queue.mjs --rollback --apply` is a valid invocation of the queue-only deleter. `docs/merge-queue-operation.md` pins apply with `--expect-id <id>`. The recorded command omits `--expect-id 24024180`; the id is still in `ruleset.id` in the same file. That is a runbook-precision gap, not a false command.\n\n### Work contract\n\nGeneration 2 `allowed_paths` / `file_writes` match the patch. Completion `files_changed` is the implementation set (scripts + verification JSON), which is the intended split from the evidence-pair commit named in the MANIFEST. `required_checks` still lists only `node --test scripts/configure-merge-queue.test.mjs`; the completion evidence also claims the merge-queue-contract suite. CI `Tools offline tests` is the path that would run both.\n\n## Mandatory probe items\n\n**Index usage.** No predicates or joins.
