I could not run tests, and the \"CI fully green\" claim and the Blacksmith failure comment are author-supplied evidence in this conversation, not something I verified.\n\n## Findings\n\nHigh-ish / correctness of the delivered claim\n\n1. The new source-system fallback covers only three of the four `*_dcpvault` source systems, so the documented rule and the issue's acceptance criterion are both false for 20th Century DCP Vault rows. The fallback clauses are `when s.source_system = 'disney_dcpvault' then 'disney'` / `'marvel_dcpvault' then 'marvel'` / `'lucasfilm_dcpvault' then 'lucasfilm-star-wars'` at `supabase/migrations/20260925174850_scraped_source_inventory_pixar_disney_dcpvault_licensor.sql:648-650` and `:668-670`, with the `else` immediately after at `:651` and `:671`; the same shape repeats in the character arm (`:1158`, `:1177`) and style-guide arm (`:1365`, `:1384`) as shown by the greps for `licensor_group_key` and `Licensor not yet determined` and by the body quoted in this packet's `patch.diff`. `plm.twentieth_century_dcp_property.source_system` is constrained to `twentieth_century_dcpvault` (`supabase/migrations/20260814010000_dcp_studio_separated_landing.sql:7813`), and the twentieth-century property arm derives `dcp-authority-conflict` / `dcp-contract-opa-conflict` / `dcp-opa-scope-conflict` / `dcp-authority-unresolved` keys for `dcpvault:` ids (that arm's CASE, quoted verbatim in this packet's `patch.diff`). Those keys match none of the new clauses, so such a row lands in `unresolved` = \"Licensor not yet determined\". That (i) contradicts `docs/db-data-admin-scraped-properties.md:36-38` (\"Authority and mapping conflicts ... never move a row into the unresolved group\"), and (ii) contradicts the issue's acceptance line \"Zero rows with source_system `*_dcpvault` in the 'Licensor not yet determined' group, in all three entity kinds\", read as written. Either the fallback must cover `twentieth_century_dcpvault`, or the docs sentence and the acceptance statement must be narrowed to the three source systems explicitly — one of the two, not neither.\n\n2. No executable evidence for the change's actual output. The changed test file only greps the function *definition text* (`supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:26-54` headings, `:60-71` keys, `:86-98` grouping clauses, `:155-163` row-key shape, `:195-222` catalog/ACL), and the only executing test asserts merely that `licensor_group_key`/`licensor_group_name` are non-empty on whatever rows come back (`supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory_calls.sql:60-66`). So neither of the two behaviours this PR exists to deliver — pixar/pixar-opa rows carrying group `disney`, and zero `*_dcpvault` rows in the unresolved group — is asserted anywhere in the repository; the completion artifact itself defers acceptance to prose outside the repository (`.agent/work/3539/2/completion.json:34-38`, \"Acceptance SQL ... listed in the completion narrative on issue #3539\"). For a semantics-only change that also feeds displayed headings, this is a proof gap, not a style note.\n\n3. Stale, now-contradicted comment inside the changed test file: `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:57` still reads \"Disney, Marvel, Pixar and Lucasfilm / Star Wars stay separate licensors\", while the same file now requires `'Disney (Pixar) - Creative (DCP Vault)'` and `'Disney (Pixar) - Submissions (OPA)'` at `:29-30`. The change updated the assertions but left the explanatory comment asserting the old rule.\n\nMedium / evidence binding\n\n4. The completion artifact is bound to a different commit than the one under review: `.agent/work/3539/2/completion.json` records `head_sha` `7beaaa07c5adbafa1a40f05539a5d6f6825a673b` and `contract_ref` `refs/db-contracts/3539/2`, while the authoritative head here is `d6c43455abacc07ff8caa445707fc2b95d56a17c` (MANIFEST section 2, which also records the head subject as \"Add agent work contract pair for issue #3539\"). Repo policy may intend the contract pair to trail the implementation, but nothing I can open verifies that the head I am reviewing is the head the recorded checks ran against.\n\n5. Sibling path with the same failure class, out of the declared scope: the owner ruling in the issue is \"pixar ... should not be its own licensor\", yet the sibling RPC's tests still pin a Pixar-named heading — `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_properties_source_purpose.sql:30` requires `'Pixar - Creative (DCP Vault)'` and `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_properties_opa_groups.sql:455` expects 64 rows named `presentation_licensor_name = 'Pixar - Submissions (OPA)'`. The #3539 scope block (quoted in this conversation) writes only `function api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory`, and the retained migration comment states `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties is unchanged and remains the Property Matching contract` (`supabase/migrations/20260925174850_scraped_source_inventory_pixar_disney_dcpvault_licensor.sql:1453`), so this does not block this PR — but it should be raised to the owner as an unresolved sibling instance rather than assumed covered.\n\nLow / residual unknowns I could not close\n\n6. Paging consumer risk is unproven but still unexamined: `licensor_key` and `row_key` genuinely are untouched (row key shape at `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:156-158`), yet two *different* `licensor_name` labels now fall under one group key — `'Disney - Submissions (OPA)'` and `'Disney (Pixar) - Submissions (OPA)'` both map to `licensor_group_key` `disney` (new migration `:648-650`, `:668-670`). Whether the Scraped Properties page renders one Disney Submissions section or two is a frontend fact (`data.designflow.app`, not in this repository) and is therefore unverified. The docs claim the page groups by key, never by splitting label text (`docs/db-data-admin-scraped-properties.md:20-23`), which is consistent, but that is a documentation assertion, not proof of the rendered page.\n\n7. Production row counts (237 / 18 / 70 quoted in the issue) and the claim that no 20th Century or other `*_dcpvault` row is currently affected are author-supplied numbers; I have no database access. Absence of such rows is not evidence that finding 1 is moot — the code path exists and is reachable by the arm's own logic.\n\n## Mandatory checks\n\n1. Index usage. The change introduces no new table predicate and no new join: every added line is a `CASE` branch over `s.licensor_key` and `s.source_system` inside the `keyed` CTE, which operates on the unioned `source_rows` result (new migration `:648-671` in the property arm, mirrored at `:1158`/`:1177` and `:1365`/`:1384`), plus label strings. Such expressions cannot use an index and need none. The paging predicate stays `k.row_key collate \"C\" > v_cursor_key` over a derived text key (`:846`-ish filter region as quoted in `patch.diff`) — no index exists or can exist for that. The inherited joins into `dcp_current_resolution`, `dcp_member_count` and `dcp_scope_summary` are against `as materialized` CTEs (the same declarations carried over from `supabase/migrations/20260917144950_db_data_admin_inventory_coke_wwe_peanuts_sesame_sections.sql:48-58` for the function header), not base tables. The one inherited base-table predicate I could see is the member-fingerprint lateral over `plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution_member` on `resolution_id`; I did not verify an index on that column and my tool budget ended before I could. To the extent this is a real index question it is pre-existing and not introduced here; I am reporting the coverage gap rather than asserting coverage. Index evidence I did open is unrelated to this function (`idx_marvel_dcp_property_core` on `core_property_id`, `supabase/migrations/20260814010000_dcp_studio_separated_landing.sql:5009-5010`), so I do not treat it as serving anything here.\n\n2. Function volatility. `stable` is correct for this body, which only reads tables and calls the gate (`perform app.require_licensing_manager_access()`); the identical declaration exists in the derived-from body (`supabase/migrations/20260917144950_db_data_admin_inventory_coke_wwe_peanuts_sesame_sections.sql:56`) and the live object's volatility is asserted at runtime by `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:197` (`p.provolatile = 's'`) with `security definer` and pinned `search_path` asserted at `:195-200` and `:202-208`. No looser-than-body marker found. The change does not touch any other function's volatility, and `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties` is not modified by this diff.\n\n3. Exact object checks. The function is asserted by exact signature, not by name: `'api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory(text,text,text,integer)'::regprocedure` (`supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:19-21`) with catalog assertions on `prosecdef`/`provolatile` (`:195-200`), `proconfig` (`:202-208`) and ACL text (`:210-222`), and the sibling is asserted exactly via `to_regprocedure('api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text,text,integer)')` (`:227-229`). Residual weaknesses worth noting rather than blocking: the ACL assertion is substring-based on `proacl` (`:213`), so it pins the named roles but not the exact ACL set; and the column/heading prerequisites of the new fallback are asserted only as string matches against `pg_get_functiondef` (`:86-98`), never against the four `*_dcpvault` source-system values the fallback depends on — which is precisely where finding 1 lives.\n\nRole, permission and boundary changes: none. The migration re-issues the same pair as its predecessor, `revoke all ... from public, anon, service_role` / `grant execute ... to authenticated` (`supabase/migrations/20260925174850_scraped_source_inventory_pixar_disney_dcpvault_licensor.sql:1455-1456`, identical to `supabase/migrations/20260917144950_db_data_admin_inventory_coke_wwe_peanuts_sesame_sections.sql:1468-1469`), and the test's forbidden-pattern list still passes with the new grouping because the conflict keys are never directly mapped (`supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:101-110`).\n\nMigration immutability: the new version `20260925174850` appears in exactly one migration file (grep for the version returns only this file plus `.agent/work` and handoff prose), and the migration declares `-- derived-from: 20260917144950` (`supabase/migrations/20260925174850_scraped_source_inventory_pixar_disney_dcpvault_licensor.sql:3`) which exists as the prior body. I could not verify that the version is not backdated behind the base branch's newest applied version — that requires git/ledger access I do not have (`scripts/check-sql.sh:212-286` performs that comparison from git), so the check-sql claim in `.agent/work/3539/2/completion.json:25-33` is unverified here. No collision protection gap was found by inspection.\n\nRollback and recovery: the migration is a `create or replace function` plus `comment on` plus a revoke/grant pair; there is no data change and no destructive statement in the diff, so a partial failure leaves either the previous body (replace failed) or the new body fully applied. No rollback-down migration is provided, which matches the derived-from pattern. I did not find a sidecar at `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925174850.json` in that directory listing, and `config/production-verification-sidecar-registry.json` (read in full) declares no entry for that version; `scripts/check_production_verification_sidecars.py:58-69` only demands a sidecar when the migration contains dynamic execution markers, and the detector blanks `grant/revoke ... execute` (`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1595-1599`), so the absence is consistent with the only marker in this file being `grant execute ... to authenticated` at `:1456`. REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\nProvisional: REVISE — the regrouping logic itself looks right, but the acceptance evidence shipped with it is contradictory and the completion artifact is bound to a different commit.\n\nEvidence base: `.ai-review-deepseek-.../patch.diff`, `identity.json`, `MANIFEST.md` in this conversation, plus files I opened with tools: `supabase/migrations/20260925223300_scraped_source_inventory_pixar_disney_dcpvault_licensor.sql`, `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql`, `docs/db-data-admin-scraped-properties.md`, `.agent/work/3539/3/completion.json`, `.agent/work/3539/3/contract.json`, and the cited supporting migrations. No tests were run (MANIFEST §5), and I have no git or database access.\n\n## Findings\n\n### High\n\n1. The new behavioural assertion contradicts the code it is guarding, and contradicts the docs. `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:304-310` raises unless **every** row with `source_system = 'disney_dcpvault'` has `licensor_group_key = 'disney'`. But `plm.dcp_property.source_system` is pinned to `disney_dcpvault` (`supabase/migrations/20260814010000_dcp_studio_separated_landing.sql:37-38`, validated at `:48`; default at `supabase/migrations/20260811050000_dcp_vault_metadata_landing.sql:699`), while the same arm derives `licensor_key` from authority first: `when x.authority_status = 'direct_lucasfilm' then 'lucasfilm-star-wars'` / `'direct_marvel' then 'marvel'` (`20260925223300...sql:309-312`) and those keys win over the new source-system fallback, which is deliberately last (`:635-652`, `:656-673`). Authority can legitimately be non-Disney for such a row — the assertion text itself is `'direct_' || r.contract_asserted_studio_code` guarded only by `mc.member_count > 0` (visible in the same migration's property arm, and identical in the derived-from body). So on any database where a `plm.dcp_property` row resolves to authoritative Marvel or Lucasfilm scope, this test raises while the code is behaving as designed. Either the invariant must be narrowed (assert only that no such row is `unresolved`, which is what finding (b) at `:293-301` already does) or the code must change the precedence for `disney_dcpvault`. The two cannot both stand.\n\n2. The documentation states the source system wins regardless of authority, which is false under the shipped precedence — and the same document says the opposite three paragraphs earlier. `docs/db-data-admin-scraped-properties.md:34-36` (\"Rows with `source_system` `disney_dcpvault` group to Disney … regardless of mapping authority status\") versus `docs/db-data-admin-scraped-properties.md:24-26` (\"DCP Vault rows under authoritative Marvel scope … belong to Marvel\"). Both are presented as current rules in the same section heading (`:18`). Only the second is what `20260925223300...sql:635-652` implements. This is not a style note: the issue's acceptance text is phrased the same absolute way (\"A row from `source_system` `disney_dcpvault` groups to Disney\"), so a reader of the doc cannot tell which rule the product actually has.\n\n3. The \"positive control\" is vacuous — the test cannot detect absence of the data it claims to prove. `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:303-310` is an `exists(... where source_system='disney_dcpvault' and group <> 'disney')` negative assertion; there is no `count(*) > 0` (or equivalent) assertion that any `disney_dcpvault` row was returned at all. `.agent/work/3539/3/completion.json:42` nevertheless records it as \"positive control that disney_dcpvault rows group to disney\". Likewise the Pixar assertion (`:284-290`) and the unresolved assertion (`:293-301`) both pass trivially if the arms return zero rows of those classes, or if the walk returns an empty page. A positive control that only fires when rows are present is not a control.\n\n### Medium\n\n4. The completion record's checks are bound to a commit that is not the reviewed head. `.agent/work/3539/3/completion.json:12` records `\"head_sha\": \"d27384711eb0e3687364c873845606a9f7324760\"`, while the authoritative head is `f104888f2f6d7e9a66d11dc6dd81956f946f766f` (`MANIFEST.md` §2) and the head subject there is \"Add agent work contract pair for issue #3539\". The three `exit_code: 0` check records (`completion.json:22-37`) therefore do not attest to the tree under review — including the \"no migration sorts before … 20260925193145\" claim (`:26`), which is the very guard that would have to hold for the renamed version. The file inventory at `completion.json:13-17` also omits the two `.agent/work` files that are in fact part of this change (`MANIFEST.md` §3).\n\n5. The `*_dcpvault` fallback's premises are pinned only as definition text, never against the objects. The tests assert the SQL string literals (`supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:96-99`) and that the function emits grouping for three arms (`:81-88`, `:90-106`), but nothing asserts that the four literals correspond to values actually stored in `plm.dcp_property` / `plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property` / `plm.marvel_dcp_property` / `plm.twentieth_century_dcp_property` or in the six `*_dcp_{character,style_guide}` tables. I verified those constraints only in the landing migrations, not from this PR: `20260814010000_dcp_studio_separated_landing.sql:29-50` (Disney set), `:411`, `:2147`, `:3244`, `:4980`, `:6233`, `:7813` (`source_system` defaults/checks per studio). That is a checked-by-hand fact, not an assertion in the repository, and the mandatory exact-object bar is not met by text matching alone.\n\n6. `source_table` allow-list vs. the twentieth-century arm (conditional, needs one more check). The only allow-list I could open is `supabase/migrations/20260830130345_opa_authority_for_dcp_creative.sql:116-122`, which permits `plm.dcp_property`, `plm.lucasfilm_dcp_property`, `plm.marvel_dcp_property` only — it does not permit `plm.twentieth_century_dcp_property`, which the twentieth-century arm joins on (`20260925223300...sql`, the `r.source_table = 'plm.twentieth_century_dcp_property'` clause in the 20th-century arm). If that list still governs, that branch can never match and the new `twentieth_century_dcpvault` grouping is exercised only through `dcpvault:%` ids. I did not search later migrations for a widening, so this is an unmet check, not a proven defect. It is also inherited from `20260917144950...`, i.e. pre-existing.\n\n7. Declared-but-absent work artifacts. The generation-3 contract declares `.agent/work/3539/2/contract.json` and `.agent/work/3539/2/completion.json` in both `allowed_paths` and `file_writes` (`.agent/work/3539/3/contract.json` in `patch.diff`), but `list_dir .agent/work/3539` returns only `3/`, and `MANIFEST.md` §3 lists only the `3/` pair as added. Either the generation-2 pair was never committed or it was removed; the contract's own file list is not satisfied by the delivered change.\n\n### Low / residual unknowns (unverified, not disproven)\n\n8. Two distinct `licensor_name` values now land in one group: `'Disney - Submissions (OPA)'` (`20260925223300...sql:277`) and `'Disney (Pixar) - Submissions (OPA)'` (`:275`, `:283`) both map to `licensor_group_key = 'disney'` (`:637`, `:658`). `docs/db-data-admin-scraped-properties.md:20-23` asserts the page groups by key so a licensor shows exactly one section; the rendering lives outside this repository. The issue's acceptance line \"No section named Pixar\" therefore cannot be closed from this diff.\n\n9. Sibling instances of the same failure class, out of the declared scope (the issue's scope block writes only `function api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory`; the migration comment at `20260925223300...sql:1459` states `api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties` is unchanged and remains the Property Matching contract):\n   - `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_properties_source_purpose.sql:30` still requires the heading `'Pixar - Creative (DCP Vault)'`.\n   - `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_properties_opa_groups.sql:455` still expects 64 rows with `presentation_licensor_name = 'Pixar - Submissions (OPA)'`.\n   - The sibling's own definition still emits those labels (`supabase/migrations/20260911170526_scraped_properties_page_asset_context.sql:249`, `:257`, `:295`, `:353`, `:414`; earlier shapes at `20260826200252_scraped_properties_evidence_contract.sql:230`, `:238`).\n   - Every migration file named `*_scraped_source_inventory*.sql` before this one still contains the old `'Pixar - …'` labels (`20260911221304...:280`, `:288`, `:325`, `:385`, `:447`, `:812`, `:818`, and the intermediate generations). Those are historical and correctly untouched, but the sibling RPC is a live one and was not raised as a follow-up in the change itself.\n   - I could not verify whether the sibling also still routes `*_dcpvault` rows into `unresolved`; that needs its body, which is not in this diff.\n\n10. Untrusted evidence I did not verify and do not treat as fact: the claim that claim #3546's missing reservation was repaired by PR #3581 (a git-ref fact; `scripts/check-migration-pr-lease.mjs:100` reads `refs/db-claims/<version>`, and I cannot read refs), the Blacksmith failure report \"all 429 migrations into an empty database applied 363\", the production counts (237/18/70) in the issue body, and the authenticated production page check. The supplied PR-comment verdicts are non-authorizing by their own text.\n\n## Mandatory whole-class checks\n\n1. Index usage. No index can serve the change and none is needed: every added line is a `CASE` branch over derived CTE columns (`s.licensor_key`, `s.source_system`) plus label strings (`20260925223300...sql:649-652`, `:670-673`, `:1157-1160`, `:1178-1181`, `:1366-1369`, `:1387-1390`), and the paging predicate is over a derived jsonb text key (`:693`). Inherited base-table predicates and their real index coverage: `m.resolution_id = t.resolution_id` (`:747`, `:784`, `:796`) is served by the leading column of the primary key `(resolution_id, submission_source_system, submission_source_table, submission_source_id)` (`20260907200221_single_creative_submission_resolution_ledger.sql:161-162`); the non-`dcpvault` resolution lookup `t.source_system = … and t.source_table = … and t.source_property_id = …` (`:753-755`) is served by `dcp_opa_property_resolution_identity_version_key` `(source_system, source_table, source_property_id, decision_version)` (`20260830130345...:110-111`). The loose assumption to call out explicitly: the `dcpvault:%` branch `t.source_property_id = k.identity_key` (`:751-752`) filters on a column that is not the leading column of that unique key (nor of the `resolution_id` PK), and my grep for any `create … index` on `plm.dcp_opa_property_resolution` returned no matches, so no index serves it as written; `approval_status in ('approved','rejected')` (`:750`) similarly has no supporting index I could find. Both are byte-inherited from `20260917144950_db_data_admin_inventory_coke_wwe_peanuts_sesame_sections.sql` (same `distinct on` shape at `:752`, same `t.source_property_id = k.identity_key` at `:774`), so this is a pre-existing coverage gap, not a regression introduced here.\n\n2. Function volatility. `api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory` is declared `stable` (`20260925223300...sql:26`), which is correct: the body only reads tables and calls the gate (`:39`); `IMMUTABLE` would be wrong and `VOLATILE` would be looser than the body. The gate it calls is itself `stable` (`20260814000000_licensing_manager_gate.sql:33`) over `app.has_role` / `app.has_explicit_app_access`, both `stable` (`20260621150815_app_core.sql:368`, `20260722002500_db_data_admin_foundation.sql:8`). The declared volatility is runtime-asserted at `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:203-208`. No function's volatility is loosened or touched by this change.\n\n3. Exact object checks. Present and genuinely exact: the function by full signature, not by name (`supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:23-24`), `prosecdef`/`provolatile` from `pg_proc` (`:203-208`), pinned `search_path` (`:210-216`), ACL text (`:218-230`), and the sibling by exact `to_regprocedure('api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text,text,integer)')` (`:235`). Gaps: the ACL assertion is substring-based on `proacl` (`:218-223`), so it pins named roles rather than the exact ACL set; the PUBLIC-exclusion branch at `:225-230` is only entered when `'=X/'` is present, so it tests one shape; the behavioural block opens with `api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory(v_kind, null, v_cursor, 1000)` (`:278`) which is a call, not an object check, so a wrong-arity sibling would fail at runtime; and — per finding 5 — the four `source_system` literals the new rule depends on are asserted only as text inside `pg_get_functiondef`, never against the `plm.*` columns or their check constraints that actually guarantee those values (`20260814010000_dcp_studio_separated_landing.sql:29-50`, `:411`, `:2147`, `:3244`, `:4980`, `:6233`, `:7813`; `20260811050000_dcp_vault_metadata_landing.sql:699`, `:751`). One further prerequisite is unasserted: the test fixture assumes an active `app.profile` with `auth_user_id` and a `licensing` role plus `plm` app access (`supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:260-273`) matching the gate's requirement (`20260814000000_licensing_manager_gate.sql:37-46`, `20260722002500_db_data_admin_foundation.sql:12-18`); the tables exist with the right uniqueness (`20260621150815_app_core.sql:26-44`), but the fixture's writes are unverified here (the transaction does end in `rollback;` at `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:318`).\n\nRoles, permissions, boundaries: unchanged by this diff — `revoke all … from public, anon, service_role` / `grant execute … to authenticated` (`20260925223300...sql:1462-1463`) reproduces the previous generation (`20260917144950...:1468-1469`), gate and pinned `search_path` preserved (`:27-28`, `:39`), no new policy, role, or grant. Verified positives: all four `*_dcpvault` systems are covered in all three arms (`:649-652`, `:1157-1160`, `:1366-1369`), Pixar groups to Disney in all three arms (`:637`, `:1145`, `:1354`) with `licensor_key` still emitted as `'pixar'` / `'pixar-opa'` (`:312`, `:372`, `:433`) and the `row_key` shape unchanged (`:630-632`, character and style-guide arms likewise), and the stale test comment was corrected (`supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:61`). Migration immutability and rollback: I found no modification to an existing migration in `MANIFEST.md` §3, the `derived-from: 20260917144950` target exists, and the migration is pure `create or replace` + `comment` + revoke/grant with no data change, so a partial failure leaves the prior body; the version-collision/backdating claim rests on the stale-head completion record (finding 4) and on git I cannot read, so it stays unverified.\n\n## Verdict\n\nTwo blocking items are concrete and evidence-backed: the new test asserts an invariant the shipped code does not implement and the docs contradict themselves about it (findings 1-3), and the completion record's checks belong to a different commit (finding 4). The core regrouping is correct, but it cannot be approved on evidence that does not describe this head and that would go red on the very data the change is about.\n\nVERDICT: REVISE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\nProvisional verdict: APPROVE — the code change implements the stated absolute source-system precedence in all three arms, keeps `licensor_key`/`row_key` untouched, and ships a synthetic test that genuinely evaluates the installed CASE; the open items below are evidence-binding, scope and pre-existing issues, not demonstrated code defects.\n\nEvidence base: the head file `supabase/migrations/20260925223300_scraped_source_inventory_pixar_disney_dcpvault_licensor.sql` (read at :1-40, :625-700, :1136-1152, :1345-1362, plus greps), `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql` (read in full, 445 lines), `docs/db-data-admin-scraped-properties.md` (:1-98), `supabase/migrations/20260814000000_licensing_manager_gate.sql` (full), `20260621150815_app_core.sql` (:1-60, :340-410), `20260722002500_db_data_admin_foundation.sql` (:1-25), `20260814010000_dcp_studio_separated_landing.sql` (:1-70 + greps), `20260830130345_opa_authority_for_dcp_creative.sql` (greps), `20260907200221_single_creative_submission_resolution_ledger.sql` (greps), the sealed `.ai-review-deepseek-4a975bcf1ae8137ff6ab5e84/MANIFEST.md` + `identity.json` + `patch.diff`, and `.agent/work/3539/4/contract.json` / `completion.json`. No tests were run, and I have no git refs, no DB, no network.\n\n## Findings\n\n### High — none demonstrated\n\nThe two behaviours this change exists to deliver are implemented and asserted:\n\n- Absolute source-system precedence is present as the first clauses of each grouping CASE, before any `licensor_key` branch: property `20260925223300_...sql:635-638`, character `:1143-1146`, style guide `:1352-1355`; names mirrored at `:656-659`, `:1164-1167`, `:1373-1376`. The `else 'unresolved'` / `'Licensor not yet determined'` fallbacks remain last (`:653`, `:674`).\n- Pixar stays Disney: `:641`, `:662` (property), `:1149`, `:1170` (character), `:1358`, `:1379` (style guide); labels say `Disney (Pixar) - …` at `:275`, `:283`, `:320`, `:380`, `:442` and the character arm at `:1032`, `:1038`. No bare `Pixar - …` label remains in this migration (repo-wide grep for `Pixar - ` hits only older migrations and the sibling's tests — see the sibling finding).\n- Row identity is unchanged: `row_key` is still `jsonb_build_array('<kind>', s.licensor_key, s.source_system, s.source_table, s.source_id)` (`:630-632`, `:1138-1140`, `:1347-1349`), and `licensor_key` literals (`'pixar'`, `'pixar-opa'`, `'dcp-vault-non-authoritative-marvel-tag'`) are untouched (`:312`, `:372`, `:433`).\n- The prior round's doc/test contradiction is gone: `docs/db-data-admin-scraped-properties.md:23-27` and `:34-39` now state DCP-Vault-by-source-system with no \"authoritative Marvel scope wins\" sentence, and `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:61` no longer claims Pixar is a separate licensor.\n\n### Medium\n\n1. Sibling instance of the same failure class, out of the declared scope. `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_properties_source_purpose.sql:30` still requires the heading `'Pixar - Creative (DCP Vault)'`, `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_properties_opa_groups.sql:455` still expects 64 rows with `presentation_licensor_name = 'Pixar - Submissions (OPA)'`, and the sibling definition still emits those labels (`supabase/migrations/20260911170526_scraped_properties_page_asset_context.sql:249`, `:257`, `:295`, `:353`, `:414`; also `supabase/migrations/20260830172356_scraped_properties_source_purpose.sql:124`, `:142`). The issue's acceptance \"No section named Pixar\" is therefore not satisfied repository-wide by this PR; `.agent/work/3539/4/contract.json` writes only `function api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory`, so this is reported for the owner rather than treated as a blocker here.\n2. Version reservation is unverifiable with my tools. Filename uniqueness holds (no other migration file carries `20260925223300`, and no migration file carries a 2026-09-26..29 timestamp per grep), and the derived-from target exists (`supabase/migrations/20260917144950_db_data_admin_inventory_coke_wwe_peanuts_sesame_sections.sql:48`, `:1465`, `:1468-1469`). But the permanent claim ref cannot be read: `scripts/recover-3539-reservation.mjs:7` shows only a repair *script* moving `20260925174850` to `20260925223300` for issue 3539/claim 3546/PR 3557, while `.agent/work/3539/4/completion.json:40` asserts the ref exists \"following merged repair PR #3581\" — author-supplied.\n3. The completion record's checks do not describe this head byte-for-byte. `.agent/work/3539/4/completion.json:12` records `head_sha` `2cafea34a6813a4603dbdda7a312be5ba9f8c1db` while the reviewed head is `1c3b715c…` (MANIFEST §2, subject \"Record corrected issue 3539 generation 4 evidence\"), and `files_changed` (`completion.json:13-17`) omits the two `.agent/work/3539/4/*` files this same change adds (MANIFEST §3). The extractor is fail-closed but brittle. `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:280-317` anchors each arm by literal `s.*,`, then `case` within 30 characters, then `end::text as licensor_group_key`, raising if any anchor is missing. ACL assertion is substring-based: `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:218-230` uses `position('authenticated=X' in v_acl)` and enters the PUBLIC-exclusion branch only when `'=X/'` is present, so it pins named roles rather than the exact ACL set. Index usage. The change introduces no new table predicate and no new join: every added line is a `CASE` branch over `s.source_system` / `s.licensor_key` plus label strings (`20260925223300_...sql:634-675`, `:1142-1183`, `:1351-1392`), and the migration adds no `CREATE INDEX` (only `create or replace function`, `comment on function`, revoke/grant at `:18-29`, `:1459`, `:1462-1463`). Function volatility. `api.db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory` is declared `stable` (`20260925223300_...sql:26`), `security definer` with `search_path` pinned to `app, public` (`:27-28`); its body only reads tables and calls the gate (`:39`). `stable` is exactly right — `immutable` would be wrong for table reads, `volatile` would be looser than the body. Supporting chain is also stable: `app.require_licensing_manager_access` (`20260814000000_licensing_manager_gate.sql:33`), `app.has_role` (`20260621150815_app_core.sql:365-381`), `app.has_explicit_app_access` (`20260722002500_db_data_admin_foundation.sql:5-19`). Runtime assertion at `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:203-208` (`p.provolatile = 's'`). No other function's volatility is touched.\n3. Exact object checks. Signature is asserted by type list, not name (`supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:23-24`), with catalog assertions on `prosecdef`/`provolatile` (`:203-208`), `proconfig` (`:210-216`) and ACL (`:218-230`); the sibling is asserted by exact `to_regprocedure('api.db_data_admin_scraped_properties(text,text,integer)')` (`:235`); the twelve landing tables are asserted by `regclass` plus a validated check constraint (`:346-373`). Roles, permissions, boundaries: unchanged. `revoke all … from public, anon, service_role` then `grant execute … to authenticated` (`:1462-1463`), same pair as the derived-from generation (`20260917144950_...sql:1468-1469`); no new role, policy or grant; gate and pinned `search_path` preserved. Confirmed the executable test block's fixture writes are inside `begin; … rollback;` (`supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory.sql:1`, `:396-400`, `:445`) and reuses the house pattern (e.g. `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_property_status_api.sql:17`).\n5. Migration immutability and rollback: no existing migration is modified (MANIFEST §3 shows only `M` on docs and the test, `A` on the three new files); the migration is pure `create or replace function` + `comment` + revoke/grant with no data DDL and no destructive statement, so partial failure leaves either the prior body or the fully applied new body; no down-migration, matching the derived-from pattern. Rollback preserves the prior capability because the replaced body is the whole change and `licensor_key`/`row_key` are unchanged.\n6. Non-vacuous coverage. The behavioural block's assertions are negative existence checks (`:410-437`) and would pass on an empty database; the requirement to be non-vacuous in an empty database is met instead by `:252-342`, which extracts each installed arm's actual group CASE from `pg_get_functiondef` and *executes* it against literal rows including a contradicting known `licensor_key` (`v_conflicting_keys = array['marvel','disney','disney','disney']`, `:262`, executed `:319-341`), plus a real Pixar clause test using `disney_opa`/`pixar-opa` (`:336-340`). Actual-row pagination is retained: `:402-442` walks pages by `next_cursor` for all three kinds with `source_system`/group checks per page.\n\n## Unverified, with the missing evidence named\n\n- Claim/reservation refs (`refs/db-claims/20260925223300`) and the PR #3581 repair — git refs I cannot read.\n- The `check-sql.sh` version-order/ledger guard: `completion.json:26-33` states it did not run locally; the Blacksmith CI failure comments in the brief are author-supplied.\n- Whether the remaining ~1400 lines of the migrated body are byte-preserved against `20260917144950`. I compared the header, all three `keyed` CASE pairs, attributes, `comment on function` and grants only; the derived-from file exists (`20260917144950_...sql:48`, `:1465`, `:1468-1469`) and the size delta is consistent with the added CASE lines plus a shorter header, but that is corroboration, not proof.\n- Production row counts (237/18/70) and the authenticated production page check: author-supplied.\n- `supabase/tests/db_data_admin_scraped_source_inventory_calls.sql`: I saw only grep hits (`:36-40`); I did not open it, so any claim about its runtime assertions is out of my evidence.\n\n## Conclusion\n\nNo defect is demonstrated in the reviewed change: the grouping logic matches the specified rule in all three arms, identity and permissions are preserved, the mandatory index/volatility/exact-object checks pass on the evidence I could open, and the earlier rounds' items (missing `twentieth_century_dcpvault`, absent executable proof, stale comment, self-contradicting docs/test, vacuous control labelling) are fixed. What remains is the out-of-scope sibling Pixar labels (finding 1), the unverifiable claim reservation and CI ledger (finding 2, item under \"Unverified\"), and the evidence-tail commit binding of the completion record (finding 3) — none of which is a defect in this diff, and the first two are enforced by their own gates rather than by this verdict. This verdict addresses the change and the repository evidence only; it does not attest the claim ref, the migration ledger run, or production state.\n\nVERDICT: APPROVE I also could not recompute the whole-source digest or the `refs/db-contracts/3555/2` sha256 (this review profile has no shell), and read access to `/home/ahazan/repos/ai-devops` was **denied**, so every cross-repository claim about `bin/ai-stepfun` and `ai-review-preflight` is UNVERIFIED here.\n**Provisional verdict: REVISE** — the in-repo mechanics are correct and fail closed, but one wrapper-keyed list the new reviewer depends on was not extended (and is outside this contract's `allowed_paths`), two in-repo \"every wrapper / every provider\" enumerations were not extended to the new object, and the activation evidence omits the doctor/preflight probe this repo's own gate runs.\n## Findings\n### High\n**H1. `ai-stepfun` was not added to `REVIEW_CALLER_VARIABLES`, and that file is outside the contract's `allowed_paths`.**\n`scripts/lib/reviewer-caller-env.mjs:15` maps eight wrappers to their caller variable — every wrapper used by a roster row *except* the new one. Its own header (`:1-14`) states the convention this repo relies on: \"Every credentialed reviewer wrapper (`ai-muse`, `ai-kimi`, …) refuses to run unless its own `AI_<PROVIDER>_CALLER` variable names the assistant driving it … it refuses BEFORE printing any check line.\"\nBoth launch paths for a drawn reviewer go through it:\n- `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2919` — `reviewerDoctor` spawns `ai-stepfun doctor` (`doctorSpawnPlan`, `:3323`) with `required:false`, so `reviewCallerEnvironment` returns `{}` (`reviewer-caller-env.mjs:41-42`) and no caller variable is set. If `ai-stepfun` follows the convention, the probe exits non-zero with no `PASS`/`FAIL` line → `unnamedDoctorFailure` (`:3317`) → `reviewerExecutionPreflight` throws \"this is a LOCAL dependency fault on this machine\" (`:6504-6507`). Every Linux draw of stepfun then burns an assignment/lease and needs `--release-failed-reviewer … --confirm-local-dependency-unfixable`.\n- `scripts/run-governed-review.mjs:824` — `prepareGovernedReview` calls it with `required:true`, whose whole purpose is to refuse early with \"Rerun with AI_STEPFUN_CALLER=claude\". For `ai-stepfun` that guard silently passes (no variable ⇒ no throw), so the actionable refusal is replaced by a later, misdiagnosed doctor fault. This is precisely the failure #2678 created the module to end (`:2913-2918`, `:3313-3316`).\nIf instead `ai-stepfun` takes no caller variable, the omission is benign but leaves stepfun as the only roster wrapper with no caller attribution — and nothing in this PR states which is true, and no test pins it. Either way this generation cannot fix it: `scripts/lib/reviewer-caller-env.mjs` is absent from `allowed_paths`/`file_writes` (`.agent/work/3555/2/contract.json:14-27,28-41`), which triggers the contract's own stop condition (\"stop if the change would need to touch a file outside allowed_paths\"). Repair: a generation-3 contract adding that file, the `'ai-stepfun':'AI_STEPFUN_CALLER'` entry (or recorded evidence that the wrapper takes none), plus a coverage test asserting every `ACTIVE_REVIEWERS` wrapper resolves a caller variable — no such invariant test exists today (`run-governed-review.test.mjs:800` only pins that an *unlisted* wrapper yields `{}`).\n**H2. The source-identity contract for `ai-stepfun` is asserted nowhere, although adding it to `GOVERNED_VERDICT_WRAPPERS` automatically makes it a \"qualified source wrapper\".**\n`scripts/run-governed-review.mjs:180` — `const SOURCE_WRAPPERS=new Set(GOVERNED_VERDICT_WRAPPERS)`. So `wrapperSourceContractArgs` (`:229-255`, called at `:457`) now appends `--base <mergeBase> --assert-head <headSha>` to `ai-stepfun`'s argv, the spawn exports `AI_REVIEW_SOURCE_RECEIPT_FILE` (`:479`), and after the review runs `validateSourceReceipt(receipt.read(), …)` (`:223-228`, called at `:503`) throws unless the wrapper wrote a receipt whose `identity.head/base/source_digest/repository` equal the trusted source.\nThe test whose title promises this coverage — `'all qualified wrappers receive immutable source arguments without rewriting prompt values'`, `scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs:22-23` — enumerates `['ai-claude-review','ai-codex-review','ai-gemini','ai-glm','ai-grok-review','ai-kimi','ai-muse','ai-qwen']` plus a separate `ai-deepseek-agent` loop (`:31`). It covered all nine previous qualified wrappers; it does not cover the tenth. Consequence if `ai-stepfun review` rejects `--base`/`--assert-head` or does not write the receipt: the reviewer runs, spends the draw and the lease, and the round dies post-hoc on \"wrapper source receipt is missing a complete packet digest\". The claim lives only in the contract's `assumptions` and in `completion.json`'s \"pinned by ai-devops tests/test-ai-stepfun.sh governed-receipt checks\" — unverifiable from this packet. Minimum in-repo repair (the file *is* allowed): drive that enumeration from `GOVERNED_VERDICT_WRAPPERS` instead of a hand-written list, so the next wrapper cannot be silently skipped.\n### Medium\n**M1. Activation evidence omits the probe this repo actually gates on.** The roster row (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:308-309`) and both doc entries (`docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md:512-520`, `docs/agents/anti-collision-summary.md:90-95`) record a live review of `94bf83c6` ending in a head-bound `VERDICT: REVISE …`, but no `ai-stepfun doctor` pass and no `ai-review-preflight usable` line showing `stepfun` ready on Linux. Mechanically, `start=(sequence-1)%ACTIVE_REVIEWERS.length` (`:6119`, also `:5655`, `:6875`) with a length that changed 5→6: on a machine where stepfun is unusable, sequence 6 wraps to index 0 and sequence 7 also starts at index 0, so the same durable sequence maps to different reviewers on different platforms and `grok-4.6` takes the wrapped draw plus the next one. No safety consequence — per-head provider exclusion and slot independence are untouched (`:6124`) — but the sentence should say the *counter* is shared while the *draw* is machine-dependent.\n### Checked and clean (no finding)\n- `SOURCE_WRAPPERS` derives from `GOVERNED_VERDICT_WRAPPERS` (`run-governed-review.mjs:180`), so no second wrapper list needed editing there.\n- `VERDICT_CONTRACT_FLAG_WRAPPERS` correctly *not* extended (`reviewer-capabilities.mjs:15`): `wrapperVerdictContractArgs` returns args unchanged for non-flag wrappers (`run-governed-review.mjs:334`), matching the recorded assumption that `ai-stepfun review` emits the head-bound line itself; the new test pins both the pass-through and the `ask`/`implement` refusal (`run-governed-review.test.mjs:925-929`), and `forbiddenGovernedSubcommand` fails closed on an unknown or absent subcommand (`reviewer-capabilities.mjs:38-51`, `'(none)'` branch).\n- `ENGINE_REVIEWER_EXCLUSION` needs no new key: `ENGINES` is exactly `{codex, claude, zcode}` (`scripts/lib/orchestrator-routing.mjs:71-104`), the key-for-key invariant test still holds (`…lanes.test.mjs:1595-1596`), and no active row declares `orchestratorEngine`, so `reviewersForOrchestrator` cannot exclude stepfun (`:678-684`) — matching the new test's `[null,'claude','codex']` loop.\n- Out-of-credit rows are real coverage, not decoration: the fixture drives the changed regex through `wrapperFailureReason` and asserts the human line reaches `REFUSED` verbatim with no private text (`run-governed-review.test.mjs:940-963`), and the fallback name map is exercised at `:965-970`.\n- Fail-closed behaviour on a machine whose preflight does not know stepfun: `reconcilePreflightRows` synthesizes `usable:false` rather than refusing the draw (`:717`), and `allocatableReviewers` skips admission validation for an already-unusable row (`:733-734`), so a malformed/absent stepfun row can neither block other reviewers nor be drawn. Worst case on Windows is a wasted draw plus a misleading \"local fault\" diagnosis (`:2911-2913` → `:6504-6507`), never an unrecordable verdict. Note `bin/ai-stepfun.cmd` exists in ai-devops (filename observed via glob; contents unreadable), so \"not on PATH\" is *not* the backstop there — the preflight verdict is the only platform gate, which is why M2(c)/M1 matter.\n- Roster/rotation tests are roster-generic and do exercise the sixth row through the stub: `…lanes.test.mjs:1004-1007`, `1018-1028`, `2605`, `2613`, `2755-2800` (including the new sixth capacity case and the `at(-1)` free-slot case), `2089`.\n- `parseReviewCursor`'s `reviewer=([a-z0-9.-]+)` grammar admits `stepfun-step-5-preview`; ref/lease naming is name-derived (`:5155`, `reviewActiveRef`), so no parser change was needed.\n- CI, not just the contract's `required_checks`, runs the roster-sensitive suites: `.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml:49` (lanes, run-governed-review, record-review-verdict) and `.github/workflows/pr-object-collision.yml:100` (lanes + reviewer-wire-budget).\n- `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs.json` legitimately unchanged: dispositions bind by `semantic_key = path:line_sha256:context-±2 significant lines` (`check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:40,80`), the inserted roster lines match no `PATTERN` term, and the nearest matching line is `:325` — far outside the ±2 window — so no context hash moved.\n- `docs/owner-rulings.md` records no reviewer-rotation rulings (no Kimi pause, no DeepSeek entry), so its omission here is consistent, not a gap. `AGENTS.md` carries no rotation list.\n## Brief sections\n**Roles and permission changes.** No grant, policy, role, or security boundary in this repository changes. The diff touches no workflow, no `.github/` file, no credential or secret handling; the only permission-relevant surface is the reviewer-draw policy, and it is *narrowed*, not widened: `ai-stepfun` joins an allowlist (`GOVERNED_SUBCOMMANDS`, `reviewer-capabilities.mjs:25`) whose semantics are \"only `review` may carry the governed prompt\", so `ask`/`implement` are newly refused for that wrapper (`run-governed-review.mjs:327-329`). The wrapper's own sandbox/approval posture (read/grep/find/ls under strict approval inside bubblewrap) lives in ai-devops and is UNVERIFIED here — read access was denied; nothing in this repo grants it new filesystem, network, or repository permission, and `readsRepository:true` only *permits recording* its verdicts (`:549-551`), which is the intended consequence of the owner instruction.\n**Objects and dependencies.** Exact objects the change depends on, all in-repo: `REVIEWERS`/`ACTIVE_REVIEWERS`/`RETIRED_REVIEWERS`/`QUARANTINED_REVIEWERS`/`OVERFLOW_REVIEWERS` (`:278-311,524,545,595-596`), `reviewerReadsRepository` (`:549`), `reviewerEmitsGovernedVerdict` (`:557`), `reviewersForOrchestrator` (`:678`), `allocatableReviewers`/`reconcilePreflightRows`/`reviewerAdmissionAllowed` (`:686-741`), `reviewerExecutionPreflight`/`reviewerDoctor`/`doctorSpawnPlan` (`:6490,2911,3323`), `assignNextReviewerOperation`/`replaceFailedReviewerOperation` (`:6119-6125,6874-6896`), `reviewerCapacityReport` (`:5575,5641`), `GOVERNED_VERDICT_WRAPPERS`/`VERDICT_CONTRACT_FLAG_WRAPPERS`/`GOVERNED_SUBCOMMANDS`/`wrapperBaseName`/`wrapperEmitsGovernedVerdict`/`forbiddenGovernedSubcommand`, `SOURCE_WRAPPERS`/`wrapperSourceContractArgs`/`wrapperVerdictContractArgs`/`wrapperSpawnPlan`/`promptHeadContract`/`validateSourceReceipt`, `OUT_OF_CREDIT_MACHINE_LINE`/`OUT_OF_CREDIT_PROVIDER_NAMES`/`outOfCreditReason`, and `REVIEW_CALLER_VARIABLES`/`reviewCallerEnvironment` (the one dependency the change *should* have touched — H1). Required external dependency stage, in order: ai-devops `bin/ai-stepfun` (merged `f1758c21`) and an `ai-review-preflight` that reports provider `stepfun` — the issue states the ai-devops mirror lands *after* this merges, so between merge and mirror the row is inert-but-safe (`preflight-no-row` ⇒ skipped). Declared scope matches the delivered diff exactly; no file outside `allowed_paths` was written, and the one file that *needs* writing is inside `allowed_paths` for the test half (H2) but not for the source half (H1).\n**Migration immutability.** Non-applicable, source-backed: the changed-file inventory contains no `supabase/migrations/**` path, no SQL, and no ledger or version-reservation file; `contract.json` declares `db_reads: []`, `db_writes: []` and `completion.json` declares `migration_versions: []`, consistent with `work_type: repo-maintenance` and the prohibited action \"do not touch any migration or database object\". No existing migration is modified, no version is reserved, and the collision-protection surfaces (`EXCLUSIVE_REFS` `:806-820`, claim/version reservation paths) are untouched by the diff.\n**Rollback and recovery.** Reverting the head commit restores the five-reviewer rotation with no database state to unwind: the roster is a frozen module constant, and the only durable state a stepfun draw creates is ordinary reviewer coordination refs (cursor/assignment/lease/verdict), which the existing release and reclaim paths already handle (`releaseFailedReviewer`, `--replace-failed-reviewer`, `reapAbandonedReviewLeases`). REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n## Evidence basis\n\nEverything below comes from the snapshot at head `318261d01efcde6245edfa418487841e9ff755d9`: I opened `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs` (all 416 lines), `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.test.mjs` (all 285 lines), `.github/workflows/tools-offline-tests.yml` (lines 230–334 plus `id: route`/`pure_prose` hits), `.agent/work/3398/2/{contract.json,completion.json}` in full, and compared against the sibling parser `scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs` (lines 120–200, 300–430, 540–600, 700–770, 880–1000), `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` (40–144), `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs` (18–75), `docs/agents/agent-work-contract-repo-maintenance-evidence.md` (50–95), and two real migrations. No shell, so no tests were executed.\n\nProvisional verdict (non-binding, stated early): REVISE.\n\n## 1. The suspected bug: confirmed, with mechanism\n\n`CREATE ROLE` with a double-spaced quoted name and a single-spaced quoted name do produce the same collision key.\n\nMechanism: whitespace is collapsed over the *whole* SQL text **before** any identifier is tokenized — `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:146` (`stripSqlComments(...).replace(/\\s+/g, ' ')`), reached from `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:201`. By the time the CREATE ROLE pattern at `:318` captures the identifier, `\"a  b\"` is already `\"a b\"`, so `roleCollisionKeys('create role \"a  b\";')` and `roleCollisionKeys('create role \"a b\";')` both return `['role \"a b\"']`. The identical collapse happens on the claim side at `:110` and `:113`, so `normalizeRoleClaim('role \"a  b\"')` also returns `role \"a b\"`.\n\nThis matters because it contradicts the module's own guarantee — `canonicalRoleName` at `:79-89` is written deliberately to preserve quoted case *and* any non-lowercase content, and invariant (1) at `:27-30` says \"NO ALIASES … Every role name is its own exact identity\"; the pre-collapse makes that promise unreachable. The repository's own convention says the same thing in words: \"Split into identifier parts WITHOUT destroying whitespace inside a quoted identifier (`\"Weird Name\"` is one legal Postgres name)\" — `scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:330-331`, restated at `:416-417`. Tabs and newlines inside a quoted identifier alias the same way.\n\nDirection of harm, stated precisely: two distinct PostgreSQL roles share one identity, so the tool reports conflicts between roles that are distinct (over-blocking) and cannot represent such a role at all. It is not a path to a missed collision, and I do not claim it is.\n\nTwo readings of the suspect, to be unambiguous: whitespace *between* tokens (`create  role  \"x\"` vs `create role \"x\"`) collapsing to one key is **correct** (same statement) and not a defect. Whitespace *inside* the quoted identifier is the defect above. No test covers it — the identity test only exercises `\"a\"\"b\"` (`scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.test.mjs:20-28`).\n\n## 2. Mandatory checklist\n\n**Index usage.** Non-applicable, source-backed: this change adds no SQL object, predicate or join. The diff touches no `supabase/` path (patch inventory; `.agent/work/3398/2/completion.json:7` records `\"migration_versions\": []`), and the module is explicitly pure/offline text analysis (`scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:40`). The only set/ordering structure is the dedup `Set` and final sort in `roleCollisionKeys` (`:393`, `:406`) — no index assumption to be loose about. No finding.\n\n**Function volatility.** Non-applicable, same basis: the change creates/modifies no database function, so there is no volatility marker to judge. `create function` appears only as a regex alternative at `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:361` and as a test fixture at `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.test.mjs:238`. No finding.\n\n**Exact object checks.** Applicable here as *exact role identity*, and it fails in several places — see H1 above and M2/M3/L1/L2 below. Note the one existence-only assertion is the CI file-presence probe (`tests-offline-tests.yml:332-333`), which is immediately followed by running the suite and mirrors the neighbouring steps (`:223-233`, `:244-246`), so it is not a finding.\n\n## 3. Findings\n\n### Blocking\n\n**B1 (H1). Quoted-identifier internal whitespace is aliased into one collision key.** `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:146`, `:110`, `:113`, `:318-321`, `:403-406`; promise broken at `:27-30`, `:79-89`. Untested (`test:20-28`).\n\n**B2. The fail-closed refusal fires on a migration already on main, so the announced integration is not usable as written.** `roleCollisionKeys` throws before extraction (`scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:391`, `:278-285`) whenever a hidden single-quoted string *starts* with `<verb> <role|user|group>` (`:250`). `supabase/migrations/20260621151419_crm_rls_realtime.sql:57` contains exactly that: `execute 'alter role authenticator set pgrst.db_schemas = ' || quote_literal(...)`. Integrating the helper as the PR describes (`#3398` outcome: the claim validator and collision parser import it) therefore hard-refuses a benign migration that is already merged, and the PR supplies no consumer contract for that refusal and no test or evidence over any real migration — the fixtures are hand-written, and the \"real-world shape\" fixture (`test:260-269`) even inverts reality: migration `20260911210709` declares its four roles at top level (`supabase/migrations/20260911210709_hts_rag_shared_schema_least_privilege_roles.sql:64-67`), not inside a `do $$ … $$` block. The completion record's coverage claim (`completion.json:18-23`) does not reach this case. Either the refusal semantics or the integration story needs a decision before merge.\n\n### Major\n\n**M1. The \"fail closed\" guarantee has openings; the code's own test covers only the closed half.** Only single-quoted literals are scanned (`scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:207-211`, `:270-275`), and a refusal requires the role verb to begin a `;`-delimited segment (`:246-256`).\n- Split concatenation evades it: `EXECUTE 'alter ' || 'role ' || quote_ident(r) || ' nologin'` yields three hidden strings that individually match nothing → no refusal and no keys. The test at `test:209-212` uses the *unsplit* form `execute 'alter role ' || …`, so it passes while the split form silently misses a dynamic role mutation.\n- Dollar-quoted dynamic SQL is classified `dollar-body` and never re-scanned (`:202-206`), and `findDynamicRoleMutations` filters to `kind === 'string-literal'` (`:273`). `EXECUTE $q$create role %I$q$` (or `format($q$create role %I$q$, …)`) therefore produces neither a refusal nor, since `%I` is not an `IDENT` (`:48`, `:318`), a key. That is a silent miss of a dynamic role mutation, contradicting invariant (4) (`:34-38`) and the contract's own stop condition (`.agent/work/3398/2/contract.json:47`).\n\n**M2. The keyword filter silently drops legitimate role names on membership/ownership paths while the create path keeps them — and can drop the whole operation.** `roleNamesFrom` (`:232-240`) and `pushOwnership` (`:128-129`) lowercase-strip the name and discard anything in `NON_ROLE_KEYWORDS` (`:55-63`, which includes `user`, `group`, `role`, `set`, `all`, `select`, `update`, `execute`, `usage`, …). `grant \"user\" to app` and `grant \"select\" to app` therefore produce *no* operation: `members` is emptied and the `members.length && grantees.length` gate (`:348`, `:355`) drops the statement, so even the grantee is unreserved — while `create role \"user\"` still yields `role user` (`:318-321`). A real membership write to a keyword-named role is thus unaccounted, and the same role has two different identities depending on which statement mentions it.\n\n**M3. Phantom role identities invented from SQL that names no role (invariant (3), `:32-33`).** The verb alternation `(?:role|user|group)` swallows `user` in the foreign-data-wrapper forms, so:\n- `CREATE USER MAPPING …` → key `role mapping` via `:318`;\n- `DROP USER MAPPING IF EXISTS …` → key `role mapping` via `:324`;\n- `ALTER USER MAPPING …` → alter op on `mapping` via `:333`.\nAnd `ALTER ROLE ALL SET …` produces a `role all` key via `:333-341` even though `all` is itself listed as a non-role word at `:58`. These assert objects that are not roles, i.e. false conflicts, and none of them is tested.\n\n### Minor\n\n**L1. Comment stripping is not double-quote aware, silently dropping real role keys.** `stripSqlComments` (`:149-192`) copies quoted identifiers verbatim while applying `--` and `/* */` handling everywhere, so `create role \"a--b\";` truncates at the `--`, leaves an unterminated `\"`, matches no `IDENT`, and yields no key and no error. Same class, pre-existing, in the parser the module claims to reuse verbatim (`scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:142-185`). No test.\n\n**L2. `IDENT` is relaxed relative to the parser's own token.** `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:48` uses `\"(?:[^\"]|\"\")*\"` where `scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:187` uses `+`. Consequence: `create role \"\"` yields the invented key `role \"\"` (`:318-321`, `:403-406`) for a name PostgreSQL rejects (zero-length delimited identifier).\n\n**L3. Membership forms and owner-clause variants silently skipped.** `ALTER GROUP g ADD USER u` / `DROP USER u` yields only `role g` (`:333-342`); `CREATE ROLE x IN ROLE y` / `IN GROUP y` yields only `role x` (`:318-321`). `ALTER TABLE ONLY t OWNER TO r` misses the dependency because `only` is consumed as the object name (`:361`), and the argument-list skip `\\([^)]*\\)` at `:361` stops early if a default value contains `)`, also losing the dependency. I found no instances of these forms under `supabase/migrations` in my greps, so these are latent rather than live; they are listed because the module's stated bar is \"no omitted unknown operation\" (`.agent/work/3398/2/contract.json:31`).\n\n**L4. Fail-closed is enforced on only one of three exported entry points.** `roleCollisionKeys` refuses (`:391`); `extractRoleOperations` merely returns `dynamicRefusals` (`:373-378`) and `roleOwnershipDependencies` (`:414-416`) returns partial results silently. The documented consumer pattern for dependencies — \"A consumer pairs these with a role DROP\" (`:409-413`) — is precisely a caller that would under-report if it ignores `dynamicRefusals`.\n\n**L5. Fixture misdescribes the real migration** (see B2): `test:260-269` wraps the four roles in `do $$ … $$`, while `supabase/migrations/20260911210709_hts_rag_shared_schema_least_privilege_roles.sql:64-67` declares them top level. Top-level is handled, so the test still passes; the comment is what is wrong.\n\n## 4. What I checked that is *not* a problem\n\n- Scope: all five changed paths are inside `allowed_paths` (`.agent/work/3398/2/contract.json:13-19`).\n- CI wiring: the added step uses the same `id: route` / `pure_prose` guard as its siblings, which does exist in the same job (`tests-offline-tests.yml:102`, `:108`, `:125`, `:328-334`), fails explicitly when the test file is absent, and matches the named-explicit style of the neighbouring `scripts/lib` steps (`:223-233`).\n- Test count: the file declares exactly 25 `test(...)` blocks (lines 20, 30, 45, 59, 70, 75, 84, 101, 116, 121, 129, 137, 152, 166, 175, 182, 197, 209, 214, 219, 229, 235, 246, 252, 262), consistent with `completion.json:22`.\n- Evidence pair topology: `completion.json:10` naming implementation head `ff42c930…` rather than the PR head, and `files_changed` (`:11-15`) listing implementation files only, are the documented convention (`docs/agents/agent-work-contract-repo-maintenance-evidence.md:88-94`; `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:25`, `:66-70`). Not a finding.\n- Truth audit: the new helper contains no line matching the audit's PATTERN (`scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs` grep returned nothing against `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:9`), so it requires no disposition catalogue (`:60`, `:127-133`).\n- Migration immutability: no migration file is added or modified by this diff, so no version reservation or immutability question arises from it; equally, the role-blind entries at `scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:984-989` are untouched, so this PR alone does not yet make `role pm_jev_triage_worker` claimable — a deferral the contract states explicitly (`.agent/work/3398/2/contract.json:7`).\n- Rollback: no database mutation exists to roll back (`contract.json:27-28`, `completion.json:16-17`); the recovery gap is on the refusal path (L4).\n\n## 5. Evidence I could not obtain (kept UNVERIFIED)\n\n- That `node --test scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.test.mjs` actually exits 0: no shell, and the packet says no tests were run (`…/MANIFEST.md` §5). Prior quoted-identity and authenticator-key defects are addressed in source; fail-closed still has a false-clear spelling, and I could not execute the test suite in this review profile.\n\n## Findings\n\n### Mandatory checklist\n\n**Index usage.** Non-applicable, source-backed. The diff adds no SQL object, predicate, or join. Changed paths are the helper, its tests, CI, and the generation-2 evidence pair. `completion.json` records `\"migration_versions\": []`. The only set/order structures are the in-memory `Set` and sort in `roleCollisionKeys` (`scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:463-483`).\n\n**Function volatility.** Non-applicable, same basis. No database function is created or altered. `create function` appears as a regex alternative at `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:421` and as a deferred-body fixture at `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.test.mjs:316`.\n\n**Exact object checks.** Applicable as exact cluster-global role identity. Quoted whitespace, quoted keywords, empty `\"\"`, `USER MAPPING`, and `ALTER ROLE ALL` on the keys path now keep or refuse a single identity. The remaining exact-object miss is B1: a migration-time `EXECUTE $tag$…$tag$` payload that names a role is stored as `dollar-body` and never asserted.\n\n### Blocking\n\n**B1. Top-level dollar-quoted `EXECUTE` of role DDL still false-clears.**\n\n`extractableAndHidden` classifies every non-`DO` dollar body as `dollar-body` (`scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:223-227`). `findDynamicRoleMutations` then scans only `string-literal` and `nested-dollar-string` (`:303-305`, `:309`). `dollar-body` is never inspected, even when the text immediately before the tag is `EXECUTE` / `EXECUTE format(`.\n\nTraced results:\n\n| SQL | Result |\n|---|---|\n| `do $$ begin execute $sql$create role dynamic_worker$sql$; end $$;` | `['role dynamic_worker']` (second pass, `:231-233`; covered at `sql-role-operations.test.mjs:262-263`) |\n| `execute $q$create role sneaky$q$;` | `[]`, no throw |\n| `execute format($q$create role %I$q$, n);` | `[]`, no throw |\n| `execute $a$create $a$ \\|\\| $b$role sneaky$b$;` | `[]`, no throw |\n\nThe first form is this repo’s usual `DO` wrapper (`supabase/migrations/20260707171500_masterdata_designer_resolution.sql:1-8` uses `execute $ddl$` inside `do $migration$`, which the second pass does see). The next three are migration-time dynamic SQL, the same hazard as `EXECUTE 'create role sneaky'`, which the keys path does refuse. Invariant (4) at `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs:34-38` and the contract stop condition at `.agent/work/3398/2/contract.json:47` require a refusal rather than an empty key set.\n\nThe first pass conflates function bodies (correctly deferred, `:313-318` in the test file) with `EXECUTE $tag$` payloads. `beginsExecutedSql` (`:146-148`) already distinguishes those; it is not applied on the first dollar pass.\n\nThe 709-migration test (`sql-role-operations.test.mjs:290-294`) only asserts `doesNotThrow`. A false clear on a `.sql` file still passes it. Current checked-in role DDL is top-level `CREATE ROLE` in `20260911210709` and the exact `alter role authenticator` string in `20260621151419:57-58`; those paths work. The hole is the untested spelling of the fail-closed rule.\n\n### Major\n\n**M1. Membership `GRANT`/`REVOKE` to `PUBLIC` (and other special grantees) drops the named member role.**\n\n`roleNamesFrom` filters unquoted `NON_ROLE_KEYWORDS` (`:260-268`), which includes `public`. The membership gate requires both sides (`:405-408`):\n\n`grant worker to public` → members `['worker']`, grantees `[]` → no operation → `roleCollisionKeys` returns `[]`.\n\nThat SQL writes membership of `worker`. `grant \"select\" to worker` is tested (`:176-177`); `grant worker to public` is not. Same drop on `revoke worker from public` / `current_user`.\n\n**M2. `CREATE ROLE x ROLE y` / `ADMIN y` / `USER y` membership is unmodelled.**\n\nPostgreSQL accepts `ROLE` / `ADMIN` / `USER` lists on `CREATE ROLE` as membership. The extra extractor only matches `IN ROLE` / `IN GROUP` (`:398-402`). `create role x role y` therefore emits only `role x`. The `IN ROLE` spelling is tested (`:156-160`); the `ROLE`/`ADMIN`/`USER` spellings are not. Contract prohibited action at `.agent/work/3398/2/contract.json:31` forbids an omitted unknown operation.\n\n**M3. Public extractors disagree on fail-closed.**\n\n- `extractRoleOperations('alter role all set work_mem=1;')` returns `{ operations: [] }` (`sql-role-operations.test.mjs:111`; regex `(?!all\\b)` at `:381`). That reads as “touches no role”.\n- `roleCollisionKeys` throws (`:457-459`, test `:112`).\n- The authenticator migration is the opposite split: `roleCollisionKeys` yields `['role authenticator']` (`:285-287`), while `extractRoleOperations` throws because `dynamicRefusals` is non-empty (`:440-444`).\n\nA future collision-parser import of `extractRoleOperations` will treat `ALTER ROLE ALL` as clear and will hard-refuse `20260621151419`. Only `roleCollisionKeys` matches the advertised exact-target story.\n\n### Minor\n\n**L1.** Fragment assembly only joins a piece that already starts with `create|alter|drop|grant|revoke` and at most four later pieces (`:311-318`). `execute 'c'||'reate'||' rol'||'e x'` yields `[]`. This is a narrower encoding than the `'alter '||'role '` case now covered at `:274-275`.\n\n**L2.** `roleOwnershipDependencies` on dynamic SQL throws (`:491-493`, tested at `:273`). That is fail-closed. A consumer that only checks `roleCollisionKeys` and then separately walks ownership can still miss an executed `ALTER … OWNER TO` hidden in a resolved dynamic string, because resolved dynamic items are merged only inside `roleCollisionKeys` (`:461-468`), and ownership is never taken from those resolved ops.\n\n**L3.** Completion evidence names implementation `head_sha` `bc4da237a4159ec1aa4060b61bf335bb5d0c1645` (`.agent/work/3398/2/completion.json:10`) with `files_changed` limited to the three implementation paths (`:11-15`). That matches `docs/agents/agent-work-contract-repo-maintenance-evidence.md:88-94` and `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:25-30,66-70`. This review profile has no shell, so ancestry of `bc4da237` under `1f967410`, the two-file evidence tail, `sha256` of `contract.json` against `1e1be3a689…`, and fetch of `refs/db-contracts/3398/2` stay unverified. Checked-in `contract.json` matches the published generation-2 comment body field-for-field, and all five diff paths sit inside `allowed_paths` (`contract.json:13-19`).\n\n### What this head does get right (prior REVISE items)\n\nTraced against `scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.mjs` and the tests:\n\n- Quoted internal whitespace is no longer collapsed (`:150-154`; test `:31-36`).\n- `\"a--b\"` / `\"a/*b*/c\"` survive comment stripping because `\"` is copied before `--` (`:163-175`; test `:39-42`).\n- `canonicalRoleName('\"\"')` is null (`:85-87`; test `:96-107`).\n- `user(?!\\s+mapping\\b)` excludes `USER MAPPING` (`:48`; test `:96-107`).\n- `ALTER ROLE ALL` is refused on the keys path (`:457-459`; test `:110-113`); `ALTER ROLE \"all\"` stays `role all` (`:113`).\n- Quoted keyword members/owners are kept (`:263-266`, `:129-130`; test `:176-179`).\n- `'alter '||'role '||quote_ident(r)` refuses (`:306-320`; test `:269-277`).\n- Nested dollar SQL inside `DO` with an exact target is keyed (`:231-233`, `:461-468`; test `:262-263`).\n- `20260621151419` `execute 'alter role authenticator set …'` keys `role authenticator` (`:57-58` of that migration; test `:285-287`).\n- `ALTER GROUP … ADD/DROP USER` and `CREATE ROLE … IN ROLE/GROUP` reserve both sides (test `:156-160`).\n- `ALTER TABLE ONLY` and `numeric(10,2)` ownership resolve (test `:223-225`).\n- `extractRoleOperations` and `roleOwnershipDependencies` throw on unresolved dynamic SQL (`:440-444`, `:491-493`; test `:272-273`).\n- Real four-role file `20260911210709:64-67` is read from disk (test `:340-348`).\n\n### CI, scope, roles, migrations, rollback\n\n- CI step `.github/workflows/tools-offline-tests.yml:332-338` uses `id: route` / `pure_prose != 'true'`, a missing-file hard fail, and `node --test scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.test.mjs`, matching sibling `scripts/lib` steps (`:223-226`).\n- No database GRANT/POLICY/ROLE is issued by this diff. Offline text accounting only.\n- No `supabase/migrations/` path is modified. Migration immutability is intact.\n- Rollback is a git revert of the five paths. No database recovery path exists, and none is required.\n- Truth-audit pattern (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:9`) has no hits in the new helper, so no new disposition catalogue is required.\n\n### Unverified (no shell in this profile)\n\n- `node --test scripts/lib/sql-role-operations.test.mjs` exit code (author claim: 35 pass).\n- `node scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` digest `162702651f60`.\n- Git ancestry/hash of the evidence pair and immutable ref as listed in L3.\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\n\nVERDICT: REVISE
