REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\nI have everything I need from read-only inspection. Note up front: this review profile has **no shell** (`MANIFEST.md` §1: \"Everything below was produced by the wrapper with a shell, because your review profile deliberately has none\"), `MANIFEST.md` §5 records that **no tests were run for this packet**, and this session is additionally in plan mode, which forbids state-modifying commands such as `git stash push`. That constrains one mandated item; I say exactly where below.\n**Provisional verdict: REVISE** — no defect found in the shipped source change; the revision ask is driven by absent mandated test evidence plus test-strength gaps. Details follow.\n---\n## Packet / commit identity (verified)\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n| head `6754166fde040509665a367101218dd230270419` | matches frozen git snapshot HEAD and `MANIFEST.md` §2 |\n| base `85566ccb392b27022fe9bbb100d308fc587b13cc` | matches HEAD's parent in the snapshot and `MANIFEST.md` §2 |\n| working tree clean, no untracked | `MANIFEST.md` §3 |\n| files changed | exactly `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs` (`MANIFEST.md` §3; `patch.diff` contains only those two) |\n| whole-source digest `7028e76b…` | **not verified** — recomputing it needs a shell |\n## What the change actually is (verified line by line)\n- `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:6657-6661` — new comment + `let completedResult=null`, declared before `try{` at `:6662`.\n- `:6730`, `:6936`, `:6959` — the **only** three `return` sites in `replaceFailedReviewerOperation` reachable after `mutexAcquired=true`; all three now assign `completedResult`. I grepped the whole function: no fourth post-mutex `return` exists, so the \"all three return sites\" claim is exactly right.\n- `:6971` — `finally{if(mutexAcquired)finalizeReviewMutexPreservingResult(ownerSha,io,completedResult)}`.\n- `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs:9267-9294` — the one new test. Nothing else added.\n## \"Must be true\" items I could verify statically — all hold\n1. **Refusal unchanged.** `finalizeReviewMutex` still throws `release of … could not be proved after atomic deletion` at `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:4686` and still wraps every failure in `RECOVERY REQUIRED … do not retry blindly` at `:4690`. The helper at `:4652-4660` never returns normally on failure — `:4655` rethrows when there is no completed result, `:4658` throws the decorated error when there is one. No `return` was added to any `finally`, so an orphaned mutex is still never assumed released.\n2. **Ladder / ref-API confirmation / allowance untouched.** `MUTEX_RELEASE_READBACK_DELAYS_MS=[0,500,1000,2000,3000,4000]` at `:4646`, the ladder at `:4680-4684`, the `readRefOverApi` confirmation at `:4685`, `releaseProofAllowance=MUTEX_RELEASE_READBACK_DELAYS_MS.length+2` at `:4666` and its reset at `:4691` — none appears in any hunk of `patch.diff`. The helper's `try{return finalizeReviewMutex(ownerSha,io)}` (`:4653`) calls it unmodified.\n3. **No ceiling widened.** `REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT = 25, REVIEW_MUTEX_SECTION_RESERVE = 15` at `:156`; the derived checks at `:1443`, `:4600`, `:4693`; the allowance short-circuit at `:1442`. None is in the diff. The change adds zero requests — it only decorates an error already being thrown.\n4. **No DB / migration / infra / secret change.** Both touched files are `scripts/*.mjs`; no `supabase/`, `.github/`, env or credential surface in the diff.\n5. **Helper decorates only on completion.** `:4655` `if(completed===undefined||completed===null)throw error`, and `completedResult` is initialised to `null` at `:6661`. Any failure before completion — preflight, eligibility, the rollback paths at `:6723-6728` and `:6960-6969` — throws byte-identically to before.\n6. **No new error masking.** `completedResult` is assigned *in the return expression itself* at all three sites, so it can only be non-null at the instant the function returns successfully. A body throw always leaves it `null`, so the `finally` cannot substitute a \"COMPLETED\" message for a genuine failure. This is the main correctness risk of the pattern and it is closed.\n7. **Truthfulness of \"COMPLETED\".** Each of the three sites returns only after its own proof: the atomic readback compares all six/seven refs to exact expected SHAs at `:6935`, the batched readback at `:6957`, and the idempotent path at `:6709`/`:6717`/`:6725`. So the decorated claim \"a retry would repeat a draw that already succeeded\" is backed by durable state, not by optimism.\n8. **Operator actually sees it.** `main` prints the full message: `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:9613` `catch (error) { console.error(\\`REFUSED: ${error.message}\\`); return 2 }`, and the replacement dispatch is `:9279`. The JSON is inside `error.message` (`:4656`), not only on the property.\n## Non-vacuity of the new test — deductive proof (execution unavailable)\nI could not run the stash/rerun cycle, so here is the static proof, which I consider conclusive on the \"fails when reverted\" half:\n- With `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` reverted, `:6971` calls plain `finalizeReviewMutex`, so the thrown error is exactly the `:4690` string. It contains no `THE OPERATION ITSELF COMPLETED` and carries no `completedResult` property.\n- The validator at `test.mjs:9286` requires `/THE OPERATION ITSELF COMPLETED/` and `:9289-9290` require `Boolean(error.completedResult?.reviewer)` and `Boolean(error.completedResult?.replacementSha)`. Both are false reverted ⇒ the validation function returns falsy ⇒ `assert.throws` fails the test. The test cannot pass vacuously.\nOn the \"passes with the fix\" half, the fixture is sound and I traced it end to end:\n- `replacementRequest` is module-scoped at `test.mjs:1938` and `failedReviewIo()` at `:1937`, so both are in scope at `:9273`/`:9284` (no `ReferenceError` risk).\n- Decisive corroboration: the **pre-existing, currently-passing** test at `test.mjs:3114-3128` uses an *identical* io shape — `failedReviewIo()` plus the same `readReviewStates` (`:3115`), `readReviewRefs` (`:3116`), `atomicReviewRefs` (`:3117`) and `atomicReviewMutexRelease` (`:3118`) overrides — and successfully returns from `replaceFailedReviewer(replacementRequest, io)`, asserting `replacement.reviewer==='qwen-3.8-max'` (`:3122`). The new test's only deltas are staleness injection scoped to post-release reads (`:9276`, `:9282`) and `io.wait=()=>{}` (`:9283`). `releasedOwner` is mutated solely inside `atomicReviewMutexRelease` (`:9281`), which only `finalizeReviewMutex:4668` calls, so nothing before the release is affected.\n- The refusal path then fires exactly as asserted: ladder reads at `:4680-4684` all return `releasedOwner===ownerSha`, `readRefOverApi` at `:4685` also returns it, `:4686` throws, `:4690` wraps, `:4656` decorates. `assert.equal(io.refs.get(MUTEX_REF),undefined)` at `:9293` holds because `:9281` really deletes via `atomicReviewRefs`.\n- No wire-budget interference: this fixture never calls `runGitHubCommand`, so `consumeReviewWireRequest` (`:1437-1447`) keeps `count=0` and `requireReviewWireCapacity(12)` at `:6909` passes; `reviewTargetEligible` short-circuits on the open PR at `:5797` and never reaches the `requireReviewWireCapacity(2)` at `:5816`.\n**Regression risk to the rest of the suite is very low:** the only behaviour change is extra text and one extra property on an error that is thrown *only* when a completed result exists. I grepped the whole test file — `/could not be proved after atomic deletion|RECOVERY REQUIRED/` matches only four lines (`test.mjs:9143`, `:9264`, `:9271` (comment), `:9285`), and the first two are `assignNextReviewer` tests. No existing test asserts a bare refusal message on the replacement path, and none asserts the absence of `completedResult`.\n## Findings\n### Blocking (evidence, not code)\n**B1 — The mandated empirical verification is absent and could not be performed.** `MANIFEST.md` §5: \"**No tests were run for this packet.** Treat this as unknown, not as a pass.\" The review request requires observed pass/fail counts both with the fix reverted and restored, plus a green `node --test scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`. My profile has no shell (`MANIFEST.md` §1) and this session is in plan mode, which forbids `git stash push`. So two of the five REVISE stop conditions — \"the new test passes with the source fix reverted\" and \"the full lanes suite is red\" — are **not established as false by observation**; I have argued them false deductively above, which is not the same thing. This must be closed by a runner that has a shell, with the four numbers recorded.\n### Medium\n**M1 — The new test proves the message carries a result, not that the result matches durable state** (`test.mjs:9284-9293`). Every assertion is against `error.message` / `error.completedResult`; the only state assertion is that the mutex ref is gone (`:9293`). It never checks that `refs/db-review-replacements/9-109-<head>-1` actually holds `completedResult.replacementSha`, that `REVIEW_CURSOR_REF` advanced, or that the drawn reviewer's lease exists. This is precisely the \"inferring existence instead of asserting the exact object\" class. The sibling fixture already shows how: `test.mjs:3126-3128` asserts `io.refs.get(failureRef)===released.failureSha` and `io.refs.get(reviewActiveRef(replacement.reviewer))===replacement.replacementSha`. Two added asserts would make the test prove that what the operator is told was drawn really is durable — which is the entire point of the fix, and the thing that would break if the `completedResult=` assignment were ever moved above the `:6935` readback.\n### Low\n**L1 — Two of the three preserved return sites are untested.** `:6730` (idempotent retry) and `:6959` (non-atomic/batched) have no refused-release coverage; only `:6936` is exercised. Their lost results are also retry-safe by construction — a re-run of `reclaimSilentReviewer` hits \"already reclaimed with immutable evidence\" (`:5311`/`:5317`), and `ensureReviewerQueueTurn` finds its prior ticket at `:5902`. So the siblings' latent gap loses a *report*, not a *draw*, and cannot produce the double-reviewer harm that motivated #2457. Deferring them is right; I would not ask this PR to widen.\n## What moves this to APPROVE\n1. **B1** — a shell-capable runner records: single-test result with `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` stashed (expect fail), single-test result restored (expect pass), and full-suite pass/fail counts from `node --test scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs`. There is no `package.json` in this checkout, so that direct invocation is the project's test entry point.\n2. **M1** — add the two durable-object assertions beside `test.mjs:9293`, reusing the pattern at `test.mjs:3126-3128`. **L1** strongly recommended in the same round; **L2**/**L3**/**L4**/**T1** may be follow-ups.\nUnambiguously: I found **no correctness, safety or scope defect** in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`. It preserves the refusal, the ladder, the ref-API confirmation and every request ceiling; it cannot mask a genuine failure; and it closes exactly the half of #2457 that #3354 left open. My REVISE rests on missing mandated verification evidence and a test that proves the message rather than the durable state — not on the fix being wrong.\nVERDICT: REVISE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### Findings and reasoning (everything the reviewer said before its verdict)\n\nI'll start with the sealed evidence packet, then inspect the source and tests against the three mandated checks and the rest of the review brief.Packet identity matches the injected head. Next I’ll read the sealed patch and the surrounding source so I can judge the mutex-release path, not just the summary.Provisional verdict: APPROVE, pending a line-by-line check that the helper still refuses, that all three return sites preserve the result, and that the new test actually pins durable state.Identity matches the injected head. I’ll confirm the commit stack, hash the contract pair, and run the lane tests so the prior “no packet test run” gap is closed with observation.Provisional assessment: the source change is correct, the refusal and request ceiling are untouched, and the prior REVISE items are closed. Expected outcome is approve of `731101e7`.\n\nPacket identity matches the injected head: base `530ffb393c7e129c7b9dbe41e0674835e66d9594`, head `731101e7ccd27d5e6c54a7f4291c924b5079cd89`, digest `8bf9c10d…`. Changed files are exactly the two scripts plus the generation-3 evidence pair. No SQL, grants, policies, migrations, or ceiling constants appear in `patch.diff`. This profile has no shell (command execution denied), so suite counts were not re-run here; non-vacuity of the new test is established from the source, and the prior round’s recorded stash cycle is in the completion report.\n\n## Findings\n\nNo blocking or medium defects in the shipped source.\n\n**What the change does.** `replaceFailedReviewerOperation` captures its completed replacement on a `completedResult` local and finalizes with the existing `finalizeReviewMutexPreservingResult` helper, matching `assignNextReviewerOperation`. The helper still calls unmodified `finalizeReviewMutex`; on failure it rethrows when `completed` is null, and otherwise throws a new `LaneError` that keeps the original message (including `RECOVERY REQUIRED`) and appends `THE OPERATION ITSELF COMPLETED` plus `JSON.stringify(completed)`.\n\n**All three post-mutex return sites assign the result**, and only after their own exact-SHA readback:\n\n- idempotent retry at `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:6730`\n- atomic draw at `:6936`\n- batched/non-atomic draw at `:6959`\n\nThere is no fourth post-`mutexAcquired=true` return. Assignment is inside the `return` expression, so a throw in the body leaves `completedResult === null` and cannot dress a genuine failure as completed. `finally` still runs only `if (mutexAcquired)`.\n\n**Refusal not weakened.** `finalizeReviewMutex` still throws `release of … could not be proved after atomic deletion` at `:4686` and still wraps every failure with `RECOVERY REQUIRED … do not retry blindly` at `:4690`. The helper never returns on that path. An orphaned mutex is still never assumed released. `recoverStaleAuthorMutex` remains a no-op when the ref is already gone (`:3500`).\n\n**Request ceiling not widened.** `REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT = 25` and `REVIEW_MUTEX_SECTION_RESERVE = 15` at `:156` are outside the diff. `releaseProofAllowance`, the `0/500/1000/2000/3000/4000` ladder, and `readRefOverApi` confirmation are untouched. The helper adds no I/O; it only decorates an error already being thrown.\n\n**Operator sees the result.** `--replace-failed-reviewer` at `:9279` sits in `main`’s try; `:9613` prints `REFUSED: ${error.message}`. The JSON is in `error.message`, not only on `error.completedResult`.\n\n**Test is non-vacuous and now pins durable state.** `#2457 a refused mutex release still reports the completed replacement instead of losing it` (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs:9272`) uses the same `failedReviewIo()` + atomic overrides as the already-passing replacement fixture at `:3114`. The compare-and-swap really deletes `MUTEX_REF`; replica ladder and ref-API confirmation keep answering with the deleted owner. Assertions require the inner refusal, `THE OPERATION ITSELF COMPLETED`, `completedResult.reviewer` / `replacementSha`, `io.refs.get(completedResult.assignmentRef) === completedResult.replacementSha`, and `io.refs.get(MUTEX_REF) === undefined`. Reverting the `finally` to plain `finalizeReviewMutex` cannot satisfy `THE OPERATION ITSELF COMPLETED` or `error.completedResult`. That is the recorded 714-pass / 1-fail result.\n\n**Siblings that still use plain `finalizeReviewMutex` do not draw a reviewer** (`reinstateReviewerExclusion`, `reclaimSilentReviewerOperation`, `reapAbandonedReviewLeasesOperation`, verdict archive, `ensureReviewerQueueTurn`, `releaseFailedReviewer`, cutover activation). Both draw paths now preserve: assign at `:6193`, replace at `:6971`. Narrowing the PR to the replacement path is correct.\n\n**Roles, grants, policies.** Not applicable. The patch contains no `GRANT`, policy, role, or security-boundary change. Sibling call paths were inspected; this is in-process git-ref coordination in `scripts/*.mjs`.\n\n**Migration immutability.** Not applicable. No `supabase/` migration is in the diff. `completion.json` records `migration_versions: []`.\n\n**Rollback / recovery.** Unchanged except the operator now keeps the completed replacement when release proof fails. Pre-completion failures still throw the undecorated error. Mutex-held rollback of a failed replacement body is unmodified.\n\n### Residual, non-blocking\n\n- Idempotent (`:6730`) and batched (`:6959`) refused-release paths are still untested; only the atomic fresh draw is. The `finally` is shared and all three sites assign `completedResult` after readback, so this is coverage, not a source defect.\n- The operator message still contains both `RECOVERY REQUIRED … do not retry blindly` and `THE OPERATION ITSELF COMPLETED -- do not retry it`. Keeping the refusal verbatim is required; wording reconciliation belongs in the shared helper as a follow-up.\n- The new test does not charge the wire budget (unlike the assign sibling), so a future ceiling regression on this path would not be caught here.\n- `completedResult.assignmentRef` is taken from the error payload. Cursor, lease, and (when there is no prior release) failure refs also receive the same SHA, so an independently constructed `refs/db-review-replacements/9-109-<head>-1` would be stricter. Mutex absence is already an exact-name check.\n\n### Mandated checks\n\n1. **Index usage — not applicable; nothing loosened.** No SQL, table predicate, or join. Lookup is by exact git ref name (`io.readRef` / `io.readReviewRefs`) or a pre-existing prefix listing bounded by `REVIEW_REF_ROW_LIMIT`. This change introduces no new scan and no index that exists but cannot be used as written.\n\n2. **Function volatility — not applicable as SQL; effect classification is correct.** No `IMMUTABLE` / `STABLE` / `VOLATILE` marker, no `CREATE FUNCTION`. `finalizeReviewMutexPreservingResult` performs side-effecting release proof and is not treated as pure. `io.readRefOverApi` is excluded from the `reviewOperationIo` cache (`listRefs`, `listReviewRefsPaged`, `getCommit`, `getPr`, `getIssue`, `getIssueComments`, `getPrReviews` only) and is re-read every call. The test double models that volatility. No marker is looser than its body.\n\n3. **Exact object checks — satisfied in source; test meets the prior M1 bar.** Source still compares mutex, failure, cursor, replacement, and lease refs to exact expected SHAs (`:6935`, `:6957`), compares release readback to the exact `ownerSha` (`:4682`, `:4685`), and calls `finalizeReviewMutexPreservingResult(ownerSha, io, completed)` with the declared three-parameter signature. The test asserts exact SHA identity at `completedResult.assignmentRef` and exact absence of `MUTEX_REF`. It infers the replacement *name* from the payload rather than constructing `refs/db-review-replacements/…` itself; that remainder is noted above and is not a source defect.\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\nVERDICT: APPROVE 731101e7ccd27d5e6c54a7f4291c924b5079cd89","author_association":"MEMBER","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5839521950/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"performed_via_github_app":null,"minimized":null},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5861715001","html_url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3522#issuecomment-5861715001","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/3522","id":5861715001,"node_id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABXWKsOQ","user":{"login":"u2giants","id":55610577,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/55610577?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants","html_url":"https://github.com/u2giants","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2026-09-28T01:28:03Z","updated_at":"2026-09-28T01:28:03Z","body":"Readiness check on current main 1660f920 plus the PR code diff: 715 focused tests pass, 0 fail; git diff --check is clean. Provisional view before finishing: the two defects that sank the prior round (a 64-slot probe cap and a dropped allowlist-consistency check) do look repaired at this head, but I found a residual instance of the same failure class plus an evidence-integrity defect. Final: REVISE.\n\n## What I verified\n\nSymmetric peer discovery, unbounded slot number. `resolvePeerSlots` (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:5687-5763) resolves slot 1 and all peer slots from one shared namespace read. The batched branch passes both prefixes (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:5723-5724`), and `readReviewRecords` serves them from a single `git ls-remote` when the wire budget is live (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2349,2357-2360`, backed by `gitRemoteRefs` at 1590-1607), so there is no fixed slot ceiling in either the batched or the `listRefs` fallback path (5747-5757). The prior round's \"slot 65\" blocker is therefore addressed, and the new test (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs:5768-5789, \"batched peer read includes an occupied slot above 64 without an extra namespace request\") pins exactly that.\n\nAllowlist consistency restored. `assertReviewerAllowlistConsistency(slotOneHistory)` is called on both branches (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:5741,5759), with `slotOneHistory` collecting slot-1 assignment and replacement records (5701-5706), and a new test covers the conflicting-allowlist refusal (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs:5784-5792).\n\nCase normalization is applied at both request boundaries (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:5938, 6631) and again inside the resolver (5688), and refs are built from the lowercased head (5691-5692, 5977, 6652-6657).\n\nDistinctness endpoint and gate still exist. The draw excludes all peer providers (5952, 6127, 6144) and the exact-head gate refuses a shared provider on the latest per-slot assignments (scripts/check-exact-head-approval.mjs:291, over slots built at :220-226); that file is not in this diff.\n\nHistorical retirement evidence is coherent. The three retired rows carry the same `semantic_key` and `line_sha256` as the historical audit (docs/verification/throughput-retired-identity-sites.json:7-8,15-16,23-24 vs docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json:1009-1010,1037-1038,1100-1101), and `scripts/throughput-guard/check-throughput-truth-audit-context.test.mjs:53,61,74` asserts field-for-field equality, \"live identity cannot already be retired,\" and `retired_by_pr === 3521`. The removed catalogue entry `…14e03f4392…` (patch.diff, dispositions file) is not a historical identity (no grep hit anywhere in docs/verification), so its removal needs no retirement record.\n\n## Findings\n\nHigh — the peer resolver is blind to the legacy unsuffixed slot-1 replacement, the same failure class this PR exists to close. `parseAssignmentRef` returns null unless a replacements ref carries the trailing `-<sequence>` (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:4244-4245), and `resolvePeerSlots` drops every row whose ref does not parse (5726, 5749, 5755). But the same file treats the unsuffixed ref `<replacementBase>` as a real slot-1 replacement link: scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:6674 (`row.ref===replacementBase`) and :6558 (`request.slot===1&&row.ref===replacementBase`), with the comment at 6671 saying the first implementation wrote exactly that form and it is preserved as the first link. For a slot 1 whose live holder is recorded only in that legacy ref, `slotOne` resolves through the assignment ref to the *superseded* reviewer, so a peer draw excludes the wrong provider and can hand a peer slot the provider that currently holds slot 1 — the duplicate-provider condition of issue #3427, now with the exclusion set computed from a stale record rather than from the live one. Whether any such ref is currently live is not something I can check (no network, no ref listing in the packet), so the live impact is unverified; the in-file inconsistency is not.\n\nMedium — the checked-in completion evidence names a different commit than the one under review. `.agent/work/3427/3/completion.json` declares `\"head_sha\": \"641e027946fecc36af0d0d0008845aeee15536e9\"` with `\"outcome\": \"ready-for-merge\"`, while the governed head is `293a2e3b948ce8d99dbed2c98f8280c3ec608a82`. Its `checks` block (812 reviewer tests, 8 identity tests, truth audit `call_sites=320 sources=76`) therefore describes another commit and cannot be read as evidence for this head. The test counts are also mutually inconsistent across the packet (PR body \"807 tests: 713 + 91\", completion \"812\", review comment 5861703385 \"810 on a clean integration\"), and the packet manifest states plainly that no tests were run.\n\nMedium — zero wire headroom on the idempotent replacement path. The idempotent retry's pre-mutex spend rises from 11 to 14 (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs:1308-1315) while the reserve stays `requireReviewWireCapacity(11)` (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:6697) against the fixed 25 ceiling, i.e. 14+11 = 25 exactly. One extra pre-mutex read on that path turns into a refusal. The direction is fail-closed, so this is fragility rather than a safety hole, but the stated \"25-request budget unchanged\" claim is true only at the exact boundary, and `assertIndependent` (6689) calling the full resolver pre-mutex is the reason for the growth.\n\nLow — duplicated slot-1 handling and a dead predicate. In the batched branch the same slot-1 assignment row is fed to `accept` twice: once through `records.matching` (5725-5731) and once through `records.get(ref)` (5733-5739), duplicating entries in `slotOneHistory`. The `returned.has(row.sha)` guard at 5729 can never fire, because `returned` is only populated later inside `filterReturned` (5715-5719, called at 5742). Both are harmless today, but they are exactly the kind of dead check that hides a future regression.\n\nLow/observational — `filterReturned` consults `readReviewReturns` only when a peer exists (5715-5716), so the resolver's answer depends on whether peers were found; that is the documented wire-cost trade (it is what moves the slot-2 total 24→23 at scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs:1257), but it means the same head can be resolved with or without return filtering depending on peer occupancy, which is worth a comment or a test asserting the no-peer case.\n\n## Mandatory checks\n\n1. Index usage — non-applicable, with a source-backed reason: the diff contains no SQL or schema object; changed files are `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, its test, two verification JSON catalogues, and two `.agent/work/3427/3/*.json` records. The nearest analogue is the ref-namespace lookup, which the change narrows to the exact issue/pr/head prefix (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:5691-5692) and serves with one `git ls-remote` (2358-2360, 1602), with cost pinned by test (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs:1161-1165). No loose or unused index assumption is introduced.\n2. Function volatility — non-applicable in the SQL sense; no function marker is touched. The JS analogue is worth stating: `resolvePeerSlots` is side-effect-free but not deterministic-by-construction (it reads refs and lazily reads returns), which is why re-resolving inside the mutex at 5962 and 6163 is required; that ordering is preserved, not changed, by this diff.\n3. Exact object checks — present and adequate: exact ref identity is asserted on the wire call in the new test (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs:5770), exact per-field equality of every retired identity's `line_sha256`/`disposition`/`reason` is asserted at scripts/throughput-guard/check-throughput-truth-audit-context.test.mjs:53,64, and `retired_by_pr` is pinned at :74. One caveat: I confirmed the `semantic_key`/`line_sha256` agreement in the historical audit by grep, but the `disposition`/`reason` agreement is only asserted by that test, which I could not run.\n\n## Other brief sections\n\nMigration immutability: satisfied — no `supabase/migrations` path appears in the changed-file inventory, and the retired-identity ledger is guard-tested against unexplained loss (check-throughput-truth-audit-context.test.mjs:60-63, 80-83). Rollback and recovery: the assignment rollback path is untouched (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:6194-6200) and the resolver performs no writes, so it owes no rollback; the `SLOT_INDEPENDENCE_CONFLICT` recovery body itself I did not read, so its partial-failure behaviour remains unverified. Roles and permissions: no grant, policy, or security boundary is modified by this diff.\n\nUnverified, and needed before an approve on the wire-budget and case-normalization claims: whether the pre-existing `headPattern` used at scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:5930 admits uppercase input (the new test at scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs:5796-5804 draws with an uppercase head and would be unreachable otherwise); whether any live ref of the unsuffixed slot-1 replacement form exists in the remote repository; and any actual test execution, since the packet states none was run and the completion record belongs to a different commit.\n\nVERDICT: REVISE The reviewer findings are kept below with every parseable decision line voided. Acting on them requires a fresh governed review at this head.\n\n## Provisional verdict\n> VOIDED REVIEWER LINE - **APPROVE** (provisional, stated before I finished the sibling-path and budget analysis). The single blocking finding from the prior governed round — the peer resolver's blindness to the legacy unsuffixed slot-one replacement — is fixed in-source and covered by a discriminating regression test that exercises both read paths. The prior round's Medium evidence finding is **refuted** by the repository's own Git evidence checker, which is designed for exactly the `head_sha`-names-the-implementation-commit shape this packet carries. My final verdict is at the bottom; findings and unverified items are below.\n---\n## 1. Sealed packet verification\n- `MANIFEST.md` §2 base `5f91f2f6…`, head `246ed2ed…` matches `identity.json` (`base`, `head`, `merge_base`, `source_digest ce44ab98…`) and the runner-injected authoritative head. The directory matches the commits under review; I reviewed the right tree.\n- Changed-file inventory in `MANIFEST.md` §3 (6 files) matches the injected inventory exactly, and matches `patch.diff`'s hunks. Working tree clean, no untracked files.\n- `MANIFEST.md` §5: **no tests were run for this packet.** I have read-only file/search tools and no shell in this profile, so I could not execute `node --test`, `check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs`, `git diff --check`, or any `git` ancestry predicate. Every \"tests pass\" figure (813 / 8 / `call_sites=320 sources=76`) remains an author claim. Where I could substitute static verification, I did, and I say so per finding.\n- Access note: reads of `/home/ahazan/repos/shared-db-3521-repair` were denied; all evidence below is from the sandbox snapshot, which the manifest states has identical paths.\n## 2. Evidence format: verified against the checker, not by equality\nI read `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs` rather than comparing `completion.head_sha` to the PR head:\n- `:26` requires `report.head_sha` to be an exact 40-hex SHA — `8a2f24b8141fbf25c37b78cab1dff5487e01a95a` qualifies.\n- `:29` requires `report.head_sha` to be an **ancestor of** `prHeadSha`, not equal to it. The equality test the prior round applied is not the repository's rule.\n- `:66-71` requires `changedFiles(report.head_sha, prHeadSha)` to equal exactly this contract's own pair, resolved by `acceptableEvidencePairs(contract)` (`scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs:105-113`) → sorted `[\".agent/work/3427/3/completion.json\", \".agent/work/3427/3/contract.json\"]`. That is precisely what the packet's inventory shows following the implementation commit.\n- `:52-57` (#2845) requires `report.base_sha` to equal `mergeBase(prBaseSha, prHeadSha)`. `completion.json` records `5f91f2f6…`, which is the packet's own merge base. ✓\n- `:59-65` requires `changedFiles(mergeBase, report.head_sha)` to equal `files_changed` byte-for-byte. Findings\n### Medium\n**M1 — Same failure class, sibling consumer not closed: the merge gate cannot see the legacy slot-one holder.** `scripts/check-exact-head-approval.mjs:448` drops every ref `parseAssignmentRef` rejects (`if (!parsed || parsed.pr !== pr) return []`), so `liveBySlot` (`:218-227`) for slot 1 falls back to the **superseded** assignment when the live holder is recorded only in `refs/db-review-replacements/<i>-<p>-<head>`. The duplicate-provider refusal at `:288-293` then compares the superseded reviewer, and `:286` demands an APPROVE for the superseded `assignment_sha`. This is the exact class the prior round rated High in the resolver, surviving in the gate that actually authorizes merges. Two mitigations, which is why I rate it Medium and not blocking: (a) it fails closed — a replaced reviewer cannot hold an APPROVE for that assignment sha, because `validateTerminalReviewerFailure` requires `confirmNoVerdict`/`confirmNoArtifact` (`:6528`) — so the outcome is a refusal, not a duplicate-provider merge; (b) it is pre-existing on main, the file is not in this diff, and `scripts/check-exact-head-approval.mjs` is **not** in the generation-3 contract's `allowed_paths`, so repairing it here would violate the published contract. It needs a follow-up issue. Note the in-repo inconsistency: `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:7038-7040` admits the legacy form and `check-exact-head-approval.mjs:448` does not.\n**M2 — The slot-one idempotent retry still answers with the superseded reviewer, now disagreeing with the resolver.** `assignNextReviewerOperation`'s replacement branch filters with `inReviewReplacementNamespace` (`:5985`, defined `:5677-5680`, requires a `-\\d+` tail), so the legacy row is dropped and control falls to `io.readRef(assignmentRef)` at `:6042`, returning the superseded reviewer; `replaceFailedReviewerOperation`'s `history` at `:6754` filters the same way (its `priorReplacement` lookup at `:6676-6678` is the one place that does handle the legacy form). After this diff the same command therefore excludes provider Y from peer draws while handing back provider X as slot 1's live answer. Fail-closed direction, pre-existing lines, unreachable unless a live pre-#2077 unsuffixed ref still names a current PR head (no writer produces that form today: `replacementRef` is always `${replacementBase}-${request.failedSequence}`, `:6663`). Report as a follow-up alongside M1.\n**M3 — The written budget derivation the code cites was not re-derived, and the model now sits exactly on the ceiling.** `REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT`/`REVIEW_MUTEX_SECTION_RESERVE` at `:162` cite `docs/verification/reviewer-assignment-api-budget-2026-08-28.md` and instruct \"Re-derive it from a written measurement rather than widening it\". This diff moves the pinned measurements — first replacement pre-mutex 10→11 (`test.mjs:1310`), idempotent retry 11→14 (`test.mjs:1315`), slot-2 total 24→23 (`test.mjs:1258`), 10,000-history total 21→20 with `historyScans` 0→1 (`test.mjs:1165-1168`) — but neither that document (whose table at `:131-137` still reads \"First replacement, pre-mutex 8 | 9\" and \"Idempotent replacement retry, pre-mutex 9 | 10\") nor the `:162` comment was updated, and neither is in the changed-file inventory. The ceiling was **not** widened, which is the part the contract prohibits, and the doc was already drifting before this PR; but the idempotent path now has zero slack in the model (14 + 11 = 25 at `:6701`). That doc is outside the generation-3 `allowed_paths`, so this is a required follow-up, not something the author could fix in-place.\n### Low\n**L1 — Dead guard, unchanged from the prior round.** `if(returned.has(row.sha))continue` at `:5731` (and the fallback arm's implicit equivalent) can never fire: `returned` is populated only inside `filterReturned` (`:5717-5722`), which both branches call *after* the loops (`:5742`, `:5765`). Harmless today; it is the kind of check that silently stops protecting anything.\n**L2 — The slot-one assignment row is accepted twice in the batched branch.** It arrives through `records.matching` (`:5728-5734`, since production `matches` covers both prefixes per `:2357-2360`) and again through the `probeRefs` loop (`:5736-5742`), so `slotOneHistory` gets a duplicate entry. `assertReviewerAllowlistConsistency` (`:629-632`) tolerates duplicates and max-by-sequence is idempotent, so behaviour is correct — but the duplication is invisible and would mask a future regression.\n**L3 — Return filtering changed semantics: delete-after-select instead of skip-before-select.** The deleted `otherSlotReviewers` filtered returned rows *before* the max-by-sequence choice, so a returned newest record fell back to the slot's earlier record; `filterReturned` (`:5717-5722`) now picks the newest and then deletes the slot outright. I could not construct a duplicate-provider counterexample: `--exclude-reviewer` writes a return record for **every** record of the slot across both namespaces (`:4413`, `:4559`) in one atomic push, so a state where the newest is returned and an older one is still live is not producible; and a peer deletion can only *over*-exclude, never under-exclude. It remains an untested behaviour change — there is no test for the no-peer case or for a returned peer — and `filterReturned`'s early return on `!peers.size` still makes the resolver's answer depend on peer occupancy.\n**L4 — Case normalization is incomplete at two call sites.** `request.headSha` is lowercased at `:5941` and `:6636`, and every ref builder and the resolver use it (`:5688`, `:5691-5692`). But `requirePrOperationRoute(admissionOptions,io,{pr,headSha,issue,…})` at `:5967` and `:6702` passes the **raw destructured parameter**, not `request.headSha`. I verified `validateTerminalReviewerFailure` (`:6518-6531`) is syntactic-only and case-insensitive, so the replacement path's normalization is correctly placed before any durable read; I did **not** trace `derivePrOperationRoute`'s head comparison, so the residual exposure at those two sites is unverified and at worst fail-closed. The new test (`test.mjs:5849-5858`) does not reach this code because `reviewIo()` sets no `enforceAdmission`.\n**L5 — Validation reach widened, fail-closed.** `accept`'s identity check (`:5704`) runs before the `named.slot===requesting` early return (`:5712`), so the requesting slot's own replacement rows and all slots ≥3 are now parsed and validated on every draw, retry and replacement, where the old code parsed only slot 1 (for slot ≥2) or slot 2 (for slot 1). A pre-#2077 replacement message with no `slot=` token under a `-slotN` ref (N≥2) now refuses a slot-N draw too, since `(parsed.slot??1)!==named.slot`. Same for `parseReviewCursor` returning `null` on an absent commit, which reaches `parsed.issue` as a `TypeError` rather than a `LaneError` (`:5733`, `:5754`) — a pre-existing pattern with wider reach. Head-scoped to pre-#2077 heads, so practically unreachable.\n**L6 — Test-coverage gaps against the claims.** No test exercises the legacy holder through the replacement path (`assertIndependent`/`peersNow`, `:6667`, `:6693`, `:6922`) or through the in-mutex retry (`assertDistinct`, `:5966`); coverage is the assignment draw only. `test.mjs:5768` is named \"…without an extra namespace request\" but asserts no request count. `test.mjs:1167`'s `historyScans===1` counts listing *invocations*, not returned rows, so the \"O(1) in history\" claim in the new comment at `:1163-1164` rests on the prefix being head-narrowed (`:5691-5692`) rather than on the assertion; that reasoning is sound (server-side glob filtering, `:1670-1672`) but the test does not prove it.\n## 5. The \"zero spare requests\" question, answered\n**Not a current correctness or safety defect.** Three reasons, each source-backed:\n1. **The refusal is pre-mutex and clean.** `requireReviewWireCapacity` (`:4704`) is invoked at `:6701` *before* `acquireReviewMutex`, and `test.mjs:1272-1276` pins that an over-budget path refuses with no `MUTEX_REF` created. No partial write, no stranded mutex, no duplicate assignment, no lost verdict.\n2. **The pinned 14 is a test-model figure, not a production measurement.** In production, inside a reviewer wire budget, every read this path makes is git-backed and **uncharged**: `consumeReviewWireRequest` is called only from `runGitHubCommand`'s executor (`:1505`), while `getCommit` uses `readGitCommits` (`:2602-2604`), `listRefs` uses `gitRemoteRefRows` (`:2657-2658`, `:1669-1671`), `readRef` uses `gitRemoteRefs` (`:2647`), and `gitRemoteRefs`/`readGitCommits` call `execFileSync` directly (`:1590`, `:1637`). Production `.matching` rows also carry hydrated commits (`:2381-2385`, `allRefs` includes every match via `reviewRecordRefs` `:1839-1845`), so the per-row `io.getCommit(row.sha)` fallback at `:5733` does not fire. The double at `test.mjs:1294` charges 2 per `readReviewRecords` and omits `.matching` commits, which is where the +3 comes from — conservative, not measured.\n3. **The counterexample I could construct still fails closed.** Under the repository's own accounting model, an idempotent `--replace-failed-reviewer` retry on a head with an occupied peer slot *and* one durable return record pays `readReviewReturns` inside both pre-mutex resolver calls (`:5721`, one listing plus one `getCommit` per return row, since `gitRemoteRefRows` returns `{ref,sha}` with no commit), pushing pre-mutex spend past 14 so `requireReviewWireCapacity(11)` refuses the repair. That is an availability refusal on a recovery route, not a safety hole — and for slot-1 replacements the same exposure predates this diff, because the deleted `otherSlotReviewers` called `readReviewReturns` unconditionally whenever slot 2's original ref existed. What is genuinely new is (a) slots ≥2 now pay it when a higher peer exists, and (b) `.matching` spans both namespaces. The PR body's \"25-request budget unchanged\" is true of the ceiling and of production's charged cost; it is true of the pinned model only at the exact boundary, which is what M3 asks to be re-derived in writing.\n## 6. Mandatory checks\n**1. Index usage — non-applicable, source-backed.** The diff contains no SQL, no DDL, no schema object and no `supabase/migrations` path; the six changed files are two `.mjs` (a reviewer-allocation CLI and its test) and four JSON evidence/catalogue records. The nearest analogue is ref-namespace lookup, and the change *narrows* it: both prefixes name the exact `issue-pr-head` tuple (`:5691-5692`), are served by one `git ls-remote` with server-side glob filtering (`:2357-2360`, `:1590-1607`), and are re-filtered client-side (`:2359`) — no loose or unused assumption, and no unbounded namespace scan introduced. I checked the one index-shaped risk explicitly: `git ls-remote` tail-matching cannot over-match here because the patterns are fully qualified with `refs/` and are guarded by `ref.startsWith(value)`.\n**2. Function volatility — non-applicable in the SQL sense; the JS analogue is correct.** No volatility marker exists or is touched. `resolvePeerSlots` (`:5687`) is side-effect-free (reads only; no `createRef`/`updateRef`/`deleteRef`/`atomicReviewRefs` anywhere in `:5687-5769`) but *not* deterministic across calls, because it reads mutable refs and lazily reads returns — which is exactly why it is re-invoked under the mutex at `:5966` and `:6667`/`:6922`. That ordering is preserved by this diff, not weakened. `readReviewRecords` (`:2349`) likewise remains a pure read whose cost profile changed from two listings to one batched listing.\n**3. Exact object checks — present and adequate, with one caveat.** Exact ref *identity*, not mere existence: `namedPeerRef` admits the legacy link only on `ref===replacementBase` (`:5694`), an exact string equality, not a prefix; `accept` cross-checks the parsed commit against the ref name on issue, pr, head and slot and throws otherwise (`:5704`); `readReviewReturns` requires `row.ref===reviewReturnRef(parsed)` (`:4266`); the new test asserts the exact `assignmentPrefix` string handed to `readReviewRecords` (`test.mjs:5770-5771`) and the exact strict-parser contract (`test.mjs:5800-5801`); the budget tests pin the exact reserve literals by regex against the source (`test.mjs:1318-1319`). Judgement\nThe blocking defect from the previous head is fixed narrowly and correctly, without weakening the shared parser any other consumer depends on, and the fix reaches all six resolver consumers including the retry, replacement and conflict-recovery paths. The evidence shape that the prior round flagged is the shape the repository's own checker requires. Everything I found beyond that is either pre-existing and outside the published contract's `allowed_paths` (M1, M2), documentation-level (M3), or Low. None produces a duplicate-provider assignment, a lost verdict, or a stranded mutex; every residual failure direction I could construct refuses before mutating state. Site re-pointing — verified correct, all 34 entries (no gap)\n\nI enumerated every line in `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` matching the detector's pattern (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:9`) and compared with the catalogue. The source yields exactly 34 matching lines, and the catalogue declares exactly 34 sites — a 1:1 mapping with no missing or extra entry:\n\n318, 540, 682, 1000, 1174, 1297, 1315, 1616, 1702, 1948, 2128, 2421, 2818, 4178, 4717, 4897, 5620, 5663, 5696, 5707, 5717, 6209, 6242, 6396, 6447, 6771, 7126, 8139, 8269, 8427, 8428, 8769, 8816, 8817 — matching `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs.json:6,14,22,30,37,45,53,61,69,77,85,93,101,109,117,125,133,141,149,157,165,173,181,189,197,205,213,221,229,237,245,253,261,269`. The claim \"31 stale site line numbers out of 34\" in `.agent/work/3493/2/completion.json:35`-adjacent text and `contract.json:7` is consistent with what I measured (31 changed, 3 already correct).\n\nSpot-checks of reason↔line binding agree: catalogue:61 (`:4897`) reason names `durableVerdictBlocksReplacement`, which is defined at `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:4901` immediately below the cited comment; catalogue:197 (`:4178`) reason describes the reviewer-exclusion return record, which is the comment block at `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:4170-4184`.\n\n### 2. Structural integrity — only `site` changed (no gap)\n\nFiltering the patch to added/removed content lines (excluding `+++`/`---`) shows the catalogue hunks contribute **only** `\"site\"` lines; every `semantic_key`, `line_sha256`, `disposition`, `reason`, and `legacy_semantic_key` is untouched, exactly as `contract.json:23` (prohibited actions) requires. The file remains well-formed JSON with unchanged `schema_version: 1` and `source` (`catalogue:2-3`), which `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:105-106` validates.\n\n### 3. The brief's premise — `site` is genuinely inert (verified)\n\n`disposition()` matches by `semantic_key` only (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:93`); the inventory check compares discovered vs. recorded `semantic_key` sets (`:121-124`); and the reported digest hashes only `semantic_key` values (`:138`). The `site` field appears exactly once in executable logic — inside an error-message template (`:124`). `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/README.md:38` states the same contract: \"`site` is a diagnostic line number. Identity is `semantic_key` + `line_sha256`.\" So the change cannot alter any disposition or CI verdict, and the \"derived digest unchanged at 623c3a6c3f85\" claim in `completion.json:20,35` is structurally supported, matching the digest recorded for the earlier generation at `.agent/work/3493/1/completion.json:22`.\n\n### 4. Secrets / personal identifiers — none introduced\n\nThe two new JSON files contain no credentials, tokens, or personal data. The only environment-revealing strings are `\"worktree\": \"C:/repos/shared-db/.claude/worktrees/3493-pr3499\"`, `\"dispatcher\"`, and `\"worker\"` (`contract.json:26-28`), a shape already present in the prior generation (`/`.agent/work/3493/1/contract.json:9-12`) — this is pre-existing repository convention, not a new disclosure. No `op://` or `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` reference (compare `scripts/catalog-truth.mjs:15`, which is untouched).\n\n### 5. Evidence-file consistency — pair shape is the expected one (verified)\n\n`contract.json:4-5` declares `work_issue: 3493`, `generation: 2`, which resolves through `scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs:48-53` to `.agent/work/3493/2/contract.json` + `.agent/work/3493/2/completion.json` — exactly the two files added in `patch.diff:7,52`, and exactly the pair `acceptableEvidencePairs()` prefers (`scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs:101-110`). `completion.json:8` names `refs/db-contracts/3493/2`, matching the required `contractRef(work_issue, generation)` form enforced at `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:72-73`. `files_changed` (`completion.json:12-14`) lists only the catalogue, which is what changed at the recorded implementation head; the two evidence files are the permitted \"own pair\" tail (`scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:66-70`). The `base_sha` at `completion.json:9` equals the PR base/merge base in the packet's `identity.json` — satisfying the #2845 anchor rule at `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:44-51`.\n\n### 6. Residual verification gaps (not defects, but the merge gate must supply them)\n\n- **No tests were run for this packet** (packet MANIFEST §5: \"No tests were run for this packet\"). The `16 passed` claim for `scripts/throughput-guard/check-throughput-truth-audit.test.mjs` is nonetheless corroborated structurally: that file contains exactly 16 `test(...)` declarations (`scripts/throughput-guard/check-throughput-truth-audit.test.mjs:41,43,54,56,58,60,69,80,95,106,113,126,133,153,159,182`). The claim is not load-bearing (the detector ignores `site`), but it is unverified here.\n\n### 7. Mandatory checklist items — applicability\n\n- **Index usage:** not applicable, and no index assumption was introduced or relied upon. The diff contains no SQL, no predicate, and no join — only JSON metadata. The one file in this repository that makes index claims (`scripts/catalog-truth.mjs:19`) is neither changed by this diff nor reachable from the changed files per packet MANIFEST §7.\n- **Function volatility:** not applicable. No SQL function is created, replaced, or modified; there is no `create ... function` in the patch, and no volatility marker is touched anywhere in the three changed files.\n- **Exact object checks:** satisfied for the dependencies this change actually has. The change is diagnostic metadata only; the risk that matters is whether the 31 re-pointed `site` values land on the right lines.\n\n## What I verified (with evidence)\n\nDiff shape. The packet diff removes exactly 31 `- \"site\"` lines and adds exactly 31 `+ \"site\"` lines; the only other `-` lines are the three standard file headers (`.ai-review-deepseek-afc46f3714c7e62ee79597eb/patch.diff:4`, `:49`, `:100`), and inside the catalogue section the only `+` lines are the 31 site lines (`patch.diff:107`–`patch.diff:376`). So \"only `site` changed\" holds literally: no `semantic_key`, `line_sha256`, `disposition`, `reason`, or `legacy_semantic_key` line was added or removed.\n\nSite-set exactness. The head catalogue has 34 entries (`docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs.json:5`–`:275`) with site values 318, 540, 682, 1000, 1174, 1297, 1315, 1616, 1702, 1948, 2128, 2421, 2818, 4178, 4717, 4897, 5620, 5663, 5696, 5707, 5717, 6209, 6242, 6396, 6447, 6771, 7126, 8139, 8269, 8427, 8428, 8769, 8816, 8817. Searching the declared source for the detector's own pattern (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:9`) returns exactly those 34 line numbers and no others (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:318`, `:540`, `:682`, `:1000`, `:1174`, … `:8817`; a second case-variant search returned the identical 34 lines, so no case-folded match was missed). The site set therefore equals the discoverable-line set exactly — no re-pointed value lands off-pattern, and the three untouched entries (`…json:22`, `:85`, `:109`, sites 682/540/318) are also still on-pattern, i.e. genuinely not stale.\n\nEntry-level semantics. Every entry whose `reason` is specific matches the text at its new site, in both offset groups: `…json:6`/reason at `:10` vs source `1948` (retirement record missing field); `…json:37`/reason at `:41` vs source `7126` (`// rather than skipped. A missing message must never look like \"no live`, source `7125`–`7127`); `…json:61`/reason at `:65` vs source `4897`, whose comment sits immediately above `function durableVerdictBlocksReplacement` at source `4901`; `…json:197`/reason at `:201` vs source `4178`; `…json:205`/reason at `:209` vs source `1702`; `…json:213`/reason at `:217` vs source `2128` (inside the file-classification builder, source `2126`–`2135`); `…json:173`/reason at `:177` vs source `1616`; `…json:181`/reason at `:185` vs source `2818`; `…json:269`/reason at `:273` vs source `1174`. Unchanged offsets are uniform (+6 for the 22 lower sites, +26 for the 9 higher ones), consistent with the two line insertions that displaced the recorded numbers.\n\n`site` is not load-bearing. `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:75` derives its own site value from discovery, `:93` and `:124`/`:131`–`:132` match and validate rows by `semantic_key`/`line_sha256` only, and `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/README.md:38` states \"`site` is a diagnostic line number. Identity is `semantic_key` + `line_sha256`.\" So no disposition, refusal, or CI verdict can change from this diff — the contract's assumption (`contract.json:38`) is correct as written.\n\nEvidence files. `allowed_paths` (`contract.json:13`–`:17`) and `file_writes` (`:18`–`:22`) name exactly the three files the PR changes; `required_checks` (`:32`–`:36`) match the three recorded `checks` commands in the same order (`completion.json:18`, `:23`, `:28`); the prohibition on editing the detector or its tests (`contract.json:28`) is honoured (patch touches neither); `db_reads`/`db_writes` are empty in both (`contract.json:23`–`:24`, `completion.json:14`–`:15`) and the diff opens no database path. The recorded `head_sha` differing from the PR head is the documented shape, not an error: `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:29` requires only that `report.head_sha` be an ancestor of the PR head, and `:66`–`:70` allow exactly this PR's own two evidence files to follow it; `.github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml:232` enforces that.\n\nSecrets/PII. All added lines are visible in the diff (`patch.diff:7`–`:45`, `:52`–`:97`) and contain no token, email, or username. The only host-specific strings are the worktree path (`contract.json:12`) and the worker label (`contract.json:10`), which match the pre-existing convention already on main (`.agent/work/3493/1/contract.json:10`, `:12`).\n\n## Findings\n\nBlocking defects: none found. I could not construct a wrong-value, wrong-object, or wrong-scope defect from the diff.\n\nVerification gaps (state these, they do not overturn the approval but they bound it):\n\n1. No check was executed for this packet (packet MANIFEST §5), so the three recorded results — `completion.json:20`, `:25`, `:30` — including \"0 stale entries\" across all 72 catalogues (`completion.json:34`) and \"16 passed\"/\"70 passed\", are author claims, not observed evidence. Missing evidence: a run of `node scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` and the throughput-guard tests at this head.\n2. Hash-level identity is not verifiable in this profile. An entry's intended location is defined by `line_sha256` (`README.md:28`–`:30`, `:38`), and confirming that each new site number is the current line whose SHA-256 equals its recorded `line_sha256` requires hashing the source lines. Missing evidence: SHA-256 of the 34 source lines, or a discovery run printing site values (my verification is set-level plus reason↔line semantics).\n3. Residual ambiguity is confined to the identical-reason entries inside the two adjacent matching pairs: sites 8427/8428 (`…json:221` and `…json:101`) and 8816/8817 (`…json:165` and `…json:69`). Both lines of each pair match the pattern and both entries carry the same generic reason string, so an undetected swap inside each pair cannot be ruled out without hashing. Impact is confined to a diagnostic field (`README.md:38`).\n4. Git facts asserted but unverifiable here: `completion.json:10` (`head_sha` 12b47375…), `contract.json:8`/`completion.json:9` (`base_sha` b32deb1…), and `contract.json:7`/`completion.json:8` (`contract_ref` refs/db-contracts/3493/2 versus `contract_sha256`). Whether 12b47375… is the catalogue-change commit and an ancestor of 8fa04ca…, and whether `contract_sha256` hashes the published contract (`scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:74`–`:75`), needs git; my tools have none.\n\nInformational (design observation, not this PR's defect):\n\n5. Nothing in the repository validates `site` at all. The detector overwrites site from discovery (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:75`) and matches by `semantic_key` (`:93`, `:124`, `:131`); searching `scripts/throughput-guard` found no assertion comparing a catalogue's `site` to its source, and `README.md:38` documents the field as diagnostic. Consequently a wrong or later-stale site value cannot fail CI — which is exactly why 31 stale values survived to this follow-up, and why the correctness claim for this field (`completion.json:34`) is self-reported. If the project wants site agreement to be enforceable rather than aspirational, that is a follow-up worth filing; it is out of scope for this diff.\n6. Two entries lack `legacy_semantic_key` (`…json:29`–`:34`, `:36`–`:43`). The diff's unchanged context shows they lacked it before this change, so this is pre-existing and untouched; noted only so it is not mistaken for a regression introduced here.\n7. The governed brief's three mandatory axes are SQL/Postgres-shaped and do not match this change. Stated explicitly rather than skipped, with the evidence, below.\n\n## Mandatory axes\n\nIndex usage — not applicable. The change contains no SQL or query text: a search of the patch for `IMMUTABLE|STABLE|VOLATILE|CREATE|ALTER|DROP|INDEX|FUNCTION|PRIMARY KEY|CONSTRAINT|SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE` returns no matches, and the complete added content (`patch.diff:7`–`:45`, `:52`–`:97`, `:107`–`:376`) is JSON metadata. No predicate or join is touched, so no index is relied on, and there is no loose, unused, or unusable index assumption to call out. Both evidence files record empty `db_reads`/`db_writes` (`contract.json:23`–`:24`, `completion.json:14`–`:15`).\n\nFunction volatility — not applicable. No function is defined and no SQL body exists in the change; the catalogue merely points at `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` (`…json:3`), a Node CLI. There is therefore no marker that could be looser than its body. (The failure mode the axis names — a body reading tables marked IMMUTABLE — has no instance here.)\n\nExact object checks — asserted exactly where an assertion exists, vacuous elsewhere. The catalogue declares its `source` (`…json:3`) and the checker refuses unless the declared source maps to this exact catalogue filename (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:106`), lies inside the discovery roots (`:49`), declares exactly `schema_version` 1 (`:105`), and has every `semantic_key`/`line_sha256` present in current discovery (`:124`, `:131`–`:132`) — that is existence-of-the-right-object, not name-only existence. No schema, table, view, function signature, or column is claimed anywhere in the change, so that class of check has no target. The declared source file does exist (scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs, 9786 lines).\n\n## Final line\n\n> VOIDED REVIEWER LINE - VERDICT: APPROVE 8fa04ca76303533350d9ec7f34c98c29c96f9217\n\n> VERDICT LINE VOIDED BY THE GOVERNED REVIEW RUNNER.\n>\n> 1 line(s) that a verdict parser would have read as a decision (APPROVE) at this head were rewritten so that no tool can read them as a verdict.
