REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\nRead the sealed MANIFEST, the full 750-line `patch.diff`, the new reporter and its tests at head, the producer it consumes (`scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs`), the evidence gate (`scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs`, `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs`, `scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs`), the truth-audit disposition rules, the drift alarm workflow, and the repo's evidence-path policy doc. No files were edited; this was a read-only review, and I ran no shell (this profile has none), so every hash-dependent and git-history-dependent claim below is marked UNVERIFIED rather than assumed.\nProvisional verdict: **REVISE** — additive, read-only, correctly scoped, but the reporter can restate an unverified/empty read as a clean ledger, can silently drop every owner attribution, and can print an issue number as a \"source PR\".\n## Verified first (what holds)\n- **Packet identity.** Manifest base `f627783…`, head `0977f0c…`, whole-source digest `bb97e67…`, clean working tree, 6 added files — matches the injected authoritative head and the brief's inventory exactly. I reviewed that head and nothing else.\n- **Shape compatibility with the producer is real, not assumed.** `runDriftCheck` returns `{projectRef, baseRef, target, drift, fileByVersion, pendingClassifications}` (`scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:413`) and `main()` reads precisely those top-level keys (`scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.mjs:272,277,280,284-285`). Every drift sub-field the report renders matches `computeDrift`/`assessDrift` (`:206-212`, `:233-238`).\n- **A failed upstream check cannot ride the pipe into a clean report.** On `Unknown` the check writes only to stderr and returns 2 without printing JSON (`:477-486`), so the reporter receives empty stdin and refuses (`:256-259`). The residual \"failed read looks clean\" pathways are findings H1 and M5 below.\n- **Read-only claim holds in source.** Imports are only `node:child_process`, `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url` (`:29-32`); the sole subprocess is `git log` (`:165`). No DB client, no token, no network, no dispatch, no write. No grant/role/policy/`permissions:` surface changes — the script is wired into no workflow (grep over `.github/**` for `report-ledger-drift-status`: zero matches), so the \"Role and permission changes\" section is **non-applicable on source**, not merely absent.\n- **Migration immutability: non-applicable on source.** No `.sql`, no migration, no version reservation in the diff; `migration_versions: []`; `db_reads: []`/`db_writes: []` in both contract and completion, consistent with the code.\n- **#2508 is not closed.** The only closing keyword in the packet is `Closes #3587` (PR body). `docs/verification/ledger-drift-2508-status-20260925.md` states \"**Stays OPEN — blocked on production applies.**\"; the script and tests cite #2508 only as motivation. No production or database action appears anywhere in the diff.\n- **One-pair evidence, path and binding checks pass on the face of the files.** Exactly one pair in the net diff (`.agent/work/3587/1/`), and no `.agent/work/3518/*` or `.agent/work/2508/*` exists in the tree, so `resolveEvidencePair` classifies `current`, not `partial`/`conflicted` (`scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs:70-90`). `contract_ref` equals `contractRef(3587, 1)`; `pr: 3518` and `outcome: \"ready-for-merge\"` satisfy `validatePullRequestCompletion` (`scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs:246-252`); `files_changed` (4) ⊆ `allowed_paths` (6); all three `required_checks` are recorded with `exit_code: 0`. The checked-in contract matches the JSON published in the issue comment field-for-field.\n- **Disposition catalogue is complete and correctly keyed.** The audit's `PATTERN` (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:10`) matches exactly four lines in the new script — 25, 63, 262, 266 — and the catalogue carries exactly those four sites, at those line numbers, with reasons that describe the actual line text; `dispositionFileName('scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.mjs')` equals the catalogue filename (`:46-51`); `.test.` files are excluded from discovery (`:65`), so the new test file needs no catalogue. UNVERIFIED offline: the `line_sha256`/`semantic_key` digests and the recorded audit exit 0 (no shell available to recompute).\n## Findings\n### High\n**H1 — The reporter can present an unverified, empty, or partial read as a clean ledger, and invents the target when absent.** `scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.mjs:261-268` validates only four facts (`drift.mergedCount`/`appliedCount` are numbers; `actionableMergedNotApplied`/`mergedNotApplied` are arrays). Everything else it *renders* is defaulted: `target: result.target ?? 'production'` (`:284`), `baseRef = result.baseRef ?? 'origin/main'` (`:277`), `projectRef ?? 'unknown'` (`:285`), `intentionallyExcluded/foreignTarget/appliedNotMerged ?? []` (`:91-93`), `kind ?? 'genuinely-pending'` (`:73`). `drift.driftFound` is never read; the verdict is re-derived at `:100`. Consequences, all reachable from the tool's own documented interface (`--json drift.json`, `--json -`):\n- A JSON with `mergedCount: 0, appliedCount: 0, actionableMergedNotApplied: [], mergedNotApplied: []` — the exact signature of a failed query, credential, or permission — prints `Applied in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations: **0**` followed by `**No actionable drift.**` and exits 0. The producer refuses this shape on purpose: *\"the migration ledger came back EMPTY… zero rows means the query, the credential or the permission failed — not that nothing is applied\"* (`scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:193-199`), and *\"no migration files found on the base branch… that would report every applied row as an orphan and every real gap as clean\"* (`:185-192`). The reporter is now the one place in the chain where that refusal can be undone — on production drift alarm #2508, whose whole failure mode is a comment that reads as clean.\n- A JSON missing `target` is reported **as production**, naming production holders and demanding production applies (`:120`) from absent data. `projectRef ?? 'unknown'` is honest; `target ?? 'production'` is not.\n- A JSON whose `driftFound` is `true` but whose arrays are empty/stale is reported as \"No actionable drift.\", contradicting the check that produced it.\n- A JSON missing a per-version classification gets an invented `genuinely-pending` (`:73`) where the producer throws `Unknown(\"pending migration X has no classification\")` (`:227`) and requires exact key-set equality plus a non-empty reason (`:135-148`).\nFix: assert every field the report renders (presence + type, not `??`), refuse on `mergedCount === 0 || appliedCount === 0` with the producer's reasoning, require `typeof drift.driftFound === 'boolean'` and refuse (or print the check's own verdict) when it disagrees with the derived state, require `target`/`baseRef`/`projectRef` instead of defaulting them, and refuse a missing classification instead of defaulting `kind`.\n### Medium\n**M2 — Attribution failure is silent and indistinguishable from \"no PR number in history\".** `attributeVersions` swallows every git error with a bare `catch { continue }` (`:169-172`) — absent local `origin/main`, shallow CI clone, non-repo, `maxBuffer` overflow (`:167`) — and `buildStatusRows` then renders `pr: null` as `unattributed` (`:111`). The output is a complete-looking promotion table with no owner and no statement that git history was unreachable, exit 0. The repo's own standard for this same baseRef resolution is the opposite and is documented as such: `resolveFreshBaseRef` throws `Unknown` because *\"an unresolvable base ref must be loud rather than silent\"* (`scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:324-346`). For a tool whose entire stated purpose is \"WHO owns its promotion\" (`:9`), degrading the answer silently is the failure the tool exists to remove. Fix: count failures, distinguish `git-failed` from `no-pr-in-subject` on the row, and print an explicit line (\"attribution unavailable for N of M versions: git history not reachable at `<baseRef>`\").\n**M3 — Invented PR ownership: an issue number is printed under a column headed `source PR`.** `prNumberFromSubject` accepts any `#(\\d+)` as a last resort (`:56-57`), and its own doc comment concedes the number may be a *work issue* reference (`:47-48`). That value is rendered as `#<n>` in a table whose header is `| version | source PR | file |` (`:108-113`) and is republished as \"source PR\" in `docs/verification/ledger-drift-2508-status-20260925.md:38-45` for all six pending versions. Nothing in the row, the report, or the doc distinguishes a merge-commit-derived PR number (`Merge pull request #N`, reliable) from a bare-`#N` guess; `rows[].commit` and `rows[].subject` are captured (`:75-76`) and never rendered, so a reader cannot check the derivation. The test suite bakes the ambiguity in: `prNumberFromSubject('migration: re-reserve 20260911204023 as 20260911212849 (#2746)') === 2746` is asserted as correct with no evidence 2746 is a PR. Fix: rename the column to `source PR / issue`, or carry and print the derivation (`merge|squash|bare`) and mark `bare` as unverified, or drop the fallback. This is the precise \"inventing PR ownership\" risk the review brief names, and it lands in a document people will quote on #2508.\n**M4 — No escaping of interpolated strings in markdown destined for an issue comment.** `projectRef`, `target`, `baseRef` (`:95,:97,:120`), `row.version` and `row.file` inside code spans and a pipe table (`:112-113`), and orphan `version` taken from the **database ledger** (`:131`) are interpolated raw. A `|` breaks the table; a backtick breaks the code span; a `\\n` injects arbitrary lines into a comment that later agent sessions read as authority — including a forged `**Holders:**` line or a forged `Closes #2508`. The producer asserts `/^\\d{14}$/` on every version it emits (`:168-173`); the reporter re-asserts nothing about the versions it prints, and it accepts arbitrary JSON from a file or stdin. Fix: validate versions against `/^\\d{14}$/` and strip/escape backticks, pipes, and control characters in every interpolated string.\n**M5 — The documented pipeline masks the drift verdict.** `check … --json | report … --json -` exits **0** whenever the check exits **1 (DRIFT)**, because the reporter always returns 0 after printing (`:290`) and a shell without `pipefail` reports only the right-hand status. That pipeline is advertised three times: the script header (`:22-23`), `USAGE` (`:~218`), and `docs/verification/ledger-drift-2508-status-20260925.md:57-59`. Wired as documented into a scheduled job, it would silently disarm the alarm. The current alarm workflow is unaffected — it uses the non-JSON path with `tee` (`.github/workflows/migration-ledger-drift.yml:108`). Fix: propagate the check's verdict (exit 1 when `driftFound`), or state in all three places that the pipeline's status is the *reporter's*, never the drift verdict, and require `set -o pipefail`.\n**M6 — The header's exit-code contract contradicts the code.** `:25-27` says exit 2 covers *\"no actionable versions to attribute\"*; the code prints `**No actionable drift.**` and returns 0 (`:100-103`, `:290`). In a tool whose interface to an alarm pipeline *is* its exit codes, and in a repo that documents exit semantics this carefully elsewhere (`check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:449-451`), the comment is wrong and will be trusted.\n**M7 — The tests do not cover the seam that matters, and one is misnamed.** `main()`'s happy path is never exercised: the only two CLI tests are refusals, and `'CLI refuses invalid JSON'` passes a nonexistent path, so it actually exercises the read failure at `:248-251` and leaves the `JSON.parse` refusal (`:256-259`) untested — while `completion.json` claims \"refusal paths\" are proven. The fixture `sampleDrift` nests `fileByVersion` and `pendingClassifications` **inside** `drift`, but the producer emits them at the **top level** (`:413`) and `main()` must splice them in (`:279-281`); so the unit tests validate a shape the tool never receives and never validate the shape it does — exactly the seam where a mismatch would yield an all-`unattributed` report and still exit 0. `assert.throws(() => { throw new Unknown('x') }, Unknown)` is tautological and proves nothing about the tool. Also untested: stdin (`--json -`), the fallback-to-oldest-entry branch (`:~187`), the 0-count/absent-field cases in H1, and any escaping case for M4.\n**M8 — The evidence pair's own gate was never run in the recorded evidence, and its topology cannot be confirmed from the packet (UNVERIFIED).** `completion.json.checks` lists three test suites, the truth audit, and `git diff --check` — but neither `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs --validate-completion` nor `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs --contract-file … --report-file … --pr-base-sha … --pr-head-sha …`, which is what actually judges this pair (`.github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml:225-232`). That gate requires exactly: an implementation commit containing **no** evidence files, then the two evidence files **alone** on top (`docs/agents/agent-work-contract-repo-maintenance-evidence.md`, \"The path, in order\", steps 3-4; `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T1825Z-…-wrapup.md:97`: *\"Interleaving breaks `verifyGitEvidence` permanently at that head\"*). Here `report.head_sha` is `60eee73…`, whose subject is *\"chore(evidence): move reporter proof to tooling issue 3587\"* — an evidence-titled commit — and PR head `0977f0c…` is *\"chore(evidence): bind PR 3518 to reporter issue 3587\"*. If the pair was introduced at `60eee73`, then `changedFiles(mergeBase, head_sha)` includes the pair while `files_changed` lists only four files (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:60-67`) **and** the tail changes one file instead of the required two (`:71-77`) — both refuse. If the pair was introduced at `0977f0c`, both pass and the recorded `files_changed` is correct. I cannot resolve which from the sealed packet: no shell/git in this review profile, the manifest records that no tests were run, and `.git/logs/HEAD` contains only the snapshot checkout line. This is reported as UNVERIFIED, not as proven broken — but the pair asserts its own topology in `assumptions_resolved` (\"exactly one evidence pair for #3587 follows the implementation\") without recording the verifier output that would prove it. Also unverifiable offline: `contract_sha256` equality against the published `refs/db-contracts/3587/1` (`:78-81`), and every recorded exit code and test count. Fix: record the two verifier commands and their output in `completion.json.checks`.\n### Low\n**L9 — `attributeVersions` is documented as injectable but is not fully injectable, and reports an unpinned snapshot.** It captures module-level `repoRoot` derived from `import.meta.url` (`:34`, used at `:165`), so no test can point it at a fixture repository — the reason M7's attribution tests can only assert on argv, never on real history behaviour. It also walks the **local** `origin/main` without fetching, while the producer fetches before listing files (`:334-337`); the report prints the ref *name*, never the resolved SHA, the drift-run identity, or the check's verdict, so a pasted comment cannot be tied to the snapshot it described. That is the same lesson the repo already encoded for evidence pairs (#2845, `agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:33-49`) and the same staleness the tool exists to remove (`:9-11`).\n**L10 — `baseRef` from untrusted JSON is placed in git argv *before* the `--` guard** (`:165`), so a value beginning with `-` is parsed as a git option rather than a revision — e.g. `--output=<path>` creates/truncates a file, `--ext-diff`/textconv can execute a helper. That contradicts the header's \"It never writes\" (`:18-19`). The `file` values *are* correctly guarded by `--`. Sibling instance of the same class in the producer: `--base-ref` values go unvalidated into `git rev-parse` (`:337`) and `git ls-tree` (`:352`). Fix: reject a leading `-` and restrict to a ref charset (or `rev-parse --verify` first) in both places.\n**L11 — The clean-state early return discards counts it just computed.** `:100-103` returns before the non-actionable listing block at `:123-125`, so with 0 actionable and 0 orphans the report prints only \"No actionable drift.\" and never the `excluded`/`foreign` numbers from `:91-92` — i.e. today's real shape minus the six actionable versions would report \"23 retired / 1 foreign-target\" nowhere, despite the parenthetical promising visibility.\n**L12 — `kind` and `reason` are computed per row (`:73-74`) and never rendered.** The report asserts \"genuinely-pending\" in a heading (`:106`) without the guard's reason, which is the only thing that makes a row actionable to a reader six weeks later — the stated design goal (`:84-86`).\n**L13 — Evidence-document inaccuracies.** `docs/verification/ledger-drift-2508-status-20260925.md:66` says \"(16 tests)\"; the test file contains 18 `test()` calls and `completion.json` records \"18 passed\" (the PR body repeats 16). Same document: header \"**Date:** 2026-09-25 (4:22 AM EST)\" versus \"2026-09-25 06:22 UTC\" two sections later — 06:22Z is 02:22 EDT, not 4:22 EST. It cites main as `4b74a8696` (9 characters) where this repo's evidence standard is an exact 40-character SHA (`SHA_PATTERN`, `agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:11`). And it pins neither the drift JSON nor the base commit its six attributions were computed at, so the table cannot be reproduced or re-checked — while being the artifact that will be quoted on #2508.\n**L14 — `readFileSync(0, 'utf8')` (`:248`)** throws `EAGAIN` on a non-blocking stdin pipe on some platforms and blocks indefinitely when stdin is a TTY; both are reachable from the advertised `--json -`. The `EAGAIN` case is at least reported as `UNKNOWN` exit 2 rather than as clean, so it fails safe — but the primary documented usage can fail spuriously.\n**L15 — The new test file is wired into no CI job.** No workflow references `report-ledger-drift-status` (grep over `.github/**`: zero matches), and top-level `scripts/*.test.mjs` are enumerated per job rather than globbed (`plan_orchestrator_throughput_guard_truth.md:263` explicitly forbids globbing them into the shallow tools job). The 18 tests are local-only, so the refusals they prove can rot unnoticed. Contract `required_checks` covers them locally only.\n**L16 — Rollback coupling between the script and its disposition catalogue.** Reverting `scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.mjs` without also reverting `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~report-ledger-drift-status.mjs.json` fails the truth audit: *\"disposition catalogue describes a source with no discovered call sites and must be retired\"* (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:119`). The two must move together. A full revert of the merge is otherwise clean — additive files only, no DB state, no reserved version, no workflow depending on them, so rollback preserves the prior capability exactly (the drift check is untouched by this PR).\n**L17 — Minor parser/robustness notes.** A repeated `--json` silently last-wins (`:~207`); `--json -h` treats `-h` as a filename; `class Unknown extends Error {}` (`:36`) never sets `name`, and `main()` prints `String(error.message)` for *any* error type (`:232`), so a non-`Unknown` bug is reported as though it were a typed refusal. `fileByVersion` keys in the producer are `filename.slice(0,14)` (`:402`), so two files sharing a 14-digit prefix would silently collide and this reporter would attribute the wrong file — pre-existing, but newly load-bearing as the attribution key.\n## Mandatory additional checks\n**1. Index usage — NON-APPLICABLE, source-backed.** The six changed files contain no SQL and no database object. `contract.json` and `completion.json` both declare `db_reads: []`, `db_writes: []`, matching the code: the script imports only `node:child_process`, `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url` (`:29-32`) and its one subprocess is `git log` (`:165`). The only ledger read in this flow is the pre-existing constant `SELECT` in `check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs` (`fetchAppliedVersions`, \"THE STATEMENT IS A CONSTANT\", `:370-380`), which this PR does not touch. No predicate and no join is introduced, so no index obligation arises and no loose index assumption is made. The lookup-cost analogue *is* satisfied and I verified it: attribution is scoped to the actionable versions only (`:270-276`), not all 700+ merged versions, and version→file / version→attribution are object-key lookups. The one residual is the pre-existing 14-character prefix key collision noted in L17.\n**2. Function volatility — NON-APPLICABLE for SQL** (no function is created or altered; nothing in the diff carries or needs an `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` marker). **The JS analogue is correct**, and I checked it rather than inferring it: the section banner \"Pure logic — no network, no filesystem\" (`:38-40`) contains exactly `prNumberFromSubject`, `buildStatusRows`, `formatStatusReport`, and all three are genuinely free of I/O and of module state; the I/O section holds only `attributeVersions`. One defect against that declared contract: `attributeVersions` is presented as injectable via `run`/`baseRef` but closes over module-level `repoRoot` (`:34`), so its filesystem dependency is not injectable (L9).\n**3. Exact object checks — NON-APPLICABLE for schema/table/view/function/column** (none is asserted because none is created, altered, or read by this diff; the `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` reference at `:97` is prose in a rendered string, not a query). **Applied to what the change actually depends on, it under-asserts**, which is the substance of H1/M4/M6: it validates 4 of the ~12 fields it renders (`:261-268`), never checks `driftFound`, never checks that version strings satisfy the producer's `/^\\d{14}$/` invariant before printing them, treats absent `fileByVersion`/`pendingClassifications`/`intentionallyExcluded`/`foreignTarget`/`appliedNotMerged`/`target`/`baseRef` as tolerable defaults rather than as a wrong-object refusal, and has no way to confirm the JSON came from the check it names (the producer emits no schema/version marker to check against). A renamed producer field would silently render `**0** retired/deliberately-held, **0** foreign-target` — a wrong number printed as fact.\n## Bottom line\nNothing here writes to a database, dispatches a workflow, touches production, exceeds the contract's `allowed_paths`, closes #2508, or breaks an existing gate; the rendering and first-parent attribution logic is sound and matches the producer's real output shape. But the reporter's refusal discipline is materially weaker than the producer it reports on, in the specific direction the brief asks about: it can call an empty or partial read \"No actionable drift\", it can lose every owner attribution without saying so, and it can print an issue number as a `source PR` in a document that will be quoted on the production alarm. H1, M2, M3, M5, M6 and M7 are all inside the added files and fixable in this PR without widening its scope; M8 needs the pair's own gate output recorded. I could not verify the digest-bound values (`line_sha256`, `semantic_key`, `contract_sha256`) or any recorded exit code, and the manifest confirms no tests were run for this packet, so those remain UNVERIFIED rather than accepted.\nVERDICT: REVISE The topology point fails loudly as a red check if wrong; it cannot merge silently.\nPrior Lows L9 (injectability), L10 (`baseRef` before the `--` guard), L11 (discarded non-actionable counts), L12 (`kind`/`reason` never rendered), L13 (doc inaccuracies), L14 (`readFileSync(0)` EAGAIN), L16 (rollback coupling) and the `Unknown.name` half of L17 are all fixed; L15 and the residual halves of L9/L17 survive and are restated below.\n## New findings\n### Medium\n**N1 — This PR carried a reviewed truth-audit disposition catalogue for its ledger-truth claims at its previous head and no longer does, because the rewrite reworded every tracked phrase out of the file; the published contract still says the catalogue is part of the delivered scope.**\n- The gen-1 contract lists `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~report-ledger-drift-status.mjs.json` in **both** `allowed_paths` and `file_writes` (`contract.json:19, 27`), and its first assumption is \"The PR changes only the reporter, its tests, **disposition catalogue**, verification document, and this evidence pair\" (`contract.json:38`). No such file is in the net diff or in the tree at head — the directory holds 76 catalogues plus `README.md`, none for this script.\n- The prior review recorded the audit at `0977f0c` as `call_sites=328 sources=77`, with the catalogue carrying four sites at lines 25, 63, 262, 266. `completion.json:35-38` now records `call_sites=324 sources=76`. Exactly one source and exactly four call sites left discovery between two heads of the same PR.\n- I confirmed the mechanism instead of inferring it. `PATTERN` (`check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:10`) tracks `missing | never created | not applied | NOT_DERIVABLE | _created_by_applied_dynamic_ddl`, and the rewritten reporter matches none of them — a case-insensitive character-class grep over `scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.mjs` returns zero hits. The audit passes.\nWhy this is a finding and not a bookkeeping nit: the guard exists so that an assertion that merged work is not applied carries a hand-written, substantive reviewed reason (dispositions `README.md`: \"refuses unless **every** discovered call site carries a hand-written disposition with a substantive reason\"). The producer's identical assertions *are* catalogued — `scripts~check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs.json` dispositions precisely the `MERGED BUT NOT APPLIED` header and the file's header claim, both as `excluded` with reasons. The reporter now makes the same claim, in output destined for production drift alarm #2508, with zero reviewed dispositions, because its wording no longer trips a lexical pattern. A green derived count is not coverage.\nI am not asserting bad faith — the rewording may well have fallen out of the H1/M3 rewrites, and retiring a catalogue whose source has no sites is *required* by `:118`, so the author handled that half correctly. But the PR lost reviewed coverage of this claim class between two heads, and the published contract's declared scope and the delivered scope now disagree with nothing recording the difference. Under this repo's own evidence discipline — \"An evidence pair naming a base nobody is reviewing is worse than an absent one, because it reads as coverage and survives a skim\" (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:36-46`) — an unrecorded divergence between declared and delivered scope is the same shape.\nFixable inside the already-published `allowed_paths`, so no new generation is needed: either restore the natural phrasing and ship the catalogue with substantive reasons, or record an explicit reviewed rationale (catalogue `README.md` or the verification doc) for why a pure renderer of already-validated producer output carries no tracked truth claim. Separately, note in `completion.json.assumptions_resolved` that the catalogue was retired rather than written, so the contract's `assumptions[0]` and the delivery do not silently contradict each other.\n### Low\n**L1 — The reporter asserts a 14-digit invariant on `appliedNotMerged` that the producer never guarantees.** `assertVersions` covers `drift.appliedNotMerged` (:64, :49-53), but those values come straight from the ledger: `fetchAppliedVersions` returns `String(row.version)` with no format check (`read-preview-ledger.mjs:16`). Only `readPreviewLedger` — a different consumer — enforces `/^\\d{14}$/` (`:31`). One hand-applied ledger row with a non-canonical version, which is precisely the orphan case this tool exists to escalate, makes the reporter exit 2 with \"drift.appliedNotMerged must be an array of unique 14-digit versions\" and emit no report at all, while the producer still exits 1 and prints the row. Fail-closed and loud, so not a safety bug — but the tool becomes unusable in the exact scenario it was built for. Validating orphan versions separately and rendering an unparseable one as an explicit malformed-ledger row would keep the refusal without losing the report.\n**L2 — `REF` is narrower than the ref syntax the producer accepts.** `/^[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+$/` (:46) rejects `~`, `^`, `:` and `@{…}`, so `check … --base-ref origin/main~1 --json | report … --json -` yields valid producer JSON that the reporter refuses at :60. Fail-safe, but a documented-usage dead end; either widen the charset while keeping the leading-`-` and `..` guards, or state in `USAGE` that only plain ref names are accepted.\n**L3 — The new test file is wired into no CI job.** No workflow references `report-ledger-drift-status` anywhere in the tree; the only hits are the script, its test and the doc. Its sibling is enumerated twice (`.github/workflows/migration-ledger-drift.yml:92`, `.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml:49`). All 26 tests — including every refusal this review relies on — are local-only and can rot unnoticed; the contract's `required_checks` binds one run, not the future. `migration-ledger-drift.yml:92` already runs the producer's tests and owns this alarm; adding the file there is a one-line change. This compounds N1: with no CI coverage of the tests and no reviewed disposition of the claim, nothing automated protects the safety property this head was revised to add.\n**L4 — The report is still not bound to the snapshot it describes.** `formatStatusReport` prints the `baseRef` *name* (:129, :140) and never a resolved commit SHA, and `attributeVersions` walks local `origin/main` without fetching (:200-210) while the producer fetches before listing files (`check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:331-347`). Under the documented `--json drift.json` usage (:21, :260), attribution is computed against today's history for a drift snapshot taken at an unknown earlier commit, and nothing in the pasted comment lets a reader detect that. This is the same lesson the repo encoded for evidence pairs at #2845 (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:36-58`). Printing the resolved base SHA would close it.\n**L5 — `buildStatusRows`' exported contract is undocumented and takes a shape no producer emits.** It reads `drift.fileByVersion` and `drift.pendingClassifications` (:107-124), which `main` splices in (:325-328); the JSDoc (:103-106) documents only `attribution`. The unit tests use the nested shape, the CLI the flat producer shape, and only `main` bridges them. One sentence would stop the next caller passing producer output directly into a TypeError.\n**L6 — Minor parser notes, unchanged.** A repeated `--json` silently last-wins (:236-249); `--json -h` treats `-h` as a filename and reports \"could not read drift JSON\" rather than help (:240-241, :290-292). Both fail closed.\n**L7 — The PR description now contradicts the committed evidence.** It claims \"16 new tests\" (the file has 26; `completion.json:22` records 26) and that the run \"correctly attributes all 6 genuinely-pending versions to their **source PRs**\" — the framing M3 removed, and which the committed doc hedges as \"commit reference (PR or issue; unverified)\" (doc:31, 42-45). The description is not part of the sealed diff, so this is advisory: update it before merge so the human-readable record does not outrun the artifact people will quote on #2508.\n### Informational\n**I1 — Sibling instance of the fixed baseRef-injection class, still open in the producer, outside this diff.** The reporter now rejects a leading `-` and `..` (:60, :201) and places the migration path after `--` (:207). `check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs` still passes an unvalidated `--base-ref` value into `git rev-parse` (:337) and `git ls-tree` (:353) *before* the `--` guard. Operator-supplied rather than remote input, and pre-existing — reported only because the brief asks for sibling instances of each failure class, and because this PR fixed its own copy.\n**I2 — `fileByVersion` is keyed by `filename.slice(0,14)` in the producer (`:402`)**, so two migration files sharing a 14-digit prefix would silently collapse and the reporter would attribute the wrong file. No such pair exists today and no subdirectory exists under `supabase/migrations` (both verified), and the reporter's `startsWith` check (:79) cannot detect the collision if one is ever introduced. Pre-existing; newly load-bearing as the attribution key.\n## Mandatory additional checks\n**1. Index usage — NON-APPLICABLE, source-backed, not inferred from absence.** No SQL and no database object appears in any of the five changed files. `contract.json:29-30` and `completion.json:16-17` both declare `db_reads: []` / `db_writes: []`, and the code agrees: the only imports are `node:child_process`, `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url` (:29-32), and the only subprocess is `git log` (:207). `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` appears at :140 purely as rendered prose inside a Markdown string, never as a query. No join is introduced. One honest caveat: `readStdin` (:34-39) reads the real `process.stdin` and has no seam of its own — it is reachable only through `main`'s `stdin` parameter, which the tests do exercise (test:222-226), so the purity contract is not violated, but the TTY refusal at :35 is untested.\n**3. Exact object checks — NON-APPLICABLE for schema/table/view/function-signature/column**, and precisely why: this change creates, alters, drops and queries no database object. It asserts nothing about `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` because it never reads it; the only code that does is `fetchAppliedVersions`, which posts one constant statement through the Management API (`read-preview-ledger.mjs:6, 12`) and is not modified here. There is no object identity for this diff to assert, and no name-existence check that could be mistaken for a right-object check. **Applied to the object the change actually depends on — the producer's JSON contract — the under-assertion that drove prior H1/M4/M6 is fixed**, and I verified every assertion against the producer's real return (`:413`) rather than against the fixture: all twelve rendered fields are asserted for presence and type, `driftFound` is checked *and* cross-checked against an independent re-derivation (:68-69), version strings are held to the producer's `/^\\d{14}$/` invariant before rendering (:45, :64), the classification partition and key set are held to exact equality with `mergedNotApplied` (:65-67, :72), and the kind vocabulary is an exact copy of the producer's exported `PENDING_KINDS` (:75 vs `check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:88`). Two residual exactness gaps, both fail-closed and both worth recording: the reporter still cannot confirm the JSON came from `check-migration-ledger-drift` at all, because the producer emits no schema or version marker to check against — a renamed producer field would render `**0** retired/deliberately-held, **0** foreign-target` as fact rather than refusing; and the `appliedNotMerged` 14-digit assertion (L1) claims an invariant the producer does not actually enforce, which is the mirror-image defect of the same class. Adding a `schema` marker to the producer's JSON would make this check exact in the only place it can be.\n## Governed brief sections\n**Role and permission changes — NON-APPLICABLE, source-backed.** No grant, role, policy, RLS rule, `permissions:` block or workflow file is touched; all five entries in the packet's `git diff --name-status` are additions and none is under `.github/`. The reporter is wired into no workflow (tree-wide grep → zero matches outside the script, its test and the doc), so no existing job's token, permission set or trigger surface changes, and no sibling call path is affected. The alarm workflow is untouched and still uses the non-JSON path with `tee` (`migration-ledger-drift.yml:108`), so the reporter cannot alter the alarm's behaviour or exit semantics. The script holds no credential: it never reads `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, never invokes `gh`, never opens a socket — one `git log` subprocess (:207) and one operator-supplied file read (:290).\n**Objects and dependencies — VERIFIED as declared, with one discrepancy.** Derived from source: no schema, table, view, function signature or column. The real dependency is the producer's JSON contract, which I derived from `runDriftCheck`'s return statement (`:413`) rather than from the fixture; it matches both what `validateDriftResult` asserts and what `main` consumes (:313-336). No dependency stage is required — no migration must be applied, no secret is needed, and there is no ordering against another lane. The one scope discrepancy is N1: three implementation files were delivered where the published contract's assumption names four.\n**Migration immutability — NON-APPLICABLE, source-backed.** No `.sql` file appears in the diff and `migration_versions: []` (`completion.json:6`) is consistent with that. No version is reserved, renumbered or superseded, so no collision surface is touched and `scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.mjs` has nothing to judge. My profile has no shell, so every hash-dependent, exit-code and git-topology claim is marked UNVERIFIED rather than accepted, and I substituted static cross-checks wherever one was possible.\n**Provisional verdict, stated early in case this run is cut short:** both blocking findings from the prior round are genuinely fixed and I verified the mechanism of each rather than accepting the claim; every prior High and Medium remains fixed at this head; my new findings are all Low/informational and none can produce a false clean report, a silent attribution loss, a mislabeled PR, an unsafe comment, or a wrong exit code. **APPROVE**, with the gaps below listed for a later batch.\n## Packet identity\nThe sealed packet matches the injected authoritative head exactly: base `3ba1b77df0e8e0bc52ac3b36df5741d676feb3f3`, head `048308299568270a3b50b605b197d0f44185deb5`, whole-source digest `c2fccd3569377bc67490b021e741baebe360d70b1662c485f88576b123801ea7`, clean working tree, seven files, identical to the brief's inventory. I reviewed that head and nothing else. I read the full 935-line `patch.diff`, both new scripts at head, the producer (`scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs`), `scripts/orchestrator-flow/read-preview-ledger.mjs`, the truth audit and its disposition README plus the producer's own catalogue, the evidence gates (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs`, `agent-work-contract.mjs`, `lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs`, `lib/work-dependencies.mjs`), `.github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml` and `.github/workflows/migration-ledger-drift.yml` in full, and the on-disk migration layout.\n## Disposition of the prior REVISE findings\n**N1 — the truth-audit catalogue that disappeared. FIXED, and I verified the mechanism end to end.** The natural phrasing is restored: `scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.mjs:166` now reads *\"The supplied drift-check result lists these reviewed, merged migrations as **not applied** in this database.\"* A pattern grep over the reporter for the audit's tracked terms (`missing`, `never created`, `not applied`, `NOT_DERIVABLE`, `_created_by_applied_dynamic_ddl`) returns **exactly one** hit, at line 166. The new catalogue `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~report-ledger-drift-status.mjs.json` carries **exactly one** site, `scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.mjs:166`. That satisfies every rule the audit enforces: the count-equality bijection (`catalogue.sites.length !== discoveredKeys.size` refuses), `dispositionFileName('scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.mjs')` equals the catalogue's filename, `catalogue.source` matches so `readCatalogues` will not throw, `schema_version` is 1, `disposition` is `excluded` (one of the two allowed values), and the reason is ~180 characters against the 20-character floor. The reason is also **factually accurate**, which is the part that matters: line 166 is inside `if (actionable > 0)`, it is a statement about the supplied JSON, and the reporter performs no database read — imports are only `node:child_process`, `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url`, and its only subprocesses are `git rev-parse` (:241) and `git log` (:209). It is a more substantive reason than the boilerplate the producer's own catalogue carries at site `:26`. `completion.json` `assumptions_resolved[1]` records that \"the catalogue is delivered rather than silently retired\", closing the declared-vs-delivered divergence. Declared and delivered scope now agree **exactly**: the gen-2 contract's seven `allowed_paths` are precisely the seven files in the net diff.\n**L3 — reporter tests outside every CI job. FIXED.** `.github/workflows/migration-ledger-drift.yml:92` now runs `scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.test.mjs` beside the producer's tests in the existing read-only drift job. A grep over `.github/` for `report-ledger-drift-status` returns exactly that one hit, so there is one wiring and no double-run.\nI independently corroborated the recorded test evidence rather than accepting it: the reporter test file has **28** top-level `test()` calls (matching \"28 passed\"), the drift file **35**, `check-worktree-freshness.test.mjs` **4** — summing to **67**, exactly the recorded count for the workflow command, and the recorded command string is byte-identical to line 92. The truth-audit test file has **16**, matching \"16 passed\". The recorded counts are consistent with the files at head; the exit codes themselves remain author claims.\n**H1 — unverified/empty/partial read reported clean; invented target. REMAINS FIXED.** `validateDriftResult` (:62-89) asserts rather than defaults: `target` whitelisted to exactly the two `PROJECT_REFS` keys; `projectRef` pattern-checked; `baseRef` REF-checked with no leading `-` and no `..`; `mergedCount`/`appliedCount` safe integers ≥ 1, so the failed-query/credential/permission signature is UNKNOWN, mirroring `computeDrift`'s own refusals; the four version arrays held to unique 14-digit strings; `intentionallyExcluded ∪ foreignTarget ∪ actionableMergedNotApplied` held to an **exact partition** of `mergedNotApplied`; `driftFound` checked *and* cross-checked against a re-derivation identical to `assessDrift`'s; `fileByVersion`/`pendingClassifications` required objects with a key set exactly equal to `mergedNotApplied`, each row carrying a known `kind` and a non-empty `reason`; every actionable file held to `supabase/migrations/<version>*.sql`. I checked each assertion against what the producer actually emits, not against the fixture: `runDriftCheck` returns `{projectRef, baseRef, target, drift, fileByVersion, pendingClassifications}`; `assessDrift` assigns each version to exactly one list and sets `driftFound = actionable>0 || appliedNotMerged>0`; `PENDING_KINDS` is character-for-character the reporter's allowed list; `computeDrift` throws on an empty merged set or empty ledger, so the ≥1 floor never refuses legitimate output. I also confirmed no nested directory exists under `supabase/migrations` (glob → none) and that all six doc-named migration files exist at head with those exact names, so the prefix assertion holds for every real file.\n**M2 silent attribution loss — REMAINS FIXED.** `attributeVersions` throws `Unknown` on any git failure and on an empty introducing-commit list; `resolveBaseCommit` throws on failure and on a non-40-hex result; `main` maps both to exit 2 (:343-344). No `catch { continue }` and no reachable silent `unattributed` row. Tested at :187, :192, :266.\n**M3 issue number printed as a source PR — REMAINS FIXED.** `prNumberFromSubject` (:101) returns `null` unless the subject is `Merge pull request #N` or a trailing `(#N)`; the bare-`#N` fallback is gone; the column is `merge/squash PR reference` and the introducing commit is rendered beside it. The doc labels the same numbers \"commit reference (PR or issue; unverified)\" and states the snapshot \"does not independently prove that each number names a PR\". Test :37 asserts `migration work for issue #2746` → `null`.\n**M4 unsafe Markdown — REMAINS FIXED.** `safeText` (:47) strips C0/DEL, converts backticks to `'` and escapes `|`; applied to target, projectRef, baseRef, baseSha, file basename, commit, kind, reason and orphan version. Newline removal is the load-bearing control and it is tested by asserting rendered line count, not a substring (:279-286).\n**M5 pipeline masks the verdict — REMAINS FIXED.** `main` returns `result.drift.driftFound ? 1 : 0` (:361); `set -o pipefail` is stated in the header, in `USAGE` (:274) and in the doc. Exit 2 = UNKNOWN\", matching :150 and :361.\n**M7 producer-shaped CLI seam — REMAINS FIXED.** `sampleResult` places `fileByVersion` and `pendingClassifications` at the **top level** with `drift` carrying only the producer's eight keys, structurally identical to `runDriftCheck`'s return; three tests drive `main()` through that shape (:244, :258, :266); the `JSON.parse` refusal is genuinely exercised (:273); `Unknown.name` is set and tested (:312).\n**M8 pair-gate proof — as addressed as it can be.** `completion.json` records `--validate-completion` at exit 0. `agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs` is still not recorded and cannot be: it requires `--pr-head-sha`, the commit carrying the report itself. CI runs it (`.github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml:230-233`). I statically verified everything that gate checks: `report.base_sha` = `3ba1b77…` equals this packet's base; both SHAs are 40-hex; `files_changed` (5) is lexicographically sorted and inside `allowed_paths`; `contract_ref` = `refs/db-contracts/3587/2` = `contractRef(3587, 2)`; `outcome: ready-for-merge` with `pr: 3518`, `migration_versions: []` and no `merge_sha` satisfies both `validateCompletionRecord`'s ready-for-merge branch and `validatePullRequestCompletion`; all four `required_checks` appear verbatim at exit 0 with non-empty evidence; `resolveEvidencePair` over the seven-file diff yields exactly one group with both halves → `current`, not `partial`/`conflicted`; and the checked-in contract matches the published comment JSON field-for-field.\nPrior Lows L1 (orphan 14-digit over-assertion), L2 (REF too narrow), L4 (report not bound to a snapshot), L6 (parser last-wins / `--json -h`) and the `Unknown.name` half of L17 are all fixed; L5 survives in part and is restated below.\n## New findings\n### Low\n**NEW-1 — `validateDriftResult` omits the one cross-field identity the producer guarantees by construction, and the test fixture violates it.** `computeDrift` builds both lists from two sets, so for any genuine producer output `mergedCount - appliedCount === mergedNotApplied.length - appliedNotMerged.length` must hold. Nothing in :62-89 asserts it. The fixture proves the gap is real rather than theoretical: `sampleDrift` declares `mergedCount: 706, appliedCount: 676` (difference 30) with `mergedNotApplied` of length 3 and `appliedNotMerged` empty (difference 3) — an arithmetically impossible drift result that passes validation. The doc's real numbers (706/676, 30 merged-not-applied, 0 orphans) *do* satisfy the identity, which confirms it is the right check. Consequence: a truncated, hand-edited or partially forged `--json drift.json` with consistent-looking arrays but inconsistent counts is accepted, and this is the last standing check between such a file and a clean report — e.g. `{mergedCount:706, appliedCount:676, mergedNotApplied:[], …, driftFound:false}` passes every current assertion and prints \"**No actionable drift.**\" with exit 0. Fix: assert the identity in `validateDriftResult` and correct `sampleDrift` to a consistent triple. Evidence: `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs` `computeDrift`; `scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.mjs:62-89`; `scripts/report-ledger-drift-status.test.mjs:54-58`. I am classifying this Low, not blocking: it is a narrower instance of the provenance gap the prior round already accepted as a residual (the producer emits no schema marker), it cannot make the reporter accept anything `check-migration-ledger-drift` would have refused, and the report's footer attributes every claim to \"a `check-migration-ledger-drift --json` result\" rather than asserting live truth.\n**NEW-2 — `formatStatusReport` derives the actionable count and the clean/dirty decision from `rows.length`, not from the drift it prints beside them.** `:139` `const actionable = rows.length` drives both the `**No actionable drift.**` branch (:150) and the \"Promotion candidates — N genuinely-pending version(s)\" heading, while the counts above come from `drift`. In `main` they are always equal; the function is exported, so a caller passing rows built from a different drift gets a heading that contradicts its own table. Fix: derive `actionable` from `drift.actionableMergedNotApplied.length`, or assert the two agree.\n**NEW-3 — `buildStatusRows` (:115) dereferences `drift.pendingClassifications[version].kind` and `drift.fileByVersion[version]` unguarded.** `main` validates first, so the CLI is safe, but an external caller passing producer output directly gets a `TypeError` where the module's own discipline promises an `Unknown`. The JSDoc now says the caller must splice in the two top-level maps (prior L5, partly fixed) but still does not state the precondition that every actionable version carries a classification and a file.\n**NEW-4 — the clean path now hard-depends on a resolvable git ref it does not need.** `main` calls `resolveBaseCommit` unconditionally at :343 before `attributeVersions`, so a verified-clean result (`actionable` empty, nothing to attribute) still exits 2 when `origin/main` cannot be resolved locally — reachable from the advertised `--json drift.json` usage on a checkout without the remote ref. Fail-closed and loud, so not a safety bug, but the tool's most-quoted output is now gated on git. Consider resolving lazily only when `actionable.length > 0`, or emitting the clean report with an explicit \"attribution history unavailable\" line.\n**NEW-5 — `safeText` (:47) does not neutralize `<` and `>`.** Interpolated producer strings, notably `reason` (derived by the production guard from repository data), can therefore carry raw HTML into a comment destined for #2508. GitHub sanitizes script and event-handler HTML, so this is not an XSS vector, and the control that actually prevents authority forgery — control-character stripping, so no forged `**Holders:**` or `Closes #2508` line can be injected — is present and tested. Recorded as residual.\n**NEW-6 — a reporter-test regression now reddens the scheduled drift job without filing the throttled alarm issue.** The tests run at :92, *before* the ledger comparison, so on failure `steps.check.outcome` is `skipped`, not `failure`, and the alarm step's `if: failure() && steps.check.outcome == 'failure' && github.event_name == 'schedule'` does not fire. The run is still visibly red, so this is not a silent failure, and the property is pre-existing for the two test files already in that step — this PR widens it by one file. If any red scheduled run should alarm, the condition should drop the `steps.check.outcome` clause.\n**NEW-7 — advisory, outside the sealed diff.** The PR body still says \"26 reporter tests pass\"; the file at head has 28 and `completion.json` records 28. Update the description before merge so the human-readable record does not contradict the artifact people will quote on #2508. The rest of the body is now consistent with the code (merge/squash labeling, unverified historical references).\n### Informational\n**I1 — the disposition covers line 166 only; line 167 makes the same claim class and is not tracked.** `:167` \"*Any object they create is **absent from the live catalog***\" does not trip the lexical pattern, so it carries no reviewed disposition. It is immediately hedged with the exact warning the guard exists to enforce (\"Do not read that absence as 'the work was never done' (issue #892)\"), and the producer's equivalent lines are dispositioned, so the substance is covered. But the class the prior review named remains structurally live: only the phrase \"not applied\" keeps this file in discovery, so a future reword of :166 silently removes coverage again. It would fail loudly — retiring a catalogue whose source has no sites is required by `run()` — which is the correct behaviour, and worth stating in the catalogue README rather than leaving to memory.\n**I2 — sibling instance of the fixed baseRef-injection class, still open in the producer, outside this diff.** The reporter rejects a leading `-` and `..` (:46, :210, :242) and pathspec-guards the file after `--`. `check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs` still passes an unvalidated `--base-ref` value into `git rev-parse` and `git ls-tree` before any `--` guard. Operator-supplied rather than remote input, and pre-existing; reported because the brief asks for sibling instances and because this PR fixed its own copy.\n**I3 — `fileByVersion` is keyed by `filename.slice(0,14)` in the producer**, so two migration files sharing a 14-digit prefix would collapse and the reporter would attribute the wrong file. I checked the live risk rather than restating it: the two files that share a suffix — `20260911212849_shared_style_group_sku_key.sql` and `20260917112129_shared_style_group_sku_key.sql` — have **distinct** 14-character prefixes, and no nested directory exists, so there is no collision today. Pre-existing; newly load-bearing as the attribution key.\n## Mandatory additional checks\n**1. Index usage — NON-APPLICABLE, source-backed, and I checked the one place an assumption could hide.** No SQL appears in any of the seven changed files. `contract.json` and `completion.json` both declare `db_reads: []` / `db_writes: []`, and the code agrees: the reporter's only imports are `node:child_process`, `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url`, and its only subprocesses are `git rev-parse` (:241) and `git log` (:209). `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` at :142 is rendered prose inside a Markdown string, never a query. The single ledger read in this flow is the pre-existing constant `select version from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations order by version` (`scripts/orchestrator-flow/read-preview-ledger.mjs`), untouched by this PR: it has **no WHERE clause and no join**, so there is no predicate for an index to serve and no join to plan, and `ORDER BY version` is served by the ledger's version key, which the producer documents as the sole key (\"Supabase keys the ledger on the version ALONE\"). **No loose, unused, or unusable index assumption is made anywhere in this change.** The place one could have been introduced is the new `assertOrphanVersions` (:55), and it points the other way: it *relaxes* the version format precisely because `fetchAppliedVersions` applies no format filter (`String(row.version)`, unvalidated) — only `readPreviewLedger`, a different consumer, enforces `/^\\d{14}$/`. So the reporter does not assume a constraint the ledger does not have, which was prior L1 and is now correct. The lookup-cost analogue is satisfied and verified: attribution is scoped to `actionableFiles`, built only from `actionableMergedNotApplied`, so today's data costs six pathspec-scoped `git log` invocations rather than 706, each with a 1 MiB `maxBuffer` whose overflow refuses rather than truncates.\n**2. Function volatility — NON-APPLICABLE for SQL:** no database function is created or altered and nothing in the diff carries or needs an `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` marker. **The JS analogue is correct, checked against the declared banners rather than accepting them.** The \"Pure logic — no network, no filesystem\" banner (:91-93) covers exactly `prNumberFromSubject` (:101), `buildStatusRows` (:115) and `formatStatusReport` (:137); all three are free of I/O, module state, `Date` and `Math.random`. `validateDriftResult` (:62), `assertVersions` (:49), `assertOrphanVersions` (:55) and `safeText` (:47) are also pure and sit above the banner. REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\nProvisional verdict: REVISE — offline tests pin real structure but leave several live-assertion components unasserted and several false controls narrower than claimed.\r\n\r\nFindings — scripts/issue-2863-live-proof.test.mjs vs .github/live-proofs/2863.sql (head 3a5ef8b743a19c0d7b21ecad60c53b35745d8086):\r\n\r\nHigh — live components a weakened probe could drop while offline stays green:\r\n\r\n1. Positivity / ordering / equality guards never asserted. 2863.sql:12-14 (`r.rows_unchanged > 0`, `r.rows_fetched >= r.rows_unchanged`, `r.finished_at >= r.started_at`) and :35,37 (`r.rows_fetched > 0`, `r.rows_fetched = r.rows_unchanged`, `r.finished_at >= r.started_at`). Test file has no assertion containing `> 0`, `>=`, `finished_at >=`, or prod `rows_fetched = r.rows_unchanged`. Dropping any of them passes every test.\r\n2. Prior-run binding not pinned. 2863.sql:18-21,43 (`prior.endpoint = r.endpoint`, `prior.company_code = r.company_code`, `prior.request_params->>'fullSnapshot' = 'true'`, `->'coveredKeys' =`, `->>'prodOrderNo' =`). Test :65-69 checks only `prior.status` + `finished_at <`; test :78-82 checks only substrings `fullSnapshot`/`coveredKeys`/`prodOrderNo`. A probe joining any prior succeeded run regardless of company/params passes.\r\n3. Prior idempotence/history not pinned. 2863.sql:24-25 (`prior.rows_inserted = 0`, `prior.rows_updated = 0`, `NOT EXISTS ... c.run_id = prior.id`). Test :42-54 checks `r.`-scoped predicates only, with the `(?<![a-z])r\\.` guard deliberately excluding `prior.` — so the prior-side predicates are explicitly unasserted. Sibling of the same class in both CTEs.\r\n4. Prod population-count assertion truncated. 2863.sql:47-49 ends `d.prod_order_no::text = r.request_params->>'prodOrderNo') = r.rows_fetched`; test :75 checks only `/d\\.prod_order_no::text = r\\.request_params/`. Operator after `request_params`, extraction operator, and `= r.rows_fetched` RHS are unasserted — `<>`, `>=`, or a literal RHS passes.\r\n5. RLS/privilege posture is existence-only, not exact-object. 2863.sql:54-61 (census `= 2` with `nspname='coldlion'`, `relname IN (...)`, `relkind='r'`, `relrowsecurity`; `NOT EXISTS ... has_table_privilege(roles.name, t.name, 'SELECT,...,TRIGGER')`). Test :136-142 checks `/relrowsecurity/`, `/anon/`, `/authenticated/`, service_role SELECT x2 only. Dropping the `NOT EXISTS` denial (e.g. granting anon SELECT) while the words survive elsewhere passes. This is the exact-object failure the brief calls out: name-exists instead of right-object.\r\n6. False-control structural gate covers only 5 shapes, so \"fails loudly\" is overclaimed. `assertStructuralComplete` (:95-102) checks witness conjunction, `r.rows_inserted`, change_log, `prior.rows_fetched`, hardcoded-count — but not `rows_updated`, endpoint, status, conservation (:62), table counts (:71-76), RLS, or shape guard. Proof: commenting out only `rows_updated` (test :116-121 comments out both together) still matches `r\\.rows_inserted = 0` and passes the gate. No false control drops endpoint, conservation, table-count, or RLS predicates.\r\n\r\nMedium — hardening gaps in the same class:\r\n\r\n7. Per-CTE splitter is fragile and asserts at module scope. :17-24 regex `name AS \\(([\\s\\S]*?)\\)\\s*,?\\s*(?:prod_replay|SELECT)` relies on CTE order/names; a reordered probe or third CTE silently mis-splits. `assert.ok` at :20 runs at import time, outside any `test()`, so a missing CTE throws outside the runner's per-test reporting.\r\n8. `stripComments` (:9-13) runs before literal handling, so `--` or `/*` inside a string literal is treated as a comment start. Intended division (literals are real content) is defeated for any literal containing those sequences; same noise-handling class as the `stripSqlNoise`/`stripComments` split at :89/:95.\r\n9. `assert.throws(...)` at :107,:113,:120 with no message matcher counts any throw (including a TypeError from the helper itself) as a loud failure.\r\n10. Sample-ID ban at :32 (`10111|10119|17303|7263`) is a known-value denylist; a newly hardcoded key passes. `LANDING_COUNT` (:87) covers numeric totals only.\r\n\r\nMandatory three (floor):\r\n\r\n- Index usage: N/A, no gap. The change is test-only string matching; it creates no predicates, joins, or indexes and names none. Probe runtime predicates (`sync_run(endpoint, company_code)`, `change_log(run_id)`, `prepack_detail/prod_detail(run_id, company_code)`) are unchanged and out of scope — the test file correctly makes no index claim.\r\n- Function volatility: N/A, no gap. No `CREATE FUNCTION` and no volatility marker in the change or probe. Only referenced DB functions are `has_table_privilege` (system, correctly non-IMMUTABLE) and `count(*)`; the JS helpers (`stripComments`, `cteBody`, `assertStructuralComplete`) are not DB functions.\r\n- Exact object checks: partial fail — table names (`coldlion.prepack_detail`, `prod_detail`, `change_log`) and endpoints are pinned (:36-39, :52, :72-75), but RLS census, full privilege list, comparison operators, and param-value equalities are substring/existence checks per items 2, 4, 5 above.\r\n\r\nWhat is good (not gaps): comment-stripping before assertions (:9-14), per-CTE pinning so one endpoint cannot satisfy the other, hardcoded-total shape with `stripSqlNoise` scoping (:87-90), both single-witness-drop controls (:104-114), write-keyword controls via `probeShapeProblem` (:131-134), hardcoded-count positive+negative pair (:123-129).\r\n\r\nNo migration, DB write, or probe SQL change in scope; nothing here is production-dangerous, so this is REVISE, not REJECT. Tighten: assert positivity/ordering/equality predicates, prior company/param equalities with operators and values, prior idempotence/history, full prod count comparison with RHS, exact RLS census and NOT EXISTS privilege-denial shape, and extend `assertStructuralComplete` (or add controls) to cover each newly pinned predicate single-drop.\r\n\r\nVERDICT: REVISE The RLS assertions explicitly check roles (`anon`, `authenticated`, `service_role`) and exact permissions rather than inferring existence.\n\nVERDICT: APPROVE 0780a340968707b9b41924d78d51df6ae90c3494","author_association":"MEMBER","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5862285291/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"performed_via_github_app":null,"minimized":null},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5862332848","html_url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3515#issuecomment-5862332848","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/3515","id":5862332848,"node_id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABXWwZsA","user":{"login":"u2giants","id":55610577,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/55610577?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants","html_url":"https://github.com/u2giants","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2026-09-28T02:43:17Z","updated_at":"2026-09-28T02:43:17Z","body":"GOVERNED REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n## Provisional verdict\n\nProvisional: REVISE. The rebind itself is coherent and the probe/evidence mechanics check out on the readable evidence, but the hardened test suite leaves two predicates the proof depends on completely unpinned, so the change does not fully deliver the \"fail loudly on an inauthentic or incomplete proof\" goal it claims (`contract.json:7`).\n\nI could not run `node --test` (no shell) and could not read git history, refs, or hashes; those limits are named explicitly below rather than papered over.\n\n## Findings\n\n### High — coverage gaps inside the change's own claim\n\nF1. The source table of both CTEs is never asserted, at all. `.github/live-proofs/2863.sql:9,17,33,40` read `coldlion.sync_run`, but `scripts/issue-2863-live-proof.test.mjs` contains no occurrence of `sync_run` (grep of that file for `sync_run`: no matches). The same file does pin the other objects it depends on: `coldlion.prepack_detail` / `coldlion.prod_detail` (`:90-92`), `coldlion.change_log` (`:59`), the `coldlion` namespace (`:175`), `relkind`/`relrowsecurity` (`:177`). The omission is inconsistent within the file, and it is exactly the \"check that a name merely exists is not a check that the right object exists\" failure mode. The sibling run table is named in-repo at `supabase/migrations/20260818232639_coldlion_raw_landing_spine.sql:157` (\"ingest.sync_run is unchanged and still serves other sources\"), so a mutation swapping `coldlion.sync_run` for another run table would keep all 21 assertions green, including every false control (`:135-171`). Fix: assert `/FROM coldlion\\.sync_run/` (both the `r` and `prior` aliases) and add a false control that swaps it.\n\nF2. The replay run's own full-snapshot identity predicate is unpinned. `2863.sql:11` requires `r.request_params->>'fullSnapshot' = 'true'` on the *replay* run. The only assertion that mentions `fullSnapshot` on the replay side is the token-level `/fullSnapshot/` at `scripts/issue-2863-live-proof.test.mjs:98`, and that token is also satisfied by the *prior* predicate at `2863.sql:20` (pinned separately, and correctly, at `test.mjs:79`). Deleting `2863.sql:11` therefore leaves every test green, and no false control covers it. This is the same class of weakening the false controls exist to catch. Fix: add `assert.match(prepack, /r\\.request_params->>'fullSnapshot' = 'true'/)` plus a false control that comments that line out.\n\n### Medium\n\nF3 (mandatory check 1 — index usage). The predicates the pinned probe depends on are only partly index-served:\n- `2863.sql:28,50` `d.run_id = r.id`: `run_id` is unindexed by design — `supabase/migrations/20260916001944_coldlion_prepack_and_prod_detail_landing.sql:208-211` says \"No secondary indexes\", so only the `company_code` lead of the PK (`:123`, `:185`) can be used, and the `run_id` equality is a recheck.\n- `2863.sql:49` `d.prod_order_no::text = r.request_params->>'prodOrderNo'` is the \"index exists but cannot be used as written\" case: the unique index `(company_code, prod_order_no, prod_line_seq)` (`:186`) indexes `prod_order_no` as **bigint**, and the predicate casts the column to `text`, so that index cannot serve it (only the `company_code` prefix). Writing `d.prod_order_no = (r.request_params->>'prodOrderNo')::bigint` would be index-servable.\n- `2863.sql:18,41` `prior.company_code = r.company_code` and `:11,43` `request_params->>'…'`: `coldlion.sync_run.company_code` / `request_params` are unindexed. The only sync_run indexes are `(endpoint, started_at desc)`, `(status, started_at desc)` and the **partial** `(endpoint, window_from, window_to) WHERE window_from is not null` (`20260818232639:146-154`); the partial window index cannot be used for the probe's endpoint filter because the query does not imply `window_from IS NOT NULL`, and `window_from` is NULL for these endpoints by comment (`:165-166`).\n- Positively: `coldlion.change_log` run_id lookups (`2863.sql:15,25,38`) are served by the `run_id` index (`20260818232639:346`).\nThis is a live production read (`shared-db-live-proof.yml:34-45`, 15-minute job timeout at `:18`), so it will scan rather than block, but the assumptions are loose and should be stated or fixed under a separate claim.\n\nF4. Nothing automated runs the hardened tests. A grep of `.github` for `2863` returns no matches, and no workflow globs `scripts/*.test.mjs` (the globs in use are `tools/*.test.mjs`, `scripts/throughput-guard/*.test.mjs`, `scripts/orchestrator-flow/*.test.mjs`, `scripts/historical-item-mg-reclassification/*.test.mjs` — `tools-offline-tests.yml:94,183-194`). The only execution record for the new false controls is the hand-typed command in `completion.json:16-22`. If the point is to \"fail loudly\", the file should be added to an existing required check's explicit list (e.g. the one at `migration-author-lease.yml:49` or `tools-offline-tests.yml:110-173`).\n\nF5 (exact-object check 3, RLS). The assertion labelled \"census\" overstates what it proves. `test.mjs:174` says \"exactly 2 tables with RLS in coldlion\", but the query it pins (`2863.sql:54-56`) counts only rows where `c.relname IN ('prepack_detail','prod_detail')`, so `= 2` can never be a census — it only proves both *named* tables have RLS. The negative posture (`2863.sql:57-61`, pinned at `test.mjs:179-181`) and the positive posture (`2863.sql:62-63`, pinned at `:183-184`) are otherwise exact and well covered.\n\n### Low\n\nF6. Token-presence assertions that create false confidence: `test.mjs:97-101` (`/fullSnapshot/`, `/coveredKeys/`, `/prodOrderNo/`) and `test.mjs:175` (`n.nspname = 'coldlion'`) assert a token is somewhere in the text; stronger siblings exist (`:78-82`, `:176-177`), so these are redundant-at-best and actively misleading in the case of `fullSnapshot` (finding F2).\n\nF7. False-control names overstate specificity. `test.mjs:157-160` comments out `AND r.rows_unchanged > 0` by prefixing `--`, which also removes `rows_inserted`/`rows_updated` on the same line (`2863.sql:12`), so the throw may come from the idempotence check rather than positivity; `:152-155` similarly takes `prior.company_code` with it. `assert.throws` still passes, but the control does not isolate the predicate it names.\n\nF8. The hardcoded-total guard is shape-only and trivially evadable (`= 42::int`, `= 6*7`, a CTE-declared constant); `test.mjs:104` only bans `= <bare digits>` after a landing count. The header comment at `:103` is honest about being a shape check, but it should not be read as \"counts are derived, never hardcoded\".\n\nF9. `cteBody` (`test.mjs:16-21`) splits CTEs by regex with the terminator set hardcoded to `prod_replay|SELECT`; a nested subquery ending `) SELECT` inside `prepack_replay` would truncate the captured body. Not a live defect against today's probe (`2863.sql:7-51`), but a fragile basis for structural assertions.\n\n### Mandatory checks 2 and 3 — what I could verify\n\nCheck 2 (function volatility): not applicable to this diff, and I verified that rather than assumed it.
