The reviewer findings are kept below with every parseable decision line voided. Acting on them requires a fresh governed review at this head.\n\n## Provisional verdict\n> VOIDED REVIEWER LINE - **REVISE** — stated up front, before the detail. The change is additive and touches no existing object, so nothing here is dangerous to `main` today. But one header line will break the production promotion lane with no override path, and the migration's central factual claim (\"Column shapes match the dflow sources\") is false in two columns in a way that makes the new `plm` home reject writes the live writer currently makes. Both are fixable in this file before merge; after merge the bytes are immutable.\n## Sealed-evidence verification\nRead `.ai-review-qwen-mimo-rev-s1-qw3/MANIFEST.md` first, as instructed.\n| Manifest claim | Verified | How |\n|---|---|---|\n| head = `87ff50ea3fbb8a76f33f7e7f684e639bfdcaa9e7` | ✅ | Session git snapshot: detached HEAD at `87ff50ea`, subject \"Add agent work contract evidence for #3498\" |\n| base = `a5c1f0fb6c11549c9d0a0b8b66114ebd7ac8907d` | ✅ | Same snapshot: `a5c1f0fb` is an ancestor, 2 commits below head |\n| 3 files added, working tree clean, no untracked | ✅ | `patch.diff` lists exactly those 3; all 3 present on disk |\n| Patch matches disk | ✅ | Read `supabase/migrations/20260925044029_*.sql` directly — 85 lines, byte-identical to the `patch.diff` hunk; `.agent/work/3498/1/completion.json` likewise |\n| Whole-source digest `4d40625a…` | ⚠️ **not recomputable** | This review profile has no shell tool, so I could not re-hash the tree. There is no `SEAL.txt`/`seal.json` in the packet to cross-check against. I substituted content comparison against `patch.diff` for every changed file. Treat the digest itself as unverified. |\n| \"No tests were run for this packet\" | ✅ noted | I did not run `scripts/check-sql.sh` or the ephemeral contract suite; `completion.json`'s claim of a passing run is the author's, not mine |\nAnti-collision rule 5 (duplicate version) checked directly: `supabase/migrations/20260925*` matches exactly one file. No version collision. `plm.item_user_assignment` / `plm.item_workflow_action` appear nowhere else in the repo — including `supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql` — so `CREATE TABLE` without `IF NOT EXISTS` cannot collide on a from-empty replay. `plm` itself is created at `20260621150714_foundation.sql:10`.\n## Findings\n### Blocking\n**B1 — `-- derived-from:` carries prose, which the parser refuses, and there is no override path.**\n`supabase/migrations/20260925044029_…sql:3`\n```sql\n-- derived-from: dflow.item_user_assignment, dflow.item_workflow_action (live shapes)\n```\n`AGENTS.md §5.0-D` (`docs/agents/merge-protocol.md`) requires the value to be one or more exact 14-digit versions, or the single word `none`, and says explicitly: *\"never broaden the normal parser to accept prose.\"* `scripts/migration_derivation.py:52` matches this line (`DECLARATION_RE` accepts any `-- derived-from:` comment anywhere in the file), then `parse_declaration` (`:176-215`) splits on commas and raises:\n> `20260925044029: \\`-- derived-from: dflow.item_user_assignment\\` is not a 14-digit migration version … Prose in a header comment is what failed on 2026-08-24.`\n`scripts/test_migration_derivation.py:98-103` pins exactly this refusal (`test_refuses_prose_where_a_version_belongs`).\nWhy this is not a cosmetic nit:\n- `assert_declarations_present` will **not** catch it at PR time — `declaration_required` (`migration_derivation.py:259-282`) only mandates a declaration for versions containing `create or replace function|procedure|view` (`REPLACE_RE`, `:57-60`), and this file has none. So `test_the_whole_repository_satisfies_the_mandate` passes and CI goes green.\n- The failure surfaces later, in the promotion lane. `scripts/production_migration_guard.py:1348` calls `declared_bases(version, path=migration)` for **every candidate version** while classifying holds, and `assert_declared_bases_present` (`:1550-1568`) calls `assert_derivation_bases`, which calls `declared_bases` at `migration_derivation.py:377`. `DerivationError` is deliberately *not* translated to `GuardError` — only `DerivationRefusal` is (`:1563-1564`) — so it escapes as an unhandled authoring fault, potentially aborting classification for the whole pending queue, not just this version.\n- `--derivation-override` cannot rescue it. `parse_overrides` (`:326-347`) requires both `VERSION` and `BASE` to be exact 14-digit versions, and `declared_bases` raises *before* the override map is ever consulted.\n- Once merged, the bytes are immutable (`§5.0-E`: *\"Once the migration applies, its bytes are immutable\"*; `migration_derivation.py:139-141`: *\"A merged migration must never be edited merely to repair its metadata\"*). The only remaining routes are the byte-pinned `IMMUTABLE_NON_LEDGER_DERIVATIONS` registry — described in-file as a narrow historical exception — or retiring and re-issuing the version. That is precisely the three-retirement outcome `§5.0-D` exists to prevent.\nFix, either of:\n- Delete line 3 and move the provenance to ordinary prose that does **not** use the reserved label (this is what `IMMUTABLE_NON_LEDGER_DERIVATIONS` documents as the correct handling of prose under a reserved label), **or**\n- Name the real ledger bases. They exist and are all applied: `-- derived-from: 20260901221310, 20260904143518, 20260905053422, 20260907121732`. This is also more truthful — the shapes were re-derived from those four files' cumulative effect, and the sibling migrations use exactly this form (`20260904143518:5`, `20260905053422:3`, `20260907121732:4`).\n**B2 — `actor_identity_source` and `actor_identity_email` do not match the source, and the divergence makes the new table reject the live writer's rows.**\n`20260925044029_…sql:40-41`, contradicting the header at `:6` (\"Column shapes match the dflow sources\") and the table COMMENT at `:78` (\"Shape matches the dflow source\").\nThe live `dflow` columns, from `20260907121732_designflow_trusted_backend_actor.sql:12-24`:\n```sql\nadd column actor_identity_source text not null default\n  (case when nullif(current_setting('request.designflow.actor_id', true), '') is not null\n        then 'designflow_jwt' else 'supabase_auth' end),\nadd column actor_identity_email text default\n  (lower(nullif(btrim(coalesce(\n     nullif(current_setting('request.designflow.actor_email', true), ''),\n     auth.jwt() ->> 'email')), '')));\n```\nThe `plm` copy replaces the first with the constant `'supabase_auth'` and drops the second's default entirely.\nThis is not a style difference; it is a write-compatibility break. `dflow.record_item_workflow_action` — last re-created at `20260905053422:431-441`, and *not* re-created by `20260907121732` — inserts only:\n```\nrfq_item_id, actor_user_id, actor_auth_user_id, prior_step_id, new_step_id,\naction_key, correlation_key, routing_context,\nsource_action_id, fallback_recipient_user_id, fallback_reason, requires_admin_review\n```\nIt never names `actor_identity_source` or `actor_identity_email`; it relies wholly on those defaults, and it sets `actor_auth_user_id := auth.uid()`, which is NULL in a backend-JWT session. Repoint that function at `plm.item_workflow_action` as written and every DesignFlow-backend write gets `actor_identity_source = 'supabase_auth'` with `actor_auth_user_id IS NULL`, which violates the very constraint this migration copies at `:68-74` → SQLSTATE 23514. Because the same function also updates `plm.\"RFQItem\"` and inserts notifications, the whole transaction rolls back. Supabase-auth writes still succeed, so this fails only on the backend path — the harder one to notice.\nSecond, quieter consequence: even on the Supabase-auth path, `actor_identity_email` now defaults to NULL, so the audit fact the source column exists to capture (`20260907121732:131-132`: *\"Normalized email presented by the verified identity token when the action was recorded\"*) silently stops being recorded for new rows.\nFix: copy both default expressions verbatim, or — if a constant default is a deliberate hardening — say so in the header and drop the \"shapes match\" claim from both COMMENTs, and record that the repointed writer must supply both columns explicitly.\n**B3 — Three of the omitted foreign keys are not cross-schema, so the stated rationale does not cover them; one of them leaves a paid-for index with nothing to serve.**\nHeader rationale at `:6-8`: *\"Cross-schema foreign keys into dflow.\\* are deliberately omitted so the plm homes do not couple to the landing schema.\"*\nThe source FKs were re-pointed at `plm` objects on 2026-09-04. `20260904143518_canonical_designflow_workflow_contract.sql:10-27`:\n```sql\nalter table dflow.item_user_assignment\n  add constraint item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_fkey\n    foreign key (rfq_item_id) references plm.\"RFQItem\"(\"rfqItem_id\") on delete cascade not valid;\nalter table dflow.item_workflow_action\n  add constraint item_workflow_action_rfq_item_id_fkey\n    foreign key (rfq_item_id) references plm.\"RFQItem\"(\"rfqItem_id\") on delete restrict not valid,\n  add constraint item_workflow_action_prior_step_id_fkey\n    foreign key (prior_step_id) references plm.\"RFQStep\"(\"RFQStep_id\") not valid,\n  add constraint item_workflow_action_new_step_id_fkey\n    foreign key (new_step_id) references plm.\"RFQStep\"(\"RFQStep_id\") not valid;\n```\nSo `rfq_item_id` (`:16`, `:37`), `prior_step_id` (`:42`) and `new_step_id` (`:43`) would reference **`plm`-to-`plm`** — same schema, no coupling to the landing schema at all. Only the four `dflow.users` references (`user_id`, `assigned_by_user_id`, `actor_user_id`, `fallback_recipient_user_id`) are genuinely cross-schema, and those the rationale does cover.\nThe clearest case is the self-reference. `20260905053422:50-65` explains at length why the FK is composite:\n> *\"a return may only answer a handoff recorded against the SAME RFQ item … carrying rfq_item_id through the reference makes it structural, so no future writer — function, backfill or manual repair — can bind a return to another item's handoff.\"*\nThis migration **includes the unique key that exists solely to be that FK's target** (`:52`, `CONSTRAINT item_workflow_action_id_rfq_item_key UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)`) but **omits the FK**. A self-FK is intra-table and inline-expressible, so it costs no extra claim object — unlike a standalone index (see N1 below, `check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:507` emits both an `index` and a `table` key for every `CREATE INDEX`). The result is the exact shape the review brief asks me to call out: **an index that exists but cannot be used as written.** `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` is dead weight — its leading column is already the primary key, so no planner will ever prefer it for an `id` lookup, and with no FK referencing it, it enforces nothing that the PK does not. Every insert maintains it for no benefit.\nFix: add the three intra-`plm` FKs inline (`NOT VALID` if you want to mirror the source's legacy-tolerance, plain `VALID` if the tables start empty — they do), or drop `:52` and narrow the header rationale to the four `dflow.users` references it actually applies to.\n### Should fix\n**S1 — Mandatory check 1 (index usage): no predicate the tables will ever be queried by is served.**\nThe migration creates zero indexes beyond the primary keys and the two inline UNIQUE constraints. Every secondary index from the sources is absent:\n| Serves | Source definition | Present in `plm`? |\n|---|---|---|\n| `rfq_item_id = ? AND function_key = ? AND user_id = ? AND effective_to IS NULL FOR UPDATE` — `dflow.set_item_user_assignment`, `20260904143518:98-104` | `item_user_assignment_one_active` UNIQUE `(rfq_item_id, function_key, user_id) WHERE effective_to IS NULL`, `20260901221310:17-19` | ❌ |\n| `rfq_item_id = ? AND function_key = ? AND effective_to IS NULL` — recipient fan-out in `record_item_workflow_action`, `20260904143518:225-231` | `item_user_assignment_active_lookup` `(rfq_item_id, function_key, effective_from, id) INCLUDE (user_id) WHERE effective_to IS NULL`, `20260901221310:21-24` | ❌ |\n| Item history ordered by time | `item_workflow_action_item_time` `(rfq_item_id, occurred_at, id)`, `20260901221310:40-41` | ❌ |\n| `source_action_id = ?` (the reverse handoff lookup, `20260905053422:154`) **and** the \"one return per handoff\" invariant | `item_workflow_action_one_return_per_source` UNIQUE `(source_action_id) WHERE source_action_id IS NOT NULL`, `20260905053422:96-98` | ❌ |\n| \"latest still-open handoff on this item in this direction\" | `item_workflow_action_open_handoff_lookup` `(rfq_item_id, occurred_at DESC, id DESC) INCLUDE (actor_user_id)`, `20260905053422:100-103` | ❌ |\n| `requires_admin_review` queue | `item_workflow_action_admin_review` `(rfq_item_id, occurred_at) WHERE requires_admin_review`, `20260905053422:105-107` | ❌ |\nNote the last row: the migration copies the `requires_admin_review` **column** (`:51`) but not the index that makes it queryable, so the plm home carries a filter column with no way to use it. Same for `user_id` / `assigned_by_user_id` on `item_user_assignment` — \"which items is this person on\" is a sequential scan.\nI accept the procedural justification for the deferral: `check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:502-518` emits an `index` object key for every standalone `CREATE INDEX`, and `CLAIM_KINDS` (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:1262`) lists `index` separately, so adding them would have breached the contract's stop condition *\"Stop if the migration would write any object outside the two claimed tables\"* (`.agent/work/3498/1/contract.json:44-47`). The header is honest about it (`:9-10`). But two of the six are **invariant-bearing partial unique indexes**, not performance aids, and the deferral is recorded in `completion.json:41` in one clause that does not name them. Consequence: as written, the \"final plm home\" cannot hold rows under the integrity contract the sources enforce. The follow-up claim must name all six explicitly, and nothing in the repo says so.\n**S2 — The append-only property is asserted in the COMMENT and enforced nowhere.**\n`:77-78` states *\"Append-only workflow action history\"*; `:33` states *\"assignment history\"*. The sources enforce this with triggers: `item_user_assignment_immutable_history` and `item_workflow_action_immutable` (`20260901221310:105-107`, `:118-120`), backed by `dflow.reject_item_assignment_history_rewrite()` and `dflow.reject_item_workflow_action_rewrite()`. The contract tests assert the behaviour (`supabase/tests/designflow_item_assignment_action_history_contracts.sql:134-176`). The `plm` copies have neither trigger nor function, so the documented invariant is a comment. Triggers and functions are separate `CLAIM_KINDS` entries, so the deferral is again procedurally explicable — but the COMMENT states as a property of the table something the schema does not guarantee, and a COMMENT is what a future reader trusts.\n**S3 — Mandatory check 3 (exact object checks): the migration asserts nothing about the objects it claims to copy.**\nThe file's entire premise is `derived-from … (live shapes)` and *\"Column shapes match the dflow sources\"* (`:6`), yet it contains no assertion of any kind — no `to_regclass('dflow.item_user_assignment')`, no column-set/type/nullability/default comparison against `pg_attribute` or `information_schema.columns`. It infers the source shape and the inference is already wrong in two columns (B2). Had the file carried a catalogue-level shape assertion, B2 would have failed the apply instead of landing silently in `main`.\nThis is cheap to add and compatible with the verify-cost guard: `scripts/check-migration-verify-cost.mjs` forbids a verification block that *reads* a `plm` relation (`READ_CONTEXT` + `PLM_OBJECT`, `:~250-270`) or *calls* a `plm` routine, but it explicitly permits catalogue lookups — its own header names `to_regprocedure('plm.finalize_…')`, `has_table_privilege(…, 'plm.x', 'select')` and `pg_get_viewdef(…::regclass)` as the permitted shape, because a name inside a string literal is blanked in the `scannable` view. So a `do $verify$ … $verify$` block comparing `pg_attribute attname/atttypid/attnotnull/attndims` and `pg_get_expr(adbin, adrelid)` for the two `dflow` sources against the two new `plm` tables, filtered by `nspname` from a **string**, passes that guard. Add it, and make the comparison cover column *defaults*, which is where B2 lives.\nA `supabase/tests/plm_item_homes_shape_contracts.sql` would do the same job durably and is wired into CI the moment it is committed (`.github/workflows/database-contract-tests.yml:31-33` — *\"THE FILE LIST IS A GLOB, NOT A LIST\"*). No guard requires a test for a new table, but the dflow sources each have one, and this is the change that most needed one.\n**S4 — RLS enabled with zero policies sets the trap the sibling migration documents.**\n`:80-81` enable RLS; no `CREATE POLICY` follows; `:82-83` revoke everything from `PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role`. Fail-closed today, and `plm` is not PostgREST-exposed anyway (`docs/agents/references-and-runbooks.md:21` — `pgrst.db_schemas` = `public, graphql_public, api, crm, pim, core, app`), so nothing is reachable. But `20260901221310:296-306` warns about precisely this construction:\n> *\"Enabling RLS with no policy would additionally revoke the intended `authenticated` SELECT.\"*\nThe house pattern for new `plm` tables is RLS **plus** a policy **plus** grants — see `20260726180000_coldlion_licensor_property_phase6_parallel_run.sql:135-160` (`enable row level security` → `create policy … for select to authenticated using (app.has_role('administrator'))` → `grant select … to authenticated; grant all … to service_role`). The next session will add `GRANT SELECT` and see an empty result set, which reads as \"no rows yet\" rather than \"RLS is filtering everything\". Two related precision points:\n- `REVOKE ALL … FROM service_role` blocks the very session that is supposed to move rows, and revoking from `PUBLIC` does not touch the table owner. Migrations apply as `postgres`, which owns these tables and therefore **bypasses RLS** — there is no `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. So the lockout rests entirely on the REVOKEs, not on RLS, and any future `SECURITY DEFINER` function owned by `postgres` (this repo's standard `plm` access pattern) walks through both.\n- `designflow`, the production backend role the sibling migration explicitly grants to when present (`20260907121732:107-116`), is absent from both the REVOKE and any GRANT list.\n**S5 — Identity sequences are not aligned, and no artifact records the obligation.**\nBoth tables use `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` (`:15`, `:36`), so both start at 1 while `dflow.item_user_assignment.id` and `dflow.item_workflow_action.id` have been advancing since 2026-09-01. When rows move, the `plm` identities must be advanced past `max(id)` or the first post-migration insert collides on the PK. There is also `app.user_notification.workflow_action_id`, currently FK'd to `dflow.item_workflow_action(id)` (`20260904143518:50-53`), which must be re-pointed. Row movement is legitimately out of scope here — but `docs/designflow-master-data-migration/designflow-schema-segregation.md:22-24` states the transition rule (*\"Sequence tables to move only after the runtime search_path change, or land copies in both schemas during the transition\"*), and this PR is the \"land copies in both schemas\" half of it. Neither `contract.json` nor `completion.json` mentions sequences.\n**S6 — The handoff record understates what was deferred.**\n`.agent/work/3498/1/completion.json:41` records one clause: *\"Cross-schema FKs and partial unique indexes deferred so the claim writes exactly the two tables.\"* Not recorded: the four non-unique lookup indexes (S1), the two immutability triggers and their functions (S2), the intra-`plm` FKs that the rationale does not actually cover (B3), grants and policies (S4), identity-sequence alignment (S5), the `actor_identity_*` default divergence (B2), or the segregation-doc update (N3). `AGENTS.md`'s session wrap-up convention requires *\"an explicit handoff with the next exact action\"*; this is not that. Two smaller defects in the same file: `head_sha` is `c5a5770588…`, one commit behind the PR head `87ff50ea` under review, and `files_changed` lists one file where the diff has three. Also, the third `checks` entry puts prose (`\"object keys of the migration match the claim writes exactly\"`) in the `command` field, which `docs/agents/anti-collision-summary.md:64-67` requires to be a rerunnable command.\n### Minor / informational\n**N1 — Inline UNIQUE constraints create unclaimed index objects.** `:52-53` create `plm.item_workflow_action_id_rfq_item_key` and `plm.item_workflow_action_correlation_key_key`, which are real indexes in the `plm` namespace. `check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:502-518` only emits `index` keys for standalone `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX`, so the collision guard never sees these. Not the author's fault — it is a parser blind spot — but it does mean the \"exactly the two tables\" reasoning is applied asymmetrically: indexes that could be hidden inside `CREATE TABLE` were included, and the one so hidden (`:52`) is the one with no consumer.\n**N2 — No `lock_timeout` / `statement_timeout`.** Both sibling migrations set them (`20260904143518:7-8`, `20260905053422:42-43`, `20260907121732:7-8`, `20260828052706:1-2`). This file sets neither. Low impact — `CREATE TABLE` on brand-new objects and `REVOKE` on empty tables take no long-held locks — but it is a departure from the immediate neighbours.\n**N3 — `docs/designflow-master-data-migration/designflow-schema-segregation.md:152-153` is now false.** Both rows still say *\"`plm` table not yet created\"*, and §3's `plm | 74` count and the §10 document history stop at the 2026-09-24 docs PR (#3497). No guard enforces this (no script references the file), and the contract's `allowed_paths` (`contract.json:14-18`) scoped the author out of `docs/`, so this is a follow-up rather than a defect of this diff. It should be named as one.\n**N4 — Explicit `BEGIN;` / `COMMIT;` (`:12`, `:85`) is redundant and slightly fragile.** `.github/workflows/database-contract-tests.yml:341-344` applies every migration with `psql --single-transaction` — *\"matches how the Supabase CLI applies a migration\"* — so the file already lands atomically. The inner `COMMIT;` ends that transaction early; psql's trailing `COMMIT` then warns `there is no transaction in progress`. Harmless **because `COMMIT;` is the last statement**: any future statement appended after it would run in autocommit and silently lose the atomicity the CI comment claims. Precedent exists in both directions (~65 existing migrations carry `begin;`/`commit;`; the three closest siblings do not). `scripts/run-preview-rehearsal-transaction.mjs:47` refuses `begin`/`commit`, but that validator is scoped to `AI-PERF-*` rehearsal fixtures, not migrations, so it does not apply here.\n**N5 — Mandatory check 2 (function volatility): nothing to audit in this diff, and that is the answer.** The migration creates no function, procedure, or trigger, so there is no `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` marker present to be wrong. For completeness on the adjacent surface: the three `DEFAULT clock_timestamp()` expressions (`:20`, `:23`, `:47`) call a genuinely VOLATILE function, which is correct for a per-row default and matches the sources (`20260901221310:9,12,36`) — it is a deliberate divergence from the `default now()` used elsewhere in `plm` (e.g. `20260726180000:74,115`) and I would keep it, since `occurred_at` is used for ordering (`order by a.occurred_at, a.id`). The real volatility-adjacent defect in this file is B2: the source's `actor_identity_source` default is a STABLE expression over `current_setting(text, boolean)` and `auth.jwt()`, and this migration replaces it with a constant, changing behaviour rather than mislabeling a marker.\n## Coverage statement\nPer `docs/agents/anti-collision-summary.md:62-64`, what I actually examined:\n- **The diff in REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n# Review: PR 3510 (issue #3498) at ae06eeeea21a231d80945f51c73fbffd2a87e865\r\n\r\nScope reviewed: `supabase/migrations/20260925044029_plm_item_user_assignment_and_workflow_action.sql` (100 lines, on disk) vs `patch.diff` hunk (100 lines) — byte-identical. Evidence pair `.agent/work/3498/2/{contract,completion}.json` reviewed. Sources re-read: `20260901221310`, `20260904143518`, `20260905053422`, `20260907121732`, siblings `20260911214438` / `20260917022233`, `20260905042713`, `20260810180000` lineage. No shell/database in this profile, so guard/cmd claims below are read-verified, not re-executed.\r\n\r\nAll three prior rounds' blockers are **verified fixed** at this head: `derived-from:` now names four real ledger versions (`:3`, all four files exist on disk); both `actor_identity_*` defaults are copied verbatim (`:40-52` vs `20260907121732:14-26`); intra-`plm` FKs plus the composite self-FK are present (`:16`, `:37`, `:53-54`, `:64-67`); header rationale is narrowed to `dflow.users` (`:6-8`), which is factually accurate.\r\n\r\n## Mandatory check 1 — index usage\r\n\r\n- **No loose/unusable index remains.** `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` (`:63`) now backs the composite self-FK (`:64-67`) — the orphan-index finding from prior rounds is closed. `UNIQUE (correlation_key)` (`:68`) serves the correlation-idempotency predicate. PKs serve `id` lookups.\r\n- **Join coverage of this change:** the migration issues no queries. FK enforcement probes hit parent PKs (`plm.\"RFQItem\"`, `plm.\"RFQStep\"`), which are indexed. Child-side FK columns carry no index, so a parent-side `DELETE` would scan the child — harmless on empty tables; note for the mover session.\r\n- **Gap (carried deferral, applies to both tables):** zero indexes leading with `rfq_item_id`. All six source indexes are still absent — `item_user_assignment_one_active` (partial unique), `item_user_assignment_active_lookup`, `item_workflow_action_item_time`, `item_workflow_action_one_return_per_source` (partial unique), `item_workflow_action_open_handoff_lookup`, `item_workflow_action_admin_review`. The header (`:9-10`) discloses only the *partial unique* deferral; the four plain lookup indexes are silently absent. The two partial-unique ones are integrity invariants, not performance aids — if rows land before they exist, later `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` can fail on duplicates. This is contract-blessed (gen-2 contract assumptions) and free to fix pre-load in the wiring session on still-empty tables, so I hold it as a tracked follow-up, not a merge blocker.\r\n\r\n## Mandatory check 2 — function volatility: no defect\r\n\r\n- The change creates zero functions/procedures/triggers, so no volatility marker exists to be wrong.\r\n- Adjacent facts verified: `clock_timestamp()` (VOLATILE) as DEFAULT (`:20`, `:23`, `:58`) is legal, per-row, and matches sources exactly. The `current_setting(...,true)` / `auth.jwt()` expressions in the restored defaults are STABLE-bodied session readers used inside DEFAULTs (which carry no marker) — behavior fixed, nothing mislabeled. CHECK helpers (`lower`, `btrim`, `jsonb_typeof`) are IMMUTABLE, as CHECKs require.\r\n- Low hardening note (both tables, inherited from `#1987` sources): CHECKs call unqualified `lower/btrim/jsonb_typeof` (`:25`, `:29`, `:70-71`, `:80`) while the new defaults qualify `pg_catalog.` — a hostile `search_path` entry could shadow the CHECK helpers. this needs revision rather than approval. I read the migration in full (`supabase/migrations/20260925044029_plm_item_user_assignment_and_workflow_action.sql:1-100`), the two evidence files (`.agent/work/3498/2/completion.json` in full; `contract.json` via the packet's `patch.diff`), and the source lineage it names. The change is genuinely additive and cannot damage an existing object, and the three machine-gate/write-compatibility blockers from the earlier rounds are indeed fixed at this head — but mandatory checks 1 and 3 are still unmet, one \"shape matches the source\" claim is still false, and the deferred work is recorded nowhere durable.\n\n## What I verified fixed at this head\n\n- **`derived-from:` is parseable** (`…044029_….sql:3` names `20260901221310, 20260904143518, 20260905053422, 20260907121732`, all four a 14-digit version, no prose). All four files exist in `supabase/migrations/` (`grep` hits at `20260901221310_…sql`, `20260904143518_…sql`, `20260905053422_…sql`, `20260907121732_…sql`).\n- **Both actor-identity defaults are copied verbatim**: `…044029_….sql:40-52` is textually identical to `20260907121732_designflow_trusted_backend_actor.sql:14-26`, including the `pg_catalog.current_setting(…, true)` / `auth.jwt() ->> 'email'` derivation and `pg_catalog.` qualification.\n- **Intra-`plm` FKs and the composite self-FK are present**: `…044029_….sql:16`, `:37`, `:53-54`, and `:63-67` (the `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` plus `FOREIGN KEY (source_action_id, rfq_item_id) → (id, rfq_item_id)`), matching `20260905053422_workflow_action_handoff_integrity.sql:56-65`. The prior \"index existing but unusable\" finding for that constraint is therefore closed — it now has its intended consumer.\n- **The FK rationale is now accurate**: the header narrows the deferral to `dflow.users` (`…044029_….sql:6-9`), and the item/step references do point at `plm.\"RFQItem\"`/`plm.\"RFQStep\"` (`20260904143518_canonical_designflow_workflow_contract.sql:10-28`), which exist (`supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:791`, `:919`, `:2285`, `:2288`).\n- **The additive-only claim is true**: the file contains only `CREATE TABLE`, `COMMENT ON TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE … ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `REVOKE`, and `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` (`…044029_….sql:12`, `:14-30`, `:35-90`, `:95-100`). No existing object is altered, dropped or renamed.\n- **`completion.json`'s `head_sha 7d809e42…` and single-entry `files_changed` are the required shape, not a discrepancy**: `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:53-70` requires `files_changed` to equal the merge-base..`head_sha` diff and permits only the PR's own two evidence files to follow `head_sha`, which is exactly what `.agent/work/3498/2/completion.json:9-13` records and what `MANIFEST.md` §2 describes (\"Rebind agent work contract evidence … after refreshing onto origin/main\").\n\n## Mandatory check 1 — index usage\n\n**1 (High). The change creates no secondary index at all, so the column both tables are organised around has no serving index — and the header discloses only half the deferral.** The file contains no `CREATE INDEX` (verified by reading all 100 lines); the only indexes that result are the two PKs and the two inline UNIQUE constraints at `…044029_….sql:63`, `:68`. Every index the sources rely on is absent:\n\n| Absent index | Source |\n|---|---|\n| `item_user_assignment_one_active` UNIQUE `(rfq_item_id, function_key, user_id) WHERE effective_to IS NULL` | `20260901221310_….sql:17-19` |\n| `item_user_assignment_active_lookup` `(rfq_item_id, function_key, effective_from, id) INCLUDE (user_id) WHERE effective_to IS NULL` | `20260901221310_….sql:21-24` |\n| `item_workflow_action_item_time` `(rfq_item_id, occurred_at, id)` | `20260901221310_….sql:40-41` |\n| `item_workflow_action_one_return_per_source` UNIQUE `(source_action_id) WHERE source_action_id IS NOT NULL` | `20260905053422_….sql:96-98` |\n| `item_workflow_action_open_handoff_lookup` `(rfq_item_id, occurred_at desc, id desc) INCLUDE (actor_user_id)` | `20260905053422_….sql:101-103` |\n| `item_workflow_action_admin_review` `(rfq_item_id, occurred_at) WHERE requires_admin_review` | `20260905053422_….sql:105-107` |\n\nTwo of these are integrity invariants, not performance aids — `one_active` is the only enforcement of \"one active assignment per (item, function, user)\" and `one_return_per_source` is, per `20260905053422_….sql:90-95`, the mechanism by which \"one handoff can never be returned twice\". The header discloses only the *partial unique* deferral (`…044029_….sql:9-10`); the four plain lookup indexes are silently absent, and `requires_admin_review` is copied as a column (`:62`) with nothing to query it by. Deferring the two partial uniques is *safe today* only while the tables are empty; if rows land first, the later `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` fails on duplicates. Note also that adding `CREATE INDEX` would have emitted both an `index` and a `table` object key (`scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:502-521`, \"an index is a write to its table\"), and `index` is a separately claimable kind (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:1268`) — so naming them was a claim-authoring choice by the same dispatch, not an external constraint.\n\n**2 (Medium). The self-FK's referencing columns are unindexed.** `…044029_….sql:64-67` makes `(source_action_id, rfq_item_id)` a child key with `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, but no index leads with `source_action_id`; the `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` at `:63` serves the *referenced* side only. A parent-side delete must scan the child. Harmless on empty tables, worth recording for the mover. The same applies to the other FK children (`rfq_item_id`, `prior_step_id`, `new_step_id`), which have no leading index either.\n\n**3 (Low). Inline-index invisibility.** The two indexes that *are* created come from inline constraints (`:63`, `:68`), which the collision extractor does not emit (its index rule is `CREATE INDEX`-only, `scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:502-521`). The \"exactly the two tables\" reasoning is therefore applied asymmetrically: the index that could be hidden inside `CREATE TABLE` was included, and the ones that could not were dropped.\n\n## Mandatory check 2 — function volatility\n\n**No defect; stated explicitly rather than left vacuous.** The migration creates zero functions, procedures, triggers or views (verified by reading all 100 lines), so no marker exists that could be wrong. Adjacent facts I did check:\n\n- `clock_timestamp()` as a column DEFAULT (`…044029_….sql:20`, `:23`, `:58`) is legal, VOLATILE, evaluated per row, and an exact match for the sources (`20260901221310_….sql:9`, `:12`, `:36`). It is the correct choice here: a STABLE `now()` would stamp bulk-copied rows identically and break `occurred_at` ordering.\n- The restored default expressions (`…044029_….sql:41-45`, `:47-52`) embed `pg_catalog.current_setting(text, true)` and `auth.jwt()`, both non-IMMUTABLE, used inside a DEFAULT (which carries no marker) — correct, and identical to `20260907121732_….sql:14-26`.\n- The CHECK helpers `lower` / `btrim` / `jsonb_typeof` are IMMUTABLE, which is what a CHECK requires.\n- The omitted source trigger functions (`20260901221310_….sql:87`, `:117`, which carry no explicit marker and so correctly default to VOLATILE) are not reproduced — that is finding 6 below, not a volatility defect.\n\n**4 (Low, hardening). CHECK/default expressions mix qualified and unqualified calls.** `…044029_….sql:47-49` qualify `pg_catalog.lower` / `pg_catalog.btrim` / `pg_catalog.current_setting`, but `:24-25`, `:69-70`, `:80` call bare `lower` / `btrim` / `jsonb_typeof`, and `:50` calls bare `auth.jwt()`. CHECK expressions are planned in the inserting session's `search_path`, so a hostile `public.lower(text)` could shadow them. Inherited from the sources (`20260901221310_….sql:6`, `:13`, `:14`), and cheap to fix in a brand-new table — but note the repo's own #2496 qualified calls for exactly this reason (`20260907121732_….sql:21-25`), so the fix direction is house style.\n\n## Mandatory check 3 — exact object checks\n\n**5 (High). The file asserts nothing about the objects it depends on, and this is an unmet mandatory check, not a style note.** There is no `DO` block, no `to_regclass`, no `pg_attribute` / `pg_constraint` / `pg_indexes` / `pg_policies` / `has_table_privilege` probe, and no post-create assertion; the file goes from the header to `COMMIT;` (`…044029_….sql:12`, `:100`). Nothing verifies:\n\n- that schema `plm` exists (it does — `20260621150714_foundation.sql` is in the tree — but the file does not check it);\n- that `plm.\"RFQItem\"(\"rfqItem_id\")` and `plm.\"RFQStep\"(\"RFQStep_id\")` exist with those exact columns (`ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:791`, `:919` show the tables; the file infers the columns);\n- that the two new tables do *not* already exist (plain `CREATE TABLE` on collision does fail, which is the safe direction, so this is the lesser half);\n- that the copied CHECKs, the composite FK, the `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` pair and the RLS/`REVOKE` state actually landed as intended.\n\nThe repository's doctrine is explicit and I verified the text: \"Before trusting a migration: confirm the OBJECT exists (`to_regclass`), never just the ledger row.\" (`docs/agents/section-4-anti-collision-rules.md:1173-1174`, mirrored at `docs/agents/anti-collision-summary.md:156-157`). The house exemplar does exactly this — `supabase/migrations/20260920202755_hts_rag_classification_jobs.sql:104-166` asserts relation kind, `pg_class.relrowsecurity`, exact `pg_get_constraintdef` strings, policy counts, column attributes and `has_table_privilege`. Whatever the truth of the \"catalogue-only checks are permitted\" reading, the point is that this file's own claims (`:3` \"live shapes\", `:6`, `:33`, `:93` \"Shape matches the dflow source\") are asserted nowhere and — see finding 6 — are demonstrably not true. Any addition must stay catalogue-only; I cannot re-derive the guard's exact predicate from the tools I have, so I record only that a verification block is what the doctrine requires and that the sibling precedent proves the shape exists.\n\n## Other findings\n\n**6 (High). \"Shape matches the dflow source\" is still false: one CHECK was not copied.** `20260905053422_….sql:185-191` installs `item_workflow_action_return_names_its_source` (`routing_context ->> 'return_to_original_handoff' is distinct from 'true' or source_action_id is not null`). The migration copies `routing_context` (`…044029_….sql:57`) and `source_action_id` (`:59`) and five other CHECKs from that same migration (`:69-89`), but not this one, and does not disclose the omission. Without it the plm home accepts a return action with a NULL `source_action_id` — the \"unclosable open handoff\" state that `20260905053422_….sql:179-184` says must \"stop the apply loudly\". This is the fourth consecutive round in which the parity claim has been shown false; the claim should either be made true or narrowed in the header and both COMMENTs (`…044029_….sql:6`, `:33`, `:93`).\n\n**7 (Medium). Column order diverges from the source in the table whose purpose is to receive its rows.** `actor_identity_source` / `actor_identity_email` sit 5th/6th (`…044029_….sql:40`, `:46`), because the plm table is written fresh; in dflow they were appended last by `ADD COLUMN` (`20260907121732_….sql:12-26`). Column set, types, nullability and defaults match; only order differs. A positional or `SELECT *` mover (`INSERT INTO plm.item_workflow_action SELECT * FROM dflow.item_workflow_action`) mis-maps from position 5 — it fails loudly (integer into text has no assignment cast), but it is a trap planted in the path this migration exists to prepare, and the mover contract should explicitly mandate column lists. `plm.item_user_assignment` matches position-for-position (`…044029_….sql:14-23` vs `20260901221310_….sql:3-15`).\n\n**8 (Medium). Append-only is asserted in a COMMENT and enforced by nothing.** `…044029_….sql:93` says \"Append-only workflow action history\" and `:33` says \"assignment history\". dflow enforces both with row triggers: `item_user_assignment_immutable_history` → `dflow.reject_item_assignment_history_rewrite()` (`20260901221310_….sql:113-115`, function at `:87-111`) and `item_workflow_action_immutable` → `dflow.reject_item_workflow_action_rewrite()` (`:127-129`). The plm tables have no trigger and no guard function, so UPDATE and DELETE are unrestricted while the catalogue states otherwise. Procureally explicable (a trigger function would add a `function plm.*` key outside the claim), but then the COMMENT must not assert the property, or must say it is not yet enforced.\n\n**9 (Medium). Nothing records the mover session's obligations.** `…044029_….sql:15`, `:36` use `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`, so both identities start at 1 while the `dflow` ids have been advancing since 2026-09-01 (`20260901221310_….sql:4`, `:27`); a mover preserving `id` needs `OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE` plus `setval` past `max(id)`. Separately, `app.user_notification.workflow_action_id` is FK'd to `dflow.item_workflow_action(id)` (`20260904143518_….sql:49-53`) and must be re-pointed. Neither the header (`…044029_….sql:5-6`), the COMMENTs, nor `.agent/work/3498/2/completion.json:39-47` names either. Also unrecorded: grants for the writer role (`designflow`, per `20260907121732_….sql:116-124`), the four `dflow.users` FKs, the trigger functions, and the six indexes — the evidence file records the deferrals in one clause and `completion.json:39-41` records only the three fixed blockers.\n\n**10 (Medium). Access posture is conventional but its rationale and a live consequence are unstated.** `…044029_….sql:95-98` enables RLS with zero policies and revokes ALL from `PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role`. The posture matches the nearest plm sibling exactly, including its own revoke (`20260911214438_plm_factory_time_templates.sql:96-97`), which carries the explanatory comment this file omits (`20260911214438_….sql:94-95`, \"the DesignFlow API connects as the table owner. No browser or service-role access\"). It is not, however, a no-op: `20260710135975_reconcile_service_role_grants.sql:14` set a schema-wide default, and `20260810180000_plm_default_privilege_hole_and_pg17_maintain_revokes.sql:252-253` narrowed it to `arwd` (asserted from `pg_default_acl` at `:399-411`), so these tables are born with `service_role=arwd` and the `REVOKE` removes it. That is deliberate here, but it means any non-owner writer gets `permission denied` until the wiring session grants, and the RLS lock is carried only by the REVOKEs — `postgres` owns the tables and bypasses RLS because there is no `FORCE`. `plm` is not PostgREST-exposed (`docs/agents/references-and-runbooks.md:21`), so the `anon`/`authenticated` revokes are belt-and-braces. One line of rationale, as in the sibling, would make the intent legible.\n\n**11 (Low). Evidence-source hygiene.** `completion.json:34` records a `command` that is prose (\"object keys of the migration match the claim writes exactly\") rather than a rerunnable command, and the `check-sql.sh` evidence string (`:26`) cites Guard B, expected-count, verify-cost and EOL-reference but not the live-ledger comparison. I cannot re-execute any of it from this profile (below).\n\n**12 (Low). The authoritative doc goes false on merge.** `docs/designflow-master-data-migration/designflow-schema-segregation.md:152-153` still reads \"`plm` table not yet created\" for both rows, and the history row at `:328` records the 2026-09-24 placement but not the creation. The author was correctly scoped out (`patch.diff` shows `allowed_paths` limited to the migration plus the four `.agent/work/3498/{1,2}` files), so this is an orchestrator follow-up that must be named, not a diff defect. `:317` (\"Recreate cross-schema FKs and verify grants/RLS\") is the documented procedure this migration partly departs from.\n\n**13 (Low). `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;` with `COMMIT` last** (`…044029_….sql:12`, `:100`) is harmless and matches the sibling (`20260911214438_….sql:19`, `:99`), but any statement appended after that `COMMIT` would run in autocommit. Consistency note only.\n\n**14 (Low). No `lock_timeout` / `statement_timeout`.** The direct sources set both (`20260905053422_….sql:39-40`, `20260907121732_….sql:6-7`); the plm sibling does not (`20260911214438_….sql` has none). `CREATE TABLE` on brand-new objects takes no contended lock, so this is consistency-only.\n\n## Limits on this review (missing evidence, not inferred absences)\n\n- No shell, git or database in this profile: I did **not** run `scripts/check-sql.sh`, the Python/Node guard suites, or any contract test, and `MANIFEST.md` §5 records that no tests were run for the packet. The `check-sql.sh` exit-0 claim in `.agent/work/3498/2/completion.json:24-27` is therefore credible-but-unreproduced by me.\n- I could **not** verify that `20260925044029` is unique in `supabase/migrations/` or is the newest version — my directory listing was truncated before that version, and I have no git history. The version reservation (#3502) and the `refs/db-contracts/3498/2` ref/sha are GitHub-side and unreachable.\n- I could not recompute the whole-source digest `fb4d89b0…`; I compared the on-disk migration (read in full) against the `patch.diff` text supplied in this conversation instead.\n- `docs/agents/anti-collision-summary.md:61-62` requires **two** independent reviewers for migrations and RLS work; this is one.\n- I did not open `.agent/work/3498/2/contract.json` with a tool; I relied on the `patch.diff` text supplied in the conversation for its `allowed_paths`, `db_writes` and `assumptions`.\n\n## Assessment\n\nNothing in this diff endangers the existing database: it is purely additive, creates two empty tables, alters no existing object, and fails closed on access. The `derived-from:` header, the two actor-identity defaults, and the intra-`plm` FK set (including the composite self-FK that gives `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` its purpose) are all verified fixed at this head, and the header's remaining rationale is factually correct. I do not agree with the most recent round's approval, for four reasons that are all evidence-backed above: mandatory check 3 is still unmet for a file whose central claim is a derivation from live shapes; the file still ships no index leading with `rfq_item_id` while disclosing only half of what it drops, and two of the dropped indexes are the integrity invariants a \"final home\" must hold before rows arrive; the \"shape matches\" claim remains false because `item_workflow_action_return_names_its_source` was not copied; and the append-only property is asserted in the catalogue with nothing enforcing it. The change *creates* four predicates that no index serves: the RI triggers it installs on two live tables scan unindexed FK child columns.**\nThis is not a prediction about future app queries — it is a cost this migration attaches to objects that already exist. `:27`, `:48`, `:64`, `:65` create four FKs whose **parents are live**. PostgreSQL installs an internal RI trigger on each parent; on parent `DELETE` (or key `UPDATE`) the parent fires a probe of the form `SELECT 1 FROM ONLY <child> WHERE <childkey> = $1 [FOR KEY SHARE]`:\n- `DELETE FROM plm.\"RFQItem\"` → cascade probe on `plm.item_user_assignment.rfq_item_id` (`:27`) **and** restrict probe on `plm.item_workflow_action.rfq_item_id` (`:48`).\n- `DELETE FROM plm.\"RFQStep\"` → NO ACTION probes on `plm.item_workflow_action.prior_step_id` (`:64`) and `.new_step_id` (`:65`).\nNeither table has an index leading with any of those four columns. Mandatory check 2 — function volatility\n**No defect.** The change creates zero functions, procedures, triggers and views — all 135 lines read — so no `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` marker exists that could be wrong, and specifically nothing that reads a table carries an `IMMUTABLE` label. It is the **correct** choice and an exact match for `20260901221310:9`, `:12`, `:36`. A STABLE `now()` would stamp every row of a bulk copy identically and destroy the `occurred_at` ordering that `item_workflow_action_open_handoff_lookup` and the `order by … occurred_at desc, id desc` handoff resolution depend on. The `plm` sibling's `DEFAULT now()` (`20260911214438:72-73`) is the wrong model to copy here, and this file correctly did not copy it.\n- Consequence worth recording: `effective_from` (`:31`) and `created_at` (`:34`) on one row receive two independent `clock_timestamp()` evaluations and are **not** guaranteed equal. Same in the source; do not assume equality.\n- The restored DEFAULT expressions at `:51-63` embed `pg_catalog.current_setting(text, true)` and `auth.jwt()`, both STABLE session readers. A DEFAULT carries no volatility marker, so nothing is mislabelled.\n- CHECK helpers `lower`, `btrim`, `jsonb_typeof`, `~` are all IMMUTABLE, which is what a stored CHECK requires.\n- The omitted source trigger functions (`20260901221310:87`, `:117`) carry no marker and so correctly default to VOLATILE. Their absence is F11, not a volatility defect; if added later they must stay VOLATILE.\n**F5 (Low, hardening). A stored CHECK is re-planned in the *inserting session's* `search_path`, and `pg_catalog` is implicitly first only when it is not named in that path — so a role with `search_path = public, pg_catalog` and a hostile `public.lower(text)` could shadow them. Inherited verbatim from `20260901221310:6`, `:13`, `:14`; the repo's own #2496 hardened exactly this by qualifying (`20260907121732:16-23`). A mover preserving `id` needs `OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE` **and** `setval` past `max(id)`, or the first native insert collides on the PK.\n- `app.user_notification.workflow_action_id` is FK'd to `dflow.item_workflow_action(id)` (`20260904143518:49-53`, corroborated by `foreign-keys.csv:158`) and must be re-pointed.\n- Column order (`:51`, `:57` at positions 5-6; in `dflow` they were appended last by `20260907121732:12-23`) means a positional `INSERT … SELECT *` mover mis-maps from position 5. Disclosed at `:6-8` and `:109`. It fails loudly (integer→text has no assignment cast), but the mover contract must forbid positional loads.\n**F15 (Low-Medium). No `lock_timeout` / `statement_timeout`, where the change locks two live tables.** All three direct sources set both (`20260904143518:7-8`, `20260905053422:39-40`, `20260907121732:6-7`) — and they are exactly the migrations that add FKs to live tables. An inline `REFERENCES` acquires `ShareRowExclusiveLock` on the **referenced** relation, which conflicts with the `RowExclusiveLock` taken by INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. So during the apply, writes to live `plm.\"RFQItem\"` (~6783 rows, `idx_scan=1489`) and `plm.\"RFQStep\"` block, and with no `lock_timeout` the migration waits indefinitely behind any in-flight writer while every later writer queues behind it. The \"brand-new objects only\" framing in earlier rounds is not exact. Stated fairly, there is counter-precedent: the nearest `plm` sibling also omits both while adding an inline FK to a live `plm` table (`20260911214438:70`, no `lock_timeout` in the file), and no `2026092*` migration sets one. The sibling it copies carries the explanation — `20260911214438:94-95`: *\"Same access model as plm.\\\"FactoryTime\\\": the DesignFlow API connects as the table owner. No browser or service-role access.\"* One line here would record that the deny-all is deliberate, and that a non-owner writer (the production `designflow` role, `20260907121732:41-46`) needs a grant from the wiring session.\n**F17 (Low). Mandatory check 1 — index usage: no defect\n- **No unserved predicate or join.** The change issues no queries; the only predicates it *creates* are the five RI probes tabulated above, and each has a matching leading index.\n- **No index that exists but cannot be used as written.** `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` (`:81`) is the referent of the composite self-FK (`:82-85`) — the sole reason it exists in the source. `UNIQUE (correlation_key)` (`:86`) serves the correlation-idempotency equality that `dflow.record_item_workflow_action` relies on (`20260905053422:441`) and reproduces the name Postgres auto-generates for the source's inline `unique` (`20260901221310:34`), which is what makes an `on conflict (correlation_key)` inference work against the new table. The two PKs serve `id`.\n- **Loose-index assumptions I checked and rejected as non-issues**, since these are the ones a reviewer is most likely to raise wrongly: (a) `item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_idx` is **not** redundant with `item_user_assignment_one_active` — the latter is partial (`WHERE effective_to IS NULL`), so it cannot serve the CASCADE probe, which must see every row; (b) `item_workflow_action_source_action_rfq_item_idx` only partly overlaps the partial unique `one_return_per_source` — the RI probe matches both columns and a partial index is usable only if the planner proves `source_action_id IS NOT NULL` from a parameterised equality, so the dedicated non-partial composite is correct, not redundant; (c) `item_workflow_action_rfq_item_id_idx` is not subsumed by `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` (non-leading column, no skip scan) nor by `(source_action_id, rfq_item_id)` (non-leading).\n- **The two partial unique integrity predicates are exact.** `item_user_assignment_one_active (rfq_item_id, function_key, user_id) WHERE effective_to IS NULL` (`:46-48`) is byte-identical to `20260901221310:17-19`; `item_workflow_action_one_return_per_source (source_action_id) WHERE source_action_id IS NOT NULL` (`:123-125`) is byte-identical to `20260905053422:96-98`. Mandatory check 2 — function volatility: no defect, stated non-vacuously\nThe change creates **zero** functions, procedures, triggers and views across all three SQL artifacts (219 + 91 + 82 lines read), so no `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` marker exists that could be wrong — and specifically nothing that reads a table carries `IMMUTABLE`. What I checked so the answer is not empty:\n- `clock_timestamp()` (VOLATILE) as a column DEFAULT at `:32`, `:35`, `:76` is legal, evaluated per row, and byte-identical to the sources (`20260901221310:9`, `:12`, `:36`). Keeping it over the STABLE `now()` used by the nearest plm sibling (`20260911214438:72-73`) is the **correct** call: a STABLE default would stamp every row of a bulk copy with one identical timestamp and destroy the `occurred_at` ordering the deferred `open_handoff_lookup` and the `order by … occurred_at desc, id desc` handoff resolution depend on. Consequence to record: `effective_from` (`:32`) and `created_at` (`:35`) receive two independent evaluations and are **not** guaranteed equal — same as the source; never assume equality.\n- The two derived DEFAULTs (`:58-70`) embed `pg_catalog.current_setting(text, boolean)` and `auth.jwt()`, both STABLE session readers. A DEFAULT carries no volatility marker, so nothing is mislabelled. Substituting a constant here — the earlier rounds' defect — would have been a *behavioural* break, not a marker error, and it is not present.\n- Every CHECK helper is IMMUTABLE, as a stored CHECK requires: `pg_catalog.lower`, `pg_catalog.btrim`, `pg_catalog.jsonb_typeof`, `~`, `->>`, `IS DISTINCT FROM`.\n- The omitted source trigger functions (`20260901221310:87-129`) carry no marker and correctly default to VOLATILE; their absence is a disclosed deferral (`:19-21`, `:128`), not a volatility defect. If the wiring session adds them they must stay VOLATILE.\n- The catalogue routines the verify block calls (`to_regclass`, `pg_get_expr`, `pg_get_constraintdef`, `has_table_privilege`) sit in an anonymous `DO` block, which has no marker; `has_table_privilege` is session-dependent, which is correct and intended for a one-shot apply-time assertion.\n## 5. Mandatory check 3 — exact object checks: substantially met, two depth gaps\n**What is asserted exactly rather than inferred:**\n- Dependencies are engine-asserted with schema, relation **and** column: `REFERENCES plm.\"RFQItem\"(\"rfqItem_id\")` (`:28`, `:55`), `REFERENCES plm.\"RFQStep\"(\"RFQStep_id\")` (`:71`, `:72`), self-reference `REFERENCES plm.item_workflow_action(id, rfq_item_id)` (`:84`). Object collision fails closed (plain `CREATE TABLE`, no `IF NOT EXISTS`).\n- Post-create: `to_regclass` + `relkind='r'` + `relrowsecurity` (`:154-158`); exact column counts 9 and 16 (`:146-153`); zero `pg_policies` for the exact `(schemaname, tablename)` pair (`:160-165`); the 3×7 privilege sweep (`:166-172`); `pg_attrdef`/`pg_get_expr` on both derived defaults (`:177-194`); `pg_constraint` on `conrelid` **and** `confrelid` **and** exact `conname` **and** `contype='f'` **and** `pg_get_constraintdef` shape for the composite self-FK (`:195-201`); all seven index names (`:202-213`). Every failure path raises, so the block fails closed — and if a table were missing, `to_regclass` returns NULL, the count is 0, and `0 <> 9` raises.\n- The contract test asserts the *right object* for the two invariants, not just a name: `pg_index.indisunique` plus the deparsed `indpred` (`:78-90`).\n**Gaps:**\n**M1 (Medium). The migration's seven index assertions are name-resolution only.** `IF pg_catalog.to_regclass('plm.' || index_name) IS NULL` (`:211`) is satisfied by *any* relation of that name — a table, view, sequence or composite type would pass. Nothing at apply time asserts `relkind='i'`, `indrelid`, the key columns, uniqueness, or the partial predicate. This is precisely the pattern the checklist names: a check that a name merely exists is not a check that the right object exists. The artifact that does prove the two integrity invariants (`:78-90` of the test) runs only in CI, not on production. The in-repo gold standard for the stronger form is `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:613-628`, which pins the full `indexdef` string per index. Cheap fix inside the same guard-permitted block: join `pg_index`/`pg_class` and compare `pg_get_indexdef(indexrelid)` for all seven.\n**M2 (Medium). The default assertions are substring LIKEs, not equality** (`:183-184`, `:191-192`). `%request.designflow.actor_id%` **and** `%supabase_auth%` is satisfied by an *inverted* CASE (`then 'supabase_auth' else 'designflow_jwt'`) — a silent provenance mis-attribution on an append-only actor-attribution audit table, and the exact defect class that took three earlier rounds. The catalogue-only fix is available and stays inside `check-migration-verify-cost.mjs`: compare `pg_get_expr` of the plm column against `pg_get_expr` of the corresponding `dflow` column, both read from `pg_attrdef` — no data read.\n**M3 (Low-Medium). The live proof asserts no foreign key at all,** while issue #3498's own `live_assertion` requires \"intended foreign keys and seven claimed indexes\". Two independent in-repo artifacts establish this: `docs/verification/cloudsql-designflow-capture-2026-08-10/designflow-capture.txt:652` and `:793` show the identity columns `RFQItem.rfqItem_id` (BY DEFAULT) and `RFQStep.RFQStep_id` (ALWAYS) with an **empty** default field, while `:288` and `:316` show serial columns rendering `nextval('designflow.\"…_id_seq\"'::regclass)`; and Supabase's own introspection query captured at `docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260904T212459Z/run2/pg-stat-statements-top300.json:1062` has to *synthesize* `nextval(...)` from `pg_depend` for `attidentity` columns precisely because `ad.adbin` is not there. I verified the remaining 9 + 16 columns by hand against the four sources: names, types, typmods, nullability, defaults and `attidentity` all match, so the signature equality should hold. The contract test is safe on this axis regardless — it compares `atthasdef` and `attidentity` (`:21`, `:26`, `:31`, `:36`) rather than rendered text, which is the more robust choice and correctly side-steps the ordinal divergence.\n## 6. Role, permission and security-boundary assessment\n- **Grants changed: none.** The change contains no `GRANT` anywhere in all three artifacts.\n- **Revokes changed: two** (`:134-135`), `REVOKE ALL ON TABLE … FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role`. **These are not no-ops.** `20260710135975:14` set `alter default privileges in schema plm grant all on tables to service_role`, narrowed by `20260810180000:253-254` (`alter default privileges for role postgres in schema plm revoke truncate, references, trigger, maintain on tables from service_role`, whose own comment states \"After this runs, a newly created plm table hands service_role a, r, w, d only\"). Both tables are therefore born with `service_role=arwd` and these REVOKEs remove it. `PUBLIC`, `anon` and `authenticated` held nothing.\n- **Net boundary:** only the owner (`postgres`, the migration role) can read or write either table. `plm` is not in prod `pgrst.db_schemas` (`docs/agents/references-and-runbooks.md:21`: `public, graphql_public, api, crm, pim, core, app`), so neither table is PostgREST-reachable in any role; the `anon`/`authenticated` halves are belt-and-braces and `service_role` is the operative one — which is now the one asserted (`:170`).\n- **Posture is house convention, and the rationale is now documented.** `:132-135` matches the nearest plm sibling exactly, including its bare revoke with no compensating grant (`20260911214438:94-97`), and `:130-131` carries the explanatory comment the earlier rounds asked for (\"Deny-by-default until DesignFlow wiring explicitly grants its backend role. No browser or service-role access is available at this stage.\"). This is **not** the #2662 defect remediated by `20260914155226`, which was zero-policy RLS **plus** grants; here there are no grants, so deny-all is coherent and fail-closed.\n- **Sibling call paths: none exist.** Repo-wide sweep for both table names returns only this migration, its contract test, its live proof, the segregation doc and three stale HANDOFF rows. No view, function, trigger, policy, publication, test or other migration references either table, and no FK from any other table points at them. Nothing can inherit or bypass this posture, and the `dflow` originals with their two SECURITY DEFINER writers (`20260901221310:338-350`) are untouched.\n- **Obligation created for the successor, correctly recorded:** the production writer role `designflow` (`20260907121732:41-46`) gets nothing here and needs an explicit grant before anyone but the owner can use these tables. SQL syntax and runnability\n**Migration (219 lines).** `BEGIN;` (`:22`) … `COMMIT;` (`:218`), COMMIT last, so atomicity holds and nothing runs in autocommit. `SET LOCAL lock_timeout='5s'` / `statement_timeout='5min'` (`:23-24`) sit inside the transaction, so they take effect and revert at COMMIT without leaking into the applier's session — a strictly better form than the sources' non-`LOCAL` `set` (`20260905053422:39-40`, `20260907121732:6-7`). The `DO $verify$` block (`:138-216`) is valid plpgsql throughout: `FOREACH … IN ARRAY` over declared scalars, `SELECT count(*) INTO` a declared integer, a simple `CASE` returning integer, `EXISTS`/`NOT EXISTS` over `pg_catalog.pg_class`/`pg_policies`/`unnest(...) CROSS JOIN unnest(...)`, `pg_get_expr(adbin, adrelid) LIKE`, and `pg_get_constraintdef(oid) LIKE` where `oid` correctly resolves to the `pg_constraint` column. `has_table_privilege(text, text, text)` resolves to the `(name, text, text)` overload through the implicit `text→name` cast, and the identical call shape is already proven in this repository by `.github/live-proofs/2863.sql:60`.\n**Guards hand-applied — all pass.**\n- `check-migration-verify-cost.mjs`: the block **is** inspected (tag `$verify$` signals it, `:171-176`), and `PATTERNS` run against the *scannable* view in which every string literal's contents are blanked (`:112-118`), so all `'plm.'` and `'plm.item_workflow_action'` fragments reduce to `''`. No unterminated literal, dollar tag or quoted identifier — note the regex literal `'^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$'` is safe because `scanSql` consumes it in its single-quote branch before the `$`-tag branch. **Passes.**\n- `check-expected-count-patterns.mjs`: not applicable — the file never mentions `expected_counts`; `expected_columns` is a different identifier and the guard's regexes require `expected_counts ->>` or `expected_counts ?`.\n- Issue #1684 EOL guard: not applicable, the file never mentions `properties_and_characters`.\n- `check-live-proof-probe.mjs`: `evaluateProbe` (`:161-186`) finds a changed migration, resolves the contract at `.agent/work/3498/4/contract.json` via `resolveEvidencePair`, reads `work_type: structural`, `work_issue: 3498`, `application_return_to: popcre/shared-db` from the issue's single `db-work-scope` block, and finds the probe present in the PR — then `probeShapeProblem` passes: one statement (single trailing `;`), starts with `WITH`, ends `AS passed`, and contains **no write keyword**, because the `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`TRUNCATE` words appear only inside string literals that `scanProbeSql` collapses to `''`. `scripts/test_shared_db_live_proof.py:92-98` also passes (no interior semicolon after comment-stripping; `\\bas passed\\b` present). Rollback and recovery\n- **Partial failure mid-file:** everything sits in one transaction (`:22` … `:218`) with COMMIT last, and CI adds `--single-transaction`, so a failure anywhere leaves neither table and no index. No half-created pair is reachable.\n- **Recovery after a successful apply:** drop the two tables (they are independent of each other; the self-FK dies with its table). Both are empty, referenced by nothing, and read by no view, function, publication, trigger or test — the sweep in §6 proves there is no dependent. Dropping them also removes the four internal RI triggers from `plm.\"RFQItem\"` and `plm.\"RFQStep\"`, restoring those parents exactly.\n- **Original capability preserved:** no `dflow` object is altered, dropped or renamed, no function body is replaced, and the existing `dflow.item_*` tables, their six indexes, their two immutability triggers, their grants and their two SECURITY DEFINER writers are all untouched. The DesignFlow capability this change is meant to eventually replace is fully intact on the day this merges.\n- **Version rollback:** `20260925044029` is permanently retired and never reusable (`docs/agents/anti-collision-summary.md:36`), so a rollback-and-reissue needs a further supersession through the governed lane. Ledger-row rollback must not use `supabase migration repair --status reverted` (`anti-collision-summary.md:39-41`).\n## 10. Impact on existing RFQ tables\n- `plm.\"RFQItem\"` and `plm.\"RFQStep\"` are live (`ci-bootstrap:792`, `:920`, PKs at `:2285`, `:2288`) and gain four internal RI triggers from `:28`, `:55`, `:71`, `:72`.\n- **Lock bounds:** an inline `REFERENCES` takes `ShareRowExclusiveLock` on the referenced relation, which conflicts with the `RowExclusiveLock` taken by INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE — so during the apply, writes to both live parents block. This is bounded: `SET LOCAL lock_timeout='5s'` (`:23`) aborts the whole transaction atomically after 5s, and `statement_timeout='5min'` (`:24`) caps the total. The earlier rounds' \"brand-new objects only\" framing was not exact; the bound is what makes it acceptable, and it is now present.\n- **Ongoing cost:** every `DELETE FROM plm.\"RFQItem\"` now pays a CASCADE probe into `item_user_assignment` and a RESTRICT probe into `item_workflow_action`; every `DELETE FROM plm.\"RFQStep\"` pays two NO ACTION probes. All four are index-served (§3), so the cost is bounded and small. `ON DELETE RESTRICT` is non-deferrable and fires immediately, so the probe is paid even while the child is empty — identical to dflow (`20260904143518:21-23`). **G7** below.\n- **New destructive path, intended parity:** `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `plm.item_user_assignment.rfq_item_id` (`:28`) means deleting an RFQItem will cascade-delete assignment rows. Empty today, so no behaviour change; after row movement this is a live cascade on a live table. It mirrors dflow exactly (`20260904143518:13-15`), so it is intended parity rather than a new hazard — but the mover session should know it exists.\n- **No other impact:** no `ALTER`/`DROP`/`RENAME` of any existing object, no DML, no publication change, no grant, no type regeneration (`types/` contains neither table, and `plm` is not PostgREST-exposed, consistent with the scope block's `generated_types: not-applicable`).\n## 11. Remaining findings\n**G1 (Medium, governance — orchestrator confirmation required before merge; not a defect in the diff).** No repo-side claim-ledger row records either the new version or the nine-object expansion. `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T1226Z:119`, `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T1750Z:111` and `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T2305Z:95`, `:104` all still read `20260925044029` with only `table plm.item_user_assignment`, `table plm.item_workflow_action`; the newest HANDOFF (`2026-09-27T2359Z:85`) lists #3502 as open with no version at all. Claim #3502's row was not brought to that form, and the PR body still says \"Claim #3502 reserves migration version 20260925044029\". `anti-collision-summary.md:31-32` makes the **claim issue body** authoritative, not the HANDOFF prose, and that body is GitHub-side — I cannot read it from this checkout. **What the orchestrator must confirm before merge:** that claim #3502's live `db-claim` block reserves `20260925222635` and lists all nine objects, and that `refs/db-claim-supersessions/3502-20260925044029` exists. The three HANDOFF rows should also be corrected or superseded so the next session does not re-derive the wrong version.\n**G2 (Medium, unrecorded mover hazard).** The four parent FKs here are **VALID** (`:28`, `:55`, `:71`, `:72` — no `NOT VALID`), while every corresponding dflow FK was added `NOT VALID` (`20260904143518:13-15`, `:21-28`). VALID on empty tables is correct and strictly stronger, and it is the right choice for a declared final home. But it means the deferred row movement inherits a constraint dflow never enforced: because `NOT VALID` skips existing rows, dflow may hold rows whose `rfq_item_id`, `prior_step_id` or `new_step_id` resolves to nothing in `plm.\"RFQItem\"`/`plm.\"RFQStep\"`. Those rows were tolerated for three weeks and will be **refused with SQLSTATE 23503** on insert into plm. Assessment\nNothing in this change can damage the existing database. It is strictly additive — `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX`, `COMMENT ON TABLE`, `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `REVOKE`, one catalogue-reading `DO` block, `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` — with no `ALTER`/`DROP`/`RENAME` of any existing object, no DML, no row movement and no grant. It is version-clean and newest in-tree, atomic with COMMIT last, bounded by `SET LOCAL` timeouts, and deny-by-default with the operative `service_role` half now actually asserted. Rollback is a drop of two empty, unreferenced tables that also removes the four RI triggers it added to the live RFQ parents, leaving the original dflow capability untouched.\nAll three mandatory checks are met, and the two gaps I found (M1, M2) are about the *depth* of assertions that are themselves correct — not about a present defect. I verified the seven index definitions, both partial-unique predicates, all 9 + 16 columns and both derived defaults line-by-line against the four source migrations, and hand-applied five separate guards to the actual bytes: verify-cost, expected-count, EOL, probe-shape, and the object-key extractor that produces the nine claimed writes. The post-apply catalog verifier derives a rich target list from this file, so promotion will be provable rather than silent — a material improvement over the head the prior round refused. The change also newly carries an executable, non-quarantined, gating CI contract test and a read-only production probe riding in the implementation PR as #3127 requires, and it is the first head in this PR's history where the recurring falsified-parity class is covered by two machine comparisons rather than by prose.\nEvery blocking finding from the five prior rounds is closed and I re-derived each from source rather than from the summaries. I also corrected one thing I initially suspected and then refuted with in-repo evidence (§5): the live proof's default-signature comparison is **not** broken by identity-column sequence names, because identity columns carry no `pg_attrdef` row.\nWhat remains is: two assertion-depth improvements (M1, M2) and one live-proof completeness gap (M3), all correctable in artifacts this PR owns; one governance confirmation only the orchestrator can perform (G1); one unrecorded mover hazard that follows from a deliberate and correct choice in this file (G2); and five Lows. None can damage an existing object, and none requires this file's SQL to be different today.
