Whole-source digest `e284d3b6…` was not recomputed (no shell).\n\n## 1. Index usage (mandatory)\n\nPredicates this migration installs, and the index that serves each:\n\n| Predicate this file creates | Serving index |\n|---|---|\n| `ON DELETE CASCADE` from live `plm.\"RFQItem\"` into `item_user_assignment.rfq_item_id` (`:28`) | `item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_idx` (`:44-45`) |\n| `ON DELETE RESTRICT` from `plm.\"RFQItem\"` into `item_workflow_action.rfq_item_id` (`:55`) | `item_workflow_action_rfq_item_id_idx` (`:115-116`) |\n| `plm.\"RFQStep\"` probe on `prior_step_id` (`:71`) | `item_workflow_action_prior_step_id_idx` (`:117-118`) |\n| `plm.\"RFQStep\"` probe on `new_step_id` (`:72`) | `item_workflow_action_new_step_id_idx` (`:119-120`) |\n| Self-FK child `(source_action_id, rfq_item_id)` (`:82-85`) | `item_workflow_action_source_action_rfq_item_idx` (`:121-122`), same column order |\n| Referenced side of that self-FK | `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` (`:81`) |\n| One active assignment per `(rfq_item_id, function_key, user_id)` where `effective_to IS NULL` | `item_user_assignment_one_active` (`:46-48`), matching `20260901221310:17-19` |\n| One return per source handoff | `item_workflow_action_one_return_per_source` (`:123-125`), matching `20260905053422:96-98` |\n| Correlation idempotency | inline `UNIQUE (correlation_key)` (`:86`) |\n| `id` lookups | primary keys |\n\nNo leftover “index exists but cannot be used as written.” `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` is the referent of the composite self-FK, matching `20260905053422:50-65`.\n\nLoose-overlap checks that are **not** defects: `item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_idx` is required beside the partial unique `one_active`, because CASCADE must see closed rows; `item_workflow_action_source_action_rfq_item_idx` is required beside `one_return_per_source`, because the RI probe is two-column and the unique is partial on `source_action_id IS NOT NULL`; `item_workflow_action_rfq_item_id_idx` is not subsumed by `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` (non-leading column).\n\nFour source lookup indexes remain absent and are named individually in the header (`:15-18`): `item_user_assignment_active_lookup`, `item_workflow_action_item_time`, `item_workflow_action_open_handoff_lookup`, `item_workflow_action_admin_review`. Tables are created empty; those four are deferred until a successor, before the first row. Integrity indexes ship now, so a later unique build cannot fail on duplicates created in this home. Repo-wide, nothing yet reads either `plm` table.\n\n## 2. Function volatility (mandatory)\n\nThe change creates zero functions, procedures, triggers, or views across the migration, contract test, and live proof, so no `IMMUTABLE` / `STABLE` / `VOLATILE` marker exists that could be wrong.\n\nAdjacent constructs checked:\n\n- `clock_timestamp()` as DEFAULT (`:32`, `:35`, `:76`) is VOLATILE, evaluated per row, and matches `20260901221310:9,12,36`. A STABLE `now()` would stamp a bulk copy identically and destroy `occurred_at` ordering. `effective_from` and `created_at` receive two independent evaluations and are not guaranteed equal — same as the source.\n- Actor defaults (`:58-70`) embed `pg_catalog.current_setting(text, true)` and `auth.jwt()` inside a DEFAULT (no marker), textually matching `20260907121732:14-26`.\n- CHECK helpers are `pg_catalog.lower` / `btrim` / `jsonb_typeof` (`:37`, `:41`, `:88`, `:90`, `:98`) — IMMUTABLE, as a stored CHECK requires.\n- Omitted append-only trigger functions stay successor work; if added they must remain VOLATILE.\n\n## 3. Exact object checks (mandatory)\n\nDependencies are named with schema, relation, and column: `REFERENCES plm.\"RFQItem\"(\"rfqItem_id\")` (`:28`, `:55`), `REFERENCES plm.\"RFQStep\"(\"RFQStep_id\")` (`:71-72`), self-FK `REFERENCES plm.item_workflow_action(id, rfq_item_id)` (`:82-85`). Those fail the apply if schema, table, or column is wrong. Both parents exist with those primary keys (`ci-bootstrap:791-792`, `:919-920`, `:2285`, `:2288`). Collision fails closed (`CREATE TABLE` without `IF NOT EXISTS`).\n\nPost-create catalogue block (`:138-216`) asserts, per table: column count 9 / 16 via `pg_attribute`; `to_regclass` with `relkind = 'r'` and `relrowsecurity`; zero `pg_policies` for the exact `(schemaname, tablename)` pair; the three-role × seven-privilege matrix including `service_role`; actor default expressions containing `request.designflow.actor_id` / `supabase_auth` and `request.designflow.actor_email` / `auth.jwt()`; composite self-FK by `conname`, `contype = 'f'`, `confrelid` self, and `pg_get_constraintdef` fragment; all seven claimed index names via `to_regclass('plm.' || index_name)`.\n\nThe SQL contract test additionally `EXCEPT`-compares `(attname, atttypid, atttypmod, attnotnull, atthasdef, attidentity)` against `dflow.*` (`:20-40`) — order-independent, which is the right design given the disclosed ordinal divergence — and checks `indisunique` plus predicates on the two partial uniques (`:79-88`). CI globs `supabase/tests/*.sql` (`.github/workflows/database-contract-tests.yml:29-32`, `:628`) and wraps this file in `begin; \\ir …; rollback;` (`:679`). It is not on `ci-quarantine.txt`.\n\nThe `$verify$` body reads `pg_catalog.pg_attribute` / `pg_class` / `pg_policies` / `pg_constraint` / `pg_attrdef` only. `plm.` names sit in string literals, which `check-migration-verify-cost.mjs` blanks before matching `FROM/JOIN` + `plm.object`. Hand-applied: the guard permits this shape.\n\nResidual depth (non-blocking): migration index assertions are name-resolution (`to_regclass` is any relation of that name); default assertions are distinctive `LIKE` fragments rather than full `pg_get_expr` equality. The contract test proves uniqueness and predicates for the two integrity indexes. The live proof proves full default-signature equality against `dflow` (`:45-58`), which closes the inverted-CASE hole the `LIKE` pair would miss. Identity columns carry no `pg_attrdef` row, so sequence names cannot break that equality.\n\n## Role, grants, RLS\n\nNo `GRANT` anywhere in the three SQL artifacts. Two `REVOKE ALL ON TABLE … FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role` (`:134-135`). These are not no-ops: `20260710135975:14` plus `20260810180000:252-253` leave a new `plm` table with `service_role=arwd`; the REVOKEs remove it. `PUBLIC` / `anon` / `authenticated` held nothing.\n\nNet boundary: only the owner can read or write. `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` with zero policies (`:132-133`) matches sibling `20260911214438:94-97`, and `:130-131` now carries the rationale. `FORCE` is omitted, so the owner still bypasses RLS; the closed door is the REVOKE, and the probe now tests `service_role`, the role that actually held the privilege. This is fail-closed empty-table posture, not the #2662 zero-policy-plus-grants defect.\n\n`plm` is outside PostgREST `pgrst.db_schemas`. No other migration, view, function, or test in this tree referenced these tables before this change. Existing `dflow` writers are untouched. DesignFlow backend grants remain a named successor obligation (`completion.json` `assumptions_resolved[4]`; `contract.json` `prohibited_actions[4]`).\n\n## Additive structure, FKs, successor obligations\n\nPurely additive: `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX`, `COMMENT ON TABLE`, `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `REVOKE`, one catalogue-reading `DO` block, `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` last (`:22`, `:218`). No `ALTER`/`DROP`/`RENAME` of any existing object, no DML, no row movement, no grant.\n\nIntra-`plm` FKs are present, including the composite self-FK. Cross-schema `dflow.users` FKs remain omitted with an accurate rationale (`:8-11`). Header count “two source integrity indexes and five FK child-side indexes” matches the seven `CREATE INDEX` statements. Column names, types, nullability, and defaults match the four-source cumulative shape, including nullable `actor_auth_user_id` and both derived actor defaults. `item_workflow_action_return_names_its_source` is present (`:108-112`). Column order on `item_workflow_action` still places `actor_identity_*` at positions 5–6; the header (`:6-8`), action COMMENT (`:127-128`), and completion require explicit mover column lists. Append-only is described as deferred (`:19-20`, `:128`).\n\n`SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` / `statement_timeout = '5min'` (`:23-24`) sit inside the transaction. Inline `REFERENCES` takes `ShareRowExclusiveLock` on live `plm.\"RFQItem\"` / `plm.\"RFQStep\"` for the apply; the 5s lock timeout aborts the whole transaction atomically. After apply, parent DELETE pays indexed probes. `ON DELETE CASCADE` on assignments (`:28`) mirrors dflow (`20260904143518:13-15`); empty today.\n\nParent FKs are VALID (empty children). dflow’s corresponding FKs were `NOT VALID`. That is the right choice for a declared final home, and it is a mover hazard: a dflow row whose `rfq_item_id` / step ids do not resolve in `plm` will be refused with `23503` on insert. It is not among the seven successor obligations in `completion.json`. Non-blocking here — nothing moves rows, and `prohibited_actions[4]` gates movement — but the mover session must name it.\n\n`-- derived-from: 20260901221310, 20260904143518, 20260905053422, 20260907121732` (`:3`) is one line, four 14-digit tokens, all four files present. `parse_declaration` accepts it.\n\nObject keys: `CREATE INDEX` emits `index plm.<name>` and `table plm.<table>` (`check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:502-521`). Seven index keys plus two tables match gen-4 `db_writes` and issue #3498’s claimed writes. Inline UNIQUEs and FKs add no extra claim keys.\n\n## Version ordering and evidence pair\n\nOn-disk `20260925*` files: `20260925061508`, `20260925193145`, `20260925222635`. No `20260925044029_*.sql`. Globs for `20260926*`, `2026093*`, `202610*` are empty, so `20260925222635` is the newest version in this tree. Guard B vs claimed origin/main newest `20260925193145` holds lexicographically (`222635` > `193145`). Duplicate-version guard has a single claimant. Guard B2 (live ledger) is explicitly unrun (`completion.json:38`) and remains a promotion gate.\n\nEvidence pair: only `.agent/work/3498/4/` exists (generations 1–3 retired). `resolveEvidencePair` therefore yields `current`, not `conflicted`. `completion.json` records `head_sha 05994ebf…` and `files_changed` of the four implementation files; the PR-head diff inventory is those four plus the two gen-4 evidence files. That is the required “only this pull request’s own two evidence files may follow `report.head_sha`” shape (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:62-71`; `acceptableEvidencePairs` for issue 3498 generation 4). `report.base_sha` equals the packet merge-base `5f91f2f6…`. Git ancestry of `05994ebf` relative to `a4b093b` was not computed in this profile; the packet inventory is consistent with that rule.\n\n`contract.json` `base_sha f6277830…` is the published immutable contract base; the completion report carries the current merge-base. That split is the required shape (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:40-50`). Gen-4 `prohibited_actions[3]` names `20260925222635` with supersession of `20260925044029`, matching the filename. Session HANDOFF notes still print the old version; those files are outside this diff. Claim #3502’s live GitHub body was not fetched.\n\n## Live proof token\n\n`.github/live-proofs/3498.sql:82` is `) as passed;` — lowercase `as`, matching house probes (`3043.sql`, `3174.sql`, `3009.sql`) and the case-sensitive gate `scripts/test_shared_db_live_proof.py:97` (`r\"\\bas passed\\b\"`). The JS lexer (`check-live-proof-probe.mjs:133`) is case-insensitive and would have accepted `AS passed`; the Python unittest would not. This is the correction relative to `d51c9633`.\n\nProbe shape: one `WITH`/`SELECT`, single trailing `;`, no write keyword outside literals (`INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`TRUNCATE` sit in privilege-name strings that `scanProbeSql` collapses). Runtime contract is one row, one boolean column named `passed`. Riding the probe in the implementation PR is what #3127 requires.\n\nThe live proof does not assert foreign keys. Issue #3498’s `live_assertion` names “intended foreign keys and seven claimed indexes.” Indexes are name-counted (`:70-81`); FKs are engine-asserted at apply and the self-FK is asserted in the migration verify block and the contract test. Residual completeness, not an apply-time hole.\n\n## Rollback and recovery\n\nMid-file failure sits in one transaction with `COMMIT` last; CI adds `--single-transaction`. Recovery after a successful apply is `DROP TABLE plm.item_workflow_action;` then `DROP TABLE plm.item_user_assignment;` — empty, unreferenced, which also removes the RI triggers from the RFQ parents. Original `dflow` capability is unchanged. `20260925044029` is permanently retired and never reusable.\n\n## Residual findings (none blocking)\n\n1. **Catalog COMMENT overstates deferral** (`:50-51`): it says lookup indexes on `item_user_assignment` are deferred, while `item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_idx` and `item_user_assignment_one_active` already ship. The remaining deferred lookup is `item_user_assignment_active_lookup`. Append-only deferral in that COMMENT is accurate.\n2. **Migration index assertions are name-only** (`:211`); the contract test deep-checks only the two partial uniques.\n3. **Default assertions in the migration are `LIKE` fragments** (`:183-184`, `:191-192`); the live proof’s full signature equality is the stronger check.\n4. **Live proof omits FK `pg_constraint` probes**, while the issue’s live assertion names intended foreign keys.\n5. **VALID parent FKs vs dflow `NOT VALID`** is an unrecorded mover hazard (see above).\n6. **Neither artifact asserts `relforcerowsecurity`.** With zero grants this is coherent; sibling omits `FORCE` too.\n7. **Session HANDOFF notes** still print claim #3502 as `20260925044029` with two tables only. Outside this diff; gen-4 contract is the in-tree authority.\n8. **Guard B2** unrun; promotion still owns live-ledger comparison.\n9. **`~` and `'{}'::jsonb`** still resolve through the inserting session’s `search_path`. Every function call is now `pg_catalog.`-qualified.\n\n## Limits\n\nNo shell: digest not recomputed; `check-sql.sh`, derivation parser, collision extractor, and contract tests not executed. Manifest §5: no tests were run for this packet. SQL and guards were hand-applied from source. GitHub-side claim #3502 body, supersession ref, and `refs/db-contracts/3498/4` object were not fetched; in-tree gen-4 files are consistent with the quoted sha256 `6c34ba0d…`. Preview/production ledgers were not queried. Migrations and RLS still need two independent exact-head reviews; this is one slot. Earlier recordings at other SHAs carry no authority here.\n\nThe change is additive, deny-by-default, atomic, version-clean in this tree, and it closes the three slot-2 blockers with indexes, probes, and a consistent reserved version. The live-proof spelling matches the required lowercase `as passed` token. Mandatory check 2 — function volatility\n**No defect, stated non-vacuously.** The change creates zero functions, procedures, triggers and views across all three SQL artifacts, so no `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` marker exists that could be wrong — and specifically nothing that reads a table carries `IMMUTABLE`. What I checked so the answer is not empty:\n- `clock_timestamp()` as a column DEFAULT (`:32`, `:35`, `:76`) is VOLATILE, legal in a DEFAULT, evaluated per row, and byte-identical to the sources (`20260901221310:10`, `:13`, `:36`). Keeping it over the STABLE `now()` used by the nearest `plm` sibling (`20260911214438:72-73`) is the **correct** call: a STABLE default would stamp every row of a bulk copy with one identical timestamp and destroy the `occurred_at` ordering the deferred `open_handoff_lookup` and the `order by … occurred_at desc, id desc` handoff resolution depend on. Consequence to record (F15): `effective_from` and `created_at` receive two independent evaluations and are not guaranteed equal — same as the source.\n- The two derived DEFAULTs (`:58-63`, `:64-70`) embed `pg_catalog.current_setting(text, boolean)` and `auth.jwt()`, both STABLE session readers. A DEFAULT carries no marker, so nothing is mislabelled; they are textually identical to `20260907121732:14-26`. Substituting a constant here — the earlier rounds' defect — would have been a behavioural break, and it is not present.\n- Every function call inside a stored CHECK is IMMUTABLE, as a stored CHECK requires: `pg_catalog.lower`, `pg_catalog.btrim` (`:37`, `:88`, `:98`), `pg_catalog.jsonb_typeof` (`:41`, `:90`), `->>`, `IS DISTINCT FROM`. Findings\n### F1 — High (blocking): the durable production proof omits the foreign keys its own assertion names, and asserts the seven indexes by name only\nIssue #3498's `live_assertion` — the text `build_proof` copies **verbatim** into the durable proof record (`shared_db_live_proof.py:377-395`) — requires the tables to exist \"with source-matching column types and defaults, **intended foreign keys** and seven claimed indexes, RLS enabled with zero policies, and no anon/authenticated/service_role table privileges\".\n`.github/live-proofs/3498.sql` proves: version applied (`:21-24`), `relkind`/`relrowsecurity` (`:25-34`), column counts (`:35-44`), full column-signature equality against `dflow` including default expressions (`:45-58`), zero policies (`:59-63`), the 3×7 privilege sweep (`:64-69`), and seven index **names** (`:70-81`, `to_regclass(...) IS NOT NULL` = 7). It contains **no `pg_constraint` reference at all** — I swept every committed probe for `pg_constraint` and there is not one. So none of the five FKs, and in particular neither `ON DELETE` semantic (CASCADE on `item_user_assignment.rfq_item_id`, RESTRICT on `item_workflow_action.rfq_item_id` and on the self-FK), is verified anywhere on production; and the seven indexes are verified as names, not as definitions.\nThis is not compensated by another gate. `production_catalog_verification.py` derives targets from the SQL (`CREATE_TABLE_RE:201`, `CREATE_INDEX_RE:236`, `ALTER_RELATION_RE:221` + `ROW_SECURITY_RE:232`, `GRANT_RE:252` + `GRANT_OBJECT_RE`/`GRANT_ROLES_RE`) — all five match this file's UPPERCASE statements after `strip_sql` lowercases, and the `\\s+` in `CREATE_INDEX_RE` spans the newline before `ON`, so all seven indexes are derived. But derivation yields existence/ownership, RLS state and privilege expectations only: there is **no FK derivation regex**, and exact `pg_get_indexdef` equality exists only in hand-authored contracts (`INDEXDEF_NORMALIZE:671`, `:691-693`, `CATEGORY_ORDERLIST_BRIDGE_COVERING_INDEX:4107-4132`), with no sidecar for `20260925222635`.\nWhy this is blocking rather than a note: the probe is hash-bound into the qualification manifest (`probe_sha256`, `qualification_bindings:262-291`) and re-derived by `--complete-outcome` from the committed bytes on main. Once the production apply records `result: passed` against that assertion text, the durable evidence for #3498 permanently certifies an FK verification that never happened. The fix is a handful of read-only lines in a file this PR owns, and it stays inside the probe shape gate (one statement, no write keyword, `as passed`):\n- add a `pg_constraint` assertion over the five FKs by `conrelid`/`confrelid`/`conname`/`contype='f'`/`convalidated`/`confdeltype` (`c` for the CASCADE, `r` for the two RESTRICTs);\n- replace the name count with `pg_get_indexdef` equality (or the `pg_index` + key-column form the sibling probes already use).\nSibling evidence that the strong form is house practice for probes: `.github/live-proofs/2357.sql:87-91` joins `pg_index`/`pg_class` and matches `pg_get_indexdef(i.indexrelid) like '%'||ic.key_pattern||'%'`; `.github/live-proofs/2506.sql:18-19` selects `i.indisvalid, pg_get_indexdef(c.oid)`. Ours is the weakest index assertion among the committed probes.\n### F2 — Medium-High: the gating CI test does not compare default expressions, so the defect class that took three rounds is unguarded before apply\n`supabase/tests/plm_item_assignment_action_homes_contract.sql` compares `plm` against `dflow` on `(attname, atttypid, atttypmod, attnotnull, atthasdef, attidentity)` in a symmetric `EXCEPT`/`UNION ALL`/`EXCEPT`. That is the right axis set for the disclosed ordinal divergence — order-independent by construction — but `atthasdef` proves only that a default *exists*, never what it says.\nMeanwhile the migration's own apply-time assertion is substring-only (`:177-194`): `pg_get_expr(...) LIKE '%request.designflow.actor_id%' AND ... LIKE '%supabase_auth%'`. An **inverted** CASE (`then 'supabase_auth' else 'designflow_jwt'`) satisfies both substrings and would silently reverse actor provenance on an append-only attribution table while passing the apply check.\nNet effect: the only exact comparison of the two `actor_identity_*` defaults is the production probe, i.e. **after** apply. One-line fix in the test this PR already ships: `LEFT JOIN pg_catalog.pg_attrdef` and add `pg_get_expr(d.adbin, d.adrelid)` to both arms of the `EXCEPT` tuple. I checked that this would pass rather than create a new red: no migration after the four declared bases touches either `dflow` table (the `alter table dflow.item_*` sweep returns only `20260904143518`, `20260905053422`, `20260907121732`), neither bootstrap file defines them, and both sides' expressions reference only `pg_catalog`/`auth` objects, so the deparses are identical.\nPositive control I verified while checking this: the test **fails closed** if either side is missing. Append-only deferral in the same COMMENT is accurate, as is `:127-128`.\n### F7 — Low: the privilege assertion does not prove the ACL is otherwise empty\nThe 3-role × 7-privilege sweep (`:166-172`, mirrored in the test and the probe) is the right shape and covers the operative role — new `plm` tables are born with `service_role=arwd` (`20260710135975:14`, narrowed by `20260810180000`, asserted from `pg_default_acl` at `20260905042713:205-222`), which is exactly what `:134-135` strips. Since there is no `FORCE`, the owner and any `BYPASSRLS` role are exempt and the REVOKE — not RLS — is the real barrier; `:130-131` says so in prose. A future `alter default privileges in schema plm grant … to <new role>` would not be caught. Cheap stronger form: `aclexplode(relacl)` with `grantee NOT IN (0, relowner)` counted at zero.\n### F8 — Low: LIKE patterns treat `_` as a wildcard\n`'%request.designflow.actor_id%'` (`:183-184`, `:191-192`) and `'%FOREIGN KEY (source_action_id, rfq_item_id)%'` (`:200`) each contain `_`, which in LIKE matches any single character, so the assertions are looser than they read. Harmless here; use equality or escape underscores if exactness is wanted (and see F2 for the stronger fix).\n### F9 — Low: the live proof is coupled to the continued existence and shape of the tables it exists to replace\n`:45-58` compares `plm` signatures against `dflow`. Once the wiring session legitimately diverges the two, or drops `dflow.item_*` after movement, this committed probe begins to fail — and because the runner binds the proof to the exact probe bytes, repairing it means editing the durable #3498 artifact and re-qualifying. Its failure mode is also unhelpful: with a `dflow` side absent, `jsonb_object_agg` over zero rows yields NULL, `NULL = NULL` yields NULL, the whole `AND` chain is NULL, and `require_passed` reports *\"probe did not return exactly one row with passed = true\"* (`shared_db_live_proof.py:61-66`) rather than naming the missing side. Name a successor obligation to retire the probe with the `dflow` tables.\n### F10 — Low: `db_reads` is declared but never exercised\n`contract.json` and `completion.json:19-22` declare reads of both `dflow` tables; the migration contains no `SELECT` from either (its only reads are `pg_catalog.*` at `:148`, `:156`, `:162`, `:179`, `:187`, `:195`). The derivation was a hand transcription, now backstopped by two machine comparisons — but those cover columns and (post-apply) defaults only, never the CHECK set, the FK set or the index set against the sources.\n### F11 — Low: the segregation doc still contradicts itself on the `plm` table count\nThis PR updates rows 24a/24b (`:152-153`, now accurate: \"Final `plm` home … Row movement, DesignFlow grants, and append-only wiring remain separate work\") and adds history row `:329` (\"Added their final `plm` structural homes under #3498. Source rows remain in `dflow` until separately governed movement and wiring\") — both close the earlier staleness finding. But §4.3's heading (`:112`) still reads *\"`plm` — PLM operational + config (72 tables)\"* while §3 (`:63`) now reads **74** \"(72 + 2 added 2026-09-24)\". The file is already in this PR's `allowed_paths`, so the one-token fix is in-lane.\n### F12 — Low (informational): residual unqualified resolution inside stored CHECKs\nEvery function call is now `pg_catalog.`-qualified, which closes the practical half of the earlier shadowing finding. The `~` operator (`:37`, `:88`) and the `'{}'::jsonb` casts (`:34`, `:75`) still resolve through the inserting session's `search_path`. Inherited shape from `20260901221310:7`, `:14`; negligible.\n### F13 — Informational: append-only is deferred, and now truthfully documented\n`:19-20` and `:128` state that triggers are deferred and the property is not yet enforced, so the catalogue no longer asserts something the schema lacks. The sources enforce it with `item_user_assignment_immutable_history` and `item_workflow_action_immutable` (`20260901221310:113-129`), and `20260905053422:31-36` explains that append-only is *why* \"handoff is closed\" is modelled as a child row rather than a flag on the parent. Must land before rows; recorded at `completion.json.assumptions_resolved[4]` and gated by `contract.json.prohibited_actions[4]`.\n### F14 — Informational: real but bounded impact on two live tables\nInline `REFERENCES` takes `ShareRowExclusiveLock` on the already-live `plm.\"RFQItem\"` and `plm.\"RFQStep\"` for the apply transaction, so writes to those parents block during the apply. It is bounded by `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` and `statement_timeout = '5min'` (`:23-24`) — `SET LOCAL` being a strictly better form than the sources' session-level `set` (`20260905053422:40-41`, `20260907121732:8-9`) because it cannot leak into the applier's session. After apply, `ON DELETE RESTRICT` adds a permanent, non-deferrable, index-served probe to the RFQItem DELETE path, and `ON DELETE CASCADE` adds a new cascade path into `item_user_assignment`. Both mirror `dflow` exactly (`20260904143518:13-23`), so this is intended parity, not a new hazard — but the mover session should know the cascade exists.\n### F15 — Informational: `effective_from` ≠ `created_at`\nTwo independent `clock_timestamp()` evaluations per row (`:32`, `:35`). Same as the source; never assume equality in the mover or in any reconciliation.\n## 7. Role, permission and security-boundary assessment\n- **Grants changed: none.** No `GRANT` appears in any of the three SQL artifacts.\n- **Revokes changed: two** (`:134-135`), `REVOKE ALL ON TABLE … FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role`. These are **not** no-ops: the only default privilege in `plm` is `service_role` (`20260710135975:14`, narrowed to `arwd`, asserted at `20260905042713:205-222`), so both tables are born with `service_role=arwd` and these statements remove it. `PUBLIC`, `anon` and `authenticated` held nothing. I swept every `alter default privileges` in `supabase/migrations/`: no grantee other than `service_role` is configured for `plm`, so the revoke list covers every role that could hold a privilege at creation.\n- **Net boundary:** only the owner (`postgres`, the migration role) can read or write either table. `plm` is not in prod `pgrst.db_schemas` (`docs/agents/references-and-runbooks.md:21`), so neither table is PostgREST-reachable in any role; the `anon`/`authenticated` halves are belt-and-braces and `service_role` is the operative one — which is now the tested half in all three artifacts.\n- **Posture is house convention and the rationale is documented:** `:130-135` matches the nearest `plm` sibling including its bare revoke with no compensating grant (`20260911214438:94-97`), and `:130-131` carries the explanatory comment earlier rounds asked for. This is not the #2662 defect remediated by `20260914155226` (zero-policy RLS **plus** grants); with no grants, deny-all is coherent and fail-closed.\n- **Sibling call paths: none exist.** Sweeps return only this PR's own three artifacts, the segregation doc and three stale HANDOFF rows. Nothing can inherit or bypass this posture; the `dflow` originals and their two SECURITY DEFINER writers (`20260901221310:338-350`) are untouched.\n- **No premature grants, no row movement:** confirmed — the file contains only `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX`, `COMMENT ON TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE … ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `REVOKE`, one catalogue-reading `DO` block and `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`. No `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`COPY`, no `GRANT`, no `ALTER`/`DROP`/`RENAME` of any existing object.\n- **Obligation created for the successor, correctly recorded:** the production writer role `designflow` (`20260907121732:41-46`) gets nothing here and needs an explicit grant before anyone but the owner can use these tables; named at `completion.json.assumptions_resolved[4]` and gated by `contract.json.prohibited_actions[4]`.\n## 8. Version, claim scope, immutability, evidence-pair tail\n- `-- derived-from: 20260901221310, 20260904143518, 20260905053422, 20260907121732` (`:3`) is four 14-digit comma-separated tokens; `parse_declaration` (`migration_derivation.py:175-213`) requires `VERSION_RE.fullmatch` per token, forbids mixing with `none`, and forbids self-reference — all satisfied, and all four base files exist on disk. Exactly one such line in the file. The prose-under-a-reserved-label class stays closed.\n- **Version ordering against current main holds in this tree.** `*222635*` matches exactly one file; `2026092[6-9]*`, `2026093*` and `20261*` are all empty; the newest other September versions present are `20260925193145` and `20260925061508`, both from the merged main baseline, and `…25222635` sorts after `…25193145`. So the duplicate-version guard (`check-sql.sh:158-166`) and Guard B (`:185-285`) pass. **Unverifiable here:** whether live `origin/main` has since gained a version above `20260925222635`, and Guard B2 against preview/production ledgers — which `check-sql.sh:485-486` skips with a WARNING when no ledger source is configured, and which `completion.json.checks[0].evidence` correctly does not claim.\n- **Object keys match the claim exactly.** Hand-tracing `dispatchObjectKeys` through the index rule (`check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:503-521`, which infers the schema from the `ON` target when the index name is unqualified and emits *both* `index` and `table` keys — \"an index is a write to its table\"), plus `CREATE TABLE`, `COMMENT ON TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE … ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and `REVOKE … ON TABLE` (whose `view` `relationGuess` half is deleted because the matching `CREATE TABLE` was noted), and with the `DO` body's literals collapsed: **exactly nine keys — the two tables and the seven indexes.** Identical to `contract.json.db_writes`, `completion.json.db_writes`, and issue #3498's `db-work-scope.writes`. Inline FKs and constraints contribute zero keys (no `references`/`constraint` pattern exists), so the five FKs cost nothing against the claim.\n- **Evidence pair is the only tail.** `completion.json:9` records `head_sha 05994ebf853fb1bf3d02981bee4f8911064d72e6` — the commit directly below `a4b093b2` — with `base_sha 5f91f2f6…` and `files_changed` naming exactly the four non-evidence files. That is the required shape (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:36-70`: `head_sha` an ancestor of the PR head, `files_changed` equal to the merge-base..`head_sha` diff, and only the contract's own two evidence files following). `contract.json.base_sha f6277830…` differing from the PR base is also the required shape, since the published contract is immutable and the current base is recorded by the completion report. Only `.agent/work/3498/4/` exists, so evidence resolution is unambiguous. Consequence to state plainly: **the recorded `check-sql.sh` exit 0 was measured at `05994eb`, not at the bytes under review** — though `a4b093b` is the evidence rebind, so no SQL byte differs. I verified the SQL independently rather than relying on it.\n- **No existing migration is modified**; `20260925222635_*.sql` is new, so `check-applied-migration-edit.mjs` has nothing to object to, and the retired `20260925044029` is permanently unreusable (`anti-collision-summary.md:31-36`).\n## 9. Rollback and recovery\n- **Partial failure mid-file:** everything sits in one transaction (`:22` … `:218`) with `COMMIT` last, and CI adds `--single-transaction` (`database-contract-tests.yml:341-344`), so a failure anywhere leaves neither table, neither COMMENT, no index, no RLS change and no revoke. No half-created pair is reachable. The inner `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` produce harmless warnings under the wrapper; nothing follows `:218`, so atomicity holds.\n- **Recovery after a successful apply:** drop the two tables (they are mutually independent; the self-FK dies with its table). Both are empty, referenced by nothing, and read by no view, function, publication, trigger, policy or test — the sweeps in §6/§7 prove there is no dependent. Dropping them also removes the four internal RI triggers from `plm.\"RFQItem\"` and `plm.\"RFQStep\"`, restoring those parents exactly.\n- **Original capability preserved:** no `dflow` object is altered, dropped or renamed; no function body is replaced; the `dflow.item_*` tables, their six indexes, their two immutability triggers, their grants and their two SECURITY DEFINER writers are untouched. `app.user_notification.workflow_action_id → dflow.item_workflow_action(id)` (`20260904143518:49-53`) is untouched and is a named successor re-point.\n- **Version rollback:** because `20260925044029` is permanently retired, a rollback-and-reissue needs a further governed supersession; ledger repair must not use `supabase migration repair --status reverted`.\n## 10. Test coverage\n`supabase/tests/plm_item_assignment_action_homes_contract.sql` is a real gate, not decoration: the runner globs rather than lists (`database-contract-tests.yml:29-31`, `:628`), wraps it `begin; \\ir …; rollback;` (`:679`) — compatible with the file's single `DO $test$` block and absence of transaction control — and any non-quarantined failure exits 1 (`:701-705`). I read `supabase/tests/ci-quarantine.txt` in full: **this file is not listed**, and the quarantine's own header forbids parking a test that found a real defect. It runs after both migration passes and after the bootstrap, so both `plm` and `dflow` exist by then.\nCoverage it provides: column counts, full plm↔dflow column-shape parity (order-independent), RLS state, zero policies, the 3×7 privilege matrix, the composite self-FK by `contype`/`confrelid`/`pg_get_constraintdef`, all seven index names, and `indisunique` + deparsed `indpred` for both partial uniques. Coverage it does **not** provide: default expressions (F2), the five non-unique indexes' key columns, the four parent FKs, the CHECK-constraint set, and any behavioural case — there is no negative test that a duplicate active assignment or a second return against one handoff is actually refused. Both `dflow` sources have behavioural contract tests; these homes have a catalogue one. Acceptable for empty, unreachable tables, but it is the reason F1–F3 matter: the catalogue is all anyone is checking.\n## 11. Successor obligations — accurate, with one omission\nI checked each recorded claim against source rather than accepting it. Header `:11-14` (\"two source integrity indexes and five FK child-side indexes ship … before any row movement\") counts correctly against `:44-48` and `:115-125`. The four deferred indexes at `:15-18` are exactly the four non-integrity source indexes (`20260901221310:21-24`, `:40-41`; `20260905053422:101-107`). The FK rationale at `:8-11` is factually right: the four genuinely cross-schema references are `user_id`, `assigned_by_user_id` (`20260901221310:8-9`), `actor_user_id` (`:30`) and `fallback_recipient_user_id` (`20260905053422:67-69`), all to `dflow.users`, and every intra-`plm` reference is present. `completion.json.assumptions_resolved[4]` names seven obligations (four lookup indexes, append-only enforcement, user FKs, DesignFlow grants, identity-sequence adjustment, explicit mover column list, notification FK re-point), and `contract.json.prohibited_actions[4]` gates row movement on them. Column-order divergence is disclosed at `:6-8` and `:127-128`, and the mover rule that follows from it (explicit column lists, never positional `SELECT *`) is recorded. **The one omission is F5** (VALID vs `NOT VALID`).\n## 12. Limits on this review\nNo shell, git or database: the sealed packet is absent (§0), the whole-source digest was not recomputed, no guard or test was executed, and all six guard conclusions above are hand-applied from the guard's own source. Unreachable GitHub-side facts: claim #3502's live body, `refs/db-contracts/3498/4`, `refs/db-claim-supersessions/3502-20260925044029`, live `origin/main`, and both ledgers — so \"version reserved\", \"no higher version on main\", \"the four declared bases are applied in the target ledger\" (required by `assert_derivation_bases` at promotion) and \"Guard B2 clean\" all remain **unverified, not passed**. The four ancestry/diff facts required by `agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs` were not computed. No behavioural fact was established against a database. `anti-collision-summary.md:61-62` requires two independent reviewers for migration-plus-RLS work; this is one slot at this exact head, and the two-slot sign-off recorded at `d51c9633` is a different head and carries no authority here.\n## 13. Assessment\nNothing in this change can damage the existing database. It is strictly additive — two empty tables, seven indexes on those tables, two COMMENTs, RLS enabled with zero policies, two revokes, one catalogue-reading `DO` block, `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` — with no existing object altered, dropped or renamed, no DML, no row movement and no grant. It is version-clean and newest in-tree, atomic with `COMMIT` last, bounded by `SET LOCAL` timeouts, deny-by-default with the operative `service_role` half actually asserted in three separate artifacts, and its nine object keys match the claim exactly. Rollback is a drop of two empty, unreferenced tables that also removes the RI triggers it added to the live RFQ parents, leaving the original `dflow` capability untouched.\nEvery blocking finding from the five prior rounds is closed, and I re-derived each from source rather than from the summaries: the lineage header parses; both actor-identity defaults are textually identical to `20260907121732:14-26`; the intra-`plm` FK set including the composite self-FK is present and gives `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` its purpose; `item_workflow_action_return_names_its_source` landed (`:108-112`, faithful to `20260905053422:185-191`); all five FK child probes are indexed; the privilege sweep covers the role the revoke acts on; `lock_timeout`/`statement_timeout` are set; every CHECK helper is qualified; the append-only COMMENT is truthful; the segregation rows and history are updated; and the one-token proof spelling now satisfies both the offline lexer and the case-sensitive repository unittest, with no sibling probe left in the same class. Mandatory checks 1 and 2 carry no defect.\nWhat stops me from signing off on my own judgement is mandatory check 3 applied to the two evidence artifacts, plus one governance confirmation.\nFirst, the durable production proof omits a named element of the assertion it certifies. #3498's `live_assertion` requires \"intended foreign keys and seven claimed indexes\"; `.github/live-proofs/3498.sql` contains no `pg_constraint` reference at all and asserts the seven indexes by name existence only. `build_proof` copies that assertion text verbatim into a hash-bound record that `--complete-outcome` re-derives, so after the production apply the permanent evidence for #3498 will state that FKs were verified when they never were, and no other gate covers it — `production_catalog_verification.py` derives no FK expectation from SQL, and its exact-`indexdef` contracts are hand-authored per object with no sidecar here. Committed probes `2357.sql:87-91` and `2506.sql:18-19` show the stronger index form is already house practice for this artifact type.\nSecond, the same name-only weakness is in the migration's own verify loop (`:202-213`), which a relation of any kind would satisfy — directly below the standard set by `20260925193145:540-575`, the newest migration on the merged main baseline, in the same `plm` schema under the same `$verify$` tag and the same cost guard, whose comment states the rule (\"each index must exist on the right table with the right key columns and predicate\").\nThird, the one gating artifact that runs before apply compares `atthasdef` but never the default expression, while the apply-time check is a substring LIKE that an inverted CASE would satisfy. Mistranscribed `actor_identity_*` defaults are the exact defect class that took three rounds of this PR, and after these two changes the only exact comparison of them happens post-apply, on production.\nNone of this requires the migration's SQL to be different: I would not change a line of the two `CREATE TABLE` statements, the seven index definitions, the constraint set, the access posture or the transaction shape. The corrections are confined to the two evidence artifacts this PR already owns (a `pg_constraint` assertion and `pg_get_indexdef` equality in the probe; `pg_get_expr(adbin, adrelid)` in the test's `EXCEPT` tuple; `relkind='i'` + `indrelid` + definition in the migration's index loop), plus four cheap accuracy items in files already in-lane (F5's mover hazard in the header and segregation rows, F6's COMMENT wording, F11's stale \"(72 tables)\" heading, F7's ACL/`relforcerowsecurity` assertion). They are cheapest now, because after merge the migration's bytes are immutable and the proof is hash-bound.\nSeparately and not author-actionable: the orchestrator must confirm claim #3502's live body and the supersession ref reserve `20260925222635` with all nine objects before Guarded Merge, and correct the three HANDOFF ledger rows and the PR body, which still pin `20260925044029` (F4). Tracked follow-ups that do not require these bytes to change and should be named in a durable handoff rather than only in `completion.json`: the four lookup indexes before any row insert, append-only triggers, `dflow.users` FKs and `designflow` grants, identity `setval` with `OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE`, explicit-column-list mover rules, the `app.user_notification` re-point, the VALID-vs-`NOT VALID` rejection hazard, and retirement of the live proof alongside the `dflow` tables.\nI made no edits, ran no state-changing tool, touched no database, merged nothing, deployed nothing, and revealed no secret.\nVERDICT: REVISE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n# Governed structural review — popcre/shared-db PR #3510, issue #3498, head `c20efc295fc9c9f345f783150c8893d7b1708f55`\n\nProvisional read (stated before the detail, per the packet): this head is strictly additive structure for two empty `plm` homes; the three depth gaps the prior slot-2 round raised at `a4b093b2` (foreign keys absent from durable proof, index names-only assertions, no in-CI default-expression equality) are addressed in the bytes I read; what remains is one unverified resolution risk in the catalogue key-name comparison that would fail the apply itself, plus a set of in-lane disclosure and record items.\n\n## Coverage statement\n\nOpened and read in full this session: `supabase/migrations/20260925222635_plm_item_user_assignment_and_workflow_action.sql` (lines 1–140 and 140–260), `supabase/tests/plm_item_assignment_action_homes_contract.sql` (1–126), `.github/live-proofs/3498.sql` (1–128), `supabase/tests/ci-quarantine.txt` (1–79).\n\nSource lineage opened: `supabase/migrations/20260901221310_designflow_item_assignment_action_history.sql:1-60`, `supabase/migrations/20260904143518_canonical_designflow_workflow_contract.sql:1-60`, `supabase/migrations/20260905053422_workflow_action_handoff_integrity.sql:1-200`, `supabase/migrations/20260907121732_designflow_trusted_backend_actor.sql:1-40`.\n\nReferents and precedent opened: `supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:786-796`, `:914-924`, `:2285`, `:2288`; `supabase/tests/dam_order_list_count_index_contracts.sql:20-45`; `scripts/test_shared_db_live_proof.py:60-140`; `.github/live-proofs/2863.sql:40-63`; `.github/live-proofs/3174.sql:1-20`; `scripts/check-migration-verify-cost.mjs:24-25`, `:225-279`.\n\nRepo-wide greps run: `plm.item_user_assignment|plm.item_workflow_action`; `20260925222635|20260925193145`; `2026092[6-9][0-9]{4}`; `indkey`; `int2vector|oidvector`; `alter default privileges in schema plm`; `grant .*on table plm\\.`; `unnest|indkey|name\\[\\]` under `.agent`; segregation-doc table counts.\n\nNot run / not reachable: no shell, git history or database in this profile. `bash scripts/check-sql.sh`, `python3 -m unittest scripts.test_shared_db_live_proof`, the CI contract run, guard suites and the whole-source digest `6e344731208935304a6b6129157842a31e03d4b29352a9c1d38a4c9241850d2b` were not executed or recomputed; the packet states no tests were run (MANIFEST §5). Claim #3502's live issue body, `refs/db-contracts/3498/5` and the supersession ref are GitHub-side. My `list_dir` of `supabase/migrations` was truncated before the end of the directory, so filename-level proof that no version sorts after `20260925222635` is not complete from this profile.\n\n## Findings\n\n### Mandatory check 1 — index usage: no defect, one residual access-path gap, all disclosed\n\nEvery predicate this change *creates* has a serving index. The change issues no queries; the predicates it installs are the four parent-side RI probes plus the self-FK child probe:\n\n| Predicate installed by the migration | Serving index |\n|---|---|\n| `ON DELETE CASCADE` probe from live `plm.\"RFQItem\"` into `rfq_item_id` (`…222635…sql:30`) | `item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_idx` (`:46-47`) |\n| `ON DELETE RESTRICT` probe from `plm.\"RFQItem\"` (`:57`) | `item_workflow_action_rfq_item_id_idx` (`:117-118`) |\n| `plm.\"RFQStep\"` probe on `prior_step_id` (`:73`) | `item_workflow_action_prior_step_id_idx` (`:119-120`) |\n| `plm.\"RFQStep\"` probe on `new_step_id` (`:74`) | `item_workflow_action_new_step_id_idx` (`:121-122`) |\n| self-FK child `(source_action_id, rfq_item_id)` (`:84-87`) | `item_workflow_action_source_action_rfq_item_idx` (`:123-124`), same column order |\n| referenced side of that self-FK | `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` (`:83`) |\n\nThe \"index that exists but cannot be used as written\" class is closed: `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` (`:83`) is the referent of the composite self-FK at `:84-87`, which is exactly why the pair exists in the source (`20260905053422:56-65`, whose comment explains the composite reference exists so a return can only answer a handoff on the same RFQ item). I checked the three overlaps a reviewer is most likely to call redundant and each holds: `item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_idx` is required beside the partial unique `one_active` (`:48-50`) because the CASCADE probe must see closed rows; `item_workflow_action_source_action_rfq_item_idx` is required beside the partial unique `one_return_per_source` (`:125-127`) because a partial index needs the predicate proved; and `item_workflow_action_rfq_item_id_idx` is not subsumed by `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` because `rfq_item_id` is the non-leading column.\n\nThe four deferred lookup indexes are named individually at `:17-20` (`item_user_assignment_active_lookup`, `item_workflow_action_item_time`, `item_workflow_action_open_handoff_lookup`, `item_workflow_action_admin_review`) and are a source-backed non-applicable today: a repo-wide grep for both table names returns only this migration, its contract test, its live proof, the segregation doc, three HANDOFF ledger rows and the `.agent` evidence pair — **no view, function, trigger, policy, publication or other test reads either table, and no FK from any other table points at them.** `item_user_assignment_active_lookup` is additionally largely served already by the shipped `one_active` (same `(rfq_item_id, function_key)` leading columns, same `WHERE effective_to IS NULL`, `user_id` in the key). The other three are ordering/partial-predicate indexes that must land before a writer is repointed; the contract gates movement on that (`…3498/5/contract.json` `prohibited_actions[4]`).\n\n### Mandatory check 2 — function volatility: no defect, stated non-vacuously\n\nAll 260 lines read; the artifact creates **zero** functions, procedures, triggers and views — only `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE INDEX`/`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX`, `COMMENT ON TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE … ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `REVOKE`, one catalogue-reading `DO` block and `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`. So no `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` marker exists that could be wrong, and nothing that reads a table carries `IMMUTABLE`. What I checked so the answer is not empty:\n\n- `clock_timestamp()` as a column DEFAULT (`:34`, `:37`, `:78`) is VOLATILE, legal in a DEFAULT, evaluated per row, and byte-matches the sources (`20260901221310:9`, `:12`, `:36`). This is the correct choice: a STABLE `now()` would stamp every row of a bulk copy with one timestamp and destroy the `occurred_at` ordering the deferred handoff-resolution path depends on. Consequence to record: `effective_from` (`:34`) and `created_at` (`:37`) receive two independent evaluations and are **not** guaranteed equal — same as the source.\n- The two derived DEFAULTs (`:60-65`, `:66-72`) embed `pg_catalog.current_setting(text, boolean)` and `auth.jwt()`, both STABLE session readers, inside a DEFAULT (which carries no marker) — correct, and semantically identical to `20260907121732:14-26`. This closes the behavioural break of the earlier rounds: `dflow.record_item_workflow_action`'s INSERT list omits both columns, so the defaults *are* the provenance mechanism, and the copied `item_workflow_action_actor_provenance` CHECK (`:103-109`) is now satisfiable on the backend path.\n- Every CHECK helper is `pg_catalog.`-qualified (`:39`, `:43`, `:90`, `:92`, `:100`) and IMMUTABLE, as a stored CHECK requires. I record for the next round that the earlier \"hostile `search_path` could shadow the CHECK helpers on insert\" mechanism is not how PostgreSQL evaluates a stored CHECK: a CHECK expression is stored as a parsed node tree with resolved function OIDs at DDL time (`pg_constraint.conbin`), so the qualification here is harmless defensive style rather than a correctness fix. The residual unqualified items are the `~` operator (`:39`, `:90`) and the `'{}'::jsonb` literals (`:36`, `:77`), resolved at DDL time too. Negligible, recorded so it is not re-raised as a defect.\n- The omitted append-only trigger functions (`20260901221310` immutability triggers, cited by the header at `:21-22` and the COMMENT at `:130`) correctly default to VOLATILE in the source; their absence is the deferred obligation below, not a volatility defect. If added later they must stay VOLATILE.\n\n### Mandatory check 3 — exact object checks: substantially met, with one unverified resolution risk in the vehicle\n\nWhat is asserted exactly, in all three artifacts:\n\n- Dependencies are engine-asserted with schema, relation **and** column: `REFERENCES plm.\"RFQItem\"(\"rfqItem_id\")` (`:30`, `:57`), `REFERENCES plm.\"RFQStep\"(\"RFQStep_id\")` (`:73`, `:74`), self-reference `REFERENCES plm.item_workflow_action(id, rfq_item_id)` (`:86`). All fail the apply if schema, relation or named column is wrong. I confirmed both targets exist with exactly those columns and matching primary keys: `ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:791-792` (`\"rfqItem_id\" integer GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY NOT NULL`), `:919-920` (`\"RFQStep_id\" integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY NOT NULL`), PKs at `:2285` (`RFQItem_pkey`) and `:2288` (`RFQStep_pkey`).\n- Post-create, catalogue-only: `to_regclass` + `relkind = 'r'` + `relrowsecurity` (`:157-163`), exact column counts 9 and 16 (`:148-156`), zero `pg_policies` for the exact `(schemaname, tablename)` pair (`:164-169`), the 3-role × 7-privilege `has_table_privilege` sweep (`:170-176`), the five FKs by `conname` + `conrelid` + `confrelid` + `contype='f'` + `convalidated` + `confdeltype` + ordered child/parent key names (`:197-223`), and all seven claimed indexes by schema, relation kind, access method, table, uniqueness, validity/readiness/liveness, key-column order and deparsed partial predicate (`:224-256`). Collision fails closed (`:28`, `:55` — plain `CREATE TABLE`, no `IF NOT EXISTS`).\n- The CI test goes past names for the two integrity invariants: `indisunique` plus deparsed `indpred` (`supabase/tests/plm_item_assignment_action_homes_contract.sql:92-124`), and it is **not** on the quarantine list (`supabase/tests/ci-quarantine.txt`, all 79 lines read — the file is absent), so a failure of it fails the job.\n\nI verified the arithmetic these assertions rest on rather than trusting it. Column counts: `item_user_assignment` has 9 (`:29-37`); `item_workflow_action` has 16 (`:56-82`). The `= 11` index total is correct: 3 on the assignment table (PK + `rfq_item_id_idx` + `one_active`) plus 8 on the action table (PK + two inline UNIQUE constraints at `:83` and `:88` + five `CREATE INDEX`) — which also matches the exception message's \"four primary/constraint indexes\". The `trim(both '()' from pg_get_expr(indpred, …))` normalization at `:250` is sound for exactly these two predicates: it yields `effective_to IS NULL` and `source_action_id IS NOT NULL`, and `coalesce(…, '')` gives `''` for the five non-partial indexes. The ordered key-name arrays are compared as `text[]` on both sides at all six sites (`:208-217`, `:245-249`; test `:76-85`, `:113-117`; proof `:81-90`, `:117-121`) — the `name[]` vs `text[]` defect the completion note says the prior head hit is addressed.\n\n**F1 (Medium-High, must be executably confirmed before merge): the index key-column comparison calls `unnest(i.indkey)` without the `::smallint[]` cast that every comparable committed probe in this repository uses.** `…222635…sql:246`, `supabase/tests/plm_item_assignment_action_homes_contract.sql:114`, `.github/live-proofs/3498.sql:118`. `pg_index.indkey` is `int2vector`, not an array type; every other index-key probe in this repository casts it explicitly — `supabase/tests/dam_order_list_count_index_contracts.sql:31` and `:61` (`unnest(i.indkey::smallint[]) with ordinality`), `supabase/tests/opa_property_character_landing_contracts.sql:144` (`from unnest(i.indkey::smallint[]) u(attnum)`), and the in-repo catalogue query at `docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260904T212459Z/queries.md:129` (`(x.indkey::smallint[])[0:…]`). The migration's copy is inside the `$verify$` block, so if the call does not resolve, the **apply itself** fails, not merely a test. I could not execute it (no shell; the packet records no test run), so I do not assert that it fails — but the completion note's account of the prior CI failure (\"`name[]` versus `text[]` catalogue comparison\", `.agent/work/3498/5/completion.json:59`) only evidences an element-type mismatch on the array comparison, which does not prove the `unnest` call resolved first. This is the same artifact class that has already failed ephemeral CI once at a prior head, the fix is one token per site, and after merge the migration's bytes become immutable. This is the item that decides my verdict.\n\n**F2 (Low-Medium): the migration's own default-expression assertion is a substring test that an inverted CASE would satisfy.** `…222635…sql:186-187` requires `pg_get_expr(...) LIKE '%request.designflow.actor_id%'` AND `LIKE '%supabase_auth%'`; `:194-195` likewise for the email. An inverted CASE (`then 'supabase_auth' else 'designflow_jwt'`) satisfies both substrings and would silently reverse provenance on an append-only attribution table while passing the apply-time check. This is materially improved over prior rounds because the CI test now compares **full `pg_get_expr` equality** against `dflow` across a symmetric `EXCEPT` (`plm_item_assignment_action_homes_contract.sql:19-47`) and the durable proof compares full signatures (`3498.sql:2-19`, `:45-58`), so the class is covered by two other artifacts. The residual is that the apply-time assertion, which is the one that fails closed on production, is the weakest of the three. Also note the `_` wildcards in those LIKE patterns and in nothing else — the FK assertion at `:203-217` no longer uses a LIKE fragment, which is an improvement.\n\n**F3 (Low): the item_user_assignment table COMMENT misstates the deferral it carries.** `…222635…sql:53` reads \"Four lookup-only indexes and append-only enforcement are deferred to the wiring session\" on the table for which `:46-50` already ships two indexes and only one lookup index (`item_user_assignment_active_lookup`) is deferred. The table COMMENT is the durable, byte-immutable sentence a future reader trusts; the header at `:13-20` is precise about the split. The action table's COMMENT (`:130`) is accurate.\n\n### Mandatory-adjacent findings\n\n**F4 (Medium, unrecorded interaction): `ON DELETE CASCADE` into an append-only history table is created now, while the append-only trigger that is supposed to protect it is deferred.** `…222635…sql:30` declares `rfq_item_id … REFERENCES plm.\"RFQItem\"(\"rfqItem_id\") ON DELETE CASCADE`, mirroring `20260901221310:5`, and the source is guarded by a `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` immutability trigger per the header's own disclosure at `:21-22`. The two properties interact on a live parent: when the deferred trigger lands, a cascade delete propagating from `plm.\"RFQItem\"` is itself a DELETE on the child, so assignment history either makes `DELETE FROM plm.\"RFQItem\"` fail for items that have history, or the append-only property is porous through the cascade path. I did not read `20260901221310:113-129` in this session, so I state the dflow side as asserted by the source lineage rather than verified by me. Either way the interaction must be decided in the wiring session, and it belongs with the \"append-only enforcement\" obligation now recorded only in `.agent` evidence and the segregation doc.\n\n**F5 (Medium, governance; orchestrator action, not a diff defect). Every readable repo-side claim record still pins the superseded version and the two-object scope.** `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T1226Z-edge-dev-mimo-orch-successor-3496.md:119`, `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T1750Z-edge-dev-mimo-orch-3535-fresh-session.md:111` and `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T2305Z-edge-dev-mimo-orch-3552-wrapup.md:104` all read `| #3502 | #3498 | 20260925044029 | ` with only `table plm.item_user_assignment`, `table plm.item_workflow_action`; the migration and both evidence files name `20260925222635` with nine objects (`.agent/work/3498/5/contract.json:14`, `:34-42`, `:48`). Repo policy makes the claim issue body authoritative rather than these notes, and I cannot read that body from this checkout, so this is a named missing-evidence item rather than a proven defect: the orchestrator must confirm claim #3502's live `db-claim` block reserves `20260925222635` with all nine objects and that the supersession ref exists, then correct the three ledger rows and the PR body. Version ordering inside this tree is otherwise clean: `20260925222635` is the only file with that version (grep returns it only as this migration's filename plus the evidence, proof and `.agent` references), and `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T2305Z-…:20` records main's maximum as `20260925193145`, corroborated by `.agent/work/2357/13/completion.json:7` — consistent with `.agent/work/3498/5/contract.json:60`.\n\n**F6 (Medium, tracked successor obligation, correctly gated). Integrity and access properties of a declared \"final home\" are still absent, though now disclosed rather than asserted.** Append-only is stated as not yet enforced (`:21-22`, `:53`, `:130`); the four lookup indexes are deferred (`:17-20`); the cross-schema `dflow.users` FKs are omitted with a rationale at `:8-10` that I confirmed is factually right — the item and step references were re-pointed into `plm` by `20260904143518:10-28`, so only `user_id`, `assigned_by_user_id` (`20260901221310:7-8`), `actor_user_id` (`:29`) and `fallback_recipient_user_id` (`20260905053422:69-70`) genuinely point at `dflow.users`. Rows cannot move until a successor owns these (`contract.json` `prohibited_actions[4]`), and dropping the tables is complete recovery. I would record the honest reason for deferring the user FKs as the one the header gives is weaker than the real one: an FK to `dflow.users` installs an RI trigger on a live table outside this claim, not merely \"coupling\".\n\n**F7 (Medium, access boundary). The REVOKE removes a live inherited privilege and no grant replaces it; the durable assertion does not cover the whole ACL.** `…222635…sql:137-138` revokes ALL from `PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role`, and I verified the operative default privilege it strips exists: `supabase/migrations/20260710135975_reconcile_service_role_grants.sql:14` sets `alter default privileges in schema plm grant all on tables to service_role`, corroborated by the comment references in `20260810180000_plm_default_privilege_hole_and_pg17_maintain_revokes.sql:42`. So these are not no-ops; a new `plm` table is born with `service_role` holding rights and these statements remove them. That is deliberate and now documented (`:132-134`), and it is coherent: `postgres` owns the tables, no policy exists, so only the owner can read or write. Two gaps in the *assertion* rather than the posture: nothing asserts `relforcerowsecurity` (so the \"RLS is on\" claim does not state the owner/`BYPASSRLS` exemption), and nothing asserts the ACL is otherwise empty (a future `alter default privileges … to <new role>` would not be caught). The privilege matrix (`:170-176`, test `:58-62`, proof `:64-69`) does correctly sweep `service_role`, which was the vacuous-probe defect of the earlier round — that fix is real and it is the role the revoke actually acts on. Obligation correctly recorded: the production writer role gets nothing here and needs a successor grant.\n\n**F8 (Low). Nothing in the migration asserts the shape it claims for defaults with equality; only distinctness is inferred.** Covered by F2. Related: the verify block asserts the two derived defaults by substring, and the CI test's full-expression comparison runs only in CI, not on the production apply path.\n\n**F9 (Low, evidence hygiene).** `.agent/work/3498/5/completion.json:9` records `head_sha 12fa2bf770fc1b2de802d05cabca186e4b44cb2a`, one commit below the reviewed head `c20efc29…` — the required evidence-pair shape, but it means the recorded `check-sql.sh` exit 0 and the 28-test `scripts.test_shared_db_live_proof` run were measured one commit earlier. `.agent/work/3498/5/contract.json:8` carries `base_sha 13d0d888…`, which equals this packet's base, so that is consistent. The third recorded check is a rerunnable command with an exit code, so the \"prose in the command field\" defect of earlier rounds is gone.\n\n**F10 (Low, durable-artifact lifecycle). The live proof is coupled to the continued existence and shape of the `dflow` landing tables it exists to replace.** `.github/live-proofs/3498.sql:2-19`, `:45-58` compares `plm` signatures against `dflow`. Once the wiring session legitimately diverges the two, or drops `dflow.item_*` after movement, the committed probe begins to fail, and because the runner binds the proof to the exact probe bytes the repair means editing a durable artifact. Its failure mode is also unhelpful: with the `dflow` side absent, the aggregate over zero rows compared to a populated one yields a boolean false rather than naming the missing side. Worth one line in the file and a named successor obligation to retire it alongside the `dflow` tables. I confirmed the proof's own shape requirements are met: one statement, single trailing `;` at `:128`, lowercase `as passed`, no write keyword outside string literals — matching `scripts/test_shared_db_live_proof.py:92-98` exactly.\n\n**F11 (Low). Identity sequences restart at 1** (`:29`, `:56`), while the `dflow` ids have been advancing since September 2026; the mover needs `OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE` plus `setval` past `max(id)`. This is recorded in the `.agent` completion evidence and generically in the segregation doc, but not in the migration header, which is the durable byte-immutable record. Related: `app.user_notification.workflow_action_id` still points at `dflow.item_workflow_action(id)` (`20260904143518:49-53`) and is untouched — correctly out of this change's scope, but it needs a named re-point.\n\n**F12 (Low). No `relforcerowsecurity` and no sequence/column-comment parity assertions,** and the seven source `COMMENT ON COLUMN` statements are not reproduced. The header's parity claim at `:6-8` is now correctly scoped to \"types, nullability, defaults\" and does not claim comment or constraint-set parity, so this is a completeness note rather than a false claim.\n\n## What is right\n\nStrictly additive: two empty tables, seven indexes on those tables, two table COMMENTs, RLS enabled with zero policies, two revokes, one catalogue-reading `DO` block, `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` (`:24`, `:260`) with `COMMIT` last — no `ALTER`/`DROP`/`RENAME` of any existing object, no DML, no row movement, no grant. The column set, types, nullability, defaults and identity shape all match the four-source cumulative shape, including nullable `actor_auth_user_id` (`:59` vs `20260907121732:13`) and the six CHECKs including `item_workflow_action_return_names_its_source` (`:110-114` vs `20260905053422:187-191`). Lineage is machine-parseable: `:3` names four 14-digit versions, all four present on disk. Independent Verification of Generation-6 Targeted Changes\n\n##### A. Explicit `pg_index.indkey::smallint[]` Casts\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260925222635_plm_item_user_assignment_and_workflow_action.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-b80b79f32a16-codex-governed-pr3510-slot1-bde29aac-5b453c1ff79e/supabase/migrations/20260925222635_plm_item_user_assignment_and_workflow_action.sql#L249), [`supabase/tests/plm_item_assignment_action_homes_contract.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-b80b79f32a16-codex-governed-pr3510-slot1-bde29aac-5b453c1ff79e/supabase/tests/plm_item_assignment_action_homes_contract.sql#L114), and [`.github/live-proofs/3498.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-b80b79f32a16-codex-governed-pr3510-slot1-bde29aac-5b453c1ff79e/.github/live-proofs/3498.sql#L120), `unnest(i.indkey::smallint[]) WITH ORDINALITY AS k(attnum, ordinal)` is now explicitly cast.\n- PostgreSQL catalog column `pg_index.indkey` is of type `int2vector`. While `pg_constraint.conkey` is native `smallint[]`, `int2vector` requires array unnesting semantics. The explicit cast `i.indkey::smallint[]` guarantees standard 1-D array unnesting across engine versions, ordering column names deterministically by `k.ordinal` into `text[]` before comparison against `expected.key_names`. All three files share the exact same cast and ordinal join structure.\n\n##### B. Exact Actor-Default Equality at Apply\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260925222635_plm_item_user_assignment_and_workflow_action.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-b80b79f32a16-codex-governed-pr3510-slot1-bde29aac-5b453c1ff79e/supabase/migrations/20260925222635_plm_item_user_assignment_and_workflow_action.sql#L186-L199), the catalog verification block verifies:\n  `pg_catalog.pg_get_expr(dd.adbin, dd.adrelid) = pg_catalog.pg_get_expr(sd.adbin, sd.adrelid)`\n  for both `actor_identity_source` and `actor_identity_email` against live `dflow.item_workflow_action`.\n- The column default expressions defined in lines 67–79 match source migration `20260907121732_designflow_trusted_backend_actor.sql:14-26` verbatim (dynamic session derivation via `current_setting('request.designflow.actor_id', true)` and `auth.jwt() ->> 'email'`). The assertion enforces exact string equality of the deparsed expression, preventing literal degradation.\n\n##### C. Five Foreign Key Semantics and Validation\n- Five intra-schema foreign keys are installed and verified in [`supabase/migrations/20260925222635_plm_item_user_assignment_and_workflow_action.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-b80b79f32a16-codex-governed-pr3510-slot1-bde29aac-5b453c1ff79e/supabase/migrations/20260925222635_plm_item_user_assignment_and_workflow_action.sql#L37-L94) and tested in CI/live proofs:\n  1. `item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_fkey`: `plm.item_user_assignment(rfq_item_id) REFERENCES plm.\"RFQItem\"(\"rfqItem_id\") ON DELETE CASCADE` (`confdeltype = 'c'`).\n  2. `item_workflow_action_rfq_item_id_fkey`: `plm.item_workflow_action(rfq_item_id) REFERENCES plm.\"RFQItem\"(\"rfqItem_id\") ON DELETE RESTRICT` (`confdeltype = 'r'`).\n  3. `item_workflow_action_prior_step_id_fkey`: `plm.item_workflow_action(prior_step_id) REFERENCES plm.\"RFQStep\"(\"RFQStep_id\")` (`confdeltype = 'a'`, NO ACTION).\n  4. `item_workflow_action_new_step_id_fkey`: `plm.item_workflow_action(new_step_id) REFERENCES plm.\"RFQStep\"(\"RFQStep_id\")` (`confdeltype = 'a'`, NO ACTION).\n  5. `item_workflow_action_source_action_id_fkey`: `plm.item_workflow_action(source_action_id, rfq_item_id) REFERENCES plm.item_workflow_action(id, rfq_item_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` (`confdeltype = 'r'`).\n- All 5 FKs are verified with `convalidated = true`. Total foreign key count on both tables is strictly asserted to equal 5.\n\n##### D. Seven Claimed Indexes and Total Index Count of 11\n- Seven non-primary index definitions are declared and asserted across migration lines 228–255, test lines 93–120, and live proof lines 99–125:\n  1. `item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_idx` (`rfq_item_id`)\n  2. `item_user_assignment_one_active` UNIQUE (`rfq_item_id`, `function_key`, `user_id`) `WHERE effective_to IS NULL`\n  3. `item_workflow_action_rfq_item_id_idx` (`rfq_item_id`)\n  4. `item_workflow_action_prior_step_id_idx` (`prior_step_id`)\n  5. `item_workflow_action_new_step_id_idx` (`new_step_id`)\n  6. `item_workflow_action_source_action_rfq_item_idx` (`source_action_id`, `rfq_item_id`)\n  7. `item_workflow_action_one_return_per_source` UNIQUE (`source_action_id`) `WHERE source_action_id IS NOT NULL`\n- Total index count across both relations in `pg_index` is asserted to equal exactly 11:\n  - `plm.item_user_assignment` (3 indexes): PK `item_user_assignment_pkey`, `item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_idx`, and unique partial `item_user_assignment_one_active`.\n  - `plm.item_workflow_action` (8 indexes): PK `item_workflow_action_pkey`, unique constraint `item_workflow_action_id_rfq_item_key`, unique constraint `item_workflow_action_correlation_key_key`, child FK indexes on `rfq_item_id`, `prior_step_id`, `new_step_id`, composite child index on `(source_action_id, rfq_item_id)`, and unique partial `item_workflow_action_one_return_per_source`.\n\n##### E. Additive and Deny-by-Default Boundary\n- The migration only creates new relations and indexes in schema `plm`. No pre-existing table or index is modified, renamed, or dropped.\n- Both tables enable row-level security (`relrowsecurity = true`) with zero policies in `pg_policies`.\n- Explicit `REVOKE ALL ON TABLE ... FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role` removes default grants.\n- The boundary is verified via `has_table_privilege` across `anon`, `authenticated`, and `service_role` for all seven table privilege types (`SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `TRUNCATE`, `REFERENCES`, `TRIGGER`).\n\n##### G. Absence of Row Movement and Role Grants\n- The migration executes no DML (`INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`).\n- No `GRANT` statement is issued. Application row movement and role access are reserved for the subsequent DesignFlow cutover.\n\n##### H. Safe Version Ordering and Lineage\n- Migration timestamp `20260925222635` sorts strictly after the newest migration on `main` (`20260925193145`).\n- The `-- derived-from:` header lists four 14-digit timestamps (`20260901221310, 20260904143518, 20260905053422, 20260907121732`), containing no prose and resolving cleanly through the derivation parser.\n\n##### I.
