Mandatory check 1 — index usage\n\nEvery predicate this change *creates* has a serving index. The change issues no queries; the predicates it installs are the referential-integrity probes PostgreSQL attaches to the four live parents plus the self-reference:\n\n| Predicate installed | Serving index |\n|---|---|\n| `ON DELETE CASCADE` probe from `plm.\"RFQItem\"` into `rfq_item_id` (`20260925222635...:37`) | `item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_idx` (`:53-54`) |\n| `ON DELETE RESTRICT` probe from `plm.\"RFQItem\"` (`:64`) | `item_workflow_action_rfq_item_id_idx` (`:124-125`) |\n| `plm.\"RFQStep\"` probe on `prior_step_id` (`:80`) | `item_workflow_action_prior_step_id_idx` (`:126-127`) |\n| `plm.\"RFQStep\"` probe on `new_step_id` (`:81`) | `item_workflow_action_new_step_id_idx` (`:128-129`) |\n| Composite self-FK child key `(source_action_id, rfq_item_id)` (`:91-94`) | `item_workflow_action_source_action_rfq_item_idx` (`:130-131`), same column order |\n| Referenced side of that self-FK | `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` (`:90`) |\n| Correlation idempotency equality | `UNIQUE (correlation_key)` (`:95`) |\n| `id` lookups | both primary keys (`:36`, `:63`) |\n\nThe \"index that exists but cannot be used as written\" class is closed: `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` (`:90`) is the referent of the composite self-FK (`:91-94`), exactly as in the source (`20260905053422:56-65`), so it is used as written rather than being dead weight.\n\nLoose-overlap assumptions I tested and rejected as redundancy claims, since these are the ones most often raised wrongly: `item_user_assignment_rfq_item_id_idx` is required beside the partial unique `one_active` (`:55-57`) because the cascade probe must see closed rows and a partial index cannot; `item_workflow_action_source_action_rfq_item_idx` is required beside the partial unique `one_return_per_source` (`:132-134`) because the RI probe is two-column and the unique is partial; `item_workflow_action_rfq_item_id_idx` is not subsumed by `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` because `rfq_item_id` is the non-leading column and there is no skip-scan.\n\nBoth integrity predicates are byte-faithful: `one_active (rfq_item_id, function_key, user_id) WHERE effective_to IS NULL` matches `20260901221310:17-19`; `one_return_per_source (source_action_id) WHERE source_action_id IS NOT NULL` matches `20260905053422:96-98`.\n\nThe four deferred lookup indexes are named individually (`:15-21`) and are a source-backed non-applicable today: a repo-wide sweep for both table names returns only this migration, its contract test, its live proof, the segregation doc and three stale HANDOFF rows — **no view, function, trigger, policy, publication or other test reads either table, and no FK from any other table points at them.** They are gated by `.agent/work/3498/6/contract.json` `prohibited_actions[4]`. Residual: no index leads with `user_id` / `assigned_by_user_id` on the assignment table — the source has none either, so this is dropped parity, not a new gap (informational).\n\nNo sibling instance of this failure class remains in the diff: the only `pg_index.indkey` uses are at `:249` (migration), `:114` (test) and `:120` (proof), all cast `::smallint[]`; the other `indkey` uses in the repository (`supabase/tests/sesame_landing_contracts.sql:212`, `wildbrain_landing_contracts.sql:705`, `popdam_tag_count_narrow_eligibility_contracts.sql:13`, `plm_prod_order_milestone_schedule_factory_time_idx_contracts.sql:12`) are pre-existing and use the supported `= any(indkey)` / `indkey[0]` forms, outside this diff.\n\n## 3. Mandatory check 2 — function volatility\n\nNo defect, and stated non-vacuously: the change creates **zero** functions, procedures, triggers and views across all three SQL artifacts (263 + 126 + 130 lines read), so there is no `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` marker in this change that could be wrong, and specifically nothing that reads a table carries `IMMUTABLE`.\n\nAdjacent constructs I did check: `clock_timestamp()` used as a column DEFAULT (`:41`, `:44`, `:85`) is VOLATILE, evaluated per row, and textually matches the sources (`20260901221310:9,12,36`). The two derived DEFAULTs (`:67-79`) embed `pg_catalog.current_setting(text, true)` and `auth.jwt()`, both non-IMMUTABLE session readers, inside a DEFAULT, which carries no marker — correct, and identical to `20260907121732:14-26`. Every function call inside a stored CHECK is `pg_catalog.`-qualified and IMMUTABLE (`:46`, `:50`, `:97`, `:99`, `:107`). The only unqualified operators/types (`~` at `:46`, `:97`; `'{}'::jsonb` at `:43`, `:84`) are resolved when the CHECK expression is parsed at DDL time, so a later `search_path` cannot re-resolve them — informational only. If the deferred append-only triggers are added by the wiring session they must stay VOLATILE (the source's `dflow.reject_item_*_rewrite()` functions at `20260901221310:87-129` carry no marker and correctly default to VOLATILE).\n\n## 4. Mandatory check 3 — exact object checks\n\nThe change asserts far more than \"the name exists\":\n\n- Dependencies are engine-asserted with schema, relation **and** column: `REFERENCES plm.\"RFQItem\"(\"rfqItem_id\")` (`:37`, `:64`), `REFERENCES plm.\"RFQStep\"(\"RFQStep_id\")` (`:80`, `:81`), self-reference `REFERENCES plm.item_workflow_action(id, rfq_item_id)` (`:93`). The referents exist with exactly those PK columns (`ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:791-792`, `:919-920`, `:2285`, `:2288`). Object collision fails closed (plain `CREATE TABLE`, no `IF NOT EXISTS`).\n- The apply-time catalogue block (`:147-261`) asserts, per table: exact column counts 9/16 (`:156-163`); `relkind = 'r' AND relrowsecurity` (`:164-170`); zero `pg_policies` for the exact `(schemaname, tablename)` pair (`:171-176`); the 3-role × 7-privilege `has_table_privilege` sweep (`:177-183`); the two actor defaults compared by **full deparsed expression equality** against `dflow.item_workflow_action`, requiring exactly 2 matches (`:188-199`); all five FKs by `conname` + `conrelid` + `confrelid` + `contype='f'` + `convalidated` + `confdeltype` + ordered child and parent key names (`:200-226`); and all seven claimed indexes by schema, `relkind='i'`, access method, `indrelid`, uniqueness, validity/readiness/liveness, `indexprs IS NULL`, key count and ordered key names, plus predicate equality (`:227-259`).\n- The CI contract test repeats the same catalogue assertions and additionally compares the complete column signature `(attname, atttypid, atttypmod, attnotnull, atthasdef, attidentity, pg_get_expr(...))` against the `dflow` source with a symmetric `EXCEPT` (`test:19-47`) — order-independent, which is the right design given the disclosed ordinal divergence.\n- The live proof repeats the shape, RLS, zero-policy, privilege, five-FK and seven-index assertions for production (`live-proofs/3498.sql:22-130`), driven by the version string (`:24-26`).\n\nI hand-checked the arithmetic and the definitions rather than trusting the messages: 9 and 16 columns count correctly against the four-source cumulative shape; the index total is 11 (3 on the assignment table: PK + `rfq_item_id_idx` + `one_active`; 8 on the action table: PK + two inline UNIQUEs + five `CREATE INDEX`), matching the `= 11` assertion and the exception wording.\n\nResidual depth gaps (none of which is a present defect):\n- Nothing asserts `relforcerowsecurity`, and nothing asserts the ACL is otherwise empty beyond the three swept roles (a later `alter default privileges in schema plm grant … to <new role>` would not be caught). Note the `anon` half covers `PUBLIC` transitively, since a PUBLIC grant is inherited by `anon`.\n- The CHECK-constraint set is not asserted or compared to the source; it is created inline in the same statement, so a failure would abort the apply, but there is no independent proof it landed.\n- `pg_get_indexdef` equality is not used; the assertions instead pin `indrelid`, key order/names, uniqueness and predicate, which is equivalent-or-stronger in kind. Committed probes `2357.sql:87-91` and `2506.sql:18-19` use a different strong form; both are covered by the seven-index assertion here.\n- The proof's index assertions are name-plus-definition; the migration's are the same, so a same-name wrong-definition leftover cannot pass anywhere (each assertion can fail).\n\nGuard compatibility, hand-applied: the `$verify$` block is signalled (`check-migration-verify-cost.mjs:177-200`), and `PATTERNS` run over the scannable view in which every string literal's contents are blanked (`:98-113`), so every `'plm.…'` fragment reduces to `''`; the only read contexts in the block are `INTO`, `FROM pg_catalog.…`, `FROM unnest(...)`, `JOIN pg_catalog.…` — none followed by a `plm` object — and no `SET search_path`/`set_config` appears anywhere in the file, so `searchPathReachesPlm` returns −1 for both block and file scope (`:234-258`, `:304-323`). It passes.\n\n## 5. Role, permission and security boundary\n\nGrants changed: none, anywhere in the three artifacts. Revokes: two (`:144-145`), `REVOKE ALL ON TABLE … FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role`, preceded by `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` with zero policies (`:142-143`) and a rationale comment (`:139-141`). This matches the nearest `plm` sibling exactly, which also ships a bare revoke with no compensating grant (`20260911214438:96-97`), so it is house convention rather than a defect; it is also not the zero-policy-plus-grants posture remediated by `20260914155226`.\n\nThe operative role is asserted, which was the substantive fix over earlier rounds: the privilege sweep includes `service_role` (`:177-183`, `test:58-62`, `proof:66-71`), which is the role a fresh `plm` table is born with via default privileges. `plm` is outside PostgREST exposure (`docs/agents/references-and-runbooks.md:21`), so the `anon`/`authenticated` halves are belt-and-braces. No sibling call path exists that could inherit or bypass this posture: no other migration/view/function/test references either table, and no FK from any other table points at them. No `GRANT` is issued, so the DesignFlow backend role needs a successor grant — recorded at `completion.json:57` and gated by `contract.json` `prohibited_actions[4]`.\n\n## 6. Objects, dependencies, version and claim scope\n\nObjects created: exactly the two `plm` tables and the seven claimed indexes, whose names match the issue's `writes` list and `.agent/work/3498/6/contract.json` `db_writes` one-for-one. Inline FKs and inline UNIQUE constraints add no claim keys beyond the tables. `derived-from:` (`:3`) is one line naming four 14-digit versions, matching `VERSION_RE` (`scripts/migration_derivation.py:48`) and the comma-split validator that refuses any non-14-digit token (`:198-200`); all four files exist and I read each. Nothing in the repository except this migration creates either `plm` table, and the version string appears only in this migration's filename, the evidence pair, the live proof and the packet.\n\nApply-time coupling worth recording: the verification block reads the **source** schema's catalogue (`'dflow.item_workflow_action'::regclass` at `:191`) and aborts the apply if those defaults are absent or different. That is deliberate parity and fails closed; the header documents the derivation (`:3`) but not this hard apply-time dependency. In every target ordered by version this is satisfiable (`20260901221310` creates the table, `20260907121732:14-26` sets the defaults, both older than this version; the CI baseline defines no `dflow.item_*` table at all, so there is nothing to conflict with).\n\nRollback and recovery: everything sits in one transaction with `COMMIT` last (`:31`, `:263`), so a mid-file failure leaves neither table, no index, no RLS change and no revoke; CI additionally applies with a single transaction. Recovery after success is a drop of two empty, unreferenced tables, which also removes the four RI triggers this change attaches to the live `plm.\"RFQItem\"`/`plm.\"RFQStep\"`. No `dflow` object is altered, dropped or renamed, so the original capability is untouched. Bounded by `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` and `statement_timeout = '5min'` (`:32-33`), which is a stronger form than the sources' session-level `set` (`20260905053422:39-40`).\n\n## 7. Everything about the change's *behaviour* at this head is therefore inferred from the bytes (reading is strong for DDL but cannot substitute for applying it). Fail-closed and intended, but the header should say so, since it currently documents the derivation rather than the hard dependency.\n\n**F4 — Low: assertion depth.** No `relforcerowsecurity` assertion, no ACL-emptiness assertion beyond the three swept roles, and no CHECK-set parity assertion (`:147-261`, `test:49-62`).\n\n**F5 — Low: the live proof is coupled to the source tables it exists to replace.** `live-proofs/3498.sql:47-60` compares `plm` signatures against `dflow`; if the source is retired or legitimately diverges the committed probe fails, and with the `dflow` side absent the comparison yields NULL rather than naming the missing side. That is honest and complete for this diff; the durable record is thin because `.agent/work/3498/6/` is per-claim evidence, so the orchestrator should carry these into the successor contract.\n\n**F7 — Informational.** `item_user_assignment_active_lookup` is deferred but is largely served already by the shipped `one_active` (same `(rfq_item_id, function_key)` leading columns, same `WHERE effective_to IS NULL`, `user_id` in the key); the other three deferred indexes cover ordering and the `requires_admin_review` predicate, which nothing queries yet. No index leads with `user_id`/`assigned_by_user_id` on the assignment table — the `dflow` source has none either, so it is parity rather than a regression.\n\n**F8 — Informational.** `effective_from` (`:41`) and `created_at` (`:44`) receive two independent `clock_timestamp()` evaluations and are not guaranteed equal; same as the source. The mover must not assume equality.\n\nCompensating positive controls I verified so these are not mistaken for false passes: the contract test fails closed if either side is missing (a missing `plm` table gives count 0; a missing `dflow` table makes the `EXCEPT` return every `plm` row); the migration's verification raises on a missing table, a wrong column count, `relkind` ≠ `'r'`, RLS off, a policy, any of the 42 privilege combinations, either actor default, any of the five FK facts, or any of the seven index facts; and every assertion in the migration, the test and the proof can fail. The append-only claim is now truthful (\"not yet enforced\", `:60`, `:137`), and the earlier vacuous `anon`-only privilege probe is gone. The `derived-from:` prose class is closed (`:3`; `scripts/migration_derivation.py:52,198-200`), and there is no remaining `LIKE`-based shape assertion in the change (the earlier `'%request.designflow.actor_id%'` substring test is replaced by full `pg_get_expr` equality at `:188-199`). The segregation doc is now self-consistent: 74 tables at `:63` and `:277`, created-home wording at `:152-153`, and a history row; the only surviving \"not yet created\" text is the removed-line text inside the packet's `patch.diff`, not the document.\n\n## 8. Assessment\n\nI re-derived every previously raised blocking finding from source rather than from the summaries, and all of them are closed in these bytes: the lineage header parses; both actor-identity defaults are textually identical to `20260907121732:14-26`; the intra-`plm` FK set including the composite self-FK is present and gives `UNIQUE (id, rfq_item_id)` its purpose; the sixth CHECK landed (`:117-121`, faithful to `20260905053422:185-191`); the seven index objects and the 11-index total are asserted; the FK child columns are indexed; the privilege sweep covers the role the revoke actually strips; the timeouts are set; the CHECK helpers are qualified; the append-only COMMENT is truthful; the `item_user_assignment` COMMENT no longer overstates the deferral; the docs rows are updated; and the one cast class my predecessor flagged as an unverified resolution risk is now explicit in all three artifacts.\n\nThe change is additive: two empty tables, seven indexes on those tables, two table comments, RLS with zero policies, two revokes, one catalogue-only `DO` block and `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` with `COMMIT` last. No existing object is altered, dropped or renamed, no DML, no row movement, no grant. It fails closed on collision, on a missing dependency, and on any shape divergence. Mandatory checks 1 and 2 carry no defect; mandatory check 3 is met well beyond name resolution, with the depth gaps in F4 recorded rather than glossed.\n\nWhat stops me from calling this fully verified is not in the changed files: the version reservation rests on in-tree records I cannot confirm against the authoritative claim body (F1), and no execution result is attributable to this exact head (F2). I record those as unverified rather than inferring them and hand them to the orchestrator, which owns the claim ledger and the merge gate. On the change itself I found nothing that blocks, and nothing that a further authoring round could improve without touching bytes that are already correct — so refusing here would cost a round for facts this profile cannot reach and the author cannot fix in-lane. I therefore record no refusal, and the residual obligations in F3–F8 stay attached to this head as orchestrator-carried work.\n\nVERDICT: APPROVE [20260924174155_popdam_search_semantic_score_floor.sql](/d/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-claude-pr3489-slot1-muse-7e3da4fa30a0/supabase/migrations/20260924174155_popdam_search_semantic_score_floor.sql), its predecessor [20260901130428_popdam_ranked_filter_parity.sql](/d/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-claude-pr3489-slot1-muse-7e3da4fa30a0/supabase/migrations/20260901130428_popdam_ranked_filter_parity.sql:85) (prior 7-arg definition, compared line-by-line), the foundation migration's index set (`idx_dam_search_documents_embedding_hnsw` HNSW cosine with `WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL`, GIN `search_tsv`, trgm indexes on title/path/customer/program), both updated contract tests, `behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql` (all of T1–T8), `contract.json`/`completion.json`, and helper volatilities (`require_dam_access` STABLE plpgsql, `expand_dam_search_queries` STABLE sql, `assets_thumbnail_min_date` STABLE sql definer).\r\n\r\n## Findings — High / Medium\r\n\r\nNone. All ten checklist items hold: floor is inside `semantic_candidates` only (migration lines 55–56) with the identical `greatest(0,1-(d.embedding <=> p_query_embedding))` expression in SELECT and WHERE; null floor reduces to a tautology so the set matches the prior definition exactly; keyword leg untouched and keyword rows enter `candidate_ranks` with `semantic_rank = null` (lines 62–63); 7-arg drop (line 7) and 8-arg create plus revoke/grant (lines 132–133, authenticated + service_role only) are in the same migration; clamp `greatest(0,least(1,…))` (lines 27–28); pagination/facets/offset-limit block (lines 110–129) is byte-identical in structure to the predecessor; trailing param with default keeps existing 7-arg call sites (including the style-group rollup) bound.\r\n\r\n## Findings — Low / Informational\r\n\r\n- Floor predicate is a filter, not index-served. The HNSW index serves the `ORDER BY d.embedding <=> p_query_embedding LIMIT 20000` ordering and its partial predicate matches `d.embedding IS NOT NULL`, but `greatest(0,1-dist) >= threshold` cannot be an index condition as written. No action needed: no index type could serve that expression, the scan is bounded by LIMIT 20000, and floor-plus-top-N is sound (top-N by distance are the highest scores, so filtering them misses nothing). Same file, lines 50–57. Sibling check: the distance expression is evaluated twice per row (WHERE + SELECT list); negligible at this limit, noted only.\r\n- Clamp boundaries untested. T6 pins floor 0 and 1 but no out-of-range case (e.g. 1.5 behaves as 1.0, -0.5 as 0). Code is correct (lines 27–28); only coverage is missing. Edge observation: `NaN` input clamps to 1 (fail-closed, strictest floor) — safe direction.\r\n- Facets under a floor unasserted. T5 checks `total_count`/`has_more`/page sizes but never that `facets` reflect the floored set. `matched_assets` derives from the same `visible_assets` CTE (lines 114–115), so the code is correct; only the assertion is missing.\r\n- No combined `p_min_rank` + floor test. The blended-rank `HAVING` (line 65) is unchanged and still applies after the floor, which matches the stated contract, but no behaviour test exercises both knobs together.\r\n- Migration asserts no dependencies inline (no DO-block checking `require_dam_access`, `expand_dam_search_queries`, `dam_search_documents` columns); exact-object pinning lives in the contract tests (`to_regprocedure` on the exact 7-arg/8-arg signatures, `pg_get_functiondef` substring pins, grant checks) instead. Adequate as a pair; noted for the record. The anon-lacks-EXECUTE checks transitively cover the PUBLIC pseudo-role revoke, so that is not a gap.\r\n\r\nNo tests were run in this packet (stated unknown); findings above are from static inspection against the predecessor definition.\r\n\r\nVERDICT: APPROVE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n## Provisional verdict\n\nProvisional verdict: REVISE — the migration itself is substantively correct on all four behaviours the brief names (floor confined to the semantic leg, null floor behaviour-preserving, 7-arg dropped and 8-arg created with correct grants, clamping in [0,1]), but the change leaves the repository's post-apply **exact-object** contracts still probing the object it drops, ships **no sidecar** for the new migration, and adds behaviour tests that are unexecuted and one of which contradicts its own fixture.\n\n## Coverage\n\nRead in full: `supabase/migrations/20260924174155_popdam_search_semantic_score_floor.sql` (136 lines), prior definition `supabase/migrations/20260901130428_popdam_ranked_filter_parity.sql` (207 lines), both modified test files, `.agent/work/3457/1/{contract.json,completion.json}`, `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py` (targeted), `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/` (listing + `20260831212757.json`), and the index/helper definitions in `20260713221518_dam_hybrid_search_foundation.sql`, `20260831074401_popdam_ranked_search_entitlement_performance.sql`, `20260830110517_popdam_effective_asset_filters.sql`, `20260714173500_dam_search_synonyms.sql`.\n\nVerified correct (no finding):\n\n- Floor is applied only in `semantic_candidates`, before the union that feeds `candidate_ranks`: `20260924174155...sql:50-57` vs the blend at `:62-65`. The keyword arm (`:39-49`) and the blend are untouched.\n- Null-floor equivalence is structural, not incidental: the new body is textually identical to `20260901130428...sql:97-201` except for `:27-28` (the clamp) and `:55-56` (the floor conjunct). With `p_min_semantic_score` null, the added conjunct short-circuits and the CTE is the prior CTE.\n- Clamping is real and *used*: the clamped value is projected as `params.min_semantic_score` (`:28`) and the floor compares against `p.min_semantic_score` where `p` is the `params` alias (`:53`, `:55-56`) — i.e. the clamped column, not the raw parameter.\n- `greatest(0, 1-(...))` clamps `semantic_rank` into [0,1] (`:52`), so the floor and the score share one range.\n- Keyword survival with `semantic_rank` null holds: a keyword hit excluded from the semantic leg yields `max(NULL) = NULL` in `candidate_ranks` (`:60`) and survives via the `coalesce` in the rank expression (`:61`).\n- Grants: `revoke all ... from public, anon` then `grant execute ... to authenticated, service_role` on the exact 8-arg identity (`:132-133`), matching the test reductions at `supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:141-148` and `supabase/tests/popdam_ranked_filter_parity_contracts.sql:33`.\n- 7-arg callers keep working: `public.search_assets_full_text` and `public.search_style_groups_full_text` call with 7 args (`20260831074401...sql:372`, `:410-411`); because `p_min_semantic_score` carries `default null` (`:14`), those calls now resolve to the 8-arg object with a null floor — behaviour-preserving by construction.\n\n## Findings\n\n### High\n\n**H1. Four post-apply catalog contracts still probe the exact 7-arg object this migration drops, and the change did not update them.**\n`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1176-1177` and `:1199-1200` bind contracts `popdam_ranked_search_single_heap_fetch_v3` and `popdam_ranked_search_rank_keys_through_visibility_v4` to `to_regprocedure('public.search_dam_documents(text,jsonb,integer,integer,text[],extensions.vector,real)')` — the signature dropped at `20260924174155...sql:7`. `popdam_ranked_search_narrow_visibility_v1` probes the same signature at `:1055` and calls `has_function_privilege('anon', <7-arg>, 'EXECUTE')` at `:1066-1068`, and `popdam_ranked_search_private_keyed_visibility_v2` at `:1084`.\n\nTwo consequences, both bad, and both avoidable by the same edit the author already made to the SQL test files:\n\n1. If a contract runs after this migration lands, `to_regprocedure(<7-arg>)` returns NULL, `select ... from pg_proc p where p.oid = NULL` returns zero rows, and the wrapping `(select ...)` yields NULL — not the single true row `expected_count: 1` demands (see the sidecar shape at `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260831212757.json:10`). A correct promotion goes red.\n2. Supersession will not save it. Objects are keyed by full signature on purpose — `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1683-1687` (\"a different overload is a different object\") — so even if the new migration ships a sidecar asserting the 8-arg routine, it does **not** supersede a check asserting the 7-arg routine. `mark_superseded_contract_checks` (`:1721-1775`) compares object keys, and these keys differ.\n\nThe author recognised exactly this class and fixed it for `supabase/tests/` — `.agent/work/3457/1/completion.json:37` states \"existing supabase/tests contract files pinned the 7-arg signature and were updated in the same PR so CI does not fail\" — but the derivation in `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py` was left pinned to the old signature. This is the item-3 obligation of the brief: asserting the right object, not a name that merely exists.\n\n**H2. No post-apply verification sidecar for the new migration.**\n`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1788` loads `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/{version}.json` per allowlisted version. A repository-wide search for `20260924174155` returns matches only in `.agent/work/3457/1/*` and the review packet — nothing under `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/`. Every neighbouring ranked-search migration in that chain does carry one (`20260831212757.json`, `20260831221607.json`, and the directory listing). So this change modifies a `security definer` function's signature and ACLs with no catalog assertion of the resulting state — the exact \"proves that it WROTE, not WHAT it wrote\" gap the module's own docstring is built around (`:5-9`). I could not run the verifier, so I state the absence of a sidecar file as evidenced by search, not the outcome of a run.\n\n**H3. No executed test evidence for the new floor.**\n`MANIFEST.md` §5 states no tests were run for this packet, and `.agent/work/3457/1/completion.json:34` positions the T1–T8 file as \"authored ... for preview execution after merge\". The declared outcome `\"ready-for-merge\"` (`completion.json:4`) therefore rests on static checks only (`completion.json:24-33`). Every behavioural claim in the brief — null-floor parity, keyword survival, floor=1, clamping — is asserted by an unexecuted file.\n\n### Medium\n\n**M1. `T6` contradicts its own fixture and is floating-point fragile.**\n`.agent/work/3457/1/behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql:233-236` asserts that `search_dam_documents('zz3457 absent query','{}'::jsonb,50,0,null,qemb,null,1.0)` returns 0 rows. But the semantic leg is independent of the query text — it joins only on `p_query_embedding is not null and d.embedding is not null` (`20260924174155...sql:53`) — and the fixtures make `sem-high`'s embedding *exactly* the query embedding: the update at `behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql:110-114` writes `[1,0,…,0]`, and `qemb` is built as `[1,0,…,0]` at `:135`. Cosine distance is 0, `greatest(0, 1-0) = 1.0 >= 1.0` passes the clamped floor, so a semantic hit is returned. The test passes only if `real`-precision vector arithmetic yields a hair-below-1.0 similarity instead of exactly 1.0 — i.e. the assertion is a coin flip, not a contract. Either drop the fixture's exact match or assert the exact-match row is the one returned.\n\n**M2. The in-repo contract checks for the floor are textual, so they cannot falsify the property they name.**\n`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:128-134` asserts only that the strings `p_min_semantic_score`, `min_semantic_score` and `p.min_semantic_score is null` appear in `pg_get_functiondef`. A definition that applied the floor *both* inside the semantic leg and after the blend still contains all three literals; a body containing the parameter name alone satisfies `:128-131`. Same for the clamp: nothing asserts `least(1, p_min_semantic_score)`. These are existence-of-name checks, not checks that the right object/behaviour exists.\n\n**M3. The floor makes the semantic leg's `limit 20000` bound post-filter rows, weakening the HNSW path.**\n`idx_dam_search_documents_embedding_hnsw` is created as `using hnsw (embedding extensions.vector_cosine_ops) where embedding is not null` (`20260713221518_dam_hybrid_search_foundation.sql:69-72`), and the semantic leg's `order by d.embedding <=> p_query_embedding limit 20000` (`20260924174155...sql:57`) with join predicate `d.embedding is not null` (`:53`) is index-eligible as written. That part is sound. But the new floor predicate (`:55-56`) is a filter on the same distance expression the index orders by, so the `20000` cap now bounds *survivors*, not *candidates*: with a high floor the leg can return far fewer than 20000 rows even when qualifying documents exist beyond the HNSW search window. This is a silent recall cliff that `total_count` will faithfully report as small, not as truncated — worth naming in the migration comment. Also note the performance advisor reports this index unused: `docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260904T212459Z/run1/advisors-performance.json:8164` (\"Index `idx_dam_search_documents_embedding_hnsw` … has not been used\"), so the \"index-backed\" assumption for the semantic leg rests on definition, not on observed use.\n\n**M4. Evidence files are bound to a different head than the reviewed one.**\n`.agent/work/3457/1/completion.json:11` records `head_sha: 4a5592f584011d10c1a440ae7591f010fc6d7f10`, and the reviewed head is `35794d8c609083520ed5a87281a259631745a14b` (`MANIFEST.md` §2). The contract pair therefore does not describe the commit under review. `contract.json:31` also pins `refs/db-contracts/3457/1` with `contract_sha256` (`completion.json:9`); I could not resolve that ref with the tools available, so I do not assert whether it matches. Separately, `completion.json\":20` declares `\"db_reads\": []` although the function body reads `public.dam_search_documents`, `public.assets`, `public.style_groups`, `public.asset_effective_tags`, and `public.admin_config` (via `assets_thumbnail_min_date()`).\n\n### Low\n\n**L1.** The clamped floor silently widens the accepted range: `greatest(0,least(1,p_min_semantic_score))` (`:27-28`) turns a caller's `1.5` into `1.0` and a negative into `0.0`, with no error and no note in the function comment (`:135-136`). The comment documents the *effect* of the floor but not the clamp.\n\n**L2.** The distance is computed up to three times per row (`:52` for the projection, `:55-56` for the floor, `:57` for the ordering) and the floor's copy is wrapped in `greatest`, which will normally prevent the planner from commoning them up. Not a correctness bug; a per-row cost on the hot path.\n\n**L3.** Documentation outside the change is now stale: `docs/unified-supabase-schema-map.md:104` still describes `search_dam_documents(query, limit, document_types, query_embedding)`. Reachable from the changed object, though not in the changed-file list.\n\n### Not a finding (checked and cleared)\n\n- Item 1, index usage for the *changed* predicates: the floor predicate itself has no index and needs none — it is a filter, not a probe. The two joins the change relies on are indexed: the text leg's `d.search_tsv @@ any(...)` (`:38`) is served by `idx_dam_search_documents_tsv` (`20260713221518...sql:54-55`), and the style-group expansion join `a.style_group_id = c.style_group_id and not a.is_deleted` (`:73`) is served by `assets_style_group_id_active_idx`, whose predicate `is_deleted = false and style_group_id is not null` matches the query as written (`20260831093107_popdam_ranked_search_keyed_visibility.sql:4`). The change does not add an index assumption, and it does not remove one; the index assertion in the existing test (`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:192-194`) is unchanged and still exact.\n- Item 2, volatility: the marker is `language sql stable security definer` (`:18`), byte-identical in that clause to the prior definition (`20260901130428...sql:93`). The body reads tables and calls `stable` helpers (`public.require_dam_access()` at `20260831074401...sql:4-19`, `public.expand_dam_search_queries(text)` at `20260714173500_dam_search_synonyms.sql:72-77`, `public.assets_thumbnail_min_date()` at `20260830110517_popdam_effective_asset_filters.sql:203-214`). STABLE is the correct marker for a read-only body, and nothing in the change loosens it; there is no IMMUTABLE claim to falsify.\n- The drop/create ordering at `:7` then `:9` is correct, and the drop's argument list uses `extensions.vector(384)` consistently with the create, grant and comment (`:9-14`, `:132-135`) — the object identity is spelled exactly, not inferred, in the migration itself.\n\n## Missing evidence\n\nI could not execute anything, so the following are reported as unverified rather than asserted: whether the promotion allowlist will place `20260924174155` in the same ordered batch as `20260831212757`/`20260831221607` (this determines whether H1 bites in the same run or a later one); whether `has_function_privilege` raises `undefined_function` or returns false for a dropped signature in the target's PostgreSQL version (H1 holds under either, via the `to_regprocedure` path); and whether a public-schema `alter default privileges ... grant execute on functions` exists that would leave unintended grantees on the new 8-arg object despite `revoke all ... from public, anon` at `:132`. Also note `MANIFEST.md` §5: no tests were run for this packet, so none of the behavioural claims are independently corroborated.\n\nVERDICT: REVISE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n**Provisional verdict: REVISE** — one High defect in the T1–T8 behaviour fixtures (T3 contradicts the specified semantics and sibling T4); everything else in the migration, probes, and sidecar checks out statically.\r\n\r\n## Findings\r\n\r\n### High\r\n\r\n- **T3 asserts removal of a document that must survive as a keyword hit — it will FAIL against a correct implementation.** `.agent/work/3457/1/behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql:171-176` asserts `count(*) = 0` for the `sem-low` doc under `floor=0.5` with query `'zz3457 sem low'`. But the fixture title is `'zz3457 sem low unrelated'` (`:91-94`), which contains the full query string: it matches the full-text leg (`search_tsv @@ tsq`, migration `:38`) and the substring leg (`'%zz3457 sem low%'` ILIKE, migration `:47-49`). Per the contract the floor applies only inside `semantic_candidates` (migration `:55-56`), so this keyword hit must survive with `semantic_rank = null` — exactly what T4 (`:189-201`) asserts for the identically-structured `mixed` doc. T3 and T4 are mutually inconsistent; T4 matches the spec, so T3 is wrong. Fix: give the below-floor doc text that does not keyword-match its query (a true semantic-only fixture), or align T3's expectation with T4. This is the same defect a prior reviewer raised against this exact gen-1 file, still unfixed at this head.\r\n\r\n### Medium\r\n\r\n- **Behaviour tests remain unexecuted; no pass evidence exists at this head.** Packet `MANIFEST.md §5` states no tests were run. `.agent/work/3457/4/completion.json:46-49` reports 244 pytest passes at implementation head `f44472ca8`, but that covers the catalog-probe/sidecar unit tests, not the T1–T8 SQL, which `completion.json:72` still concedes \"remains a preview-execution artifact.\" The T3 defect above is exactly what execution would have caught. At minimum T3–T4 need a preview run with reported notices before merge.\r\n\r\n### Low\r\n\r\n- **In-repo contract checks for the floor are textual and cannot falsify misplacement.** `supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:128-133` asserts only that the literals `p_min_semantic_score`, `min_semantic_score`, `p.min_semantic_score is null` appear in `pg_get_functiondef`. A body that applied the floor after the blend as well as in the leg would still contain all three strings. Behavioural coverage for placement rests entirely on the (currently broken, unexecuted) T-file.\r\n- **Stale header comment in behaviour file.** `.agent/work/3457/1/behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql:52` says \"three documents\" but four rows are inserted (`:69-79`); declared `ids text[]` (`:125`) is never used.\r\n- **Sidecar hash binding taken as reported, not verified.** `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925175038.json:4` carries a well-formed `migration_sha256`, and the version is registered (`config/production-verification-sidecar-registry.json:245-246`), but this sandbox has no execution, so byte-binding of the hash to the migration file could not be recomputed. Same applies to `contract_sha256` in `.agent/work/3457/4/completion.json:10`.\r\n\r\n### Verified correct — no finding (mandatory gates + focus areas)\r\n\r\n- **Migration SQL behaviour 1–4.** Floor lives only in `semantic_candidates` before blend (`supabase/migrations/20260925175038_popdam_search_semantic_score_floor.sql:50-57`); keyword arm (`:39-49`) and blend/HAVING (`:58-65`) untouched; keyword hits excluded from the leg yield `max(NULL)=NULL` and survive via `coalesce` (`:59-61`); null floor reduces the conjunct to TRUE, preserving the prior definition; clamp `greatest(0,least(1,…))` is computed in `params` and the clamped CTE value is what the leg filters on (`:27-28` → `:55-56`); pagination/facets block unchanged (`:110-129`); 7-arg dropped and 8-arg created/granted in one migration (`:7`, `:132-133`); trailing param with `default null` keeps existing 7-arg callers bound with null floor.\r\n- **Grants/roles.** `revoke all … from public, anon` covers the PUBLIC pseudo-role, then `grant execute … to authenticated, service_role` on the exact 8-arg identity (`:132-133`); `service_role` grant is pinned in `supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:145-146`, anon-denial in both contract files and the catalog probes.\r\n- **Index usage (mandatory).** New floor predicate is a filter on a computed distance — no index can serve it as written, and none is needed (bounded `LIMIT 20000` scan). REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\nProvisional verdict: REVISE — the migration body itself checks out statically against its declared predecessor, but the change ships no executed evidence for the behaviour it exists to guarantee, its in-repo pin for the floor's *placement* is textual only, and several load-bearing facts (sidecar hash binding, query-expansion token behaviour the T-file depends on, pass-2 replay interaction) are unverified in this packet.\n\n## What I actually opened and verified\n\nMigration (`supabase/migrations/20260925175038_popdam_search_semantic_score_floor.sql`, 136 lines, all read):\n\n- `:7` drops the 7-arg identity with `extensions.vector(384)` spelled exactly, and **without `cascade`** — consistent with the repo's doctrine that a bare drop fails closed when something depends on it (`scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py:155-158`).\n- `:9-15` creates the 8-arg signature with `p_min_semantic_score real default null` trailing; `:18` `language sql stable security definer`; `:19-20` pinned `search_path` and `statement_timeout='8s'`.\n- `:27-28` clamps into `[0,1]` as `min_semantic_score`, and `:55-56` filters against `p.min_semantic_score` (the clamped column), not the raw parameter.\n- `:50-57` confines the floor to `semantic_candidates`, before the union at `:62-63` and the blend/`having` at `:61,:65`. Keyword rows enter that union with `null::real semantic_rank` (`:62`), `max(NULL)` is NULL, and the rank expression uses `coalesce` (`:61`) — keyword hits below the floor survive with `semantic_rank` null, as specified.\n- `:132-133` `revoke all … from public, anon` then `grant execute … to authenticated, service_role`, on the exact 8-arg identity; `:135-136` comment.\n\nPredecessor comparison (`supabase/migrations/20260901130428_popdam_ranked_filter_parity.sql:85-207`): the new body is textually the same CTE chain, and the only deltas I can see are the clamp (`:27-28`) and the floor conjunct (`:55-56`). With a null floor the conjunct short-circuits to TRUE, so the null-floor path is behaviour-preserving by construction, not by assertion.\n\nSibling callers stay bound because the new parameter carries a default: `public.search_assets_full_text` calls with 7 args at `supabase/migrations/20260831074401_popdam_ranked_search_entitlement_performance.sql:372`, and `public.search_style_groups_full_text` at `:410-411`; the same wrapper shapes are re-declared at `supabase/migrations/20260831041629_popdam_authorized_ranked_search.sql:129-154`.\n\nSidecar and registry (`scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925175038.json:1-19`, `config/production-verification-sidecar-registry.json:244-247`): present, schema_version 1, `migration_version` matches, two checks — a `catalog_contract` on `popdam_ranked_search_rank_keys_through_visibility_v4` and a `catalog_absence` on the exact dropped 7-arg identity — and the version is declared for issue 3457. The absence object uses `extensions.vector` without the typmod (`:15`); typmod is not part of function identity, so `to_regprocedure` resolves it (`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:2019-2023`), and the loader also requires the full signature charset (`:452-454`, `:1883-1889`), so the probe is a routine probe, not a bare-name relation probe.\n\nCatalog probes: every `search_dam_documents` probe in `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py` now binds the 8-arg identity — `:1055`, `:1066`, `:1068`, `:1084`, `:1177`, `:1179`, `:1181`, `:1200`, `:1202`, `:1204`. I found no surviving 7-arg *presence* assertion; the only remaining mentions are the intentional absence assertions (`scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925175038.json:15`, the T8 block at `.agent/work/3457/1/behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql:15`, and the absence assertion at `supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:98`). That closes the H1 class from the earlier round.\n\n## Findings\n\nHigh\n\nNone that I can substantiate from the sealed source. The migration's four stated behaviours are verified statically as described above.\n\nMedium\n\n- The change's core claim — the floor is applied *only* inside the semantic leg — has no assertion that can falsify misplacement at this head. The in-repo pin is string presence in `pg_get_functiondef` (`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql`, added pins per the `patch.diff` hunk `@@ -119,6 +125,13 @@`: `position('min_semantic_score' …)`, `position('p_min_semantic_score' …)`, `position('p.min_semantic_score is null' …)`). A body that floored the semantic leg *and* re-filtered after the blend would still contain all three literals. The post-apply sidecar inherits the same weakness because its forward check is that same contract (`scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925175038.json:7-11`), and the sidecar carries no behavioural or row-count check at all — its two checks bind strictly to `catalog_contract`/`catalog_absence` (`:5-17`, kinds validated at `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1830-1842`). So the one artifact that could falsify post-blend application is the behaviour file — which was not run.\n- No executed test evidence exists at this head for any behavioural claim. The sealed packet states \"No tests were run for this packet\" (`MANIFEST.md` §5), and the T1–T8 file declares itself preview-only (`.agent/work/3457/1/behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql:2`). Every runtime claim — null-floor parity, keyword survival with `semantic_rank` null, floor=1 → zero rows, clamping — rests on an unexecuted file plus the textual pins above.\n- The T-file's own expectations depend on an unopened function's token behaviour. T3 (`behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql:171-176`) asserts zero rows for `sem-low` (title `alpha beta gamma delta`, path `zz3457-sem-low.ai`, `:91-94`) under query `'zz3457 sem low'`; T6 (`:238-244`) asserts zero rows for query `'zz3457 absent query'`. Both hold only if `public.expand_dam_search_queries` does not emit a query fragment that the substring leg (`:47-49`, pattern `'%' || query || '%'`) or the tsquery leg (`:38`) can match — for example a fragment matching `zz3457-kw-only.ai` or `zz3457-sem-low.ai`. I did not open that function, so this is an unverified dependency, not a proven defect; it is precisely what a preview run would settle.\n\nLow\n\n- The clamped floor silently widens the caller's range: `greatest(0,least(1,p_min_semantic_score))` (`:27-28`) maps `1.5`→`1.0` and negatives→`0.0` with no error, and the function comment (`:135-136`) documents the floor but not the clamp. `NaN` compares above every other `real` in this engine's ordering, so it clamps to `1.0` (strictest) — fail-closed, but undocumented and unasserted.\n- The distance is evaluated three times per surviving row (`:52` projection, `:55-56` filter, `:57` ordering) and the filter copy is wrapped in `greatest`, which normally prevents the planner from commoning them up. Per-row cost only, on a 20000-row ceiling.\n- `.agent/work/3457/5/completion.json:12` records `head_sha` `7f9e9de8…` while the reviewed head is `e090b64c…`; the packet's own framing (`MANIFEST.md` §2, the head commit subject \"…bind #3457 contract pair generation 5 to implementation head 7f9e9de8\") explains the tail as an evidence-binding commit, but no artifact in this change binds the reviewed head, so the pairing is unverifiable here.\n- `docs/unified-supabase-schema-map.md:104` still describes `search_dam_documents(query, limit, document_types, query_embedding)` — reachable documentation of the changed object that this change does not refresh. Out of the declared scope, flagged only.\n- T-file hygiene: the header says \"four documents\" and inserts four (`:52`, `:81-98`) — fine — but the declared `ids text[]` (`:125`) is unused.\n\nRollback and recovery\n\n- The migration runs as one implicit transaction: I read all 136 lines and there is no `begin`/`commit`, so a failure in the create, revoke, grant or comment rolls the drop back and the 7-arg capability survives. The drop is non-`cascade`, so a real dependency would abort the migration rather than silently remove a dependent (`scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py:155-158`).\n- The change ships no down migration. Reverting after commit means a new migration that recreates the 7-arg identity and re-grants it; the prior body remains available as history in `supabase/migrations/20260901130428_popdam_ranked_filter_parity.sql:85-207`, so recovery is possible, but it is not part of this change and no artifact asserts it.\n- Migration immutability: the changed-file inventory (`MANIFEST.md` §3) shows one added migration and no modified migration; the superseded `20260924174155` filename appears only in prose (`HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T1226Z-edge-dev-mimo-orch-successor-3496.md:116`) and in the contract/completion rationale, not as a migration or sidecar on disk (`grep` for both versions returned no `supabase/migrations/20260924174155*` or `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260924174155.json`). I cannot verify the supersession itself without history.\n\n## Mandatory checks\n\n1. Index usage — every predicate the change relies on either keeps its serving index or is explicitly un-indexable, and I am naming the loose assumption.\n   - Text leg `d.search_tsv @@ any(...)` (`:38`) is served by the GIN index `idx_dam_search_documents_tsv` (`docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260904T212459Z/run1/indexes.json:509-510`).\n   - Style-group expansion join (`:73`) is served by `assets_style_group_id_active_idx`, whose predicate `is_deleted = false and style_group_id is not null` matches the query as written (`docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260904T212459Z/run1/indexes.json:3176-3177`).\n   - The new floor predicate (`:55-56`) is a filter over a computed distance. No index type can serve `greatest(0,1-(embedding <=> q)) >= threshold` as written — this is a real loose assumption and I am calling it out, not glossing it: it is acceptable only because the leg is bounded by `order by … limit 20000` (`:57`).\n   - Loose assumption, unused index: the semantic ordering's assumed index `idx_dam_search_documents_embedding_hnsw` (HNSW cosine, `where embedding is not null`, `docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260904T212459Z/run1/indexes.json:1181-1182`) is reported by the repo's own performance advisor as never used — `docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260904T212459Z/run1/advisors-performance.json:8164`. So \"the semantic leg is index-backed\" rests on definition, not observed use.\n   - Semantic consequence worth naming: because the WHERE clause is applied before the `limit 20000` in the same CTE, that cap now bounds *survivors*, not candidates. A selective floor can therefore return fewer than 20000 rows even when qualifying documents exist beyond the search window, and `total_count` reports the smaller number faithfully rather than signalling truncation. The migration comment (`:135-136`) documents the floor but not this interaction.\n\n2. Function volatility — the changed function's marker is correct; the callee markers are not evidenced in this packet.\n   - `search_dam_documents` is `language sql stable security definer` (`:18`), byte-identical to the prior definition's clause (`supabase/migrations/20260901130428_popdam_ranked_filter_parity.sql:93`). Its body only reads tables and calls accessors (`:29`, `:33`, `:77`); STABLE is the right marker and nothing here loosens it. There is no IMMUTABLE claim to falsify.\n   - I did not open `public.require_dam_access`, `public.expand_dam_search_queries` or `public.assets_thumbnail_min_date` in this packet, so I cannot independently confirm their markers. This is a named gap, not a cleared item; it is not a correctness break by itself (a STABLE body may call a VOLATILE function), but the brief asks for it and I will not assert what I did not read.\n\n3. Exact object checks — exact where it matters, loose in two places I will name.\n   - The migration names the dropped and created routine with full schema-qualified signatures including `extensions.vector(384)` in the DDL (`:7`, `:9-15`), the revoke/grant (`:132-133`) and the comment (`:135-136`).\n   - The catalog probes and the contract tests use the full 8-arg identity rather than an inferred name, and the 7-arg absence is asserted both in-repo (`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:97-101`) and post-apply (`scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925175038.json:12-17`). Because the absence probe is `to_regprocedure(<full signature>) is null` with `expected_count 1`, a missing object fails closed.\n   - Loose: the probes spell the vector argument as `extensions.vector` without `(384)` (e.g. `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1055`). Same type OID, so resolution succeeds, but it is textually looser than the DDL.\n   - Loose: the ACL assertion is not exhaustive. The change asserts anon denial and authenticated/service_role grants (in-repo and in the probes), and revokes `public, anon` (`:132`). Nothing in the change asserts that *no other* grantee holds EXECUTE on the new routine — e.g. a grant inherited from an `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` on `public` functions would survive the revoke. I did not find and did not open evidence of such a default-privilege rule over `public` functions, so I state this as an assertion-completeness gap, not a live hole.\n\nSibling search for the same failure classes: the H1 class (probes pinned to a superseded signature) is clean — the only remaining 7-arg literals are the three intentional absence assertions named above. The pass-2 replay class is not clean-by-evidence: the repo's replay lane re-runs earlier files after later ones (`scripts/check_pass2_routine_supersession.py:1-53`), and the ranked-search chain is a family of files that each end by `create or replace`-ing the then-current `search_dam_documents` overload (e.g. `supabase/migrations/20260901130428_popdam_ranked_filter_parity.sql:85-89`). If any of those older files is a pass-2 replay file, replaying it after `20260925175038` would recreate the dropped 7-arg overload, and both the in-repo absence assertion (`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:97-101`) and the sidecar absence check would go red. I have no evidence either way about which files are pass-2, so I am reporting it as an open risk with named missing evidence rather than as a defect.\n\n## Missing evidence\n\n- Executed results for `.agent/work/3457/1/behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql` (packet §5: none were run). This is the single largest gap: it is the only artifact that can falsify floor misplacement and the only one covering keyword-survival and clamp behaviour.\n- A recomputation of `migration_sha256` `8b7351cf1ac598399b6896544f3e27574bd071925d291e1f4cc1dd13af4a993b` (`scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925175038.json:4`) against the migration's LF-canonical bytes (`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1806-1822`). I cannot hash without execution; if it does not bind, the sidecar is inert and the H2 fix is void — this is the contract's own stop condition (`scripts/check_pass2…` no; `.agent/work/3457/5/contract.json:68-70`).\n- The body of `public.expand_dam_search_queries` (relevant to T2/T3/T6 expectations) and the markers of `require_dam_access` / `assets_thumbnail_min_date` (relevant to check 2).\n- Which migrations the pass-2 replay lane re-runs, and whether that lane restores a routine that a later migration dropped rather than merely replaced.\n- Whether a default EXECUTE privilege over `public` functions exists that the revoke at `:132` does not cover.\n- Whether `7f9e9de8…` (`.agent/work/3457/5/completion.json:12`) and the reported green runs at `.agent/work/3457/5/completion.json:46-64` correspond to the tree under review — no history or runner access.\n- The regenerated baseline's correctness as a whole: `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json:3-6` changed `detector_source_sha256` and `total_migration_files` 674→708 with `matched_count` unchanged at 103; I can confirm the file changed as claimed but cannot recompute either digest (`scripts/check-production-verification-sidecars.mjs:41-42`).\n\n## Bottom line\n\nThe migration is, on static reading, a correct and minimal implementation of the contracted behaviour: exact signatures, correct grants, floor confined to the semantic leg before the blend, null floor behaviour-preserving, non-cascading drop, single-transaction recovery. What the change does not carry is proof that any of the behaviour works — the one falsifying artifact is unexecuted, the post-apply sidecar proves the signature swap and the 7-arg removal but writes nothing about the floor, and its hash binding is unverifiable here. Those gaps should be closed with a preview run and an executed-evidence record before this merges; that is a REVISE, not a rejection of the design.\n\nVERDICT: REVISE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\nReview of PR #3489 (issue #3457) at head `51b6bbd359b932301d49ad10a1dd1eb574b5b65d`. I read the migration, both behavior-test copies, both contract tests, the sidecar + registry, all `search_dam_documents` probes, the predecessor definition, `expand_dam_search_queries`, helper volatilities, index definitions, wrapper callers, and the gen-8 evidence pair.\r\n\r\n## High\r\n\r\n**H1. The `DROP` of the 7-arg overload will be refused on any full-shape database — the migration cannot deploy as written.**\r\n`supabase/migrations/20260925175038_popdam_search_semantic_score_floor.sql:7` drops `public.search_dam_documents(text,jsonb,int,int,text[],extensions.vector(384),real)` bare (no `CASCADE`). Two SQL-language dependents still call that exact overload and were never redefined afterward: `public.search_assets_full_text` ([20260831074401…sql:367-374](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3457-3489-final-s2-7e3da4fa30a0\\supabase/migrations/20260831074401_popdam_ranked_search_entitlement_performance.sql:367), call at :372) and `public.search_style_groups_full_text` (:376-424, call at :410-412). Postgres records dependencies from SQL-function bodies to called functions, so a RESTRICT drop errors (`cannot drop … because other objects depend on it`) — this is also the repo's own stated doctrine ([production_business_risk_gate.py:155](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3457-3489-final-s2-7e3da4fa30a0\\scripts/production_business_risk_gate.py:155): \"Without CASCADE, Postgres refuses the drop while anything depends on it\"). Every predecessor drop in this chain removed only the dependent-free 4-arg legacy overload ([20260831093107…sql:44-46](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3457-3489-final-s2-7e3da4fa30a0\\supabase/migrations/20260831093107_popdam_ranked_search_keyed_visibility.sql:44), `20260831212757…sql:9-11`, `20260831221607…sql:8-10`), so there is no precedent for this succeeding. Effect: line 7 errors on production and full replays; the single implicit transaction rolls back, so capability is preserved but the deploy fails closed. Fix in the same migration: drop the two wrappers first, then the 7-arg, create the 8-arg, re-create the wrappers (their 7-arg calls rebind to the 8-arg via `default null`), and re-apply their `revoke`/`grant` ACLs. Note: this is incompatible with the brief's claimed ephemeral-CI PASS — T8 green requires the DROP to have succeeded in a DB containing the wrappers. Either the claim does not reflect a full-shape apply or execution will prove the analysis wrong; REVISE requires an executed apply log on a full-shape DB either way. Unverifiable in this shell-less packet (MANIFEST §5: no tests run); stated plainly.\r\n\r\n## Medium\r\n\r\n**M1. Floor-placement pins are textual only, and their behavioral backstop is execution-unverified in-packet.**\r\n[popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:128-134](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3457-3489-final-s2-7e3da4fa30a0\\supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:128) (and T8 in both behavior files) assert only that the literals `p_min_semantic_score` / `min_semantic_score` / `p.min_semantic_score is null` appear in `pg_get_functiondef`. A body that floored the semantic leg *and* re-filtered after the blend would still contain all three. Falsification rests entirely on T3/T4/T6, whose CI PASS is claimed in the brief but not evidenced in the sealed packet. Static inspection confirms correct placement (floor only at migration :55-56, keyword arm :39-49 and blend/HAVING :58-65 untouched), so this is a proof gap, not a suspected defect.\r\n\r\n## Low / informational\r\n\r\n- **T6's zero-row assertion is global, not fixture-scoped** ([behavior.sql:242-252](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3457-3489-final-s2-7e3da4fa30a0\\supabase/tests/popdam_semantic_score_floor_behavior.sql:242)). Any ambient row keyword-matching `zz3457 absent query` or with a ~1.0 embedding breaks it. Currently safe (sibling fixtures use `zz1703` tokens without embeddings), but scoping to fixture `entity_id`s would make it robust. T1/T5/T7 use relative assertions and are fine.\r\n- **Idempotency claim overstates**: only `dam_search_documents` is delete-then-insert (:85-88); `assets`, `auth.users`, `app.profile`, `app.app_access` inserts (:62-77) are plain `INSERT`. Fine under the single `begin`/`rollback` wrapper; a re-run without rollback hits PK conflicts.\r\n- **Stale preview copy ships**: [.agent/work/3457/1/behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql:81-98](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3457-3489-final-s2-7e3da4fa30a0\\.agent/work/3457/1/behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql:81) still inserts `search_tsv` explicitly, which errors on the `GENERATED ALWAYS` column (confirmed at `20260713221518…sql:33-42`). Dead artifact diverging from the fixed CI copy; delete or sync it.\r\n- **Probe spelling looseness**: probes and the sidecar absence object spell `extensions.vector` without `(384)` (e.g. `production_catalog_verification.py:1055`, sidecar :15). Same type OID — typmod is not part of function identity — so resolution succeeds; textual looseness only.\r\n- **ACL completeness gap**: anon-denial and authenticated/service_role grants are pinned, and `revoke … from public, anon` covers the pseudo-role, but nothing asserts no *other* grantee (e.g. via `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES`) holds EXECUTE on the 8-arg. Named gap, not a live hole.\r\n- **Clamp is silent**: `greatest(0,least(1,…))` (:27-28) maps 1.5→1.0, negatives→0.0 with no error and no mention in the function comment (:135-136). `NaN` clamps to 1.0 (fail-closed). T6 covers the behavior; only the comment is silent.\r\n- **Distance evaluated 3×/row** (:52 projection, :55-56 filter, :57 ordering); per-row cost bounded by `LIMIT 20000`. No action.\r\n- **Pass-2 replay unverified in-packet**: older chain files contain 7-arg `CREATE OR REPLACE` bodies, so cleanliness depends on the replay lane's file selection. The brief claims the supersession check is clean; the script was not executed here.\r\n- **Traceability notes**: `completion.json:12` `head_sha` (`c9da5597`) is the implementation head, not the reviewed evidence-binding tail (`51b6bbd`) — documented pattern, `base_sha` matches; `db_reads` includes `admin_config` but omits `app`-schema reads via `require_dam_access` (granularity nit); `docs/unified-supabase-schema-map.md:104` still describes the 4-arg-era signature (out of scope); sidecar `migration_sha256` and `contract_sha256` are well-formed but hash binding is not recomputable without execution; Blacksmith \"all 429 migrations…\" failures at older heads have truncated titles and no logs in-packet — cannot implicate this migration, noted as unverified external signal.\r\n\r\n## Verified correct (mandatory gates + focus areas)\r\n\r\n- **Migration behavior**: floor confined to `semantic_candidates` before blend; null floor reduces the conjunct to TRUE (body otherwise byte-identical to predecessor `20260901130428…sql:85-207`); clamp computed in `params` and the clamped CTE value is what the leg filters on; keyword hits survive with `semantic_rank = null` via `max(NULL)` + `coalesce`; 7-arg drop + 8-arg create + grants in one transaction; return columns and `p_min_rank` unchanged; trailing `default null` keeps 7-arg call sites bound. `derived-from: 20260901130428` header correct; predecessor present and unedited.\r\n- **Migration immutability**: one added migration, zero modified migrations; superseded `20260924174155` fully absent from migrations, sidecars, and registry.\r\n- **Sidecar/registry**: [20260925175038.json](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3457-3489-final-s2-7e3da4fa30a0\\scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925175038.json:1) well-formed with forward `catalog_contract` (key exists at `production_catalog_verification.py:1183`, all pinned substrings still present in the new body) plus exact 7-arg `catalog_absence`; registered for issue 3457 (registry :245-246).\r\n- **Catalog probes**: all four `search_dam_documents` probes and grant checks bind the 8-arg identity (:1055, :1066-1068, :1084, :1176-1181, :1199-1204); unit-test pins updated to 8-arg.
