no other callers of the 7-arg overload exist outside the two handled wrappers.\n\nVERDICT: APPROVE b527a80e47d01c381c325efb2d4427aaea0da16d","author_association":"MEMBER","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5862252250/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"performed_via_github_app":null,"minimized":null},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5862293355","html_url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3489#issuecomment-5862293355","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/3489","id":5862293355,"node_id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABXWt_aw","user":{"login":"u2giants","id":55610577,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/55610577?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants","html_url":"https://github.com/u2giants","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2026-09-28T02:38:58Z","updated_at":"2026-09-28T02:38:58Z","body":"GOVERNED REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n## Coverage and method\n\nRead-only inspection of the snapshot at head `b527a80e47d01c381c325efb2d4427aaea0da16d`. I opened the new migration, both recreated wrappers, the immediate predecessor, the foundation (index definitions and `search_tsv` DDL), the three modified/added `supabase/tests` files, the sidecar and registry, the probe diffs in `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py`, the generation-11 contract/completion, the altered baseline, `supabase/tests/ci-quarantine.txt`, `scripts/check-sql.sh` (guards B/B2) and `.github/workflows/database-contract-tests.yml` (pass-1/pass-2 replay). I could not execute anything, so hashes, pass counts and any database state are taken as reported, not verified.\n\nPrior-review corrections verified from source:\n- Stale version references: `.agent/work/3457/11/contract.json:74` and `.agent/work/3457/11/completion.json:7,42` name only `20260925222432`; the retired `20260925175038`/`20260924174155` appear nowhere in `supabase/migrations/` or `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/` (grep).\n- Duplicate preview fixture: `supabase/migrations/20260713221518_dam_hybrid_search_foundation.sql:33-42` is `search_tsv ... generated always ... stored`; the `.agent/work/3457/1/behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql` hunk in the packet patch now inserts without `search_tsv` and its T3 fixture is genuinely semantic-only (title `alpha beta gamma delta`, query `zz3457 sem low`).\n- Exactly one evidence pair is added (inventory in the packet manifest §3).\n\n## Findings\n\n### High\n\n**H1 — The one artifact that can falsify the change's core claim is still unexecuted, and the in-repo pin cannot falsify it.** The migration's defining property is that the floor is applied *only* inside the semantic leg. The in-repo assertion is string presence in the function definition — `supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:128-134` (`position('min_semantic_score' …)`, `position('p_min_semantic_score' …)`, `position('p.min_semantic_score is null' …)`) and the identical T8 block at `supabase/tests/popdam_semantic_score_floor_behavior.sql:31-34`. A body that floored the semantic leg *and* re-filtered after the blend still contains all three literals. The only falsifying artifact is `supabase/tests/popdam_semantic_score_floor_behavior.sql`, and the packet manifest §5 states plainly: **\"No tests were run for this packet.\"** Static reading agrees the placement is correct (`20260925222432...sql:59-60` in `semantic_candidates`, keyword arm `:43-53` and blend `having` `:69` untouched, null floor short-circuits to TRUE), but that is my reading, not evidence.\n\n**H2 — Version-ordering / immutability hazard that I cannot clear with the tools I hold.** The change is one added migration plus a verification sidecar that the repo treats as a mandatory artifact per version: `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925222432.json:1-19` and its declaration at `config/production-verification-sidecar-registry.json:244-247`. The reviewed head is **not** the commit on `main` — `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json` changes `detector_source_sha256` and `total_migration_files` 674→708 in the same commit, i.e. the branch edits an artifact whose contract is a function of the merged migration set. The evidence supplied also states the version was deliberately moved backwards (\"version supersession to 20260925222432 (backdated version guard)\"), and this repository has two guards aimed exactly at that (`scripts/check-sql.sh:185-286` Guard B against the base branch, `:288-485` Guard B2 against a live ledger). Whether Guard B/B2 passed for this version, and whether `20260925222432` sorts after `main`'s newest version and after the newest applied version in preview/production, is **not verifiable from this snapshot** — I have no git history, no network, and no ledger. Per the evidence boundary I will not infer it. This needs an explicit, source-backed statement from the author lane (guard output plus the comparison version) before merge.\n\n### Medium\n\n**M1 — Two assertions that decide whether the floor exists at all are global `count(*)`, not fixture-scoped, and share a live corpus.** `supabase/tests/popdam_semantic_score_floor_behavior.sql:242-252` and `:256-267` assert `count(*) = 0` over a query with no `entity_id` scope. The fixtures deliberately write rows with *underived* embeddings — `:81-84` inserts `array_fill(0.5, [384])` and `:105-118` inserts `array_fill(0.0,[384])` for sem-high before the later `update`s — so if the basis vectors stay as inserted (no `update` matching, or a re-run that skips fixtures), every fixture row would sit in the semantic leg for *any* non-null `qemb` and pass. That the suite passes only because the updates succeed is a fixture-integrity gap, not a proven pass. (Whether the updates actually match is decided by `order of statements within one rolled-back transaction`, which I cannot run.)\n\n**M2 — Most behaviour calls pass `qemb` without pinning `p_document_types`, so ambient rows decide the counts on the shared ephemeral database.** `supabase/tests/popdam_semantic_score_floor_behavior.sql:142-147, 214-217, 259-267, 280-282`. With a non-null query embedding the semantic leg's only predicates are `p_document_types is null or …` and `d.embedding is not null` (`20260925222432...sql:57-58`), so any pre-existing `dam_search_documents` row whose embedding scores at or above the floor participates. `supabase/tests/ci-quarantine.txt:66` records that this lane's database carries real DAM assets (\"the facets are computed from deployed DAM assets and style groups; an empty database has none and none may be invented\"). Every one of these assertions should be scoped to the fixture `entity_id`s, exactly as T2/T3/T4 already are (`:157-190`). Same class as the dossier's earlier T6 note, but it applies to T1/T5/T6/T7 in one file.\n\n**M3 — The evidence binding does not describe the tree under review.** `.agent/work/3457/11/completion.json:12` records `head_sha: 5c6851b13c22a3e4360f38f6c9e779cf73efaa56` while the authorised head is `b527a80e…`; the sidecar's `migration_sha256` (`…fd68e575…`) and the contract's `contract_sha256` (`dcfeb653…`) are well-formed but **I cannot recompute either** (no execution), and all five reported check outcomes (`completion.json:36-60`) plus the `total_count`/`total_migrations` change in the baseline are taken as reported. Since the generation-11 fix *also* synchronised the behaviour fixture in the same tree, I cannot confirm that the reported green run covered the code being reviewed. This is the same class of finding recorded against generation 10 in the supplied comment history.\n\n### Low / informational\n\n- **L1 — Floor placement and clamp are pinned only textually, and the comment is silent on the clamp.** `20260925222432...sql:31-32` maps `1.5→1.0` and negatives `→0.0` (NaN clamps to 1.0, fail-closed) whereas the comment at `:139-140` documents the floor's effect only. T6 covers the numeric cases (`behavior.sql:238-267`).\n- **L2 — `LIMIT 20000` now bounds post-filter survivors, not candidates.** `20260925222432...sql:59-61`: with a highly selective floor the leg can return far fewer than 20 000 rows even when qualifying documents exist beyond the HNSW window, and `total_count` (`:121-127`) reports the small number faithfully rather than as truncation. Not asserted anywhere; worth one comment line.\n- **L3 — The distance is computed three times per surviving row** (`:56` projection, `:60` filter, `:61` ordering) and the filter copy is wrapped in `greatest`, which normally blocks the planner from commoning them up. Bounded by the 20 000 cap.\n- **L4 — Exact-object spelling looseness.** DDL/grants/comment spell `extensions.vector(384)` (`:11, 136-137, 139`) while the probes and the sidecar absence check spell `extensions.vector` without the typmod (`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1055, 1177, 1200`; `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925222432.json:15`). Same type OID — typmod is not part of function identity — so resolution succeeds; textually looser, not a failure.\n- **L5 — ACL completeness gap.** `revoke all … from public, anon` then `grant execute … to authenticated, service_role` (`:136-137`, `:205-208`) is asserted for `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` only (`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:141-148`). Nothing asserts that no *other* grantee (e.g. via `alter default privileges`) holds EXECUTE on the new 8-arg object. Pre-existing pattern; named, not a live hole I can prove.\n- **L6 — `search_style_groups_full_text` was recreated without its immediate predecessor's ordering tail.** The new body (`:199-202`) ends at the final `group by`, while `20260831074401_popdam_ranked_search_entitlement_performance.sql:418-423` ends with `order by max(x.rank) desc, x.style_group_id limit greatest(1,least(coalesce(p_limit,10000),20000))`. The recreated body matches the *earlier* generation (`20260831041629`, per the supplied comment history) and the head CI exercised it, so I am naming the divergence for reconciliation rather than calling it a defect: at least one of the two is not what the author believes.\n- **L7 — Documentation drift reachable from the changed object.** `docs/unified-supabase-schema-map.md:104` still describes `search_dam_documents(query, limit, document_types, query_embedding)`; out of the declared scope, flagged only.\n- **L8 — The behaviour file ships twice** (`supabase/tests/popdam_semantic_score_floor_behavior.sql` and `.agent/work/3457/1/behavior_tests_t1_t8.sql`), byte-identical in the packet patch. Synchronising by hand is what produced the previous `search_tsv` defect; consider a single source.\n- **L9 — Baseline churn is unverifiable here.** `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json:3-6` changes the detector digest and `total_migration_files` 674→708 with `matched_count` unchanged at 103. I can confirm the file changed as claimed; I cannot recompute either digest.\n\n### Mandated checks — explicit conclusions\n\n1. **Index usage — pass, with the loose assumptions named.** Text leg `d.search_tsv @@ any(...)` (`:42`) is served by the GIN index on the generated `search_tsv` (`20260713221518_dam_hybrid_search_foundation.sql:33-42, 54-55`); the `length(q.query_text) >= 3`-guarded ILIKE legs (`:36, 51-52`) are served by the four trgm GINs (`:57-67`); the semantic leg's `order by d.embedding <=> p_query_embedding limit 20000` (`:61`) is eligible for the partial HNSW index whose predicate matches the leg's `d.embedding is not null` (`:69-72` vs `:57`); the style-group expansion join (`:77`) is served by `assets_style_group_id_active_idx`, whose partial predicate `is_deleted = false and style_group_id is not null` matches the query as written (`20260831093107_popdam_ranked_search_keyed_visibility.sql:4-6`); the rest rides `assets`/`dam_search_documents` PKs, `asset_effective_tags` (`:95`) and `admin_config` via `assets_thumbnail_min_date()` (`20260830110517_popdam_effective_asset_filters.sql:203-214`). **The floor predicate itself (`:59-60`) is an expression on a computed distance; no index type can serve it as written, and none is needed** — it is a filter, not a probe, and it is acceptable only because of the `limit 20000` bound, which is exactly why L2 matters. I am also naming the loose assumption explicitly: \"the semantic leg is index-backed\" rests on index *eligibility*, not observed use.\n2. **Function volatility — pass.** `search_dam_documents` is `language sql stable security definer` (`:22`), byte-identical in that clause to the predecessor (`20260901130428…:93`); its body only reads. Callees verified at their definitions: `public.require_dam_access()` plpgsql `stable` (`20260831074401…:4-19`), `public.expand_dam_search_queries(text)` sql `stable` (`20260714173500_dam_search_synonyms.sql:72-78`), `public.assets_thumbnail_min_date()` sql `stable` (`20260830110517…:203-214`). Both recreated wrappers are `language sql stable security definer` (`:146, 155`). No `IMMUTABLE` claim anywhere in reach, and nothing in the change loosens a marker.\n3. **Exact object checks — pass on identity, loose on assertion breadth.** The drop, the create, both revokes/grants, the comment and the recreate calls all name the full schema-qualified routine including `extensions.vector(384)` (`:9-14, 136-140, 144, 153, 205-208`); the absence of the 7-arg overload is asserted exactly by `to_regprocedure(...) is null` (`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:97-101`; sidecar `…json:13-17` with `expected_count: 1`), which fails closed, and the four post-apply probes bind the surviving 8-arg identity (`production_catalog_verification.py:1055, 1066-1068, 1084, 1177-1181, 1199-1204`). The loosenesses are L4 and L5, and the behavioural (as opposed to identity) claims are H1/M2.\n\n### Other review areas — conclusions\n\n- **Roles/permissions:** no new role, policy or RLS change; the only ACL movement is the 8-arg grant plus re-applied wrapper grants (`:136-137, 205-208`), matching the predecessor's shape (`20260901130428…:203-204`). `anon` denial is pinned in both contract files and in the probes. Residual: L5.\n- **Objects/dependencies:** the drop-then-recreate-in-one-transaction sequence for the two SQL-language dependents (`:9-11`) is the correct shape for recorded body dependencies (the two wrappers are the only SQL-body callers of the 7-arg overload I found: `20260831074401…:372, 410-411`), and their bodies are recoverable from history. Trailing `default null` keeps any surviving 7-arg call site bound. Residual: L6.\n- **Migration immutability:** one added migration, no modified migration in the inventory; the retired filenames appear only in historical prose (`HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T1226Z-edge-dev-mimo-orch-successor-3496.md:116`). Unverifiable here: whether `20260925222432` respects the no-backdating guards (H2).\n- **Rollback/recovery:** the file has no `begin`/`commit`, so a failure in any later statement rolls the whole apply back to the 7-arg capability; the drops are non-cascading, so a real dependency aborts rather than silently removing a dependent. No down migration (standard for this repo); the prior bodies remain in `20260901130428…:85-207` and `20260831074401…:367-424`.\n- **Contextual risk worth naming (not a defect in this diff):** the packet records Blacksmith \"all 429 migrations into an empty database applied 363 and…\" failures at earlier heads, and `supabase/tests/ci-quarantine.txt:16-48` documents that this from-empty lane already fails 66 of 429 migrations. That lane cannot certify DDL that depends on a populated database, so the migration's real verification has to be the preview/promotion path and the sidecar.\n\n## Missing evidence I am naming rather than inferring\n\n1. Executed results for `supabase/tests/popdam_semantic_score_floor_behavior.sql` at this head (manifest §5: none run). This is the only falsifier for floor placement and the only coverage for keyword survival and clamp behaviour.\n2. `scripts/check-sql.sh` Guard B / B2 output for version `20260925222432`, and the newest version on `main` and in the live preview/production ledgers, plus confirmation that `main` does not already carry this version and its sidecar.\n3. Recomputable digests: sidecar `migration_sha256` (`fd68e575…`) and `contract_sha256` (`dcfeb653…`), and the regenerated `detector_source_sha256` / `total_migration_files: 708`.\n4. Whether the reported green runs (`completion.json:36-60`) were executed on a tree that includes the T3 fixture and preview-fixture corrections in this head.\n5. Which `dam_search_documents` rows the from-empty/preview database holds (relevant to M1/M2) and what pass-2 replay leaves behind for routines in this chain (`.github/workflows/database-contract-tests.yml:463-546`, `scripts/check_pass2_routine_supersession.py`).\n\n## Bottom line\n\nStatically, the migration does what the contract says: exact signature swap in one transaction, floor confined to the semantic leg before the blend, clamp computed in `params` and — importantly — the *clamped* column is what the leg filters on, null floor behaviour-preserving because the body is otherwise byte-identical to the predecessor, keyword hits surviving with `semantic_rank` null, grants narrowed to `authenticated`/`service_role`, and every predicate the change relies on either keeps a serving index or is explicitly un-indexable. The mandated three checks come out clean, with named loosenesses. What is not clean is the evidence and the fixtures: the one artifact that could falsify placement did not run (H1), the new T1/T5/T6/T7 counting is unscoped against a shared corpus with underived fixture embeddings (M1/M2), the binding records a different head than the one under review (M3), and the version-ordering/immutability question around a deliberately backdated version carrying a mandatory sidecar cannot be answered with what I hold (H2). That is a revise-and-resubmit, not a rejection of the design.\n\nVERDICT: REVISE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n## Coverage and method\n\nI read the full new migration, the predecessor definitions it derives from, both wrapper definitions it replaces, the modified contract tests, the catalog probes, the sidecar and registry, the baseline file, and the CI quarantine list. I did not run anything (no execution), so all runtime and hash claims are treated as reported, not observed.\n\nEvidence base actually opened: `supabase/migrations/20260925222432_popdam_search_semantic_score_floor.sql` (all 208 lines), `supabase/migrations/20260831074401_popdam_ranked_search_entitlement_performance.sql:1-22,360-434`, `supabase/migrations/20260831041629_popdam_authorized_ranked_search.sql:120-162`, `supabase/migrations/20260831093107_popdam_ranked_search_keyed_visibility.sql:1-14`, `supabase/migrations/20260713221518_dam_hybrid_search_foundation.sql:1-120`, `supabase/migrations/20260714173500_dam_search_synonyms.sql:60-100`, `supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:85-370`, `supabase/tests/ci-quarantine.txt`, `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1140-1215` (+ grep of every `search_dam_documents` occurrence), `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925222432.json`, `config/production-verification-sidecar-registry.json:230-249`, `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json:1-12`, plus `list_dir` of `.agent/work/3457` (contains only `1/` and `13/`). The authored tests are quoted verbatim in the conversation's packet patch (`@@ -0,0 +1,332 @@`), so I cite them from there; the file itself is byte-identical per the same patch.\n\nWhat checks out statically: the floor is confined to `semantic_candidates` before the blend (`20260925222432…sql:54-61`), the clamp is computed in `params` and the *clamped* column is what the leg filters on (`:31-32` → `:59-60`), the keyword arm and blend are untouched (`:43-53`, `:62-69`), the 8-arg identity is spelled exactly in DDL/grant/comment (`:13-19`, `:136-137`, `:139-140`), the 7-arg absence is asserted fail-closed by `to_regprocedure(...) is null` plus `expected_count: 1` (`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:97-101`, sidecar `:12-17`), wrappers are dropped before the 7-arg drop to satisfy recorded body dependencies (`:9-11`), and the final evidence set is exactly one pair (`list_dir .agent/work/3457` → `1/`, `13/` only).\n\n## Findings\n\n### High\n\n**H1 — T3's \"semantic-only\" fixture is not semantic-only: its `path` is inside `search_tsv`, so the keyword leg returns the row and the assertion fails.**\nThe sem-low fixture is written with title `'alpha beta gamma delta'` but path `'zz3457-sem-low.ai'` (`supabase/tests/popdam_semantic_score_floor_behavior.sql`, packet patch lines ≈89-92). `search_tsv` is generated from `title || path || customer || program || search_text` (`20260713221518_dam_hybrid_search_foundation.sql:33-42`), and the `simple` configuration's parser splits hyphenated/dotted strings into their parts, so that row's tsvector contains the lexemes `zz3457`, `sem` and `low`. The keyword leg is `d.search_tsv @@ any(array(select q.tsq from queries q))` (`20260925222432…sql:41-42`) and the query `'zz3457 sem low'` becomes `zz3457 & sem & low` (packet patch ≈ line 134). The row therefore enters `keyword_candidates`, survives with `semantic_rank = null`, and T3's first assertion — `count(*) = 0` under `floor = 0.5` for asset `…012`, else `raise exception 'T3 FAIL: semantic-only below-floor doc was not removed'` (packet patch ≈ lines 171-176) — goes red. The file's own header claims the opposite (\"does not keyword-match query `'zz3457 sem low'`\", packet patch ≈ lines 4-8) and attributes the verification to the synonym expansion only, which is not where the tokens come from. This is the same class of defect earlier rounds fixed by changing the *title*; the *path* was left in the tsvector. Fix: give the sem-low fixture a path/title with no token overlap with its query (as the sibling docs already do for `zz3457-kw-only`), or scope the assertion to `semantic_rank is not null`.\nThis also puts the claimed CI result in direct tension: T1–T8 PASS at implementation SHA `4fe70ee7` is asserted (`completion.json` checks block, `.agent/work/3457/13/completion.json`) but that claim is author-supplied, and the packet's own manifest states no tests were run for this packet. One of the two is wrong and only execution can say which; at minimum the fixture must be corrected and the run repeated.\n\n### Medium\n\n**M2 — the recreated `search_style_groups_full_text` silently loses the `ORDER BY … LIMIT` tail of the version it replaces, so `p_limit` is ignored and result order is unspecified.**\nThe version being replaced ends with `order by max(x.rank) desc,x.style_group_id limit greatest(1,least(coalesce(p_limit,10000),20000))` (`20260831074401_popdam_ranked_search_entitlement_performance.sql:418-423`; the earlier generation had the same tail at `20260831041629_popdam_authorized_ranked_search.sql:150-153`). The recreated body ends at `group by c.style_group_id;` with no ordering and no limit (`20260925222432…sql:194-202`). Consequences: the wrapper no longer honours `p_limit` (it returns every rolled-up group), the deterministic ranking callers previously got is gone, and the top-N bound is removed from a path that a live workload calls with an explicit limit (`docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260904T212459Z/run1/pg-stat-statements-top300.csv:862,1030`). No assertion in the change can catch it: the only checks on this wrapper are `position('max(d.rank)*0.8' …)` and \"`search_dam_documents` appears exactly once\" (`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:167-175`), both of which still pass with the tail deleted. This is an undeclared behavioural change in a function the contract lists as a dependency, and it is not in `db_writes`.\n\n**M3 — nothing in the change asserts that the floor exists, or where it is applied.**\nThe in-repo pin is literal presence in `pg_get_functiondef` — `position('min_semantic_score' …)`, `position('p_min_semantic_score' …)`, `position('p.min_semantic_score is null' …)` (`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:128-134`) — and T8 repeats the same three literal checks (packet patch, T8 block). A body that applied the floor inside the semantic leg *and* re-filtered after the blend contains all three strings, and the clamp is not asserted at all. The post-apply sidecar picks the forward contract `popdam_ranked_search_rank_keys_through_visibility_v4` (`scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925222432.json:7-11`), whose body (`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1183-1205`) asserts rank-key projection, `require_dam_access`, `statement_timeout`, and grants — nothing about `p_min_semantic_score`, keyword survival, or `semantic_rank null`. So the only post-apply artifact that could falsify misplacement is the behaviour file, which is the artifact under H1.\n\n**M4 — the declared write set understates the migration.**\n`db_writes` in both the contract and the completion lists only `function public.search_dam_documents` (`.agent/work/3457/13/contract.json`, `.agent/work/3457/13/completion.json`, both quoted in the packet patch), while the migration drops and recreates two more `security definer` functions with ACLs (`20260925222432…sql:9-10`, `:144-208`). The generation history shows this was a known claim-write gap (\"claim writes update for wrapper functions\" in generations 10–13 goals) and it is still not reflected in `db_writes`. Also `db_reads` lists `public.admin_config` (read two hops away) but omits the `app.profile` / `app.app_access` tables read by `require_dam_access()` (`20260831074401_popdam_ranked_search_entitlement_performance.sql:4-19`) — inconsistent granularity in the same field.\n\n**M5 — evidence binding and version ordering are not verifiable from what I hold.**\n`completion.json` binds `head_sha: 4fe70ee7…` while the reviewed head is `91830a87…`, and every check outcome in it (including the pytest count, the `cmp` of the two behaviour files, and the ephemeral-database run) is reported, not observable here; the packet manifest states plainly that no tests were run for this packet. Likewise the contract's assumption that `20260925222432` sorts after current main max `20260925193145`, and that the migration applies cleanly against a live ledger, needs history and ledger access I do not have. These are gaps to close with evidence, not defects I can assert — but they are exactly the facts that decide deployability, and one of them (Guard B2 / live ledger) is conceded as unrun in the completion itself.\n\n### Low / informational\n\n- **Clamp is silent:** `greatest(0,least(1,p_min_semantic_score))` (`:31-32`) maps `1.5 → 1.0`, negatives → `0.0`, and `NaN` → `1.0` (fail-closed), and the function comment (`:139-140`) documents the floor but not the clamp. T6 covers the numeric cases only.\n- **`LIMIT 20000` now bounds post-filter survivors, not candidates** (`:59-61`): with a selective floor the semantic leg can return far fewer than 20 000 rows even when qualifying documents exist beyond the HNSW window, and `total_count` (`:120-127`) reports the smaller number faithfully rather than signalling truncation. Worth one comment line.\n- **Distance evaluated up to three times per row** (`:56` projection, `:60` filter, `:61` ordering); the filter copy is wrapped in `greatest`, which normally blocks the planner from commoning them up. Bounded by the 20 000 cap.\n- **Exact-object spelling looseness:** the probes and the sidecar absence object spell `extensions.vector` without `(384)` (`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1177,1200`; sidecar `:15`). Typmod is not part of function identity, so resolution succeeds — textually looser than the DDL, not a failure.\n- **ACL completeness gap:** `revoke all … from public, anon` then `grant execute … to authenticated, service_role` (`:136-137`, `:205-208`), asserted only for `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` (`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:141-148`). Nothing asserts that no *other* grantee holds EXECUTE — a live class in this repository, which already carries `supabase/migrations/20260810180000_plm_default_privilege_hole_and_pg17_maintain_revokes.sql` (seen in the migrations listing). The DROP+CREATE at `:9-10`/:144/:153 also discards any pre-existing non-declared grants the wrappers held.\n- **Bare (non-cascading) drop of the 7-arg depends on a complete dependent list** (`:11`). I found the two SQL-body callers and dropped them first (`:9-10`; callers at `20260831074401:372,410-411`), and a repo-wide grep surfaced no other repository object referencing the overload. But `supabase/tests/ci-quarantine.txt:23-29` records that this repository was adopted on top of an already-populated database and carries `supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql` schema that no migration creates; I did not open that file, so I cannot rule out another dependent there or in production. Unverified, named.\n- **Documentation drift reachable from the changed object:** `docs/unified-supabase-schema-map.md:104` still describes `search_dam_documents(query, limit, document_types, query_embedding)`. Out of the declared scope, flagged only.\n- **Baseline churn is not recomputable here:** `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-baseline-20260828.json:3,5` changes the detector digest and `total_migration_files` 674→708 with `matched_count` unchanged at 103. Confirmed as changed; digests not verifiable without execution.\n\n## Mandatory checks\n\n1. **Index usage — pass, with the un-indexable predicate named.** `d.search_tsv @@ any(...)` (`20260925222432…sql:41-42`) is served by the GIN index on the generated tsvector (`20260713221518…sql:33-42,54-55`). The four ILIKE legs are guarded by `length(q.query_text) >= 3` (`:36`) and backed by the title/path/customer/program trgm GINs (`20260713221518…sql:57-67`). The semantic ordering `order by d.embedding <=> p_query_embedding limit 20000` (`:61`) is eligible for the partial HNSW index (`20260713221518…sql:69-72`) whose predicate `embedding is not null` matches the leg's join condition (`:57`). The style-group expansion join `a.style_group_id = c.style_group_id and not a.is_deleted` (`:77`) is served by `assets_style_group_id_active_idx` with predicate `is_deleted = false and style_group_id is not null` (`20260831093107_popdam_ranked_search_keyed_visibility.sql:4-6`). The new floor predicate `greatest(0,1-(d.embedding <=> p_query_embedding)) >= p.min_semantic_score` (`:59-60`) is an expression over a computed distance: **no index type can serve it as written**, and none is needed because it is a filter rather than a probe — acceptable *only* because of the `limit 20000` bound, which is why the recall-cliff note above matters. The loose assumption is explicit: \"the semantic leg is index-backed\" rests on index *eligibility*, not on observed use.\n2. **Function volatility — correct where I could read the body; one callee unverified.** The changed function is `language sql stable security definer` (`:22`), correct for a read-only, table-reading body; both recreated wrappers are likewise `stable` (`:146`, `:155`). Callees verified at their definitions: `public.require_dam_access()` plpgsql `stable` (`20260831074401:4-8`), `public.expand_dam_search_queries(text)` sql `stable` (`20260714173500_dam_search_synonyms.sql:74-76`). I located but did not read `public.assets_thumbnail_min_date()` (definition at `20260830110517` and `20260827183011`); its marker is **not verified in this round** and I will not assert it. No `IMMUTABLE` claim exists anywhere in reach, so there is no over-strong marker to falsify.\n3. **Exact object checks — exact on identity, weak on behaviour.** The drop, create, revoke/grant, comment, and both wrapper recreate calls name the fully qualified routine including `extensions.vector(384)` (`:11`, `:13-19`, `:136-140`, `:144`, `:153`, `:205-208`); the 7-arg absence is asserted exactly and fails closed (`supabase/tests/popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:97-101`, sidecar `:12-17` with `expected_count: 1`); all four post-apply probes bind the surviving 8-arg identity (`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:1055,1066-1068,1084,1177-1181,1199-1204`) and `scripts/test_production_catalog_verification.py:2169-2172,2308-2312,2470-2487` were updated with them. The looseness is the type-spelling nit above and the fact that the *behavioural* property the change exists to deliver is pinned only by string presence (M3).\n\n## Other review areas\n\n- **Roles and permissions:** no new role, policy, RLS or grant target is introduced; the only ACL movement is the 8-arg grant plus re-applied wrapper ACLs (`:136-137`, `:205-208`), matching the predecessor shape (`20260901130428:203-204`). `anon` denial is pinned in both test files (`:141-148`; `popdam_ranked_filter_parity_contracts.sql:31-35`) and in the probes. Residual: ACL completeness (Low above). The DAM gate is retained at `:33` and the function remains `security definer` with `search_path` pinned (`:22-24`).\n- **Objects and dependencies:** the drop-then-recreate ordering for the two SQL-language dependents is the right shape for recorded body dependencies, and their 7-arg call sites rebind to the 8-arg through the trailing default (`:17-18`). Residual: the completeness of the dependent list, and M2's body divergence for one of them.\n- **Migration immutability:** one added migration, no modified migration in the inventory; the retired `20260924174155`/`20260925175038` filenames did not appear in any grep I ran over `supabase/migrations`. The no-backdating question is M5.\n- **Rollback/recovery:** the file contains no `begin`/`commit` (I read all 208 lines), so a failure anywhere rolls the whole apply back to the 7-arg capability; the drops are non-cascading, so a real dependency aborts rather than silently removing a dependent; no down migration is shipped (repo pattern), and the prior bodies remain recoverable from `20260901130428:85-207` and `20260831074401:367-424`.\n- **Evidence pair count:** `.agent/work/3457` contains only `1/` and `13/` (`list_dir`), consistent with the brief's claim that generation 13 is the only final pair.\n\n## Missing evidence I am naming rather than inferring\n\n1. Executed results for `supabase/tests/popdam_semantic_score_floor_behavior.sql` at the reviewed head, including the T3 block — the packet manifest says no tests were run, while the completion asserts T1–T8 PASS at `4fe70ee7`, and H1 makes those two statements mutually exclusive. This needs a rerun after the fixture fix.\n2. The identity of `4fe70ee7` versus `91830a87` (evidence-only tail or not), and the byte-equality of the two behaviour files as `cmp` claims — no history access.\n3. Guard B/B2 output for `20260925222432`, and the newest version in the live preview/production ledgers.\n4. Recomputable digests: sidecar `migration_sha256` (`fd68e575…`), `contract_sha256` (`e84c4c63…`), and the regenerated `detector_source_sha256` / `total_migration_files: 708`.\n5. Whether `supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql` (referenced from `supabase/tests/ci-quarantine.txt:23-25`) or any production object holds another recorded dependent on the 7-arg overload, and whether an `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` rule over `public` functions exists that the revoke at `:136` does not cover.\n6. The volatility marker of `public.assets_thumbnail_min_date()`.\n7. Which `supabase/tests/*.sql` files the CI lane quarantines today (the list I read does not contain this new file, but I cannot verify the live runner's selection).\n\n## Bottom line\n\nStatically, the migration does what the contract says: exact signature swap in one transaction, floor confined to the semantic leg before the blend, clamped value computed in `params` and consumed by the leg, null floor behaviour-preserving by construction, keyword hits surviving with `semantic_rank null`, grants narrowed to `authenticated`/`service_role`, and every predicate the change relies on either keeping a serving index or being explicitly and justifiably un-indexable. The three mandatory checks come out clean with the named loosenesses. What is not clean: the T3 fixture is not the \"semantic-only\" document it claims to be, because the path it was given is inside the generated tsvector (H1); the recreated style-group wrapper loses the `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` tail of the function it replaces, so `p_limit` is now ignored (M2); no artifact in the change asserts that the floor exists or where it is applied (M3); the declared write set omits the two wrapper functions (M4); and the version-ordering, tree-identity, hash-binding and execution evidence are all unverifiable from the sealed source (M5). That is a revise-and-resubmit, not a rejection of the design.\n\nVERDICT: REVISE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n# Governed review: popcre/shared-db PR #3489 (issue #3457), head `6c85a2b3`, gen-14 contract\n\nRead in full: the migration, both T1–T8 copies, both modified contract tests, sidecar + registry, all `search_dam_documents` probes, predecessor wrapper definitions, foundation index/tsvector DDL, REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### Findings and reasoning (everything the reviewer said before its verdict)\n\nI'll start with the sealed MANIFEST and the offloaded prompt sections so the review is against the exact assigned head.Generation 15 is the T3 fixture rename after Muse H1. I’ll read the migration, tests, contract pair, and sidecar next and keep a provisional REVISE until those checks close.T3 title/path are now `cerulean lampstone`; next I’ll confirm token overlap, wrappers, probes, sidecar hash, and the three mandatory gates.Provisional verdict: **APPROVE**. Generation 15 fixes Muse generation-14 H1 in source: the T3 title and path no longer share query tokens, the no-embedding exclusion and null-floor control remain, and the migration body is unchanged.\n\nReviewed head `ef7fd917ae84eafd0c8830414ea0716050b064a6` against base `15f18e1bbfe0e6db41a1dee21e404b425d6459f9`. Opened the migration, predecessor `20260901130428`, both wrapper predecessors, foundation tsvector/indexes, `expand_dam_search_queries`, all three callee volatility definitions, both T1–T8 copies, both contract tests, sidecar, registry, catalog probes, and the generation-15 evidence pair. Packet ran no tests; hash and CI claims are reported, not observed.\n\n## Generation-14 H1 — resolved in source\n\nT3’s document is title `'cerulean lampstone canvas'` / path `'cerulean-lampstone.ai'` (`supabase/tests/popdam_semantic_score_floor_behavior.sql:74,95-97`, identical preview copy). Those strings contain none of the query tokens `zz3457`, `sem`, or `low`.\n\n`search_tsv` is `to_tsvector('simple', title || path || customer || program || search_text)` (`20260713221518_dam_hybrid_search_foundation.sql:33-42`). The simple parser yields `cerulean`, `lampstone`, `canvas`, `ai`. Query `'zz3457 sem low'` expands to whole-query variants only (`20260714173500_dam_search_synonyms.sql:72-156`); no synonym row matches those terms (`:41-65`). The tsquery is `zz3457 & sem & low`, and `'%zz3457 sem low%'` misses both title and path.\n\nDirect no-embedding exclusion is retained (`popdam_semantic_score_floor_behavior.sql:202-208`): null `p_query_embedding` empties the semantic join (`20260925222432…sql:57`), so a non-zero count would prove a keyword leak. Null-floor positive control is retained (`:209-215`). Floor `0.5` still expects removal (`:196-201`). Migration bytes are the same 8-arg body as generation 14.\n\n## Findings\n\n**High:** none  \n**Medium:** none\n\n**Low / informational**\n\n- Floor-placement pins remain string presence in `pg_get_functiondef` (`popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:128-134`, T8 at behavior `:28-36`). T3/T4 are the behavioral falsifiers; this packet did not execute them (`MANIFEST` §5). Completion reports ephemeral CI run `36376264683` at implementation SHA `ec76d698…` (`completion.json:68-71`); that run is not in this packet.\n- Sidecar `migration_sha256` `644ce75a…` (`scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260925222432.json:4`) is well-formed; this environment could not recompute LF-canonical SHA-256 of the migration bytes.\n- `completion.json:12` binds implementation head `ec76d698…`; the reviewed evidence-tail is `ef7fd917…`. Several check rows still cite SHA `8ddd5605` and generation-13 log paths (`:39-60`). Documented evidence-tail pattern.\n- Probe/sidecar identities spell `extensions.vector` without `(384)` (e.g. `production_catalog_verification.py:1055`, sidecar `:15`). Typmod is not function identity; resolution succeeds.\n- `revoke … from public, anon` plus grants to `authenticated, service_role` (`20260925222432…sql:136-137,207-210`) is asserted only for those three roles (`popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:141-148`). No assertion that no other grantee holds `EXECUTE`.\n- Clamp `greatest(0,least(1,…))` (`:31-32`) is silent in the function comment (`:139-140`). T6 covers `1.5` and `-0.5` (`behavior.sql:281-307`).\n- `LIMIT 20000` (`:59-61`) bounds post-filter survivors. A selective floor can shrink recall that `total_count` reports as small.\n- Dual T-file copies must stay in sync by hand. They match in this tree (337 lines each).\n\n## Focus areas (verified from source)\n\n**Floor placement and keyword survival.** Floor lives only in `semantic_candidates` (`:54-61`), comparing the clamped `params.min_semantic_score` (`:31-32` → `:59-60`). Keyword arm (`:43-53`) and blend `HAVING` (`:62-69`) are unchanged from `20260901130428:112-136`. Keyword rows enter with `null::real semantic_rank` (`:66`); `max(NULL)` stays null; `coalesce` keeps the keyword rank (`:65`). Null floor short-circuits the conjunct to true.\n\n**Wrappers, 7-arg retirement, three writes.** Dependents drop first (`:9-10`), then the 7-arg (`:11`), then 8-arg create (`:13-18`) with `p_min_semantic_score real default null`. `search_assets_full_text` (`:144-151`) matches `20260831074401:367-374`. `search_style_groups_full_text` ends `order by max(c.rank) desc, c.style_group_id limit greatest(1,least(coalesce(p_limit,10000),20000))` (`:199-204`), matching `20260831074401:418-423`. `db_writes` lists all three functions (`.agent/work/3457/15/contract.json:47-51`, `completion.json:32-36`). Absence of the 7-arg is fail-closed via `to_regprocedure(…) is null` (authorized contracts `:97-101`, T8 `:17-20`, sidecar `:12-17`).\n\n**Grants and entitlement.** `revoke all … from public, anon` then `grant execute … to authenticated, service_role` on the 8-arg and both wrappers (`:136-137,207-210`). `require_dam_access()` remains in `params` (`:33`). Non-DAM denial is still exercised with a 7-arg call that binds through the trailing default (`popdam_authorized_ranked_search_contracts.sql:339-343`).\n\n**Sidecar, registry, evidence pair.** Sidecar `20260925222432.json` carries forward contract `popdam_ranked_search_rank_keys_through_visibility_v4` and 7-arg `catalog_absence`. Registry entry `version: \"20260925222432\"`, `issue: 3457` (`config/production-verification-sidecar-registry.json:244-247`). Diff adds only `.agent/work/3457/15/{contract,completion}.json`. Retired versions `20260924174155` / `20260925175038` are absent from migrations, sidecars, and tests. New version `20260925222432` is later than main max `20260925193145`. One added migration, zero modified migrations. Catalog probes bind the 8-arg identity (`production_catalog_verification.py:1055,1066-1068,1084,1177-1181,1199-1204`).\n\n**Rollback.** The file has no inner `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`; a failed statement rolls back to the 7-arg capability. Drops are non-`CASCADE`. Prior bodies remain in `20260901130428` and `20260831074401`.\n\n## Mandatory checks\n\n**1. Index usage — pass, with the unindexable predicate named.**  \n`d.search_tsv @@ any(...)` (`:42`) is served by GIN `idx_dam_search_documents_tsv` (`20260713221518:54-55`). `length(q.query_text) >= 3` ILIKE legs (`:36,51-52`) are served by the four trgm GINs (`:57-67`). Semantic `order by d.embedding <=> p_query_embedding limit 20000` (`:61`) is eligible for partial HNSW `idx_dam_search_documents_embedding_hnsw` whose predicate `embedding is not null` matches the join (`:69-72` vs `:57`). Style-group expansion (`:77`) is served by `assets_style_group_id_active_idx` (`20260831093107:4-6`). Tag filter (`:95`) is served by `asset_effective_tags_asset_tag_scope_uidx` / `asset_effective_tags_tag_asset_idx` (`20260830110517:24-28`). The floor predicate `greatest(0,1-(d.embedding <=> …)) >= p.min_semantic_score` (`:59-60`) is a computed-distance filter; no index can serve it as written. Acceptable only under the `LIMIT 20000` bound. HNSW backing is eligibility; the repo advisor records that index unused (`docs/verification/database-efficiency/20260904T212459Z/run1/advisors-performance.json:8164`).\n\n**2. Function volatility — pass.**  \n`search_dam_documents` is `language sql stable security definer` (`:22`); table-reading body, not `IMMUTABLE`. Wrappers are `STABLE` (`:146,155`). Callees at definition: `require_dam_access()` plpgsql `STABLE` (`20260831074401:4-8`), `expand_dam_search_queries(text)` sql `STABLE` (`20260714173500:74-76`), `assets_thumbnail_min_date()` sql `STABLE` (`20260830110517:203-206`). No over-strong marker in reach.\n\n**3. Exact object checks — pass on identity.**  \nDrop, create, revoke, grant, and comment use the full `extensions.vector(384)` identities (`:9-18,136-140,144,153,205-210`). 7-arg absence uses `to_regprocedure(…) is null` with sidecar `expected_count: 1`. 8-arg presence uses `to_regprocedure` / `::regprocedure` in T8, authorized contracts, parity contracts, and all four catalog probes. Named looseness is the typmod spelling and the textual floor pins above.\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\n\nVERDICT: APPROVE The reviewer findings are kept below with every parseable decision line voided. Acting on them requires a fresh governed review at this head.\n\n**Provisional verdict:** lean REVISE — migration body is sound, but the PR's only live test evidence is unrunnable as written and nothing was executed.\n\n## Coverage\n\nRead in full: `supabase/migrations/20260924174251_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql` (all 253 lines), `.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql` (all 208 lines), `caller_contract.md`, `contract.json`, `completion.json`, the derived-from legacy source `supabase/migrations/20260917005221_popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue.sql` (function body lines 81–235), the production pin `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:4604-4625`, and table DDLs (queue/table definitions in `20260917005221:29-39`, `20260905104802:192-286`, `style_guide_files` baseline `010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:2184-2204`). No tests were run for this packet (per MANIFEST §5) and this session has no shell — all verification below is by inspection.\n\n## Findings — High\n\n**H1. Behavior-test fixture is invalid as written, and no test was ever executed — the PR has zero executed coverage.**\n`.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql:20-30` (`pg_temp.mk_sg_file`) explicitly inserts `licensor_name`, but that column is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (split_part(relative_path,'/',1)) STORED` (`010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:2202`) — the insert errors. It also omits `basename_no_ext` and `normalized_name`, both `NOT NULL` without defaults (`010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:2191,2195`). The committed contract test for the same table confirms the correct shape: it derives licensor from the path and supplies both columns (`supabase/tests/popsg_bounded_crawl_and_search_contracts.sql:18-32`, comment at :21-22). So test 4 (the only live proof of the change-night queue drain) cannot pass as committed, and per MANIFEST §5 it was never run. Require the fixture fix plus one real execution (at minimum the `search`-step portion, which is runnable inside a transaction) before merge.\n\n## Findings — Medium\n\n**M1. Catalog self-check pins less than the constraints require; constraint 1 rests on structure + an external contract, not on any in-PR assertion.**\nThe `do $verify$` block (`20260924174251:202-253`) checks both overloads exist (exact `to_regprocedure` signatures — good) and the new overload's grants plus body-shape substrings, but it does not assert `md5(prosrc)` of the legacy 2-arg body, `prosecdef`/`search_path` of the new overload, or the `sgfolders_licensor_property_uidx` precondition for CONCURRENTLY. The substring `position(...)` checks are shape heuristics, not exact-object assertions (they would also match inside a comment). I verified constraint 1 structurally myself — the migration contains no DDL addressing the 2-arg body (only a `comment on`, lines 193-194, which does not affect `prosrc`), and the external pin `md5(prosrc)='52b676f90e4500dc323c2f9e6e6f3c97'` lives in `production_catalog_verification.py:4618-4621` — but nothing in the PR would fail loudly if the legacy body were ever touched. Consider adding one `prosecdef` assertion for the new overload and a legacy-md5 assertion to the verify block.\n\n**M2. `refresh_completed_at` is stamped on every `search` call, including non-final partial batches.**\n`20260924174251:175-182` stamps unconditionally on `search`/`all` regardless of whether the queue drained. The caller loop (`caller_contract.md:51-58`) stops on a partial batch, so on a change night the run records completion-stamp after the first batch while thousands of files remain unsynced. Lifecycle completion is caller-gated so this is not a correctness bug, but the stamp no longer means \"refresh work finished\" — worth one clarifying sentence in the contract, since downstream readers (and the CHECK-gated `completed` transition) may assume it does.\n\n## Findings — Low / observations\n\n**L1. Concurrent callers on the same `p_run_id` double-count.** Candidates are selected with plain `order by ... limit` and no locking (`20260924174251:99-100`), so two concurrent `search` calls process overlapping rows; upserts are idempotent but `search_documents_synced` accumulates twice (lines 175-182). Inherited verbatim from the legacy body, not introduced here — noting for the record.\n\n**L2. `search` with `v_batch = 0` (batch ≤ 0) skips the sync but still stamps completion** (lines 61, 175). Same as legacy. A caller passing 0 marks freshness without syncing. Consider refusing non-positive batch on the `search` step or documenting it.\n\n**L3. CONCURRENTLY legality depends on one-RPC-statement-per-step; callers must not wrap steps in an explicit transaction.** The design is correct — a single-statement RPC is an implicit transaction, in which `REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY` is legal (this is also why the legacy function works in production and why the tests correctly avoid executing matview steps inside `BEGIN`, `behavior_tests.sql:185-186`). But `caller_contract.md` never states the prohibition, and wrapping the three steps in one transaction would fail at the first refresh. One sentence would close this.\n\n**L4. Index usage (mandatory check): all serving indexes exist; one predicate deliberately has none.** Queue→files→documents→pdf_text joins all hit PKs (`20260917005221:29-32` queue PK; `style_guide_files`, `search_documents`, `pdf_text` PKs per baseline/`20260905104802`); `order by q.style_guide_file_id limit` is served by the queue PK; run updates are by PK. The retire predicate `q.queued_at < v_started` (line 152) has no index — acceptable: the queue is narrow and churn-heavy, and the anti-join probe dominates anyway. The `(p_run_id is null or f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id)` filter needs no index because the queue (not a files scan) drives the plan. No loose index assumptions found.\n\n**L5. Volatility (mandatory check): correct.** Both overloads declare no volatility marker, so both are VOLATILE — correct for bodies that refresh matviews and write tables. No IMMUTABLE/STABLE mislabeling anywhere in the change, including the `pg_temp` helper.\n\n**L6. Exact-object checks (mandatory check): adequate but partial.** `to_regprocedure` with fully quantified signatures (migration lines 207-212; behavior tests 49-60) asserts exact overloads, not mere names. Grants are asserted per-role for the new overload (migration 219-226; tests 61-67) and definer posture for legacy (tests 195-202). Gaps are M1 above; the `has_function_privilege('public', ...)` idiom at line 224 matches established repo precedent (e.g. `20260902031743:79`) and is valid.\n\n**L7. Security posture: clean.** No dynamic SQL; `p_step` appears only in static comparisons and a `%`-format RAISE (lines 39-43) — no injection surface. `SECURITY DEFINER` + `SET search_path TO 'public'` matches legacy (lines 28-30 vs legacy 89-91). Unknown/NULL `p_step` raises before any run-state write (validation at 39-43 precedes the update at 45) — fail-closed. `CREATE OR REPLACE` on a new signature plus explicit revoke-from-public/anon/authenticated and grant-to-service_role-only (196-199) correctly neutralizes the default PUBLIC execute grant. No timeout GUC anywhere. `completion.json` head (`73420801`) vs PR head (`5918e171`) is explained by the documented evidence-rebind commit; implementation files attested unchanged.\n\n## Verdict\n\n> VOIDED REVIEWER LINE - REVISE for one concrete reason (H1): fix the `mk_sg_file` fixture (drop explicit `licensor_name`, add `basename_no_ext`/`normalized_name`) and execute the behavior tests at least through the live `search`-step drain; optionally adopt M1 (legacy-md5 + prosecdef assertions) and the one-line caller warnings (M2/L3). The migration logic itself — step gating, stamp-on-search-only, grants, definer/search_path, CONCURRENTLY-per-statement design — is correct as written.\n\n> VOIDED REVIEWER LINE - VERDICT: REVISE 5918e1716cf6b15336179f0d0165f39f79cfdf59\n\n> VERDICT LINE VOIDED BY THE GOVERNED REVIEW RUNNER.\n>\n> 2 line(s) that a verdict parser would have read as a decision (REVISE) at this head were rewritten so that no tool can read them as a verdict. Details below.\n\n## Coverage\n\nFiles read (all line ranges refer to the snapshot in this review directory):\n\n- `supabase/migrations/20260924174251_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql` (full, 1–253) — the new 3-arg overload, grants, self-check.\n- `supabase/migrations/20260917005221_popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue.sql` (full, 1–254) — the `derived-from` source; legacy 2-arg body (81–235) used as the byte-identity reference.\n- `.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql` (full, 1–208) — the 6 committed behavior checks.\n- `.agent/work/3458/1/caller_contract.md` (full, 1–76), `contract.json` (full), `completion.json` (full).\n- `supabase/migrations/20260905104802_popsg_bounded_reconcile_pdf_text_and_search.sql` (1–200, 230–287, 940–1051) — table DDLs, legacy grants (977–980), index/CONCURRENTLY preconditions.\n- `supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql` (2173–2204) — `style_guide_crawl_runs` / `style_guide_files` baseline DDL including the generated column.\n- `supabase/migrations/20260723170000_popsg_file_tags.sql` (94–96) — `tag_names` / `tag_search_text` nullability.\n- `supabase/tests/popsg_bounded_crawl_and_search_contracts.sql` (1–120) — the existing (correct) fixture pattern for comparison.\n- `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py` (4604–4625) — the pinned `popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue_v1` contract, including `md5(p.prosrc)='52b676f90e4500dc323c2f9e6e6f3c97'` for the legacy 2-arg form.\n- `docs/verification/database-efficiency/.../run1/indexes.csv` — index inventory (`idx_sgf_crawl_run_id`, PKs).\n\nNo tests were run in this packet (per MANIFEST §5); all findings below are from code reading.\n\n## Findings — blocking\n\n### 1. Committed behavior-test fixture cannot execute, so check 4 is not evidence\n\n[behavior_tests.sql:11–32](/.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql)\n\n- The helper inserts `licensor_name` explicitly (line 22), but that column is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (split_part(relative_path, '/', 1)) STORED` ([baseline:2202](/supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:2202)). Postgres rejects explicit writes to a generated column, so every `mk_sg_file` call fails.\n- The same insert omits `basename_no_ext` and `normalized_name`, both `NOT NULL` with no default ([baseline:2191,2195](/supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:2191)). That is a second, independent null-violation failure.\n- The repo already documents the correct pattern: the existing contracts test notes the generated column and omits it while supplying `basename_no_ext` and `normalized_name` ([contracts:18–32](/supabase/tests/popsg_bounded_crawl_and_search_contracts.sql:18)). The new fixture does the opposite.\n- Impact: check 4 (change-night search batches, queue drain, stamp assertions, lines 124–178) — the only live-execution check in the file — cannot run. Checks 0–3, 5, 6 are catalog/substring asserts and do run, but the PR's core claim (bounded batches drain 25 files, each statement bounded) has no executable proof. Fix the fixture to match the contracts-test column list.\n\n### 2. Neither the migration self-check nor the behavior tests pin the legacy body hash\n\n- Hard constraint 1 requires the legacy 2-arg body to stay byte-identical, with `md5(prosrc)` pinned by `popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue_v1` ([verification:4618–4621](/scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:4618)).\n- The migration `do $verify$` block ([migration:202–253](/supabase/migrations/20260924174251_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:202)) only asserts `to_regprocedure(...) is null` for the legacy signature (existence, not content), privilege posture of the *new* overload only, and substring presence inside the *new* body. It never computes `md5(prosrc)` for either overload.\n- Behavior test 2 ([behavior_tests.sql:96–105](/)) likewise checks only substrings (`CONCURRENT refresh missing`, `queue scan`, `reactivation clause`); test 6 ([behavior_tests.sql:195–202](/)) checks only grants/definer posture. A legacy rewrite preserving those substrings would pass both.\n- Structurally the constraint does hold in this diff (the migration file contains no `CREATE` for the 2-arg form, only a `COMMENT ON` at lines 193–194, which does not alter `prosrc`), but the in-PR verification does not prove it. Add an `md5(prosrc) = '52b676f90e4500dc323c2f9e6e6f3c97'` assertion for the legacy overload (and fail closed if the pin ever rotates), rather than restating the DDL via substrings.\n\n## Findings — medium\n\n### 3. `search` with an empty/zero batch still stamps the run complete\n\n[migration:61,175–182](/supabase/migrations/20260924174251_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:61)\n\n- The search block is gated on `v_batch > 0`, but the completion stamp (`refresh_completed_at`, accumulator) is gated only on `v_step in ('all','search')`. A `search` call with `p_search_batch_size = 0` (or negative, clamped to 0 at line 33) syncs nothing yet stamps `refresh_completed_at` and (with `+0`) closes the run while the queue is still full.\n- Stamping on a genuinely empty queue is intended ([caller_contract.md:60–62](/)), but a zero-batch call against a non-empty queue is indistinguishable from it. Gate the stamp on `v_batch > 0`, or on the queue being empty for the run, so a degenerate batch cannot close out real work.\n\n### 4. Concurrent callers on the same `p_run_id` double-count the accumulator\n\n[migration:101–143,175–182](/supabase/migrations/20260924174251_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:101)\n\n- Two simultaneous `search` calls select overlapping candidates (no `SKIP LOCKED` / claim step). The upsert itself is idempotent via `ON CONFLICT`, but each call adds its own `v_synced` to `search_documents_synced`, so the same documents are counted twice. `refresh_completed_at` is last-writer-wins. Two concurrent matview-step callers can also collide on `REFRESH CONCURRENTLY` of the same matview.\n- The nightly caller is single-threaded per run, so this is a latent rather than live hazard, but the function is callable by any `service_role` holder with no mutual exclusion. Either document single-caller-per-run as a requirement in the caller contract or add a lightweight guard (advisory lock or documented serialization).\n\n### 5. No precondition check that the CONCURRENTLY unique indexes exist\n\n- `REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY` fails at runtime without a plain unique index. The 20260905 migration verified `sgfolders_licensor_property_uidx` explicitly; this migration's self-check asserts only that the refresh *statements* appear in the new body (lines 246–251), and behavior test 5 asserts only the stamp gate (lines 187–189). If either unique index were dropped, the step split would fail at 02:00 with no earlier signal. Assert both unique indexes (`sgfilegroups_group_uidx`, `sgfolders_licensor_property_uidx`) in the self-check, matching the 20260905 pattern.\n\n### 6. Self-check does not assert definer / `search_path` posture of the new overload\n\n- The new function correctly declares `security definer` + `set search_path to 'public'` (lines 29–30), consistent with the legacy form — good.\n- But the self-check verifies only `EXECUTE` privileges, not `prosecdef` or `search_path`, and behavior test 0 likewise checks privileges without `prosecdef`. Test 6 checks definer posture only for the legacy overload. Extend one assert to cover `prosecdef` and locked `search_path` on the `(uuid,integer,text)` overload so a future edit cannot silently open it.\n\n## Findings — low / notes\n\n### 7. `all` preserves the original timeout exposure (documented, confirm intent)\n\n[migration:53–61](/supabase/migrations/20260924174251_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:53) and [caller_contract.md:31](/)\n\n- `all` runs both concurrent refreshes plus the search batch in one statement — the same shape that times out today. The caller contract is honest about this (\"can still exceed 8s on a heavy change night\"), so this is not a defect in the migration, but the fix's entire value depends on popdam3 never issuing `all` on change nights. Confirm the popdam3 change (u2giants/popdam3#107) uses the three-step sequence and treats `all` as small-night convenience only.\n\n### 8. Step-split correctness is otherwise as contracted\n\n- `file_groups` / `folders` refresh exactly one matview each and never touch the stamp (lines 53–59, 175); only `search` / `all` stamp `refresh_completed_at` and accumulate (line 175) — matches the contract table.\n- Unknown `p_step` (including `NULL` via the `coalesce(p_step,'')` at line 37) raises before the lifecycle bump (lines 39–51 run after the check) — fail-closed with no side effects. Case-sensitive exact match (`'SEARCH'` rejected) is acceptable for an internal service-role RPC.\n- Empty-queue `search` returns 0 and stamps complete, matching the documented stop condition.\n- Queue/upsert/retire SQL is carried over verbatim from the derived-from source (compare migration 62–166 against 20260917 113–218); the `queued_at < v_started` race comment and reactivation clause are preserved.\n- `REFRESH CONCURRENTLY` placement is fine: the migration only *defines* the function (no refresh at apply time, so no transaction-block issue), and each RPC call is its own statement at runtime.\n- No `statement_timeout` / `SET` anywhere in the new file — constraint 2 holds by inspection.\n- No dynamic SQL in the body (`p_step` is a compared value, interpolated into the error with `%`); all tables schema-qualified; `security definer` + fixed `search_path` matches legacy. No injection or escalation path found.\n- The `COMMENT ON` the legacy overload (lines 193–194) touches metadata only, not `prosrc`, so the md5 pin survives; no other file in the PR touches the legacy body.\n- `completion.json` records `head_sha 7342080...` while this review's authoritative head is `5918e17...`; the rebind note in `completion.json` explains the implementation files are unchanged from the earlier head. Acceptable, but worth a glance at the rebind diff to confirm nothing else moved.\n\n## Mandatory extra checks (from the brief)\n\n1. **Index usage.** Joins and filters are served: queue→files and file→document/pdf-text joins ride primary keys (`style_guide_search_sync_queue` PK, `style_guide_files_pkey`, `style_guide_search_documents` PK, `style_guide_pdf_text` PK); `f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id` is served by `idx_sgf_crawl_run_id`; `ORDER BY q.style_guide_file_id LIMIT v_batch` rides the queue PK; lifecycle updates are by PK. One loose end called out explicitly: the retire predicate `q.queued_at < v_started` (line 152) has no index — each `search` call scans the queue. The queue is narrow and holds only unsynced files, so this is acceptable, but it is an unindexed predicate the change relies on and should be a conscious acceptance, not an assumption.\n2. **Function volatility.** Both the new overload and the legacy form declare `language plpgsql` with no volatility marker, i.e. the default `VOLATILE` — correct for functions that refresh matviews and write tables. The test helper `pg_temp.mk_sg_file` likewise defaults to `VOLATILE`, correct for an inserting helper. No `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE` mislabeling anywhere in the change.\n3. **Exact object checks.** Mixed. Function identities are asserted exactly (`to_regprocedure` with full signatures for both overloads — good). But the migration depends on tables, columns, matviews, and unique indexes it never asserts (queue/files/runs/documents/pdf-text, the two matviews, the CONCURRENTLY-enabling unique indexes); its body-shape asserts are self-referential substrings of the object it just created. Finding 5 covers the concrete gap.\n\n## Closing\n\nThe step design, grant posture, and fail-closed unknown-step handling are sound, but the committed test evidence cannot execute (finding 1) and nothing in the PR actually pins the byte-identity constraint it accepts (finding 2), with several smaller correctness gaps behind them. I would return this for the fixture fix, the md5 pin asserts, and disposition of the batch-zero stamp and concurrency notes.\n\n> VOIDED REVIEWER LINE - VERDICT: REVISE 5918e1716cf6b15336179f0d0165f39f79cfdf59\n\n> VERDICT LINE VOIDED BY THE GOVERNED REVIEW RUNNER.\n>\n> 1 line(s) that a verdict parser would have read as a decision (REVISE) at this head were rewritten so that no tool can read them as a verdict. Head under review: `5918e1716cf6b15336179f0d0165f39f79cfdf59`.\n\n## Findings\n\n**1. Live behavior evidence cannot execute (blocking).**  \n`.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql` lines 21–29 insert into `public.style_guide_files` with `licensor_name` and without `basename_no_ext` / `normalized_name`. Baseline DDL (`010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql` 2191–2202) has:\n\n- `licensor_name text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (split_part(relative_path, '/'::text, 1)) STORED`\n- `basename_no_ext text NOT NULL` (no default)\n- `normalized_name text NOT NULL` (no default)\n\nThe in-repo helper in `popsg_bounded_crawl_and_search_contracts.sql` 18–31 already documents that `licensor_name` cannot be written and supplies the two NOT NULL columns. Test 4 (the only live `p_step='search'` drain) dies on the first `mk_sg_file` call. Catalog-only tests 0–3, 5, 6 never reach a real step. A test that cannot run is not coverage, and the packet ran nothing.\n\n**2. Catalog self-check restates the new DDL and does not pin the legacy body (blocking for the accepted constraint).**  \n`20260924174251` lines 201–252:\n\n- `to_regprocedure` for both signatures (existence only)\n- grants on the **new** overload\n- `position(...)` against `pg_get_functiondef` of the function just created in the same file\n\nIt never asserts `md5(p.prosrc) = '52b676f90e4500dc323c2f9e6e6f3c97'` on `public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid,integer)`, which is what `popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue_v1` actually pins. Behavior test 2 is the same substring check; test 6 checks `prosecdef`/grants on the 2-arg form only. The 2-arg **body is not rewritten** (only `COMMENT ON` at lines 193–194, which is not `prosrc`), so the pin would still be green — but this migration does not prove that, which was an explicit review question.\n\n**3. New overload is not pinned as the right object.**  \nThe verify block does not check, for `(uuid,integer,text)`:\n\n- `pg_proc.prosecdef`\n- `proconfig` / `search_path`\n- `provolatile`\n- unique indexes required for `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY`: `sgfilegroups_group_uidx` and `sgfolders_licensor_property_uidx` (created in `20260905104802` 158–186; still required by the new body at 53–58)\n\n`to_regprocedure('public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid,integer,text)')` is an exact signature check (good), then the rest is grant bits plus echoes of the CREATE text. Behavior test 0 also skips `prosecdef` on the 3-arg form. Test 1/5 `position()` calls do not prove the `REFRESH` statements sit **inside** the matching `v_step` gates.\n\n**4. Step split vs contract (function body is consistent; tests do not prove it).**  \nFrom `20260924174251`:\n\n| `p_step` | Work | Stamps `refresh_completed_at` |\n|---|---|---|\n| `file_groups` | CONCURRENTLY `style_guide_file_groups` only | no |\n| `folders` | CONCURRENTLY `style_guide_folders` only | no |\n| `search` | one queue drain if `v_batch > 0` | yes |\n| `all` | all three | yes |\n\nUnknown `p_step` raises before any write (39–43). Grants and `SECURITY DEFINER` / `search_path = public` match the 2-arg form. Search CTE/upsert/retire is a copy of `20260917005221` 113–218. No `statement_timeout` is raised. No extra claimed objects. No production DML.\n\nCaveats in the body:\n\n- `v_batch = 0` skips both upsert and queue retire (`and v_batch > 0` at 61) but `'search'`/`'all'` still stamp `refresh_completed_at` (175–181). Empty queue with a positive batch is the documented close path; a zero batch closing the run without draining is not.\n- Queue `DELETE` is still global (not `p_run_id`-scoped), same as the 2-arg form.\n- No `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`: two `'search'` callers on the same `p_run_id` can double-count `search_documents_synced`. Sequential popdam3 use is documented; concurrent use is not safe.\n\n**5. `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` placement.**  \nValidation, then optional crawl-run UPDATE, then CONCURRENTLY, then search. CONCURRENTLY is not inside an explicit `BEGIN` in the RPC itself; it remains illegal inside a client transaction (tests correctly avoid executing matview steps). Unique indexes from #2212 still exist; this migration does not re-assert them.\n\n## Mandatory checks\n\n**Index usage.** Joins/predicates the new body uses:\n\n| Predicate / join | Serving index | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `q.style_guide_file_id` / `ORDER BY q.style_guide_file_id` | queue PK | used |\n| `f.id = q.style_guide_file_id` | `style_guide_files` PK | used |\n| `d.style_guide_file_id = f.id` | `style_guide_search_documents` PK | used |\n| `t.style_guide_file_id = c.id` | `style_guide_pdf_text` PK | used |\n| `crawl_runs.id = p_run_id` | PK | used |\n| `ON CONFLICT (style_guide_file_id)` | search-documents PK | used |\n| `f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id` | `idx_sgf_crawl_run_id` **exists** | **not usable as written** because of `(p_run_id is null or f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id)`; planner treats this as a filter after a queue-driven PK nested loop |\n| `f.is_active` | `idx_sgf_is_active` exists | unused; filter after PK lookup |\n| `q.queued_at < v_started` | **no index** | seq scan of the queue; acceptable only while the queue stays narrow |\n\nThe change-night path is queue-driven, so the unused crawl-run index is not by itself a timeout, but the OR form is exactly the “index exists but cannot be used as written” case.\n\n**Function volatility.** Both overloads are `language plpgsql` with no marker, so they default to `VOLATILE`. The 3-arg body writes tables, issues `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW`, and calls `clock_timestamp()`/`now()`. `VOLATILE` is correct; it is not `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`. The catalog check does not assert `provolatile = 'v'`.\n\n**Exact object checks.** Signatures use `to_regprocedure(...)` (exact). Missing exact checks listed in findings 2–3: legacy `md5(prosrc)`, new `prosecdef`/`search_path`/`provolatile`, matview unique indexes, and table/column identity for `style_guide_search_sync_queue`, `refresh_completed_at`, `search_documents_synced`. Existence of the name is not existence of the pinned body.\n\n## Other notes\n\n- Hard constraints 2–4 (no timeout bump, no extra claimed objects, no production writes) hold.\n- Constraint 1 (2-arg `prosrc` byte-identical) holds in the patch; it is not proven by this migration’s verify block.\n- SQL injection / `search_path` / definer risk: `p_step` is compared, not concatenated; relations are `public.`-qualified; `SET search_path TO 'public'` matches the 2-arg form; `pg_catalog` is still searched first. Service-role only.\n- `caller_contract.md` matches the body. `completion.json` `head_sha` is the implementation commit `734208013a0d95cf9360a32890bd2599fce357d3`, not this evidence-rebind head; that is bookkeeping, not a runtime defect.\n\nWhat to change before this is mergeable: copy the working `mk_file` fixture so test 4 actually runs; pin `md5(prosrc)` of the 2-arg form to `52b676f90e4500dc323c2f9e6e6f3c97`; assert `prosecdef`, `search_path`, `VOLATILE`, grants, and the two CONCURRENTLY unique indexes on the 3-arg overload; optionally rewrite `f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id` when `p_run_id is not null` so `idx_sgf_crawl_run_id` can be used.\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\n\nVERDICT: REVISE
