REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n# Review — PR #3487 (issue #3458), head `5918e1716cf6b15336179f0d0165f39f79cfdf59`\r\n\r\n## Coverage (files read)\r\n\r\n- `supabase/migrations/20260924174251_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql` (all 253 lines) — the change under review\r\n- `supabase/migrations/20260917005221_popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue.sql` (all 254 lines) — the declared `derived-from` source\r\n- `supabase/migrations/20260905104802_popsg_bounded_reconcile_pdf_text_and_search.sql` (lines 55–260, 261–600, 599–1053) — table/index DDLs, legacy function lineage, grant pattern, volatility markers\r\n- `supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql` (lines 2173–2204) — `style_guide_crawl_runs` / `style_guide_files` column nullability, defaults, generated column\r\n- `supabase/migrations/20260723170000_popsg_file_tags.sql` (lines 94–96) — `tag_names` / `tag_search_text` defaults; no defaults added to `basename_no_ext` / `normalized_name`\r\n- `supabase/migrations/20260915143302_public_style_guide_files_has_talent_likeness.sql` (all) — only other `style_guide_files` ALTER; nullable, irrelevant\r\n- `supabase/tests/popsg_bounded_crawl_and_search_contracts.sql` (all 679 lines) — committed fixture pattern (`mk_file`) the new evidence deviates from\r\n- `.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql` (all 208 lines), `caller_contract.md` (all 76 lines), `contract.json`, `completion.json` — claimed evidence and contracts\r\n- `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py` (lines 4615–4625) — external `popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue_v1` pin (`md5(prosrc) = 52b676f9…`)\r\n\r\nI could not execute anything (no shell in this session): `check-sql.sh`, `test_migration_derivation.py`, and the behavior tests were read only, never run.\r\n\r\n## What the migration gets right\r\n\r\n- **Legacy 2-arg body untouched (constraint 1 holds structurally).** The new file contains no `CREATE` of the `(uuid,integer)` form — only a `COMMENT ON` (lines 193–194), which does not alter `prosrc`. The external catalog pin on `md5(prosrc)` therefore cannot break from this file.\r\n- **Step split is correct.** `file_groups` / `folders` / `search` gates (lines 53–59, 61) each do exactly what `caller_contract.md` promises; only `search` / `all` stamp `refresh_completed_at` and accumulate `search_documents_synced` (lines 175–182); matview steps leave the run in `refreshing`. Unknown or null `p_step` raises fail-closed (lines 39–43).\r\n- **Grants and posture match legacy.** `SECURITY DEFINER` + `SET search_path TO 'public'` (lines 29–30), revoke from `public`/`anon`/`authenticated` + grant to `service_role` only (lines 196–199). The `has_function_privilege('public', …)` idiom in the self-check has precedent in applied migrations (e.g. `20260902031743`).\r\n- **No timeout raised anywhere** (no `statement_timeout` / `set_config` / `ALTER ROLE/DATABASE` in the file), no data writes, no objects beyond the claimed function name.\r\n- **No injection / privilege-escalation surface.** No dynamic SQL; `p_step` is used only in static comparisons; every relation is schema-qualified; `search_path` is fixed.\r\n- **Volatility (mandatory check 2): pass.** The new function carries no marker, so it is `VOLATILE` by default — correct for a body that writes tables. Siblings are consistent: `preview_stale_sg_files` and `search_style_guide_library` are `STABLE` (read-only), writers are default-`VOLATILE`. No `IMMUTABLE`-on-a-reading-body anywhere in this change.\r\n\r\n## High severity\r\n\r\n**H1. The committed behavior-test fixture cannot execute — the \"live\" evidence (test 4) never ran.**\r\n`.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql`, `pg_temp.mk_sg_file` (lines 21–30):\r\n\r\n1. It inserts `licensor_name` explicitly, but `licensor_name` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (split_part(relative_path,'/',1)) STORED` (`010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:2202`) — the insert fails outright. The committed fixture in `popsg_bounded_crawl_and_search_contracts.sql:20–32` deliberately omits it with a comment saying exactly why.\r\n2. It omits `basename_no_ext` and `normalized_name`, both `NOT NULL` with no default (baseline lines 2191, 2195; no later migration adds defaults — verified by case-insensitive search over `supabase/migrations`). The committed fixture supplies both.\r\n\r\nEither defect alone aborts the file at test 4's first insert, so the change-night drain/batching proof and the closing `all 6 checks passed` notice are unachievable as written. Tests 0–3/5–6 are catalog/shape checks that could run, but the file as a whole cannot complete. A test that cannot execute is not evidence. Fix the fixture to mirror the committed `mk_file` (drop `licensor_name`, add `basename_no_ext` + `normalized_name`), run it against preview/an ephemeral DB, and record the run before merge.\r\n\r\n## Medium severity\r\n\r\n**M1. The migration self-check does not pin what the brief asks about.** The `DO $verify$` block (lines 202–253) asserts both overloads exist via exact `to_regprocedure` signatures (good — exact, not name-only) and checks grants plus `position()` substrings of the *new* function's own source. It does not md5-pin the legacy body (relies entirely on the external `popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue_v1` contract, which does exist — verified in `production_catalog_verification.py:4618–4624`) and asserts none of the depended-on objects (queue table, search-document/pdf-text tables, both matviews, `crawl_runs` stamp columns). The substring checks restate the DDL in the same file rather than proving behavior. Recommend adding a legacy-`prosrc` md5 assertion to the `DO` block so the byte-identical guarantee is enforced at apply time, not just in CI.\r\n\r\n**M2. Concurrent `search` callers on the same `p_run_id` can double-count.** The candidate CTE (lines 62–100) has no `FOR UPDATE … SKIP LOCKED`, so two overlapping `search` steps select the same rows; the upsert is idempotent but each caller's `v_synced` accumulates into `search_documents_synced` (line 180). Inherited from the legacy shape and unlikely with a single nightly caller, but two stepped callers racing (e.g. retry + loop) inflate the counter. Consider `SKIP LOCKED` or documenting single-caller discipline.\r\n\r\n**M3. `search`/`all` stamp completion on partial or empty work.** `v_batch = 0` skips the sync yet still stamps `refresh_completed_at` (lines 61, 175–182); a caller that stops looping early leaves queued entries while the run becomes eligible for `completed` via the CHECK constraint. Same-as-legacy semantics and the loop-until-partial protocol in `caller_contract.md:49–62` mitigates it, but the footgun is now easier to pull since steps are separate calls. Worth one sentence in the function `COMMENT`.\r\n\r\n## Low severity / explicit mandatory-check callouts\r\n\r\n- **Index usage (mandatory check 1).** Every driver is served: `crawl_runs` by PK `id`; queue→files/docs/pdf-text joins by PKs; `ORDER BY q.style_guide_file_id LIMIT` by the queue PK btree. Two loose-but-immaterial spots, called out explicitly: (a) the retire `DELETE … WHERE q.queued_at < v_started` (line 152) has no index on `queued_at` — a full scan of a narrow queue table, no new index warranted; (b) the `f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id` filter cannot use `idx_sgf_reconcile_root_active_run_id(root_label, crawl_run_id, id)` as written (no `root_label` equality) — but it filters post-join queue-narrowed rows, never drives a scan. The `md5(…)` expression predicates likewise filter PK-joined rows only.\r\n- **Exact object checks (mandatory check 3): partial.** Function identities are asserted exactly (`to_regprocedure` with full signatures, lines 208–213). Everything else is inferred: dependent tables/columns/matviews are never asserted, and step isolation is asserted by substring, not behavior (unavoidable for `CONCURRENTLY` inside a test transaction — the established repo pattern, and honestly labeled in the test header).\r\n- **`REFRESH … CONCURRENTLY` placement is unchanged and sound.** Same single-statement RPC posture as the proven legacy path; each step is its own statement, which is the entire point of the change. `all` is honestly documented as still able to exceed the ceiling on heavy nights (`caller_contract.md:31`).\r\n- **Error message echoes `p_step` (line 41–42).** No sensitive data involved; not an issue, noted for completeness.\r\n- **`completion.json` cites only static checks** (`check-sql.sh`, derivation test, `diff --check`) — consistent with H1: no live run of the behavior tests is evidenced anywhere.\r\n\r\n## Outcome\r\n\r\nThe migration SQL itself is sound — legacy body preserved, grants/posture consistent, step semantics match the contract, no timeout or scope violations. But the brief forbids approval without coverage, and the only new live coverage (behavior test 4: queue drain, bounded batches, run stamping) is committed in a form that cannot execute due to two independent fixture defects. That must come back fixed with a recorded run; I would send this back for that fix plus consideration of M1–M3.\r\n\r\nVERDICT: REVISE 5918e1716cf6b15336179f0d0165f39f79cfdf59","author_association":"MEMBER","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5835219335/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"performed_via_github_app":null,"minimized":null},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5835262697","html_url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3487#issuecomment-5835262697","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/3487","id":5835262697,"node_id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABW88K6Q","user":{"login":"u2giants","id":55610577,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/55610577?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants","html_url":"https://github.com/u2giants","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2026-09-25T15:48:32Z","updated_at":"2026-09-25T15:48:32Z","body":"## Review round at head \\5918e171\\ — both durable verdicts are REVISE\n\nSerialization with #3103 is resolved (no collision; #3103 merged docs-only). REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n**Provisional verdict: REVISE** — the step split is sound and legacy-preserving, but the review surfaced mandatory-category gaps (unindexed predicate, loose index/object checks) plus test-provenance issues that should be fixed before merge.\r\n\r\n# Findings — PR #3487 (head `b53854c273d164ab3f68fca22afbfdf6441ddf66`), issue #3458\r\n\r\n## High\r\n\r\n1. **Retire predicate has no serving index.** The `search` step's queue-retire DELETE filters `q.queued_at < v_started` ([migration](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:151)), but the queue table carries only `style_guide_file_id uuid primary key` ([20260917005221](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260917005221_popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue.sql:29)) and this migration adds no index. Every `search` call therefore seq-scans the queue plus one correlated NOT EXISTS probe per row. On the change nights this PR exists for, that is the step's own scaling predicate with nothing serving it. Add `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ... ON public.style_guide_search_sync_queue (queued_at)` or document why the scan is bounded.\r\n2. **Test evidence is bound to a different head.** [completion.json](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\.agent\\work\\3458\\2\\completion.json:33) records `head_sha 143007b…` and check evidence \"at implementation head 143007b…\", but the authoritative PR head is `b53854c…` (a \"rebind … to refreshed implementation head\" commit). The 44-test green run therefore does not attest the reviewed commit, and the packet itself reports **no tests run**. Re-run `check-sql.sh`, `test_migration_derivation.py`, and the behavior tests at `b53854c` or narrow the verdict to the tested SHA.\r\n\r\n## Medium\r\n\r\n3. **`crawl_run_id` predicate relies on a loose index.** `WHERE (p_run_id IS NULL OR f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id)` ([migration](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:86)) is servable only by `idx_sgf_crawl_run_id ON style_guide_files (crawl_run_id)` (baseline-verified) — a bare single-column btree with no `is_active` coverage, so the `AND f.is_active` filter is applied post-scan. The only covering partial index, `idx_sgf_reconcile_root_active_run_id ON (root_label, crawl_run_id, id) WHERE is_active` ([20260905104802](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260905104802_popsg_bounded_reconcile_pdf_text_and_search.sql:126)), leads with `root_label` and cannot serve this `crawl_run_id`-only predicate as written. Inherited verbatim from the legacy body, but the new `search` step re-relies on it per call — call the looseness out or add a `(crawl_run_id) WHERE is_active` index.\r\n4. **CONCURRENTLY index checks are name-only.** The verify block asserts each matview has *a* unique index with a given `relname` ([migration](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:275)) but, unlike the sibling contract test ([contracts](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\tests\\popsg_bounded_crawl_and_search_contracts.sql:87)), does not check `indexprs IS NULL AND indpred IS NULL` (plain-column, non-partial — exactly what CONCURRENTLY requires) nor the indexed columns / `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`. A same-named expression or partial unique index would pass the gate and then fail at REFRESH time.\r\n5. **Object checks infer tables/columns instead of asserting them.** The verify block pins both function signatures exactly via `to_regprocedure` ([migration](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:207)), plus definer/search_path posture and the legacy `md5(prosrc)` pin — all good. But nothing asserts the depended-on `style_guide_search_sync_queue` / `style_guide_search_documents` / `style_guide_pdf_text` / `style_guide_crawl_runs` tables, their columns (`search_documents_synced`, `refresh_completed_at`, `lifecycle_state`), or the queue trigger; and the matview \"checks\" are `'...'::regclass` casts ([migration](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:279)), which match any relation kind (table/view/matview pass alike) and raise an unhandled error instead of a clean failure when the relation is absent. Assert `relkind = 'm'`, the queue's `relkind = 'r'` + RLS posture (as the catalog contract does for the queue), and the consumed columns.\r\n6. **Body-shape assertions match comments too.** Both the migration verify ([migration](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:230)) and the behavior tests ([tests](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\.agent\\work\\3458\\1\\behavior_tests.sql:78)) use `position('<sql fragment>' in pg_get_functiondef(...))`. A fragment appearing only in a comment satisfies the check without the statement existing. Same class in both files — anchor on executable structure or accept the brittleness explicitly.\r\n7. **`search` with `v_batch = 0` still stamps completion.** The sync is guarded by `v_batch > 0` ([migration](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:61)) but the `refresh_completed_at` stamp + `+ v_synced` accumulation are not ([migration](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:175)). A `search` call with `p_search_batch_size = 0` (inside the documented 0..50000 clamp, [contract](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\.agent\\work\\3458\\1\\caller_contract.md:30)) drains nothing yet marks the run refreshed. Inherited from the legacy shape, but the caller contract's footgun #2 ([contract](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\.agent\\work\\3458\\1\\caller_contract.md:71)) doesn't name the `batch = 0` case. Either skip the stamp when `v_batch = 0` or document it.\r\n\r\n## Low\r\n\r\n8. **Behavior tests never execute the matview steps.** `file_groups`/`folders`/`all` are asserted by body shape only because `REFRESH CONCURRENTLY` is illegal in the test transaction ([tests](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\.agent\\work\\3458\\1\\behavior_tests.sql:197)); live coverage is `search`-only, plus no cases for `p_run_id IS NULL` drain, `p_step = 'all'`, `p_step NULL`, or `batch = 0`. Acceptable given the Postgres restriction, but the matview-only return contract (`synced = 0`, stamp untouched) is unverified anywhere.\r\n9. **Stale migration reference in test header.** [behavior_tests.sql](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\.agent\\work\\3458\\1\\behavior_tests.sql:2) says \"Run … after 20260924174251 applies\" — the superseded generation-1 version; the live file is `20260925171844`.\r\n10. **No rollback path for the new overload.** Forward-only migration is the repo norm and `CREATE OR REPLACE` re-runs cleanly, but there is no documented down-step (`DROP FUNCTION public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid,integer,text)`) and the migration additionally rewrites the legacy overload's `COMMENT` ([migration](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:193)) — catalog metadata on the object claimed \"byte-identical\" (prosrc unaffected, but a rollback would leave the new comment behind).\r\n11. **Exact-multiple loop cost.** The caller loop `while (synced >= 5000)` ([contract](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\.agent\\work\\3458\\1\\caller_contract.md:57)) issues one extra empty `search` call (re-stamping `refresh_completed_at`) whenever the queue total is an exact multiple of the batch. Harmless; note or use `synced == batch → continue` deliberately.\r\n\r\n## Verified clean (mandatory items + normal review)\r\n\r\n- **Volatility: PASS.** The new overload, the legacy overload, and `pg_temp.mk_sg_file` ([tests](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\.agent\\work\\3458\\1\\behavior_tests.sql:11)) declare no marker → `VOLATILE`, correct for bodies that write. No `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`-over-table-reads anywhere in the change; the `STABLE`-marked `preview_stale_sg_files` is read-only and out of scope.\r\n- **Roles: PASS.** New overload revokes `public`/`anon`/`authenticated` and grants `service_role` only ([migration](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-review-3487-s1-feb966be2260\\supabase\\migrations\\20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:196)); verify block re-checks all three negatives plus `public`; `SECURITY DEFINER` + fixed `search_path = 'public'` asserted for the new overload. Legacy grants untouched.\r\n- **Migration immutability / dependencies: PASS.** New file only; prior migrations unedited; `derived-from: 20260917005221` correct; legacy `prosrc md5` pin matches the live catalog contract `popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue_v1` (which uses `exists()` on the 2-arg form, so the added overload doesn't break it); `claim #3483` scope respected; no `statement_timeout` raised anywhere.\r\n- **Join/key indexes that ARE served:** `q.file_id → f.id`, `d`/`t` lookups by `style_guide_file_id`, `ON CONFLICT (style_guide_file_id)`, `crawl_runs WHERE id`, and `ORDER BY q.style_guide_file_id LIMIT` (queue PK order) — all PK-served.\r\n\r\nNet: the split design, fail-closed `p_step` gate, stamp gating (`search`/`all` only), and legacy preservation are right; fix the `queued_at` index question, tighten the name-only checks, and re-bind test evidence to `b53854c` before merging.\r\n\r\nVERDICT: REVISE b53854c273d164ab3f68fca22afbfdf6441ddf66","author_association":"MEMBER","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5839175131/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"performed_via_github_app":null,"minimized":null},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5840212785","html_url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3487#issuecomment-5840212785","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/3487","id":5840212785,"node_id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABXBqTMQ","user":{"login":"u2giants","id":55610577,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/55610577?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants","html_url":"https://github.com/u2giants","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2026-09-25T21:56:03Z","updated_at":"2026-09-25T21:56:03Z","body":"GOVERNED REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\nReview of PR #3487 (head `896f5c29`) — split of `refresh_style_guide_matviews` into steppable RPCs (issue #3458). Prior findings are addressed (stamp gated on `v_batch > 0`, CONCURRENTLY checks assert plain-column non-partial, `queued_at` scan documented as bounded). The following gaps remain. All file paths are workspace-relative.\r\n\r\n## High\r\n\r\n1. **Retire scan has no serving index; boundedness is by assertion, not by index.** The retire predicate `q.queued_at < v_started` (supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:151-152) has no index: the queue table's only key is the PK on `style_guide_file_id` (supabase/migrations/20260917005221_popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue.sql:29-32). The migration itself admits this (20260925171844:201-207) and accepts a \"bounded by change volume\" argument. That is an explicit unindexed predicate on the change's own delete path: a backlog night (or any caller that stops draining) makes the queue large and this DELETE scans it fully, plus one correlated NOT EXISTS subquery per row. Per the mandatory index check this must be recorded as a gap even though it is documented.\r\n2. **The only files-side index cannot serve the candidates filter as written.** The candidates CTE filters `f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id AND f.is_active` with no `root_label` predicate (20260925171844:86-87). The available index is `idx_sgf_reconcile_root_active_run_id ON (root_label, crawl_run_id, id) WHERE is_active` (supabase/migrations/20260905104802_popsg_bounded_reconcile_pdf_text_and_search.sql:126-128) — leading column `root_label` is unconstrained here, so the index cannot be used as written for this filter. The join `f.id = q.style_guide_file_id` is PK-served, but the selective `crawl_run_id` filter is not. This is the \"exists but cannot be used as written\" case.\r\n3. **Zero-batch search leaves the run stuck in `refreshing` with no documented recovery.** With explicit `p_search_batch_size = 0` (or negative, silently clamped at 20260925171844:33), `v_batch = 0` skips both the search block (line 61) and the completion stamp (line 175). The run was already stamped `refreshing` (lines 45-51) and nothing ever stamps `refresh_completed_at`. The caller contract instead says `search` always stamps, and that \"an empty-queue call still stamps\" (.agent/work/3458/1/caller_contract.md:30-31,62) — true only when `v_batch > 0`. Negative input clamping to a silent no-op rather than raising compounds it.\r\n4. **Race-safety comment misstates locking; the DELETE can block under the 8s ceiling.** The comment claims the trigger's `queued_at` re-stamp \"locks the entry, so a change that races this call is re-checked and kept\" (20260925171844:148-150). A concurrent UPDATE takes a row lock; this function's DELETE then *waits* on that lock (no `SKIP LOCKED` / `NOWAIT`), burning the 8s statement budget instead of skipping. Inherited from the legacy body, but the comment presents it as a safety property of the new step.\r\n\r\n## Medium\r\n\r\n5. **Retire DELETE is not scoped to `p_run_id` while the sync CTE is.** The candidates CTE filters `(p_run_id is null or f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id)` (line 86); the retire DELETE (lines 151-165) has no `p_run_id` predicate at all — one run's `search` step retires queue entries belonging to other runs. Mostly benign (only satisfied entries retire), but the per-run caller loop (`while synced >= batch`, caller_contract.md:51-57) counts only its own run's rows while deletion is global — asymmetric and untested.\r\n6. **Matview steps are proven by body-shape only, never executed.** Behavior tests admit `REFRESH CONCURRENTLY` is illegal in the test transaction and assert only substrings (behavior_tests.sql:193-197). The genuinely new code paths (`file_groups`, `folders`, and especially `all`, which still combines two CONCURRENTLY refreshes plus search in one statement) have zero live execution evidence. The contract concedes `all` \"can still exceed 8s\" (caller_contract.md:31) — i.e. the default convenience step retains the exact failure mode this PR exists to fix.\r\n7. **Concurrent search workers double-process.** `ORDER BY q.style_guide_file_id LIMIT v_batch` with no `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` means two overlapping `search` calls for the same run select the same rows; the upsert is idempotent so this is wasted work under the ceiling, not corruption — but it directly eats the 8s budget the split was meant to protect.\r\n8. **Rollback has no path.** The migration has no DOWN / reversal: rolling back the new overload requires a manual `DROP FUNCTION public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid,integer,text)`. The migration also rewrites the `COMMENT ON` the legacy 2-arg overload (lines 193-194) — comment-only, does not disturb the pinned `prosrc` md5, but it does mutate the \"byte-identical\" object's catalog metadata and the verify block does not pin the comment.\r\n9. **Deploy-blocking coupling by design.** The verify block fails the *entire migration* (and everything after it) if the legacy `prosrc` md5 drifts (lines 264-270) or if either matview index is renamed (lines 285-304). Fail-closed is the right posture, but a rename of `sgfilegroups_group_uidx` / `sgfolders_licensor_property_uidx` now blocks all later migrations at deploy time rather than at the dependent change.\r\n\r\n## Low\r\n\r\n10. **Exact-object checks cover the new signature and CONCURRENTLY indexes well, but not the dependencies.** The verify block asserts exact overload signatures via `to_regprocedure`, exact index names with `indisunique AND indexprs IS NULL AND indpred IS NULL`, grants, and `SECURITY DEFINER` + `search_path` (lines 215-304). It does *not* assert: the queue/files/documents/pdf-text/crawl-runs tables or any of the dozen columns the body reads/writes (`crawl_run_id`, `tag_search_text`, `search_documents_synced`, …); that the two `::regclass` targets are actually matviews (`relkind = 'm'` — a plain table of the same name passes); the queue trigger's existence; or the return-table shape. A renamed column fails at first RPC call, not at migration time.\r\n11. **Function volatility: correct, but only implicitly.** The new overload carries no volatility marker, so it defaults to VOLATILE — correct for a writer (refreshes, upserts, deletes). No IMMUTABLE/STABLE mis-marking is introduced. The test helper `pg_temp.mk_sg_file` (behavior_tests.sql:11-31) is likewise unmarked `LANGUAGE sql` doing INSERTs — VOLATILE by default, correct by accident; an explicit `VOLATILE` would prevent a future \"cleanup\" from mis-marking it.\r\n12. **Role posture is correct; test coverage of it is asymmetric.** The migration revokes `public`/`anon`/`authenticated` and grants `service_role` only (lines 196-199) and the verify block asserts all three denials (lines 230-234). The behavior tests (test 0, lines 60-66) check only `authenticated`/`anon`, not the `public` role — sibling check missing. Legacy-overload grants are asserted only in behavior test 6, not in the migration verify block.\r\n13. **Behavior-test gaps (all in .agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql).** NULL `p_step` (coalesced to `''`, rejected) is untested — only `'nope'` is (lines 118-126); the `v_batch = 0` no-stamp path is untested; cross-run retire scoping is untested; the `md5` expressions compared per-row (`d.source_identity IS DISTINCT FROM md5(...)`, migration lines 94-98, 161-165) are unindexable by construction and evaluated row-by-row under the ceiling on every call.\r\n\r\nContract/code contradictions to fix in one pass: caller_contract.md:30 (\"search … stamps\") and :62 (\"empty-queue call still stamps\") vs migration line 175 (`v_batch > 0` gate); caller_contract.md:72 (\"stamped on every search/all call\") holds only for `v_batch > 0`.\r\n\r\nVERDICT: REVISE 896f5c29ecc81df3a0982aa5674b19d0595b9d08","author_association":"MEMBER","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5840212785/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"performed_via_github_app":null,"minimized":null},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5840626682","html_url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3487#issuecomment-5840626682","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/3487","id":5840626682,"node_id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABXCDj-g","user":{"login":"u2giants","id":55610577,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/55610577?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants","html_url":"https://github.com/u2giants","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2026-09-25T22:38:15Z","updated_at":"2026-09-25T22:38:15Z","body":"GOVERNED REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### Findings\r\n\r\n#### 1. Index Usage\r\n\r\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L603-L618), the queue cleanup statement executes `delete from public.style_guide_search_sync_queue q where q.queued_at < v_started and not exists (...)`. The queue table `public.style_guide_search_sync_queue` possesses only a primary key on `style_guide_file_id`, with no index on `queued_at`. This forces a sequential scan across `style_guide_search_sync_queue`. The migration explicitly documents this loose index assumption in lines 653–659 as an accepted trade-off based on change-volume boundedness.\r\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L538-L552), the `candidates` CTE filters on `(p_run_id is null or f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id)`. Because query execution is ordered by `q.style_guide_file_id` (PK) with primary-key lookups on `f.id`, an index on `f.crawl_run_id` cannot drive or constrain the initial index scan on `q`. Non-matching run entries must be filtered sequentially per queued item.\r\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L737-L756), the `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` statements for `public.style_guide_file_groups` and `public.style_guide_folders` are verified against exact plain-column, non-partial unique indexes (`sgfilegroups_group_uidx` and `sgfolders_licensor_property_uidx`), satisfying PostgreSQL's prerequisite for concurrent matview refresh.\r\n\r\n#### 2. Function Volatility\r\n\r\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L471-L483), [`public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid, integer, text)`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L471-L483) does not declare an explicit volatility category (`IMMUTABLE`, `STABLE`, or `VOLATILE`). PostgreSQL assigns default volatility `VOLATILE` (`provolatile = 'v'`). Because the routine modifies database state across multiple tables and materialized views, `VOLATILE` is the exact required volatility.\r\n- In [`.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql#L17-L37), [`pg_temp.mk_sg_file`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql#L17-L37) also defaults to `VOLATILE`, matching its DML `INSERT` behavior.\r\n\r\n#### 3. Exact Object Checks\r\n\r\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L663-L757), the migration's `$verify$` block explicitly asserts exact function signatures via `to_regprocedure` for both `public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid,integer,text)` and `public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid,integer)`, verifies security definer settings and `search_path=public`, pins the MD5 digest of the legacy 2-arg routine body to `'52b676f90e4500dc323c2f9e6e6f3c97'`, and checks the non-partial, non-expression index properties on both materialized views.\r\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L662-L758), the `$verify$` block does not directly check the presence or column shapes of the dependent base tables read and written by the routine body (`public.style_guide_crawl_runs`, `public.style_guide_search_sync_queue`, `public.style_guide_files`, `public.style_guide_search_documents`, `public.style_guide_pdf_text`).\r\n- In [`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/scripts/production_catalog_verification.py#L3225-L3233), routine privilege checks on overloaded functions without typed parameter resolution record `service_role` execute grants as RECORD rather than evaluating them directly. The migration's `$verify$` block correctly supplements this by validating `has_function_privilege('service_role', 'public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid,integer,text)', 'execute')`.\r\n\r\n#### 4. Role Changes and Security Posture\r\n\r\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L648-L651), API access is revoked from `public`, `anon`, and `authenticated`, with execution granted strictly to `service_role`.\r\n- `security definer` execution with an explicit `search_path to 'public'` ensures immunity against search-path poisoning.\r\n\r\n#### 5. Dependency Correctness and Migration Immutability\r\n\r\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L4-L6), `-- derived-from: 20260917005221` accurately references the base queue migration, satisfying derivation tracking in [`scripts/migration_derivation.py`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/scripts/migration_derivation.py).\r\n- No historical migration files were modified or deleted; the legacy 2-arg function `public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid, integer)` remains intact with unchanged source digest.\r\n\r\n#### 6. Rollback Safety\r\n\r\n- The steppable overload is strictly additive. Rollback can be performed cleanly by executing `drop function public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid, integer, text);` without mutating table schemas or disturbing the legacy 2-arg routine.\r\n\r\n#### 7. Test Coverage and Documentation Alignment\r\n\r\n- In [`.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql#L197-L203), Test 5 inserts a crawl run row into `v_run2` (`insert into public.style_guide_crawl_runs ... returning id into v_run2;`), but `v_run2` is never subsequently used because `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` cannot be executed inside a transaction block.\r\n- In [`.agent/work/3458/1/caller_contract.md`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/.agent/work/3458/1/caller_contract.md#L288-L291) and [`supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-c2d7c545fce2-mimo-review-3487-s1-1790375506342-feb966be2260/supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L627), the completion stamp update is conditioned on `v_batch > 0`. When called with `p_search_batch_size = 0`, the search sync and completion timestamp updates are bypassed; while empty-queue behavior is documented in `caller_contract.md`, caller behavior when explicitly passing batch size 0 is omitted from `caller_contract.md` and untested in `behavior_tests.sql`.\r\n\r\nVERDICT: APPROVE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n**Provisional verdict: REVISE** — no correctness bug in the migration body, but several small gaps plus zero execution evidence for the behavior tests.\r\n\r\n# Findings\r\n\r\n## Medium\r\n\r\n**M1. No execution evidence for the behavior tests.**\r\n`.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql` is committed but lives outside the `supabase/tests/` CI path, the packet states no tests ran, and `completion.json` claims only static checks (`check-sql.sh`, derivation tests, `git diff --check`). The only live proof of the new search step (test 4) has therefore never been shown passing. Related: test 4 measures per-batch `v_elapsed_ms` ([behavior_tests.sql](.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql:153)) but never asserts it — timing is notice-only. Request: run the file once on preview/ephemeral and paste the output.\r\n\r\n## Low\r\n\r\n**L1. Index gap (documented/accepted): `q.queued_at < v_started` has no index.**\r\n[20260925171844](supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:152) — the queue's PK is `style_guide_file_id` alone ([20260917005221](supabase/migrations/20260917005221_popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue.sql:29)), so the retire DELETE full-scans the queue each `search` call. The in-file note ([20260925171844](supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:201)) and `completion.json` accept this as bounded-by-delta. Calling it out per the mandatory index check; no action beyond the existing documentation.\r\n\r\n**L2. Index that exists but cannot serve as written: `f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id`.**\r\n[20260925171844](supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:86). The only files index containing `crawl_run_id` is `idx_sgf_reconcile_root_active_run_id (root_label, crawl_run_id, id) WHERE is_active` ([20260905104802](supabase/migrations/20260905104802_popsg_bounded_reconcile_pdf_text_and_search.sql:126)) — leading column `root_label` is unconstrained here, so it cannot seek on `crawl_run_id` (FK at baseline `010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql:6440` creates no index). Practically bounded (plan drives from the delta-sized queue via PK lookups, filter applied post-fetch on ≤ `v_batch` rows) and inherited byte-for-byte from the legacy body — same class, same line in both overloads. No action; recorded as the known looseness.\r\n\r\n**L3. Prior-round fix is unpinned: nothing asserts the `v_batch > 0` stamp gate.**\r\nThe gate exists in code ([20260925171844](supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:175)), but test 5 only checks the substring `if p_run_id is not null and v_step in ('all', 'search')` ([behavior_tests.sql](.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql:195)), which passes with or without the `and v_batch > 0` conjunct — and the migration verify block pins the other gates ([20260925171844](supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:238)) but not this one. Sibling of the same class: the whole search block including queue-retire is gated on `v_batch > 0` ([20260925171844](supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:61)), equally unpinned. Suggest extending the position-check to include `and v_batch > 0` in both places.\r\n\r\n**L4. `batch = 0` corner contradicts the caller contract.**\r\nCode: explicit `p_search_batch_size = 0` (or negative, clamped) skips sync, retire, *and* stamp (lines 61, 175). Contract table says `search` stamps \"yes\" ([caller_contract.md](.agent/work/3458/1/caller_contract.md:29)) and footgun 2 says the stamp lands \"on every `search` / `all` call\" ([caller_contract.md](.agent/work/3458/1/caller_contract.md:71)). One sentence (\"a zero/negative batch is a lifecycle-touch no-op: no sync, no retire, no stamp\") closes it.\r\n\r\n**L5. Stale migration reference in test header.**\r\n\"after 20260924174251 applies\" ([behavior_tests.sql](.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql:3)) names the superseded gen-1 version; the claim now ships `20260925171844`.\r\n\r\n**L6. Exact-object gap: queue table and all referenced columns are inferred, not asserted.**\r\nThe verify block pins both overload signatures, grants (4 roles), definer/search_path, body-shape gates, the legacy md5, and both CONCURRENTLY indexes exactly — but never asserts `style_guide_search_sync_queue`, `style_guide_files`/`_documents`/`_pdf_text`/`_crawl_runs` columns. `CREATE FUNCTION` does not validate plpgsql bodies, so a renamed column fails only at first RPC call. Ordering (`derived-from: 20260917005221`) makes this safe in practice; cheapest fix is one `to_regclass` loop for the five relations.\r\n\r\n**L7. CONCURRENTLY checks omit `indisvalid`.**\r\n[20260925171844](supabase/migrations/20260925171844_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql:285) — an `INVALID` leftover unique index (failed `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`) would pass the check yet fail `REFRESH CONCURRENTLY` at runtime. Same omission at both index branches. One-word hardening (`and i.indisvalid`).\r\n\r\n**L8. Duplicated search-sync logic (2-arg frozen vs 3-arg copy).**\r\nForced by the md5-freeze constraint and documented, but any future queue-logic fix must land in two bodies. Observation only.\r\n\r\n## Verified clean (mandatory checks + prior findings)\r\n\r\n- **Volatility:** no `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE` markers anywhere in the change; new overload, legacy overload, trigger fn, and `pg_temp.mk_sg_file` (`language sql` with an `INSERT`) all resolve to default `VOLATILE` — correct. No finding.\r\n- **CONCURRENTLY plain-column non-partial checks:** `indexprs IS NULL AND indpred IS NULL` present for both indexes (migration lines 291-292, 300-301); both backing indexes are plain-column (`sgfilegroups…` on 5 cols, `sgfolders…` on 2 cols, both `nulls not distinct`). Addressed.\r\n- **Stamp gating:** `v_batch > 0` present (line 175); footgun 2 correctly describes partial/empty-queue stamping. Addressed, save L3/L4 edges.\r\n- **Race-safety comment** (lines 145-150) correctly describes `queued_at` re-stamp locking. Addressed.\r\n- **Roles:** new overload revoked from `public`/`anon`/`authenticated`, granted to `service_role` (lines 196-199), mirroring legacy; `has_function_privilege('public',…)` matches wide repo precedent. No change to legacy grants. No finding.\r\n- **Migration hygiene:** single new versioned file, no edits to prior migrations, no transaction-control statements (failed apply rolls back atomically), no statement-timeout changes, `comment on` the legacy overload is metadata-only (prosrc pin unaffected). Version-collision and dependency-ordering checks clean.\r\n\r\nSuggested handling: fix L3/L4/L5 (one-line edits each), optionally L6/L7, then run the behavior file once and attach output — that closes M1 and this review can approve.\r\n\r\nVERDICT: REVISE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### Governed Review Findings — popcre/shared-db PR #3487 (Issue #3458)\n\nReview of pull request #3487 at exact head [`7b92775c1d683718a17d325c44bd6976671d79dd`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/.ai-review-gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3/MANIFEST.md#L26).\n\n---\n\n### 1. Mandatory Check: Index Usage\n\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L151-L166), the queue retirement query executes `delete from public.style_guide_search_sync_queue q where q.queued_at < v_started and not exists (...)`. The queue table `public.style_guide_search_sync_queue` has only its primary key on `style_guide_file_id`, without an index on `queued_at`. This forces a sequential scan across `style_guide_search_sync_queue` followed by correlated subquery evaluation. This loose index assumption is explicitly documented and accepted in lines 201–207 based on change-night queue volume being bounded.\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L83-L100), the `candidates` CTE filters by `(p_run_id is null or f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id)`. The candidates query is driven by an index scan on `q.style_guide_file_id` (PK) with subsequent primary-key lookups on `f.id`. Any index that includes `crawl_run_id` (such as `idx_sgf_reconcile_root_active_run_id`, which has leading column `root_label`) cannot be used as written to drive or constrain candidate discovery; the run filter is applied post-lookup.\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L281-L306), unique indexes supporting `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` for `public.style_guide_file_groups` (`sgfilegroups_group_uidx`) and `public.style_guide_folders` (`sgfolders_licensor_property_uidx`) are verified as valid, plain-column, non-partial unique indexes (`indisunique and indisvalid and indexprs is null and indpred is null`), satisfying PostgreSQL requirements.\n- All join predicates and target updates (`style_guide_crawl_runs.id`, `f.id = q.style_guide_file_id`, `d.style_guide_file_id = f.id`, `t.style_guide_file_id = c.id`) are served by primary keys.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Mandatory Check: Function Volatility\n\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L19-L31), `public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid, integer, text)` does not set an explicit volatility clause, correctly defaulting to `VOLATILE` (`provolatile = 'v'`). Because the routine executes DML (`UPDATE`, `INSERT`, `DELETE`), refreshes materialized views, and evaluates non-deterministic clock calls (`clock_timestamp()`, `now()`), `VOLATILE` is the required volatility category.\n- The legacy overload `public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid, integer)` remains unchanged and defaults to `VOLATILE`.\n- In [`.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/.agent/work/3458/1/behavior_tests.sql#L11-L17), the test fixture helper `pg_temp.mk_sg_file` defaults to `VOLATILE`, matching its `INSERT` behavior.\n- No mutating function or query in the change is marked `IMMUTABLE` or `STABLE`.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Mandatory Check: Exact Object Checks\n\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L210-L308), the migration's `$verify$` block asserts exact objects:\n  - Both routine signatures are pinned via `to_regprocedure('public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid,integer,text)')` and `to_regprocedure('public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid,integer)')`.\n  - The legacy 2-argument overload source hash is pinned to `md5(p.prosrc) = '52b676f90e4500dc323c2f9e6e6f3c97'`, preventing drift from the production catalog contract `popsg_refresh_search_sync_queue_v1` in [`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/scripts/production_catalog_verification.py#L4618-L4621).\n  - Security definer posture (`prosecdef`) and `search_path=public` are validated for the 3-argument overload.\n  - Concurrently-enabling unique indexes `sgfilegroups_group_uidx` and `sgfolders_licensor_property_uidx` are validated for validity, uniqueness, non-partiality, and lack of expression index attributes.\n- Note on inferred object existence: Base tables (`public.style_guide_crawl_runs`, `public.style_guide_files`, `public.style_guide_search_sync_queue`, `public.style_guide_search_documents`, `public.style_guide_pdf_text`) and individual columns referenced in the body are resolved at runtime rather than asserted in the verification block.\n\n---\n\n### 4. Statement Ceiling and Correctness Assessment\n\n- Splitting the operation into steppable units (`'file_groups'`, `'folders'`, `'search'`, and convenience `'all'`) allows the caller (`popdam3`) to invoke each step in a dedicated RPC statement. This directly prevents statement timeouts against the 8-second authenticator ceiling on change nights.\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L39-L43), validation of `p_step` executes fail-closed: unknown or null steps raise an exception before updating `lifecycle_state` or executing any refresh.\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L175-L182), the completion timestamp `refresh_completed_at` is updated only when `v_step in ('all', 'search') and v_batch > 0`. A zero or negative batch does not mark the run refreshed. This matches the updated documentation in [`.agent/work/3458/1/caller_contract.md`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/.agent/work/3458/1/caller_contract.md#L60-L64).\n- The transaction prohibition for callers is explicitly documented in [`.agent/work/3458/1/caller_contract.md`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/.agent/work/3458/1/caller_contract.md#L67-L71), noting that wrapping steps in a single transaction block causes `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` to fail.\n\n---\n\n### 5. Role Grants and Security Boundary\n\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot1-gen3-cb8a38e77272/supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L196-L199), execute privileges on the new overload are revoked from `public`, `anon`, and `authenticated`, and granted strictly to `service_role`.\n- The routine uses `SECURITY DEFINER` with fixed `search_path TO 'public'`. No dynamic SQL is present; parameters are passed as static binds or values.\n\n---\n\n### 6. Legacy Function Preservation and Scope Boundaries\n\n- The migration does not modify the body of `public.refresh_style_guide_matviews(uuid, integer)`. This unindexed predicate is explicitly documented in lines 201–207 as an accepted trade-off: change-night queue volume is bounded to delta rows, and adding an index on `queued_at` would violate the admitted single-object claim scope.\n- In [`supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-8765a5c1742f-codex-gemini-3487-slot2-rebuild-cb8a38e77272/supabase/migrations/20260928003740_popsg_refresh_steps_under_ceiling.sql#L83-L100), the `candidates` CTE filters by `(p_run_id is null or f.crawl_run_id = p_run_id)`. The index `idx_sgf_reconcile_root_active_run_id` (on `root_label, crawl_run_id, id WHERE is_active`) has leading column `root_label` unconstrained and cannot serve this predicate. Mandatory checks\r\n\r\n1. **Index usage**:\r\n   The scope of this PR is repository maintenance only, adding JavaScript modules and tests for evidence contract lineage. There are no SQL schema changes, table queries, joins, or table-level predicates. Consequently, no database indexes are relied upon or affected.\r\n\r\n2. **Function volatility**:\r\n   No PostgreSQL or database functions are introduced or modified; hence, no SQL volatility attributes (`IMMUTABLE`, `STABLE`, `VOLATILE`) apply. At the JavaScript layer, the utility functions (`lineageContractHash`, `sortValue`, `parseEvidenceParent`, `validateGenerationLineage`, `bindPredecessor`, `resolveCurrentPair`, `refuseCommittedMutation`, `planSuccessor`, `isRealEvidenceRecord`, `classifyAgentPaths`) are pure, side-effect-free, and return frozen data structures without mutating arguments.\r\n\r\n3. **Exact object checks**:\r\n   No database objects (schemas, tables, views, columns, or function signatures) are created or referenced. The logic operates strictly on Git commit SHAs (validated against exact 40-character hexadecimal patterns), Git contract refs (`refs/db-contracts/<work_issue>/<generation>`), relative evidence paths matching `KEYED_EVIDENCE_PATTERN` or `LEGACY_PAIR`, and canonical JSON object structures.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### Findings\r\n\r\n#### 1. Incomplete negative fixture for forged parent digests\r\n- **Path**: [scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.test.mjs#L654-L662](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-11bb11489c6c-claude-s3445gemini2-93f3f3506358/scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.test.mjs#L654-L662)\r\n- **Detail**: The test `'real Git-history negative fixtures: rewrite, fake parent, highest-filename'` intends to verify that forged predecessor bindings are refused. However, the test implementation is:\r\n  ```javascript\r\n  // Forged predecessor digest.\r\n  const forged = v1Root({\r\n    schema_version: LINEAGE_SCHEMA_VERSION,\r\n    generation: 2,\r\n    evidence_parent: { work_issue: ISSUE, generation: 1, contract_sha256: '0'.repeat(64) },\r\n  })\r\n  const lineage = validateGenerationLineage(forged)\r\n  assert.notEqual(lineage.evidence_parent.contract_sha256, lineageContractHash(v1Root()))\r\n  ```\r\n  In this test, `validateGenerationLineage(forged)` succeeds because `validateGenerationLineage` only validates that `contract_sha256` is a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal string. Rather than asserting refusal via `assert.throws`, the test merely asserts inequality between `'0'.repeat(64)` and `lineageContractHash(v1Root())`. There is no check in `validateGenerationLineage`, `verifyGitEvidence`, or an exported validator verifying that `contract.evidence_parent.contract_sha256` matches the predecessor contract's digest.\r\n\r\n#### 2. Missing predecessor generation ordering check\r\n- **Path**: [scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs#L241-L248](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-11bb11489c6c-claude-s3445gemini2-93f3f3506358/scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs#L241-L248)\r\n- **Detail**: In `validateGenerationLineage(contract)`, when `schema_version === 2` and `generation > 1`, the code verifies that `parent !== null`:\r\n  ```javascript\r\n  const parent = parseEvidenceParent(contract[EVIDENCE_PARENT_FIELD], { workIssue })\r\n  if (generation === 1 && parent !== null) {\r\n    throw new EvidenceLineageError('generation 1 is the chain root and must carry evidence_parent null')\r\n  }\r\n  if (generation > 1 && parent === null) {\r\n    throw new EvidenceLineageError(`generation ${generation} must name its predecessor in evidence_parent; only generation 1 is a root`)\r\n  }\r\n  ```\r\n  However, it does not check that `parent.generation < generation`. A successor contract can specify its own generation (`parent.generation === generation`) or a future generation (`parent.generation > generation`) as its `evidence_parent`, and `validateGenerationLineage` will accept it. In an append-only predecessor chain, the predecessor must precede the successor.\r\n\r\n#### 3. `resolveCurrentPair` and mutation refusal unintegrated in `verifyGitEvidence`\r\n- **Path**: [scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs#L68-L85](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-11bb11489c6c-claude-s3445gemini2-93f3f3506358/scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs#L68-L85)\r\n- **Detail**: `verifyGitEvidence` imports only `validateGenerationLineage`, `classifyAgentPaths`, and `EvidenceLineageError` from [scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-11bb11489c6c-claude-s3445gemini2-93f3f3506358/scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs). It does not invoke `resolveCurrentPair`. In lines 68–72, `verifyGitEvidence` still relies on `acceptableEvidencePairs(contract)` from [scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-11bb11489c6c-claude-s3445gemini2-93f3f3506358/scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs), which unconditionally includes `LEGACY_PAIR`. Consequently, a `schema_version: 2` contract paired with the legacy files in `afterImplementation` would bypass `resolveCurrentPair`'s legacy restriction (`a schema_version 2 contract must use its keyed pair, not the legacy paths`). Furthermore, `refuseCommittedMutation` is never executed during git verification.\r\n\r\n#### 4. Ecosystem schema constraint blocks `schema_version: 2` publication and verification\r\n- **Path**: [scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs#L53](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-11bb11489c6c-claude-s3445gemini2-93f3f3506358/scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs#L53), [scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs#L79-L90](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-11bb11489c6c-claude-s3445gemini2-93f3f3506358/scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs#L79-L90), and [scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs#L75](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-11bb11489c6c-claude-s3445gemini2-93f3f3506358/scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs#L75)\r\n- **Detail**: `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs` defines `CONTRACT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` and rejects any contract where `contract.schema_version !== 1` or any unknown property outside `CONTRACT_REQUIRED` and `generation`. In `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs` line 75:\r\n  ```javascript\r\n  const published = validateContract(io.readPublishedContract(report.contract_ref))\r\n  ```\r\n  Because `validateContract` is called on the published contract ref, any pull request attempting to publish or verify a `schema_version: 2` contract (or a contract specifying `evidence_parent`) will throw `ContractError: contract schema_version must be 1` or `ContractError: contract has unknown field evidence_parent`.\r\n\r\n#### 5. I did not stop at the first gap; all findings are in one pass.\n\n## Findings\n\n### High — acceptance criteria partially implemented (library exists, no gate enforces it)\n\n**H1. Forged `contract_sha256` parent digests pass every gate — `verifyPredecessorBinding` has zero production callers (criterion 2 partial).**\n`verifyGitEvidence` ([scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-claude-shared-db-3380-pr3445-61da10e33b31/scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:81)) calls `validateGenerationLineage`, `resolveCurrentPair`, `classifyAgentPaths`, `refuseCommittedMutation` — but never `verifyPredecessorBinding`. The \"contract_sha256 binding\" of criterion 2 is therefore shape-checked, not authenticity-checked, at enforcement time.\n\n**H2. Publish-before-record is unenforced — nothing calls `planSuccessor`/`assertGenerationWriteAllowed`, and the latter cannot check publication (criterion 5 partial).**\nThe refresh writer ([scripts/refresh-code-pr-branch.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-claude-shared-db-3380-pr3445-61da10e33b31/scripts/refresh-code-pr-branch.mjs:58)) rebinds `completion.json` in place via `rebindCompletion` and never calls `planSuccessor` or `assertGenerationWriteAllowed`. The brief's question 4 (\"does it refuse recording new results when the successor has not been published?\") answers **no**. Criterion 4 holds, but via pre-existing code, not the new function.\n- **O2. `.agent/` unknown-path coverage is split across two mechanisms.** `classifyAgentPaths` runs only on `actualFiles` (merge-base→head_sha); tail-range extras are caught by the exact tail-match at [git-evidence.mjs:67-72](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-claude-shared-db-3380-pr3445-61da10e33b31/scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:67). REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\nProvisional verdict: REVISE — sound design and thorough unit tests, but the forged-parent check is not wired into the enforcement gate.\n\nCoverage: I examined all six PR files — [scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-1-51d7f8f9ed7e\\scripts\\lib\\evidence-generation-lineage.mjs), [scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.test.mjs](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-1-51d7f8f9ed7e\\scripts\\lib\\evidence-generation-lineage.test.mjs), [scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-1-51d7f8f9ed7e\\scripts\\agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs), [scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-1-51d7f8f9ed7e\\scripts\\agent-work-contract.mjs), [.agent/work/3380/6/contract.json](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-1-51d7f8f9ed7e\\.agent\\work\\3380\\6\\contract.json), [.agent/work/3380/6/completion.json](D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-1-51d7f8f9ed7e\\.agent\\work\\3380\\6\\completion.json) — plus supporting reads of `scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs` and `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.test.mjs`.\n\nMandatory checks 1–3: this is a scripts/tooling-only change (no SQL, no schema, no migrations). (1) Index usage: N/A — the change contains no table predicates or joins and makes no index assumptions. (2) Function volatility: N/A — no PostgreSQL functions are created or altered; there are no IMMUTABLE/STABLE/VOLATILE markers in scope (all new functions are Node.js). (3) Exact object checks: partially applicable via analogues — the change does assert exact git ref (`contractRef(issue, generation)`, git-evidence.mjs:73), exact whole-contract sha256 (`contractHash` comparison, git-evidence.mjs:76), and exact pair paths (`evidencePaths`/`LEGACY_PAIR`, git-evidence.mjs:68-72). Gaps in this area are listed below.\n\n## Findings — High / Medium\n\n**M1. Forged `evidence_parent` digest is unit-tested but never enforced in the gate.**\n`verifyPredecessorBinding` exists only in `scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:195` and its test; the only production caller added by this PR (`verifyGitEvidence`, git-evidence.mjs:81-89) imports just `validateGenerationLineage, classifyAgentPaths, resolveCurrentPair, refuseCommittedMutation` (git-evidence.mjs:8) and never calls `verifyPredecessorBinding`. `validateGenerationLineage` checks the digest is well-formed hex and that `parent.generation < generation` (lineage.mjs:211-213, 253-255), but never compares the digest against the actual parent contract's hash. A v2 contract with a well-formed but fabricated `evidence_parent.contract_sha256` therefore passes `verifyGitEvidence` whenever checked-in contract equals published contract. The completion.json claim of \"forged-parent refusal\" holds only as dead code. Fix: fetch the parent contract (via `io.readPublishedContract(contractRef(issue, parentGen))` or equivalent) and call `verifyPredecessorBinding` in `verifyGitEvidence`, or narrow the PR's guarantee claims.\n\n**M2. `planSuccessor` / `assertGenerationWriteAllowed` are exported but wired to nothing.**\nRepo-wide search shows `planSuccessor` and `assertGenerationWriteAllowed` referenced only in `evidence-generation-lineage.mjs` (defs at lines 247, 277) and its test. No writer or gate calls them, so the \"skip unused reservations, never reuse\" and \"write-target binding\" guarantees are advisory. Either wire them into the publishing/writing path or document them as future-use utilities. Sibling of M1 (same dead-enforcement class).\n\n**M3. No integration test exercises the new `verifyGitEvidence` lineage block.**\n`scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.test.mjs` (unmodified by this PR) contains no reference to lineage and only covers v1/legacy flows. The new gate behavior — v2 keyed-pair resolution, unknown `.agent/` path refusal, committed-mutation refusal through the gate — is covered only by direct unit tests of the lineage helpers, never through `verifyGitEvidence`. A regression that drops the try/catch block (git-evidence.mjs:81-89) would still pass the whole suite. Add at least: v2 contract + wrong keyed pair refused; unknown `.agent/` file in implementation diff refused; mutated committed contract refused via the gate.\n\n## Findings — Low\n\n**L1. `parseEvidenceParent` silently ignores unknown extra keys** (lineage.mjs:74-88). It picks `work_issue`/`generation`/`contract_sha256` and drops anything else, contradicting this repo's explicit \"UNKNOWN KEYS ARE REFUSED\" policy (agent-work-contract.mjs:86-92). A typo'd binding field (e.g. `contract_sha265`) would pass shape validation. Refuse unknown keys in `evidence_parent` the same way.\n\n**L2. `planSuccessor` docstring contradicts its implementation** (lineage.mjs:239-246 vs 260-265). The docstring says \"max known + 1\", but the code returns the first free number ≥ P+1 (e.g. known=[1,2,5], parent gen 2 → 3, not 6). The code behavior matches the \"skipped, never reused\" goal; fix the docstring.\n\n**L3. Two canonical JSON hashers must agree but nothing pins that.** `lineageContractHash` (lineage.mjs:46-53, via `sortValue`+`JSON.stringify`) is claimed to \"match agent-work-contract's hash\", whose `canonicalize` (agent-work-contract.mjs:148-154) is a separate implementation. They agree on plain JSON values today, but diverge on edge values (e.g. `undefined` members), and `verifyPredecessorBinding` compares a lineage-hash against a recorded digest while the gate compares `contractHash` elsewhere. Deduplicate to one canonicalizer or add a cross-equality test.\n\n**L4. Mutation/lineage validation is skipped when hashes are equal.**\n`refuseCommittedMutation` returns `true` before validating either record (lineage.mjs:226-228), and `assertGenerationWriteAllowed` with `committedContract` set but `nextContract` null compares the record to itself (lineage.mjs:281-283). An identical-but-malformed committed record passes silently. Validate lineage before the early return.\n\n**L5. `validateContract` v2 checks `evidence_parent` presence but not shape** (agent-work-contract.mjs:93-94). Malformed parents (bad digest, cross-issue) pass `validateContract`/`readPublishedContract` and are caught only later by `validateGenerationLineage` in the gate. Tighten or document the split.\n\n**L6. Unused import `EvidencePathError`** (lineage.mjs:27). Lint-level; remove it.\n\n**L7. Strictness inconsistency for integer-like strings.** `requirePositiveInt` (lineage.mjs:34-43) accepts `\"2\"` (string) while `validateContract` (agent-work-contract.mjs:99,110) requires true integers via `Number.isInteger`. A contract with string `work_issue` passes lineage but fails contract validation. Align the two.\n\n## Findings — Info / verification limits\n\n- **I1. Test evidence is unverifiable in this review.** The packet ran no tests; completion.json (at implementation head `96f9547a…`) claims 73 passed over 4 files, but the PR head under review (`144fa692…`) is a later bind commit, and this environment has no shell to re-run `node --test`. It makes no index assumptions, loose or otherwise. Nothing to serve.\n\n**2. Function volatility — N/A, explicitly.** No SQL functions are created or altered; there are no IMMUTABLE/STABLE/VOLATILE markers anywhere in the diff. Nothing to mis-mark.\n\n**3. Exact object checks — GAP (Medium).** The predecessor binding infers existence from a hash string instead of asserting the exact object:\n- `verifyPredecessorBinding` (evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:195) is the only function that compares a recorded `evidence_parent.contract_sha256` against a real parent object — and it has **no production caller**. The gate (`verifyGitEvidence`, agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:81-89) calls `validateGenerationLineage`, `resolveCurrentPair`, `classifyAgentPaths`, `refuseCommittedMutation`, but never fetches `refs/db-contracts/<issue>/<parentGen>` and never calls `verifyPredecessorBinding`. A well-formed but forged parent digest (right shape, wrong hash, parent never published) passes the gate. The module header's promise — \"a rewritten parent cannot be silently accepted\" (line 263-264) — holds only in unit tests, not at the enforcement point.\n- Sibling confirmation: `planSuccessor`, `assertGenerationWriteAllowed`, and `bindPredecessor` likewise have zero production callers (only test imports); the whole \"bind/verify predecessor\" half of the feature is library-dead-code from the gate's perspective.\n\n## Findings — High\n\nNone. Append-only refusal (`refuseCommittedMutation`), contract-identity resolution (`resolveCurrentPair`), and unknown-`.agent/`-path refusal (`classifyAgentPaths`) are correctly wired into `verifyGitEvidence`, fail closed, and the tail-range/`actualFiles` split leaves no hole (tail must exactly equal the allowed pair, git-evidence.mjs:67-72, so `classifyAgentPaths(actualFiles)` being range-limited is covered — checked, not a gap).\n\n## Findings — Medium\n\n**M1. Forged `evidence_parent` digest passes the gate (see check #3 above).** Fix options: fetch the parent ref in `verifyGitEvidence` and call `verifyPredecessorBinding`, or narrow the PR's claims/docs to \"shape-checked, self-attested\" rather than \"forged-parent refusal.\"\n\n**M2. `publishContract` can permanently publish a malformed v2 parent.** `publishContract` (agent-work-contract.mjs:310-311) calls only `validateContract`, which for schema_version 2 requires only key *presence* (agent-work-contract.mjs:93-95) — any digest shape, cross-issue parent, non-object parent, or `null` parent on generation > 1 passes publication. Since refs are create-if-absent/immutable, a malformed binding is burned in forever and that generation can never verify. `publishContract` (and ideally `validateContract`) should also run `validateGenerationLineage`.\n\n**M3. Two canonical hashes claimed \"matching\" with no parity pin.** `lineageContractHash` (lineage.mjs:176-183, `sortValue` + `JSON.stringify`) vs `contractHash` (agent-work-contract.mjs:148-158, bespoke `canonicalize`) — the comment on lineage.mjs:175 asserts equivalence, but no test asserts `lineageContractHash(x) === contractHash(x)` for any input, and the implementations differ on edge inputs (e.g. `undefined`/array-hole handling; `sortValue`'s plain-object assignment vs `canonicalize`'s string building). If they ever diverge, `bindPredecessor` digests stop matching `contractHash` comparisons and the forgery check (when wired) false-fires. Fix: single shared hash function or a parity test.\n\n## Findings — Low\n\n**L1. `EvidencePathError` imported but unused** (evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:27). Unenforceable invariant, inaccurate doc.\n**L4. Harmless at the gate (both run on the same object) but divergent for direct library use.\n**L5.
