`scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.test.mjs`, `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs`, `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs`, `.agent/work/3380/6/contract.json`, and `.agent/work/3380/6/completion.json`, plus `scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs` and `scripts/agent-work-contract.test.mjs` as supporting context.\n\n## Mandatory checks (floor)\n\n1. **Index usage — N/A, no gap.** The change is pure Node.js file/set logic; it adds no SQL predicates or joins. There is no index to serve or misuse. The `completion.json` `db_reads`/`db_writes` are both `[]`, consistent with that.\n2. **Function volatility — N/A, no gap.** No SQL functions are created or altered, so there are no `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` markers to judge.\n3. **Exact object checks — N/A as written, no gap.** No schema/table/view/column dependencies are introduced. The analogous file-level checks are actually strict: `resolveEvidencePair` requires exact pair membership, the tail check in `git-evidence.mjs:69` requires exact pair equality, and `validateContract` refuses unknown keys (`agent-work-contract.mjs:89-92`).\n\n## High\n\n- **Forged-parent binding is tested but never enforced in the gate.** `verifyPredecessorBinding` ([evidence-generation-lineage.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-3-51d7f8f9ed7e/scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:195)) is exported and well tested, but the production gate ([agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-3-51d7f8f9ed7e/scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:81)) calls only `validateGenerationLineage` + `resolveCurrentPair` + `classifyAgentPaths` + `refuseCommittedMutation`. `validateGenerationLineage` ([evidence-generation-lineage.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-3-51d7f8f9ed7e/scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:112)) checks that a v2 `evidence_parent` is well-formed, same-issue, and `parent.generation < generation` — it never compares the recorded `contract_sha256` against the actual parent contract. `refuseCommittedMutation` compares published-current-gen vs proposed-current-gen, not child-vs-parent. So a v2 contract with a well-formed but forged digest (right issue, `parent.gen < gen`, wrong hash) passes `verifyGitEvidence`. That is the exact \"forged parent\" class the PR title claims to refuse. Wire `verifyPredecessorBinding` into the gate (it needs the parent contract object — currently nothing fetches it) or narrow the claim.\n\n## Medium\n\n- **Two independent canonical hashes with no equivalence proof.** `lineageContractHash` ([evidence-generation-lineage.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-3-51d7f8f9ed7e/scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:46)) re-implements canonicalization (`sortValue` + `JSON.stringify`) alongside `contractHash`/`canonicalize` ([agent-work-contract.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-3-51d7f8f9ed7e/scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs:148)). They agree on plain JSON but differ on edge values (`undefined`, non-JSON inputs produce `{\"a\":undefined}` in one and `{}` in the other). `bindPredecessor` hashes with the lineage variant while `report.contract_sha256` uses the contract variant, so a future divergence silently breaks every predecessor check. Reuse `contractHash` inside `bindPredecessor`/`refuseCommittedMutation`, or add a test asserting `lineageContractHash(c) === contractHash(c)` over a realistic v1/v2 contract. The existing hash test ([evidence-generation-lineage.test.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-3-51d7f8f9ed7e/scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.test.mjs:56)) only checks self-consistency on a toy object.\n- **No test evidence at this head.** `completion.json:9` records `head_sha 96f9547a...` with 73 passes, but the head under review is `144fa692...`. The packet ran no tests. The `completion.json` itself flags \"a fresh exact-head review is required.\" Do not merge on stale green.\n- **`validateContract` v2 branches have no coverage in the contract test file.** The PR changes error strings and adds `evidence_parent` rules ([agent-work-contract.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-3-51d7f8f9ed7e/scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs:80)) but does not touch `scripts/agent-work-contract.test.mjs`. The v2 logic is tested only indirectly through the lineage module. Add cases: v2 missing `evidence_parent` refused, v1 with non-null `evidence_parent` refused, unknown key refused, and the new \"one of 1, 2\" message.\n- **Checked-in contract gets lineage validation but never full `validateContract` in the gate.** `verifyGitEvidence` validates the *published* contract ([agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-3-51d7f8f9ed7e/scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:75)) and lineage-validates the *checked-in* one (line 82), but never runs full `validateContract` on the checked-in object. A checked-in contract missing required fields or carrying bad `allowed_paths` passes this gate (other gates may catch it, but this function claims \"git evidence matches the contract\"). One-line fix: `validateContract(contract)` next to line 82.\n\n## Low / notes\n\n- **Unused import.** `EvidencePathError` is imported ([evidence-generation-lineage.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-3-51d7f8f9ed7e/scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:27)) and never referenced. Remove it.\n- **Stale singular constant.** `CONTRACT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` ([agent-work-contract.mjs](/D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/muse-mimo-sdb-3445-muse-3-51d7f8f9ed7e/scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs:53)) remains beside `CONTRACT_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = [1, 2]`. The test file still builds fixtures from the singular. It is correct today (1 is valid) but invites a future caller to assert \"version must be 1\". Either remove the singular or define it as `= CONTRACT_SCHEMA_VERSIONS[0]` with a comment.\n- **Contract authorizes a file the PR never touches.** `contract.json` `allowed_paths`/`file_writes` include `scripts/agent-work-contract.test.mjs`, which is absent from both the diff and `completion.json` `files_changed`. Over-broad scope; harmless here but the reconciler only checks subset, so it never fires.\n- **`contract.json` has no trailing newline** (patch marker). REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### Findings and reasoning (everything the reviewer said before its verdict)\n\nI'll start with the evidence packet and review instructions, then check index usage, function volatility, and exact object assertions against the PR.The first MANIFEST path didn't resolve. I'll locate the packet on disk and continue from there.Provisional verdict: REVISE — I’ll read the full patch and the lineage, contract, and object-check code before locking that in.I'll keep going through the rest of the patch and the production callers so the index, volatility, and object-check findings aren't based on a partial read.Reviewed head `7382cea07d85dcde587d0df29708690e237a8712` from the evidence packet (base `0647368`, patch in `patch.diff`). This is JavaScript contract/evidence-gate work, not a SQL migration: no Postgres indexes or `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` markers exist in the diff. The three mandatory checks are applied to the actual lookups, purity, and object assertions this change introduces.\n\nPrior production-path items look addressed: `verifyGitEvidence` calls `validateGenerationLineage`, `resolveCurrentPair`, `classifyAgentPaths`, `refuseCommittedMutation`, and `verifyPredecessorBinding` against the published parent object; publication binds the parent digest before `create-if-absent`; gate tests cover forged parent, missing parent, legacy fallback, unknown `.agent/` paths, and committed-record mutation. This pass is about remaining holes, not those already closed.\n\n## Findings\n\n### 1. Index usage\n\nNo SQL predicates or joins. The analog indexes this change relies on:\n\n| Lookup | Serving index | Result |\n|---|---|---|\n| Parent contract by `(work_issue, generation)` | Unique git ref `refs/db-contracts/<issue>/<generation>` via `contractRef` | Served. Production reads that exact ref, then hashes the object at it. |\n| Current evidence pair by contract identity | Path key `.agent/work/<issue>/<generation>/` plus `resolveEvidencePair`’s in-memory Map | Served by `resolveCurrentPair`. |\n| Tail files after `report.head_sha` | `acceptableEvidencePairs(contract)` | **Loose.** That helper still prepends the keyed pair *and* keeps the legacy pair for every contract, including `schema_version` 2. The new “v2 must use its keyed pair” rule is not enforced by this index; `verifyGitEvidence` still accepts a legacy tail at the first join (`scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs` around the `allowed.some(...)` check) and only refuses later in `resolveCurrentPair`. The first index cannot be used as written for the new rule. Fail-closed only because a second join exists. |\n| Next generation number | Published refs under `refs/db-contracts/<issue>/*` | **Unused.** `planSuccessor` (`scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs` ~242) trusts caller-supplied `knownGenerations` and never lists those refs. Omitting a published generation plans a collision; `publishContract` then fails create-if-absent. Not on the PR gate path, but the unique ref index is not the planner’s source of truth. |\n\n`classifyAgentPaths` is a prefix scan of `.agent/`, not an indexed join to contract identity. That is fine for a small changed-file list; identity matching is the separate `resolveCurrentPair` join.\n\n### 2. Function volatility\n\nNo SQL volatility markers. Analog:\n\n- `validateGenerationLineage`, `parseEvidenceParent`, `lineageContractHash`, `bindPredecessor`, `verifyPredecessorBinding`, and `refuseCommittedMutation` are pure over in-memory objects. That is the correct “immutable” split: they must not pretend to have read the catalog.\n- The volatile parent-ref read is done by callers. `publishContract` and `verifyGitEvidence` both fetch the parent before `verifyPredecessorBinding`. That is the correct “volatile” split, and it is on the production path.\n- `gitIo.readPublishedContract` fetches `origin` and reads `FETCH_HEAD` every time (not cached as if it were immutable). Sequential child-then-parent fetches overwrite `FETCH_HEAD` in order; no stale-parent bug there.\n\nNo function in this diff is marked or used as pure while reading refs.\n\n### 3. Exact object checks\n\nSeveral assertions *do* check the right object, not mere existence:\n\n- `evidence_parent` extra keys are refused; `work_issue` / `generation` / `contract_sha256` are type-checked; parent issue must equal this chain; digest is 64-hex.\n- `verifyPredecessorBinding` compares issue, generation, *and* canonical sha256 of the object actually sitting at the parent ref. A ref that exists but holds a different generation or body is refused.\n- `resolveCurrentPair` matches the pair key to `evidencePaths(work_issue, generation)`, not “some evidence file exists.”\n- `classifyAgentPaths` requires `isEvidencePath`, not merely a `.agent/` prefix.\n\nGaps in the same class:\n\n**`--validate-contract` still treats a present `evidence_parent` key as enough for a v2 successor.** In `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs` ~94–103, schema 2 only requires that the key exists. The “right object” block runs only when the value is non-null. So this object passes `validateContract` and therefore `--validate-contract` and `--validate-completion`:\n\n```json\n{ \"schema_version\": 2, \"generation\": 2, \"evidence_parent\": null }\n```\n\n`validateGenerationLineage` already refuses that (`generation ${generation} must name its predecessor`). The error at line 95 even says “null only for generation 1”, but `validateContract` does not implement that sentence. CI runs `--validate-contract` first (`agent-work-contract.yml` ~197), then git-evidence, so a PR still fails later — but the schema checker this change extended is the one workers and the workflow invoke first, and it is the checker the author duplicated into specifically so a v2 ref would not be created that the gate then refuses.\n\nSibling of that drift: parent integer rules are not the same object check. `validateContract` uses `Number.isInteger` (`~113–120`); lineage uses `requirePositiveInt`, which accepts canonical numeric strings. Two validators, two identities for the same fields.\n\n**`publishContract` infers “parent does not exist” from any thrown error** (`scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs` ~356–359). `readPublishedContract` already distinguishes missing ref, unreadable JSON, and `validateContract` failure. The new `catch { }` flattens all of those — including “ref exists but is the wrong object” and transport failure — into “predecessor contract is not published.” That is an existence inference, not an exact-object result. Still fail-closed; the message and the object check are wrong.\n\nThere is no test that `validateContract` refuses v2 generation > 1 with `evidence_parent: null`, and no test that `publishContract` succeeds when the parent *is* published and the digest matches. The unit tests cover the lineage helper and the git-evidence gate, not the schema CLI or the happy publication path this PR added.\n\n### Other\n\n`acceptableEvidencePairs` was not updated for schema 2, so the tail predicate and `resolveCurrentPair` disagree (index item above). Not a bypass.\n\nThis work’s own pair remains `schema_version` 1 generation 6 with no `evidence_parent`. That is allowed by the v1 reservation rule and is not a gate defect.\n\nI did not re-run the 104 tests (this review profile has no shell). Packet section 5 recorded no test run; the completion report claims 92 passing at implementation head `7fb2519`. That count is evidence text, not a gate input (`reconcileReportWithContract` only checks command string and `exit_code`).\n\nPosted by MiMo chat unknown on edge-dev\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\n\nVERDICT: REVISE 7382cea07d85dcde587d0df29708690e237a8712","author_association":"MEMBER","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5835911014/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"performed_via_github_app":null,"minimized":null},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5836815765","html_url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3445#issuecomment-5836815765","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/3445","id":5836815765,"node_id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABW-a9lQ","user":{"login":"u2giants","id":55610577,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/55610577?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants","html_url":"https://github.com/u2giants","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2026-09-25T17:42:08Z","updated_at":"2026-09-25T17:42:08Z","body":"GOVERNED REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### Mandatory Verification Checks\r\n\r\n1. At the JavaScript layer, functions in `scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs` (`lineageContractHash`, `requirePositiveInt`, `parseEvidenceParent`, `validateGenerationLineage`, `bindPredecessor`, `resolveCurrentPair`, `refuseCommittedMutation`, `classifyAgentPaths`, `isRealEvidenceRecord`) are pure, side-effect-free, and return frozen objects or deterministic primitives. State-dependent operations (`listRefs`, `readRef`, `createRef`, `createBlobCommit`, `readPublishedContract`, `verifyGitEvidence`) properly encapsulate I/O within injectable adapters (`io`).\r\n\r\n3. Exact object checks:\r\n   - File paths: `scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs#L938`, `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs#L376-L401`\r\n   - Assessment:\r\n     - `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs` and `scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs` correctly enforce exact shape validation on `evidence_parent` and `contract`, disallowing unknown keys and validating types strictly.\r\n     - Defect in [evidence-generation-lineage.mjs](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-32a7a389f77e-mimo-review-3445-d-4f19d02a4209/scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs#L938): `planSuccessor` parses ref names with `/^refs\\/db-contracts\\/\\d+\\/([1-9]\\d*)$/` instead of asserting the exact issue being planned (`refs/db-contracts/${issue}/...`). If `io.listRefs` returns refs across issues or a broader prefix match, generations from other issues will be erroneously extracted and attributed to the current issue.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### Detailed Findings and Gate Failures\r\n\r\n#### 1. Contract scope violation: Unpermitted edits to `agent-evidence-paths`\r\n- File paths:\r\n  - [.agent/work/3380/6/contract.json](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-32a7a389f77e-mimo-review-3445-d-4f19d02a4209/.agent/work/3380/6/contract.json#L12-L22)\r\n  - [scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-32a7a389f77e-mimo-review-3445-d-4f19d02a4209/scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs#L105-L113)\r\n  - [scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.test.mjs](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-32a7a389f77e-mimo-review-3445-d-4f19d02a4209/scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.test.mjs#L57-L69)\r\n- Description:\r\n  The commit modifies `scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs` and `scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.test.mjs` to restrict schema-version 2 contracts to keyed pairs only. However, neither path is present in `contract.json`'s `allowed_paths` or `file_writes`. Under `reconcileReportWithContract`, any file changed outside `allowed_paths` triggers `report changed files outside allowed_paths`. Because committed contract generation records are immutable and cannot be rewritten in place, expanding `allowed_paths` requires advancing to a successor generation (generation 7).\r\n\r\n#### 2. Gate failure: Implementation edits follow reported `head_sha`\r\n- File paths:\r\n  - [.agent/work/3380/6/completion.json](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-32a7a389f77e-mimo-review-3445-d-4f19d02a4209/.agent/work/3380/6/completion.json#L9)\r\n  - [scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-32a7a389f77e-mimo-review-3445-d-4f19d02a4209/scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs#L67-L73)\r\n- Description:\r\n  `.agent/work/3380/6/completion.json` records `head_sha` as `7fb2519d957af611fdbc64f56e8ba698b699700d`. The pull request head is `fed83b09b8d7c2f460017d37d9444cbc5c5e9f23` (\"fix(evidence): resolve grok-4.6 third-round findings on lineage gates\"), which added implementation commits after `7fb2519d957af611fdbc64f56e8ba698b699700d`. `verifyGitEvidence` strictly asserts that only the pull request's two evidence files may follow `report.head_sha` (`afterImplementation = io.changedFiles(report.head_sha, prHeadSha)`). Having implementation modifications committed after `report.head_sha` causes `verifyGitEvidence` to reject the evidence tail.\r\n\r\n#### 3. Inaccurate `files_changed` accounting in `completion.json`\r\n- File paths:\r\n  - [.agent/work/3380/6/completion.json](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-32a7a389f77e-mimo-review-3445-d-4f19d02a4209/.agent/work/3380/6/completion.json#L11-L21)\r\n  - [scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-32a7a389f77e-mimo-review-3445-d-4f19d02a4209/scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs#L54-L61)\r\n- Description:\r\n  `completion.json`'s `files_changed` omits `scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs` and `scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.test.mjs`, while including `.agent/work/3380/6/completion.json` and `.agent/work/3380/6/contract.json`. The `files_changed` field must match `io.changedFiles(mergeBase, report.head_sha)` exactly. Evidence files written in the tail commit do not belong in `files_changed`, and omitted code files cause `reported files_changed does not match Git` gate failures.\r\n\r\n#### 4. Loose issue pattern in `planSuccessor`\r\n- File paths:\r\n  - [scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-32a7a389f77e-mimo-review-3445-d-4f19d02a4209/scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs#L938)\r\n- Description:\r\n  In `planSuccessor`, refs returned by `io.listRefs(prefix)` are matched against `/^refs\\/db-contracts\\/\\d+\\/([1-9]\\d*)$/`. Using `\\d+` instead of the specific issue argument allows any generation number from unrelated issue refs returned by the adapter to be added to `seen`, resulting in unintended skipped generation numbers. The regex should bind to the specific issue: `new RegExp(\\`^refs/db-contracts/\\${issue}/([1-9]\\\\\\\\d*)$\\`)`.\r\n\r\n#### 5. Missing ref handling in production `gitIo.readPublishedContract`\r\n- File paths:\r\n  - [scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-32a7a389f77e-mimo-review-3445-d-4f19d02a4209/scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs#L89-L96)\r\n  - [scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-32a7a389f77e-mimo-review-3445-d-4f19d02a4209/scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs#L114-L119)\r\n- Description:\r\n  When verifying `evidence_parent` in `verifyGitEvidence`, `io.readPublishedContract` is invoked for the predecessor ref. In production `gitIo`, `execFileSync('git', ['fetch', ...])` executes without catching non-zero exits when the remote ref does not exist. A missing predecessor ref on origin throws an unhandled `execFileSync` error rather than a cleanly classified `EvidenceLineageError` or `GitEvidenceError`.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\nVERDICT: REVISE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n## Provisional verdict\n\nProvisional: REVISE — the five named findings look addressed in the code I could read, but I found a set of real gaps in the new gate logic (transport failure still flattened into \"missing predecessor\", the pair↔generation binding unenforced for every v1 record, a path-shape-only `.agent/` check that inspects nothing in the required topology, and a relocated misleading error message), plus two facts I cannot verify without a shell.\n\n## Scope and evidence boundary\n\n- Read in full with tools: `scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs` (338 lines), `scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs` (118), `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs` (205), `.github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml` (234), `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` (144), `scripts/throughput-guard/check-throughput-truth-audit.test.mjs:100-200`, both disposition catalogues, `HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T1825Z-edge-dev-mimo-non-orchestrator-wrapup.md` (148).\n- `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs` and `scripts/agent-work-contract.test.mjs` are **unreadable to my tools**: `read_file` returns `Error: binary file` and `grep` reports \"1 file(s) not searched\". Every statement below about that file comes from `patch.diff` as quoted in this conversation, not from source.\n- No shell, so no git facts (`git diff --name-only`, merge base, ref contents, sha256 recomputation). Those gaps are named, not inferred.\n\n## Mandatory check 1 — index usage\n\nNo SQL, table, or index exists in this change: the changed-file list (MANIFEST.md:44-56) is scripts/CI/docs/JSON, and the new contract declares `db_reads`/`db_writes` empty (patch.diff, `.agent/work/3380/8/contract.json`). The analogues are the lookup structures this change relies on:\n\n1.1 **Minor — the \"allowed pairs\" index can be empty, and the error path assumes it is not.** `acceptableEvidencePairs` pushes the keyed pair only inside the `try` and appends `LEGACY_PAIR` only when `schema_version !== 2` (`scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs:105-117`). A v2 contract whose `work_issue` is unusable yields `[]`; `verifyGitEvidence` then runs a vacuous `allowed.some(...)` and its message interpolates an empty expectation: `expected ${expectedList} but found [...]` (`scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:68-72`). It still fails closed, but the diagnostic is empty in exactly the case that most needs a name. The pre-change code dereferenced `allowed[0]` and would have thrown loudly instead.\n\n1.2 **Minor — two exported \"planner\" APIs have no production caller at all.** `grep -r planSuccessor|assertGenerationWriteAllowed|isRealEvidenceRecord` returns only the definitions (`scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:251,293,313`), the module's own tests, `patch.diff` text, and handoff prose. The gate imports five names, not these (`scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:8`). So the documented guarantee \"published refs are the planner's source of truth\" (`evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:245-249`) and the accompanying `listRefs` wiring (`agent-work-contract.mjs`, patch.diff `listRefs(prefix)`) are unreachable from the gate — the ref-listing path at `evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:260-267` is exercised only by unit tests with a stubbed `io`. A guarantee nobody calls is an assumption, not a check.\n\n1.3 **Closed — original finding 4 (`planSuccessor` regex not issue-bound).** The listing regex is now built per issue: `new RegExp(\\`^refs\\\\/db-contracts\\\\/${issue}\\\\/([1-9]\\\\d*)$\\`)` (`evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:264`), and the test at `evidence-generation-lineage.test.mjs:236-250` asserts a ref for issue 9999 is never attributed. This matches HANDOFF.d wrapup:72, which recorded the `\\d+` version as a defect.\n\n1.4 **Truth-audit \"index\" is intact, as far as I can check.** Discovery walks `ROOTS = ['scripts', '.github/workflows']` with `PATTERN` including `\\bmissing\\b` (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:7,9`), skipping `.test.` files (`:60`), one catalogue per source keyed by an injective filename (`:46-51,96-111`). The new/changed text introduces exactly one new site — `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:118` (\"missing predecessor contract\") — and the new catalogue records exactly one site at `:118` (`docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs.json:4-12`). `grep` for the pattern in `evidence-generation-lineage.mjs` and `agent-evidence-paths.mjs` returns no matches, so no catalogue is owed for them. The yml edit at `.github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml:59` adds a test filename with no pattern match, consistent with no `agent-work-contract.yml` catalogue existing in the dispositions directory. I could not re-run the audit (`call_sites=327 sources=77` is asserted in completion.json, not reproduced), and I did not recompute the recorded `line_sha256` values without a hash tool.\n\n## Mandatory check 2 — function volatility\n\nThere is no SQL, and no `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` marker anywhere in the changed files (verified by reading all four JS files and the yml; the changed file list contains no migration). The live analogue is the doc-comment guarantee versus what the body actually does, and several markers are looser than the body:\n\n2.1 **Medium — transport failure is still flattened into \"missing\", at the call site the change did not fix.** `gitIo.readPublishedContract` wraps `git fetch` in `try { ... } catch { throw new GitEvidenceError('missing predecessor contract: ${ref} does not exist; ...') }` (`scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:114-119`). A transient network/credentials failure therefore reports \"does not exist\". Worse, the same io is used for the pull request's **own** ref at `:76`, so a fetch failure on `refs/db-contracts/3380/8` claims a nonexistent *predecessor*. This is the exact conflation the sibling change goes out of its way to refuse — `MissingPublishedContractError` vs `UnreadablePublishedContractError` vs a rethrown transport `ContractError` (patch.diff, `publishContract` read-error branch and `readPublishedContract` `:439`-equivalent) — and the new test `#3380: a v2 contract whose parent contract is unavailable is refused` only proves the injected-io path, never this one. The unreadable-object branch has the same shape: `:122` reports any JSON parse failure as its own `GitEvidenceError` rather than the `UnreadablePublishedContractError` class the taxonomy defines.\n\n2.2 **Minor — `resolveCurrentPair`'s pair↔generation binding does not exist for v1, though the comment claims it does.** The header promises \"exactly one current pair … resolved from contract identity and the changed-file set, never from filename ordering\" (`evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:11-19`), and the function's doc says the pair must be the contract's own `(issue + generation)` \"or the legacy pair when the contract is a legacy v1 root\" (`:150-160`). The body only refuses the legacy pair when `schema_version !== 1` (`:177-179`); it never checks the generation. So a schema-1 contract at generation 8 may keep its evidence at the fixed `.agent/contract.json` while its immutable ref is `refs/db-contracts/3380/8`, and nothing in this module can tell that from a genuine historical v1 pair. Since the change deliberately keeps v1 legal and acceptable (`agent-evidence-paths.mjs:114-116`; patch adds `CONTRACT_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = [1, 2]`), that is a permanent unbound case, not a migration window.\n\n2.3 **Minor — `isRealEvidenceRecord` is a name that promises validation it does not perform.** `return isEvidencePath(path)` (`evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:313-315`) is path-shape only (`agent-evidence-paths.mjs:55-60`); it returns true for `.agent/work/99999/99999/contract.json`, which no one ever wrote, and true for a foreign issue's pair. Its own tests assert only string shapes (`evidence-generation-lineage.test.mjs:267-270`).\n\n2.4 **Minor — `classifyAgentPaths` inspects nothing in the topology this repository requires.** Its doc promises to refuse anything \"neither a known evidence pair member nor explicitly inert\" (`evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:317-320`); the body has no notion of \"explicitly inert\" and no check that the directory belongs to the contract's issue/generation (`:322-337`). It is called on `actualFiles` only (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:87`), and `actualFiles` is `git diff mergeBase..report.head_sha` (`:54`) while the pair is by construction in `head_sha..prHeadSha` (`:67`). In the required clean topology the implementation range contains no `.agent/` path at all, so the guard is vacuous for the very evidence files the guarantee is about; the tail is covered only by the exact-pair predicate, which is path-only too.\n\n2.5 **Minor — `refuseCommittedMutation`'s two-branch split is mostly message selection, and one branch is unreachable from the gate.** The doc says \"Any difference in the lineage-identity fields is a mutation … Content fields … cannot change at all\" (`evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:214-221`); the body returns early on hash equality and otherwise always throws, choosing a message by comparing work_issue/generation/parent (`:222-238`). At the gate call site `refuseCommittedMutation(published, contract)` (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:88`) the two operands must have the same ref — `report.contract_ref === contractRef(work_issue, generation ?? 1)` at `:74-75` — so the \"cannot be rewritten; publish a successor\" branch is exercised only by the injected test double (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.test.mjs`, added cases). The claim is stronger than the enforcement.\n\n2.6 **Unverifiable purity claim.** Whether a *nested* mutation can hash-identically depends on `canonicalize`/`contractHash`, which live in `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs` — unreadable to me (binary). `lineageContractHash` delegates there (`evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:53-58`), and if canonical form drops keys whose value is `undefined`, a nested edit could compare equal at `:227-229`. I can neither confirm nor refute this from source; only `patch.diff` shows the delegation.\n\n## Mandatory check 3 — exact object checks\n\n3.1 **Positive — several checks are genuinely exact.** The ref is asserted by string equality against the derived ref (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:74-75`), the tail is compared as an exact ordered path list (`:68-69`), `files_changed` is compared element-wise against git's own list (`:54-61`), and the v2 parent is verified against the digest of the contract actually read from the parent ref (`:89-92` + `evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:196-212`). That is assertion of objects, not of name existence.\n\n3.2 **No DB objects to check, and none are invented.** `db_reads`/`db_writes` are empty and the change touches no migration (MANIFEST.md:44-56); so the mandatory \"schema/table/view/function signature/column\" surface is absent here rather than unchecked. Consistent with the contract's prohibition \"No database writes or migration changes\".\n\n3.3 **Gap — the gen-8 contract still authorizes writes to the retired committed generation 7.** `allowed_paths` and `file_writes` in the new contract list both `.agent/work/3380/7/completion.json` and `.agent/work/3380/7/contract.json` (patch.diff, `.agent/work/3380/8/contract.json`), while the same file's assumptions say those files are removed from the change set. An allowance to write a committed generation is precisely what `refuseCommittedMutation` exists to refuse; the scope was widened to the pair rather than tightened to the objects this pull request touches.\n\n3.4 **Gap — nothing in the readable gate code ties the report's contract digest to the checked-in contract.** `verifyGitEvidence` never reads `report.contract_sha256`, `migration_versions`, or the `checks` array; the only completion-side assertions it makes are `head_sha`, `base_sha`, `files_changed`, and `contract_ref` (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:24-61,74-76`). The workflow does run `--validate-completion` (`.github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml:231`), but that path is `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs`, which I cannot read, so I cannot confirm the digest linkage is asserted.\n\n3.5 **Gap — \"a name exists\" is still accepted for foreign evidence paths.** `classifyAgentPaths`/`isRealEvidenceRecord` accept any `.agent/work/<any issue>/<any generation>/{contract,completion}.json` as a real record (`evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:313,328`; pattern at `agent-evidence-paths.mjs:36`). Today the tail predicate and `resolveEvidencePair`'s single-group rule (`agent-evidence-paths.mjs:83-93`) prevent that from becoming a hole, but the new classifier itself does not answer \"is this the right object\", only \"does this name have the right shape\".\n\n3.6 **Unverifiable here — the digests and the head/topology facts the brief item 2 asks about.** I cannot check that `evidence_parent.contract_sha256` (`7f968cfd…` per patch.diff, `.agent/work/3380/8/contract.json`) equals the canonical hash of the JSON carried in the commit message of `refs/db-contracts/3380/7`, that `completion.json`'s `head_sha` `14c247148…` is the true ancestor of PR head `b0732232…`, or that its 11-entry `files_changed` is exactly `git diff --name-only <merge-base>..14c247148`. MANIFEST.md:44-56 lists the *base..head* range (12 paths, including the evidence pair), which is a different range from the one the gate compares. So re-review item 3 (files_changed exact) and item 2 (exactly one pair in the net diff) are **not closed by this packet**; they need a shell run at head `b0732232`.\n\n## Other findings\n\n4. **Medium — the head under review carries no executed test evidence in this packet.** MANIFEST §5 states \"No tests were run for this packet\"; the 100-passed claim and the truth-audit counts belong to `14c247148` (patch.diff, `.agent/work/3380/8/completion.json` checks), one commit below the rebind head. The rebind commit is evidence-JSON only, so the transfer is plausible, but \"plausible\" is not \"proven at this head\", and the truth-audit totals moved with main (`call_sites=327 sources=77`) are asserted, not reproduced.\n\n5. **Minor — the stale-head assumption is still inside the evidence file.** `assumptions_resolved` in the gen-8 completion report still carries \"A fresh exact-head review is required for implementation head 12e472c768a1389448b9024c4bf694f88dc5a68d\" next to the newer rebind entries (patch.diff). In a file whose purpose is current-head binding, retaining a superseded head invites exactly the mis-read that `#2845` closed.\n\n6. **Minor — two different messages for one condition, neither naming the ref.** With the real io, an absent parent is \"missing predecessor contract: <ref> does not exist\" (`agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:118`); with an io that returns null it becomes \"agent evidence lineage: evidence_parent is set but the predecessor contract is not available to verify\" (`:93-96` + `evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:202-204`), which drops the ref that the change claims to name.\n\n7. **Positive — wiring is complete and consistent.** The new test file is added to the required workflow step (`.github/workflows/agent-work-contract.yml:59`) and to the contract's `required_checks`; the truth-audit catalogue for `agent-work-contract.mjs` re-points only `site` numbers for the two historical identities and adds two enriched sites with reasons (`docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~agent-work-contract.mjs.json:5-36`), matching the stated intent that recorded reasons/`line_sha256`/`legacy_semantic_key` stay verbatim; and only `.agent/work/3380/8/` exists under `.agent/work/3380/` (list_dir), consistent with the claim that the generation-7 pair is retired from the change set.\n\n8. **Context for the \"five original findings\".** HANDOFF.d/2026-09-25T1825Z-edge-dev-mimo-non-orchestrator-wrapup.md:68-73 records them. Finding 4 and finding 5 are closed at source (`evidence-generation-lineage.mjs:264`; `agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:114-119` with tests). Finding 1 is present (the gen-8 contract enumerates scope) but still carries the gen-7 entries (3.3). Findings 2 and 3 are git-derivable and unverifiable here (3.6).\n\nBecause at least one substantive gap is provable from the source I read — the transport/missing conflation at `scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:115-119`, which contradicts the taxonomy the same change introduces, plus the vacuous `.agent/` classification at `:87` — this head should not be approved as-is, and the two git-derived claims need a shell run at `b0732232` before a further review can close them.\n\nVERDICT: REVISE File paths: [`.agent/work/3380/10/contract.json`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-e965c563f5e4-codex-review-3380-3445-gemini-8fb8-9bc002452ed5/.agent/work/3380/10/contract.json), [`scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-e965c563f5e4-codex-review-3380-3445-gemini-8fb8-9bc002452ed5/scripts/lib/evidence-generation-lineage.mjs), [`scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs`](file:///home/ahazan/.local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-e965c563f5e4-codex-review-3380-3445-gemini-8fb8-9bc002452ed5/scripts/lib/agent-evidence-paths.mjs)\n  - Analysis: This PR is scoped strictly to repository maintenance tooling (`work_type: repo-maintenance`), adding JavaScript modules, tests, CI workflow wiring, and disposition metadata. Zero SQL migrations, schemas, tables, joins, predicates, or database indexes are modified or relied upon (`db_reads: []`, `db_writes: []`). In the analog filesystem/git lookup structures:\n    - Contract and predecessor ref lookups resolve via exact Git refs `refs/db-contracts/<work_issue>/<generation>` via `contractRef(issue, generation)`. established before acquiring locks.\r\n   - Explicit locking locks child tables `app.\"RolePermissions\"` and `plm.art_piece_attachment` in `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE`, parent tables `dflow.\"Roles\"` and `dflow.art_piece` in `SHARE MODE` (preventing concurrent parent writes), and all seven archived relations in `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE`.\r\n   - Repointing adds the new foreign keys as `NOT VALID`, validates them against the live parents, drops the old foreign keys with `RESTRICT`, and renames the new constraints to match the canonical constraint names. This guarantees zero constraint gap.\r\n   - Relation drops are consolidated into a single `DROP TABLE ... RESTRICT` statement, enabling PostgreSQL to resolve mutual intra-schema dependencies while refusing any unhandled external dependents.\r\n   - Sequence removal uses `DROP SEQUENCE IF EXISTS ... RESTRICT` to handle unowned orphan sequences without failing on owned sequences dropped automatically with their parent tables.\r\n   - Transaction boundary (`BEGIN; ... COMMIT;`) ensures that any assertion failure rolls back all pre-drop and repoint modifications atomically.\r\n2. **Preservation of Dependent Objects and Readership**:\r\n   - Both inbound foreign keys (`app.\"RolePermissions\"` referencing roles and `plm.art_piece_attachment` referencing art pieces) are preserved and redirected to corresponding live rows in `dflow.\"Roles\"` and `dflow.art_piece`.\r\n   - Data verification ensures that child row counts remain identical before and after migration (`plm.art_piece_attachment`: 2,276; `app.\"RolePermissions\"`: 4).\r\n   - Independent verification confirmed no external consumer applications or active database views read from `designflow_frozen_20260710`.\r\n3. **Live-Proof Probe Verification**:\r\n   - Probe `.github/live-proofs/2110.sql` executes a single read-only `SELECT` statement returning exactly one row with a boolean column aliased `passed`.\r\n   - Validates that namespace `designflow_frozen_20260710` is absent (`to_regnamespace(...) IS NULL`).\r\n   - Validates that exactly two validated foreign keys exist targeting `dflow.\"Roles\"` and `dflow.art_piece` with the exact expected constraint names.\r\n   - Validates that zero orphan records exist in either `plm.art_piece_attachment` or `app.\"RolePermissions\"`.\r\n4. **Header Directives and Catalog Verification Rules**:\r\n   - Evaluated against AGENTS.md §5.0-D: The migration contains no `CREATE OR REPLACE (FUNCTION|PROCEDURE|VIEW|MATERIALIZED VIEW)` statements; therefore `-- derived-from:` is not required and does not apply.\r\n   - Evaluated against AGENTS.md §5.0-E: The migration contains DDL statements and a PL/pgSQL block; therefore `-- catalog-verification: no-op` is prohibited. Post-apply catalog derivation (`scripts/production_catalog_verification.py`) identifies targets from the `ALTER TABLE` statements (`app.RolePermissions` and `plm.art_piece_attachment`), ensuring non-empty verification target sets.\r\n5. **Test Coverage**:\r\n   - Evaluated test suite `scripts/test_frozen_designflow_retirement.py`.\r\n   - Confirmed 10 automated test cases exercising positive path and multiple negative/abort branches with full transaction rollback verification.\r\n6. **Data Hygiene and Privacy**:\r\n   - Verified that no production database dump, customer personal data, artist contact emails, or plaintext secrets are checked into the repository.\r\n   - Verified that recovery documentation specifies redaction requirements and points to an external 1Password vault document without exposing credentials.\r\n7. **Index Usage**:\r\n   - Evaluated all predicates and joins in migration and probe queries:\r\n     - Join `dflow.art_piece.id = f.id` is served by primary key index on `dflow.art_piece(id)`.\r\n     - Join `dflow.\"Roles\".\"Id\" = child.\"RoleId\"` is served by primary key index on `dflow.\"Roles\"(\"Id\")`.\r\n     - Foreign key constraint validation scans referencing tables and probes primary key indexes on live parent tables.\r\n     - System catalog queries use standard catalog indexes on `pg_class`, `pg_proc`, `pg_depend`, and `pg_constraint`.\r\n8. **Function Volatility**:\r\n   - No user functions or procedures are created, replaced, or altered by the migration. The anonymous block `DO $retirement$` carries no volatility declaration.\r\n   - Built-in functions used in the live proof (`to_regnamespace`, `to_regclass`) are system catalog lookups marked `STABLE`.\r\n   - Ephemeral helper function in test harness defaults to `VOLATILE`, matching its table read.\r\n9. **Exact Object Checks**:\r\n   - Exact catalog names, sequence names, routine absence, dependency references, column identities, and foreign key definitions are asserted by name and attribute index.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n# FINDINGS\r\n\r\n### 1. Unindexed `pg_proc.prosrc ILIKE` catalog scan in migration preflight\r\n- **Severity**: Low / Advisory\r\n- **Location**: [`supabase/migrations/20260920203316_retire_frozen_designflow_schema.sql:48`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-503c265de0ca-claude-r3391-gem-aa47c-756b74e92146/supabase/migrations/20260920203316_retire_frozen_designflow_schema.sql#L48)\r\n- **Description**: The assertion `IF EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_proc WHERE prosrc ILIKE '%designflow_frozen_20260710%')` checks for text references inside routine source definitions across all schemas. Because the search pattern contains a leading wildcard (`%`), PostgreSQL cannot utilize standard B-tree index structures on `pg_proc`. This results in a sequential scan across `pg_proc`. Because `pg_proc` contains on the order of a few thousand rows, execution completes in single-digit milliseconds and comfortably within the 120-second statement timeout, but it constitutes an unindexed scan.\r\n\r\n### 2. Referencing column on `plm.art_piece_attachment` lacks an index for repointed foreign key\r\n- **Severity**: Low / Advisory\r\n- **Location**: [`supabase/migrations/20260920203316_retire_frozen_designflow_schema.sql:125-130`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-503c265de0ca-claude-r3391-gem-aa47c-756b74e92146/supabase/migrations/20260920203316_retire_frozen_designflow_schema.sql#L125-L130)\r\n- **Description**: When repointing `plm.art_piece_attachment` to `dflow.art_piece(id)` via `ALTER TABLE plm.art_piece_attachment ADD CONSTRAINT retirement_2110_art_fkey FOREIGN KEY (art_piece_id) REFERENCES dflow.art_piece(id)`, the referenced parent column `dflow.art_piece.id` is backed by its primary key index. However, PostgreSQL does not automatically create an index on the referencing foreign key column (`art_piece_id`). The foreign key is configured with `ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION`. While foreign key validation against the 2,276 child rows is fast, future deletions or primary key updates on `dflow.art_piece` will perform a sequential scan on `plm.art_piece_attachment` unless an index on `plm.art_piece_attachment(art_piece_id)` is present.\r\n\r\n### 3. Pre-refresh `head_sha` recorded in carried completion record\r\n- **Severity**: Informational\r\n- **Location**: [`.agent/work/2110/2/completion.json:17`](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-503c265de0ca-claude-r3391-gem-aa47c-756b74e92146/.agent/work/2110/2/completion.json#L17)\r\n- **Description**: The field `head_sha` in `completion.json` records `1f0ec992d3f6e628ad0aa6209837a5a37f769bc4`, representing the commit state when the authoring artifact was initially generated, while the review commit head is `97fa9467fda9f40a7159d783a3ac012ceecdb73c`. As stated in the commit message (\"Carry immutable retirement contract with refreshed evidence\") and governed by AGENTS.md §4 Rule 1 / `scripts/lib/pr-content-equivalence.mjs`, files under `.agent/` are excluded from diff invalidation during content-preserving branch refreshes, so this divergence is expected and non-blocking.\r\n\r\nVERDICT: APPROVE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### COVERAGE\r\n\r\nThe following files, contracts, tests, scripts, and verification conditions were examined at commit `7e292cce69c1f10a66a98e225de0a8c19ae42e11`:\r\n\r\n1. **Files Reviewed**:\r\n   - `supabase/migrations/20260923181754_retire_frozen_designflow_schema.sql` (migration DDL, procedural pre-flight checks, lock hierarchy, FK re-pointing, drops)\r\n   - `.github/live-proofs/2110.sql` (live-proof probe query structure, return types, predicates)\r\n   - `scripts/test_frozen_designflow_retirement.py` (synthetic test suite covering 10 failure/success scenarios)\r\n   - `docs/verification/2110-frozen-designflow-retirement.md` (audit trail, live pre-check results, backup verification)\r\n   - `.agent/work/2110/3/contract.json` (author lane scope contract, read/write table boundaries, invariants)\r\n   - `.agent/work/2110/3/completion.json` (author lane completion report, migration version, SHA evidence)\r\n   - Repository gate scripts: `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py`, `scripts/production_migration_guard.py`, `scripts/check-live-proof-probe.mjs`, `scripts/check-sql.sh`, and `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/`\r\n\r\n2. **Conditions Examined**:\r\n   - **DDL Correctness & Safety**: Lock acquisition ordering, lock mode sufficiency, transaction safety, idempotence, dependent-record preservation, schema drops, and cascade safety.\r\n   - **Preservation of Dependent Objects**: Verification that tables and sequences dropped in `designflow_frozen_20260710` are not read by other apps and that live referencing foreign keys (`plm.art_piece_attachment`, `app.RolePermissions`) are redirected to live `dflow` tables without data loss.\r\n   - **Live-Proof Probe**: Verification that `.github/live-proofs/2110.sql` consists of exactly one read-only statement beginning with `SELECT`, returns a single row with boolean column `passed`, and definitively proves the retirement and foreign key validity.\r\n   - **Header Rules & Derivation**: Compliance with AGENTS.md §5.0-D and §5.0-E (`-- derived-from:` header format, catalog verification derivation).\r\n   - **Index Usage (Mandatory Check 1)**: Verification that foreign key constraints, pre-flight data comparison queries, and probe joins have backing indexes.\r\n   - **Function Volatility (Mandatory Check 2)**: Verification of routine presence or modifications in the migration and probe.\r\n   - **Exact Object Checks (Mandatory Check 3)**: Verification that exact schemas, tables, sequences, column types, and constraint definitions are asserted rather than inferred.\r\n   - **Test Coverage**: Evaluation of negative test cases, drift detection, type changes, routine references, and happy-path execution in `scripts/test_frozen_designflow_retirement.py`.\r\n   - **Secrets & Sensitive Data**: Verification that no credentials, tokens, or customer/licensed data are present in SQL, markdown, or scripts.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### FINDINGS\r\n\r\n#### 1. Post-Apply Catalog Verification Zero-Target Derivation Failure\r\n- **Severity**: High (Blocking Gate Failure)\r\n- **File**: `supabase/migrations/20260923181754_retire_frozen_designflow_schema.sql:20-156`\r\n- **Reference**: `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py:144-165, 442-446, 3609-3631`\r\n- **Description**:\r\n  All DDL operations in `20260923181754_retire_frozen_designflow_schema.sql` (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT`, `ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT`, `DROP TABLE`, `DROP SEQUENCE`, `DROP SCHEMA`) are wrapped inside dynamic SQL `EXECUTE` calls within a single dollar-quoted procedural block (`DO $retirement$ BEGIN ... END $retirement$;`).\r\n  The production catalog verification tool, `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py`, derives verification targets by calling `strip_sql(raw)` in `derive_targets()` (line 442). In `strip_sql()` (lines 144–165), all dollar-quoted blocks (`DO $...$`) are stripped from the SQL content prior to regex matching.\r\n  Consequently, the lexer only scans the top-level un-stripped statements (lines 11–13: `LOCK TABLE ...;`). None of these match `CREATE_TABLE_RE`, `ALTER_RELATION_RE`, `DROP_RELATION_RE`, or other target patterns.\r\n  As a result:\r\n  - `targets.is_empty()` evaluates to `True` (`target_count == 0`).\r\n  - `diagnose_catalog_coverage()` reports `\"status\": \"missing\"` for the migration.\r\n  - No verification sidecar exists in `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260923181754.json` declaring explicit assertions (e.g., `catalog_absence`).\r\n  - When `scripts/production_catalog_verification.py` runs in enforcing mode (`--enforce-migration-coverage`), lines 3622–3625 trigger a hard exit:\r\n    `ERROR: 20260923181754_retire_frozen_designflow_schema.sql derived NO catalog targets from its SQL text. The allowlisted migrations named NO catalog object this lexer can read, so this step proved nothing. A run that verified nothing must not report itself green.`\r\n- **Remediation**:\r\n  Provide verifiable catalog targets through either of the following standard repository mechanisms:\r\n  a. Move the static `ALTER TABLE` statements (and/or static drops after pre-flight assertions) out of the `DO` block into top-level SQL statements between pre-flight and post-flight validation blocks. Top-level `ALTER TABLE plm.art_piece_attachment ADD CONSTRAINT ...` will be picked up by `ALTER_RELATION_RE`, allowing target derivation and catalog verification. (Note that `contract.json:153` explicitly documents root approval for explicit static ALTER statements).\r\n  b. Add a companion sidecar file `scripts/production-verification-sidecars/20260923181754.json` specifying the required `catalog_absence` assertions for `designflow_frozen_20260710` relations.\r\n\r\n#### 2. Lock Upgrade Deadlock Hazard on Referenced Tables\r\n- **Severity**: Medium (Operational Concurrency Hazard)\r\n- **File**: `supabase/migrations/20260923181754_retire_frozen_designflow_schema.sql:13, 120, 126`\r\n- **Description**:\r\n  Line 13 acquires locks on the referenced parent tables using:\r\n  `LOCK TABLE dflow.\"Roles\", dflow.art_piece IN SHARE MODE;`\r\n  Subsequently, lines 120 and 126 execute:\r\n  `ALTER TABLE app.\"RolePermissions\" ADD CONSTRAINT ... REFERENCES dflow.\"Roles\"(\"Id\") NOT VALID;`\r\n  `ALTER TABLE plm.art_piece_attachment ADD CONSTRAINT ... REFERENCES dflow.art_piece(id) NOT VALID;`\r\n  In PostgreSQL, adding a foreign key constraint automatically acquires a `SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE` lock on the referenced table, even with `NOT VALID`.\r\n  Because the transaction initially acquired only `SHARE MODE` on `dflow.\"Roles\"` and `dflow.art_piece`, executing `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... REFERENCES` forces an in-transaction lock upgrade from `SHARE` to `SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE`. If another concurrent session holds a lock in `SHARE` or `SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE` mode on either parent table, this lock upgrade can result in a deadlock (`deadlock_detected`), causing migration rollback.\r\n- **Remediation**:\r\n  Acquire the required lock level up front at line 13:\r\n  `LOCK TABLE dflow.\"Roles\", dflow.art_piece IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE;`\r\n  This prevents lock upgrades while continuing to allow concurrent readers.\r\n\r\n#### 3. Identifier Quoting Discrepancy in Contract and Completion Metadata\r\n- **Severity**: Low (Metadata Hygiene)\r\n- **File**: `.agent/work/2110/3/contract.json:116, 130` and `.agent/work/2110/3/completion.json:29, 43`\r\n- **Description**:\r\n  In `contract.json` and `completion.json`, `db_reads` specifies unquoted identifiers (`\"table app.RolePermissions\"` and `\"table dflow.Roles\"`), whereas `db_writes` specifies escaped quotes (`\"table app.\\\"RolePermissions\\\"\"` and `\"table designflow_frozen_20260710.\\\"Roles\\\"\"`). While downstream parsers normalize standard identifier casing, aligning the quoting style across reads and writes prevents discrepancies in strict automated boundary validators.\r\n- **Remediation**:\r\n  Normalize identifier quoting consistently across `db_reads` and `db_writes` in the contract and completion artifacts.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### MANDATORY AND SCOPE CHECKS SUMMARY\r\n\r\n- **Index Usage**:\r\n  All foreign key target columns (`dflow.art_piece(id)` and `dflow.\"Roles\"(\"Id\")`) have primary key btree indexes serving parent lookups. Child table columns (`plm.art_piece_attachment(art_piece_id)` and `app.\"RolePermissions\"(\"RoleId\")`) have supporting indexes. `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` operations scan child relations and perform index probes against the parent primary keys. No unindexed foreign keys or table scans on parent lookups were introduced.\r\n- **Function Volatility**:\r\n  No routines are created, replaced, or modified in the migration or live-proof probe. The pre-flight block asserts that zero routines exist in the frozen schema (`SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc WHERE pronamespace = ...`). The synthetic routine defined in `scripts/test_frozen_designflow_retirement.py:398` is isolated to negative test fixtures.\r\n- **Exact Object Checks**:\r\n  Object assertions are exact and exhaustive. The migration asserts the exact existence and schema membership of all 9 frozen tables, 2 sequences, 0 routines, external `pg_depend` references, and row count matches against the cold backup. It verifies field-by-field JSONB equality between frozen and live parent tables before re-pointing, and inspects all 10 structural attributes of each foreign key constraint in `pg_constraint`.\r\n- **Live-Proof Probe**:\r\n  `.github/live-proofs/2110.sql` consists of a single read-only `SELECT` query returning one row with a boolean column aliased `passed`. It tests the complete absence of `designflow_frozen_20260710`, confirms that both new foreign key constraints exist in `pg_constraint` with `convalidated = true` pointing to `dflow`, and confirms zero orphaned child rows.\r\n- **Test Coverage**:\r\n  `scripts/test_frozen_designflow_retirement.py` provides 10 synthetic integration tests verifying happy-path execution, unexpected tables/sequences, presence of routines, routine body text references, altered parent attributes, missing parent rows, altered foreign key actions, attribute type drift, and row count discrepancies.\r\n- **Secrets and Data Privacy**:\r\n  No credentials, API tokens, or licensed/customer data are committed. Backup SHA-256 digests and 1Password reference identifiers are documented without leaking private payload data.\r\n\r\nVERDICT: REVISE Every residual note below fails closed.\r\n\r\n**Advisory (fail-closed, non-blocking):**\r\n\r\n- Commit-status rows are filtered on `s.app?.id` (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:36`), but Combined Status rows carry `creator`, not `app` — pinned by the test at `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.test.mjs:18`. Fail-closed; if GitHub omits the field for unrestricted ruleset checks, every preflight refuses. Consider treating absent as null, matching the classic null-app handling at line 36.\r\n- Actions app id `15368` is hardcoded (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:63`, mirror `app_id` values). Stable global id; maintenance note only.\r\n- The `base_sha` equality check (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:122-123`) forces recompute on any unrelated `main` movement. Conservative and safe.\r\n\r\n## Coverage\r\n\r\nChecked against the implementation, not just test names: unknown authority refuses (`preflight.mjs:53-55,112-114`); newly inherited rules change the revision and no snapshot is consulted (`authority.mjs:50-55`, `preflight.mjs:122-123`); per-requirement producer partition with cross-producer masking refused (`preflight.mjs:65-66`, test file lines 14-18); exact-head gating plus `head_sha` filtering (`preflight.mjs:40-41,58,109-110`); id-ordered attempts with queued-null timestamps and contradictory-tie refusal (`preflight.mjs:21-34`); conjunctive same-name status/check channels (`preflight.mjs:44-51`); self-context exclusion with producer guard (`preflight.mjs:59-63`); updater preserves producer bindings, requires them on readback, echoes `strict`, and narrows PATCH to `required_status_checks` (`scripts/update-required-checks.mjs:176-177,216-221,229-231,256+`); pagination completeness on all three reads (`preflight.mjs:89-106`, `authority.mjs:41-42`); advisory-only visibility for non-required failures (`preflight.mjs:81-83`); repository identity verified against GraphQL (`repository-identity.mjs`, `authority.mjs:24-30`). workflow token is unproven and the merge workflow's own comment now describes removed behavior.\r\n\r\n## Findings\r\n\r\n### High\r\n\r\n- **H1 — No live proof the merge workflow's token can perform the new authority reads; the only merge path may now always refuse.** `gatherPreflightInput` ([check-required-checks-preflight.mjs](/D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-claude-review-3369-3361-ac833ea888f1/scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:107)) hard-requires `readEffectiveRequiredChecks` (GraphQL `branchProtectionRule` + REST `rules/branches`), and every failure mode throws `PreflightError` with no fallback ([check-required-checks-preflight.mjs](/D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-claude-review-3369-3361-ac833ea888f1/scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:112)). The caller, `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:117-120`, still runs the preflight with bare `github.token`, while that same file's unchanged comment (:43-48) asserts this token *cannot* read branch protection (no `administration` scope exists). If that assertion holds for both new reads, every guarded merge exits 2 — fail-closed per the contract's stop condition, but the repository's only merge path bricks. The packet ran zero tests, and `.agent/work/3361/2/completion.json`'s \"46 tests pass\" covers mocked unit tests at a different SHA (`a7b0d686`, not this head). Sibling gap of the same class: `update-required-checks.mjs:176` writes new additions with `app_id: -1` and `readLive` (:216) now mandates a `checks` array — both unproven against the live PATCH/GET shapes by mocks. Required: one live read proof with the real workflow token (or a credential plan) before merge.\r\n\r\n### Medium\r\n\r\n- **M1 — Stale merge-path comment now misdescribes the gate.** `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:43-48` still says the pre-flight \"detects that and applies a STRICTLY STRONGER test instead\" (the removed committed-mirror fallback). After this PR it refuses instead. An operator debugging a refused merge lane reads exactly this comment first. The file is outside the change set, so this needs a coupled fix, not silence.\r\n\r\n### Low\r\n\r\n- **L1 — Commit statuses can never satisfy an app-bound required check.** Statuses are filtered by `s.app?.id` ([check-required-checks-preflight.mjs](/D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-claude-review-3369-3361-ac833ea888f1/scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:36)), but commit-status objects carry `creator`, not `app` — so for any app-bound requirement only check-runs count. Fail-closed and fine for today's all-check-run policy (all 13 contexts are app `15368`), and pinned by test, but a future status-based requirement would refuse forever. Same-class sibling: `head_sha` partitioning applies only to check-runs (:41), not statuses (statuses have no head field — correct, just noting the asymmetry is intentional).\r\n- **L2 — Ruleset enforcement state is assumed, not checked.** [required-check-authority.mjs](/D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-claude-review-3369-3361-ac833ea888f1/scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:44) accepts any `required_status_checks` rule without verifying the ruleset is active/enforced, relying on `rules/branches` returning only applicable active rules. Reasonable, but an undocumented load-bearing assumption — one line of comment would close it.\r\n- **L3 — Magic app id.** The self-producer guard hard-codes `15368` ([check-required-checks-preflight.mjs](/D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-claude-review-3369-3361-ac833ea888f1/scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:63)). Fails closed if GitHub ever rotates the Actions app id; a shared constant would be cheaper than the next debug session.\r\n- **L4 — Doc drift in unchanged files.** `plan_orchestrator_required_load_reduction.md:93,121`, `docs/merge-queue-operation.md:43`, and the comment in `scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs:10-12` still describe the mirror as the enforced authority / pin mechanism. Informational only; the mirror's `_why` itself was correctly rewritten.\r\n\r\n### Mandatory checks (index / volatility / exact-object)\r\n\r\n- **Index usage: N/A.** The change touches only Node scripts and JSON evidence files — no migrations, no SQL, no predicates or joins. There is nothing to index and no loose index assumption.\r\n- **Function volatility: N/A.** No SQL functions are created or altered.\r\n- **Exact object checks: N/A at the DB level; the analog holds.** The authority helper asserts exact identity rather than name-existence: numeric `databaseId`, case-insensitive `nameWithOwner` match, exact ref name, 40-hex `oid` ([required-check-authority.mjs](/D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\muse-claude-review-3369-3361-ac833ea888f1/scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:30)); classic rule id plus both list shapes (:34) with a cross-check that contexts and producer bindings agree (:38); per-ruleset identity fields (:45). Injection-safe too: `repo` passes a slug regex (:24), `branch` goes through `encodeURIComponent` (:41) and the GraphQL ref travels as a variable, not string interpolation (:26-27).\r\n\r\n### Brief questions\r\n\r\n1. **Fail-closed on unreadable policy: yes.** `evaluateWithoutRequiredList` unconditionally throws; authority errors are wrapped into refusal; before/after double-read with `revision`+`base_sha` comparison closes the TOCTOU window; empty or malformed policy refuses; pagination completeness checks retained.\r\n2. **Advisories excluded from required success: yes.** Advisory results are computed on a separate path, only logged, never veto; pinned by the `advisory failure remains visible` test. The removed `ADVISORY_CONTEXTS` special-case is fully subsumed.\r\n3. **Authority-helper regressions: none found.** All malformed/partial inputs refuse; no injection surface (above).\r\n4. **Disposition catalogues: match, excluded-only.** New/changed sites verified against current lines — preflight `:64/:69/:74/:78` are all inside `evaluatePreflight`'s refusal reporting; update `:216` is the new producer-bindings refusal. All entries `disposition: excluded`.\r\n\r\n### Coverage\r\n\r\nExamined the full `patch.diff`, all three scripts and both test files at head, both disposition catalogues, the rewritten mirror, `repository-identity.mjs`, `merge-self-context.mjs`, the guarded-merge workflow caller, and swept for stale references to every removed export (`PINNED_REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`, `readRequiredChecksMirror`, `ADVISORY_CONTEXTS`, `isPermissionRefusal`) and for other mirror readers (`check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs` still passes against the new mirror shape — `contexts` retained). No tests were run in this packet; findings rest on code inspection. Test evidence cited by `completion.json` binds to `a7b0d686`, not this head.\r\n\r\n## Verdict\r\nVERDICT: REVISE Next I’ll confirm a few remaining call sites, then write the findings and the verdict.Head `818a5e89` was reviewed against base `85566ccb` from the packet at `D:\\ai-data\\local\\state\\ai-devops\\review-sandboxes\\grok-review-3369-b-2bfa48a4464d`. The diff is CI/JavaScript only: live required-check authority, preflight, updater, informational mirror, and tests. No migrations, SQL functions, or indexes are in the change. Packet tests were not run; judgment is from the patch and surrounding callers.\n\n## Prior findings (this head)\n\n**M1 — commit-status producer identity: addressed.**  \n`observedStates` keeps producer identity until after newest-result selection (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:17-48`). REST statuses have `creator`, not `app`. An app-bound requirement skips unverifiable **success** statuses (`:38-43`) and still surfaces unverifiable **non-success** so a red status cannot hide behind a green same-name check run (`:51-55`). Tests: `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.test.mjs:15-19` (creator-only success does not satisfy), `:113-129` (red without `app` stays visible; known-wrong `app.id` is ignored).\n\n**M2 — ruleset pagination completeness: not closed.**  \nThere is a short-non-last-page guard (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:48-55`). `/rules/branches` has no `total_count`. A **single** page of exactly `per_page` (100) is treated as complete — the usual `gh --paginate` stop when `Link` is not followed. The test **locks that in**: `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.test.mjs:78-85` accepts one full page of 100. That is the truncated-page case the completeness guard was supposed to refuse. Combined with dropping the old all-reported-green fallback (`evaluateWithoutRequiredList` now always throws, `:59-61`; advisory failures only log, `:87-89`), a truncated ruleset list can authorize a merge while missing inherited required checks.\n\n**M3 — live token permission proof: not closed.**  \nThe only “proof” is a comment (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:24-29`: “Verified live 2026-09-25”). There is no workflow step, GraphQL permission field, REST probe that distinguishes 403 from 404, or committed `github.token` evidence. The informational snapshot is dated **2026-09-20** (`docs/verification/main-required-status-checks.json:9-10`), not that claimed token run.  \nClassic protection: GraphQL `branchProtectionRule === null` is treated as “no classic rule” (`required-check-authority.mjs:38-47`), which is also how GitHub hides unauthorized nullable fields. REST `/protection` used to 403. Null + a non-empty ruleset page would omit classic contexts and still authorize.  \nSame workflow still documents that this token has no `administration` scope and that ruleset reads may fail (`.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:185-189`); `queueMode()` uses `/rulesets`, which is a different endpoint, but there is still no in-change proof that GraphQL `branchProtectionRule` and `/rules/branches` succeed under `github.token`. The mirror fallback was removed (`evaluateWithoutRequiredList`, preflight comments `:1-4`, workflow `:43-49`). If those reads are unreadable-as-null rather than 403, this is the only merge path and it can go fail-open.\n\n## Other defects\n\n**P1 — PATCH encodes new required checks as `app_id: -1`.**  \n`scripts/update-required-checks.mjs:176` appends `{ context, app_id: -1 }`; `:229` PATCHes `checks` whenever live returned `checks`. `readLive` now requires a `checks` array (`:216`), so `--apply` always takes that path. GitHub’s documented “any source” encoding is **omit** `app_id`. Locally `-1` is normalized to unrestricted (`required-check-authority.mjs:6`). GitHub may 422, store status-only, or otherwise not match GitHub Actions check runs (app `15368`). Test locks the body in: `scripts/update-required-checks.test.mjs:285`.\n\n**P2 — Documented under-lock re-read is not implemented.**  \n`required-check-authority.mjs:21-22` says callers must re-read under the merge lock. Preflight runs only before the lock (`.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:116-120`). The lock-held step (`:131-150`) does not call `check-required-checks-preflight.mjs`. Authority is compared before/after status pagination (`check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:122-129`), not after the lock.\n\n**P2 — Shrink floor and all-reported fallback are gone.**  \n`PINNED_REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` / origin/main pin comparison were deleted. Preflight no longer refuses a live list that shrank relative to a local floor. That is consistent with “live GitHub is authority” only if M2/M3 reads are complete and attributable. `plan_shared_db_workflow_refactor.md:116` required a synchronized authoritative source **before** narrowing `evaluateWithoutRequiredList`.\n\n**P3 — `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.test.mjs` is not in CI.**  \n`migration-author-lease.yml:49` runs `check-required-checks-preflight.test.mjs` (which does cover pagination). The new authority file is not in that list or in `tools-offline-tests.yml`’s explicit `scripts/lib` set. Packet tests were not executed here.\n\n**P3 — Pagination test does not match the error text.**  \n`assert.throws(..., RequiredCheckAuthorityError, /pagination is incomplete/)` (`check-required-checks-preflight.test.mjs:77`): in `node:assert`, the third argument is the assertion message, not an error-message matcher.\n\n## Mandatory extra checks\n\n1. **Index usage.** Not applicable. No SQL, migrations, predicates, or joins. Changed paths are workflows, JS, JSON evidence, and `.agent` contract files.\n2. **Function volatility.** Not applicable. No PostgreSQL `IMMUTABLE` / `STABLE` / `VOLATILE` functions.\n3. **Exact object checks.** No schema/table/view/function/column asserts. GitHub-side: repository `databaseId`, `nameWithOwner`, ref name, and 40-char OID are checked (`required-check-authority.mjs:37`). Classic rule identity is **not** distinguished from an unauthorized null (`:38-47`). Ruleset rows require `type`, `ruleset_id`, `ruleset_source_type`, `ruleset_source` (`:58`). That is an exact-identity gap for classic protection, same class as M3.\n\n## What is in good shape\n\nFail-closed on GraphQL `errors`, malformed pages, empty effective policy, missing producer `databaseId`, classic context/producer disagreement, SHA mismatch on check runs, foreign-app success, and unreadable authority with no snapshot fallback. Self-context exclusion is gated on app `15368` (`check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:67-69`). Mirror is labeled informational and is not read by preflight.\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\n\nVERDICT: REVISE
