This is CI/JavaScript only — no SQL indexes, volatility markers, or database objects.\n\nThe six claimed fixes are mostly in place: producer identity no longer treats `creator` as an app, a full last ruleset page requires a confirming empty next page, GraphQL `null` is probed as 404 vs 403 vs 200, PATCH omits `app_id` for any-source checks, the merge step re-runs preflight under the lock with `PREFLIGHT_WAIT_SECONDS=0`, and `required-check-authority.test.mjs` is on the lease CI line with a matcher that can actually fail.\n\nTwo gaps remain, both on the new live-authority path.\n\n## Findings\n\n**Ruleset any-source encoding is treated as unreadable** — `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:6` and `:92`\n\nGitHub’s documented any-source ruleset check **omits** `integration_id` (same encoding P1 just fixed on the classic PATCH: absence of the id, not `-1`). The reader does `requirements.push({ context: item.context, app_id: item.integration_id })` and then `appId()` only accepts `null` or `-1` as unrestricted. `undefined` (omitted key) throws `required check producer identity is unreadable`.\n\nClassic GraphQL `app: null` is mapped to `null` first, so it works. Rulesets do not get that mapping. An inherited org ruleset with an any-source required check — the case this work exists to notice — makes the only merge path refuse. Tests all pass `integration_id` explicitly; omitted/`undefined` is untested.\n\nFix: treat omitted `integration_id` like classic `app: null` (`item.integration_id ?? null`, still refuse `0` and other junk) and add a test that a ruleset check with no `integration_id` becomes `{ context, app_id: null }`.\n\n**P1’s regression test still never runs in CI** — `scripts/update-required-checks.test.mjs:280` and `.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml:49`\n\nThe PATCH-omits-`app_id` assertion lives only in `update-required-checks.test.mjs`. No workflow invokes that file. The lease job was updated to run `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.test.mjs` next to the preflight tests, but not this suite. A later change can put `app_id: null` back in the PATCH body and CI will stay green.\n\nAdd `scripts/update-required-checks.test.mjs` to that same `node --test` line (or another required job that already lists these scripts).\n\n### Six claimed fixes\n\n| Claim | Status |\n|---|---|\n| M1 creator vs app | Holds. Success without `app` cannot satisfy an app-bound requirement; `creator.id === 15368` is tested as insufficient; red statuses without `app` stay visible. |\n| M2 ruleset pagination | Holds. Short non-last page refuses; a full last page requires an empty confirming `page=N+1`; tests cover truncated, confirmed, and partial-last. |\n| M3 404 vs 403 vs 200 | Holds in code and unit tests. Residual: REST `GET .../protection` is admin-only, and this workflow token has no `administration` scope, so a GraphQL unauthorized `null` will always take the 403 path. That is fail-closed, not fail-open. |\n| P1 omit `app_id` | Holds in `applyUnion`, but see the CI gap above. |\n| P2 under-lock re-read | Holds. The merge step re-invokes the live preflight with wait 0; `gatherPreflightInput` re-reads authority before and after status collection. |\n| P3 authority tests in CI | Holds for `required-check-authority.test.mjs`; pagination matchers return a boolean. |\n\n### Extra checks (indexes / volatility / exact objects)\n\nNot applicable. This head does not add or change schema, tables, views, functions, or indexes. No predicates, joins, or `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` markers. Identity checks that do exist are GitHub-side (`repository.databaseId`, `nameWithOwner`, `ref.name`, `target.oid`), not database objects.\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\n\nVERDICT: REVISE af8f922448e7f76194f67652bca10ddca52b5df3","author_association":"MEMBER","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5836415566/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"performed_via_github_app":null,"minimized":null},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5837223629","html_url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3369#issuecomment-5837223629","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/3369","id":5837223629,"node_id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABW-z2zQ","user":{"login":"u2giants","id":55610577,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/55610577?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants","html_url":"https://github.com/u2giants","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2026-09-25T18:10:51Z","updated_at":"2026-09-25T18:10:51Z","body":"GOVERNED REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n## Provisional verdict\n\nProvisional verdict: REVISE. The rewritten gate is coherent, fail-closed, and stronger in the areas the brief claims were fixed, but its central new assumption (that the workflow token can read the two newly used API surfaces) is load-bearing, unproven by any evidence in this packet, and its failure mode is \"every merge refuses\" on the repository's only merge path. Several smaller gaps are listed below.\n\n## Coverage\n\nExamined (opened in full unless noted): `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs` (1-100), `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs` (1-160), `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs` (1-353), `scripts/update-required-checks.test.mjs` (1-297), `scripts/lib/github-transport.mjs` (1-422), `scripts/lib/repository-identity.mjs` (1-143), `scripts/lib/merge-self-context.mjs` (1-11), `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` (1-144), `scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs` (1-315), `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml` (1-256), `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~update-required-checks.mjs.json` (1-53), `.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml:46` and `:49`, `.github/workflows/merge-queue-gate.yml:160-200`, `.github/workflows/shared-supabase-migrations.yml:995-1020`, plus the packet (`MANIFEST.md`, `patch.diff`). Grep sweeps for the removed exports and for context producers were truncated (\"search stopped after 30s\", two binary-classified files unsearched), so consumer coverage is not exhaustive — that limitation is carried into the findings.\n\n## Findings\n\n**Medium — the new authority reads are load-bearing and unverified against a real token.** `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:24-32` *asserts* that the GraphQL `branchProtectionRule` read and `REST /rules/branches` need only `contents:read`, and that `administration:read` is not needed. The only probe in the file (`:55-69`) runs *after* GraphQL already returned null and distinguishes 404 from 403; a 403 refuses (`:64`). There is no step anywhere in `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml` (read in full; permissions block `:29-49`, steps `:56-256`) that first proves the token can complete these reads. If either assumption is false, the outcome is exactly the class this PR exists to end (see the workflow's own comment `:43-49`): every merge refuses, permanently, at `:120`. No run link, no test against a real token, and no test execution is present in the packet (\"No tests were run for this packet\", MANIFEST §5). This is the one gap I would not waive.\n\n**Low — change detection compares serialized payloads, so representational jitter refuses the merge.** `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:129` refuses when `before.revision !== authority.revision`, and the revision is `sha256(JSON.stringify({... sources }))` over the raw GraphQL rule object and the raw rules array (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:98`). Any key-order or representational difference between the two consecutive reads produces \"effective settings or protected branch changed during the read; authorization must be recomputed\" — an unactionable refusal on the only merge path. Excluding `capturedIso` (`:99`) shows the author considered stability, but the serialized-payload comparison itself is not normalized.\n\n**Low — one exact-object check is shape-only.** `evaluatePreflight` accepts `authority.revision` on format alone (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:64`; `/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/`), never recomputing the digest the reader produced. In production this is harmless because `gatherPreflightInput` compares two independently read revisions, but as a check on \"the right object\" it verifies that a revision-shaped string exists, not that the object is the one it claims to be — the class the brief's item 3 names.\n\n**Low — the A GitHub Actions app id is a bare literal.** `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:69` hardcodes `15368` for the self context's producer and asserts it against nothing live; `required-check-authority.mjs` derives producer ids from the payload but nothing checks this constant against a read object. Fail-closed (a mismatch refuses), so a liveness rather than a security gap. The sibling constant is exact: `SELF_CHECK_RUN = 'merge'` (`:12`) matches the job name in `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:52`.\n\n**Low — a dead fail-closed branch and a test that never reaches the live path.** `protectionUnreadable` (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:63`) is unreachable from `gatherPreflightInput`, which returns only `{authority, statuses, checkRuns, sha}` (`:130`). `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.test.mjs:11` calls `evaluatePreflight({authority, sha, ...})` directly with a synthetic authority, so the shape-only acceptance above is exactly what the suite proves.\n\n**Low — quota multiplier on the only merge path is unmeasured.** Each poll attempt now performs two full authority reads (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:122` and `:128`), each ≥3 API calls (GraphQL query, optional `/protection` probe, paginated `/rules/branches` plus a confirming page read when the last page is exactly 100 — `required-check-authority.mjs:72, 84`), whereas the previous single read was one call. With the default `PREFLIGHT_WAIT_SECONDS=900` / `PREFLIGHT_POLL_SECONDS=30` (`:137-138`) that is roughly an order of magnitude more calls per merge attempt. The pre-lock quota step (`.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:110-115`) budgets for the preflight's *old* cost, and the under-lock call is intentionally wait-free (`:157`). No measurement is offered.\n\n**Low — files the change does not touch now state falsehoods about the change's subject.** `scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs:11-13` still calls the committed mirror \"the list the guarded merge pre-flight enforces\" and derives its emitter-coverage list from it (`:21`, `:26`, `:53`); after this change the mirror is informational (`docs/verification/main-required-status-checks.json`, `_why`) and a context that is live-only via a ruleset would be enforced by the preflight while this merge_group emitter test never learns of it. `scripts/lib/merge-self-context.mjs:9` likewise still says the pre-flight \"reads a docs mirror\".\n\n**Low — the disposition catalogues record stale site numbers, and their digests were not verified.** `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~check-required-checks-preflight.mjs.json:14` records `site …:78` and `:22` records `:74`, while the head's matching lines are 70/75/80/84 (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:70-84`). This is cosmetic *if* the audit compares only `semantic_key` and `line_sha256` — which is what `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:124,132` actually does — but because no test was run I cannot confirm the recorded digests still match, and this audit is a CI gate (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` is invoked from `.github/workflows/tools-offline-tests.yml:95`). `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json` is edited here although the audit module declares it \"retained as historical evidence only; it is never read\" (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:15-16`).\n\n**Low — incompletely ruled out: consumers of deleted exports.** `PINNED_REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`, `MIRROR_BOOTSTRAP_MAIN_SHA`, `parsePinnedFloor`, `readRequiredChecksMirror`, `ADVISORY_CONTEXTS`, `PREFLIGHT_SOURCE_PATH`, `isPermissionRefusal` are all removed; my greps found references only in plan documents (`plan_orchestrator_required_load_reduction.md:93`, `plan_bounded_session_handover.md:88`, `plan_shared_db_workflow_refactor.md:256`) and the changed files, but the sweep was truncated with `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs` and `tools/promote-coldlion-source-owned.mjs` unsearched. A residual importer would be a red build or a broken gate.\n\n## The three mandatory items\n\n1. **Index usage.** Inapplicable as framed: this change touches no SQL, view, or database object (changed set per MANIFEST §3 is `.mjs`, `.yml`, `.json`; `contract.json` declares `\"db_reads\": []`, `\"db_writes\": []`). No predicate or join here relies on a database index. The nearest analogue is the in-memory lookup structure in `observedStates`, keyed `${kind}:${name}` in a `Map` (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:22`) — O(1), with no assumption that could be \"loose or unused\". The one join-like step, the cross-channel merge at `:50-56`, cannot silently drop a channel: both channels are inserted under distinct keys before merging, and a success never overwrites a red, nor may two differing non-successes collapse (`:55`).\n2. **Function volatility.** Inapplicable as framed (no SQL functions with volatility markers). The analogue holds: `evaluatePreflight`, `observedStates`, `normalizeRequirements`, and `collectPages` are pure over their arguments; the single time dependency is the injected `now = () => new Date()` (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:33`), whose effect is deliberately excluded from `revision` (`:98-99`) so that two reads of unchanged settings yield an identical revision — the property `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:129` depends on. No marker is looser than its body.\n3. **Exact object checks.** Substantially satisfied and stronger than the design it replaces: the reader asserts repository `databaseId`, `nameWithOwner`, ref name, target oid, rule id, and requires the classic context list and producer list to agree exactly (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:40, 44, 48`), and refuses an empty effective policy rather than reading it as \"nothing required\" (`:96`). The two gaps are the shape-only revision check and the bare `15368` literal named above.\n\n## What would clear this\n\nEvidence that the workflow token completes both new reads on the real repository (a run link from the guarded lane, or a preflight-time permission probe that refuses with a distinguishable message before the authority read becomes the gate), plus a run of the three test files and of `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs`. None of that evidence is in this packet, and the packet explicitly reports no tests were run.\n\nVERDICT: REVISE Runtime comments/probe text no longer say `contents:read` is enough. `SYNC_TOKEN` is not live-testable from this snapshot; the probe is the intended live proof, but the documented dispatch cannot pass that token until this YAML is already on `main`.\n\n## Findings\n\n### P1 — This head cannot land on the only merge path\n\nThe documented dispatch is `gh workflow run guarded-migration-merge.yml` with no `--ref`, so GitHub runs **main’s** workflow YAML. Main’s preflight step (base `95c5db5e`) still has only `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`. The job then checks out **this head** and runs the new fail-closed script.\n\n- `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:136-147` maps `AUTHORITY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SYNC_TOKEN }}` only in the **new** YAML.\n- `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:203-211` probes in-process so a missing YAML probe step still names the denial — it does **not** invent a token main never passed.\n- With `AUTHORITY_TOKEN` empty, `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:147-150` and `:209-211` use `github.token`, which live run `36186790619` already proved cannot read GraphQL `branchProtectionRule` / REST `/rules/branches`.\n- The committed-mirror fallback that let main merge without that read is gone (`evaluateWithoutRequiredList` at `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:65-66` always throws).\n\nDispatching this PR the documented way therefore reproduces the live 403 and refuses. `--ref` on the feature branch would pick up the new YAML, but that runs untrusted workflow text and is not the protocol (`trusted-policy` exists specifically so exact-head approval stays on main).\n\nFix: land a YAML-only predecessor that adds `AUTHORITY_TOKEN` while the old script/fallback still lives on the checked-out head, **or** keep a one-time unset-token bootstrap (loud, tested, removed once this YAML is on main). Do not recommend `--ref` as the normal merge path.\n\n### P2 — Generation-4 contract still records the live-disproven `contents:read` claim\n\n`.agent/work/3361/4/contract.json:60`:\n\n> Workflow token can complete GraphQL branchProtectionRule and REST rules/branches reads with contents:read\n\nThis round exists to kill that claim. Probe/comments now say the opposite (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:42-47`, `:134`; `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.test.mjs:119`). Completion even “resolves” it as false (`.agent/work/3361/4/completion.json:42`). The immutable gen-4 contract still publishes the false belief. If `refs/db-contracts/3361/4` already matches this file, that needs generation 5 rather than a silent edit.\n\n### P2 — Load-bearing token split is unwitnessed\n\n`tokenScopedRead` (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:122-130`) is the actual fix: swap `GH_TOKEN` only around authority reads, restore it for `/status` and `/check-runs` (`:153-155`). Nothing in `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.test.mjs` or `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.test.mjs` sets `AUTHORITY_TOKEN` or asserts which env `gh` saw per endpoint. A regression that never swaps, or that leaves the PAT on for status writes/`gh pr merge` in the under-lock step (`guarded-migration-merge.yml:160-185`), would stay green.\n\n`SYNC_TOKEN` cannot be exercised from this sandbox. Until a guarded-merge run with main’s YAML actually passing `AUTHORITY_TOKEN` is green, the probe is not live proof for this head.\n\n### P2 — Permission probe can report success on an unauthorized GraphQL null\n\n`probeAuthorityReadPermissions` (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:135-138`) only checks `ref.name === branch`. It does not require a non-null `branchProtectionRule` and does not run the REST `/protection` 404-vs-403 probe that `readEffectiveRequiredChecks` uses (`:70-89`). GitHub hides unauthorized nullable fields as `null`. If GraphQL returns 200 with `branchProtectionRule: null` and `/rules/branches` is readable, the dedicated YAML probe step prints “proven” (`check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:194-195`) and gather later fail-closes. Align the probe with the gather null-distinction so a denied classic-protection read is named at probe time.\n\n## Mandatory extra checks (index / volatility / exact objects)\n\nNot applicable. No migration or database object is in the diff (`contract.json:48-52`, `completion.json:27-28`). There are no predicates, joins, indexes, or `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` markers to review.\n\nGitHub identity **is** checked exactly: repository `databaseId`, `nameWithOwner`, ref name, and 40-character `oid` (`required-check-authority.mjs:59-60`), not merely that a branch name exists.\n\n## What this round did get right\n\n- Authority reads are wrapped with `AUTHORITY_TOKEN`; status/check pagination stays on the default `json`/`GH_TOKEN`.\n- Canonical `stableStringify` digest and `computeRevision(authority)` rebind (`required-check-authority.mjs:11-23`, `check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:74`).\n- `GITHUB_ACTIONS_APP_ID = 15368` is a named, tested constant.\n- Dead `protectionUnreadable` / committed-mirror authorize path is gone; unreadable settings refuse.\n- Workflow/script comments name admin / Administration:read / GitHub App and say `contents:read` is not enough (except the gen-4 contract assumption above).\n- Disposition catalogues were rewritten onto the new sites; stale preflight refusal sites were dropped from the 2026-08-28 audit.\n- Completion’s first `checks[].command` equals the contract `required_checks` string exactly (`.agent/work/3361/4/contract.json:56` and `completion.json:33`). Packet shape matches “implementation then the two evidence files on top” (`head_sha` `8cfdd49d…` vs PR head `ea332508…`). Tests were not run in this packet.\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\n\nVERDICT: REVISE ea332508b981627d5c1110dcfdd9ac5be39d407d","author_association":"MEMBER","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5840386747/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"performed_via_github_app":null,"minimized":null},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/comments/5861551452","html_url":"https://github.com/popcre/shared-db/pull/3369#issuecomment-5861551452","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/popcre/shared-db/issues/3369","id":5861551452,"node_id":"IC_kwDOTAehpM8AAAABXWAtXA","user":{"login":"u2giants","id":55610577,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjU1NjEwNTc3","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/55610577?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants","html_url":"https://github.com/u2giants","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/u2giants/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2026-09-28T01:07:41Z","updated_at":"2026-09-28T01:07:41Z","body":"GOVERNED REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n# Review of PR #3369 at head d7ed59c3ff23eeecbd6dda3849988a5d6e4da420\n\nBase `1660f92020a132d15465c1da5e860fdd281b7e24`; packet `MANIFEST.md` and `patch.diff` read in full, plus the post-change sources. `MANIFEST.md` §5 states plainly: **\"No tests were run for this packet.\"** Every test result below is therefore a claim about source text, not an executed suite. `completion.json` records `head_sha` `d4a22a70f1e58975085de44d00689ca4aeaf51fa`, not the reviewed head, and \"57 passed, 0 failed\" (`.agent/work/3361/6/completion.json:8,32`) — that is the author's claim at a different commit and I did not verify it.\n\n## What I confirmed is fixed\n\nThe four prior P2s are genuinely addressed in the source, not just in comments:\n\n- `tokenScopedRead` swaps `GH_TOKEN` for the authority reads and restores it (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:122-131`), and the mechanism actually reaches the child process: `runGitHubCommand` passes no explicit `env` to the executor (`scripts/lib/github-transport.mjs:311-313,332`), so the child inherits the mutated `process.env`. Pinned by `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.test.mjs:84-98`.\n- The probe now rejects a null classic rule (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:139`).\n- Ruleset any-source checks with an omitted `integration_id` are treated as unrestricted (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:112`), while the classic sibling keeps a separate path (`:66`).\n- The revision is canonical and rebound (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:11-24`, `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:74`).\n- The committed mirror no longer authorizes anything: `evaluateWithoutRequiredList` throws unconditionally (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:65-67`) and the mirror's `_why` says so (`docs/verification/main-required-status-checks.json`, first line of the patch hunk).\n- Both new test files are in the lease CI list (`.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml:49`), which was the open gen-3 finding; the gen-6 contract now lists that workflow in `allowed_paths`/`file_writes` (`.agent/work/3361/6/contract.json:10,41`).\n\n## Findings\n\n### High — a repo-scoped classic PAT is handed to code from the reviewed pull request head\n\n`.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:136-141` adds a step that runs `node scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs --probe-permissions` with `AUTHORITY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SYNC_TOKEN }}` in the environment. The checkout is taken at `inputs.head_sha` (`:64-66`), and the script invoked is the one in **that** checkout, not the `trusted-policy` copy (`:74-79`), which is used only for `check-exact-head-approval.mjs` (`:100,178`). The same secret is in the env of the pre-flight step (`:145`) and of the under-lock step that also runs head code (`:162,185`).\n\nThe contract states the token is \"a classic PAT with repo scope\" (`:53`; `.agent/work/3361/6/contract.json:25`). `repo` scope on a classic PAT is read/write on the repository including administration endpoints. So the reviewed head's own JavaScript executes with a credential that can read *and* rewrite the very branch protection this gate exists to enforce. The workflow's own comments claim exact-head approval stays on protected main precisely so a head cannot judge itself (`:176-178`); the authority read is the one part of the gate that is still supplied by head code, now with an admin-capable token attached. A malicious or careless head change to `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs` — and this PR changes exactly that file — gets that token on the next dispatch.\n\nI could not verify from the hunks whether the `AUTHORITY_TOKEN` bindings at `:145` and `:162` predate this change or arrive with it; the diff hunk `@@ -150,6 +176,13 @@` adds only the `PREFLIGHT_WAIT_SECONDS=0` line, which suggests those env blocks are unchanged base context supplied by the prerequisite. The probe step at `:136-141` is unambiguously *added* here. Either way the changed file is the workflow that carries the exposure, and the brief asks me to inspect every changed grant and its sibling call paths — the siblings are `:147` and `:185`. Required before merge, or a documented, reviewed acceptance of it.\n\n### Medium — the probe and the gather disagree, so \"proven\" can be followed by an immediate refusal\n\n`probeAuthorityReadPermissions` refuses unless `branchProtectionRule?.id` is non-empty (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:139`). The reader does **not** require that: on `branchProtectionRule === null` it probes REST `/protection` and accepts a clean 404 as genuine absence, provided the rulesets supply checks (`:70-90`, `:116`). For a branch protected by rulesets only, the gather would authorize and the probe would refuse — and `main()` runs the probe first (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:211`), so the merge refuses before the authoritative read is ever attempted. The gen-6 contract asserts the probe \"requires non-null branchProtectionRule **or** the documented REST /protection null-distinction, aligned with the gather\" (`.agent/work/3361/6/contract.json:26`); the second half of that sentence is not implemented. Today's live classic rule (`BPR_kwDOTAehpM4E2ure` in the mirror blob) makes this latent, not active.\n\nSibling of the same class, in the other direction: the probe accepts an empty ruleset page (`:147` checks only `Array.isArray` and page shapes), while the gather refuses `!pages.length` with \"effective ruleset read is incomplete\" (`:93`). So the probe can print \"Authority-read permissions proven\" and the gather can refuse one call later with a different message — the confusion the probe was added to remove.\n\n### Medium — `checks`, the list actually enforced, is outside the revision digest\n\n`computeRevision` digests exactly `{repository_id, repository, branch, sources}` (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:22-24`). `evaluatePreflight` accepts `authority.revision` after confirming only that equality (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:74`), and the enforcement loop then iterates `authority.checks` (`:75,81-89`). The comment at `:70-73` claims the rebind \"refuses an authority whose recorded revision does not match what it actually carries\" — it refuses a mismatch in `sources`, not in `checks`. In production `checks` is derived from `sources` by the same reader, so this is not presently exploitable, but the guarantee as documented is broader than the code, and any future caller that constructs an authority object (the tests do exactly that) can vary `checks` freely while keeping the digest valid.\n\nSame class: `probeAuthorityReadPermissions` verifies only `ref.name === branch` (`:138`) plus rule-id presence (`:139`) — it does not check `databaseId`, `nameWithOwner`, or the 40-hex `oid` that the reader insists on (`:60`). A mis-resolved repository could pass the probe and fail the gather.\n\n### Medium-low — the mirror is labelled informational but is still an input to a settings-mutating tool\n\n`_why` now reads \"INFORMATIONAL effective required-check readback, never merge authority\" (`docs/verification/main-required-status-checks.json`, patch hunk 1). `scripts/configure-merge-queue.mjs:96` defines `COVERED_CONTEXTS_PATH = 'docs/verification/main-required-status-checks.json'`, reads its `?.contexts` (`:288`), and feeds it to `assertLiveContextsCovered` inside `planActivation` (`:175-178`) — a writer of merge-queue rulesets. The file is not read-only evidence for that consumer. The new value is the union of classic and ruleset contexts (`scripts/update-required-checks.mjs:249`), so the coverage check is at least as strong as before, but the \"informational only\" wording is inaccurate for this path and the two readers now have different recovery semantics.\n\n### Low — a dead fail-closed function with a misleading test\n\n`evaluateWithoutRequiredList` is exported and throws unconditionally; nothing outside the test file calls it (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:65-67`; only importers found are `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.test.mjs:3,40`). The test passes `mirrorContexts` and `expires` keys the function ignores (`test.mjs:40`), which reads as coverage of a snapshot-expiry rule that does not exist in code.\n\n### Low — the classic `app` field has the same omitted-vs-null asymmetry that was just fixed for rulesets\n\n`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:66` maps `item.app === null ? null : item.app?.databaseId`. If GitHub omits the `app` key rather than returning `null`, `appId(undefined)` refuses \"required check producer identity is unreadable\" and the *entire* authority read fails — every merge refuses. Line `:112` was just corrected to `?? null` for the ruleset sibling; the classic path kept the strict form. Fail-closed, so this is a liveness risk, not a bypass, and I could not confirm GitHub's behaviour for an omitted `app` from this snapshot.\n\n### Low — `stableStringify` is not total\n\n`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:11-17` interpolates `JSON.stringify(value)` directly. For `undefined` (and for function/symbol values) that returns the value `undefined`, which interpolates as the four-character string `undefined`; `NaN` becomes `null`. Two distinct objects can therefore serialize identically. Not reachable from a JSON API read, so this is a defensive note on a function whose documented job is canonicality.\n\n### Low — `repo` validation permits `..` segments\n\nBoth `/^[\\w.-]+\\/[\\w.-]+$/` checks (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:54,131`) accept `../..` and similar, and the value is interpolated into `repos/${repo}/...`. In production `repo` comes from `resolveRepositoryIdentity()` (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:141,207,190`), and `deps.repo` is a test seam, so this is theoretical; it is the same class the earlier review raised about the slug regex and it is unchanged.\n\n### Low — unverified disposition digests and the audit gate\n\n`docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~check-required-checks-preflight.mjs.json` records four sites and `scripts~update-required-checks.mjs.json` records six (`:6,14,22,30,38,46` of that file). My greps of the live sources found the discovery pattern (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:9`) at exactly four lines in the preflight (`:80,85,90,94`) and six in the updater (`:134,140,216,262,267,268`), so the **counts** are consistent. The audit compares `semantic_key` and `line_sha256` (`:122-124,131-132`), and I cannot compute SHA-256 here, so the digests are unverified in this packet — and the `site` line numbers recorded (`:131,137,247,252,253`) do not match the current lines, which is cosmetic only if the digests match. The directory listing I read contains no catalogue for the new `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs`; the audit requires one for any discovered source containing a pattern match (`:127-129`), so this holds only if that new file contains none — on the full text I read, it does not. `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json` is edited here although it is declared \"retained as historical evidence only; it is never read\" (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:15-16`, `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/README.md:74-75`). This whole gate is unrun.\n\n### Low — contract plumbing I could not verify\n\n`completion.json` names `contract_ref refs/db-contracts/3361/6` and `contract_sha256 3a30f81d…`; `verifyGitEvidence` requires the checked-in contract to hash-match the published ref (`scripts/agent-work-contract-git-evidence.mjs:73-75`). I have no network and no hashing tool, so the immutable ref is unverified. The `head_sha` (`d4a22a70`) is not the reviewed head (`d7ed59c3`); that passes only if `d4a22a70` is an ancestor and the sole successor commits are the gen-6 evidence pair (`:66-71`), which the reported `files_changed` shape implies but I did not confirm in git. The contract's `base_sha` is `95c5db5e…` while `completion.json` records `1660f920…`; `verifyGitEvidence` tolerates that, and the completion's value agrees with the review base.\n\n## The three mandatory checks\n\n**1. Index usage.** Not applicable to this change at the database level, and I state that from source rather than assumption: the changed set is `.mjs`, `.yml` and `.json` (packet §3 file list), and both evidence files declare empty database surfaces (`db_reads: []`, `db_writes: []` — `.agent/work/3361/6/contract.json:46-47`, `.agent/work/3361/6/completion.json:23-24`). There are no predicates or joins. The nearest analogue is the in-memory lookup in `normalizeRequirements`, keyed by `JSON.stringify(item)` in a `Map` (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:27-32`) — O(1), no loose index assumption. No index exists here that is unused or unusable as written.\n\n**2. Function volatility.** Not applicable as framed: no SQL function is created or altered. The JavaScript analogue holds and is deliberate: `computeRevision` (`:22-24`) is pure over four fields and **excludes** `capturedIso`, which is what makes the before/after comparison at `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:160` meaningful; the only time dependency is the injected `now = () => new Date()` (`:53`). No marker is looser than its body. The `stableStringify` totality gap above is the one place where a purity claim is weaker than the comment asserts.\n\n**3. Exact object checks.** Substantially satisfied, and stronger than what it replaced: repository `databaseId` as a positive safe integer, case-insensitive `nameWithOwner` equality, exact `ref.name`, 40-hex `oid`, non-empty classic rule `id`, and a two-way agreement check that the classic context list and the producer list name exactly the same contexts (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:60,64,68`); each ruleset row must carry `type`, integer `ruleset_id`, `ruleset_source_type` and `ruleset_source` (`:109`); an empty effective policy refuses rather than reading as \"nothing required\" (`:116`). The gaps are the ones reported above: `checks` is outside the digest, and the probe checks a strictly weaker object identity than the gather.\n\n## Related refusals and sibling paths\n\nI swept for consumers of the removed exports. `PINNED_REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`, `MIRROR_BOOTSTRAP_MAIN_SHA`, `parsePinnedFloor`, `readPinnedFloor`, `readRequiredChecksMirror`, `parseMirror`, `ADVISORY_CONTEXTS`, `PREFLIGHT_SOURCE_PATH` and `isPermissionRefusal` appear only in plan documents (`plan_orchestrator_required_load_reduction.md:94,122`, `plan_bounded_session_handover.md:88,143`, `plan_shared_db_workflow_refactor.md:116,256`) and in the packet's own diff. Two files could not be searched by the tool (`scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs`, `tools/promote-coldlion-source-owned.mjs` — reported as binary); a residual importer there would be a red build, not a fail-open, and I could not rule it out.\n\nSibling readers of the mirror that still work because `contexts` was retained: `scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs:22,67`, `scripts/documents-fast-ci-workflow.test.mjs:94`, `scripts/configure-merge-queue.mjs:96,288` (the last is the finding above). The advisory path now only logs (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:98,214`), so a non-required failure cannot veto a merge — verified in code and consistent with the acceptance criterion.\n\nThe prior REVISE findings I can confirm from this head are resolved; I am not re-raising them. The test suite's own results, the disposition digests, the published contract ref, and the live token's actual read capability (`docs/verification/main-required-status-checks.json` `capturedIso 2026-09-28T00:47:14.780Z` is a committed readback, not a run link) remain unverified, and no run of `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` exists in this packet.\n\nVERDICT: REVISE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n## Provisional verdict\n\nNot approvable as it stands. I read the reviewed head directly (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs`, `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs`, `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs`, `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml`, both test suites' entry wiring, the rewritten mirror, and the gen-8 evidence pair). The core refactor is fail-closed and the prior PAT-exposure and probe-mismatch findings look fixed, but the workflow reorder moves a refusal path under the repository-wide lock, the lock is acquired by trusted main and released by head code, and the required-check evidence at this exact head is unverified — including an in-conversation CI report of two failures of a required test.\n\n## Findings\n\n**Medium — the coordination-guard step, including the self-service-additive boundary classifier, now runs after the merge lock is taken.** The step sits at `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:155-168`, after lock acquisition (`:119-129`) and the under-lock authority read (`:130-154`); it has no `working-directory`, so it runs pull-request-head scripts (`node scripts/check-self-service-additive-lane.mjs --pr ...` at `:168`, plus `git fetch`/freshness/lease/live-proof at `:162-166`). The code it replaced carried an explicit invariant in the removed comment (patch hunk `@@ -96,48 +104,21 @@`): the boundary classifier was \"Placed BEFORE the quota check and the merge lane so an out-of-boundary pull request is refused having taken no lock at all\". An out-of-boundary PR now takes the exclusive merge lane and performs two token-bearing authority reads before being refused, and the surviving comment at `:107-108` only claims quota exhaustion waits outside the lock. Fail-closed, but a documented safety/liveness property was dropped without replacement text.\n\n**Medium — the merge lock is acquired from trusted main and released from the pull-request head.** Acquire runs `node scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --acquire-merge` under `working-directory: trusted-policy` (`:121,:126`), while release (`:287`) runs `node scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --release-merge` with no working-directory, i.e. the head's copy. A head that changes the lock ref shape or `ownerSha` derivation can fail release or mismatch it, leaving the repository-wide merge lane held — the one shared resource whose loss blocks every merge.\n\n**Low — the two token-bearing steps run *all* their `gh` reads on the repo-scoped PAT, which the code comment contradicts.** `export GH_TOKEN=\"$AUTHORITY_TOKEN\"` at `:96` and `:144` makes the PAT the step's default token, so the `tokenScopedRead` swap (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:119-128`) is a no-op in production and the status/check pagination reads (`:151-152`) also carry an admin-capable credential. The comment at `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:115-118` claims \"every other read stays on the caller's default token\"; the accurate claim is the workflow-level one at `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:54-55` (other *steps* keep `github.token`). Sibling effect: the transport's host quota latch is keyed on `GH_TOKEN` (`scripts/lib/github-transport.mjs:187`), so a genuinely differing per-read token would split the latch identity.\n\n**Low — a file declared \"never read\" is edited by this change.** `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json` is modified (sites removed) although `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:15-16` declares it \"retained as historical evidence only; it is never read\". Either the edit is inert scope noise or the declaration is stale; both weaken the artifact's evidential claim.\n\n**Low — disposition-catalogue `site` numbers do not match the head, and the digests are unverifiable here.** `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~check-required-checks-preflight.mjs.json:6,14,22,30` records 80/94/90/85, while the matching lines at head are `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:77,82,87,91` (four `missing` sites — count agrees). The audit compares only `semantic_key` and `line_sha256` (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:123,131-132`), so line drift is cosmetic *only if* the recorded digests still match; I cannot compute SHA-256 in this sandbox, so whether `node scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` passes at this head is unverified. That script is a required check (`.github/workflows/tools-offline-tests.yml:152`, inside \"Tools offline tests\").\n\n**Low — the gen-8 contract lists a retired evidence pair.** `.agent/work/3361/8/contract.json` carries `.agent/work/3361/7/contract.json` and `.agent/work/3361/7/completion.json` in `allowed_paths`/`file_writes`, but `.agent/work/3361` contains only `8/` at this head (listing), and the changed-file inventory contains only the gen-8 pair. This is the same class the wrap-up handoff records for another PR (`HANDOFF.d/2026-09-27T2359Z-edge-dev-mimo-non-orchestrator-wrapup2.md:69`). Whether the contract validator refuses it is unverified — `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs` was not readable by the grep tool (reported as binary), which is missing evidence, not proof of safety.\n\n**Unresolved required-check evidence — an in-conversation CI report names a failing test on this PR.** The last comment in the supplied evidence block reports two Blacksmith failures of `database-only workflow acquisitions supply admission while guarded merge rederives its route` on PR #3369. That test (`scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.test.mjs:3435-3456`) requires exactly 4 `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs --acquire-` invocations across `guarded-migration-merge.yml`, `shared-supabase-migrations.yml`, and `preview-ledger-orphan-reconciliation.yml`, each with `--pr`, and `--head-sha` for the guarded one; I confirmed the guarded workflow still supplies exactly one (`:126`). Whether the other two files supply the remaining three at this head I could not check before my tool budget ran out. If those failures are at `eec03469`, a required job is red (`.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml:49`) and nothing here can authorize a merge.\n\n**Other unverified facts (named, not inferred).** `completion.json` binds `head_sha` `03bc526c1bbe1ad638d1692a21c8e1253e00e529` (`.agent/work/3361/8/completion.json:10`), not the reviewed head — consistent with the evidence-pair rule, but the git topology itself is not checkable here. The \"78 passed, 0 failed\" claim (`:31-34`) and the truth-audit pass claim (`:36-39`) are author claims at that other SHA. The live capability of `secrets.SYNC_TOKEN` is a run-link claim in a comment (`.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:50-56`), and `docs/verification/main-required-status-checks.json:10-11` is a committed readback, not a run link. One claim *is* consistent with evidence in this conversation: `contract_sha256` `1bbd901f444c713fc4d234af6608bd35b443f90e89970b30e76300974f7359b5` (`.agent/work/3361/8/completion.json:8`) matches the gen-8 contract copy published at `refs/db-contracts/3361/8`.\n\n**What is in good shape.** Both token-bearing reads are trusted-main only: the steps use `working-directory: trusted-policy`, `export PATH=\"$TRUSTED_PATH\"`, `NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH/BASH_ENV` cleared, HEAD==origin/main and clean-tree checks, and the `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/trusted-policy/...` executable path (`:84-106`, `:131-154`); `secrets.SYNC_TOKEN` occurs exactly twice in the workflow (`:86`, `:133`) and the first pull-request-head script now runs at `:162`. The revision digest binds the normalized check list, not just `sources` (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:24-26`), and `evaluatePreflight` recomputes it and refuses a mismatch (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:71`). Every authority-read failure is wrapped into a refusal with no mirror fallback (`:146-149`), the `protectionUnreadable`/mirror authorize path is gone, an empty effective policy refuses (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:115`), and a ruleset full-`per_page` page requires a confirming empty next page (`:102-105`). The probe now checks `databaseId`/`nameWithOwner`/oid and the null-classic-rule REST distinction (`:130-140`, `:55-65`), so probe and gather agree. Both new test files are on the lease CI line (`.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml:49`).\n\n## Mandatory extra checks\n\n1. **Index usage — not applicable, from source.** The changed set is `.mjs`, `.yml` and `.json` (packet §3), and both evidence files declare empty database surfaces (`.agent/work/3361/8/completion.json:27-28`). No predicate, join, or table is added or altered. The nearest analogue is the in-memory `Map` keyed `` `${kind}:${name}` `` (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:28`), O(1) with no loose or unused assumption.\n2. **Function volatility — not applicable, from source.** No SQL function is created or altered. The JavaScript analogue holds: `computeRevision` (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:24-26`) hashes a fixed five-field object and does not include `capturedIso`, which is exactly why the before/after comparison at `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:157` is meaningful; the only time dependency is the injected `now` (`:66`). `stableStringify` refuses `undefined`/non-finite values rather than mis-serializing them (`:12-19`).\n3. **Exact object checks — satisfied on the GitHub-side objects.** Positive-integer `databaseId`, case-insensitive `nameWithOwner` equality, exact ref name, 40-hex `oid` (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:73`), classic rule `id` plus both lists required to name the same contexts (`:77-81`), ruleset `type`/`ruleset_id`/`ruleset_source_type`/`ruleset_source` (`:108`), 64-hex revision recomputed rather than pattern-matched (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:66,71`), and 40-hex reviewed head (`:66,137`). There is no database object here to assert exactly.\n\n## Verdict content follows\n\nEvidence is sufficient to refuse this head, not sufficient to approve it: no fail-open path was found, but the reorder takes the shared lock before a known refusal class, release runs head code against a main-acquired lock, and the exact-head required-check and digest evidence is missing or contradicted by an in-conversation CI failure report.\n\n> VOIDED REVIEWER LINE - VERDICT: REVISE eec03469a817bf4c6fb585552c503b7c83524d8e\n\n> VERDICT LINE VOIDED BY THE GOVERNED REVIEW RUNNER.\n>\n> 1 line(s) that a verdict parser would have read as a decision (REVISE) at this head were rewritten so that no tool can read them as a verdict. I found no fail-open path, no mirror/snapshot authorization, and no path where the authority PAT reaches pull-request-head code — but the exact-head required-check evidence is unverified (no tests were run for this packet), one changed contract file points at paths that do not exist at this head, and the previously-flagged \"historical audit is never read\" claim is contradicted by a test that does read it.\n\nReviewed directly with tools: `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs` (1-155), `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs` (1-216), `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml` (1-306), `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs` (120-300), `scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs` (255-320), `scripts/throughput-guard/check-throughput-truth-audit-context.test.mjs` (1-67), `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs` (1-60), `.agent/work/3361/10/contract.json` (1-77), both throughput-disposition catalogues, and the historical audit at 596-625.\n\n## What the brief asked me to verify — and what I could confirm\n\n**Authority PAT confinement.** `secrets.SYNC_TOKEN` appears only in two step environments (`.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:88`, `:141`). Both steps declare `working-directory: trusted-policy` (`:85`, `:138`), run the protected-main executable path (`:108`, `:161`), and no longer contain the removed `export GH_TOKEN=\"$AUTHORITY_TOKEN\"` — the only exports are `export PATH=\"$TRUSTED_PATH\"` (`:97`, `:151`). `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` is set alongside (`:87`, `:140`), and `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:119-128` swaps `process.env.GH_TOKEN` only around an authority call and restores it — so ordinary status/check reads (`:151-152`) keep the limited token. The first pull-request-head script is `node scripts/check-main-tip-freshness.mjs` at `:169`, after both token steps. The gen8 PAT-exposure finding is resolved.\n\n**Self-service boundary before the lock.** The classifier now runs under `working-directory: trusted-policy` at `:109-113`, before quota (`:116`) and lock (`:126`). Pinned by `scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs:265`, `:270`, `:290-294`.\n\n**Lock release through protected main, pinned to its preflight SHA.** `:290` `working-directory: trusted-policy`, `:294` `TRUSTED_MAIN_SHA: ${{ steps.trusted_preflight.outputs.sha }}` (written at `:107`), `:304` `test \"$(git rev-parse HEAD)\" = \"$TRUSTED_MAIN_SHA\"`, `:305` cleanliness, then `:306` release. The gen8 finding is resolved.\n\n**`tokenScopedRead` / probe alignment.** `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:139` now probes the null-classic case through `confirmClassicProtectionAbsent` (`:55-65`), which the reader also uses (`:88`), so probe and gather no longer disagree. `:111` maps an omitted ruleset `integration_id` to `null`, and `:79` maps an omitted classic `app` to `null`.\n\n## Findings\n\n### Unverified, blocking for an approve\n\n- **The exact-head required-check evidence does not exist in this packet.** The packet's own manifest states plainly: \"**No tests were run for this packet.**\" (`.ai-review-deepseek-ee6f022b66dd8a4acf9a23b2/MANIFEST.md` §5). I cannot run them (read-only, no shell). The claimed 104/1/7/2 passing suites and the truth-audit pass are recorded only as free text against a different commit (patch, `.agent/work/3361/10/completion.json`). The suites *are* wired into CI (`.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml:49`, `.github/workflows/tools-offline-tests.yml:152`), so the gate exists — but existence of the gate is not evidence the gate is green at `7af29c86`. No run link, no exit-code evidence at this head.\n- **Disposition digests are unverifiable here.** The audit compares `semantic_key` and `line_sha256` (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:96`, `:113`, `:116` reference `readCatalogues`/`run`; the comparison semantics are past my read window and I could not compute SHA-256 in any case). The recorded `line_sha256` values in `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~check-required-checks-preflight.mjs.json:8,16,24,32` are carried over unchanged from the historical artifact even though the recorded `site` ordinals moved (`:6` says 77, historical said 197). Cosmetic **only if** the digests still match; I cannot establish that.\n\n### High\n\n- **The changed contract references paths that do not exist at this head.** `.agent/work/3361/10/contract.json:17-18` and `:48-49` list `.agent/work/3361/9/contract.json` and `.agent/work/3361/9/completion.json` in `allowed_paths` and `file_writes`, but `list_dir .agent/work/3361` returns only `10/`. So the gen10 contract claims write access to a retired generation's evidence pair that is absent from the head. Whether the contract validator refuses this is **missing evidence**: `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs` is unreadable to my grep tool (\"binary file\", returned for both `allowed_paths|files_changed|file_writes` and a second probe). This is the same class prior rounds refused on (contract/evidence pair drift).\n\n### Medium\n\n- **Omitted producer identity is normalized in two readers but not in the third.** `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:7` (`appId`) treats only `null` and `-1` as unrestricted; `undefined` throws `required check producer identity is unreadable`. It is applied to every check at `:32`, whereas the classic reader at `:79` uses `item.app == null ? null : …` and the ruleset reader at `:111` uses `item.integration_id ?? null` — those two accept omission, `appId` does not. Two live paths hit the strict form: (a) `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs:216` now requires `parsed.checks`, and `verifyReadback` (`:260-261`) funnels it through `validateLiveDocument` → `normalizeRequirements` (`:148-152`), so a REST readback that *omits* `app_id` for an \"any-source\" check — the exact encoding this PR's PATCH now emits (`:232`) — turns a successful write into a reported readback failure; (b) `--refresh-mirror` (`:296`) reads through the same `normalizeRequirements`. Fail-closed (liveness, not bypass), but it is the same omission-vs-null asymmetry that was fixed for rulesets at `:111` and left in `appId`.\n- **The \"never read\" claim about the historical audit is false, and this PR edits that artifact.** `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:15-16` declares `HISTORICAL_AUDIT` \"retained as historical evidence only; it is never read\", and `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/README.md:74-75` repeats it. `scripts/throughput-guard/check-throughput-truth-audit-context.test.mjs:49` reads that exact file and, for every historical row, requires exactly one current catalogue row with identical `line_sha256`, `disposition` and `reason` (`:51-57`). So the artifact is a second source of truth for an invariant — and because the test only iterates the rows currently in that file (`:51`), an author can satisfy it by deleting a historical row alongside its catalogue entry, with no record of what was dropped. This PR does exactly that kind of edit (patch removes eight `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs` rows). The **good news**, verified by reading: the three preflight rows retained at `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json:602-621` all have matching `legacy_semantic_key`, `line_sha256`, `disposition` and reason in `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~check-required-checks-preflight.mjs.json:11,19,27`, and the five `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs` rows (historical `:2030-2059`) match `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~update-required-checks.mjs.json:11,19,27,35,43`. The gen10 goal of restoring the invariant appears met on inspection; the *claim* and the deletability are the defects.\n- **The mirror now records ruleset contexts alongside classic ones, and the two consumers want different things.** `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs:249` builds `contexts` as the union of `authority.checks` for the `--refresh-mirror` path (`:296`), while the classic-only path (`:249` with `authority` absent) keeps `validated.contexts`. A ruleset-only context therefore lands in the same `contexts` array that the merge-queue coverage check reads as the classic list. I verified this only from the patch hunk (`scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs` header, lines 9-14 of the patch), not from a tool read of that header at head, so I mark the downstream consequence as patch-sourced and unverified.\n\n### Low\n\n- **The two token-bearing steps do not clear `LD_PRELOAD`/`LD_LIBRARY_PATH`; the release step does.** `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:92-94` and `:146-148` clear `NODE_OPTIONS`, `NODE_PATH`, `BASH_ENV`; `:296-300` additionally clears `LD_PRELOAD` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. I found no exploitable path — no PR-head shell code runs before `:169`, and neither `GITHUB_ENV` nor any prior step executes checked-out code — but the hardening is inconsistent in the file that carries the secret.\n- **Release may not run on cancellation or timeout, and I could not verify a lock TTL.** The release condition is `always() && steps.merge_lock.outputs.owner_sha != '' && (steps.guarded_merge.outcome == 'success' || steps.revoke_authorization.outcome == 'success')` (`:289`), and `revoke_authorization` is `if: failure() && …` (`:283`). A **cancelled** run or the `timeout-minutes: 30` budget (`:62`) satisfies neither branch, so the repository-wide merge lane is not released by this workflow. Whether `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` expires the lane is **missing evidence** — I did not read the lock implementation. This is the post-merge recovery question the second brief asked about, and it is unanswered in the changed files.\n- **Quota multiplier is acknowledged but unmeasured.** One authority read costs a GraphQL call plus a paginated REST call plus a possible confirming page (`required-check-authority.mjs:91`, `:103`) and a possible `/protection` probe (`:57`); `gatherPreflightInput` performs two full authority reads (`check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:150`, `:156`), and `main()` probes unconditionally first (`:208`). The workflow says so itself: \"the absolute quota cost is not yet metered per merge\" (`guarded-migration-merge.yml:121-123`). Note `scripts/lib/github-transport.mjs:187` keys the host quota latch on `GH_TOKEN`, so the per-read token swap correctly splits latch identity rather than merging it.\n- **The committed mirror remains a second copy of the required list with no live re-validation.** `docs/verification/main-required-status-checks.json` now embeds a full `authority` snapshot (patch hunk), and `_why` asserts it is \"informational … never merge authority\". Nothing in the guarded path reads it any more (`check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:2-4`, `:148` \"no snapshot fallback\"), so a stale mirror is now undetectable by the merge gate — correct by design, but any remaining consumer of `contexts` inherits that.\n\n## The three mandatory checks\n\n1. **Index usage — not applicable, and I state that from source rather than assumption.** This change touches no SQL: the changed-file inventory (`MANIFEST.md` §3) is `.mjs`, `.yml` and `.json`, and both evidence files declare empty database surfaces (`.agent/work/3361/10/contract.json:30-31`). There are no predicates, joins, tables or views. The nearest analogue is the in-memory `Map` keyed `` `${kind}:${name}` `` at `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:28` — O(1), with no loose, unused or unusable index assumption, and no lookup that can silently drop a channel (both channels are inserted under distinct keys before the merge at `:56-62`).\n2. **Function volatility — not applicable as framed; the JS analogue is correct.** No SQL function is created or altered. `computeRevision` (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:24-26`) hashes a fixed five-field object and deliberately excludes `capturedIso`; that exclusion is exactly why the before/after comparison at `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:157` is meaningful. The only time dependency is the injected `now` (`required-check-authority.mjs:66`). `stableStringify` (`:12-19`) refuses `undefined`, functions, symbols, bigints and non-finite numbers rather than mis-serializing them, which is a *tighter* contract than the comment needs. No marker is looser than its body.\n3. **Exact object checks — substantially satisfied, with the gaps named above.** Repository `databaseId` as a positive safe integer, case-insensitive `nameWithOwner` equality, exact `ref.name`, 40-hex `oid` (`required-check-authority.mjs:73`); classic rule `id` plus both lists required to name the same contexts (`:77-81`); ruleset `type`/`ruleset_id`/`ruleset_source_type`/`ruleset_source` (`:108`); an empty effective policy refuses rather than reading as \"nothing required\" (`:115`); the revision is recomputed rather than pattern-matched (`check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:71`), so a shape-only 64-hex string cannot authorize; the reviewed head is asserted 40-hex (`:66`, `:137`). The residual exact-identity gaps are the omitted-`app_id` asymmetry in `appId` (`required-check-authority.mjs:7`/`:32` vs `:79`/`:111`) and the fact that `probeAuthorityReadPermissions` verifies the same repo/ref/oid triplet as the reader (`:138`) — that one is now aligned.\n\n## Coverage and limitations\n\nI did not read `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs:300-353`, `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:60-144`, `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs`, `scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs` (unreadable to grep), or `scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs` outside 255-320. Two files were unsearchable by grep (`scripts/agent-work-contract.mjs`, `tools/promote-coldlion-source-owned.mjs`), so a residual importer of the removed exports (`PINNED_REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`, `readRequiredChecksMirror`, `ADVISORY_CONTEXTS`, `parsePinnedFloor`, `isPermissionRefusal`, `PREFLIGHT_SOURCE_PATH`, `MIRROR_BOOTSTRAP_MAIN_SHA`) cannot be fully ruled out — a residual importer would be a red build, not a fail-open. No tests were executed; every test claim in this review is a claim about source text. No live GitHub read was possible, so `secrets.SYNC_TOKEN`'s actual capability to complete the GraphQL and rules reads remains unproven by evidence I hold, exactly as prior rounds recorded.\n\nVERDICT: REVISE Remaining gaps are a maintenance-CLI footgun and incomplete exact-head execution evidence, not a bypass.\n\nReviewed head `87aaa63f5f6729aebbbb1c845420c52c12ec0430` against base `5f91f2f6582df8eb7774cf48aa1849e5891a0b02`. Packet `MANIFEST.md` and `patch.diff` were read in full, then the post-change sources for the guarded merge workflow, authority helper, preflight, updater, lock recovery (`scripts/lib/exclusive-lease.mjs`), historical archive, gen-11 evidence pair, and the tests that actually loaded.\n\n## Findings\n\n**Blocking — none.** No fail-open, stale-snapshot authorization, settings mutation, or `AUTHORITY_TOKEN` path into pull-request-head code.\n\n**Claimed gen-11 fixes that hold in source**\n\n- `appId` treats omitted producer identity as unrestricted (`value == null || value === -1`) at `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:7`. The first pull-request-head script is `node scripts/check-main-tip-freshness.mjs` at `:173`, after both token steps. A full last ruleset page needs a confirming empty next page (`:102-105`).\n- Gen-11 contract lists only `.agent/work/3361/11/{contract,completion}.json` (`contract.json:21-22`). Runtime audit wording now says the historical file is unused at runtime and pinned by a test (`check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:15-16`; `check-throughput-truth-audit-context.test.mjs:69-81`).\n- Removed mirror-authorize exports are gone from `scripts/`. Remaining mentions are plan-document history.\n\n**Lock recovery vs prior cancellation/quota notes**\n\nCancelled and timed-out runs are terminal conclusions (`exclusive-lease.mjs:55`). Recovery is a live GitHub-run query plus a 10-minute grace (`evaluateRecovery` at `:164-198`); there is no lease clock, by documented design (`:10-37`). The workflow release step still requires `guarded_merge` success or `revoke_authorization` success (`guarded-migration-merge.yml:293`), and `revoke_authorization` is `if: failure()` (`:287`), so a cancelled or timed-out job leaves the ref held until recovery. The apply path writes classic readback only (`:342-344`), and `mirrorDocument` keeps whatever `validated.contexts` it is given (`:251`). (`check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:71`).\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\n\nVERDICT: APPROVE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\nI reviewed the head contents directly (not just the quoted diff) and verified the gen-12 claim, the workflow wiring, the truth-audit disposition machinery, and the mirror's consumers.\n\n## Provisional verdict\n\nProvisional lean: APPROVE. The gen-12 fix is real and pinned; no fail-open path, no PR-head exposure of `AUTHORITY_TOKEN`, and no stale-mirror authorization. Residual items below are liveness/cosmetic, not bypasses.\n\n## Verification of the claimed gen-12 fix and regressions\n\n- Refresh path: `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs:294-303` now derives the merge-queue baseline from the **classic** source only (`authority.sources?.classic`, `classic.requiredStatusCheckContexts`, `classic.requiresStrictStatusChecks`) and refuses when that baseline is unreadable/empty (\"cannot refresh classic coverage baseline without readable classic required checks\", :299). The inherited-ruleset union is kept separately through the full `authority` object (:300, :245, :252).\n- End-to-end regression exists for exactly the ruleset-only case: `scripts/update-required-checks.test.mjs:304-316` asserts `mirror.contexts == ['classic']` while `mirror.authority.checks` keeps `ruleset-only`. Sibling pin at :299-303.\n- Consumers are unharmed: `scripts/configure-merge-queue.mjs:288` reads only `?.contexts`; `scripts/check-merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs:22,67` and `scripts/documents-fast-ci-workflow.test.mjs:94,119` read `contexts`. No consumer reads the new top-level `checks`, so the union-in-baseline regression is gone and nothing else inherits it. I also confirmed the base 5f91f2f6→head diff does not touch `configure-merge-queue.mjs` or those readback artifacts, and `docs/verification/main-required-status-checks-readback-20260925.json` still holds the same 16 contexts the mirror carries.\n- Removed exports have no remaining importers in `scripts/`: grep for `PINNED_REQUIRED_CONTEXTS|readRequiredChecksMirror|ADVISORY_CONTEXTS|isPermissionRefusal|PREFLIGHT_SOURCE_PATH|MIRROR_BOOTSTRAP_MAIN_SHA|parsePinnedFloor|readPinnedFloor|evaluateWithoutRequiredList` returns only plan documents and the packet itself.\n- CI wiring is present: `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.test.mjs` and `scripts/update-required-checks.test.mjs` are on the lease line (`.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml:49`).\n- Disposition machinery is self-consistent: `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs` has **no** PATTERN hits (`no matches`), so no catalogue is required for it (and none exists); `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs` has exactly 4 hits at lines 77/82/87/91, matching its catalogue's 4 refreshed entries; `scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:9` matches and its catalogue records site 9. Historical preflight identities: 15 in `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json:603-701`, of which 3 remain live (0d141019, 2c084b9a, 4e36f9dd) and 12 are retired (`docs/verification/throughput-retired-identity-sites-3369.json`, 12 `\"state\": \"retired\"`). The 12 retired hashes are exactly the 12 non-live historical hashes.\n- Token confinement reads as claimed: `secrets.SYNC_TOKEN` occurs only at `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:88` and :143, both steps are `working-directory: trusted-policy` (:85, :140), run the pinned protected-main executable `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/trusted-policy/scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs` (:110, :165), clear `NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH/BASH_ENV/LD_PRELOAD/LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (:92-96, :148-152), and the first PR-head script is `node scripts/check-main-tip-freshness.mjs` at :173. Contract/allowed-path cleanliness is fine: `.agent/work/3361` contains only `12/`, and `completion.json:11-28` lists exactly the 17 non-evidence changed files (base→head diff has 19), with the evidence pair in `file_writes`.\n\n## Findings\n\n**Medium — the coordination-guard step now runs while the repository-wide merge lane is held.** `.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:166-178` runs PR-head `bash scripts/check-sql.sh`, `check-production-verification-sidecars.mjs`, `check-main-tip-freshness.mjs`, `check-migration-pr-lease.mjs`, `check-live-proof-probe.mjs` with no `working-directory`, i.e. from the head checkout, and it sits *after* lock acquisition (:128-138) and the under-lock read (:139-165). In the base this same step sat before the quota check/lock (patch hunk `@@ -95,49 +106,28 @@`). It is fail-closed and the contract's prohibition (\"do not execute a pull-request-head script before either token-bearing preflight\") forces it there, but the surviving comment at :116-117 only claims *quota* waits outside the lock, so a previously documented safety/liveness property (out-of-boundary PRs refused \"having taken no lock at all\") is now true only for the classifier at :111-115, not for the guards. Recommend restoring a pre-lock copy of the guards that do not need head code, or documenting the extra lock-hold cost.\n\n**Low — stale `site` ordinals in one catalogue, refreshed in the other.** `docs/verification/throughput-dispositions/scripts~update-required-checks.mjs.json:6,14,22,30,38` record ordinals 131/253/252/247/137 while the head's PATTERN matches are at `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs:134,140,264,269,270` (count 6 = recorded 6; the newly added entry at :46/216 is correct). `run()` compares only `semantic_key` and `line_sha256` (`scripts/check-throughput-truth-audit.mjs:124-133`), so this is cosmetic *only if* the carried-over digests still match — which I cannot compute here (missing evidence: no hashing tool). The sibling catalogue was refreshed for this PR (`scripts~check-required-checks-preflight.mjs.json` site ordinals 77/82/87/91 match the head's four matches), so the two files were handled inconsistently.\n\n**Low — contradiction between the new immutability pin and the declared write set.** `scripts/throughput-guard/check-throughput-truth-audit-context.test.mjs:72` now asserts the historical record's sha256 is fixed (\"must not be edited or pruned\"), yet `.agent/work/3361/12/contract.json` still lists `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json` in `allowed_paths`/`file_writes` (it is not in `completion.json` `files_changed`, i.e. not actually changed). Harmless, but the generation is declaring a write it must never make.\n\n**Low — new post-write failure mode in `--apply`.** After a successful PATCH and readback, `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs:343-345` re-reads live authority and throws (exit 1) if `authority.sources.classic.requiredStatusCheckContexts` does not match the REST readback, leaving the committed mirror un-refreshed. Fail-closed and clearly worded, but it is a new exit-1-after-write path (GraphQL/REST can lag each other).\n\n**Low — the mirror's `checks` and `contexts` now mean different things in one document.** `scripts/update-required-checks.mjs:251-252` writes `contexts` (classic only) beside `checks` (classic ∪ rulesets). Safe today because no consumer reads `checks`, but the document no longer has one meaning for \"required checks\" and the `_why` (:244) does not say which field is the baseline.\n\n**Low — probe and gather still disagree in one direction.** `scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:147-148` accepts any array-shaped rules page, while the reader applies the short-non-last-page and full-last-page confirmation drill-down (:92-105). The probe can print \"permissions proven\" and the gather can refuse one call later with a different message. (The null-classic half *is* aligned: :139 uses `confirmClassicProtectionAbsent`, same as :88.)\n\n**Residual/out-of-scope (not introduced by this change).** Release still requires `guarded_merge` success or `revoke_authorization` success (`.github/workflows/guarded-migration-merge.yml:293`), so a cancelled/timed-out run leaves the lane for out-of-band recovery; the added authority reads' quota cost is explicitly unmetered (:123-125); `SYNC_TOKEN`'s live capability is a comment reference (:50-56) plus a committed readback, not a diff-contained proof; `docs/merge-queue-operation.md:53` and the plan documents still describe the mirror as the pin/authority (unchanged files).\n\n## The three mandatory checks\n\n1. **Index usage — not applicable, from source.** The changed set is `.mjs`, `.yml` and `.json` under `scripts/`, `.github/workflows/`, `docs/verification/` and `.agent/work/` (I read every changed source; no `supabase/`, no migration or SQL file appears), and both evidence files declare empty database surfaces (`.agent/work/3361/12/completion.json:30-31`). There are no predicates or joins. The nearest analogue is in-memory: the `Map` keyed `` `${kind}:${name}` `` (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:28`) and `normalizeRequirements`' `JSON.stringify(item)`-keyed `Map` (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:33`) — O(1), no loose or unused-index assumption.\n2. **Function volatility — not applicable as framed.** No SQL function is created or altered. The JavaScript analogue is correct and deliberate: `computeRevision` hashes exactly `{repository_id, repository, branch, sources, checks}` and excludes `capturedIso` (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:24-25`, `:118`), which is precisely why the before/after comparison at `scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:157` is meaningful; the only time dependency is the injected `now` (`:66`). `stableStringify` refuses `undefined`/non-finite/non-JSON values (`:13`) — tighter than the comment requires, so no marker is looser than its body.\n3. **Exact object checks — no database objects; the GitHub-side analogue holds.** Positive `databaseId`, case-insensitive `nameWithOwner` equality, exact `ref.name`, 40-hex `oid` (`scripts/lib/required-check-authority.mjs:73`, and the same triplet in the probe at `:138`); classic rule `id` plus a two-way agreement check that the context list and producer list name the same contexts (`:77-81`); per-ruleset `type`/`ruleset_id`/`ruleset_source_type`/`ruleset_source` (`:108`); the revision is **recomputed**, not pattern-matched, and a shape-only 64-hex string cannot authorize (`scripts/check-required-checks-preflight.mjs:66,71`); the reviewed head is asserted 40-hex (`:66`) and check runs are filtered by `head_sha` (`:53`).\n\n## Evidence I could not establish\n\nTest execution, the sha256 values in the disposition catalogues, the pinned sha256 of `docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json`, the published `refs/db-contracts/3361/12` hash, the git topology (`bd0fc79c…` → `13ca94cf…`), GitHub CI status, and the live read capability of `secrets.SYNC_TOKEN`. The author's supplied run outputs and CI JSONs are consistent with the source but are unverifiable here; I treated them as claims, not proof.\n\nVERDICT: APPROVE
