REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### Findings and reasoning (everything the reviewer said before its verdict)\n\nI'll start from the evidence packet and the actual diff, then check the sandbox scope rule, turn-budget behavior, and the three mandatory SQL checks.The first path didn’t resolve; I’ll locate the evidence packet from the sandbox and the worktree next.Evidence packet is in hand; next I’ll read the patch and the files that implement the sandbox scope and turn-budget changes.The first hunks are in; I’ll keep reading the rest of the patch and the surrounding call sites.Provisional leaning is REVISE until I finish the scope-rule, `PROJECT_REFS`, and workflow-matrix checks. Next I’ll read the live sources and every consumer.I’ll trace `PROJECT_REFS` consumers, the classifier’s `designflow-nonprod` name, and whether `\\bdflow\\b` can miss owed migrations.The classifier and `PROJECT_REFS` split look intentional; I’m checking whether the `dflow` text rule or git grep can still hide owed sandbox migrations.Coverage is complete: the `dflow` text rule can hide migrations this database is already recorded as owing, so this is a revise. Details are below.\n\n## Findings\n\n### Issue 1 — Severity: bug\n- **File:** `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:155`\n- **Description:** Sandbox scope can hide a migration this database is actually owed. `sandboxInScopeVersions` keeps a merged version only when it is already in the sandbox ledger, or when `version >= baseline` and the file matches `\\bdflow\\b`. That filter runs **before** `classify_pending_version`, so it never consults `FOREIGN_TARGET_MIGRATIONS`.\n\n  The repo already records `20260909121403` as targeting `designflow-nonprod` (`scripts/production_migration_guard.py:298-314`). `supabase/migrations/20260909121403_hts_rag_split_isolated_schema.sql` has **zero** `dflow` tokens (it creates `hts_rag_split`). If that version is missing from the ledger, the scope rule drops it from `mainVersions`, `computeDrift` never sees it, and the job can go green.\n\n  Same heuristic also drops post-baseline DesignFlow-database work that does not mention `dflow`:\n  - `20260904172420` (`public.hts_rag_*`, after the test baseline `20260904143518`, no `dflow`)\n  - `20260916232818` (`hts_rag` RLS for `designflow_hts_*` roles, no `dflow`)\n\n  Sibling contrast: `20260911210709` is in scope only because a comment says it does **not** touch `dflow`. The follow-on on the same HTS surface is invisible. Under-reporting is fail-open for those versions: excluded work is not classified, not listed, and does not fail the check. Over-reporting would have been acceptable; this is the opposite.\n- **Suggestion:** Union into sandbox scope every merged version whose recorded target is `designflow-nonprod` (read the existing registry; do not re-approximate it with a word search). Keep the `dflow` match as an additional over-report, not as the only owed-set. Add a test that `20260909121403` stays in sandbox `inScope` when it is on main and absent from the ledger. Do not treat “already applied, so it stayed in scope” as coverage of the missing-ledger case.\n\n### Issue 2 — Severity: suggestion\n- **File:** `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:338`\n- **Description:** After the scope filter, a clean sandbox run still prints `NO DRIFT. Every version merged to the base branch has a ledger row`. That sentence is false once hundreds of merged versions have been excluded. The SCOPE block above it is honest; this line is what gets quoted.\n- **Suggestion:** Qualify the clearance with the scoped set (for example “every in-scope merged version”), so a green run cannot be read as a whole-tree clearance.\n\n---\n\nAttack questions that did **not** yield a defect:\n\n- **Applied versions in scope masking orphans:** `inScope` is filtered from merged-on-main only. An applied version with no file on main cannot enter `inScope`, so it remains in `appliedNotMerged`. The applied-union only prevents a **false** orphan when the file exists on main but does not match `dflow`.\n- **`PROJECT_REFS` split:** `PROJECT_REFS` is still `{production, preview}`. `check-applied-migration-edit.mjs` still iterates that map; `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` still uses `PROJECT_REFS.preview`; `readPreviewLedger` still cross-checks production/preview only. Sandbox is only on `LEDGER_PROJECT_REFS`, which only the drift checker uses for `--target`.\n- **Turn budget / fewer turns:** `turnBudgetFor` is `>= 20` for every finite non-negative size; unknown size is 40; wrappers with no policy are unchanged; an explicit `--max-turns` is not overridden. `changedMigrationLines` never throws. Measurement failure still launches the review (intentional; not a skip). Non-Grok wrappers do not receive `--max-turns`.\n- **Workflow matrix silent skip:** Unknown dispatch target exits 1. Push/schedule emit `[\"production\",\"sandbox\"]`. `fail-fast: false`. Missing `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` fails the check step. Alarm titles are per-target so production’s throttle still matches. An empty matrix is not reachable from this script.\n- **Fail-closed elsewhere:** Empty sandbox ledger, empty `dflow` grep, empty in-scope set, and `git grep` failure all raise `Unknown` (exit 2). The fail-open hole is specifically the scope exclusion of owed versions, not those paths.\n\nMandatory SQL checks (this change adds no migration SQL):\n\n1. **Index usage:** The only statement is the existing `select version from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations order by version`. No new predicate or join. `ORDER BY version` is served by that table’s primary key on `version`. No unused-index assumption in new code.\n2. **Function volatility:** No new SQL functions; nothing to mark `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE`.\n3. **Exact object checks:** The ledger read names `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations.version` and refuses rows without `version`. The **scope** rule does not assert an exact schema/table/target: it infers “touches `dflow`” from a word in the file. That is the Issue 1 hole (`20260909121403` is owed by registry, not by that word).\n\n## Coverage statement\n\nExamined the packet `MANIFEST.md`, `identity.json`, and full `patch.diff` (head `3f87309ee7f3111c1761b0900707d002356265b2` vs base `18c2610526e9b34a9d5af3818853cf1fb63e8979`).\n\nRead in full: `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs`, `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.test.mjs` (sandbox tests), `scripts/orchestrator-flow/read-preview-ledger.mjs`, `scripts/orchestrator-flow/read-preview-ledger.test.mjs`, `scripts/lib/reviewer-turn-budget.mjs`, `scripts/lib/reviewer-turn-budget.test.mjs`, `scripts/run-governed-review.mjs` (budget application, `wrapperSourceContractArgs`, `wrapperSpawnPlan`, `wrapperFailureReason`), `scripts/run-governed-review.test.mjs` (#2492 tests), `.github/workflows/migration-ledger-drift.yml`, `.github/workflows/migration-author-lease.yml` (test-list delta).\n\nTraced `PROJECT_REFS` consumers: `check-applied-migration-edit.mjs` (`Object.entries(PROJECT_REFS)`), `manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs` (`PROJECT_REFS.preview`). Read `classify_pending_version` / `FOREIGN_TARGET_MIGRATIONS` / `KNOWN_MIGRATION_TARGETS` in `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` and the related tests in `scripts/test_production_migration_guard.py`.\n\nChecked migration text for `dflow` on `20260909121403` (none), `20260911210709` (comment-only), `20260905072856`, `20260909084253`, `20260904172420` (none), `20260916232818` (none). Packet tests were not re-run here.\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\n\nVERDICT: REVISE Packet tests were not re-run here.\n\n## Issues\n\n### Issue 1 -- Severity: suggestion\n- File: `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:365`\n- Description: The SCOPE block printed on every sandbox run still describes the old rule (“already in this ledger, or touches the `dflow` schema and is not older than the derived baseline”). The clearance sentence is fixed; this paragraph is now the line that understates what was compared.\n- Suggestion: Restate the three actual disjuncts (applied, registry target, surface ∩ ≥ baseline) REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\nFresh round — re-checking the sandbox scope, registry, and turn-budget fixes line by line.I've mapped the full diff — now digging into the scope logic, ledger split, and budget math to verify each risk.Core logic checks out — now hunting edge cases and confirming no other guard changes behavior.## Findings\r\n\r\n### Blocking — none found\r\n\r\nNo blocking defect was found at this head. The two prior-round defects are confirmed fixed in the code as written, and the round-2 suggestion (scope paragraph understating the rule) is confirmed fixed: `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs` lines 359–376 now print all three disjuncts with the registered count and the derived baseline.\r\n\r\n### Low / informational (non-blocking, reported together per the single-round instruction)\r\n\r\n1. Surface match is case-sensitive — `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:149`, `SANDBOX_SURFACE_PATTERN`, consumed via `git grep --extended-regexp` at line 568 without `-i`. A future migration naming only an uppercase token (`HTS_RAG`, `DFLOW`) with no lowercase occurrence would miss the text disjunct. Not blocking today: I verified the only migration carrying uppercase tokens (`supabase/migrations/20260909121403_hts_rag_split_isolated_schema.sql`, lines 7 and 56) also carries lowercase `hts_rag` occurrences and is additionally covered by the registry disjunct. The registry backstop covers every recorded version regardless of text. A case-insensitive grep would close the class entirely in the over-reporting direction this file already prefers.\r\n\r\n2. `registeredCount` counts every registry entry for the target, not the subset present on main — `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs:198`. If a registered version is ever deleted or renumbered off main, the printed \"(N version(s))\" in the scope paragraph overstates the compared set. Cosmetic only; today the single registry entry (`20260909121403`, verified in `scripts/production_migration_guard.py:298-315`) is on main.\r\n\r\n3. One sandbox test is not fully hermetic — `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.test.mjs`, the \"classifies against the registry name\" test supplies no `registryTargetVersions` override, so it shells out to the real `production_migration_guard.py`. It passes today only because no fixture version is registered; a future registry entry colliding with a fixture version would change its scope assertions. Test hygiene only.\r\n\r\n4. Operator-override detection is exact-token only — `scripts/lib/reviewer-turn-budget.mjs:126`, `list.includes(policy.option)`. A `--max-turns=NN` (equals-form) caller arg would not be detected and would produce a duplicated flag. Latent only: I grepped all `--max-turns` uses in the repo and every caller uses separate-token form, so no current path triggers it.\r\n\r\n5. If the new `targets` job itself fails on the scheduled leg, no throttled alarm issue is filed (the alarm step lives in the `drift` job, which is then skipped). The run itself is still red and visible, and this matches the pre-existing shape where pre-check failures never alarmed either. Noted for completeness, not a regression.\r\n\r\n### Attack points from the brief — all confirmed held\r\n\r\n- Owed-set shrinkage: a registered version is in scope regardless of baseline (`sandboxInScopeVersions`, lines 189–191); registry read/parse failure is `Unknown`, never an empty set (lines 533–555); empty ledger, empty surface read, and empty scope all throw `Unknown` (lines 167–199); applied-on-main versions stay in scope (line 190, first disjunct). Under-reporting is closed; the missing trailing `\\b` (line 149, documented at 147–148) errs toward over-reporting, which is the stated-safe direction.\r\n- Orphan masking: no masking. The scope filters `mainVersions` only, so an applied version with no file on main is absent from `inScope` and still surfaces via `computeDrift`'s `appliedNotMerged` (lines 297–326, called with the narrowed set at 623). The pinned test guards the converse (applied-on-main never reported as orphan).\r\n- `PROJECT_REFS` split: `PROJECT_REFS` is byte-identical (2 entries) and every iterating consumer is unchanged — `scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.mjs:66-67,146,289-300` iterates the same two ledgers; `scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:9367,9437,9454` uses only `.preview` equality; `read-preview-ledger.mjs:41-42` cross-checks unchanged. `LEDGER_PROJECT_REFS` is consumed only by the drift script (line 597).\r\n- Fewer turns: impossible by construction. `turnBudgetFor` returns `>= policy.base` for every input including `0`, negative, `NaN`, `null`, and `undefined` (`reviewer-turn-budget.mjs:77-83`); an operator-supplied flag is left untouched (lines 126–128); unknown wrappers get byte-identical args (line 125); measurement catches everything and yields `null`, which maps to the raised `unmeasured: 40` floor (lines 93–112, 79).\r\n- Fail-closed: every new failure path is `Unknown`/exit 2 or an explicit refusal; unknown `--target` and unknown dispatch input both refuse; the JSON/human report paths share one `formatReport`.\r\n- Matrix silent skip: push/schedule check exactly `[\"production\",\"sandbox\"]`; dispatch checks exactly the named target after validating it against the known triple; `fail-fast: false` keeps one target's failure from hiding the other; per-target alarm titles preserve the production throttle string byte-for-byte while giving the sandbox its own.\r\n\r\n### Mandatory floor items\r\n\r\n1. Index usage: nothing to index. The change adds no SQL predicate or join; the single constant statement (`select version from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations order by version`, `read-preview-ledger.mjs:21`) is unchanged, and a full read plus sort of the tiny ledger table is the pre-existing, correct access path.\r\n2. Function volatility: no database functions are created, replaced, or re-marked. The only new \"functions\" are JavaScript module functions; there is no `IMMUTABLE`/`STABLE`/`VOLATILE` marker anywhere in the diff.\r\n3. Exact object checks: no new database-object dependency is introduced. The ledger table/column reliance (`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations.version`) is pre-existing, and `fetchAppliedVersions` validates the `version` field per row rather than assuming shape (`read-preview-ledger.mjs:31`).\r\n\r\n## Coverage\r\n\r\nRead in full at this head: the complete `patch.diff` (all hunks); `scripts/check-migration-ledger-drift.mjs` (727 lines, including scope rule, registry reader, surface grep, `runDriftCheck`, and CLI); `scripts/orchestrator-flow/read-preview-ledger.mjs` (47 lines); `scripts/lib/reviewer-turn-budget.mjs` (150 lines); `.github/workflows/migration-ledger-drift.yml` (230 lines); `scripts/production_migration_guard.py` lines 290–340 (registry contents and known targets); `scripts/check-applied-migration-edit.mjs` lines 135–303 (ledger iteration and preview-only guard); `scripts/run-governed-review.mjs` lines 418–509 (budget wiring and refusal text). No migration files are in the change set (confirmed via the packet file list). Tests were not executed (read-only review; the packet records no test run, so suite results are taken from the author's completion evidence, not re-proven here).\r\n\r\nVERDICT: APPROVE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### Findings and reasoning (everything the reviewer said before its verdict)\n\nI'll start with the evidence packet and repository AGENTS.md, then inspect the actual changes against main.Evidence packet is in place. Next I’ll read AGENTS.md and the committed patch, then compare the migration, tests, and live proof against main.AGENTS.md is loaded. I’ll now read the full patch and the predecessor migration so I can compare the detector bodies.The patch is large, so I’ll load the new migration, predecessor, tests, and live proof next and compare the detector bodies.I have the new bodies. Next I’ll locate the predecessor migration and compare the exact DesignFlow-gate deletions.Predecessor found. I’ll read its detector bodies and grants, then diff them against the new migration.I’ll check downstream consumers of `designflow_ok`, live-proof conventions, and whether the committed body hashes match the new function sources.I’ll extract the function bodies, hash them against the live-proof MD5s, and confirm HEAD plus public-wrapper/grant behavior.The packet matches head `dcac0d06d17af87df642a71ac96eea6488aef2e8` on base `70b0cad2`. I compared the new migration to predecessor `20260905043023`, then read the focused suite, live proof, public wrappers, and cutover composer.\n\n## Findings\n\nNo blocking defect in the two admitted function bodies. The change retires only the DesignFlow **runtime** freshness/status/consecutive-failure legs and leaves the rest of both detectors intact.\n\n### What the migration actually changes\n\nAgainst `20260905043023_coldlion_taxonomy_health_live_hash_guard.sql`:\n\n- `plm.check_taxonomy_sync_health`: removes the DesignFlow missing/failed/stale issues, `v_df_prev`, and `two_consecutive_failures` for DesignFlow. ColdLion missing/failed/stale/consecutive-failure logic is unchanged (`20260920151128` lines 201–232). Historical DesignFlow `sync_run` is still selected and returned as `designflow_run_id`.\n- `plm.record_taxonomy_parallel_observation`: removes the DesignFlow lane freshness block that used to increment `v_unexplained` and set `v_designflow_ok`. `v_pass` no longer requires `v_designflow_ok` (lines 668–673). Baseline/link pins still include `designflow_source_ref_count` (lines 549–604). Live licensor-status hash refusal, prior nondrill drift, append-only insert, and drill isolation are unchanged.\n- `v_designflow_ok` is initialized true with an explicit comment that this is “not required,” not a successful run (lines 401–402). Return JSON, observation `details`, and `ingest.sync_run` metadata all carry `designflow_lane: {status: retired, required: false}` (health 301, 340; observation 677, 724, 833). That is not a fabricated DesignFlow `sync_run`: failed historical rows are still inserted/read as failed.\n\nPublic wrappers remain the original SQL delegates in `20260726180000` (`select plm....`). This file does not replace them. `CREATE OR REPLACE` of an existing signature keeps ACLs; the suite and live proof re-check `anon`/`authenticated` denied and `service_role` allowed.\n\n### False-green / compatibility\n\n`designflow_ok = true` is overloaded by design. It is always paired with `designflow_lane` in detector output and persisted `details`. Cutover readiness (`tools/evaluate-coldlion-licensor-property-cutover-readiness.mjs` lines 239–262) keys off `health.ok` and latest nondrill `pass`, not `designflow_ok` alone. Old failed observations still trip `recent_nondrill_observation_failed` when `observation_date >= today-1` (health 258–269), so this does not by itself declare global cutover readiness.\n\nThe first contract assertion would fail if the DesignFlow **missing-run** gate were still present (no DesignFlow row yet, `ok`/`pass` must be true). The later failed-DesignFlow insert (test lines 49–54) would fail if the **failed-run** gate remained.\n\n### ColdLion refusal paths\n\nPreserved in source. The new suite exercises:\n\n| Path | Test evidence |\n|---|---|\n| Stale ColdLion | test line 57–59, `interval '-100 years'` / `max_success_age: -100 years` |\n| Two consecutive ColdLion failures | test lines 61–66 |\n| Missing/unreadable baseline | test lines 88–92 |\n| Unreviewed live hash | test lines 73–86; SQL null-or-not-in guard at migration 158–170 and 510–522 |\n| Drill isolation | test lines 93–94 |\n| Historical DesignFlow **reference** pins | test lines 68–70 |\n\n`missing_run` for ColdLion is not independently asserted. The health block is byte-identical to the predecessor, so this is a coverage gap, not a regression.\n\n### Null-safe tests\n\nExpected success uses `IS NOT TRUE` (fails on false **or** null). Expected failure uses `IS NOT FALSE` and `IS NOT TRUE` on `@>` (fails on true **or** null). Jsonb lane identity uses `IS DISTINCT FROM`. That is fail-closed, not false-green.\n\n### Live proof\n\n`.github/live-proofs/3175.sql` is a single `WITH`/`SELECT` returning `passed`. It does not call either detector. Shape matches `check-live-proof-probe.mjs` (SELECT/WITH, no write keyword, `as passed`). It binds ledger version `20260920151128`, `md5(prosrc)` for both signatures, `prosecdef`, and EXECUTE ACLs. Shell was denied here, so those MD5s were not independently recomputed; they are the intended post-apply bind, not a runtime detector call.\n\n### Non-blocking residuals (not required to merge)\n\n- Health `two_consecutive_failures` for DesignFlow is not negatively tested; one failed DesignFlow row would not fire it even if that block were left behind. Product source removes the block (`v_df_prev` is gone).\n- Observation unreadable-baseline early return is not called in the suite (health unreadable is).\n- Live proof hashes `prosrc` only, so `search_path` (`proconfig`) is not in the MD5. The migration still sets `search_path = plm, core, ingest, public`. ACL/`prosecdef` are checked separately.\n- `.agent/completion.json` still records `head_sha` `c9dd4108…`; admitted SQL/test/proof paths are the ones under review.\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\n\nVERDICT: APPROVE This matches the pre-existing design and has negligible cost due to low partition cardinality, but should be noted.\r\n\r\n#### Finding 2: Implicit volatility declaration\r\n- **Severity**: Low / Informational\r\n- **File**: [supabase/migrations/20260923173656_retire_designflow_taxonomy_health_lane.sql#L5-L13](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-d9610f1c389d-claude-r3175-s2-cc2b-f7d311b4e724/supabase/migrations/20260923173656_retire_designflow_taxonomy_health_lane.sql#L5-L13), [supabase/migrations/20260923173656_retire_designflow_taxonomy_health_lane.sql#L355-L363](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-d9610f1c389d-claude-r3175-s2-cc2b-f7d311b4e724/supabase/migrations/20260923173656_retire_designflow_taxonomy_health_lane.sql#L355-L363)\r\n- **Detail**: Neither function explicitly specifies `VOLATILE` in its header. PostgreSQL defaults to `VOLATILE` when omitted, ensuring catalog correctness, but declaring volatility explicitly would prevent ambiguity during schema audits.\r\n\r\n#### Finding 3: Comprehensive verification and live probe safety\r\n- **Severity**: Informational\r\n- **File**: [.github/live-proofs/3175.sql](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-d9610f1c389d-claude-r3175-s2-cc2b-f7d311b4e724/.github/live-proofs/3175.sql#L1-L18), [supabase/tests/taxonomy_retired_designflow_lane_contracts.sql](file:///D:/ai-data/local/state/ai-devops/review-sandboxes/gemini-d9610f1c389d-claude-r3175-s2-cc2b-f7d311b4e724/supabase/tests/taxonomy_retired_designflow_lane_contracts.sql#L1-L102)\r\n- **Detail**: The live proof is strictly a read-only query using `with ... select` without calling detector functions, returning exactly one row with a boolean column aliased `passed`. The contract test suite executes in a rollback transaction and exercises all failure modes, security boundaries, and decoupled DesignFlow behaviors without regression.\r\n\r\nVERDICT: APPROVE `supabase/migrations/20260920005114_revoke_authenticated_from_unused_definer_views.sql:9-14` issues exactly six `REVOKE SELECT ... FROM authenticated` statements, one per in-scope view, using `ON TABLE` which is the correct relation syntax for views.\r\n- No GRANT, no owner change, no view redefinition, no RLS/policy text in the file. Tests re-assert anon denial for the inventory view (`supabase/tests/source_capture_inventory_contracts.sql:22`, `sega_landing_contracts.sql:1628`, `wildbrain_landing_contracts.sql:1993`).\r\n- Inherited-grant risk checked: no replacement broad-role grant, no `TO public`, no function-grant change. The untouched `api.source_capture_inventory_exact(text)` ACL is explicitly pinned (`source_capture_inventory_contracts.sql:27-44`), including the authenticated-EXECUTE preservation and anon-EXECUTE denial.\r\n\r\n**Service-role / internal compatibility — preserved:**\r\n- Dedicated grant contract `supabase/tests/issue_2662_unused_view_grants_contracts.sql:18-21` requires `NOT authenticated` plus `service_role` SELECT on all six views, then proves 42 authenticated denials across seven role variants including administrator and empty-role (lines 23-37) and six service_role reads (lines 38-41).\r\n- OPA definition and server path intact: pre-grant logic checks run as owner (lines 86-97), denial loop covers all three studio views × seven principals (`opa_property_studio_resolution_contracts.sql:105-121`), service fixture access re-proved (lines 122-129).\r\n- CRM/PM visibility logic intact: grant-matrix assertion exempts only the two picker views (`app_serving_status_contracts.sql:69-72`), barrier/`security_invoker=false` options still asserted for all six serving views (lines 59-68), and hidden/visible vendor semantics re-proved via service_role (`lines 189-211`).\r\n\r\n**Denial-test quality — meaningful (fails at grant, not zero rows):**\r\n- New tests catch `insufficient_privilege` explicitly rather than asserting empty results (`issue_2662...:32-36`; `opa_...:115-119`). Sibling-contract updates flip the assertion polarity correctly (`source_capture...:22-24`; `sega...:1628-1630`; `wildbrain...:1993-1995`).\r\n\r\n**Sibling controls — preserved:**\r\n- Four browser-facing pickers pinned unchanged with live reads (`issue_2662...:44-51`); DAM picker path still authenticated (`app_serving_status_contracts.sql:217-225`); open Styles access untouched per instruction.\r\n\r\n**Transaction safety / idempotence — acceptable:**\r\n- Six bare REVOKEs with no DDL; Supabase runs each migration in a transaction. A repeated apply emits only a WARNING for an absent grant, not an error, so re-run is safe. No `IF EXISTS` syntax exists for REVOKE and none is required here.\r\n\r\n**Live probe — complete and correctly shaped:**\r\n- `.github/live-proofs/2662.sql:2-8` returns a single row with lowercase `as passed`, counts exactly six `api` relations, constrains `relkind='v'`, and requires both `NOT authenticated SELECT` and `service_role SELECT`. Single-statement SELECT-only probe suitable for the shared proof workflow.\r\n\r\n**Sibling-class sweep:**\r\n- Searched all `grant/revoke` history for the six objects; no additional anon/public grant, no second grant path, no missed alias. The twelve `db_writes` claim entries are the documented conservative table+view parser aliases for the same six catalog views, not extra objects; no schema change is hidden there.\r\n- Out-of-scope over-grants (if any) remain governed by successors 3327/3328/3329/2326 per the bounded-scope statement; treating this subset as a full audit clear would be wrong, and the migration/probe headers explicitly disclaim that.\r\n\r\n**Evidence notes (not defects):**\r\n- `.agent/completion.json:57,62,67` cites ephemeral run 35518490787 (190 passed, 0 unquarantined failures), local 42-deny/6-read/4-sibling fixture, and 6 Python probe tests; packet itself ran no tests (§5 unknown). Author attests SQL byte-identical after main integration to `70b0cad2`; the diff confirms only `.agent` bookkeeping plus the six-view files changed.\r\n- Minor coverage observation: the new six-view contract does not assert anon denial for the five non-inventory views, but anon was never granted there and inventory anon coverage plus creation-time revokes close the gap — no revision warranted.\r\n\r\n## Coverage\r\n\r\nRead the manifest, full `patch.diff` (10 files), the migration, the live proof, all six changed test files in full (plus surrounding context for sega/wildbrain grant blocks), both `.agent` evidence files, and grant/revoke history for the six views (creation grants, anon revocations, inventory re-grants). Verified privilege boundary, inherited grants, service compatibility, denial-test meaningfulness, sibling controls, transaction safety, probe shape, and claim-alias explanation. No database, secret, or licensed-row access performed.\r\nVERDICT: APPROVE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### Findings and reasoning (everything the reviewer said before its verdict)\n\nI'll start with the evidence-packet manifest, then read AGENTS.md, the actual diff, and the six-view privilege changes against the review criteria.Provisional stance is hold until the migration, tests, live proof, and privilege claims are checked. Next I’ll read AGENTS.md and the packet files.I’ll read the full patch next, then the migration, tests, live proof, and `.agent` evidence against the privilege-boundary criteria.The patch is a bounded `REVOKE SELECT` on six views. I’ll inspect view definitions, existing grants, and the six tests for inherited-privilege and denial-path gaps.The first search hit the review cwd, not the sandbox. I’ll rerun it against the packet checkout.Original grants differ across the six views. I’ll read the creating migrations and later recreates to see whether `service_role` and `PUBLIC` still hold SELECT.Inspected the evidence packet at HEAD `4a76f2dbeefbde1adebc1f28e124c3e0983b706e` versus base `70b0cad2ff730732866e6cd1c9f9b128262877b6`. The patch is a bounded `REVOKE SELECT` on six `api` views, plus matching tests, live-proof probe, and `.agent` records. Identity, `AGENTS.md` live-proof rule, creating migrations, default `service_role` grants, and later `source_capture_inventory` re-grants were checked against the privilege-boundary criteria.\n\n## Findings\n\nNo blocking defects. The migration removes only `authenticated` `SELECT`, leaves definitions/owners/policies/`service_role`/sibling grants untouched, and the tests prove grant-boundary denial rather than empty-result hiding.\n\n### Privilege boundary\n\n`supabase/migrations/20260920005114_revoke_authenticated_from_unused_definer_views.sql:9-14` issues six `REVOKE SELECT ON TABLE … FROM authenticated` statements and nothing else. That is the correct object-type keyword for views. PostgreSQL `REVOKE` is idempotent (missing privilege is a notice, not an error) and is transactional under the ordinary Supabase migration wrapper.\n\nInherited grants were checked against catalog history:\n\n- `has_table_privilege('authenticated', …)` includes `PUBLIC` and role inheritance. The new contract fails if that effective privilege remains (`issue_2662_unused_view_grants_contracts.sql:19-20`).\n- `GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA api TO authenticated` (`20260621151155_api_rls_realtime.sql:468`) is a snapshot of objects that existed then, not a future default.\n- OPA views already `REVOKE ALL FROM public, anon` (`20260825203652_opa_property_studio_resolution.sql:330-333`). `source_capture_inventory` does the same on every recreate; the last authenticated re-grant is `20260910155753_all_licensor_property_source_coverage.sql:977-978`, which is before this revoke.\n- CRM/PM factory views were granted only to `authenticated` (`20260723223000_protect_app_picker_serving_contracts.sql:80-85`). `anon` was never granted. `service_role` keeps `ALL` from `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA api GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO service_role` (`20260710135975_reconcile_service_role_grants.sql:16`), which predates those views. This migration adds no replacement grant.\n\n### Service-role / internal compatibility\n\n`issue_2662_unused_view_grants_contracts.sql:20,38-41` requires `service_role` `SELECT` and actually `SET LOCAL ROLE service_role` before `SELECT EXISTS`. OPA fixture rows are re-read as `service_role` with administrator JWT (`opa_property_studio_resolution_contracts.sql:122-128`). CRM/PM visibility fixtures remain (`app_serving_status_contracts.sql:189-211`).\n\n`api.source_capture_inventory_exact` is not in the patch. It remains `SECURITY DEFINER` (`20260825011609_source_inventory_bounded_reads.sql:11-26`). The authenticated RPC call is unchanged (`source_capture_inventory_contracts.sql:84-86`).\n\nDAM/Styles siblings stay on the browser path: `api.dam_factory_list` is still selected as `authenticated` (`app_serving_status_contracts.sql:217-225`).\n\n### Meaningful denial tests\n\n`issue_2662_unused_view_grants_contracts.sql:23-37` is 6 views × 7 JWT principals (viewer, vendor, designer, administrator, sales, licensing, empty roles) = 42 authenticated attempts. A successful `SELECT` that returns zero rows does **not** count as a deny; only `insufficient_privilege` sets `v_denied`. OPA uses the same fail-closed pattern (`opa_property_studio_resolution_contracts.sql:103-120`), including administrators.\n\nSibling controls: `api.crm_customer_picker_list`, `api.pm_customer_list`, `api.dam_customer_list`, `api.dam_factory_list` must still have authenticated `SELECT` and must execute (`issue_2662_unused_view_grants_contracts.sql:44-51`). Factory grant polarity in `app_serving_status_contracts.sql:69-72` now expects authenticated `SELECT` only on the four still-browser views.\n\nGrant assertions for `api.source_capture_inventory` were flipped in the three live tests that still check them (`source_capture_inventory_contracts.sql:22-25`, `sega_landing_contracts.sql:1628-1631`, `wildbrain_landing_contracts.sql:1993-1996`): `anon` still denied, `authenticated` now denied, `service_role` still required.\n\n### Live probe\n\n`.github/live-proofs/2662.sql:2-8` is one read-only `SELECT` returning a single boolean column aliased `as passed`. It requires all six names to exist as views (`relkind = 'v'`), authenticated to lack `SELECT`, and `service_role` to retain `SELECT`. That matches `AGENTS.md` and `scripts/test_shared_db_live_proof.py:83-88`. It does not hash view definitions; that is correct for a revoke-only change.\n\n### Scope / evidence notes (non-blocking)\n\n- This PR closes only the six named views. Remaining #2662 class findings stay with #3327 / #3328 / #3329 / #2326.\n- `.agent/completion.json:11` still records implementation `head_sha` `5f1b7daea1170a57c2a6a3db7bccb79b66ccb9b5`. The reviewed commit is the later evidence-bind at `4a76f2dbeefbde1adebc1f28e124c3e0983b706e`. Contract `db_writes` lists table aliases plus views; those are parser keys for the same six catalog views, not extra objects.\n- Later landings that copy the old `GRANT SELECT … TO authenticated, service_role` on `api.source_capture_inventory` would re-open that view; the flipped tests now fail closed if that happens.\n- `AGENTS.md` still shows `select * from api.source_capture_inventory` as an operator query. That file is outside this change set; those sessions use `service_role`/`postgres`, not the authenticated Data API.\n\n### Coverage\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n| Only authenticated `SELECT` removed | Yes, six `REVOKE`s |\n| Definitions / owners / options / policies unchanged | Yes; no `CREATE`/`ALTER`/`POLICY` |\n| `service_role` SELECT preserved | Required in tests + live probe; default privileges already granted |\n| `source_capture_inventory_exact` untouched | Yes; authenticated EXECUTE test unchanged |\n| 42 authenticated denials | 6×7 in `issue_2662_unused_view_grants_contracts.sql` |\n| 6 service reads | Same file, plus OPA fixture reads |\n| 4 sibling browser controls | Same file |\n| OPA synthetic fixtures | Retained under `service_role` |\n| CRM/PM visibility fixtures | Retained |\n| Live probe shape | `as passed`, six views, grant polarity |\n| Preview/production apply | Not authorized by this review |\n\n\n---\n## Verdict\nVERDICT: APPROVE REVIEW FINDINGS — NON-AUTHORIZING UNLESS THE MATCHING CREATE-ONLY VERDICT ARTIFACT EXISTS\n\n### Review Findings for PR #3304 (Issue #2662)\r\n\r\n#### 1.
